units.tr: [illegible, ~8 letters] through Christ, Gal. 4.5; Eph. 1.5. Adoption and election are free, Eph. 1.4, from which the salvation of men flows as from a true, innate spring, vv. 7, 13. It is commended in 1 John 3.1. Adoption as the final restoration, or the enjoyment of adoption, Rom. 8.22. The Spirit of adoption, v. 15. See SPIRIT OF ADOPTION. The adoption of the Jews, Rom. 9.4. Examples of adoption: Ephraim and Manasseh, Gen. 48.5; Moses, Exod. 2.10; Esther, Esth. 2.7. Religious adoration, Gen. 22.5; 24.26, etc. Worship, Gen. 18.2. Idolatrous worship, Exod. 20.5, etc. Unlawful worship, Zeph. 1.5; Acts 10.25; 10.19, 20; 22.8.

units.la: ADORATIO: Vide DEVS adorādus. Adorationis cultū, vt suam Sanctis deferunt, adoratione defendere possint, Angelis & hominibus tributū esse, his locis probare niituntur Notificij, Gen. 18. 2. & 19. 1. & 23. 12. & 27. 29. & 33. 3. & 42. 6. 43. 26. Exo. 18. 7. Nū. 22. 31. 1. Sam. 20. 41. & 25. 23. & 28. 14. Sam. 9. 6 & 14. 3. 1. Reg. 1 15. Esth. 3. 2. Dan. 2. 46. Act. 10. 25. Sed hæc testimonia vel exempla adorationē ciuilē tātūm reiiciūt, nō religiosā soli Deo debitā, de qua frequēs in Scripturis mētio, probatis exēplis cōfirmata. Gē. 24. 26. &c. 47 Exod. 4. 31. Ios. 5. 14. Iudic. 7. 15. Matt. 4. 10. Apoc. 19. 4. 10. & 9. Adoratio illegitima, Sophō 1. 5. Ioan. 4. 22. Act 10. 25. 10. 19. 10. Adoratio impia idololatrarū cētiēs Dānata in V. & N.
units.tr: ADORATION. See God to be adored. That the adoration which they offer to the saints may be defended as adoration, and that it is owed to angels and men, they try to prove from these places: Gen. 18.2; 19.1; 23.12; 27.29; 33.3; 42.6; 43.26; Exod. 18.7; Num. 22.31; 1 Sam. 20.41; 25.23; 28.14; 2 Sam. 9.6; 14.4; 1 Kings 1.15; Esth. 3.2; Dan. 2.46; Acts 10.25. But these testimonies or examples reject only civil adoration, not the religious adoration owed to God alone, of which Scripture makes frequent mention, confirmed by proven examples: Gen. 24.26, etc.; Exod. 4.31; Josh. 5.14; Judg. 7.15; Matt. 4.10; Rev. 19.4, 10; 22.9. Unlawful adoration, Zeph. 1.5; John 4.22; Acts 10.25. The impious adoration of idolaters is condemned throughout the Old and New Testaments.

units.la: Vide Deus adorādus. Sācti nō adorādi. Ciuilē verò, quæ ad vius huius συναξίας spectat, etiā Ministris Dei tribui posse, 1. Pet. 2. sed cautè, Isa. 42. 8. Ier. 17. 5. Quod ad duleię, latreię, & hyperduleię distinctionē attinet ineptā eā & falsā esse manifestè ostenditur ex Rom. 1. 9. & 16. 18. vbi hæc inter se commutantur. Vide
units.tr: See God to be adored. Saints are not to be adored. Civil honour, however, which relates to the use of this συναξία [synaxia, assembly], can also be given to the ministers of God, 1 Pet. 2; but cautiously, Isa. 42.8; Jer. 17.5. As for the distinction between dulia [δουλεία], latria [λατρεία] and hyperdulia [ὑπερδουλεία], that it is absurd and false is clearly shown from Rom. 1.9 and 16.18, where these terms are used interchangeably. See

units.la: VLIA. Adoratio vera & adoratores veri qui, Ioan. 4. 23.
units.tr: ADORATION. True adoration and true worshippers, John 4.23.

units.la: AMELECH, idolū Sepharuaim, 2. Reg. 17. 31. Vide IDOLOVM catalogus) in cuius igne Sepharuēi comburebant filios suos, ibid.
units.tr: ADRAMMELECH, idol of Sepharvaim, 2 Kings 17.31. See the catalogue of idols. In his fire the Sepharvites burned their sons, ibid.

units.la: AMELECH, fratris sui Sarasar subsidio vsus, patrem suum Sennacherib occidit, 2. Reg. 19. 37. Esaiæ 37. 38.
units.tr: ADRAMMELECH, with the help of his brother Sharezer, killed his father Sennacherib, 2 Kings 19.37; Isa. 37.38.

units.la: STARE, de eo etiam dici potest, qui sedet, vt Marc. 9. 1. & 11. 5. Act. 7. 55.
units.tr: STAND, can also be said of one who sits, as Mark 9.1; 11.5; Acts 7.55.

units.la: VENA: Aduenę commendantur, Exod. 22. 21. & 23. 9. Leuit. 19. Deut. 10. 19. & 24. 17. & 26. 12. Zach. 7. 10. Ezech. 22. 7. Deut. 31. 19. Psal. 146. 9. Aduenis vt Deuteronomium legatur, iubeus, Deut. 31. 12. (Vide DECIMÆ: & Peregrinus.)
units.tr: STRANGERS are commended, Exod. 22.21; 23.9; Lev. 19; Deut. 10.19; 24.17; 26.12; Zech. 7.10; Ezek. 22.7; Deut. 31.19; Ps. 146.9. The command is that Deuteronomy be read to the strangers, Deut. 31.12. (See TITHES and STRANGER.)

units.la: Adventus Domini expectandus, Matt. 24. 42. & 25. 13. & 26. 40. Mar. 13. 33. Luc. 12. 40. & 21. 34. Rō. 13. 12. Eph. 6. 18. Colos. 4. 1. 1. Thes. 5. 6. 1. Petr. 4. 7. & 5. 8. Apocal. 3. 3. & 16. 15. Aduētus Christi ad iudicium signa, Matt. 24. 4. Mar. 13. 22. vt furis in nocte, Luc. 12. 39. 1. Thess. 5. 2. 2. Petr. 3. 10. Apoc. 3. 3. & 16. 15. qualis futurus sit Luc. 17. 26. curiosa eius inquisitio damnatur, 1. Thess. 5. 1. Vide CHRISTVS.
units.tr: The coming of the Lord is to be awaited: Matt. 24.42; 25.13; 26.40; Mark 13.33; Luke 12.40; 21.34; Rom. 13.12; Eph. 6.18; Col. 4.1; 1 Thess. 5.6; 1 Pet. 4.7; 5.8; Rev. 3.3; 16.15. The signs of Christ's coming to judgment, Matt. 24.4; Mark 13.22; that he will come like a thief in the night, Luke 12.39; 1 Thess. 5.2; 2 Pet. 3.10; Rev. 3.3; 16.15. What manner of coming it will be, Luke 17.26. Curious inquiry into it is condemned, 1 Thess. 5.1. See CHRIST.

units.la: ADVERSARIVS: Aduersarij Dei, Vide DEI hostes.
units.tr: ADVERSARY: Adversaries of God. See DEI hostes.

units.la: ADVERSARII amandi. Vide INIMICI.
units.tr: ADVERSARIES, to be loved. See INIMICI.

units.la: ADVERSARII Israelitarum Iosaphat tempore mutuis viribus conciderunt, 2.Par.20.v.22.23. Aduersarij Salomonis 1.Reg.11.v.14 23. [Aduersarius noster, 1.Pet.5.8. ]
units.tr: ADVERSARIES of the Israelites: in the time of Jehoshaphat they fell by each other's hands, 2 Chron. 20.22-23. Adversaries of Solomon, 1 Kings 11.14, 23. [Our adversary, 1 Pet. 5.8.]

units.la: ADVLATIO siue assentatio, κολακία, est immodica & nimia erga alterius vel praesentis vel absentis laudatio ac praedicatio nobis facta, vt illi placeamus & applaudamus. Assentator igitur est blandus inimicus.
units.tr: FLATTERY, or fawning, κολακία [κολακία], is an immoderate and excessive praise and commendation of another, whether present or absent, offered to us so that we may please him and win his applause. A flatterer, therefore, is a smooth enemy.

FLATTERY is an evil thing and therefore to be detested: Ps. 12.4; 28.3; Prov. 24.28; 27.6, 14; 28.23; Eccles. 7.6; Matt. 12.20; 14.5; 18.15; Rom. 9.4; 12.18; 16.18; 1 Cor. 4.2; 5.7; 11.17; Gal. 6.12; 1 Thess. 1.6; 2.5.

units.la: ADVLATIONIS exempla. Core & eius complices, Numeri. Doeg Idumaeus, 1. Sam.22,9. Amalechita, 2. Sam.1,10. chab & Baana, 4.8. Absalom, 15,3. Siba, 16, 1. Sedechias Regum 22,11,2. Paral.18,10. Pseudoprophetae, 1.Reg.22. 2.Paral.18.11.Mich.3.5. Pseudoprophetae & Sacerdotes Zech.13.v.10.16. & 22.28. Ierem.6.14. & 8.11. Thren.2. niores Roboam consiliarij, 2.Paral.10. Principes Iudae 17.Hostes Iuda & Beniamin, 1.Esdr.4.14. Mamuchan, 1.16. Regis Assueri ministri, 3.4. amici Aman, eiusque Zares, 5.14. Praefecti Darij regis, Dan.6.7. Filia Herodiadis Matth.14.6. Discipuli Pharisaeorum & Herodiani, 22. Herodes Agrippa, Actor.12.3. populus adstans Herodi cionanti, v.21.22. Iudaei, 17.7. accusatores Pauli, 23.4. tullus, 24.2. Felix adulatur Iudaeis, 24,27. Festus Iudaeis 9. Agrippae, v.26. quidam schismatici Ecclesiae Romanae Rom.16.18. Adulationis punitae exempla: Core, Dathan, biron, eorumq; complices, Numer.16 v.31.32.33. Amalech ta, 2. Sam.1.15. Rechab & Baana, 4.12.
units.tr: EXAMPLES OF FLATTERY. Korah and his accomplices, Numbers. Doeg the Edomite, 1 Sam. 22.9. The Amalekite, 2 Sam. 1.10. Rechab and Baanah, 2 Sam. 4.8. Absalom, 15.3. Ziba, 16.1. Zedekiah, 1 Kings 22.11; 2 Chron. 18.10. False prophets, 1 Kings 22; 2 Chron. 18.11; Micah 3.5. False prophets and priests, Zech. 13.10, 16; 22.28; Jer. 6.14; 8.11; Lam. 2. The younger counsellors of Rehoboam, 2 Chron. 10. The princes of Judah, 17. The enemies of Judah and Benjamin, Ezra 4.14. Mamuchan, Esth. 1.16. The ministers of King Ahasuerus, Esth. 3.4. The friends of Haman, and his Zeresh, Esth. 5.14. The prefects of King Darius, Dan. 6.7. The daughter of Herodias, Matt. 14.6. The disciples of the Pharisees and the Herodians, Matt. 22. Herod Agrippa, Acts 12.3. The people standing by while Herod harangued, vv. 21-22. The Jews, Acts 17.7. The accusers of Paul, Acts 23.4. Tertullus, Acts 24.2. Felix flatters the Jews, Acts 24.27. Festus to the Jews, 25.9; to Agrippa, v. 26. Certain schismatics of the Roman Church, Rom. 16.18. Examples of punished flattery: Korah, Dathan, Abiram and their accomplices, Num. 16.31-33. The Amalekite, 2 Sam. 1.15. Rechab and Baanah, 2 Sam. 4.12.

units.la: ADVLATOR cui similis, Prouerb.29.5. quàm iniqui, Psal. 3. Adulatores Regum damnantur, Ose.7.3.
units.tr: A FLATTERER, like to one who is like this, Prov. 29.5; how wicked he is, Ps. 3. Flatterers of kings are condemned, Hos. 7.3.

units.la: ADVLTERIVM est, cùm thorus coniugalis (quod debet vnius viri cum vna muliere) à marito vel vxore violatur.
units.tr: ADULTERY is when the marriage bed, which ought to belong to one man with one woman, is violated by a husband or wife.

units.la: ADVLTERIVM damnatur & prohibetur, Gen.20.3.&26. Exod,20.14. Leuit.18.20.&20.10. Deut.5.18. & 22,v.23. Iudic.19,2.2. Sam.11.4. & 12.10. Iob.24.15. & 31.1. Psal.73. Prouer.5.v.3.8.20. & 6.v.24.32. Esa.57.3.&c. Ierem.2. 3.1. & 5.7. & 13.27. Ose.2.4. & 4.2. Malach.3.5. Matt.5.27. 14.3. & 19.18. Marc.10.19. Ioan.8.3.1. Corinth.6.10. 1.T. 4.3. Hebr.13.4. Iac. 4.4. Adulterium committere in corde. Matth.5.28. est libidinosè aspicere, & concupiscere muem nuptam, aut innuptam. Adulterium spirituale, Vide SCORTATIO spiritualis. Adulterium pro idololatria, Aooc.2.22. Adulterij mala, 2. Sam. 12.10. & 13.v.22.29. pœna, Leuit.20.10. Deut.22.v.22.23.24. Iob.31.9.c. Ioan.8.5.1.Cor.5.9 10.Heb.13.4. Adulterij & furti collatio, Prouer.6.v.29.30. Adulterium solum est quod coniugium dissoluit, Matt.5.32. Vide Marc.10.2. Luc.16.18. Adulterium ex solo intuitu, Matth.5.28.&c.
units.tr: ADULTERY is condemned and forbidden: Gen. 20.3; 26; Exod. 20.14; Lev. 18.20; 20.10; Deut. 5.18; 22.23; Judg. 19.2; 2 Sam. 11.4; 12.10; Job 24.15; 31.1; Ps. 73; Prov. 5.3, 8, 20; 6.24, 32; Isa. 57.3, etc.; Jer. 2.3; 3.1; 5.7; 13.27; Hos. 2.4; 4.2; Mal. 3.5; Matt. 5.27; 14.3; 19.18; Mark 10.19; John 8.3; 1 Cor. 6.10; 1 Tim. 4.3; Heb. 13.4; James 4.4. To commit adultery in the heart (Matt. 5.28) is to look lustfully at, and desire, a woman who is married or unmarried. Spiritual adultery: see SCORTATIO spiritualis. Adultery for idolatry: Rev. 2.22. The evil of adultery: 2 Sam. 12.10; 13.22, 29. Its punishment: Lev. 20.10; Deut. 22.22-24; Job 31.9ff.; John 8.5; 1 Cor. 5.9-10; Heb. 13.4. Comparison of adultery and theft: Prov. 6.29-30. Adultery alone is what dissolves marriage: Matt. 5.32; see Mark 10.2; Luke 16.18. Adultery from the look alone: Matt. 5.28, etc.

units.la: Adulterij exempla: Ruben, Gen.35.22. Beniamitæ, Iudic.19.25. Dauid, 2. Sam.11.4. Herodes, Matt.14.4. Marc.6.17. Luc.3.19. mulier quædam, Ioan.8.2. Corinthius incestuosus, 1. Cor.5.1. Adulterij puniti exempla: Tribus Beniamin, Iudic.20.46. Dauid, 2. Sam. 12.10. Pharao Rex Ægyp. Gen.12.17. Israelita cum Moabitide, Num.25.8. (Vide SCORTATIONIS punitæ exempla.) Achab & Sedecias, Ierem.29.23.
units.tr: EXAMPLES OF ADULTERY: Reuben, Gen. 35.22. The Benjamites, Judg. 19.25. David, 2 Sam. 11.4. Herod, Matt. 14.4; Mark 6.17; Luke 3.19. A certain woman, John 8.2. The incestuous Corinthian, 1 Cor. 5.1. Examples of punished adultery: The tribe of Benjamin, Judg. 20.46. David, 2 Sam. 12.10. Pharaoh, king of Egypt, Gen. 12.17. An Israelite with a Moabite woman, Num. 25.8 (see the punished examples under SCORTATIO). Ahab and Zedekiah, Jer. 29.23.

units.la: ADULTERI à regno Dei excludendi, 1. Cor.6.9. Hebr.13.4. Adulteræ remittuntur peccata, Ioan.8.3. Adulterorum appellatio, Iac.4.4. metaphoricè sumpta, visitato sacro Scripturæ more, pro iis, qui Dei amori mundum & suas voluptates anteponunt.
units.tr: ADULTERERS are to be excluded from the kingdom of God, 1 Cor. 6.9; Heb. 13.4. Adulterous women have their sins forgiven, John 8.3. The term "adulterers" (James 4.4), used metaphorically, according to the custom of Holy Scripture, refers to those who put the world and its pleasures before the love of God.

units.la: Adulter, Idololatra, impius, Esai.57.3.8. Ierem.9.2. Adulterinus, Spurius, Hebr.12.8. mundi voluptatibus planè addictus, Iacob.4.4.
units.tr: Adulterer: an idolater, an impious man, Isa. 57.3, 8; Jer. 9.2. Adulterine, a bastard, Heb. 12.8. Wholly given over to the pleasures of the world, James 4.4.

units.la: Adultera mulier, Leuit.20.10. Deut.22.12. Iudic.11.2. Prou.30.20. Ezech.16.32.38. & 23.45. Osee 3.1. & 4.13. Rom.7.3. Adulterina, degener Matth.12.39 & 16.4. Marc.8.38. Idolatra, impia, Ezech.23.45. mundi profanis deliciis vendita, Iac.4.4.
units.tr: Adulterous woman: Lev. 20.10; Deut. 22.12; Judg. 11.2; Prov. 30.20; Ezek. 16.32, 38; 23.45; Hos. 3.1; 4.13; Rom. 7.3. Adulterine, degenerate: Matt. 12.39; 16.4; Mark 8.38. An idolatrous, impious woman, Ezek. 23.45. Sold to the profane delights of the world, James 4.4.

units.la: Adulterans, 1. adulterium committens, Osee.7.4. Cauponans, corrumpens, 2. Cor.2.17.&4.2. Adulterata, impio cultu polluta, Ezech.23.37.
units.tr: Adulterating: (1) committing adultery, Hos. 7.4; (2) peddling, corrupting, 2 Cor. 2.17; 4.2. Adulterated, polluted by impious worship, Ezek. 23.37.

units.la: Adulterium, Idololatria, impietas in Deum, Ierem.13.27. Ezech.23.43. Osee.2.2.]
units.tr: Adultery, idolatry, impiety against God: Jer. 13.27; Ezek. 23.43; Hos. 2.2.]

units.la: DVOCATVS noster. Vide CHRISTVS, & πϋρ ἀκλητος.
units.tr: Our ADVOCATE. See CHRIST, and [παράκλητος].

units.la: DVRAM, Quæstor ærarius Dauidis, 2. Sam.20.24. postea minister à tributis ipsi Roboam, lapidibus obruitur, 1. Reg.12.18.2. Paral.10.18.
units.tr: ADORAM, the treasurer of David, 2 Sam. 20.24; afterwards minister over the tribute under Rehoboam himself, he was stoned with stones, 1 Kings 12.18; 2 Chron. 10.18.

units.la: DVRAM, vrbis à Roboamo ædificatæ nomen, 2. Paral.11.v.6.9.
units.tr: ADORAIM, the name of a city built by Rehoboam, 2 Chron. 11.6, 9.

units.la: EDIFICARE, Domum quam ædificant impij, vt plurimùm non habitant, Deuter.28.30. domus recens ædificata Deut. 20,5. [metaphoricè significat, formare de materia præiacen. Genes 2 22. Continuare munus & posteritatem, 1. Sam. 2.35. & 2 Reg. 11.38. Dare nomen familiæ, Ruth. 4,11. Ecclesiam injtau-re, Psal. 51,20. & 69,36. & 102.17. & 147,2. Pro. 9,1. Cant. 8, Esai. 58.12. & 60.10. & 61,4. Ierem. 30,18. & 31,4,28. Amos 4.14. Mich. 7,11. Matth. 16,18. Act. 20.32. Rom. 15,20. Instaurare, erigere, homines fouere & pristinæ conditioni restituere, Iob. 22, Psal. 28,5. Ierem. 12,16. & 18,9. & 24.6. & 31,28. & 33, 7. & 45, 10. & 45,4. Malach. 1,4. Premere dolorib. Thren. 3,5. Promou-re, institutum opus perficere, Psal. 127, 1. Regere Eccl. Remp. bene aut male, Ierem. 1,10. Ezech. 13, 10. Habac. 2. Rem domesticam curare ut decet, Prou. 14, 1. & 24, 3, mortuum corpus suscitare, Mar. 14,58. Sapienter disponere, Amos 9.6. Stabilire, Psal. 89,3,5. Seipsum & alios in vera pietate instituere, 1. Cor. 8 1,10. & 10,23. & 14,4,17. Galat. 2,18. & 1. Thes. 5.11.
units.tr: TO BUILD. A house which the impious build, for the most part they do not inhabit, Deut. 28.30. A newly built house, Deut. 20.5. [Metaphorically it means: to form from matter lying ready, Gen. 2.22; to continue an office and posterity, 1 Sam. 2.35; 2 Kings 11.38; to give a name to a family, Ruth 4.11; to build up the Church, Ps. 51.20; 69.36; 102.17; 147.2; Prov. 9.1; Song 8; Isa. 58.12; 60.10; 61.4; Jer. 30.18; 31.4, 28; Amos 9.14; Mic. 7.11; Matt. 16.18; Acts 20.32; Rom. 15.20; to restore, raise up, cherish people and return them to their former condition, Job 22; Ps. 28.5; Jer. 12.16; 18.9; 24.6; 31.28; 33.7; 45.4, 10; Mal. 1.4; to weigh down with sorrows, Lam. 3.5; to advance and bring to completion a work begun, Ps. 127.1; to govern the Church or commonwealth well or badly, Jer. 1.10; Ezek. 13.10; Hab. 2; to manage household affairs as is fitting, Prov. 14.1; 24.3; to raise a dead body, Mark 14.58; to arrange wisely, Amos 9.6; to establish, Ps. 89.3, 5; to instruct oneself and others in true piety, 1 Cor. 8.1, 10; 10.23; 14.4, 17; Gal. 2.18; 1 Thess. 5.11.]

units.la: [AEDES, domus, Genes. 39. 5. Exo. 12.13. Leuit. 14,34. & 25. Deut. 19,1. Iudic. 18, 22. Latibula, Mich. 7,17. Palatia, Sphæ-dicæ habitationes, Esth. 2,14. Pro. 30 28. Esai. 13,22. Amos 1, 12. & 2, 2, 5. & 3, 9, 10, 11, 15. Templum Dei, 2. Reg. 11,11 Chron. 29.3.19. Nehem 6.10. Ezech. 41.v.26. Luc. 11.51. Templum idoli, 2. Reg. 10. 27. Templum idoli effigies, Act. 24.]
units.tr: [HOUSE, dwelling: Gen. 39.5; Exod. 12.13; Lev. 14.34; 25; Deut. 19.1; Judg. 18.22. Hiding places, Mic. 7.17. Palaces, the women's dwellings, Esth. 2.14; Prov. 30.28; Isa. 13.22; Amos 1.12; 2.2, 5; 3.9, 10, 11, 15. The Temple of God, 2 Kings 11.11; 1 Chron. 29.3, 19; Neh. 6.10; Ezek. 41.26; Luke 11.51. A temple of an idol, 2 Kings 10.27. An image of the temple of an idol, Acts 24.]

units.la: AEDIFICATIO Dei, 1. Cor. 3.9. edificationi in primis seruiendum, Rom. 14.19. & 15.2. 1. Cor. 10.24. & 14.v.3,5,12,19,26. Cor. 10.8. & 12.19. Eph. 4.ver.12.29, Col. 4,6.1. Thes. 4. 12. 5.11.1. Tim. 1,4.2. Tim. 2.v.14.15. Tit. 1.9. & 2 1. Hebr. 5. 12. Petr. 2.12. Aedificatio pars prophetiæ, 1. Cor. 14.3. Aedificandi verbo, Rom. 14.19. 1. Corint. 8.1. & alibi, ματα ποιεῖν, sæpe apud Paulum significantur omnia officia, quæ proximo debemus, vel ut Christo adiungatur, vel ut ei iam adiunctus quotidie magis ac magis coalescat. Dicitur enim fideles esse templum Dei, in quo videlicet per Spiritum sanctum resideat, Rom. 8, 11.1. Cor. 3.16. & 6,19.2. Cor. 6.1. Et totus fidelium cœtus ingenti alicui ciuitati, id est, nouæ Hierusalem comparatur, ex ipsis fidelibus quasi viuis lapidibus constructæ, ut perelegantèr ac plane diuinitùs scribitur, Esaiæ 54.v.11. Apocal. 21.v.16. Aedificandi verbum in vitio positum, 1. Cor. 8.10.
units.tr: EDIFICATION of God, 1 Cor. 3.9. Edification must above all be served: Rom. 14.19; 15.2; 1 Cor. 10.24; 14.3, 5, 12, 19, 26; 2 Cor. 10.8; 12.19; Eph. 4.12, 29; Col. 4.6; 1 Thess. 4.12; 5.11; 1 Tim. 1.4; 2 Tim. 2.14-15; Titus 1.9; 2.1; Heb. 5.12; 1 Pet. 2.12. Edification is part of prophecy, 1 Cor. 14.3. Edifying by the word, Rom. 14.19; 1 Cor. 8.1, and elsewhere. [οἰκοδομεῖν] is often used by Paul to signify all the duties we owe to our neighbour, either to join him to Christ or, once joined, to grow together with him more and more each day. For the faithful are said to be the temple of God, in which, namely, the Holy Spirit dwells: Rom. 8.11; 1 Cor. 3.16; 6.19; 2 Cor. 6.16. And the whole assembly of the faithful is compared to some great city, that is, the new Jerusalem, built out of the faithful themselves as living stones, as is written most elegantly and plainly by divine inspiration: Isa. 54.11; Rev. 21.16. The word "to build" is used in a bad sense in 1 Cor. 8.10.

units.la: AEGRITVDO: Aegritudinis causa peccatum est, Exo. 15.2. Leuit. 26.16. Num. 12.1. &c. Deut. 7.15. & 28.27. 2. Sam. 2. 15.2. Regum 5,27.2. Paral. 21.18. Ioan. 5. 14, Exemla: Aegpti otij,Exodi,9.10. units.tr: SICKNESS: Sickness is caused by sin: Exod. 15.2; Lev. 26.16; Num. 12.1, etc.; Deut. 7.15; 28.27; 2 Sam. 2.15; 2 Kings 5.27; 2 Chron. 21.18; John 5.14. Examples: the plague of Egypt, Exod. 9.10; the pestilence sent for David's sin, 2 Sam. 24.15; Gehazi, 2 Kings 5.27; the leprosy of Uzziah, inflicted from heaven, 2 Chron. 26.21; the sores with which David was struck, Ps. 38.6; the paralytic, Matt. 9.2; the man who was infirm for thirty-eight years, John 5.5; the Corinthians, 1 Cor. 11.29-30; the extraordinary disease of King Jehoram, on account of idolatry, 2 Chron. 21.19. See MORBUS. God the Healer, Exod. 15.26.

units.la: AGROTI olim vngebantur oleo, non sacramento salutis æ- ternæ consequendæ,vt nonnulli impie nugantur,sed valetudinis miraculo reparandæ causa,Iac.5.v.14 15. Exemplum: Apostolo,Marc.6.13. ægroti sanantur ad vmbram Petri,Actor.5.15.ad tactum fudar.jPaul.19.12.Aegroti variis morbis curati. Vide MIRACVLA.
units.tr: THE SICK were formerly anointed with oil, not as a sacrament for obtaining eternal salvation, as some impiously babble, but for the purpose of restoring health by a miracle, James 5.14-15. Example: by the Apostles, Mark 6.13. The sick were cured in the shadow of Peter, Acts 5.15; by touching Paul's handkerchiefs, Acts 19.12. Sick people cured of various diseases. See MIRACLES.

units.la: Aegroti visitandi & consolandi sunt, Genesis, 48.1.2.Reg.8.9 & 13 14.Iob.2.11.Psalm.41.4.Eccles.7 39.&38.13 Matth.5.v.37.40 Ioan.11.3 2.Corint.1.4.Rom.14.7.&10.13. Ezech.18.21.&33.11.1.Thess.4,13 c. Quomodo se viri Sancti in morbo & decessu ab hac vita gesserint,legatur Gen.49.1.&c.50.24.Deu.31,22.Ios.13.1.&c.23.1.&c.24 1.&c.1.Sam.2,1.&c.2.Reg.2.v.1,7.2.Paral.32,24.Esaiæ 38.1. Aegrotorum munus,Iac.5.14. Ps.50.15. post recuperatam sanationem:Ezechias,Isa,39.9.ferè ad finem vsque. Dauid, Ps. 103. Mulier quædam:Luc. 13.13. Vnus ex decem leprosis, Luc.17.12.V.Eccles.38.9.
units.tr: The sick are to be visited and comforted: Gen. 48.1, 2; 2 Kings 8.9, 13–14; Job 2.11; Ps. 41.4; Eccles. 7.39, 38.13; Matt. 5.37, 40; John 11.3; 2 Cor. 1.4; Rom. 14.7, 10.13; Ezek. 18.21, 33.11; 1 Thess. 4.13. How the holy men conducted themselves in sickness and at their death may be read at Gen. 49.1 etc., 50.24; Deut. 31.22; Josh. 13.1 etc., 23.1 etc., 24.1 etc.; 1 Sam. 2.1 etc.; 2 Kings 2.1, 7; 2 Chron. 32.24; Isa. 38.1. The duty of the sick: James 5.14; Ps. 50.15. After recovery: Hezekiah, Isa. 39.9, almost to the end. David, Ps. 103. A certain woman, Luke 13.13. One of the ten lepers, Luke 17.12. See Ecclus. 38.9.

units.la: EGYPTIACA captivitas prædicitur, Genes. 15,13. incipit, Exod.1,8.Act.7,18 ex tus ex ea promittitur, Genes. 15, 16. & 48.21.& 50.24. Exodi 3,17.& 6,6. adimplctur, & exeunt sexcenta millia virorum.Exodi 12. v.37. 51 & 13,1.&c.14,1.&c.Num.33,1.Deut.16,1.Osææ 13,4.Mich 6.4. In Aegyptū redire improbe flagitat populus,Exod.14, 11. & 16,3. & 17, 3.Num. 11, 5.& 14, 4. & 20. 3. Aegyptiaca redemptio frequenter in memoriam revocatur, tanquam summum Dei beneficium,Exod.20 2.Leuitici 22,33.&26,13. Deut.4.37. &5,6.&7,8.&8 14 & 16 6.Iud.2.1.&6 8.1.Sam.10,18.2.Reg.17.7.Mich.6,4.
units.tr: The Egyptian captivity is foretold at Gen. 15.13; it begins at Exod. 1.8 and Acts 7.18. Deliverance from it is promised at Gen. 15.16, 48.21, 50.24; Exod. 3.17, 6.6. It is fulfilled, and six hundred thousand men come out: Exod. 12.37, 13.1 etc., 14.1 etc.; Num. 33.1; Deut. 16.1; Hos. 13.4; Mic. 6.4. The people wickedly demand to return into Egypt: Exod. 14.11, 16.3, 17.3; Num. 11.5, 14.4, 20.3. The redemption from Egypt is often brought to mind as the highest benefit of God: Exod. 20.2; Lev. 22.33, 26.13; Deut. 4.37, 5.6, 7.8, 8.14, 16.6; Judg. 2.1, 6.8; 1 Sam. 10.18; 2 Kings 17.7; Mic. 6.4.

units.la: Aegyptus (regio media inter Africam & Asiam) variis plagis affligitur, Exodi 7,1.&c.8,1. &c.9,1.&c.10.1.&c.11.1.&.vt prædixit Dominus,Genes.15,14. Exodi 3,19. expugnatur à Rege Babyloniæ,2.Reg.24 7.Ierem.46,2. [Aegyptus mystica, Apoc.11,8.] Aegyptij prodeunt in pugnam cōtra Iudam,2.Par.12,2. Aegypti captivitas reducenda, Ezech 29.14. Aegypti idola destruenda, Ezech. 30,13. Plagæ Psalm. 78.v.48,49.50.51.52.53.& 105.v.26. uique ad v.39.& 135,v[?] 8.9.& 136.ver. 10.15. Eius vastatio ac ruina prædicitur,E[?] 19.v.1.2.3.4.& 20.3.Ierem.43.11.& 44.30.& 46. v.2.14.[?] &c.Ezech.29.1.&c.& 30. 1.&c.31. 1.&c.32,12. Ioël.3.19. Ægyptij Iudæis non abominandi,Deuter.23.7.cum Hebr[?] non comedebant, Genef. 43, 32. aquis obruti pereu[?] Exodi 14. 27. Psalm.106. 11. eorum conuersio prædicit[?] Esa.19.v.18,22. AEgyptiorum & Assyriorum collatio, E[?] 52.4.
units.tr: Egypt (a country lying between Africa and Asia) is afflicted with various plagues: Exod. 7.1 etc., 8.1 etc., 9.1 etc., 10.1 etc., 11.1 etc., as the Lord foretold at Gen. 15.14 and Exod. 3.19. It is conquered by the king of Babylon: 2 Kings 24.7; Jer. 46.2. [Mystical Egypt, Rev. 11.8.] The Egyptians go out to battle against Judah: 2 Chron. 12.2. The captivity of Egypt is to be reversed: Ezek. 29.14. The idols of Egypt are to be destroyed: Ezek. 30.13. The plagues: Ps. 78.48–53 and 105.26 onwards to v. 39; Ps. 135.8–9; Ps. 136.10, 15. Its devastation and ruin are foretold: Ezek. 19.1–4, 20.3; Jer. 43.11, 44.30, 46.2, 14 etc.; Ezek. 29.1 etc., 30.1 etc., 31.1 etc., 32.12; Joel 3.19. The Egyptians were not to be abominated by the Jews: Deut. 23.7; they did not eat with the Hebrews, Gen. 43.32. Overwhelmed by the waters, they perished: Exod. 14.27; Ps. 106.11. Their conversion is foretold: Isa. 19.18, 22. Comparison of the Egyptians and the Assyrians: Isa. 52.4.

units.la: AELAM nomen regionis, unde Elamitæ principes Persid[?] Esai.11. 11. Ierem.25.25.& 49,34. Ezech.32.24. Dan.8.[?] eius excidium prædicitur, Ierem. 49.36. eius restitutio[?] 38.39.
units.tr: ELAM, the name of a region, whence the Elamite princes came: Isa. 11.11; Jer. 25.25, 49.34; Ezek. 32.24; Dan. 8.2. Its destruction is foretold at Jer. 49.36; its restoration at Jer. 49.38–39.

units.la: [AELAM F.Sem.Gen.10.22. F. Sefac Beniamitæ,1.Par.8.2[?] Ianitor templi,1.Par.26.3. nomen duorum ex primorib[?] post reditum.Esdr.2.7.31.Nehem.7.12.34.]
units.tr: [ELAM, son of Shem, Gen. 10.22. Elam, son of Shephatiah the Benjamite, 1 Chron. 8.2? Gatekeeper of the temple, 1 Chron. 26.3. The name of two of the first families after the return: Ezra 2.7, 31; Neh. 7.12, 34.]

units.la: ÆMVLATIO,est duplex: nam & in laude & in vitio hoc n[?] men ponitur.In laude, Aemulatio ζῆλος, est virtutis alie[?] imitatio,1.Cor.12.31. Ambite dona potiora. Altera in [?] tio,quæ vulgo φθόνος vocatur,est ægritudo,si eo, quod q[?] concupierit alius potiatur,ipse careat.
units.tr: EMULATION is twofold, for the word is used both in praise and in blame. In praise, emulation (zēlos) is the imitation of a virtue: 1 Cor. 12.31, "Covet earnestly the better gifts." The other kind, commonly called envy (phthonos), is a distress, if another attains what one has himself desired and one lacks it.

units.la: ÆMVLATIO damnatur,Rom.13.13.2.Cor.12.20.Gal.5.20.I[?] 3.14. Vide ZELVS. Aemulationis damnatæ exempla: Iofu[?] Numer. 11.28. Pharisæi, Matth. 9.11. Apostoli,Luc.9.4[?] Ioannis discipuli,Ioan.3.26.Exorcistæ Iudæi,Act.19.13.[?]
units.tr: EMULATION is condemned: Rom. 13.13; 2 Cor. 12.20; Gal. 5.20; James 3.14. See ZEAL. Examples of condemned emulation: Joshua, Num. 11.28; the Pharisees, Matt. 9.11; the Apostles, Luke 9.49; the disciples of John, John 3.26; the Jewish exorcists, Acts 19.13.

units.la: [Aemulatio,feruor.Hebr.10.27.Inuidia,Rom.13.13.Zelus,R[?] 10.2.2.Cor.7.7.11.& 9.2.Philip. 3. 6. Zelotypia, Psal. 78.[?] Cantic.8.6.Ezech.8.3.Amor vehemens 2.Cor, 11.2.
units.tr: [Emulation, fervour: Heb. 10.27. Envy, Rom. 13.13. Zeal, Rom. 10.2; 2 Cor. 7.7, 11, 9.2; Phil. 3.6. Jealousy, Ps. 78; Song 8.6; Ezek. 8.3. Vehement love: 2 Cor. 11.2.]

units.la: Aemulator,i.Zelotes Deus dicitur,Exod.34.14.Deut.4.24.[?] 5.9.& 6 15.Ios24.19.Nahum.1.2.]
units.tr: The emulator, that is, the zealot, is called God: Exod. 34.14; Deut. 4.24, 5.9, 6.15; Josh. 24.19; Nah. 1.2.]

units.la: Aeneas paralyticus virtute Christi à Petro curatur,Act.[?] 34.
units.tr: Aeneas, a paralytic, is healed by Peter through the power of Christ: Acts 9.34.

units.la: AENIGMA,pro obscuritate.1. Cor.13.12. Aenigma Samsoni[?] Iudic. 14. 14. Aenigmata Solomoni proposita, 1. Re[?] 10.1.
units.tr: ENIGMA, for obscurity: 1 Cor. 13.12. The riddle of Samson: Judg. 14.14. The riddles of Solomon proposed: 1 Kings 10.1.

units.la: AENON,iuxta Salim oppidum,haud longè à Iordane,vbi b[?] ptizabat Iohannes, Ioh.3.23.
units.tr: AENON, a town near Salim, not far from the Jordan, where John was baptising: John 3.23.

units.la: AEQVALITAS: inter diuites & pauperes sanctos,2. Cor.8.1[?] 14.15.
units.tr: EQUALITY: among the rich and the poor saints: 2 Cor. 8.14–15.

units.la: AEQVITAS priuata,ἰσότης, est hominis cuiusuis priuati,q[?] tolerat infirmitatem proximi.2. Tegit arcana errata.3. An[?] bigua facta aut dicta nō in deteriore,sed potius in melio[?] parten parte interpretatur: vbi non apparent manifesta malitiæ indicia: sed fanat arcana delicta, doctrina, consilio, admonitione, & fraterna obiurgatione. Denique remittit offensas, cedit de iure suo, cùm in bonis defendendis ac retinendis, tùm in malis propulsandis ac iniurijs vlciscendis, pacis retinendæ causâ. Phil.4,5. Moderatio vestra, τὸ ἐπιεικὲς ὑμῶν omnibus hominibus innotescat.
units.tr: Private EQUITY (isotēs) belongs to any private person who bears with the weakness of his neighbour. (1) It covers hidden errors. (2) It interprets doubtful deeds or words in the better part rather than the worse, where no clear signs of malice appear, and it heals hidden faults by teaching, counsel, admonition and brotherly rebuke. (3) Finally, it forgives offences and gives up its own right, both in defending and keeping good things and in warding off evils and avenging injuries, for the sake of keeping peace. Phil. 4.5: "Let your moderation (to epieikes hymōn) be known to all men."

units.la: Summa est ϑεμείεα Christi, qui poenas peccatorum nostrorum in se transtulit, pro inimicis orauit, & resipiscentibus omnib. peccatoribus perpetuò veniam paratam reliquit.
units.tr: The sum is the clemency of Christ, who took the punishments of our sins upon himself, prayed for his enemies, and left pardon always ready for all sinners who repent.

units.la: Æquitas est durioris legis sententiæ mitigatio quædam ex æqua & humana mentis illius interpretatione.
units.tr: Equity is a certain softening of the severity of a law, by a fair and humane interpretation of its meaning.

units.la: QVITAS sectanda, Psal.37,37. Aequitatis & iustitiæ exempla: Abraham, Genes.13,8. Iacob,30,v.31,32,33. Iosua cum Principibus, Ios.9.19. Filiæ Salphaad, Numer. 27,7. Adonibezech, Iudic.1.v.6,7. Samuel.1. Sam.15,v.32,33. Dauid,1.Sam. 6.23,& 30,23.2. Sam. 24,24. Assuerus, Esth. 7,9. Darius Daniel.6,24. Homo regius, Matt.18.34. Nicodemus, Ioan. 7,51. Tribunus profanus, Act. 21,38. Vide IVSTITIAE exempla.
units.tr: EQUITY is to be pursued: Ps. 37.37. Examples of equity and justice: Abraham, Gen. 13.8; Jacob, 30.31–33; Joshua with the princes, Josh. 9.19; the daughters of Zelophehad, Num. 27.7; Adoni-bezek, Judg. 1.6–7; Samuel, 1 Sam. 15.32–33; David, 1 Sam. 16.23 and 30.23; 2 Sam. 24.24; Ahasuerus, Esther 7.9; Darius, Dan. 6.24; the king's servant, Matt. 18.34; Nicodemus, John 7.51; the profane tribune, Acts 21.38. See examples of JUSTICE.

units.la: EQVANIMITAS, Est fortitudo animi, per quam eundem animum semper in omnibus rebus retinemus, ne in rebus secundis extollamur, vel aduersis frangamur.1.Cor. 7.30. ER(Act.22.23.1.Cor.9 26. 1.Thess.4.17.Apoc.9.2.) Est elementū subtilissimū, humidū & calidū, gravius igne, terra & aqua levius, respirationis & emissionis vocis causa: incolor, i. suapte natura colorem non possidens, nitidum, translucens (nam luminis est susceptiuū,) & tribus sensibus nostris subseruiens (per ipsum enim videmus, audimus, & olfacim) susceптiuū caloris & frigoris, siccitatis & humiditatis.
units.tr: EQUANIMITY is strength of mind, by which we keep the same mind in all things, so that we are neither lifted up in prosperity nor broken in adversity: 1 Cor. 7.30. AIR (Acts 22.23; 1 Cor. 9.26; 1 Thess. 4.17; Rev. 9.2) is the most subtle element, moist and warm, heavier than fire, lighter than earth and water, and the cause of breathing and of the emission of voice. It is colourless, that is, by its nature possesses no colour; it is bright and transparent (for it receives light), and it serves our three senses (for through it we see, hear and smell). It is receptive of heat and cold, of dryness and moisture.

units.la: AERVMNA, ægritudo animi & corporis, Genes.3.16. Eccl.2, 23.&5.16. Marc.4,19.2.Cor.11.27.]
units.tr: ANGUISH, distress of mind and body: Gen. 3.16; Eccles. 2.23, 5.16; Mark 4.19; 2 Cor. 11.27.]

units.la: ETATVM & personarum officia describuntur, Tit.2,1.&c. V. suis locis singulas ætates.
units.tr: The duties of the ages and persons are described: Titus 2.1 etc. See the individual ages in their own places.

units.la: AETERNI vocabulū accipitur proprie & improprie.1.Proprie, pro eo quod caret principio & fine. Sic Deus dicitur Aeternus, Gen.21,32. Exod.3,14. Psa.90,2.& 93,2.& 102,13. Esai.43,10. Thren.5,19. Ioan.17,5. Rom.16,26. 1. Timoth. 1,17. Quoties Iehouæ nomen in scripturis occurrit, pro ratione circunstantiarū loci occurrentis vel de Deo essentialiter, vel personaliter cōsiderato sumitur. Vide Exo.20, 2. Esai.45,5. Ephes.1,4. Apoc.1,4,8. Hose.12,10. Amos,5,8.
units.tr: The word ETERNAL is taken properly and improperly. (1) Properly, for that which has neither beginning nor end. So God is called eternal: Gen. 21.33; Exod. 3.14; Ps. 90.2, 93.2, 102.13; Isa. 43.10; Lam. 5.19; John 17.5; Rom. 16.26; 1 Tim. 1.17. Whenever the name Jehovah occurs in Scripture, it is taken, according to the circumstances of the place, either of God considered essentially or of God considered personally. See Exod. 20.2; Isa. 45.5; Eph. 1.4; Rev. 1.4, 8; Hos. 12.10; Amos 5.8.

units.la: 14. Psalm. 135. 3. Ioan. 1 1. & iæpissime sequentib. capitib. Edilius æternus dicitur. Hebr. 7.24. 2. Non ita proprie vocabulum Aeterni sumitur, i. pro verustissimo quolibet, quod proprie sempiternum appellamus: quod videlicet cum tempore incœpit esse, & in tempore esse desinit. Dicitur autem Sempiternum, quasi semper æternum, i. sen per cum tempore durans. Sic Mundus & Tempus sempiterna sunt, quæ tamen æterna etiam, sed improprie, dicuntur, vt Apostolus, 2. Timoth. 1 9. & Tit. 1, 2. tempora æterna appellantur, quæ finem habitura sunt. Apocal. 10 6. Montes æterni dicuntur, qui ab initio conditi sunt. (De mundi fine lege Matth. 24. 38. 1. Corinth. 7, 30. 1. Ioan. 2, 17.) 2. Pro diuturno seu longiore tempore, quod proprie Temporale dicitur, quod in tempore incœpit & desinit esse. Sic tribuitur Aeterni vocabulum Sacrificiis veteribus, Leuitic. 6. 22. duraturis vsque ad Christi manifestationem per Euangelium, Sacerdotio Christi, 1 Psalm. 110. 4. Hebr. 5. 6. & 7, 17. Hic Aeternitas vsque ad mundi finem extenditur, quando Mediatoris officium cessabit, deletis Ecclesiæ aduersariis, quum Deus erit omnia in omnibus. 3. Pro Perpetuo, quod in tempore incœpit esse, sed caret fine. Hoc sensu tribuitur verbo Dei prædicato, Esai. 40, 8. 1. Petr. 1, 25. Illius efficacia manet in æternum, ministerium vero quale instutum est in Ecclesia militante, cessabit in die resurrectionis novissimæ. Tribuitur etiam cælo & terræ, quo eorum substantiam. Et igni gehennæ, Matth. 25, 41. Vitæ beatæ in cælis, Ioan. 3. 16, 36. Morti, 2. Thessal. 1, 9. Iudicio, ab effectu, Hebr. 6, 2. Testamento, Hebr. 13. 20. Angelis electis, animabus, Dei gloriæ & operibus superis cælestibus.
units.tr: Ps. 135.3; John 1.1, and very often in the following chapters. Hence the Eternal One is so called: Heb. 7.24. (2) The word eternal is not taken so properly, that is, for any very ancient thing, which we properly call sempiternal: that which began with time and ceases to be in time. It is called sempiternal, as if "always eternal," that is, enduring always with time. Thus the world and time are sempiternal, which are nevertheless also called eternal, though improperly, as in the Apostle, 2 Tim. 1.9 and Titus 1.2, where times are called eternal which are destined to have an end. Rev. 10.6: mountains are called eternal which were founded from the beginning. (On the end of the world see Matt. 24.38; 1 Cor. 7.30; 1 John 2.17.) (3) For a long or longer time, which is properly called temporal, that which began in time and ceases to be. The name eternal is given thus to the old sacrifices, Lev. 6.22, which were to endure until the manifestation of Christ through the Gospel; to the priesthood of Christ, Ps. 110.4; Heb. 5.6, 7.17. Here eternity extends until the end of the world, when the office of the Mediator will cease, the adversaries of the Church being destroyed, when God will be all in all. (4) For perpetual, which began to be in time but has no end. In this sense it is given to the word of God preached, Isa. 40.8; 1 Pet. 1.25. Its efficacy remains for ever; but the ministry, as it is established in the militant Church, will cease on the day of the last resurrection. It is also given to heaven and earth, as to their substance; and to the fire of hell, Matt. 25.41; to the blessed life in heaven, John 3.16, 36; to death, 2 Thess. 1.9; to judgement, from its effect, Heb. 6.2; to the testament, Heb. 13.20; to the elect angels, to souls, to the glory of God and to the heavenly works above.

units.la: AETHIOPIA, regio Aphricæ ampla, eius excidium prædicitur, Esaiæ 20 3. Soph. 2 12. Aethiopes vincuntur ab Asa 2. Paral. 14, 12. Aethiopem baptizat Philippus. Act. 8, 38.
units.tr: ETHIOPIA, a large region of Africa. Its destruction is foretold: Isa. 20.3; Zeph. 2.12. The Ethiopians are conquered by Asa: 2 Chron. 14.12. Philip baptises an Ethiopian: Acts 8.38.

units.la: V. CHVS. (ἀιθ. ἐφ, ardens.
units.tr: See CHUS (Hebrew, "burning").

units.la: AFFECTVS, πάθος, est animi commotio naturalis, per quam ad aliquid expetendum sponte ferimur. Affectus, quidam laudabiles, quidam non.
units.tr: AFFECTION, pathos, is a natural stirring of the mind, by which we are carried spontaneously towards something to be desired. Some affections are praiseworthy, some are not.

units.la: AFFECTVS mortificandi, Vide CARO, Affectus humani exempla: Moyses filiis Caath propinquis suis nullum dedit plaustrum, &c. Numer. 7. v. 8. 9. morituros soli cite rogauit Dominum, 27. v. 15, 16. Iosua tribui suæ partem dedit portionem, Iof. 17, 14. Eli, 1. Sam. 4. v. 17. 18.
units.tr: Affections to be mortified: see FLESH. Examples of human affections: Moses gave no wagon to his kinsmen, the sons of Kohath, etc., Num. 7.8–9; he asked the Lord alone for those about to die, 27.15–16; Joshua gave his tribe a portion, a share, Josh. 17.14; Eli, 1 Sam. 4.17–18.

units.la: Christus, Matth. 12. v. 49. 50. Ioan. 19. 26. Mater filiorum Zebedæi, Matth. 20. 21. Affectus inter le contrarij, Matth. 8. 8. 8. Ioan. 21. 18. Roman. 7. 15. Galat. 5. 17. 1. Petr. 1, 6.
units.tr: Christ, Matt. 12:49–50; John 19:26. The mother of the sons of Zebedee, Matt. 20:21. Conflicting affections: Matt. 8:8; 8:8; John 21:18; Rom. 7:15; Gal. 5:17; 1 Pet. 1:6.

units.la: FINITAS, συγγένεια, propinquitas ex cognati nuptiis contracta, vel hominum affinium inter ipsos coniunctio.
units.tr: AFFINITY [συγγένεια]: kinship contracted through marriage with relatives, or the connection between persons who are related by marriage.

units.la: FINITAs: Affinitas impiorum noxia, Exod. 34. 16. Deu. 7. v. 3. 4. 2. Cor. 6, 14. Exemplum: Ochosias, 2. Reg. 8. 27. Salomo, 1. Reg. 11. 1. Affinitatis gradus in lege prohibiti, Levit. 18. v. 6. usque ad 18.
units.tr: AFFINITY: The affinity of the wicked is harmful, Exod. 34:16; Deut. 7:3–4; 2 Cor. 6:14. Examples: Ahaziah, 2 Kings 8:27; Solomon, 1 Kings 11:1. The degrees of affinity forbidden in the law, Lev. 18:6 to 18.

units.la: AFFIRMATIONES interdum apud Hebræos per interrogationem efferri solitæ, Ioan. 6. 70.
units.tr: AFFIRMATIONS, which the Hebrews sometimes express by means of a question, John 6:70.

units.tr: Second, because they are themselves a source of great consolation to the godly, and they are honourable: John 21:19; Acts 5:41; Gal. 6:17; Eph. 3:13; Phil. 1:20; 1 Pet. 4:14, 16; Rev. 14:13.

units.tr: Fourthly, because the afflictions of Christ and of the faithful are common: Matt. 25:42, 45; John 15:18, 20; Acts 9:4; 22:7; 9:5; 22:8; Rom. 8:28, 29; 2 Cor. 1:5; 4:10; 13:4; Phil. 3:8; Col. 1:24; Phil. 1:23; 1 Pet. 1:11; 4:13; 5:9.

Fifthly, because they are foreordained for the godly and therefore inevitable, and very useful: Job 2:10; 5:9; Matt. 5:10; 10:17, 38; 16:20, 21, 24; 20:23; 24:9; Mark 2:19; 8:31, 34; 13:9, 13, 37; Luke 9:23; 14:27; 18:31, 32, 33; 21:12; 24:46.

units.tr: LAMB: the offering of a lamb, Lev. 3:7. The Paschal lamb, Exod. 12:3, called the Passover, that is, the passing over, v.11; used for the lamb to be sacrificed at the passing over, a metonymy. The Lamb who takes away the sins of the world, John 1:29, 36. Foreordained before the foundation of the world, 1 Pet. 1:19, 20. Slain, Rev. 13:8. See CHRIST. Christ is called the Son of God, thirdly, because priest, etc. The same yesterday and today, Heb. 13:8. By the one offering of himself, Heb. 7:27, he has perfected for ever those who are sanctified, 10:14. See CHRIST. The Lamb, Rev. 5:6, with the book sealed with seven seals, v.1, takes it, v.7; is found worthy to receive the book and open its seals, v.9; is sung by the voices of all creatures, v.11, 12, 13. He opens the first seal, 6:1; the second, v.3; the third, v.5; the fourth, v.7; the fifth, v.9; the sixth, v.12; the seventh, 8:1. He stands upon Mount Zion together with his chaste worshippers, 14:1, 4. His victory is remarkable, 17:14. [Of the Lamb of God and of Christ, ascending: John 21:15, 16, 17.]

units.tr: Aaron, that is, a strong mountain, son of Amram, Exod. 6:20, a remarkable man, called by God and joined to his brother Moses, Exod. 4:14. He took Elisheba as his wife, Exod. 6:23. He was chief of the priestly tribe of Levi, v.16, 18, 20. Aaron and Hur wait for Moses at the foot of the mountain while he speaks with God, Exod. 24:14. Aaron with his sons is created priest, Exod. 28:1; 29:1, etc.; Lev. 8:2, etc.; Num. 3:10; Deut. 18:5; Heb. 5:4, as the Lord had prescribed, Exod. 29:1, etc. His priestly dignity and that of his sons, Exod. 28:1, etc. Those who are unwilling to acknowledge his authority perish by an unusual kind of death, Num. 16:3, 11, 30. By a miracle he is shown to be chosen above all others for the priesthood, Num. 17:5, 8. After the offering is made outside, he blesses the people with his hands, Lev. 9:22; Num. 6:23, 24. He receives in perpetuity, as his priestly office, the offerings and first fruits from the people, Num. 18:8, 9, 11, 12, and the tithe of the tithes from the Levites, v.26, 28. He makes the golden calf which the Israelites worship, Exod. 32:4; for this he is rebuked by Moses, v.21. For Miriam, who was leprous, he intercedes, Num. 12:11, 12; he murmurs against Moses, v.1. He received the offerings made to the Lord by the people, Num. 18:8. He dies, Num. 20:28; 33:38; Deut. 10:6; 32:50. His sons, 1 Chr. 6:50. His inheritance is God himself, Num. 18:20. The offering of him and his sons, Lev. 6:20. His excellence, Ps. 99:6. His sins, Exod. 32:21; Num. 12:11; 20:12; Deut. 10:6; 32:51. His rod blossoms, Num. 17:8. Eleazar succeeds him in the high priesthood on his death, Num. 20:26; Deut. 10:6. The praise of Aaron, Ecclus. 45:8 to v.28.

units.la: [ALTISSIMVS Deus dicitur simpliciter, non adiuncto a quo,vtNum.24.16.Ps.18.14.46.& 87.5.Esai.14,14.Huc pertinent aequipollentia epitheta, nempe Excelsus, Psal 113, 148,6. Qui habitat in caelis,Psal.2.4.& 123 1.Dicitur etiam, addito Dei nomine,Genes.14 18.Iob.31,28.& frequenter in Psalmis.Altissimus, Deus Pater,Luc.1.32.& 8.28. Altissimi nomen Filii Dei etiam tribuitur,qui est Altissimi Filius, & Altissimus (nempe aequalis Patri) merito nominatur,Luc.1 32.& Luc.8,28: Christus Filius Dei Altissimi dicitur,v.autem eiusd.1.cap.Spiritus S.nominatur virtus Altissimi,nempe Dei Patris & Filij,vtpote ab vtroque procedens. Christus item Oriens ex alto nominatur,Luc.1,78.nempe ex altissimis locis, seu summo caelo prodiens. Tandem Altissimi nomen rebus creatis tribuitur variis locis, Numer.34. Deut.3 5.Matth.21.9.Luc.2.14.]
units.tr: ALTISSIMUS (Most High) is called God simply, without adding whose. See Num. 24.16; Ps. 18.14; 46 and 87.5; Isa. 14.14. To this belong the equivalent epithets: Excelsus (Most High), Ps. 113 and 148.6; Magnus (Great), Ps. 95.3; He who is in heaven, Matt. 6.9; He who dwells on high and in the heights, Isa. 57.15; Ps. 113.4; He who dwells in the heavens, Ps. 2.4 and 123.1. It is also used with the addition of the name of God, Gen. 14.18; Job 31.28, and frequently in the Psalms. Altissimus is God the Father, Luke 1.32 and 8.28. The name of the Most High is also given to the Son of God, who is the Son of the Most High, and who is rightly called Most High (that is, equal to the Father), Luke 1.32 and 8.28: Christ is called the Son of the Most High God, and in the first chapter of the same Gospel the Holy Spirit is named the power of the Most High, namely of God the Father and the Son, since he proceeds from both. Christ is also named the Dayspring from on high, Luke 1.78, that is, coming forth from the highest places, or the highest heaven. Finally, the name Most High is given to created things in various places: Num. 34; Deut. 3.5; Matt. 21.9; Luke 2.14.

units.tr: AMALEK, son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau, is born, Gen. 36.12, from whom the Amalekites descend and take their name. They are defeated by the Israelites, Exod. 17.13; they defeat the Israelites, Num. 14.45; they are ordered to be killed, 1 Sam. 15.2; their memory is to be blotted out, Exod. 17.14; they are defeated by the Simeonites, 1 Chr. 4; they are slaughtered, Judg. 7.1, etc.; they are utterly destroyed, 1 Sam. 15.2, according to the words of Exod. 17.14; Num. 24.20; Deut. 25.19. See Midianites. (Amalek means "a people licking.")

units.tr: BITTERNESS, or bitter resentment, πικρία, is the bitter and unwelcome thought of an injury done to us, a rankling and feeling that bites our breast and heart and begins to stir and inflame us against the one who inflicted it. It makes those by whom we think we have been wronged bitter, grievous and unwelcome to us. Ps. 10.7; Rom. 3.14. [πικρία]

units.la: AMBITIO (contraria modestiæ) est immoderata honoris appetitio, & vitiosa cupiditas gloriæ & nominis excellentiæ supra cæteris, in actionibus non necessariis, fiducia propriæ sapientiæ & virium.
units.tr: AMBITION (contrary to modesty) is an immoderate desire for honour, and a faulty craving for glory and for excellence of name above others, in matters that are not necessary, with confidence in one's own wisdom and strength.

units.la: AMBULARE, Ambulare ex Hebraeorum idiotismo, pro, vivere, & vitam instituere, Marc.7.5. Luc.16. Act.14.16. 2.Corinth.5.7. Vide VIA. Ambulare secundum carnem prohibetur, 2.Cor.10.2. Ambulare secundum hominem (quod idem est) malum est, 1.Cor.3 3. Ambulare in carne, pro, vita ista caduca, 2.Corint.10.3. (Vide CARO.) Ambulare spiritu praecipitur, Galat.5.16. per fidem, 2. Cor.5.7. in luce 1. Ioh.1.7. in veritate, 3.Ioh.v.3. in viis Dei, Iof.22.5. Ambulare in tenebris, Ioh.12.35. in prauitate cordis. Deu.29.v.19 20.
units.tr: To WALK. By the Hebrew idiom, "to walk" means to live and to order one's life: Mark 7.5; Luke 16; Acts 14.16; 2 Cor. 5.7. See WAY. To walk according to the flesh is forbidden, 2 Cor. 10.2. To walk according to man (which is the same) is evil, 1 Cor. 3.3. To walk in the flesh means to live this frail life, 2 Cor. 10.3 (see FLESH). To walk in the Spirit is commanded, Gal. 5.16; to walk by faith, 2 Cor. 5.7; in the light, 1 John 1.7; in truth, 3 John 3; in the ways of God, Josh. 22.5. To walk in darkness, John 12.35; in perversity of heart, Deut. 29.19–20.

units.la: AMEN, Amen, vox est Hebræa, ab eodem verbo deductum, quo fides, seu veritas. Est autem duplex eius vsus principalis: nempe, tum in affirmando, tum in optando: & significat idem quod verè & confirmatò, vt sic loquar. Amen pacta affirmationis, pro ipsa veritate, Apoc.3.14. pro iuris randi nota, Esa.65.16. Matth.5.18. Marc.3.28. Ioh.14.12. & 20. clausulæ loco adhibita in sacris precibus, Matth.6.13. Amen particula vsitata Ecclesiæ, suum cum Pastore in pu-blicis precibus præeunte assensum testificanti, Deut.27.15. ad finem vsque, 1.Paral.16.36. Neh.8.6. Ps.106.48. 1.Cor.14.16. Amen subscriptionis signum. Rom.1.25. 2.Cor.1.20. voti faciendi nota, Ier.11.5. & 28.6. 2.Cor.13.13. Gal.1.5. 6.18. Eph.3.21. & 6.24. Phil.4.23. Apoc.22.v.20.
units.tr: AMEN. Amen is a Hebrew word, derived from the same verb from which the word for faith or truth comes. Its principal use is twofold: both in affirming and in wishing, and it means the same as "truly" and "assuredly", so to speak. Amen as a formula of affirmation, standing for truth itself, Rev. 3.14; as a mark of swearing an oath, Isa. 65.16; Matt. 5.18; Mark 3.28; John 14.12 and 20. Used in place of a closing formula in sacred prayers, Matt. 6.13. The particle customary in the Church, by which the people testify their assent to the minister leading the public prayers, Deut. 27.15, to the end; 1 Chr. 16.36; Neh. 8.6; Ps. 106.48; 1 Cor. 14.16. Amen as a sign of subscription, Rom. 1.25; 2 Cor. 1.20. As a mark of making a vow, Jer. 11.5 and 28.6; 2 Cor. 13.13; Gal. 1.5 and 6.18; Eph. 3.21 and 6.24; Phil. 4.23; Rev. 22.20.

units.la: AMENTIA: Amentia percutiuntur transgressores præcepturum Dei, Deut.28.28. Amentia obiici solita interdum la-storibus fidelibus. Vide PASTOR & INSANIA.
units.tr: MADNESS: Transgressors of God's commandments are struck with madness, Deut. 28:28. Madness is sometimes a charge commonly thrown at the faithful by their reproachers. See PASTOR and INSANITY.

units.la: AMICITIA, φιλία, est mutuus & reciprocus duorum inter se affectus, ex mutua & honesta consuetudine atque com-municatione primùm ortus: postea mutuo pacto & speciali vinculo vltrò citròque in Dei gloriam testatus, & in -tius vitæ durationem & tempus vtrinque confirmatus promissus.
units.tr: FRIENDSHIP, φιλία, is the mutual and reciprocal affection of two people for each other. It first arises from a mutual and honourable association and fellowship, and is afterwards bound by a mutual pact and a special tie, freely and on both sides attested to the glory of God, and promised to be confirmed for the duration of life and over time.

units.la: AMICITIA syncera esse debet, 2.Reg.10.15. Rō.12.9.1. Ti.1.1.1. Ioh.3.18. plerùque ex diuitiis nascitur, Prou.19.4. eius-dem fragilitas, 18.24. Amicitia mundi, inimicitia Dei, Iac.4.4. Amicitiæ exempla: Iacobi erga Rachaelem, Gen.29.18. Ruben erga Ioseph, 37.v.21.22. Ruth erga Noemi, Ruth.1.16. Ioa-thæ erga Dauidem, 1.Sam.18.verf.1.3.4. & 20.42. & 23. Dauidis erga Ionathan, 2.Sam.1.26. & 9.7. 1.Sam.18.3. Abe-neri & Dauidis, 2.Sam.3.v.12.13. Chuzi & Dauidis, 17.v.6.14. Hiram & Salomonis, 1.Reg.5.12. Iehu & Ionadab, 2.Reg.10.15. Aman & amicorum eius, Esth.5.10. Iob & Eliphas, Iob.2.11. Iudæorum erga Demetrium, 1.Mach.10.25.26. Demetrij erga Ionatham, 11.v.20.24.25.26. Ionatæ erga Romanos & Spartanos, 12.v.1.2.3. Demetrii & Simonis, 14.38. Athenobii & Antiochi, 15.32. Christi & Lazari, Ioh.11.11. Christi & Apostolorum, Ioh.15.v.14.15. Pilati & Herodis, Luc.23.12. Asiæ Principum erga Paulum, Act.31. Vide AMOR.
units.tr: FRIENDSHIP ought to be sincere: 2 Kings 10:15; Rom. 12:9; 1 Tim. 1:1; John 3:18. It most often arises from riches (Prov. 19:4), and its frailty is shown at Prov. 18:24. The friendship of the world is enmity with God (James 4:4). Examples of friendship: Jacob towards Rachel (Gen. 29:18); Reuben towards Joseph (Gen. 37:21-22); Ruth towards Naomi (Ruth 1:16); Jonathan towards David (1 Sam. 18:1, 3, 4; 20:42; 23); David towards Jonathan (2 Sam. 1:26; 9:7; 1 Sam. 18:3); Abner and David (2 Sam. 3:12-13); Hushai and David (2 Sam. 17:6, 14); Hiram and Solomon (1 Kings 5:12); Jehu and Jehonadab (2 Kings 10:15); Haman and his friends (Esth. 5:10); Job and Eliphaz (Job 2:11); the Jews towards Demetrius (1 Macc. 10:25-26); Demetrius towards Jonathan (1 Macc. 11:20, 24-26); Jonathan towards the Romans and Spartans (1 Macc. 12:1-3); Demetrius and Simon (1 Macc. 14:38); Athenobius and Antiochus (1 Macc. 15:32); Christ and Lazarus (John 11:11); Christ and the apostles (John 15:14-15); Pilate and Herod (Luke 23:12); the princes of Asia towards Paul (Acts 19:31). See LOVE.

units.tr: God's love toward creatures is not a passion arising from some apprehended good, but the very simple essence of God, well disposed toward the things he has created and blessing them in his own way.

units.tr: Among other things, God loves human beings, as appears from the creation of man: Gen. 1:26; Ps. 8:5; from his fatherly care: Zech. 1; Luke 21:18; Mark 6:25 etc.; Acts 17:28; Heb. 1:14. From redemption: John 3:16; Rom. 8:33 etc. From his infinite mercy: Exod. 6. From the gift of regeneration and of the Holy Spirit: Rom. 8:1, 8. He loves the elect freely and perpetually: 1 John 4:10; Rom. 9:13; Jer. 31:3; and 33. In Christ: Rom. 8:33 etc. Therefore he is to be sincerely worshipped and loved: Deut. 6:5; John 14:23; John 4:24; Rev. 16.]

units.la: [AMOR sui caecus, 2. Tim. 3. 2. φιλαυτία, Est cum quis se, suaque omnia vel corporis vel animi bona pluris facit, quam vel in se sint, vel aestimare oporteat. Qui amor cum vera animi demissione & humilitate pugnat.
units.tr: [Blind self-love, 2 Tim. 3:2. Self-love [φιλαυτία]: it is when someone values himself and all his goods, whether of body or of mind, more highly than they are in themselves or ought to be esteemed. This love struggles against true humility and lowliness of mind.

units.la: AMOR ut plurimum homines caecos reddit. Exempla: Achem, Genes. 34, 12. Samson, Iudic. 16, 4. Amnon, 2. Sam. 1. Salomon, 1. Reg. 11, 3. duo senes, Daniel. 13. v. 8, 9. Amoris exempla, Isaac amabat Esaum, Rachel Iacobum, Genes. 28. Iacob Rachelem, 29. vers. 18, 20, 30, Israel Iosephum, 3. Deus Patres, Deut. 10. 15. Dauid Ionatham, & contra Sam. 18, 1. 2. Sam. 1, 26. Roboam Maachae filiam, 2. Paral. 21. Iesus Lazarum, Ioan. 11. v. 3, 4, 5. 36. Ioannem, 20, 2. Petrus Christum, 21. v. 15, 16, 17. Paulus Christum, 1. Cor. 16. Philipp. 1, 23, & 3, 8. Vide AMICITIAE exempla. Amor proximorum, Deo & hominibus gratus, Eccles. 25, 2. amor mulierum idololatriae deditarum captus Salomon, idolum colit, 1. Reg. 11. 4.
units.tr: Love for the most part makes people blind. Examples: Shechem, Gen. 34:12; Samson, Judges 16:4; Amnon, 2 Sam. 1; Solomon, 1 Kings 11:3; the two elders, Dan. 13:8, 9. Examples of love: Isaac loved Esau, Rachel loved Jacob, Gen. 28; Jacob loved Rachel, 29:18, 20, 30; Israel loved Joseph, 37:3; God loved the Fathers, Deut. 10:15; David loved Jonathan, and conversely, 1 Sam. 18:1; 2 Sam. 1:26; Rehoboam loved Maacah's daughter, 2 Chron. 11:21; Jesus loved Lazarus, John 11:3, 4, 5, 36; John, 20:2; Peter loved Christ, 21:15, 16, 17; Paul loved Christ, 1 Cor. 16; Phil. 1:23 and 3:8. See the examples of FRIENDSHIP. The love of neighbours, pleasing to God and men, Ecclus. 25:2. Solomon, captivated by the love of women given over to idolatry, worshipped an idol, 1 Kings 11:4.

units.la: AMORRHAEVS, filius Chanaan, Genes. 10, 16. (i. Iebusaeus) quax).
units.tr: AMORRHAEUS, son of Canaan, Gen. 10:16 (i.e. the Jebusite).

units.la: AMORRHAEI, Genes. 14. v. 7, 10. occidunt Israelitas, Deut. 44. eos penitus occidi iubet Deus, 20, 17. bellum inferunt Gabaonitis, quod pacem cum Iosue fecissent, Iosh. 10, 1. & eos contra Gabaonitas pugnantes, vincit Iosue, vers. 1. tributarii sunt filiis Iosephi, Iudic. 1, 35. Salomoni Regi, 1. Reg. 9, 21. non patiuntur Israelem per terminos suos proficisci, Num. 21, 23. Iudic. 11. v. 19, 20. caeduntur a Codorlaomor, Genesis 14, 7. Amorrhaeorum urbes habitat Israel. Num. 21. 24. 25.
units.tr: The Amorites: Gen. 14:7, 10. They slay Israelites, Deut. 1:44. God orders that they be utterly destroyed, 20:17. They make war on the Gibeonites, who had made peace with Joshua, Josh. 10:1; and Joshua conquers them when they fight against the Gibeonites, v. 1. They are tributary to the sons of Joseph, Judges 1:35; and to King Solomon, 1 Kings 9:21. They do not allow Israel to pass through their borders, Num. 21:23; Judges 11:19, 20. They are struck down by Chedorlaomer, Gen. 14:7. Israel inhabited the cities of the Amorites, Num. 21:24, 25.

units.tr: AMPHIPOLIS, a city of Macedonia: Acts 17:1, through which Paul travelled on his way to Thessalonica.

units.tr: AMPHORA, a vision or ephah, designating the transfer of Judah into Babylon: Zech. 5:5.

units.tr: AMRAM, son of Kohath, father of Moses and Aaron: Exod. 6:20 (i.e. high people).

units.la: AMRI, siue HOMRI pater impij Regis Achab, 1. Reg. 16.29. &c. Rex Israel constituitur, 1. Regum 16. 16. impius est, verf. 25.26. moritur, verf. 28. contra Amri, Michae 6.16.
units.tr: AMRI, or OMRI, father of the impious King Ahab: 1 Kings 16:29 etc. He is made King of Israel, 1 Kings 16:16; he is impious, vv. 25, 26; he dies, v. 28. Against Omri, Micah 6:16.

units.tr: NAMELECH, the idol of Sepharvaim: 2 Kings 17:31. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: ANANIAS Pseudopropheta, propketat contra Ieremiam, Ierem.28.1. Mors eius praedicitur, v.16.
units.tr: ANANIAS, the false prophet, prophesied against Jeremiah: Jer. 28:1. His death is foretold, v. 16.

units.la: ANANIAS, Ecclesiam agri precio fraudat, Actor. 5. 2. quam ob rem obiurgatus a Petro moritur, v. 5. (.i. gratia Dei)
units.tr: ANANIAS defrauds the Church of the price of a field: Acts 5:2. For this reason, rebuked by Peter, he dies, v. 5. (i.e. grace of God).

units.la: ANANIAS, Pastor Damascenus ad Paulum mittitur, Act.9.11. eum baptizat, v.18. eius encomium, 22.12.
units.tr: ANANIAS, the minister of Damascus, is sent to Paul, Acts 9.11. He baptizes him, v.18. His commendation: Acts 22.12.

units.la: ANANIAS, Princeps Sacerdotum, hypocrita, Act.23.3. percuti iubet Paulum, ibid. cui Paulus Dei iudicium denuntiat.
units.tr: ANANIAS, the high priest, a hypocrite, Acts 23.3, orders Paul to be struck, ibid. Paul announces God's judgment against him.

units.la: ANATHEMA, pro re execranda, Rom.9.3.1.Cor.12,3.&16. 22. Gal.1.v.8.9. De anathemate qui accepisset, iubet Deus comburi, Iof.7 15.anathema erat Iericho, 6,17. Anathema fit, qui Christum non amat, 1.Cor.16 22. aut docet per aliud saluari nos posse, quam per Christum, Galat.1,9.anathema (id est, deuotus sempiterno exitio) esse pro fratribus suis optat Paulus, Rom.9, 3. anathema maranatha, 1. Corinth. 16. 22. designatur hic species extremi anathematis.
units.tr: ANATHEMA, a word for a thing to be detested: Rom. 9.3; 1 Cor. 12.3 and 16.22; Gal. 1.8-9. God commands that whatever has been devoted under the ban be burned, Josh. 7.15. Jericho was anathema, 6.17. Whoever does not love Christ is anathema, 1 Cor. 16.22, and so is whoever teaches that we can be saved through anything other than Christ, Gal. 1.9. Paul wishes to be anathema (that is, doomed to eternal destruction) for his brothers, Rom. 9.3. "Anathema maranatha," 1 Cor. 16.22, here denotes the extreme form of anathema.

units.la: ANATHOTH, ciuitas Beniamin, Ierem. 32. verf. 7. 8. vbi & Ieremias est natus, 1. 1. & 29, 27. & Abiathar Sacerdos, 1. Reg.2.26. Anathothitae nolunt Ieremiam audire, Ierem. 11.21.
units.tr: ANATHOTH, a city of Benjamin, Jer. 32.7-8, where Jeremiah was also born, 1.1 and 29.27, and Abiathar the priest, 1 Kings 2.26. The men of Anathoth were unwilling to hear Jeremiah, Jer. 11.21.

Ruth ipsius Booz, Ruth. 2. 13. ancillam vendita filia, Exodi 21, 7. in ancillam vendita fratri suo Hebræo, quomodo libertate donata, Deut. 15. cum ancilla dormientis poena, Leuit. 19. 20. ancillæ Iudaeorum ex peregrinis erant & aliis nationibus, non ex fratribus, & possidebantur vt iumenta, Leuit. 25. 44. Ancillas dant marito suo Rachel & Lea, ex quibus suscipsunt liberos, Genes. 30. v. 3. 9. Ancillę humilitas Hebraismus, pro ancilla humilis. Luc. 1. 48. ad ancillæ vocem abnegat Petrus Christum, Matth. 26. 70. Marc. 14. 68. Luc. 22. 57. Ioan. 18. 25. [Ancillæ sapientiæ, Ministri verbi Dei, Prov. 9. 3.]
units.tr: servant of God: the mother of David, Ps. 86.16 and 116.16; the virgin Mary, Luke 1.38, 48; the handmaids of God, Acts 2.18. Abigail calls herself David's maidservant, 1 Sam. 25.24, 41. Anna, the maidservant of Eli the priest, 1 Sam. 1.16. Mary, the Lord's maidservant, Luke 1.38. Ruth, the maidservant of Boaz himself, Ruth 2.13. A daughter sold as a maidservant, Exod. 21.7. A man who sold himself as a servant to his Hebrew brother, and how he was given his freedom, Deut. 15. The penalty for sleeping with a maidservant, Lev. 19.20. The maidservants of the Jews were from foreigners and other nations, not from their brothers, and they were owned like beasts of burden, Lev. 25.44. Rachel and Leah gave their maidservants to their husband, from whom they received children, Gen. 30.3, 9. "Humility of the handmaid" is a Hebraism for a humble maidservant, Luke 1.48. Peter denies Christ at the voice of a maidservant, Matt. 26.70; Mark 14.68; Luke 22.57; John 18.25. [Maidservants of wisdom: ministers of the Word of God, Prov. 9.3.]

units.la: ANDREAS frater Simonis Ioh. 1. 40. eius ciuitas Bethsaida: Ioan. 1. 45. vocatur à Christo, Matth. 4. v. 18. 19. Marc. 1. 16. Ioan. 1. 40. Petrum ad Christum adducit, Ioan. 1. v. 41. 42. 43. (ιλαρὶς, fortissimus Gr.)
units.tr: ANDREW, brother of Simon, John 1.40; his city was Bethsaida, John 1.45. He is called by Christ, Matt. 4.18-19; Mark 1.16; John 1.40. He brings Peter to Christ, John 1.41-43. (Greek: "manly, most valiant" [ἀνδρεῖος].)

units.la: ANDRONICVS, cognatus Pauli, ante quem fuit ad Christum conuersus, Rom. 16. 7.
units.tr: ANDRONICUS, a kinsman of Paul, who was converted to Christ before him, Rom. 16.7.

units.la: ANGARIARE, Matth. 5. 41. & 27, 32. est cogere ad currendum vel ferendum aliquid. Est autem ex nomine Persico Angari factum. Angari enim Persis dicebantur, quos hodie Persas dicimus.
units.tr: ANGARIARE, Matt. 5.41 and 27.32, means to compel someone to run or to carry something. The word is derived from the Persian word angari, for the Persians were called angari, whom we today call Persians.

units.la: ANGELI à Deo creati sunt, Colos. 1. 16. Angelos bonos non esse qualitates, aut inspirationes sine substantia, sed veri spiritus naturæ subsistentis (quorum ministerio Deus utitur ad salutem piorum) contra Sadducæos & Libertinos, qui Angelorum & animarum hypostasin negabant, & etiamdum negant, probatur Daniel. 7. 10. Matth. 26. 53. & 18. 10. & 22. 30. & 24. 36. & 25. 31. Lucæ 15. 10. & 22. Actor. 7. 53. Galat. 3. 19. Hebr. 1. 4. & 2. 16. 1. Timoth. 5. 21. &c.
units.tr: ANGELS were created by God, Col. 1.16. Good angels are not qualities or inspirations without substance, but true spirits of a subsistent nature, through whose ministry God serves the salvation of the pious. This is proved against the Sadducees and Libertines, who denied, and still deny, the hypostasis of angels and souls: Dan. 7.10; Matt. 26.53; 18.10; 22.30; 24.36; 25.31; Luke 15.10 and 22; Acts 7.53; Gal. 3.19; Heb. 1.4 and 2.16; 1 Tim. 5.21, etc.

units.tr: Good angels have appeared to men. Examples: to Hagar, the maidservant of Sarai, Gen. 16.7; to Abraham, 18.2 and 22.11; to Lot, 19.1; to Jacob, 28.12, 31.11 and 32.1; Hosea 12.4; to Balaam, Num. 22.22; to the Israelites, Judg. 2.1; to Gideon, 6.12; to the mother of Samson, 13.3; to his father, v.9, etc.; to David, 2 Sam. 24.17; to Elijah, 1 Kings 19.5 and 1 Kings 13; to Elisha and his servant, 2 Kings 6.17; to Isaiah, Isa. 6.6; to Daniel, Dan. 6.22, 9.21 and 10.8; to the prophet Zechariah, Zech. 1.8-9; to Joseph, the husband of Mary, Matt. 1.20 and 2.13, 19.

units.tr: The angel wrestles with Jacob, Genesis 32.24; Hos. 12 v. 3, 4. The angel does not want a burnt offering offered to himself but to God, Judges 13.16. The angel does not want to be worshipped by John, Apoc. 19.10 & 22 v. 8, 9. The angel of the Lord strikes the camp of the Assyrians, 2 Kings 19.35; 2 Chron. 32.21; Isa. 37.36. (He strikes) the people of David, 2 Sam. 24.16; (he strikes) Herod, Acts 12.23. Angels are ministers of Christ, Matt. 4.11; 13.41; 24.31; 25.31; 26.53; 28.2; Mark 1.13; 13.27; Luke 22.43; John 1.51; Apoc. 19.10 & 22.9. (They are) of God, Psalm 103.21; 104.4; Heb. 1.7. They minister to the pious, Gen. 19.15; 22 v. 11, 12; 1 Kings 19.5; 2 Kings 19.35; Psalm 34.8; Matt. 4.6; 18.10; Luke 4.10; Daniel 3 (or so, 28); 6.22; Tobit 5 v. 5, 6, 22; 12.15; Matt. 24.31; Mark 13.27; Luke 16.22; Acts 5.19; 12 v. 7, 11, 15; 27.23; Heb. 1.14.

units.tr: See the OFFICE of ANGELS.

units.la: Angeli boni irę Dei Ministri, Genes. 18.16. Exodi 12.29. 2.Sam.24.v.16. 17. Act. 12. 23. Angeli messoribus similes, Matth.13.39. Angeli viri dicti, Genes.18.2.& 19.5. Lucæ 24. 4. Act.1.10. Filij Dei dicuntur, Iob.1 6. vt a filiis hominum discernantur: verùm humanitus id de Deo dicitur, & sumpta à Regibus terrenis similitudine, vt 1.Reg. 22.19. Vide FILII Dei. Angeli virtutis Christi, 2. Thess. 1.7. Angeli cum Deo collati mundi non sunt, Iob.4.18. invitantur ad dandam Deo gloriam, Psalm.97. 7.& 103. 20 gloriam Deo tribuunt, Esa.6.3, Luc. 2. 14. Apoc.4.8. & 5 v.11. 12. Angeli diem iudicij ignorant, Matt. 24.36. Mar 13.32.
units.tr: Angels, the good ones, are ministers of God's wrath: Gen. 18.16; Exod. 12.29; 2 Sam. 24 v. 16, 17; Acts 12.23. Angels are likened to reapers, Matt. 13.39. Angels are called men, Gen. 18.2 & 19.5; Luke 24.4; Acts 1.10. They are called sons of God, Job 1.6, so that they may be distinguished from the sons of men; but this is said of God in a human manner, and the likeness is taken from earthly kings, as in 1 Kings 22.19. See SONS of God. (They are called) angels of Christ's power, 2 Thess. 1.7. The angels, compared with God, are not pure, Job 4.18. They are invited to give glory to God, Psalm 97.7 & 103.20. They ascribe glory to God, Isa. 6.3; Luke 2.14; Apoc. 4.8 & 5 v. 11, 12. The angels do not know the day of judgment, Matt. 24.36; Mark 13.32.

units.la: ANGELORVM cultus superstitiosus, Col. 2.18. gaudium eorum ob resipiscentiam peccatoris, Luc. 15. 7. profectus quem ex Euangelij propagatione faciunt, Ephes. 3.10. 1. Petr. 1 12. desiderant introspicere in illa mysteria, quę nobis annuntiantur in Euangelio, versic.12. Angelus Græcis etiam de hominibus dicitur, Matth.11. 10. Marc.1.2. Angelorum nomine appellantur Doctores, Esa. 33.7. Malac. 2.7.& 3 1, Matth. 11.10, Marc.1.2, Luc.7.27. Gal.4.14. Apoc. 2.1.&c.
units.tr: The superstitious worship of angels, Col. 2.18. Their joy over the repentance of a sinner, Luke 15.7. The progress which they make through the spread of the gospel, Eph. 3.10; 1 Pet. 1.12. They desire to look into those mysteries which are announced to us in the Gospel, verse 12. The word angel is also used among the Greeks of men, Matt. 11.10; Mark 1.2. Teachers are called by the name of angels, Isa. 33.7; Mal. 2.7 & 3.1; Matt. 11.10; Mark 1.2; Luke 7.27; Gal. 4.14; Apoc. 2.1, etc.

units.la: Angelorum officium: Adstant in conspectu Dei, eúmque celebrant, Esa.6.3. Psa.148.2. Luc.2.14. Apoc.4.8. & 5.ver.11. 12. Ministri sunt Dei in patefacienda voluntate sua, Gene. 21 12. 2. Reg. 1.15. Luc.1 26. Act.7.53. Gal.3.19. annûtiant futura, Daniel.8.19. & 9.23. Zach.1.9. & 2.4. & 4.1. & 5.1. variis de rebus monent pios, Matth. 1. 20. & 2. v. 12. 13. liberant eos ab hostibus, ac defendunt, 2. Reg. 6. 17. & 19. 35.2. Paral 32,21. Esa.37,36. Psalm.91.11. & 34. 8. Matth.4. 6. & 18 10. Act.12. 11. delectantur ministerio Euangelij de Christo, piorumque salute, & illa promovent, Act.8.26. & 10. 3. & 16 9. Luc.2.10. &c. 1. Petr. 1.12. defendunt pios ecclesiae Doctores, 2. Reg. 6 17. Act.12.11. pugnant pro Ecclesia, 2 Reg.19,35. 2. Paral 32.21. Esa.37.36. Psalm.34. 8 Dan.10.v.13.20. Zach.1.12. pro politia & eius pace.2.Reg. 19.35. Act. 2.23. pro oeconomia & infantibus in ea, piis parentibus ac familia, Genes.32.1. Psalm.34.8.& 91, 11. Matt. 18 10 procurant nuptias, Ger.24.7. Tob.7.8.&c. animas piorum deportant in vitam aeternam, Luc.16.22.
units.tr: The office of angels: They stand in the sight of God and praise him, Isa. 6.3; Psalm 148.2; Luke 2.14; Apoc. 4.8 & 5 v. 11, 12. They are ministers of God in making known his will, Gen. 21.12; 2 Kings 1.15; Luke 1.26; Acts 7.53; Gal. 3.19. They announce future things, Dan. 8.19 & 9.23; Zech. 1.9; 2.4; 4.1; 5.1. They warn the pious of various matters, Matt. 1.20; 2 v. 12, 13. They free them from enemies and defend them, 2 Kings 6.17 & 19.35; 2 Chron. 32.21; Isa. 37.36; Psalm 91.11; 34.8; Matt. 4.6; 18.10; Acts 12.11. They delight in the ministry of the Gospel about Christ and in the salvation of the pious, and promote it, Acts 8.26; 10.3; 16.9; Luke 2.10, etc.; 1 Pet. 1.12. They defend the teachers of the Church, 2 Kings 6.17; Acts 12.11. They fight for the Church, 2 Kings 19.35; 2 Chron. 32.21; Isa. 37.36; Psalm 34.8; Dan. 10 v. 13, 20; Zech. 1.12. They fight for the commonwealth and its peace, 2 Kings 19.35; Acts 2.23. They care for households and the infants in them, for pious parents and their families, Gen. 32.1; Psalm 34.8 & 91.11; Matt. 18.10. They arrange marriages, Jer. 24.7; Tobit 7.8, etc. They carry the souls of the pious into eternal life, Luke 16.22.

units.la: Ad Angelorum ordines novem constituendos, ex sententia Dionysij cuiusdam, arrepta est occasio ex hisce locis, Esa.6.v.1.6. &c. Dan.10.13. Rom. 8,38. Ephes.1.21. & 3. 10. Coloss.1.16. 1. Thess. 4.16. Iudae v. 9. &c. in quibus fit mentio Angelorum, Archangelorum, Principatuum, Potestatum, Virtutum, Dominationum, Seraphim, Cherubim, & Thronorum, ac pro ordinibus Angelorum eos agnoscunt nonnulli, quam in sententiam videtur etiam Athanasius Tomo 4, operum, q.4. inclinare. Angelorum nomina, quae in sacris literis [Canonicis] inueniuntur: Gabriel, Dan.8.16. & 9.21. Luc,1.v.19. 26. Michael, Dan. 12. 1. Iudae v.9. Apoc.12.7.
units.tr: For fixing the nine orders of angels, according to the opinion of a certain Dionysius, an occasion was taken from these passages: Isa. 6:1, 6, etc.; Dan. 10:13; Rom. 8:38; Eph. 1:21 and 3:10; Col. 1:16; 1 Thess. 4:16; Jude v. 9, etc. In these passages mention is made of angels, archangels, principalities, powers, virtues, dominions, seraphim, cherubim and thrones. Some acknowledge these as the orders of angels, and Athanasius, in volume 4 of his works, question 4, seems to incline to this view. The names of angels found in the sacred [canonical] books are: Gabriel (Dan. 8:16; 9:21; Luke 1:19, 26); Michael (Dan. 12:1; Jude v. 9; Rev. 12:7).

units.la: Angeli pro Angelica natura, Hebr.2 16. Angelis linguae tribuuntur a Paulo,1. Cor.13. 1. per hyperbolen, ex hypothesi, maxima emphaseos gratia, ac si diceret: Si linguae essent aliquae Angelorum, & ego eas tenerem, neque illis uterer ad commodum proximi, id vero nihil aliud esset, quam inanis & obstrepera loquacitas. Similis est hyperbole Rom.8.38. ubi cum res omnes creatas summas, medias, & infimas nominasset, addit: Neque vlla alia res creata. Item Gal.1.8. vbi si de malis Angelis loquitur, friget, atque adeo absurdus est sermo: Sin de bonis, in eos non cadit falsa praedicatio: Relinquitur ergo, illud quoque dictum ὑπερ Coloss, ex hypothesi intelligendum esse. Sic panis tribuitur Angelis, Psalm.78.25.& 105 40. hoc est, quo etiam Angeli vti potuissent, si pane vescerentur, vel [illegible, ~3 letters] ipsum Angeli administrabant. Angeli infantium [?]lent faciem Patris qui in cœlis est, Matt. 18. 10. Ange-lum cum hominibus locutionis exempla. Vide LOQVV-TIO. &c.
units.tr: Angels stands for the angelic nature (Heb. 2:16). Tongues are attributed to angels by Paul (1 Cor. 13:1) by hyperbole, on a hypothesis, as a figure of great emphasis, as if he said: "If I had the tongues of angels and did not use them for my neighbour's benefit, that would be nothing but empty and noisy chatter." Rom. 8:38 is a similar hyperbole, where, after naming all created things, high, middle and low, he adds: "nor any other created thing." Likewise Gal. 1:8: if he speaks there of evil angels, the sentence is flat and absurd; if of good angels, a false preaching does not fall upon them. It remains, therefore, that the passage in Col. (2:18) too must be understood on a hypothesis. So bread is attributed to angels (Ps. 78:25; 105:40), that is, bread which they also could have used if they fed on bread, or the angels themselves administered it. The angels of infants always see the face of the Father who is in heaven (Matt. 18:10). Examples of the angel speaking with men. See SPEECH, etc.

units.la: ELORVM lapsus ter in Sacris literis expresse notatur, Ioann. 8 44. Iudæ vers. 6. 2. Petr. 2. 4. Vide 1. Corinth. 6. 3. Ioan. 3. 8.
units.tr: The fall of the angels is expressly noted three times in Sacred Scripture: John 8:44; Jude v. 6; 2 Pet. 2:4. See 1 Cor. 6:3; John 3:8.

units.la: ANGELI reprobi, seu mali spiritus, 1. Sam. 16. v. 14. 15. eos non [?] malos affectus aut perturbationes sine essentia & natu-ra subsistentes. Vide DIABOLVS.
units.tr: Reprobate angels, or evil spirits (1 Sam. 16:14, 15), are not [?] evil affections or disturbances subsisting without essence and nature. See DEVIL.

units.la: ANGELI pro Diabolo, 1. Cor. 6. 3. Angelus Satanæ. 2. Cor. 11. transformat se in Angelum lucis, 2. Corint. 11. 14. Vide DIABOLVS.
units.tr: Angels for the Devil (1 Cor. 6:3); "the angel of Satan" (2 Cor. 11:14); he transforms himself into an angel of light (2 Cor. 11:14). See DEVIL.

Psalm. 34. 8. & 91. 11. & 97. 7. & 103. 20. & 148. 2. Esai. 37. 36. Dan. 6. 22. Zach. 2. 3. & 12. 8. in nouo Testamento autem hæc denominatio plusquam centies & quadragesies occurrit. 3.
