Nuncius malorum & calamitatum, Psal. 78. 49. Mo-ses & Aaron mali Angeli vocantur, quòd Ægyptiis dura prædixerint. 6. Carnifex Dei vel hominum, Prou. 17. 11. 7. Pseudodoctores, Apoc. 9. 14. 8. Sacerdos sub lege, diuinæ voluntatis interpres, Malac. 2. 7. 9. Præcursor Christi, Io. Baptista, Malac. 3. 1. Matth. 11. 10. Marc. 1. 2. Luc. 7. 27. Ibi Angelus idem ac Legatus. 10. Ministri Ecclesiæ sub Nouo Test. Angeli dicuntur, Apoc. 1 2. & 3. cap. item 14. v. 6. 8. 9. vt plerique sentiunt. 11. Homo à Deo missus, Iudic. 2. 1. & 5. 23. Iob. 33. 23. 12. Homo ab homine missus, Esai. 18. 2. & 33. 3. 7. 13. Angeli, viri fortes, potentes, authoritate præditi, Iob. 41. 16. Psal. 138. 1. ]
units.tr: [The Angel of the LORD, Christ Jehovah, before the incarnation, performing by a certain prelude the office of Mediator, in the history of the Patriarchs and Israelites (Gen. 48:16; Exod. 13:1; 14:19; 23:20, 23; Num. 20:16; 22:22, etc.; Judg. 5:23; 3:3, 16, 17; Isa. 63:9; Hos. 12:4, 5; Zech. 1:9; 2:3–6, chapters 2.) The angel of God is understood as a blessed, created spirit, sent by God for the sake of ministry on account of the elect (Gen. 9:1, 15; 2:17; 28:12; 32:1; Ps. 34:8; 91:11; 97:7; 103:20; 148:2; Isa. 37:36; Dan. 6:22; Zech. 2:3; 12:8). In the New Testament, however, this designation occurs more than one hundred and forty times. 3. The good and evil angel (Acts 23:8; Rom. 8:37). 4. The evil angel and reprobate angels (Matt. 25:41; 1 Cor. 6:3; 2 Cor. 12:7; 2 Pet. 2:4; Jude 6; Rev. 9:11; 12:7, 9). 5. Messenger of evils and calamities (Ps. 78:49). Moses and Aaron are called evil angels, because they foretold harsh things to the Egyptians. 6. Executioner of God or of men (Prov. 17:11). 7. False teachers (Rev. 9:14). 8. Priest under the law, interpreter of the divine will (Mal. 2:7). 9. Forerunner of Christ, John the Baptist (Mal. 3:1; Matt. 11:10; Mark 1:2; Luke 7:27). There, angel is the same as legate. 10. Ministers of the Church under the New Testament are called angels (Rev. 1:2 and chapter 3; likewise 14:6, 8, 9), as most think. 11. A man sent by God (Judg. 2:1; 5:23; Job 33:23). 12. A man sent by a man (Isa. 18:2; 33:7). 13. Angels, strong and powerful men endowed with authority (Job 41:16; Ps. 138:1).]

units.la: ANGVLVS, in ædificiis, locis abditis, agris, regionibus, vestimentis, extremitas constans ex duabus lineis in idem acumen & punctum definentibus, Exod. 25. 12. Deut. 22. 12.2.Reg.14.15.2.Par.28 24.Iob.1.19. Prou. 21.9. Matth. Act.26.26. Apoc.7.1.& 20.8. Angulus mysticus, fundamentum, seu lapis aut petra totam Dei Ecclesiam sustinens in eo compactam, Psalm. 118. 22. Matth. 21. 42. Act. 4.11. 1 Petr.2.7. Angulus, Tribus populi. Iudic. 20.2. 2. Sam.14. Esai.19.13.
units.tr: ANGLE, in buildings, hidden places, fields, regions, garments: an extremity consisting of two lines meeting in one point and terminating in the same apex (Exod. 25:12; Deut. 22:12; 2 Kings 14:15; 2 Chron. 28:24; Job 1:19; Prov. 21:9; Matt. 26:26; Acts 26:26; Rev. 7:1 and 20:8). The mystical corner: the foundation, or stone or rock, sustaining the whole Church of God, compacted in it (Ps. 118:22; Matt. 21:42; Acts 4:11; 1 Pet. 2:7). Corner: the tribes of the people (Judg. 20:2; 2 Sam. 14; Isa. 19:13).

units.la: ANGVSTA & lata porta, V. Porta.
units.tr: NARROW and wide gate, see GATE.

units.la: ANIMA hominis, est substantia invisibilis ad Dei imaginem condita: cuius ipse vita est per Christum, quæque super sibi à Deo data mouet agitatque omnia & singula membra corporis, in quo inest, usque vitam dat, quæque ratiocinatur & disquirit de iis rebus, quæ sub corporis sensum non cadunt.
units.tr: SOUL of man is an invisible substance created in the image of God, whose life is itself through Christ; which, having been given to it by God above, moves and drives all and each of the members of the body in which it dwells, gives life until death, and which reasons and inquires about those things that do not fall under the bodily senses.

units.la: [Anima, pro sanguine animantis, vel bruti, vel ratione præditi. Deut.12.23. Ion.1.14. Anima sepulchri, Esai.5.14. Habac.2 5. Anima pro vita, Gen.9.5. Exod.4.19. Leu.24.18. Deut.16.6. Iudic.9.17.1. Sam.20.1.1. Reg.2.23. Est.7.3. Iob. 2.4.6. Psal.33 19.& 49.9 16. Esa.38.17. Ier.4.30. Matt.2.20.& 6.25. Ioan.10.11.&c.15.26.
units.tr: [Soul, for the blood of a living creature, whether brute or endowed with reason (Deut. 12:23; Jonah 1:14). Soul of the grave (Isa. 5:14; Hab. 2:5). Soul for life (Gen. 9:5; Exod. 4:19; Lev. 24:18; Deut. 16:6; Judg. 9:17; 1 Sam. 20:1; 1 Kings 2:23; Esth. 7:3; Job 2:4, 6; Ps. 33:19; 49:9, 16; Isa. 38:17; Jer. 4:30; Matt. 2:20; 6:25; John 10:11; 15:26, etc.]

units.la: Animæ vox tribuitur etiam cadaueri, & homini mortuo; Leuit. 19. 28. & 21. v. 1. 11. Num. 5. 2. & 6. 6 & 9. 6. 7. Osee. 4. Agg. 2. 14. item sepulchro, aut, vt alij, inferno, Esa. 51. 23. Anima Christi turbata, Ioh. 12. 27.
units.tr: The word soul is also attributed to a corpse and a dead man (Lev. 19:28; 21:1, 11; Num. 5:2; 6:6; 9:6, 7; Hos. 4; Hag. 2:14); likewise to a sepulchre or, as others say, to hell (Isa. 51:23). The soul of Christ troubled (John 12:27).

units.la: Immortalitatis animæ exempla: in Henoch, Gen. 5. 24. Abrahamo, 25. v. 7. 8. Isaaco 35. 29. Iacob, 49. v. 29 33. appa-rione Dei Moysi facta, Exod. 3. v. 15. 16. quo ipso probat & Christus resurrectionem futuram, & Sanctos mortuos Deo viuere, Matth. 22. 31. Core cum complicibus suis, Numer. 16. v. 31. 32. Psalm. 106. v. 16. 17. Saule, 1. Sam. 28. 11. Nam si Saul credidisset Samuelem, quoad animam extinctum, non petiuisset eum exsuscitari. Dau de, 2. Sam. 12. v. 22. 23. & 18. 33. In Regibus, qui dormiuisse cum Patribus suis dicuntur: Roboamo, 1. Reg. 14. 31. Iosaphato, 22. 51. Ioram, 2. Reg. 8. 24. Iehu, 10. 35 Ieroboamo, 14. 29. Manahem, 15. 22. Ioatham, v. 38. Achaz 16. 20. Ezechia, 20. 21. Manasse, 21. 18. Abia, 1. Reg. 15. 8. Ozia, 2. Para. 26. 23. Vnde sequitur, eos viuere post mortem corporis, & in vniuersali iudicio eos tandem resurrecturos, vt id in dormientibus apparet. Item in resuscitatis a mortuis, ab Elia, 1. Reg. 17. 22 Elisæo, 2. Reg. 4. 33. & 13. 21. Christo, Matth. 9. 25. Luc. 7. 15. Ioh. 11. 43. Petro, Act 9. 40. Paulo, 20. 10. Præterea in Elia, 2. Reg. 2. v. 9. 11. Iobo, Iob, 13. 15. & 19. 25. Nabuchodonosor, Esa. 14. v. 8. 9. 11. & ex dicto Christi, Matt 10. 28. in Christo ipso resurrectionis & vitæ æternæ autore, Psal. 6. Matth. 27. 50. Luc. 23. 46. Lazaro & diuite, Luc. 16. v. 22. 23. Villico iniquo, Lucæ 16. 9. latrone ad dextram Christi pendente, 23. 43. Vide 1. Cor. 15. 12. 1. Thess. 4. v. 13. 14. 1. Tim. 4. 8. Hebr. 12. 9. Vide RESVRRECTIO. Animarum castitas, 1. Cor. 7. 9. 1. Pet. 1. 22. Animas per patientiam possidere, Luc. 21. 19. est vita tranquilla & beata perfrui. Animam suam, id est, vitam diligere, ex Hebraeorum diotissimo dicuntur ij, qui nihil habent hac vita charius. Contrà, non diligere animam suam ij dicuntur, qui non dubitant illam periculis exponere, quoties ita facto opus est, Apoc. 12. 11. Animam invenire (id est vitam servare) Matt. 10 39. & 16.25. Marc. 8.35. Luc. 9.24. & 17.33. Ioh. 12.25. dicitur, qui praesenti vitae consulit. Videtur enim perisse, qui in certo vitae discrimine versatur, & e contrario velut seipsum recuperare, qui ex eo saluus evadit. Dicuntur tamen haec ex vulgari hominum opinione, qui quoniam de futura vita non cogitant, periisse putant eos qui moriuntur, & evasisse qui ex morte elabuntur.
units.tr: Examples of the immortality of the soul: in Enoch, Gen. 5. 24; in Abraham, 25. v. 7. 8; in Isaac, 35. 29; in Jacob, 49. v. 29. 33; in the appearance of God made to Moses, Exod. 3. v. 15. 16, by which very thing Christ also proves both the future resurrection and that the holy dead live to God, Matt. 22. 31; in Korah with his companions, Num. 16. v. 31. 32; Ps. 106. v. 16. 17; in Saul, 1 Sam. 28. 11, for if Saul had believed that Samuel, as to his soul, was extinct, he would not have sought to have him raised. In David, 2 Sam. 12. v. 22. 23 & 18. 33. Among the kings, who are said to have slept with their fathers: Rehoboam, 1 Kings 14. 31; Jehoshaphat, 22. 51; Joram, 2 Kings 8. 24; Jehu, 10. 35; Jeroboam, 14. 29; Menahem, 15. 22; Jotham, v. 38; Ahaz, 16. 20; Hezekiah, 20. 21; Manasseh, 21. 18; Abijah, 1 Kings 15. 8; Uzziah, 2 Chron. 26. 23. Whence it follows that they live after the death of the body, and that in the general judgment they will at last rise again, as appears in those who sleep. Likewise in those raised from the dead: by Elijah, 1 Kings 17. 22; by Elisha, 2 Kings 4. 33 & 13. 21; by Christ, Matt. 9. 25, Luke 7. 15, John 11. 43; by Peter, Acts 9. 40; by Paul, 20. 10. Moreover, in Elijah, 2 Kings 2. v. 9. 11; in Job, Job 13. 15 & 19. 25; in Nebuchadnezzar, Isa. 14. v. 8. 9. 11; and from the saying of Christ, Matt. 10. 28, in Christ himself, the author of resurrection and eternal life, Ps. 6; Matt. 27. 50; Luke 23. 46; in Lazarus and the rich man, Luke 16. v. 22. 23; in the unjust steward, Luke 16. 9; in the thief hanging at Christ's right hand, 23. 43. See 1 Cor. 15. 12; 1 Thess. 4. v. 13. 14; 1 Tim. 4. 8; Heb. 12. 9. See RESURRECTION. The chastity of souls, 1 Cor. 7. 9; 1 Pet. 1. 22. To possess souls through patience, Luke 21. 19, is to enjoy a quiet and blessed life. To love one's soul, that is, one's life, is the expression used, after the most idiomatic Hebrew usage, of those who hold nothing dearer than this life. On the contrary, those are said not to love their soul who do not hesitate to expose it to dangers whenever there is need, Rev. 12. 11. To find the soul (that is, to save one's life) Matt. 10. 39 & 16. 25; Mark 8. 35; Luke 9. 24 & 17. 33; John 12. 25, is said of one who looks after the present life. For he seems to have perished who is in a certain peril of life, and conversely, he who escapes safe from it seems, as it were, to recover himself. Yet these things are said according to the common opinion of men, who, since they do not think about the future life, suppose that those who die have perished, and that those who slip out of death have escaped.

units.la: ANIMAS quorundam piorum, statim post mortem cum Christo in vita aeterna esse probatur, contra ψυχοπαννυχίας & Purgatorij figmentum, ex Luc. 23.43. 2. Cor. 5 8. Philip. 1.23. Apoc. 14.13. Vide PURGATORIUM. ¶ Animas humanas, qui non ex traduce oriri, sed à Deo creari, & diuinitus in corpora infundi asserunt, (quae sententia à Classicis quibusque & probatissimis sacrae Theologiae Doctoribus recepta videtur) partim Scripturae testimoniis, partim argumentis physicis probare nituntur. Illud autem ante omnia hoc loco expendere, & probe tenere operaepretium fuerit. Non de eo hic quaeri: Anne animae rationales sint Dei creaturae? Quis enim sanae mentis de eo dubitet, cum animae non minus quam corpora humana Dei sint figmenta? Sed quaeritur: Anne ex anima Patris, Filij anima per traducem propagetur, virtute divina? quae etiam cum media adhibet, operari & creare dicitur, Ioannis 5.17.
units.tr: That the souls of certain pious people are, immediately after death, with Christ in eternal life is proved, against the vigil for souls [ψυχοπαννυχίας] and the fiction of Purgatory, from Luke 23. 43; 2 Cor. 5. 8; Phil. 1. 23; Rev. 14. 13. See PURGATORY. ¶ Those who maintain that human souls are not derived by traduction but are created by God and infused into bodies by divine action (an opinion which seems to have been received by all the most approved classical teachers of sacred theology) strive to prove it partly by testimonies of Scripture, partly by physical arguments. It will be worth weighing and firmly holding this point above all. Here the question is not this: Are rational souls creatures of God? For who of sound mind would doubt that, since souls, no less than human bodies, are the handiwork of God? But the question is this: Is the soul of the son propagated from the soul of the father by traduction, by divine power? Which power, when it employs means, is also said to work and to create, John 5. 17.

units.la: Testimonia haec sunt: Eccles. 12.7. vbi duo notanda veniunt. Primò, quòd anima rationalis hoc corporis ergastulo soluta, ad Deum reuerti expresse dicatur: Secundò, quòd Deus illam dedisse dicatur. Etsi autem corpus etiam a Deo dari non eo inficias, tamen alia longè ratione dari animam, quam corpus, ex comparatione, quae eo loci exprimitur, contendo. Neque tamen inde sequitur, quod quemadmodum corpus e terra est, ita & spiritus seu anima hominis sit a substantia Dei: sed illud sequitur; quemadmodum corpus ex terra sumptum in terram reuertitur, eamque ob causam pulueris nomen obtinet: ad eundem modum anima redit ad Creatorem suum, a quo profecta fuerat, v. 9. Huc faciunt & verba Petri, 1. Pet. 4.19. vbi Deum κτιστὴν, id est, Conditorem vocans, iubet vt fideli Conditori animam animas nostras commendemus. Item precatio Christi commendantis animam suam in manus Dei, Luc. 23. 46. Stephani, in manus Christi, Act.7.59. Antithesis etiam omnino poscere videtur, Heb.12,9. vbi πατέρες τῶν σαρκῶν opponuntur πατρὶ πνευμάτων. Nec est, vt excipiat quispiam, Deum non animarum saltem, sed & corporum factorem & Conditorem esse, ideóque Deum non posse diuinum infundere animas corporibus: Dicitur enim Deus, Pater κατ' ἐξοχὴν, quod in creandis animabus adhibeat hominum operam, ac in corporibus in lucem proferendis. Deinde, quia eos spiritus sui virtute miraculose reformat. Nec abludunt ab his illa etiam Sacrae Scripturae dicta, quae habentur Num.16.22. Ps.33.15. Zachar.12.1. Eodem pertinet & illud Ioan.5.17. Inter cetera aut Dei opera animarum ceu nobilissimarum hominis creationem referri debere, cuilibet liquere potest. Neque interim pugnat cum illo Christi dicto Moses, Genesis 2.v.2.3. cum illud dictum Mosis, non neget, continuando & propagando species iam creatas operari perpetuo: sed significet, Deum nouas rerum species produxisse, desiisse. Vnde Augustinus scite inquit: Hoc & nunc non instituendo quod non erat, sed multiplicando quod erat.
units.tr: These are the testimonies: Eccl. 12. 7, where two things are to be noted. First, that the rational soul, released from this prison of the body, is expressly said to return to God. Second, that God is said to have given it. Although I do not deny that the body too is given by God, I contend that the soul is given in a quite different way from the body, from the comparison which is expressed in that place. Nor does it follow from this that just as the body is from the earth, so the spirit or soul of man is of the substance of God. Rather, what follows is this: just as the body taken from the earth returns to the earth, and for this reason has the name of dust, so in the same way the soul returns to its Creator, from whom it had gone forth, v. 9. The words of Peter also favour this, 1 Pet. 4. 19, where, calling God the Creator [κτιστὴν], he bids us commend our souls to a faithful Creator. Likewise the prayer of Christ commending his soul into the hands of God, Luke 23. 46; that of Stephen, into the hands of Christ, Acts 7. 59. The antithesis also seems entirely to demand it, Heb. 12. 9, where the fathers of our flesh [πατέρες τῶν σαρκῶν] are set against the Father of spirits [πατρὶ πνευμάτων]. Nor is there any reason for someone to object that God is the maker and creator not only of souls but also of bodies, and therefore God cannot infuse divine souls into bodies. For God is called Father par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν], because in creating souls he employs the labour of men, and in bringing bodies into the light. Then, because by the power of his Spirit he miraculously reshapes these same souls. Nor do those sayings of Holy Scripture, which are found in Num. 16. 22; Ps. 33. 15; Zech. 12. 1, differ from these. To the same point belongs also John 5. 17. That among the other works of God the creation of human souls, as the most noble, ought to be counted, is clear to anyone. Nor does it meanwhile conflict with that saying of Moses, Gen. 2. 2. 3., that God rested, for it does not deny that God works perpetually by continuing and propagating the species already created; it signifies that God ceased to produce new kinds of things. Whence Augustine aptly says: "He both now works, not by instituting what did not exist, but by multiplying what did exist."

units.la: Argumenta sunt: Nulla substantia incorporea, seu spiritualis est partibilis. Anima rationalis in homine est substantia spiritualis & incorporea. Ergo. Vnde sequitur illam non per generationem, sed per creationem existere.
units.tr: The arguments are these: No incorporeal or spiritual substance is divisible. The rational soul in man is a spiritual and incorporeal substance. Therefore. Whence it follows that it exists not by generation but by creation.

units.la: Secundum: Inorganica organico modo ab organicis oriri non est consentaneum: Atqui anima rationalis est inorganica. Etsi enim in hac vita sæpenumero vtitur beneficio organorum corporis, tamen non modò dum in corpore actus habet reflexos, numerat, ratiocinatur, intelligit singularia & vniuersalia, colligit ex causis effectus, primorum notitiam habet, sed etiam vbi e corpore euocata est, suam habet ἐνέργειαν, & motus organicos. Ergo. Tertium: essentia intelligens & immortalis dignior est, quam vt ex facultate atque potentia materiae possit eliciri. Neque enim elementari naturae sunt insitae notitiae. Igitur anima humana est essentia intelligens, immortalis & in homine præstantissima. Ergo. Quartum: Dato vno conuenienti, plura sequi necesse est. Sed concessa hypothesi: Anima est ex traduce: sequitur absurdum, videlicet: Aut totam animam traduci, aut eius partem aliquam. Atqui tota non, nam totius traductio inferret partis interitum. Pars non, quia partitio in simplici & incorporea essentia nullum habere locum potest. Requirit autem ad traductionem, posse aliquid de essentia animae partis decidi. Haec de Problemate est quorundam magni nominis Theologorum sententia, de qua tamen modeste ingeniis salva conscientia licet ἐπέχειν, & suspensum tenere iudicium, donec confirmentur. Addi potest superioribus testimoniis & illud Esaiae 57. 16. ubi expresse Deus animas fecisse dicitur.
units.tr: Secondly: it is not consistent for inorganic things to arise from organic things in an organic way. But the rational soul is inorganic. Although in this life it often makes use of the benefit of the bodily organs, yet not only while it is in the body does it perform reflexive acts, count, reason, understand singulars and universals, infer effects from causes, and know first principles, but also when it has been called out of the body it has its own activity [ἐνέργειαν] and organic motions. Therefore... Thirdly: an intelligent and immortal essence is too noble to be drawn out of the faculty and power of matter. For innate notions do not belong to elemental nature. Therefore the human soul is an intelligent, immortal essence, the most excellent thing in man. Therefore... Fourthly: once one suitable thing is granted, many things must follow. But if the hypothesis is conceded that the soul comes by traduction, an absurdity follows: either the whole soul is transmitted, or some part of it. But not the whole, for the transmission of the whole would imply the perishing of the part. Not a part, because division cannot take place in a simple and incorporeal essence. Yet traduction requires that some part of the essence of the soul be detached. This is the opinion of certain theologians of great name on the Problem, about which, however, modest minds may, with conscience intact, suspend judgement and hold off until it is confirmed. To the above testimonies one may also add that passage of Isaiah 57.16, where God is expressly said to have made souls.

units.la: [ANIMAL, est illud rerum creatarum & corporearum genus quod sentit & movetur, seu quod vivit & respirat.
units.tr: [ANIMAL is that kind of created and corporeal thing which feels and moves, or which lives and breathes.

units.la: Animalibus a se creatis Deus benedixit: Gen.1.22. Alimenta paravit, & parat: v.30. Iob.39 3. Psal.104.27. Eadem hominis imperio subiecit: Gen.1.28. Ps.8.7. Ad vescendum Gen.9.3.2. Tim.4.4. Deut.14.4. Ad vestimentorum usum Gen. 3. 21. Iob.31.16. Ad alios infinitos usus, etiam ad eruditionem: Iob.12.7. Interroga pecus, & docebit te, &c. Vide Psal.32.9. Pro.6.6. Ioh.10 3. Quibus non est abutendum: Pr 12.10. Exod.20 10.1. Cor.9.9. Sed inde bonitas Dei, &c. celebranda: Ps.8. Iob 39. &c. Esa.1.2. Psal.104 24. &c. Psal 148.10. Psalm bestiae, & omnia iumenta: reptilia, & aves alatae, &c. laudent nomen Iehovae. Vide Bestia.]
units.tr: God blessed the animals he had created (Gen. 1.22). He provided and provides food for them (v. 30; Job 39.3; Ps. 104.27). He subjected them to the rule of man (Gen. 1.28; Ps. 8.7), for eating (Gen. 9.3; 1 Tim. 4.4; Deut. 14.4), for the use of clothing (Gen. 3.21; Job 31.16), and for countless other uses, including instruction (Job 12.7: "Ask the beast, and it will teach you," etc.). See Ps. 32.9; Prov. 6.6; John 10.3. They are not to be abused (Prov. 12.10; Exod. 20.10; 1 Cor. 9.9). Rather, from them the goodness of God is to be celebrated, etc. (Ps. 8; Job 39, etc.; Isa. 1.2; Ps. 104.24, etc.; Ps. 148.10: "Beasts, and all cattle, creeping things and feathered birds, etc., praise the name of Jehovah"). See Beast.]

units.la: ANIMALIA omnia a Deo creata, Gen.1.25. Animalia mutabilia quae, Leuit.11 3. Deut.14.v.4.5.6. immunda quae, Leuit.11 4. Deut. 14. 7. Animalia quae humanum sanguinem fuderint, punienda, Gen.9.5. Exod.21.28. Animantium esca, Genes.1.29. Psal.104.14. & 147.8. Animalia quatuor divinae maiestatis gloriam celebrantia, Apocal. 4. 8. Animalis homo Rom.8.6. 1.1. Cor.2.14.
units.tr: ALL ANIMALS were created by God (Gen. 1.25). Animals which are clean (Lev. 11.3; Deut. 14.4–6) and unclean (Lev. 11.4; Deut. 14.7). Animals which have shed human blood are to be punished (Gen. 9.5; Exod. 21.28). Animals as food (Gen. 1.29; Ps. 104.14; 147.8). The four animals celebrating the glory of the divine majesty (Rev. 4.8). Man is animal (Rom. 8.6; 1 Cor. 2.14).

units.la: ANNA, uxor Elcanae: Vide HANNA. (id est, gratiosa.)
units.tr: ANNA, wife of Elkanah. See HANNAH. (That is, gracious.)

units.la: ANNA, filia Phanuel, Prophetissa laudat Dominum, Luc.2.36.
units.tr: ANNA, daughter of Phanuel, a prophetess who praises the Lord (Luke 2.36).

units.la: ANNAS, Caiphae socer, Princeps Sacerdotum, Ioannis 18.13. Actor.4.6.
units.tr: ANNAS, father-in-law of Caiaphas, the High Priest (John 18.13; Acts 4.6).

units.la: ANNVLVS: Annuli aurei in summitate rationalis, Exod. 28 23.
units.tr: ANNULET: the golden rings on the breastpiece (Exod. 28.23).

units.la: ANNVS: Annus Iubilaeus, Leuit.25.10. Anno septimo debitae remittebantur, Deut.15.1. &c. Annorum Solis & Lunae cursu facta distinctio, Gen.1.14. Anni septuaginta captivitatis Babylonicae praefixi 2.Para.36.21. Ierem.25.11. & 29.10. Daniel.9.2. Anni quadringenti servitutis Aegyptiacae, Gen.15.13. eorum initium fieri debet ab initio exorti seminis A-brahae, id est, à nato Isaaco, ex quo Abraham consecutus promissionis semen: de quo agitur in illa prædictione, præcise impletur, cùm Israelitæ ex Ægypto educuntur. Annorum vero quadringentorum triginta, quorum fit mentio Exod. 12 49. Gal. 3. 17. nitium fieri debet ab initio peregrinationis Abrahami, Anni 70. vel 80. vitæ humanæ affixi, in deserto, Psalm. 90. 10. non autem hominibus, neque ad mundi finem. Annales, Esth. 2. 2 .& 6 1.
units.tr: ANNUS (year): the Year of Jubilee (Lev. 25.10). In the seventh year debts were remitted (Deut. 15.1, etc.). The distinction of years was made by the course of the Sun and Moon (Gen. 1.14). The seventy years of the Babylonian captivity were fixed in advance (2 Chron. 36.21; Jer. 25.11; 29.10; Dan. 9.2). The four hundred years of Egyptian servitude (Gen. 15.13) must be reckoned from the beginning of Abraham's seed as it arose, that is, from the birth of Isaac, from whom Abraham had the seed of promise, which is the subject of that prediction; it was precisely fulfilled when the Israelites were led out of Egypt. But the four hundred and thirty years mentioned at Exod. 12.40 and Gal. 3.17 must be reckoned from the beginning of Abraham's sojourning. The seventy or eighty years of human life are fixed for the desert (Ps. 90.10), but not for men, nor for the end of the world. ANNALS: Esth. 2.23 and 6.1.

units.la: CHRISTVS quis, & eius regnum, Esai. 11. 4. Dan. 7. v. 19. & 8. v. 9. 23. & 9. 27. & 12. 11. Zach. 11. 15. Mat. 24. 24. Marc. 6. Ioh. 5. 43. Act. 20. 29. 2. Thess. 2. 3. 1. Tim. 4. 1. 2. Thess. 2. 4. Apoc. 6. sceleratus filius perditionis, & homo peccati vocatur, 2. Thess. 2. 3. seductor est, Matth. 24. 5. 2. Thess. 2. verf. 9. 10. 2. Ioh. v. 7. [præ se ferens se esse Deum, 2. Thess. 2. 4. Impius iniquitatis mysterium id. v. 8.] superbia eius, 2. Thess. 2. 4. iniquitatis mysterium iam nunc operabatur, v. 7. suo tempore revelandus, v. 6. reprobis adoratur, Apoc. 13. 8. verbo Dei interficiendus, 1. Thess. 2. 8. Antichristi miracula mendacia, quibus eius imperium stabiliri oportuit, v. 9. eius imperium caducum, verf. 8. Antichristi multi, 1. Ioh. 2. 18. e fidelium coetu exituri, verf. 19. Antichristi revelati certissima τεκμήρια, 1. Timoth. 4. 1.
units.tr: CHRIST, who and of what kingdom (Isa. 11.4; Dan. 7.19; 8.9, 23; 9.27; 12.11; Zech. 11.15; Matt. 24.24; Mark 6; John 5.43; Acts 20.29; 2 Thess. 2.3; 1 Tim. 4.1; 2 Tim. 3.2; 1 John 2.18, 22; 4.3; 2 John 7; Jude 10; Rev. 11.7; 12.8; 14.9; 19.20; 20.2, 8). He is already in the world (1 John 4.3). He is a blasphemer against God and a sworn enemy of God (2 Thess. 2.4; Rev. 6). He is called the wicked son of perdition and the man of sin (2 Thess. 2.3). He is a deceiver (Matt. 24.5; 2 Thess. 2.9–10; 2 John 7). [Professing himself to be God, 2 Thess. 2.4. The impious one, the mystery of iniquity, v. 8.] His pride (2 Thess. 2.4). The mystery of iniquity was already at work, v. 7. He is to be revealed in his own time, v. 6. He is adored by the reprobate (Rev. 13.8). He is to be slain by the word of God (2 Thess. 2.8). The lying miracles of Antichrist, by which his rule had to be established, v. 9. His rule is transitory, v. 8. Many Antichrists (1 John 2.18) are to go out from the company of the faithful, v. 19. The most certain tokens of the revealed Antichrist (1 Tim. 4.1).

units.la: ANTIOCHIA civitas Syriæ suscipit Apostolorum de Christo prædicationem, Act. 11. v. 19. 26. Antiochiæ erant Doctores & Prophetæ, v. 27. & 13. 1. Antiochenses primi dicti sunt Christiani, Act. 11. 26. Antiochena synodus, 15. 6. Vide Gal. 2. 11. Alia est Antiochia in Pisidia, 2. Tim. 3. 11.
units.tr: ANTIOCH, a city of Syria, received the preaching of the Apostles concerning Christ (Acts 11.19, 26). There were teachers and prophets at Antioch (v. 27; 13.1). The Antiochenes were the first to be called Christians (Acts 11.26). The Synod of Antioch (15.6). See Gal. 2.11. There is another Antioch, in Pisidia (2 Tim. 3.11).

units.la: ANTIPAS (Apoc. 2. 13.) fidelis Martyr Christi.
units.tr: ANTIPAS (Rev. 2.13), a faithful martyr of Christ.

units.la: ANTIQVVS dierum, Deus Dan. 7. 9. 13. 22. Antiquitas, Esa. 23. 7. Ezech. 16. 55.]
units.tr: ANCIENT OF DAYS, God (Dan. 7.9, 13, 22). Antiquity (Isa. 23.7; Ezek. 16.55).]

units.la: ANTIQVAS vias inquirendas & observandas, & à novis declinandum esse probant Pontifici, ut rancinas suas & impias, quas vocant, Traditiones, solo antiquitatis nomine Christiano orbi obtrudere possint, Iere. 6. 16. Prov. 22. 28. Eccl. 8. 11. & 39. 2. Rom. 16. 17. Gal. 1. v. 6. 7. 8. 1. Timoth. 6. 20. 2. Tim. 4. 3. 2. Pet. 3. 17. 1. Ioh. 2. 24. 2. Ioh. v. 7. Iudæ v. 18. 19. 20. Verùm antiquitas, quæ cum Christo & doctrina ipsius nova consentit, quanti fieri debeat, docemur, Ioh. 10. 8. quò
units.tr: That the ancient ways are to be sought out and observed, and that one must turn away from new ones, is proved by the Papists, so that they may thrust their rancid and impious so-called Traditions upon the Christian world on the sole ground of their antiquity (Jer. 6.16; Prov. 22.28; Eccl. 8.11; 39.2; Rom. 16.17; Gal. 1.6–8; 1 Tim. 6.20; 2 Tim. 4.3; 2 Pet. 3.17; 1 John 2.24; 2 John 7; Jude 18–20). But we are taught how highly antiquity ought to be valued, when it agrees with Christ and his new doctrine (John 10.8), to which

units.la: pertinet aureum illud Chrysostomi dictum : Consuetudo longa sine veritate, vetustas erroris est: Et illud Cypriani lib.2.Epistolarum,epist.2.ad Donatum : Si solus Christus audiendus est, non debemus attendere, quid aliquis aliud nos faciendum putauerit; sed quid, qui ante omnes et Christus, prior fecerit. Neque enim hominis consuetudinem sequi oportet, sed Dei veritatem. Vbi allegat & illud Esa.29.v.13.14.Matt.15.9.(V.Traditio.)
units.tr: pertains that golden saying of Chrysostom: "Long custom without truth is the antiquity of error." And that saying of Cyprian in Book 2 of his Epistles, Epistle 2, to Donatus: "If Christ alone is to be heard, we ought not to attend to what anyone else has thought we should do, but to what Christ, who is before all, did first. For we ought to follow not human custom but the truth of God." Where he also cites Isa. 29.13–14 and Matt. 15.9. (See Tradition.)

units.la: ANTITHESES Hebraeis, cum certissime quippiam affirmant volunt, vsitatae,Ioh.1.20 & 3.v.15,16.17 36.& 5.24.
units.tr: ANTITHESES: the Hebrews used them when they wished to affirm something most certainly (John 1.20; 3.15–17, 36; 5.24).

units.la: ANVS quales esse debeant,& quod earum sit officium, Tit. v.3.4.5.[Honorandae,1.Tim.5.2.]
units.tr: AGES: what they ought to be, and what their duty is (Titus 2.3–5). [They are to be honoured, 1 Tim. 5.2.]

Iacob,28.17.& 32.7.& 34.30.Ruben,22.Israelitae, Exodi 14.10.Dauid, 1. Sam.20.1.2.Sam.24.1. 1.Paralip.21.13 [Populus Dei,Ps.102.1.]Ioseph Marię Deiparae vir,Matth.1.19.Christus,26.42.Marc.14 36.Luc.22. 43.44.Maria Magdalena,Marc.16.3.Oeconomus,Luc.16. Discipuli Christi, Ioh.13.22. Petri auditores, Act.2.37. Sacerdotes,4.16.Petrus,10.19.& 12.9.Paulus, Philipp.1.23.Epaphroditus:Philip.2.26.
units.tr: ANXIETY: anxiety joined with distrust is very harmful (Matt. 6.25; Luke 12.22; Phil. 4.6). See CARE. Examples of anxiety: Abram (Gen. 12.12); Lot (19.8); Abraham (21 and 22.8); Isaac (26.7); Jacob (28.17; 32.7; 34.30); Reuben (22); the Israelites (Exod. 14.10); David (1 Sam. 20.1; 2 Sam. 24.1; 1 Chron. 21.13); [the people of God, Ps. 102.1]; Joseph, husband of Mary the Mother of God (Matt. 1.19); Christ (26.42; Mark 14.36; Luke 22.43–44); Mary Magdalene (Mark 16.3); the steward (Luke 16); the disciples of Christ (John 13.22); the hearers of Peter (Acts 2.37); the priests (4.16); Peter (10.19; 12.9); Paul (Phil. 1.23); Epaphroditus (Phil. 2.26).

units.tr: [BOAR: a persecutor of the Church of God (Ps. 80.14). See Ps. 68.31.]

units.tr: [BEES (Deut. 1.44; Judg. 14.8): the symbol of a tyrant and a persecutor of the Church (Ps. 118.12; Isa. 7.18).]

units.tr: [APEX: the smallest point (Matt. 5.18; Luke 16.17).]

units.tr: To open the mouth through parables, a Hebraism: to speak in parables (Matt. 13.35). To have the mouth opened, meaning the use of the voice to be restored (Luke 1.64).

units.la: APOLLOS Iudaeus,vir doctus & facundus,Actor.18.24.1.Corinth.1.12.& 3.4.& 16.12.Exactius ab Aquila edoctus,Act.18.26.
units.tr: APOLLOS, a Jew, a learned and eloquent man, Acts 18:24; 1 Cor. 1:12; 3:4; 16:12. He was more accurately instructed by Aquila, Acts 18:26.

units.la: APOLOGIA : Apologiae exemplum: Pauli, Act.22.1.& 23.1. 24.10.& 26.1.Vide EXCVSATIO.
units.tr: APOLOGY: an example of an apology is that of Paul, Acts 22:1; 23:1; 24:10; 26:1. See EXCUSE.

units.la: APOSTASIA, in negotio religionis proprie ad eos pertinet, qui deserta vera religione, ad infamis religionis homines descisc unt, & non perseuerant in suscepta semel vera fide, qua fuerant imbuti & instituti. Contraria est perseuerantiae Christianae.
units.tr: APOSTASY, in matters of religion, properly belongs to those who, having forsaken the true religion, go over to men of infamous religion, and do not persevere in the true faith once professed, in which they had been imbued and instructed. It is the opposite of Christian perseverance.

Luc.6. 13.interdum etiam Christo tribuitur, Hebr 3.1. Apostoli vocabantur duodecim,etiam tum cum expuncto Iuda undecim tantum essent, 1.Corinth.15 5. generaliter pro tota Ecclesia Ierosolymitana, Act.15 33.pro Sapientibus & Scribis,Luc.11.49.vt patet ex Matth.23.34.
units.tr: APOSTLE: the name of apostle is sometimes extended to all ministers of the Word of God, Rom. 16:7; 2 Cor. 8:23; Phil. 2:25; sometimes it is restricted to the twelve, Matt. 10:2; Luke 6:13; sometimes it is also applied to Christ, Heb. 3:1. The twelve were called apostles even when, Judas having been removed, there were only eleven, 1 Cor. 15:5. It is used generally for the whole Church of Jerusalem, Acts 15:33; and for the wise men and scribes, Luke 11:49, as is clear from Matt. 23:34.

units.tr: APOSTLES are God's servants, 1 Cor. 3:9; dispensers of the mysteries of God, 4:1 (see the praises of MINISTERS). All were of equal dignity, 2 Cor. 11:5. They are said to judge the world, Matt. 19:28 (see SAINTS will judge the world). They are called reapers, John 4:38. They are the salt of the earth and the light of the world, Matt. 5:13-14. They are ministers, not lords, Matt. 20:26-27; Mark 10:43-44; Luke 22:25-27; 1 Cor. 3:5; 4:1-2; 2 Cor. 1:24; 4:5; Col. 1:23, 25. The apostles were beloved of Christ, John 13:1, and chosen, v. 18. Some apostles were more intimate with Christ, Matt. 17:1; Mark 9:2; 26:37; 14:33; Luke 8:51; 9:28; John 13:24. They received the Holy Spirit in tongues of fire, Acts 2:3. They were pleasing to the people, Acts 4:33. They were poor, Acts 3:6. They were witnesses of Christ, Luke 24:48; John 15:27; 21:24; Acts 1:8, 22; 2:32; 3:15; 4:33; 5:32; 10:39, 42; 13:31; 1 Cor. 15:15; 1 John 4:14. They were sent to preach the gospel throughout the whole world, Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:15; John 17:18; 20:21; Acts 1:8; 1 Cor. 12:28; Eph. 4:11. They were endowed with the Holy Spirit, Luke 24:49; John 20:22; Acts 1:8; 2:2-4. They were thrown into prison, Acts 4:3; 5:18. They were led out of prison by an angel, v. 19; 12:7. They taught in the Temple, 5:21, 42. They were beaten for the gospel, v. 40. They spoke from the Holy Spirit, Matt. 10:20; Luke 12:12; 2 Pet. 1:21.

units.tr: The CONDITION of the apostles: Matt. 10:16, 23; Luke 11:49; John 15:8; 16:20. Their dignity and excellence: Matt. 11:11. Their teaching: John 17:20. Their letter to the Gentiles: Acts 15:23. The gospel: 2 Cor. 4:3; Gal. 1:8-9. Their faith: Matt. 16:16; Mark 8:29; Luke 9:20; John 6:66-69; 16:27-30; 17:7-8. Their office: Matt. 10:7; 28:19; Mark 6:12; 16:15; Luke 9:2; John 15:16. Their names: Matt. 10:2-4; Mark 3:16, etc.; Luke 6:14, etc.; Acts 1:13. Prayer for the success of Christ's kingdom, Acts 4:24. Authority given by Christ, Matt. 10:1; 16:19; Mark 3:15; 6:7, 13; Luke 9:1; John 20:23; Acts 3:12; 4:10, 30; 5:5, 9; 9:34; 13:11; given by God, Acts 19:11; 2 Cor. 10:4. Ordinances: what they commanded to be observed, Acts 15:29; 16:4; 1 Thess. 4:2. Prerogative: Matt. 13:16. The apostles and prophets had the Spirit of God: Exod. 4:12; 2 Sam. 23:2; Dan. 9:10; Zech. 7:7; Matt. 10:20; Mark 13:11; John 14:17; Acts 1:5; 2:4; 4:31; 9:17; 19:6; 1 Cor. 2:12; 12:3; 2 Cor. 13:3; 1 Thess. 4:8; 2 Tim. 3:16; 1 Pet. 1:11; 2 Pet. 1:21. What was received from them is to be held fast, Rev. 2:25.

units.tr: Examples of appearances and special revelations of God: to Adam and Eve, Gen. 3:8-9; to Cain, 4:9; to Noah, 6:13-14; 7:1; 8:15; 9:1; to Abraham, 12:7; 17:1; 18:1; to Lot, 19:1; to Abimelech, 20:3; to Rebekah, 25:22-23; to Isaac, 26:2, 24; to Jacob, 28:11-13; 32:30; 35:9; 48:3; to Moses, Exod. 3:2; to Balaam, Num. 22:20; to Joshua, Josh. 1:1-2; to the Israelites, Judg. 1:2; to Gideon, 6:11; to Samuel, 1 Sam. 3:20; to David, 2 Sam. 2:12; to Nathan, 2 Sam. 7:4-5; to Solomon, 1 Kings 3:5; 9:1-3; to Elijah, 1 Kings 19:9-11; to Isaiah, Isa. 6:1-11; to Jeremiah, Jer. 1:2; to Ezekiel, Ezek. 1:3; to Daniel, Dan. 7:9-10; 10:5; to Christ at his baptism, Matt. 3:16; to Peter, James and John, Matt. 17:2-5; to Stephen, Acts 7:55-56; to Paul, Acts 16:8-10; 23:10-11; Gal. 1:12; 2:2; 2 Cor. 12:4; to Ananias, Acts 9:10; to the evangelist John, Rev. 1:13, etc. (See VISIONS, which were once frequent among the servants of God.)

units.la: APPETITVS ὁρεξις, est alicuius rei extra nos positæ persecutio,vel fuga,ex sensuum iudicio excitata , Rom.1.27.Exarserunt sua libidine , &c. compensationem quam oportuit erroris sui,in se recipientes.
units.tr: APPETITE [ὄρεξις] is the pursuit or avoidance of something placed outside us, aroused by the judgment of the senses, Rom. 1:27: "They burned in their lust, etc., receiving in themselves the recompense that was due for their error."

units.la: APPONERE cor, Exod.7.23.pro adiicere animum,Iob 1. 8.Ezech.40.4.aduertere animum aut adhibere.
units.tr: To APPLY the heart, Exod. 7:23, means to pay attention, to give heed: Job 1:8; Ezek. 40:4; to attend to or apply the mind.

units.la: [AQVA hæc inferior , est substantia quædam corporea, quæ sua natura fluida est , non stans, neque etiam viscosa aut vnctuosa, sed liquida, & resolui facilis, omnis liquationis causa in rebus concretis, non solida, neque renitens, humida & humectans, non sicca aut arefaciens. Habet enim has omnes proprietates, Psal. 104. 10. 11.]
units.tr: [WATER, this lower water, is a certain corporeal substance, which by its nature is fluid, not standing still, nor viscous or oily, but liquid and easily dissolved; the cause of all liquefaction in concrete things, not solid nor resisting, moist and moistening, not dry or drying. For it has all these properties, Ps. 104:10-11.]

units.la: QVA: Aqua e petra educitur, Exodi 17. 6. Num. 20. v. 10. 11. Psalm. 105. 41. Aquae nihil nocumenti aut obstaculi afferunt populo Dei, Exodi 14. 22. Psalm. 66. 6. Esa. 43. 2. Ion. 2. 5. Aqua nominatur persecutio, Psalm. 144. 7. Prou. 17. 14. Matt. 7. 25. Luc. 6. 48. Apoc. 12. 15. Aquae assimilantur cognitio Dei & dona Spiritus Sancti, Esaiae 11. 9. & 12. 3. & 35. 6. & 43. 20. & 44. 3. Ezech. 47. 1. &c. Zach. 14. 8. Ioan. 4. 10. & 7. 38. Aquam emunt filij Israel a filiis Esau, Deut. 2. 6. Aquae verbo Dei in unum locum congregatae, Genes. 1. 9. 10. Psalm. 33. 7. Aqua benedicta, (Vide BENEDICTIO.) Aquae diluvij, Genes. 7. 17. operuerunt terram diebus centum quinquaginta, 24. potest decrescere incipiunt, cap. 8. 1. &c. Aquae amarae dulces redduntur, Exodi 15. 25. Aquae contradictionis, 17. 7. Numer. 20. v. 11. 13. Aquae Iordanis siccantur, Ios. 3. 15. pallio Eliae diuiduntur, 2. Reg. 2. 8. Aquae mortiferae Elisaei ministerio sanantur, 2. Reg. 2. 21. Aquae obediunt Deo, Psalm. 104. 10. Aquae e Templo manantes, Ezech. 47. 1. (V. Amos 5. 8.)
units.tr: WATER: Water is brought out of the rock, Exod. 17:6; Num. 20:10-11; Ps. 105:41. Waters bring no harm or hindrance to the people of God, Exod. 14:22; Ps. 66:6; Isa. 43:2; Jonah 2:5. Persecution is called water, Ps. 144:7; Prov. 17:14; Matt. 7:25; Luke 6:48; Rev. 12:15. The knowledge of God and the gifts of the Holy Spirit are likened to water, Isa. 11:9; 12:3; 35:6; 43:20; 44:3; Ezek. 47:1, etc.; Zech. 14:8; John 4:10; 7:38. The children of Israel bought water from the children of Esau, Deut. 2:6. The waters gathered into one place by the Word of God, Gen. 1:9-10; Ps. 33:7. Holy water (see BLESSING). The waters of the flood, Gen. 7:17, covered the earth for one hundred and fifty days, v. 24; they begin to decrease, 8:1, etc. Bitter waters are made sweet, Exod. 15:25. Waters of strife, Exod. 17:7; Num. 20:11, 13. The waters of the Jordan are dried up, Josh. 3:15; divided by the mantle of Elijah, 2 Kings 2:8; deadly waters are healed by the ministry of Elisha, 2 Kings 2:21. The waters obey God, Ps. 104:10. Waters flowing from the Temple, Ezek. 47:1. (See Amos 5:8.)

units.la: Aquae viuae allegorice, pro immensa illa charitate Dei erga nos in Filio effusa in corda nostra per Spiritum Sanctum in vitam aeternam, Ioan. 4. 10. cuius fit mentio Rom. 5. 5. pro donis Spiritus Sancti instar aquae effundendis, Esa. 44. 3. & 55. 1. Ioel 2. 28. Ioan. 7. 38. 39. Actor. 2. 17. Similis est metaphora Hebraeis familiaris, Ierem. 2. 13. Ioel. 3. 18. Zachar. 13. 1. Aqua, 1. Ioan. 5. 6. secundum nonnullos pro ablutione a peccato. Tribuitur etiam Spiritus Sancti gratiae, vt iam dictum est, Hebraeor. 10. 22. quoque ab effectu, vel ex antithesi externarum purificationum legis comparata.
units.tr: Living water, allegorically, means that immense love of God toward us poured out through the Son into our hearts by the Holy Spirit, for eternal life, John 4:10, of which mention is made in Rom. 5:5; it means the gifts of the Holy Spirit, to be poured out like water, Isa. 44:3; 55:1; Joel 2:28; John 7:38-39; Acts 2:17. A similar metaphor is familiar to the Hebrews, Jer. 2:13; Joel 3:18; Zech. 13:1. Water, 1 John 5:6, is according to some the washing away of sin. The Spirit's grace is also attributed to it, as has already been said, Heb. 10:22; it is compared from its effect, or from the contrast with the external purifications of the law.

units.la: Aquae denotatio varia est. 1. Aquarum moles seu ingens vt mare, seu minor vt vis multarum aquarum simul collectarum, Aqua dicitur frequenter in Scripturis, praesertim Gen. a 1. c. ad 10. Sumitur pro aqua dulci fontium, fluminum, piuuiae, puteorum, Gen. 18. 4. Exo. 2. 10. & 4. 9. Deut. 2. 6. Ios. 3 8. 13. 15. Iud. 1. 15. Psal. 13. & 78. 16. 20. Eccles. 2. 6. Dan. 1. 12. Ioann. 1. 26. & 2. 7. 9. & 4. 7. Act. 8. 36.
units.tr: The meaning of water is various. (1) A mass of waters, whether vast like the sea or smaller like the force of many waters gathered together, is frequently called water in Scripture, especially Gen. 1 to 10; Job 26:10; 28:25; Ps. 29:3; 77:18; 136:6; Prov. 8:24, 28-29; 30:4; Isa. 40:12; 54:9; 1 Pet. 3:20; 2 Pet. 3:5-6; Rev. 1:15; 14:2; 19:6. (2) It is taken for sweet water of springs, rivers, rain, and wells, Gen. 18:4; Exod. 2:10; 4:9; Deut. 2:6; Josh. 3:8, 13, 15; Judg. 1:15; Ps. 78:16, 20; Eccles. 2:6; Dan. 1:12; John 1:26; 2:7, 9; 4:7; Acts 8:36.

units.tr: 1 Tim. 5:23, etc. (3) Waters in general, sweet and salt, Lev. 11:34, etc. (4) Waters, for the free benefits of God and the effects of the Holy Spirit, Isa. 12:3; 55:1; Jer. 2:13; 17:13; Ezek. 16:4, 9; 47:12; Zech. 14:8; John 3:5; 4:10-11, 13-14; 7:38; Heb. 10:22; 1 John 5:6, 8; Rev. 7:17; 21:6; 22:1, 17. (5) Waters signify calamities, Ps. 18:17; 32:6; 66:12; 69:2, 15-16; 124:4-5; 144:7; Lam. 3:54; Ezek. 7:17; 21:7; 26:19; 27:26, 34; Jonah 2:6. (6) Waters signify the army of a people, Jer. 47:2; Rev. 17:1, 15. (7) Waters signify the source of human generation, Isa. 48:1, 8. (8) Waters signify tears, Ps. 119:136; Jer. 9:1, 18; Lam. 1:16; 3:48.

units.la: AQVILA Iudæus, hospes Pauli, Actor. 18.v.2.3.1. Corinth. 16.19. Pauli adiutor, Roman. 16.3.
units.tr: AQUILA, a Jew, Paul's host, Acts 18.2, 3; 1 Cor. 16.19; Paul's helper, Rom. 16.3.

units.la: AQVILA avis, eam non comedebant Iudæi, Leuit. 11.13. Deut. 14.12. natura eius, Iob. 39.v.30 31.32. 33. In senectute renovatur, Psal. 103.5. Ila. 40.31. Aquilæ parabola, Ezech. 17.3. Aquilæ illuc congregabuntur, ubi fuerit cadauer, Matth. 24.28. Lucæ 17.37. Paræmia, Ezech. 17.3. [Aquilo pars Septentrionalis, cuius mentio frequens in Scriptura. Aquilo ventus Iob. 26.6. Prou. 25.23. In Cant. c. 4. v. 16. etiam mysticum quod denotat, ut pleraque huius libelli fere omnia.]
units.tr: AQUILA, the bird: the Jews did not eat it, Lev. 11.13; Deut. 14.12. Its nature: Job 39.30, 31, 32, 33. It is renewed in old age, Ps. 103.5; Isa. 40.31. The parable of the eagle, Ezek. 17.3. "Wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will gather," Matt. 24.28; Luke 17.37. A proverb, Ezek. 17.3. [Aquilo, the northern region, which is mentioned often in Scripture. Aquilo as wind, Job 26.6; Prov. 25.23. In Cant. ch. 4 v. 16 it also denotes something mystical, as nearly everything does in this little book.]

units.tr: [AR, a city and region of the Moabites, Num. 21.25; Deut. 2.9, 18, 29; Isa. 15.1.]

units.tr: ARA: See ALTAR.

units.la: ARABIA Petræa Iudæ Aegyptóq; confinis, eius excidium prædicitur, Esa. 21.13. Arabes vastant terram Iuda, 2. Paral. 21.v.16.17. vincuntur ab Ozia Rege Iuda, 2. Paral. 26.7. Audiunt Apostolos: Act. 2.11.26.
units.tr: ARABIA Petraea, bordering on Judah and Egypt, whose destruction is foretold, Isa. 21.13. The Arabians lay waste the land of Judah, 2 Chron. 21.16, 17; they are defeated by Uzziah, king of Judah, 2 Chron. 26.7. They hear the apostles, Acts 2.11, 26.

units.la: ARAD Rex Cananæorum, pugnat contra Israel, Num. 21.1.
units.tr: ARAD, king of the Canaanites, fights against Israel, Num. 21.1.

units.tr: ARADIUS, son of Canaan, Gen. 10.18. See Arvadite.

units.tr: ARAM, also called Ram (son of Hezron), begat Amminadab, Ruth 4.19; 1 Chron. 2.10; Matt. 1.4; Luke 3.33.

units.la: ARAN, filius Thare, Gen. 11.26. genuit Loth. v.27. moritur, v.28.
units.tr: ARAN, son of Terah, Gen. 11.26; begat Lot, v.27; dies, v.28.

units.la: ARBITRIVM, vide Liberum arbitrium.
units.tr: ARBITRIUM: see Free will.

units.la: ARBOR: Arbores creantur, Gen. 1.11. Arbor μετωνυμικῶς pro fructu, Gene. 2.16. & 3.1. Arbor scientiæ, 2, 9. metonymice sic dicta ab effectu, quia gustaturi fructum illius, experturi erant quantum bonum amitterent, eius visum interdicit Deus homini, v. 17. Arbores fructiferæ in urbium euersione reseruandæ, Deut. 20.19. nisi expresso & extraordinario Dei mandato quod fit succindi præcipiantur. 2. Reg. 3.v.19.25. Arbor vitæ, typus immortalitatis, Gene. 2.9. Apoc. 2.7. de ea ne edat Adam, è Paradiso eiicitur. Ge[?] 3.1[?]
units.tr: ARBOR: trees are created, Gen. 1.11. "Tree" is used metonymically for its fruit, Gen. 2.16; 3.1. The tree of knowledge (2.9) is so called metonymically from its effect: those about to taste its fruit were to learn how much good they would lose. God forbids man to see it, v.17. Fruit trees are to be spared when cities are overthrown, Deut. 20.19, unless by an express and extraordinary command of God they are ordered to be cut down, 2 Kings 3.19, 25. The tree of life is a type of immortality, Gen. 2.9; Rev. 2.7. Adam is cast out of Paradise so that he may not eat of it. Ge[?] 3.1[?]

units.la: 3.v.22 23.24. Vide Leuit.19.23.24.25. Arbori fructiferæ confertur vir bonus Ps.1.Mat.7.17.& malus putri,v.18.
units.tr: 3.22, 23, 24. See Lev. 19.23, 24, 25. A good man is compared to a fruitful tree, Ps. 1; Matt. 7.17; a wicked man to a rotten one, v.18.

units.la: ARCA: Arca construitur à Noë iubente Domino, Gen. 6.14. Sap,10.4.& 14.6.Matth.24.38.Luc.17.27. ea fuit Baptismi figura,1.Pet.3 v.20.21.
units.tr: ARK: the ark is built by Noah at the Lord's command, Gen. 6.14; Wisd. 10.4; 14.6; Matt. 24.38; Luke 17.27. It was a figure of baptism, 1 Pet. 3.20, 21.

units.la: ARCA Noë fuit sacramentum extraordinarium, in qua Noë cum suis est à communi πανολπρία in aquis diluuij conseruatus, vt ipsi significaretur & obsignaretur conseruatio ab æterna pernicie per Christum:1.Pet.3.20 21.
units.tr: Noah's ark was an extraordinary sacrament, in which Noah and his family were preserved from the common [πανωλεθρία, universal destruction] in the waters of the flood, so that their preservation from eternal destruction through Christ might be signified and sealed to them: 1 Pet. 3.20, 21.

units.la: ARCA fœderis: ea vt construatur, iubet Dominus, Exodi 25. 10. fit à Beseleel,37.1. Rex gloriæ dicitur, sacramétali loquédi forma, quia signum erat, & ceu Sacramentum præsentiæ IEHOVAE, Psal.24.v.7.8. (solent enim Sacramenta nominibus earum rerum, quarum sunt Sacramenta, appellari, vt Circumcisio vocatur fœdus, Genes.17.10. Agnus Paschalis vocatur Pascha, id est transitus: Exo.12.11. pro agnus ad significandum transitum adhibitus: metonymia. Vide similes locos, Gen.33.20.Exo.17.15. Iudic.6.24. Ier.23.6.& 33.16. Ezech.48.35.) Itat in medio Iordanis dum transit populus, Iosuæ 3.17. locus pedum Dei vocatur, Esaiæ 60.13. à Silo adducitur in castra Israelitarum,1.Sam.4.4. capitur à Philistæis,v.11. collocatur iuxta Dagon,5.2. eius præsentia Dagon corruit,vers.3. cum muneribus remittitur à Philistæis,6.v.8.10.11. in ædibus Abinadab quiescit in Gabaa,7.1. adducitur à Dauide cum gaudio,2.Sam.6.v.3.4.5.1.Para.13.v.7.8. apud Obededom ponitur,2.Sam.6.v.10.11,1.Para.13. versic. 13.14. hinc in Ierusalem perfertur, 2. Sam.6.12.1.Paral.15.1.à Leuitis tantum ferebatur,1. Par.15.v 2.14. 15. reducitur in Ierusalem,2.Sam.15.v.25.29. in Templum infertur,1.Reg.8.v.4.6.2.Par.5 v.4.5.7. quid in ea continebatur,Exo.16.33.34.Deut.10.2.& 31.26.1. Reg.8.9.2,Par.5.10.Hebr.9 4.
units.tr: ARK of the covenant: the Lord commands that it be made, Exod. 25.10; it is made by Bezalel, 37.1. It is called the King of glory, in the sacramental manner of speaking, because it was a sign and, as it were, a sacrament of the presence of JEHOVAH, Ps. 24.7, 8. (For sacraments are usually named after the things of which they are sacraments, as circumcision is called a covenant, Gen. 17.10, and the Passover lamb is called Pascha, that is, passing over, Exod. 12.11, the lamb being used to signify the passing over: a metonymy. See similar passages, Gen. 33.20; Exod. 17.15; Judg. 6.24; Jer. 23.6; 33.16; Ezek. 48.35.) It stood in the middle of the Jordan while the people crossed, Josh. 3.17; it is called the footstool of God, Isa. 60.13. It is brought from Shiloh into the camp of Israel, 1 Sam. 4.4; captured by the Philistines, v.11; placed beside Dagon, 5.2; at its presence Dagon falls, v.3; sent back with gifts by the Philistines, 6.8, 10, 11; rests in the house of Abinadab in Gibeah, 7.1; brought by David with joy, 2 Sam. 6.3, 4, 5; 1 Chron. 13.7, 8; placed at the house of Obed-edom, 2 Sam. 6.10, 11; 1 Chron. 13.13, 14; from there carried into Jerusalem, 2 Sam. 6.12; 1 Chron. 15.1; carried only by the Levites, 1 Chron. 15.2, 14, 15; brought back into Jerusalem, 2 Sam. 15.25, 29; brought into the temple, 1 Kings 8.4, 6; 2 Chron. 5.4, 5, 7. What was contained in it: Exod. 16.33, 34; Deut. 10.2; 31.26; 1 Kings 8.9; 2 Chron. 5.10; Heb. 9.4.
ROYAL ARK: 2 Chron. 24.8, 10, 11; Ezra 6.8; 7.11.

units.la: ARCARIVS, arcæ custos, thesaurarius,Esth.3.9.Rom.16.23.]
units.tr: ARCHIVIST (ARCARIUS), keeper of the chest, treasurer, Esth. 3.9; Rom. 16.23.

units.la: ARCANVM: Arcana reuelare malum,Prouerb.11,13.& 25.v.9. 10. Exemplum: Christus,Matth.20.17. Vide MYSTERIVM. [Arcana iudicabuntur: Rom.2.16. Arcana verba,2.Cor.12.4. arcana secretorum, i. Thesauri, Esai.45.3. Arcanum, i. Sanctuarium Dei, Ezech.7.22.]
units.tr: SECRET (ARCANUM): revealing secrets is an evil, Prov. 11.13; 25.9, 10. Example: Christ, Matt. 20.17. See MYSTERY. [Secrets will be judged, Rom. 2.16. Secret words, 2 Cor. 12.4. Secret things of secrets, that is, treasures, Isa. 45.3. A secret, that is, the sanctuary of God, Ezek. 7.22.]

units.la: ARCHANGELVS: Archangelus Michael vocatur,Iudæ v.9. vox eius,1. Thess.4,16.
units.tr: ARCHANGEL: the archangel Michael is named, Jude v.9; his voice, 1 Thess. 4.16.

units.la: ARCHELAVS, loco Herodis patris Rex in Iudæa, Matthæi 2. 22.
units.tr: ARCHELAUS, king in Judea in place of his father Herod, Matt. 2.22.

units.la: ARCHIPPVS, verbi Minister, Col. 4,17. Philem. v.2.
units.tr: ARCHIPPUS, minister of the Word, Col. 4.17; Philem. v.2.

units.la: [ARCHISYNAGOGVS, Marc. 5,22. 35,36,38. Luc. 13,14. Act. 18.8. Synagogæ princeps.]
units.tr: [ARCHISYNAGOGUE, Mark 5.22, 35, 36, 38; Luke 13.14; Acts 18.8. Ruler of the synagogue.]

units.la: ARCHITECTVS: Paulus architectus sapiens, 1.Cor. 3,10.
units.tr: ARCHITECT: Paul is a wise architect, 1 Cor. 3.10.

units.la: [ARCHITRICLINVS, Ioann. 2.8.9.]
units.tr: [ARCHITRICLINUS, John 2.8, 9.]

units.la: [ARCTVRVS, syderis nomen, Iob. 9,9. & 38,32. Amos, 5,8.]
units.tr: [ARCTURUS, the name of a star, Job 9.9; 38.32; Amos 5.8.]

units.la: ARCVS Dei in nube, signum fœderis inter Deum & homines constituitur, Gen. 9. 13. ad v.18. usque. Ezech. 1,28. Arcus Dei, i. potentia quam exerit in homines, Psal. 7,13. Thren. 2,4. & 3,12. Hab. 3,9. Apoc. 6,2. Arcus hominis, arma bellica & vis armorum, Gen. 48.22. Iosh. 24.12. 2. Reg. 6,22. Psalm. 44,7. & 46,10. Esai. 41,2. Ierem. 49,35. & 51.56. Ezech. 39,3. Ose. 1,5. Zach. 9,10. Arcus, robur & artes impiorum, Psal. 11,2. & 37,14,15. & 58,8. & 64,4. ] Arcu iactis sagittis Ionathas patris sui voluntatem Dauidi significat, 1. Sam. 20,20 &c. Arcu missis sagittis, Ioas ab Elisæo liberationem Israelis discit, 2. Reg. 13. v.16.17.
units.tr: The bow of God in the cloud is established as the sign of the covenant between God and men, Gen. 9.13 to v.18; Ezek. 1.28. The bow of God, that is, the power he exerts over men, Ps. 7.13; Lam. 2.4; 3.12; Hab. 3.9; Rev. 6.2. The bow of man, that is, weapons of war and the force of arms, Gen. 48.22; Josh. 24.12; 2 Kings 6.22; Ps. 44.7; 46.10; Isa. 41.2; Jer. 49.35; 51.56; Ezek. 39.3; Hos. 1.5; Zech. 9.10. The bow, that is, the strength and arts of the wicked, Ps. 11.2; 37.14, 15; 58.8; 64.4. By shooting arrows from a bow, Jonathan signals his father's will to David, 1 Sam. 20.20, etc. By shooting arrows from a bow, Joash learns from Elisha of Israel's deliverance, 2 Kings 13.16, 17.

units.la: ARDOR: ardore percutiuntur præceptorum Dei transgressores, Deut. 28,22. V. Esa. 33.14. 2. Pet. 3.12. Iac. 1.11.
units.tr: BURNING (ARDOR): transgressors of God's precepts are struck with burning, Deut. 28.22. See Isa. 33.14; 2 Pet. 3.12; James 1.11.

units.la: AREOPAGVS, vicus erat Athenis: unde Paulus Athenien-sem compellauit: Act. 17.19.22. Unde Dionysius Areopagita ad fidem conuersus est, v.34. Ac postea ibidem Episcopus factus, Teste Eusebio.
units.tr: AREOPAGUS was a hill at Athens, from which Paul addressed the Athenians, Acts 17.19, 22. From there Dionysius the Areopagite was converted to the faith, v.34, and afterward was made bishop there, as Eusebius witnesses.

units.la: ARETAS rex, socer Herodis, cuius præfectus in Damasco paulum prehendere nitebatur: 2. Cor. 11.32.
units.tr: ARETAS the king, father-in-law of Herod, whose governor in Damascus sought to seize Paul, 2 Cor. 11.32.

units.la: AREVNA, aliàs Ornan, aream Dauidi vēdit, 2. Sam. 24. v.16,18. 20,22,23,24. 1. Paral. 21. v.24,25. ad construendum altare.
units.tr: ARAUNAH, otherwise Ornan, sold the threshing floor to David, 2 Sam. 24.16, 18, 20, 22, 23, 24; 1 Chron. 21.24, 25, for building an altar.

units.la: ARGENTVM: [purum, conflatum, percussum. Vide Siclus, talentum.] Argentum, aurum, æs & ferrum in expugnatione lo-richuntis Domino consecrantur, Ioh. 6. v.19,24. Argento abundant Ierosolymitani Salomonis tempore, 1. Reg. 10.2. 2. Paral. 9,27.
units.tr: SILVER: [pure, smelted, struck. See Shekel, talent.] Silver, gold, bronze and iron were consecrated to the Lord at the taking of Jericho, Ioh. 6.19, 24. Jerusalem abounded in silver in Solomon's time, 1 Kings 10.2; 2 Chron. 9.27.

units.la: [Argenteus, numi species, Gen. 20,16. & 45,22. Iudic. 16,5. 17,2,4,10,2. Sam. 18,12. 2. Reg. 6,5.2. Paral. 1,17. Cantic. 8,1. Esai. 7,23. Ierem. 32 9. Ose. 3,2. Zach. 11,12,13. Matth. 26,15. & 27,v.3,4,6,9. Argenreus, nomen adiect. vasa, idolum, candelabra. Argentea, &c.]
units.tr: [Silver, a kind of coin, Gen. 20.16; 45.22; Judg. 16.5; 17.2, 4, 10; 2 Sam. 18.12; 2 Kings 6.5; 2 Chron. 1.17; Song 8.1; Isa. 7.23; Jer. 32.9; Hos. 3.2; Zech. 11.12, 13; Matt. 26.15; 27.3, 4, 6, 9. Silvern, as an adjective: vessels, idol, candlesticks. Silver, etc.]

units.la: ARGVERE: Arguendus frater, non odio prosequendus, Leuit. 19,17. (Vide Admonitio.)
units.tr: TO ARGUE: a brother is to be reproved, not pursued with hatred, Lev. 19.17. (See Admonition.)

units.la: ARGVMENTVM, Genes.39.16. Acto.1.3. Hebr.11.1. Argumenta carnis, Iob.4.7.
units.tr: ARGUMENT: Gen. 39.16; Acts 1.3; Heb. 11.1. Arguments of the flesh, Job 4.7.

units.la: ARIDA: Arida vocatur terra, Gen.1, 10. Psalm. 95.5. Matth. 23.15. Aridus, arida, succo & vigore exhaustus. Esai. 35.7. & 44.3. & 56.3.
units.tr: DRY: the land is called dry, Gen. 1.10; Ps. 95.5; Matt. 23.15. Dry: parched, drained of sap and vigour. Isa. 35.7; 44.3; 56.3.

units.la: ARIDVS, gratia Dei vacuus, Luc. 23. 31. Arida ossa mortuorum instar, Ezech. 37.4.
units.tr: DRY, empty of God's grace, Luke 23.31. Dry bones like those of the dead, Ezek. 37.4.

units.la: [ARIEL, Leo Dei, altare Hierosol. Esai.29.1. 2.7. Ezech.43. 15.16.
units.tr: [ARIEL, Lion of God, the altar at Jerusalem, Isa. 29.1, 2, 7; Ezek. 43.15, 16.]

units.la: [Ariel, proprium nomen, Num. 26. 17. Esdr.8. 16. 1. Chron. 11.22.
units.tr: [Ariel, a proper name, Num. 26.17; Ezra 8.16; 1 Chron. 11.22.]

units.la: ARIMATHEA, vrbs in monte Ephraim, quae fuit patria Samuelis, Prophetae (1.Sam.1.1.) & Ioseph, qui corpus Christi sepultura mandauit, Luc. 23 30. &c.
units.tr: ARIMATHEA, a town on the mountain of Ephraim, the homeland of Samuel the prophet (1 Sam. 1.1), and of Joseph, who entrusted the body of Christ to burial, Luke 23.30, etc.

units.la: ARIOCH, rex Ellasaris. Gen.14.19. Arioch, praefectus satellitum, Dan.2.14. 15. 24.25.
units.tr: ARIOCH, king of Ellasar, Gen. 14.19. Arioch, commander of the guards, Dan. 2.14, 15, 24, 25.

units.la: ARIOLI & Aruspices, Dan.2.v.2.27. & 4.6.& 5.v. 7, 11. Act. 19,13. Vide DIVINI, INCANTATORES, Astrologia.
units.tr: SOOTHSAYERS and augurs, Dan. 2.2, 27; 4.6; 5.7, 11; Acts 19.13. See DIVINERS, ENCHANTERS, Astrology.

units.la: ARISTARCHVS Pauli comes, Actor. 19, 29. & 20.4. & 27, 2. Col.4, 10. Philem.v.24. [Aristobulus, Rom 16 10.]
units.tr: ARISTARCHUS, companion of Paul, Acts 19.29; 20.4; 27.2; Col. 4.10; Philem. v.24. [Aristobulus, Rom. 16.10.]

units.la: ARMA, Arma piorum quae, & qualia, 2. Corinth.10,4. Ephe. 6,13 1. Ioan.3.9. Vide PII. ARMA Pastorum, Vide PASTOR, [Arma bellica, & Venatoria, Deut.1 41. Gen.27.3.]
units.tr: ARMS: what and what kind of arms the godly have, 2 Cor. 10.4; Eph. 6.13; 1 John 3.9. See PIOUS. ARMS of the Pastors: see PASTOR. [Weapons of war and of hunting, Deut. 1.41; Gen. 27.3.]

units.la: [ARMA Spiritualia, Rom.6,13. & 13,12.2. Cor. 6,7. & 10,4.
units.tr: [Spiritual arms, Rom. 6.13; 13.12; 2 Cor. 6.7; 10.4.]

units.la: ARMAGEDDON, Apoc,16,16. Hebraea vox, quae idem est ac mons seu montana Megiddonis. Vide 2. Reg.23, 30, 2. Par. 35,22, Zach.12,11.]
units.tr: ARMAGEDDON, Rev. 16.16. A Hebrew word, which is the same as the mountain or hill country of Megiddo. See 2 Kings 23.30; 2 Chron. 35.22; Zech. 12.11.]

units.la: ARMAMENTARIVM: Armamentaria clypeorum & hastarum per singulas ciuitates Iuda,2. Paral.11.12.
units.tr: ARMOURY: armouries of shields and spears in each city of Judah, 2 Chron. 11.12.

units.la: ARMATVRAE militis Christiani perelegans descriptio Ephes.6.14.&c.
units.tr: A most elegant description of the armour of the Christian soldier, Eph. 6.14, etc.

units.la: ARMATVS validus, Luc.11,21.
units.tr: ARMED, strong, Luke 11.21.

units.la: [Armenia, (Hebr. Ararat; Gen.8,4,2. Reg.19,37.] regio Asiae.
units.tr: [Armenia (Hebrew Ararat; Gen. 8.4; 2 Kings 19.37), a region of Asia.]

units.la: ARMENTVM magnum pecus, minori (quale est ouis, agnus, oppositum, Gen.13 5.& 18,7. & 26,14. & saepius apud Moses & Prophetas.
units.tr: ARMENTUM: a large herd, as opposed to smaller cattle, such as sheep and lambs. Gen. 13.5; 18.7; 26.14; and often in Moses and the Prophets.

units.la: ARMIGER Abimeleci, Iudic. 9,54. Ionathanis, 1. Sam. 14,1. &c. Ioabi,2. Sam,23,37, 1. Chr.11.39. Goliath. 1. Sam. 17, 7. 41. Sanlis,1.Sam.31,v.4. 5,6. 1.Par.10. 4 5.& 11.39. Armigeri decem Ioabi, 2.Sam.18,15.
units.tr: ARMIGER: the armour-bearer of Abimelech, Judg. 9.54; of Jonathan, 1 Sam. 14.1, etc.; of Joab, 2 Sam. 23.37; 1 Chr. 11.39; of Goliath, 1 Sam. 17.7, 41; of Saul, 1 Sam. 31.4, 5, 6; 1 Chr. 10.4, 5; and 11.39. Ten armour-bearers of Joab, 2 Sam. 18.15.

units.la: ARMILLA, externum manus hominis ornamentum preciosum, Gen.24,22,30, 47. & 38, 18, 25. Exod. 35,22. Nu.31,
units.tr: ARMILLA: a precious ornament worn on the human hand, Gen. 24.22, 30, 47; 38.18, 25; Exod. 35.22; Num. 31.50; Isa. 3.19; Ezek. 16.11; 23.42. ARMILLA: a bracelet, Job 40.21.

units.la: 50. Esai.3,19. Ezech. 16.11.& 23.42. Armilla, spina,Iob,40, 21.
units.tr: (continued from the previous unit's references as printed).

units.la: ARMVS pecudis offerebatur sub lege & sacerdoti dabatur, Leuitic.7.32.&c.& 8,25,26. & 9,21,& 10,14.Num.6 19. & 18.18. Deut.18. 3. Ezech. 24. 4. Armus Sauli reseruatus, 1. Sam. 9. 24.
units.tr: ARMUS: the shoulder of a sacrificial animal was offered under the law and given to the priest, Lev. 7.32, etc.; 8.25, 26; 9.21; 10.14; Num. 6.19; 18.18; Deut. 18.3; Ezek. 24.4. The shoulder of Saul was reserved, 1 Sam. 9.24.

units.la: ARNON torrens celebris,Nu.21,13. &c. Deut.2 24 &c.Iof.12, 1.2.& 13,9.16. Iudic.11,13,18, 22.2. Reg.10.33 Esai.16,2.
units.tr: ARNON: a famous torrent, Num. 21.13, etc.; Deut. 2.24, etc.; Josh. 12.1, 2; 13.9, 16; Judg. 11.13, 18, 22; 2 Kings 10.33; Isa. 16.2.

units.la: [AROER, oppidum, cuius frequens mentio, Num.32. 34. Deut.2.36. Iosu.12. 12. Iudic. 11.26.2. Reg. 10.33.1. Chr. 5. 8. Esai.17.2. Ierem.48 19.
units.tr: AROER: a town often mentioned, Num. 32.34; Deut. 2.36; Josh. 12.2; Judg. 11.26; 2 Kings 10.33; 1 Chr. 5.8; Isa. 17.2; Jer. 48.19.

units.la: AROMATA, ad cibum,ad corporis ornatum,ad sacrificia, & ad funerum medicationem conducentia, Gen.37,25. & 50, 26.Exo.31,11. 2.Reg.20.13. 2.Para.16,14.Ester. 2. 12. Cant. 3,6, Marc.16,1. Ioan.19.40.
units.tr: AROMATICS: serving for food, for adorning the body, for sacrifices, and for the embalming of the dead, Gen. 37.25; 50.2, 26; Exod. 30.23; 2 Kings 20.13; 2 Chr. 16.14; Esth. 2.12; Song 3.6; Mark 16.1; John 19.40.

units.la: ARPHAD, nomen oppidi celebris,2.Reg.18 34.& 19,13. Esai. 10.9.Ierem.49 23.
units.tr: ARPHAD: the name of a famous town, 2 Kings 18.34; 19.13; Isa. 10.9; Jer. 49.23.

units.la: ARPHAXAD patriarcha,Gen.10.22,24.Luc.3.35.] filius Sem, i.sanans vastationem.
units.tr: ARPHAXAD, the patriarch, son of Shem, Gen. 10.22, 24; Luke 3.35; i.e. healing the devastation.

units.la: ARRHABO,Vide PIGNVS, Arrhabo Spiritus,2. Cor. 1. 22. & 5.5.Vide PIGNVS,& SPIRITVS Sanctus.
units.tr: ARRHABO: see PLEDGE. The earnest of the Spirit, 2 Cor. 1.22; 5.5. See PLEDGE and the HOLY SPIRIT.

units.la: ARROGANTIA ὑπερηφανία est per quâ temeritas atque impudentia vrnam sibi comparat authoritatem Iacob.4.16. Gloriamini de arrogantia vestra: o mnis eiusmodi gloriatio mala est, 1. Ioh. 2. 16.Fastus vitę, non est ex patre, sed ex mundo&c.
units.tr: ARROGANCE (ὑπερηφανία [hyperēphania]) is that by which rashness and impudence win for themselves an unwarranted authority, James 4.16: "You glory in your arrogance; all such glorying is evil." 1 John 2.16: "The pride of life is not of the Father, but of the world," etc.

units.la: ARROGANTIA vitanda,Rom.12.16. Exempla: Cain, Genes.4. 9.Simeon & Leui,34.30. Pharao,Exod.5 2.&15.9.Goliath, 1.Sam.17.v.4.8.Roboam,2,Paral.10.14. Nabuchodonosor, Daniel,3.14. Iudæi, Ioan.18.30.Pilatus, 19.10. summus Sacerdos,Act.5.28.Herodes,12.23. Antichristus, 2 Thess.2.4. Vide Rom.1 30 2.Tim.3.2.
units.tr: ARROGANCE to be avoided, Rom. 12.16. Examples: Cain, Gen. 4.9; Simeon and Levi, 34.30; Pharaoh, Exod. 5.2; 15.9; Goliath, 1 Sam. 17.4, 8; Rehoboam, 2 Chr. 10.14; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3.14; the Jews, John 18.30; Pilate, 19.10; the high priest, Acts 5.28; Herod, 12.23; Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2.4. See Rom. 1.30; 2 Tim. 3.2.

units.la: ARTAXERXES,Longimanus, Rex Persarum , accipit literas plenas querelis aduersus Iudæos, 1.Esdr.4.v.7.17.respondet,iubens ædificationem Templi impediri, 4. 21. [Artaxerxes Mnemō,Esdr. 6.14.Nehem.2.1.& 5.4.& 13.6.]permittit, 7.1. &c.Esdram ducem Israelis constituit, 7.21. se Regem Regum venditat,v.12.
units.tr: ARTAXERXES Longimanus, king of the Persians, receives letters full of complaints against the Jews, 1 Esdras 4.7, 17; he replies, ordering that the building of the Temple be hindered, 4.21; [Artaxerxes Mnemon, Ezra 6.14; Neh. 2.1; 5.14; 13.6;] he permits it, 7.1, etc.; he appoints Ezra leader of Israel, 7.21; he styles himself King of Kings, v. 12.

units.la: ARS, τέχνη, est cuiusque rei scientia, usu, vel traditione,vel ratione percepta, tendens ad usum aliquem vitæ necessarium.
units.tr: ART, τέχνη [technē], is knowledge of anything, grasped by practice, by tradition or by reason, aiming at some practical use necessary for life.

units.la: Ascendere & descendere, Ioannis, 4. 47. ex Hebraeorum idiotismo sæpe dicitur, pro venire, nulla locorum habita ratione. Ascendit super cor, phrasi Hebraica dicitur, pro subiit animum, Ieremiæ 7.31. & 19.5. Ascendere in cœlum, Ioannis 3,13. allegoricè, pro spiritualis intelligentiæ luce præditum esse.
units.tr: To ascend and to descend, John 4.47, is often used in the Hebrew idiom for to come, with no regard to place. "He ascended upon the heart" is a Hebrew phrase meaning it came into his mind, Jer. 7.31; 19.5. To ascend into heaven, John 3.13, allegorically means to be endowed with the light of spiritual understanding.

units.la: [Ascendere, proprie, sursum scandere, de loco inferiore in superiorem ferri ac moueri, Gen. 13.1. Ps. 139.8. & alibi passim. Ad hanc significationem refertur articulus de ascensione Christi. Secundò, de Deo humanitus dicitur, Genes. 17.22. Exod. 33 3. Psa. 18.9. Esa. 19.1. Ezech. 11.23. Habac. 3.8. Tertiò, de affectibus um Deo attributis, tum humanis dicitur, Exod. 2.23. Psal. 18.9. Ierem. 3.16. & 19.5. & 32.35. Luc. 24.38. Quartò ad Angelos accommodatur, Genes. 28.12. Ioan. 1.52. Quintò, de Christo, Iehouæ Angelo, dicitur, Iudic. 13.20. Sextò, de mentis ascensu, seu de intelligentia mysteriorum Dei, Ioann. 3.13.
units.tr: [To ascend, properly, to climb upward, to be carried and moved from a lower place to a higher, Gen. 13.1; Ps. 139.8, and everywhere else. To this meaning belongs the article on the ascension of Christ. Secondly, it is said of God in human terms, Gen. 17.22; Exod. 33.3; Ps. 18.9; Isa. 19.1; Ezek. 11.23; Hab. 3.8. Thirdly, it is said of God's attributed affections, both divine and human, Exod. 2.23; Ps. 18.9; Jer. 3.16; 19.5; 32.35; Luke 24.38. Fourthly, it is applied to angels, Gen. 28.12; John 1.52. Fifthly, it is said of Christ, the Angel of Jehovah, Judg. 13.20. Sixthly, of the ascent of the mind, or the understanding of the mysteries of God, John 3.13.]

units.la: TORGIA, est sancti & naturalis affectus, qui ϛοργὴ dicitur, contemptio, vel obliteratio propter odium, vel lucri vel aliam quamlibet turpem causam, Esa.49.15. Exempla Saulis in Dauidem generum, 1. Sam.19.14. Et in filium Ionathan:1.Samuel.20.33. Vide Roman.1,28.2. Tim 3.3. Vide Storge.
units.tr: STORGE is the holy and natural affection, which is called στοργή: contempt or forgetting out of hatred, or for gain, or for some other base cause. Isaiah 49.15. Examples: Saul against his son-in-law David, 1 Samuel 19.14; and against the son of Jonathan, 1 Samuel 20.33. See Romans 1.28; 2 Timothy 3.3. See Storge.

units.la: Astrologia. Astrologi iudiciarij sunt ij, qui que priuatim vel publicè, vel ex hominum deliberatione, vel ex sola Dei ipsius voluntate geruntur & fiunt, ex astris pendere censent, eaque se posse denuntiare venditant. Vide Diuini, Arioli. Damnatur Deut.18.10. Hier.10.2. vt blasphema & idololatriæ plena, cum astris tribuat, quod Dei proprium est: Pro.21.1. Dan.2. salsissima, vt rerum euentus semper comprobauit. Quia homines à pietate ad impietatem trudit, dum eos ad astra remittit. Vnde Astrologi olim Dei hostes sunt habiti. Quia eorum iudicia irrita facit Deus: Esa 44.24. & 47.13. Et grauis poena imminet iis, qui ab astrologia pendent: Esa.2.6. Leuit.20.6. & astrologis ipsis.
units.tr: ASTROLOGY. Judicial astrologers are those who, whether privately or publicly, whether by human deliberation or by the sole will of God himself, judge that things are carried on and come to pass as depending on the stars, and who boast that they can foretell them. See DIVINERS, AUGURS. Condemned in Deuteronomy 18.10 and Jeremiah 10.2 as blasphemous and full of idolatry, since it ascribes to the stars what is proper to God: Proverbs 21.1; Daniel 2. It is most false, as the outcome of events has always proved. It thrusts men from piety into impiety, while it sends them back to the stars. Hence astrologers were once regarded as enemies of God, because God makes their judgments void: Isaiah 44.24; 47.13. A grave punishment hangs over those who depend on astrology: Isaiah 2.6; Leviticus 20.6; and over the astrologers themselves.

units.la: ATAXIA, Ἀταξία, inordinatio (vt ita dicam) est externa vitæ dissolutio, quæ vel in singulis, vel in toto Reip. ordine apparet manéque impunita: qualis fuit viuendi ratio Sodomitis, & est vbicunque externæ disciplinæ honestas inter homines nulla viget, opponitur honestati. Vide 2. Thess.3.11. & 1. Thess.5.14.
units.tr: ATAXIA [Ἀταξία], disorder (as I may call it) is the outward dissolution of life, which appears either in individuals or in the whole order of the commonwealth, and goes unpunished. Such was the way of life of the Sodomites. It is found wherever no outward discipline of honesty flourishes among men, and it is opposed to honesty. See 2 Thessalonians 3.11; 1 Thessalonians 5.14.

units.la: ATRIVM legale, Tabernaculi, & eius forma, Exod.27.9. Atrium Sacerdotum extruitur, 2. Paral.4.9. Atrium templi duplex: Atrium Sacerdotum seu interius: & Atrium populi, quod Basilica, siue Basilica grandis dicitur, 2. Paral.4.&6.13. Alibi dicitur Porticus Salomonis, Act.3.11. & 5.1. Hoc Atrium Templi nomine sæpe intelligitur in novo Testamento, vt Matth.21.12. Act.3.1. quoniam populus ultrà non progrediebatur, sed in illo adorabat. In hoc atrio concionabatur Christus, & ex eo eiecit vendentes & ementes, Matt.21.12. [Atrium hominis, Esther.4.11.&5.1. 6.4.5. Marc.14.54. & 15.16. Ioh.18.15. Atrium mysticum, Apoc.11.2.]
units.tr: The legal ATRIUM of the Tabernacle, and its form, Exodus 27.9. The court of the priests is built, 2 Chronicles 4.9. The temple court was double: the court of the priests, or inner court, and the court of the people, which is called the Basilica, or great Basilica, 2 Chronicles 4 and 6.13. Elsewhere it is called Solomon's Porch, Acts 3.11; 5.12. In the New Testament the name of the temple court is often understood by this, as in Matthew 21.12; Acts 3.1, since the people did not go further but worshipped in it. In this court Christ preached, and from it he drove out those who sold and bought, Matthew 21.12. [The court of a man, Esther 4.11; 5.1; 6.4, 5; Mark 14.54; 15.16; John 18.15. The mystical court, Revelation 11.2.]

Reg.5.16. Samuel,1. Sam.12.3. Daniel, Dan.5.17. Petrus, Act.8.20. Paulus, Act.20.33. Salomo, Prov.30.8. Dauid: Ps.119.36. Moses, Num.16.15.]
units.tr: AVARICE is an excessive regard for our own things, either from distrust of God's promises, or from zeal for acquiring or keeping money and not giving it. Examples of avarice: Elisha, 2 Kings 5.16; Samuel, 1 Samuel 12.3; Daniel, Daniel 5.17; Peter, Acts 8.20; Paul, Acts 20.33; Solomon, Proverbs 30.8; David, Psalm 119.36; Moses, Numbers 16.15.

AVARICE is condemned: Exodus 18.21; 20.17; 22.25; 23; Leviticus 19.13; 25.36; Deuteronomy 16.19; 17.17; 23.20; 25; Joshua 7.20; 1 Samuel 8.3; 25.3, 10; 1 Kings 21.2; 2 Kings 5.20, 22; Nehemiah 5.7; Job 20.15; 27.8; Psalm 15.5; 36.4; 62.10; 119.36; Proverbs 1.19; 8.10; 11.28; 12.27; 14.31; 15.27; 16.27; 17.8; 22.16; 23.4; 28.16; 29.4; 30.8; Ecclesiastes 2.26; 4.8; 5.9; 6.1, 2; Isaiah 1.23; 3.13, 14; 5.8; 8.23; 10.1, 2; 30.12; 32.5; 33.15, 16; 56.11; 57.17; 61.8; Jeremiah 6.13; 8.10; 22.17; 48.7; Ezekiel 16.49; 18.8, 9; 22.12, 13, 27; 33.31; 46.18; Amos 2.7; 4.1; 5.11, 12; 8.4, etc.; Micah 2.2; 3.5, 11; 6.11, 12; Nahum 3.1; Habakkuk 2.9, 12; Ecclesiasticus 14.3; 31.5; 41.4; Zechariah 7.10; Malachi 1.13, 14; Matthew 6.19, 24; 26.14; 27.3; Mark 7.22, 23; 8.36; Luke 9.3; 11.42; 12.15; 16.13; John 12.4; Acts 5.1; 8.19; 20.33; 24.26; Romans 1.29; 1 Corinthians 6.10; 2 Corinthians 9.5; Ephesians 5.3, 5; Philippians 4.11; Colossians 3.5; 1 Thessalonians 2.5; 4.6; 1 Timothy 3.3; 6.5, 9, 10; 2 Timothy 3.2; Titus 1.7, 11; Hebrews 13.5; James 2; 1 Peter 5.2; 2 Peter 2.3; Revelation 2.4. Avarice is idolatry, Ephesians 5.5; Colossians 3.5; it is the root of all evils, 1 Timothy 6.10. The avarice of the Pharisees: see PHARISEES. The avarice of false prophets: see FALSE PROPHETS. The avarice of priests: see PRIEST. The evils of avarice: Proverbs 27; Jeremiah 6.13; Ezekiel 22.12, 13, 15; Micah 2.2, 3; Matthew 5.12, 15.

Miseri sunt, ac vani sunt,
units.tr: AVARICIOUS men are despisers of the word of God, Matt. 6.24; 13.22; Mark 4.18-19; Luke 8.14; 26.14. They are cruel, Prov. 12.10; Isa. 5.1-2; Jer. 22.13; Ezek. 22.12, 27, 29; Mic. 2.2; 2.9-10; Zeph. 3.3; James 2.15-16. The cruelty of the avaricious is shown in the Pharisee, Matt. 15.5-6; Mark 7.11-12. They are like the husbandmen, Matt. 21.34-35; Mark 12.2-3, 5; Luke 20.10. They are false ministers, 2 Pet. 2.15. They are idolaters, Eph. 5.5, and avarice is called idolatry, Col. 3.5. This is said less of the emotion of misers, who neglect God for their treasure and depend wholly on their wealth rather than on the one God. (Otherwise the same could be said of gluttons and nearly all who are strongly attached to some thing, such as those whose god is their belly, Rom. 16.18; Phil. 3.19.) Rather, it is because misers think their life rests in their possessions, which cannot be said of the fornicator and others. So avarice is plainly called a species of idolatry, Col. 3.5. They are wretched and vain.

units.la: AUDACIA

est, quæ plura quàm decet pericula & alia suscipit,propriæ penè vitæ contemptu,2.Pet.2.10. Audaces sibi placentes,Ecclesiastic.8.18. Cum audace ne facias iter, ut non sit gravis in te: hic enim pro voluntate sua factus est,& vnà peribis huius insipientia,& cap.22 5. Patré, virúmque pudore afficit audax filia: sed apud utrosque ignominiosa futura est.
units.tr: is that which undertakes more dangers and others than is fitting, almost with contempt for one's own life, 2 Pet. 2.10. Bold men who please themselves, Ecclesiasticus 8.18: "Do not go on a journey with a bold man, lest he be a burden to you; for he does according to his own will, and you will perish together with his folly." And 22.5: "A bold daughter brings shame on her father and her husband, but she will be dishonoured by both." ## HEARING

units.la: AVDIO

proprie significat, Auditus sensu percipio,& metaphoricè pro sequentibus auditum affectibus aut motibus accipitur:nempe, credo,intelligo, approbo, sequor. De Deo humanitus etiam sæpe dicitur, & significat sæpius, penitus video, nonnunquam exaudio, sicut ex contextus circumstantiis facile constant.] Pro.1.5. Iacob.1.19.
units.tr: properly means to perceive by the sense of hearing, and metaphorically it is taken for the affections or movements that follow hearing, namely to believe, understand, approve, follow. Of God it is also often said in human terms, and it means most often to see clearly, sometimes to hear favourably, as is easily clear from the circumstances of the context. Prov. 1.5; James 1.19.

units.tr: Birds are created by God's word, Gen. 1.20. They are subjected to man, Gen. 9.2; Ps. 8.7-9, for the glory of the craftsman, ibid.; Ps. 148.10. Their flesh is for man's food, Gen. 9.2-3; 1 Tim. 4.3-4; Acts 10.12-13. God feeds them, Matt. 6.26. Birds with their young are not to be taken, Deut. 22.6. The ritual of offering birds, Lev. 1.14. Unclean birds, which are not to be offered, Lev. 11.13.

units.la: AVRIS, A Deo datur: Pro.20.12. Etiam spiritualis: vt Dauid, Aures perfodisti mihi: Psalm.40.7. Israeli: Nondum dedit vobis Iehoua aures ad audiendum vsque in diem hunc, Deut.29.4. Sic tempore Messiae praedicitur fore, vt Aures audientium auscultent: Isa.32.3. Et surdorum patefiant, idem, 35.5. Alias sermo cor non penetrat. Audietis, & non intelligetis. Esa.6.9. Act.28.26. Officium & vsus. Qui habet aures ad audiendum, audiat, Matth.13. Quod ad incrementum, Prou.15.21. & 18.15. Auris verba probat, Iob.34. Abusus, quod ad legem: Pro.28.9. Quod ad pauperes, Pro. 21.13. Sic Epulo clamans non exauditur, Iob.15.21. In auribus improbi sonus pauorum est.
units.tr: The ear is given by God, Prov. 20.12. It is also spiritual, as David says: "You have pierced my ears," Ps. 40.7. To Israel: "The LORD has not yet given you ears to hear, to this day," Deut. 29.4. So in the time of the Messiah it is foretold that the ears of hearers shall listen, Isa. 32.3, and the ears of the deaf shall be opened, ibid. 35.5. Otherwise the word does not penetrate the heart. "You will hear and not understand," Isa. 6.9; Acts 28.26. Office and use: "He who has ears to hear, let him hear," Matt. 13. For growth: Prov. 15.21; 18.15. The ear tests words, Job 34.3. Its abuse, as regards the law: Prov. 28.9. As regards the poor: Prov. 21.13. So the rich man crying out is not heard, Job 15.21. "In the ears of the wicked is the sound of terrors."

[The ear is properly of man, but it is attributed to God...] whose ears are open to the just, Ps. 34.16, and to the meek, Ps. 10.17; James 5.4. Otherwise false gods, Ps. 17.
