units.tr: God is a helper, Deut. 33.26; 2 Chr. 32.8; Isa. 44.2; 50.9. Men as helpers, Isa. 31.3; 63.5; Lam. 1.7; Ezek. 30.8; 31.21.

units.la: AVXILIUM commendatur,Gal.5.13.Pro.24.11.12. Vide Simile membrorum,1.Cor.12.14. Exempla:Vxorae tempore belli cum commiseratione afflictorum ab vxore constanter, sibi temperantis,2.Sam.11.11. Mardochaei Estheram ad populo in summas angustias redacto succurrendum hortantis:
units.tr: Ibid. 4.13. The curse of Meroz and of its inhabitants, because they did not help God's suffering people. But Jael, who killed the enemy, was blessed, Judg. 5.23. See 2 Chron. 19.2.

units.la: Ibid.4.13 Merots, & habitatorum eius maledictio, quod populo Dei laboranti non succurrissent. Iahelis vero,quae eram occiderat benedictio, Iudic.5.23. Vide 2.Chr.19.2.
units.tr: Ibid. 4.13: Meroz, and the curse upon its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the people of God in its distress. But the blessing of Jael, the wife of Heber, Judg. 5.23. See 2 Chr. 19.2.

units.la: auxilium nostrum,Psal.124.8.&146.5.Heb.13.9. Deus auxilium eorum,qui ad ipsum recurrunt: Psal.31.20.&62.9. Orphanorum:Psal.10.14. Dauidis.Psal.27.9.&62.8. Israelis a tyrannide Pharaonis miraculose erepti: Exod.14.13.&c. Elisaei a Syriis,2.Reg.16.16. Pauli, 2.Tim.4.16,17. Resas Asa,2.Chr.14.11.
units.tr: our help, Ps. 124.8; 146.5; Heb. 13.9. God is the help of those who flee to him: Ps. 31.20; 62.9. Of orphans: Ps. 10.14. Of David: Ps. 27.9; 62.8. Of Israel, miraculously rescued from the tyranny of Pharaoh: Exod. 14.13, etc. Of Elisha against the Syrians, 2 Kings 16.16. Of Paul, 2 Tim. 4.16, 17. Asa's prayer, 2 Chr. 14.11.

units.la: filia Caleb,1.Par.2.49. Othonieli nubit,Iof.15.Iud.17.1.
units.tr: Daughter of Caleb, 1 Chr. 2.49. Marries Othniel, Josh. 15; Judg. 17.1.

units.la: EL, Vide HAZAEL.
units.tr: EL. See HAZAEL.

units.la: RIAS, qui & Oz as, filius Amasiae, Rex Iuda constituitur. 2.Reg.14.21. 2.Par.26.1. vincit Philistaeos & Ammonitas.
units.tr: AZARIAH, who is also called Uzziah, son of Amaziah, is made king of Judah. 2 Kings 14.21; 2 Chr. 26.1. He conquers the Philistines and the Ammonites.

units.la: tas, v. 7. agriculturæ deditus, v. 10. vsurpat Sacerdotum officium, & ob id lepra feritur, v. 19. leprosus moritur, 2. Reg. 15.7. 2. Paral. 26.23. reliquit filium Ioatham Regem, 2. Reg. 15.32. 1. Paral. 3.12. appellatur Ozias, 2. Paral. 26.19. Matth. 9. Matthat, Luc. 3.29. (i. auxilium Domini.)
units.tr: Uzziah, v. 7. Devoted to agriculture, v. 10. Usurps the office of the priests, and for this is struck with leprosy, v. 19. Dies a leper, 2 Kings 15.7; 2 Chr. 26.23. Leaves his son Jotham as king, 2 Kings 15.32; 1 Chr. 3.12. Is called Azariah, 2 Chr. 26.19. Matth. 9. Matthat, Luke 3.29. (i.e., the help of the Lord.)

units.la: Azarias Propheta, filius Obed, 2. Paral. 15.1. eius prophetia, v. 2. mittitur ad Regem Asa. v. 2.
units.tr: Azariah the prophet, son of Oded, 2 Chr. 15.1. His prophecy, v. 2, is sent to King Asa, v. 2.

units.la: Azarias Pontifex, 2. Paral. 26.17. & 31.10. Azariæ aliæ decem & septem varii nominis & officij occurrunt in libris Chronicorum, & Nehemiæ.
units.tr: Azarias, who is also Abednego, Dan. 1.7. Concerning whom the prayer is in ch. 3, v. 28.

units.la: Azarias, qui & Abdenago, Dan. 1.7. De quo oratio c. 3. 28.
units.tr: Azeka, a town, Josh. 10.10; 1 Chron. 12.36.

units.la: Azeca, oppidum, Ios. 10.10. 1. Chr. 12.36.
units.tr: Azotus, a town of Palestine: Acts 8.40.

units.la: Azotus oppidum Palæstinæ: Act. 8.40.
units.tr: Azor, son of Eliakim, Matt. 1.13. Azor, a city in the tribe of Asher, Josh. 11.10.

units.la: Azor, filius Eliakim, Matt. 1.13. Azor Vrbs in Tribu Aser, Ios. 11.10.
units.tr: Azor, son of Eliakim, Matt. 1.13. Azor, a city in the tribe of Asher, Josh. 11.10.

units.la: Azymus, sine fermento: Estis azymi, 1. Cor. 5.7. Prima dies azymorum, Matt. 26.17. V. Solennitas.
units.tr: Unleavened, without leaven: "You are unleavened," 1 Cor. 5.7. "The first day of unleavened bread," Matt. 26.17. See SOLEMNITY.

units.la: B.
units.tr: B.

units.la: Aal, idolum Samaritanorum, 1. Reg. 16. (Vide Idolorum catalogus,) eius altaria destruuntur à Gedeone, Iudic. 6. v. 25. 2. Sacerdotes à Iehu, 2. Reg. 10.25. à populo 11. 2. Paralip. 23. v. 17. à Iosia, 2. Reg. 23. 2. Paral. 34. 4. statua & templum, 2. Reg. 10. 26. 2. Paral. 23.17. vasa comburuntur, 2. Reg. 23.4. Sacerdotes occiduntur, 1. Reg. 18.40. 2. Reg. 10.25. & 23.5. Baal dominus, patronus.
units.tr: Baal, the idol of the Samaritans, 1 Kings 16. (See Catalogue of Idols.) Its altars were destroyed by Gideon, Judg. 6:25; its priests by Jehu, 2 Kings 10:25; by the people, 2 Chron. 23:17; by Josiah, 2 Kings 23; 2 Chron. 34:4. Its statue and temple were destroyed, 2 Kings 10:26; 2 Chron. 23:17. Its vessels were burned, 2 Kings 23:4. Its priests were killed, 1 Kings 18:40; 2 Kings 10:25 and 23:5. Baal means lord, patron.

units.la: Baalim pro tutelaribus & minimis diis. Iudic. 2. 11. & 3. & 8.33. & 10.6. 1. Sam. 7.4. & 12.10. 1. Reg. 16.31. & 18.18. 2. Paral. 33.3 & 34.4. Ier. 2.23. i. domini patroni.
units.tr: Baalim, the guardian and lesser gods: Judg. 2:11; 3:7 and 8:33; 10:6; 1 Sam. 7:4 and 12:10; 1 Kings 16:31 and 18:18; 2 Chron. 33:3 and 34:4; Jer. 2:23. That is, lords, patrons.

units.la: Baal, nomen loci, Iosu. 15.60. 1. Chr. 4.33. & 5.23. nomen Ioel vitæ, 1. Chr. 8.30. & 9.36.
units.tr: Baal, a place name, Josh. 15:60; 1 Chron. 4:33 and 5:23; a name of a man of the tribe of Reuben (Joel), 1 Chron. 8:30 and 9:36.

units.la: Baala, vrbs Iosu. 15.9. 10.11. 29. Baalath vrbs, Iosu. 19. 1. Reg. 9.18.
units.tr: Baalah, a city of Judah, Josh. 15:9; 10:11, 29. Baalath, a city, Josh. 19; 1 Kings 9:18.

units.la: Baal-Berith idolum. Vide Idolorum catalogus.
units.tr: Baal-Berith, an idol. See Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: Baal-Gad, oppidum, Iosu. 11.17. & 12.7. & 13.5.
units.tr: Baal-Gad, a town, Josh. 11:17; 12:7; 13:5.

units.la: Baal-Hasor, villa, 2. Sam. 15.23.
units.tr: Baal-Hazor, a village, 2 Sam. 13:23.

units.la: Baal Hermon, mons, Iudic. 3.3.
units.tr: Baal-Hermon, a mountain, Judg. 3:3.

units.la: Baalis, rex, Ierem. 40.14.
units.tr: Baalis, a king, Jer. 40:14.

units.la: Baal-Peor vel Baalphegor. Vide Idolorum catalogus.
units.tr: Baal-Peor or Baal-Phegor. See Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: AAL-PHARASIM, nomen loci, 2.Sam.5.20.1. Paral.14.11. hic vicit Philisthæos Dauid, unde & locus sic dictus est, ibid.V. Isa.28.21.i. Dominus diuisionum.
units.tr: BAAL-PERAZIM, a place name, 2 Sam. 5:20; 1 Chron. 14:11. Here David defeated the Philistines, and the place was so named from this, ibid. See Isa. 28:21, i.e., Lord of divisions.

units.la: AAL-ZEBVB, Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: BAAL-ZEBUB. See Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: AAL-ZEPHON, Vide ibidem.
units.tr: BAAL-ZEPHON. See the same place.

units.la: AANA, alter Princeps exercitus Saulis, 2.Sam.4.2. hic & Rechab commilito Isboseth occidunt, verf.6.7. eius caput Dauidi afferunt, verf.8. ob id occidi iubentur à Dauide, v.12.
units.tr: ABNER, the other commander of Saul's army, 2 Sam. 4:2. Here he and Rechab, fellow soldiers of Ish-bosheth, kill him, vv. 6–7. They bring his head to David, v. 8; for this reason David orders them to be killed, v. 12.

units.la: AASA, impius Rex Israel, 1, Reg.15.16. Rama urbem ædificat, v.17. domum Ieroboam euertit, v.29. Cum omni progenie sua extirpatur, 16.v.4.11. iuxta verbum Iehu, ver.1.2.3.
units.tr: BAASHA, an impious king of Israel, 1 Kings 15:16. He builds the city of Ramah, v. 17, and overthrows the house of Jeroboam, v. 29. He is cut off with all his family, 16:4, 11, according to the word of Jehu, vv. 1–3.

units.la: ABEL, quæ & Babylon, à confusione linguarum sic dicta, Genes.11.9. principium regni Nimrod, 10.10. turris Babel ædificatur, 11.5. ratio appellationis, verf.9. [Chaldæorum metropolis & regnum, sæpissime occurrit apud Phophetas.]
units.tr: BABEL, which is also Babylon, so called from the confusion of tongues, Gen. 11:9. The beginning of Nimrod's kingdom, 10:10. The tower of Babel is built, 11:5. The reason for the name, v. 9. [The metropolis and kingdom of the Chaldeans, which occurs very often in the Prophets.]

units.la: ABYLONICA captiuitas septuaginta annorum prædicitur, Leuit.26.31. Deut.4.26. & 28.36.2. Reg.20.17. & 23.27. Esa. 39.6. Ierem.9.21. & 16.13. & 20.4. eius executio, 2. Paralip. 36.18. Babylonicæ captiuitatis causa, 2. Reg.17.ver.7.13.18. finis prædicitur, Leuit.26.42. Deut. 4.29. & 30.2.1. Reg.8. 46.2.Paral.6.v.24.37. Esaiæ 14.1.& 40.1.& 48.20. Ierem.12. 15.& 31.9.& 32.37. Ezech.11.17. Dan.9.v.2. 25. liberatio fit, 1. Esdr.1.1.& 2.1. &c.
units.tr: The Babylonian captivity of seventy years is foretold, Lev. 26:31; Deut. 4:26 and 28:36; 2 Kings 20:17 and 23:27; Isa. 39:6; Jer. 9:21, 16:13 and 20:4. Its execution, 2 Chron. 36:18. The cause of the Babylonian captivity, 2 Kings 17, vv. 7, 13, 18. Its end is foretold, Lev. 26:42; Deut. 4:29 and 30:2; 1 Kings 8:46; 2 Chron. 6:24, 37; Isa. 14:1, 40:1 and 48:20; Jer. 12:15, 31:9 and 32:37; Ezek. 11:17; Dan. 9:2, 25. Deliverance takes place, 1 Esdras 1:1 and 2:1, etc.

units.la: ABYLONII quales hostes, Ierem.6.v.22.23.&c. Babylonis interitus prædicitur, Psalm.137, v.8.9. Esa.13.1.& 14.22.& 21. 1.& 47.1. Ierem.25.12.& 50.v.1.2. Apoc.14.8.& 16.19.& 17.1. & 18.2. &c.
units.tr: What kind of enemies the Babylonians were, Jer. 6:22–23, etc. The destruction of Babylon is foretold, Ps. 137:8–9; Isa. 13:1, 14:22, 21:1 and 47:1; Jer. 25:12 and 50:1–2; Rev. 14:8, 16:19, 17:1, 18:2, etc.

units.la: ABYLON altera in Ægypto, quæ & Cayrus & Babylis dicitur. Hinc priorem Epistolam scripsit Petrus, 1.Petr.5.13.
units.tr: Another Babylon in Egypt, which is also called Cairo and Babylis. Peter wrote his first Epistle from here, 1 Pet. 5:13.

units.la: ABYLON pro sede Antichristi, Apoc.14.8. eius turpitudinis nota, 17.5. eius ruina, 18.v.1 2.3.10 21.
units.tr: Babylon for the seat of Antichrist, Rev. 14:8. The mark of its shame, 17:5. Its ruin, 18:1–2, 3, 10, 21.

units.la: ABYLONII, 2.Reg.17.30.& 20,12. Esdr.4.9.
units.tr: Babylonians, 2 Kings 17:30 and 20:12; Ezra 4:9.

units.la: ACCHVS idolum, Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: ACCHUS, an idol. See Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: BACVLVS varia significat, 1. proprie est scipio, fustis, Genes. 32.10.& 38.18.25. Exod.12.11.& 21.19. Num.21.18.1. Sam.17. 40.2.Reg.4,29.31. Esai.10.15.& 28,27. Zach. 8.4. Secundo, figurate significat auxilium diuinum, Psalm.23.4. Tertio, arma noxia, robur, Esai.10.5 24.& 14.5. Ierem. 48. 17. Ezech. 29.6.& 39.9. Quarto, diuinæ indignationis instrumentum, Esai.10.5. Quinto, auxilii humanum, 2.Reg.18.21. Esai.36.6. Sexto, idolum, Ose.4.12. Septimo, vis arcana creaturis Creatore prout & quantumlibet concessa, Leui.26.26. Ez 4.16. & 5.16. & 14.16.]
units.tr: STAFF (BACULUS) has various meanings. 1. Properly it is a staff or club: Gen. 32:10 and 38:18, 25; Exod. 12:11 and 21:19; Num. 21:18; 1 Sam. 17:40; 2 Kings 4:29, 31; Isa. 10:15 and 28:27; Zech. 8:4. Second, figuratively it signifies divine help, Ps. 23:4. Third, a harmful weapon, strength, Isa. 10:5, 24 and 14:5; Jer. 48:17; Ezek. 29:6 and 39:9. Fourth, an instrument of divine indignation, Isa. 10:5. Fifth, human help, 2 Kings 18:21; Isa. 36:6. Sixth, an idol, Hos. 4:12. Seventh, a hidden power granted to creatures by the Creator, as far as it is granted, however great, Lev. 26:26; Ezek. 4:16, 5:16 and 14:16.]

units.la: BALA ciuitas, quæ & Segor, Gen.14.2. siue Thohar: quæ pro cibus Loth reseruata fuit: Gen.19.20. [nomé viri, 1.Par.5. & 7.13.]
units.tr: BALA, a city, which is also Zoar, Gen. 14:2, or Thoar, which was spared for Lot's sake, Gen. 19:20. [Also the name of a man, 1 Chron. 5 and 7:13.]

units.la: BALA, ancilla Rachel, Gene.29.v.28.29. ea concubina à Rachele Iacobo datur, 30.3. parit Dan, v.5. 6. & Nephtali, v. 8. Ruben incestu eam polluit, 35.22. eius filij, v.25.
units.tr: BILHAH, the maidservant of Rachel. Gen. 29:28–29. Rachel gives her as a concubine to Jacob, 30:3. She bears Dan, v. 5–6, and Naphtali, v. 8. Reuben defiles her by incest, 35:22. Her sons, v. 25.

units.la: BALAAM, filius Beor ariolus, Numer. 22.5. vocatus vt maledicer Israelitis, benedicit, Num.23. 11. Deut.23.v.4.5. Ie 24.v.9.10. Nehem.13.2. Christi aduentum prædicit, Num. 24.17. doctrina Balaam, Apoc.2.14. impietas, Mich.6.5. iniquissima, 2.Pet.2.15. gladio occiditur, Nu.31.8. [Balaam ciuitas, 1.Par.6.70. (Bileam, i.confusus populus.)
units.tr: BALAAM, son of Beor, a soothsayer, Num. 22:5. Called to curse the Israelites, he blesses them, Num. 23:11; Deut. 23:4–5; Josh. 24:9–10; Neh. 13:2. He foretells the coming of Christ, Num. 24:17. The teaching of Balaam, Rev. 2:14. His impiety, Mic. 6:5. His most wicked deeds, 2 Pet. 2:15. He is killed by the sword, Num. 31:8. [Balaam, a city, 1 Chron. 6:70. (Bileam, that is, confused people.)]

units.la: BALAC, Rex Moab, timens Israelitas, Balaam vt eis maledicere accessit, Numer. 22. v. 2.3.4.5.6. Iof.24.9. Vide Iudic.11. Mich.6.5. Apoc.2.14. (i.exterminans.)
units.tr: BALAK, king of Moab, fearing the Israelites, approached Balaam to have him curse them, Num. 22:2–6. Josh. 24:9. See Judg. 11; Mic. 6:5; Rev. 2:14. (That is, one who destroys.)

units.la: BALAENA, Cete, Iob. 40.20. est à Deo, Gen.1.21. Pf.104.25. (Vide Leuiathan, & Cetus.)
units.tr: BALAENA, a whale, Job 40:20. It is from God, Gen. 1:21; Ps. 104:25. (See Leviathan and Cetus.)

units.la: BALDAD Suhites, amicus Iob, cum duobus aliis amicis Iob inuisit, Iob.2.11. eius contra Iob disputatio, 8.v.1.2.3.4.& v.1.2.3. pro quo Iob orauit, cap.42.8.
units.tr: BILDAD the Shuhite, a friend of Job, who visited Job with two other friends, Job 2:11. His dispute against Job, 8:1–4 and vv. 1–3. For him Job prayed, chap. 42:8.

units.la: BALTASAR, Rex Babylonis, conuiuium celebrat, Danielis videt visionem horrendam, v. 5. turbatur ea, v 6.9. visionem exponit Daniel, v.17, &c. occiditur, & regnum eius transfertur ad Darium, v 30.
units.tr: BELSHAZZAR, king of Babylon, holds a banquet; he sees a dreadful vision of Daniel, v. 5; he is troubled by it, vv. 6, 9. Daniel explains the vision, v. 17, etc. He is killed, and his kingdom is transferred to Darius, v. 30.

units.la: [BALTASAR, nomen Danieli in Babylone impositum, Dan. 1.7. & 2.26. & 4.5.&c. & 5 12. & 10.1.]
units.tr: [BELTESHAZZAR, the name given to Daniel in Babylon, Dan. 1:7; 2:26; 4:5, etc.; 5:12; 10:1.]
[The sacred belt, Exod. 28:4, 39; 29:5, 9; 39:5, 21; Lev. 8:7. The military belt, Deut. 13:13; 1 Sam. 18:4; 2 Kings 3:21; Job 12:18; Ezek. 23:15.]

units.la: BANAIAS, filius Ioiadæ, vir fortissimus, 2.Sam.23.20. Dauid satellitio præpositus, v.23. Dux Cerethi & Pelethi, 20. Ioabum iussu Salomonis occidit, 1.Regum 2. v.29.31. (. ædificator domini.)
units.tr: BENAIAH, son of Jehoiada, a very brave man, 2 Sam. 23:20. Set over David's bodyguard, v. 23. Commander of the Cherethites and Pelethites, v. 20. He kills Joab by Solomon's order, 1 Kings 2:29, 31. (Builder of the Lord.)

units.la: BAPTISMVS, est sacramentum institutum à Christo in noui Testamento, quo abluimur aqua, in nomine Patris, Filij, Spiritus sancti, ad significandum nos recipi in gratiam Patre, propter sanguinem Christi pro nobis effusum, & generari ipsius spiritu ad vitæ nouitatem.
units.tr: BAPTISM is a sacrament instituted by Christ in the New Testament, by which we are washed with water in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, to signify that we are received into grace by the Father on account of the blood of Christ poured out for us, and are begotten by his Spirit to newness of life.

units.la: BAPTISMA, pro cruce Christi, & afflictionibus, Matthæi 22. Marc. 10. v. 38.39. Luc 12.50. Pro donis Spiritus Sancti visibilibus, Act.1.5. Baptismus Ioannis pro toto Ioannis ministerio, & doctrina, Matth.21.25. Marc.11 30. Luc.20.4. & 7. 29. Actor.10.37. & 13.24. & 18.25, & 19 3. Baptismus Ioannis, & Baptismus Christi vnus & idem, Act.19 4. Baptismus est tessera, siue exemplar nostrae regenerationis, Roman.6. 3. est signum spiritualis resurrectionis, v. 4. 5. symbolum sanctificationis, Ephes.5.26. Baptisma, sacramentum vnum est, Ephes.4. 5. figuratum per arcam Noe, 1. Pet. 3. v.20.21. à Christo institutum & praeceptum, Matth.28.19. Marc.16. 16. Ioann.3.22. poenitentiae symbolum est, Lucae, 3 3. & lavacrum regenerationis, à fine, quia eo nos ducit, & hic eius finis est, Tit.3.5. fidei sigillum, Matth.28.19. Marc.16.16. Act.2.41. & 8.ver.37.38. & 10.ver.47.48. & 16. v.14 15. 30.31. 32.33.34. & 18.8.
units.tr: BAPTISM stands for the cross of Christ and afflictions, Matt. 20:22; Mark 10:38–39; Luke 12:50. It stands for the visible gifts of the Holy Spirit, Acts 1:5. The baptism of John stands for the whole ministry and teaching of John, Matt. 21:25; Mark 11:30; Luke 20:4 and 7:29; Acts 10:37, 13:24, 18:25 and 19:3. The baptism of John and the baptism of Christ are one and the same, Acts 19:4. Baptism is a token or pattern of our regeneration, Rom. 6:3. It is a sign of spiritual resurrection, vv. 4–5. A token of sanctification, Eph. 5:26. Baptism is one sacrament, Eph. 4:5, prefigured by the ark of Noah, 1 Pet. 3:20–21. Instituted and commanded by Christ, Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:16; John 3:22. It is a symbol of repentance, Luke 3:3; and a washing of regeneration, from its end, because it leads us to that end, and this is its purpose, Titus 3:5. A seal of faith, Matt. 28:19; Mark 16:16; Acts 2:41, 8:37–38, 10:47–48, 16:14–15, 30–34, 18:8.

units.la: [Baptismus adumbrat mortificationem & viuificationem nostram, Rom.6.3. peractam Christi morte & resurrectione, verf.7. Stipulatio bonae conscientiae dicitur, 1. Petr.3.21. id est, obligatio mutua Dei & hominis baptizati: Dei quidem, testantis se recipere personam baptizatam in gratiam: Personae vero baptizatae, dantis fidem Deo, quod rite eum colere velit. Unde illud quoque patet: Baptismi veritatem non in externa ablutione positam esse, sed in bono conscientiae testimonio, 1. Petri 3.21. Baptisma Externum, cuius homo minister est, Matth.3.11. Luc.3.16. Internum, seu Spiritu Sancto & igne, cuius minister Christus, Matth.3.11. Marc.1.8. Luc.3 16. Ioan.1.33 Act.1.5. & 2.4. & 11.15.
units.tr: [Baptism shows forth our mortification and quickening, Rom. 6:3, accomplished by the death and resurrection of Christ, v. 7. It is called the pledge of a good conscience, 1 Pet. 3:21, that is, a mutual obligation between God and the baptized man: on God's part, testifying that he receives the baptized person into grace; on the part of the baptized person, pledging faith to God that he wishes to worship him rightly. Whence this also is clear: the truth of baptism does not consist in external washing, but in the good testimony of a conscience, 1 Pet. 3:21. External baptism, whose minister is a man, Matt. 3:11; Luke 3:16. Internal, or with the Holy Spirit and fire, whose minister is Christ, Matt. 3:11; Mark 1:8; Luke 3:16; John 1:33; Acts 1:5, 2:4, 11:15.]

units.la: PTISMATIS fructus, seu finis duplex: Remissio peccatorum, Acto.2 38. Coloss.2.12.13. Et renouatio, seu Regeneratio, Act.2.38. Coloss.2.11. Eo pertinent hae phrases: Baptizari in mortem Christi, pro percipere mortis Christi vim, extinguendo peccato, Roman. 6. 3. Baptizari in Christo, vel in Christum, pro, cum Christo coalescere, aut baptizari, vt cum Christo per baptismum coalescentes, vim ipsius percipiamus, extinguendo peccato, & creando nouo homine, Rom.6 3. Galat.3.27. Baptizari in nomine, vel in nomen IESV Christi, est Christo per baptismum nomen dare, Christoque nos consecrare, cuius mortis, sepulturae, ac resurrectionis simus participes in baptismo, cum peccatorum remissione, Actor.2.38. & 8.16. & 19.5.
units.tr: The fruit or end of baptism is twofold: the remission of sins, Acts 2:38; Col. 2:12–13; and renewal, or regeneration, Acts 2:38; Col. 2:11. To this belong these phrases: to be baptized into the death of Christ, meaning to receive the power of Christ's death by extinguishing sin, Rom. 6:3. To be baptized in Christ, or into Christ, meaning to coalesce with Christ, or to be baptized so that, coalescing with Christ through baptism, we receive his power, extinguishing sin and creating a new man, Rom. 6:3; Gal. 3:27. To be baptized in the name, or into the name of Jesus Christ, is to give oneself by baptism to Christ, and to be consecrated to Christ, of whose death, burial and resurrection we are made partakers in baptism, together with the remission of sins, Acts 2:38; 8:16; 19:5.

units.la: Neque enim eo loci baptismi formula praescribitur, sed finis & scopus baptismi declaratur. Baptizari in eius nomen (vtpote Patris, Filij & Spiritus Sancti, Matth.28.19) dicimur, cui nos per baptismum dicamus & consecramur: quamobrem recte negat Apostolus, 1. Corinth. 1. v. 13. quèquam Corinthiorum in nomen suum fuisse baptizatos. Baptizari in vnum corpus, 1. Corinth.12.v.13.27. est baptizari vt omnes in Christo capite coalescant, & vnum corpus fiant, adeò vt Ecclesia tota nihil aliud sit, quam vnus Christus, quoniam videlicet totum corpus mysticum à capite denominatur, & Ecclesia tota dicitur Christus. Corinth.12.v.12.13. Baptizari in remissionem peccatorum, hoc est, vt peccata Christi sanguine abluantur, Act. 38. Baptizari in mortem Christi, Rom. 6.3. seu pro mortuis, 1. Corinth.15.29. id est, vt mors extinguatur, & in Christi mortem peccatum in ipsis moriatur, & aboleatur, vel baptizari in resurrectionem à mortuis, cuius symbolum est baptismus, Roman.6.3. quamuis ibi de spirituali resurrectione, id est, regeneratione agatur. Baptizari in Mosis auspiciis ac ductu baptizari, 1. Corinth.10.2. baptizari in baptisma Ioannis, est doctrinam, quam Ioannes annunciabat, ac baptismi symbolo obsignabat, profiteri baptismo adhibito amplecti, Actor. 19.3. Baptizari aqua est aqua immergi, quae est externa baptismi forma. Matth. 3.11. Baptizari Spiritu Sancto & igni, ibid. ipsa Spiritus Sancti dona denotat, quibus fideles coelitus visibili signo imbuebantur interdum ante baptismum aquae, Act.10.47. interdum post baptisma, 19.5.
units.tr: Nor does this passage prescribe the form of baptism; it sets out the end and purpose of baptism. We are said to be baptized into the name of him (namely of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, Matt. 28:19) to whom through baptism we are dedicated and consecrated. So the Apostle rightly denies that any of the Corinthians had been baptized in his own name (1 Cor. 1:13). To be baptized into one body (1 Cor. 12:13, 27) means to be baptized so that all are joined together in Christ their head and become one body, so much so that the whole Church is nothing other than the one Christ, since the whole mystical body takes its name from the head, and the whole Church is called Christ (1 Cor. 12:12, 13). To be baptized into the remission of sins, that is, so that sins are washed away by the blood of Christ (Acts 2:38). To be baptized into the death of Christ (Rom. 6:3), or for the dead (1 Cor. 15:29), that is, so that death is extinguished and sin dies and is abolished in them through the death of Christ; or to be baptized into the resurrection from the dead, of which baptism is the symbol (Rom. 6:3), although there the spiritual resurrection, that is, regeneration, is what is in view. To be baptized under the guidance and leadership of Moses (1 Cor. 10:2). To be baptized into the baptism of John is to profess the doctrine that John proclaimed and sealed with the sign of baptism, and to embrace it with baptism applied (Acts 19:3). To be baptized in water is to be immersed in water, which is the outward form of baptism (Matt. 3:11). To be baptized with the Holy Spirit and with fire (ibid.) denotes the gifts of the Holy Spirit themselves, with which the faithful were sometimes endowed from heaven by a visible sign before the water of baptism (Acts 10:47), and sometimes after baptism (Acts 19:5).

units.la: Ex quibus omnibus recto sanae mentis aequilibritatis patet Baptismi vocabulum in triplici potestate significatione vsurpari: Vna propria, cùm immersionem, seu tinctionem declarat, quae ab effectu ablutionis seu lauacrum dicitur, Tit. 3.5. Translatitia duae, quarum vna est, cùm pro donorum Spiritus Sancti quasi effusio accipitur, Actor.1.5. & 2.2. & 10.47. & 11.16. Altera, cùm pro Ioannis doctrina & ministerio accipitur, Matth.21.25. Act.13.24. & 18.25. & 19.v.3.4. Quod autem de Baptismi nomine est dictum, baptizandi etiam verbo accommodandum est. Baptizare enim dicitur Minister, qui aqua tingit: Baptizari, qui aqua tingitur: Baptizare dicitur Deus, cùm Spiritus sui dona impertitur. Baptizatur Spiritu Deo, qui Spiritus donum accipit. Baptizauit Ioannes baptismo poenitentiae, cùm resipiscentiam doceret, eius symbolo ymbolum baptismum administraret. Baptizati sunt in baptisma Ioannis, quicunque eo doctrinæ genere fuerunt instituti.
units.tr: From all these things it is plain, to a sound and balanced mind, that the word baptism is used in a threefold sense. The first is its proper sense, when it denotes immersion or dipping, which from its effect is called washing or a laver (Titus 3:5). There are two transferred senses. One is when it is taken for a kind of outpouring of the gifts of the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:5; 2:2; 10:47; 11:16). The other is when it is taken for the doctrine and ministry of John (Matt. 21:25; Acts 13:24; 18:25; 19:3, 4). What has been said about the name baptism must also be applied to the verb to baptize. For the minister who sprinkles with water is said to baptize, and the one who is sprinkled with water is said to be baptized. God is said to baptize when he bestows the gifts of his Spirit; a man is baptized in the Spirit of God when he receives the gift of the Spirit. John baptized with the baptism of repentance, when he taught repentance and administered the sign of baptism as its symbol. Those are said to be baptized into John's baptism who were instructed in that kind of doctrine.

units.la: Baptisma infantibus minimè negandum, Genef.17. 14. Exod.4.v.24.25.26. Matth.11.28. & 18.14. & 19.13. Marc. 10.14. Lucæ 18.15. Ioann.3.5. Actor.2.v.39.4. & 16.v.15.33. & 18.8. 1.Corint.1.26. & 7.14. & 10.2. & 15.22. 1.Tim.2.4. Heb. 6.2. Baptizata integra domus, 1.Cor.1.16. Actor.16.v.15.33. & 18.8. ¶Pædobaptismum impugnat Anabaptistæ ex Mat. 28.19. Marc. 1, 4. & 16. v. 15.16. Baptismatis forma, Matth. 28.19. Baptisma non iterandum, Ephes.4.5. Heb.6.4.& 10. 26. idem Circumcisionis quoque sacramentum declarat, cui Baptismus successit, Gen.17.14. 1.Cor.10.2. Baptismatis administratio ei commissa, cui & verbi prædicatio, Matth.28.19. Itaque, Aut concionatus Minister propria manu baptizat. Exempla: Ioannes Baptista, Matth.3.v.3. Marc.1.4. Ioan.1.v.23.33. Philippus, Act.8, v.35.38. Paulus, 1.Corinth.1.16.
units.tr: Baptism is by no means to be denied to infants (Gen. 17:14; Exod. 4:24–26; Matt. 11:28; 18:14; 19:13; Mark 10:14; Luke 18:15; John 3:5; Acts 2:39; 4:?; 16:15, 33; 18:8; 1 Cor. 1:26; 7:14; 10:2; 15:22; 1 Tim. 2:4; Heb. 6:2). The whole household was baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; Acts 16:15, 33; 18:8). ¶ The Anabaptists attack infant baptism from Matt. 28:19; Mark 1:4; and 16:15, 16. The form of baptism is Matt. 28:19. Baptism is not to be repeated (Eph. 4:5; Heb. 6:4; 10:26). The same passage also declares the sacrament of circumcision, to which baptism succeeded (Gen. 17:14; 1 Cor. 10:2). The administration of baptism is committed to the one to whom the preaching of the Word also belongs (Matt. 28:19). Therefore, either the minister who preaches baptizes with his own hand. Examples: John the Baptist (Matt. 3:3; Mark 1:4; John 1:23, 33); Philip (Acts 8:35, 38); Paul (1 Cor. 1:16).

units.la: Aut administri alicuius, qui concioni interfuisset, opera vtebatur, Exempla: Christus, Ioann.4.v.1.2. Petrus, Act.10.10.48. Baptismatis à Discipulis Christi administrati exempla: à Ioanne Baptista, Matt.3.6.13.14. Marc.1.4. Ioan.1.33. & 3.23.& 10.40. Actor.19.4. à Discipulis Christi, Iohann.1.22.& 4.v.1.2. à Petro, Actor.2.v.38.41. & 10.47. à Philippo, 8.v.12.37.38. ab Anania, 9.17. à Paulo & Sila, 16.v.33. à Paulo, 18.8.& 19.4.1.Corinth.1.16. Baptizati accipiunt Spiritum Sanctum, Actor.2.38.& 9.3. induunt Christum, Galat.3.27. Baptizatur Simon Magus, Actor.8.13. Eunuchus, v.38. Cornel.10.47. Baptisma Ioannis unde, Matth.21.25. Marci 11.30. Luc.20.4. Baptizare se missum esse quo sensu neget Paulus, 1.Cor.1.17. Vide Pavlvs.
units.tr: Or he used the help of some assistant who had been present at the sermon. Examples: Christ (John 4:1, 2); Peter (Acts 10:10, 48). Examples of baptism administered by the disciples of Christ: by John the Baptist (Matt. 3:6, 13, 14; Mark 1:4; John 1:33; 3:23; 10:40; Acts 19:4); by the disciples of Christ (John 1:22; 4:1, 2); by Peter (Acts 2:38, 41; 10:47); by Philip (Acts 8:12, 37, 38); by Ananias (Acts 9:17); by Paul and Silas (Acts 16:33); by Paul (Acts 18:8; 19:4; 1 Cor. 1:16). Those who are baptized receive the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:38; 9:3); they put on Christ (Gal. 3:27). Simon Magus was baptized (Acts 8:13); the eunuch (Acts 8:38); Cornelius (Acts 10:47). Whence John's baptism (Matt. 21:25; Mark 11:30; Luke 20:4). In what sense Paul denies that he was sent to baptize (1 Cor. 1:17). See Paul.

units.la: Christus nullo pollutus peccato, nec baptismo egens, non pro se, sed propter nos baptizatus est: Matt. 3.13. ad finem vsque. 1. vt omnem iustitiam impleret. 2. vt Baptismum Iohannis in propria persona confirmaret. 3. vt in seipso nostrum B. sanctificaret. 4. vt baptismo initiatum sciremus in munus suum (Vide Circuncisio.)
units.tr: Christ, polluted by no sin and having no need of baptism, was baptized not for himself but for us (Matt. 3:13 to the end). (1) So that he might fulfil all righteousness; (2) so that he might confirm John's baptism in his own person; (3) so that he might sanctify our baptism in himself; (4) so that we might know that we are initiated by baptism into his office. (See Circumcision.)

units.la: ¶Baptismum omnia peccata tollere, hisce testimoniis probant Pontificij, Gen.17.14. Esa. 44.3. Ezec.36.25. Zach. 13.1. Matt.18.14.& 28.19. Marc.1.4.& 16.16. Ioan.1.33.& 18.9. Roman.6.v.3. 4.5.6.&c. 1.Cor.6.11. Eph.5.26. Col.2. 11.&c. Tit.3.5.&c. Hebr.10.22. quod verum est, non de morbo seu radice mali & materia ipsa : sed de forma, hoc e[?]condonātur peccata omnia in Baptismo,& originale,& actualia.Vide CONCVPISCENTIA.
units.tr: ¶ The Papists prove from these testimonies that baptism takes away all sins: Gen. 17:14; Isa. 44:3; Ezek. 36:25; Zech. 13:1; Matt. 18:14; 28:19; Mark 1:4; 16:16; John 1:33; 3:5; Rom. 6:3–6; 1 Cor. 6:11; Eph. 5:26; Col. 2:11; Titus 3:5; Heb. 10:22. This is true, not of the disease or root of evil and its matter itself, but of its form: that is, all sins, both original and actual, are forgiven in baptism. See CONCUPISCENCE.

units.la: ¶Quòd item Baptismus saluet, probant ex 1.Petr. 3. Baptismum necessarium esse ad salutem, probant nonnulli ex Genes.17. 14. Ioan.3 5.quæ dicta non intelligenda sunt quasi Circumcisionis & Baptismi sacramento simpliciter adstricta sit gratia Dei, & salus hominum, ac proinde absolute, ac sine exceptione sit necessarium.
units.tr: ¶ That baptism likewise saves, they prove from 1 Pet. 3. Some prove from Gen. 17:14 and John 3:5 that baptism is necessary for salvation. These sayings are not to be understood as if the grace of God and the salvation of men were simply bound to the sacrament of circumcision and baptism, so that baptism is necessary absolutely and without exception.

units.la: Baptismus Nubis & maris, fuit sacramentum extraordinarium in V. T. quo Israelitæ sub nube illa existentes, & per mare transeuntes, omnes administro Mose baptizati sunt nube & mari: quod κοινωνίαν [?] cum Christo ipsis obsignabatur. Exod.14.13 19.22. Ps.78.13.14.15.1.Cor.10.1.2.
units.tr: The baptism of the cloud and the sea was an extraordinary sacrament in the Old Testament, by which the Israelites, who stood under that cloud and passed through the sea, were all baptized by Moses in the cloud and in the sea; this was sealed to them as a communion [κοινωνίαν] with Christ. Exod. 14:13; 19:22; Ps. 78:13–15; 1 Cor. 10:1, 2.

units.la: [Baptismata,1. Lotiones Iudaicæ & legales, Marc. 7.4.Hebr.9[?].10.]
units.tr: [Baptisms: 1. Jewish and legal washings (Mark 7:4; Heb. 9:10).]

units.la: BARRABAS, homicida & seditiosus, Marc.15. 7. Luc. 23. Christo præfertur, Matt.27.21.Marc.15. 11.Luc.23. 18. Ioan. 18.40. Act.3.14.
units.tr: BARABBAS, a murderer and rebel (Mark 15:7; Luke 23:19), is preferred to Christ (Matt. 27:21; Mark 15:11; Luke 23:18; John 18:40; Acts 3:14).

units.la: BARACH, filius Abinoam, creatur dux exercitus Israelitarum. Iudic.4.6. in bellum ire non vult, nisi Debora comitatus. v.8. ideò victoriæ honore priuandus, v.9. agit Deo gratias ob partam victoriam. c. 5.1.2.(i.fulgur.)
units.tr: BARAK, son of Abinoam, is made commander of the army of the Israelites (Judg. 4:6). He does not wish to go to war unless accompanied by Deborah (v. 8), and therefore is to be deprived of the honour of victory (v. 9). He gives thanks to God for the victory won (ch. 5:1, 2). (i.e., lightning.)

units.la: BARACHIAS, pater Zachariæ, Esa. 8.2. Matth.23.35.
units.tr: BARACHIAS, father of Zechariah (Isa. 8:2; Matt. 23:35).

units.la: BARBA, non tondenda Leuiticis sacerdotibus, Leuit.19.27. 21 5. Barbæ dimidiam partem seruorum Dauidis rasit Hanon, 2.Sam.10.4. V.Psal.133.2.
units.tr: BEARD, not to be shaved by the Levitical priests (Lev. 19:27; 21:5). Hanun shaved off half the beards of David's servants (2 Sam. 10:4). See Ps. 133:2.

units.la: BARBARI, pro rudibus & ineruditis, Rom.1.14.1. Cor.14. barbari humaniter Paulum excipiunt, Actor.28.2.
units.tr: BARBARIANS, used for the rude and unlearned (Rom. 1:14; 1 Cor. 14). The barbarians received Paul kindly (Acts 28:2).

units.la: BAR-IESVS, qui & Elymas, Pseudopropheta Iudæus, Actor.13. 6. Paulo resistit, v.8. visu priuatur ab eo, v. 10.11. Vnde Proconsul in fide confirmatur, v.12.
units.tr: BAR-JESUS, also called Elymas, a Jewish false prophet (Acts 13:6). He opposes Paul (v. 8), is deprived of sight by him (vv. 10, 11). Whence the proconsul is confirmed in the faith (v. 12).

units.la: BAR IONA. beatus es Simon Bar-iona: Mat.16.17.
units.tr: BAR-JONA: "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jona" (Matt. 16:17).

units.la: BARNABAS ponit precium agri ad pedes Apostolorum, Act.4. 37. (i.filius consolationis.)
units.tr: BARNABAS lays the price of a field at the feet of the Apostles (Acts 4:37). (i.e., son of consolation.)

units.la: BARNABAS ducit Paulum ad Apostolos, 9. 27. Antiochiam mittitur, 11.22. Illic docet, 13.1. & 15.35. destinatur ministerio Gentium vnà cum Paulo, 13. 2. laudatur, 15.25. discedit à Paulo, & cur, v.39.
units.tr: BARNABAS brings Paul to the Apostles (Acts 9:27). He is sent to Antioch (Acts 11:22). There he teaches (Acts 13:1; 15:35). He is appointed, together with Paul, to the ministry to the Gentiles (Acts 13:2). He is praised (Acts 15:25). He parts from Paul, and why (v. 39).

units.la: BARSABAS, qui & Ioseph Iustus: hic cum Matthia in Apostolatum offertur Deo ab Ecclesia, Act.1.23.(i.filius reuertens.
units.tr: BARSABBAS, also called Joseph the Just: he, together with Matthias, is offered to God by the Church for the apostolate (Acts 1:23). (i.e., the son who returns.)

units.la: BARTIMAEVS cæcus mendicat, Marc. 10. 46. Christi opem implorat, & visu donatur, v.46.47.48.51.52.
units.tr: BARTIMAEUS, a blind beggar, implores Christ's help and is given sight (Mark 10:46; vv. 47, 48, 51, 52).

units.la: BARTHOLOMAEVS, creatur Apostolus, Matth. 10.3. Mar.3.18. Luc.6.14. Act.1.13 (filius suspendentis aquas)
units.tr: BARTHOLOMEW is made an Apostle (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:14; Acts 1:13). (son of one who holds back the waters.)

units.la: BARUCH, filius Neriæ, Ierem.32.12. scriba Ieremiæ, Ierem.36. iubetur Templum ingredi, volumen lecturus, v. 5. 6. id restat, v.8.10. pusillanimitatis à Ieremia reprehenditur, 45. 1.3 4. (id est, benedictus.)
units.tr: BARUCH, son of Neriah (Jer. 32:12), scribe of Jeremiah (Jer. 36). He is commanded to enter the Temple to read the scroll (v. 5, 6). This remains (vv. 8, 10). He is rebuked by Jeremiah for faintheartedness (ch. 45:1, 3, 4). (i.e., blessed.)

units.la: BARZELLAI, Vide BERZELLAI.
units.tr: BARZILLAI: see BERZELLAI.

units.la: BASAN regnum, vocatur terra Gigantum, Deut.3 13. dimidiæ tribui Manasse sorte obtigit, ibid. (i.pinguedo,)
units.tr: BASHAN, a kingdom, called the land of giants (Deut. 3:13). It fell by lot to the half-tribe of Manasseh (ibid.). (i.e., fatness.)

units.la: BASEMATH, filia Salomonis, vxor Achimaas, 1. Regum 4.15. Basmath, vxor Esau, Gen.26.34.
units.tr: BASEMATH, daughter of Solomon, wife of Ahimaaz (1 Kings 4:15). Basemath, wife of Esau (Gen. 26:34).

units.la: BATHVEL filius Nachoris fratris Abrahæ, pater Rebeccæ, Genef.22.23. dat filiam Rebeccam Isaaco in vxorem, 24. v 50. BATHVEL (id est, virgo Dei.)
units.tr: BETHUEL, son of Nahor, brother of Abraham, father of Rebekah (Gen. 22:23). He gives his daughter Rebekah to Isaac as wife (Gen. 24:50). BETHUEL (that is, virgin of God.)

BLESSED are those who (Ps. 1:1; 32:1, 2; 106:3; 112:1, 2; 119:1, 2; 128:1; 144:15; 146:5; Prov. 3:13; 8:32, 34; 16:20; 28:14; 29:18; Isa. 30:18; 56:1, 2; Jer. 17:7; Matt. 5:3–11; 11:6; Luke 6:20–22; 7:23; 11:28; 14:13, 14; John 20:29; Rom. 4:7, 8; James 1:12, 25; 5:11; 1 Pet. 4:14; Rev. 1:3; 14:13; 16:15; 19:9; 20:6; 22:7, 14). BLESSED are the eyes (Luke 10:23). It is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). BLESSED are those who die in the Lord's cause (Rev. 14:13). BLESSED are those who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Rev. 19:9).

units.la: BEATITAS: Rom. 4.9. Gal.4.15. Beatitudo hominis, est communicatio Dei, & fruitio bonorum cœlestium. Hæc est vita æterna, vt te esse illum solum verum Deum cognoscant, & quem misisti Iesum Christum: Ioh.17.3. V.1. Ioh.1.v.1.2.3.4.] Beatus cui non imputat Deus peccata, qui audit verbum Dei & custodit illud, qui credit & sperat in Deum qui timet eum, & observat mandata eius, qui persecutionem patitur pro iustitia, qui suffert tentationem, qui moritur in Domino. Psal.32.2. Luc.11 28. Ps.32.12.& 34.9.& 128.1. Mat. 5.10. Iacob.1,12. Apoc.14.13.]
units.tr: BLESSEDNESS: Rom. 4.9. Gal. 4.15. The blessedness of man is communion with God and the enjoyment of heavenly goods. This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent: John 17.3. V.1. John 1.1, 2, 3, 4. Blessed is the one whose sins God does not impute, who hears the word of God and keeps it, who believes and hopes in God, who fears him and observes his commandments, who suffers persecution for righteousness, who endures temptation, who dies in the Lord. Ps. 32.2. Luke 11.28. Ps. 32.12; 34.9; 128.1. Matt. 5.10. James 1.12. Rev. 14.13.

units.la: BEL-PHEGOR, Moabitarum idolum, cui initiantur Israelitæ, Numer.25. v.2.3. (Vide IDOLORVM catalogu:)& ob id à Mose occidi iubentur, v.5. Deut.4.3. Iosue 22.17. (Baal-pehor.i.idolum hiatus.)
units.tr: BEL-PHEGOR, the idol of the Moabites, to which the Israelites were initiated, Num. 25.2, 3. (See the catalogue of IDOLS.) On account of this, they were ordered by Moses to be put to death, v. 5. Deut. 4.3. Josh. 22.17. (Baal-peor, that is, the idol of the gaping mouth.)

units.la: BEL-ZEBVB, (id est, Dominus muscarum, vel, quòd propter victimarum copiam, muscarum examine templum eius scateret: vel, quòd auxilium aduersus muscas, quæ lo- co infestæ essent, petitum sit ab eo idolo, sic appellatum idolum Accaronitarum, consulitur ab Ochozia ægrotan- te, 2.Reg.1.2. V. quid inde consecutum sit.
units.tr: BEL-ZEBUB (that is, the lord of flies, or because, owing to the abundance of victims, the temple swarmed with a cloud of flies; or because help against the flies, which were a nuisance in the place, was sought from that idol). The idol of the Accaronites was so called. It was consulted by Ahaziah when he was sick, 2 Kings 1.2. See what followed from this.

units.la: BEELZEBVB Christum vocârunt Iudæi, Matt.10.25.
units.tr: The Jews called Christ BEELZEBUB, Matt. 10.25.

units.la: BEEL-ZEBVB (princeps Dæmoniorum) in eius nomine eiice- re Dæmonia, dicitur Christus, Matth.12.24. Marc. 3.22, Luc. 11.15. Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: BEEL-ZEBUB (the prince of the demons): by his name Christ is said to cast out demons, Matt. 12.24; Mark 3.22; Luke 11.15. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: BEERI, (.i.puteus meus) pater Oseæ prophetæ : 1.v.1.
units.tr: BEERI (that is, my well), the father of the prophet Hosea, Hos. 1.1.

units.la: BEHOR, (seu Bosor 2.Pet.2.15.) pater impij Balaam : Num. 22.5.
units.tr: BEOR (or Bosor, 2 Pet. 2.15), the father of the wicked Balaam, Num. 22.5.

units.la: BEL, idolum Babyloniorum. Vide IDOLORVM catalogus. eius ruina, Esa.46.1. Ierem.50.2. & 51.44.
units.tr: BEL, the idol of the Babylonians. See the catalogue of IDOLS. Its ruin: Isa. 46.1; Jer. 50.2; 51.44.

units.la: [BELA, Beniamin filius Gen.46.21.1.Chr.8.1.3. Bela, Idum. rex, Gen.36.32.1.Chr.1.43.44.]
units.tr: [BELA, son of Benjamin, Gen. 46.21; 1 Chr. 8.1, 3. Bela, king of Edom, Gen. 36.32; 1 Chr. 1.43, 44.]

units.la: BELIAL, Satan. cum Belial nulla est Christo concordia, 2. Corinth.6.15.
units.tr: BELIAL, Satan. There is no agreement between Christ and Belial, 2 Cor. 6.15.

units.la: [Belial, nequam, Deut.13.13. Iudic.19.22.1.Sam.1.16.2. Sam.16.7.& 22.5. Nahum.1.15.
units.tr: [Belial, wickedness, Deut. 13.13; Judg. 19.22; 1 Sam. 1.16; 2 Sam. 16.7; 22.5; Nahum 1.15.]

units.la: BELLARE: Bellandi dexteritas à Deo, Psalm.18.35.& 144.1. Bellator Deus, Exod.15.3. Ierem.20.11.
units.tr: TO WAGE WAR: The skill of warfare comes from God, Ps. 18.35; 144.1. God is a warrior, Exod. 15.3; Jer. 20.11.

units.tr: WAR is sent by God on account of the sins of the people, and therefore it is a punishment for sin, Lev. 26.24, 25; Deut. 28.36, 49; Judg. 2.13; 3.1, 8; 4.1; 6.1; 10.6; 13.1; 1 Kings 8.33; Isa. 5.25; Jer. 5.15. How war is to be waged, Deut. 20.10, 11, 12; 23.9. It is to be undertaken with God as author and with his counsel. Examples: the Israelites, Judg. 1.2; 20.18. Saul, 1 Sam. 14.37; 28.5, 6. David, 23.2; 30.8; 2 Sam. 5.19; 1 Chr. 14.10. Wars undertaken without the approval of God do not succeed. Examples: the Israelites, Num. 14.43, 44, 45; Deut. 1.43, 44. Ahab, 1 Kings 22.17, 35. Examples of wars undertaken by the faithful and accomplished by divine power: by Abraham, Gen. 14.14, 15, 16; by the Hebrews, Exod. 17.9, 10, 11; Num. 31.7; Josh. 6.20; 7.4; 8.4, 24; 10.11, 42; by Judah, Judg. 1.4; by Judah and his brother Simeon, v. 17; by Barak, 4.14; by Gideon, 7.7, 16; by Abimelech, 9.42, 43, 45, 52; by Jephthah, 11.32; by Samson, 14.19; 15.7; by the tribe of Dan, 18.11; by the Benjamites, 20.21, 25; by the Israelites, v. 35; by the Philistines, 1 Sam. 4.10; by the Israelites, 7.10; by Saul, 1 Sam. 11.11; 15.5, 6; by Jonathan, 14.11, 12, 13, 14; by David, 17.48; 2 Sam. 5.17, 25; by the young men of Benjamin, 2.15; by the servants of David, v. 31; by Joab, 10.9, 13; 18.14; by Ahab, 1 Kings 20.20, 29; by Joram, Jehoshaphat and Edom, 2 Kings 3.6, 7, 9, 24; Samaria, 6.24; 7.6, etc.; by Joash, 14.7; by Jeroboam, vv. 16, 28; by Hezekiah, 18.8; by Abijah, 2 Chr. 13.17; by Asa, 14.12; by Jehoshaphat, 20.23, 24, 25; by Pekah, 28.6; Judith, Judith 16.7, 8, 9, 10. Spiritual war: with what weapons it must be fought, Rom. 13.12; 2 Cor. 10.4; Eph. 6.11; Gal. 5.17. [War: disputes, quarrels, James 4.1.]

units.la: BENHADAD Syriæ Rex suasu Regis Asa, vrbes Israel percutit, 1. Reg.15.20. bibit temulentus, cap.20.16. fugit ante exercitum Israel, v.20. dimidicat cum Israelitis, v.26.29. iterum fugit, v.30. amicè recipitur ab Achab, v.33. fœdere inito elabitur, v.34. cuius rei reprehensus Achab, mortis subeundæ pro eo minas audit à Deo, v.42. obsidet Samariam, 1.Reg.20.1 & 2. Reg.6.24. ægrotus consulit Dominum, 8.9. moritur v.15. (Vide ante Tit. Beniamin) filius oiulatus.
units.tr: BEN-HADAD, king of Syria, at the urging of King Asa, struck the cities of Israel, 1 Kings 15.20. He drank himself drunk, ch. 20.16. He fled before the army of Israel, v. 20. He made a truce with the Israelites, v. 26, 29. He fled again, v. 30. He was kindly received by Ahab, v. 33. After a covenant was made he escaped, v. 34. Ahab was rebuked for this, and he heard from God threats of death to be undergone on his account, v. 42. He besieged Samaria, 1 Kings 20.1, 2; 2 Kings 6.24. Sick, he consulted the LORD, 8.9. He died, v. 15. (See above under Tit. Benjamin.) A son who was lamented.

units.tr: TO BLESS [is ascribed to God, to man, and to Christ. For God blesses creatures in various ways, men, and the elect in Christ. And Christ blessed, Matt. 14.19; Mark 8.6; 10.16; Luke 24.50; Acts 3.26. Man blesses God, himself, and other men, in various ways according to his calling. Creatures also bless the Lord, Ps. 103.21, 22.] to give thanks, Gen. 14.20; 24.27, 48; Exod. 18.10; Deut. 8.10; Judg. 5.2, 9; Ruth 4.14; 1 Sam. 9.13; 25.32, 39; 2 Sam. 13.25; 18.28; 22.47; 1 Kings 1.48; 5.7; 8.15; 10.9; 1 Chr. 16.36; 29.10, 20; 2 Chr. 2.12; 6.4; 9.8; 20.26; 31.8; 1 Esd. 7.27; Neh. 8.6; 9.5; Job 1.21; Ps. 16.7; 26.12; 34.2; 41.14; 63.5; 66.8, 20; 68.20; 72.18, 19; 96.2; 103.1, 2, 20, 21, 22; 104.1, 35; 106.48; 113.2; 115.18; 119.12; 124.6; 134.1; 135.19, 20, 21; 144.1; Ezek. 3.12; Dan. 2.19, 20; 3.28; 4.34; Zech. 1.5; Matt. 14.19; 26.26; Mark 6.41; 8.7; 14.22; Luke 1.64, 68; 2.28; 9.16; 24.30, 53; Rom. 1.25; 9.5; 1 Cor. 14.16; 2 Cor. 11.31; Eph. 1.3; James 3.9; 1 Pet. 1.3; Rev. 4.9; 5.12; 7.12. To do good to the needy, Prov. 11.25. To bless oneself, that is, to congratulate and please oneself, Deut. 29.19; Ps. 49.19; Isa. 65.16. To bless the cup, that is, to sanctify and consecrate, 1 Cor. 10.16. To bless, that is, to pray well for someone, Gen. 47.7, 10; 1 Sam. 25.14; 2 Sam. 13.25; 1 Kings 1.47; 2 Kings 10.15; Matt. 5.44; Rom. 12.14; 1 Pet. 3.9. See the examples of the blessing by which one man blesses another. For to curse or speak evil, by antiphrasis, 1 Kings 21.13; Job 1.5, 11; 2.5, 9. For the ability to increase is granted, Gen. 1.22, 28; 9.1; 12.2; 17.20; 24.35; 26.12; 28.3. For to praise and extol, Matt. 21.9; Mark 11.9. For men are said to bless God when they proclaim his praises; conversely, God blesses men when he makes them happy.

units.tr: BLESSING, for a gift, an offering, or a bounty and beneficence (for the word to bless means not only to speak well, but also to confer a benefit), Gen. 33.11; Josh. 15.19; 22.7; Judg. 1.15; 1 Sam. 25.27; 30.26; 2 Kings 5.15; 2 Cor. 9.5. For happiness, Deut. 11.26; Ps. 24.5; Prov. 24.25; Isa. 19.24. For good things received from God, Deut. 12.15; 16.10, 17; 30.1, 19; Joel 2.14; Mal. 2.2; 3.10. For the benefit of adoption, Gal. 3.14. To command a blessing, for to bless, Lev. 25.21; Deut. 28.8; Ps. 133.3. To be a blessing, for to praise, Gen. 12.2; Zech. 8.13; Ps. 37.26. To make a blessing with someone, that is, to accept the conditions one proposes, Isa. 36.16.

units.tr: The blessing of God, for his favour, Ps. 3.9; Prov. 10.6, 22; Isa. 44.3. The blessing of God is always necessary, 1 Tim. 6.17; 1 Pet. 3.9. The blessing of God toward those who fear him, Exod. 23.25; Lev. 25.21; Deut. 7.13; 11.27; 15.5, 6; 28.1, 2, 3; 1 Chr. 17.27; 2 Chr. 31.10; 1 Esd. 8.22; Ps. 24.5; 29.11; 34.9; 128.5, 6; 132.16; 133.3; Prov. 3.33; 10.6; Isa. 61.9; Jer. 31.12; Mal. 3.10. How effective the blessing of God is, 1 Chr. 17.27; Prov. 10.22.
