Item Gal.3.8. pro gratuita ex foedere adoptione, cui opponitur maledictio, Benedictus qui venit in nomine Domini, Matt.23.39. Marc.11 9. Luc.13.35. [Benedictus, vir fidelis, Gen.24 31.Populus Dei, Pf.33.12. & 65.5. & 144.15. Esa.65.23.]
units.tr: BLESSED of the Father, Matt. 25.34; Mark 11.10: for happy, fortunate, and abundantly benefited by God. Likewise Gal. 3.8: for the free adoption under covenant, to which cursing is opposed. "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord," Matt. 23.39; Mark 11.9; Luke 13.35. [Blessed, a faithful man, Gen. 24.31. The people of God, Ps. 33.12; 65.5; 144.15; Isa. 65.23.]

units.la: <bl>B</bl>ENEFACERE, pro beneficio afficere, vel bonum opus & charitatis officia proximo praestare. Matt.12.12. Luc.6.9.
units.tr: TO DO GOOD: to bestow a benefit upon someone, or to render a good work and the offices of charity to a neighbour. Matt. 12.12; Luke 6.9.

units.la: <bl>B</bl>ENEFICENTIA, est virtus quae communicat facultates & operas, vbi & quando decet, & mediocritatem efficit inter profusionem & sordes.
units.tr: BENEFICENCE is the virtue that shares its resources and labours where and when it is fitting, and keeps the mean between lavishness and meanness.

units.la: <bl>B</bl>ENEFICENTIA in pauperes commendatur, Exod.23.11. Levit.19.10. Deut.15.8. Pf.112.v.5 6.7. Prou.1.v.9.27. & 11.v.11. 25. & 14.v.21 31. Esa.58.v.7.10. Dan.4 27. Matth. 10.42. & 19. 21. & 25.v.34-35. Marc.9.41. & 10.21. Luc.11.41. & 12.33. & 14. v 13.14. & 16 9. & 18.22. Galat.6.v.9 10.Phil.4.14. Eph.1.15. & 4.28.1. Tim.6.18. Tit.3.1, Heb.13.16. Iac.1.27, & 2.13.1. Iohan. 3. v.17. 18. Vide DANDVM sine acceptione personarum & ELEEMOSYNA. Beneficentia erga inimicos coleda, Pro.25. 21.Rom.12.20. Beneficentia erga omnes communis, Matt. 5.44. Rom.12.20. Galat.6.10.1.Thess.5.15. 2.Thess.3.13. Beneficentiae bona, Prou.11.24. & 22.v.9.16. & 28.27. Matth. 6.4.Luc.11.41.2.Cor.9.8 9.10.
units.tr: Beneficence toward the poor is commended: Exod. 23.11; Lev. 19.10; Deut. 15.8; Ps. 112.5-7; Prov. 1.9, 27; 11.11, 25; 14.21, 31; Isa. 58.7, 10; Dan. 4.27; Matt. 10.42; 19.21; 25.34-35; Mark 9.41; 10.21; Luke 11.41; 12.33; 14.13-14; 16.9; 18.22; Gal. 6.9-10; Phil. 4.14; Eph. 1.15; 4.28; 1 Tim. 6.18; Titus 3.1; Heb. 13.16; James 1.27; 2.13; 1 John 3.17-18. See GIVING without respect of persons, and ALMSGIVING. Beneficence toward enemies is to be practised: Prov. 25.21; Rom. 12.20. Universal beneficence: Matt. 5.44; Rom. 12.20; Gal. 6.10; 1 Thess. 5.15; 2 Thess. 3.13. Blessings of beneficence: Prov. 11.24; 22.9, 16; 28.27; Matt. 6.4; Luke 11.41; 2 Cor. 9.8-10.

units.la: Beneficentiae in pauperes exempla: Booz in Ruth, Ruth, 2. v.8.14.15.16.17. Tobias in pauperes, Tob.1.19. Iob in pauperes, Iob 29.15.16. Samaritanus in viatorem caesum, Luc.10. v.34.35. Zachaeus in pauperes, 19.8. Cornelius in pauperes, Act. 10.2. Antiocheni in fideles Iudaeae, 11.29. Macedonica Ecclesia in eosdem, Rom.15.26.2.Corinth.8.2.3. Hebraei in pauperes, Heb.6 10. Gaius in fideles hospites, 3.Iohan.v.5. Vide ELEEMOSYNAE exempla.
units.tr: Examples of beneficence toward the poor: Boaz in Ruth, Ruth 2.8, 14-17. Tobit toward the poor, Tob. 1.19. Job toward the poor, Job 29.15-16. The Samaritan toward the wounded traveller, Luke 10.34-35. Zacchaeus toward the poor, Luke 19.8. Cornelius toward the poor, Acts 10.2. The Antiochenes toward the faithful in Judea, Acts 11.29. The Macedonian church toward the same, Rom. 15.26; 2 Cor. 8.2-3. The Hebrews toward the poor, Heb. 6.10. Gaius toward the faithful strangers, 3 John 5. See the examples under ALMSGIVING.

units.la: BENEFICIVM: Beneficia facile obliuioni traduntur. Exempla: Laban, Gen.31 5. Pincerna Pharaonis, 40.23. Pharao, Exod.1.8. Ioas rex Iuda, 2.Paral.24.v.21.22.
units.tr: BENEFIT: Benefits are easily given over to forgetfulness. Examples: Laban, Gen. 31.5. Pharaoh's cupbearer, Gen. 40.23. Pharaoh, Exod. 1.8. Joash king of Judah, 2 Chron. 24.21-22.

units.la: <bl>B</bl>ENEVOLENTIA, εὔνοια, est animi nostri charitas siue affectus, quo etiam ignoto & absenti, i. quem nunquam vidimus, bona esse volumus & desideramus, tum propter communem nostram in omnes homines charitatem, tum propter ipsius absentis egregiam virtutem & Dei donum, quod nobis innotuit, & in eo honoratum esse cupimus, 1.Corinth. t.Corinth.7.3. Eph.6.7.Serui facientes ex animo quæ vult Deus,cum beneuolentia seruientes Domino.
units.tr: BENEVOLENCE, eunoia, is the charity or affection of our mind by which we wish and desire good things even for one who is unknown and absent, that is, whom we have never seen. We do so both out of our common charity toward all men, and on account of the outstanding virtue of the absent person and the gift of God that has become known to us; and we desire that he be honoured in it. 1 Cor. 7.3; Eph. 6.7: "Servants, doing with good will what God wills, serving the Lord with goodwill."

units.la: BENEVOLENTIA, Græcis εὐδοκία, pro Euangelio,Luc.2.14. pro gratuito & infinito Dei in electos amore,Eph.1.v.5.9. pro mutua hominum inter se amicitia, qua fit vt alij aliorum commodis studeant,Rom.10.1.pro charitate, qua homines Deum diligunt,Philip.1.15.
units.tr: BENEVOLENCE, in Greek eudokia, is used for the Gospel, Luke 2.14; for the free and infinite love of God toward the elect, Eph. 1.5, 9; for the mutual friendship of men, by which some seek the advantage of others, Rom. 10.1; and for the charity by which men love God, Phil. 1.15.

units.la: BENHADAD filius Hazael Rex Syriæ, subiicit sibi Israelem, 2.Reg.13.3. Vide post Tit.Bellum.
units.tr: BEN-HADAD, son of Hazael, king of Syria, subjected Israel to himself, 2 Kings 13.3. See below, Tit. Bellum.

units.la: BENIAMIN (à matre Rachele Ben-oni,id est filius doloris vel luctus:à patre Iacobo Ben-iamin, id est,filius dexteræ,hoc est,charus & æque dilectus,vt homini est dextera, appellatus)nascitur, Gen.35.18. descendit cum fratribus in Ægyptum,43.15.eius benedictio,49.27.Deut.33.12.filij,Gen.46.21.1.Paral.7.6.sors,Iof.18.11.
units.tr: BENJAMIN (called by his mother Rachel Ben-oni, that is, son of sorrow or mourning, but by his father Jacob Ben-iamin, that is, son of the right hand, meaning dear and equally loved, as the right hand is to a man) was born, Gen. 35.18. He went down with his brothers into Egypt, Gen. 43.15. His blessing, Gen. 49.27; Deut. 33.12. His sons, Gen. 46.21; 1 Chron. 7.6. His lot, Josh. 18.11.

units.la: BENIAMINITAE abutuntur vxore Leuitæ, Iud. 19.25. vincuntur ad Israelitis,20.35.
units.tr: The BENJAMITES abused the Levite's wife, Judg. 19.25. They are defeated by the Israelites, Judg. 20.35.

units.la: BENIGNITAS, χρηστότης, vel beneficentia, est animi affectio, quæ propter Dei præceptum gratis sua tribuit cuilibet egeno, & quicquid potest egenti, etiam non petenti libenter largitur. Anselmus. Gal.5.22. Fructus Spiritus est charitas,benignitas, 1. Cor.13.4. Charitas patiens est, benigna est. Prou.20.28. Benignitas & fides custodiunt regem, & sustentat benignitate solium suum. Exod. 24.7. Vide Dei benignitas.
units.tr: KINDNESS, chrestotes, or beneficence, is a disposition of the mind which, because of God's command, gladly gives its own goods freely to any needy person, and willingly bestows on the one in need whatever it can, even without being asked. Anselm. Gal. 5.22: "The fruit of the Spirit is love, kindness..." 1 Cor. 13.4: "Love is patient, love is kind." Prov. 20.28: "Kindness and faithfulness guard the king, and he upholds his throne by kindness." Exod. 24.7. See God's kindness.

units.la: BENIGNITAS,pro morum facilitate. Vide MANSVETVDO. pro liberalitate, Vide LIBERALITAS. Benignitatis diuinæ erga homines exempla: Erga Abrahamum,ad quem benignè respondet, Gen.18.v.23.26. &c. Loth,vxorem & filias eius, 19.16. Iacobum, quem ab Esau, Laban & aliis benignè defendit, 28.15. & 31. 24.Israelitas, quos benignè protexit,Exod.13.v.21.22.&14.verf.21.22.&16.ver.13.14.&17.6.Num.24.9. Deuter.29.5. Iohan.3.verf.15.16. Mosen, Exod.33.11. Num.12.8. Deut.34.7. Iosuam, Iof.1.1.2. Gedeonem,Iudic.6.37.Eliam,1.Reg.17.6.Ieremiam, Ierem.7.v.15.16.langui-dos & morbidos, Matth.4.23.Vide MIRACVLA. Petrum, Matth.14.31.Mariam Magdalenam,quam Christus piè defendit contra Pharisæum malè de ea cogitantem, Luc.7.39. contra sororem de illa conquerentem, 10.38. contra Discipulos, Marc.14.3.&c. erga filium prodigum, Luc.15.20.cæcum natum è synagoga eiectum, & à Christo receptum,Iohan.9.v.35.36. Zachæum,Luc.19.5.&c.Latronem, Luc. 23. 43. Petrum ter Christum negantem, Luc. 22. 61. Thomam ante incredulum, Iohan. 20. 28. Paulum in ipso persecutionis actu conuersum, Act. 9. 4. Ioannem Apoc-tolum multiplici revelatione ornatum, Apoc. 1. 17. &c.
units.tr: KINDNESS, for gentleness of manners: see MEEKNESS. For liberality: see LIBERALITY. Examples of divine kindness toward men: toward Abraham, to whom God kindly answers, Gen. 18.23-26, etc. Lot, with his wife and daughters, Gen. 19.16. Jacob, whom he kindly defended against Esau, Laban and others, Gen. 28.15; 31.24. The Israelites, whom he kindly protected, Exod. 13.21-22; 14.21-22; 16.13-14; 17.6; Num. 24.9; Deut. 29.5; John 3.15-16. Moses, Exod. 33.11; Num. 12.8; Deut. 34.7. Joshua, Josh. 1.1-2. Gideon, Judg. 6.37. Elijah, 1 Kings 17.6. Jeremiah, Jer. 7.15-16. The lame and the sick, Matt. 4.23. See MIRACLES. Peter, Matt. 14.31. Mary Magdalene, whom Christ piously defended against the Pharisee who thought ill of her, Luke 7.39; against her sister who complained about her, Luke 10.38; against the disciples, Mark 14.3, etc. The prodigal son, Luke 15.20. The man born blind, cast out of the synagogue and received by Christ, John 9.35-36. Zacchaeus, Luke 19.5, etc. The thief, Luke 23.43. Peter, who denied Christ three times, Luke 22.61. Thomas, though an unbeliever, John 20.28. Paul, converted in the very act of persecution, Acts 9.4. John the Apostle, adorned with manifold revelations, Rev. 1.17, etc.

units.la: BERNICE soror Agrippæ postremi regis Iudæorum: Act. 25. 13. 23. & 26. 30.
units.tr: BERNICE, sister of Agrippa, the last king of the Jews: Acts 25.13, 23; 26.30.

units.la: BEROEA civitas in Macedonia. illuc aufugit Paulus, Act. 17. 10. Iudæi illius loci verbum Dei alacriter excipiunt, v. 11. horum multi cum Græcis matronis Pauli prædicationi credunt, v. 12. Vbi Iudæi concitantes turbam, Paulum alibi ire coegerunt, v. 13. 14.
units.tr: BEREA, a city in Macedonia. Paul fled there, Acts 17.10. The Jews of that place received the word of God eagerly, v. 11. Many of them, with Greek matrons, believed Paul's preaching, v. 12. But the Jews there stirred up the crowd and forced Paul to go elsewhere, vv. 13-14.

units.la: BER-SABEE, finis seu terminus terræ Israel, austrum versus, 1. Sam. 3. 20. illic percutit fœdus Abraham cum Abimelech Rege Gerar, Gen. 21. v. 22. 27. illius nominis ratio, v. 31. & 26. 33. [Idololatria Israelitarum pollutus, Amos 5. 5. & 8. 14.] Beerschebah, puteus iuramenti, Gen. 21. 31.
units.tr: BEERSHEBA, the end or boundary of the land of Israel, toward the south, 1 Sam. 3.20. There Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech, king of Gerar, Gen. 21.22-27. The reason for the name is given at v. 31; see also 26.33. [Polluted by the idolatry of the Israelites, Amos 5.5; 8.14.] Beersheba, the well of the oath, Gen. 21.31.

units.la: BERZELLAI vir ditissimus, & beneficus in Davidem, 2. Sam. 19. 32. eius ætas, v. 35. beneficium suum remetiri Davidem non patitur, v. 36. benedicitur & exosculatur à Davide, v. 39. [Barzillai, i. ferrum meum.)
units.tr: BARZILLAI, a very rich man and generous toward David, 2 Sam. 19.32. His age, v. 35. He does not allow David to repay his kindness, v. 36. He is blessed and kissed by David, v. 39. [Barzillai means "my iron."]

units.la: [Berzellai Sacerdos,] Scripturam genealogiæ suæ profere non valens, à sacerdotij dignitate reiicitur, 1. Esdr. 2. 62. Nehem. 7. 63.
units.tr: [Barzillai the priest,] unable to produce the record of his genealogy, is rejected from the dignity of the priesthood, 1 Esd. 2.62; Neh. 7.63.

units.la: BESELEEL, seu Betsaleel, i. umbra Dei, filius Vri, insignis artifex Tabernaculi, repletur Spiritu Dei, Exod. 31. v. 2. 3. & 35. 30. & 36. 1.
units.tr: BEZALEEL, or Betsaleel, that is, shadow of God, son of Uri, an outstanding craftsman of the Tabernacle, filled with the Spirit of God, Exod. 31.2-3; 35.30; 36.1.

units.la: BESTIA: bestiæ & bruta animantia non crudeliter tractanda, Genes. 33. 13. Exod. 23. 12. Num. 22. v. 23. 28. Deut. 5. 14. & 22. 10. Prov. 12. 10. Eccl. 7. 22. bestias quatuor vidit Daniel, Dan. 7. 3. primæ effigies, v. 4. secundæ, v. 5. tertiæ, v. 6. quartæ, v. 7. 8. 19. Vide Animal.
units.tr: BEAST: beasts and brute animals are not to be treated cruelly: Gen. 33.13; Exod. 23.12; Num. 22.23, 28; Deut. 5.14; 22.10; Prov. 12.10; Eccl. 7.22. Daniel saw four beasts, Dan. 7.3: the first in figure, v. 4; the second, v. 5; the third, v. 6; the fourth, vv. 7-8, 19. See ANIMAL.

units.la: BESTIA abyssi, Apoc. 11. 7. Bestia laniat duos testes à Deo excitatos, ibid. Bestia multiceps, quæ maximâ Mundi partem per idolatriam seduxerat, describitur: & ipsa ab alia bestia descendere confirmatur, 13. v. 11. 12. eius character, v. 16. numerus, v. 18. pœna eorum qui imaginem illius adorârint, 19. 20. eam vitare monemur, 14. 9. Victores bestiæ laudant Deum, 15. 3. Bestia meretricem magnam portans, 17. 7. mysterium & exitium, v. 11. apprehenditur, & in stagnum ardens coniicitur, 19. v. 20. 21. V. Leuit. 26. 22.
units.tr: BEAST of the abyss, Rev. 11.7. The beast tears the two witnesses raised up by God, ibid. The many-headed beast, which had led the greater part of the world astray through idolatry, is described; and it is confirmed that it rises from another beast, 13.11-12. Its mark, v. 16; its number, v. 18. The punishment of those who worshipped its image, 19.20. We are warned to avoid it, 14.9. The conquerors of the beast praise God, 15.3. The beast carrying the great harlot, 17.7. Its mystery and destruction, v. 11, is seized and cast, burning, into a lake, 19.20-21. See Lev. 26.22.

units.la: BESTIAE noxiæ in Ægypto immissæ, Exo. 8. 17. [Bestiæ impij ob crudelitatem ita nominati, Psal. 73. 19. Tit. 1. 12. 1. Co. 15. 32.
units.tr: BEASTS sent upon Egypt, Exod. 8.17. [Beasts: wicked men so called for their cruelty, Ps. 73.19; Titus 1.12; 1 Cor. 15.32.

units.la: BETHABARA, (id est, domus deserti,) Ioan.1.28. (alias Bethbara, id est domus prandij, Iudic.7.24.) locus est ad Iordanem, ubi Iohan.baptizabat.
units.tr: BETHABARA (that is, house of the desert), John 1.28 (otherwise Bethbara, that is, house of the feast, Judg. 7.24), is a place by the Jordan where John was baptizing.

units.la: BETHANIA, hoc est, domus afflictionis, vel domus gratiæ Dei, vicus non procul ab vrbe Ierosolyma, Ioannis 11.18. nobilis resurrectione Lazari, 12.2. & Christi ad cælos ascensione, Luc.24.50.
units.tr: BETHANY, that is, house of affliction, or house of God's grace, a village not far from the city of Jerusalem, John 11.18, famous for the resurrection of Lazarus, 12.2, and for Christ's ascension into heaven, Luke 24.50.

units.la: BETH-AVEN, i. domus vanitatis, Iof.8.12. Of.4.15. &5.8.&10.5.
units.tr: BETH-AVEN, i.e. house of vanity, Josh. 8.12; Hos. 4.15; 5.8; 10.5.

units.la: BETHEL (id est, Domus Dei,) quæ & Luza, quare, & à quo primùm sic dicta: est vrbs in tribu Beniamin distans tribus milliaribus à Hierosolymis: Gen.28.17.19. capitur à filiis Ioseph, Iudic.1.v.22.25. illic colebatur & consulebatur Deus, 20.18. 1.Sam.10 3. illic vitulum adorandum collocat Ieroboam, 1. Reg.12 29. [Ideo postea non Bethel, sed Bethauen, id est, Domus vanitatis & confusionis dicta est, Ose.4.15. & 5.8.& 10.5 ] Vide IEROBOAM.
units.tr: BETHEL (that is, House of God), also called Luz, why and by whom it was first so named: a town in the tribe of Benjamin, three miles from Jerusalem, Gen. 28.17, 19. It was taken by the sons of Joseph, Judg. 1.22–25. There God was worshipped and consulted, Judg. 20.18; 1 Sam. 10.3. There Jeroboam set up a calf to be worshipped, 1 Kings 12.29. [Therefore afterwards it was called not Bethel but Beth-aven, that is, House of vanity and confusion, Hos. 4.15; 5.8; 10.5.] See JEROBOAM.

units.la: BETH-LEHEM (id est domus panis) quę & Ephrata, id est, terra fructifera, seu pullulans, ædificatur à Roboamo, 2. Paral. 11.6. Christi in terris ortu nobilitatur, Mich.5.2. Matth.2.v.1.5 6. Luc.2.4. Ioh.7.42.
units.tr: BETHLEHEM (that is, house of bread), also called Ephrata, that is, fruitful or sprouting land, built by Rehoboam, 2 Chr. 11.6. It was made famous by Christ's birth on earth, Mic. 5.2; Matt. 2.1, 5, 6; Luke 2.4; John 7.42.

units.la: BETH-LEHEM duæ, altera in tribu Iuda, quæ & Ephrata cognomin. altera in tribu Zabulon, in Galilæa inferiore.]
units.tr: There were two Bethlehems: one in the tribe of Judah, also called Ephrata; the other in the tribe of Zebulun, in lower Galilee.]

units.la: BETHORON (domus iræ) vrbs in Tribu Ephraim, Iof.10.10. Duplex superior & inferior 16.5. & 18.13. Leuitis concessa, 21.22. vtraque à Solomone munita: 2. Chr.8.5.
units.tr: BETHORON (house of wrath), a town in the tribe of Ephraim, Josh. 10.10. There were two, upper and lower, 16.5; 18.13. It was given to the Levites, 21.22; both were fortified by Solomon, 2 Chr. 8.5.

units.la: BETHPHAGE (domus maxillarum) villula in monte Oliveti, ad quam venit Christus: Matt.21.1. Marc.11.1. Luc.19.29.
units.tr: BETHPHAGE (house of jaws), a small village on the Mount of Olives, to which Christ came, Matt. 21.1; Mark 11.1; Luke 19.29.

units.la: BETH-SABEA (seu Batscheba) filia Eliam, Vriæ vxor formosa, 2. Sam.11.v.2 3. adulterio à Dauide corrumpitur, v.4. parit, v.27. ei nibit, v.27. parit Salomonem, 12.24. ei suplicat pro Salomone filio, 1.Reg.1.v.15.16.17. (i. filia iuramenti.)
units.tr: BATHSHEBA (or Beth-sabea), daughter of Eliam, beautiful wife of Uriah, 2 Sam. 11.2, 3. She was corrupted in adultery by David, v. 4; she conceived, v. 27; she married him, v. 27; she bore Solomon, 12.24; she pleaded with him on behalf of her son Solomon, 1 Kings 1.15–17. (That is, daughter of the oath.)

units.la: BETH-SAIDA, (id est, domus venationis,) civitas natalitiis Petri, Philippi, & Andreæ clara, Ioh.1.45. & 12.21 obiurgatur à Christo, Matt.11.21. Luc.10.13.
units.tr: BETHSAIDA (that is, house of hunting), a city famous as the birthplace of Peter, Philip and Andrew, John 1.45; 12.21. It was rebuked by Christ, Matt. 11.21; Luke 10.13.

units.la: BETH-SAMITAE, conspecta Dei arca læti holocaustum offerunt, 1.Sam.6.15. percutiuntur à Deo propter inspectu arcæ finum, v.19. percussi eum pro vero Deo agnoscunt, v.20.
units.tr: The men of BETH-SHEMESH, seeing God's ark, joyfully offered a burnt offering, 1 Sam. 6.15. They were struck by God for looking into the ark, v. 19; when they were struck, they acknowledged him as the true God, v. 20.

units.la: BETSER, alias Bosor, vrbs fugitiuorum in tribu Ruben, Leuitis data, Deut.4.43. Iof.20 8.& 21.36.
units.tr: BETSER, otherwise Bosor, a city of refuge in the tribe of Reuben, given to the Levites, Deut. 4.43; Josh. 20.8; 21.36.

units.la: BIBLIOTHECA, 1.Esdr.5.17.& 6.1.2. Marc.2.13.
units.tr: LIBRARY, 1 Esd. 5.17; 6.1, 2; Mark 2.13.

units.la: LIBERE proprie sumptum, verbum notæ significationis & frequenter occurrens. Synecdochicè, pro conuiuari, Gen. 43 34. sic & comedere nonnunquam, vt Esth.3.15. & 7.1. Bibere vinum in coena, quod sacramentaliter est sanguis Christi, Matt.26.27.1.Cor.11 25 28. Bibere aquam à Christo datam, Ioan.4 14. Adiunctis subiectis verbum illud varias habet significationes, quæ partim ad prauos affectus & tristes effectus ac euentus referuntur: partim ad lætos, salutares & beatos. De prima signific. vide Iob.5.5. & 15.16 & 21.20. & 34 7. Pf.75.9. Prou.4 17. & 26.6. Esa.51.17.22.Ierem. 2.18. & 25.v.16 26.27.28.& 49.12.& 51.7. Ezech.23.33. 34. & 34 19. Abd.1 16. Habac.2.16. Apoc.14.10. & 16.6. & 18 3. De altera, vid. Prou.9.5. Cantic.5.1. Esa.65.13. Ier.22.15. Ezech.34 18. Zach.9 15. Luc.22.30. Ioan.4 14. & 6.v.53.54.56 & 7.37.1. Cor.10 4.
units.tr: LIBERE, properly taken, a word of well-known meaning that occurs frequently. By synecdoche, it means to feast, Gen. 43.34; so also sometimes to eat, as Esth. 3.15; 7.1. To drink wine at the supper, which sacramentally is the blood of Christ, Matt. 26.27; 1 Cor. 11.25, 28. To drink the water given by Christ, John 4.14. With the added objects, that word has various meanings, which partly refer to bad feelings and sad effects and outcomes, partly to joyful, saving and blessed ones. On the first meaning see Job 5.5; 15.16; 21.20; 34.7; Ps. 75.9; Prov. 4.17; 26.6; Isa. 51.17, 22; Jer. 2.18; 25.15–16, 26–28; 49.12; 51.7; Ezek. 23.33–34; 34.19; Obad. 1.16; Hab. 2.16; Rev. 14.10; 16.6; 18.3. On the second, see Prov. 9.5; Song 5.1; Isa. 65.13; Jer. 22.15; Ezek. 34.18; Zech. 9.15; Luke 22.30; John 4.14; 6.53, 54, 56; 7.37; 1 Cor. 10.4.

units.la: <bl>Bibere</bl>, afflictiones & mortem indicat, Pf.110.7. Matth 20. 22. & 26.42.]
units.tr: <bl>To drink</bl> indicates afflictions and death, Ps. 110.7; Matt. 20.22; 26.42.]

units.la: [Bibliotheca, Esdr.5.17. & 6.1.21 23.]
Bigamia, Vide Polygamia.
units.tr: Bigamy, see Polygamy.

units.la: Bithinia regio minoris Asiæ, proxima Troadi, Act.16.7. Pet.1.2.
units.tr: Bithynia, a region of Asia Minor, next to Troas, Acts 16.7; 1 Pet. 1.2.

units.la: Binis tunicis indui, qui dicantur. Vide Indui binis, &c.
units.tr: Those who are said to be clothed in two tunics. See Clothed in two, etc.

units.la: Binomii: Binomiorum exempla: Rahuel, Iethro, Exo.2.18. & 3. Gedeon, Ierobaal, Iudic.6.32. Achimelech, Abiathar, Sam.21.2. Marc.2.26. Salomon, Iedidia, 2.Sam.12.v.24.25. Sennacherib, Sargon, 2. Reg.18.13. Esa.20.1. Eliacim Ioachim, 2.Reg.23 34. Ozias, Azarias, 2.Reg.15.1.2. Par.26.23. Mathania, Sedecias, 2. Reg.24.17. Nehemias, Athersatha, Nehem.8.9. Esther, Edessa, Esth.2.7. Daniel, Baltassar, Ananias, Sidrach: Misael, Mesach: Azarias, Abdenago, Daniel, 1.7. Simon, Cephas, siue Petrus, Iohann. 1. 42. Ioseph, Barsabas, Actor. 1.23. Iosès, Barnabas, 4.36. Tabitha, Dorcas, 9.36. Bar-iesu, Elymas, 13.v.6.8. Paulus, Saulus, v.9.
units.tr: Binomials. Examples of binomials: Raguel, Jethro, Exod. 2.18; 3. Gideon, Jerubbaal, Judg. 6.32. Abimelech, Abiathar, 1 Sam. 21.2; Mark 2.26. Solomon, Jedidiah, 2 Sam. 12.24, 25. Sennacherib, Sargon, 2 Kings 18.13; Isa. 20.1. Eliakim, Jehoiakim, 2 Kings 23.34. Uzziah, Azariah, 2 Kings 15.1, 2; 2 Chr. 26.23. Mattaniah, Zedekiah, 2 Kings 24.17. Nehemiah, Athersatha, Neh. 8.9. Esther, Hadassah, Esth. 2.7. Daniel, Belteshazzar; Hananiah, Shadrach; Mishael, Meshach; Azariah, Abednego: Daniel 1.7. Simon, Cephas, or Peter, John 1.42. Joseph, Barsabbas, Acts 1.23. Joses, Barnabas, 4.36. Tabitha, Dorcas, 9.36. Bar-Jesus, Elymas, 13.6, 8. Paul, Saul, v. 9.

units.la: <bl>Blasphemare</bl>, pro impiè loqui, Matth.9.3. Marc.2.7. Luc.5.21. [& 22.65. Iac.2.7.2. Petr.2.2.10. Iud.v.8.10. Apoc.6.&c.]
units.tr: <bl>To blaspheme</bl>, to speak impiously, Matt. 9.3; Mark 2.7; Luke 5.21. [And 22.65; Jas. 2.7; 2 Pet. 2.2, 10; Jude 8, 10; Rev. 6, etc.]

units.la: <bl>Blasphemia</bl>, est maledicentiæ species, cùm quid Deo tribuitur, aut de eo negatur. per quod illius naturæ fit iniuria, aut cùm bonorum existimationi, quos tamen pietas nobis commendat, derogamus (Blasphemia in Spiritum S. Vide peccatorum remissio.)
units.tr: <bl>Blasphemy</bl> is a species of slander, when something is ascribed to God or denied of him, by which an injury is done to his nature, or when we detract from the reputation of good men, whom piety nevertheless commends to us. (Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit: see forgiveness of sins.)

units.la: <bl>Blasphemia</bl>, pro obtrectatione, calumnia, & sermone. quo aliena fama læditur, Matth. 15. 19. Blasphemia in Spiritum Sanctum non remittitur, Matthæi 12. 32. Marc. 3. 29. Luc. 12. 10. Hebr. 6. 4. & 10. 26. 1. Ioan. 5. 16. 2. Petr. 2. 20. Blasphemia damnatur, Exodi 27. 7. Deut. 5. 11. 2. Tim. 3. 2. 1, Cor. 12. 3. Col. 3. 8. 1. Pet. 4. 4. Blasphemiæ nomina, Apocal. 13. 1.
units.tr: <bl>Blasphemy</bl>, for detraction, calumny, and speech by which another's reputation is harmed, Matt. 15.19. Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit is not forgiven, Matt. 12.32; Mark 3.29; Luke 12.10; Heb. 6.4; 10.26; 1 John 5.16; 2 Pet. 2.20. Blasphemy is condemned, Exod. 27.7; Deut. 5.11; 2 Tim. 3.2; 1 Cor. 12.3; Col. 3.8; 1 Pet. 4.4. Names of blasphemy, Rev. 13.1.

units.la: Vide PECCATVM in Spiritum Sanctum. Blasphemia in Deum exempla: in Satana, Genesis 3. vers. 4. 5. Matth. 4. 9. Luc. 4. 7. Pharaone, Exodi 5. 2. filio Salumith Israelitidis, Leuit. 24. 11. familiaribus Regis Syriæ, 1 Reg. 20. 23. Sedecia, 22. 24. 2. Paral. 18. 23. Rabsacé, 2. Reg. 18. v. 30. 35. & 19. v. 10. 22. 23. 28. Senacherib. 2. Paral. 32. 10. Esa. 36. v. 15. 18. 20. & 37. v. 6. 10. 17. Rege Tyri, Ezech. 28. 2. Nabuchodonosor, Dan. 3. v. 14. 15. Esa. 1. 4. & 5. 24. Matth. 9 34. Ioan. 7. 20. & 9. v. 16. 24. & 10. 20. Scribis & Pharisæis, Matth. 9 34. & 12. 24. Marc. 3. 22. Luc. 11. 15. Ioan. 7 20. & 9. v. 16. 24. & 10. 20. summis Sacerdotibus, Principibus populi, Scribis & Pharisæis, Matth. 27. 41. Marc. 15. 31. Luc. 22. v. 64. 65. & 23. 37. latrone, v. 39. Pauli hostibus, Actor. 13 45. & 18. 6. & 19 8. 9. Rom. 3. 8. Antichristo, 2. Thessal. 2. 4. Apocal. 13. v. 5. 6. & 16. v. 9. 11. 21. Paulo ante conversionem, 1. Corinth. 15. 9. 1. Tim. 1. 13.
units.tr: See SIN against the Holy Spirit. Examples of blasphemy against God: against Satan, Gen. 3.4, 5; Matt. 4.9; Luke 4.7. Pharaoh, Exod. 5.2; the son of Shelomith the Israelitess, Lev. 24.11; the courtiers of the king of Syria, 1 Kings 20.23; Zedekiah, 22.24; 2 Chr. 18.23; Rabshakeh, 2 Kings 18.30, 35; 19.10, 22, 23, 28; Sennacherib, 2 Chr. 32.10; Isa. 36.15, 18, 20; 37.6, 10, 17; the king of Tyre, Ezek. 28.2; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3.14, 15; Isa. 1.4; 5.24; Matt. 9.34; John 7.20; 9.16, 24; 10.20. The scribes and Pharisees, Matt. 9.34; 12.24; Mark 3.22; Luke 11.15; John 7.20; 9.16, 24; 10.20. The chief priests, rulers of the people, scribes and Pharisees, Matt. 27.41; Mark 15.31; Luke 22.64, 65; 23.37. The thief, v. 39. Paul's enemies, Acts 13.45; 18.6; 19.8, 9; Rom. 3.8. Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2.4; Rev. 13.5, 6; 16.9, 11, 21. Paul before his conversion, 1 Cor. 15.9; 1 Tim. 1.13.

units.la: ASPHEMIAE poena, Leuit. 24. v. 16 23. Deuter. 13. v. 9. 10. Dan. 3 29.
units.tr: The punishment of blasphemy: Lev. 24.16, 23; Deut. 13.9, 10; Dan. 3.29.

units.la: ASPHEMARI pro impium iudicari, 1. Cor. 10. 30.
units.tr: To be blasphemed means to be judged impious, 1 Cor. 10.30.

units.la: PANERGES (id est, filij tonitrui) Marc. 3. 17. sic dicti Iacobus & Ioannes filii Zebedæi: quia Christus eis daturus erat sonoram vocem, quam tonarent in toto orbe.
units.tr: BOANERGES (that is, sons of thunder), Mark 3.17. James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were so named because Christ was going to give them a loud voice, which they would thunder throughout the whole world.

units.la: UNITAS hominis, Psalm. 37. 3. & 38. 21. & 119. 66. Gal. 5. 22. Ephes. 5. 9.
units.tr: GOODNESS of man, Ps. 37.3; 38.21; 119.66; Gal. 5.22; Eph. 5.9.

units.la: UNUM, varias habet acceptiones.
units.tr: GOOD has various meanings.

units.la: Primum enim, idem est ac Benedictio Dei, rerum terrenarum, Spiritualium, nec non cælestium respectu, pro ut contextuum circumstantiæ demonstrant. In eum sensum cadunt sequentes loci, Gen. 50. 20. Deut. 30. 19 2. Sam. 7. 28. 1. Reg. 8. 56. 66. Nehe. 5 19. & 13. 31. Psal. 27. 13. & 65. 5. & 86. 17. Prou. 13. 21. & 16. 20. & 17. 20. & 18. 22. & 19. 8. Eccles. 8. 12. 13. Ierem. 5. 25. & 17. 6. & 18. 10. & 21. 10. & 24. 5. & 29. 32. & 31. 12. 14. Thren. 3. 38. Ezech. 36. 11. Ose. 3. 5. & 8. 3. Amos. 9. 4. Zach. 1. 17. Luc. 1. 53. Rom. 8. 28. & 10. 15. & 14. 16. Hebr. 9. 14. & 19. 1.
units.tr: First, it is the same as the blessing of God, in respect of earthly things, spiritual things, and heavenly things too, as the circumstances of the contexts show. The following passages fall in that sense: Gen. 50.20; Deut. 30.19; 2 Sam. 7.28; 1 Kings 8.56, 66; Neh. 5.19; 13.31; Ps. 27.13; 65.5; 86.17; Prov. 13.21; 16.20; 17.20; 18.22; 19.8; Eccl. 8.12, 13; Jer. 5.25; 17.6; 18.10; 21.10; 24.5; 29.32; 31.12, 14; Lam. 3.38; Ezek. 36.11; Hos. 3.5; 8.3; Amos 9.4; Zech. 1.17; Luke 1.53; Rom. 8.28; 10.15; 14.16; Heb. 9.14; 19.1.

units.la: Secundò, significat beneficium aliquod à Deo vel homine homini præstitum: vt Genes. 44.4. Exod. 18.9. Num. 1e 29. Iosu. 24.20. Iudic. 8.35. 1. Sam. 24.18 19. & 25 21. 2. Sam. 16.12. 2. Paral. 6.41. & 7.10. 24.16. Psalm. 13.6, & 35. 12. & 38 21. & 84.12. & 103.5. & 107.9. & 109.5. Prouer. 17. 13. & 31.12 Eccl. 9.8. Esai. 63.7. Ier. 18.20. & 33 9. Matth. 7 10. Luc. 11 1j Gal. 6 18. Philem. 1.14.
units.tr: Secondly, it signifies some benefit bestowed by God or by a man upon another man, as in Gen. 44.4; Exod. 18.9; Num. 1e 29; Josh. 24.20; Judg. 8.35; 1 Sam. 24.18, 19, & 25.21; 2 Sam. 16.12; 2 Chron. 6.41, & 7.10, 24.16; Ps. 13.6, & 35.12, & 38.21, & 84.12, & 103.5, & 107.9, & 109.5; Prov. 17.13, & 31.12; Eccl. 9.8; Isa. 63.7; Jer. 18.20, & 33.9; Matt. 7.10; Luke 11.1; Gal. 6.18; Philem. 1.14.

units.la: Tertiò, id quod est commodum, conueniens, expediens: vt Gen. 2.18. & 34.22 Psalm. 119.71. Eccl. 5.17. & 8 15. Esa. 41.7. Mich. 1.12. Matth. 15.26. & 17.4. & 18.8. 9. & 26 24. Marc. 7.42. &c. Roman. 14. 21. 1. Corinth. 7. vers. 1,8. 2 6. & 9.15. Ephes. 28.
units.tr: Thirdly, that which is convenient, suitable, expedient, as in Gen. 2.18, & 34.22; Ps. 119.71; Eccl. 5.17, & 8.15; Isa. 41.7; Mic. 1.12; Matt. 15.26, & 17.4, & 18.8, 9, & 26.24; Mark 7.42, etc.; Rom. 14.21; 1 Cor. 7 vers. 1, 8, 2.6, & 9.15; Eph. 2.8.

units.la: Quartò, hac voce designantur delitiæ, voluptates, lætitiæ, Eccl. 2.v.1.24. & 4.8 & 6 3. & 11 9. Luc. 16.25.
units.tr: Fourthly, this word designates delights, pleasures, joys, Eccl. 2 vers. 1, 24, & 4.8, & 6.3, & 11.9; Luke 16.25.

units.la: Sextò, signif. dulce, Prou. 24.13.
units.tr: Sixthly, it signifies what is sweet, Prov. 24.13.

units.la: Septimò, idem est ac eximium, laude dignum, Ioan. 1.14.
units.tr: Seventhly, it is the same as outstanding, worthy of praise, John 1.14.

units.la: Octauò, signif. fruges terræ: Esdr. 9.12. Nehem. 9 36. Esai. 1.19 Ierem. 2.7.
units.tr: Eighthly, it signifies the fruits of the earth: Ezra 9.12; Neh. 9.36; Isa. 1.19; Jer. 2.7.

units.la: Nonò, denotatur hac voce gloria Dei, Exod. 33.19. & iustitia Messæ, Ose. 14 3.
units.tr: Ninthly, by this word is denoted the glory of God, Exod. 33.19, and the righteousness of the Messiah, Hos. 14.3.

units.la: Vndecimò, denotat id quod pingue est, Leuitic. 27.33. & salubre, Prouer. 25.27. Esai. 55.2. & placidum sermonem, 2. Sam. 1.22. Ier. 31.32. & prosperitatem, Deu. 23.6. 1. Sam. 20.12. 1. Reg. 1.42.
units.tr: Eleventhly, it denotes what is fat, Lev. 27.33, and wholesome, Prov. 25.27; Isa. 55.2, and pleasant speech, 2 Sam. 1.22; Jer. 31.32, and prosperity, Deut. 23.6; 1 Sam. 20.12; 1 Kings 1.42.

units.la: BONVS Deus, Bonæ Creaturæ, Bona vita, fama, mors, &cæt. hominis, Bonæ res, &c. Vide subiecta. nempe DEVS CREATURA, HOMO. & quod dictum est præceden. sectione de BONO.
units.tr: GOOD God; good creature; good life, fame, death, etc. of man; good things, etc. See what is set out below, namely GOD, CREATURE, MAN; and what was said in the preceding section on GOOD.

units.la: BONVS vir, Boni interdum ob malos plectuntur, Iof.7.12. Boni pro malis non puniendi, Deuter. 24.16. Ezech.18. 20.2. Reg.14.6. Bonus Deus solus, Matth. 19.17. Marcio.18. Luc.18.19.
units.tr: A GOOD man: good people are sometimes punished on account of the wicked, Josh. 7.12. Good people are not to be punished for the wicked, Deut. 24.16; Ezek. 18.20; 2 Kings 14.6. God alone is good, Matt. 19.17; Marcion 18; Luke 18.19.

units.la: Bonorum inter malos latentium exempla:
units.tr: Examples of good people hidden among the wicked:

units.la: Noe cum domo sua inter filios Dei à filiabus hominum corruptos, & diluuio absorptos, Gen.6.9.&7.7. Loth inter Sodomitas pessimos, 13.v.11.13. Abraham inter Chananæos, v.12. Ioseph inter Ægyptios, 39.v.7.8. Samuel inter perversos & impios Heli filios, 1.Sam.2.v.25.26. Elias cum septem millibus virorum inter Israelitas idololatras, 1. Reg. 19. ver.9 10.14.18. Roman.11.v.4.5. Mardochæus inter servos Assueri, Esth.3. 2.Iob qui gentilis fuisse, & de Esau descendisse dicitur, inter reliquos gentiles. Iob 1.1. Ieremias inter concaptiuos, Ierem.43.v.1.2.3.4. Ezechiel inter scorpiones, Ezec. 2.6. Daniel, Sidrach, Misach, Abdenago inter idololatras, Dan. 3.v.16.17.&6.10. Centurio inter Israelitas, Matth. 8.10. Ioseph Arimathæus inter Iudæos, Marc. 15.43. Nicodemus inter Pharisæos, Ioan.3.v.1.2.&19.39. Cornelius Centur. inter gentes, Act.10.v.1.2.
units.tr: Noah with his household among the sons of God, corrupted by the daughters of men and swallowed up by the flood, Gen. 6.9, & 7.7. Lot among the most wicked Sodomites, 13.11, 13. Abraham among the Canaanites, v. 12. Joseph among the Egyptians, 39.7, 8. Samuel among the perverse and impious sons of Eli, 1 Sam. 2.25, 26. Elijah with seven thousand men among the idolatrous Israelites, 1 Kings 19 vers. 9, 10, 14, 18; Rom. 11.4, 5. Mordecai among the servants of Ahasuerus, Esth. 3. Job, who is said to have been a Gentile and descended from Esau, among the rest of the Gentiles, Job 1.1. Jeremiah among his fellow captives, Jer. 43.1, 2, 3, 4. Ezekiel among scorpions, Ezek. 2.6. Daniel, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego among idolaters, Dan. 3.16, 17, & 6.10. The centurion among the Israelites, Matt. 8.10. Joseph of Arimathea among the Jews, Mark 15.43. Nicodemus among the Pharisees, John 3.1, 2, & 19.39. Cornelius the centurion among the Gentiles, Acts 10.1, 2.

units.la: Bonorum per malos oppressionis exempla:
units.tr: Examples of the good oppressed by the wicked:

units.la: Cain Abelem, Gen.4.8. Sodomitæ Loth, 19.9. Ismael Isaacum, 21.9. Gala-t.4.29. Esau Iacobum, Genes.27.41. Ægyptij Israelitas, Exodi 1.ver.11.12. Abimelech septuaginta fratres, Iudicum 9.5. Saul Dauidem, 1.Sam.19.ver.19.70 Absalom Dauidem, 2.Sam.15 14. Iezabel Eliam, 1.Reg.19. verfic.1 2. Ioram Elisæum, 2.Regum 6.ver.30.31.32. Ioas Zachariam. 2. Paral. 24.22. Aman Mardochæum, Esther 3. versi. 5.6. Phassur Ieremiam, Ierem.20. verfic. 1.2. Ierias & Principes Sedechiæ Ieremiam, Ier.37.v.14.15. Nabuchodonosor tres adolescentes, Dan.3.verfic.19.20. Darius Danielem, eum in lacum leonum coniiciens, Dan.6.16. Herodes Ioannem Baptistam, Matth. 14.ver.6.7.8 9.10. Iudæi Christum, 27.34.
units.tr: Cain kills Abel, Gen. 4.8. The Sodomites (oppress) Lot, Gen. 19.9. Ishmael (persecutes) Isaac, Gen. 21.9; Gal. 4.29. Esau (seeks to kill) Jacob, Gen. 27.41. The Egyptians oppress the Israelites, Exod. 1.11-12. Abimelech (kills) seventy brothers, Judg. 9.5. Saul pursues David, 1 Sam. 19.ver.19.70. Absalom (rises against) David, 2 Sam. 15.14. Jezebel (seeks the life of) Elijah, 1 Kings 19.1-2. Joram (threatens) Elisha, 2 Kings 6.30-32. Joash kills Zechariah, 2 Chron. 24.22. Haman (plots against) Mordecai, Esther 3.5-6. Pashhur (strikes and imprisons) Jeremiah, Jer. 20.1-2. Jeremiah is (accused) by Jerias and the princes of Zedekiah, Jer. 37.14-15. Nebuchadnezzar (throws into the furnace) three young men, Dan. 3.19-20. Darius casts Daniel into the lions' den, Dan. 6.16. Herod (imprisons and beheads) John the Baptist, Matt. 14.6-10. The Jews (crucify) Christ, Matt. 27.34.

units.la: Marc.15 27.Lucæ 23.33.Ioan.19. 18. Principes Sacerdotum [?] Apostolos,Actor.5.17.18.Iudæi Paulum & Barnabam,13. 45.46 50.Iudæi & Magistratus Paulum & Silam de ciuitate te Philippis expellunt,16.v.18.23.24.39.
units.tr: Mark 15.27; Luke 23.33; John 19.18. The chief priests [?] (persecute) the apostles, Acts 5.17-18. The Jews (persecute) Paul and Barnabas, Acts 13.45-46, 50. The Jews and the magistrates expel Paul and Silas from the city of Philippi, Acts 16.18, 23-24, 39.

units.la: Bona opera,pietáque in Deum vera commendantur, E[?] xodi 19.5. & 20.2 &c. & 23.v.19. 25. Deuter.5.ver.6.&c.12. Iosu. 22.5. 1. Sam. 15.22. Psalm. 2.10. & 40.7. & 50.14. Proverb. 3.1. & 14.31. Esaiæ 1.16. & 58. 6. Ierem. 22. Ezech. 18.6. Oseæ 6.6. Michæ 6.8. Zachar. 7.9.& 8.16. Eccles.35.12.Matth.5. v.24.29 39.Luc.1.75.& 3 11 Ioann.1.26. Rom.12.1.&c. & 13.1. &c.& 14.17. Philipp.3.3.Iac.1.2
units.tr: Good works and true piety towards God are commended: Exod. 19.5; 20.2 etc.; 23.19, 25; Deut. 5.6 etc.; 12; Josh. 22.5; 1 Sam. 15.22; Ps. 2.10; 40.7; 50.14; Prov. 3.1; 14.31; Isa. 1.16; 58.6; Jer. 22; Ezek. 18.6; Hos. 6.6; Mic. 6.8; Zech. 7.9; 8.16; Ecclus 35.12; Matt. 5.24, 29, 39; Luke 1.75; 3.11; John 1.26; Rom. 12.1ff; 13.1ff; 14.17; Phil. 3.3; James 1.2.

units.la: Vide OPERA. Bona opera glorificant Patrem cœlestem
units.tr: See WORKS. Good works glorify the heavenly Father.

units.la: Matth.5.16. Bonis operibus testanda est vitæ nouitas,
units.tr: Matt. 5.16. The newness of life is to be attested by good works.

units.la: Ioann.5.7. Bonis operibus mercedem deberi, quibus testimonium probent Pontificij. Vide MERCES. Bonus thesaurus,Luc.6.45.Bonitas Dei commemoratur,
units.tr: John 5.7. Reward is owed to good works, by which the Papists try to prove merit. See REWARD. Good treasure, Luke 6.45. The goodness of God is commemorated.

units.la: Petr.1.3.
Boos, vir diues & potens,Ruth.2.1.&c.ducit Ruth vxorem
units.tr: Boaz, a rich and powerful man, Ruth 2.1ff, takes Ruth as his wife.

units.la: 4.13.[filius Rahab Hierichuntinæ,& abauus Dauidis,Matth.
units.tr: 4.13 [son of Rahab of Jericho, and ancestor of David, Matt.

units.la: Bos animal brutum:Eius oblatio,Leuitici 31. Bos cornupeta, Exodi 21.29. Bos alium Bouem occidens, v. 35. Bos duo in frusta concisi mittuntur per omnes Israel partes
units.tr: Ox, an animal: its offering, Lev. 31. An ox that gores, Exod. 21.29. An ox that kills another ox, v. 35. Oxen cut into pieces are sent through all the regions of Israel, 1 Sam. 11.7.

units.la: 1.Sam.11.7. Boum triturantium os non alligandum,Deut.
units.tr: The mouth of an ox treading out grain is not to be muzzled, Deut. 25.4; 1 Cor. 9.9; 1 Tim. 5.18.

units.la: 25.4.1.Cor.9.9.1 Tim.5.18. Boues fusiles in Templo Salomonis collocati,2.Paral. 4.3. Agnoscit possessorem suum
units.tr: Bronze oxen placed in Solomon's Temple, 2 Chron. 4.3. It knows its owner,

units.la: Botsra Idumeæ metropolis,Gen.36.33. Esai.34.6. & 63.
units.tr: Bozrah, metropolis of Edom, Gen. 36.33; Isa. 34.6; 63.

units.la: Ierem.49.13. Amos1.12.
Brachivm; [ pro corporis hum. parte notiss. Gene.49.2.
units.tr: Arm [a well-known part of the body], Gen. 49.2.

units.tr: 31.17; Isa. 17.5; Ezek. 4.7 and 13.20; Dan. 2.32] for power

units.tr: and strength [divine and human], Gen. 49.24; Exod.
Jer. 17.5 and 21.5 and 27.5 and 32.17, 21 and 48.25. Ezek.

[Brachium, ramus arboris, Ezech. 17. 9. Brauium, 1. Cor. 9.24. Philip. 3.14.] βεαβεῖον, præmium victoriæ, metonymice. REVITAS vitæ humanæ, Vide VITA humana.
units.tr: Dan. 11.6, 15, 22, 31; Hos. 7.15 and 11.3; Zech. 11.17; Luke 1; John 12.38; Acts 13.17. For the Gospel: John 12.38, which is "the power of God unto salvation to everyone who believes", Rom. 1.16. [Arm, a branch of a tree, Ezek. 17.9. Prize, 1 Cor. 9.24; Phil. 3.14.] [βραβεῖον], the prize of victory, by metonymy. VITALITY of human life. See LIFE, human.

units.la: Byssus in tabernaculo Exod. 25. 4. &c. in domo diuitum, Prov.31.22. Luc.16.19. Byssus mysticus Israelitarum Ezech. 16.11. 13. &c. meretricis magnæ, Apocal.18.12. 16. Ecclesiæ Dei ornatus, seu fidelium puritas figuratè depicta, Apocalyps.19. 8.14.]
units.tr: Fine linen in the tabernacle, Exod. 25.4 etc.; in the houses of the rich, Prov. 31.22; Luke 16.19. The mystical fine linen of the Israelites, Ezek. 16.11, 13 etc.; of the great harlot, Rev. 18.12, 16. The adornment of God's Church, or the purity of the faithful, depicted figuratively, Rev. 19.8, 14.

units.la: C
units.tr: C

units.la: AAT H, filius Leui Genes.46.11. eius filij, Exodi 6.18. Num.3.19. eorum sors & vrbes, Ios. 21. 5. leges Rehath:is fuit auus Mosis & Aaronis: Exod.6.20. (.i.obtusus.)
units.tr: AARON, son of Levi, Gen. 46.11; his sons, Exod. 6.18; Num. 3.19; their lot and cities, Josh. 21.5. Kohath was the grandfather of Moses and Aaron, Exod. 6.20. (i.e., obtuse.)

units.la: CADAVER suspensi è patibulo auferendū, Deut. 21. v.22.23. (Cadauer interdum animæ nomine intelligēdū. Vide ANIMA.) Vbi cadauer, illuc aquilę &c. Mat.24.28.
units.tr: A CORPSE of one hanged on a gibbet must be taken down, Deut. 21.22-23. (A corpse is sometimes to be understood under the name of soul. See SOUL.) Where the corpse is, there the eagles gather, etc., Matt. 24.28.

units.la: ADERE humi, 2. Reg.10.10. Matth.10.29. Actor.27.34. ex Hebræorum idiotismo dicitur quod perit & aboletur. [Per composita sua, Concido, Decido, &c. ab aliis exponitur. Item per similia verba, sed cum maiore emphasi, vt collabor in terrā, obcumbo, procido, corruo, deiicior, Supernè Decido, Irruo, Labor, ]Collabor, &c.
units.tr: To fall to the ground, 2 Kings 10.10; Matt. 10.29; Acts 27.34. By Hebrew idiom it is said of what perishes and is destroyed. [By its compounds, concido, decido, etc., it is explained by others. Likewise by similar words, but with greater emphasis: collabor in terram, obcumbo, procido, corruo, deiicior; supine decido, irruo, labor,] collabor, etc.

units.la: ADES, locus indeserto Tsin, vbi Maria sepulta fuit: Num. 20. 1. Et Moses percussa rupe aquam populo murmuranti dedit, v.11. Vide Ezech.47.19.
units.tr: ADES, a place in the desert of Zin, where Miriam was buried: Num. 20.1. And Moses, having struck the rock, gave water to the murmuring people, v. 11. See Ezek. 47.19.

units.la: AECITAS tum corporis, tum animi, Genes. 19. 11. Deut. 28. 28. 2.Reg.6.18.& 25. 7. Psal.69.2. & 146. 8. Esa.6. 10.& 29.18.& 35.5.& 42.v.7.16.18.& 43.8.& 56.10 & 59. 10. Matt. 15.14.Mar.8.18. Luc.4.19. Ioan.9.v.1.4.& 12.40. Act. 9. v.8. 18.& 13 11.Rom.1.21.& 11 10.2. Cor.4.4. Ephes.4.18 2. Petr. 1.9.1.Ioan.2.11. Apocal.3 17. Cæcitas corporalis à Deo, Exodi,4.11, Cæcitatis & excæcationis externæ exempla: Sedechias, 2.Reg.25.7. Ierem.39. 7. duo cæci, Matth 9. 27. & 20. 30. Cæcus, Matth.12, 22. Bartimæus, Mar.10.46. Cæcus natus, Ioan.9. 1. Paulus Act.9.8. Elymas, Act.13.11. Cæcitas cordis, pœna peccati, Deut. 28.v.28.29. damnatur, Marc.3.5. Ioan. 3.19. & 9. 39.& 12.46.Rom. 12. 25.Ephe. 4.18. 2.Tim.3.8.2. Petr.1.9. Cæcitatis interna exempla:Pharisæi,Mat.12.v.13.14. Mar. 3.v.5 6.Iudai Luc.23 18.Ioan.11·37. 2.Corinth. 4.v. 3.4. Cæcitas Iudæorum, Vide IVDAEI.Oculus eram cæco, Iob.29.15.
units.tr: BLINDNESS, both of body and of mind, Gen. 19.11; Deut. 28.28; 2 Kings 6.18 and 25.7; Ps. 69.2 and 146.8; Isa. 6.10 and 29.18 and 35.5 and 42.7, 16, 18 and 43.8 and 56.10 and 59.10; Matt. 15.14; Mark 8.18; Luke 4.19; John 9.1-4 and 12.40; Acts 9.8, 18 and 13.11; Rom. 1.21 and 11.10; 2 Cor. 4.4; Eph. 4.18; 2 Pet. 1.9; 1 John 2.11; Rev. 3.17. Bodily blindness comes from God, Exod. 4.11. Examples of outward blindness and blinding: Zedekiah, 2 Kings 25.7; Jer. 39.7; two blind men, Matt. 9.27 and 20.30; a blind man, Matt. 12.22; Bartimaeus, Mark 10.46; a man blind from birth, John 9.1; Paul, Acts 9.8; Elymas, Acts 13.11. Blindness of heart, the punishment of sin, Deut. 28.28-29, is condemned, Mark 3.5; John 3.19 and 9.39 and 12.46; Rom. 12.25; Eph. 4.18; 2 Tim. 3.8; 2 Pet. 1.9. Examples of inward blindness: the Pharisees, Matt. 12.13-14; Mark 3.5-6; the Jews, Luke 23.18; John 11.37; 2 Cor. 4.3-4. The blindness of the Jews, see JEWS. "I was eyes to the blind," Job 29.15.

units.la: CAECO non nocendum,Leuit. 19. 14. Deut.27.18. Cæci cæcum ducentis conditio,Matth.15.14. Luc.6. 39. Cæci illuminantur,Vide MIRACVLA.
units.tr: The blind must not be harmed, Lev. 19.14; Deut. 27.18. The condition of a blind man leading a blind man, Matt. 15.14; Luke 6.39. The blind are enlightened, see MIRACLES.

units.la: [CAELVM, varias habet significationes. 1. Intelligitur hoc nomine tota aeris & æthereæ regionis ab aquis & terra ad orbem Lunæ expansio. 2.Omnium cælestium Sphærarum, seu planetarum & stellarum fixarum, nec non primi mobilis ambitus amplissimus. 3. Beatorum habitatio, & diuinæ gloriæ lucidissima beatissimáque quies ac sedes, 4.Tota illa compages, mare & terram circumplectens, quæ aerem, ætheream regionem, & cœlos aspectabiles continet. 5. Lucida illa pars,à crassiori & terrea longissimo interuallo distincta. 6 Deum ipsum, vel eius vocationem, mandatum,& approbationem.7.Cælum nouum, Esai. 65, 17. & 66, 22. 2.Pet.3,13.Apoc. 21.1.Vide COELVM.
units.tr: [HEAVEN has various meanings. 1. By this name is understood the whole expanse of the air and the ethereal region, from the waters and earth up to the orb of the Moon. 2. The whole circuit of all the heavenly spheres, or of the planets and fixed stars, and also of the primum mobile. 3. The dwelling of the blessed, and the most bright and blessed rest and seat of divine glory. 4. That whole structure, embracing sea and land, which contains the air, the ethereal region, and the visible heavens. 5. That bright part, distinguished from the denser and earthly part by a very great interval. 6. God himself, or his calling, command and approval. 7. The new heaven, Isa. 65.17; 66.22; 2 Pet. 3.13; Rev. 21.1. See HEAVEN.]

units.la: CAEREMONIA, Vide CEREMONIA.
units.tr: CEREMONY, see CEREMONY.

units.la: CAESAR, primi Imperatoris Romani nomen proprium ad posteros deriuatum, Luc.3.1. Ioan.19.12.Act.25. v. 10. 11.12. 21.& 26 32. Cæsari principi ve tributa soluenda, Matth.22. 21. Marc. 12. 17. Luc.20.25.Rom.13. 7. Cæsarem appellat Paulus,Act.25.11. [Cæsaris domus, pro nonnullis Cæsaris domesticis,Philip.4 22.Quatuor Cęsares tempore Christi Pauli,Augustus,Tiberius,Claudius,Nero.] Vide Iohann. 19. 15.
units.tr: CAESAR, the proper name of the first Roman emperor, passed down to posterity: Luke 3.1; John 19.12; Acts 25.10-12, 21; 26.32. Tribute is to be paid to Caesar or the prince, Matt. 22.21; Mark 12.17; Luke 20.25; Rom. 13.7. Paul appeals to Caesar, Acts 25.11. [Caesar's household, for some of Caesar's servants, Phil. 4.22. Four Caesars in the time of Christ and Paul: Augustus, Tiberius, Claudius, Nero.] See John 19.15.

units.la: CAESAREAE duæ vrbes eodem nomine Vna Cæsarea Philippi,dicta Matt.16 13. Sic dicta quòd Philippus, Herodis Tetrarchæ frater eam condidisset. Altera ab Herode Antipatri filio restaurata, olim Turris Stratonis dicta. [Act. 8. 40.& 9.30.& 10. 1.& 11.11. & 12. 19. & 18. 22. ] Cæsareæ conuenit Paulus Philippum Euangelistam Act. 21,8. [Vide etiam c.23.& 25.]
units.tr: CAESAREA, two cities of the same name. One is Caesarea Philippi, mentioned in Matt. 16.13, so called because Philip, brother of Herod the tetrarch, had founded it. The other, restored by Herod, son of Antipater, was formerly called Strato's Tower. [Acts 8.40; 9.30; 10.1; 11.11; 12.19; 18.22.] Paul met Philip the evangelist at Caesarea, Acts 21.8. [See also ch. 23 and 25.]

units.la: CAIPHAS,princeps Sacerdotum, Matth.26. v. 3,57. Luc. 3, 2 Ioan.11, 49.Actor.4, 6. prophetat, Ioan.11.v. 49, 50. & 18, 14.Christum de Discipulis & doctrina interrogat, Ioann. 18,19.(i.Inuestigator, sagax,vel vomens ore.
units.tr: CAIAPHAS, high priest, Matt. 26.3, 57; Luke 3.2; John 11.49; Acts 4.6. He prophesied, John 11.49-50; 18.14. He questioned Christ about his disciples and his teaching, John 18.19. (That is, an investigator, shrewd, or vomiting from the mouth.)

units.la: CAIN(id est,acquisitus)Genes.4,1. ratio appellationis, ibid. primogenitus Adam nascitur,verfic.1. Agricola est,verfic. 2. munus quod offert Deo reiicitur, versic. 5. occidit fratrem Abelem, & quare, versi. 8.2. Ioan. 3.versi.12. Hebr. 12.24. a Deo maledicitur, Genesis 4, 11. ciuitatem extruit, versic. 17. ex Diabolo est, 1. Ioann. 3 12. [Via Cain, Iud. versicul. 11.]
units.tr: CAIN (that is, acquired), Gen. 4.1. The reason for the name, ibid. He is born the firstborn of Adam, v. 1. He is a farmer, v. 2. His offering to God is rejected, v. 5. He kills his brother Abel, and why, v. 8. 1 John 3.12; Heb. 12.24. He is cursed by God, Gen. 4.11. He builds a city, v. 17. He is of the Devil, 1 John 3.12. [The way of Cain, Jude v. 11.]

units.la: MINAN vitæ tempus, Gen. 5,14. [Genealogia, Luc. 3,36.37.]
units.tr: CAINAN, the length of a life-span, Gen. 5.14. [Genealogy, Luke 3.36-37.]

units.la: KALAMITAS, Vide AFFLICTIO, OPERATIO, TRIBULATIO.
units.tr: CALAMITY, see AFFLICTION, OPERATION, TRIBULATION.

units.la: CALAMVS, instrumentum quo pingimus literas, Psalm. 45. 2.3. Iohan. 13. Instrumentum ad mensurandum, Ezech. 40. ver. 3.5.6 7. & 41.8. & 42.16. &c. & 48, 8. Aromatis species, Esa. 43 24. Ierem. 6.20. Ezech. 27.19. Ramus in candelabro tabernaculi, Exod. 25.v.31 32. &c. & 30 23. & 37.17. &c. pro arundine, Esa. 42.3 Matt. 12.20.
units.tr: REED, the instrument with which we write letters, Ps. 45.2-3; John 13. An instrument for measuring, Ezek. 40.3, 5-7; 41.8; 42.16, etc.; 48.8. A kind of spice, Isa. 43.24; Jer. 6.20; Ezek. 27.19. A branch in the lampstand of the tabernacle, Exod. 25.31-32, etc.; 30.23; 37.17, etc. For a reed, Isa. 42.3; Matt. 12.20.

units.la: CALCANEVS, Genes. 3 15. Psal. 49.6. & 56,7. Ioan. 13,18.]
units.tr: CALCANEUS (heel): Gen. 3:15. Ps. 49:6 and 56:7. John 13:18.

units.la: CALCEAMENTVM: Calceamenta Israelitarum per desertum non attrita, Deut. 8, 4. & 29,5. Calceamenta in pedibus conedentium Agnum Paschalem, Exodi 12,11.
units.tr: CALCEAMENTUM (shoe): The shoes of the Israelites did not wear out in the desert, Deut. 8:4 and 29:5. Shoes on the feet of those eating the Passover lamb, Exod. 12:11.

units.la: CALCEI detractio & traditio signum erat alienatæ possessionis & translatę: Deut. 25 9. Ruth. 4.7. In ornamenta calceamentorū. &c. Isa. 3.18. In eos qui pro pari calceorū iustum vēdūt: Amos. 2.6. Baptista se indignū dicit qui calceamenta seu soleas Christi, oportet aut soluat (quibus verbis infimi serui conditio notatur) Matt. 3.11. Marc. 1.7. Luc. 3.16. Calceamenta ne sint Apostolis remoræ: Matt. 10.10.
units.tr: Removing a shoe and handing it over was a sign of alienated and transferred possession: Deut. 25:9; Ruth 4:7. On the adornments of shoes, etc., Isa. 3:18. Against those who sell the righteous for a pair of shoes, Amos 2:6. The Baptist says he is not worthy to carry (or loosen) the shoes or sandals of Christ, words which denote the condition of the lowest servant: Matt. 3:11; Mark 1:7; Luke 3:16. Shoes are not to be a hindrance to the Apostles: Matt. 10:10.

units.la: CALCULUS, 2 Sam. 17.13. Esai. 6. 6. Calculus albus, Apoc. 2,17.
units.tr: CALCULUS (pebble): 2 Sam. 17:13; Isa. 6:6. A white stone: Rev. 2:17.

units.la: CALDARIA, 1. Sam. 2 14.]. 1. lebes, siue ahenum.
units.tr: CALDARIA (cauldrons): 1 Sam. 2:14. (1) A kettle or bronze pot.

units.la: CALEB, filius Iephone, Numer. 14,6 filius Hesronis, 1. Par. 2, 18. vir pius terram chanaan cum Iosua laudat, Num. 14. v. 7,8. terra Chanaan illi promittitur, v. 24. Deut. 1. v. 35.36. hanc sibi dari postulat, Iosue 14. v. 6,12. & 21, 12. Iudic. 1,20. 1 Paral. 6,56. Senectus eius florens & fortis, Iosue 14. v. 10.11. tres filios & nac possessione sua expellit, Iosue 15.14. (. omni corde adhærens Deo.)
units.tr: CALEB, son of Jephunneh, Num. 14:6; son of Hezron, 1 Chr. 2:18. A pious man who praised the land of Canaan with Joshua, Num. 14:7, 8. The land of Canaan is promised to him, v. 24; Deut. 1:35, 36. He asks that this be given to him, Josh. 14:6, 12; 21:12; Judg. 1:20; 1 Chr. 6:56. His old age is flourishing and strong, Josh. 14:10, 11. He drives out three sons and their possession, Josh. 15:14. (Clinging to God with his whole heart.)

units.la: CALENDAE, prima dies mensis, Numer. 10,10. & 28 11. Esai. 1. 4. Ezech. 45 17. & 46. .1,3,6.]
units.tr: CALENDS, the first day of the month: Num. 10:10; 28:11; Isa. 1:14; Ezek. 45:17; 46:1, 3, 6.

units.la: CALIGO metaphorice, pro longe miserrima viuendi conditione, 2. Petri 2 4. Caligo tenebrarum, pro densissimis tenebris, per Hebraismum, 2. Petr. 2.17. Iudæ v. 13.] Caligo, i. aeris opacitas, aliquoties diuinæ maiestatis velum, Gen. 15.17. Exo. 19.9. & 20.21. & 24.16. Psal. 18. 10. & 97.2. Caligo, i. miseria & graui s calamitas, vel externa, vel interna, Pro.
units.tr: CALIGO (darkness), used metaphorically for the most wretched condition of living: 2 Pet. 2:4. "Caligo tenebrarum" (the darkness of gloom) for the thickest darkness, by a Hebraism: 2 Pet. 2:17; Jude v. 13. Caligo, that is, the opacity of the air, is sometimes a veil of divine majesty: Gen. 15:17; Exod. 19:9; 20:21; 24:16; Ps. 18:10; 97:2. Caligo, that is, misery and grave calamity, either external or internal: Prov.

units.la: 15. Act.13 11 Iudæ.6.] V. Tenebræ.
units.tr: Acts 13:11; Jude 6. See TENEBRAE.

units.la: CALIX iræ,furoris, Esaiæ 51.17. Ierem.25.15. Psalm.60.5. & 75.9. Apocal.16.19. Vide POCVLVM. Calix pro morte & cruce Matth. 20. ver. 22.23. Marc.10.v.38.39.& 14.36. Luc.22.42 Ioan.18 11. pro pœna, Psalm.11.6.& 75.v.8.9. Threm,4. 21. Ezech.23.v.31 32.33. Apocal.14.10.& 16.19. Calix mysticus benedictionis tum extra sacramenti consideration tum in Cœna Domini, Pf.16.5. & 23.5.1. Cor. 10. & 11. cap. Calicis nomen in S. Cœna, duplici metonymia vurpatur. Priore pro vino ꝙ continet: posteriore, pro sanguine, cui symbolū est, ac tessera, Luc.22,20.1. Cor. 10.16.21.& 11.25.
units.tr: CALIX (cup) of wrath and fury: Isa. 51:17; Jer. 25:15; Ps. 60:5; 75:9; Rev. 16:19. See POCULUM. A cup for death and the cross: Matt. 20:22, 23; Mark 10:38, 39; 14:36; Luke 22:42; John 18:11. For punishment: Ps. 11:6; 75:8, 9; Lam. 4:21; Ezek. 23:31-33; Rev. 14:10; 16:19. The mystical cup of blessing, both apart from consideration of the sacrament and in the Lord's Supper: Ps. 16:5; 23:5; 1 Cor. 10 and 11. The name "cup" in the Holy Supper is used by a double metonymy: the former for the wine it contains, the latter for the blood, to which it is a symbol and token: Luke 22:20; 1 Cor. 10:16, 21; 11:25.

units.la: CALVARIA, locus vbi crucifixus est Christus, Matt.27.33. Marc. 15.22. Luc.23 33. Ioan.19.17.
units.tr: CALVARY, the place where Christ was crucified: Matt. 27:33; Mark 15:22; Luke 23:33; John 19:17.

units.la: CALVITIVM : Caluitij pro mortuis accersiti vsus Iudæ prohibitus, Deut.14.1. quare, v,2. Caluitium, signum tristitiæ & doloris gentibus, Esaiæ 15 2. Caluus Elizæus:2, Reg. 2.23.
units.tr: BALDNESS: Baldness made for the dead was forbidden to the Jews, Deut. 14:1; why, v. 2. Baldness was a sign of sadness and grief among the nations: Isa. 15:2. Bald Elisha: 2 Kings 2:23.

units.la: CALVMNIA, διαβολή, est culpæ & peccati alicuius attributio falsò à nobis facta proximo, qua tamen caret, vt ipse aliis puteat, illiusque existimatio apud bonos viros imminuatur.
units.tr: CALUMNY (διαβολή) is the false attribution by us to a neighbour of some fault or sin which he in fact lacks, so that he is thought of by others in a certain way and his reputation among good men is diminished.

units.la: CALVMNIA vitanda est, vt quæ à Deo damnetur, Exodi 20. 16. Leuit.19.16. Deut.5.20. Psal.15.3. Luc.3.14. Calumniæ exempla. Vide ACCVSATIO falsa.
units.tr: Calumny is to be avoided, as it is condemned by God: Exod. 20:16; Lev. 19:16; Deut. 5:20; Ps. 15:3; Luke 3:14. Examples of calumny: see ACCUSATIO falsa.

units.la: CALVMNIATORES damnantur, 2. Tim.3.3. occasio illis amputanda, 2.Cor.11.12.1.Petr.2.12. sancta conuersatione vincendi, 3.16.
units.tr: Calumniators are condemned: 2 Tim. 3:3. Occasion is to be cut off from them: 2 Cor. 11:12; 1 Pet. 2:12. They are to be overcome by holy conduct: 3:16.

units.la: CAMOS, Vide CHAMOS.
units.tr: CAMOS: See CHAMOS.

units.la: CAMELVS, Camelum non comedebant Iudæi, Leuit. 11.4. Deut. 14,7. Camelus, Matth.19.24. Marci 10.25. Luc.18.25. secundum Theophylactum, pro fune Ancorario: secundum Caninum autem & alios quosdam, pro ipso animali, illamque locutionem esse proverbialem, qua sermonis absurditate emphasis notetur. Iobo ter mille: Iob.1.3.
units.tr: CAMEL: Jews did not eat the camel: Lev. 11:4; Deut. 14:7. Camel: Matt. 19:24; Mark 10:25; Luke 18:25. According to Theophylact it means a ship's anchor rope; according to Caninius and some others, the animal itself, and the expression is proverbial, marking emphasis through the absurdity of the saying. Job (had) three thousand (camels): Job 1:3.

units.la: CANA, ciuitas Galilææ, Ioan. 2. 1. ibi Christus aquam in vinum mutat, v.7.9. Vnde oriundus erat Nathanael: Ioh. 21. 2. vbi cuiusdam regij filius à Christo absente sanatur. Ioh. 4. 46. &c. Est etiam Cana maior ciuitas in tribu Asher prope Sidon & Tyr: Iosf.19.28. Vnde mulier chanaæa, cuius fides à Christo magna prædicatur: Matth.15.22. &c.
units.tr: CANA, a city of Galilee: John 2:1. There Christ changes water into wine: vv. 7, 9. Nathanael was from there: John 21:2. There a royal official's son is healed by Christ while he is absent: John 4:46, etc. There is also Cana, a larger city in the tribe of Asher near Sidon and Tyre: Josh. 19:28. Whence came the Canaanite woman, whose great faith is praised by Christ: Matt. 15:22, etc.

units.la: [illegible, ~12 letters]V.Chanaan,
units.tr: See CHANAAN.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] NDACE, nomen commune omnibus reginis Æthiopum, Act.8.27.
units.tr: CANDACE, a common name for all the queens of the Ethiopians: Acts 8:27.

units.la: [illegible, ~4 letters] ANDELABRA, Eximij doctores & serui Dei, Apoc.11.4.]
units.tr: CANDELABRA: Eminent teachers and servants of God: Rev. 11:4.

units.la: [illegible, ~4 letters] NDELABRVM: Candelabri Mosaici situs & forma, Exod.25.v.31 36.37 & 37.v.17.18.19,& 40.24. Num.8.4. Candelabra aurea decem fabricantur,2.Paral.4.7. Candelabri aurei visio,Zach.4 2. Candelabrorum aureorum septem visio, Apoc.1.12. eorundem mysterij explicatio,v.20.
units.tr: CANDELABRUM: The position and form of the Mosaic candelabrum: Exod. 25:31-37; 37:17-19; 40:24; Num. 8:4. Ten golden candelabra are made: 2 Chr. 4:7. Vision of a golden candelabrum: Zech. 4:2. Vision of seven golden candelabra: Rev. 1:12; explanation of their mystery: v. 20.

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters] NIS precium Domino non offerendum, Deut.23 18.[Canis pro persecutore, Ps.22.17.21 pro mercenario & impuro seipsum pascente, Esa.56.10.11.]Canes sanguinem Achab linxerunt, 1.Reg.22 38. Comedunt corpus Iezabelis, 2.Reg.9.v.10.35.36. Canam se vocat Azael coram Elisæo, 2.Reg.8.13. Canem mortuum se vocat Dauid coram Saule, 1.Sam.24 15.Canes vocantur gentes à Christo,Matt.15.26. Canes vocantur contemptores verbi Dei, Matt.7.6.2.Pet.2.22. Apoc.22 15.Canes Pseudoapostoli,Phil.3 2.
units.tr: CANIS (dog): A dog's price is not to be offered to the Lord: Deut. 23:18. A dog stands for a persecutor: Ps. 22:17, 21; for a hireling who feeds himself impurely: Isa. 56:10, 11. Dogs licked up Ahab's blood: 1 Kings 22:38. They ate Jezebel's body: 2 Kings 9:10, 35, 36. Hazael calls himself a dog before Elisha: 2 Kings 8:13. David calls himself a dead dog before Saul: 1 Sam. 24:15. The Gentiles are called dogs by Christ: Matt. 15:26. Despisers of the word of God are called dogs: Matt. 7:6; 2 Pet. 2:22; Rev. 22:15. False apostles are dogs: Phil. 3:2.

units.la: NOPVS idolum.Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: CANOPUS, an idol. See the catalogue of idols.

units.la: NTICVM nouum, Apoc.5.9.&14.3. Canticum Mosis, Exod.15.v.1.2.3.alterum eiusdem,Deut.32.v.1.2.3. Deborae & Barac,Iudic.5.v.1.2. Dauidis pro liberatione ab hostibus, 2.Sam.22.v.1.2 3.4. Esaiae, Esa.5.2. Mariae virginis,Luc.1.v.46.47.48.Zachariae,Luc.1.v.68. Angelorum,2.13, Esa.6.3. Apoc.4.8. Simeonis, Luc. 2.v.28.29.30 31.32. Cantica spiritualia piis canenda,Ps.119.v.54 171. Eph.5.19. Coloss.3.16. Annae matris Samuelis,1.Sam.2.1.&c.
units.tr: CANTICUM (song), new: Rev. 5:9; 14:3. The song of Moses: Exod. 15:1-3; another of the same: Deut. 32:1-3. Of Deborah and Barak: Judg. 5:1, 2. Of David for deliverance from enemies: 2 Sam. 22:1-4. Of Isaiah: Isa. 5:2. Of Mary the virgin: Luke 1:46-48. Of Zechariah: Luke 1:68. Of the angels: Luke 2:13; Isa. 6:3; Rev. 4:8. Of Simeon: Luke 2:28-32. Spiritual songs to be sung by the pious: Ps. 119:54, 171; Eph. 5:19; Col. 3:16. Of Hannah, mother of Samuel: 1 Sam. 2:1, etc.

units.tr: CAPERNAUM (1. a pleasant village, or village of consolation), a city of Galilee in which Jesus began to preach: Matt. 4:17; Luke 4:31. units.tr: CAPILLI (hairs): All the hairs of believers are preserved by God: Matt. 10:30; Luke 21:18. The hairs of Absalom and their weight: 2 Sam. 14:26. Cor.13.12. Carnalia bona pro temporalibus, 1.Cor.9.11. [Carneus,1.imbecillis, 2. Paral.38. Hexilis item & docilis, Ezech.11 19. & 36.26.
units.tr: A carnal man, Rom. 7.14; 1 Cor. 3.1. [Carnal: soft and fleshy, as opposed to stony, 2 Cor. 3.3.] A carnal tunic, Judg. 5.23. [Carnal: (1) secular and temporary, Eph. 6.5; Col. 3.21.] "Carnal" is used of those who are in the flesh, [(1) not yet spiritually regenerate], and so cannot please God, Rom. 8.5, 8; and of those who are indeed in the Spirit but are still as yet [νεόφυτοι] and like tender infants, 1 Cor. 3.1. The Apostle explains this in the same place by the word "infants," and sets out what it is to be carnal: namely, to be subject to the weakness of human judgment. This indeed befalls in some measure even those who are otherwise spiritual, since we all know in part, 1 Cor. 13.12. Carnal goods are temporal goods, 1 Cor. 9.11. [Fleshy: (1) weak, 2 Chr. 38; likewise pliable and teachable, Ezek. 11.19; 36.26.]
