units.tr: DISCIPLES of Christ, who: see DISCIPLES OF CHRIST. Disciples of Christ baptize, John 4.2. Seventy-two disciples are sent out, Luke 10.1. The disciples of Christ make progress little by little.

units.la: Matt.13.36. Marc.7.17. Luc.9.45. Ioan.2.v.19.22.& 12.16. 13.v.7.33.36.& 16.v.12.17. Act.10.v.34.35.& 11.16. Discipulorum dispersio, Act.8 1. Discipulorum Christi praerogatiua. Matth.11.11. & 13.v.11.16.17. Discipulorum Christi itupi Matt.17.17. Vide APOSTOLI.
units.tr: Matt. 13.36; Mark 7.17; Luke 9.45; John 2.19, 22; 12.16; 13.7, 33, 36; 16.12, 17; Acts 10.34, 35; 11.16. The dispersion of the disciples, Acts 8.1. The prerogative of Christ's disciples, Matt. 11.11; 13.11, 16, 17. The dullness of Christ's disciples, Matt. 17.17. See APOSTLES.

units.la: DISCORDIA, Est animorum sententiae & orationis in re qua consentire plures debuerunt, dissensus a charitate Christiana dissidens.
units.tr: DISCORD is a dissent of minds and opinions about a matter on which several ought to agree; a dissension at odds with Christian charity.

units.la: DISCORDIA vitanda, Prou. 6.19.& 15.18.& 16.28 & 17.15. 18.6.& 30.10. Matth.12.24. Luc.11.17. 1. Cor.14.33. 2. Cor. 20. Gal.5.v.15 20.2. Tim.2.23. Discordiae, dissensionis, & earum exempla: Cain & Abel, Gen.4.8. Pastores Abrahae Loth,13.7. Reges Chanaan,14.4 Sodomitani contra Lot 19.9. Pastores Gerarae & Isaac,26.20. Esau aduersus Iacob,27.41. Iacobus aduersus Labanem, 31.36. Simeon Leui aduersus Hemor & Sichem, Gen.34.25. duo Hebraei Exod.2.13. Congregatio aduersus Mosen & Aaronem,16. Mosen,17.3. Num.21.v.4.5. Abimelech & fratres, Iudic. Tribus Ephraim aduersus Iephthe, 12. v. 1.3. Israelitae Beniamitae, 20.13. Saul in Dauid, 1. Sam.18.8.9. 2.Sam. Absalom in Dauidem patrem suum, 2. Sam.15.10. Israelis in Dauidem Regem, 19 41. duae Mulieres, 1.Reg.3.22. Ieroboam & Israelitae, 12.16. Discipuli Christi, Luc.22.24. Iudaei, Iohan.6.52.& 10.19. Turba, Ioh.7.43. inter Pharisaeos & populum,9.16. Ierusalem ciuitas, Act.11.2. multitudo quidam ex Iudaeis,15.2. inter Paulum & Barnabam, v. Ephesij,19.28. Asiatici Iudaei & Ierusalem, 21.30. Pharisaei & Sadducaei,23.7. inter Corinthios, 1.Cor.1.v.11.12.& 3.4. & 11.18. Discordiae & contentiones Euangelij occasione excitandae praedicuntur, Matth.10.35. Marc.3.12. Luc. v.49.51.
units.tr: DISCORD to be avoided, Prov. 6.19; 15.18; 16.28; 17.15; 18.6; 30.10; Matt. 12.24; Luke 11.17; 1 Cor. 14.33; 2 Cor. 12.20; Gal. 5.15, 20; 2 Tim. 2.23. Discords, dissensions, and their examples: Cain and Abel, Gen. 4.8. The herdsmen of Abram and Lot, 13.7. The kings of Canaan, 14.4. The men of Sodom against Lot, 19.9. The herdsmen of Gerar and Isaac, 26.20. Esau against Jacob, 27.41. Jacob against Laban, 31.36. Simeon and Levi against Hamor and Shechem, Gen. 34.25. Two Hebrews, Exod. 2.13. The congregation against Moses and Aaron, 16; Moses, 17.3; Num. 21.4, 5. Abimelech and his brothers, Judg. 9. The tribe of Ephraim against Jephthah, 12.1, 3. The Israelites and the Benjamites, 20.13. Saul against David, 1 Sam. 18.8, 9; 2 Sam. Absalom against his father David, 2 Sam. 15.10. The Israelites against King David, 19.41. Two women, 1 Kings 3.22. Jeroboam and the Israelites, 12.16. The disciples of Christ, Luke 22.24. The Jews, John 6.52 and 10.19. The crowd, John 7.43; between the Pharisees and the people, 9.16. The city of Jerusalem, Acts 11.2. A certain multitude of the Jews, 15.2; between Paul and Barnabas, v. The Ephesians, 19.28. The Asian Jews and Jerusalem, 21.30. The Pharisees and Sadducees, 23.7. Among the Corinthians, 1 Cor. 1.11, 12; 3.4; 11.18. Discords and contentions are foretold as to be stirred up on account of the Gospel: Matt. 10.35; Mark 3.12; Luke 12.49, 51.

units.la: DISCRETIO, Est examen & disquisitio diligens inter duorum alterum reipsa tale est, quale nobis apparet: aliarum falsam tantum illius, quod esse creditur imaginem speciem externam prae se fert & gerit. Esa.5.20. Deuter. 15.&c.
units.tr: Discernment is a careful examination and investigation of two things, to see whether one is really what it appears to us to be. The other only bears and displays an outward likeness of what is believed to be its image. Isa. 5:20; Deut. 15, etc.

units.la: DISCRETIO Christianis omnibus necessaria, Hebr.5.14. Ioan.2.20. V.1. Cor.12.10.1. Thess.5.22. Iob.34.3.
units.tr: Discernment is necessary for all Christians. Heb. 5:14; John 2:20; 1 Cor. 12:10; 1 Thess. 5:22; Job 34:3.

units.la: DISPENSATORIS iniqui factum iniquum non laudauit. Interfamilias, Luc.16.8. sed prudentiam eius duntaxat approbauit, qui sibi voluerit in futurum prospicere. V. Luc.12. &c.1. Cor.4.1.2. Tit.1.7.1. Pet.4.10. Gen.43.16.1.Reg.18. Dis ISPERSIO fidelium & eius vtilitas, Act.8.1.4.& 11.v.19.20. Dispersis Israeliticis scribunt Apostoli, Iac.1.1.1.Pet.1.1.sic capitur hoc vocabulum, Ioan.7.35. ISCRIMEN rerum temporalium & spiritualium, 2. Cor.4. 18. Discrimen electorum. Vide ELECTI. Discrimen Gentium & Iudaeorum, Vide IVDAEI. ISPVTATIONES quae vitandae, 1.Tim.6.v.4.5. 2.Tim.2.23. Tit.3.9. Disputationum imitandarum exempla: Quidam de Synagogis, Act.6.9. Paulus, 9.22.& 17.17.& 18. v.4.19.& 19.v.8. 9.& 20.7.& 24.25. Iudaei, 28.29. Disputatio, disceptatio in corde, Iob 21.4. Eccl.3.11. ISSIDIVM, Est apertum ab eo, a quo nos laesos putamus, dimittendum ne iam cum eo simus, & vllo modo communicemus & versemur. Iohan.7.45. V.Schisma. ISSIDIVM inter cognatos Euangelii causa, Vide DIVI- SIO. ISSIMVLANDVM nonnunquam, Prouerb. 12. 16. & 17.9. & 29.11. Dissimulationum exempla: Loth, Genes.19.16. Ioseph 42. 9. Saul, 1.Sam.10.27.& 28.8. Dauid, 21.v.10.11.12.13. Psal.38. v.14. Ioab, 2.Sam.18.16. vxor Ieroboam, 1.Reg.14.4. Aman, Esth. 5.v.9.10. Iob, Iob.3.26. Ezechias, Esa.36.21. Ieremias, Ier.38.27. IVINITAS Christi. Vide CHRISTVS Deus.
units.tr: The unjust deed of the dishonest steward the Lord did not praise (Luke 16:8), but only approved his prudence, in that he provided for the future. See Luke 12, etc.; 1 Cor. 4:1–2; Titus 1:7; 1 Pet. 4:10; Gen. 43:16; 1 Kings 18. The dispersion of the faithful and its usefulness: Acts 8:1, 4; 11:19–20. The apostles write to the dispersed Israelites: James 1:1; 1 Pet. 1:1. This word is used in this way in John 7:35. The peril of temporal and spiritual things: 2 Cor. 4:18. The peril of the elect: see ELECT. The distinction between Gentiles and Jews: see JEWS. Disputes to be avoided: 1 Tim. 6:4–5; 2 Tim. 2:23; Titus 3:9. Examples of disputations to be imitated: some from the synagogues (Acts 6:9); Paul (Acts 9:22; 17:17; 18:4, 19; 19:8–9; 20:7; 24:25); the Jews (Acts 28:29). Disputation and debate in the heart: Job 21:4; Eccl. 3:11. Separation (issidium): this is a open withdrawal from the one by whom we think we have been wronged, so that we are no longer with him and have no fellowship or dealings with him in any way (John 7:45). See SCHISM. Separation among kinsfolk for the sake of the Gospel: see DIVISION. Dissimulation, which is sometimes necessary (Prov. 12:16; 17:9; 29:11). Examples of dissimulation: Lot (Gen. 19:16); Joseph (Gen. 42:9); Saul (1 Sam. 10:27; 28:8); David (1 Sam. 21:10–13; Ps. 38:14); Joab (2 Sam. 18:16); the wife of Jeroboam (1 Kings 14:4); Haman (Esth. 5:9–10); Job (Job 3:26); Hezekiah (Isa. 36:21); Jeremiah (Jer. 38:27). The divinity of Christ: see CHRIST, God.

units.la: IVES: non in Deo, id est, qui non apud Deum, vel Dei respectu est dives, Luc.12.21. vbi iubemur thesaurizare, v.33. (Matth.6.20.) in coelis, ac proinde ab vnica Dei prouidentia pendere, qua de re 1.Tim.6. v.17.18. Dives non honorandus ob rerum caducarum opulentiam, Iac.2.v.2.3. Dituitis luxuriantis historia, Luc.16.19. Diuitis persona non consideranda, Leuit.19.15. Diuitis & pauperis collatio, Prouerb.28.6. eorum discrimen, 18.23. Diuites quomodo se gerere debeant, Iac.1.10. vanis tentationibus obnoxij, 1.Tim.6.9. difficulter seruabuntur, Matt.19.v.23.24. Marc.10.v.24. Luc.18.24.25. Diuites pij a Regno Dei non excludendi, 1.Cor.1.26.1.Tim.2.v.1.2.3.4.& 6.17. Diuites huius mundi, infelices ac vani, Iob.27.v.16.19. Psal.49.v.11.18. Eccl.5.v.9 10. Luc.6.24. Iac.1.10.& 5.1. Diuites mali reprehendendi, Mich. 6 12. Diuitibus in hoc seculo: hoc est, rerum ad hanc vitam pertinentium, copia locupletatis quid faciendum, 1.Tim. moth. 6.17. &c. Diuitum crudelitas, Iac.2.6. praesumtio, Prouerb. 21. 7. & 28. 11. Diuitibus cauendum maxime ne Dei obliuiscantur, Deut.6.12. Prouerb.30.8,9. Dives & pauper obuiant sibi inuicem,22.2.
units.tr: RICH, not in God: that is, one who is not rich before God or in relation to God (Luke 12:21), where we are commanded to lay up treasure (v. 33; Matt. 6:20) in heaven. Accordingly, he depends on the one providence of God alone; on this matter see 1 Tim. 6:17–18. The rich man is not to be honoured for the wealth of perishable things (James 2:2–3). History of the luxurious rich man (Luke 16:19). The person of the rich man is not to be regarded (Lev. 19:15). Comparison of rich and poor (Prov. 28:6); their difference (Prov. 18:23). How the rich ought to conduct themselves (James 1:10). The rich are exposed to vain temptations (1 Tim. 6:9); they will be saved with difficulty (Matt. 19:23–24; Mark 10:24; Luke 18:24–25). The godly rich are not to be excluded from the kingdom of God (1 Cor. 1:26; 1 Tim. 2:1–4; 6:17). The rich of this world are unhappy and vain (Job 27:16–19; Ps. 49:11, 18; Eccl. 5:9–10; Luke 6:24; James 1:10; 5:1). The wicked rich are to be rebuked (Mic. 6:12). What is to be done with the rich in this age, that is, those made wealthy by an abundance of things pertaining to this life (1 Tim. 6:17, etc.). The cruelty of the rich (James 2:6); their presumption (Prov. 21:7; 28:11). The rich above all must take care not to forget God (Deut. 6:12; Prov. 30:8–9). The rich man and the poor man meet one another (Prov. 22:2).

units.la: DIVITIAE, pro immensa copia, abundantia, aut magnitudine, Rom.2.4.& 9.23.& 11.33.1.Cor.1.5.pro cognitione evangelii in vitam æternam, Rom. 11.12.Diuitiæ non noxiæ, Matt.13.22.Marc.4.19. Luc.8.14.1.Tim.6.9. Exempla, Adolescens quidam, Matt.19.22. Marc.10.22. Diues quidam, Lucæ 18.23.Diuitiæ hominum in manu Dei, Gen.31.9.Prou.22.2.Diuitiæ spirituales, Rom.8.23.1.Cor.1.5.2.Cor.6.10.& 9.11. Eph.1.v.7.18.& 2.7. Col.1.27.& 2.3.1.Tim.6.18.Iacob 2.5.Diuitiæ fidelium, 1.Tim.6.6.Diuitiæ impiorum inutiles, Iob.20.15. Prou.10.2.& 11.4.& 15.16. 17.16.Ezech.7.19.Mich.6.10.alio transferentur, Iob 21.Diuitiæ malæ sunt, Amos 3.10. & possessoribus noxiæ, Sophoniæ 1.18. Diuitiarum spes fallax, Psal.49.v.7.18.& 52.9.& 62.11.& Ezech.7.19.1.Timoth.6.17. Diuitiis non fidendum, Matt.19.23. Diuitiis & Deo simul seruire nemo potest, Matt.6.24.
units.tr: RICHES, for an immense supply, abundance or greatness (Rom. 2:4; 9:23; 11:33; 1 Cor. 1:5); for the knowledge of the gospel leading to eternal life (Rom. 11:12). Riches are not harmful (Matt. 13:22; Mark 4:19; Luke 8:14; 1 Tim. 6:9). Examples: a certain young man (Matt. 19:22; Mark 10:22); a certain rich man (Luke 18:23). The riches of men are in the hand of God (Gen. 31:9; Prov. 22:2). Spiritual riches (Rom. 8:23; 1 Cor. 1:5; 2 Cor. 6:10; 9:11; Eph. 1:7, 18; 2:7; Col. 1:27; 2:3; 1 Tim. 6:18; James 2:5). The riches of the faithful (1 Tim. 6:6). The riches of the wicked are useless (Job 20:15; Prov. 10:2; 11:4; 15:16; 17:16; Ezek. 7:19; Mic. 6:10); they will be transferred to another (Job 21). Riches are evil (Amos 3:10) and harmful to their possessors (Zeph. 1:18). The hope of riches is deceptive (Ps. 49:7, 18; 52:9; 62:11; Ezek. 7:19; 1 Tim. 6:17). One must not trust in riches (Matt. 19:23). No one can serve God and riches at the same time (Matt. 6:24).

units.la: Diuitias etiam boni possident: Bonorum diuitias possessorum exempla: Abraham, Gen.13.2.Abraham & Loth, Isaac,26.13. Laban,30.v.40.43.Iacob,32.10.&c. Esau, 36. Ioseph,41.52.Filii Ruben & Gad,Num.32.1.Booz, Ruth 2. 1.Vir quispiam,1.Sam.25.2.Berzellai,2.Sam.19.32.Saul 1.Reg.16.14.Sunamitis mulier,2.Reg.4.8. Naaman, 5. Iosaphat, 2.Par.17.5. Ezechias,32.27. Assuerus, Esth.1.1. Iob.1.3.& 42.12.Rex,Matt.18.23. Adolescens,19.22.Ioseph Arimathæus, 27.57. multi diuites, Marc.12.42.quidam diuites,Luc.12.16.& 16.19.Zachæus,19.2.
units.tr: The good also possess riches. Examples of good men who possessed riches: Abraham (Gen. 13:2); Abraham and Lot; Isaac (Gen. 26:13); Laban (Gen. 30:40, 43); Jacob (Gen. 32:10, etc.); Esau (Gen. 36); Joseph (Gen. 41:52); the sons of Reuben and Gad (Num. 32:1); Boaz (Ruth 2:1); a certain man (1 Sam. 25:2); Barzillai (2 Sam. 19:32); Saul (1 Sam. 16:14); the Shunammite woman (2 Kings 4:8); Naaman (2 Kings 5); Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 17:5); Hezekiah (2 Chron. 32:27); Ahasuerus (Esth. 1:1); Job (Job 1:3; 42:12); a king (Matt. 18:23); the young man (Matt. 19:22); Joseph of Arimathea (Matt. 27:57); many rich men (Mark 12:42); certain rich men (Luke 12:16; 16:19); Zacchaeus (Luke 19:2).

units.la: DIVINI Ægyptiaci somnia Pharaonis interpretari nequeunt, Gen.41.8. Nabuchodonosoris itidem somnium diuinare non possunt, Dan.4.4.Diuini non consulendi, Leuit. 19.31.& 20.6. Deut.18.11.Esa.8.19.Diuini morte digni, Leuit. 20.27.Diuini consuluntur.Exemplum:Rex Babyl, Ezech.21.26. Diuinis Israelitæ credunt, 2.Reg.17.17. Diuinorum dicta irrita facit Deus, Esai.44.25. Diuini à bonis Reges sublati,1.Sam.28.3.2.Reg.23.24. Diuinos de reducendis arca consulunt Philistæi, 1.Sam.6.2. Vide INCANTATIONES,& Astrologia.
units.tr: DIVINERS: the Egyptian diviners could not interpret Pharaoh's dreams (Gen. 41:8); likewise they could not divine the dream of Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 4:4). Diviners are not to be consulted (Lev. 19:31; 20:6; Deut. 18:11; Isa. 8:19). Diviners are worthy of death (Lev. 20:27). Diviners are consulted. Example: the king of Babylon (Ezek. 21:26). The Israelites believed diviners (2 Kings 17:17). God makes the words of diviners void (Isa. 44:25). Diviners were removed by good kings (1 Sam. 28:3; 2 Kings 23:24). The Philistines consulted diviners about returning the ark (1 Sam. 6:2). See ENCHANTMENTS and Astrology.

units.la: DIVISIO maris rubri, Exod. 14.21. Diuisio inter cognatos evangelii causa,Matth.10.v.34.35.36.37. Luc.14.26. Elias pallio diuisit aquas,2.Reg.2.8.
units.tr: DIVISION of the Red Sea (Exod. 14:21). Division among kinsfolk for the sake of the gospel (Matt. 10:34–37; Luke 14:26). Elijah divided the waters with his mantle (2 Kings 2:8).

units.la: DIVORTIUM inter virum & mulierem non temere fiat, Matth.5.32.& 19.7.&c, 1.Cor.7.v.10.13. Vide Coniugium.
units.tr: DIVORCE between a man and a woman should not be undertaken rashly (Matt. 5:32; 19:7, etc.; 1 Cor. 7:10–13). See Marriage.

units.la: UGIUM,Deut.24.1.&c. V.Libellus repudij.
units.tr: DIVORCE (?) Deut. 24:1, etc. See Bill of divorce.

units.la: DOCERE: Docendi dexteritas a Deo, Esa. 50.4. Docendum Dei verbum, Matth.28.19. Vide Dei verbum.
units.tr: TO TEACH: the skill of teaching comes from God (Isa. 50:4). The Word of God is to be taught (Matt. 28:19). See the Word of God.

units.la: DOCILITAS,Est superbiae frenatio, per quam ita animum regimus, ne admiratione propriae sapientiae aliorum iudicia contemnamus, sed vt alios placide audiamus, & veris argumentis conuicti cedamus. Huic aduersatur pertinacia in erroribus, abundantia in proprio sensu, & temeraria praesumptio scientiae.
units.tr: DOCILITY is the taming of pride, by which we so govern our mind that, through admiration for our own wisdom, we do not despise the judgments of others, but gladly hear others and yield when we are convinced by true arguments. Stubbornness in errors, excessive attachment to one's own opinion, and rash presumption of knowledge are opposed to this.

units.la: DOCILITAS*, & omnis in religionis negocio praeiudiciorum eiectio necessaria est, Ioann. 1.47. Docilitas Dei donum est,Deut.29.4.1.Reg.3.9.Esa.50.4.Ier.24.7. Ezech. 11.19.& 6.26.Lucae 21.15.1.Thess. 2.13. Docilitas in Pastoribus necessaria,2.Tim.2.24.25.
units.tr: DOCILITY, and the casting out of all prejudice in the business of religion, is necessary (John 1:47). Docility is God's gift (Deut. 29:4; 1 Kings 3:9; Isa. 50:4; Jer. 24:7; Ezek. 11:19; 36:26; Luke 21:15; 1 Thess. 2:13). Docility is necessary in ministers (2 Tim. 2:24–25).

units.la: Docilitatis exempla: Populus Israeliticus, Nehem.8.v.4.5. multitudo, Luc.8.4.&21.38.Act.2.v.6.8. 16. 17. Thessalonienses, 1.Thess.2.13.
units.tr: Examples of docility: the people of Israel (Neh. 8:4–5); the crowd (Luke 8:4; 21:38; Acts 2:6, 8, 16–17); the Thessalonians (1 Thess. 2:13).

units.la: DOCTORES in Ecclesia a Deo constituti, Roman.12. v.7.1.Corin.12.28.Ephes.4.11.1.Petr.4.11. Doctores qui admittendi, Matth.5.19. Doctores in Antiochia insignes, Act.13.1. Doctores falsi ambitiosi,2.Petr.2.10. cauendi, Luc.6.39. Doctores falsi in Ecclesiam irrupturi,1.Timoth.4.1.2. Petr.1.2.3.
units.tr: TEACHERS appointed by God in the Church (Rom. 12:7; 1 Cor. 12:28; Eph. 4:11; 1 Pet. 4:11). Teachers who are to be admitted (Matt. 5:19). Distinguished teachers at Antioch (Acts 13:1). Ambitious false teachers (2 Pet. 2:10) are to be guarded against (Luke 6:39). False teachers who are about to break into the Church (1 Tim. 4:1–2; 1 Pet. 1:2–3).

units.la: DOCTRINA, pro actu docendi, Marci 4.2.&12.38. Doctrina sana semper in Ecclesia vigere debet, Genesis 48.21. Exodi 12.24. Deut. 11. 19. Eccles. 12.11. Esa.59.21. Zachar.1.5. &c.1.Tim.4.13.2.Timot.4.2. Tit.2. 1.2. Petr.1. 15. Doctrina generalis ex particulari, 1. Cor.5.7.&6 7.1.Tim.2.8.&5.8. Hebr.5.4.&10.v.24.30. 1.Petr. 2.19. & 3.v.7.15.1.Ioann.4.4. Particularis ex generali, Col.1.21.1. Thess.4.3.2.Petr.2.10.1. Ioan.2.13. Doctrina Apostolorum & Prophetarum Ecclesiae fundamentum, Ephes. 2. 20. Doctrina Christi, Vide CHRISTVS.
units.tr: DOCTRINE, for the act of teaching (Mark 4:2; 12:38). Sound <hi>doctrine</hi> must always flourish in the Church (Gen. 48:21; Exod. 12:24; Deut. 11:19; Eccl. 12:11; Isa. 59:21; Zech. 1:5, etc.; 1 Tim. 4:13; 2 Tim. 4:2; Titus 2:1–2; 1 Pet. 1:15). <hi>General</hi> doctrine from the particular (1 Cor. 5:7; 6:7; 1 Tim. 2:8; 5:8; Heb. 5:4; 10:24, 30; 1 Pet. 2:19; 3:7, 15; 1 John 4:4). <hi>Particular</hi> doctrine from the general (Col. 1:21; 1 Thess. 4:3; 2 Pet. 2:10; 1 John 2:13). The doctrine of the apostles and prophets is the foundation of the Church (Eph. 2:20). Doctrine of Christ: see CHRIST.

units.la: Doctrina Dei perspicua,Esaiae 45.19.& 48.16.Doctrina & veritas in Rationali iudicio,Exodi 28.30. Doctrinae Evangelicae certitudo, Ioannis 19 35.Galat.1.8. Ephes.4. vers.13. 14.2.Timoth.3.14.Hebr.13.9.1. Ioann.4.14. Doctrina mala cauenda,Matthaei 16 6.Ioan.10.8.Gal.5.8.Philip.3.2. Hebr. 13.9.Doctrinae sane contemptus noxius, Prou.1.7.& 17.16. & 23.9.2. Timoth.4.3. Doctrinae rectum iudicium manat ex timore Dei,Ioann.7.17. Doctrinae puritas in Ecclesia necessaria , Esaiae 30. v. 20. 21. Doctrinae Evangelicae sum[?]
units.tr: The plain doctrine of God (Isa. 45:19; 48:16). Doctrine and truth in the rational judgment (Exod. 28:30). The certainty of <hi>evangelical</hi> doctrine (John 19:35; Gal. 1:8; Eph. 4:13–14; 2 Tim. 3:14; Heb. 13:9; 1 John 4:14). <hi>Bad</hi> doctrine is to be guarded against (Matt. 16:6; John 10:8; Gal. 5:8; Phil. 3:2; Heb. 13:9). The contempt of <hi>sound</hi> doctrine is harmful (Prov. 1:7; 17:16; 23:9; 2 Tim. 4:3). The right judgment of doctrine flows from the fear of God (John 7:17). The <hi>purity</hi> of doctrine is necessary in the Church (Isa. 30:20–21). <hi>Evangelical</hi> doctrine sum[?]

units.la: Actor.40.21. Doctrinæ quæ homines à Christo abducunt, pestiferæ, Ioannis 10.8. Doctrinæ impiæ quàm efficax est, Thessa.2.9.2.Tim.2.13.Tit.1.11.Heb.13.9.
units.tr: Acts 40:21. Doctrines which draw men away from Christ are deadly (John 10:8). How effective impious doctrine is (2 Thess. 2:9; 2 Tim. 2:13; Titus 1:11; Heb. 13:9).

units.la: ¶ Doctrinam Apostolorum scriptam & non scriptam firmiter tenendam esse, vt traditiones, quas vocant, ... dere nobis possint Pontifici probare conantur, sed ... ex Rom.16.17.Gal.1.v.8.11.2.Thess.2.15. 1.Corint.11. atqui sciendum est, non scriptæ, quam ipsi iactitant ... strinæ Lydium lapidem esse scriptam doctrinam.
units.tr: That the doctrine of the apostles, written and unwritten, is to be firmly held; as for the so-called traditions ... which the Papists try to prove can be ... from Rom. 16:17; Gal. 1:8, 11; 2 Thess. 2:15; 1 Cor. 11. But it must be understood that the unwritten doctrine, which they themselves boast of ..., is the Lydian touchstone of written doctrine.

units.la: TRADITIONES.
units.tr: TRADITIONS.

units.la: DOEG (.i.solicitus) Idumæus Dauidem prodit. 1.Sam.22.18. Sacerdotes Saulis mandato occidit, v.18. Iudicium ... eum: Psal.52.
units.tr: DOEG (that is, anxious), the Edomite, betrays David. 1 Sam. 22.18. At Saul's command he kills the priests, v.18. Judgment ... him: Psalm 52.

units.la: DOLOR: Doloris exempla: Eua, Gen.3.16. Isaac, 24.67. Sicut ... 34.25. Israelitæ, Exodi 3.v.7.8. Anna Elcanæ ... Sam.1.v.15.16. Vxor Phinees,4.19. Dauid,2.Sam.1.26. 1.2. Mater Iabes,1.Paral.4.9. Ala,2.Paral.16.12. Filiusmitidis,2.Reg.4.20. Iob, Iob 2.13.&7.5.&10.20.&30.v.16.17. Dauid,Psal.13.3.&18.5.&31.v.10.11.&356.&94.19. Esaias,Esa.21.3. Messias,53.3. Baruch,Ier.43. Damascus,49.24. Ieremias,Thren.5.v.15.16.17. Iob. Maria,Luc.2.48. Paulus,Roman.9.2. Dolores mortis pro mors dolorum corporis & cruciatus animi plenis 2.24. Psal.18.5.
units.tr: Examples of grief: Eve, Gen. 3.16. Isaac, 24.67. Like ... 34.25. The Israelites, Exod. 3.7-8. Hannah, wife of Elkanah, 1 Sam. 1.15-16. The wife of Phinehas, 4.19. David, 2 Sam. 1.26; 1.2. The mother of Jabez, 1 Chron. 4.9. Asa, 2 Chron. 16.12. The son of the Shunammite woman, 2 Kings 4.20. Job, Job 2.13; 7.5; 10.20; 30.16-17. David, Ps. 13.3; 18.5; 31.10-11; 35.6; 94.19. Isaiah, Isa. 21.3. The Messiah, 53.3. Baruch, Jer. 43. Damascus, 49.24. Jeremiah, Lam. 5.15-17. Job. Mary, Luke 2.48. Paul, Rom. 9.2. "Pains of death" is put for the deadly pains of the body and the torment of the mind: Acts 2.24. Ps. 18.5.

units.la: DOLVS, Fraus: Dolus malus (est enim etiam bonus dolus vt Iurisconsulti aiunt, cùm aliud agitur, aliud simulatur, aut dissimulatur in damnum & perniciem alterius, sua priuetur.
units.tr: DOLUS, Fraud: malicious deceit. (For there is also a good deceit, as the jurists say, when one thing is done and another is pretended or dissembled, to the loss and ruin of another, who is deprived of his own.)

units.la: Prohibetur, Leu.25.14. Sophon.3.13. Quàm sit effraudulentus Deum nosse recusat: Ier.9.6. male parat fruitur: Pro.12.27. Non dimidiat dies suos: Psal.55.23. animum: Marc.7.22. Deo abominationi est: Psal.5.6. Eius alius fruetur: Pro.28.10. V.technas fraudulentorum tionis diuinæ minas: Ier.9.6. 1.Thess.4.6. Remedium 32.2.&Psal.15. Ioh.1.48. Luc.19.8. Eph.4.28.
units.tr: Forbidden: Lev. 25.14. Zeph. 3.13. How deceitful it is: he refuses to know God, Jer. 9.6. He prepares badly and does not enjoy: Prov. 12.27. He does not halve his days: Ps. 55.23. ... Mark 7.22. It is an abomination to God: Ps. 5.6. Another will enjoy his: Prov. 28.10. ... the divine threats: Jer. 9.6; 1 Thess. 4.6. Remedy: 32.2 and Ps. 15. John 1.48. Luke 19.8. Eph. 4.28.

units.la: DOLVS, Ieremi.9.6. Psal.35.20. Pro.1.17. Marci 7.22. Act. natur, Rom.1.29. 1.Thess.4.6. 1.Pet.2.1. Doli exempla: Iacob, Gen.34.14. Abner,2.Sam.3.27. impij & hostes ... Psal.27.3.&35.20.&36.3.&38.13.&57.5. Doeg Idumaeus, 52.v.3.4. populus Iudaicus, Ier.9.8. Principes Sacerdotum & Seniores, Matt.26.4. Insidiatores Christi, Luc.2. lymas Magus, Act.13.10. (Vide FRAVS,&Astutia.)
units.tr: DOLUS (deceit): Jer. 9.6. Ps. 35.20. Prov. 1.17. Mark 7.22. Acts ... nature: Rom. 1.29. 1 Thess. 4.6. 1 Pet. 2.1. Examples of deceit: Jacob, Gen. 34.14. Abner, 2 Sam. 3.27. The wicked and enemies ... Ps. 27.3; 35.20; 36.3; 38.13; 57.5. Doeg the Idumaean, Ps. 52.3-4. The Jewish people, Jer. 9.8. The chief priests and elders, Matt. 26.4. The plotters against Christ, Luke 2. Elymas the magician, Acts 13.10. (See FRAUD and CUNNING.)

units.la: OMESTICI Dei, fideles, Ephes.2 19. Domestici hominis inimici eius, Matth. 10. 36. Domesticorum habenda ratio, 1.Timoth.5.8. Exemplum: Dauid, Psalm.101. v 2.6. Domestici fidei Gal.6 10. vocantur, qui per fidem sunt in eadem atque nos familia Domini. Vide Prouerb. 31. 15. 21.& 1. Cor.16 19.
units.tr: DOMESTICS of God: the faithful, Eph. 2.19. A man's domestics are his enemies, Matt. 10.36. The care of one's household, 1 Tim. 5.8. Example: David, Ps. 101.2, 6. The domestics of the faith, Gal. 6.10, are those who through faith are in the same family of the Lord as we are. See Prov. 31.15, 21; 1 Cor. 16.19.

units.la: DOMINATVS, pro Senatorum aut aliorum quorumuis Magistratuum, & in eminentia quapiam constitutorum, collegio,2,Pet.2.10. Iudæ.8.
units.tr: DOMINATION is put for the college of senators or of any other magistrates set in some eminence: 2 Pet. 2.10. Jude 8.

units.la: DOMINVS reipsa vnus est,1.Cor.8:6.Ephes 4.5. Domini per similitudinem multi sunt,1.Cor.8.5. Dominis duobus, id est, inter se repugnantibus, seruire nemo potest,Mat.6.24. Dominorum & Dominarum erga seruos & ancillas officium & potestas,Exo.21.v.2 20.26.Leuit.19.13. & 25. 39. Deut.5. v.14.21.& 15 v.12.16 & 24.15. Iob.31 13. Prou.29 19. Eccl.7. 20 & 33.31.& 42.5.Eph.6.9.Col.4.1.
units.tr: LORD: in reality there is one, 1 Cor. 8.6; Eph. 4.5. Lords by likeness are many, 1 Cor. 8.5. No one can serve two lords, that is, lords who are at odds with one another, Matt. 6.24. The duty and power of masters and mistresses towards male and female servants: Exod. 21.2, 20, 26; Lev. 19.13 and 25.39; Deut. 5.14, 21; 15.12, 16; 24.15; Job 31.13; Prov. 29.19; Eccl. 7.20; 33.31; 42.5; Eph. 6.9; Col. 4.1.

units.la: DOMINVS Iehoua,Iehoua Elohim,Adonai:Iehoua essentiā, Elohim personas,Adonai dominationem respicit.]
units.tr: LORD Jehovah, Jehovah Elohim, Adonai: Jehovah regards the essence, Elohim the persons, Adonai the dominion.

units.la: [Dominus, Pater, Filius,Spiritus Sanctus, frequentissimè nomine Iehouæ, nonnunquam Elohim apud vulgatum interpretem, rarius Adonai, sæpissimè dominus Deus, i.Iehoua Elohim, exprimitur. Dominus in N. T. κύριος appellatur.
units.tr: [Lord, Father, Son, Holy Spirit, is most often expressed by the name Jehovah, sometimes by Elohim in the Vulgate translator, more rarely by Adonai, and very often by "Lord God," that is, Jehovah Elohim. Lord in the New Testament is called kyrios [κύριος].]

units.la: De personis in Deo, Dominus etiam dicitur: Dominus Pater,Psalm.2.v.2.7.& 110.v.1.4.Prou.8.22. Matth.11.25. & 21.40.Luc.1.32. & 4. 18. Act. 3.22.& 4.26.Hebr.7.21.Apoc. 11.15. Dominus,Pater & Filius,Gen.1.2.Iudic.3 10. Esai.40. 13.Ezech.11.5.Act.5.9. 2. Cor.3.17. Dominus, Filius Dei Patris,Gen.16.13.& 18.1.&c. Iof.5.14: Iudic.6.24,Psalm.2.12, & 102.26.& 110.1.Esai.6.1.& 40.3.Ier.23 6.Malac.4.5.In N. T.(excenta testimonia occurrunt, quæ Filium Dei Dominum appellant.
units.tr: Concerning the persons in God, Lord is also said: Lord the Father, Ps. 2.2, 7; 110.1, 4; Prov. 8.22; Matt. 11.25; 21.40; Luke 1.32; 4.18; Acts 3.22; 4.26; Heb. 7.21; Rev. 11.15. Lord, Father and Son, Gen. 1.2; Judg. 3.10; Isa. 40.13; Ezek. 11.5; Acts 5.9; 2 Cor. 3.17. Lord, Son of God the Father, Gen. 16.13; 18.1, etc.; Josh. 5.14; Judg. 6.24; Ps. 2.12; 102.26; 110.1; Isa. 6.1; 40.3; Jer. 23.6; Mal. 4.5. In the New Testament innumerable testimonies occur which call the Son of God Lord.

units.la: Dominus,Spiritus S.1.Cor.12.4.5. 2.Cor.3.18. 2.Thess. 3.5. Vide Exo.17.2.Deut.32. 12. Cum quibus confer Esai. 63. v. 10.14.Item confer Psal.95.7.& Heb.3 7.&c. Deinde Esai.9. & Act.28.25. Tertiò,Esai.54.13 & Ioann.14.40.& 16.3.Denique Ier.31,31.Hebr.10.15.& Deut.9.24.Act.7.52.& Ezec. 3.16.Item Apoc.20.28.
units.tr: Lord, Holy Spirit: 1 Cor. 12.4-5; 2 Cor. 3.18; 2 Thess. 3.5. See Exod. 17.2; Deut. 32.12. With these compare Isa. 63.10, 14. Likewise compare Ps. 95.7 and Heb. 3.7, etc. Then Isa. 9 and Acts 28.25. Thirdly, Isa. 54.13 and John 14.40 and 16.3. Finally, Jer. 31.31; Heb. 10.15; Deut. 9.24; Acts 7.52; Ezek. 3.16. Likewise Apoc. 20.28.

units.la: Dominus, qui iure summo re quapiam potitur & qua frui liberè potest,Matth.12.6. Marc.2.28.Luc.6.5.Dominus,Domini, Angelus,Angeli, Gen.19.v.2 8. Act.10.4.Apocal.7. 14.Dominus,de homine,hero, marito.primis &cæt. dicitur: & frequenter occurrit.
units.tr: Lord is one who by supreme right possesses some thing and can freely enjoy it: Matt. 12.6; Mark 2.28; Luke 6.5. Lord, lords: of an angel, angels, Gen. 19.2, 8; Acts 10.4; Rev. 7.14. Lord is said of a man, a master, a husband, and so on, and it occurs frequently.

units.la: Domus discalceati, Deut. 25 10. Domus leprosa mundanda, quomodo, Leu. 14. 36. Domus Regia in Ierusalem incerta, tur, Ier. 52 13. Domus pro iis qui in eadem domo versantur, synecdoche, Matt. 10.12. pro hospitio, 9.28. Domus appellatio interdum eos etiam comprehendit, qui vel cognationem attingebat eiusdem familiae ciues, vel ex illorum fratribus oriundi, vt apparet ex Luc. 1. 27. Domus Israel, id est gens Israelitica, Matth. 15.24. Super domos proclamarentur Apostoli Euangelium, Matt. 10.27. id est, in ipsis tectis, populo circonstanti, ac praetereunti: ita erant fabricata aedium summa, vt in illis ambulare & sari possent, vt liquet ex Deut. 22.8. 2. Sam. 11.2. Act. 10. Domus super petram aedificata firma manebit, Psalm. 118. Matt. 7.24. & 16.18. Luc. 6.48. Rom. 8.35. Domus terrestris & caelestis, 2. Cor. 5.1.2. Pet. 1.14. Domus vendita, & eius lex vit. 25.25. Domus custos, mulier, 1. Tim. 5.13. Tit. 2.5. ita mo docenda mulier, 1. Cor. 14.35.
units.tr: The house of the unshod man, Deut. 25.10. The leprous house to be cleansed, how, Lev. 14.36. The royal house in Jerusalem is uncertain, Jer. 52.13. House for those who dwell in the same house, a synecdoche, Matt. 10.12; for lodging, 9.28. The name house sometimes also comprehends those who were of the same family, citizens, or descended from their brothers, as appears from Luke 1.27. The house of Israel, that is, the Israelite nation, Matt. 15.24. "Upon the housetops the apostles were to proclaim the Gospel," Matt. 10.27, that is, on the very roofs, to the people standing around and passing by; the tops of the buildings were made so that they could walk and rest on them, as is clear from Deut. 22.8; 2 Sam. 11.2; Acts 10. A house built upon the rock will remain firm: Ps. 118; Matt. 7.24; 16.18; Luke 6.48; Rom. 8.35. An earthly and a heavenly house: 2 Cor. 5.1-2; 2 Pet. 1.14. A house sold, and its law: Lev. 25.25. The keeper of the house is a woman: 1 Tim. 5.13; Titus 2.5. Thus the woman is to be taught: 1 Cor. 14.35.

units.la: [Domus significat 1. Aedes pauperum, diuitum, pro pum 2. familiam & quaecunque sunt in domo. 3. Popu- lus, vt domus Israel populum Israeliticum indicat. 4. Tribus & partem populi, vt Domus Aaron, pro tribu Leui ca. 5. Varia loca. Secundo Domus nomine mortale corpus intelligitur, Iob 14.19. Eccles. 12.3. 2. Corinth. 5.1. & 2. chrum, Eccles. 12. 7. Tertio, Scriptura domum Dei fre- quenter profert in medium: quo nomine significatur ille gratiosam & peculiarem Dei praesentiam indicans. Tabernaculum. 3. Templum Hierosolymitanum. 4. Ecclesiam, primum ex Iudaeis, deinde ex Iudaeis & Gentibus constitutam. 5. Coelum beatorum, Ioann. 14.2. 2. Cor. 5. Quarto, domus mysticae meminit Salomon, Cant. 1.1. 4. & 8. v. 2. 16.]
units.tr: [House signifies: 1. The dwellings of the poor and of the rich. 2. The family and whatever is in the house. 3. A people: as the house of Israel indicates the Israelite people. 4. A tribe and part of a people: as the house of Aaron stands for the tribe of Levi. 5. Various places. Secondly, by the name house the mortal body is understood: Job 14.19; Eccl. 12.3; 2 Cor. 5.1; and Eccl. 12.7. Thirdly, Scripture often brings forward the house of God: by this name is signified that gracious and peculiar presence of God. 1. The tabernacle. 2. The Temple of Jerusalem. 3. The Church, first formed from the Jews, then from Jews and Gentiles. 4. The heaven of the blessed: John 14.2; 2 Cor. 5. Fourthly, Solomon mentions the mystical house: Cant. 1.1, 4; 8.2, 16.]

units.la: Domus spiritualis aedificatio: 1. Petr. 2.5. Hebr. 3. v. 5. 6. Terrestris, Psalm. 127. 1. Prou. 24.27. iniuste domus corruit, Hier. 22. 13. Prouerb. 14. 11. Eccles. 21. 9. 2. Ideo modo domus sit regenda: Prou. 15.6. & 27.23. Eccl. 34. V. Pro. 31.10.
units.tr: The spiritual house is a building: 1 Pet. 2.5; Heb. 3.5-6. The earthly house: Ps. 127.1; Prov. 24.27. The house of the unjust falls: Jer. 22.13; Prov. 14.11; Eccl. 21.9. 2. Therefore, how a house is to be ruled: Prov. 15.6; 27.23; Eccl. 34; Prov. 31.10.

units.la: DONA Dei. Vide Dei dona. Donorum Dei abusus, eiusque exempla: Agar, Gen. 16. v. 3.4.5.6. Esau, 25. v. 31.32. Hebr.
units.tr: GIFTS of God. See Gifts of God. Examples of the abuse of God's gifts: Hagar, Gen. 16.3-6. Esau, Gen. 25.31-32. Heb. 12.

units.la: Vide CONTEMTVS, & ABVSVS.
units.tr: See CONTEMPT and ABUSE.

units.la: DONORVM oblatorum exempla: Seruus Abraham, Gen. 24. 53. Populus Israeliticus ad fabricationem Tabernaculi. ixo.36.v.5.6.Dauid,1.Sam.30.26. Assuerus, Esth.2. 18. Co-nati Iob,Iob.42.11. Christus,Luc.7.21.Pilatus Marc.15.45. Sidd Mvnervm oblatorum exempla.
units.tr: Examples of offered gifts: Abraham's servant, Gen. 24.53. The Israelite people for the making of the Tabernacle, Exod. 36.5-6. David, 1 Sam. 30.26. Ahasuerus, Esth. 2.18. The comforters of Job, Job 42.11. Christ, Luke 7.21. Pilate, Mark 15.45.

units.la: ONEC particula,interdum ita refertur ad tempus praecedens,vt de sequenti non affirmetur contrarium: quod satis indicant vel postrema Euangelij Matthaei verba, Matth. 28.20. Ex quibus verbis non potes colligere Christum nobiscum non futurum post consummationem seculi. Talia sunt & illa,Gen.28.15.Psal.57.1.& 110.1.2.Sam.6.23.Matt.1.25. & 5.26.Donec reddideris,&c.Matt.5.26.prouerbialiter dicitur de eo,qui cum summo iure agitur.
units.tr: UNTIL is a particle which sometimes refers to a preceding time in such a way that the contrary is not affirmed of what follows. The last words of Matthew's Gospel sufficiently show this: Matt. 28.20. From these words you cannot conclude that Christ will not be with us after the consummation of the age. Such are also Gen. 28.15; Ps. 57.1; 110.1-2; 2 Sam. 6.23; Matt. 1.25; 5.26. "Until you have paid," etc., Matt. 5.26, is proverbially said of one who is dealt with by the strictest law.

units.la: ORCAS,Act.9.3.6.a mortuis excitata,Act.11. v.40. Vide Tabita, Ioppensis d scipula.
units.tr: DORCAS, Acts 9.36, raised from the dead, Acts 11.40. See Tabitha, the disciple of Joppa.

units.la: ORMIRE & exurgere, apud Hebraeos prouerbium, pro seurum esse,Psal.3.6.Marc.4.26. Dormire & obdormiscere, pro mori & reponi in sepulchro,quasi in lecto,Gen. 47.30. Deut.31.16.2.Sam.7.12.1.Reg.2.10. &c.Esa.14.v.8.18.Matth. 7.52.Luc.8.52.Ioann.11.11.Actor.13.36.1.Cor.11.30.& 15. 8.1.Thess.4.v.13.14. 2.Petr.3.4.vnde dormientes, pro mortuis,Daniel 12.2.]
units.tr: To sleep and to rise up: among the Hebrews a proverb, meaning to be secure, Ps. 3.6; Mark 4.26. To sleep and to fall asleep, meaning to die and be laid in the sepulchre as in a bed: Gen. 47.30; Deut. 31.16; 2 Sam. 7.12; 1 Kings 2.10, etc.; Isa. 14.8, 18; Matt. 27.52; Luke 8.52; John 11.11; Acts 13.36; 1 Cor. 11.30; 15.6; 1 Thess. 4.13-14; 2 Pet. 3.4. Hence "sleepers" for the dead: Dan. 12.2.

units.la: DORMIRE,est peccati caligine premi,Rom.13 11.12.13. Eph. 5.14.1.Thess.5.v.6 7.]
units.tr: To sleep is to be pressed down by the darkness of sin: Rom. 13.11-13; Eph. 5.14; 1 Thess. 5.6-7.

units.la: RACHMA, Numus est valens solidos Turonenses tres cum semisse,Didrachmum, Vide supra loco.Drachmae perditae similitudo,Luc.15.8.
units.tr: DRACHMA, a coin worth three and a half Tours solidi; the didrachm, see above in its place. A likeness of the lost drachma: Luke 15.8.

units.la: RACO,idolum Babyloniorum. Vide Idolorum catalogus.
units.tr: DRAGON, an idol of the Babylonians. See the Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: Draco vincitur a Michaele,Apoc.12.7.
units.tr: The dragon is conquered by Michael: Rev. 12.7.

units.tr: DRAGON, a tyrant: Ps. 74.13-14; Isa. 51.9; Ezek. 29.3; 32.2. Dragon, a whale: Ps. 104.26. Dragon, Satan: Rev. 12.3, etc.; 13.1, 4, 11; 16.13; 20.2. The dragon is a wild beast of the fields, of the serpent kind, which feeds on the wind: Jer. 14.6.

units.la: RVSILLA, Felicis Praefecti vxor, audit doctrinam Euangelij a Paulo,Act.24.24.25. (Gr.i,rote conspersa.)
units.tr: DRUSILLA, wife of the governor Felix, hears the doctrine of the Gospel from Paul: Acts 24.24-25. (In the Greek, "sprinkled with dew.")

units.la: DVBITARE debere nos de remissione peccatorum, gratia Dei & vita aeterna,probare nituntur Pontificij ex Exo. 32. 30.Iof.14.12.1.Sam.14.36.Ioel.2.14.Ioan.3.9.Soph.2.1.Dan. 4.24. Amos 5.15 Act.8.22.2.Tim.2.25. Vide Certos non esse,&c.&,Fotte,& Desperatio.
units.tr: That we ought to doubt about the remission of sins, the grace of God and eternal life: the Papists try to prove this from Exod. 32.30; Josh. 14.12; 1 Sam. 14.36; Joel 2.14; John 3.9; Zeph. 2.1; Dan. 4.24; Amos 5.15; Acts 8.22; 2 Tim. 2.25. See "That they are not certain," etc., and "Chance," and "Despair."

units.la: DVBITATIO, De gratia Dei,est neque assentiri firmiter verbo Dei,ac in hoc promissioni gratiae, neque omnino repugnare, sed fluctuare nunc in vnam, nunc in alteram partem languidè inclinare,Eph.4.14, lege locum. Iacob.1.6.
units.tr: DOUBT concerning the grace of God is neither to assent firmly to the Word of God and to the promise of grace in it, nor altogether to resist, but to waver now to one side, now to the other, leaning feebly. Eph. 4.14; read the passage. James 1.6.

units.la: Iudæ.v.12.Heb 2.
units.tr: Jude v.12. Heb. 2.

units.la: DVBITATIO tollenda, Hebr.12.v.12.13. Vide Perseuerentia,
units.tr: DOUBT to be removed: Heb. 12.12-13. See Perseverance.

units.la: DVLEAE & latreæ, quam Pontificij constituunt, differentia ex Scripturæ sacræ autoritate tollitur, in qua frequenter hæc inter se commutantur, & vnum alteri substituitur simili dicendi genere, Matth. 4.10. Act.20.19. Rom.1.9.& 8.& 12.11.& 14.18.& 16.18. Eph.6.7. Phil.2.22. Col.3,24.
units.tr: The difference between dulia and latria, which the Papists establish, is removed by the authority of holy Scripture, in which these are frequently interchanged, and one is substituted for the other in the same manner of speaking: Matt. 4.10; Acts 20.19; Rom. 1.9; 8; 12.11; 14.18; 16.18; Eph. 6.7; Phil. 2.22; Col. 3.24.

units.la: LATREA.
units.tr: LATREA.

units.la: DVPLICITAS Deo exosa, Ezec.20.39. Iac.1.8. Apocal.3 v. 16. Purificate corda vos duplices animo: Iac.4.8.
units.tr: DOUBLE-MINDEDNESS is hateful to God: Ezek. 20.39. James 1.8. Rev. 3.16. Purify your hearts, you double-minded: James 4.8.

units.la: DVRITIES, Est sensus naturalis prorsus hebes, & nullum rum humanæ carni acerbarum gustum retinens: vel quiam callum propter assiduas afflictiones obduxerit, quòd naturâ sensus iudicio priuatus sit. Hic certe animque sensus nostri status minimè est probandus: sed plerunque ferus & inhumanus: vt Iob 6.12. apparet. Et qui patiter afflictiones ferunt, quâ eas non sentiunt: non patentes, sed stipites potiùs sunt & dicendi & censendi.
units.tr: HARDNESS. It is a natural sense that is wholly dull and keeps no taste of what is bitter to human flesh; or it is a sense that, because of constant afflictions, has had a callus grow over it, so that by nature it is deprived of its power of judgment. Certainly this state of our sense and mind is by no means to be approved; it is for the most part savage and inhuman, as Job 6.12 shows. And those who bear afflictions without feeling them are not to be called or judged patients, but rather blocks of wood.

units.la: DVRITIES: Duritiei sine obstinationis in malo exempla: Gen.4.13. Pharao Exo.5.2. Israelitæ, 32.v.7.8.9.10. Deu 27.1. Sam.8.v.19.20.2. Pa. 30.v.8.9. Filij Heli, 1. Sam. 23.24.25. Saul,15.v.29 30. Nabal,1.Sam.25 3. filij Saruiae Sam.3 39. Viri Iudæ, 2.Par.24.v.17.18.19.20.21. Iudæis ctor.7.v.51.52. Vide OBSTINATIONIS exempla.
units.tr: HARDNESS. Examples of hardness, or of obstinacy in evil: Gen. 4.13. Pharaoh, Exod. 5.2. The Israelites, Exod. 32.7–10. Deut. 27.1. 1 Sam. 8.19–20. 2 Par. 30.8–9. The sons of Eli, 1 Sam. 2.23–25. Saul, 1 Sam. 15.29–30. Nabal, 1 Sam. 25.3. The sons of Zeruiah, 2 Sam. 3.39. The men of Judah, 2 Par. 24.17–21. The Jews, Acts 7.51–52. See the examples under OBSTINACY.

units.la: Dux nostrer Deus, Vide DEVS Dux nostrer.
units.tr: God our Leader. See GOD, Our Leader.

units.la: DVCIBVS & Præsidibus parendum, 1. Petr. 2. 14. Rom. &c.
units.tr: Leaders and governors are to be obeyed: 1 Pet. 2.14; Rom., etc.

Act.14.12. Præfectus aulæ, 2. Paral. Legislator, Gubernator, Iudex, Genes.49.10.1. Petr. 2 Præfectus multis familiis, prouinciæ, vel regioni, Ge 20.& 36.15.&c. Primarius inter Ecclesiæ seruos, 1. Par. 20. Ierem.29.26. Qui alios in via salutis ducere & i tuere velle videtur, Matth. 15.14. & 23,ver.16 24. Ron 2.19. Primarius inter regni regísque consiliarios & ser Eith.1.14. & 9.3. Princeps Populi, Rex 1,Sam.9.16. 2. 5.2.2. Reg.20.5. Ezech.21.30. Summus Dux, 2. Par 13.2.]
units.tr: Leader, head of a family or tribe: Num. 7.30; 10. A commander in war: Gen. 26.26. A companion or comrade: Ps. 55.14. A great ruler: Isa. 13.2; 32.8. A husband: Prov. 2.17. The Messiah: Dan. 9.15. A spokesman: Acts 14.12. A prefect of the court: 2 Par. A lawgiver, governor, judge: Gen. 49.10; 1 Pet. 2. A prefect over many families, a province or a region: Gen. 20; 36.15, etc. The chief among the servants of the Church: 1 Par. 20; Jer. 29.26. One who seems to want to lead and guide others in the way of salvation: Matt. 15.14; 23.16, 24; Rom. 2.19. The chief among the councillors and officers of the kingdom and of the king: Esth. 1.14; 9.3. A prince of the people: 1 Sam. 9.16; 2 Sam. 5.2; 2 Kings 20.5; Ezek. 21.30. The supreme leader: 2 Par. 13.2.

units.la: DYSENTERIA, est intestinorum exulceratio cũ inflãmat & excretione sanguinolenta, ventrem magnis doloribus orminibusque exercens, Act.28.8.
units.tr: DYSENTERY is an ulceration of the intestines with inflammation and a bloody discharge, afflicting the belly with great pains and cramps: Acts 28.8.

units.tr: E

units.la: EBRIETAS, μέθη, est effectus vinolentiæ & crapulæ, quia est tum Ligamen ipsum rationis (vt aiunt) ex nimia & immoderata vini sumptione & bibtione contingens: tum nimia ipsa vini cuiuslibet assumptio. Vide Inebriari.
units.tr: DRUNKENNESS, μέθη [methē], is the effect of wine-drinking and of excess, since it is either the very loss of reason (as they say) arising from excessive and immoderate taking and drinking of wine, or the excessive intake of any wine at all. See INEBRIATE.

units.la: EBRIETAS damnatur, Deut. 21.20. Prouerb. 20.1. & 31.4. Eccles. 10.16. Esaiæ 5. verf. 11.22. & 28.1. Luc. 21.34. Roman. 13.13. 1. Corinth. 6.10. Galat. 5.21. Ephes. 5.18. 1 Thessal. 5.8. 1. Tim. 3.3. Tit. 1.7. & 2.3. 1. Pet. 4.3. Ebrietatis incommodA, Genes. 19.32. 1. Reg. 16.9. Prouerb. 21.17. & 23.30. & 31. 1. Cor. 6.10. Iram Dei provocat, Esa 5. v. 11. 13. & 28.1. Dan. 2. Ioël. 1. v. 4.5. mentem alienat, Pro. 23.31. Eccles. 19.2. Esa. 28.7. Osee 4.11. ad libidinem incendit, Prou. 20.1. & 23.31. &c. Ephes. 5.18. facultates dissipat, Pro. 21.17. & 23.20,21. Eccles. 19.1. secreta detegit, Pro. 31.4. Abac. 2.15. ad furorem & ixas excitat, Prou. 20.1 & 23.29. Eccles. 31.40. Osee 7.5. Notet vt serpens: Prou. 23.31.32. Regno Dei excludit, 1. Cor. 6.10. Gal. 5.21
units.tr: Drunkenness is condemned: Deut. 21.20; Prov. 20.1; 31.4; Eccl. 10.16; Isa. 5.11, 22; 28.1; Luke 21.34; Rom. 13.13; 1 Cor. 6.10; Gal. 5.21; Eph. 5.18; 1 Thess. 5.8; 1 Tim. 3.3; Titus 1.7; 2.3; 1 Pet. 4.3. The evils of drunkenness: Gen. 19.32; 1 Kings 16.9; Prov. 21.17; 23.30; 31; 1 Cor. 6.10. It provokes the wrath of God: Isa. 5.11, 13; 28.1; Dan. 2; Joel 1.4–5. It alienates the mind: Prov. 23.31; Eccl. 19.2; Isa. 28.7; Hos. 4.11. It kindles lust: Prov. 20.1; 23.31, etc.; Eph. 5.18. It squanders goods: Prov. 21.17; 23.20–21; Eccl. 19.1. It discloses secrets: Prov. 31.4; Hab. 2.15. It stirs up rage and quarrels: Prov. 20.1; 23.29; Eccl. 31.40; Hos. 7.5. Note how it bites like a serpent: Prov. 23.31–32. It shuts out from the kingdom of God: 1 Cor. 6.10; Gal. 5.21.

units.la: Ebrietatis exempla, Noë, Genes. 9.21. Nabal, 1. Sam. 25.36. Benadad, 20.16. (Vide COMESSATIONIS exempla.) In ebrietate extinctorum exempla: Philisthæi, Iudic. 16. v. 25.30. Amnon, 2. Sam. 13.28. Ela, 1. Reg. 16.9. Balthasar, Dan. 5. v. 1 2. 3.4.30.
units.tr: Examples of drunkenness: Noah, Gen. 9.21. Nabal, 1 Sam. 25.36. Ben-hadad, 1 Kings 20.16. (See the examples under REVELRY.) Examples of those killed while drunk: the Philistines, Judg. 16.25, 30. Amnon, 2 Sam. 13.28. Elah, 1 Kings 16.9. Belshazzar, Dan. 5.1–4, 30.

units.la: [Ebrietas Spiritualis, Ier. 13.13. Ezech 23 33. & 39 19. Esai. 28. v. 1.3.]
units.tr: Spiritual drunkenness: Jer. 13.13; Ezek. 23.33; 39.19; Isa. 28.1, 3.

units.la: EBRIOSI fugiendi, Prou. 23 20. 1. Cor. 5 11.
units.tr: Drunkards are to be avoided: Prov. 23.20; 1 Cor. 5.11.

units.la: [Ebrius, ebria, ærumnis & afflictionibus oppressus. Esai. 51.21. Ier. 23.9. ebria sanguine, meretrix mystica, Apoc. 17.6.]
units.tr: Drunk, a woman drunk, oppressed by troubles and afflictions: Isa. 51.21; Jer. 23.9. Drunk with blood, the mystical harlot: Rev. 17.6.

units.tr: ERON, see HEBRON.

(vide Matth.5.14.) columna-rio,Esa. 60.8. columnæ, 1.Timoth.3.15. Vide, Eccl. est columna & stabilimentum veritatis. Septimò, pro natu Ecclesiastico,Matth.18.17.quia nimirum cogitur mine totius Ecclesiæ. Alibi vocatur à Paulo Presbyterium,seu collegium Seniorum, 1. Timoth.4.14. Obseruandum autem est,Ecclesiæ vocabulum vnico hoc saltem noui Testamenti loco (Matth.18.17.) de Iudæis dici, communi-ter alioquin generales cœtus peculiari nomine sortiuntur Synagogæ appellari: quamuis Græci interpretes idem vocabulum attribuant eorum congregationi,etiam in veteri Testamento,1.Paral.13. vers.2.9. Euangelista itaque Seniorum collegio, dixit Ecclesiam. Lucas autem Presbyterium populi,Luc.22.66. vide Mar.5.22. Octauò, pro uium conuentu,seu multitudine in Theatrum concurrente,Act.19.v.32.39.
units.tr: CHURCH: in Latin ecclesia, in Greek ἐκκλησία [ekklēsia]. First, for a material temple (as they call it): Deut. 23.1; Judg. 20.2; Ps. 68.27; Lam. 1.10; Joel 2.16; 1 Cor. 11.18; 14.34. Second, for the household of some family of believers: Rom. 16.5; 1 Cor. 16.19; Col. 4.15. Third, for the assembly of one province: 1 Kings 8.14; Acts 9.31; 11.26; 12.1; 13.1; 15.3; 19.32; 20.17; Rom. 16.11; 1 Cor. 1.2; 16.1–2; 2 Cor. 8.1; Gal. 1.2; 1 Thess. 1.1, etc.; 1 Pet. 5.13; Rev. 2.1, etc.; 3.1. Fourth, for some distinguished body of believers who share together in the Word and the sacraments: Acts 20.28; 1 Cor. 11.22; 14.4; Gal. 1.13. Fifth, for the assembly of the faithful: Num. 19.20; 20.4; 1 Sam. 17.47; 1 Kings 8.14, 55; 2 Par. 29.1, etc.; 2 Par. 1.5; Ps. 22.26; 26; 35.18; 107.32; 150.1; Matt. 16.18; Acts 5.11; 8.1; 4; Rom. 16.16, 23; 1 Cor. 6.5; 11.16; 12.28; 14.5; 2 Cor. 8.18, 23–24; 11.8; 12.13; Eph. 5.23; Phil. 4.15; Josh. 1.15; 1 Tim. 3.5, 15; Rev. 1.11; 22.16. Sixth, for the multitude of the faithful spread throughout the whole world, and then it is compared to a candlestick: Rev. 1.20; to a city: Eph. 2.19; Rev. 21.2 (see Matt. 5.14); to a dovecote: Isa. 60.8; to a pillar: 1 Tim. 3.15. Note: the Church is the pillar and support of the truth. Seventh, for an ecclesiastical body: Matt. 18.17, because it is clearly represented by the whole Church. Elsewhere Paul calls it the presbytery, or college of elders: 1 Tim. 4.14. It must be observed that the word ecclesia is used of the Jews in this one place of the New Testament only (Matt. 18.17); otherwise general assemblies commonly receive the particular name synagogue, although the Greek interpreters apply the same word to their congregation even in the Old Testament, 1 Par. 13.2, 9. The Evangelist therefore called the college of elders the Church, but Luke called it the presbytery of the people, Luke 22.66; see Mark 5.22. Eighth, for a crowd or multitude gathered in a theatre: Acts 19.32, 39.

units.tr: The Church is called the mystical body of Christ: Rom. 12.5; 1 Cor. 10.17; 12.27; Eph. 1.22–23; 4.4, 12; Col. 1.18, 24; 5.23. She is not contentious: 1 Cor. 11.16. She is the house of God: 1 Tim. 3.15; Heb. 3.3, 6; 1 Pet. 2.5; 4.17; Eph. 2.21; 1 Pet. 2.4–5, where there is an allusion to the structure of the Old Testament temple. So individual faithful people are called the temple of the Lord: 1 Cor. 3.16; 6.19; 2 Cor. 6.16. She is a minister of the gospel: Isa. 41.27. Spotless: Song 4.7; Eph. 5.27. Washed by Christ: Eph. 5.26; Titus 2.14. Mother of the pious: Isa. 54.13; 66.10; Gal. 4.26. She bears children with difficulty: Rev. 12.2. Precious to Christ: Acts 20.28; 1 Pet. 1.18. The fullness of Christ: Eph. 1.23. The bride of God: Ps. 45.11–12; Ezek. 16.8; Hos. 2.19–20; Matt. 6.15, 24; 2 Cor. 11.2; Eph. 5.32; Rev. 19.7; 21.2, 9. Beloved of God: Ps. 87.2–3. See also Song 2.2, etc. Subject to Christ: Eph. 5.24. Founded upon Christ: Isa. 28.16; Ps. 118.22; Matt. 16.18; 21.42; Luke 20.17; Acts 4.11; 1 Cor. 3.11. Endowed with the Holy Spirit: John 4.16. Exposed to various afflictions: Dan. 12.1; Zech. 14.5. She can never perish: Gen. 22.17; Matt. 16.18; Rom. 8.7. She is universal: Matt. 8.11; John 10.16; Gal. 4.26.

units.la: ECCLESIA, Columna & stabilimentum veritatis dicitur, 1. Tim. 3. 15. non simpliciter, sed hominum respectu: nam alisoquin ipsum hoc firmamentum lapide illo angulari nititur, Eph. 2. 20. Vide ECCLESIAE fundamentum Christus. Si quærat quis, quare hæc epitheta tribuantur Ecclesiæ? Quia videlicet non alibi habitat Dei veritas in mundo, nec alibi quàm penes Ecclesiam quærenda hominibus, eam inuenire cupientibus. Ecclesia enim est, quæ filios Dei gignit, & educat per verbi Dei prædicationem, & verè bonorum operum exempla. Alibi meræ tenebræ, mendacia, errores, imposturæ, superstitiones, vertiginis & stuporis spiritus, omnes denique corruptelæ omnia latè possident: ex quorum collatione intelligi demum potest, quid veritatis nomine significetur. Sunt autem multis modis inepti & impudentes, qui ex hoc loco ita amplificant Ecclesiæ auctoritatem, quasi veritatem ipsam gignat, ac instar primi fundamenti sustineat, cùm Ecclesia ipsa alio fundamento, id est, Christo nitatur, Ephe. 2. 20. nec procreatrix, sed retis sit duntaxat, altrix & conseruatrix veritatis inter homines: vt ipsa à Verbo, non autem Verbum ab ipsa pendeat.
units.tr: The Church is called "the pillar and ground of the truth," 1 Tim. 3.15; not absolutely, but with respect to men; for otherwise this very firmament rests upon that corner stone, Eph. 2.20. See: the foundation of the Church is Christ. If anyone asks why these epithets are attributed to the Church: it is because God's truth dwells nowhere else in the world, nor is it to be sought by men who want to find it anywhere but with the Church. For the Church is that which begets and brings up the sons of God through the preaching of God's Word and through true examples of good works. Elsewhere there are only pure darkness, lies, errors, impostures, superstitions, a spirit of giddiness and stupor, and finally all corruptions holding sway far and wide; from comparing these it can at last be understood what is meant by the name of truth. There are, however, many who are foolish and shameless in the ways they use this passage to magnify the authority of the Church, as if it begot the truth itself and bore it up like the first foundation, whereas the Church itself rests on another foundation, that is, Christ (Eph. 2.20). It is not the begetter of truth but only its receptacle, nurse and preserver among men, so that the Church depends on the Word, and not the Word on the Church.

units.la: Ecclesiæ corpus in duas partes quasi distribuit Apostolus, Col.1 20. Ephes.1.10, quibus in locis τῶν πάντων, id est, omnium nomine intelligendum est totum Ecclesiæ corpus (quod alibi 2. Cor.5.19. simili dicendi genere Mundus appellatur) quod postea in duas veluti partes dividitur: in quæ in cœlis, & ea quæ in terris sunt: per illa simplicissime intelliguntur fideles, ante Christi aduentum mortui: hæc verò, quos Christus viuos deprehendit, vel qui sint eius aduentum consecuti: quorum rursus duas species fecit Paulus, quæ tamen in vnum corpus coaluerunt, Iudæi nimirum & Gentes.
units.tr: The Apostle divides the body of the Church, as it were, into two parts: Col. 1. 20; Eph. 1. 10. In these places the phrase "of all things" [τῶν πάντων] must be understood to mean the whole body of the Church (which elsewhere, in 2 Cor. 5. 19, by a similar way of speaking, is called the world). This body is afterwards divided, as it were, into two parts: those who are in heaven and those who are on earth. By the former are simply understood the faithful who died before Christ's coming; by the latter, those whom Christ finds alive, or who attain to his coming. Paul made two kinds of these again, which nevertheless grew together into one body, namely Jews and Gentiles.

units.la: ECCLESIA coetus sacer, omnium Electorum Dei a condito mundo, usque ad diem nouissimum: quorum quamplurimi viuunt iam in coelis, alij in terris, alii nascituri sunt, qui e terris suo ordine in coelis recipientur. 2. Ecclesia significat coetum eorum, qui primum ante Christi in carne manifestationem, deinde sub Euangelio veram religionem professi sunt, profitentur & profitebuntur in praesenti vita. 3. Significat coetum aliquem numerosum, vel exiguum, hominum in aliqua regione, ciuitate, oppido, vico, familia, eandem veram religionem profitentium. 4. Ecclesiasticum Senatum, seu presbyterium: quia nimirum cogitur totius cuiusdam Ecclesiae particularis nomine, in qua presbyteri seu seniores conueniunt certo numero: Matthaei 18.17. 5. Coetus profanus seu conuentus ciuium, voce praeconis e reliqua turba, quasi nominatim ad comitia vocatus, &c. Psal.26.5.& 107.32. Actor.19.verf.32.& 40.]
units.tr: [The Church is a holy assembly of all the elect of God from the creation of the world until the last day: of whom very many now live in heaven, others on earth, and others are yet to be born, who will be received into heaven from the earth in their order. 2. Church signifies the assembly of those who first, before the manifestation of Christ in the flesh, and then under the Gospel, professed the true religion, profess it now, and will profess it in the present life. 3. It signifies any assembly, large or small, of men in some region, city, town, village, or family, professing the same true religion. 4. The ecclesiastical senate, or presbytery: because it is gathered in the name of some particular Church, in which the elders or seniors meet in a certain number: Matt. 18. 17. 5. A profane assembly, or gathering of citizens, called as it were by name by the herald's voice from the rest of the crowd, as to an assembly, etc.: Ps. 26. 5. & 107. 32. Acts 19. v. 32. & 40.]

units.la: ECCLESIAM errare non posse, vt quae sit veritatis firmamentum, 1.Tim.3.15. his locis probare conantur Pontificij, Esai.29.21. Matt.16.18.& 28.20. Luc.22.32. Ioan.14.16.& 16. & 17.v.11.20. 1.Tim.3.v.15.&c. 1.Ioan.2.27. eamque Christo, tanquam capiti, eiusque Vicario Pontifici Romano subiici debere, hisce testimoniis, Esai. 43.9. Iohann. 10.16.
units.tr: The Papists try to prove from these passages that the Church cannot err, as being the pillar and ground of truth: 1 Tim. 3. 15. Isa. 29. 21. Matt. 16. 18. & 28. 20. Luke 22. 32. John 14. 16. & 16. & 17. v. 11. 20. 1 Tim. 3. v. 15. etc. 1 John 2. 27. And they try to prove by these testimonies, Isa. 43. 9. John 10. 16, that it ought to be subject to Christ as its head, and to his Vicar, the Roman Pontiff.

units.la: 1. Cor.12.12. Eph.3.6. At quemadmodum lubenter & animo damus, Ecclesiam capiti suo Christo subiectam debere, vtpote à quo illa viuificum hauriat succum, Eph.5.23. ita constanter negamus, Pontificem Romanum Christi Vicarium esse, eique Ecclesiam subiici debere: vtpote pestilentissimum à Diabolo, omnis mendacij patre, hunc succum in membra sibi subiecta late diffundat & seminet. V. Iob.8.12. & 10.4.5. & 11.9.10.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 12. 12. Eph. 3. 6. But just as we gladly and readily grant that the Church ought to be subject to its head Christ, from whom it draws its life-giving sap (Eph. 5. 23), so we steadfastly deny that the Roman Pontiff is Christ's Vicar and that the Church ought to be subject to him: since he, most pestilential, from the Devil, the father of all lies, spreads and sows this sap widely into the members subject to him. See Job 8. 12. & 10. 4. 5. & 11. 9. 10.

units.la: ECCLESIASTICAE functiones, & earum genera ac ordines.
units.tr: ECCLESIASTICAL offices, and their kinds and orders.

units.tr: See DIACONIA.

units.la: ECCLESIASTICA iurisdictio paucissimis verbis explicatur à Paulo, 1. Cor. 5.4. &c. nempe quis sit huius ordinis administer & vindex, quibus sit haec autoritas commissa, quae sint obnoxij, de quibus causis ibi sit agendum, quomodo eo cendum hoc iudicium, quanta vis illius, & quis eius sit nempe Ecclesiae sordium purgatio, & ipsius peccantis: quae omnia in tyrannidem tum Episcopalem, Papisticam, sunt commutata. Vide EXCOMMVNICATIO.
units.tr: Church jurisdiction is explained in very few words by Paul, 1 Cor. 5.4 etc.: namely, who is the administrator and avenger of this order, to whom this authority has been committed, who are liable to it, what cases are to be heard there, how this judgment is to be conducted, what its force is, and what its purpose is, namely the purging of the filth of the Church and of the sinner himself. All of these have been turned into tyranny, both episcopal and Papist. See EXCOMMUNICATION.

units.tr: Good education: examples of the education and instruction of children. Noah, Gen. 9.23. Lot and his family, honourably brought up and endowed with good morals, and therefore delivered, Gen. 19.16; 37.10; 42.1, 2. Eli, 1 Sam. 2.22, 23. David, 1 Kings 1; 1 Chron. 28.9. Job, Job 1.4, 5. The parents of Jesus, Luke 2.41. To this belongs also the education of Moses, Acts 7.22; Timothy, 2 Tim. 1.5; 3.14, 15. That chosen lady to whom John addressed his Epistle, 2 John 4. EFFEMINATE men: 1 Kings 14.24; 15.12; 22.47; 2 Kings 23.7; Job 6.14; Prov. 18; Isa. 3.4; Hos. 4.14; 1 Cor. 6.9. The needy must be helped, Prov. 28.27. (See BENEFICENCE and ALMSGIVING.) James 2.15. Want consumes the transgressors of God's commandments, Deut. 6.20, 21, 22. Want is the wages of the sluggard. See SLOTH, NEGLIGENCE, IDLENESS. The disadvantages of want, Prov. 10.9. ELON, a city in the tribe of Judah, whose king was Debir, Josh. 10.3; it is besieged by Joshua, Josh. 10.34; taken, v. 35. ELON, king of Moab, subdues Israel, Judg. 3.14; is killed by Ehud, v. 21. EREDI: see INGREDI. THE DEPARTURE of the children of Israel from Egypt, Exod. 12.41. EHUD: see AHOD. ELAH, king of Israel, 1 Kings 16.6, 7, 8; is killed by Zimri his servant, v. 9, while he was drinking to drunkenness, ibid. The boasting of the Corinthians rebuked by Paul, 1 Cor. 4.7. ELAH, or Helam, son of Shem, Gen. 10.22, from whom the Persians sprang. Elam, the province of the Persians, who are also called Elamites, Gen. 14.1; Dan. 8.2; Isa. 11.11; Acts 2.9. ELKANAH, the Levite of Ephraim, father of Samuel, a bigamist, 1 Sam. 1.1, 2. Six others bear this name. ELDAD and Medad prophesy, Num. 11.26; Moses does not envy them, v. 29. ELEAZAR, "God is help," son of Aaron, Exod. 6.23; 28; he is put in his father's place, Num. 20.28; Deut. 10.6; he divides the land of Canaan with Joshua, Josh. 14.1, according to the command of the Lord, Num. 34.17. He is consecrated priest, Lev. 8.24 etc.; he dies and is buried, Josh. 24.33. He had a son called Phinehas, Exod. 6.25, who succeeds his dead father in the high priesthood, Num. 25.7, 11, 12, 13. ELEAZAR, son of Eliud, Matt. 1.15; son of Phinehas, Ezra 8.33; Phinehas the father, Judg. 20.25. ELEAZAR, one of David's mighty men, 2 Sam. 23.9.

units.la: ELECTIO hominum ad salutem æternam, Luc.10.20.Rom.8.29.& 9.11.Eph.1.4.2.Tim.2 19.1.Pet.1.v.2.&c.Firma est, stabilita,& inuariabilis,Rom.8.38 & 11.v.2.5.29.Eph.4.1.1.Tit.1.5.24.1.Ioan.2.19.& 3.9. dicuntur tamen excidere à gratia Galat.5.4. qui illius adipiscendi iter erant tantum ingressi, quod etiam reprobis contingit, cùm aliqui sint etiam in veram fidem gradus. dicitur item electio confirmari, 2 Pet.1.10.non in sese,quæ alioquin in sese firma est,nec vnquam labascere potest, cùm nitatur Dei propositò inuiolabili, in nobis nihilominus confirmanda est.Confirmatur autem ex effectis fidei,id est, Spiritus fructibus in nobis. Nam iustus est,qui facit iustitiam,& qui iustificatus est,idem vocatus est,cum iustificatio fit per fidem, fides ex auditu. Porrò vocatus est, electus est ex Dei propositò. Vndè vocatio & vocationis basis quomodo magis ac certius confirmetur: quamuis vno Dei proposito, certo & æterno fulciatur. Sed electio, quæ temporarias actiones spectat,non est inuariabilis, vt Saulì & Iudæ contigit.
units.tr: ELECTION of men to eternal salvation: Luke 10.20; Rom. 8.29; 9.11; Eph. 1.4; 2 Tim. 2.19; 1 Pet. 1.2 etc. It is firm, stable and unchangeable, Rom. 8.38; 11.2, 5, 29; Eph. 4.1; Titus 1.5; 2 Tim. 2.24; 1 John 2.19; 3.9. Yet they are said to fall away from grace, Gal. 5.4, those who had only entered upon the way of obtaining it; this also happens to the reprobate, since some have also attained a degree of true faith. Likewise election is said to be confirmed, 2 Pet. 1.10; not in itself, for in itself it is firm, and can never totter, since it rests on God's inviolable purpose; nevertheless it is to be confirmed in us. It is confirmed, however, from the effects of faith, that is, from the fruits of the Spirit in us. For he is righteous who does righteousness, and he who has been justified is also called, since justification comes through faith, and faith through hearing. Moreover, he is called and elected from God's purpose. Hence how the calling and the basis of the calling are confirmed more fully and more certainly, although it is supported by God's one purpose, certain and eternal. But election, which regards temporary actions, is not unchangeable, as happened to Saul and to Judas.

units.la: Electionis causæ omnes à Petro enumerantur,1.Pet.1.2. Efficiens summa causa, Dei Patris præscitum. Formalis causa efficax :nam tum demum re ipsa eligimur,cùm æternum suum decretum in nobis per vocationem perducimur. Finis duplex, subalternus, sanctificatio electorum, ultimus, gloria Dei, Eph.1.6. Materia,Christi obedientia. Vide has causas & Eph.1.v.3.4.vbi expressè legitur: Quos elegerit?nempe Deus.Quos elegerit? Nos.In quo?In Christo.Quando?Ante mundi constitutionem. Ad quid? Vt sint sancti, &c. verf.4. & ad laudem gloriosæ Dei gratiæ, verf.6. Quomodo, seu quo respectu elegerit? Gratuitò. mirum.
units.tr: All the causes of election are listed by Peter, 1 Pet. 1.2. The efficient and highest cause is the foreknowledge of God the Father. The formal cause is efficacious: for we are truly elected only when, through calling, his eternal decree is brought about in us. The end is twofold: the subordinate end is the sanctification of the elect; the ultimate end is the glory of God, Eph. 1.6. The matter is the obedience of Christ. See these causes also in Eph. 1.3, 4, where it is plainly read: Whom did he elect? Namely God. Whom did he elect? Us. In whom? In Christ. When? Before the foundation of the world. For what? That they should be holy, etc., v. 4; and to the praise of the glory of his grace, v. 6. How, or in what respect, did he elect? Freely. Wonderful!

units.tr: Election is founded on the good pleasure of God, Rom. 9.11; Eph. 1.9. The end is, Deut. 26.19; Eph. 1.4, 5, 6; 1 Pet. 1.2. It is free, not from works, Deut. 7.8; Rom. 2.11; 9.11; 11.5; Eph. 1.4; 2 Tim. 1.9; James 1.18; 2.5; 2 Pet. 1.10; 1 John 4.10. Whence the election of grace is called, by a Hebraism, free election, from the Greek, Rom. 11.5.

units.tr: ELECTION, by metonymy, for the elect themselves, Rom. 11.7. Election is the cause of good works, Eph. 1.4. Passages rashly twisted to deny particular election: Rom. 11.1.

units.tr: The elect alone are capable of divine wisdom, Matt. 11.25; 13.11. They are dear to God, Mal. 1.2; Zech. 2.8; Matt. 24.22; John 3.16; Rom. 5.8; 8.37. They are given to Christ by the Father, Isa. 8.18; John 6.37; 10.29; 17.6; 18.9. They are freed from the power of Satan, Eph. 2.2 etc. They are few, Matt. 20.16. See FAITHFUL. The elect alone are endowed with the Holy Spirit, John 14.17; they are chosen out of the world, John 15.19; 17.6; Gal. 1.4. They are vessels of honour, Rom. 9.21; 2 Tim. 2.21; of mercy, Rom. 9.23. They alone believe God, Isa. 53.1; 54.13; John 6.45; 10.26; Acts 13.48; Rom. 10.16; 2 Tim. 3.16, 17; Titus 1.1; 3.6; Heb. 8.11; 2 Pet. 1.3. They cannot perish, Matt. 24.24; Mark 13.22; Luke 19.9; John 6.37, 39; 10.28; 17.12; 18.9; 2 Thess. 2.13; 1 John 2.19; Rev. 13.8. They alone truly know God, John 17.6; they alone persevere, 1 John 2.19; they alone are to be saved, Rev. 21.27; they are drawn by the Father, John 6.44; their names are written in heaven, Luke 10.20; Phil. 4.3; Rev. 3.5; 20.15; 21.27. See BOOK OF LIFE. The number of the elect is known to God alone, 1 Kings 19.18; Rom. 11.3, 4; 2 Tim. 2.19. Their prerogative, Matt. 13.11.

units.la: LECTOS posse excidere à Dei gratia, & excutere Spiritum Sanctum, vt probent nonnulli, abuntur locis,1.Sam.16. 14.Psal.51.13.Luc.11.24.&c.Rom.11.v.20.21.22. 1.Cor.9.27.& 10.12.Philip.2.12. Gal.5.4.1.Tim.1.19.& 4.1.Heb.6.v.4.5.6. & 10.26.2.Thess.5.19.Eph.4 30.2.Pet.1.10. Vide ELECTIO. Electi, ne Spiritum extinguant, monentur, 1.Thessal. 5.19. quòd, etsi electio firma & certa est, minimè tamen frustrà præcipitur, etiamsi id fieri nequaquam possit: quia ideò non éxtinguitur in electis, quia eum fouent: vt tem foueant, huiusmodi exhortationibus adducunt. Nam qui constituit Spiritum in electis suis nunquam extinguere prorsus, simul patefecit quibus rationibus illum fouere, tuo videlicet in pietate progressu. Nihil itaque facit hic locus ad euertendam electionis nostræ certitudinem, & inuiolabilem firmitudinem. Vide Perseuerantia.
units.tr: That the elect can fall from God's grace and drive out the Holy Spirit, as some maintain, wrongly appealing to passages: 1 Sam. 16.14; Ps. 51.13; Luke 11.24 etc.; Rom. 11.20, 21, 22; 1 Cor. 9.27; 10.12; Phil. 2.12; Gal. 5.4; 1 Tim. 1.19; 4.1; Heb. 6.4, 5, 6; 10.26; 1 Thess. 5.19; Eph. 4.30; 2 Pet. 1.10. See ELECTION. The elect are warned not to quench the Spirit, 1 Thess. 5.19; for although election is firm and certain, the exhortation is nevertheless not given in vain, even though this can by no means happen: because the Spirit is not quenched in the elect for this reason, that they cherish him; and they urge such exhortations so that they may cherish him. For he who determined that the Spirit should never be utterly quenched in his elect has at the same time shown by what means they are to cherish him, namely in their progress in piety. Therefore this passage does nothing to overthrow the certainty of our election and its inviolable firmness. See Perseverance.

units.la: ELECTVS in præsenti vito dicitur, qui à Deo vel immediatè vel mediatè, ad functiones publicas, politicas aut ecclesiasticas, vocatur. 2. Electus ad participationem, fœderatu gratuiti, nempe populus Israelis. 3. Electus ad vitam æternam, quicunque est membrum Christi. 4. Electus dicitur Christus mediator, nempe quatenus à Patre constitutus est Ecclesiæ rex, doctor, sacerdos, & seruator Ecclesiæ. Par.23.5. Esai.42.1. & 43.10. Agg.2.24. Matt.12.18. Luc.2.1. Pet.2.v.4.6. 5 Electus homo ab homine, variis de causis & ad multiplices rerum vsus vel abusus. 6. Electus, admodum Præstans, eximius, fortis, lectiss. Gen.23.6. 7. Electus à Deo, vt tabernaculi sedes, ciuitas Ierosol, templum. Electus ad Dei iudicia exequenda, Ier.49.19 & 50.44.
units.tr: Elect in the present life is said of one who is called by God, either immediately or mediately, to public, political or ecclesiastical functions. 2. Elect to participation in the covenant of grace, namely the people of Israel. 3. Elect to eternal life, whoever is a member of Christ. 4. Elect is called Christ the mediator, namely insofar as he was appointed by the Father to be king, teacher, priest and saviour of the Church. Par. 23.5; Isa. 42.1; 43.10; Hag. 2.24; Matt. 12.18; Luke 2.1; 1 Pet. 2.4, 6. 5. Elect: a man chosen by a man, for various reasons and for many uses or abuses of things. 6. Elect: very distinguished, outstanding, brave, most choice. Gen. 23.6. 7. Elect by God, like the seat of the tabernacle, the city of Jerusalem, the temple. Elect to carry out God's judgments, Jer. 49.19 and 50.44.

units.la: ELIGERE in Christo, nihil aliud est, quàm gratis destinare adoptioni per Christum, vt patet ex Eph.1.5.
units.tr: To elect in Christ is nothing other than to destine freely to adoption through Christ, as is clear from Eph. 1.5.

units.la: ELEEMOSYNA, est misericordiæ actus exterior, qui se aliis opis vel corporalis vel spiritualis præstatione ergâ egentem profert & patefacit. Est enim vel corporalis vel spiritualis eleemosyna, quia vtrique nostri parti conferens est.
units.tr: Almsgiving is an outward act of mercy, which shows itself and is displayed toward a needy person by giving help, either bodily or spiritual. For there is either bodily or spiritual almsgiving, since it benefits either part of our nature.

units.la: ELEEMOSYNA, speciatim stipem quæ pauperibus erogatur significat: Generaliter verò omne genus beneficii, quo miseros confertur, atque adeò omnia charitatis officia complectitur, Matth.6.2. alias dicitur Miseratio, 9 13.
units.tr: Almsgiving properly signifies the alms distributed to the poor. In general, however, it means every kind of kindness shown to the wretched, and so it embraces all the duties of charity, Matt. 6.2. Elsewhere it is called mercy, Matt. 9.13.
