units.la: crificium Deo gratum, Philipp. 4.18. Hebr. 13.16. Eleemosy-na exempla: Abdias, 1. Reg. 18.13. Tabitha, Actor. 9.36. Cor-nelius Centurio. 10. v. 1.2.3. 4. (Vide BENEFICENTIAE exempla.) Iob. 31.16. Zachæus, Luc. 19.8.
units.tr: sacrifice pleasing to God, Phil. 4.18; Heb. 13.16. Examples of almsgiving: Obadiah, 1 Kings 18.13; Tabitha, Acts 9.36; Cornelius the centurion, Acts 10.1, 2, 3, 4. (See examples of BENEFICENCE.) Job 31.16. Zacchaeus, Luke 19.8.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters]IGANS, i. pulcher, speciosus, bona forma: Exod. 2.2.2. Sam. 4.27. Ier. 46.20. Hebr. 11.23.
units.tr: Beautiful: i.e. handsome, comely, of good form. Exod. 2.2; 1 Sam. 4.27; Jer. 46.20; Heb. 11.23.

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters]IMENTA Physica, ex quibus res sub cœlo componuntur, [illegible] lore soluenda, 2. Petr. 3.v.10.12. Ignis, aer, aqua, & terra.
units.tr: Elements (physical), from which things under heaven are composed and by heat are to be dissolved, 2 Pet. 3.10, 12. Fire, air, water and earth.

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters]IMENTA mundi Paulo sunt rudimenta, seu ceremoniæ [illegible] egales, post Christi plenam manifestationem: quibus [illegible] Dominus Ecclesiam suam Iudaicam quasi sub pæda-[illegible] ogo erudiit, Colossens. 2.8. vt explicatur copiosè Ga-[illegible] t. 4. v. 3.9. vbi etiam pro rudimentis capiuntur. Infirma [illegible] nt & egena, Galat. 4.9. Catecheseos religionis Christia-[illegible] æ prima fundamenta. Heb. 5.12.
units.tr: Elements of the world are, for Paul, the rudiments, or ceremonies, once the full manifestation of Christ has come. By these the Lord trained his Jewish Church as under a tutor, Col. 2.8. This is explained at length in Gal. 4.3, 9, where they are also called rudiments. Weak and needy, Gal. 4.9. The first foundations of the catechesis of the Christian religion, Heb. 5.12.

units.la: [illegible]HANAN, vnus ex fortissimis ducibus in exercitu Daui-[illegible] s, 2. Sam. 23.24. 1. Chron. 11. 26.
units.tr: Elhanan, one of the bravest leaders in David's army, 2 Sam. 23.24; 1 Chron. 11.26.

units.la: [illegible] phas, 1. Reg. 10.22.
units.tr: [...]phas, 1 Kings 10.22.

units.la: [illegible] (i. Deus meus) Sacerdos in Silo, 1. Sam. 2. 11. immorige-[illegible] s filios habet, v. 12.17. vnde increpatur ob indulgentiam [illegible] 27. &c. Audita poena subeunda, Deo acquiescit, 3. 18. nun-[illegible] captæ arcæ accepto concidit, & fractis cervicibus mo-[illegible] tur, 4.18. Iudicauerat Israelem 40. annis: ibid.
units.tr: Eli (i.e. my God): a priest in Shiloh, 1 Sam. 2.11. He had disobedient sons, vv. 12, 17, for which he is rebuked for his indulgence, v. 27, etc. Having heard the punishment he must undergo, he submits to God, 3.18. When the ark was taken, he fell, and with his neck broken he died, 4.18. He had judged Israel for forty years, ibid.

units.la: [illegible]AB, 1. Deus meus pater, filius primogenitus Isai, frater [illegible] auidis, 1. Sam. 16.6.
units.tr: Eliab (i.e. my God is father): firstborn son of Jesse, brother of David, 1 Sam. 16.6.

units.la: [illegible]AB, nepos Ruben, pater Datha & Abiron: Num. 16.1. He-[illegible] os sub Dauide, 1. Chro. 12.9. Leuita, 1. Chro. 15.20. & 16.5.
units.tr: Eliab: grandson of Reuben, father of Dathan and Abiram, Num. 16.1. ... Hebrews under David, 1 Chron. 12.9. Levite, 1 Chron. 15.20; 16.5.

units.la: IACIM, filius Iosiæ, qui & Ioacim, 2. Reg. 23.34. & [illegible] 4.1.2. Paral. 36.4. Nepos Zorobabel in geneal. Christi: [illegible] Matt. 1.13.
units.tr: Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, who is also called Joiakim, 2 Kings 23.34; 24.1, 2; 2 Chron. 36.4. Grandson of Zerubbabel in Christ's genealogy, Matt. 1.13.

units.la: IACIM, Præfectus domus Ezechiæ, 2. Regum 18.18. E-[illegible] iæ 22. 20. & 36. 3.22. Chron. 36.4. Eliacim filius A-[illegible] ud Matth. 1.13. & Luc. 3.30. Sacerdos, Nehem. 12. 49. No-[illegible] en signif. Dei resurrectio.
units.tr: Eliakim, prefect of the household of Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18.18; Isa. 22.20; 36.3, 22; 2 Chron. 36.4. Eliakim, son of Abiud, Matt. 1.13 and Luke 3.30. Priest, Neh. 12.49? The name signifies God's raising up.

units.la: [illegible]AS, (i. Deus meus,) Thesbites Propheta, vir pilosus, & zo-[illegible] na pellicea cinctus renibus, 2. Reg. 1.8. ficcitatem futuram [illegible] ob Achab Regis peccata, illi denunciat, 1. Reg. 17.1. pasci-[illegible] ur a coruis, v. 6. Vide Corvvs, a Vidua, v. 15. precibus a [illegible] eo hospitis filij resurrectionem impetrat, v. 22. constan-[illegible] m, & verum le præbet, 18.18. 2. Reg. 1.16. eius sacrificium igni cœlesti absumitur, 1. Reg. 18. 38. fugit Iezabelem, 1. Reg. 19. 3. pascitur ab Angelo, v. 7. Ie à Deo solum relictum queri. v. 10. Rom. 11. 3. Achabum ob occisum Naboth argu. Reg. 21. 19. ad Ioram regem Iuda scribit, 2. Paral. 21. cum Eliæo aquam siccis pedibus transit, 2. Reg. 2. 8. in. lum rapitur, v. 11. cum Christo loquitur, Mat. 17. 3. Eliæ. lus, 1. Reg. 19. 10. Elias dicitur à Christo Ioannes Baptista, Matth. 11. 14. non persona, Ioann. 1. 21. (quo modo nec Ioannes se esse Eliam, ibid.) sed spiritu ac virtute Eliæ. Lucas explicat, Lucæ 1. 17.
units.tr: Elijah (i.e. my God): the Tishbite prophet, a hairy man girded with a leather belt about his loins, 2 Kings 1.8. He announces to King Ahab a future drought on account of his sins, 1 Kings 17.1. He is fed by ravens, v. 6; see Ravens. He stays with the widow, v. 15. By prayer he obtains from God the resurrection of her host's son, v. 22. He is steadfast and shows himself true, 18.18; 2 Kings 1.16. His sacrifice is consumed by heavenly fire, 1 Kings 18.38. He flees from Jezebel, 1 Kings 19.3. He is fed by an angel, v. 7. He complains that he alone has been left by God, v. 10; Rom. 11.3. He rebukes Ahab for the killing of Naboth, 1 Kings 21.19. He writes to Jehoram, king of Judah, 2 Chron. 21. He crosses the Jordan with Elisha on dry feet, 2 Kings 2.8, and is taken up into heaven, v. 11. He speaks with Christ, Matt. 17.3. Elijah is called by Christ John the Baptist, Matt. 11.14, not in person (John 1.21; nor did John himself say that he was Elijah, ibid.) but in the spirit and power of Elijah. Luke explains this, Luke 1.17.

units.la: [ELIASAPH, unus ex ducibus Israelitarum in deserto, Num. 1. & 2. 7. & 10. cap.]
units.tr: [ELIASAPH, one of the leaders of the Israelites in the desert, Num. 1 and 2.7 and chap. 10.]

units.la: ELIASIB, i. Deus conversionis, Sacerdos magnus, muror Ierusalem instaurationi manum admouet, Nehem. 3. 1.
units.tr: Eliashib, i.e. God of conversion: high priest, who laid his hand to the restoration of the wall of Jerusalem, Neh. 3.1.

units.la: [ELIEL, bellator Strenuus, 1. Chr. 11. 46. miles fortiss. 1. Chr. 11. Dux belli, 1. Chr. 5. 24. Trium Leuitarum insignium, men, 1. Chr. 6. 34. & 15. 9. 15. & 2. Chron. 31. 31. signif. Ieus meus Deus.
units.tr: [ELIEL, a vigorous warrior, 1 Chron. 11.46; a most brave soldier, 1 Chron. 11; a leader in war, 1 Chron. 5.24. Of three notable Levites, 1 Chron. 6.34 and 15.9, 15; 2 Chron. 31.31. Signifies: my God is God.]

units.la: ELIEZER, filius Dodani, Propheta, Iosaphat Regem arguit, 2. Paral. 20. 37. (i. Deus adiutor meus) Aliorum nomen, nempe filij Mosis Oeconomi patr. Abraham, &c.
units.tr: Eliezer, son of Dodavah, a prophet, who rebuked King Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 20.37. (i.e. God my helper.) The name of others: namely, the son of Moses, the steward of the household of Abraham, etc.

units.la: ELIMELECH Bethlehemita, cum uxore & Noemi peregrinatur in regione Moabitide: & ibidem moritur, Ruth 1. 2. 3. Socer Ruth. 1. (i. Deus meus rex.)
units.tr: Elimelech of Bethlehem, with his wife and Naomi, sojourned in the land of Moab and died there, Ruth 1.2, 3. Father-in-law of Ruth, Ruth 1. (i.e. my God is king.)

units.la: ELIPHAZ, (Dei obrizum) de tribus amicis Iob primus, Iob. 2. 11. eius cum Iobo disceptatio, 4. 2. & 5. 1. &c. 15. 1. reprehenditur à Deo, 42. 7. &c.
units.tr: Eliphaz (gold of God): the first of Job's three friends, Job 2.11. His dispute with Job, 4.2; 5.1, etc.; 15.1. Rebuked by God, 42.7, etc.

units.la: ELISABETH. Vide ELIZABETH,
units.tr: Elisabeth. See ELIZABETH.

units.la: ELISAEVS, (i. Dei Salus, vel Deus saluans,) Minister eum Prophetam vngi iubet Deus, 1. Reg. 19. 16. patrem Eliam sequatur, relinquit, v. 20. 21. consulitur à Iosaphat Israel, atque Idumeorum Regibus, 2. Reg. 3. v. 11. 12. transit Iordanem. 2. 14. sanat aquas lethales, sale in eas immittit, 2. Reg. 2. 20. Psalte canente prophetat, 3. v. 15. 16. exercitus Israelis aquas à Deo impetrat, v. 17. pauperculæ viduæ filium multiplicat, 4. v. 3. 4. 5. 6. Hospitæ sterili filium impetrat, v. 16. cuius mortui resurrectionem precibus impetrat, v. 34. pulmentum amarum dulce reddit, panes fam is tempore multiplicat, ver. 43. Naaman leprosum sanat, 5. verf. 9. 10. eius munera recusat, ver. 16. rem natare fecit, 6. 6. eius in Regem Israelis seue v. 13.14. Hazaeli præsenti quæ facturus erat mala prædicit, 2. Reg. 8.12. victoriam Ioas Regi contra Syros promittit, 13.17. moritur, v. 20. ossium eius contactu mortuus excitatur, v. 21.
units.tr: Elisha (i.e. God's salvation, or God who saves): a minister. God commands that this prophet be anointed, 1 Kings 19.16. He leaves his father Elijah to follow him, v. 20, 21. He is consulted by Jehoshaphat, king of Israel, and by the kings of the Edomites, 2 Kings 3.11, 12. He crosses the Jordan, 2.14. He heals the deadly waters by casting salt into them, 2 Kings 2.20. He prophesies while a psaltery is played, 3.15, 16. The army of Israel obtains water from God through him, v. 17. He multiplies the son of a poor widow, 4.3, 4, 5, 6. He obtains a son for a barren hostess, v. 16. By prayer he obtains the resurrection of her dead son, v. 34. He turns bitter pottage sweet, and in a time of famine multiplies bread, v. 43. He heals Naaman the leper, 5.9, 10. He refuses his gifts, v. 16. He made an iron axe-head float, 6.6. His [words] concerning the king of Israel [...], vv. 13, 14. He foretells to Hazael the evils he was about to inflict, 2 Kings 8.12. He promises King Joash victory over the Syrians, 13.17. He dies, v. 20. A man who touches his bones is raised from the dead, v. 21.

units.la: HV Buzites ad Iobum reprehendendum tribus eius amicis se adiungit, Iob. 32. v. 2. eius in Seniores reuerentia, v. 6.7. eius de afflictione & agendi ratione Iobi sententia, 10. 11. &c. & 34. 1. &c. 36. 1. &c. 37. v. 1. 2. &c. [Elihu, dux Elihu, 1. Paral. 12. 20. frater Dauidis, 1. Par. 27. 18. Eliud F. Achin, Matt. 1. 14.] (Deus meus iste.)
units.tr: Elihu the Buzite joins three of Job's friends in rebuking him, Job 32:2. His reverence for the elders, v. 6, 7. His opinion on Job's affliction and conduct, 10, 11, etc., and 34:1 etc., 36:1 etc., 37:1, 2 etc. [Elihu, leader Elihu, 1 Chron. 12:20; brother of David, 1 Chron. 27:18; Eliud son of Achim, Matt. 1:14.] (He is my God.)

units.la: ELIZABETH filia Aminadab: vxor Aaronis: Exod. 6.23. ELIZABETH vxor Zachariæ, Luc. 1.5. Spiritu Sancto repleta est, v. 41. eius de Christo & matre eius Maria iudicium, 42. concepit, v. 24. parit Ioannem Baptistam, v. 57. (pro Elischeba. 1. Dei mei iusiurandum.)
units.tr: ELIZABETH, daughter of Amminadab and wife of Aaron, Exod. 6:23. ELIZABETH, wife of Zechariah, Luke 1:5. Filled with the Holy Spirit, v. 41. Her judgment about Christ and his mother Mary, 42. She conceived, v. 24. She bore John the Baptist, v. 57. (For Elisheba. 1. My God's oath.)

units.la: ELON Zabulonites, Iudex Israelis, Iudic. 12.11. decem annos Israelem iudicat, ibidem. moritur, ver. 12. (i. quercus aut fortis.)
units.tr: ELON the Zebulunite, judge of Israel, Judg. 12:11. He judged Israel for ten years, ibid. He died, v. 12. (I.e. oak or strong.)

units.la: ELOQVENTIA, Exodi 4.10. Dei donum & opus est, v. 11. Eloquentiæ exempla: Aaron, v. 14. Apollos, Act. 18.24. Tertullus, 24.14. [Omnium autem eloquentiam longe superauit Christus, vt Euangelistæ testantur. Vide Psal. 45.3. Esai. 50. 4. Matt. 7.28. Luc. 2 47. & 4.22. Paulus hominum aliorum eloquentiam superauit. Act. 14.12. & 24.26. & 26. v. 14.28 31.32.]
units.tr: ELOQUENCE, Exod. 4:10. It is a gift and work of God, v. 11. Examples of eloquence: Aaron, v. 14; Apollos, Acts 18:24; Tertullus, 24:14. [But Christ far surpassed the eloquence of all men, as the evangelists testify. See Ps. 45:3, Isa. 50:4, Matt. 7:28, Luke 2:47 and 4:22. Paul surpassed the eloquence of other men, Acts 14:12, 24:26, 26:14, 28, 31, 32.]

units.la: ELOQVIA & eloquium Dei, id est, Sermo voluntatem eius in lege & Euangelio patefactam continens.]
units.tr: The ELOQUIA and eloquium of God, that is, the Word containing his will made known in law and Gospel.

units.la: ELVL, mensis Augusto nostro respondens, Nehem. 6.15.
units.tr: ELUL, a month corresponding to our August, Neh. 6:15.

units.la: ELYMAS, (Vide BAR-IESV.) Act. 13.8 (1. Magus.)
units.tr: ELYMAS (see BAR-JESUS), Acts 13:8. (A magician.)

units.la: EMAEI (i. formidabiles) Gigantes erant, quos Moabitæ à terra ipsorum expulerunt: Deut. 2.9. Gen. 14.5.
units.tr: The EMIM (i.e. terrible) were giants whom the Moabites drove out of their land, Deut. 2:9; Gen. 14:5.

units.la: EMATH, ciuitas & regiuncula in terra Chanaan. 2. Syriæ pars ad Chananeæ terræ limites. 3. turris in ciuit. Ierusal.]
units.tr: HAMATH, a city and small region in the land of Canaan. 2. A part of Syria bordering on the limits of the land of Canaan. 3. A tower in the city of Jerusalem.

units.la: EMMANVEL, vel Immanu-El, 1. nobiscum Deus: Christi Dei-hominis primarium nomen, Esai. 7. 14. & 8. 8. Matt. 23.]
units.tr: EMMANUEL, or Immanu-El, 1. God with us: the chief name of Christ the God-man, Isa. 7:14; 8:8; Matt. 1:23.

units.la: EMTIONIS exempla: Abraham emit seruos, Gen. 17.27. spluncam duplicem, 23.16. Iacob parte agri, 33.16. Putiphar sephu, 37.36. Iacob & filij eius frumentum, 42. v.1.2. Iosep terram Aegypti, 47.20. Dauid area, 2.Sam.24.24. Amri tem Samariae, 1.Reg.16.v.23.24. Negociatores Regis, 2.Ral.1.v.16.17. Ieremias agrum, Iere.32.7. Principes Sacerdotum agrum Figuli. Matth.27.7. Ioseph sindonem, Marc.15.46. Maria Magdalena, &c. aromata, 16.v.1.2. Filius Dei Ecclesiam suam, Act.20.28. 1.Corint.6.20. & 7.23. 1.Pet.1.19. 2.Pet.2.1.
units.tr: Examples of buying: Abraham bought slaves, Gen. 17:27; a double cave, 23:16. Jacob bought part of a field, 33:16. Potiphar bought Joseph, 37:36. Jacob and his sons bought grain, 42:1, 2. Joseph bought the land of Egypt, 47:20. David bought a threshing floor, 2 Sam. 24:24. Omri bought the hill of Samaria, 1 Kings 16:23, 24. The king's merchants, 2 Kings 1:16, 17. Jeremiah bought a field, Jer. 32:7. The chief priests bought the potter's field, Matt. 27:7. Joseph bought a linen cloth, Mark 15:46. Mary Magdalene, etc., bought spices, Mark 16:1, 2. The Son of God bought his Church, Acts 20:28; 1 Cor. 6:20; 7:23; 1 Pet. 1:19; 2 Pet. 2:1.

units.la: EMAVS, (i. Aurora.) [vicus in quem] proficiscuntur duo Discipuli, Luc.14.13. quibus Christus patefecit se resurrexe, &c.
units.tr: EMMAUS (i.e. dawn), [a village] to which two disciples set out, Luke 24:13, and to whom Christ revealed that he had risen, etc.

units.la: EMOR, Dinam vxorem filio suo Sichem petit, Gen.34.8. cui filio occiditur, v.26. (Hamor.i. Asinus.)
units.tr: HAMOR (EMOR), asks for Dinah as wife for his son Shechem, Gen. 34:8, and his son is killed, v. 26. (Hamor, i.e. ass.)

units.la: ENACIM (gigantes) Deut.2.10.11. interficiuntur à Iosua, Ios. 11.v.21.22. eorum possessio datur Calebo, Iudic.21.12.
units.tr: The ANAKIM (giants), Deut. 2:10, 11. They are killed by Joshua, Josh. 11:21, 22. Their possession is given to Caleb, Judg. 1:12.

units.la: ENCAENIA (id est, instauratio, siue renouatio) festum à Machabæis institutum, 1.Mach.4.59. Ierosolymis celebratum, Ioh.10.22. vnde ἐγκαίνια dicuntur, quæ sacro vsui vebantur initiantur, Heb.9.18. & 10.20.
units.tr: ENCAENIA (i.e. renewal or restoration), a feast instituted by the Maccabees, 1 Macc. 4:59, celebrated at Jerusalem, John 10:22. Hence they are called ἐγκαίνια [enkainia], things dedicated to sacred use, Heb. 9:18 and 10:20.

units.la: ENOCH, Vide HENOCH. ENON, V. Aenon.
units.tr: ENOCH, see HENOCH. ENON, see AENON.

units.la: ENOS, filius Seth, Gen.5.6. quàdiu vixerit, v.11. (i. vir homo.)
units.tr: ENOS, son of Seth, Gen. 5:6. As long as he lived, v. 11. (I.e. man, a human being.)

units.la: EPAENETVS, in Achaia primus credidit, Rom.16.5. (Ἐπαίνετος laudabilis.)
units.tr: EPAENETUS, the first to believe in Achaia, Rom. 16:5. (Ἐπαίνετος [Epainetos], praiseworthy.)

units.la: ΣΥΤΟΛΗ, Luc.1.6. ea Legis pars est, quæ Moralis dicitur, qua præcipitur quid Deo, quid proximo debeamus. δικαιώματα sunt sacri ritus, atque adeò tota Lex ceremonialis. Κρίματα verò ea Legis pars, quæ ad ciuilem politiam & forenses controuersias pertinet, quæ Iudicialis appellatur.
units.tr: COMMANDMENT [ἐντολή], Luke 1:6. It is the part of the Law called moral, in which it is prescribed what we owe to God and what we owe to our neighbour. Righteousnesses [δικαιώματα] are the sacred rites, and so the whole ceremonial law. Judgments [κρίματα] are the part of the Law which pertains to civil polity and legal disputes, and which is called judicial.

units.la: EPAPHRAS Colossensium Minister, Coloss.1.7. vocatur Christi seruus, 4.12. Pauli in captiuitate socius, Philem.v.23. (Epaphras, spumans G.)
units.tr: EPAPHRAS, minister of the Colossians, Col. 1:7. He is called Christ's servant, 4:12, and Paul's fellow-prisoner, Philem. 23. (Epaphras, foaming.)

units.la: EPAPHRODITVS, (i. venustus) Philippensium Apostolus. Philipp.2.25. & 4.18. Paulo captiuo fideliter ministrans.
units.tr: EPAPHRODITUS (i.e. charming), apostle of the Philippians, Phil. 2:25; 4:18. Faithfully ministering to Paul in captivity.

units.la: EPHA vetus mensura Hebræorum, cuius homer est decima. Exod.16.37.
units.tr: EPHAH, an old Hebrew measure, of which the homer is the tenth part, Exod. 16:37.

units.la: Eph., filius Madian, nepos Abrahæ: Gen.25.4.
units.tr: Epher, son of Midian, grandson of Abraham, Gen. 25:4.

units.la: EPHESVS, vrbs celeberrima in Asia minore: vbi Paulus biennium euangelizauit: Act.19.9. ac Timotheum Episcopum constituit. 1.Tim.1.3.
units.tr: EPHESUS, a most famous city in Asia Minor, where Paul preached the gospel for two years, Acts 19:9, and appointed Timothy bishop, 1 Tim. 1:3.

units.la: EPHESIORVM ciuitas, magnæ Dianæ cultrix, Act.19.v.35. 5. Ephesij duodecim, primariæ eorum Ecclesiæ sunt, Act. 9. v. 1. 6. negant se audiuisse an sit Spiritus Sanctus, id est, non vigeant Spiritus Sancti dona in Ecclesia, 19. 2. Ephesij redentes curiosarum artium libros comburunt, v. 19. Ephesiorum gloria.
units.tr: The city of the Ephesians, a worshipper of great Diana, Acts 19:35. 5. The twelve Ephesians are the chief members of their church, Acts 9:1. 6. They deny that they have heard whether there is a Holy Spirit, that is, the gifts of the Holy Spirit do not flourish in the Church, 19:2. The Ephesians, returning, burn books of curious arts, v. 19. The glory of the Ephesians.

units.la: EPHOD, vestis Sacerdotalis, Exodi 25.7. Ephod Gedeonis, fuit idololatriia à Gedeone institueta, contra Dei verbum, in patria sua Ophra, bona quidem intentione, sed quæ toti populo Israel offendiculum præbuit, Iudic. 8. 27. Vide IDOLORVM catalogus. Ephod lineo indutus Samuel, seruit Domino, 1. Sam. 2. 18. Ephod lineo indutus Dauid, 2. Sam. 6. 14. Ephod ex auro, hyacintho, purpura, cocco bis tincto, & byssο contexta, quæ propria erat Sacerdotum, Exo. 28. 6.
units.tr: EPHOD, a priestly garment, Exod. 25:7. The ephod of Gideon: it was an idolatry instituted by Gideon, against the word of God, in his native Ophrah; it was done with good intention, but it became a stumbling-block to the whole people of Israel, Judg. 8:27. See the catalogue of IDOLS. Samuel, wearing a linen ephod, served the Lord, 1 Sam. 2:18. David, wearing a linen ephod, 2 Sam. 6:14. The ephod of gold, hyacinth, purple, twice-dyed scarlet and fine linen woven together, which was proper to the priests, Exod. 28:6.

units.la: EPHRAIM (id est, fructuosus effectus, filius Ioseph secundus, Genes. 41. 52. Manasse fratri præfertur, 48. 16. eius sors, Ios. 16. 4. Vide Iudic. 8. 1. &c. [Ab eo tribus & eiusdem regio denominata est. Frequenter apud Prophetas significat Ephraimitas & Israelitas, seu decem tribus quæ à regno Iuda seu Dauidis domo defecerunt.]
units.tr: EPHRAIM (i.e. made fruitful), the second son of Joseph, Gen. 41:52. He was preferred to his brother Manasseh, 48:16. His lot, Josh. 16:4. See Judg. 8:1 etc. [From him the tribe and its region were named. Often in the Prophets it signifies the Ephraimites and Israelites, or the ten tribes which fell away from the kingdom of Judah or the house of David.]

units.la: EPHRAIM oppidum prope Iericho, vbi Christus septimo & octauo die ante Pascha cum Discipulis commoratus est. Ioan. 11. 54. fit eius mentio 2. Sam. 13. 23.
units.tr: EPHRAIM, a town near Jericho, where Christ stayed with his disciples for seven or eight days before the Passover, John 11:54. It is mentioned in 2 Sam. 13:23.

units.la: EPHRATA, quæ & Bethlehem dicta est, vrbs fuit Dauidis in tribu Iuda: vbi natus est Christus, Gen. 35. 16. Mich. 5. 2. (i. terra fructifera). V. Bethlehem.
units.tr: EPHRATHAH, which is also called Bethlehem, was a town of David in the tribe of Judah, where Christ was born, Gen. 35:16; Mic. 5:2. (I.e. fruitful land.) See Bethlehem.

units.la: EPHRON, ciuis Hebron, à quo Abrahamus emit agrum ad sepulturam vxoris suæ: Gen. 23. 8. &c.
units.tr: EPHRON, a citizen of Hebron, from whom Abraham bought a field for the burial of his wife, Gen. 23:8 etc.

units.la: EPIMENIDES, poeta Cretensis, citatus à Paulo, Tit. 1. 12.
units.tr: EPIMENIDES, a Cretan poet, quoted by Paul, Titus 1:12.

units.la: EPICVREI, secta philosophorum orta ab Epicuro, affirmante voluptatem esse summum bonum, cum Stoicis aduersus Paulum disputant, Actor. 17. 18. voces eorum, Esa. 22. 13. & 28. 15, 1. Corinth. 15 32. Esa. 56. 11. 12. EPISCOPATVS, Psalm. 109. 8. Actor. 1. 20. 1. Tim. 3 1.]
units.tr: EPICUREANS, a sect of philosophers arising from Epicurus, who affirmed that pleasure is the highest good. They dispute with Paul, together with the Stoics, against him, Acts 17:18. Their words: Isa. 22:13; 28:15; 1 Cor. 15:32; Isa. 56:11, 12. EPISCOPACY, Ps. 109:8; Acts 1:20; 1 Tim. 3:1.

units.la: EPISCOPVS noster Christus. Vide CHRISTVS. Episcopus ἐπίσκοπος dictus, quòd illum oporteat quasi speculatorem in doctrinam & mores gregis sibi commissi inquirere, Act. 20. 28. Episcopi interdum generali nomine Presbyteri vocantur, Act. 20. 17. 28. 1. Tim. 5. 17. Episcopi quales esse debeant, Vide PASTORES. V. Esa. 56. 10.
units.tr: EPISCOPUS, our Christ. See CHRIST. The bishop is called ἐπίσκοπος [episkopos] because he ought, like a watchman, to inquire into the doctrine and morals of the flock committed to him, Acts 20:28. Bishops are sometimes called by the general name of presbyters, Acts 20:17, 28; 1 Tim. 5:17. For what bishops ought to be, see MINISTERS. See Isa. 56:10.

units.la: Episcopus, commune nomen eorum, qui verbo & gubernationi Ecclesiæ præsunt: puta Pastorum, Doctorum & Presbyterorum, Phil. 1. 1. Episcopus vnius vxoris vir debet, 1, Tim. 3. 2. Ergo qui coniugatos excludit ab Episcopatu, quia coniugati sunt, Antichristum se prodit, 4. 3. Episcopi & Diaconi, vnà cum vxoribus, liberis & familiis eleganter depinguntur, 3. v. 2. 8. Tit. 1. verf. 7. &c. probandi sunt, primùm, deinde ministrent, 1. Timoth. 3. 10.
units.tr: Bishop, the common name of those who preside over the Word and the government of the Church, namely pastors, teachers and presbyters, Phil. 1:1. A bishop must be the husband of one wife, 1 Tim. 3:2. Therefore whoever excludes married men from the episcopate, because they are married, betrays himself as Antichrist, 4:3. Bishops and deacons, together with their wives, children and households, are elegantly portrayed, 3:2, 8; Titus 1:7 etc. They are to be tested first, and then minister, 1 Tim. 3:10.

units.la: EPISTOLA Apostolorum ad Antiochenos missa, Act. 23. Epistolæ ad Romanos scriptæ ratio explicatur, Rom. 15. 15. Epistola ad diuersas Ecclesias scripta, Apoc. 2. 1. &c.
units.tr: The EPISTLE sent by the Apostles to the Antiochenes, Acts 23. The manner of writing the Epistle to the Romans is explained, Rom. 15:15. An epistle written to various churches, Rev. 2:1 etc.

units.la: EPISTOLA Pauli Corinthij vocantur, 2. Cor. 3. 2. Christi, 3. Vide LITERAE.
units.tr: EPISTLE: Paul's letters are called the Corinthians, 2 Cor. 3.2; Christ's are called the third, 3. See LETTERS.

units.la: EPVLAE in sacrificiis, Deut. 12. v. 12. 18. & 14 26. & 15. 10 16. v. 11. 14. & 26. 11. & 27, 7. 1. Sam. 9 13. Exempla: [Iethro, socer Mosis, Exod. 18. 12. ] Israelitæ, 1. Paral. 29. 22.
units.tr: FEASTS in sacrifices, Deut. 12.12, 18; 14.26; 15.10; 16.11, 14; 26.11; 27.7; 1 Sam. 9.13. Examples: [Jethro, father-in-law of Moses, Exod. 18.12]; the Israelites, 1 Chr. 29.22.

units.la: EPVLARI & lætari, coram Domino, Deut. 16. 11. & 26. 11. epulandum & exultandum nobis ob Pascha nostrum immolatum, 1. Cor. 5. v. 7. 8.
units.tr: TO FEAST AND REJOICE before the Lord, Deut. 16.11 and 26.11. We must feast and exult, because our Passover has been sacrificed, 1 Cor. 5.7, 8.

units.la: EQVI fortitudo à Deo est, Iob. 39. 22. &c. Equi albi visio, Apoc. 6. v. 2. rufi, v. 4. nigri, v. 5. pallidi, v. 8. Equorum Salmonis numerus, 1. Regum 4. 26. Equites eius, 10. 26. Equi ne multiplicet sibi Rex, Deut. 17. 16. Qui fidunt equis: Iob 20. 8. ruunt, v. 9. Ne sitis vt equi, Psal. 32. 9. Equitatus Pharaonis, & Chananæorum, Equitatus regius Iosaphati, 2. Chr. 18. 30. Equitatus mysticus: Cantic. 1. 4.
units.tr: HORSE. Strength of the horse is from God, Job 39.22, etc. Vision of a white horse, Rev. 6.2; of a red one, v. 4; of a black one, v. 5; of a pale one, v. 8. The number of Solomon's horses, 1 Kings 4.26; his horsemen, 10.26. The king must not multiply horses for himself, Deut. 17.16. Those who trust in horses, Job 20.8, fall, v. 9. Be not like the horse, Ps. 32.9. The cavalry of Pharaoh and of the Canaanites; the royal cavalry of Jehoshaphat, 2 Chr. 18.30. Mystical cavalry, Song 1.4.

units.la: ER, filius Iudæ primogenitus, Genes. 38. 3. nequam est, & id à Domino occiditur, v. 7. 1. Par. 2. 3. (Er, i. vigilans.)
units.tr: ER, the firstborn son of Judah, Gen. 38.3, was wicked, and for this the Lord slew him, v. 7; 1 Chr. 2.3. (Er, i.e. watchful.)

units.la: ERASTVS, procurator vrbis Corinthi, Rom. 16. 23. comes fuit à Paulo aliquandiu profectionum eius: cum Timotheo missus fuit in Macedoniam: Act. 19. 21. Sed Paulo Romæ captiuo Corinthi mansit: 2. Tim. 4. 20.
units.tr: ERASTUS, steward of the city of Corinth, Rom. 16.23. He was for some time a companion of Paul on his journeys, and was sent with Timothy into Macedonia, Acts 19.21. But when Paul was a prisoner at Rome, he remained at Corinth, 2 Tim. 4.20.

units.la: [ERROR, pro deceptione, Ephes. 4. 14. 22. 1. Thessal. 2. 3. Thess. 2. 11. 1. Timoth. 4. 1. Iud. 11. pro illusione, Esai. 3. 10. pro imagine, Esai. 45. 16. pro incogitantia, Gen. 42. 12. Eccles. 10. 8. pro stoliditate, Eccles. 1. 17. & 2. ve. 2. 12. & 7. 25. & 10. 13. pro vanitate, Iob. 15. 31. Esai. 30. 28.]
units.tr: [ERROR, for deception, Eph. 4.14, 22; 1 Thess. 2.3; 2 Thess. 2.11; 1 Tim. 4.1; Jude 11; for delusion, Isa. 3.10; for image, Isa. 45.16; for thoughtlessness, Gen. 42.12; Eccl. 10.8; for stupidity, Eccl. 1.17 and 2.12 and 7.25 and 10.13; for vanity, Job 15.31; Isa. 30.28.]

units.la: ERRORES difficilè corriguntur, Act. 10. 45. erroris efficacia, 2. Thess. 2. 11.
units.tr: ERRORS are with difficulty corrected, Acts 10.45. The efficacy of error, 2 Thess. 2.11.

units.la: ERVESCENTIAE exempla: Serui Eglon, Iudic. 3 v. 24. 25. Elæus, 2. Reg. 3. 14. Esdras, 1. Esdr. 8. 22. aduersarij Christi, Luc. 13. 17.
units.tr: EXAMPLES OF EFFERVESCENCE: the servants of Eglon, Judg. 3.24, 25; Elisha, 2 Kings 3.14; Ezra, 1 Esd. 8.22; the adversaries of Christ, Luke 13.17.

units.la: BESCERE nemo debet euangelium, Psalm. 40. 11. Marc. 8.38. Luc. 9.26. Rom. 1,16. 2. Tim. 1.8. erubescendum pro-ter peccata, Ezech. 16. 52.
units.tr: TO BE ASHAMED. No one ought to be ashamed of the gospel, Ps. 40.11; Mark 8.38; Luke 9.26; Rom. 1.16; 2 Tim. 1.8. To be ashamed on account of sins, Ezek. 16.52.

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters]IAS filius Amos, Esa. 1.1. tempus prophetiae eius, ibid. [vo-tur & mittitur, 6.8. & 49.1. nudus est & discalceatus, 20.3. [illegible, ~3 letters]echiam animat, 2. Regum 19.6. Esai. 37.6. increpat eum, [illegible, ~2 letters]3. videt gloriam Christi, 6.1. Ioan. 12. 41. orat contra Sen-cherib 2. Par. 32.20. (Iesaiahu. i. salus Domini.)
units.tr: [...]IAH, son of Amoz, Isa. 1.1. The time of his prophecy, ibid. He is called and sent, 6.8 and 49.1. He is naked and barefoot, 20.3. He encourages [Hezekiah], 2 Kings 19.6; Isa. 37.6. He rebukes him, [...]. He sees the glory of Christ, 6.1; John 12.41. He prays against Sennacherib, 2 Chr. 32.20. (Isaiah, i.e. the salvation of the Lord.)

units.la: [illegible, ~3 letters]IAS, Athaliae F. Esdr. 8.7. Merari nepos, Esdr. 8. 19. Re-hab. F 1. Par. 26.25.]
units.tr: [...]IAH, son of Athaliah, Ezra 8.7; grandson of Merari, Ezra 8.19; son of Rehabiah, 1 Chr. 26.25.

Hebr. 12.16. seruus fratris constituitur, 27.37. vxorem du-it Ismaelitidè, 28. 9. fratri obuiam proficiscitur, 32 6. pla-tur. 33.4. reuertitur in Seir, v.16. ditissimus est, 36.v.6. 7. Vide EDOM.
units.tr: ESAU (i.e. complete, for he came forth more perfect than boys usually are, namely furnished with hair) is born the firstborn of Isaac, Gen. 25.25. He is loved by his father, v. 28. Edom is called [...], v. 30 and 36.1. He sells his birthright to his brother Jacob, 25.33; Heb. 12.16. He is made a servant of his brother, 27.37. He takes a wife from the Ishmaelites, 28.9. He goes to meet his brother, 32.6. [...], 33.4. He returns to Seir, v. 16. He is very rich, 36.6, 7. See EDOM.

units.la: [illegible, ~1 letter]H, idolum in πυρέῳ. Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: [...]H, an idol in pyreo [πυρέῳ]. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: [illegible, ~1 letter]RAS Scriba, Babylone Ierusalem conscendit, 1. Esdr. 7.6. [illegible, ~1 letter]iuinæ Legis interpres, ieiunium publicum edicit, 8. v.21, [illegible, ~1 letter]3. orat pro peccatis populi, 9.v.5.6. Separat mulieres gen-tiles ex Israel, 9.v.1. &c. 10.1. &c. præle git librum Legis, Esd. 8.v.23. appellatur Iosedec, 1. Paral. 6. 15. (Esra. i. auxi-liator.
units.tr: EZRA the scribe went up from Babylon to Jerusalem, 1 Esd. 7.6. He is an interpreter of the divine Law; he proclaims a public fast, 8.21. He prays for the sins of the people, 9.5, 6. He separates the Gentile women from Israel, 9.1, etc.; 10.1, etc. He reads the book of the Law, Ezra 8.23. He is called Jozadak, 1 Chr. 6.15. (Ezra, i.e. helper.)
