units.tr: [Workmanship, work: Num. 8.4; Ps. 92.5; Hos. 13.2; Eph. 2.10.]

units.la: FALLACIA diuitiarū sermonē suffocat Mat.13.22. Elymas pnus dolo proconsulē à fide auertere querens, cęcus reddit Act.13.8. Pseudodoctorum cauenda, Col.2.8. & peccati, Heb. 3.13. Adulatoris: Pro.26.28. Formæ & vanæ pulchritudinis, 31.30. V. Dolus.
units.tr: The deceitfulness of riches chokes the word, Matt. 13.22. Elymas the sorcerer, seeking by guile to turn the proconsul from the faith, is made blind, Acts 13.8. Deceivers are to be avoided, Col. 2.8; and sin, Heb. 3.13. Of a flatterer: Prov. 26.28. Of beauty that is false and vain: Prov. 31.30. See DECEIT.

units.la: FALLACIAE exempla: Serpens, Gen.3.4. duæ filiæ Loth, 19.3 Rebecca, 27.v.6.7. Rachel, 31.35. Thamar, 38.v.13.14. Vxor Putiphar is, 39.v.17.18. Rahab. Iof.2.v.4.5.6. Iahel, Iudic. 4.v.16.17.18. Dalila, 16.v.15.16. Michol, 1.Sam.19.v.12. 13.14.15.16.17. Ionathas, 20.21.22. Dauid, 26. verf. 10.11. Mulier Thecuitius, 2.Sam.14.6. Mulier quædam, 17. (Vide MVLIERVM astutiæ: & ASTVTIAE mulierum exempla.)
units.tr: Examples of DECEIT: the serpent, Gen. 3.4; the two daughters of Lot, 19.31; Rebekah, 27.6–7; Rachel, 31.35; Tamar, 38.13–14; the wife of Potiphar, 39.17–18; Rahab, Josh. 2.4–6; Jael, Judg. 4.16–18; Delilah, 16.15–16; Michal, 1 Sam. 19.12–17; Jonathan, 20.21–22; David, 26.10–11; the woman of Tekoa, 2 Sam. 14.6; a certain woman, 17. (See CUNNING OF WOMEN, and examples of the cunning of women.)

units.la: FALSITAS, ψευδος. Est in verbis & sermone affirmatio, aut negatio, vel narratio de re aliter quam res est, à nobis, sciẽtibus, siue ignorantibus, & rem ita se habere existimantibus facta. Vnde distinguitur sæpe qui falsum dicit, ab eo qui mentitur, Psal.58.4. Ioh.8.44. Rom.1.25. 2. Ephes. 4.21. Thes.2.11.12.1. Ioh.2.21.27. Apoc.21.27.& 22.15.
units.tr: FALSEHOOD, falsity [ψευδος]. In words and speech it is an affirmation, denial, or narration about a thing otherwise than the thing is, done by us, whether knowing or not knowing, and thinking the thing to be so. Hence one who says what is false is often distinguished from one who lies: Ps. 58.4; John 8.44; Rom. 1.25; Eph. 4.21; 2 Thess. 2.11–12; 1 John 2.21, 27; Rev. 21.27 and 22.15.

units.la: FALSVS Propheta, Vide PSEVDOPROPHETAE.
units.tr: FALSE prophet. See FALSE PROPHETS.

units.la: FALSVM Testimonium non dicendum, Exo.20.16. Deut. 5.20.
units.tr: A false testimony is not to be spoken, Exod. 20.16; Deut. 5.20.

units.la: FALX, [Deut.16.9.& 23.25. Ioel.3.13. Marc.4.29. Figurate sumitur, Esai.2.4 & 18.5. Ierem. 50.16. falx mystica, Apoc.14.14. ad finem usque.)
units.tr: SICKLE, [Deut. 16.9 and 23.25; Joel 3.13; Mark 4.29]. Taken figuratively, Isa. 2.4 and 18.5; Jer. 50.16. The mystical sickle, Rev. 14.14 to the end.

units.la: FAMA bona præstantior diuitiis, eóque expetenda, Prouer. 22.1. Eccle.7.v.1.2. Eccl.41.v.15.16. quatenus illius habendi ratio, Rom.12.17.2. Cor.5.12.&6.4.&8.2.&13.7.1. Tim. 7.1. Pet.2.12.&3.16. Philip.4.8. Famæ bonæ exempla: Salomé 1.Reg.10.v.1.2.2. Paral.9.v.1.2. Matt.12.42. Luc.11.31. Mardochæus, Esth.9.4. Ioannes Baptista, Matt.11.11. Christus 9.31.&14.1.2. Luc.4.14. Zacharias & Elisabeth, Luc.1.6. Simeon, 2.25. Paulus, 2.Cor.6.v.4.8. Famæ malæ exempla: Filii Heli, Ophni & Phinees, 1.Sam.2.v.23.24.
units.tr: A good name is more excellent than riches, and therefore to be desired, Prov. 22.1; Eccles. 7.1–2; Ecclus. 41.15–16. How far it is to be considered: Rom. 12.17; 2 Cor. 5.12; 6.4; 8.2; 13.7; 1 Tim. 3.7; 1 Pet. 2.12; 3.16; Phil. 4.8. Examples of good name: Solomon, 1 Kings 10.1–2; 2 Chr. 9.1–2; Matt. 12.42; Luke 11.31. Mordecai, Esth. 9.4. John the Baptist, Matt. 11.11. Christ, 9.31; 14.1–2; Luke 4.14. Zechariah and Elizabeth, Luke 1.6. Simeon, 2.25. Paul, 2 Cor. 6.4–8. Examples of bad name: the sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, 1 Sam. 2.23–24.
FAMINE is from God: Gen. 41.30, 32; Lev. 26.20, 26; Deut. 28.18; 2 Kings 8.1; Ps. 105.16; Isa. 3.1; Ezek. 4.16 and 5.17

Fames ob violatam Gabaonitis fidem, 2.Sam. 1.1. Ad preces,& conuersionem excitat, 1.Reg.8.35. Amos 6.Psal.107.
units.tr: 14.13. §.13. See AFFLICTIONS from God. Sin is the cause of famine: Amos 4.6. How great an evil famine is: Lam. 4.9. Famine and love: charity: Gen. 12.10; 26.1; 42.1; 43.1, etc.; 44.1, etc.; 47.1, etc.; Exod. 16.3; Deut. 28.53 and 32.24; Ruth 1.1; 2 Sam. 21.1 and 24.13; 1 Kings 8.37 and 18.2; 2 Kings 4.38 and 6.25 and 8.1; 25.3; 2 Chr. 6.28 and 20.9; Ezra 5.1, etc.; Ps. 37.19; Isa. 13, etc.; Jer. 14.1, 12; 15.2 and 29.17 and 34.17; Ezek. 5.12, 16 and 6.11; Joel 1.1, etc.; Amos 4.6; Hag. 1.6, 10 and 2.17; Matt. 24.7; Luke 4.25 and 15.14; Acts 7.11 and 11.28; Rom. 8.34; 1 Cor. 8.14 and 11.27; Rev. 6.8 and 18.8. Famine is twofold: of the word of God, namely, and of perishable bread, Amos 8.11. See on 1 Sam. 1.2; 1 Chr. 15.3; Hos. 3.4 and 4.1. Famine is foretold, Ezek. 4; Acts 11.28. Famine because of the violated faith to the Gibeonites, 2 Sam. 1.1. It stirs up to prayer and conversion, 1 Kings 8.35; Amos 6; Ps. 107.

units.la: Tempore Famis Deus suos fouet: Psalm.33.18.& 37.19.& 37.5.Pro.10.3.1.Reg.17.1.Gen.50.19.Ps.107.5.6.8.9.Luc.4. 26.V.Rom.8.34.
units.tr: In time of famine God cherishes his people: Psalm 33.18; 37.19; 37.5; Prov. 10.3; 1 Kings 17.1; Gen. 50.19; Ps. 107.5, 6, 8, 9; Luke 4.26; cf. Rom. 8.34.

units.la: Famis in diuersis locis & temporibus exempla: Tempore Abrahæ, Gen.12.10. Isaaci 26.1. Iacob & Iosephi, 41.v.53.54. 42.5.& 43.v.1.2.& 45.v.5.6.& 47.v.13.20. Iud. Ruth.1. 1. Vuidis.2.Sam.21.1.Eliæ in Samaria,1.Reg.18.2. Luc.4.25. Misæi,2. Reg.4.38.& 8.1.Ioram Regis Israel,in Samaria,6. 25.26.27.in Ierusalem tempore Sedechiæ, 25.3.Ierem. v.4.5.6. Thren.4 4.1. Nehemiæ tempore, Nehem.5.v.1. 3.in prodigo Filio,Luc.15. 14. Claudij Cæsaris temporis, Actor.11.28. Miserandam etiam & stupendam famem minatur Moses populo Israelitico, si diuinæ Legis custodiam abiicientes,Deo rebelles esse perrexerint, Deur.28. 51.52.53. 57. &c. ita vt liberos etiam proprios comedere ogantur: quod ante Christum natum factum esse legi-us,2.Regum 6. v. 28.29. Idem factum esse in obsidione Hierosolymorum Titi Vespasiani tempore testatur Iosephus. Lib. 7. de bello Iudaico. c. 8. Vide GRAVISSIMAM Dei comminationem,Leuitici 26.26. Ierem.19. 9.Ezech. 16.
units.tr: Examples of famine in various places and times: in the time of Abraham, Gen. 12.10; of Isaac, 26.1; of Jacob and Joseph, 41.53, 54; 42.5; 43.1, 2; 45.5, 6; 47.13, 20; in the days of the Judges, Ruth 1.1; in the time of David, 2 Sam. 21.1; of Elijah in Samaria, 1 Kings 18.2; Luke 4.25; of Elisha, 2 Kings 4.38; 8.1; under Joram, king of Israel, in Samaria, 6.25, 26, 27; in Jerusalem in the time of Zedekiah, 25.3; Jer. 4.5, 6; Lam. 4.4, 9; in the time of Nehemiah, Neh. 5.1, 3; in the prodigal son, Luke 15.14; in the time of Claudius Caesar, Acts 11.28. Moses also threatens a dreadful and appalling famine to the people of Israel if, casting off the keeping of the divine Law, they persist in rebelling against God: Deut. 28.51, 52, 53, 57, etc., so that they are compelled even to eat their own children. That this happened before Christ's birth we read in 2 Kings 6.28, 29. Josephus testifies that the same happened during the siege of Jerusalem under Titus Vespasian, Book 7 of The Jewish War, ch. 8. See also God's most grievous threat, Lev. 26.26; Jer. 19.9; Ezek. 16.

units.la: ELICIS succurrendum: Mat.25 35.42. Vide Eleemosyna, Beneficentia.
units.tr: Help the hungry: Matt. 25.35, 42. See Almsgiving, Beneficence.

units.la: FAMILIAE cura habenda,Prou.27.23. 1. Tim.5. 8. Familiam ducebat Abraham,Gen.18.19. V.Pro.31.15.&c.
units.tr: Care of the household is to be taken: Prov. 27.23; 1 Tim. 5.8. Abraham led his household: Gen. 18.19. See Prov. 31.15, etc.

units.la: FAMILIARITAS nimia interdum periculosa,Prou.25.17. Vi- Amicus:&Amicitia.Et Pro.23.12.3.
units.tr: Excessive familiarity is sometimes dangerous: Prov. 25.17. See Friend and Friendship. Also Prov. 23.12; 3.

units.la: FAMULI: Famulorum & famularum officium, Vide SERVORUM & ancillarum officium.
units.tr: SERVANTS: the duty of male and female servants. See the duty of servants and maidservants.

units.la: FASTVS, Vide AMBITIO, & SVPERBIA.
units.tr: Pride. See Ambition and Arrogance.

units.la: FATVVS, pro insipido, vel saporis experte, Matt. 5. 13. pro stulto, & quasi cerebro vacuo, v. 22. Fatue, qui dixerit fratri quid commereatur, ibid. Vide HOMICIDARVM, qui communi hominum opinionem homicidij rei apud Deum censetur, gradus. V. Stultus.
units.tr: FOOLISH: used of the tasteless, or what has lost its savour, Matt. 5.13; of the stupid, as if empty-headed, v. 22: "Whoever says to his brother, 'You fool,' ..." See the degrees of homicide, which in the common opinion of men is held guilty of murder before God. See Foolish.

units.la: FEBRIS: Febri percutiuntur Præceptorum Dei violatores, Deut. 28. 22. Febribus quidam leuantur, Vide MIRACVLA. Febris est calor non naturalis, qui in corde accensus per venas & arterias in totum corpus deriuatur, sitim accendit non nisi noxia appetentem, vires debilitat, facultates sive actiones naturales impedit.
units.tr: FEVER: Violators of the commandments of God are struck with fever, Deut. 28.22. Some are relieved of fevers; see Miracles. A fever is an unnatural heat, kindled in the heart and spread through the veins and arteries into the whole body; it inflames a thirst that craves only what is harmful, weakens the strength, and impedes the natural faculties or actions.

units.la: FEL draconum, vinum Iudæorum, Deut. 32. 33. Fel germinans radix in corde infidelis, 29. 18. Fel amaritudinis plenus, Actor. 8. 23. est interior cordis malitia, & virus illius Diabolicæ impietatis, quo Magus ille totus erat oppletus, alludere autem videtur Petrus ad locum Deut. 29. 18. Radix fel, & absinthium germinans, euellenda, ibid. V. Hebr. 12. 15.
units.tr: GALL of dragons, the wine of the Jews, Deut. 32.33. A root bearing gall and wormwood in the heart of the unbeliever, Deut. 29.18. "Full of the gall of bitterness," Acts 8.23: this is the inner malice of the heart and the poison of that devilish impiety with which that magician was wholly filled. Peter seems to allude to Deut. 29.18: "A root that bears gall and wormwood, to be uprooted," ibid. See Heb. 12.15.

units.la: FELIX, Iudææ Præses, Act. 23. 24. Paulum vinctum humaniter tractat, 24. 24. auaritiæ studio liberationem Pauli differt, v. 27. ad Pauli de iudicio diuino concionem expauescit, v. 25. 26. Iudæis gratificatus Paulum vinctum relinquit, v. 28.
units.tr: FELIX, governor of Judaea, Acts 23.24. He treats Paul, who is in chains, humanely (24.24); out of eagerness for money he delays Paul's release (v. 27); he is alarmed by Paul's sermon on divine judgment (vv. 25, 26); to please the Jews he leaves Paul in chains (v. 28).

units.la: FEMINALIA Aaronis & filiorum eius, Exodi 28. versici 42. 43.
units.tr: The linen breeches of Aaron and his sons, Exod. 28, verses 42, 43.

units.la: FEMVR, femori manum admouendi mos, Genes. 24. 2. & 47. 29. qui ritus olim visitatus fuit in iis iuramentis, quæ superiores à domesticis exigebant.
units.tr: The custom of placing the hand under the thigh, Gen. 24.2 and 47.29. This rite was formerly observed in those oaths which superiors exacted from their servants.

units.la: FERIAE. Vide SOLENNITAS.
units.tr: FEAST DAYS. See Solemnity.

units.la: FFROCES vrsæ conferuntur, 2. Sam. 17. 8.
units.tr: Foxes are compared to bears, 2 Sam. 17.8.

units.la: FERMENTVM: Fermento in Paschæ celebratione non vtendum, Exodi 12. 15. & 13. v. 6. 7. qui fermentum comedisset in Paschae celebratione, moriebatur, v. 15. Fermentum in oblationibus non permiscendum, Leuitic 2. 11. Fermentum in bonam partem, Matt. 13. 33. vbi Ecclesia comparatur fermento repositio in farina. In malam, pro pestilenti doctrina, Matth. 16. 6. Luc. 12. 1. Galat. 5. 9. Allegoricas pro eadem accipi potest & Leuit. 2. 11. & 6. 16. Deut. 16. 3. Fermentum veteris malitiæ expurgandum, 1. Corint. 5. 6. 7. 8. Fermentum parabola. V. PARABOLA.
units.tr: LEAVEN: Leaven is not to be used in the celebration of the Passover, Exod. 12.15; 13.6, 7. Whoever ate leaven during the Passover celebration was to die, v. 15. Leaven is not to be mixed into the offerings, Lev. 2.11. Leaven in a good sense, Matt. 13.33, where the Church is compared to leaven hidden in flour. In a bad sense, for pernicious teaching: Matt. 16.6; Luke 12.1; Gal. 5.9. It may be taken allegorically in the same sense, also Lev. 2.11; 6.16; Deut. 16.3. The leaven of old malice is to be purged out, 1 Cor. 5.6, 7, 8. Leaven as a parable. See Parable.

units.tr: IRON is taken from the dust: Job 38.2.

units.tr: IRON: Elisha makes iron float, 2 Kings 6.6.

units.la: REVM cœlum peccatoribus, Leuitic. 26.19. Deuter. 23. Ferreum iugum inobedientibus v.48. minatur eus,
units.tr: An IRON sky for sinners, Lev. 26.19; Deut. 28.23. He threatens an iron yoke for the disobedient, v. 48.

units.la: ILITAS magna in terra Ægypti,Genesis 41.47. à Deo Esa.55.10.Leuit.26.3.&c. Act.14.17.
units.tr: FERTILITY: great fertility in the land of Egypt, Gen. 41.47; from God, Isa. 55.10; Lev. 26.3, etc.; Acts 14.17.

units.la: OR spiritus,piis necessarius,Romano.12.11.Apocal 3. 6.
units.tr: FERVOUR of spirit, necessary for the godly, Rom. 12.11; Rev. 3.6.

units.la: NATIO bona commendatur, Hebr.4.11 2. Petr.3.12. Fenationis bonæ exempla: Abraham, Genef.10.6. Loth 19. Rachel.31 34.Vxor Manue,Iudic.13.10. David, 1 Samu. 48.2.Sam.15.14. Abigail,1.Sam.25.18. Semei,2.Sam.19. Mulieres, Matth. 28 8. Bartimæus cæcus, Marci 10. Maria,Lucæ 1.31.1.Pastores, 2.19.Zachæus, 19.6. duo discipuli,24.33.Samaritana,Ioan.4.29 Paulus, Act.20.16. Philipp.2.28.1.Thessal.2.17. Timotheus, 2. Timoth. 4.9. Titus,Tit.3.12.
units.tr: Good lending is commended, Heb. 4.11; 2 Pet. 3.12. Examples of good lending: Abraham, Gen. 10.6; Lot, 19; Rachel, 31.34; the wife of Manoah, Judg. 13.10; David, 1 Sam. 18.2; 2 Sam. 15.14; Abigail, 1 Sam. 25.18; Shimei, 2 Sam. 19; the women, Matt. 28.8; blind Bartimaeus, Mark 10; Mary, Luke 1.31; the shepherds, 2.19; Zacchaeus, 19.6; the two disciples, 24.33; the Samaritan woman, John 4.29; Paul, Acts 20.16; Phil. 2.28; 1 Thess. 2.17; Timothy, 2 Tim. 4.9; Titus, Titus 3.12.

units.la: Festinatio vitiosa cauenda, Prouerb.18.13.& 19.2.& 28.v.22. Esaiæ 59.7. Rom.3.15 1.Timot.5.22. Iac.1.19 Festinatio nimia corrigenda,2.Petr.3. v.8,9 10. Festinationis malæ exempla:Nutrix Miphibosepth: 2. Sam.4.4. Eunuchus Abdi,1.Reg.22.v.9.11.Cursores Assueri, Esth.3.15. Samsai criba,1.Esdr.4.23. Peccatores,Prouer.1.16.Esa.59.7.Rom. 3.15. Nabuchodonosor,Daniel.2.13.Iudei,Agg 1.9.quidam Militibus.Matt.27.48.Herodias filia,Marci 6.25. summi sacerdotes,15.1.
units.tr: Haste is to be avoided when it is faulty: Prov. 18.13; 19.2; 28.22; Isa. 59.7; Rom. 3.15; 1 Tim. 5.22; Jas. 1.19. Excessive haste is to be corrected: 2 Pet. 3.8, 9, 10. Examples of wrongful haste: the nurse of Mephibosheth, 2 Sam. 4.4; the eunuch Abdi, 1 Kings 22.9, 11; the runners of Ahasuerus, Esth. 3.15; Shamsai the scribe, 1 Esd. 4.23; sinners, Prov. 1.16; Isa. 59.7; Rom. 3.15; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 2.13; the Jews, Hag. 1.9; certain soldiers, Matt. 27.48; Herodias's daughter, Mark 6.25; the chief priests, 15.1.

units.la: VCAM in oculo fratris aspicere, Matth.7.3.quo in loco commnatur,non qui vel fratris, vel suos errores videt & infligit,sed qui in alienos intuetur, studio reprehendendi, ipse autem dissimulat.
units.tr: To see the splinter in a brother's eye, Matt. 7.3. The passage condemns not the person who sees and rebukes his brother's errors, or his own, but the one who looks at the faults of others, eager to find fault, while he himself overlooks his own.

units.la: TVM: Festum pro toto azymorum spatio, Matth.26. festorum institutio,Exodi 23.versic.13.14.15.16. Vide SOLENNITATES. Et Amos, 5.21. Matth. 26.5. Ioh. 2. 13.
units.tr: FEAST: the feast for the whole span of the unleavened bread, Matt. 26. The institution of the feasts, Exod. 23.13, 14, 15, 16. See Solemnities. Also Amos 5.21; Matt. 26.5; John 2.13.

units.la: vs,Iudææ Præfectus,Act.14.27.& 25.4.9.12.14.
units.tr: FESTUS, governor of Judaea, Acts 24.27; 25.4, 9, 12, 14.

units.la: vs à Christo maledicitur: Matt.21.19. Ficuum siccarum massa apponitur ulceri Ezechiæ Regis,qua etiam sanatur, Reg.20.7.Ficus parabola,Matt.24.32. Marc.13.28. Luc.13. (V,PARABOLA.)V.Gen.3.7.
units.tr: A FIG-TREE is cursed by Christ, Matt. 21.19. A mass of dried figs is applied to the ulcer of King Hezekiah, by which he is also healed, 2 Kings 20.7. The fig tree as a parable, Matt. 24.32; Mark 13.28; Luke 13. (See Parable.) See Gen. 3.7.

units.la: EVSSIO cauenda,Pro. 6.1.&c.& 17.18.& 26.16.Ec.8.16.& 9.19,&c.Nō tamē plane pro illo spōdere prohibet Soloiomo:quum hoc bonorum exemplis confirmetur (Gen. 42 37: & 43.8.9. & doceatur Eccle.29.19):sed temere tenda, aut si fideiusseris, mox fides liberanda. (Vide Sudere.)
units.tr: Suretyship is to be avoided: Prov. 6.1, etc.; 17.18; 26.16; Eccles. 8.16; 9.19, etc. Yet Solomon does not entirely forbid standing surety, since this is confirmed by the examples of good men (Gen. 42.37; 43.8, 9) and taught in Ecclesiasticus 29.19; but one must not rashly undertake it, and if you have stood surety, you must soon free yourself from the bond. (See Suretyship.)

units.la: FIDELIS Deus dicitur, id est, verax, benignissimé & firme ilans prom iis gratuitis erga suos, Deut.7.9. & 32. 14513. Esai. 49 7. 1.Corinth. 1.9. & 10.13.2.Corinth. 1 Thessal.5.24. 2.Thess.3.3. Hebr.10.23.& 11.11.1.Petr.4. Ioan.1 9 ]
units.tr: God is called FAITHFUL, that is, true, most kindly and firmly holding to the gratuitous promises made to his own: Deut. 7.9; 32.4; Isa. 49.7; 1 Cor. 1.9; 10.13; 2 Cor. 1; 1 Thess. 5.24; 2 Thess. 3.3; Heb. 10.23; 11.11; 1 Pet. 4; 1 John 1.9.

units.tr: Jesus Christ is FAITHFUL, God-man: 2 Tim. 2.13; Heb. 3.2; Rev. 1.5; 3.14; 19.11. The word of God is called faithful, that is, true and unchanging, Ps. 19.8; 89.29; Isa. 25.1; 1 Tim. 1.15; 3.15; 4.9; 2 Tim. 2.11; Titus 1.9; Rev. 21.5; 22.6.

units.la: FIDELIS pro constanti, quique praestat reuera quod promisit,1.Thess.5.24. Fidelem seu fidum sermonem vocat Iesus, Tit.1.9. cui merito fides adhiberi possit, siue qui non quam fallat, quamobrem etiam veritatis nomine signatur, Ioann.17.17. Nomen fidelis nunc iis tribuitur ... nibus, qui fidem & religionem Christianam profitentur, 1.Corinth.7.v.12.13 14.nunc solis electis conuenit, 1.Timoth. 4.10.
units.tr: FAITHFUL means steadfast, one who in fact performs what he has promised: 1 Thess. 5.24. Jesus calls it a faithful or trustworthy saying, Titus 1.9, which may rightly be relied upon, or one who will not deceive; for this reason it is also marked with the name of truth, John 17.17. The name "faithful" is now given to those who profess the Christian faith and religion, 1 Cor. 7.12, 13, 14; and now it belongs only to the elect, 1 Tim. 4.10.

Fratres Christi, Psalm.22.23. Vide CHRISTVS. Gens sancta,1.Petri 2.9.gloria Dei, 2. Corinth.8. mundi Domini,1.Corinth.3.22.mundi & Angelorum, dices futuri, 1.Cor.6.v.2.3. units.tr: FAITHFUL: In Holy Scripture the faithful are named from faith, not so much because they keep a given faith, but because they believe the promises. All the faithful are equal through faith, 1 Pet. 3; conformed to Christ, Rom. 8.29; 2 Cor.; given to Christ, Ps. 101.6; Isa. 8.18; John 6.37, 39; 8.29; 17.24; 18.9. They are the household of God and fellow citizens of the saints, Eph. 2.19; Heb. 3.6; 1 Pet. 2.5. Elected before the foundation of the world, Eph. 1.4; exposed to slanders, 1 Pet. 4.16. Children of light, Eph. 5.8, both because they are illumined in themselves by the true light and walk in it, and because they also shine before others, Matt. 5; so much so that they even condemn and convict the lives of the wicked, Rom. 2.27. Brothers of Christ, Ps. 22.23. See Christ. A holy nation, 1 Pet. 2.9; the glory of God, 2 Cor. 8; lords of the world, 1 Cor. 3.22; of the world and of the angels, who will judge the world in the future, 1 Cor. 6.2, 3. See Saints.

units.tr: FAITHFUL: living stones, 1 Pet. 2.5; lights in the world, Phil. 2.15; exposed to the cross, 2 Tim. 3.12; 1 Thess. 3.3; 1 Pet. 2.21; 3.19; 5.9. (See Godly, and Affliction in the world.) Few, Ps. 59.16; Rom. 10.16; 1 Cor. 1.21; 2 Thess. 2.10; 1 John ... have the Spirit, Rom. 8.22; Jas. 1.18. They are holy, Dan. 1.7; 8.26, 28; 1 Cor. 1.2; 2 Cor. 1.1; Eph. 1.1; 2 Thess. 1.10; Heb. 13.24; 1 Pet. 1.2, 15. Priests and kings, Rom. 12.1; 1 Pet. 2.5, 9; Rev. 1.6; 5.10. Temples of God, Lev. 26.12; 1 Cor. 3.16; 6.16; 2 Cor. 6.16; Eph. 2.20, 21, 22; 4.30; 1 Pet. 2.5, in whom God dwells through the Holy Spirit, Rom. 8.11. The assembly of the faithful is likened to a great city, that is, the new Jerusalem, made from the faithful themselves as if from cut stones, as is written in Isa. 54; Rev. 21. Hence also the expressions "to build" and "edification", Rom. 14.19. See Edify, Eph. 2.21.

units.tr: The servants of God are so called, that is, those who are faithful and steadfast in the word and in the profession of godliness: Num. 12. 7; 1 Sam. 2. 35; 3; Matt. 24. 45; 25. 21, 22, 23; Eph. 6. 21; Col. 1. 7; 4. 9; 1 Tim. 1. 12; 2 Tim. 2. 2; Heb. 3. 6; 1 Pet. 5. 12; Acts 2, verses 10, 13. Faithful women: 1 Tim. 3. 11. Faithful towards neighbours: 1 Sam. 22. 14; Ps. 101. 2, 3; Prov. 3; Dan. 6. 4; Luke 16. 11, 12. Things are called faithful in various ways: certain things, devoted to God and held by him in a singular kindness: 1 Sam. 2. 35; 20. 28; 2 Sam. 7. 16; 1 Kings 11. 38; Prov. 6. 18; Isa. 1. 21, 26; 7. 10; 22. 23, 25; 33. Faithful promises of God, that is, ratified and unchangeable: Isa. 55. 3; 1. 13. 34. A faithful interpretation, that is, true and most certain: Dan.

units.la: ...in sacris literis variè capitur:
units.tr: ...is taken in various ways in Holy Scripture:

units.la: [?]rimò, significat veritatem & constantiam in seruandis promissis, Psal.25.10.& 86.15, Rom.3.3.
units.tr: First, it signifies truth and constancy in keeping promises: Ps. 25. 10; 86. 15; Rom. 3. 3.

units.la: secundò,accipitur pro ipsa doctrina fidei, seu pro Euangelio, cui creditur,idque per Metonymiam subiecti,Rom.10. Ephes.4.5.1.Tim.1.19. Hoc sensu dicitur fides Apostolica, seu doctrina.
units.tr: Secondly, it is taken for the very doctrine of faith, or for the Gospel, which is believed, and this by metonymy of the subject: Rom. 10; Eph. 4. 5; 1 Tim. 1. 19. In this sense it is called the apostolic faith, or doctrine.

units.la: tertiò,sumitur pro complemento, seu impletione promissionum diuinarum in Veteri Testamento factarum,seu rebus ipsis promissis olim , & suo tempore exhibitis, §.3.23.
units.tr: Thirdly, it is taken for the fulfilment or completion of the divine promises made in the Old Testament, or for the things themselves promised, once displayed in their proper time: §. 3. 23.

units.la: quartò , capitur pro obligatione illa , facta in Baptismo, profitendi veram religionem,&ad credendum in hunc quem, in cuius nomen baptizamur, 1.Tim.5.11.12.
units.tr: Fourthly, it is taken for that obligation, made in baptism, of professing the true religion and of believing in him into whose name we are baptized: 1 Tim. 5. 11, 12.

units.la: quintò , denotat externam religionis & fidei professionem, Iac.2.24.
units.tr: Fifthly, it denotes the external profession of religion and faith: Jas 2. 24.

units.la: sextò,significat notitiam, assensionem & persuasionem, gratia Dei, temporariam, vt quæ in Christo radices agant, sicut dicitur Luc.8.13. Quæ species dicitur fides historica.
units.tr: Sixthly, it signifies knowledge, assent and persuasion, temporary grace of God, such as things that take root in Christ, as is said in Luke 8. 13. This kind is called historical faith.

units.la: septimò,declarat notitiam beneficij Christi, qualis est in Rom.11.20.
units.tr: Seventhly, it declares knowledge of the benefit of Christ, such as is in Rom. 11. 20.

units.la: octauò,sumitur pro fidelitate in faciendo officio, & a fraude & furandi cupiditate alieno, studiosoque seruandi atque tuendi aliorum facultates & bona, Tit.2.10.
units.tr: Eighthly, it is taken for fidelity in performing one's duty, and for abstaining from fraud and the desire to steal, and for an earnest keeping and protecting of the goods and property of others: Titus 2. 10.

units.la: nonò,idem est quod iustitia, Psal.119.75.
units.tr: Ninthly, it is the same as righteousness: Ps. 119. 75.

units.la: decimò , denotat quandoque certam persuasionem, de aliquo effectu miraculoso , conceptam ex revelatione aut promissione singulari,1.Corin.12.9.& 13.2.Mat.17.20.Luc.17.6. Hanc appellant fidem miraculorum.
units.tr: Tenthly, it sometimes denotes a certain persuasion about some miraculous effect, conceived from a special revelation or promise: 1 Cor. 12. 9; 13. 2; Matt. 17. 20; Luke 17. 6. This they call the faith of miracles.

units.la: undecimò,indicat fiduciam consequendi bonum aliquod externum & corporale,Act.14.9.
units.tr: Eleventhly, it indicates confidence of obtaining some external and bodily good: Acts 14. 9.

units.la: duodecimò , vsurpatur pro certa notitia & securitate liberatis Christianę,in reb.adiophoris seu indifferentibus, Roman.14.v.1.22. Tu fidem habes,hoc est , tu certus es ac securus libertatis Christianæ, in rebus adiaphoris.
units.tr: Twelfthly, it is used for the certain knowledge and security of Christian liberty in things adiaphora, or indifferent: Rom. 14, verses 1, 22. "You have faith," that is, you are certain and secure of Christian liberty in things adiaphora.

units.la: Decimotertiò, accipitur etiam pro spe, per metonymiam causæ efficientis, 1.Pet.1.5. vbi dicitur, nos virtute Dei custodiri per fidem ad salutem: cùm tamen per spem propriè hoc fiat. Est enim illa salutis plenè occupandæ patiens expectatio.
units.tr: Thirteenthly, it is also taken for hope, by metonymy of the efficient cause: 1 Pet. 1. 5, where it is said that we are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, although this is properly done through hope. For that is a patient expectation of fully attaining salvation.

units.la: Decimoquartò, tanquam μέτρον vocabulum sumitur, pro constantia in officio, aut instabilitate, 1.Samuel. 23.
units.tr: Fourteenthly, taken as a term of measure, it is used for steadfastness in duty, or for instability: 1 Sam. 23.

units.la: Decimoquintò, significat studium & zelum in observanda religione Christiana, Rom.1.8.
units.tr: Fifteenthly, it signifies zeal and eagerness in observing the Christian religion: Rom. 1. 8.

units.la: Decimosextò, denotat speciali ter fidem salutificam & salutificans dicitur, fidei talis datur definitio: Fides est firma & constans animi persuasio, qua certus est apud se unusquisque fidelium, non modò verum ac firmum esse in verbum Dei, ac præsertim promissiones Dei de gratuita per Christum reconciliatione: sed etiam istas (à Spiritu Sancto edoctus) credit ad se proprie & peculiariter pertinere: qua, inquam, universalem illam propositionem vitæ æternæ per sanguinem Christi omnibus credentibus acquisitæ singuli amplectuntur, ac sibi ipsis applicant. Aliter: Fides est, firma nostræ in Christo electionis persuasio. à Paulo sic definita: Fides, est hypostasis rerum quæ sperantur, & ἔλεγχος eorum, quæ non videntur, Hebr.11.1. Debet enim fides de rebus sperandis, non visis, nec apparentibus, perinde certò statuere, ea iam subsistere præsentes, & in conspectu haberi. Fides ad res medias, seu indifferentes restringitur. Rom.14.22.
units.tr: Sixteenthly, it denotes especially saving faith, and it is called saving and saves. The definition of faith is given thus: Faith is a firm and constant persuasion of the mind, by which each one of the faithful is certain within himself, not only that the word of God is true and firm, and especially the promises of God concerning gratuitous reconciliation through Christ, but also (taught by the Holy Spirit) believes that these things pertain to himself, properly and personally; by which, I say, each one embraces and applies to himself that universal proposition of eternal life, acquired for all believers through the blood of Christ. Otherwise: Faith is a firm persuasion of our election in Christ. Paul defined it thus: Faith is the substance [ὑπόστασις] of things hoped for, and the proof [ἔλεγχος] of things not seen, Heb. 11. 1. For faith ought to determine with equal certainty concerning things hoped for, not seen, nor appearing, that they already subsist, and are held in sight as present. Faith is restricted to middle things, or indifferent ones: Rom. 14. 22.

units.tr: Faith ought not to be feigned, 1 Tim. 1.5. It is the support of the godly, 2 Cor. 1.24. It is called the fruit of the lips, Isa. 57, because it comes from hearing, Rom. 10.17. It is the mother of invocation, Rom. 10.14. Dead, without works, James 2.17, 26. See INVOCATION. Paul calls it mutual faith, Rom. 1.12, so that he may help them and they in turn may help him. Faith that is necessary: Matt. 9.2, 22; 21.21. John 8.24; 18. Acts 8.37; 16.31; 20.21. Gal. 5.22. 1 Tim. 1.19; 6.11. 2 Tim. 2.22. Heb. 11.6. James 1.6. 1 Pet. 5.9. 1 John 3.23. It works through love, Gal. 5.6. Each person requires his own faith, Hab. 2.4; John 3.36; Rom. 1.17; Gal. 3.11; Heb. 10.38. Faith is in some measure called a work, John 6.29. The sense is: this is finally the work that God demands from you, that you believe in him. Faith is therefore improperly called a work, as the law of faith is by Paul, Rom. 3.27; see also 2 Thess. 1.11; Phil. 1.6. It is rare on earth, Luke 18.8, and by no means subject to men, 2 Cor. 1.24.

units.tr: Faith ought not to be feigned (1 Tim. 1.5). It is the support of the godly (2 Cor. 1.24). It is called the fruit of the lips (Isa. 57). It comes by hearing (Rom. 10.17), and is the mother of invocation (Rom. 10.14). Faith without works is dead (James 2.17, 26). See VSICARE. Paul calls faith "mutual" (Rom. 1.12), so that he might help them and they in turn might help him. Faith that is necessary (Matt. 9.2, 22; 21.21. John 8.24; 18. Acts 8.37; 16.31; 20.21. Gal. 5.22. 1 Tim. 1.19; 6.11. 2 Tim. 2.22. Heb. 11.6. James 1.6. 1 Pet. 5.9. 1 John 3.23). Faith works through love (Gal. 5.6). Each person needs his own faith (Hab. 2.4. John 3.36. Rom. 1.17. Gal. 3.11. Heb. 10.38). Faith is in some measure called a work (John 6.29). The sense is: this is at last the work which God demands of you, that you believe in him. Faith is therefore improperly called a work, as Paul calls it the law of faith (Rom. 3.27); see also 2 Thess. 1.11 and Phil. 1.6. It is rare on earth (Luke 18.8), and by no means subject to men (2 Cor. 1.24).

units.tr: Faith The ordinary cause of faith is the Word of God (John 17.21. Rom. 10.17), whence it is also called the fruit of the lips (Isa. 57.19). The communication of faith, according to Paul, is (Philem. 6) the duties of kindness flowing toward the saints from a living faith. The Domestics of faith are those whom Paul calls such; see Domestics of faith. The effects of faith: it makes sons of God (Gal. 3.26); it justifies (Gen. 15.6. Hab. 2.4. Acts 13.39. Rom. 1.17; 3.22, 25, 30; 4.5, 24; 5.1; 10.4, 6, 10. Gal. 2.16; 3.6. Eph. 2.8); it makes us not ashamed (Rom. 9.33; 10.11. 1 Pet. 2.6); it purifies hearts (Acts 15.9); it saves (Luke 7.50; 8.12. Eph. 2.8. 1 Pet. 1.9). The remaining fruits of faith: (Dan. 6.23. Matt. 8.13; 9.29; 15.28; 17.20; 21.22. Mark 2.5; 5.34; 7.29; 9.23; 10.52; 11.23. units.la: ¶Fidei Implicitæ patroni,satis esse statuunt, si in genere credant homines,quod credit Ecclesia, nec de singulis intelligendis laborant. Et hæc fides dicitur vulgò Fides implicita. Ad eam euertendam locus accommodatus,Abac.2.4.Rom.1.17.& 16.19.1.Cor.11.28.2.Pet.1.5.
units.tr: ¶ The advocates of implicit faith hold that it is enough if men believe in general what the Church believes, and do not labour to understand the particulars. This faith is commonly called implicit faith. A passage suited to overturning it: Hab. 2.4. Rom. 1.17; 16.19. 1 Cor. 11.28. 2 Pet. 1.5.

A multitude of believers, and noble men and women of Thessalonica, Gentiles, Acts 17 vv. 11, 12. Crispus, 18.8. A multitude of believers, 19.17, and 21 vv. 20, 25. Romans, Rom. 1.8. Corinthians, 1 Cor. 3.5, and 15 vv. 1, 2. Philippians, Phil. 2.17. Ephesians, Eph. 1.15. Colossians, Col. 1 vv. 3, 4. Thessalonians, 1 Thess. 1 vv. 3, 8, and 3.6; 2 Thess. 1.3. Philemon, Philem. vv. 4, 5. Thyatira, Rev. 2.19. That faith is called a work is shown from John 6.29, Phil. 1.6, and 2 Thess. 1.11; see above, FAITH is called a work. And that faith without works does not justify, that is, does not make a man righteous before God, is shown from 1 Cor. 13.2, Gal. 5.6, and James 2.24. Likewise, the Papists contend that faith does not make us certain of the free forgiveness of sins. See CERTAIN.

units.la: FIDES temporaria, altera fidei species, Matt.13. v. 5. 6. 7. Marc. 4.v.4.5.6.7. Hebr.6.4.5. Fidei temporariæ exempla, Vide APOSTASIA.
units.tr: Temporary faith, another kind of faith, Matt. 13.5, 6, 7; Mark 4.4, 5, 6, 7; Heb. 6.4, 5. For examples of temporary faith, see APOSTASY.

units.la: FIDELITAS Est dictorum, promissorúmque constantia. Infidelitas est inconstantia: cui adiunctæ sunt Vanitas, & leuitas animi, per quam facilè & sine vlla vel sine probabili ratione à pactione discedimus. Vanitas vide suo loco.
units.tr: Faithfulness is steadfastness in words and promises. Unfaithfulness is inconstancy, to which are joined vanity and levity of mind, through which we easily and without any, or without any plausible, reason depart from a pact. Vanity: see in its place.

units.la: FIDELITAS seruanda est, Prouerb. 25.14. & 28.20. Luc. 16,10. 1. Cor. 4 2. Eph. v.5.6, Col.3.22. 1. Tim.6.v.1.2. Tit. 2. v.9. 10. 1. Petr. 2. 18. Fidelitatis exempla: Eliezer seruus Abraham, Gen.15. 2.& 24 33. Iacob, 31.40. Ioseph.39.8.& 41.v.47. 8.Moses, Num.12.7. Heb.3.2. Rahab, Ios.2.4. Iosue, Ios.6.17. Nuntij, v. 23. Principes Israel, 9. 18. Iosue & fortissimi belatores.10.7. Samuel, 1. Sam.3.v.19.20. Ionathas, 19.1, &20. v.32.35. Dauid, 22. v.14.23. & 24.8.& 26. v.9. 10. Viri Iabes Galaad, 31.12. Vrias, 2. Sam. 11. 11. Ioab. 12. 27. 26. Ethai Gethæus.15.22. Populus, 18.3. Iuda, 20.2, Abisai, 21.17. Elias, 1. Reg.18.v.15.16. Iosaba filia Ioram, 2. Reg. 12.2. Ioiada, v.4. tres Viri, 1. Paral. 11.18.19. Aedificatores Templi, 2. Paral.34.12. Deus, 1. Corinth.10.13.1. Timot. 15. & 4. 9. Paulus, Gal.6.17. Syluanus: 1. Petr.5.12. Antipas, Apoc. 2.13.
units.tr: Faithfulness must be kept: Prov. 25.14 and 28.20; Luke 16.10; 1 Cor. 4.2; Eph. 5.5, 6; Col. 3.22; 1 Tim. 6.1, 2; Titus 2.9, 10; 1 Pet. 2.18. Examples of faithfulness: Eliezer, servant of Abraham, Gen. 15.2 and 24.33; Jacob, 31.40; Joseph, 39.8 and 41.47; Moses, Num. 12.7; Heb. 3.2; Rahab, Josh. 2.4; Joshua, Josh. 6.17; the messengers, v. 23; the princes of Israel, 9.18; Joshua and the most valiant warriors, 10.7; Samuel, 1 Sam. 3.19, 20; Jonathan, 19.1 and 20.32, 35; David, 22.14, 23, and 24.8, and 26.9, 10; the men of Jabesh-gilead, 31.12; Uriah, 2 Sam. 11.11; Joab, 12.27; Ittai the Gittite, 15.22; the people, 18.3; Judah, 20.2; Abishai, 21.17; Elijah, 1 Kings 18.15, 16; Jehosheba, daughter of Joram, 2 Kings 12.2; Jehoiada, v. 4; three men, 1 Chron. 11.18, 19; the builders of the Temple, 2 Chron. 34.12; God, 1 Cor. 10.13; 1 Tim. 1.5 and 4.9; Paul, Gal. 6.17; Silvanus, 1 Pet. 5.12; Antipas, Rev. 2.13.

units.la: FIDUCIA in solo Deo collocanda, Esai 2. 22. Ier.17.5.7. Zach. 4.6. Psalm.20.v.8.9. Fiducia in Pastoribus requiritur, Eph. 6.19. Fiduciæ exempla: Fratres. Philip. 1.14. [Fiducialiter, 1.
units.tr: [Trust must be placed in God alone: Isa. 2.22; Jer. 17.5, 7; Zech. 4.6; Ps. 20.8, 9. Trust in ministers is required, Eph. 6.19. Examples of trust: the brothers, Phil. 1.14. Boldly, 1.
Confidently, freely: Ps. 12.6; Prov. 3.5, 26, and 14.26; Isa. 12 and 14.30; Hos. 2.18; Acts 9.28, 29, and 14.3, and 18.26.]

units.la: FIGMENTVM [Psalm. 103.14 Habac.2.18. ] de fictor nullo iure conqueri potest, Roman.9.20. Esa.45.9. Ieren 18.6
units.tr: FIGMENT [Ps. 103.14; Hab. 2.18] No one can lawfully complain against the maker: Rom. 9.20; Isa. 45.9; Jer. 18.6.

units.la: FIGVLVS ex terra quaecunque vult pro arbitrio fingit, Ie 18.6. Rom.9.21. V. Psal.29. Apoc.2.27. Mat.27.7.
units.tr: POTTER: from earth, he shapes whatever he wishes at his discretion: Jer. 18.6; Rom. 9.21; see Ps. 2.9; Rev. 2.27; Matt. 27.7.

units.la: FIGVRA [ character. Hebr.1.3. forma, Ezech.43.11. Species vultus & oris.2 Reg.1.7. Mens. Dan.4.33. Mundi species, splendor, facies, 1. Cor.7.31. Typus, 1. Cor.10. verf.6. vestigium, Ioan.20.25.
units.tr: FIGURE [impression: Heb. 1.3; form: Ezek. 43.11; appearance and countenance of the face: 2 Kings 1.7; mind: Dan. 4.33; appearance, splendour, face of the world: 1 Cor. 7.31; type: 1 Cor. 10.6; trace, mark: John 20.25.

units.la: Figurae, Imagines, 2. Reg.23,24. Amos, 5.26. Act.7.43. militudines Num.12 8, Stigmata, notae, Leu.19.28.]
units.tr: Figures, images: 2 Kings 23.24; Amos 5.26; Acts 7.43; likenesses: Num. 12.8; marks, brands, signs: Lev. 19.28.]

units.la: FILIA non prostituenda, Leuit.19.29. Filia pro nepte Exodi 2.21. vt liquet ex Exodi 3.1. Filiarum appellatio tota posteritas includitur, Luc.1.5. Filiae nomen etiam vrbibus tribuitur, Matt. 21.5. cuius rei exempla plura tant in Threnis Filiae Ierusalem, pro, mulieres Ierosolymitanae, Luc.23.28.
units.tr: DAUGHTER not to be prostituted: Lev. 19.29. A daughter for a granddaughter: Exod. 2.21, as is clear from Exod. 3.1. Under the name of daughters the whole posterity is included: Luke 1.5. The name daughter is also given to cities: Matt. 21.5. Many examples of this are found in the Lamentations: "Daughter of Jerusalem" for the women of Jerusalem: Luke 23.28.

units.la: [FILIA, filiae, partim de sponsa Christi Ecclesia, partim piis animabus dicitur. Saepius autem nomine filiae & filiarum, vrbes, oppida, prouinciae, villae, pagi intelliguntur, ex Hebraeorum idiotismo.
units.tr: [DAUGHTER, daughters, is said partly of the Church, the bride of Christ, and partly of pious souls. But more often under the name of daughter and daughters are understood cities, towns, provinces, villages and districts, from the Hebrew idiom.

units.la: Filiae, pro ramis arborum, Genef.49,22. filiae pharethi 1. sagittae. Thren.3.13. filiae sanguisugae, 1. hirudines, Pro 30.15. filiae carminis, 1. voces canorae, symphoniae musi les, filiae Belial, & hominum, 1. mulieres impiae, Gen.6.v.1 4.1. Sam.1.16. Confidentes filiae, 1, vrbes luxu diffluentes omnia tuta sibi somniantes, Esa.32.9. filiae delicatae, vrb opulentissimae, Ierem.49.4. filiae multitudinis, vrbes f quentissimae, Cant.7.4. filiae vrbis, mulieres Ierosolyr tanae, Thren.3.51.
units.tr: Daughters, for the branches of trees: Gen. 49.22; daughters of the bow, that is, arrows: Lam. 3.13; daughters of the leech, that is, leeches: Prov. 30.15; daughters of song, that is, tuneful voices, concerts of music; daughters of Belial and of men, that is, impious women: Gen. 6.1, 4; 1 Sam. 1.16. Confident daughters, that is, cities flowing with luxury, dreaming that everything is safe for themselves: Isa. 32.9. Delicate daughters, the most wealthy city: Jer. 49.4. Daughters of a multitude, the most populous cities: Song 7.4. Daughter of the city, the women of Jerusalem: Lam. 3.51.

units.la: Filia vaga, Iudaea, Ierem.31.22. filia populi, Ierusal sepe apud Ieremiam. vnum quodque Iudeae oppia Esai.22.24.]
units.tr: Wandering daughter, Judea: Jer. 31.22. Daughter of the people, Jerusalem, often in Jeremiah. Each single town of Judea: Isa. 22.24.]

units.la: FILIVS eum significat, humano more, qui ex viro & m liere ortus & natus est. filius hominis, homo. filius, a ptiuus, seu adoptatus ab homine, Actor.7.21. Hebr.11. Subditus & obsequens 2.Reg.8,9,& 16.7. filius annorum triginta, 1. annos 30. natus, & sic de caeteris. (Vide 1. Sa 13.1.& 2. Sam.5.4. Ierem.52 1.& sa pisf.in hist.Regum, hus Olei, cliúus vberrimus & pinguis, Esai .5.1. Ipro ne-pote, 2. Sam.19.24. Prouerb.13.22.& 17.6. Ierem .27.7. Ezech.37.25. pro posteris ex aliqua familia oriundis, Matthaei 22.42. Filij nomen pullo asini attributum legitur, 21 5. Filius sapiens extra periculum est, Prouerb.29.28. Filij pro parentibus non puniendi Deut.24.16.2.Reg.14.6. Ierem. 31.29.30.Ezech. 18. versi, 4.19.20. Filij erudiendi, & corripiendi, Prouerb,13.24, & 19,18 & 29.v.15.17.Hebr.12. ver.8.9.
units.tr: SON denotes, in the human manner, one who is born and begotten of a man and a woman. Son of man means man. A son, adopted or taken as a son by a man: Acts 7.21; Heb. 11. A subject and obedient son: 2 Kings 8.9 and 16.7. A son of thirty years, that is, thirty years old, and so on for others. (See 1 Sam. 13.1 and 2 Sam. 5.4; Jer. 52.1, and the histories of the Kings.) A son of oil, a very fruitful and fat hill: Isa. 5.1. A grandson: 2 Sam. 19.24; Prov. 13.22 and 17.6; Jer. 27.7; Ezek. 37.25. For descendants sprung from some family: Matt. 22.42. The name son is attributed to the colt of an ass: read 21.5. A wise son is out of danger: Prov. 29.28. Sons are not to be punished for their parents: Deut. 24.16; 2 Kings 14.6; Jer. 31.29, 30; Ezek. 18 vv. 4, 19, 20. Sons are to be trained and corrected: Prov. 13.24, 19.18, 29.15, 17; Heb. 12 vv. 8, 9.

units.la: Lii Belial, pro hominibus nequam, 1. Reg. 21.10. Filij Carnis, pro naturali modo procreatis, Roman .9.8. seu, quorum non alia ratione pater est Abraham, quám ea ipsa, qua solent, consueto naturae ordine, homines ex hominibus gigni, qui alias filii secundum carnem dicuntur, Gal.4,v.23.29. Filii contumaciae Hebraeis dicutur Ephes.2.2. homines praefracti & contumaciae dediti. Filius Dei Iesus Christus. Hebr.1.5. dicitur vnctus esse, Esa. 61,1. Hebr.1.9. quod eatenus intelligatur, quatenus Verbum caro factum est, effuso in eum Spiritu sine mensura Ioan.3.34. si quidem omnis in eo Deitas corporaliter sibi domum fixit, Col.2.9. In Filio locutus fuisse dicitur Deus, Hebr .1.1. sed secus quàm in Prophetis .Fuit enim Filius, & est veré & σωματικῶς siue ϑεοδίδας Deus, Coloss.2.9. Prophetae veró duntaxat divino Spiritu acti, 1.Pet.1.21.
units.tr: Sons of Belial, for worthless men: 1 Kings 21.10. Sons of the flesh, for those procreated in the natural way: Rom. 9.8; or, those whose father Abraham is by no other reason than that by which men are commonly begotten of men in the usual order of nature; these are otherwise called sons according to the flesh: Gal. 4.23, 29. Sons of disobedience, a Hebraism in Eph. 2.2: men stubborn and given over to obstinacy. The Son of God is Jesus Christ. Heb. 1.5. He is said to have been anointed: Isa. 61.1; Heb. 1.9. This is to be understood so far as the Word was made flesh, the Spirit being poured out upon him without measure: John 3.34, since all the Deity dwells bodily in him: Col. 2.9. God is said to have spoken in the Son, Heb. 1.1, but otherwise than in the Prophets. For the Son was and is truly and bodily [σωματικῶς], or God-taught [θεοδίδας], God: Col. 2.9. The Prophets, however, were only moved by the divine Spirit: 1 Pet. 1.21.

units.la: Filii Dei, propiis ex Sethi posteris oriundis, Gen.6.2. sicut filiae hominum, pro impiis filiabus ex Caini familia. vers.2 pro piis Deo charis,& Christi cohaeredibus, Matt.5.v.9.45.Ioan.1.12. Roman.8.9.1.Ioan.3.9.vt explicat Paulus, Rom.8.v. 16.17.Filii Dei dicuntur etiam Angeli. Iob.1.6. Psal.89.7. Vide ANGELVS. Item Principes, Ps.82. 6.Ephraim primogenitus dicitur, Ier. 31.9. sed longè secus quam Christus, qui est vnigenitus Dei Filius, Ioan.1.18. & 3.v.16.18.1. Ioan.4.9.vt illud Hebr.1,5. omittam, è cuius dicti consideratione diligenti id ipsum manifeste euincitur.
units.tr: Sons of God, properly, those descended from the posterity of Seth: Gen. 6.2, just as the daughters of men are impious daughters from the family of Cain, v. 2. Pious people dear to God and fellow heirs of Christ: Matt. 5.9, 45; John 1.12; Rom. 8.9; 1 John 3.9, as Paul explains, Rom. 8.16, 17. Angels are also called sons of God: Job 1.6; Ps. 89.7; see ANGEL. Likewise princes: Ps. 82.6. Ephraim is called firstborn: Jer. 31.9, but far otherwise than Christ, who is the only-begotten Son of God: John 1.18; 3.16, 18; 1 John 4.9. I pass over that passage, Heb. 1.5, from whose careful consideration the same thing is clearly proved.

units.la: Filii Diaboli qui dicantur, Ioan.8.44. Vide DIABOLVS. Filii Ecclesiae, Vide ECCLESIA: Filii filiorum, pro nepotibus, atque adeò tota interdum posteritate, Ierem. 27.7. Ezech.37.25. Filii Hebraeis generaliter dicuntur, qui sunt alicui rei peculiariter destinati & addicti: vt, FILI; Gehennae, dicuntur, qui exitio & interitui sunt addicti, Matt. 23.15. Filius Hominis, pro humana Christi natura, Ioan. 27. vbi notandum est, quòd Filij hominis nomen r[?] nisi vni Christo, de se loquenti tribuatur in Euangel[?] historia. Filius hominis, seu homo Christus dicitur [?] cœlo descendisse, Ioan.3.13. primò incarnationis diuinæ naturæ: secundò modi conceptionis respectu. Idem cœlo esse dicitur Ioan.6.62. per communicationem idiomatum, qua proprietas diuinæ naturæ tribuitur humanæ naturæ in concreto, vt summa illa duarum in Christo substantiarum coniunctio significetur. Filij hominum pro ijs hominibus, 1.Sam.1.19. Marc.3.28. Apocal.1.13. Filij Illiues damnantur, Prou.13.1. Filij iniquitatis pro hominibus iniquissimis, 2 Sam.3.34. &7.10. Filij irę pro irę destinatis, & damnatis coram Deo, Ephes.2.3. Filii lucis, pro hominibus lucis participibus, seu quos Deus Spiritus sancti luce illustrauit, Lucæ 16.8. Ioann.12.36. Eph.5.8. quos aliàs Paulus πνευματικὸς, hoc est, spirituales vocat, 1 Cor. 2.15.
units.tr: Sons of the Devil, so called: John 8.44; see DEVIL. Sons of the Church: see CHURCH. Sons of sons, for grandchildren, and sometimes the whole posterity: Jer. 27.7; Ezek. 37.25. In Hebrew, sons are generally those who are particularly destined and devoted to something: thus the sons of Gehenna are those devoted to destruction and ruin: Matt. 23.15. Son of Man, for the human nature of Christ: John 3.27. Here it must be noted that in the Gospel history the name Son of Man is attributed to no one but Christ speaking of himself. The Son of Man, or man Christ, is said to have descended from heaven, John 3.13: first, with respect to the incarnation of the divine nature; second, with respect to the manner of conception. The same is said to be in heaven, John 6.62, by communication of properties, by which the property of the divine nature is attributed to the human nature in the concrete, so that that supreme union of the two substances in Christ is signified. Sons of men, for those men: 1 Sam. 1.19; Mark 3.28; Rev. 1.13. Wicked sons are condemned: Prov. 13.1. Sons of iniquity, for the most wicked men: 2 Sam. 3.34 and 7.10. Sons of wrath, for those destined and condemned to wrath before God: Eph. 2.3. Sons of light, for men who share in the light, or whom God has illumined with the light of the Holy Spirit: Luke 16.8; John 12.36; Eph. 5.8; whom Paul elsewhere calls spiritual [πνευματικὸς], that is, spiritual: 1 Cor. 2.15.

units.la: Filij mortis, pro morti addictis, seu qui capitalis criminis rei sunt. 1. Sam.20.3. &26.16. 2 Sam.12,5. pro iam morti tradendis, Ps.79.11, &102.21. Filij promissionis Hebræi dicuntur, quibus Deus promissiones destinauit, Rom.8. Gal.4.28. &quos Deus dat Abrahæ, quia sic illi vitæ est, vt eos in Abrahæ illo semine adoptet, per quod ipse Abraham, & eius germana posteritas cœlestis hereditatis fit particeps. Aliâs dicuntur Filij per promissionem: Gal.4.28. Item Filij secundum Spiritum, hoc est, diuinitus & spirituali ratione procreati, Gal.4.29. Filij pacis, Hebraico more vocantur, qui doctrinæ pacis, siue euangelij fauent, Luc.10.6. Filius perditionis, pro exitio voto, Ioan.17.12. Sic autem dicitur Iudas proditor, non modò quia periit, sed etiam quia huic exitio erat destinatus ac deuotus, vt patet ex Act.1.16. &4.v.27.28. Filij prophetarum, Vide Prophetæ.
units.tr: Sons of death: those given over to death, or those guilty of a capital crime. 1 Sam. 20:3; 26:16; 2 Sam. 12:5. Those who are now to be handed over to death: Ps. 79:11; 102:21. Sons of promise: the Hebrews are so called, those to whom God addressed his promises, Rom. 8; Gal. 4:28, and whom God gives to Abraham, because it is life to them that he adopts them in that seed of Abraham, through which Abraham himself and his true heavenly posterity become partakers of the heavenly inheritance. Elsewhere they are called sons through the promise, Gal. 4:28. Likewise sons according to the Spirit, that is, born of God and by a spiritual reason, Gal. 4:29. Sons of peace, in Hebrew manner, are those who favour the doctrine of peace, or the gospel, Luke 10:6. Son of perdition, for one devoted to destruction, John 17:12. Judas the traitor is so called not only because he perished, but also because he was destined and devoted to this destruction, as is clear from Acts 1:16; 4:27-28. Sons of the prophets: see Prophets.

units.la: Filij Rebelles parentibus quomodo tractandi, Deut. 21.v.18.19.20.21. Filij regni, pro omnibus in genere ingenis, & regni incolis, Matth.8.12. pro iis qui sunt in regno, id est, in Ecclesia, vt etiam sint ex Ecclesia, 13.38. Filij resurrectionis, pro resurrectionis participibus, Luc.20.36. Filij roboris, pro strenuis, 2 Sam.13.28. &17.10.1 Reg. 15.2. Filij sæculi huius pro hominibus præsenti vitæ addictis, Luc.16.8. quos Paulus ψυχικὸς vocat, hoc est, animales. & [?]σαρκικὸς, hoc est carnales, 1. Cor. 2.14. Alias tamen interdum, Filij seculi huius dicuntur, quicunque adhuc in viuis sunt, siue boni sint, siue mali, Luc. 20 34. Filij stulti, patres tristitia afficiunt, Prou. 17.25. & 19.13. Filij subductionis dicuntur, qui quodam impetu in partem aliquam feruntur, Hebr. 10.39. Hebraismus. Eo enim loci subintelligi videtur filiorum nomen. Filij thalami dicuntur Matt. 9.15. qui cum sponso versantur, & quos sponsus in suum vsq; thalamum admittit.
units.tr: Rebellious sons, how they are to be treated: Deut. 21:18-21. Sons of the kingdom, for all the natives of the kingdom in general and the inhabitants of the kingdom, Matt. 8:12; for those who are in the kingdom, that is, in the Church, and who are also of the Church, 13:38. Sons of the resurrection, for participants in the resurrection, Luke 20:36. Sons of strength, for the valiant, 2 Sam. 13:28; 17:10; 1 Kings 15:2. Sons of this age, for men devoted to the present life, Luke 16:8, whom Paul calls psychikos, that is, animal, and sarkikos [σαρκικός], that is, carnal, 1 Cor. 2:14. Elsewhere, however, the sons of this age are sometimes said to be all who are still alive, whether good or bad, Luke 20:34. Foolish sons cause grief to their fathers, Prov. 17:25; 19:13. Sons of drawing back are said of those who are carried by some impulse in a certain direction, Heb. 10:39. This is a Hebraism, for the word "sons" seems to be understood there. Sons of the bridechamber are called those who attend the bridegroom and whom the bridegroom admits into his own bridal chamber, Matt. 9:15.

units.la: Filij captiuitatis, interemptorum, pauperum, stultorum, tumultus, per auxesin, & abstractè, dicuntur captiui, interempti, pauperes, stulti, seditiosi, ex Hebraeorum idiotismo. Filij Aegypti, Aethiopum, Ammon, Assur, Babylonis, Edom, pro Aegyptiis, Aethiopibus, Ammonitis, Babyloniis, Idumaeis, &c. Filij Enacim, Gigantes, ex Enaco gigante Chananaeo orti.
units.tr: Sons of captivity, of the slain, of the poor, of fools, of tumult: by auxesis and abstractly, the captives, the slain, the poor, the foolish and the seditious are called such, from the Hebrew idiom. Sons of Egypt, of the Ethiopians, of Ammon, of Assur, of Babylon, of Edom, for Egyptians, Ethiopians, Ammonites, Babylonians, Idumaeans, etc. Sons of Anak: giants, descended from Anak, the Canaanite giant.

units.la: Filij Aquilae, pulli Aquilae, Prou. 30.17. filij Basan, arietes, Deut. 32.14. Filij rupicabrarum, capri sylvestres, Iob 39.7. Filij superbiae, feræ, quae non facile cicurantur, Iob. 41. 25. Filij Arcturi Iob. 38.32. Filius unicornium, pullus monoceros, Iob.39.6.7. Ps.29.6.
units.tr: Eaglets, the sons of the eagle, Prov. 30:17; sons of Bashan, rams, Deut. 32:14; sons of the rock-goats, wild goats, Job 39:7; sons of pride, wild beasts that are not easily tamed, Job 41:25; sons of Arcturus, Job 38:32; son of the unicorns, a young unicorn, Job 39:6-7; Ps. 29:6.

units.la: Filij Oleae, arbores misticae (nempe Zorobabel dux populi, & Iesua Sacerdos) dona Spiritus S. repraesentantes, Zach. 4.14.
units.tr: Sons of the olive, mystical trees (namely Zerubbabel, the leader of the people, and Joshua the priest), representing the gifts of the Holy Spirit, Zech. 4:14.

units.la: Filij boni ex malis parentibus orti: Ezechias Achazi filius, 2 Paralip .28.27. Iosias Ammonis filius, 33.25. & 34.2. Filij mali ex bonis parentibus orti: Cain Adae filius, Gen. 4.1. Cham filius Noë, 9.22. Ismael Abrahae filius, 21. vers. 20,21. Esau Isaaci filius, 25.25. Filij Heli Sacerdotis, 1. Sam. 2.v.12.25. Filij Samuelis, 8.3. Ammon filius Davidis, 2. Sam.
units.tr: Good sons born of bad parents: Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, 2 Chron. 28:27; Josiah, son of Amon, 33:25; 34:2. Bad sons born of good parents: Cain, son of Adam, Gen. 4:1; Ham, son of Noah, 9:22; Ishmael, son of Abraham, 21:20-21; Esau, son of Isaac, 25:25; the sons of Eli the priest, 1 Sam. 2:12, 25; the sons of Samuel, 8:3; Amnon, son of David, 2 Sam. 13:1-2.

units.la: 13.v.1.2. Abfalom filius Dauidis, 15.v.1.2. Roboam Salo-nis filius, 1.Reg.11.43. qui consilium iuuenum secutus, su-duas tantum Tribus regnat, 2.Paral.10.6. Vide Eccles.4. 26.27.28.29. Ioram filius Iosaphat, 2.Paralip.21.4. Mana-Ezechiae filius, 33.2. Filij inobedientis poena, Deuteron. 18. Prouer.20.20. Filij Abrahae fideles. Rom.9.v.7. 8. ABRAHAE filij.
units.tr: Absalom, son of David, 2 Sam. 15:1-2. Rehoboam, son of Solomon, 1 Kings 11:43, who, following the counsel of the young men, reigned over only two tribes, 2 Chron. 10:6. See Eccles. 4:26-29. Jehoram, son of Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 21:4. Manasseh, son of Hezekiah, 33:2. The punishment of disobedient sons: Deut. 18; Prov. 20:20. Faithful sons of Abraham: Rom. 9:7-8. Sons of Abraham.

units.la: Filij castigandi, Prou. 13.24. & 19. 18. & 22.15. & 23. 13. 15.26. Eccles.30.1. &c. docendi mysterium Pascha, Exod. 12.27, & 13.8. nempe nos esse liberatos ex captivitate Ægyptiaca, hoc est, Diabolica, Deuteron.4.9. & 6.20. ad finem usque. quare primogenita Deo offerenda, Exodi 13.v.12. filiorum primogenitorum redemptio. Exod.34.20. Num. 15.16. Filios consecrant idolis per ignem Israelitae, 2.Esdr. 17.17. in filios Dei adoptati sumus per Christum Ephes.1.5.
units.tr: Sons to be chastised: Prov. 13:24; 19:18; 22:15; 23:13; 15.26; Eccles. 30:1, etc. The mystery of the Passover to be taught: Exod. 12:27; 13:8, namely that we have been freed from Egyptian captivity, that is, from the devil; Deut. 4:9; 6:20 to the end. Why the firstborn are to be offered to God: Exod. 13:12; the redemption of the firstborn sons: Exod. 34:20; Num. 15:16. The Israelites consecrated their sons to idols by fire, 2 Esdr. 17:17. We have been adopted as sons of God through Christ, Eph. 1:5.

units.la: [Sequitur alia filiorum Nomenclatura, faciliori distinctione descripta, ne quid iuniores a nobis desiderent.]
units.tr: [Another nomenclature of sons follows, described with an easier distinction, so that the younger readers may lack nothing from us.]

units.la: Filiorum Gratiae caput Iesus Christus, Filius Dei, aeternus aeterni Patris filius, patri consubstantialis, & aequalis, in carne manifestandus. & tandem manifestatus, Psal. 2. Prouerb.30.4. Matth.3.17. & 16.16. & 17.5. &c. In N.T. plusquam ducenta de Filio Dei testimonia occurrunt. Vide CHRISTVS.
units.tr: The head of the sons of grace is Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the eternal Son of the eternal Father, consubstantial and equal with the Father, to be manifested in the flesh, and at last manifested: Ps. 2; Prov. 30:4; Matt. 3:17; 16:16; 17:5, etc. In the New Testament more than two hundred testimonies concerning the Son of God occur. See CHRIST.

units.la: Filius David, & filius hominis, Iesus Christus Dei filius conceptus de Spiritu Sancto, natus ex Maria Virgine. Esai. 51.1.4. & 9.5.6. Dan.7.13. Matth. 1.1. Vide centum alia testimonia in N.T. Filius Dei & Ecclesiae mysticus, nepe Christus, Apoc.12.v.4.5. Ps.2.9.
units.tr: Son of David and son of man, Jesus Christ, the Son of God, conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary: Isa. 51:1, 4; 9:5-6; Dan. 7:13; Matt. 1:1. See a hundred other testimonies in the New Testament. Son of God and mystical son of the Church, namely Christ: Rev. 12:4-5; Ps. 2:9.

units.la: Filij Dei, Angeli electi. Iob.1.6. & 38.7. Pro veram religionem profitentes, Gen.6.4. Electi, fideles filij Dei numbra, & vera Ecclesia catholica, Ps.73.15. Osee.1.10. Ioan. 12. Rom.5.2. Galat. 3.26. 1.Ioann.3.1. &c. Filij Abrahae, credentes in Christum, Matt.3. 9. Luc.3.8. & 19.9. Ioan.8. Filij Dei & Israelis, Israelitae veri & spirituales, ex Iacob oriundi, fide Christo adhaerentes. Gentiles item, per fidem Israelitis adiuncti, Esai.43.5.6. & 45.11. &54.13. Osee.1.Ap. 7.4.&c.& 21.12. Act.3.25.
units.tr: Sons of God: elect angels, Job 1:6; 38:7. Those who profess the true religion, Gen. 6:4. The elect, faithful sons of God in number, and the true catholic Church: Ps. 73:15; Hos. 1:10; John 12; Rom. 5:2; Gal. 3:26; 1 John 3:1, etc. Sons of Abraham: believers in Christ, Matt. 3:9; Luke 3:8; 19:9; John 8. Sons of God and of Israel: true and spiritual Israelites, descended from Jacob, cleaving to Christ by faith. Likewise Gentiles, joined by faith to Israel: Isa. 43:5-6; 45:11; 54:13; Hos. 1:10; Rev. 7:4; 21:12; Acts 3:25.

units.la: Filij Lucis, Luc.16.8. Ioan.12.36. Eph.5.8.1. Thess.5.5. Filij Sponsi, Amici & discipuli Christi, Mat. 9. 15. Marc. 2. Luc.5.34. filij gratiae, nempe quibus foedus suum obtulit: qui ante Christi adventum filij Israelis, post Christum ascendit. i ascensionem Christiani dicti sunt: Actor.11.26.
units.tr: Sons of light: Luke 16:8; John 12:36; Eph. 5:8; 1 Thess. 5:5. Sons of the bridegroom, the friends and disciples of Christ: Matt. 9:15; Mark 2; Luke 5:34. Sons of grace, namely those to whom he offered his covenant; those who before Christ's coming were sons of Israel, after Christ's ascension were called Christians: Acts 11:26.

units.la: Filij Israelis, Israelitæ, Iacobi patriarchæ, qui Israel conominatus est, proles & posteri, Genes.32.32. Exod. 1.7. Vide sexcenta alia eiusmodi dicta in Bibliis. Filij Israel & Ephraim, Israelitæ, qui à domo Dauidis, Ieroboami impulsu, defecerunt, & regnum decem tribuum, quod Israeliticum appellatur, erexerunt, tandemque ab Assyriorum rege deportati sunt, 1.Reg. 12. v. 24.33. & 2.Reg. 8.12. Psal.78.9. Ierem.31.20. Osc.1.10. &c.
units.tr: Sons of Israel: Israelites, the offspring and descendants of Jacob the patriarch, who was named Israel, Gen. 32:32; Exod. 1:7. See six hundred other such sayings in the Bible. Sons of Israel and Ephraim: Israelites who, at the instigation of Jeroboam, revolted from the house of David and set up the kingdom of the ten tribes, which is called Israelite, and who were at last carried away by the king of the Assyrians: 1 Kings 12:24, 33; 2 Kings 8:12; Ps. 78:9; Jer. 31:20; Hos. 1:10, etc.

units.la: Filij Iuda, 1. Iacobi siue Israelis posteri, qui successoribus Dauidis, post defectionem decem tribuum, adhæserunt, 1. Reg.12.17.2. Reg.18.4.2. Par.10.17. & 13.18. & 28.10. Ezec.18.9. &c. Filij Israel, & Iuda, 1. Iudæi, post reditum ex captivitate Babylonica, Esdr.6.16. Nehem.1. 1.Ezec.1.3. Dan.3. Osc.1.11. Ioel.3.6. Abd.12. Luc.1.16. Act.5.21. & 9.15. &c. units.tr: Sons of Judah: the descendants of Jacob or Israel who adhered to the successors of David after the defection of the ten tribes: 1 Kings 12:17; 2 Kings 18:4; 2 Chron. 10:17; 13:18; 28:10; Ezek. 18:9, etc. Sons of Israel and Judah: the Jews, after their return from the Babylonian captivity: Ezra 6:16; Neh. 1:1; Ezek. 1:3; Dan. 3; Hos. 1:11; Joel 3:6; Obad. 12; Luke 1:16; Acts 5:21; 9:15, etc. Sons of God: all the most noble and powerful: Ps. 82:6; 89:7. Sons of the prophets, or disciples: 1 Kings 20:35; 2 Kings 2:3, 5, 7, 15; 4:38; 5:22; 6:1; 9:1.

units.tr: Son of God: a man acceptable to God, whom he favours with a singular kindness, 2 Sam. 6:14; 1 Par. 17:13; 22:10; 28:6; Ps. 2:7; Isa. 1:2. units.tr: That the wives might be fruitful, like Rachel and Leah, the people prayed over the marrying virgins, Ruth 4:11. (See Barren, and Woman.)

units.la: Foedus in genere, est mutua pactio duarum partium, qua altera alteri se certis conditionibus obligat ad aliquid faciendum, dandum vel accipiendum, adhibitis signis & symbolis externis, ad solennem testificationem, confirmationis causa, vt promissio sit inuiolabilis. Hinc Foederis Dei definitio colligitur, nempe quod sit Mutua pactio inter Deum & homines, qua Deus confirmat hominibus se iturum eis propitium, remissurum peccata, donaturum iustitiam nouam, spiritum sanctum, & vitam aeternam, per & propter Filium mediatorem: Vicissim homines se obligant Deo ad fidem & poenitentiam, hoc est, ad acciendum vera fide hoc tantum beneficium, & ad praestan- dam Deo veram obedientiam, Sacramenta sunt huius foe- deris seu Testamenti signa.
units.tr: A covenant in general is a mutual agreement between two parties, by which one binds itself to the other, under certain conditions, to do, give or receive something. External signs and symbols are added for solemn witness and confirmation, so that the promise may be inviolable. From this the definition of God's covenant is drawn: it is a mutual agreement between God and men, by which God assures men that he will be favourable to them, forgive their sins, bestow a new righteousness, the Holy Spirit and eternal life, through and for the sake of the Son as Mediator. In turn, men bind themselves to God to faith and repentance, that is, to accept this benefit alone with true faith, and to render to God true obedience. The sacraments are the signs of this covenant or testament.

units.la: [Foedus gratiae, Esai. 55. 3. 4. Act. 3. 25. 26. Hebr. 13 20. foedus Ezech. 34. 25. Testamentum, Hebr. 9. 16. 17. foedus Abrahami, Act. 3. 25. Euangelij. Quod ad eius externam oeconomiam & administrationem attinet, dicitur vetus vel nouum. Vetus, quatenus erat reconciliatio veteris populi cum Deo per Christum exhibendum. Nouum, quatenus est reconciliatio noui populi cum Deo per Christum in carne iam exhibitum. Conueniunt Vetus & Nouum foedus in multis. 1. In Causa efficiente & principali. Nam idem est foederis autor, Deus: Esai. 54. 5. 6. Coniunx tuus erit opifex totus, est. 2. In Causa ... : nam vtrumque foedus nullis hominum meritis, sed sola, eaque miranda Dei vocantis ... & mi sericordia, factum est. Luc. 1. cap. 54. 55. 78. vers. 3. In causa meritoria, ... : nam vtriusque foederis fundamentum vnum idemque est Christus: Hebr.
units.tr: [Covenant of grace, Isa. 55:3, 4; Acts 3:25, 26; Heb. 13:20; covenant, Ezek. 34:25. Testament, Heb. 9:16, 17; covenant of Abraham, Acts 3:25; of the gospel.] As to its external economy and administration, the covenant is called old or new. Old, insofar as it was the reconciliation of the old people with God through Christ, who was yet to be exhibited. New, insofar as it is the reconciliation of the new people with God through Christ, now exhibited in the flesh. The Old and New Covenants agree in many respects. 1. In the efficient and principal cause: for the author of both covenants is the same, God (Isa. 54:5, 6: "Your husband will be your maker"). 2. In the cause ...: for both covenants were made not by any merits of men, but by the sole and wonderful mercy of God who calls (Luke 1:54, 55, 78; verse 3). 3. In the meritorious cause ...: for the foundation of both covenants is one and the same, Christ (Heb.

Vetus tantum tantum populum pertinuit: Novum ad omnes populos spectat.2. Vetus Christum exhibendum variis cerimoniis adumbrabat: Novum (teste Apostolo, Hebr.7.11.) ... stum iam vere exhibitum clare praedicat. 3. In veteri dere Dominus caelestem haereditatem sub terrenis beneficiis contemplandam & quodammodo degustandam habuit: sub Novo recta ad vitae aeternae meditationem nostras dirigit, istiusmodi terrenis subsidiis, qualibus apud Israelitas adhibebat, omissis. 4. Vetus fuit obscurum Hebr.9.8. Novum autem est illustrius, Ioan.1.v.vlt.5. Secundum sanguine sanctum fuit: Novum novo modo sanctum, nempe reali morte Christi. 6. Vetus ordinatum circumcisione & Agno Paschali obsignabatur: Novum sacramentis obsignatur, nempe Baptismo & Coena Domini. Unde consequitur fideles post Christi adventum meliore frui conditione, quod ad foederis administrationem, quam fideles ante Christi adventum habuerunt: Matt.13.16.17.1.Petr.1.10.&c.
units.tr: [Illegible Greek marginal references partly cut off at the left edge.] 13:8; Rev. 13:8), on whose intercession, faith and satisfaction all believers, from the beginning of the world to its end, are reconciled to God. See further Gen. 3; Ps. 40:8; Heb. 9:10; 10:9. He was surety not only for the adopted sons by his manifestation in the flesh, but also for those who were from the beginning of the world. 4. In matter: for the thing promised in both covenants is the same, namely the Son of God made man (Rom. 1:1, 2, and passim elsewhere). 5. In the essential form: in both there is a mutual obligation between God and the elect; the one indeed wholly gratuitous, the other owed by them. 6. In the end: just as the new covenant, so also the old looked both to stir up the desire for blessed immortality and to confirm that same hope. 7. In effect: because each covenant brought justification and regeneration to believers on both sides (John 8:58: "Abraham saw my day," etc.). In subject ω: for God made both covenants with the elect. 9. In the added internal sealing: for both covenants were sealed to believers, old and new, by the same Holy Spirit. They differ also in some respects. 1. The Old pertained only to one people; the New looks to all peoples. 2. The Old foreshadowed the Christ to be exhibited by various ceremonies; the New (as the Apostle testifies, Heb. 7:11) ... clearly proclaims him as already truly exhibited. 3. Under the old, the Lord had the heavenly inheritance to be contemplated and in some measure tasted under earthly benefits; under the New he directs our thoughts straight to the meditation of eternal life, with such earthly aids as he used among the Israelites set aside. 4. The Old was obscure (Heb. 9:8); the New is more illustrious (John 1, last verse). 5. The old was consecrated by blood; the New is consecrated in a new way, namely by the real death of Christ. 6. The Old was ordained and sealed by circumcision and the Paschal Lamb; the New is sealed by sacraments, namely Baptism and the Lord's Supper. Whence it follows that believers after Christ's coming enjoy a better condition, as regards the administration of the covenant, than believers before Christ's coming had (Matt. 13:16, 17; 1 Pet. 1:10, etc.).

units.tr: FORM: Christ was in the form of God, Phil. 2.6, that is, in that majesty and glory of the Godhead which is one and the same nature; and therefore Christ is true God. Form signifies that abject and feeble nature and condition of man, Phil. 2.7, both in itself, when compared with the excellence of God, and indeed on account of sin. The Lord did not assume sin but abolished it; yet the weakness flowing from that source remains, apart from the one sin, and he took upon himself the dreadful punishment of our sins, as the Apostle explains in the same place. ANT: the industry of the ant, Prov. 6.6 & 30.25. The fearful should not go forth to war, Deut. 20.8. FURNACE: Egypt an iron furnace, Deut. 4.20. FORNICATION provokes the wrath of God, Deut. 2.21; Prov. 23.27; Lev. 19.3; Jer. 5.7; Hos. 4.14; 1 Cor. 6.v.9.13.15; Col. 3; Heb. 13.4. It enervates the body and consumes one's resources, Joel 1.12; Prov. 23.27 & 29.3 & 31.3; Eccl. 9.6. It brings infamy, Ecclus. 9.10 & 41.20. See ADULTERY and HARLOTRY. Occasions of fornication are to be avoided, Eccl. 9.v.4.12 & 4. Fornication is forbidden not only in the outward act but also in the affections, Exod. 20.17; Mark 5.28. Spiritual fornication: Deut. 31.16; Judg. 2.17 & 8.v.27.33; Isa. 1.21 & 57.3; Jer. etc.; Ezek. 6.9 & 16.15 etc.; Hos. 1.2 & 2.4 & 4.15; Rev. 3. See spiritual HARLOTRY. STRONG: God is our strength, Josh. 22.22; 2 Sam. 22.3. THE MIGHTY MEN of David, 2 Sam. 23.8; 1 Chron. 11.10. Examples of strength and of bodily vigour. See examples of the robust.

units.la: FORTITVDO, ἀνδρεία, Est ea animi firmitas, quæ omnia periculna, maximè præmeditata, & quæ oportet & vbi oportet, lubens subit propter officium faciendum. Greg. l. 8. Moral. Fortitudo iustorum est, carnem vincere, propriis voluptatibus contraire, delectationem vitæ præsentis extinguere, huius mundi aspera pro æternis præmiis amare, prosperitatis blandimenta contemnere, aduersitatis metum in corde superare.
units.tr: FORTITUDE, [ἀνδρεία]. It is that firmness of mind which gladly undergoes all dangers, especially those foreseen, and which ought to be undergone, and where it ought to be undergone, for the sake of performing one's duty. Gregory, Moral Reflections, book 8. The fortitude of the just is to overcome the flesh, to oppose one's own pleasures, to extinguish delight in the present life, to love the harshnesses of this world for the sake of eternal rewards, to despise the allurements of prosperity, and to overcome in the heart the fear of adversity.

units.la: FORTE: Forte interdum non dubitantis est particula, sed a difficultate ad fiduciam gratiæ & promissionum Dei animum erigentis, Ioel.2.14. Additur autem hæc particula tum ad notandum humanitus rei difficultatem, tum comparandum & confirmandum in eadem spe animum audientium, Iosh.14.12. vide & Ex.32.30.1. Sam.14,6. Ier.2.Soph.2.3. units.tr: PERHAPS: "perhaps" is sometimes a particle not of one who doubts, but one that lifts the mind from difficulty to trust in the grace and promises of God, Joel 2.14. This particle is added both to note the difficulty of a matter from a human standpoint and to prepare and strengthen the minds of the hearers in the same hope, Josh. 14.12; see also Exod. 32.30; 1 Sam. 14.6; Jer. 2; Zeph. 2.3; Dan. 6.6; Amos 5.15; Acts 8.22; 2 Tim. 2.25.
