Sic omnes Christiani Fratres dicuntur, Matt.23. Fratres a Paulo vocati etiam malitiosi Doctores, 1.Cor.4. tum vt personæ mutatio intelligeretur, tum vt sequeretur grauissimæ reprehensionis asperitas mitigaretur. Frater Christianus ob cibum non perdedus Rom.14.15. Frater abcesses a fide occidendus, Deut.13.v.6.9. pro Fratribus Christianis animas ponere debemus, 1.Ioan.3.16. Fratris absque beris mortuiuxor ab altero fratre ducenda. Gen.38.8. Deut.5. Fratri peccanti quoties ignoscendum, Mat.18.v.21.22. Luc.17.4. inter Fratres primogenitus Christus. Rom.8.29. Fratres in negotio non opprimendus, nec circumveniendus, 1.Thess.4.6. Fratrem qui odit in tenebris est, 1.Ioan.2.9. homicida est, 3.15. mendax est, 4.20. Fratrum concordia, Vide CONCORDIA. Fratres Christi spirituales. Vide CHRISTI fratres. Fratres spirituales, vide CHRISTVS Fratres Ioseph descendunt in Ægyptum, Gen. 42. 3. agnoscuntur ab eo, v. 8. Vide IOSEPH. Falsi fratres, 2. Cor. 11. 26. Gal. 2. 4. 2. Tim. 4. v. 14. 15. 1. Ioan. 2. 19.
units.tr: BROTHERS used for the sons of brothers, that is, for kinsmen of the same family line, 2 Kings 10, as appears from 2 Chr. 22.8. So also Gen. 13.8, as is clear from Gen. 11.26-27. Brothers and sisters are used for relatives, Matt. 12.47; 13; Mark 3.31 and 6.3; John 2.12. Brothers are those who profess the same religion, even if the one is king and the other a subject, the one a leader and the other a companion, the one a teacher and the other a disciple: Deut. 17.20; 1 Sam. 30.23; Matt. 28.10. So all Christians are called brothers, Matt. 23. Paul calls even malicious teachers brothers, 1 Cor. 4, both so that the change of person might be understood and so that the harshness of a very grave rebuke might be softened. A Christian brother is not to be destroyed on account of food, Rom. 14.15. A brother who turns away from the faith is to be put to death, Deut. 13.6, 9. We ought to lay down our lives for Christian brothers, 1 John 3.16. The widow of a man who died without children is to be taken by another brother, Gen. 38.8; Deut. 5. A brother who sins is to be forgiven as often as he repents, Matt. 18.21-22; Luke 17.4. Christ is the firstborn among brothers, Rom. 8.29. A brother is not to be oppressed or circumvented in business, 1 Thess. 4.6. He who hates his brother is in darkness, 1 John 2.9; is a murderer, 3.15; is a liar, 4.20. For the concord of brothers, see CONCORD. For the spiritual brothers of Christ, see CHRIST, brothers. For spiritual brothers, see CHRIST. Joseph's brothers go down into Egypt, Gen. 42.3; they are recognized by him, v. 8. See JOSEPH. False brothers: 2 Cor. 11.26; Gal. 2.4; 2 Tim. 4.14-15; 1 John 2.19.

units.la: [Distinctius ita loquimur.
units.tr: [We speak more distinctly in this way.

units.la: 1. Frater, natus iisdem parentibus: vel etiam patris aut matris eiusdem filius, Gen. 4. 2. & 37. 2. 2. Sam. 7. 20.
units.tr: 1. A brother, born of the same parents, or also a son of the same father or mother: Gen. 4.2 and 37.2; 2 Sam. 7.20.

units.la: 3. Homo Israelita, stirpis & gentis ex Iacobo patr. oriundae, nempe Israeliticae, in 12. tribus distinctae: vel eiusdem, vel varie tribus, Ex. 2. v. 11. 18, & 32, 27, Deut. 15, v. 2. 7, 9. 11, 12, Ester. 10, 3, Mat. 10, 11, Act. 7, 2.
units.tr: 3. A man of Israel, of the stock and nation descended from the patriarch Jacob, namely an Israelite, distinguished into the twelve tribes; or of the same tribe, or of various tribes: Ex. 2.11, 18 and 32.27; Deut. 15.2, 7, 9, 11, 12; Esther 10.3; Matt. 10.11; Acts 7.2.

units.la: 4. Frater, iure religionis, seu eiusdem caelestis benedictionis consors atque particeps in Christo Mediatore, Rom. 1, 13. 1. Cor. 1, 26, 2. Pet. 1, 10, & 3, 17, 1. Io. 2, 11, Ap. 1, 9, & 12, 10
units.tr: 4. A brother by right of religion, or a partner and sharer in the same heavenly blessing in Christ the Mediator: Rom. 1.13; 1 Cor. 1.26; 2 Pet. 1.10 and 3.17; 1 John 2.11; Rev. 1.9 and 12.10.

units.la: 5. Frater, iure naturae, humanitatis, patriae, vicinitatis, &c. Amicus, conterraneus, contribulis, popularis, proximus, &c. Gen. 19. 7. & 24. 4. 1. Sam. 30. 23. 1. Reg. 13. 30. Matth. 18. v. 15. 21.
units.tr: 5. A brother by right of nature, of humanity, of country, of neighbourhood, etc.: a friend, a fellow countryman, a fellow tribesman, a compatriot, a neighbour, etc. Gen. 19.7 and 24.4; 1 Sam. 30.23; 1 Kings 13.30; Matt. 18.15, 21.

units.la: 6. Frater, discipulus, 1. Par. 25, v. 7, 9, 10, Socius, Similis, Iob. 30, 23, Pro. 18, 9, Ioel, 2, 8.]
units.tr: 6. A brother, that is, a disciple: 1 Chr. 25.7, 9, 10; a companion, a like one: Job 30.29; Prov. 18.9; Joel 2.8.]

units.la: FRATERNITAS pro fratrum coetu & coniunctione, Zach. 11, 14, 1 Pet. 2, 17, & 5, 9, Fraternitas diligenda, Rom. 12, 10, 1, Thess. 4, 9, Heb. 13, 1, 1. Pet. 1. 22, & 2, 17, & 3, 8. 2, Pet. 1, 7. ps. 133. 1. c. v. pro. 18. 19.
units.tr: BROTHERHOOD, for the assembly and fellowship of brothers: Zech. 11.14; 1 Pet. 2.17 and 5.9. The brotherhood is to be loved: Rom. 12.10; 1 Thess. 4.9; Heb. 13.1; 1 Pet. 1.22, 2.17, 3.8; 2 Pet. 1.7; Ps. 133.1; cf. Prov. 18.19.

units.la: FRAVS prohibetur, Pf. 101, 5, Ier. 5, 26, 27. & 6, 13, & 9. 5. 6. Marc. 10, 19, Leu. 19, 13, 1. Cor. 6. 8. 1. Pet. 2. 1. Fraudis exempla: Cain, Gen. 4, 8, Iacob. 27, v. 18, 19, 20, & 30, v. 31, 32, 33, Thamar, 38, v. 13, 14, Obstetrix, v. 27, 28, Gabaonitae, Ios. 9. v. 4, 22, 23, Ananias & Saphira. Act. 5, 2. (Vide ASTVTIA, CALLIDITAS, DOLVS). Fraus ferenda, non inferenda, 1. Cor. 6. 7. 8.
units.tr: FRAUD is forbidden: Ps. 101.5; Jer. 5.26-27, 6.13, 9.5-6; Mark 10.19; Lev. 19.13; 1 Cor. 6.8; 1 Pet. 2.1. Examples of fraud: Cain, Gen. 4.8; Jacob, Gen. 27.18-20 and 30.31-33; Tamar, 38.13-14; the midwife, v. 27-28; the Gibeonites, Josh. 9.4, 22-23; Ananias and Sapphira, Acts 5.2. (See CUNNING, CRAFTINESS, GUILE.) Fraud is to be endured, not inflicted: 1 Cor. 6.7-8.

units.la: FRAVDVLENTORVM merces, Pro. 28, 10. & 12. 27. Fraudulenti non saluabuntur, 1. Cor. 6. 8. 9.
units.tr: The wages of the fraudulent: Prov. 28.10 and 12.27. The fraudulent will not be saved: 1 Cor. 6.8-9.

units.la: FRVCTVS, Opus ipsum hominis, sive malum, sive Deo acceptum, Esai. 10. 12, Ezech. 17. 8, Ose. 14. 8, Amos 6, 12. Matt. 3. 8. Ioan. 4. 36, Heb. 12. 11. Iaco. 3. v. 17. 18. 11. Benedictio multiplex, piis collata, Prou. 11. 30. Ro. 1. 13. Phil. 1. 21. 2. Pet. 1. 8. 111. Quicquid est eximium in homine, vel loco, Amos. 2. 9. 1v. Merces, praemium, Pf. 58. 12. Esa. 3. 10. Ier. 6. 19. & 17, 10. Mich. 7. 13. v. Profectus, 1. Cor. 14. 14. vi. Fructus, Labiorum, verba & voces, Esa. 57. 19. Hebr. 13. 15. Fructus ventris, proles, Gen.30,2, Deut.7.13. Psal.132.11. Thren. 2.20. Luc.1.42. Actor.2.30. VII. fructus, terrenæ benedictiones impiis collatæ, Ier.12.2. fœtus & pulli quadrupedum, Deut. 28.4. & 30.9.
units.tr: FRUIT: the man's own work, whether evil or acceptable to God: Isa. 10.12; Ezek. 17.8; Hos. 14.8; Amos 6.12; Matt. 3.8; John 4.36; Heb. 12.11; James 3.17-18. (ii) The manifold blessing bestowed on the pious: Prov. 11.30; Rom. 1.13; Phil. 1.21; 2 Pet. 1.8. (iii) Whatever is excellent in a man or a place: Amos 2.9. (iv) Reward, prize: Ps. 58.12; Isa. 3.10; Jer. 6.19 and 17.10; Mic. 7.13. (v) Progress: 1 Cor. 14.14. (vi) The fruit of the lips, words and voices: Isa. 57.19; Heb. 13.15. Fruit of the womb, offspring: Gen. 30.2; Deut. 7.13; Ps. 132.11; Lam. 2.20; Luke 1.42; Acts 2.30. (vii) Fruit, earthly blessings bestowed on the wicked: Jer. 12.2; the young and offspring of quadrupeds: Deut. 28.4 and 30.9.

units.la: Fructus mysticus, i. gustus vitæ æternæ, tum in præsenti vita imperfectè, tum perfectè in futura, Cantic.2. 3. & 4. v.13. 16. & 7. 8. & 8. v.11. 12. Apoc.22.2.]
units.tr: Mystical fruit, that is, a taste of eternal life, imperfectly in the present life and perfectly in the future: Song 2.3, 4.13, 16, 7.8, 8.11-12; Rev. 22.2.]

units.la: FRVCTVS & arbor, Matt.7.18. Fructus iustitiæ & peccati, Rom. 6. v.21.23. à fructibus cognoscitur arbor, Matth. 7. 17. Luc æ 6.44. Fructus spiritus qui sint, Gal.5.22.
units.tr: FRUIT and tree: Matt. 7.18. The fruit of righteousness and of sin: Rom. 6.21, 23. A tree is known by its fruit: Matt. 7.17; Luke 6.44. What the fruits of the Spirit are: Gal. 5.22.

units.la: FRVGALITAS, Est virtus media inter prodigalitatē & avaritiā, quum nec nimis parcè rebus utimur, nec nimis luxuriosè. (Sunt enim frugi homines, quos Græci σωφρονας dicunt, qui in omni re motus animi moderantur.) Est igitur moderata & qualis oportet, pecuniæ, rerumque aliarū a hanc vitam necessariarum conseruatio, & earundem quantum oportet & quando oportet insumptio.
units.tr: FRUGALITY is a virtue lying between prodigality and avarice, when we use things neither too sparingly nor too extravagantly. (For those are the frugal men whom the Greeks call sōphronas, who govern the movements of their mind in every matter.) It is therefore the moderate and proper keeping of money and of the other things necessary for this life, and their spending as much as is fitting and when it is fitting.

units.la: FRVGALITAS commendatur, Pro.27.23. &c. Fruges consumuntur inobedientibus, Deut. 28.42.49.50.51. v. pro.3.9. Deut.26.2.
units.tr: FRUGALITY is commended: Prov. 27.23 etc. Fruits are consumed by the disobedient: Deut. 28.42, 49-51; see Prov. 3.9; Deut. 26.2.

units.la: FRVMENTVM dat Deus diligentibus se, Deut.11.14. Psal.147.14.
units.tr: GRAIN: God gives it to those who love him: Deut. 11.14; Ps. 147.14.

units.la: FVCVS Iesabelis, 2.Reg.9.30. filiarum Sionis, Esai.3.16. &c. fucus Iesabelis mysticæ, nempe falsa doctrina, Apocal. 2.20. fucus item impiorum Iudæorum, Ier.4.30.
units.tr: The PAINT of Jezebel, 2 Kings 9.30; of the daughters of Zion, Isa. 3.16 etc. The paint of mystical Jezebel, namely false doctrine, Rev. 2.20; likewise the paint of the impious Jews, Jer. 4.30.

units.la: FVGERE persecutionem aliquatenus licitum est, & necessarium, Matt.10.23. Fuge exempla: Rex Sodomorum, Gen.14. 10. Agar, 16.6. Iacob, 27.43. & 31.21. Moses, Ex.2.15. Act.7.29. Israelitæ, Ex.14.5. Ios.7.4.1. Sam.4.10. & 17.24. & 31.1. Moses & Aaron, Num.16.42. quinq. Reges Ios.10.16. Adonibezec Iudic.1.6. Sisara, 4.v.15.16.17. Madianitæ, 7.21. Zebee & Salmana, 8.12. Iothā, 9.21. Iephthe, 11.v.2.3. Israelitæ & Beniamin, 20.v.32.47. Vir quidā, 1.Sā.4.16. Philisthæi, 19.8. Dauid v.10.& 20.1.& 21.10.& 22.1.2. Sam.15.14. Abiathar, 1.Sā.21. quadringenti Viri, 1.Sam.30.17. Abner, 2. Sam.2.24. Berothitæ & Nutrix Miphibosetheth, 4.4. Filij Dauidis, 13.25. Absalom, v.34. Ioab, 1.Reg.2.28. Serui Semei, v.39. Adad & Ri Idumæi, 11.17. Syri & Benadad, 20.v.20.30. Elias, 1.Reg. 17.v.5.9.& 19.3. Moabitæ, 2.Re.3.24. Ochosias. 9.27. Adramelech, Sarasar filij Sennacherib, 19.37. Tobias, Tob.1.24. Sedechias, & viri bellatores, 2.Reg.25.4. Iere. 39.4. & 52.7. Ismahel Nathaniæ filius, &c. Ier.41.15. Ionas, Iō.1.3. Iosep cum Maria matre Iesu, Mat.2.13. Christus, 12.15. Mar.14.50. Ioant Ioan.6.15.& 7.1.& 8.59. Discipuli Mat.26.56. Paulus, Act.9. 25.& 17.14. Paulus & Barnabas,14.6. Mulier, Ap.12,v. 6.14.
units.tr: FLEEING from persecution is in some measure lawful and necessary: Matt. 10.23. Examples of fleeing: the king of Sodom, Gen. 14.10; Hagar, 16.6; Jacob, 27.43 and 31.21; Moses, Ex. 2.15; Acts 7.29; the Israelites, Ex. 14.5; Josh. 7.4; 1 Sam. 4.10, 17.24, 31.1; Moses and Aaron, Num. 16.42; five kings, Josh. 10.16; Adonibezek, Judg. 1.6; Sisera, 4.15-17; the Midianites, 7.21; Zebah and Zalmunna, 8.12; Jotham, 9.21; Jephthah, 11.2-3; the Israelites and Benjamin, 20.32, 47; a certain man, 1 Sam. 4.16; the Philistines, 19.8; David, v. 10 and 20.1, 21.10, 22.1-2; 2 Sam. 15.14; Abiathar, 1 Sam. 21; four hundred men, 1 Sam. 30.17; Abner, 2 Sam. 2.24; the Berothites and the nurse of Mephibosheth, 4.4; the sons of David, 13.25; Absalom, v. 34; Joab, 1 Kings 2.28; the servants of Shimei, v. 39; Hadad the Edomite, 11.17; the Syrians and Ben-hadad, 20.20, 30; Elijah, 1 Kings 17.5, 9 and 19.3; the Moabites, 2 Kings 3.24; Ahaziah, 9.27; Adrammelech and Sharezer, sons of Sennacherib, 19.37; Tobit, Tob. 1.24; Zedekiah and the fighting men, 2 Kings 25.4; Jer. 39.4 and 52.7; Ishmael son of Nethaniah, etc., Jer. 41.15; Jonah, Jon. 1.3; Joseph with Mary the mother of Jesus, Matt. 2.13; Christ, 12.15; Mark 14.50; John, John 6.15, 7.1, 8.59; the disciples, Matt. 26.56; Paul, Acts 9.25 and 17.14; Paul and Barnabas, 14.6; a woman, Rev. 12.6, 14.

units.la: FULMEN, est exhalatio calida & sicca, quæ in hac expansione ita refrigerata est, ut quanquam calida manet, lucem tamen emittere & ignem concipere non possit: sed propter tum molem ipsam suã,& propter vim magnã frigoris sese opponentis,& illam exhalationem ac molē repercutientis celerrimè delabitur: & à Deo in terrã tanquam telü certissimum contorquetur. Efficies causa Deut.Iob.38.35.& 28.26 ps.104.4.& 144.6.& 97.3.&78.47. (Contra Priscillianistas Hæreticos aliter sentientes.) Ad potentiam & iustitiam Dei patefaciendam: ps.29.3.c.& 78.47. Eccl.39.34.
units.tr: Lightning is a hot and dry exhalation which, in this expanse, is so cooled that, although it remains warm, it cannot emit light or catch fire. Because of its own mass and the great force of the opposing cold, which drives back that exhalation and mass, it falls very swiftly, and God hurls it to earth like a most certain missile. Efficient cause: Job 38:35; 28:26; Ps. 104:4; 144:6; 97:3; 78:47. (Against the Priscillianist heretics, who think otherwise.) To display the power and justice of God: Ps. 29:3; 78:47; Ecclus. 39:34.

units.la: Olympus Episcopus Arrianus triplici ictu fulminis attritus, quòd in Christum & Trinitate multa blasphema etiam fatetur. Sabellicus.
units.tr: Olympus, an Arian bishop, was struck by a triple bolt of lightning, because he professed many blasphemies about Christ and the Trinity. Sabellicus.

units.la: FULGUR, est mirè calida, siccaque exhalatio, quæ postquam in sublimi evecta est, undiq. vi frigoris à Deo cōstringitur, comprimiturq; ex quo ignis dissilit & emicat, & tonitru sive sonus vehemens fracta nube tandem auditur. Exod.19.16.2. Reg.22.15. Iob.38.35. ps.144.6.
units.tr: A flash of lightning is an exhalation of wondrous heat and dryness which, once raised on high, is constricted and compressed on every side by the force of cold from God. From this, fire leaps out and flashes, and thunder, or a violent sound, is finally heard when the cloud is broken. Exod. 19:16; 2 Kgs. 22:15; Job 38:35; Ps. 144:6.

units.la: FUNCTIONES Ecclesiasticæ,& earum genera, Vide DIACONIA.
units.tr: Ecclesiastical functions and their kinds: see DEACONS.

units.la: FUNDA, funditor. Iud.20.16. Dauid,1.Sam.17.40.49.50.(v.25.29.) 1.par.12.2.2.par.26.14. Iob.41.19. Zach.9.15.v. Sagitta, FUNDAMENTUM Ecclesiæ Christus, 1.Cor.3.11. Eph.2.20.1 Pet.2.6. Vide CHRISTVS. ¶ Apostolos etiam esse, Eph.2.20. Apo c.21.24.& peculiariter Petrum, Mat.16.18.& 21.v.15.17. cuius fides nunquam deficiet, Luc.22.31. docent cacodæmonis religionis propugnatores. Vide CHRISTVS. Fundamentum pro doctrina, Eph.2.20. Fundamentum aliud potest non potest, præterquam quod positum est, quod est Christus,1.Cor.3.11.
units.tr: A sling; a slinger. Judg. 20:16. David: 1 Sam. 17:40, 49, 50 (v. 25, 29); 1 Chr. 12:2; 2 Chr. 26:14; Job 41:19; Zech. 9:15. See ARROW. FOUNDATION: the Church's foundation is Christ, 1 Cor. 3:11; Eph. 2:20; 1 Pet. 2:6. See CHRIST. ¶ That the apostles are also foundations, Eph. 2:20; Rev. 21:14, and particularly Peter, Matt. 16:18; 21:15, 17, whose faith will never fail, Luke 22:31, is taught by the champions of the devil's religion. See CHRIST. A foundation for doctrine: Eph. 2:20. No one can lay another foundation besides that which has been laid, which is Christ, 1 Cor. 3:11.

units.la: FUNICVLVS, pro parte hæreditaria, Iof.17.v.5.14. quia funiculis hæreditas in partes diuidebatur: Metonymia.
units.tr: A measuring cord, for a hereditary portion: Josh. 17:5, 14, because inheritances were divided by cords. Metonymy.

units.la: FUROR impiorum, Vide IMPIVS. Furore percutit Deus inobedientes, Deut.28.28.v. Pro 6.34.& 15.1.& 27.4.
units.tr: The fury of the wicked: see WICKED. God strikes the disobedient with fury, Deut. 28:28. Prov. 6:34; 15:1; 27:4.

units.la: FUR nocturnus impune occidi potest, Ex.22.2.&c.
units.tr: A nocturnal thief may be killed with impunity, Exod. 22:2, etc.

units.la: Parabola furis Mat.24.43. Ap.3.3.2. Pet.3.v.9.10.11.v. plagiū.
units.tr: The parable of the thief, Matt. 24:43; Rev. 3:3; 2 Pet. 3:9–11. Kidnapping.

units.la: FURTVM, Est rei alienæ inuito domino, nullóq; magistratu iubente, vel iure permittente, cōtractio facta. Quæ si in re sacra fit, est sacrilegiū: si in re & pecunia publica, est peculatus: si in re priuata, est furtum, vel quod est manifestum, vel non manifestum.
units.tr: Theft is the making of a contract over another's property, against the owner's will, with no magistrate ordering it and no law permitting it. If it is done in a sacred thing it is sacrilege; if in public property or public money it is peculation; if in private property it is theft, either manifest or non-manifest.

units.la: Furti igitur reus est, non solùm qui rem ipsam alienam vel surripit, vel mala fide possidet, vel ad se recipit: verum etiam qui vetus pro nouo supponit, qui falso pondere ac mensura vtitur, qui tempore & loco constitutis rem alienam, cui debet, mala fide, non restituit.
units.tr: So the guilty of theft are not only those who steal another's property or possess it in bad faith or take it back for themselves, but also those who substitute old goods for new, who use false weights and measures, and who, in bad faith, do not return another's property that they owe at the appointed time and place.

units.la: FVRTVM prohibetur, committitur & punitur, Exo. 20.15. & 21.16. & 22.1. Leu. 19.11. Deu. 5.19. & 24.7. Ios. 7.v.1.19. Prou. 6.30. Ose. 4.2. Ier. 7.9. Zac. 5.3. Mat. 19.18. Ioan. 12.6. 1. Cor. 6. 10. Eph. 4.28, Tit. 2.10. 1. Pet. 4.15. Apoc. 9.21. poena furti. Exo. 22.v.1.4. Pro. 6.31.1. Cor. 6.10.1. Thess. 4.6. Furti & scortationis collatio. Pro. 6.v.30.31.32.33. Furti & furtum exempla Rachel, Gen. 31.19. Achan, Ios. 7.v.10.20. Soror Ochoziae, 2 Reg. 11.2. Principes Iudaeorum, Esa. 1.23. Iudas Iscariotes Ioan. 12.6. cum fure non versandum, Prou. 29.24. & 28.24. FVRES dicuntur, verbi Dei & doctrinā veram adulterantes Ier. 23.30. Ioan. 10.1. fures laborent: & ad quid, Eph. 4.28.
units.tr: Theft is forbidden, committed and punished: Exod. 20:15; 21:16; 22:1; Lev. 19:11; Deut. 5:19; 24:7; Josh. 7:1, 19; Prov. 6:30; Hos. 4:2; Jer. 7:9; Zech. 5:3; Matt. 19:18; John 12:6; 1 Cor. 6:10; Eph. 4:28; Titus 2:10; 1 Pet. 4:15; Rev. 9:21. The punishment of theft: Exod. 22:1, 4; Prov. 6:31; 1 Cor. 6:10; 1 Thess. 4:6. The pairing of theft and fornication: Prov. 6:30–33. Examples of theft and thieves: Rachel, Gen. 31:19; Achan, Josh. 7:10, 20; the sister of Ahaziah, 2 Kgs. 11:2; the leaders of the Jews, Isa. 1:23; Judas Iscariot, John 12:6. One must not associate with a thief, Prov. 29:24; 28:24. THIEVES are called those who adulterate the word of God and true doctrine, Jer. 23:30; John 10:1. Thieves labour; and to what end? Eph. 4:28.

units.la: ΦΥΛΑΚΗ, pro carcere, Mat. 5.25. pro vigilia, 14.25.
units.tr: Prison [φυλακή], for a jail, Matt. 5:25; for a watch, Matt. 14:25.

units.la: ΦΥΛΑΚΤΗΡΙΟΝ, filum erat, vel vitta hyacinthina in fimbria angu li, quo conspecto, memoria edictorum legitimorum conseruaretur: unde & φυλακτήριον, quasi conseruatorium dictum, Num. 15.38. Vel erant laminę aut membranulę quaedam ex Dei instituto fronti alligatę, Ex. 13.16. Deut. 6. quo ritu abusi sunt postea Iudaei ad superstitionem: quibus similes sunt, qui hodie amuleta de collo suspendunt, quibus initium Euangelij secundùm Ioannem inscriptum habent. Vide Mat. 23.5. v. Fimbriae.
units.tr: Phylactery [φυλακτήριον]: this was a thread, or a blue-violet fringe, on the hem of a garment, which when seen would keep the memory of the lawful commandments alive; hence it was also called phylactery, as if it were a keeping-place. Num. 15:38. Or there were certain thin plates or parchments tied to the forehead by God's institution, Exod. 13:16; Deut. 6, a rite which the Jews later abused for superstition. Those who today hang amulets from their necks, on which they have written the beginning of the Gospel according to John, are similar to them. See Matt. 23:5; Fringes.

units.la: G
units.tr: G

units.la: AAL filius Obed, pugnat aduersus Abimelech, Iud. 9.39. in fugam conuertitur, v.41. vrbe expellitur, v.41 (1. Abiectio siue abominatio.)
units.tr: Aal, son of Obed, fights against Abimelech, Judg. 9:39; he is turned to flight, v. 41; he is expelled from the city, v. 41. (1. Rejection or abomination.)

units.la: GABAON, metropolis Heuaeorum Ios. 10. obsidetur à quinq. Regib. v. 5. eius obsidi soluitur à Ios. v. 9.10. Leu. adscribitur, 21.17. (Gib. 1. collis) GABAONITAE: eorum calliditas, Iosue 9.v.3.4.5.6. eos foedus recipit Iosua, v.15. eorum calliditas reprehenditur, v.22. foedus cum eis confirmatur, sed ea lege, vt ligna caedant, & aquas portent in vsum Israelitarum, v.23.24. propter occisos à Saule Gabaonitas, fames ingens in Israel. Sam. am.21.v.12.crucifigunt septem filios Saulis v.9.10.
units.tr: Gibeon, a chief city of the Hivites, Josh. 10, is besieged by five kings, v. 5; its siege is lifted by Joshua, vv. 9–10. It is assigned to the Levites, 21:17. (Gib: a hill.) The GIBEONITES: their cunning, Josh. 9:3–6; Joshua receives them into covenant, v. 15; their cunning is rebuked, v. 22; the covenant with them is confirmed, but on this condition, that they cut wood and carry water for the use of the Israelites, vv. 23–24. On account of the Gibeonites slain by Saul, a great famine fell on Israel, 2 Sam. 21:12; the seven sons of Saul are crucified, vv. 9–10.

units.la: BRIEL Angelus, Danielis doctor, Dan.8.16. & 9.v.21.22. i Deo ad Zachariam missus, Lucæ 1. v.11.19. ad Deiparam Virginem, v 26.(1.fortitudo Dei.)
units.tr: GABRIEL, the angel, teacher of Daniel, Dan. 8:16; 9:21–22; sent by God to Zechariah, Luke 1:11, 19; and to the Virgin Mother of God, v. 26. (1. The strength of God.)

units.la: D (id est, turma) filius Iacob ex Lea nascitur, Gen.30.9.e- is benedictio, 49.19.Deut.33.20. Filij, Gen.46.16.
units.tr: Dan (that is, troop), son of Jacob, born of Leah, Gen. 30:9. His blessing: Gen. 49:19; Deut. 33:20. The sons: Gen. 46:16.

units.la: DITAE recipiunt suam hæreditatem, Num.32.1.&c.Deu. .12.Ios.13.4.
units.tr: The daughters receive their inheritance, Num. 32:1, etc.; Deut. 12; Josh. 13:4.

units.la: AD, idolum. Vide DOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: AD, an idol. See the catalogue of DOLORS.

units.la: D, Propheta Domini, admonet Dauidem, ne maneat, in terra Moabitarum, 1.Sam.22.5.1.Paral.21.9. nuntiat eidem ram Dei, 2.Sam.24.v.11.18.1.Par.21.11.
units.tr: D, a prophet of the Lord, warns David not to remain in the land of Moab, 1 Sam. 22:5; 1 Chr. 21:9; announces to him the word of God, 2 Sam. 24:11, 18; 1 Chr. 21:11.

units.la: IVS Macedo, qui & Caius, Pauli comes, Act.19.26.&20. .Rom.16.23.1.Cor.1.14.
units.tr: Jus of Macedonia, who is also called Gaius, Paul's companion, Acts 19:29; 20:4; Rom. 16:23; 1 Cor. 1:14.

units.la: LAAD siue Gilead nomen loci, (id est, cumulus testimonii) Gen.31.47.cur sic nominatur, v.48.
units.tr: Laad or Gilead, the name of a place (that is, heap of witness), Gen. 31:47. Why it is so named: v. 48.

units.la: LAAD, regio Galilææ vltra Iordanem, Orientem versus, Rubenitis & Gaditis habitanda cedit, Num.32.39.Deut.3. v.10.12.Ios.13.8. [Galaad, Pater Gedeonis, Iud.11.1.]
units.tr: Laad, a region of Galilee beyond the Jordan, toward the east, which was given to the Reubenites and Gadites to inhabit, Num. 32:39; Deut. 3:10, 12; Josh. 13:8. [Gilead, father of Gideon, Judg. 11:1.]

units.la: Galatia regio minoris Asiæ. Act.16.6.1. Cor.16.1.Gal.1.2. .1.Pet.11.
units.tr: Galatia, a region of Asia Minor. Acts 16:6; 1 Cor. 16:1; Gal. 1:2; 1 Pet. 1:1.

units.la: LATAE laudantur a Paulo, Galat.4.14.ab eodem obiurgantur, v.16.&3.1.eorum erga Paulum amor, 4.15.inconstantia.1.6.& 3 3.& 4.9.
units.tr: The Galatians are praised by Paul, Gal. 4:14, and rebuked by the same, v. 16; 3:1. Their love towards Paul, 4:15; their inconstancy, 1:6; 3:3; 4:9.

units.la: GALGAL, siue Galgala, loci nomen, Ios.4.19.ratio eius nominis, 5. 9.ibi circumciditur populus, & celebrat Pascha, 5.v. 7.10. egreditur inde ad liberandos Gabaonitas, 10.7.restitutur, v.43.(1.rota seu sphæra.)
units.tr: Gilgal, or Galgala, the name of a place, Josh. 4:19; the reason for the name, 5:9. There the people are circumcised and celebrate the Passover, 5:7, 10. From there they set out to free the Gibeonites, 10:7; it is restored, v. 43. (1. A wheel or sphere.)

units.la: GALILAEA regio duplex, Superior, quæ Gentium cognominata est, sita in tribu Nephthali & Aser: inferior in trib. Zabulon & Issachar, circa Tiberiadem & lacum Genezareth anum posita, vtramq. Christus præsentia & prædicatione sua beauit, totámq. bis circumiuit, Ios.13.2.& 20.7.1. eg.9.11.Esai.9.1.Matth.2.22.& 4.v.23.& 17.22. & frequens mentio harum, occurrit apud Euangelistas, Act.9.31.& 10. 7.& 13 31.]
units.tr: Galilee is a twofold region: Upper, which is called Galilee of the Gentiles, lying in the tribes of Naphtali and Asher; and Lower, in the tribes of Zebulun and Issachar, situated around Tiberias and the Lake of Gennesaret. Christ blessed both with his presence and preaching, and went round the whole of it twice. Josh. 13:2; 20:7; 1 Kgs. 9:11; Isa. 9:1; Matt. 2:22; 4:23; 17:22. Frequent mention of these occurs in the Evangelists, Acts 9:31; 10:37; 13:31.

units.la: GALILAEA Gentium a Christo illuminatur, Matt.4.v.15.16 Galilæi Christum excipiunt, Ioan. 4, 45.in Galilæa incipit Christus prædicare. Matt.4.12. Actor.10.37.
units.tr: Galilee of the Gentiles is illuminated by Christ, Matt. 4:15–16. The Galileans receive Christ, John 4:45. Christ begins to preach in Galilee, Matt. 4:12; Acts 10:37.

units.la: Galliæ, proconsul Achaiæ, qui Iudæos Corinthi accusantes Paulu hæreseos depulit a Tribunali: Act.18.14.
units.tr: Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, who, when the Jews of Corinth accused Paul of heresy, drove them away from the tribunal, Acts 18:14.

units.la: AMALIEL Dux Manassitarum, Num.1.10. Pharisæus, vir peritus Legis, Act.5.v.34. eius de Apostolis dimittédis cõl liũ.5.v.38.39. Pauli præceptor, Act.22.3.1. Retributio Dei)
units.tr: Gamaliel, leader of the Manassites, Num. 1:10. A Pharisee, a man skilled in the Law, Acts 5:34. His counsel on dismissing the apostles, Acts 5:38–39. Paul's teacher, Acts 22:3. (Retribution of God.)

units.la: GAMARIAS. pius & fidelis consiliarius, contradicens Ioachin regi Iudæ comburenti concionesᵢ & insidianti vitæ Hieremiæ. Hier.36.10.
units.tr: Gemariah, a pious and faithful counsellor, who opposed King Jehoiakim of Judah when he burned the sermons and plotted against the life of Jeremiah. Jer. 36:10.

units.la: GARIZIM, mons benedictionis, Deut.27.12. (12. Scissores)
units.tr: Gerizim, the mountain of blessing, Deut. 27:12. (12. Cutters.)

units.la: GATH, ciuitas Palæstinæ, in qua Gigantes erant, vt Goliath 1.Sa.17.23. Ad Achis regē Gath Dauid aufugit. 2.Sam.21.1
units.tr: Gath, a city of Palestine, in which there were giants, such as Goliath, 1 Sam. 17:23. David fled to Achish, king of Gath, 2 Sam. 21:1.

units.la: GAVDENDVM cum gaudentibus, Rom.12.15.
units.tr: One must rejoice with those who rejoice, Rom. 12:15.

units.la: GAVDERE & lætari honestè licet, 1. Par.29 9.2. Esdr.12.43 Ps.68.4. Luc.1.14.1.Thess.1.6.& 5.16.
units.tr: It is lawful to rejoice and be glad honestly: 1 Chr. 29:9; Ezra 12:43; Ps. 68:4; Luke 1:14; 1 Thess. 1:6; 5:16.

units.la: GAVDENDVM non est Gentilium more, Eccles.2.2.& 7.3. O sæx 9.1. Amos.6.3.4.5.8. Pro.2.14. Iacobi 4.9.
units.tr: One must not rejoice after the manner of the Gentiles: Eccl. 2:2; 7:3; Hos. 9:1; Amos 6:3–8; Prov. 2:14; James 4:9.

units.la: GAVDIVM piorum, Est lætitia fidelium, quæ ex cognitione Dei, ac bonitatis eius erga nos per Iesum Christum senti & gustu nascitur. ps.34.9. Gustate & videte bonum esse le houam. phil.4.4. Gaudete in Domino semper.
units.tr: The joy of the godly is the gladness of the faithful, which arises from the knowledge of God and of his goodness towards us through Jesus Christ, felt and tasted. Ps. 34:9: "Taste and see that the LORD is good." Phil. 4:4: "Rejoice in the Lord always."

units.la: Gaudium impiorũ est, vana & momentanea & phreneticorũ gaudio similis (quia non in Domino, sed plerunq. i malis & fallacibus rebus situm est) oblectatio. Isa.22.1 &c.pro.2.14. Lętantur qui malefaciũt, & exultant in rebu pessimis, quorũ viæ peruersæ sunt. Gaudij impiorũ mis exitus Iob.20.5. pro.14.13.& 17.5. Luc.6.25. Isa.22.13.&c. Exépla: Baltazar, Dan.5.4. Israelitæ, Act.7.41. Philistini, Iud 16.25.30. Hamã, Est.7.10. Achab, 1.Reg.21.16.19. v. Ier.7.3
units.tr: The joy of the impious is a vain and momentary delight, like the joy of madmen, because it rests not in the Lord but mostly in evil and deceitful things. Isa. 22:1ff.; Prov. 2:14: "The wicked rejoice in doing evil and exult in the worst things, whose ways are perverse." The end of the impious joy: Job 20:5; Prov. 14:13; 17:5; Luke 6:25; Isa. 22:13, etc. Examples: Belshazzar, Dan. 5:4; the Israelites, Acts 7:41; the Philistines, Judg. 16:25, 30; Haman, Esth. 7:10; Ahab, 1 Kgs. 21:16, 19. See Jer. 7:3.

units.la: GAVDIVM pro rebus secundis & prosperis, 1. Corinth.7.3 Hebraismus: Gaudiũ quàm bonum, Pro.17.22. Gaudiu verum à Deo Esd.6.22. Neh.12.42.43. Gaudiũ verũ quali Deu.12.18.& 16.11.& 26.11. Ps.9.v.2.15.& 13.5.& 14.7.& 1 9.& 31.8.& 32.11.& 33.21.& 35.9.& 40.17.& 48.12.& 51.10. 53.7.& 58.11.& 63.v.6.8.& 64.11.& 66.2.& 68.5.& 69.33. 70.5. & 71.23.& 86.10.& 89.17.&90.v.14.15.& 92.5.& 9 1.& 97.v.8.12.& 100.1.& 104.34.&105.3.& 107.42.& 119.7 & 122 1.& 149.v.2.5. Pr.13.9.& 21.15.& 29.v.2.6. Cant. 1. Esa.9.2. Gal.5.22. (Vide Piorvm gaudium) Gaudium vel quod, Luc.10.20. Gaudiũ in afflictionibus, Matth.5.v.11.1 Act.5.41.& 20.24. Rō.5.3. Co.1.24. He.10.34.&11.25. Gaud ob piorũ liberationem, Ps.35.27. Ph.1.v.25.26. [Gaudiũ ve rum à Spiritu Sancto proficiscitur, Rom.12.12.& 14.17. Ga 5.22. Philip. 4.4. 1.Thess.5.16. gaudium salutis æternæ, Sa 1.v.1.7. Esa.25.18.& 26.1.& 32.20.& 63.13. [Vide Beati pp. gaudium Christi, Vide Christvs.)
units.tr: JOY, for prosperous and favourable circumstances: 1 Cor. 7.3. A Hebraism: "How good is joy" (Prov. 17.22). True joy from God: Ezra 6.22; Neh. 12.42–43. True joy of what kind: Deut. 12.18; 16.11; 26.11; Ps. 9.2, 15; 13.5; 14.7; 19; 31.8; 32.11; 33.21; 35.9; 40.17; 48.12; 51.10; 53.7; 58.11; 63.6, 8; 64.11; 66.2; 68.5; 69.33; 70.5; 71.23; 86.10; 89.17; 90.14–15; 92.5; 91; 97.8, 12; 100.1; 104.34; 105.3; 107.42; 119.7; 122.1; 149.2, 5; Prov. 13.9; 21.15; 29.2, 6; Song 1; Isa. 9.2; Gal. 5.22. (See the joy of the godly.) Joy in or because of something: Luke 10.20. Joy in afflictions: Matt. 5.11; Acts 5.41; 20.24; Rom. 5.3; Col. 1.24; Heb. 10.34; 11.25. Joy at the deliverance of the godly: Ps. 35.27; Phil. 1.25–26. [True joy comes from the Holy Spirit: Rom. 12.12; 14.17; Gal. 5.22; Phil. 4.4; 1 Thess. 5.16. Joy of eternal salvation: Sir. 1.1, 7; Isa. 25.18; 26.1; 32.20; 63.13.] [See Blessed, the joy of Christ; see Christ.]

units.la: Gaudij veri exempla: Anna, 1.Sam.2.1. Saul & viri Israe
units.tr: Examples of true joy: Hannah, 1 Sam. 2.1. Saul and the men of Israel

units.la: 15.2. Mulieres Israeliticæ, 18.7. Dauid & Israelitæ, 2. Sam. verf 5.14.15. Populus, 1. Reg. 1. v. 39.40.45. & 8.66. 2. Reg. 1.20. Dauid cum toto Israel, 1. Par. 13.8. & 29.22. Hiram, 1. Reg. 5.7. Leuit. 2 Par. 5. 12. Populus Israeliticus, 7.10. Habitatores Ierusalem, 20.27. Populus terræ, 23. verf. 13.21. Populus à captiuitate redux, 1. Esdr. 6.16. Neh. 8. verf. 12.18. 12. 42. Ciuitas Susan, Esth. 8.15. Iudæi, ver. 16.17. Magi, Matth. 2.10. Magdalena & altera Maria, 28. 8. septuagin- ta duo Discipuli, Luc. 10.17. Discipuli, 24.41. Act. 5. 41. & 3.52. & 15.3. Ioan. 20.20. Samaria, Act. 8.8. Rhode puella, 1.14. Custos carceris, 16 34. Paulus, 2. Corinth. 7. v. 4.7.13. Philem. v. 7.
units.tr: 15.2. The Israelite women, 18.7. David and the Israelites, 2 Sam. 5.14–15. The people, 1 Kings 1.39–40, 45; 8.66; 2 Kings 1.20. David with all Israel, 1 Chron. 13.8; 29.22. Hiram, 1 Kings 5.7. The Levites, 2 Chron. 5.12. The Israelite people, 7.10. The inhabitants of Jerusalem, 20.27. The people of the land, 23.13, 21. The people returning from captivity, Ezra 6.16; Neh. 8.12, 18; 12.42. The city of Susa, Esth. 8.15. The Jews, 8.16–17. The Magi, Matt. 2.10. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, 28.8. The seventy-two disciples, Luke 10.17. The disciples, 24.41; Acts 5.41; 13.52; 15.3; John 20.20. Samaria, Acts 8.8. Rhoda the maidservant, 12.14. The jailer, 16.34. Paul, 2 Cor. 7.4, 7, 13; Philem. 7.

units.la: GAZA ciuitas Palæstinæ à filiis Iuda capta, Iudic. 1. 18, eius excidium prædicitur, Amos. 1.6. Act. 8.26.
units.tr: GAZA, a city of Palestine captured by the sons of Judah, Judg. 1.18. Its destruction is foretold, Amos 1.6; Acts 8.26.

units.la: GEBER, vrbs obsessa à Iosua, Ios. 10 33. Nec tamen inde exulsus fuit Chananatus, Ios. 16 10. In sorte tribus Ephraim Leuitis separata: c. 21. v. 21. A Pharaone (occiso Chananeo) iccensa est, & Solomoni in dotem suæ filiæ data: 1. Reg. 9. 6. Et ab hoc postea ædificata: v. 17.
units.tr: GEBER, a city besieged by Joshua, Josh. 10.33. Yet the Canaanites were not driven out from there, Josh. 16.10. Allotted within the tribe of Ephraim and set apart for the Levites, ch. 21.21. Burned by Pharaoh (after he had killed the Canaanite) and given to Solomon as a dowry for his daughter, 1 Kings 9.16. And afterwards rebuilt by him, v. 17.

units.la: GAZOPHYLACIVM grande, Nehemiæ tempore, Nehem. 13. à Ioiada constitutum, 2. Reg. 12.9 &c. sic vocatur aliqua templi regio seu arca conferendis oblationibus destinata, Ioan. 8.20. Marc. 12.41. ad finem vsque Luc. 21.1. (Vox ex Persico & Græco composita).
units.tr: GAZOPHYLACIUM, a great one, in the time of Nehemiah, Neh. 13; set up by Jehoiada, 2 Kings 12.9 etc. Some region or chest of the temple intended for receiving offerings is so called, John 8.20; Mark 12.41; as far as Luke 21.1. (The word is compounded from Persian and Greek.)

units.la: GIDEON, præter spem Israelitis liberator à Deo excitatur, Iudic. 6.14. signo se confirmari petit, verf. 17. signum obtinet v. 18.19.20. Ara Bahalis destruere iubetur, v. 25 id praestat, v. 27. ob id Ierobaal dicitur, v. 32. partem exercitus dimittere iubetur, 7. v. 2.4.5. Zebali & Salmana occidit, 8.21. Ephod confecto, Israeli idololatriæ occasionem præbuit, v. 27. (Vide EPHOD) Polygamus erat, v. 30. filios septuaginta habebat, v. 30. Moritur. 27. (GIDEON. 1. exterminator, denoliens.)
units.tr: GIDEON, a deliverer raised up by God for Israel contrary to hope, Judg. 6.14. He asks to be confirmed by a sign, v. 17, and obtains the sign, vv. 18–20. He is ordered to destroy the altar of Baal, v. 25, and does so, v. 27; for this he is called Jerubbaal, v. 32. He is ordered to dismiss part of the army, 7.2, 4–5. He kills Zebah and Zalmunna, 8.21. Having made an ephod, he gave Israel an occasion for idolatry, v. 27. (See EPHOD.) He was a polygamist, v. 30, and had seventy sons, v. 30. He dies, v. 27. (GIDEON: one who exterminates, who tears down.)

units.la: GEHENNA: Gehennæ vox Hebræa est, ex duabus גֵּי Ge, & הִנֹּם Hinnom, Ios. 15.8. composita, & vallem Hinnom declarat (qui locus Hierosolymæ vicinus erat.) quæ etiā Tophet dicitur, in qua olim Israelitæ superstitionibus vicinarum gentium addicti, filios suos Diis alienis adolebāt, inaudita quadā immanitate. Tophet dicebatur à sono tympanorum, quibus interea omnia resonabant, ne miserè ardētium iulatus exaudiretur. v. Esa. 30.33. Inde factum, vt acciperetur pro reproborum supplicio, & loco cruciatus in æternum reprobis destinato, ybi perpetuò torquebitur than cum Angelis suis, Mat.5.22. Mar.9.43. Vide & Le 18.21.& 20.2. Ios.1,8.2. Reg. 23.10. Iere. 7. v. 31.32.33. 19.5. Gehennæ filius quis dicatur, Vide Filius gehenn
units.tr: GEHENNA: the word Gehenna is Hebrew, compounded of two words, גֵּי Ge and הִנֹּם Hinnom (Josh. 15.8), and denotes the valley of Hinnom, a place near Jerusalem. It is also called Tophet, where once the Israelites, given over to the superstitions of the neighbouring nations, burned their sons as offerings to foreign gods with an unheard-of cruelty. It was called Tophet from the sound of the drums, which then resounded on every side, so that the wretched howling of those being burned might not be heard. See Isa. 30.33. Hence it came to be used for the punishment of the reprobate, and for the place of torment destined for the reprobate in eternity, where the devil with his angels will be tormented forever, Matt. 5.22; Mark 9.43. See also Lev. 18.21; 20.2; Josh. 1.8; 2 Kings 23.10; Jer. 7.31–33; 19.5. Who is called a son of Gehenna? See Son of Gehenna.

units.la: GEHON siue Gichon, fluuius, in paradiso oriens: Gen. 2.
units.tr: GEHON or Gihon, a river rising in Paradise: Gen. 2.

units.la: GEMITVS, quis probandus, quis improbandus, Exod. 2.2. Ezech.9.4.2. Mach.6.30. Rom.8.22. Iac.5.9. Act.7.34.
units.tr: GROANING: which is to be approved, which to be disapproved: Exod. 2.23; Ezek. 9.4; 2 Macc. 6.30; Rom. 8.22; James 5.9; Acts 7.34.

units.la: GENEALOGIA Genealogiæ non magnopere cur dæ, 1 Tim.1 4. Tit.3.9. Genealogia Adam, Israel, Christ. Vide in suis propriis nominibus V. Hebr.7.3
units.tr: GENEALOGY. Genealogies are not to be greatly cared about: 1 Tim. 1.4; Titus 3.9. Genealogy of Adam, of Israel, of Christ. See under their own names. Heb. 7.3.

units.la: GENERATIO, Græcis & pro historica rerum narratione, Genes.6.9.& 25.19.& 37.2.& sic accipi debet hoc vocabulum, manifestum est: quia hic titulus genera-tim ad totam historiam accommodatur, quæ postea subiun-gitur, vt sit sensus: Hæc sunt quæ acciderunt Noe, Isaac, &c. pro primo ortu & origine, Genes.2.4. pro generis si-putatione & genealogia, 10.1.& 25.12.& 36,1. Ruth. 4. pro vnius seculi, seu ætatis hominibus, Gen.15.16. Hebr. 3.10. id est, pro progenie vnius ætatis, Matt.11.16.& 23. pro ætate 24.34. pro certo hominum genere, & spec- Luc.16.8. pro natiuitate, Matt.1.18. Generatio spiritua- Ioan.1,13.1. Cor.4.15. 1.Ioh.5.18.
units.tr: GENERATION. The Greeks also use it for the historical narration of events: Gen. 6.9; 25.19; 37.2. That this word must be understood so is clear, because this title applies generally to the whole history that follows, so that the sense is: These are the things that befell Noah, Isaac, etc. It means the first origin and beginning: Gen. 2.4. It means the reckoning of a lineage and genealogy: 10.1; 25.12; 36.1; Ruth 4.18. It means the people of one age or lifetime: Gen. 15.16; Heb. 3.10, that is, the offspring of one generation: Matt. 11.16; 23.36. It means an age: 24.34. It means a certain kind of men: Luke 16.8. It means birth: Matt. 1.18. Spiritual generation: John 1.13; 1 Cor. 4.15; 1 John 5.18.

units.la: [Generatio, pro duratione perpetua, Esai.53.8. Act.8. pro cogitatione, Gen.31.3. pro genitura, Ezec.16.3.1. Ti 2.15. pro gente & natione Matth.12.39.41.42. &c, Act 40. Hebr. 3.10. pro genere, Luc.16.8. Hebr.7.6, pro na-uitate, Matth.1,18. pro origine Genes.2.1. pro progeni- Matth.1.17. Generatio Dei, seu qui genitus est ex Dec Ioan.5.18.]
units.tr: [Generation, meaning continuous duration: Isa. 53.8; Acts 8.33. Meaning thought: Gen. 31.3. Meaning begetting: Ezek. 16.3; 1 Tim. 2.15. Meaning a people or nation: Matt. 12.39, 41–42, etc.; Acts 2.40; Heb. 3.10. Meaning a kind: Luke 16.8; Heb. 7.6. Meaning birth: Matt. 1.18. Meaning origin: Gen. 2.1. Meaning offspring: Matt. 1.17. The generation of God, that is, one begotten of God: John 5.18.]

units.la: GENERANDI vim indidit Deus omnibus quę super te-ram sunt, Gen.1 11.& 9.v.1,7.
units.tr: God implanted the power of generating in all things that are upon the earth: Gen. 1.11; 9.1, 7.

units.la: Tophet dicebatur à sono tympanorū, quibus inten- omnia resonabant, ne miserè ardentium eiulatus exau-retur. V. Esa.30.33.
units.tr: Tophet was so called from the sound of the drums, which resounded on every side, so that the wretched howling of those being burned might not be heard. See Isa. 30.33.

units.la: GENS, nempe Israelitica, in 12 tribus distincta, sub Rob-mo in regnum Iudaicum & Israeliticum diuisa, tandem dæorum gens & natio dicta, Gen.12,2. Exo.19,6, Deu.4. Ezech .35.10. Luc.7.5.& 23.2. Ioan.11.v.48.50.52 & 18. Act.10.22.& 24.v.10.17.& 26.4.& 28.19.
units.tr: NATION: the Israelite nation, divided into twelve tribes, split under Rehoboam into the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, and finally called the nation and people of the Jews: Gen. 12.2; Exod. 19.6; Deut. 4; Ezek. 35.10; Luke 7.5; 23.2; John 11.48, 50, 52; 18; Acts 10.22; 24.10, 17; 26.4; 28.19.

units.la: Gens, electi Dei, Psal.33.12. Esa.16.2.1 Pet.2.9. Ap.21.
units.tr: A nation: the elect of God: Ps. 33.12; Isa. 16.2; 1 Pet. 2.9; Rev. 21.

units.la: Gens, natio populus, turba nymerosissima in quapi-reg gione viuens, Gen.15.14. Pfal.105.13. Prou.14.34. Esa.2.4. r.2.11. Ioel.3.8. Aba.1.17. Luc.21.10. Act.8.9.2. Cor.11.32.
units.tr: A nation, a people, a very numerous crowd living in some region: Gen. 15.14; Ps. 105.13; Prov. 14.34; Isa. 2.4; Jer. 2.11; Joel 3.8; Hab. 1.17; Luke 21.10; Acts 8.9; 2 Cor. 11.32.

units.la: Gens, hypocritae, impij nebulones in populo Iudaico, Pfal.43. 1. Esa.1.4. & 10.6. & 49.7.
units.tr: A nation: hypocrites, wicked scoundrels among the Jewish people: Ps. 43.1; Isa. 1.4; 10.6; 49.7.

units.la: Gens figuratè sumitur pro locustarum numerosissimis minibus què fruges terrę vorarunt & consumpserunt, Ioel.1.6.
units.tr: A nation is figuratively taken for the very numerous locusts and swarms that devoured and consumed the fruits of the earth: Joel 1.6.

units.la: Gentes synecdochicè pro primis parentibus & stirpi-us duarum gentium, Gen.25.23.
units.tr: Nations, by synecdoche, for the first parents and the stocks of the two nations: Gen. 25.23.

units.la: Gentes, populi, vel multi, vel omnes, præter Iudæos: ex-a fœdus, incircuncisi, Gentiles: quorum magna pars ad Christi cognitionem adducta per Euangelium, familia Dei per fidem in Mediatores insita est. Gen. 10. 5. & 22. & 49. 10. Exo.30.10. Leu.1.8.24. Iud.2.21. Sam.8.20.2. Reg.16.3.2. Par.9.14. Esdr.4.10. Pfal.2.v.1.8. Esa.2.2. Ioel.2. Malach.1.11. Act.13.v.47.48. Rom.1.5. & 3.29. & 11.v.12. 25.1. Cor.1.23. Eph.2.11. Apoc.11.2. & 22.2.
units.tr: Nations, peoples, whether many or all, apart from the Jews: aliens from the covenant, uncircumcised, Gentiles; a large part of whom has been brought to knowledge of Christ through the Gospel, and by faith in the Mediator has been grafted into the family of God. Gen. 10.5; 22; 49.10; Exod. 30.10; Lev. 1.8, 24; Judg. 2.21; 1 Sam. 8.20; 2 Kings 16.3; 2 Chron. 9.14; Ezra 4.10; Ps. 2.1, 8; Isa. 2.2; Joel 2; Mal. 1.11; Acts 13.47–48; Rom. 1.5; 3.29; 11.12, 25; 1 Cor. 1.23; Eph. 2.11; Rev. 11.2; 22.2.
Nations, inhabitants of the world: Isa. 40.15, 17; Matt. 20.25; 24.14; 25.32; 28.19; Rev. 12.15.
Nations, the slaves of Antichrist: Rev. 13.7; 14.8; 16.2; 17.15; 18.3, 23; 20.3, 8.

units.la: GENTES: Gentes omnes in gloriam Dei creatæ, Deut.26.19. ut paulatim ejectæ e terra Chanaan, 7.22. cur ibidem re-ctæ, Iud.3.1. Gentes ignorantiæ prętextu non excusandę Rom.2.14. Gentes pro nationibus à Dei cultu & fœdere alienis, 1.Cor.12.2. vt explicatur Ephef. 2. v.11.12. Gentes Legem non habentes (quod tamen non simpliciter, sed κατὰ φύσιν est intelligendum, id est, habita Iudæorum ratione, quibus Deus singula Legis capita tradidit, Exo. 20.1.) quæ legis sunt, faciunt, Roman.2.14. hoc est, honesta iubent, turpia prohibent, & puniunt.
units.tr: NATIONS: all nations were created for the glory of God: Deut. 26.19; but they were gradually cast out of the land of Canaan, 7.22, and for this reason were punished there, Judg. 3.1. Nations, in ignorance, are not excused on the pretext of ignorance: Rom. 2.14. Nations, meaning peoples alien from the worship and covenant of God: 1 Cor. 12.2, as explained in Eph. 2.11–12. The Gentiles, who do not have the law (which, however, must be understood not simply but [κατὰ φύσιν] by nature, that is, in view of the Jews' situation, to whom God gave the individual chapters of the Law, Exod. 20.1), do the things of the law, Rom. 2.14: that is, they command what is honourable and forbid and punish what is shameful.

Abominations of the Gentiles are to be avoided: Deut. 12.30, 18.9; Josh. 23.12. The conduct of the Gentiles before Christ was known: Eph. 2.3; 1 Pet. 4.3; Acts 14.16. The conversion and calling of the Gentiles is foretold: Gen. 9.27, 17.5, 19, 49.10; Deut. 32.21; 2 Sam. 22.44; Ps. 2.8, 18.44, 22.29–31, 72.11, 86.1, 87.4, 96.7, 98.2, 117.1; Isa. 9.1–2, 11.10, 14.1, 42.4, 44.5, 49.20–22, 50.10, 52.15, 54.1–5, 55.4–5, 56.3, 7, 57.19, 60.3, 65.1, 66.1, 8; Jer. 3.7, 16.19; Hos. 1.10, 2.23; Joel 2.28; Zech. 2.11, 8.11; Matt. 2.18, 21, 21.43, 22.9, 28.19; Mark 11.17, 16.15; Luke 3.31–32, 13.29, 14.21–23, 24.47; John 10.16, 11.52; Acts 1.8, 2.39, 9.15, 10.15, 35, 11.20, 13.46, 27, 15.14, 17, 17.30, 28.28; Rom. 1.5, 14, 16, 9.24–25, 10.19–20, 11.11, 15.9–11, 21, Gal. 3.8, 4.27; 1 Tim. 2.6–7; 2 Tim. 1.11, 4.17; 1 Pet. 2.9; Rev. 7.9, 10.11, 14.6, 15.4, 21.24. The calling of the Gentiles was a certain hidden mystery: Rom. 16.25; Eph. 3.5–6; 1 Tim. 3.16, allegorically signified: Matt. 22.9. The Gentiles and the Jews are joined: Zech. 8.23; Acts 15.3. The Gentiles' expectation of Christ: Gen. 49.10; Isa. 11.10. The weakness of the Gentiles: Isa. 40.17; Dan. 4.32.

units.la: GENTILES, sive Gentes, sive Græci, pro Iudæis inter G cos dispersis,Ioan.7.35.& 12.20. Gentiū mores non in di,Leu.20.23.Ier.10.2.Gens non gens dicitur Mosi,D 32.21.Rom.10.19. omnes profani populi: sicut viuere dicuntur, qui æternis suppliciis sunt addicti, sed mori
units.tr: GENTILES, or nations, or Greeks, is said of the Jews dispersed among the Gentiles: John 7.35, 12.20. The customs of the Gentiles are not to be imitated: Lev. 20.23; Jer. 10.2. "Not a nation" is said by Moses of a people that is not a nation: Deut. 32.21; Rom. 10.19. All profane peoples. Just as those are said to live who are doomed to eternal punishments, but to die...

units.la: GENV omne flectendum Domino, Psal.22.30. Esai.4 Rom.14.1 .Phil.2.10.non idolis .1.Reg.19.18. Genu fl in precibus vsitata. Exempla:Salomon,1 Reg.8.54 2 P 13.Elias,1 Reg.18.42. quinquagenarius miles,Re.1.13. L tę,2.Par.29.30.Esdras,1 Esd.9.5.Serui.Regis Assueri,I 3.2.Daniel, Dan.6.10. Michæas, Mich.6 6.Pater Luna Matt. 17.14.Leprosus,Marc.1.40.Luc.5.12.Petrus,5.8. 9.40. Christus, Luc.22.41. Stephanus, Act.7.60. Pa cum suis,20.36.& 21.5.Paulus cum Ecclesia,21.5.Sunt colligant Israelitas stantes precari solitos,ex Mar.1 cùm potius verisimile sit, si non semper,at certè plera que solenni ritu flexis genibus orasse,vt apparet ex Da 10.adeò quidem,vt flectere genua pro toto Dei cult terdum accipiatur,vt 1 Reg.19.18 Mich.6.6. Est ergo sus dicti apud Marcum: Cùm apparueritis coram a Domini preces vestras fundentes,&c.Inobedientium nua vlcerātur: Deut.28.35. GERAR,metropolis terræ lestinæ in qua habitauit Abraham: Ge.20.1.Et Isaac,2 (z.6.17..1.peregrinatio
units.tr: KNEE: every knee must bow to the Lord: Ps. 22.30; Isa. 45.23; Rom. 14.11; Phil. 2.10, not to idols: 1 Kings 19.18. Bending the knee was a common custom in prayers. Examples: Solomon, 1 Kings 8.54; 2 Chron. 6.13; Elijah, 1 Kings 18.42; the captain of fifty, 2 Kings 1.13; Hezekiah, 2 Chron. 29.30; Ezra, Ezra 9.5; the servants of King Ahasuerus, Esther 3.2; Daniel, Dan. 6.10; Micah, Mic. 6.6; the father of the lunatic boy, Matt. 17.14; the leper, Mark 1.40; Luke 5.12; Peter, Luke 5.8; 9.40; Christ, Luke 22.41; Stephen, Acts 7.60; Paul with his companions, Acts 20.36, 21.5; Paul with the Church, Acts 21.5. They gather that the Israelites were accustomed to pray standing, from Mark 1..., though it is more likely that, if not always, at least most of the time, they prayed with bended knees in a solemn rite, as appears from Dan. 10. So much so that bending the knees is sometimes taken for the whole worship of God, as in 1 Kings 19.18 and Mic. 6.6. Therefore the saying in Mark: "When you shall appear before the Lord pouring out your prayers," etc. Disobedient ones are smitten in the knees: Deut. 28.35. GERAR, the chief city of the land of the Philistines, where Abraham dwelt: Gen. 20.1; and Isaac, Gen. 26.6, 17; a place of sojourning.

units.la: GERGESENI vel GERASENI, Christum vt à se discedat gant,Matth.8.34. Mar.5.17.Luc.8.37.
units.tr: GERGESENES or GERASENES, who asked Christ to depart from their territory: Matt. 8.34; Mark 5.17; Luke 8.37.

units.la: GERSON (id est,peregrinus pulsus, composita voce ex regrinatione & peregrinationis causa)filius Mosis è phora nascitur, Exodi 2.22.ratio eius nominis, ibid. 18 3. circumciditur, 4.25. [Filius Manasse, Iof.18.30. Phinees,Edr.8.2.]
units.tr: GERSHOM (that is, a stranger expelled; a compound word from "stranger" and "sojourning", the cause of the sojourn), son of Moses, born in the land of Midian: Exod. 2.22; the reason for the name, ibid. 18.3; circumcised, 4.25. [Son of Manasseh, Josh. 18.30. Phinehas, Ezra 8.2.]

units.la: GERSON,filius Leui,Num.3.17 Gersonitarum minis rium,3.25.& 4.22.fors,Iosu.21.6.1.Par.6.1.
units.tr: GERSHON, son of Levi: Num. 3.17. The ministry of the Gershonites: 3.25 and 4.22; perhaps Josh. 21.6; 1 Chron. 6.1.

units.la: VR, regio Syricæ. Ren. 3.3.1. par 2.23. & 3.2.
units.tr: UR, a region of Syria: Gen. 3.3.1; 2 Chron. 2.23, 3.2.

units.la: H, Ios .11.22. expugnatur ab Hazael, Syriæ Regè, 2 g 12.17. Gesen, vide Goschen.
units.tr: GATH: Josh. 11.22; taken by Hazael, king of Syria: 2 Kings 12.17. GESHEN, see Goshen.

units.la: HSEMANE, vallis ad radices montis Oliueti, vbi Chri- ante passionem orauit: mat 26.36. More.14. Ge, vallis, hen.1.pinguedo).
units.tr: GETHSEMANE, a valley at the foot of the Mount of Olives, where Christ prayed before his passion: Matt. 26.36; Mark 14. Ge, a valley; hen, fatness.

units.la: z 1 minilter Elisæi, 2 Regum 4.v.12.25. missus vt pue m suscitet, operam ludit, v.31. mentitus munera àNaa nn Syro sanato petit, 5.23. ob id lepra percutitur &poste eius. v.26.27. Regi Israelis, quę fecerat Eliseus, narrat, 8.5.
units.tr: GEHAZI, the servant of Elisha: 2 Kings 4.12, 25. Sent to raise the boy, he labours in vain: v. 31. Lying, he asks gifts from Naaman the Syrian, once healed: 5.23. On account of this he is struck with leprosy, and his descendants too: vv. 26–27. He tells the king of Israel what Elisha had done: 8.5.

units.la: INTES viri potentes, & Dei contemtores, Genesis 6.4. im.13.23. Deut.2.11. Gigantes quatuor à Dauide diuer- præliis percussi, 2. Sam.21.22. V.1, Sam.17.49.
units.tr: GIANTS: powerful men and despisers of God: Gen. 6.4; Num. 13.33; Deut. 2.11. Four giants were struck down by David in battles: 2 Sam. 21.22; 1 Sam. 17.49.

units.la: Gigno, 1. de Deo Patre dicitur, Psalm. 2.7. Actor.13.33. br.1.5.& 5.5. II. De generatione spirituali, hominum esertim respectu, Esai.51.18.1. Cor.4.15. Philem.10.1. Pet.
units.tr: To beget. I. Said of God the Father: Ps. 2.7; Acts 13.33; Heb. 1.5, 5.5. II. Of spiritual generation, especially with regard to men: Isa. 51.18; 1 Cor. 4.15; Philem. 10; 1 Pet. ...

units.la: III. De homine, & humana generatione, frequenter itur, Gen.4.18.&c. IV. De terra, & animantibus ratio- carentibus, Leu.11.9. Num. 18.13. Iudic.18.10. V. De re- inanimatis quas colunt idololatræ, dictum Ier.2.27.
units.tr: III. Of man and human generation, frequently: Gen. 4.18, etc. IV. Of the earth and of living creatures without reason: Lev. 11.9; Num. 18.13; Judg. 18.10. V. Of inanimate things worshipped by idolaters: said in Jer. 2.27.

units.la: dboe mons in tribu Manassis 1.Sam. 28.4. &c.31.1.1. ron.10.1.&c.
units.tr: GILBOA, a mountain in the tribe of Manasseh: 1 Sam. 28.4, etc.; 31.1; 1 Chron. 10.1, etc.

units.la: CIES, est aquarū in ima huius aeris siue expãsionis par- sistētiâ cõglobatio siue cõcretio, à Deo vi frigoris facta cõpacta. Io.38.29.&37.10. ps.14.7.17. Sa.16.22.29. Ec.3.16.
units.tr: ICE: is a congealing or solidifying of waters in the lowest part of this air or expanse, made firm by God through the force of cold. Job 38.29, 37.10; Ps. 147.17; Sir. 16.22, 29; Eccl. 3.16.

units.la: IDIVS & eius ius, Ge.9.6. Exodi 21.12. Leuit.24.17. Deut. V.II.12. Rom.13.4.1. Petr.2.14. non cuiuis permittendus. tth.26.52. Marc.14.47. Luc.22.49. Ioann.18.10. gladiū ipere dicuntur, Matth.26.52. qui gladium à Domino 1 traditum sibi ipsis vendicant & vsurpant: hoc est, præter vocationem gladio vtuntur. Apoc.13.10. Gla- s Christi & spiritus est verbum Dei, Esa.11:4. & 27.1. 31.8.& 49.2.& 66.16. Eph.6.17. Hebr.4.12.2. Thess.2.8. oc.1.16.& 2.16.& 19.15.
units.tr: SWORD and its right: Gen. 9.6; Exod. 21.12; Lev. 24.17; Deut. 32.41–42; Rom. 13.4; 1 Pet. 2.14; not to be permitted to anyone: Matt. 26.52; Mark 14.47; Luke 22.49; John 18.10. Those who take the sword are said to take up what was given to them by the Lord, i.e., those who claim and usurp for themselves the sword, that is, use it apart from a calling. Rev. 13.10. The sword of Christ and of the Spirit is the word of God: Isa. 11.4, 27.1, 31.8, 49.2, 66.16; Eph. 6.17; Heb. 4.12; 2 Thess. 2.8; Rev. 1.16, 2.16, 19.15.

units.la: adius, Dei iudicis, Gen.3.24. Iudic.7.20. Esai.27.1.& 34. 5. Ierem.12. Ezec.12.21.v.8.9.10.& 30.v.2425.
units.tr: SWORD of God the judge: Gen. 3.24; Judg. 7.20; Isa. 27.1, 34.5; Jer. 12; Ezek. 12.21; vv. 8–10; 30.24–25.

units.la: ladius Angeli Dei, Num.22.v.31.1. Chron.21.v.12.16. o. Apoc.6.4. Gen.3.24.
units.tr: SWORD of the Angel of God: Num. 22.31; 1 Chron. 21.12, 16; Rev. 6.4; Gen. 3.24.

units.la: iladius magni Principis exercitus Dei, 1. Christi Josue 5. p.19.14.15. ] GLORIA pro maiestate & splédore illo, qui es illustriores reddit, Mat.6.29. pro miseridordia, Eph. pro arca fœderis per metonymiam, 1. Sam.4.v.21.22. & Templum dicebatur habitatio gloriæ Dei, Psal. 36.8.pro honore éaque reddenda est Déo,29.2.& 1.Matth.5.16.1.Cor.10.31.Vide infrà III.
units.tr: SWORD of the great Prince, the army of God; of Christ: Josh. 5.13–15. GLORY, for that majesty and splendour which makes things more illustrious: Matt. 6.29; for mercy: Eph. ...; for the ark of the covenant by metonymy: 1 Sam. 4.21–22. The temple was called the dwelling of the glory of God: Ps. 26.8. For the honour that is to be rendered to God: Ps. 29.2; 1 Cor. 10.31; Matt. 5.16. See below, III.

units.la: Gloriæ Deo redditæ exempla: Abraham, Roman.4. 20.21. Achan,Ios.7.v.19.20. Dauid, 1.Sam.17.v.45.46. 115.1.1. Paral.29.v.10.11.Daniel.9.7.Bene operantes,Matth. 5.16. Angeli,Luc.2.v.13.14. Samaritanus à lepra mundatus. 17.15. Paulus, Rom.11.36.&16.27. Galat.1.5. Eph.3.21. Petrus,1 Pet.4.11.2.Petr.3.18.Iudas,Iudæ v.25.Ioannes Apoc. 1.6.Gloriam Deo tribue: solennis formula apud Iudæos extorquendæ veritatis, Ioann.9.24.ut apparet ex Iosue 7.19.1 Sam.6.5. Gloria Dei,pro Deo gloriosò,Exod.10. Actor.7.55.1 Corinth.2.8. Ephes.1.v.12.14.pro vita æterna,Roman.3.2. Gloria Patris,pro gloriosi Patris substantia & potestate, 6.4. Gloriam Dei mutare, est Deo gloriosò aliud amplecti,1.23.
units.tr: Examples of glory rendered to God: Abraham, Rom. 4.20–21; Achan, Josh. 7.19–20; David, 1 Sam. 17.45–46; Ps. 115.1; 1 Chron. 29.10–11; Daniel 9.7; those who work good, Matt. 5.16; the angels, Luke 2.13–14; the Samaritan cleansed of leprosy, Luke 17.15; Paul, Rom. 11.36, 16.27; Gal. 1.5; Eph. 3.21; Peter, 1 Pet. 4.11; 2 Pet. 3.18; Jude, v. 25; John, Rev. 1.6. "Give glory to God": a solemn formula among the Jews for extracting the truth, John 9.24, as appears from Josh. 7.19 and 1 Sam. 6.5. The glory of God, for the glorious God: Exod. 10; Acts 7.55; 1 Cor. 2.8; Eph. 1.12, 14. For eternal life: Rom. 3.2. The glory of the Father, for the substance and power of the glorious Father: 6.4. To change the glory of God is to embrace something other than the glorious God: Rom. 1.23.

units.la: GLORIA solida quærenda, Ioann.5.44. Gloria vana quærenda, Matth.6.2. Gal.5.26.&6.3. Philip.2.3. Gloriæ vanæ exempla: Benadad, 1 Reg.20.v.2.3.10. Sennacherib 2.Reg.18.v.33.34. Arphaxad, Iudith 1.13. Doeg,Psal. 52.v.3.4.5. Chaldæi, Esa.43.14. Nabucodonosor, Dan. 4.25. Herodes Agrippa, Act.12.v.21.22.23, Gloria fugienda, Exempla: Christus, Ioann.5.41.&8. versf. Herodes, Actor.12.23. Petrus, 10.25. Paulus & Barnabas 4.v.14.15.Paulus, Gal.1.10,&5.26.Philipp.2.3. Angeli Apoc.19.10.
units.tr: Solid glory is to be sought: John 5.44. Vain glory is to be sought: Matt. 6.2; Gal. 5.26, 6.3; Phil. 2.3. Examples of vain glory: Ben-hadad, 1 Kings 20.2–3, 10; Sennacherib, 2 Kings 18.33–34; Arphaxad, Judith 1.13; Doeg, Ps. 52.3–5; the Chaldeans, Isa. 43.14; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 4.25; Herod Agrippa, Acts 12.21–23. Glory to be shunned. Examples: Christ, John 5.41, 8; Herod, Acts 12.23; Peter, Acts 10.25; Paul and Barnabas, Acts 14.14–15; Paul, Gal. 1.10, 5.26; Phil. 2.3; the angels, Rev. 19.10.

units.la: [Variæ, Acceptiones huius vocis accuratius pauló ponimus:
units.tr: [Let us set out the various senses of this word a little more precisely:

units.la: I. Gloria Dei est Maiestas immensa & incomprehensibilis gloriosi Dei, quæ omnipotenti & sapienti modo sese hominibus & Angelis patefacit,& revelatione, varia visione, conuenientique quadam ratione percipitur. Genes.19.19. Exod.16.v.7.10. & 33.v.11. & 40.34. Leuit.9.v.6.23. Num.14.10.&16.19.42. & 1.Reg.8.11.Psal.17.15.&102.v.16,17.Esai.6.3.&66.18. ch. cap.1.2.3.8.9.10.11.43.&44.Abac.3.3.2.Petr.1.17.R 1.23.1.Cor.11.7.
units.tr: I. The glory of God is the immense and incomprehensible majesty of the glorious God, which reveals itself to men and angels in an omnipotent and wise manner, and is perceived through revelation, various visions and a certain fitting mode. Gen. 19.19; Exod. 16.7, 10, 33.11, 40.34; Lev. 9.6, 23; Num. 14.10, 16.19, 42; 1 Kings 8.11; Ps. 17.15, 102.16–17; Isa. 6.3, 66.18; Ezek. 1–3, 8–11, 43–44; Hab. 3.3; 2 Pet. 1.17; Rev. 1.23; 1 Cor. 11.7.

units.la: III. Gloria Deo attribuenda, vel attributa, quando Deus agnoscitur,& celebratur,ut decet:Ios.
units.tr: III. Glory to be ascribed, or ascribed, to God, when God is acknowledged and celebrated as is fitting: Ios.

units.la: VIV. Gloria, subiectum pro adiecto, quum de Deo citur, quicquid in Dei maiestate vel testimonio prae- tiae eius considerari potest, nempe gloriosum & ki- a cogitationem omnem celebratione dignum deno- .Nehem .9.5.Psalm.24.9.& 79.9. & 14.5.v.5.11.12.Esai. 23. & 63. v.14.15.Act.7.2.1. Corinth.2.8. Ephes.1.6.17. 16.1.Tim.1.11.Tit.2.13.Hebr.1.7.& 9.5.Iac.2.1.
units.tr: IV. Glory, a noun used for an adjective: when it is said of God, it denotes whatever in God's majesty or in the evidence of his excellence can be considered, namely that which is glorious and worthy of all thought and celebration. Neh. 9.5; Ps. 24.9 & 79.9 & 14.5; Isa. 23 & 63.14-15; Acts 7.2; 1 Cor. 2.8; Eph. 1.6, 17; 1 Tim. 1.17; 1 Tim. 1.11; Tit. 2.13; Heb. 1.7 & 9.5; Jas 2.1.

units.la: V. Gloria,quam sibi Deus tribuit, Psalm.115.1.Ierem. 11.Ioan.5.44.& 7.18.& 11.4.& 12.43.Rom.3.7.1. Corin. 31.2.Cor.4.15.& 8.v.19.23. Philip.1.v.10.11.2.Thess.1.9. etr.1.v.7.11.2.Petr.1.3.
units.tr: V. Glory which God ascribes to himself: Ps. 115.1; Jer. 11; John 5.44 & 7.18 & 11.4 & 12.43; Rom. 3.7; 1 Cor. 3; 2 Cor. 4.15 & 8.19, 23; Phil. 1.10-11; 2 Thess. 1.9; 1 Pet. 1.7, 11; 2 Pet. 1.3.

units.la: VI. Gloria, Misericordia Dei omnipotentis erga suos, 58.8.& 60.v.1.2.
units.tr: VI. Glory: the mercy of almighty God toward his own: Isa. 58.8 & 60.1-2.

units.la: IX. Praestantia hominum coram Deo, Rom. 3.23. & 7.
units.tr: IX. The excellence of men before God: Rom. 3.23 & 7.

units.la: X. Gloria,quam Deus verbo suo efficaciter operanti per S.tribuit.2.Cor.v.10.11.13.
units.tr: X. Glory which God ascribes to his Word working effectively through the Holy Spirit: 2 Cor. 5.10-11, 13.

units.la: XI. gloria, subiectum pro adiecto, r. res magnifica mia laude & honore cumulata,1. Sam.2.18.1.Corinth. 3.2. Corinth .3.v.7.8.9. Ephes .1.18.2. Thessal .1.9. br.3.6.
units.tr: XI. Glory, as a subject put for an adjective: that which is magnificent, heaped with praise and honour. 1 Sam. 2.18; 1 Cor. 3.2; 2 Cor. 3.7, 8, 9; Eph. 1.18; 1 Thess. 1.9; Hebr. 3.6.

units.la: III. Gloria, Arca foederis, templum, 1. Sam.4.14.1. 2. Psal.26.8. Esai.64. 11. Ierem.14.21.& 17.12.Templi ria,Agg.2.v.3.9.
units.tr: III. Glory: the ark of the covenant, the temple. 1 Sam. 4.14; 1 Sam. 2.26.8; Isa. 64.11; Jer. 14.21 and 17.12. Glory of the temple: Hag. 2.3, 9.

units.la: III. Gloria, magnificentia legalis & mystica, Exod. .2.40.
units.tr: III. Glory: legal and mystical magnificence. Exod. 2.40.

units.la: IV. Gloria hominis, i. varia dona, eximia, Dei
units.tr: IV. Glory of man, that is, the various excellent gifts bestowed on men by the liberality of God, the best and greatest,

units.tr: XV. Glory, the tongue of the soul. Gen. 49.6; Psal. 30.13, 9, 108.2, 169.

units.la: XVI. Gloria vana, quā homines frustrā usurpant & aliter tribuunt, Ioann.5.44.&7.18.&8.v.50.54.&12.43. Rom.4.2. Galat.5.26. Philipp.2.3.&3.19. 1.Thessal.2.6.
units.tr: XVI. Vain glory, which men falsely claim for themselves and wrongly ascribe to others. John 5.44, 7.18, 8.50, 54, 12.43; Rom. 4.2; Gal. 5.26; Phil. 2.3, 3.19; 1 Thess. 2.6.

units.la: XVII. Gloria creaturarum rationis expertium, Esai.3&60.13. Ezech.7.7.]
units.tr: XVII. Glory of creatures lacking reason. Isa. 3 and 60.13; Ezek. 7.7.

units.la: GLORIARI in Domino, est Deo totam gloriam vendicare, ne in se superbiat quispiam, 2 Cor.10.17. deinde Dei gloriam, non ad sua commoda referre quicquid habet a Domino accepit.
units.tr: TO GLORY IN THE LORD is to claim the whole glory for God, so that no one takes pride in himself; and then to refer to God's glory, not to one's own advantage, whatever one has received from the Lord. 2 Cor. 10.17.

units.la: GLORIARI secundum carnem, est gloriari de rebus externis, veluti de generis nobilitate, &c.2. Corint.11.18. Gloriari in, vel ex corde, pro vera pietate, quae in corde latet, 2. Corinth.5.12. Gloriari in, vel ex facie, pro externis sapientiae & eloquentia humanae laruis, ibid.
units.tr: TO GLORY ACCORDING TO THE FLESH is to glory in external things, such as nobility of birth, etc. 2 Cor. 11.18. To glory in the heart, or from the heart, means true piety, which lies hidden in the heart. 2 Cor. 5.12. To glory in the face, or from the face, means external masks of wisdom and human eloquence. Ibid.

units.la: GLORIATIO vera quae, Psal.5.12.&32.11.&106.47. Esaia 16. Ierem.9.23. Luc.10.20. Roman.5.v.2.3.1. Cor.1.13.8.&9.15.&15.31.2. Corinth.10.17.&12.5. Iac.1.9. Gloriatio vera exemplum: Paulus, 2 Corin.7.4. Galat.6.14. Philipp.2. Thess.1.4. Gloriatio fidelium, Vide FIDELES Gloriatio vana, Vide IACTANTIA
units.tr: TRUE GLORYING: Psal. 5.12, 32.11, 106.47; Isa. 16; Jer. 9.23; Luke 10.20; Rom. 5.2, 3; 1 Cor. 1.13, 8, 9, 15, 31; 2 Cor. 10.17, 12.5; Jas. 1.9. Example of true glorying: Paul, 2 Cor. 7.4; Gal. 6.14; Phil. 2; 1 Thess. 1.4. The glorying of the faithful: see FAITHFUL. Vain glorying: see BOASTING.

units.la: GLORIFICARE Deum iubemur in corpore nostro, 1. Cor.6.20. id est, ita ab omni scortatione abhorrere, prorsus ita, inquam, nos tum animo, tum corpore ad omnem puritatem comparare, ut nostrae omnes & cogitationes & actiones ad Dei gloriam referantur, a quo corpus, tum animum idcirco accepimus, ut utroque ipsius gloriam vteremur. Huc pertinent & loci illi quibus Dei gloriam in omnibus quaerendam esse dicimur, Iosu.7.19. Psalm.12.7. Mat.6.9. Ioan.9.24.&17.4. 12.&12.23.1. Cor.6.20.&10.31. Philip.1.20. Coloss.3.17. 32.10.
units.tr: WE ARE COMMANDED TO GLORIFY GOD IN OUR BODY, 1 Cor. 6.20. That is, we must so shrink from all fornication, and so prepare ourselves, in mind and in body alike, for all purity, that all our thoughts and actions are referred to the glory of God, from whom we received both body and mind, so that we might use both to his glory. To this belong also those passages which tell us that God's glory is to be sought in all things: Josh. 7.19; Psal. 12.7; Matt. 6.9; John 9.24, 17.4, 12, 12.23; 1 Cor. 6.20, 10.31; Phil. 1.20; Col. 3.17; Psal. 32.10.

units.la: GDOLIAS, filius Ahicam, reliquiis Iudae praeficitur, 2. [illegible, ~10 letters] 22. Ierem. 40.5. gladio interimitur, 2. Reg. 25.25. Ierem. [?] 1.2.
units.tr: GEDALIAH, son of Ahikam, is set over the remnant of Judah, 2 Kings [illegible]; Jer. 40.5; he is slain with the sword, 2 Kings 25.25; Jer. [?] 1.2.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] & Magog, gentes populo Dei inimicæ, Ezech. 38. v. 2.3. ductæ à Satana, Apoc. 20.8. ruina Gog, Ezech. 39. v. 1.4. ina Magog, verss. 6. Sepulchrum Gog, v. 11. (Gag. 1. stum.)
units.tr: [illegible] and Magog: nations hostile to the people of God, Ezek. 38.2, 3; led by Satan, Rev. 20.8. The ruin of Gog, Ezek. 39.1, 4; the ruin of Magog, vv. 6. The grave of Gog, v. 11. (Gag, 1. [illegible].)

units.la: GOTHA, Caluariæ locus, vbi Christus crucifixus est. att. 27.33. Marc. 15.22. Ioan. 19.17.
units.tr: GOLGOTHA, the place of the Skull, where Christ was crucified. Matt. 27.33; Mark 15.22; John 19.17.

units.la: GOLIATH Gethæus, Gigas, 1. Sam. 17. 23. à Dauide interfici-tur, v. 49.50 51. (i. transmigrans, exul.)
units.tr: GOLIATH the Gittite, a giant, is slain by David, 1 Sam. 17.23; vv. 49, 50, 51. (That is, one who migrates, an exile.)

units.la: GOLIATH Gethæus alter, ab Ethanam occiditur, 2. Samu. 21. 19. frater illius erat, qui à Dauide erat interfectus, 1. Paral. 20. 5. Cuius hastile erat vt iugum textorum.
units.tr: Another GOLIATH the Gittite is killed by Elhanan, 2 Sam. 21.19. He was the brother of the one whom David had slain, 1 Chron. 20.5. His spear-shaft was like a weaver's beam.

units.la: GOMER filius Iaphet, Genes. 10. v. 2.3. 1. Par. 1 v. 5.6. Gomer, populus Septentrionalis, Ezech. 38. 6. Gomer, filia Diblaim, Ose. 1.3.
units.tr: GOMER, son of Japheth, Gen. 10.2, 3; 1 Chron. 1.5, 6. Gomer: a northern people, Ezek. 38.6. Gomer, daughter of Diblaim, Hos. 1.3.

units.la: GOMER, quæ mensura, Vide OMER.
units.tr: GOMER, a measure: see OMER.

units.la: GOMORRHA à Regibus gentium expilatur, Genes. 14.11. incendio diuino perit, 19. v. 24. 2. Petr. 2.6. Iudæ. v. 7. Matth. 11.15.
units.tr: GOMORRAH is plundered by the kings of the nations, Gen. 14.11; it perishes by divine fire, Gen. 19.24; 2 Pet. 2.6; Jude 7; Matt. 11.15.

units.la: GOSEN, portio Ægypti, quam Iacob inhabitauit cum liberis suis G. 45. 10. Gen. 46.34. portio terræ Chanaan, Ios. 10.41. & 11. 16. & 15.51. Gollem, Arabs, Iudæorum hostis. 2. Esdr. 2.19. & 6. v. 1.2.6. Gozan, nomen proprium fluminis, vrbis 1. Par. 5.26. Esai. 37.12.
units.tr: GOSHEN, a part of Egypt which Jacob inhabited with his children, Gen. 45.10; Gen. 46.34; a part of the land of Canaan, Josh. 10.41, 11.16, 15.51. Geshem, an Arab, enemy of the Jews, Neh. 2.19; 6.1, 2, 6. Gozan, the proper name of a river and a city, 1 Chron. 5.26; Isa. 37.12.

units.la: GRADVS affinitatis in lege prohibiti, Leuit. 18.6. &c.
units.tr: DEGREES OF AFFINITY prohibited in the law, Lev. 18.6, etc.

units.la: GRAECVS pro dignitate, Hebraismus.
units.tr: GREEK, for dignity: a Hebraism.

units.la: GRAECI pro iis Iudæis, qui è Grecia Ierosolymam mi-grantes religionem Christi amplexi erant, Act. 6.1. Græ-ci pro omnibus nationibus, exceptis Iudæis, 14.1. & 17.4. Rom. 1.16. & 2. v. 9.10. 1. Corinth. 1.22. Gal. 3.28. Sic capi-tur & Marc. 7.26. alioqui mulier, quæ ex Syrophœ-nice erat (vt ibidem additur) quomodo Græca dici pos-sit? vbi generis vocabulum (sicut & familiæ nomen, Le-uit. 20.5. Ierem. 8.3. Act. 3.25. Mich. 3.3.) synecdochicè pro populo terræ Syrophenicæ accipitur. Græci pro politis, sapientia excultis hominibus, Roman. 1.14. Græci sa-pientiam quærunt, 1. Corint. 1.22. Vocatio eorum: R. 1.14. Gal. 3.28.
units.tr: GREEKS, for those Jews who, migrating from Greece to Jerusalem, had embraced the religion of Christ, Acts 6.1. Greeks, for all nations except the Jews, Acts 14.1, 17.4; Rom. 1.16, 2.9, 10; 1 Cor. 1.22; Gal. 3.28. So it is also taken in Mark 7.26, where the woman is described as a Syrophoenician; otherwise, how could she be called a Greek (as the passage adds)? There the general term (as also a family name, Lev. 20.5; Jer. 8.3; Acts 3.25; Mic. 3.3) is taken by synecdoche for the people of the land of Syrophoenicia. Greeks, for civilised people, men cultivated in wisdom, Rom. 1.14. The Greeks seek wisdom, 1 Cor. 1.22. Their calling: Rom. 1.14; Gal. 3.28.

units.la: GRANDO, est dissolutio nubis in guttas aquæ, quæ singulæ cum in terram decidunt, constringuntur à Deo vi frigoris. & citissimè, spicissimeque condensantur.
units.tr: HAIL is the dissolving of a cloud into drops of water, which, as each one falls to the ground, is hardened by God through the force of cold and is very quickly and tightly condensed.

units.la: Causa efficiens, Deus: Iob.38.22. Psa.148.8. (Ecclesiasti 43.16.) Duplex, Naturalis, qualis est superior descripti Miraculosa, qualis fuit in Ægypto: Exod.9.23. cuiusmodi non fuerat in tota terra.
units.tr: Efficient cause: God, Job 38.22; Psal. 148.8; (Ecclesiasticus 43.16). It is twofold: natural, such as the one described above; miraculous, such as that which occurred in Egypt, Exod. 9.23, of a kind that had not been in all the land.

units.la: Effecta: Iudiciorum Dei manifestatio, Iob.38.22. In Aegyptios, intacto Dei populo: Exod.9.19. 23.27. (Vide Sap. 16.16.) In quinque Reges: Iosu. 10.11. (Vide Ecclesiastic. 46.6.) In Gog. Eze.38.22.
units.tr: Effects: a manifestation of God's judgements, Job 38.22. Against the Egyptians, while God's people remained untouched, Exod. 9.19, 23, 27 (see Wisd. 16.16). Against five kings, Josh. 10.11 (see Ecclus. 46.6). Against Gog, Ezek. 38.22.

units.la: Visus: Laus Dei: Psal.148.7. c. Conversio hominum: Aug. 2.18. Amos.4.9. precibus Mosis grando cessavit: Exod. 9.33. ut precibus eiusdem deciderat v.2. V. Apoc.16.21.
units.tr: Uses: the praise of God, Psal. 148.7. The conversion of men, Augustine, Amos 4.9. At the prayers of Moses the hail ceased, Exod. 9.33, as it had fallen at his prayers, v. 2. See Rev. 16.21.

units.la: GRATIA in genere, pro beneficio, 2. Cor. 1.15. Ruth 2.20. Sam.2.6. & 15.20. Prov.4.9. Eccles.7.34. & 29.20, pro beneficio divino & dono Dei μετὰ χαρᾶς, 2. Corinth. 1.12. 8.1. pro consolatione, Ephes. 4.29. pro spirituali, id est, Evangelico Dei cultu, Hebr. 13.9. pro conditione illa, in qua gratuitò sumus asciti: vel etiam pro gratuita Dei benevolentia, Rom. 5.2. cui haec laus tribuenda est, ut in solidum omnia in nobis inchoet & perficiat. pro gratuitis Spiritus Sancti Donis pleno cornu per Christum è coelo in suos effusis, Ioan. 1.16. pro gratuitis Dei donis, 1. Petr. 4.10. & 5.10. 2. Petr. 3.18. pro Eleemosyna. 2. Corinth. 8.4. pro Fauore, Genes. 6.8. & 18.3. & 19.19. & 39.21. Exodi 12. Tob. 1.3. Esth. 2.17. Prov. 13.15. Eccles. 4.25. Dan. 1.9. Act. 47. & 24.27.28. & 25.9. pro gratuito & aeterno Dei fauore ac benevolentia, qua nos in Christo reconciliandos et adoptandos diligit, quae est fons quasi ex quo omnia Dei beneficia in nos promanant, Rom. 1.7. & 4.16. & 11.6. 1. Corinth. 1.3.2. Coloss. 1.2. Galat. 1.3. & 2.21. Ephes. 1.6. & 2.5. & 6.24. Philipp. 1.2. Coloss. 1.2. & 4.18. 1. Thess. 1.1.2. Thess. 1.2. 1. Tim. 1.2. 6.21. 2. Timoth. 1.2. & 4.22. Tit. 1.4. & 2.11. & 3.7. Philem. 3. Hebr. 13.25. 1. Petr. 1.2.2. Petri 1.2.2. Ioan. vers. 3. Apoc. 1.4. pro fide & eius salutiferis effectibus, Hebr. 12.15. 1. Petr. 5.12. pro gratuita per fidem in Christo Iustificatione, Act. 13.43. pro gratuita iustitiae Christi imputatione, Rom. 5.v. 17.20. pro Dei in homines Munificentia, 2. Corinth. 9.8. pro grato Obsequio, 1. Petri 2.19. pro efficaci Spiritus Sancti Praesentia, Act. 14.26. Gratiae nomen tribuitur à Paulo etiam captiuitati Philipp. 1.7. vbi gratiam, id est, peculiare & gratuitum beneficium appellat, quòd captiuus teneretur pro Christi... i nomine : qua in re certatim etiam Philippenses sele ipsi socios addiderant, vt explicatur ibidem, versic.29. Chro Vi diuina, quæ in Christi verbis totóque habitu inerat, Ioann.4.19.&c. vt qui illum audiebant (nisi qui omnis sensus erant expertes) non poterant non illum amare, respicere, completi: vt apparuit Ioan.7.46. & prædictum erat, Psalm.45.3.
units.tr: GRACE in general, for a benefit, 2 Cor. 1.15; Ruth 2.20; 1 Sam. 2.26 and 15.20; Prov. 4.9; Eccles. 7.34 and 29.20; for a divine benefit and gift of God, with joy [μετὰ χαρᾶς], 2 Cor. 1.12, 8.1; for consolation, Eph. 4.29; for spiritual worship, that is, the evangelical worship of God, Hebr. 13.9; for that condition in which we have been freely taken up, or also for the free goodwill of God, Rom. 5.2, to which this praise must be ascribed, that he begins and perfects all things in us entirely; for the free gifts of the Holy Spirit, poured out from heaven upon his own through Christ in full measure, John 1.16; for the free gifts of God, 1 Pet. 4.10, 5.10; 2 Pet. 3.18; for alms, 2 Cor. 8.4; for favour, Gen. 6.8, 18.3, 19.19, 39.21; Exod. 12; Tob. 1.3; Esth. 2.17; Prov. 13.15; Eccles. 4.25; Dan. 1.9; Acts 4.7, 24.27, 28, 25.9; for the free and eternal favour and goodwill of God, by which he loves us to be reconciled and adopted in Christ, which is, as it were, the fountain from which all God's benefits flow into us, Rom. 1.7, 4.16, 11.6; 1 Cor. 1.3, 2; Col. 1.2; Gal. 1.3, 2.21; Eph. 1.6, 2.5, 6.24; Phil. 1.2; Col. 1.2, 4.18; 1 Thess. 1.1; 2 Thess. 1.2; 1 Tim. 1.2, 6.21; 2 Tim. 1.2, 4.22; Titus 1.4, 2.11, 3.7; Philem. 3; Hebr. 13.25; 1 Pet. 1.2; 2 Pet. 1.2; 1 John v. 3; Rev. 1.4; for faith and its saving effects, Hebr. 12.15; 1 Pet. 5.12; for justification freely through faith in Christ, Acts 13.43; for the free imputation of Christ's righteousness, Rom. 5.17, 20; for God's bounty towards men, 2 Cor. 9.8; for grateful obedience, 1 Pet. 2.19; for the effectual presence of the Holy Spirit, Acts 14.26. The name of grace is also given by Paul to imprisonment, Phil. 1.7, where he calls it grace, that is, a peculiar and free benefit, because he was held captive for the name of Christ; in which matter the Philippians too had vied to join themselves as partners, as is explained in the same place, v. 29. The divine power which dwelt in Christ's words and whole bearing, John 4.19 etc., so that those who heard him (except those who were devoid of all feeling) could not help but love him and regard him; as appeared in John 7.46, and as was foretold in Psal. 45.3.

units.la: GRATIA per Christum præstita, Ioã.1.17. Gratia hominum magno animo contemnenda, Gal.1.10. Gratia Dei, Vide DEI gratia.
units.tr: GRACE bestowed through Christ, John 1.17. The grace of men is to be despised with a great spirit, Gal. 1.10. The grace of God: see DEI gratia.

units.la: GRATIARUM actio per Christum Agendæ. Exemplum: Paulus, Rom.8.
units.tr: Thanksgiving to be offered through Christ. Example: Paul, Rom. 8.

units.la: Gratiarum actio cùm piis viritim, tum Ecclesiæ toti vniuersum necessaria, Exodi 13.9. Psalm.50.15. & 106.v.7.48. Esa.42.10. & 51.3. Ose.14.2. Rom.1.21. & 14.6. Ephes.4. Phil.4.6. Coloss.1.12. & 2.7. & 3.17. & 4.2.1. Thess.3.9. & 18.2. Thessal.1.3. & 2.13.1. Tim.2.1. & 4.v.3.4. Hebr.13.15.
units.tr: The giving of thanks is necessary both for the godly individually and for the whole Church: Exodus 13:9; Psalm 50:15; Psalm 106:7, 48; Isaiah 42:10; Isaiah 51:3; Hosea 14:2; Romans 1:21; Romans 14:6; Ephesians 4; Philippians 4:6; Colossians 1:12; Colossians 2:7; Colossians 3:17; Colossians 4:2; 1 Thessalonians 3:9; 2 Thessalonians 1:3; 2 Thessalonians 2:13; 1 Timothy 2:1; 1 Timothy 4:3, 4; Hebrews 13:15.

units.tr: Examples of thanksgiving for God's benefits: Melchizedek, Gen. 14.20; Abraham's servant, 24.26-27; Jacob, 32.9-10; the Hebrews, Exod. 4.31; Moses and the Hebrews, 15.1 etc.; Miriam, v. 21; the Israelites, Num. 21.17-18 and 31.50; Joshua, Josh. 8.30; Deborah and Barak, Judg. 5.1-2; Gideon, 7.15; Hannah, 1 Sam. 1; David, 2 Sam. 7.18; 1 Chron. 29.10-11; Ps. 7.18; 51; 103.1; 104.1; Ahimaaz, 2 Sam. 18.28; Solomon, 1 Kings 3.15 and 8.56; Hiram, 5.7; Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 20.18; Ezra, Ezra 7.26; Tobias, Tob. 2.14; Isaiah, Isa. 25.1; Hezekiah, 38; Daniel, Dan. 2.19-20; the sailors and companions of Jonah, Jon. 1.6; Jonah, 2.10; the crowds, Matt. 9.8; Christ, 11.25; John 11.41; Mary, Luke 1.46; Zechariah, v. 68; the shepherds, 2.20; the paralytic, 5.25; the people, 7.16; the woman, 13.13; the Samaritan leper, 17.15-16; the blind man and the people, 18.43; the centurion, 23.47; the Caesar-born, John 9.38; the believers, Acts 2.47; the lame man, 3; the Christians, 11.18; Paul, Acts 28.15; Rom. 1.8; 6.17; 7.25; 16.25; 1 Cor. 1.4, 14; 14.18; 15.57; 2 Cor. 3; 2.14; 8.16; 9.15; Gal. 1.3; Eph. 1.3, 16; Phil. 1.3; Col. 1.3; 1 Thess. 1.2; 2.13; 1 Tim. 1.12; 2 Tim. 1.3; 4.18; Philem. 4; Heb. 11.21; Peter, 1 Pet. 5; the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders, Rev. 4.8-10; the angels, living creatures and elders, 5.9; the great multitude, vv. 10-11; the twenty-four elders, 11.17; the saints, 19.7; every creature, ch. 5, v. 13.

units.la: Gratiarum actio in Bonorum amissione. Exemplum: Iob, 1.21. Gratiarum actio pro beneficentia in pauperes.
units.tr: Thanksgiving in the loss of goods. Example: Job, 1.21. Thanksgiving for beneficence toward the poor.

Paul, Acts 27.35. Giving of thanks before and after eating, Deut. 8.10; 1 Sam. 13; Isa. 62.9; Matt. 14.19; 15.36; 26.26; Mark 6.41; 8.6; 14.22; Luke 9.16; John 6.11, 23; Acts 27.35; Rom. 14; 1 Cor. 10.30-31; 1 Tim. 4.3. After food it is commended, Deut. 8.10; Isa. 62.9; Joel 2.26. Thanksgiving for the consecration of the Lord's Supper, Matt. 26.26; Mark 14.22; Luke 22.19; 1 Cor. 11.24. Thanksgiving after the celebration of the Lord's Supper, Matt. 26.30. For the enlargement of Christ's kingdom, Rev. 11.17. For the regeneration of the Lord, Col. 1.12; 1 Pet. 1.3. For deliverance from dangers, Ps. 9.12-13; 22.27; 28.6; 30.2; 31.20, 22; 35.18; 40.2, 4; 106.48; 107.1, 15, 21, 31; 124.6; 144; Jer. 20.13. Thanksgiving for deliverance from slavery. Examples: Moses and the people, Exod. 15.1 etc.; Jethro, 18; David, Ps. 136.1-3. For a prayer heard. Examples: David, Ps. 6.9; 20.6-7; 66.20; 118.21. The wife of Tobias, Tob. 11.18-20. Daniel, Dan. 2.18, 20. His companion Azariah, vv. 16, 18-19; and 3.26. Nebuchadnezzar, v. 28. Sirach, Ecclus. 15.1-3 etc. For a good prince. Examples: Hiram, 1 Kings 5.7; the Queen of Sheba, 10.9. Examples: Solomon, 2 Chron. 6.4, 15; Zechariah, Luke 1.68-70; the virgin Mary, vv. 46, 55. For the Saviour made manifest.
