Examples: Solomon, 1 Kings 8.15-16; 2 Chron. 6.15. For its restoration, the people returning from captivity, 1 Esd. 3.11. For victory, both spiritual and bodily. Examples: the leaders of the army, Num. 31.49; Joshua, Josh. 8.25, 30; Deborah and Barak, Judg. 5.1; David, 2 Sam. 22.1-2; Ps. 18.50; 144.1; Jehoshaphat and the people, 2 Chron. 20.27-28; the people of Jerusalem, 30.13-15 etc.; Paul, Rom. 7.25; 1 Cor. 15.57.

units.la: GRATIARVM varietas fideles ad mutuam concordiam ellit, vt per illas mutuò collatas coalescant ea symmetria in vnum Christi corpus, quemadmodum membra corporis in vnum hominem coalescunt, 1. Cor. 12. v. 4. 7. 11. eaque quantumuis eximiæ sint, vitiantur, si destituuntur charitate, 1. Cor. 13. 1. gratiæ in nobis non sunt negligendæ, 1. Tim. 4. 14.
units.tr: The variety of graces leads the faithful to mutual harmony, so that, when they are joined together by one another, they cohere in that symmetry into one body of Christ, just as the members of the body cohere into one man, 1 Cor. 12.4, 7, 11. And however excellent these gifts are, they are spoiled if they are lacking charity, 1 Cor. 13.1. The graces in us are not to be neglected, 1 Tim. 4.14.

units.la: GRATIAE effecta duo commemorantur, 1. Timoth. 1. 13. 14. fides, à qua sit absorpta ignorantia: & charitas quæ idomitæ illi credulitati successit, idque ex gratia in Christo IESV. Gratiæ redundantia, pro gratia redundante, Hebraismus, Roman. 5. 17. Gratia excidere, (cùm aliâs electio sit firma & immutabilis) dicuntur, Galat. 5. 4. qui illius adipiscendæ iter erant ingressi, quod etiam reprobis contingit, cùm aliqui sint etiam ad veram fidem gradus. Vide ELECTIO. gratia excludit omnia opera in vniuersum, Tit. 3. 5. eò quòd gratia & opera sint contraria, Roman. 11. 6. gratiæ Dei συνεργοί sumus, 2. Petri. 1. 5. quia non sumus trunci aut stipites, sed oportet nos vicissim omnem diligentiam adferre: nos, inquam, qui liberum (hoc est à seruitute peccati per gratiam manumissum) arbitrium habemus. Nam alioquin ad malum præcipites feruntur, ad bonum verò non modò tardi & imbecilli, sed omni etiam bonæ voluntatis sensu prorsus destituti sumus.
units.tr: Two effects of grace are recorded: faith, by which ignorance is swallowed up, 1 Tim. 1.13-14; and charity, which followed that untamed credulity, and this from the grace in Christ Jesus. Abundance of grace, for abounding grace, is a Hebraism, Rom. 5.17. Those are said to fall from grace (although otherwise election is firm and unchangeable), Gal. 5.4, who had entered upon the way of obtaining it; this also happens to the reprobate, since some have degrees even toward true faith. See ELECTION. Grace excludes all works in general, Titus 3.5, because grace and works are contrary, Rom. 11.6. We are fellow workers [συνεργοί] with the grace of God, 2 Pet. 1.5, because we are not trunks or stumps, but we ought in turn to bring every diligence; we, I say, who have free will (that is, freed from slavery to sin through grace). For otherwise we are carried headlong to evil, and toward good we are not only slow and feeble, but altogether destitute of any sense of good will.

units.la: Quid enim habes (inquit Apostolus, de gratia, & non de natura loquens, 1. Corinth. 4. 7.) quod non acceperis? Monet ergo eo loco Petrus, ne Dei gratiæ desimus, sed omnem ea promouenda diligentiam adhibeamus. Sic 1. Ioan. 3. 18. ex Deo genitus obseruare seipsum dicitur: Agit enim quia Filius est, agit, inquam, non naturali arbitrio quod diuuet gratia: sed arbitrio quod ex peccati corruptione, cui totum (liberum arbitrium) seruiebat, manumissum, coepit ex malo bonum facere, ac quotidie magis ac magis proficit. Simpliciter exponunt nonnulli Ioannis locum: Conseruat seipsum, id est, cauet sibimetipsi. Sub gratia esse, Rom. 6. 14. dicuntur ij, qui sunt spiritu Christi donati, cuius freti virtute, reliquias etiam peccati iam inermis protinus profligent: idque ita esse explicandum, liquet ex Gal. 5. v. 23. 24.
units.tr: For what do you have (says the Apostle, speaking of grace and not of nature, 1 Cor. 4.7) that you have not received? Therefore Peter there warns us not to fail the grace of God, but to apply every diligence to advance it. So in 1 John 3.18, he who is born of God is said to keep himself: he acts because he is a Son, acts, I say, not by a natural will that grace helps, but by a will which, freed from the corruption of sin, to which the whole (free will) was enslaved, has begun to make good out of evil, and daily advances more and more. Some expound John's passage simply: he preserves himself, that is, he guards himself. Those who are endowed with the Spirit of Christ are said to be under grace, Rom. 6.14, and, relying on his power, they immediately overthrow the remnants of sin, now disarmed. That this is to be explained so is clear from Gal. 5.23-24.

Toward God: Isa. 1.2, 3. Toward parents: Eccl. 3.13, etc.; 1 Tim. 5.4. Toward the magistrate: Neh. 5.15. Toward ministers: 1 Cor. 9.9, etc.

units.la: GVLA & ingluuies,Est in cibo, somnove immoderata,& naturae atque valetudinis fines excedens, delectatio , sed in cibo maxime.Qua in re tripliciter peccari docent:in cibi nimirum substantia ipsa,si nimium exquisitus est cibus& delicatus:Quantitate,si minus est,& non ex legibus sumptuariis:Qualitate,si nimium delitiosè conditus sit cibus, qui tunc non cibus sed cupedię dicuntur.
units.tr: GLUTTONY and gorging: it lies in food or sleep taken immoderately, a pleasure that exceeds the limits of nature and health, but chiefly in food. In this matter they teach that sin is committed in three ways: (1) in the substance of the food itself, if the food is too exquisite and delicate; (2) in quantity, if it is excessive and not in accordance with the sumptuary laws; (3) in quality, if the food is seasoned too daintily, and such food is then called delicacies rather than food.

units.tr: HABEL, the second son of Adam, Gen. 4.2. He was a shepherd of sheep, ibid. He was righteous, Matt. 23.35; Heb. 11.4. His faith, v.4. His sacrifice was accepted by God, Gen. 4.4. By faith he offered God a sacrifice of greater worth than Cain's, Heb. 11.4. He was killed by his brother, Gen. 4.8. His blood cries out, v.10; Heb. 12.24. [Habel: vanity.]

units.tr: HABITACULUM: the dwelling place of God is the land of Canaan, Exod. 15 [v.13, 17]. Heaven is the dwelling of God, Deut. 26.15; 1 Kings 8 v.30, 43; 2 Chron. 6.21, etc.; Ps. 33.14; Isa. 63.15; Jer. 25.30; Zech. 2.13. The Church is the dwelling of God, Eph. 2.20, etc. The temple is the dwelling of God, 1 Kings 8.13; 2 Chron. 36.14. A dwelling of man is a tabernacle, a house, etc., Exod. 12.20 and 35.3; Ps. 55.16. A hut, Jer. 33.12; Ezek. 25.5. Caves and lairs of wild beasts, Jer. 10.22 and 49.33; Nahum 2.11. Christians who have become the dwelling of God through the Holy Spirit, Eph. 2.22. The faithful dwell in confidence, Deut. 33.28.

units.la: [HABITARE, de Deo dictum, quatenus suam gratiosam & gloriosam praesentiam in terris varie testatur, Exod.24 16. Num.35.34. Deut.2.7.2. Sam.7.v.5.6.1. Reg.6.13. &8.v.11 17. Psalm.9.12. & 132.14. & 135.21. Habitat Christus in suis Ephes.3.17. & Spiritus S. in electis Dei, Rom.8.v.9.11.1 Cor.3.16.2. Tim.1.14. Iac.4.5.
units.tr: [HABITARE, said of God, insofar as he bears witness in various ways to his gracious and glorious presence on earth, Exod. 24.16; Num. 35.34; Deut. 2.7; 2 Sam. 7.5, 6; 1 Kings 6.13 and 8.11, 17; Ps. 9.12 and 132.14 and 135.21. Christ dwells in his people, Eph. 3.17, and the Holy Spirit dwells in the elect of God, Rom. 8.9, 11; 1 Cor. 3.16; 2 Tim. 1.14; James 4.5.]

units.la: Habitare, de Deo dictum, quatenus sedem gloriosam in coelis sibi deligere voluit, Psa.2.4. & 113.5. & 123.1. Esa.33.5 & 57.15. Apoc.7.15. & 21.3. Habitare iustitia in coelis dicitur, 2. Petr.3.13. Habitare negatur Deus in templis manufactis, Act.7.48. & 17.24. 1.Reg.8.27.
units.tr: Habitare, said of God, insofar as he chose to set his glorious seat in the heavens, Ps. 2.4; 113.5; 123.1; Isa. 33.5 and 57.15; Rev. 7.15 and 21.3. Righteousness is said to dwell in the heavens, 2 Pet. 3.13. God is denied to dwell in temples made by hands, Acts 7.48 and 17.24; 1 Kings 8.27.

units.la: Habitare, i. Commorari, de Christo in carne manifesta to, & inter Iudaeos visibili praesentia versante, dictum, Io 1.14. Habitare, ad Ecclesiae militantis membra accommodatum, Psal.15.1. & 84.5. & 91.1. & 133.1. & 140.14. Esai.23.18 & 33.16. & 49.20. & 62.5. Zach.13.1. Habitare, de Ecclesia triumphante dictum, Apoc.12.12. & 13.6.
units.tr: Habitare, i.e. to sojourn, said of Christ, who was manifest in the flesh and lived among the Jews in visible presence, John 1.14. Habitare, applied to the members of the militant Church, Ps. 15.1; 84.5; 91.1; 133.1; 140.14; Isa. 23.18; 33.16; 49.20; 62.5; Zech. 13.1. Habitare, said of the triumphant Church, Rev. 12.12 and 13.6.

units.la: Habitare, de peccato in regeneratis reliquo dictum, om.7.v.17.18.20.& de malis Angelis,Matt.12. 45, Apoc. 13.
units.tr: Habitare, said of the sin that remains in the regenerate, Rom. 7.17, 18, 20; and of evil angels, Matt. 12.45; Rev. 13.

units.la: Habito, dictum de volucribus quae in ramis arbo- rum vel considerent, vel nidificant, Psalm.104.12.Matth. 13.32.Marc.4.32. De variis animalibus dictum,Esai.11.6. 13.21.&34.11.& 35.7.Ierem.50.39.Dan.4.v.21.25.]
units.tr: Habito, said of birds that either perch or nest in the branches of trees, Ps. 104.12; Matt. 13.32; Mark 4.32. Said of various animals, Isa. 11.6; 13.21; 34.11; 35.7; Jer. 50.39; Dan. 4.21, 25.]

units.la: RIEL, maritus Michol filiae Saulis, cuius quinque filios abaonitae cruci affixerunt, & cum 2. Sam.21.verf.1. 9.
units.tr: RIEL, husband of Michal, daughter of Saul, whose five sons the Gibeonites fixed to a cross, and ... 2 Sam. 21 v.1, 9.

units.la: HEREDITAS Dei, populus Israel, Exod.15.16.Deut.4.20. 9.26.&32.9 1.Reg.8 51.Vide Israel. Hereditas Levi- rum Deus.Num.18.20.Deut.4.20.& 10.9.& 18.7.Iof.1. er. 14. 33. Ezech. 44.28.Haereditatem dividere non vult Christus inter fratres,Luc.12.v.13 14.de Haereditate mor- n absque masculo,Num.27.1.2.3.c.
units.tr: HERITAGE of God: the people of Israel, Exod. 15.16; Deut. 4.20; 9.26; 32.9; 1 Kings 8.51. See Israel. God is the heritage of the Levites, Num. 18.20; Deut. 4.20; 10.9; 18.7; Josh. 13.33; Ezek. 44.28. Christ does not wish to divide an inheritance between brothers, Luke 12.13–14. The inheritance of a man who has no male heir, Num. 27.1–3, etc.

units.la: HERES vniuersorum Christus,Luc.20.14.Heb.1.2. [He- es Dei Patris. Matth.21.38. Marc. 12. 7.Luc,20. 14.Heb. 2.]
units.tr: HEIR of all things: Christ, Luke 20.14; Heb. 1.2. [Heir of God the Father: Matt. 21.38; Mark 12.7; Luke 20.14; Heb. 2.]

units.la: HAEREDIS, & haereditatis nomen Graecis & Latinis pro- prie accipitur,cum alicuius haeredem esse dicunt: pro in icuius bona post mortem succedere. Item cum ipsam possessionem hereditariam ad haeredem legitimum de- pluendam declarant.Sed ex Hebraeorum idiotismo, haere- ditas dicitur, quicquid alicui gratis cedit in possessi- em;ac nominatim quidem filij dicuntur haereditas, quae tri a Deo datur Psal.127.3. Unde patet, haeredem esse undi, apud Paulum, Rom.4.13.declarare idem quod tum mundum habere pro filius, & hac ratione qui universo mundo potiri,Sic dicitur Christus totius mun- haeres constitutus, Hebr. 1,2, in quo videlicet ipsemet ater Abraham cum toto mundo adoptatus benedicitur, id,Sic dicimur Dei haeredes correlatiue,Rom.8.17.quia ei sumus haereditas cum Christo:cum alioqui (ut dictum (t)Graecis & Latinis alicuius haeredem esse, idem decla- t,quod in alicuius bona post mortem succedere.Ex qua opria significatione consequitur, heredis vocabulum, om.8.17.accipi pro bonorum patris participe, ut sit sen- s:Nos esse haeredes,id est, bonorum patris participes, que gratis,quia filij adoptiui. Alioquin enim viuo patre ius heres dici non potest. At nunquam moritur pater, cohaeredes dicimur cum Christo. Ex quo efficitur, hæredem ex Hebræorum idiotismo dici, qui bonis sibi concessis fruitur.
units.tr: The Greek and Latin words for heir and inheritance are properly understood when people say that someone is the heir of another, meaning that he succeeds to another's goods after death. Likewise, they are used when they declare that the hereditary possession itself passes to the lawful heir. But by the idiom of the Hebrews, an inheritance is called whatever is given freely to someone as a possession; and especially children are called an inheritance, which are given by God, Ps. 127.3. From this it is clear that to be heir of the world, as in Paul, Rom. 4.13, means the same as to have the world as one's own and to take possession of the whole world. In this way Christ is appointed heir of the whole world, Heb. 1.2, in whom indeed Abraham himself, adopted with the whole world, is blessed. So we are called heirs of God by correlation, Rom. 8.17, because we are an inheritance to him together with Christ. Otherwise, as has been said, among the Greeks and Latins to be the heir of someone means the same as to succeed to someone's goods after death. From this proper meaning it follows that the word heir is taken to mean a partaker of the father's goods, so that the sense is: we are heirs, that is, partakers of the father's goods, which are given freely, because we are adopted children. For otherwise, while the father lives, one cannot be called an heir, since the father never dies. We are called co-heirs with Christ. From this it follows that by the Hebrew idiom one is called an heir who enjoys the goods granted to him.

units.la: HAEREDITAS hominis, Genes.31.14. Israelis Leuit.20.2 Deut.3.18. Psalm.135.12. hæreditas Dei, seu quam Deus dedit populo suo, nempe terrâ Chanaan, Ex.15.17 1.Sam.26.19. Psal.79.1. Esa.63.17. Ier.2.7. & 12.14. & 16.18. & 50. Ioel.2.17.
units.tr: INHERITANCE of man, Gen. 31.14; of Israel, Lev. 20.2; Deut. 3.18; Ps. 135.12. Inheritance of God, or that which God gave to his people, namely the land of Canaan, Exod. 15.17; 1 Sam. 26.19; Ps. 79.1; Isa. 63.17; Jer. 2.7; 12.14; 16.18; 50; Joel 2.17.

Inheritance of God: the Church, Deut. 9.26, 29 and 32.9; 1 Kings 8.51, 53; 2 Kings 21.14; Ps. 28.9 and 33.12 and 74.2 and 78.71 and 94.5, 14 and 106.5, 40; Isa. 19.25 and 47.6; Jer. 10.16; 12.7, 8, 9.

units.la: Hæreditas Ecclesiæ, & singulorum piorum Dei, Num. 18.20. Deut.18.2. Iof.18.7. Psal.16.v.5.6. & 37 18. Iere. 51. Ezech.44 28. Hæreditas Christi, Ioel.3.2. Mich.7.v.14. Psal.2.8. Esa.49.8. hæreditas piorum, Psal.119.111.
units.tr: Inheritance of the Church and of each of the pious: God, Num. 18.20; Deut. 18.2; Josh. 18.7; Ps. 16.5, 6 and 37.18; Jer. 51; Ezek. 44.28. Inheritance of Christ, Joel 3.2; Mic. 7.14; Ps. 2.8; Isa. 49.8. Inheritance of the pious, Ps. 119.111.

units.la: Hæreditas, æterna vita, Gal.3.18. Eph.1.v.14.18. & 5.5. Col.3.24. Heb.1.14. & 9.15.1.Petr.1 4. & 3.9.
units.tr: Inheritance: eternal life, Gal. 3.18; Eph. 1.14, 18 and 5.5; Col. 3.24; Heb. 1.14 and 9.15; 1 Pet. 1.4 and 3.9.

units.la: Hæreditas, varia retributio, tum impiis, tum piis, à Deo collata, Iob.20.29. & 27.13. & 31.2. Psal.61.6. & 127.3. Esa.17. Res hereditaria, Deut.33.4. Possessio, 2.Sam.20.1.1.Reg.12.16.]
units.tr: Inheritance: various retribution conferred by God, both upon the impious and upon the pious, Job 20.29 and 27.13 and 31.2; Ps. 61.6 and 127.3; Isa. 17. A hereditary thing, Deut. 33.4. Possession, 2 Sam. 20.1; 1 Kings 12.16.]

units.la: HAERESIS, pro secta. Act.5.17. & 15.5. & 24.14. hæreses opertet esse, & quare, 1.Cor.11.19. Vide Iudic.3.1.
units.tr: HERESY, for a sect: Acts 5.17; 15.5; 24.14. There must be heresies, and why, 1 Cor. 11.19. See Judges 3.1.

units.la: Hæresean duplex est causa: Efficiens & Finis. Efficiens duplex. Prima, & remotior, est Dei iustissima voluntas, qui sic verbi sui contemtum vlcisciitur, & suos probat, Cor.11.19.2.Thess.2.11. Secunda, & propinquior, hominum ipsorum naturalis tum rebellio, tum cæcitas & ambitio, &c.1 Tim.2.8.2.Tim.3.2.Tit.2.16. Eph.4.14.1.Thess.v.3.4.5. Finis duplex: Piorum probatio, 1.Cor.11.19. piorum iusta punitio, qui veritati Dei placidè obedire adquiescere noluerunt, 2.Thess.2.11. (Vide 1 adCorinth. 11.19.) Forma est ipse error: Materia est articulus ille quo peccatur.
units.tr: Heresy has a twofold cause: efficient and final. The efficient cause is twofold. First, and more remote, is God's most just will, who thus avenges contempt of his word and tests his own, 1 Cor. 11.19; 2 Thess. 2.11. Second, and nearer, is the natural rebellion, blindness and ambition of men themselves, etc., 1 Tim. 2.8; 2 Tim. 3.2; Titus 2.16; Eph. 4.14; 1 Thess. 5.3–5. The final cause is twofold: the proof of the godly, 1 Cor. 11.19; and the just punishment of those who were unwilling to yield calmly to the truth of God and assent to it, 2 Thess. 2.11. (See on 1 Cor. 11.19.) The form is the error itself; the matter is the article on which one sins.

units.la: HAERETICVS, Est is, qui fidei Christianæ primitiis & mentis institutus & imbutus, in aliquo verè fidei articulo & capite non solùm erat, verum etiam pertinaciter suo errori insistit. Rom.16.17.18.
units.tr: HERETIC: one who, having been instructed and imbued in the first principles of the Christian faith, not only errs in some true article and head of the faith, but also obstinately persists in his error, Rom. 16.17, 18.

units.la: HAERETICI cauendi, & fugiendi, Deut.13.1.&c.18.20.1.Reg.18.20.&c.2.Reg.10.25. Matt.7.15. Rom.16.17.2.Thess.3.2.Tim.2.17. & 3 5. Tit.3.10.11.2.Ioan.v.10. hæretici iam de à tèporibus Apostolorum extiterũt, 1. Tim.20.2. v.17.1.Ioan.2.18.2.Ioan.v.7. Apoc.2.15.Hæreticos futu-ros etiam nostris temporibus,prædictum est, Matth.24. 5.24. Ioan.5.43.1.Tim.4.1.2.Tim.3. 1.2.Petr.2.1.&3.3.Iu-dæ v.18.19.Hæreticorum mores & doctrina, ibid.Hæretici male tolerantur à Præfectis, Apoc.2.14.Hæretici à Magistratu puniendi, 1.Tim.2.2.Deut.18.20.&13.5.Ier.14. 4.15.
units.tr: HERETICS are to be guarded against and avoided: Deut. 13.1, etc. and 18.20; 1 Kings 18.20, etc.; 2 Kings 10.25; Matt. 7.15; Rom. 16.17; 2 Thess. 3.2; 1 Tim. 2.17 and 3.5; Titus 3.10–11; 2 John v.10. Heretics have already arisen since the times of the apostles, 1 Tim. 2.0 (?); v.17; 1 John 2.18; 2 John v.7; Rev. 2.15. It has been foretold that heretics will also arise in our own times, Matt. 24.5, 24; John 5.43; 1 Tim. 4.1; 2 Tim. 3.1–2; 2 Pet. 2.1 and 3.3; Jude vv.18–19. The morals and doctrine of heretics, ibid. Heretics are tolerated badly by governors, Rev. 2.14. Heretics are to be punished by the magistrate, 1 Tim. 2.2; Deut. 18.20 and 13.5; Jer. 14.4, 15.

units.la: RESISTATIO 10, seu disceptatio damnatur, Phil.2.14.1.Tim.2. Iac.1.6.Mat.21.21.Rom.4.20.Luc.17.5.
units.tr: HESITATION, or disputing, is condemned: Phil. 2.14; 1 Tim. 2; James 1.6; Matt. 21.21; Rom. 4.20; Luke 17.5.

units.la: AGAR, ancilla Saræ, ab hera hero vxor datur, Genes.16.3. grauida ex hero heram despicit, v.4. fugit iram heræ, v.6. reducitur ab Angelo, v.9. filium Ismaelem parit, v.15. eiicitur vna cum filio suo Ismaele ex ædibus Abrahami, 21. 4. Legis pactionem repræsentat, Gal.4.24. Sina mons est, 25. non illa in sese mulier, sed allegoricè considerata, hoc est, vetus illa pactio legalis in illo Arabiæ celebri monte sancita, ex aduerso respondens præsenti Ierusalem, & seruiens cum filiis suis. Sicut enim ancillæ filij sunt serui, ita vetus pactio legalis per illam ancillam adumbrata, non alios quàm maledictionis seruos gignit.
units.tr: HAGAR, the handmaid of Sarai, is given by her mistress to her master as a wife, Gen. 16.3. Pregnant, she despises her mistress, v.4. She flees from her mistress's anger, v.6. She is brought back by the angel, v.9. She bears the son Ishmael, v.15. She is cast out with her son Ishmael from the house of Abraham, 21.14. She represents the covenant of the law, Gal. 4.24. Mount Sinai is it, v.25. Not that woman in herself, but considered allegorically: that is, that old legal covenant ratified on that famous mountain of Arabia, corresponding to the present Jerusalem and serving with her children. For just as the children of the handmaid are slaves, so the old legal covenant, foreshadowed by that handmaid, begets none but slaves of the curse.

units.la: Quemadmodum autem Agar ancilla legalem pactionem adumbrabat, & non nisi seruos gignebat, hoc est, eos, qui volunt ex Lege iustificari: Ira Sara ingenua nouam pactionem repræsentabat, & filios gignebat ingenuos, liberos, & hæredes ex promissione, hoc est, qui sola fide absque vllis operum meritis iustificantur. (Hagareni per Rubenitas profligantur, 1.Par.5.v.19.20.
units.tr: Just as Hagar the handmaid foreshadowed the legal covenant and begot only slaves, that is, those who wish to be justified by the Law, so Sarah, a free woman, represented the new covenant and begot free-born children, liberi, and heirs through the promise, that is, those who are justified by faith alone, without any merit of works. (The Hagarenes are routed by the Reubenites, 1 Chron. 5.19–20.)

units.la: AGGÆVS Propheta: Prophetiæ eius tempus, Aggæi.1.1. Iudæos ad Templi instaurationem hortatur, 1.Esdræ.5.1. Aggæi 1.8. gloriam secundi Templi augustiorem & excellentiorem futuram prioris gloria prædicit. Aggei 2.ver.3. 4.5.9. (1.festiuus, solemnis.)
units.tr: AGGEUS the prophet. The time of his prophecy: Hag. 1.1. He exhorts the Jews to restore the Temple, Ezra 5.1; Hag. 1.8. He foretells that the glory of the second Temple will be more august and more excellent than the glory of the former, Hag. 2.3, 4, 5, 9. (1. festive, solemn.)

units.la: Regia ciuitas in tribu Beniamin, exploratur, Ios.7.2. expugnatur. & incenditur, 8.28. eius Rex laqueo vitam finit, v.29. (Haai,1.aceruus)
units.tr: A royal city in the tribe of Benjamin is explored, Josh. 7.2; it is taken and burned, 8.28; its king ends his life on a gallows, v.29. (Ai, a heap.)

units.la: ALIAETVM auem non comedebant Iudæi, Leuit.11.13. Deut.14.12.
units.tr: ALIAETUM: a bird the Jews did not eat (Lev. 11:13; Deut. 14:12).

units.la: HALLEL-uja Apoc.19.1.3.4.6.
units.tr: HALLELUJAH (Rev. 19:1, 3, 4, 6).

units.la: HAMAN, filius Amadathi, honoratur ab Assuero, Esth.3.1. ab omnibus adoratur, solo Mardochæo excepto, v.2 Mardochæo infensus, v.5. impetrat Iudæorum excidium, v.11. suasu vxoris patibulu Mardochæo erigit, 5.14.cui mirab li Dei prouidentia affligitur,7.10. post eius mortem, fil suspenduntur,9.14.(.i.tumultuans)
units.tr: HAMAN, son of Hammedatha, is honoured by Ahasuerus (Esth. 3:1) and adored by all except Mordecai (v. 2). He is hostile to Mordecai (v. 5) and obtains the destruction of the Jews (v. 11). At his wife's counsel he erects a gallows for Mordecai (5:14), but by God's wonderful providence he is himself struck down (7:10). After his death his sons are hanged (9:14). (i.e. tumultuous)

units.la: HANANI Propheta Regem Asa arguit, 2.Par. 16.7.mittitur in neruum,v.10.(.i.gratiosus,aut donans,vel pius.)
units.tr: HANANI the prophet rebukes King Asa (2 Chr. 16:7) and is put in the stocks (v. 10). (i.e. gracious, or giving, or pious.)

units.la: HANANIAS Pseudoprophe ta:(V.Ananias,Hananiah.i.gratia Dei.
units.tr: HANANIAS, a false prophet. (Ananias; Hananiah, i.e. the grace of God.)

units.la: HANNA,Elcanæ vxor,à Deo filium petit,& exorat, 1.Sam. v.11.19.20.24.25.eundem Deo consecrat, v.27.Alios liberos habuit.2.21.(.i.gratiosa.)
units.tr: HANNAH, wife of Elkanah, asks God for a son and obtains her request (1 Sam. 1:11, 19, 20, 24, 25). She consecrates him to God (v. 27) and afterwards has other children (2:21). (i.e. gracious.)

units.la: HANON, Rex Ammonitarum, 2.Sam.10.1. Dauid eum pe seruos solatur,vers. 2. nomine explorationis suspecti sunt v.3.quare ignominia Hanon eos affecit, vers.4.hinc bellum inter eos acerbum oritur, v.7. &c.(Hanun.i.misericors.)
units.tr: HANUN, king of the Ammonites (2 Sam. 10:1). David comforts his servants (v. 2). They are suspected of spying (v. 3), so Hanun shames them (v. 4), and from this a bitter war arises between them (v. 7), etc. (Hanun, i.e. merciful.)

units.la: HARAN,quę & Charan vrbs in Mesopotamia: Act.7.2.in e moritur Thare, Genesis 11.32. Fuit etiam HARAN filius Thare:G.11.27.
units.tr: HARAN, also Charan, a city in Mesopotamia (Acts 7:2), where Terah died (Gen. 11:32). There was also a HARAN, son of Terah (Gen. 11:27).

units.la: HAZAEL,famulus Benadad,Syriæ Regis,2.Reg.8.8. eo suffocato regnum occupat in Syria, vers.15.vrbem Geth,expugnat,12.17.Israelitas affligit,13 3.moritur,v.24.(.i.speculator Dei.)
units.tr: HAZAEL, servant of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (2 Kgs. 8:8). After suffocating his master he seizes the kingdom of Syria (v. 15), captures the city of Gath (12:17), afflicts the Israelites (13:3), and dies (v. 24). (i.e. watchman of God.)

units.la: HEBAL maledictionis mons,Deut.27.v.4.13.
units.tr: HEBAL, the mountain of cursing (Deut. 27:4, 13).

units.la: HEBDOMADARUM solennitas,Exo.34.22. hebdomadarum septuaginta visio,Dan.9.24.
units.tr: The solemnity of weeks (Exod. 34:22); the vision of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:24).

units.la: HEBER è Sçelah nascitur, Gen.11.14.ætas eius 16.17.(Eber peregrinator.)
units.tr: EBER is born of Shelah (Gen. 11:14); his age is given (vv. 16–17). (Eber, sojourner.)

units.la: [Hebrei,& Dominus Deus hebræorum,Gen.14.13. &43.3 Exod.3.18.&5.3.&7.16. &9.v.1.13.&10.3. Io.1.9. Act.6.1.
units.tr: [Hebrews, and the Lord God of the Hebrews (Gen. 14:13; 43:3; Exod. 3:18; 5:3; 7:16; 9:1, 13; 10:3; John 1:9; Acts 6:1).]

units.la: HEBRAEVM se iactat Paulus,2.Cor.11.22. Phil.3 5. cum hebraeis edere AEgyptiis illicitum,Gen.43.32.
units.tr: Paul boasts that he is a Hebrew (2 Cor. 11:22; Phil. 3:5). It was unlawful for Egyptians to eat with Hebrews (Gen. 43:32).

units.la: HEBRON(quæ & Mambre,Gen.23.19.&Arbee,35.27.)Chanaan ciuitas,capitur à Iosuah,Ios.10.36.Calebo possidendum datur,14.13.Iudic.1.10.(.i.societas.)
units.tr: HEBRON (also Mamre, Gen. 23:19, and Arba, 35:27), a city of Canaan, taken by Joshua (Josh. 10:36) and given to Caleb to possess (14:13; Judg. 1:10). (i.e. fellowship.)

units.la: HEBRON confugij ciuitas, Ios.21.11. quam Abraham inhabitauit G.13.18.
units.tr: HEBRON, a city of refuge (Josh. 21:11), which Abraham inhabited (Gen. 13:18).

units.la: HEDEN, sacer paradisi locus ad orientem(.i.voluptas deliciæ)Gen.2.8.&3 23.24.
units.tr: EDEN, the sacred place of paradise to the east (i.e. pleasure, delight). Gen. 2:8; 3:23, 24.

units.la: Helam:vitæ Elam.
units.tr: Helam: the life of Elam.

units.la: HELCIAS Sacerdos magni nominis Iosię ętate, 2.Reg.22. 2.Paral.34.6. Librum Legis in Templo reperit, v.14.(portio aut lenitas Domini.)
units.tr: HILKIAH, a high priest of great renown in the age of Josiah (2 Kgs. 22; 2 Chr. 34:6). He finds the Book of the Law in the Temple (v. 14). (portion or gentleness of the Lord.)

units.la: Sacerdos in Silo, Vide Eli. ( i. opprobrium ).
units.tr: A priest in Shiloh; see Eli. (i.e. reproach.)

units.la: ELIAS. Vide Elias.
units.tr: ELIJAH. See Elijah.

units.la: ELIOPOLIS ( id est, ciuitas Solis, Hebraicé ON i. dolor ) ... est in Aegypto, Gen. 41.45. & 46.20. Ezech. 30.16.
units.tr: HELIOPOLIS (that is, the city of the Sun; in Hebrew On, i.e. sorrow) is in Egypt (Gen. 41:45; 46:20; Ezek. 30.16).

units.la: ELISAEVS, Vide ELISAEVS. ( Elisa. 1. salus Domini ).
units.tr: ELISHA; see Elisha. (Elisha, i.e. the salvation of the Lord.)

units.la: HEMAN Nepos Samuelis. 1. par. 6.33. praerat Cantoribus a latere constitutis: cap. 25.5. (id est dextera),
units.tr: HEMAN, grandson of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:33). He presided over the singers stationed at his side (1 Chr. 25:5). (i.e. right hand.)

units.la: HEMOR occiditur a Simeone, Gen. 34.26.
units.tr: HAMOR is slain by Simeon (Gen. 34:26).

units.la: HENOCH filius Cain, Gen. 4.17. ciuitas ab eo aedificata, ibid. [Enoch. 1. consecratus Deo,)
units.tr: ENOCH, son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), and the city built by him (ibid.). (Hanoch, consecrated to God.)

units.la: HENOCH filius Iared, vir pius & Propheta, Genes. 5.20. e- is pietas, v. 22. eius contra reprobos propheria, Iudae, er. 14. fides, Hebr. 11.5. in coelum rapitur, Genes. 5.24 [ebr. 11.5. [Eius genealogia, Lucae 3.37.]
units.tr: ENOCH, son of Jared, a pious man and prophet (Gen. 5:20). His piety (v. 22); his prophecy against the reprobate (Jude 14); his faith (Heb. 11:5); he is taken up into heaven (Gen. 5:24; Heb. 11:5). [His genealogy, Luke 3:37.]

units.la: HER occiditur a Deo, Gen. 38.7. & 46.12 [ HER ex posteris Dauid, Luc. 3.28.] (Vigil, aemulus, vel effundens).
units.tr: ER is slain by God (Gen. 38:7; 46:12). [Er, among the posterity of David, Luke 3:28.] (watchful, a rival, or pouring out.)

units.la: HERBA: Herbae verbo Dei creantur cum feminibus suis, Gen. 1.11. earum visus hominibus post lapsum designatus, 18. Psal. 104.14. V. Marc. 4.28. Isa. & 45.8. Ps. 65.10. omnis caro est ut gramen, & omnis gloria hominis ut flos gramini. Exaruit gramen, & flos eius decidit. Sed verbum Domini manet in aeternum: 1. Pet. 1.24. V. Iac. 1.9.10. Isa. 40.6. Ps. 103.15.
units.tr: HERB: herbs were created by the word of God with their seeds (Gen. 1:11). Their use for men was assigned after the Fall (v. 18; Ps. 104:14; cf. Mark 4:28; Isa. 45:8; Ps. 65:10). "All flesh is as grass, and all its glory as the flower of the grass. The grass withers and its flower falls, but the word of the Lord endures for ever" (1 Pet. 1:24). See James 1:9–10; Isa. 40:6; Ps. 103:15.

units.la: HERI & nudiustertius, pars temporis proxima, pro toto praeterito tempore; synecdoche, hoc est, antea, Gen. 31.2. Exod. 4.10, & 5.7. &c. Vide CRAS. [Christus heri & hodie Hebr.]
units.tr: YESTERDAY and the day before yesterday: the nearest part of time put for all past time, a synecdoche; that is, formerly (Gen. 31:2; Exod. 4:10; 5:7, etc.). See TOMORROW. [Christ yesterday and today, Heb.]

units.la: HERMOGENES Apostata, 2 Tim. 1.15. ( 1. mercurio genitus)
units.tr: HERMOGENES, an apostate (2 Tim. 1:15). (1. born of Mercury.)

units.la: HERMON mons ( qui & Sarion, & Sanir, & Sion, &c.) Deut. 3.9. & 4.48. Psal. 133.3. (1. Destructio).
units.tr: HERMON, a mountain (which is also Sarion, Sanir, Sion, etc.) (Deut. 3:9; 4:48; Ps. 133:3). (1. Destruction.)

units.la: HERODES: Herodes tres ab Euangelistis commemorantur: Primus Herodes, cognomento Magnus, Ascalonita Balictus, sub quo natus est Christus, Matt. 2.1. Secundus Herodes Tetrarcha, Antipas dictus, Matth. 14.1, qui etsi Tetrarcha duntaxat erat, tamen ab Euangelista Marco Regis nomine ornatur, ex vulgi, ac praesertim Aulicorum more Marc 6.14. Tertius. Herodes Agrippa, Herodis magni nepos ex Aristobulo filio, cuius fit mentio Act. 12.v. 22.23. nam alteri Agrippae filio istius, non additur aui-um Herodis praenomen, Act. 25.13.
units.tr: Three Herods are mentioned by the Evangelists. The first Herod, surnamed the Great, the Ascalonite, the Idumaean, under whom Christ was born (Matt. 2:1). The second Herod, the tetrarch called Antipas (Matt. 14:1), who, although he was only a tetrarch, is given the title of king by the Evangelist Mark, after the common and especially courtly custom (Mark 6:14). The third, Herod Agrippa, grandson of Herod the Great through his son Aristobulus, mentioned in Acts 12:22–23; for the other son of Agrippa (Acts 25:13) is not given the forename of his grandfather Herod.

units.la: HERODES Ascalonita Rex Iudaeae, ob nati Christi rumorem turbatur, Matth. 2.3. Concilium Sacerdotum super hac re conuocat, v.4. Magos fraudulenter, ut sibi renuntient locum nati Christi, orat, verf.8. illi oraculo fraudulenter certiores facti ab eo sibi cauent, v.12. Herodes, ipe captus infantes occidi iubet, v.16. eius mors, v.19.20. Exitus ei miser. V. persecutorum Ecclesiæ.
units.tr: HEROD the Ascalonite, king of Judea, is troubled by rumour of Christ's birth (Matt. 2:3). He convenes a council of priests about this matter (v. 4). He craftily asks the Magi to report back to him the place of Christ's birth (v. 8). Warned by the oracle, they avoid him (v. 12). Herod, himself deceived, orders the infants to be killed (v. 16). His death (vv. 19–20); his end was wretched. See the persecutors of the Church.

units.la: HERODES Antipas, Tetrarcha Galilææ, Luc 3.1. insigni hypocrita, 13. v.31.32. eius de Christo opinio, Matt.14. v.1. Mar.6.14. Luc.9.7. vitia, Matth.14.3. Marci.6.17. Luc.3.1. occidit Ioannem Baptistam, ibid. Christum interrogi Luc.23.9. cum Pilato in gratiam redit, & quare, v.12. Act. 4.27. Ecclesiæ & veritatis hostis 4.27. V. persecutorū Ec.
units.tr: HEROD Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 3:1), a notorious hypocrite (Luke 13:31–32). His opinion about Christ (Matt. 14:1; Mark 6:14; Luke 9:7). His vices (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He killed John the Baptist (ibid.). He questions Christ (Luke 23:9). He was reconciled with Pilate, and why (v. 12; Acts 4:27). An enemy of the Church and of the truth (Acts 4:27). See the persecutors of the Church.

units.la: HERODES Agrippa, filius Aristobuli, Ecclesiam persequitur, Act.12.1. à populo adoratur, v.22. ab Angelo cæditur, v.23. eroditur à vermibus, ibid.
units.tr: HEROD Agrippa, son of Aristobulus, persecutes the Church (Acts 12:1). He is adored by the people (v. 22), struck by an angel (v. 23), and eaten by worms (ibid.).

units.la: HERODIANI in Christum conspirant, Marc.3.6. eum tentant, Matth.22.16. Mar.12.13.
units.tr: The HERODIANS conspire against Christ (Mark 3:6), and tempt him (Matt. 22:16; Mark 12:13).

units.la: HERODIAS vxor Philippi ab Herode leuiro incestis nuptiis detinetur, Mar.6.17. hæc vt dimittatur, suadet Ioan. Baptista, Mat.14.4. eius causa conijcitur in carcerem, 14. Luc.3.v.19.20. filiæ, vt ei caput petat, persuadet, Mar.14.
units.tr: HERODIAS, wife of Philip, is held in an incestuous marriage by Herod, her husband's brother (Mark 6:17). John the Baptist urges that she be dismissed (Matt. 14:4); on account of this he is cast into prison (Matt. 14; Luke 3:19–20). She persuades her daughter to ask for his head (Mark 14).

units.la: HERODIO, vel HERODIVS eo vesci non licebat Iudæis Leuit.11.19. Deut.14.16.
units.tr: HERODIO, or HERODIUS: the Jews were not allowed to eat it (Lev. 11:19; Deut. 14:16).

units.la: HEROICI impetus exempla, Vide IMPETVS Heroici.
units.tr: Heroic impulses, examples: see IMPULSE, heroic.

units.la: HERVS & hera, Vide DOMINVS: & DOMINA.
units.tr: HERUS and HERA: see LORD and LADY.

units.la: HERSON, filius Phares, genef. 46.12. Matth.1.3. requit post se Aram, & appellatur Iephone, 1. Par. 4.15.
units.tr: HEZRON, son of Perez (Gen. 46:12; Matt. 1:3). He left Aram behind him, and is called Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

units.la: [HESEBON, vrbs & regio In Galad Moabitarum, Num. 26. Deut.19.7. Ios.9.10. Esai.15.4. Ier.48.2. & 49.3.]
units.tr: [HESHBON, a city and region in Gilead of the Moabites (Num. 26; Deut. 19:7; Josh. 9:10; Isa. 15:4; Jer. 48:2; 49:3).]

units.la: HESTHER, Vide Esther.
units.tr: ESTHER; see Esther.

units.la: HETHAEVS (à quo Hethæi dicti) filius Chanaan, genitus 10.15. eius posteri deleri iubentur, Deut.20.17.
units.tr: HETH (from whom the Hittites are named), a son of Canaan, born (10:15). His descendants are commanded to be destroyed (Deut. 20:17).

units.la: HEVA (id est viuens, Gen.3.20. cur sic dicta, ibid.) ex costa Adami formatur, Genef.2.22. à serpente seducitur, 3.6. Cor. 11.3.1. Tim. 2.14. [parit filios. Gen.4.1.] punitur verf.16.
units.tr: EVE (that is, living; Gen. 3:20; why she was so called, ibid.) is formed from Adam's rib (Gen. 2:22) and seduced by the serpent (Gen. 3:6; 2 Cor. 11:3; 1 Tim. 2:14). [She bears sons, Gen. 4:1.] She is punished (v. 16).

units.la: HEVAEI omnino exterminandi, Deut.20.17. Israelitis resistunt, Iof.19. [Vide 2.Sam.24.7.1. Reg.9.20.] Eorum deus 2. Reg.17.31.11.
units.tr: The HIVITES are to be utterly exterminated (Deut. 20:17). They resisted the Israelites (Josh. 19). [See 2 Sam. 24:7; 1 Kgs. 9:20.] Their god (2 Kgs. 17:31).

units.la: [HEVILA regio Gen.2.11. & 25.18.1. Sam.15.7. nomen vallis Gen.10.v.7.29.]
units.tr: [HAVILAH, a region (Gen. 2:11; 25:18; 1 Sam. 15:7); the name of a valley (Gen. 10:7, 29).]

units.la: HEZRI ERI, filius Chelubi, vnus ex præfectis Dauidis, is præit exercentibus opus rusticum in agris. 1. Chron. 27. 26. RIEL, (adiutus à Deo) pater Saraiæ: Hier. 36. 26 DO V. Addo. L (1. vita Dei) Bethlehemita, Hierichunta instaurat, Reg. 16. 34. ob id imprecationem Iosuæ incurrit, Ios. 6. 1. Reg. 16. 34. REMIAS, Vide IEREMIAS. RVSALEM, Vide IERVSALEM.
units.tr: HEZRAI (or HEZRO), son of Chelub, one of David's prefects, who goes before those doing rustic work in the fields (1 Chr. 27:26). RIEL (helped by God), father of Seraiah (Jer. 36:26). HIEL the Bethelite (Hiel, the life of God) restores Jericho (1 Kgs. 16:34), and for this incurs Joshua's curse (Josh. 6:26; 1 Kgs. 16:34). JEREMIAH: see Jeremiah. JERUSALEM: see Jerusalem.

units.la: ARITAS, Est benigna, aperta, & candida animi nostri, dū os vel videmus, vel excipimus lætitia, quę ipso vultu & culis à nobis significatur. 2. Cor. 9. 7. Quisq. sicut præoptat arde, ita agat: non ex tristitia aut ex necessitate: Nam hilarem datorem diligit Deus.
units.tr: CHEERFULNESS: it is a kindly, open and bright state of our mind, which is signified by our face and eyes when we see or receive with joy (2 Cor. 9:7). "Let each one do as he has purposed in his heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loves a cheerful giver."

units.la: ARITAS [quibus & cur commendata,] Rom. 12. 8; N, mensura liquidorum, Exod 30. 24. Num. 28. 7. Ezech. 11. & 46. 14.]
units.tr: CHEERFULNESS [to whom and why it is commended] (Rom. 12:8). HIN, a measure of liquids (Exod. 30:24; Num. 28:7; Ezek. 46:14).

units.la: AM Odollamites (1. viuens excelse) ad quem Iuda diuer ns filiam viri Schuach duxit in vxorem: Gen. 38. 1. 2.
units.tr: HIRAH the Adullamite (i.e. living on high), with whom Judah, turning aside, took as wife the daughter of a man named Shua (Gen. 38:1–2).

units.la: Am Rex Tyri, amicus Dauidis, 2. Sam. 5. 11. 1. Paral. 14. Reg. 5. 1. per seruos Salomoni regno recens inaugurato atulatur, v. 1. 10. Cuipro lignis & auro datoSolomo dedit rbes viginti: 9. V. 11.
units.tr: HIRAM, king of Tyre, friend of David (2 Sam. 5:11; 1 Chr. 14:1; 1 Kgs. 5:1). Through his servants he congratulates Solomon on his newly inaugurated kingdom (1 Kgs. 5:1, 10). To him, in return for the timber and gold given, Solomon gave twenty cities (1 Kgs. 9:11).

units.la: AM, ğrarius, artifex eximius, 1. Reg. 7. v. 13. 14. 2. Para. 13. CVS peccatis populi onustus, figura Christi: eius oblatio, Leuit. 16. v. 20 21 22. Heb. 9 12. 13 14. & 10. 4. 5. &c.
units.tr: HIRAM, a craftsman, an outstanding artificer (1 Kgs. 7:13–14; 2 Chr. 13). The GOAT, laden with the sins of the people, a figure of Christ; its offering (Lev. 16:20–22; Heb. 9:12–14; 10:4–5, etc.).

units.la: SPANIA regio latissima Europæ. Rom. 15. v. 24. 28.]
units.tr: SPAIN, the widest region of Europe. Rom. 15. v. 24. 28.

units.la: BAB, qui & Raguel, socer Mosis, renuit cum Mose prosi-ciscì in terram promissionis, Num. 10. 29. (1. dilectus.)
units.tr: HOBAB, who is also called Raguel, Moses' father-in-law, refused to go with Moses into the land of promise. Num. 10. 29. (1. beloved.)

units.la: DIE, pro, hoc tempore, Iudic. 9. 18. synecdoche, pro toto tempore, quo nos Dominus compellat, & quo nobis offertur Euangelium, Psalmo 95 7. Hebr. 3. 15. Hodie & ras prouerbialiter dici videtur pro exiguo temporis spatio, Luc. 13. 32.
units.tr: TODAY, for this time, Judg. 9. 18. It is a synecdoche for the whole time in which the Lord calls us and the Gospel is offered to us, Ps. 95. 7; Heb. 3. 15. "Today" also seems to be used proverbially for a short span of time, Luke 13. 32.

units.la: Hodie (inquit Pater de Filio) genuite, Psal. 2, 7. Heb. 1. 5. & 5. 5. Non est igitur Filius vel adoptione, vel amoris respectu, vel simili vlla ratione, sed quia verè ex Patre genitus est ante res vllas conditas, Prouer. 8 22. Coloss. 1. 15. Sed si ita est, dices, cur additur aduerbium Hodie? nempe quia æterna quidem est illa generatio, sed suo tempore repræsentata, cum æternus ille Filius conspicuus factus est in carne. Nam ista quidem adducitur ab Apostolo pro ostendae Christi non humanitati, sed Deitati, verum ita, vt ipectetur quatenus sese in carne assumta quasi conspici dam præbet, quomodo etiam conspecta fuit eius glor quasi vnigeniti, Ioan.1.14. Potest autem hic dies acc vel in genere de tempore vtriusque naturæ in vnam pe sonam coalitionis, vt Luc.1.31.& deinceps:vel ad resur ctionem & ascensionem referri. Nam tum demum ... hic homo verum & æternum Dei Filium esse reipsa pl ne ostendit, cum antea ipsius Deitas veluti delitescerer carnis infirmitate, non nisi per vices & certis gradib sese prodens, adeo vt nostri quidem respectu tum quodammodo gentius a Patre videatur, Act.13.23. 17.31.Roman.1.4. Iesvs Christus heri & hodie ipse & secula, Hebr.13.8.
units.tr: "Today," says the Father of the Son, "I have begotten you," Ps. 2. 7; Heb. 1. 5 and 5. 5. The Son is therefore not Son by adoption, or by reason of love, or by any similar means, but because he was truly begotten of the Father before any creature was made, Prov. 8. 22; Col. 1. 15. But if it is so, you will ask, why is the adverb "today" added? Clearly because that generation is eternal, yet was displayed in its own time, when that eternal Son became visible in the flesh. For the Apostle cites this text to show the divinity of Christ, not his humanity; yet in such a way that he is seen to present himself, as it were, visibly in the flesh he assumed, just as his glory as the only-begotten was seen, John 1. 14. This day may be referred either generally to the time of the union of the two natures in one person, as in Luke 1. 31 and following, or to the resurrection and ascension. For only then did he fully show, in fact, that this man is the true and eternal Son of God, whereas before his divinity lay hidden, as it were, under the weakness of the flesh, revealing itself only by turns and by set stages. So that, with respect to us, he seems then in some way to have been begotten of the Father, Acts 13. 23; 17. 31; Rom. 1. 4. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, Heb. 13. 8.

units.la: HOEDVS quandiu lac fugit, non coquendus, Exodi 23. & 34.26. Deut.14.21.(septem autem dies erat cum mat sua:Ex.22.30.Hœdi à Christo vocantur maledicti, Mat 25.33 [Hœdi mystici, nempe electi, Cantic.1 8.] prop gus de non sibi dato hœdo queritur:Luc.15.29.
units.tr: KID. As long as it is milk it is not to be cooked, Exod. 23 and 34. 26; Deut. 14. 21. (But it was seven days old with its mother, Exod. 22. 30.) Kids are called accursed by Christ, Matt. 25. 33. [Mystical kids, that is, the elect, Cant. 1. 8.] Also a complaint about a kid not given to oneself, Luke 15. 29.

units.la: HOLDA Prophetissa, eius prophetia, 2 Reg. 22.15.2.Par 34.v.23.24.(1.orbis, aut mustela, aut rubigo.)
units.tr: HULDAH the prophetess; her prophecy, 2 Kings 22. 15; 2 Chron. 34. 23, 24. (1. a ball, or a weasel, or rust.)

units.la: HOLOCAVSTVM & eius lex, Levit. 6.9. Holocaustum ip cœlesti consumtum, 9.24.1. Reg.18.38. Holocaustoma vel holocausta Græci id sacrificiorum genus interp tati sunt, in quo tota victima Deo adolebatur, vt vel i verbi notatio declarat: ὁλοκαύτως autem, aut sacrificia, app lant ea sacrificia, in quibus pars aliqua Sacerdotibus conuiuio decidebatur, Marci 12.33. vbi his duobus sac ficiorum generibus vniuersus ille ceremonialis cul comprehenditur, in qua nonnulli hypocritæ summ pietatis collocabant,[Vide Heb.10.v.6.8.]
units.tr: BURNT OFFERING, and its law, Lev. 6. 9. A burnt offering consumed by heavenly fire, Lev. 9. 24; 1 Kings 18. 38. The Greeks interpreted holocaustoma, or holocausta, as the kind of sacrifice in which the whole victim was burned to God, as the very meaning of the word declares. But [ὁλοκαύτως], or the sacrifices, they applied to those sacrifices in which some part was distributed to the priests for a feast, Mark 12. 33, where under these two kinds of sacrifice the whole ceremonial cult is comprehended, in which some hypocrites placed the highest piety. [See Heb. 10. 6, 8.]

units.la: HOMO Homo ad imaginem Dei formatur, Genef.1.27. 5.1.& 9.6.àDeo rectus creatus,Eccles.7.29.è limo terra tus,Genesis 2.7.1.Cor.15.45.collocatur in Paradiso vo ptatis, Genef.2,v.8.15.illic corumpitur,3.v.6 7.Rom.5. Vide ADAM. Eius natura corrupta nihil nisi corrupt profert, Genef.6.5.& 8.21.Iob 15.16.Ierem.17 9. Matt. Ioan.3.19.Rom.3.4.& 8.7.Eph.2.3. Tit.3.3. Corruptio eius pœne: Prima,labor & mors, Genes.3.17. Pa-l.29.15.Iob.7.1.& 14 1.Pfal.39.6.Vani,Iob.1.21. & 8.9.& 6.Pfal.8.5.& 39.v.6.9.& 49.18. & 62. 10. & 82. 7. & 94. 9.& 103.14.& 144.4.& 146.3.4.Eccle.4.3 & 5.14.Esa.31.3. 40.7.& 51.v.8.12.Ierem.17.5.1.Corint.3.20.1.Timoth.6. Hebr.2.6.1.Petr.1 24.Morti obnoxij,Pfalm.89.49.1.Samuel.6.9.Ecclef.3.v.2.10.& 9.v.3.10.11.Roman.5.12.Hebr. 27.V.1.Cor.15.5.1.Theff.4.15.
units.tr: MAN. Man is formed in the image of God, Gen. 1. 27; 5. 1; 9. 6. He was created upright by God, Eccl. 7. 29. He was formed of the dust of the earth, Gen. 2. 7; 1 Cor. 15. 45. He was placed in the paradise of pleasure, Gen. 2. 8, 15; there he was corrupted, Gen. 3. 6, 7; Rom. 5. See ADAM. His corrupted nature produces nothing but corruption, Gen. 6. 5; 8. 21; Job 15. 16; Jer. 17. 9; Matt. 15; John 3. 19; Rom. 3. 4; 8. 7; Eph. 2. 3; Titus 3. 3. The penalties of his corruption are these: First, labour and death, Gen. 3. 17. Second, expulsion from the paradise of pleasure, v. 23. Third, generation under sin, liable to the wrath of God, Ps. 51. 6, 7; Eph. 2. Sinners, Gen. 6. 5; 8. 21; Rom. 3. 9, 12, 20, 22; 5. 12; 11. 32; Gal. 2. 17; 3. 22; Eph. 2. 3. He is called "a son of the wretched and unhappy," 2 Sam. 14. 14; 1 Chron. 29. 15; Job 7. 1; 14. 1; Ps. 39. 6. Vain, Job 1. 21; 8. 9; 6; Ps. 8. 5; 39. 6, 9; 49. 18; 62. 10; 82. 7; 94. 9; 103. 14; 144. 4; 146. 3, 4; Eccl. 4. 3, 5; 14; Isa. 31. 3; 40. 7; 51. 8, 12; Jer. 17. 5; 1 Cor. 3. 20; 1 Tim. 6; Heb. 2. 6; 1 Pet. 1. 24. Subject to death, Ps. 89. 49; 1 Sam. 6. 9; Eccl. 3. 2, 10; 9. 3, 10, 11; Rom. 5. 12; Heb. 9. 27; 1 Cor. 15. 5; 1 Thess. 4. 15.

units.la: Hominis vocabulum Primo interdum indefinite & vniuersaliter quemuis hominem significat, & pro qui-um ponitur,Hebræorum more,Mat.16.26.& 20.1. Mar. 36.Luc.18.2. Secundo, interdum de singulari quodam dicitur,Matth.12 45. Mar.14.21.Tertio, interdum per quandam similitudinem & parabolam effertur, Matth.7.9 & 23. Quarto,interdum non tam naturam,quàm eius corruptionem & errores designat, Matth. 15. 9. Roman.3.4. Quinto,collectiue significat Ecclesiam ex Iudæis & gentibus in vnum quasi corpus collectam & compactam,Eph. 15.Hunc hominem Paulus à capite,omnium præstantissima videlicet parte, vocat Christum, 1. Corinth.12.12. Sexto,qualitatum in eo respectu, homo alias internus & couus, alias externus & vetus dicitur, Ephef. 4. 24. Vide homo duplex, Septimo, homo alteram sui partem,quæ mortalis est, & spiritui opponitur, significat,2. Corinth.4.16. Octavo, relationem & ordinem si spectes, aliis celebratur in sanctis Scripturis, Homo primus secundus,1.Cor.15.47. Nono,relationis autem (quæ in summum Dominum & Patrem, ac adoptionis filios ratione,homo Dei nuncupatur is, qui fidei obedien-am eidem præstare satagit, 1. Timoth.6.11.2.Timoth.3. Decimo Christus IESVS,Redemptor mundi homo dicitur,Marci 15.39. Vndecimo, cum epithelo pecti Antichristum significat 2,Thess.2.3. Duodecimo, à gubernatoribus dicitur, alius quidem animalis, alius vero spiritualis,1 Cor.2.14.15.V.homo duplex. Decimotertio,catur & pro Filio,Matth.10.35.
units.tr: The word "man" is used in several ways. First, sometimes indefinitely and universally, meaning any man whatever, and it is used for "whoever," in the Hebrew manner, Matt. 16. 26; 20. 1; Mark 36; Luke 18. 2. Second, sometimes it is said of a certain single person, Matt. 12. 45; Mark 14. 21. Third, sometimes it is expressed by a certain likeness or parable, Matt. 7. 9 and 23. Fourth, sometimes it designates not so much nature as its corruption and errors, Matt. 15. 9; Rom. 3. 4. Fifth, it signifies collectively the Church gathered and joined together into one body, as it were, from Jews and Gentiles, Eph. 1. 5. Paul calls this man, from the head, which is the most excellent part of all, Christ, 1 Cor. 12. 12. Sixth, with respect to qualities, man is called in one respect inward and new, in another outward and old, Eph. 4. 24. See "double man." Seventh, it signifies the part of himself which is mortal and opposed to the spirit, 2 Cor. 4. 16. Eighth, if you regard relation and order, it is celebrated in the holy Scriptures in various ways: "first man," "second man," 1 Cor. 15. 47. Ninth, by reason of his relation to the supreme Lord and Father, and as an adopted son, he who labours to render faithful obedience to him is called "man of God," 1 Tim. 6. 11; 2 Tim. 3. Tenth, Christ Jesus, the Redeemer of the world, is called man, Mark 15. 39. Eleventh, with an added epithet, it signifies the Antichrist, 2 Thess. 2. 3. Twelfth, by the governors of the world men are called, some "natural," others "spiritual," 1 Cor. 2. 14, 15; see "double man." Thirteenth, it is also used for a son, Matt. 10. 35.

units.la: Homo duplex:Primus,Animalis,id est, non alia quàm sola viturali animæ luce præditus, 1.Corin.2.14.vt explicatur idæ v.19.(Animatus homo,id est,anima viuens dicitur, Corinth.15.45.per synecdochen, quod videtur animalis vocabulo optimè exprimi. Nam hoc quoque ab anima, præstantiore hominis parte, deducitur. ) Secundus, Spi-ritualis, qui Spiritu Dei regenitus ab eo ducitur & regitur. 1.Cor.2.15.
units.tr: "Double man." The first is the natural man, that is, one endowed with no other light than the living light of the soul, 1 Cor. 2. 14, as v. 19 explains. (A man made alive, that is, a living soul, is called so in 1 Cor. 15. 45, by synecdoche, which seems best expressed by the word "natural," for this too derives from the soul, the more excellent part of man.) Second, the spiritual man, who has been regenerated by the Spirit of God, is led and governed by him, 1 Cor. 2. 15.

Item σαρκικὸς, seu carnalis, secundùm carnem, Roman.8.5, vocatur à Paulo, qui non sit regeneratus ex Spiritu, mera est caro. Porrò [illegible, ~10 letters] membrorum, seu membra, exterior homo, vetus homo & caro (vt hoc plenioris explicationis gratia addatur) vocatur vniuersa hominis natura, ita vt cum iniquitas conceptus est, & in hanc lucem editus: hoc est, quicquid est in homine, vel intus, vel foris à capite ad calcem, quatenus quidem homo non est gratia regeneratus: idque esse vel ex eo liquet, quòd diserte Apostolus inter corruptissimas partes mètem numerat, Rom.1.28, 1.Timoth. 5.Tit.1.15. item Ephes. 4.23. vult renouationem ad ipsum usque mentis pertingere. Denique res ipsa ostendit nihil æquè reluctari spiritui, atque humanæ prudentiæ rationis tenebras. Ex his vicissim illud quoque intelligitur, quid vocabulum Spiritus carni oppositum, seu interior ac nouus homo declarent, quæ pro eodem accipiuntur apud Paulum, liquet ex testimoniis suprà allatis.
units.tr: The spiritual man is divided within himself, Rom. 7. 15, 19. As to the renewed, regenerate part, he is called the law of the mind, Rom. 7. 23; the inward man, 7. 22; 2 Cor. 4. 16; Eph. 3. 16; 1 Pet. 3. 4; the new man, Eph. 4. 24; Col. 3. 10; and spirit, Rom. 7. 6; John 3. 6, in the last part of the verse. See SPIRIT. As to the unregenerate part, he is called the law of the members, Rom. 7. 23; the outward man, 2 Cor. 4. 16; the old man, Eph. 4. 22; Rom. 6. 6; and flesh, John 3. 6. Likewise, "fleshly," or carnal, according to the flesh, Rom. 8. 5, is what Paul calls the man who has not been regenerated by the Spirit, who is mere flesh. Moreover, [illegible, about ten letters] of the members, or the members, the outward man, the old man and the flesh (to add this for fuller explanation) denote the whole nature of man, so that from the moment he is conceived in iniquity and brought forth into this light, that is, whatever is in man, whether inward or outward, from head to heel, insofar as he is not regenerated by grace. That this is so is clear from the fact that the Apostle expressly numbers the mind among the most corrupt parts, Rom. 1. 28; 1 Tim. 5; Titus 1. 15; likewise Eph. 4. 23 wills that renewal reach even to the mind itself. Finally, the thing itself shows that nothing resists the Spirit so much as the darkness of human prudence and reason. From these in turn it is also understood what the word "spirit," opposed to flesh, or "inward" and "new man," mean; these are taken as the same in Paul, as is clear from the testimonies cited above.

units.la: HOMICIDA, Homicidæ voluntarij censentur quicunque odio cidendi animũ sive multò ante, sive repentino animi impetu habuerunt. Imò etiam, qui de cæde expresse non cogitantes, iræ tamen vehementia impulsi proximum lædunt, ut mors inde consequatur, homicidæ sunt: nec brietas etiam homicidium excusat.
units.tr: HOMICIDE. Those are counted as voluntary homicides who have harboured the intention of killing out of hatred, whether long beforehand or from a sudden impulse of the mind. Indeed, those too are homicides who, not expressly thinking of slaughter but driven by the vehemence of anger, injure a neighbour so that death follows. Nor does drunkenness excuse homicide.

units.la: Mere fortuitum homicidium, in quo vid. appa-rat nullam lædendi cogitationem interuenisse, hac lege non comprehenditur: purgatione tamen eget, & aliqua lib-rationis formula: tum ut homicidæ ipsi consulatur a-uersus interfecti cognatos, tum ut homicidium homines discant omnibus modis execrari.
units.tr: A purely accidental homicide, in which there appears to have been no intention of harm, is not covered by this law. Yet it needs purging and some form of release: both so that the homicide himself is protected against the kinsmen of the slain, and so that men learn to detest homicide in every way.

units.la: HOMICIDA: Homicidæ fugientis lex, Deuter. 19. 4. Homi-darum mos, Iob.24.14. Eorum qui contra hominum -nionem pro homicidis apud Deum censentur, tres gradus constituuntur, Matthæi 5.22. Vnus gradus est eorum qui intus duntaxat aduersus proximum commouenti. Alter eorum, qui eò vsq; efferuescunt, ut iracundum a-quid euomant. Tertius denique eorum, qui in apertum a-quod conuiciũ erumpunt. Homicida Diabolus, Ioan.8.4. V. DIABOLVS. Homicida est, qui fratrem suum odit, 1.Io. 3.15. homicida voluntarius occidendus, Deu.19.11.&c.
units.tr: HOMICIDE: the law of the fleeing homicide (Deut. 19.4). The custom of homicides (Job 24.14). Of those who, against the commandment of men, are counted as homicides before God, three degrees are laid down (Matt. 5.22). One degree is of those who merely stir up anger inwardly against a neighbour. Another is of those who boil over so far that they spit out some angry word. The third, finally, is of those who break out into open reproach. The devil is a homicide (John 8.4; see DEVIL). Whoever hates his brother is a homicide (1 John 3.15). A voluntary homicide is to be put to death (Deut. 19.11, etc.).

units.tr: Public decency [σεμνότης], 1 Tim. 2.2. It is purity of morals, 1

units.la: nctitas & disciplina verbo Dei consentiens , quæ in rebus externis & publicis legibus sancita est, & in omni ordinum genere apparet. 1.Cor.14.40.Huic contraria est ἀταξία, 2.Thess.3,6, 1.Thess.5,14.
units.tr: ... holiness and discipline agreeing with the Word of God, which is sanctioned in external matters and public laws, and appears in every kind of order, 1 Cor. 14.40. Its opposite is disorder [ἀταξία], 2 Thess. 3.6; 1 Thess. 5.14.

units.la: HONESTAE res coram hominibus procurandæ, Rom.12,17. Philip.4.8.
units.tr: Honest conduct to be maintained before men, Rom. 12.17; Phil. 4.8.

units.la: HONESTAS externa pars Ecclesiastici ordinis, 1. Cor. 11.4.8 14.40.1,Tim.3,4,8,11.
units.tr: Decency is the external part of ecclesiastical order, 1 Cor. 11.4, 8; 14.40; 1 Tim. 3.4, 8, 11.

units.la: HONOR & eius diuersæ significationes: pro pretio & æstima tione, Coloss.2, 23. pro subsidio & quouis officij genere Matth.15.v.4,5. Rom.12.10, Ephes.6.2.1. Timoth. 5.ver.17. 1.Petr.2,17, pro reuerentia Magistratui debita, Roman 13,7. pro honesta cura ac solicitudine, 1. Petr.3.7. Honor habendus est corpori,1.Thessal.4 4, Honos Deo debitus Malach.1,6,Regi.1.Petr.2, 17. Parentibus, Deuteron.5.16 Matth.15.4,Luc.18,20,Ephes.6.v.1, 2, proximis, Rom.13 10,Philip.2.3,1.Petri 2.17, Vxori impertiendus cap. 3.v.7. Honoris Parentibus exhibiti exempla:In Sem & Iaphet, Genesis 9.23,Iuda,43,v.8,9,Iosepho,46.29,& 50.v.1,2,Dauide,1.Sam.22.3,Salomone,1.Reg.2,19. Christo,Lucæ 2,5 Ioann.8,49,& 19,versi.26,27, Vide REVERENTIA exempla.
units.tr: Honour and its various meanings: for price and esteem, Col. 2.23; for help and every kind of service, Matt. 15.4, 5; Rom. 12.10; Eph. 6.2; 1 Tim. 5.17; 1 Pet. 2.17; for the reverence due to the magistrate, Rom. 13.7; for honest care and concern, 1 Pet. 3.7. Honour is to be given to the body, 1 Thess. 4.4. Honour due to God, Mal. 1.6; 1 Pet. 2.17. To parents, Deut. 5.16; Matt. 15.4; Luke 18.20; Eph. 6 v. 1, 2. To neighbours, Rom. 13.10; Phil. 2.3; 1 Pet. 2.17. To be bestowed on a wife, 1 Pet. 3 v. 7. Examples of honour shown to parents: in Shem and Japheth, Gen. 9.23; Judah, 43 v. 8, 9; Joseph, 46.29 and 50 v. 1, 2; David, 1 Sam. 22.3; Solomon, 1 Kings 2.19; Christ, Luke 2.51; John 8.49 and 19 v. 26, 27. See the examples under REVERENCE.

GLORIA. honorat Patrem Christus,Ioann.8.49. Honorans Deum, fidens ei,honoratur 1.Sam.2.30.Non honorans filium, non honorat Patrem Ioan.5. 23. HONORARE, pro quibuslibet charitatis officiis prosequi : 1.Pet.2.17.
units.tr: Honour for those who believe in Christ, 1 Pet. 2.7. Honour is to be given to whom it is due, Rom. 13.7. Honour that comes from men is not to be magnified, Num. 16.1; Judg. 9.1; 1 Sam. 10.27; 2 Sam. 15.1; 1 Kings 1.5; Esth. 3 v. 1, etc.; 6; Eccles. 9.16 and 10 v. 29, 30; Jer. 9.23; Matt. 6.1; 8.4; 9.30; 17.9; 20.21, 26; Mark 1.44; 5.43; 7.36; 8.2; 9.9; 10 v. 5, 43; Luke 22.24; John 6.15; Rom. 8.50; 12.43; Acts 10.16; 14.14; Gal. 6.2; Phil. 2.3; 1 Thess. 2.6; 1 Pet. 5.3; John 3 v. 9; Rev. 19.10; 22.9. See GLORY. The honour of God, see GLORY. Christ honours the Father, John 8.49. Whoever honours God and trusts in him is honoured, 1 Sam. 2.30. Whoever does not honour the Son does not honour the Father, John 5.23. To honour: to pursue with any duties of love, 1 Pet. 2.17.

units.la: HORA,pro opportunitate, Ioan.11.9.pro tempore, Marc. 11.pro momento temporis,Mat.8.13. Horæ diei duodecim Ioan.11.9.Hora Christi,2.4.& 7.30.
units.tr: Hour: for opportunity, John 11.9; for time, Mark 11; for a moment of time, Matt. 8.13. The twelve hours of the day, John 11.9. The hour of Christ, John 2.4; 7.30.

units.la: [HORA, diei ciuilis 24. particula, naturalis autem duodecima : sunt enim ( inquit Christus ) diei duodecim horæ Ioann.11.9.Porrò horarum diei & noctis meminerunt Euangelistæ,Matt.20.3,&c. Marc.15.v.25, 33. Ioann & 4.v.6,52.Act.16.33. & 22.13.
units.tr: [Hour: a part of the civil day of 24 hours, but the natural day has twelve; for, as Christ says, there are twelve hours of the day, John 11.9. The Evangelists also mention the hours of the day and night, Matt. 20.3, etc.; Mark 15 v. 25, 33; John 4 v. 6, 52; Acts 16.33; 22.13.

units.la: . Hora,breue temporis monumentum, sed indefini-tum,Iob.10,14. Dan.3.v.5.6.15, Matth.26,55, Gal.2, 5,1, hess.2,17.Philem.v.15.
units.tr: Hour: a brief measure of time, but indefinite, Job 10.14; Dan. 3 v. 5, 6, 15; Matt. 26.55; Gal. 2.5; 1 Thess. 2.17; Philem. v. 15.

units.la: . Tempus cum quadam occasione agendi vel patien-tiae liquid,Matth.10,19,&26,45, Ioann.2.4. & 12.23. & 17. Iom.13.11.
units.tr: Hour: time with some occasion for acting or suffering, Matt. 10.19; 26.45; John 2.4; 12.23; 17.1; Rom. 13.11.

units.la: . Periculum quo aliquo temporis interuallo accidit, Marc.14.35. Ioann.12.27.
units.tr: Hour: a danger that comes at some interval of time, Mark 14.35; John 12.27.

units.la: . Hora,seculum,1 Ioan.2.18.
units.tr: Hour: an age, 1 John 2.18.

units.la: . Mortis momentum & tempus, Marc.13.32. Ioan.5. & 7.30.& 8.20.& 13.1.
units.tr: Hour: the moment and time of death, Mark 13.32; John 5; 7.30; 8.20; 13.1.

units.la: . Hora plane mystica & cuius consideratio mentem sublimem superat, Act.8.1.& 11.13.]
units.tr: Hour: plainly mystical, and whose consideration surpasses the lofty mind, Acts 8.1; 11.13.]

units.la: Rex Gazer occiditur a Iosua; Iof.10.33.
units.tr: King Gezer is killed by Joshua, Josh. 10.33.

units.la: EB(id est siccus)mons Dei, qui proprie Sinai(id est ru-dicitur a visione Mosi ibi oblata,Exod.3.1.&19.2.Deu. 4.v.Vnde Deus Israelem allocutus est.4.15. Quo fugit E-lias,1.Reg.19.8.
units.tr: Horeb (that is, dry), the mountain of God, which is properly called Sinai (that is, rough) from the vision of Moses shown there, Exod. 3.1; 19.2; Deut. 4. From there God spoke to Israel, 4.15. Where Elijah fled, 1 Kings 19.8.

units.la: REA seu corbes benedicuntur obedientibus Deo,Deu. 28.5.& contra v.17. Tempore famis aperit Iosephus hor-tua:Gen.41.56.Matt.3.12.& Luc.12.16.&c.
units.tr: The threshing floor or baskets are blessed to those who obey God, Deut. 28.5, and the contrary in v. 17. In time of famine Joseph opened the granaries, Gen. 41.56. Matt. 3.12; Luke 12.16, etc.

units.la: RHAEI incolae Idumaeae expulsi a filiis Esau, Deut.2.12. RT VS mysticus,Cantic.4.v.12,15.16.& 5.1.& 6.2.10.&8. Hortus Heden:Gen.2.8.Hortus sepulchri Christi,Io. 19.41.
units.tr: RHAEI, the inhabitants of Idumaea, expelled by the sons of Esau, Deut. 2.12. HORTUS, the mystical garden, Cant. 4.12, 15, 16; 5.1; 6.2, 10; 8. The garden of Eden, Gen. 2.8. The garden of Christ's tomb, John 19.41.

units.la: ANNA, solennis erat formula acclamationis,qua vte-bantur Iudaei in festo Tabernaculorum,cum ramos gesta-rent ex Domini mandato, Leuit.23.40. & significat i-llem quod Salua,vel potius, Opitulare quaeso. Hosanna recantur turbae Christo Ierusalem ingredienti, Matt.21. Ioh.12.13.Ps.118.25.
units.tr: HOSANNA was a solemn formula of acclamation which the Jews used at the Feast of Tabernacles, when they carried branches by the Lord's command, Lev. 23.40. It signifies "Save," or rather, "Help, I beseech you." The crowds cried out Hosanna to Christ entering Jerusalem, Matt. 21; John 12.13; Ps. 118.25.

units.la: EAS Propheta quo tempore propheratit,Osea 1.1.Hosea filius Nun explorator Chanaan:Num.13.17.
units.tr: HOSEA, in whose time the prophet prophesied, Hos. 1.1. Hosea son of Nun, a spy of Canaan, Num. 13.17.

units.la: PES esse in aliqua ciuitate translatitie dicitur,qui igno-rat quod caeteri isthic norint,Luc.24.18.[Hospites,extra-nei a Deo,Ephes.2.v.12.19.]
units.tr: A STRANGER (PES) is said to be in some city by transfer when he does not know what the others there know, Luke 24.18. [Strangers and foreigners to God, Eph. 2.12, 19.]

units.la: HOSPITALITAS, φιλοξενία, Est non tantum eius peregrini, cum quo amicitia nobis contracta est, vel vinculum necessitu-dinis intercedit, sed etiam cuiuslibet ignoti,humana & benigna in nostrum tectum exceptio,conuictus,&dimissio: Qualis fuit Abrahami,Gen.18.3.& Loth.G.19.1. Heb.13.2.
units.tr: HOSPITALITY (φιλοξενία) is not only the humane and kindly reception into our home, with fellowship and sending on, of a foreigner with whom we have formed a friendship or who is bound to us by ties of kinship, but also of any unknown person. Such was the hospitality of Abraham, Gen. 18.3, and of Lot, Gen. 19.1; Heb. 13.2.

units.la: HOSPITALITAS commendatur, Deuter.10.19. Esa.58.7. Matt.25.v.35.36.37. Luc.14.13. Rom.12.13. 1. Tim.3.2. Tit.1.8. Hebr.13.2.1. Petr.4.9. Iac.1.27. Hospitalitatis exempla: Abraham Genes.18.v.3.4.5. Loth.19.2. Laban.24.31. Raguel, Exodi 2.20. Rahab. Ios.2.1. Iacob.2.25. Senex Ephratæus in Gabaa, Iudic.19.20. Vidua Sareptana, 1.Reg.17.v.10.15. Vidua Sunamitis.2, Reg.4.8. Iob, Iob.31.32. Martha, Lucæ 10.38. Zachæus, 19.6. Simon Coriarius, Acto.10.6. Lydia.16.15. Aquila & Priscilla 18.3. Philippus Euangelista, 21.8. Mnason, v.16. Publius 28.7. Gaius, Rom.16.23. Gaius, 3. Ioan. v.6. Hospitalitatis fructus, Mat.10.v.40.41. Hebr.13.2. Exemplar in Abrahamo. Genes.18.v.2.3.5.8.10. Vidua pauper-cula, 1. Reg.17.20. Sunamitidis filio, 2.Reg.4.v.13.16. Inhospitalitas, V.suo loco
units.tr: HOSPITALITY is commended in Deut. 10.19; Isa. 58.7; Matt. 25.35–37; Luke 14.13; Rom. 12.13; 1 Tim. 3.2; Titus 1.8; Heb. 13.2; 1 Pet. 4.9; James 1.27. Examples of hospitality: Abraham, Gen. 18.3–5; Lot, Gen. 19.2; Laban, Gen. 24.31; Raguel, Exod. 2.20; Rahab, Josh. 2.1; Jacob, Josh. 2.25; the old man of Ephraim in Gibeah, Judg. 19.20; the widow of Zarephath, 1 Kings 17.10–15; the Shunammite woman, 2 Kings 4.8; Job, Job 31.32; Martha, Luke 10.38; Zacchaeus, Luke 19.6; Simon the tanner, Acts 10.6; Lydia, Acts 16.15; Aquila and Priscilla, Acts 18.3; Philip the evangelist, Acts 21.8; Mnason, Acts 21.16; Publius, Acts 28.7; Gaius, Rom. 16.23; Gaius, 3 John 5–6. The fruit of hospitality: Matt. 10.40–41; Heb. 13.2. An example in Abraham: Gen. 18.2, 3, 5, 8, 10. The poor widow, 1 Kings 17.20; the Shunammite's son, 2 Kings 4.13, 16. Inhospitality: in its own place.

units.la: HOSTIA, Vide SACRIFICIVM, Hostia laudis per Christum offerenda, Hebr.13.15. Hostia munda gentium, Malac.1.11. Hostiam seipsam obtulit Christus, Hebr.7.27. Hostiæ & munera Christum significabant, 9.9. &c. Hostias reiicit Deus, vnica Christi hostia contentus, 10.5.
units.tr: SACRIFICE (HOSTIA): see SACRIFICE. A sacrifice of praise to be offered through Christ, Heb. 13.15. A pure offering from the Gentiles, Mal. 1.11. Christ offered himself as a sacrifice, Heb. 7.27. The sacrifices and gifts signified Christ, Heb. 9.9, etc. God rejects sacrifices and is content with the one sacrifice of Christ, Heb. 10.5.

units.la: [Hostia propitiatoria, Christus: Hostia typica, sub lege, hostia Spiritualis, Rom.12.1. Philip.4.18. Hebr.13.v.15.16.1.Petr.2.5.]
units.tr: [Christ is the propitiatory sacrifice. A typical sacrifice under the law; a spiritual sacrifice, Rom. 12.1; Phil. 4.18; Heb. 13.15–16; 1 Pet. 2.5.]

units.la: HOSTIS: Hostes hominis, domestici eius, Matth.10.36. Hostes Præconum verbi Dei punientur, Ierem 20.11. Hostes veritatis nihil proficiunt, Ioan.12.19. Hostium furori interdum cedendum. Exempla: Ioseph, Matt.2.14. Iesus, 12.15.&14.13. Marc.3.7. Ioann.8.59.&11.54. Paulus, Actor.9.v.24.25. &17.10. Hostibus suis vindictam retribuit Deus, Deut.32.43. Hostibus tradit Deus inobedientes, 28.25.
units.tr: ENEMY (HOSTIS): a man's enemies are his own household, Matt. 10.36. The enemies of the preachers of God's Word will be punished, Jer. 20.11. The enemies of the truth accomplish nothing, John 12.19. At times one must yield to the fury of enemies. Examples: Joseph, Matt. 2.14; Jesus, Matt. 12.15; 14.13; Mark 3.7; John 8.59; 11.54; Paul, Acts 9.24–25; 17.10. God repays vengeance on his enemies, Deut. 32.43. God hands over the disobedient to their enemies, Deut. 28.25.

units.la: [Hubertas temporalis & terrestris, Gen.41.v.26.31. Deu.12.5.&30.9. Ps.65.12. Spiritualis & cælestis, Psal.36.9.10.]
units.tr: [Temporal and earthly fertility, Gen. 41.26, 31; Deut. 12.5; 30.9; Ps. 65.12. Spiritual and heavenly, Ps. 36.9–10.]

units.la: HVMANARVM actionum tria genera constituuntur: aliæ ἠθικαί, de quibus agitur Roman.12. aliæ πολιτικαί, de quibus Rom.13. aliæ ἱερπικαί, de quibus Rom.14.& ex parte c.15.
units.tr: Three kinds of human actions are distinguished: the ethical, of which Romans 12 treats; the political, of which Romans 13 treats; and the sacred, of which Romans 14 and in part chapter 15 treat.

units.la: HVMANITAS, Est virtus, cùm quis sinceram animi benevolentiam erga homines gestu, verbis, & officiis couenientibus declarat φιλανθρωπία.
units.tr: HUMANITY (φιλανθρωπία) is a virtue by which someone declares a sincere goodwill of the mind towards people through appropriate gesture, words and kindnesses.

units.la: HVMANITAS commendatur, Deuter .25.3. Proverb. 12.10. Galat 6.2. Iac.2.13. Humanitatis exempla: Hebræi, Genes. 23.v.4.6. Rebecca 24.19. Obstetrices, Exo.1.17. Booz, Rut. 2.8. David, 1. Sam.30.v.11.12. Sobi, Machir, & Berzellai, 2 Sam.17.29. Abdias, 1. Reg.18.4. Ioiabeth, 2. Paralip.22.11. Principes Ephraim, 28.15. Abdemelech, Ier.38.9. Eunuchus Reginæ Candaces, Act.8.31. Custos carceris, 16.v.33.34. Felix, 24.23. Iulius, 27.3. Melitenses Barbari, 28.2 Rahab, Heb. 11.31. [Humanitas Dei, i. amor erga homines, Tit.3 4.]
units.tr: HUMANITY is commended in Deut. 25.3; Prov. 12.10; Gal. 6.2; James 2.13. Examples of humanity: the Hebrews, Gen. 23.4, 6; Rebekah, Gen. 24.19; the midwives, Exod. 1.17; Boaz, Ruth 2.8; David, 1 Sam. 30.11–12; Shobi, Machir and Barzillai, 2 Sam. 17.29; Obadiah, 1 Kings 18.4; Jehoiada, 2 Chron. 22.11; the leaders of Ephraim, 2 Chron. 28.15; Ebed-melech, Jer. 38.9; the eunuch of Queen Candace, Acts 8.31; the jailer, Acts 16.33–34; Felix, Acts 24.23; Julius, Acts 27.3; the barbarians of Malta, Acts 28.2; Rahab, Heb. 11.31. [The humanity of God, that is, his love towards humankind, Titus 3.4.]

units.la: HVMI cadere, quid significet ex Hebræorum idiotismo, Vide CADERE humi.
units.tr: What it means to fall to the ground (HUMI cadere) in Hebrew idiom: see FALL TO THE GROUND (CADERE humi).

units.la: HVMILIS, abiectus coram Deo, pauper spiritu, 2 Sam.6.22. Psal.10.18.& 18.28. & 34.19. &.74.21.& 102.18.& 113.7.& 138.6. Prou.29.23. Esai.57.15. Luc.1 §1. Rom.12.16.2 Cor. 7.6. Iacob.4.9.10.1. Petr.3.8. & 5 5. Humilis, tenuis, miser, afflictus & patienter ferens abiectam suam sortem coram hominibus, Iob.5.11. Psa.82.3. Esai.10.2. Amos, 2.7. Malac.2.9 2. Corinth.10,1 Humilis, profundus, Leuitic.13. v.34.20.&c.& 14.37. Humilis locus, 1. campestris, in planitie situs, Deuter.1.7.
units.tr: HUMBLE: lowly before God, poor in spirit, 2 Sam. 6.22; Ps. 10.18; 18.28; 34.19; 74.21; 102.18; 113.7; 138.6; Prov. 29.23; Isa. 57.15; Luke 1.51; Rom. 12.16; 2 Cor. 7.6; James 4.9–10; 1 Pet. 3.8; 5.5. Humble also means of meagre means, wretched, afflicted, and patiently bearing one's abject lot before people, Job 5.11; Ps. 82.3; Isa. 10.2; Amos 2.7; Mal. 2.9; 2 Cor. 10.1. Humble means low, deep, Lev. 13.34; 14.37. A humble place is one lying on the plain, set in level ground, Deut. 1.7.

units.la: Humilio, de Deo, & de homine, vario respectu dicitur.
units.tr: To humble, said of God and of a human being, is used in various respects.

units.la: 1. Humiliat Deus homines, pios affligens, probans, & tandem exaltans: impios deiiciens & perdens. 2. Homo seipsum humiliat, pius corde contrito & fideli, coram Deo, modesto coram proximis, impius, simulata mente, 3. Homo hominem humiliat, vi, dolis, variis artibus. Vir mulierem humiliat eam comprimens, Deuter.21.vers.14. & 22.24.29. Thren.5.11. Christus humiliauit seu exinanivit semetipsum, Phil.2.7.]
units.tr: 1. God humbles people, afflicting, testing and at last exalting the godly, while he casts down and destroys the wicked. 2. A person humbles himself: the godly with a contrite and faithful heart before God, and modestly before neighbours; the wicked with a feigned mind. 3. A person humbles another person by force, by deceit or by various arts. A man humbles a woman by violating her, Deut. 21.14; 22.24, 29; Lam. 5.11. Christ humbled, or emptied, himself, Phil. 2.7.

units.la: HUMILITAS, ταπεινοφροσύνη, est ea virtus, quæ animum nostrum ex serio tum priuatæ inopiæ, tum totius humanæ imbecillitatis & ταπεινώσεως sensu deiicit, ut nihil magnum & eminens ipse appetat: sed etiam in delato honore & munere suam incapacitatem apud se agnoscat, & ingenuè fateatur & deploret. Humilis est, qui neque quicquam sibi arrogat, neque alios despicit, sed eos sibi præfert: itaque minimè superior esse affectat.
units.tr: HUMILITY (ταπεινοφροσύνη) is that virtue which casts down our mind, from a serious sense both of our private poverty and of all human weakness and lowliness (ταπείνωσις), so that it does not seek anything great and eminent for itself. Rather, even when honour and office are offered, it acknowledges and freely confesses and laments its own incapacity. The humble person is one who claims nothing for himself and despises no one, but prefers others to himself, and so is far from aspiring to be superior.

units.tr: Humility softens hatred. Examples: Jacob, Gen. 33; the brothers of Joseph, Gen. 50.17–19; the tribes who built the altar, Josh. 22.21–22; Gideon, Judg. 8.2; Abigail, 1 Sam. 25.24; David, 1 Sam. 26.18–19, 21; the wise woman of Abel, 2 Sam. 20.18; the third captain of fifty, 2 Kings 1.13–14; Esther, Esther 7.2. The humble are at last exalted, Deut. 26.7, 10; Job 5.11; 22.29; Ps. 18.28; 19.8; 25.9; 34.19; 147.6; 149.4; Prov. 15.25; 18.12; 29.23; Isa. 57.15; Matt. 23.12; Luke 14.11; 18.14. Examples: Moses, shepherd of his father-in-law's sheep, Exod. 3.1; David, 1 Sam. 16.11; Ps. 78.70; Esther, Esther 2.15; the tax collector, Luke 18.14; Christ, Phil. 2.9. God is the comforter of the humble and afflicted, 2 Cor. 1.3, 7. The humility of a maidservant, in the Hebrew manner, means a lowly servant of a lowly and abject condition, Luke 1.48. [Various senses of humility: 1. A lowly, contemptible, vile condition, Gen. 29.32; Deut. 26.7; Esther 5.2; Ps. 9.14; 25.18; 31.8; Luke 1.48; Phil. 3.21. 2. Contrition, Ps. 90.3; 111. 3. Dejection, ruin, Prov. 29.23; Isa. 32.19. 4. Feigned submission of mind, Col. 2.18, 23. 5. Humility of mind, a virtue opposed to pride, Prov. 11.2; 15.33; Acts 20.19; Eph. 4.2; Phil. 2.3; 3.12; James 5.10; 1 Pet. 5.5. 6. A life vexed by various troubles, Ps. 22.22.]

units.tr: Dropsy patients are healed (see MIRACLES), Luke 14:2. Dropsy, or hydropisis, is a water-in-the-tissues condition by which the body swells.

units.tr: WINTER is the coldest part of the year, midway between autumn and spring: Gen. 8:22; Zech. 14:8; Matt. 24:20; 2 Tim. 4:21. "Thou hast made summer and winter," Ps. 74:17.

units.tr: HYMENAEUS, a false apostle and seducer, is excommunicated by Paul, 1 Tim. 1:20; his erroneous teaching, 2 Tim. 2:17. (1. A wedding song, or the god of weddings.) HYMNS are to be sung by the faithful, Eph. 5:19; Col. 3:16. Examples: see CANTICLES.

units.la: HYPOCRISIS,Est in factis fictio & alia rei demonstratio, quā sit in sese,vel(vt alii volūt) simulatio eorū quæ nō insunt, & dissimulatio eorū quæ insunt. proprie tamē dicitur de nobis ipsi maiore sanctitatem vel religione quā habeamus,externo gestu & actionibus,fingētibus ac simulātib°.
units.tr: HYPOCRISY is feigning in deeds, and a display of something other than what is really in oneself; or (as others prefer) pretending to have what is not present and concealing what is. Properly, however, it is said of us when we feign, by outward gesture and action, a greater holiness or religion than we actually have.
HYPOCRISY is to be shunned: Job 15:34; Ps. 32:2; Ps. 34:14; Prov. 11:9; Prov. 16:29-30; Prov. 23:7; Prov. 26:22; Prov. 27:6; Eccl. 1:36.

units.tr: HYPOCRITE: This word is properly said of actors who sustain some character in a play. Afterwards it began to be used also in theology, for pretenders who wish to be taken for something other than what they are, Matt. 6:1-2. Hypocrites reign by the certain counsel of God, Job 34:30. Hypocrites are detestable to God, Job 13:16; Matt. 7:22-23; Luke 9:26. Hypocrites, to whom they are like, Matt. 23:27, 33; Luke 11:44. Mixed among the good, John 2:19. How they are to be treated, Matt. 3:7; 12:34, 39; 15:7-8; 16:4; 22:18; 23:13; Luke 3:7. They are not heard by God, John 9:31. They strive to harm secretly, Ps. 12:3. They provoke the wrath of God, Job 36:13. Hypocrites are called adulterers, Matt. 12:39, where there is an allusion to the passage of Isaiah 57:3. For it is customary in Scripture to call adulterers all those who fall away from the true worship of God, among whom hypocrites must be counted foremost. The condition of hypocrites is wretched, Job 15:34; 27:8. Their confidence is empty, Jer. 7:4. What fasting is like, and how abominable it is to God, Isa. 58:3; Zech. 7:5; Matt. 6:16. Their destruction, Matt. 24:51. The custom of covering impious deeds with a show of piety, and of putting trifling observances before serious matters, Gen. 37:35; 1 Kings 21:12; Matt. 15:2, 8; 16:3; 21:27; 23:4, 23, 25; 27:6; Mark 3:4; 6:26; 7:3; 14:63; Luke 6:2; 7:39, 42; 12:56; 13:15-16; 14:3-4; 18:12; 20:7; John 5:10; 12:5; 18:28. Their nature is described, Ps. 5:10. Their prayers, Isa. 1:15; Matt. 6:5; 23:14; Mark 12:40; Luke 20:47; John 9:31. Their trembling, Isa. 33:14. Their voices, Isa. 66:5; Jer. 8:8; Ezek. 33:30; Luke 13:26-27.

units.la: HYPOSTASIS, Est cuiusque individui propria ratio & consi- stentia,id est,essentia proprietatibus & accidentibus, id est,ὑπόστασις & φύσει constans.Hæc vox legitur Heb.1.3. & 11.1. Sed vide quo sensu.
units.tr: HYPOSTASIS is the proper nature and substance of each individual thing, that is, an essence constituted by its properties and accidents, that is, constituted by hypostasis [ὑπόστασις] and nature [φύσει]. This word is read in Heb. 1:3 and 11:1. But see in what sense.

units.la: HYPOSTATICA vnio,est ea assumētis & assumptæ naturæ vnio,quâ duę naturę inuicem perfectè distinctæ, vna sunt hypostasis:1.Tim.3.16.Col.2.9.Gal.4.4. hebr.2.16. hyssopi fasciculus, Exodi 12.22.[Psalm.51.9.Ioan.19.29. heb.9.19.]
units.tr: The HYPOSTATIC union is that union of the assuming and the assumed nature by which two natures, perfectly distinct from one another, are one hypostasis: 1 Tim. 3:16; Col. 2:9; Gal. 4:4; Heb. 2:16. A bunch of hyssop, Exod. 12:22 [Ps. 51:9; John 19:29; Heb. 9:19].

Diues est, 30.43. & 36.7. Electus Dei vocatur, Psal.105.6. electionis eius causa, solus in eum gratuitus Dei amor, Malach.1.2.
