Psal.105.23. Act.7.15. Peregrinum se agnoscit, Gen 47.9. Sepulchrum eligit, atque iureiurando postero ut eum illic sepeliendum curent, obstringit, ver.31. Ephraimum & Manassen adoptat, 48.5. benedicit illis, v.20. Dexteram Ephraimo, Manassi sinistram applicat, & quare, v.13,19, de iis quæ filiis euentura erant, eos prophetic monet, 49.v.1,2, moritur, v.33, plangitur, 50.3. in Speluncâ duplici sepelitur, v.13, cum Patribus suis in terra Chanaan, v.4,7, secundùm promissionem, 47.29, & secundùm mandatum, 49.29. [Iacob, frequenter apud Prophetas patriarchæ posteros, & populum Dei in Iudæa, atque adeò totam Ecclesiam significat, Esa.49.5, Ier.30.10, Mich.3.8. Rom.11.26, Vide ISRAEL.
units.tr: JACOB (that is, holding the heel; for the name is compounded of hand and heel, Gen. 25:26, but Esau contemptuously twists the name away from its true meaning, so that it means the same as supplanter, 27:36). Son of Isaac, he is born, Gen. 25:26; buys the firstborn's right from his brother Esau, v. 33; snatches away his brother Esau's blessing, 27:22-27. He sets out for Laban, 28:5; sees a ladder in a dream, v. 12. To have Rachel he serves seven years, 29:20. He is rich, 30:43; 36:7. He is called the elect of God, Ps. 105:6. The cause of his election is solely the free love of God toward him, Mal. 1:2; Rom. 9:13. He is commanded to return to his homeland, Gen. 31:3, 13. Angels meet him, 32:1. He wrestles with an angel, v. 24; Hos. 12:4. He is named Israel, and why, Gen. 32:28; 35:10; 1 Kings 18:31. He builds an altar, Gen. 33:20; 35:7; 1 Kings 18:31-32. He tries to placate his brother, Gen. 33:11. He dwells in the land of Canaan, 37:1. He mourns his sold son, v. 34. He is revived when he learns that the son lives, 45:26-27. He goes down into Egypt, 46:3; Ps. 105:23; Acts 7:15. He acknowledges himself a stranger, Gen. 47:9. He chooses a sepulchre and binds his descendants by oath to bury him there, v. 31. He adopts Ephraim and Manasseh, 48:5, and blesses them, v. 20. He places his right hand on Ephraim and his left on Manasseh, and why, v. 13, 19. He prophetically warns his sons about what was to befall them, 49:1-2. He dies, v. 33; is mourned, 50:3; is buried in a double cave, v. 13, with his fathers in the land of Canaan, v. 4, 7, according to the promise, 47:29, and according to the command, 49:29. [Jacob, often in the Prophets, signifies the patriarch's posterity and the people of God in Judah, and indeed the whole Church: Isa. 49:5; Jer. 30:10; Mic. 3:8; Rom. 11:26. See ISRAEL.]

units.la: IACOBVS Zebedæi filius frater Ioannis à Christo vocatus Matth.4.21, Mar.1.19, Luc.5.10, occiditur, Act.12.2, à Herode.
units.tr: JAMES, son of Zebedee, brother of John, called by Christ, Matt. 4:21; Mark 1:19; Luke 5:10. He is killed by Herod, Acts 12:2.

units.la: IACOBVS Alphæi filius vocatur frater Domini, Gal.1.19. Ierosolymitanæ Ecclesiæ præest, Act.12.17. & 15.13, & 21.18.
units.tr: JAMES, son of Alphaeus, is called the brother of the Lord, Gal. 1:19. He presides over the Church of Jerusalem, Acts 12:17; 15:13; 21:18.

units.la: IACOBVS seruus Domini duodecim Tribubus dispersis scribit, ac.1.1.
units.tr: JAMES, servant of the Lord, writes to the twelve dispersed tribes, Jas. 1:1.

units.la: IACTANTIA, ἀλαζονεία, est eorū Dei donorū, quæ non habemus, simulatio & nobis à nobis ipsis facta attributio
units.tr: BOASTING, [ἀλαζονεία], is the pretence of God's gifts which we do not have, and the ascribing to ourselves, by our own doing, of

units.la: priæ gloriæ causa vel etiam eorum quæ habemus bono-
units.tr: empty glory, or even of the good things we do have,

units.la: rum insolens & maior, quàm illa sint in nobis, ob eundem
units.tr: displayed in an insolent and greater way than they are in us, for the same

units.la: finem, prædicatio & venditatio. Hos Paulus 2. Tim. 3. 4.
units.tr: purpose: proclaiming and advertising them. Paul calls such men (2 Tim. 3:4)

units.la: vocat πτυφωμένος, 1. inflatos.
units.tr: [πτυφωμένος], that is, puffed up.

units.la: IACTANTIA fugienda, Proverb. 25.6. & 27.1. & 28.25. Ier. 9. 23.1. Cor. 3.21. & 4.7. & 5.6. & 8.2. Iac. 3 14. & 4.16. Iactantiæ exempla: Pharao, Exodi 5, 2, Gaal filius Obed, Iudic. 9,28. Goliat. 1, Sam. 17.8. Absalom, 2. Sam. 15.4, Adonias, 1. Reg. 1,5, Roboam, 12, v. 10, 14, Iezabel, 19,2 Ben-adad, 20,10 Rabsaces, 2, Reg. 18,33,2, Paralip. 32,13, Esai. 36,18, Aman, Esth. 5, 11, Rex Assyriorum, Esa. 10,13, Babylon, 14,13 15, & 47, v. 7, 8, Moab, Ierem. 48, v. 29 30, Tyrus & Rex Tyri, Ezech. 27, 3, & 28,2, Pharao Rex Ægypti 29, v. 3, 9, Chaldæi, Dan. 2, 4, Nabuchodonosor, 3,15, & 4 30, Israelitæ, Amos 6,13, Edom, Abd. v. 3, Ninivitæ, Sophon. 2,15. Pharisæi & Sadducæi, Matt. 3.9, Luc. 3,8, Ioan. 8,39, Diabolus, Matt. 4,9, Luc. 4.6,7, Pseudoprophetæ, Matth. 7,22, divites Adolescens, 19, 20, Marci 10,20, Filij Zebedæi, 20;22, Marci 10, 39, Petrus & reliqui Discipuli, Matt. 26, v. 33,35, Marc. 14, v. 29,31, Luc. 22 33, Ioan. 13.37, Legisperitus, Luc. 10, 29, Pharisæus, 18, v. 10.12, Princeps, v. 21. Iudæi, Ioan. 7,27, & 8, v. 33,39,41, & 9, 28. Act. 23,12, Pilatus, Ioan. 19,10, Simon Magus, Act. 8,9, Pseudoapostoli, Galat. 6,13, Iactantiæ poena, 2, Sam. 1, v. 10, 14 15, Iactantia bona, Ierem. 9.24.
units.tr: BOASTING is to be shunned: Prov. 25:6; 27:1; 28:25; Jer. 9:23; 1 Cor. 3:21; 4:7; 5:6; 8:2; James 3:14; 4:16. Examples of boasting: Pharaoh, Exod. 5:2; Gaal son of Ebed, Judg. 9:28; Goliath, 1 Sam. 17:8; Absalom, 2 Sam. 15:4; Adonijah, 1 Kings 1:5; Rehoboam, 1 Kings 12:10, 14; Jezebel, 1 Kings 19:2; Ben-hadad, 1 Kings 20:10; Rabshakeh, 2 Kings 18:33; 2 Chron. 32:13; Isa. 36:18; Haman, Esth. 5:11; the king of the Assyrians, Isa. 10:13; Babylon, Isa. 14:13-15, and 47:7-8; Moab, Jer. 48:29-30; Tyre and the king of Tyre, Ezek. 27:3, and 28:2; Pharaoh king of Egypt, Ezek. 29:3, 9; the Chaldeans, Dan. 2:4; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3:15 and 4:30; the Israelites, Amos 6:13; Edom, Obad. 3; the Ninevites, Zeph. 2:15; Pharisees and Sadducees, Matt. 3:9; Luke 3:8; John 8:39; the devil, Matt. 4:9; Luke 4:6-7; false prophets, Matt. 7:22; the rich young man, Matt. 19:20; Mark 10:20; the sons of Zebedee, Matt. 20:22; Mark 10:39; Peter and the other disciples, Matt. 26:33, 35; Mark 14:29, 31; Luke 22:33; John 13:37; a lawyer, Luke 10:29; a Pharisee, Luke 18:10-12; a ruler, v. 21; Jews, John 7:27; 8:33, 39, 41; 9:28; Acts 23:12; Pilate, John 19:10; Simon Magus, Acts 8:9; false apostles, Gal. 6:13. The punishment of boasting, 2 Sam. 1:10, 14-15. Good boasting, Jer. 9:24.

units.la: AHAZIEL, i. visio Dei, Propheta, filius Zachariæ, Spiritu Domini afflatur, 2, Paral. 20, v. 14, 15. eius prophetia, v. 16, 17.
units.tr: AHAZIEL, i.e. "vision of God," a prophet, son of Zechariah, is moved by the Spirit of the Lord, 2 Chron. 20:14, 15. His prophecy, vv. 16, 17.

units.la: AHEL, uxor Heber: ad eius tentorium pervenit Sisara fugiens, Iudic. 4, 7, quem ipsa occidit, v. 21, factúmque suum Baraco ostendit, v. 22, eius laus, 5, 24.
units.tr: AHEL, wife of Heber: Sisera, fleeing, came to her tent, Judg. 4:7, and she killed him, v. 21, and showed Barak what she had done, v. 22. Her praise, Judg. 5:24.

units.la: AHIR, Iudex Israal, Iudic. 10, 3, eius filij, vers. 4, viginti civitates ab eodem nominatæ, ibid. eius mors & sepultura, vers. 5.
units.tr: AHIR, judge of Israel, Judg. 10:3. His sons, v. 4: twenty cities named after him, ibid. His death and burial, v. 5.

units.la: AIRUS: princeps Synagogæ, Christum pro filia iam iam moritura precatur. Marci 5, v. 22, 23, Luc. 8 v. 41, 42, eius ædes adiit Christus, filiámque mortuam excitat, Matt. 9, 25, Marc. 5, 41, Luc. 8. v. 51, &c.
units.tr: JAIRUS, ruler of the synagogue, begs Christ on behalf of his daughter, who is now at the point of death, Mark 5:22, 23; Luke 8:41, 42. Christ went to his house and raised the dead girl, Matt. 9:25; Mark 5:41; Luke 8:51, etc.

units.la: ANITORES Templi Hierosolymitani constituuntur, 1. Paral. 16, v. 38, 42, & 26, 1, 2, Paral. 35, 36.
units.tr: The gatekeepers of the Temple at Jerusalem are appointed, 1 Chron. 16:38, 42; 26:1, 2; 2 Chron. 35, 36.

units.la: ANNES & Iambres impostores, Mosi resistunt, 2. Timoth. 3. 8. Exod. 7. 11.
units.tr: JANNES and JAMBRES, impostors, resist Moses, 2 Tim. 3:8; Exod. 7:11.

units.la: APHETH filius Noe, Genes. 9. 18. benedicitur à patre, v. 27. eius filij, c. 10. 2. 1. Chron. 5.
units.tr: JAPHETH, son of Noah, Gen. 9:18, is blessed by his father, v. 27. His sons, Gen. 10:2; 1 Chron. 1:5.

units.la: IASON Thessalonicus : eius domus hospitium Ecclesiæ, à circumforaneis obsidetur, Act.17.5. falsò læsæ maiestatis accusatur, v.7. eo nomine multam solui, v.9.
units.tr: JASON of Thessalonica: his house was the lodging of the Church; it was besieged by the rabble, Acts 17:5. He was falsely accused of treason, v. 7, and on that charge paid a fine, v. 9.

units.la: IAVAN filius Iapheth, Gen.10.2. ab eo oriundi Iones seu Græci, eius nomine appellantur, Ezech.27.13.
units.tr: JAVAN, son of Japheth, Gen. 10:2. From him descended the Ionians, or Greeks, and they are named after him, Ezek. 27:13.

units.la: IBIS. ea vesci Iudæis non licebat, Leuitici 11. v.3.17. Deut.14.16. [Partus ibicum incognitus, Iob.39.4.]
units.tr: IBEX. Jews were not permitted to eat it, Lev. 11:3, 17; Deut. 14:16. [The birth of the wild goats is unknown, Job 39:4.]

units.la: ICHABOD, Phinees posthumus nascitur, 1 Sam.4.20. eius nominis ratio, v.21.22. fig. vbi gloria? aut væ gloriæ.
units.tr: ICHABOD: Phinehas's posthumous son is born, 1 Sam. 4:20. The reason for the name, vv. 21, 22. Figuratively: "Where is the glory?" or "Woe to the glory."

units.la: ICONIVM ciuitas Pisidiæ, in qua Paulus prædicat Euangelium, Act.14.1. (v.c.13.14.51.
units.tr: ICONIUM, a city of Pisidia, where Paul preached the gospel, Acts 14:1 (cf. vv. 13, 14, 51).

units.la: IDIOMATVM communicatio. Vide CHRISTVS.
units.tr: COMMUNICATION OF PROPERTIES. See CHRIST.

units.la: IDIOTAE: Hoc Græco epitheto proprie significantur homines plebeij, viles, & ex medio vulgo homines, quos alij ὁι τυχόντας vocant. Iam verò, quia eiusmodi homines fere indocti sunt, & rerum imperiti, nec ita liberaliter educati, idcirco factum est, vt idiotæ dicantur qui rudes sunt, & minimè ingeniosi, aut intelligentes, Act.4.13. vide 2 Cor.11.6. Vocantur autem idiotæ in Ecclesia Dei, 1.Cor 14.16. ipsi priuati homines, vt iis opponantur, qui ministrabant: Laicos postea illos vocarunt, quibus oppositi sunt Ecclesiastici; vnde, tyrannide Ecclesiam inuadente exortus est tandem maximus abusus.
units.tr: IDIOTS: By this Greek epithet are properly meant common, base people, drawn from the ordinary crowd, whom others call [ὁι τυχόντας]. Now, because people of this kind are for the most part unlearned, inexperienced in affairs, and not liberally educated, it came about that those who are rude and not at all clever or intelligent are called idiots, Acts 4:13; see 2 Cor. 11:6. In the Church of God, however, those are called idiots, 1 Cor. 14:16, who are simply private persons, set over against those who ministered. Later they were called laymen, and the clergy were set over against them. Hence, when tyranny invaded the Church, the greatest abuse eventually arose.

units.la: IDOLVM: Idolum non faciendum, Leuit.26.1. Idola fugienda, 19.4. Deuteron.18.9. vnde traxerint originem Sap.14.15. Idola quàm noxia, Ierem.10.8. abiicenda sunt & conterenda, Genes.35.2. Exod.23.24. & 34.13. Numer.33.52. Deut.7.5. & 12.3. Ios.24.23. 1.Sam.7.3. Esaiæ 2.18. & 27.9. & 30.22. & 31.7. Mich.1.7. & 5.13. Zachar.13.2. Idolorum abolitionis exempla: A Iacobo, Genes.35.4. Moses, Exod.32.20. Gedeone, Iudic.6.v.25.26. Israelitis 10.16. 1.Sam.7.4. Asa, 1.Reg.15.v.12.13. Iosaphat.2. Paral.17.6. Elia, 1.Reg.18.40. Ioram, 2.Reg.3.v.1.2. Iehu, 10.v.26.27.28. Populo, 11.18. Ezechia, 18.4. Iosia, 23.v.14.15.2. Paralip.24.v.4.5. Dauide, 1.Paral.14.12. Asa, 2.Paral.15.v.8.16. populo Iudaico sub Ioa, 23.17. populo sub Ezechia, 30.14 & 31.1. Manasse, 33.15. Iosia 34.v.4.33. Ieremia. Ierem 51.52.
units.tr: IDOL: No idol is to be made, Lev. 26:1. Idols are to be shunned, Lev. 19:4; Deut. 18:9. Whence they derived their origin, Wis. 14:15. How harmful idols are, Jer. 10:8. They are to be cast off and broken, Gen. 35:2; Exod. 23:24; 34:13; Num. 33:52; Deut. 7:5; 12:3; Josh. 24:23; 1 Sam. 7:3; Isa. 2:18; 27:9; 30:22; 31:7; Mic. 1:7; 5:13; Zech. 13:2. Examples of the abolition of idols: by Jacob, Gen. 35:4; by Moses, Exod. 32:20; by Gideon, Judg. 6:25, 26; by the Israelites, Judg. 10:16; 1 Sam. 7:4; by Asa, 1 Kings 15:12, 13; by Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 17:6; by Elijah, 1 Kings 18:40; by Joram, 2 Kings 3:1, 2; by Jehu, 10:26, 27, 28; by the people, 11:18; by Hezekiah, 18:4; by Josiah, 23:14, 15; 2 Chron. 24:4, 5; by David, 1 Chron. 14:12; by Asa, 2 Chron. 15:8, 16; by the Jewish people under Joash, 2 Kings 23:17; by the people under Hezekiah, 2 Chron. 30:14; 31:1; by Manasseh, 33:15; by Josiah, 34:4, 33; by Jeremiah, Jer. 51:52.

units.la: IDOLORVM fabricatio ridicula, Esa.40.19. & 44.12. & 46.7. Ierem.10.3. Idolum mendacij magister, v.8. Abac.2.18. dolorum nomina abominabilia, Psal.16.4. Idolorum vanitas, 2.Reg.19.18. Psalm.115.4. & 135.15. Esa.37.19. & 41. v.21. 23.29. & 23.29.& 44.v.9.10.& 46.v.1.7.Ierem.2,28. & 10. v. 5.11.15. &11.12.&51.v.17.18.47.Daniel.5.23.Ose.14.Abac.2.v.18.19. Zach.10.2.1,Cor.8.4.& 10.19.Apocal.9.20.Idolum nihil, hoc est,inane & vanum somnium dicitur,1.Cor.8.4. Neque enim idola ex materia æstimantur,sed tum ex forma, quę res veras mentitur,tum ex inani eorum imaginatione, qui de idolo sibi aliquid non modò reale, sed etiam diuinum propter effictam formam animo concipiunt: Vnde & à vanitate denominantur Hebręis idola,eò quòd nihil sunt,1.Cor.8.4. Idoli conscientiam quid vocet Paulus,V. CONSCIENTIAM idoli, &c.
units.tr: The making of idols is ridiculous, Isa. 40:19; 44:12; 46:7; Jer. 10:3. The idol is a teacher of lies, v. 8; Hab. 2:18. The names of idols are abominable, Ps. 16:4. The vanity of idols, 2 Kings 19:18; Ps. 115:4; 135:15; Isa. 37:19; 41:21, 23, 29; 44:9, 10; 46:1, 7; Jer. 2:28; 10:5, 11, 15; 11:12; 51:17, 18, 47; Dan. 5:23; Hos. 14; Hab. 2:18, 19; Zech. 10:2; 1 Cor. 8:4; 10:19; Rev. 9:20. An idol is called "nothing," that is, an empty and vain phantom, 1 Cor. 8:4. For idols are not valued for their material, but both for their form, which misrepresents true things, and for the empty imagination of those who conceive in their minds of the idol not only something real but even something divine, on account of the shape it has been fashioned into. Hence the Hebrews also call idols by a name derived from vanity, because they are nothing, 1 Cor. 8:4. For what Paul calls "the conscience of an idol," see CONSCIENCE OF AN IDOL, etc.

units.la: DOLORVM catalogus,quorum mentio fit in sacris literis: I. Adonis,Vide Thammuz. II. Adramelech idolum Sepharuaim,speciem habens Pauonis,aut Muli, 2. Regum 17.31. III. Asdod, idolum Philistinorum, Vide Dagon. IV. Anamelech, equus aut phasianus, idolum incolarum Sepharuaim,2.Reg.17.31. V. Arza, idolum quod coluit Rex Ela domi suæ, 1. Reg. 16.9. VI. Asima,hircus syluestris, idolum Hemathæorum, 2. Reg.17.30. VII. Astaroth, idolum, seu Dea Sidoniorum, effigiem habens ouis,1.Sam.31.10.1,Reg.11.5. VIII. Baal, idolum commune,Iudic.6.25.1.Reg.16.v.31.32. & 18.21. &c. IX. Baalberith,idolum Sichimitarum,Iudic.9.4. X. Baalpeor,velBaalphegor,idolum Moabitarum,in quo præuaricati sunt Israelitæ,Num.25 v.3.5. Hieronymus ait Priapū fuisse. XI. Baalzebub, idolum Accaronitarum vel Ecronitarum,2.Reg.1.2. XII. Baalzephon, idolum Aegyptiorum: cui hanc vim attribuebant, quòd seruos fugitiuos obseruaret,& retineret, XIII. Bacchus,seu Liber. idolum 2.Machab.6.7. XIV. Bel, idolum Babyloniæ, Esai. 46.1. XV. Chamos velChemolch idolum Amorrhęorum,Ammonitarum,& Moabitarum,aliasBaalpeor dictum,Num.25. 29.Iudic.11.24.1.Reg.11.v.5.7.33.2.Reg.23.13. Ierem.48.v. 7.13. XVI. Canopus,idolum Aegyptiorum. Vide Historiam Ecclesiasticam,libro 11.capite 26. XVI. Chiun,idolum Israelitarum, quod alij Sydus, alij Saturnum interpretantur, Amos 5.26. XVII.Dagon,idolum Philistinorum,piscis formam inferne,superne autem formosæ mulieris referens, Iudic.16.23.1.Samuel.5.3.XVIII.Dianæ, Templi & cultus mentio fit 2.Machab.1. v.13.15. & vocatur ibidem Nanæa, [vide Act.19.v.34.35.] XIX. Draco,idolum Babyloniorum. XX. Ephod Gedeonis, fuit idololatria à Ge-
units.tr: CATALOGUE OF THE IDOLS mentioned in the sacred writings: I. Adonis; see Thammuz. II. Adramelech, the idol of Sepharvaim, having the form of a peacock or a mule, 2 Kings 17:31. III. Asdod, the idol of the Philistines; see Dagon. IV. Anamelech, a horse or a pheasant, the idol of the inhabitants of Sepharvaim, 2 Kings 17:31. V. Arza, the idol which King Elah worshipped in his house, 1 Kings 16:9. VI. Asima, a wild goat, the idol of the Hamathites, 2 Kings 17:30. VII. Astaroth, the idol or goddess of the Sidonians, having the image of a sheep, 1 Sam. 31:10; 1 Kings 11:5. VIII. Baal, the common idol, Judges 6:25; 1 Kings 16:31–32 and 18:21, etc. IX. Baalberith, the idol of the Shechemites, Judges 9:4. X. Baalpeor, or Baalphegor, the idol of the Moabites, in whose worship the Israelites committed whoredom, Num. 25:3, 5. Jerome says it was Priapus. XI. Baalzebub, the idol of the Accaronites or Ekronites, 2 Kings 1:2. XII. Baalzephon, the idol of the Egyptians, to which they ascribed the power of watching over and holding back runaway slaves. XIII. Bacchus, or Liber, an idol, 2 Maccabees 6:7. XIV. Bel, the idol of Babylon, Isaiah 46:1. XV. Chamos or Chemosh, the idol of the Amorites, Ammonites and Moabites, otherwise called Baalpeor, Num. 25:29; Judges 11:24; 1 Kings 11:5, 7, 33; 2 Kings 23:13; Jer. 48:7, 13. XVI. Canopus, the idol of the Egyptians; see the Ecclesiastical History, book 11, chapter 26. XVI. Chiun, the idol of the Israelites, which some interpret as a star, others as Saturn, Amos 5:26. XVII. Dagon, the idol of the Philistines, with the form of a fish below and that of a beautiful woman above, Judges 16:23; 1 Sam. 5:3. XVIII. Diana: mention is made of her temple and worship in 2 Maccabees 1:13, 15, where she is called Nanaea; [see Acts 19:34–35]. XIX. Draco, the idol of the Babylonians. XX. The Ephod of Gideon: this idolatry was instituted by Gideon against the word of God in his native Ophrah, with good intentions, but it proved a stumbling block to the whole people of Israel, Judges 8:27.

units.la: X deone instituta, contra Dei verbum, in patria sua Ophra, bona quidem intentione, sed quæ toti populo Israel offendiculum præbuit, Iudicum 8.27.xxi. Efch, idolum in πυρσίῳ, id est, Templo ignis, quod à Persis colebatur. Vide Tripartitam Historiam, libro 10. cap. 30. xxii. Fortuna, vide Gad.
units.tr: XXI. Efch, an idol in a pyreion [πυρσίῳ], that is, a temple of fire, which was worshipped by the Persians; see the Tripartite History, book 10, chapter 30. XXII. Fortuna; see Gad.

units.la: xxiii. Gad, idolum fuit militare, quod alij Martem, alij Iouem, alij Fortunam, alij exercitum cœli, aut numeros interpretabantur, Esai.65.11, xxiv. Herculi sacrificatum est à Tyriis, 2. Mach, 4.19. xxv. Iupiter Olympius, 6. 2. Vide Gad. xxvi. Iupiter Xenius, Deus gentilium, 2. Mach.6.2. xxvii.
units.tr: XXIII. Gad, a military idol, which some interpreted as Mars, others as Jupiter, others as Fortune, others as the host of heaven or the number of stars, Isaiah 65:11. XXIV. Sacrifice was offered to Hercules by the Tyrians, 2 Maccabees 4:19. XXV. Jupiter Olympius, 2 Maccabees 6:2; see Gad. XXVI. Jupiter Xenius, a god of the Gentiles, 2 Maccabees 6:2. XXVII.

units.la: Mulchom, Amos 5.26. qui & Molech, Leuit.18.21. & 20. v. 2.3.2.Reg.23.10. & Milchom, 1.Reg.11. v.5.33. 2.Reg.23.13. idolum Ammonitarum. xxix. Meni, idolum fuit Mercatorum, quod alij Mercurium, alij Fatum, alij Planetas, aut numerum stellarum interpretantur, Esa.65.11. xxix. Micha idolum in domo Micha, in monte Ephraim, in quo etiam multi ex Israel impegerunt, Iudic. 17.5. xxx. Miphlezeth (quod alij in genere idolum, alij terriculamentum, alij Priapum, alij horrendam statuam interpretantur) erat idolum Maacha, matris Asa, 1.Reg.15.13. xxxi. Nabaam, idem quod Nibchaz, idolum Heuçorum, 2.Reg 17.31. xxxii. Nanæa Templi & cultus mentio fit 2.Machab 1.v,13.15. quæ putatur esse Diana. xxxiii. Nebo, idolum Babylonicum, Esai.46.1. xxxiv. Nehushtan (id est, nihilum in diminutiua forma) idolum serpentis æneï, commi nutum ab Ezechia, 2.Reg.18.4. xxxv. Nergal, gallina sylvestris, idolum Cuthæorum, 2.Reg.17.30. xxxvi. Orimasda, idem quod infrà Vr chasdim, id est, ignis sacer. xxxvii. * Rimmon, idolum Siriacum, 2.Reg.5.18. xxxix. Remphan idolum sideris cuiusdam, de quo Stephanus mentionem facit, Actor.7.43. xxxix. Suchot-Benoth, idolum Babyloni cum, 2.Reg.17.30. xl. Sichuth, idolum Israelitarum, Amo 5.26. xli. Thartak, idolum Heuæorum, 2.Reg.17.31. xlii Thammuz, idolum populi Israelitici, quod alij Adonim, alij Bacchum interpretantur, Ezech. 8. 14. xliii Theraphim, idola quæ solebant sciscitantibus responsa dare, Gen.31.34. Ose. 3. 4. xliv. Vitulus aureus in deserto idolum Israelitarum, Exod 32. 4. xlv. Vitulus aureus in Dan, idolum Israelitarum à Ieroboamo institutum, 1.Reg.12.v.28.29. xlvi. Vitulus aureus in Bethel, idolum
units.tr: Mulchom, Amos 5:26; also called Molech, Lev. 18:21; 20:2, 3; 2 Kings 23:10, and Milcom, 1 Kings 11:5, 33; 2 Kings 23:13, an idol of the Ammonites. XXVIII. Meni, an idol of merchants, which some interpret as Mercury, others as Fate, others as the planets or the number of the stars, Isa. 65:11. XXIX. Micah, an idol in the house of Micah, on Mount Ephraim, at which many of Israel also stumbled, Judg. 17:5. XXX. Miphlezeth (which some interpret as an idol in general, others as a bugbear, others as Priapus, others as a dreadful statue) was an idol of Maacah, mother of Asa, 1 Kings 15:13. XXXI. Nabaam, the same as Nibhaz, an idol of the Avites, 2 Kings 17:31. XXXII. Nanaea, mention is made of her temple and worship in 2 Macc. 1:13, 15; she is thought to be Diana. XXXIII. Nebo, a Babylonian idol, Isa. 46:1. XXXIV. Nehushtan (that is, "a little nothing," in diminutive form), the idol of the bronze serpent, broken in pieces by Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18:4. XXXV. Nergal, a wild hen, an idol of the Cuthites, 2 Kings 17:30. XXXVI. Orimasda, the same as Ur-chasdim below, that is, sacred fire. XXXVII. * Rimmon, a Syrian idol, 2 Kings 5:18. XXXVIII. units.la: corporale, est abstinere à ciborum ordinaria pastione & comestione, in eum finem, vt ardentius Deum precemur & pœniteamus facilius. Quid prodest (inquit Hierony.) renuari abstinentia corpus, si animus intumescit superbia? quid virtutis habet vinum non bibere, & ira atque iracundia inebriari? Tunc inquam præclara est abstinentia, tunc pulchra corporis castigatio, cum est animus ieiunus à vitiis. cuiusmodi ieiunium perpetuū esse debet. Fines. I. vt lasciuiens caro fame veluti dometur. 1. Cor. 9. 25 26. 27. II. vt ad preces serio cordis affectu cōcipiendas nos ipsos præparemus: Luc. 2. 37. Act. 13. 2. & 14. 23. 1. Cor. 7. 5. III. vt nos totos cum vero animi dolore coram Deo abiiciamus & humiliemus. IIII. Dt testimoniis etiam externis tum nos ipsos, tum alios ad resipiscentiam acuamus. Ioel, 2. 14. 15. 1. Sam. 7. 5. 6.
units.tr: Bodily fasting is abstaining from the ordinary feeding and eating of food, to this end: that we may pray to God more fervently and repent more readily. What does it profit (says Jerome) to weaken the body by abstinence if the mind swells with pride? What virtue is there in not drinking wine, if one is drunk with anger and wrath? Then, I say, abstinence is excellent and the discipline of the body is fine, when the mind is fasting from vices. Such a fast ought to be perpetual. Its ends are: (1) that the wanton flesh may be tamed, as it were, by hunger, 1 Cor. 9.25.26.27; (2) that we may prepare ourselves to conceive prayers with a serious affection of heart, Luke 2.37; Acts 13.2; 14.23; 1 Cor. 7.5; (3) that we may cast down and humble ourselves completely before God with true grief of mind; (4) that by external testimonies we may stir up both ourselves and others to repentance, Joel 2.14, 15; 1 Sam. 7.5, 6.

units.la: Ieiunū miraculosū est, quo prorsus ieiunatur ab omni victu, vltra naturæ cursum & humanarū viriū potentiam: quale fuit Mosis, Eliæ, & Christi. Ex quo perperā pōtificij suū Quadragesimale ieiunij desumūt: Quia actiones miraculosæ nō proponūtur nobis imitandæ. Quia nemo sanus per se (testibus medicis) ad noue dies vitam sine cibo protrahere potest. Quia nihil illi comederunt, hi vero à quibusdam cibis vulgaribus abstinent, & delicatioribus sese farciūt. Quia quod illi semel, Spiritu Dei duce, in banū finem fecerunt;Isti quotannis,sine Dei præcepto,ac vt vitam æternā mereantur. Lomb.l.4.Scot.Dist.15. Quia isti non mediocrem quæstum faciunt ex sua ciborū dispensa-tione.Quia libertatem Christianam nouis dæmoniorum doctrinis circunscribunt.1.Tim.4.1.c.Vide Gen, 9.3. Mat. 15.11.Rom.14,3.1.Cor.8.8.& 10.25.Col.2.16.&c.Tit.1.15.
units.tr: Miraculous fasting is that by which one abstains entirely from all food, beyond the course of nature and the power of human strength, such as the fasts of Moses, Elijah, and Christ. From this the Papists wrongly derive their Quadragesimal fast, because miraculous actions are not set before us for imitation. Because no one healthy (by the testimony of physicians) can prolong life for many days without food. Because those men ate nothing, whereas these abstain from certain common foods and stuff themselves with delicacies. Because what they did once, led by the Spirit of God, for a good end, these do every year, without God's command, and so that they may merit eternal life (Lombard, bk. 4; Scotus, Dist. 15). Because these make no small profit from their dispensing of foods. Because they confine Christian liberty with new doctrines of demons, 1 Tim. 4.1. See Gen. 9.3; Matt. 15.11; Rom. 14.3; 1 Cor. 8.8; 10.25; Col. 2.16, etc.; Titus 1.15.

units.tr: No fasting apart from works of mercy, Zech. 7.5. The apostles are rebuked because they do not fast, Matt. 9.14. How fasting is to be done, Matt. 6.17. One must not set one's own fasting before God, Isa. 58.3. What kind of fast God desires, v. 6. David humbles himself by fasting, Ps. 35.13. A demon is cast out by fasting and prayer, Matt. 17.21.

units.la: Ieiuniorum indictorum exempla:à Saule,1,Sam.14.24.à Iosaphat.2.paral.20,3,à Niniuitis & eorum Rege, Ionæ 3, v.5,7,ab Esdra,1.Esdr.8.21.ab Esther & Mardochæo , Esth. 4.16.ABSTINENTIA.
units.tr: Examples of fasts appointed: by Saul, 1 Sam. 14.24; by Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 20.3; by the Ninevites and their king, Jonah 3.5, 7; by Ezra, Ezra 8.21; by Esther and Mordecai, Esth. 4.16. ABSTINENCE.

units.la: [IEIVNANDVM esse his dictis probant ηπαλοι αηπαλοι Pontificij, Ioel.2.12. Matt.6,16. Mar.2.20. Luc.2.36, &5.35. Rom.13.13. 1.Cor.7,5.2. Cor.6.5. &11.27. Act.13.v.2,3. 14.22. Eph.5.18.1. Thess.5.6. Tit.2.2.1. Pet.1.13. &5.8.]
units.tr: [The Papists, ēpaloi apaloi [ηπαλοι αηπαλοι], prove by these passages that fasting must be observed: Joel 2.12; Matt. 6.16; Mark 2.20; Luke 2.36 and 5.35; Rom. 13.13; 1 Cor. 7.5; 2 Cor. 6.5 and 11.27; Acts 13.2-3; 14.22; Eph. 5.18; 1 Thess. 5.6; Titus 2.2; 1 Pet. 1.13 and 5.8.]

units.la: [IEPHTE Galaadita ex adulterio natus, Iudic.11.1. à fratribus eiicitur, v.2. latronum, & inopum dux, miseram vitam sequitur, v.3. vocatur ad exercitus Israelitici imperatoris munus, v.5,6, temerarium eius votum, v.30, vincit Ammonitas, v.33. vlciscitur Ephraimitarum iniuriam, 12.4. moritur, v.7, (i. Aperiens.)]
units.tr: [Jephthah the Gileadite, born of an adulteress, Judg. 11.1. He is cast out by his brothers, v. 2. He becomes leader of robbers and the destitute and leads a wretched life, v. 3. He is called to the office of commander of the army of Israel, vv. 5-6. His rash vow, v. 30. He defeats the Ammonites, v. 33. He avenges the injury done by the Ephraimites, 12.4. He dies, v. 7. (i.e. Opening.)]

units.la: [IEREMIAS i. exaltatus à Domino, fidus Dei propheta, 2. Paral.36.12. ex Anahoth, Ier 29.27. tempus prophetiae eius, 1.2. vocaturad propheticum munus, v.5. orare pro populo prohibetur, 11.14. &14.11. eius maluetudo, 11.19. pugna cum rebelli populo. 15.v.20. sinceritas, 17.16. ob annuntiatum Dei verbum indigna multa sustinet, 18.19. &20.2. &26.8. &27.2. &33.1. &37.12. &38.v.4 7. idque animo constantissimo. 27.v.3 4. 7. 8. nec tamen a praedicando verbo abstinet, 37.v.9. diei natiuitatis suae maledicit, 20.14. Epistolam ad Israelitas in Babyloniam deportatos scribit, 29.1. iterum indigne tractatur in carcerem detrusus, 32.2.&37.v.12.14. &38.6. capta ciuitate, Regis Babylonij iussu conseruatur, 39.v.11.12. optio eundi cum ciuib. suis in exilium, vel domi manendi, illi conceditur, 40.4. mendacij falso accusatur, 43.2.]
units.tr: [Jeremiah, the son of Hilkiah, exalted by the Lord, a faithful prophet of God, 2 Chron. 36.12. From Anathoth, Jer. 29.27. The time of his prophecy, 1.2. He is called to the prophetic office, v. 5. He is forbidden to pray for the people, 11.14 and 14.11. His weakness, 11.19. He struggles with the rebellious people, 15.20. His sincerity, 17.16. Because he announced the word of God he endures many indignities, 18.19; 20.2; 26.8; 27.2; 33.1; 37.12; 38.4-7, and this with a most steadfast mind, 27.3-4, 7-8. Yet he does not refrain from preaching the word, 37.9. He curses the day of his birth, 20.14. He writes a letter to the Israelites carried off into Babylon, 29.1. Again he is shamefully treated and thrust into prison, 32.2; 37.12-14; 38.6. When the city is taken, he is preserved by the command of the king of Babylon, 39.11-12. He is granted the choice of going into exile with his fellow citizens or remaining at home, 40.4. He is falsely accused of lying, 43.2.]

units.la: Ieremias Sacerdos, Nehem.12.1. Ieremias, pro Zacharia, per abbreuiationem literarum, Matt.27.9.
units.tr: Jeremiah the priest, Neh. 12.1. Jeremiah, put for Zechariah by an abbreviation of letters, Matt. 27.9.

units.la: [IERICHO (i. luna, vel mensis, vel decor eius,) ciuitas in Tribu Beniamin, Num.22.1. dicta est & ciuitas palmarum, Deu.34.3,2. Par.28.15. capitur, Iosue 6.20. eam instauraturo maledicit, Iosua, v.26. ab Hiele instauratur, 1.Reg.16.34.]
units.tr: [Jericho (i.e. moon, or month, or its beauty), a city in the tribe of Benjamin, Num. 22.1. It is also called the city of palms, Deut. 34.3; 2 Chron. 28.15. It is taken, Josh. 6.20. Joshua curses the one who would rebuild it, Josh. v. 26. It is rebuilt by Hiel, 1 Kings 16.34.]

units.la: [IEROBAAL quare vocatus Gedeon, Iudic.6.32. V. Gedeon.]
units.tr: [Jerubbaal, why he is called Gideon, Judg. 6.32. See Gideon.]

units.la: [IEROBOAM, (i. diiudicans populum) filius Nabat, in Salomonem insurgit, 1.Reg.11.26. 2.Paral.13.6. in AEgyptum fugit, 1.Reg.11.40. hinc reuertitur, 12.2.3.2. Paral.10.2. à populo super Israel, seu decem Tribus Rex constituitur, 1.Reg.12.20. iuxta verbum Ahiae, 11,29. &c. Vitulos aureos conflat, 12.28. Aaronitas Sacerdotes eiicit, 2. Paral.11.14. & 13.9. pro arbitrio alios constituit, 11.15. eius manus exaresçit, & quare, 1.Reg.13.4. percussus à Deo moritur, 14.20. 2.Paral.13.20. eius domus maledicta, 1.Reg.14.10. omnino deletur, 15,29.]
units.tr: [Jeroboam (i.e. judging the people), son of Nebat, rises against Solomon, 1 Kings 11.26; 2 Chron. 13.6. He flees into Egypt, 1 Kings 11.40. He returns from there, 12.2-3; 2 Chron. 10.2. He is made king over Israel, or the ten tribes, by the people, 1 Kings 12.20, according to the word of Ahijah, 11.29, etc. He casts molten golden calves, 12.28. He casts out the Aaronite priests, 2 Chron. 11.14 and 13.9. He appoints others at his own pleasure, 11.15. His hand withers, and why, 1 Kings 13.4. Struck down by God, he dies, 14.20; 2 Chron. 13.20. His house is cursed, 1 Kings 14.10. It is utterly destroyed, 15.29.]

units.la: IEROBOAM secundus filius Ioas, regis Israel regnat, 2. Reg. 13.13. moritur, 14.29.
units.tr: Jeroboam the second, son of Joash, king of Israel, reigns, 2 Kings 13.13. He dies, 14.29.

units.la: IERVSA mater Iothan, regis Iuda, 2 Reg. 15.33. 2. Paral. 27.1.
units.tr: Jerusha, mother of Jotham, king of Judah, 2 Kings 15.33; 2 Chron. 27.1.

units.la: IERVSALEM, metropolis Iudææ, quæ & Iebus, Ios. 18.28. Iudic. 19.10.1. Paral. 11.4. & Salem, Genef. 14.18 V. Sion. Psalm. 76.3. à filiis Iuda capitur, Iudic. 1.8. quæ Tribus Iacob eam inhabitauerint, 1 Paral. 9.3. Nehem 11.1. eligitur à Deo in habitaculum, 1 Reg. 8.1. &c. 2 Paral 6.2. & 7. 16. Ciuitas sancta dicitur, Matth. 4.5. & 27.53. Ciuitas Regis magni, 5.35. Vallis visionis, Esa. 22.1. Ciuitas sanguinis, Ezech. 22.v.2.3. & 24.v.6.9. Seruorum Dei interfectrix, Matth. 23.37. Luc. 13.v.33.34. idolis dedita est, Ezech. 23.11. ob id Meretrix dicitur, Esa. 1.21. obsidetur à Rasin & Phaceę, 7.1. à Nabuchodonosore, 2. Reg. 24.10. &c Ierem. 32.2. & 39.v.1.3. & 52.4. eius excidium prædicitur, Esaiæ. 22. 1. & 29.1. Ierem. 6.1. & 9.11. & 19.3. & 21 6. & 32.29. & 34. v.2.22. & 35.17. & 37.7. & 38.3. Ezech. 15.6. Mich. 3.12. eius excidij causa, Ezech. 15 8. capitur, & ciues eius in Babyloniam deportantur, 2 Regum 24.14. & 25.ver. 8.11. vastatur ab hostibus, Psalmo 79.1. eius instauratio prædicitur, Ierem. 31.38. zach. 1.16. reædificatur, Nehem. 4.17. iterum destruenda prædicitur, Daniel. 9 26. zachar. 14.1. Matth. 24.verf. 1.2. Lucæ. 13.35. & 19.v.43.44. & 20.19. & 21.6. & 23.28. Ioann. 11.48. quod impletum fuit. V. Iosephum.
units.tr: Jerusalem, the metropolis of Judea, which is also Jebus, Josh. 18.28; Judg. 19.10; 1 Chron. 11.4, and Salem, Gen. 14.18. See Zion, Ps. 76.3. It is taken by the sons of Judah, Judg. 1.8. The tribes of Jacob inhabited it, 1 Chron. 9.3; Neh. 11.1. It is chosen by God as a dwelling place, 1 Kings 8.1, etc.; 2 Chron. 6.2 and 7.16. It is called the holy city, Matt. 4.5 and 27.53; the city of the great King, Matt. 5.35; the valley of vision, Isa. 22.1; the city of blood, Ezek. 22.2-3 and 24.6, 9; the killer of God's servants, Matt. 23.37; Luke 13.33-34. It is given over to idols, Ezek. 23.11. For this reason it is called a harlot, Isa. 1.21. It is besieged by Rezin and Pekah, Isa. 7.1; by Nebuchadnezzar, 2 Kings 24.10, etc.; Jer. 32.2; 39.1, 3; 52.4. Its destruction is foretold, Isa. 22.1 and 29.1; Jer. 6.1; 9.11; 19.3; 21.6; 32.29; 34.2, 22; 35.17; 37.7; 38.3; Ezek. 15.6; Mic. 3.12. The cause of its destruction, Ezek. 15.8. It is taken, and its citizens are carried off into Babylon, 2 Kings 24.14 and 25.8, 11. It is laid waste by enemies, Ps. 79.1. Its restoration is foretold, Jer. 31.38; Zech. 1.16. It is rebuilt, Neh. 4.17. Its destruction again is foretold, Dan. 9.26; Zech. 14.1; Matt. 24.1-2; Luke 13.35; 19.43-44; 20.19; 21.6; 23.28; John 11.48. This was fulfilled. See Josephus.

units.la: Ierusalem, typus Ecclesiæ militantis, frequenter apud Prophetas, Ierusalem, pro ciuibus vrbis & Ecclesiæ, etiam sæpius occurrit.
units.tr: Jerusalem, a type of the militant Church, frequently occurs in the Prophets. Jerusalem, for the citizens of the city and the Church, occurs even more often.

units.la: IERVSALEM cœlestis Ecclesia sancta, psal. 122 3. Esa. 33 20. & 54.11. & 60.1 &c. 62.6. & 65. verf. 16 18. Galat 4.26. Hebr. 11,10. & 12.22. Apoc. 3.12. Ierusalem noua, 21.v.2.10.
units.tr: The heavenly Jerusalem, the holy Church: Ps. 122.3; Isa. 33.20; 54.11; 60.1, etc.; 62.6; 65.16-18; Gal. 4.26; Heb. 11.10; 12.22; Rev. 3.12. The new Jerusalem, Rev. 21.2, 10.

units.la: IESSE. Vide Isai.
units.tr: Jesse. See Isaiah.

units.la: IESVS filius Iosedech, vocatur Sacerdos magnus, Aggei 1. 12. imago & figura Christi est, Zach 3.1. Templi instauratione cum zorobabele Principe seriò nauat operam, Aggæi 1.14. ad id excitatur ab Aggæo Propheta, 2.5.
units.tr: Jeshua, son of Jozadak, is called the high priest, Hag. 1.12. He is an image and figure of Christ, Zech. 3.1. With Zerubbabel the prince he eagerly labours at the restoration of the Temple, Hag. 1.14. He is roused to this by the prophet Haggai, 2.5.

units.la: IESVS, qui & Christus dicitur, Matt. 1.16. idque reuera est, Ioan .1.17. & 4. ver. 25.26. Act. 17.3. & 18.ver. 5.28.1. Ioan. 2. 22. & 5.1. eum se esse fatetur, Lucæ 22.70. Ioann. 4.25. nominis IESVS ratio, Matth. 1.21. Act. 4.12. à Deo vngitur, Psal. 45.8. Esa 61.1. Luc. 4.18. Act. 4.26, & 10,38. Hebr. 1.9. ad IESV nomen omne genu flectendum, Philip. 2. 10.329. Iesus, Iosue F. Num. Actor. 7.45. Hebr. 4.8.
units.tr: Jesus, who is also called Christ, Matt. 1.16, and really is so, John 1.17; 4.25-26; Acts 17.3; 18.5, 28; 1 John 2.22; 5.1. He confesses that he is this, Luke 22.70; John 4.25. The reason for the name Jesus, Matt. 1.21; Acts 4.12. He is anointed by God, Ps. 45.8; Isa. 61.1; Luke 4.18; Acts 4.26 and 10.38; Heb. 1.9. At the name of Jesus every knee shall bow, Phil. 2.10. Jesus, Joshua; Num.; Acts 7.45; Heb. 4.8.

units.la: IESVS
units.tr: JESUS

units.la: filius Syrach, Ecclesiastici libri autor, Eccles. 50.28.
units.tr: son of Sirach, author of the book of Ecclesiasticus, Ecclus. 50.28.

units.la: i.exploras primogenitus Gedeonis, cū adhuc puer esset, zebee & Salmana occidere iubetur, Iud.8.20.
units.tr: (i.e. one who is tested), the firstborn of Gideon, when he was still a boy, is ordered to kill Zebah and Zalmunna, Judg. 8.20.

units.la: (i.abundans dignitate) filiam qui & Raguel, Exod. 2.1.8.& 18,1,4,18. eius natu maximam vxorem ducit Moses 22.2. oues eius pascit, 3. Iosen in deserto inuisit, 18. v.1.2. 5. Deo sacrificat, v.12. Mosi dat consilium de eligendis Senioribus, v.19 21,22.
units.tr: (i.e. abounding in dignity), also called Raguel, father of Zipporah, Exod. 2.18; 3.1; 18.1, 4, 18. Moses marries his eldest daughter, Exod. 2.22. He tends his sheep. He visits Jethro in the wilderness, Exod. 18.1-2, 5. He sacrifices to God, v. 12. He gives Moses counsel on choosing elders, vv. 19, 21-22.

units.la: vxor Achab imp a est, 1 Reg.16,31,&21,25 Eliae mortem minatur, 19 2. virum suum ad malum inflammat 21.25 suppositiiis literis Naboth occidi iubet, 21.8. praecipi taca moritur, 2 Reg 9 33 a canibus comeditur, v.36. [Iezabel mystica, Apoc.2.20.]
units.tr: Wife of Ahab, an impious woman, 1 Kings 16.31 and 21.25. She threatens Elijah's death, 19.2. She inflames her husband to evil, 21.25. By forged letters she orders Naboth to be killed, 21.8. She dies by being thrown down, 2 Kings 9.33. She is eaten by dogs, v. 36. [Mystical Jezebel, Rev. 2.20.]

units.la: ἀνδρεία 2. Tim 1.7. est quae fugit honesta pericula, quae sunt subeunda pro faciendo officio, quod nimio metu percellatur is, cui illa se offerunt. Ille vero tam timidus, qui maris strepitum timet, est ignauus: cuiusmodi mors secunda manet: Apoc.21 8.
units.tr: Courage [ἀνδρεία], 2 Tim. 1.7, is that which shrinks from honourable dangers that must be faced in order to perform a duty, when one is struck with excessive fear, the one to whom those dangers present themselves. But he who is so timid that he fears the roar of the sea is cowardly; such a person awaits the second death, Rev. 21.8.

units.la: damnata. Iof.18 3 ] 2 Sam.3 33.
units.tr: condemned. Josh. 18.3; 2 Sam. 3.33.

units.la: pro spiritu Domini, Luc 3 16.1. Corinth.3.13 Ignis in Altari perpetuus, Leuit 6.12. primo coelitus demissus: 9. 24 Ignis in sabbatho non accendendus, Exodi 35.3 Ignis insatiabilis, Prouerb.30. 6. coelitus miraculo demissus, 1. Reg.18 38.2 Reg.1 14 2. Paral.7.1. exit e petra, Iudic.6 21. aeternus, Matt.25 41. Esa.66 24. Ignis consumens Deus, Deut.4 24 & 9 3. Hebr.12 29 columna deducens Israelem, Exodi 40.38. Numer.9.15. ignem, praedicationem Euangelij optat Christus accendi, Luc.12.49. Igne tribulationum probamur, 1 Corinth.3 13. Igne salietur victima, Marc. 9 49. Ignea lex, Deuter 33 2. Igneo curru tollitur Elias, 2 Reg 2 11. Ignei serpentibus percussi Israelitae, Numer.21 6. Igne combustorum exempla. Vide COMBVSTORVM & igne deuoratorum exempla: & MORTIS violentae species diuersae.
units.tr: for the Spirit of the Lord, Luke 3.16; 1 Cor. 3.13. Fire on the altar, perpetual, Lev. 6.12. First sent down from heaven, Lev. 9.24. Fire not to be kindled on the sabbath, Exod. 35.3. Insatiable fire, Prov. 30.16. Sent down from heaven by miracle, 1 Kings 18.38; 2 Kings 1.14; 2 Chron. 7.1. It comes out of the rock, Judg. 6.21. Eternal, Matt. 25.41; Isa. 66.24. God a consuming fire, Deut. 4.24 and 9.3; Heb. 12.29. A pillar of fire leading Israel, Exod. 40.38; Num. 9.15. Christ desires that fire, the preaching of the Gospel, be kindled, Luke 12.49. We are tested by the fire of tribulations, 1 Cor. 3.13. The sacrifice is salted with fire, Mark 9.49. The fiery law, Deut. 33.2. Elijah is taken up in a fiery chariot, 2 Kings 2.11. The Israelites bitten by fiery serpents, Num. 21.6. Examples of those burned by fire. See BURNED, and examples of those devoured by fire, and the various kinds of violent death.

units.la: [Varias huius vocis acceptiones ordine proponimus.
units.tr: [We set out the various meanings of this word in order.]

units.la: 1. Ignis caelestis & sacer, Gen.15.17. Leuit.9 24.& 10.2. Num 11.1. Iudic.6 21. Act.2 3 Apoc.8 5 2 Chron 7 1
units.tr: 1. Heavenly and sacred fire: Gen. 15.17; Lev. 9.24, 10.2; Num. 11.1; Judg. 6.21; Acts 2.3; Rev. 8.5; 2 Chron. 7.1.

units.la: 2 Ignis elementaris & artificialis, Genes. 11 3 Exod. 22,6.& saepiss. in Scripturis.
units.tr: 2. Elemental and artificial fire: Gen. 11.3; Exod. 22.6, and very often in the Scriptures.

units.la: 3. Spiritualis, Iudic.9.v.15.20. Rom.12.20 Iacob,3,5,& 5,3,1, Petr,1.7.
units.tr: 3. Spiritual fire: Judg. 9.15, 20; Rom. 12.20; James 3.5, 5.3; 1 Pet. 1.7.

units.la: 4. Ignis, Deus, Deut.4.24. & 9.3. Heb.12.29.
units.tr: 4. God as fire: Deut. 4.24, 9.3; Heb. 12.29.

units.la: 5. Christi oculi, seu iusta prouidentia, Apoc.1.14. & 2.18. & 19.12. eiusd. potentia summa, Apoc.10.1.
units.tr: 5. The eyes of Christ, or his just providence: Rev. 1.14, 2.18, 19.12; his supreme power: Rev. 10.1.

units.la: 6. Spiritus S. efficacia, Matt.3.11. Marc.9.49. Luc.3.16.
units.tr: 6. The efficacy of the Holy Spirit: Matt. 3.11; Mark 9.49; Luke 3.16.

units.la: 7. Verbum Dei & eiusdem probatio exactissima. 2.Sam.22.31. Psal.12.7. & 18.31. Ierem.5.14. Apoc.11.5.
units.tr: 7. The word of God and its most exact testing: 2 Sam. 22.31; Ps. 12.7, 18.31; Jer. 5.14; Rev. 11.5.

units.la: 8. Beneuolentiae diuinae signum, 1 Par.21.26. 2 Paral.7.1. Diuinae protectionis symbolum, Zach.2.5. praesentiae item diuinae signum, 1 Reg.8. ver.24.38. Charitas Christi erga Ecclesiam, Cantic.8.6.
units.tr: 8. A sign of divine goodwill: 1 Chron. 21.26; 2 Chron. 7.1. A symbol of divine protection: Zech. 2.5. Likewise a sign of the divine presence: 1 Kings 8.24, 38. Christ's love towards the Church: Song 8.6.

units.la: 9. Ignis probationis doctrinae in Ecclesia propositae, 1 Cor.3.v.13.15. Ecclesiae potestas, Abd.18.
units.tr: 9. The fire of testing the doctrine proposed in the Church: 1 Cor. 3.13, 15. The power of the Church: Obad. 18.

units.la: 10. Afflictio, persecutio, tentatio, Psalm.17.3. & 66.10. Dan.12.10. zach.13.9. Malac.3.2. Luc.12.40.
units.tr: 10. Affliction, persecution, temptation: Ps. 17.3, 66.10; Dan. 12.10; Zech. 13.9; Mal. 3.2; Luke 12.40.

units.la: 11. Fulmen, & extraordinarium ex aere incendium, Iob.1.16. Psalm.29.7. & 78.48. & 104.6. & 148.8. Hebr.1.7.
units.tr: 11. Lightning, and an extraordinary fire from the air: Job 1.16; Ps. 29.7, 78.48, 104.6, 148.8; Heb. 1.7.

units.la: 12. Ira Dei, eiusdemque in hac vita varius sensus atque effectus, Iob.15.34. Psalm.21.10. & 140.11. Esai.26.11. & 30.30. Ierem.15.14. & 17.4. Thren.1.13, Ezech.15.7. Ioel.1.19. & 2.3.30. Amos.7.4. Sophon.1.18. & 3.8. Act.2.19. Iud.23. Apoc.8.8.
units.tr: 12. The wrath of God, and its varied sense and effects in this life: Job 15.34; Ps. 21.10, 140.11; Isa. 26.11, 30.30; Jer. 15.14, 17.4; Lam. 1.13; Ezek. 15.7; Joel 1.19, 2.3, 30; Amos 7.4; Zeph. 1.18, 3.8; Acts 2.19; Jude 23; Rev. 8.8.

units.la: 13. Itati Dei, excidium comminantis, & inferentis signum, Genes.19.24. Leuitic.10.1.2.
units.tr: 13. The zeal of God, a sign of threatened and inflicted destruction: Gen. 19.24; Lev. 10.1, 2.

units.la: 14. Nouissimum & vniuersale incendium, 2 Petr.3.12. Ignis aeternus, Esai.66.24. Matth.3.12. & 5.22. & 13 verf.42.50. & 18.v.8.9. & 25.41. Hebr.10.27.2. Petr.3.7. Iud.v.7. Apocalyp. 14.10. & 19.20. & 20. verf.10. 14.15. & 21.8.
units.tr: 14. The final and universal conflagration: 2 Pet. 3.12. Eternal fire: Isa. 66.24; Matt. 3.12, 5.22, 13.42, 50, 18.8, 9, 25.41; Heb. 10.27; 1 Pet. 3.7; Jude 7; Rev. 14.10, 19.20, 20.10, 14, 15, 21.8.

units.la: 15. Ignis cordis, Psalm.39.4. Sapientia hypocritarum Esai.50.11. Sermo. impij, Prouerb.16.27. Iacob.3.6. falsa doctrina, Apocalyp.9. verf.17.18. Splendor transitorius impiorum, Iob.18.5. Mich.6.10. Clades bellica, Num.21.28. Ierem.48.45. Excidium horrendum, Apoc.17.16. & 18.8. Labor irritus, Abac.2.13. pericula grauiss. Psal.66.12. Esai.43.2. zachar.3.2. Apoc.16.8. Vr Chaldaeorum, Nehem.9.7.]
units.tr: 15. Fire of the heart: Ps. 39.4. The wisdom of hypocrites: Isa. 50.11. The speech of the wicked: Prov. 16.27; James 3.6. False doctrine: Rev. 9.17, 18. The transitory splendour of the wicked: Job 18.5; Mic. 6.10. Destruction in war: Num. 21.28; Jer. 48.45. Dreadful ruin: Rev. 17.16, 18.8. Fruitless labour: Hab. 2.13. Most grievous dangers: Ps. 66.12; Isa. 43.2; Zech. 3.2; Rev. 16.8. Ur of the Chaldeans: Neh. 9.7.]

units.la: IGNOBILES, qui Deum contemnunt, 1.Sam.2.30.
units.tr: THE IGNOBLE: those who despise God, 1 Sam. 2.30.

units.tr: IGNORANCE, for any sin: Heb. 9.7. Ignorance is to be shunned by the godly: 1 Cor. 14.20, 15.34; Eph. 4.18; 2 Thess. 1.8; Heb. 5.14, 8.11, 13.9. Ignorance is death: Eph. 4.18. How it is to be restrained: 1 Pet. 2.15. Ignorance as the cause of the Israelite captivity: Isa. 5.13. Ignorance which deserves pardon: Luke 23.34; Acts 3.17; 1 Tim. 1.13; and ignorance which does not: Rom. 1.20; Luke 12.48. Ignorance is to be tolerated in weak brethren: Phil. 3.15. See Lev. 4.2. The blindness of the Jews, signified by the word ignorance: 1 Pet. 1.14, of which mention is made in John 9.39. Wilful ignorance: 2 Pet. 3.5. The ignorance of the contentious is rightly to be scorned: 1 Cor. 14.38. Ignorance of God: see God, ignorance of. Examples of ignorance: in Abimelech, Gen. 20.4, 5; the father and mother of Samson, Judg. 14.4; Jonathan, 1 Sam. 14.27; Saul, 26.21; the two hundred men following Absalom in the revolt, 2 Sam. 15.12; the Israelites, Baruch 3.20, 21; the Pharisees, Matt. 12.6, 7, 15.14; Luke 6.39; the disciples, Luke 9.45, 18.34; John 16.17, 20.9; the Jews, John 8.27; Rom. 10.2, 3; Nicodemus, John 3.9, 10; the Sadducees, Matt. 22.29; the citizens and rulers of Jerusalem, Acts 3.17, 13.27; the Athenians, Acts 17.23; the Gentiles, Rom. 1.21; Eph. 4.18; the rulers of this age, 1 Cor. 2.8; the wise of the world, 1 Cor. 15.34; apostates, 1 Tim. 1.7; Paul, 1 Tim. 1.13; false teachers, 2 Tim. 3.7.

units.tr: MOCKERS are abominable to God: Prov. 3.32; they are severely rebuked, Isa. 57.4; they are taught in vain, Prov. 9.7, 13.1; they never grow wise, 14.6. Mockers of the word of God: Acts 2.13; 2 Pet. 3.3; Jude 18. See Word of God, and God's word. Mockers are to be mocked: Prov. 3.34; they are to be destroyed: Isa. 28.14; Ezek. 25.3, 4; Prov. 9.12, and 3.34. Examples of mockery: Noah, Gen. 9.22; Isaac, 21.9; the Israelites, Exod. 1.12, 13, 14; Balaam, Num. 22.28, 29; Gideon, Judg. 8.6; Abimelech, 9.54; Saul, 1 Sam. 10.27, 31.4; 1 Chron. 10.4; David, 1 Sam. 25.10; 2 Sam. 5.6, 6.20, 16.7; 1 Chron. 15.28. units.tr: That God himself ordered images to be made: Exod. 25.18, 19; Num. 21.8, etc. That Solomon made them: 1 Kings 6.35, 7.25, 36, 16.19; 2 Chron. 3.10, 14, 4.3. The Papist idolaters think they can prove this. They also derive the use of images from Num. 21.8; Josh. 2.26, etc.; Wisdom 16.6. [Image of God the Father, Christ: 2 Cor. 4.4; Col. 1.15. Image of God, man: Gen. 1.26; 1 Cor. 11.7. Image: (1) likeness, exemplar, namely Christ, to whom the members of the mystical body must be made conformable: Rom. 8.29; 1 Cor. 15.49; 2 Cor. 3.18; Col. 3.10. Image of man, living: Gen. 5.3. [Image for the carving and effigy of a coin: Matt. 22.20; for the work of human hands, representing something visible or invisible: Deut. 4.16; Isa. 40.18, 44.13; Hab. 2.18; Rom. 1.23; for a shadow and an appearance that quickly vanishes: Job 4.16; Ps. 39.7, 73.20; for an expressed form: Heb. 10.1. See Idol.]
Image of the beast: Rev. 13.14, 15, 16, 19.20.]

units.tr: IMITATION. Examples of good imitation: Jehoshaphat, 1 Kings 22.43; Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18.5, 6; Josiah, 22.1, 2; David, Ps. 119.14, 15, 29–34; the Ninevites, Jonah 3.10; 1 Thess. 1.6, 2.14. Imitation of God is commended: Eph. 5.1; 1 John 2.6; 2 John 4, 11, 17. Of Christ: Heb. 12.2; 1 Pet. 2.21, etc., 3.18; 1 John 3.16. Of Christ's example in Paul: 1 Cor. 11.1; 1 Thess. 1.6. Of Paul: 1 Cor. 4.16; 2 Thess. 3.7; 2 Tim. 3.10. Of the churches: 1 Thess. 2.14. Of the heirs of heaven: Heb. 6.12, 12.1. Of ministers: Heb. 13.7. Of the prophets: James 5.10, 17. Of martyrs: Heb. 12.1; James 5.11. Of holy women: 1 Pet. 3.5. Of the good, not the evil: 3 John 11. An ungodly parent is not to be imitated: Ezek. 18.14, etc.

units.la: IMMVNDITIA, Ἀκαθαρσία, est omnis pollutio corporis nostri per coitum illegitimum admissa. Estque multiplex, vt bestialitas, cum bruto animanti coitus : Sodomia, Adulterium, Raptus, Stuprum. Coitus cum dæmone.
units.tr: IMPURITY, ἀκαθαρσία [akatharsia], is every defilement of our body committed through unlawful intercourse. It is manifold: bestiality, intercourse with a brute animal; sodomy, adultery, rape, fornication; intercourse with a demon.

units.la: IMPATIENTIA, Est tanta animi timiditas & teneritudo, vt nihil omnino duri & acerbi sensus pati possit: ac ne ea quidem,quæ vulgo cæteri homines facile patiuntur & ferunt.
units.tr: IMPATIENCE is such a timidity and tenderness of spirit that it can endure absolutely nothing harsh or bitter in feeling, not even those things which other men commonly bear and endure easily.

units.la: IMPIETAS: Impietas abneganda est, Tit.2.12.omnes homines in se & sua natura sunt impij & filij iræ, Ephes.2.v.3.13.tunc impium iustificare dicitur Deus, cùm hominem Christi sui cognitione regenerat,Roman.4.5.& Christus pro impiis mortuus ,5.6.
units.tr: IMPIETY: Impiety is to be renounced, Titus 2:12. All men, in themselves and by their nature, are impious and children of wrath, Eph. 2:3, 13. God is said to justify the impious when he regenerates a man through the knowledge of his Christ, Rom. 4:5; and Christ died for the impious, Rom. 5:6.

units.tr: IMPIOUS: The impious are in the hand of God, 2 Kings 19:28. The impious are the causes of evils, Prov. 29:8. The impious are instruments of Satan, 2 Cor. 11:15; Eph. 2:2; 1 Thess. 2:18. The bread on which they feed is wickedness, Prov. 4:17. They are called stumbling-blocks, Matt. 13:41.

units.tr: The impious are abominable to God, Exod. 23:7; Psalm 1:6; 5:5, 6; 31:7; 34:17; 94:20; 119:118; Prov. 17:15. They are to be kept away from the salvation of others, Job 8:20; Psalm 119:155; Isa. 3:10, 11. They are to be admonished and seriously rebuked, Prov. 24:25; 28:4; Jer. 20:4; Ezek. 3:17; 33:9, etc. They are olives, Hos. 8:1; Titus 1:10, 11. They are destined for destruction, Job 21:30; 2 Sam. 23:6, 7; Prov. 16:4; 24:20; Zech. 11:6; Rom. 9:22. They are blinded by Satan, 2 Cor. 4:4. They are hateful to the pious, Psalm 101:4; 139:21, 22; Prov. 29:27. They are called sons of the devil, John 8:44; 1 John 3:8. They are sons of unbelief and rebellion, Eph. 2:2; 5:6; Col. 3:6. In appearance they are happy and blessed, Psalm 73:3. They are enemies of God, Job 15:25; Psalm 74:10; 83:3; 89:52. They are unknown to Christ, Matt. 7:23; 25:12. They are ensnared by Satan, 2 Tim. 2:26. They are not to be imitated, Prov. 23:17; 24:1; Isa. 8:11. They are merciless, Prov. 21:10; Rom. 1:31. They are inexcusable, 2 Chron. 24:19; 36:16; Psalm 36:4; 78:17; Ezek. 2:5; Hos. 8:4; Matt. 10:18; 21:39; 24:14; 25:45; 27:25; Luke 9:5; 10:6, 11; John 9:41; 15:22, 24; Acts 4:14, 16; Rom. 1:20; 10:18; 1 Thess. 2:10; 2 Tim. 2:25; Heb. 11:7; 1 Pet. 2:8; 2 Pet. 3:5. They are insatiable, Prov. 13:25. They are useless and unfruitful, Isa. 59:5; John 15:4; Heb. 6:8. The impious are not to be justified, Prov. 17:15; 24:24; 28:4; Isa. 5:23. They are not to be feared, Ezek. 2:6; 3:8, 9; 1 Pet. 3:14. They are wretched, Prov. 3:33; 12:21; Eccles. 8:13; John 12:19. All are dead, Col. 2:13.

units.tr: The impious are ignorant of divine things, Psalm 92:7; John 15:21; 17:25; 1 John 4:8. They deserve to be laughed at, Psalm 52:7, 8; Prov. 1:26. They are always quarrelsome, Prov. 16:28; 17:11. They are never secure, Job 15:20, 21; 18:11; Psalm 6:11; 14:5; 140:4; Prov. 28:3; Matt. 2:3. They grow numb with complacency, Prov. 21:29. They are fools, Prov. 24:8, 9.

units.tr: The impious cannot bear the Word of God. Examples: Ahab, 1 Kings 22:26, 27; 2 Chron. 18:25, 26. The prince of Judah, 24:20, 21. The Jews, 36:15, 16; John 8:43. Pashhur, Jer. 20:2. The officials of Zedekiah, 38:4. Amaziah, Amos 7:10, 11, 12. The priests, the magistrates of the Temple, and the Sadducees, Acts 4:2, 17, 18; 5:17, 33. The priests, 7:54. Elymas, 13:8. The Jews, 13:45, 50; 17:13. Felix, 24:26. False prophets, 2 Tim. 4:3. The impious are hardened by the Word of God and by miracles. Examples: Pharaoh, Exod. 8:15, 19; 32. Saul, 1 Sam. 19:11. The Jewish people, Isa. 6:9, 10. The Jews, John 8:48, 52. They harm as far as they can, not as far as their lust goes: Gen. 27:41; 31:27, 29; 35:5; 37:22; 1 Sam. 19:19, 20; 1 Kings 19:2; Neh. 6:16; Psalm 35:15; 124:1, 2; 129:2; Esth. 3:7, 29; 4:16, 17; Dan. 8:13; Matt. 26:53; Mark 6:19, 20; 14:49; Luke 13:32; 19:48; 20:19; 22:53; John 7:30; 8:20; 10:39; Acts 4:21; 5:18, 19, 26; 9:25; 12:6, 7; 14:19, 20; 17:9; 18:10; 19:30; 20:3; 21:31; 23:12; 24:26; 27:42, 43; 2 Cor. 11:33; Rev. 7:3. The impious perish by their own vices, Job 12:17; Psalm 7:16; 9:16, 17; 10:2; 57:7; Prov. 5:22; 11:6, 27; 12:26; 22:8; 26:27; 29:6; Eccles. 10:8; Isa. 33:11. They try to cover vice with vice. Examples: the brothers of Joseph, Gen. 37:32; Herod, Acts 12:3; Felix, 24:28. The impious will feel God as an avenger, Jer. 12:3; 48:44; Ezek. 6:12; 7:15; Amos 5:19; 9:1, 2; Mic. 6:14, 15. They fulfil the will of God without knowing it, Acts 4:28; 13:27, 29.

units.tr: The judgment of the wicked concerning God, Ps. 50.21. The judgment of the wicked is to be counted as nothing, 1 Pet. 4.4. The praise of the wicked is brief, Job 20.5. Examples of the licence of the wicked against the godly: the Egyptians, Exod. 1.13; Zedekiah, 1 Kings 22.24; Ahab, v.27; Joash, 2 Chron. 24.21-22; the princes of Zedekiah and Jerijah, Jer. 37.14-15 and 38.4-5; the servant of the high priest, John 18.22; the high priests and Pharisees, Acts 5.40; Ananias, Acts 23.2. The tongue of the wicked is compared to a sword, Ps. 52.4 and 57.5; to arrows and coals, Ps. 64.4 and 120.4; to the tongues of serpents, Ps. 140.4. The curses of the wicked are blessings. Examples: Balak and Balaam, Num. 23.11; Josh. 24.16; the enemies of David, Ps. 109.28; the enemies of the Apostles, Matt. 5.11. The memory of the wicked is to be blotted out, Deut. 29.20 and 32.26; Job 18.17 and 24.20; Ps. 9.6, 34.17 and 109.15; Prov. 10.7 and 12.7; Isa. 26.14 and 41.12; Rev. 18.21. The wages of the wicked, Isa. 45.24; Hos. 10.13; 2 Pet. 2.13; Rev. 16.6. The death of the wicked is most wretched, Ps. 34.22. The custom of the wicked is to overcome by clamour: Matt. 27.23-24; Mark 15.14; Luke 23.5; John 7.52; Acts 21.27-34, 36 and 22.22. The manners of the wicked, Prov. 6.12. The multitude of the wicked, Gen. 6.17, 18.32 and 37.21, 26; Num. 13.29, 31-32 and 14.29-30; 2 Sam. 15.12; 1 Kings 12.30 and 20.19; Jer. 44.15; Mic. 7.2; Matt. 7.13 and 25.41; John 18.40; Acts 28.22; Phil. 3.18; 2 Thess. 2.12.

units.tr: The name of the wicked is execrable, Isa. 65.15. The mark of the wicked, John 4.7. God sometimes uses the works of the wicked to destroy the wicked. Examples: see "God." The works of the wicked are abominable before God, Hag. 2.15; corrupt, Isa. 59.5; unfruitful, v.6; Prov. 11.18; perverse, John 7.7; dark, Isa. 29.15. The sins of the wicked ascend before God, Gen. 6.13, 4.10 and 18.20; Jonah 1.2. The prayers of the wicked are abominable to God, 1 Sam. 8.18; Job 27.9; Ps. 18.42 and 109.7; Prov. 1.28, 15.29 and 28.9; Isa. 1.15; Jer. 11.11; Ezek. 8.18; Mic. 3.4; Zech. 7.13; Matt. 6.5 and 23.14; Luke 18.11, 14; John 9.31; James 4.2-3.

units.tr: The prosperity of the wicked: 4 Ezra 3.28, 31; Job 10.3, 21.7, 20; Ps. 73.2, 8 and 92.8; Jer. 12.1; Hab. 1.13; 2 Macc. 6.1, etc. It causes wonder in the good, Job 21.7, 13; Ps. 73.2; Eccl. 7.16; Jer. 12.1; Hab. 1.13; Mal. 3.15. It is fleeting, 1 Sam. 30.16-17; Job 15.27-28, 21.7 and 24.24; Ps. 37.2, 49.7 and 73.17-18, 20.

units.tr: Examples of the fleeting prosperity of the wicked: the people of Laish, Judg. 18.7; the Amalekites, 1 Sam. 30.16; Haman, Esth. 5.11 and 7.10; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 4.28; the nobles of Israel, Amos 6.1-2, etc.; that rich impious man, Luke 16.22. The prosperity of the wicked tempts the godly, Ps. 73.2-3, 11-13. The prosperity of the wicked is not to be envied, Ps. 37.1. The prudence of the wicked, Luke 16.8.

Sudden and unforeseen punishment, dispersion and overthrow of the wicked: Gen. 7.21-22, 14.15, 19.24 and 34.25; Exod. 14.24, etc.; Lev. 10.2; Num. 11.33 and 16.31; Josh. 10.9 and 11.7; Judg. 4.20, 7.12, 8.11, 15.15, 16.28; 1 Sam. 30.16; 2 Sam. 13.28; 1 Kings 16.2-3, 18.40 and 20.13, 19; Job 4.8, 5.3, 8.13, 15.20, 18.1, etc., 20.1, etc., 27.14 and 36.12; Ps. 1.5 and 37.1, etc.; Prov. 1.27, 6.15, 10.25 and 11.7; Isa. 5.24 and 47.9; Jer. 15.8; Dan. 5.30; 1 Macc. 2.62 and 4.3; Matt. 24.38; Luke 12.20, 46, 16.23-25 and 17.27-29; 1 Thess. 5.3. The punishment of the wicked is for the good a cause of fear and caution: Deut. 13.11, 17.18, 19.20 and 21.21; Prov. 19.25 and 21.11; Eccl. 23.37; Acts 11.1; 1 Tim. 5.20. The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable to God, Gen. 4.5; Num. 16.15; 1 Sam. 15.22; Ps. 40.7, 50.9 and 51.18; Prov. 15.8 and 21.27; Eccl. 35.15; Isa. 1.11, 43.23, 61.8 and 66.3; Jer. 6.20, 7.20 and 14.12; Hos. 5.6, 8.13 and 9.4; Amos 5.21-22; Mic. 6.7; Mal. 1.7-8, 10, 13 and 2.13; Matt. 5.23, 9.13 and 12.7; Mark 12.33; Heb. 10.5. The false security of the wicked: Jer. 5.12 and 21.13; Mic. 3.11; Matt. 24.38 and 28.14; Luke 12.19 and 17.27-28; Eph. 4.19; 1 Thess. 5.3-4; Heb. 12.16-17; 1 Pet. 4.18; Rev. 18.7.

units.tr: The seed of the wicked is cursed, 2 Kings 5.27; Job 5.4, 18.19, 20.10 and 27.14; Ps. 37.28 and 109.8-10. Examples: Jeroboam, 1 Kings 15.29; Gehazi, 2 Kings 5.27; Haman, Esth. 9.7-10; Ahab and his house, 1 Kings 22.35-40, 2 Chron. 18.34, 1 Kings 21.22, 2 Kings 10.11, 17; Nebuchadnezzar, Isa. 14.19-21; Jehoiakim, Jer. 22.28; Shemaiah, 29.32; the accusers of Daniel, Dan. 6.24; the Israelites, Hos. 2.4-6. The various kinds of the wicked, Isa. 66.17. The hope of the wicked is deceptive and vain, Job 8.13-14, 11.20 and 18.14; Ps. 112.10; Prov. 10.28; Isa. 28.18 and 30.5; Jer. 2.37 and 7.4, 8; Hos. 12.1; Amos 6.1; Zech. 9.5; James 4.2. The pride of the wicked, Ps. 73.6, 74.22-23 and 83.18.

units.tr: What the wicked fear happens to them, Job 6.16, Prov. 1.26 & 10.24, Isa. 66.4, Jer. 42.16, Ezek. 11.8, John 11.48. To bring help to the wicked is harmful rather than beneficial. Examples: Benjamin, Judg. 20.48; the Syrians, 2 Sam. 10.19; Jehoshaphat, 1 Kgs. 22.32, 2 Chr. 18.31 & 19.2; the servants of Hadadezer, 1 Chr. 19.19. It is often well with the wicked on account of the pious, Jer. 5.1. Examples: the Sodomites, Gen. 18.26, 28, 29, 30, 31, 32; Zoar, Gen. 19.22; Jehoshaphat king of Judah, 2 Kgs. 3.14, 17, 18; the wise men, Dan. 2.24; those who sailed with Paul, Acts 27.24. For the wicked, anything is allowed while the wicked are in power, 2 Chr. 18.23; there is no peace, Isa. 48.22 & 57.21. The wicked are even benefited by the pious. Example: Daniel, Dan. 2.24. The wicked are to be measured by the same measure with which they measure others, Judg. 1.7, Esth. 7.10, Ps. 137.8, Isa. 22.20 & 33.1, Jer. 50.15, 51.24, 51.49, Lam. 1.22 & 3.64, Ezek. 35.15, Dan. 6.24, Joel 3.6, 3.8, Obad. v. 15, Hab. 2.8, Zeph. 3.19, Zech. 2.9, Matt. 7.2, Mark 4.24 & 11.25, Luke 6.38, Rev. 13.10 & 18.6. When the wicked reign, nothing is to be expected but ruin, Prov. 28.12. The wicked are not always answered, 2 Kgs. 18.36. It is also granted to the wicked to perform signs; see MIRACLES. God will laugh at the wicked, Ps. 2.4, 37.12-13, 59.9, Prov. 1.26.

Aliquoties Impleo significat.Satio,vitam finio,Repleo sobole terram,Officium commissum plene exequor, &c.quæ ex locorum occurrentium circumstantiis dignoscuntur.]
units.tr: [FILLING, as used of the carrying out of a command, whether of God or of man, is to be understood. For these phrases, such as "that the Scripture might be fulfilled, the word of the Lord which was spoken by the prophet," etc., occur often: Luke 4.10, John 13.18, Acts 1.16, and in many other places. 2. It is said of the law, Rom. 8.4 & 13.8, Gal. 5.14. 3. It is said of the almighty, gracious and glorious presence of God, of his Spirit, and of his various gifts: Exod. 31.3, Num. 14.21, Ps. 104.24, 104.28, 145.16, Isa. 33.5, 58.11, Jer. 23.24, Hag. 2.8, Luke 1.53, 3.5, Acts 9.17, Eph. 3.19, 4.10, 5.18, Col. 1.9, 4.12. 4. Of God's judgments upon the wicked: Jer. 13.13, Ezek. 5.13, 20.8, 20.21, 21.17. Sometimes impleo means to satisfy, to end a life, to fill the earth with offspring, to carry out a committed duty fully, etc., which are recognised from the circumstances of the places where they occur.]

Nehem. 6.14. Gal.5.12. Sic imprecantur mala: Noe, Genes.9.v. 4.25. Sacerdotes, Numer.5.v.20.21.22. Moses,16.15. Angelus, Iudic.5.23. Debora & Barac. v.31. Samson,16.28. Dauid, Sam. 24.v.12.13.14. Nehemias, Nehem.4.v.4.5.5.& 5.v. 12.13. Ieremias, Ierem. 10.v.11.25. & 17.v.17.18.& 18.v.19. 20. 21. & 20.12.& 50.v. 20.45. Christus etiam imprecatur mala Iudae proditori & synagogae Iudaicae, Psalm. 109.v.6.7.8.9.10.11.&c. Paulus, Galat.5. 12.2. Timot. 4.v. 14.15. Petrus, Actor,8.20. Angelus, Apocal.18.6. Quinetiam sibi ipsis imprecati sunt mala Prophetae,& nonnulli alij, sed cum conditione. Exempla: Moses, Exodi 32.v.31. 32. Num. 11.v.13.14.15. Elias, 1. Reg.19.4. Dauid, 1. Paral. 21.17. Psalm. 7. v. 4 5.6. Iob, Iob.6.v.8.9.10. Ieremias,Ier. 20.v.14.15.16.17.18. Ionas, Ion.4.8. Paulus,Rom.9.3. Imprecationes piis vitandae,Rom.12.14. Iacob.3.9.10.
units.tr: IMPRECATION is a practice of the Holy Spirit in the mouths of the servants of God against sinners, but it is to be feared rather than imitated. Examples: against flatterers, Ps. 12.4 & 28.4; against slanderers, Ps. 79.6, 79.12; against scorners, Neh. 5.13; against the enemies of Christ, Ps. 7.7 & 69.24; against the enemies of David's kingdom, Ps. 70.3 & 71.13; against the enemies of the Church, Judg. 5.31, Ps. 74.3, 83.10, 83.12, 137.7, Jer. 17.18; against hypocrites, Ps. 5.11, 28.4, 31.2; against idolaters, Ps. 135.18, Jer. 10.11, Hos. 9.15; against the impious and those ignorant of God, Ps. 9.18, 31.19, 59.14, 68.2, 69.3, 79.6, 83.16, Neh. 4.4, Jer. 10.25; against the ungrateful, Ps. 69.23, Rom. 11.9, Jer. 18.21-22; against persecutors, Ps. 35.26, 37.15, 69.23, 79.10, 119.78, Jer. 20.2, 50.41-45; against betrayers, Ps. 55.16, 109.6, Neh. 6.14, Gal. 5.12. Thus they call down evils: Noah, Gen. 9.25; the priests, Num. 5.20-22; Moses, Num. 16.15; an angel, Judg. 5.23; Deborah and Barak, Judg. 5.31; Samson, Judg. 16.28; David, 2 Sam. 24.12-14; Nehemiah, Neh. 4.4-5 & 5.12-13; Jeremiah, Jer. 10.11, 10.25, 17.17-18, 18.19-21, 20.12, 50.20, 50.45. Christ too calls down evils on the traitor Judas and the Jewish synagogue, Ps. 109.6-11 etc. Paul, Gal. 5.12, 2 Tim. 4.14-15; Peter, Acts 8.20; an angel, Rev. 18.6. Moreover, the prophets and some others have called down evils upon themselves, but conditionally. Examples: Moses, Exod. 32.31-32, Num. 11.13-15; Elijah, 1 Kgs. 19.4; David, 1 Chr. 21.17, Ps. 7.4-6; Job, Job 6.8-10; Jeremiah, Jer. 20.14-18; Jonah, Jon. 4.8; Paul, Rom. 9.3. Imprecations are to be avoided by the pious, Rom. 12.14, James 3.9-10.

units.la: IPRECATIO, Est oratio, per quam malum poenę, id est,afflictionem aliquā optamus proximo, nō in ipsius emendationé,nec propter Dei gloriam, sed vt satisfaciamus animi nostri impotētiae, Antichristus in die Coenae Dominicae ignes ex alto eiaculatus, diris deuouet omnes illos,qui papalem sedem impugnant.martyr. in 7. Iud. Sed impiorum contra pios execrationes Deus irritas facit:Gen.123. Psal.109.28.Pro.26.2.
units.tr: IMPRECATION is a prayer by which we wish a punishment, that is, some affliction, upon a neighbour, not for his amendment nor for the glory of God, but so that we may satisfy the impotence of our own mind. The Antichrist, on the day of the Lord's Supper, hurling fire from on high, curses with dire imprecations all those who assail the papal see. Martyrol. in 7 Jud. But God makes the curses of the wicked against the pious void: Gen. 12.3, Ps. 109.28, Prov. 26.2.

units.la: IMPVDENTIA
units.tr: Imprudence

units.la: cauenda, Eph.5.17.
units.tr: to be avoided, Eph. 5.17.

units.la: IMPRVDENTIA, Est contemptio indolentiaque earum rerum,quas verecundi reformidēt. Arist. 3. Rhet.damnatur,Rom.13.13.2.Cor.12.21.Eph.5.12. Exempla: Rachel,Gen. 30.1. Nabal,1.Sam.25,10.Iuda, Isaiae 3.8.Pseudoprophetae, Ier.8.12. Antichristi,Dan.8.23.Iudas,Mat.26.49. Ioan.18.5.
units.tr: IMPRUDENCE, is the contempt and insensitivity toward those things which modest people shrink from. Aristotle, Rhetoric 3, condemns it. Rom. 13.13; 2 Cor. 12.21; Eph. 5.12. Examples: Rachel, Gen. 30.1; Nabal, 1 Sam. 25.10; Judah, Isa. 3.8; false prophets, Jer. 8.12; Antichrist, Dan. 8.23; Judas, Matt. 26.49; John 18.5.

units.la: IMPVDICITIA, Est quae inhonestae libidinis intus ardentis signa aliqua profert externe, vel dictis vel factis. Vnde omnes gestus inhonesti,& nictus oculorum Veneris conciliandae gratia coniecti affectationes mulierum, stultiloquia, & sermo putris & obscoenus(quē Paul. Eph.4.29.& 5.4, vocat) sunt huius impudicitiae species, & partes, & effecta turpissima.
units.tr: IMMODESTY, is that which outwardly shows some sign of dishonourable lust burning within, whether in words or in deeds. Hence all dishonourable gestures and winks of the eyes, put on to win love, the affectations of women, foolish talk, and filthy and obscene speech (which Paul calls such in Eph. 4.29 and 5.4) are the kinds, parts and most shameful effects of this immodesty.

units.la: IMPVDICITIAE poena, Apocal.22.15. Impudicitia contra naturam, Genes.19.5.&38.7. Leuit.18.22.&20.13. Iudic.19.v.22.30. Rom.1.27.1. Cor.6.10. Ephes.5.12.1 Tim.1.10.2. Petr.2.v.7.8.
units.tr: The punishment of IMMODESTY: Rev. 22.15. Immodesty against nature: Gen. 19.5 and 38.7; Lev. 18.22 and 20.13; Judg. 19.22, 30; Rom. 1.27; 1 Cor. 6.10; Eph. 5.12; 1 Tim. 1.10; 2 Pet. 2.7, 8.

units.la: IMPVNITAS multis noxiis. Eccles.8.11.
units.tr: IMPUNITY is harmful in many ways. Eccl. 8.11.

units.la: INCANTATIONES & inaleficia, Exodi 7.11. & 8.18. & 22.18. Leuit.19.31.& 20.v.6.27. Numer.23,23. Deut. 18.10.1. Sam.28.7. &c.2 Reg.17.17. & 21.6. Esa.2.6. & 44.25.& 47.13. Ierem.10.2. Dan.2.v.10. Mich.5.1. Actor. 8. 9.& 13.6. & 19.19. Galat 5.20. Apoc.18.23.& 21.8. Vide DIVINI. Incantationis eiusque poenae exempla: Malefici & incantatores Pharaonis, Exodi.7.v.12.13.22. & 8 7.Pythonissa in Endor,1 Samuel.28.v.11.12.13.14.15. Magi & Arioli a Saule interfecti, v.9. Iosias 2 Reg.23.24. Vide de POENA, Leuit. 20.27. Elymas Magus, caecitate percussus, Act.13.11.Vide.MAGIA.
units.tr: INCANTATIONS and sorcery: Exod. 7.11; 8.18; 22.18; Lev. 19.31; 20.6, 27; Num. 23.23; Deut. 18.10; 1 Sam. 28.7, etc.; 2 Kings 17.17; 21.6; Isa. 2.6; 44.25; 47.13; Jer. 10.2; Dan. 2.10; Mic. 5.11; Acts 8.9; 13.6; 19.19; Gal. 5.20; Rev. 18.23; 21.8. See DIVINATION. Examples of incantation and its punishment: the sorcerers and enchanters of Pharaoh, Exod. 7.12, 13, 22; 8.7. The witch of Endor, 1 Sam. 28.11-15. The magi and augurs slain by Saul, v. 9. Josiah, 2 Kings 23.24. See on the PUNISHMENT, Lev. 20.27. Elymas the magician, struck with blindness, Acts 13.11. See MAGIC.

units.la: INCEDERE pro viuere, Vide AMBVLARE:& VIA.[Incedere, de Deo irato, peccatoribus stupidis occurrenti dictum, Leuiti.26.v.24.28.]
units.tr: To WALK for to live. See WALK and WAY. [To walk, said of God in anger meeting stupid sinners, Lev. 26.24, 28.]

units.la: INCENDIVM materiale & naturale, Iof.11.11 Iudic.1.8.& 18.27. Amos.4 11. Apoc.18. ver.9 18. Supernaturale, & a Deo noua quadam ratione immissum, Leuitic.10.6. Num.16.v.35 39.47.]
units.tr: FIRE, material and natural: Josh. 11.11; Judg. 1.8 and 18.27; Amos 4.11; Rev. 18.9, 18. Supernatural, and sent by God in some new manner: Lev. 10.6; Num. 16.35, 39, 47.

units.la: INCENSA, orationes Sanctorum, Apoc.8.4.
units.tr: INCENSE: the prayers of the saints, Rev. 8.4.

units.la: INCESTVS, Est coniunctio consanguinorum vel affinium, quae in gradu seu generationum serie tum lege ipsius honestatis (quae vulgo publica) tum lege diuinitus promulgata prohibetur. De quibus gradibus nemini mortalium remittere licet.
units.tr: INCEST is the union of blood relatives or in-laws, which is forbidden in the degrees or series of generations, both by the law of honesty itself (which is commonly called public) and by the law promulgated by God. No mortal may grant dispensation from these degrees.

units.la: INCESTVS quam execrandus, Leuitici 18.v.6.7.& 20.v.11.14.Deut 22.30.& 27.20.1.Cor.5.v.1.2.
units.tr: How execrable INCEST is: Lev. 18.6, 7; 20.11, 14; Deut. 22.30; 27.20; 1 Cor. 5.1, 2.

units.la: Incestus exempla: Loth cum filiabus, Genes.19 36. Ruben cum concubina patris,35.22. Iudas cum nuru sua Thamar,38,18, Amnon cum Thamar sorore Absalonis,2 Samu.13.14. Absalom cum concubinis patris sui,16.v.21.22. Populus Israel, Ezech.22.v.9.10.11.Amos 2.7.
units.tr: Examples of incest: Lot with his daughters, Gen. 19.36; Reuben with his father's concubine, 35.22; Judah with his daughter-in-law Tamar, 38.18; Amnon with Tamar, sister of Absalom, 2 Sam. 13.14; Absalom with his father's concubines, 16.21, 22; the people of Israel, Ezek. 22.9-11; Amos 2.7.

units.la: Herodes cum Herodiade, Matth.14.4.Marc.6.18.Luc 3.19. Corinthius cum nouerca,1 Cor.5.v.1.2.3. Incestuum poenae exempla:Ruben,Gen.49.v.3.4. Amnon,2.Sam.13.32.Absalon,18 14.Vide Leuit. 20.v.11.12.13.14.&c.
units.tr: Herod with Herodias, Matt. 14.4; Mark 6.18; Luke 3.19. The Corinthian with his stepmother, 1 Cor. 5.1-3. Examples of the punishment of incest: Reuben, Gen. 49.3, 4; Amnon, 2 Sam. 13.32; Absalom, 18.14. See Lev. 20.11-14, etc.

units.la: INCIRCVMCISVS [praeputiatus, qui extra foedus Dei est, Genes.34.14.1. Sam.17.v.26 36.&c. Suunitur etiam[pro impuro puro, & naturę vitio adhuc immersò, Leuitici 16.41. Ieremiæ 6.10. & 9.25. Actor.7.51. Incircumcisus labiis, pro infanti & indiserto, Exodi 6.12.30. Incircumcisus præputio, Phase comedere non poterat,12.48. Incircumcisi corde, qui in naturæ corruptæ vitiis adhuc hærent demersi, Act. 7.51. Incircumcisi auribus, qui vocem Dei ne audire quidem sustinent, ibid.qu iles quidem omnes sumus natura. Incircumcisa mens, Leuit.26.41. [Incircumcisus carne, ex circumcisionis neglectu, Iosu.5.67.] Vide CIRCUMCISIO.
units.tr: UNCIRCUMCISED [foreskinned: one who is outside the covenant of God, Gen. 34.14; 1 Sam. 17.26, 36, etc. It is also used for the impure and unclean, still immersed in the corruption of nature, Lev. 26.41; Jer. 6.10; 9.25; Acts 7.51. Uncircumcised in lips, for the infant and the inarticulate, Exod. 6.12, 30. Uncircumcised in foreskin, who could not eat the Passover, 12.48. Uncircumcised in heart, those still sunk in the vices of corrupt nature, Acts 7.51. Uncircumcised in ears, who cannot even bear to hear the voice of God, ibid. Indeed we are all such by nature. Uncircumcised mind, Lev. 26.41. [Uncircumcised in flesh, through neglect of circumcision, Josh. 5.6, 7.] See CIRCUMCISION.

units.la: CLINANDA corda ad Deum, Iosue 24.23.
units.tr: HEARTS to be inclined to God, Josh. 24.23.

units.la: CONSTANTIA, Est temeraria voluntatis mutatio a bono ad malum, perquam coeptum opus interrumpitur & deseritur: 2.Paral.24 21.Ierem.26.8.16. Contrarium Constantia.
units.tr: INCONSTANCY is a rash change of the will from good to evil, by which a work begun is interrupted and abandoned: 2 Chron. 24.21; Jer. 26.8, 16. The opposite of inconstancy is constancy.

units.la: CONSTANTIA damnatur, 1.Corinth.15.v.12.11.2 Corinth. 1.17. Galat.1.6. & 3 3 Ephes.4.14 Hebr.13 9 Iacobi 1.8.& 3. 10.1. Petri 5.12. Inconstantiæ exempla: Laban, Genesis 31.2. Nazareni, Luc.4.v. 22.28.29. Iudæi, Actor.2.v.6.7.12.13. & 6 12. & 13.ver 43. 44.45.50. Lycaonij,14.v.18.19. Vulgus & Magistratus Philippis,16.v.22.39. Demetrius,19.v.24 32. units.tr: INCONSTANCY is condemned: 1 Cor. 15.12; 11.2; 2 Cor. 1.17; Gal. 1.6; 3.3; Eph. 4.14; Heb. 13.9; Jas. 1.8; 3.10; 1 Pet. 5.12. Examples of inconstancy: Laban, Gen. 31.2; the people of Israel, Exod. 5.21; 14.11, 31; 15.24; 16.2; 19.8; 24.3; 32.18; Num. 11.1; 13.32; 14.4, 40; Korah, Dathan and Abiram, Num. 16.1; the Israelites, v. 41; 17.12; 25.2; Judg. 2.17; 4.1; 8.22; 1 Sam. 8.5; 2 Sam. 15.13; 1 Kings 12.16; Moses and Aaron, Num. 20.12; the Shechemites, Judg. 9.23; the men of David, 2 Sam. 20.2; Joab and Abiathar, 1 Kings 1.7; the princes of Judah, 2 Chron. 24.21; the Jews, Jer. 26.8, 16; 42.5; Azariah with the other proud men, 43.2; the crowd, John 6.15, 30; 12.17; the Pharisees and Herodians, Matt. 22.15, 16; the Nazarenes, Luke 4.22, 28, 29; the Jews, Acts 2.6, 7, 12, 13; 6.12; 13.43, 44, 45, 50; the Lycaonians, 14.18, 19; the common people and magistrates at Philippi, 16.22, 39; Demetrius, 19.24-32; the people of Ephesus, vv. 34, 35; the citizens of Jerusalem, 21.30; the Pharisees and Sadducees, 23.7; the barbarians of Melita, 28.4, 6; the Galatians, Gal. 3.1-3; 4.14, 15. Inconstancy where there is contention, Jas. 3.16.

units.tr: [INCONTINENT, intemperate, 2 Tim. 3.3; incontinence, 1 Cor. 7.5.]

units.la: INCREDVLITAS, est proprie, cum quis audito & cognito Dei verbo, ac præcipuè Euangelio de Christo,& promissione gratiæ, non assentitur. Increduli proinde non sunt proprie, nisi habitu. Idcirco infantes negationem quidem fidei habent, sed non habitum incrudelitatis: non igitur proprie increduli sunt.
units.tr: UNBELIEF properly is when someone, having heard and known the Word of God, and especially the Gospel about Christ and the promise of grace, does not assent to it. Therefore unbelievers are properly so only by habit. Accordingly infants indeed have the denial of faith, but not the habit of unbelief; they are therefore not properly unbelievers.

units.la: INCREDVTITAS damnatur, Abac. 2.4. Matth. 8. v.11.12. & 14.31. Marc.9.19 &.16 14. Lucæ 9.41 & 24.25. Ioannis.16. 9.& 20.27. Roman.2.8. Hebr.3.v.12 19.& 4.11.& 10.38, Iudæ v.5. Incredulitas cæca est,2, Thess.1,8 1. Timoth.1.13. &c. Incredulitas summum in Iudæis crimen, Rom.10. 21.& 11.31. Incredulitatis mala, Matthæi.13.58. Marci 16. 16 Ioannis 3.v.18.36 & 5.38.& 8.24. Roman.2.8.& 11.20. 2.Thess.2.v.12. Heb.3.18.19.1 Petri.4,17.Iudæ.v.5.Apocal. 21.8. Incredulitatem Discipulorum increpat Christus, Matth.17.20. Marci 9.19. Lucæ 9 41.Incredulitati suæ vt succurrat orat Christum pater Dæmoniaci, Marc.9.24. Incredulitate ablecti Iudæi,Rom.11.20.
units.tr: UNBELIEF is condemned: Hab. 2.4; Matt. 8.11, 12; 14.31; Mark 9.19; 16.14; Luke 9.41; 24.25; John 16.9; 20.27; Rom. 2.8; Heb. 3.12, 19; 4.11; 10.38; Jude 5. Unbelief is blind, 2 Thess. 1.8; 1 Tim. 1.13, etc. Unbelief is the greatest crime among the Jews, Rom. 10.21; 11.31. The evils of unbelief: Matt. 13.58; Mark 16.16; John 3.18, 36; 5.38; 8.24; Rom. 2.8; 11.20; 2 Thess. 2.12; Heb. 3.18, 19; 1 Pet. 4.17; Jude 5; Rev. 21.8. Christ rebukes the unbelief of the disciples, Matt. 17.20; Mark 9.19; Luke 9.41. The father of the demoniac asks Christ to help his unbelief, Mark 9.24. The Jews were cut off through unbelief, Rom. 11.20.
