units.tr: UNBELIEVERS are foolish, Titus 3.3; 1 Pet. 2.15. Unbelievers shall not enter into rest, Heb. 3.18. Examples of unbelief: a certain captain, 2 Kings 7.2; the Israelites, Exod. 6.9; Num. 14.11, 12; 20.10; Deut. 1.32; 9.23, 24; Ps. 106.24; the Jews, Isa. 65.2; Rom. 10.21; Jer. 7.23; Ezek. 2.6; the Nazarenes, Matt. 13.58; Mark 6.6; Peter, Matt. 14.31; the disciples of Christ, Matt. 17.17; Mark 9.19; Luke 9.40; certain disciples, Matt. 28.17; Mark 16.11, 14; Zechariah, Luke 1.20; the apostles, 24.11; Cleopas with his companion, v. 25; Nathanael, John 1.46, 47; the brothers of Christ, 7.5; the Jews, 10.25, 26; Acts 13.45; 28.24; 1 Thess. 2.15; the crowd, John 12.37; Thomas, 20.25; certain Ephesians, Acts 19.9; Paul before his conversion, 1 Tim. 1.13; the Hebrew nation, Heb. 3.18, 19. Punishment of unbelief: in Moses and Aaron, Num. 20.12, 24, 25; Deut. 32.49-51; the Israelites, Num. 14.34, 35; the captain of Samaria, 2 Kings 7.1, 2, 17, 18; the inhabitants of Jericho, Heb. 11.31; the unbelieving, Rev. 21.8.

units.la: INCREPATIO, Vide OBIVRGATIO.
units.tr: INCREPATIO: see OBIVRGATIO.

units.la: INDIA,amplissima regio Asiæ : Esther.1,1.& 8.9.
units.tr: INDIA, a very extensive region of Asia: Esther 1:1 and 8:9.

units.la: INDIGNATIO tollenda à nobis,Ephes.4.31. Col.3.8.Indignatio pro excandescentia, Vide IRA.Indignationis sanctæ exempla:Iacob.Gen.30.2.filij Israel,34.v.7.29. Iosue & Caleb.Num.14.v.6.7.Christus,Matth.16.23.& 17.17. V.IRASCI dicitur Christus, Paulus,Act.16.18.
units.tr: INDIGNATION is to be removed from us: Eph. 4:31; Col. 3:8. For indignation as excitement, see ANGER. Examples of holy indignation: Jacob, Gen. 30:2; the sons of Israel, 34:7, 29; Joshua and Caleb, Num. 14:6, 7; Christ, Matt. 16:23 and 17:17. Christ is said to be angry (ἐνεργεῖ?) in... Paul, Acts 16:18.

units.la: INDIGNITAS,Est gratiæ particularis à Deo in nos collatæ quam agnoscimus externa,vel otiosa & infructuosa possessio.Pugnat hoc vitium cum dicto Christi de Talentis, Matt.25.Et qui ita sefordidè gerunt, vt dotes animi sibi à Domino concessas de industria obscurent,sunt βάναυσοι & sordidi dicendi DOLENTIA, reiectionis signum, Ierem.5.3. Ephes.4.18. V. Rom.1.28.
units.tr: INDIGNITY is the outward or idle and unfruitful possession of a particular grace bestowed on us by God, which we acknowledge. This vice conflicts with Christ's saying about the talents, Matt. 25. Those who so foully conduct themselves that they deliberately obscure the gifts of mind granted to them by the Lord are to be called vulgar [βάναυσοι] and base. GRIEF is a sign of rejection: Jer. 5:3; Eph. 4:18. See Rom. 1:28.

units.la: DVI binis tunicis dicuntur, qui vna non contenti alteram etiam habent, vt modò hac, modò illa vtantur, Mar. 6.9. quod interdicit Christus Apostolis suis, eo nimirum sensu, & scopo, vt nullo prorsus impedimento retardentur, quos ipse vult omnino ad obeundam hanc peregrinationem, velut ad cursum paratos & expeditos esse. Induere Christum per baptismum, Gal.3.27. qui declaret, Vide CHRISTVM induere, &c. vt induamus Christum exhortatio, Rom.13.14.
units.tr: Those are said to have two tunics who, not content with one, have another as well, so that they may use now this, now that. Christ forbids this to his Apostles (Mark 6:9), plainly in the sense and with the purpose that they should be hindered by nothing at all, since he wills them wholly to undertake this journey, ready and unencumbered as for a race. To put on Christ through baptism, Gal. 3:27, which shows: see PUT ON CHRIST, etc. The exhortation to put on Christ, Rom. 13:14.

units.la: INDVLGENTIA nimia, verae σωφροσύνη contraria est, quae cū, vel plus quàm oportet, vel alio quàm decet modo diliguntur ij, quos ipsa natura nobis cōciliauit. Qualis fuit Heli amor in liberos suos Ophnin & Phineen.
units.tr: Excessive INDULGENCE is opposed to true σωφροσύνη (self-control), when those whom nature itself has joined to us are loved more than is proper, or in a way other than is fitting. Such was Eli's love for his sons Hophni and Phinehas.

units.la: INDVLGENTIA Dei, Vide DEI indulgentia. Indulgentia parentum corrumpit liberos, Prouer.13 24.1.Sam.2.29. pro.19.18.& 23.13.14. V.2.Sam.18.33.
units.tr: The INDULGENCE of God: see DIVINE INDULGENCE. Parental indulgence corrupts children: Prov. 13:24; 1 Sam. 2:29; Prov. 19:18 and 23:13, 14. See 2 Sam. 18:33.

units.la: INDVRATIO Dei opus est, quatenus ea vtitur ad punien-dam in reprobis voluntariam corruptionem, in qua indurantur. Exodi 7.v.3.22. & 8.v 19.32. & 9.12. Deut.2.30 Iosue 11.20. Rom.9.18. (Vide INDVRARE dicitur.) Induratio reprobis spontanea est, quia eorum corruptione infensus Dominus, eos sic indurat, vt eorū voluntate ad exercendum suum iudicium vtatur, Exodi 8.15. & 9.34.2 Paral.36.13. Act.13.46. Indurationis exempla: in Pharaone, Exo.7.v.22.23.& 8.15. Pharaone & servis eius, 9.v.34.& 14 5. Sehon rege, Deut.2.30. Regibus Canaham, Iosu.11.v.19. 20. Israelitis, Deut.10.16.2. Reg.17.v.14.15.16.2. Paral.30 v.7.8. Filij Heli, 1 Sam.2.25. Sedechia & vniuersis Principibus Sacerdotum, &c.2 Paral.36.v.12.13 14. Iudaeis, Nehem.9.v.16.17.29.30 Iere.5.3.& 7.25.& 16 12.& 17.23 & 19. 15. Ezech.12.2. Act.13.46. in quibusdam Ephesiis, Actor. 19.8. Indurat Deus quem vult, Rom. 9.18. ne induremus ceruices nostras, Deut.10.16 corda nostra, Psal.95.8. Hebr. 3 15.
units.tr: HARDENING is a work of God, insofar as he uses it to punish the voluntary corruption in the reprobate by which they are hardened: Exod. 7:3, 22; 8:19, 32; 9:12; Deut. 2:30; Josh. 11:20; Rom. 9:18. (See it is said to HARDEN.) The hardening of the reprobate is spontaneous, because the Lord, angered by their corruption, hardens them in such a way that he uses their will to carry out his judgment: Exod. 8:15; 9:34; 2 Chron. 36:13; Acts 13:46. Examples of hardening: in Pharaoh, Exod. 7:22, 23; 8:15; Pharaoh and his servants, 9:34; 14:5; King Sihon, Deut. 2:30; the kings of Canaan, Josh. 11:19, 20; the Israelites, Deut. 10:16; 2 Kings 17:14-16; 2 Chron. 30:7, 8; the sons of Eli, 1 Sam. 2:25; Zedekiah and all the chief priests, etc., 2 Chron. 36:12-14; the Jews, Neh. 9:16, 17, 29, 30; Jer. 5:3; 7:25; 16:12; 17:23; 19:15; Ezek. 12:2; Acts 13:46; some of the Ephesians, Acts 19:8. God hardens whom he wills, Rom. 9:18. Let us not harden our necks, Deut. 10:16, or our hearts, Ps. 95:8; Heb. 3:15.

units.la: INEBRIARI quid significet Hebraeis, Vide EBRIETAS & SATVRARI.
units.tr: For what it means to be drunk [INEBRIARI] among the Hebrews, see DRUNKENNESS and to be SATED.

units.la: [Inebriari vino, Gen.9.21 & 19.32.2 Sam.11.13. Luc.12.45. Ioann.2.10. Ephes.5.18. Inebriari, significat, affatim bibere, hilariter conuiuari, Genes.43.34. Grauissimis afflictionibus opprimi, Esai.49.26. Thren.3.15. Aspergere abundè, Esa.66.9. tempestiue irrigare, Psal.65.v.10.11. Esa.55.10. Sagittæ sanguine inebriatæ, Deut.32. 42. Gladius in cœlo inebriatus, Esai. 34.5. De effectis gratiæ Dei erga electos dictum, Psal.36.9. Cantic.5.1. Ierem.31.14.25. Zach.9.15. Item de benedictionibus variis in hac vita dictum, Prou.5.19. & 11.25. Agg.1.6. Contrà de voluptatibus illicitis vsurpatur, Prou.7.18. Item, de stupore, sopore, vertigine mentis, Esai.29.9.10. & 63.6. Ierem.25.27. & 48.26. & 51.v.7.39.57. Threu.4.21. Nahum.3.11. Abac.2.15. Apoc.17.2. Calix inebrians, i.exuberans, Psal.23.5.]
units.tr: [To be made drunk with wine: Gen. 9:21; 19:32; 2 Sam. 11:13; Luke 12:45; John 2:10; Eph. 5:18. To be inebriated signifies to drink one's fill, to feast merrily: Gen. 43:34. To be oppressed by very grievous afflictions: Isa. 49:26; Lam. 3:15. To sprinkle abundantly: Isa. 66:9. To water seasonably: Ps. 65:10, 11; Isa. 55:10. Arrows drunk with blood: Deut. 32:42. A sword drunk in heaven: Isa. 34:5. Said of the effects of God's grace toward the elect: Ps. 36:9; Song 5:1; Jer. 31:14, 25; Zech. 9:15. Likewise said of various blessings in this life: Prov. 5:19; 11:25; Hag. 1:6. On the contrary, it is used of illicit pleasures: Prov. 7:18. Likewise of stupor, lethargy, and giddiness of mind: Isa. 29:9, 10; 63:6; Jer. 25:27; 48:26; 51:7, 39, 57; Lam. 4:21; Nah. 3:11; Hab. 2:15; Rev. 17:2. A drunken cup, that is, overflowing: Ps. 23:5.]

units.la: INFAMIA, nota turpitudinis 2. Cor.6.8. Vide FAMA.
units.tr: INFAMY, a mark of disgrace: 2 Cor. 6:8. See FAME.

units.la: INFANTES, in vrbium expugnatione reseruandi, Deut.20. 14. Christo oblati, Matth.19.13. (vide & Marc.10.13.14. Luc.18.15. Infantibus similes nos esse oportet, Matt.19.14. & 18.3. sicut infantes modò geniti simus, 1.Pet.2.2. Ab Herode occisi: Matt.2.16.
units.tr: INFANTS are to be spared when cities are stormed: Deut. 20:14. Offered to Christ: Matt. 19:13 (see also Mark 10:13, 14; Luke 18:15). We ought to be like infants: Matt. 19:14 and 18:3; as newborn infants, we should be: 1 Pet. 2:2. Killed by Herod: Matt. 2:16.

units.la: INFANTIA quæ laudanda, Matth.18.v.3.4. Luc.18.16.1.Cor. 14.20. Eph.4.14.1.Petr.2.2. Infantia spiritualis, 1.Cor.3.1. Vbi infantiam opponit paulus adultæ ætati, ideoque lactis nomine prima Christianæ religionis tyrocinia significat. Petrus verò, 1.Pet.2.2. infantiam priori illi corruptissimæ vitæ opponit, & perpetuum lactis (i.veræ & synceræ doctrinæ Euangelicæ) vsum commendat: vnde patet, infantiæ nomen diuerso respectu & sensu tam à Paulo, quàm à Petro, vsurpari.
units.tr: INFANCY is to be praised: Matt. 18:3, 4; Luke 18:16; 1 Cor. 14:20; Eph. 4:14; 1 Pet. 2:2. Spiritual infancy: 1 Cor. 3:1. Here Paul sets infancy against adult age, and so by the name of milk he signifies the first rudiments of the Christian religion. Peter, however, in 1 Pet. 2:2 sets infancy against that earlier and most corrupt way of life, and commends the constant use of milk (that is, of the true and pure Gospel doctrine). From this it is clear that the name of infancy is used in a different respect and sense by Paul and by Peter.

units.la: INFATVARI, est omni acrimonia deperdita, qua res à putredine arcentur, insipidum euadere, Matth.5.13. vbi Apostoli sal terræ appellantur.
units.tr: To become INSIPID (ἄναλον) is to lose all sharpness by which things are kept from putrefaction, to become tasteless: Matt. 5:13, where the Apostles are called the salt of the earth.

units.la: INFERIORES: Inferiorum consilia non sunt contemnenda. Exempla: Vxoris Naaman pedissequa, 2. Regum 5 3. Serui Naaman, verf. 13. Abigail, 1. Sam.25.25. Ioab, 1.Par. 21.3.
units.tr: INFERIORS: the counsels of inferiors are not to be despised. Examples: the servant-girl of Naaman's wife, 2 Kings 5:3; the servants of Naaman, v. 13; Abigail, 1 Sam. 25:25; Joab, 1 Chron. 21:3.

units.la: INFERI, vel INFERNVS, pro sepulchro, Genes.42.38. & 44. 29.Iob.14.13. & 17.13. Psal.6.6. & 16.10. & 18.6. & 30.4. & 49. 15. & 94.17. & 115.17. & 141.9. Esai.38.18. Ezech.31.16. Act.2. 31. & 13.35. Inferi vel infernus, pro loco, eóque horribili, puniendis reprobis destinato, Num.16.v.30.33. Deut.32. 22. Prou.2.18. & 7.27. Psal.(11.6. & 21.11. & 40.15.) & 55.16. & 139.8. Esai.14.9. & 28.v.15.18. Esa.30.33. & 33.11. & 34.9. Amos 9.2. Abac.2.5. Matt.8.12. & 11.23. & 16.18. Luc.10.15. Apoc. 1.18. & 6.8. & 20.v.13.14. Poena in eo nunquam terminanda, Esai.66.24. Matth.25.v.41.46. Marc.9.47.48. 2.Thess. 1.9. (Vide DESCENDERE ad inferos.) Quare falsa est eorum opinio, qui Diabolos & damnatos aliquan- do saluatum iri contendunt. (Vide DIABOLI.) Infer- nus describitur Esai.30.33. Infernus cum morte à Chri- sto deuictus, Ose.13.14. [Inferus quinque significare vi- detur.
units.tr: HELL, or INFERNO, for the grave: Gen. 42:38; 44:29; Job 14:13; 17:13; Ps. 6:6; 16:10; 18:6; 30:4; 49:15; 94:17; 115:17; 141:7; Isa. 38:18; Ezek. 31:16; Acts 2:31; 13:35. Hell or the underworld, for a place, and a horrible one, destined for the punishment of the reprobate: Num. 16:30, 33; Deut. 32:22; Prov. 2:18; 7:27; Ps. 11:6; 21:11; 40:15; 55:16; 139:8; Isa. 14:9; 28:15, 18; 30:33; 33:11; 34:9; Amos 9:2; Hab. 2:5; Matt. 8:12; 11:23; 16:18; Luke 10:15; Rev. 1:18; 6:8; 20:13, 14. Punishment in it is never to end: Isa. 66:24; Matt. 25:41, 46; Mark 9:47, 48; 2 Thess. 1:9. (See DESCEND into hell.) Therefore the opinion of those is false who contend that the devils and the damned will at some time be saved. (See DEVILS.) Hell is described in Isa. 30:33. Hell was conquered with death by Christ: Hos. 13:14. [Inferus seems to signify five things.

units.la: 1. Ita nominatur Abyssus, locus in terram profundissi- mus, Vorago, Num.16.v.33. Deut.32.22. Psal.139.8. Esai.7. 11. Amos.9 2. Phil.2.10.
units.tr: 1. The abyss is so named, the place most deeply sunk into the earth, a gulf: Num. 16:33; Deut. 32:22; Ps. 139:8; Isa. 7:11; Amos 9:2; Phil. 2:10.

units.la: 2. Mors, Summorum dolorum corporis & animæ cru- ciatus ineffabilis plena, seu infimus humiliationis huma- næ gradus & status: atque irę diuinæ sensus. Psal.88.4. Act. 2.24.
units.tr: 2. Death, full of the unspeakable anguish of the greatest pains of body and soul, or the lowest grade and state of human humiliation, and the sense of divine wrath: Ps. 88:4; Acts 2:24.

units.la: 3. periculum grauissimum & lethale, Psal.30.4. & 86.13. & 116.3 Prou.23.14. Esai.28.v.15.18.
units.tr: 3. A most grievous and deadly peril: Ps. 30:4; 86:13; 116:3; Prov. 23:14; Isa. 28:15, 18.

units.la: 4. Sepulchrum, Gen.37.35. Iob.17.13. vt supra.
units.tr: 4. A sepulchre: Gen. 37:35; Job 17:13, as above.

units.la: 5. Tartarus, locus cruciandis in æternum reprobis An- gelis & hominibus destinatus, Luc.16.23. Matt.11.23.2. Pet. 2.4. Apoc.1.18. & 6.8, & 20.v.13.14.]
units.tr: 5. Tartarus, the place destined for the eternal torment of reprobate angels and men: Luke 16:23; Matt. 11:23; 2 Pet. 2:4; Rev. 1:18; 6:8; 20:13, 14.]

units.la: INFIDELITAS, seu incredulitas punitur, Gen.19.v.11.17.26. Num.11.21. & 14.v.2.11. & 20.12. Deut.9.20.2. Reg.7.v.2.17. 4.Esdr.15.4. Psal.78.32. Eccles.2.15. Matt.8.28.34. & 14.30. & 17.17. Marc.16.16. Luc.1.19.20. & 24.24. Ioan. 3.v.18.36. & 7.v.8.24. & 12.48. & 20.27. Rom. 11.20. Heb.3.18. Apoc.21. 8. Infidelitas, pro de Dei promissis dubitatione, Vide INCREDULITAS. Infidelitas, pro non præstita promissione, damnatur, Pro.25.19. Eccles.5.3. Vide FALLACIA. Infidelitas & incredulitas conjunctæ sunt, Esa.21.2. Infidelium mentes à Deo excæcatæ, 2.Corinth.4.4. cum infidelibus nullum commercium habendum, 6.14. V. Fidelitas.
units.tr: UNBELIEF, or incredulity, is punished: Gen. 19:11, 17, 26; Num. 11:21; 14:2, 11; 20:12; Deut. 9:20; 2 Kings 7:2, 17; 1 Esdras 15:4; Ps. 78:32; Eccles. 2:15; Matt. 8:28, 34; 14:30; 17:17; Mark 16:16; Luke 1:19, 20; 24:24; John 3:18, 36; 7:8, 24; 12:48; 20:27; Rom. 11:20; Heb. 3:18; Rev. 21:8. Unbelief, as doubt about God's promises: see INCREDULITY. Unbelief, as failure to keep a promise, is condemned: Prov. 25:19; Eccles. 5:3. See DECEIT. Unbelief and incredulity are joined: Isa. 21:2. The minds of unbelievers are blinded by God: 2 Cor. 4:4. One must have no fellowship with unbelievers: 2 Cor. 6:14. See FAITHFULNESS.

units.la: INFIRMA ex consequenti, pro contemtis & vilibus, 1.Corinth.1.27. & 12.22.2. Corinth.13 9. Sic infirmitates vocat Paulus, 12.10.ea, propter quæ abiectus & vilis habebatur. Infirma in mundo eliguntur à Deo, & cur, 1.Corinth. 1.28.
units.tr: WEAK, by consequence, for the despised and worthless: 1 Cor. 1:27; 12:22; 2 Cor. 13:9. Paul calls by the name of weaknesses, 2 Cor. 12:10, those things on account of which a man was held abject and worthless. The weak things of the world are chosen by God, and why: 1 Cor. 1:28.

units.la: INFIRMITAS, pro humiliatorum abiectione, Gallat.4.13. pro imbecillitate, quæ in hominibus maxima est, Matt.26.41. Infirmitas corporalis, Vide AEGRITUDO.
units.tr: WEAKNESS, for the abjection of the humbled: Gal. 4:13; for feebleness, which is greatest in men: Matt. 26:41. Bodily weakness: see SICKNESS.

units.la: INFIRMI, pro absolute & omnino ad opus bonum ineptis Rom.5.6. pro imbecillis in fide; & horum babenda est ratio, Luc.22.32. Act.20.35. Rom.14.1. & 15.1. 1. Cor. 8.v.9. & 10.v.28.29.1. Thes.5.14. eorúmque ignorantia toleranda, non fouenda,Rom.14 1. Infirmitatis in fide exempla : Moses,Numer.11,v.21.22.Gedeon,Iudic.6 v.13.14. 15. Petrus, Matt.14.v.30.31.Discipuli,8.26.& 26 56.Mar.14 50. Ioan. 11.8.Nicodemus,Ioan.3 2. Pater Dæmoniaci , Marc 9.24. multi Principes,Ioan.12.42. Ioseph. Arimathæus,19.38. Infirmi pro ægrotis. Vide AEGROTVS : & ÆGRITVDO.
units.tr: WEAK, absolutely and entirely unfit for good work: Rom. 5:6; for those weak in faith, and account must be taken of them: Luke 22:32; Acts 20:35; Rom. 14:1; 15:1; 1 Cor. 8:9; 10:28, 29; 1 Thess. 5:14; and their ignorance is to be tolerated, not fostered: Rom. 14:1. Examples of weakness in faith: Moses, Num. 11:21, 22; Gideon, Judg. 6:13-15; Peter, Matt. 14:30, 31; the disciples, 8:26 and 26:56; Mark 14:50; John 11:8; Nicodemus, John 3:2; the father of the demoniac, Mark 9:24; many leaders, John 12:42; Joseph of Arimathea, John 19:38. Weak, for the sick: see SICK and SICKNESS.

units.la: [Infirmus,Æger, morbo affectus,Psal.63. Debilis corpore, Leuit.25.35. Animo debili, seu in fide nutans, nec satis adhuc confirmatus, Act.20 35.Rom.14.v.12.1. Cor.17.&c. Despectus,abiectus, vilis 2. Cor.4.10 & 11 21.& 13.v. 49.1.Thes.5 14.Impotens, nullius visus extra Christum, post eius manifestationem,Gal.4.9.Nudus,non munitus, caducus,Gen.42 9.2.Par.34.10.]
units.tr: [Weak, sick, afflicted with disease: Ps. 63. Feeble in body: Lev. 25:35. Feeble in spirit, or wavering in faith, not yet sufficiently confirmed: Acts 20:35; Rom. 14:12; 1 Cor. 17, etc. Despised, abject, worthless: 2 Cor. 4:10; 11:21; 13:9; 1 Thess. 5:14. Powerless, of no account outside Christ, after his manifestation: Gal. 4:9. Naked, unarmed, frail: Gen. 42:9; 2 Chron. 34:10.]

units.la: INFOECVNDA nulla obedienti Deo,Exo.23.26. Deut.7.14. V.sterilis.
units.tr: BARREN: no one obedient to God: Exod. 23:26; Deut. 7:14. See STERILE.

units.la: INFELIX.(V.miser.)Rom.7.24.suo loco.
units.tr: UNHAPPY. (Or: wretched.) Rom. 7.24, in its place.

units.la: INGRATITVDO, Ἀχαριστία,Est nostri officij aduersusnostros benefactores prudens prætermissio, aut impudens denegatio.Natura enim ipsa nos obligat ad εὐχαριστεῖν. Hoc autem vitium semper apud omnes Gentes grauissimum habitum est,& homine indignum.Ingratus est qui dissimulat:ingratior qui non reddit : ingratissimus omnium qui oblitus est.Bernardus.Luc.6.35.
units.tr: INGRATITUDE, ἀχαριστία [acharistia]. It is the careless neglect, or shameless denial, of our duty toward our benefactors. For nature itself binds us to give thanks [εὐχαριστεῖν, eucharistein]. This vice has always been regarded as the most serious among all nations and unworthy of a human being. The ungrateful man is one who conceals a benefit; the more ungrateful, one who does not repay it; the most ungrateful of all, one who forgets it. Bernard. Luke 6.35.

INGRATITUDE and its punishment: Gen. 31.1 and 40.23; Exod. 1.8; Deut. 13.3, etc.; Judg. 2.1, and 6.8, and 8.33, and 12.1; 1 Sam. 10.18, and 12.8, and 25.3, 10; 2 Sam. 14.30; 2 Chron. 24.21; Prov. 17.13; Isa. 1.2, and 5.4; Jer. 2.5, 6; Ezek. 16.1, etc.; Hos. 10.1, and 13.2, 6; Mic. 6.3; Matt. 11.20; Luke 17.18; John 11.46; Rom. 1.21; 2 Tim. 3.2; Deut. 32.18; Jer. 8.7.

units.la: Ingratitudo damnatur,Eccl.9.15,Rom.1.18. Col.2.7.& 3.15.1.Tim.5.4.2. Tim.3 2.2.Pet.1.9.& 2.20.Ingratitudinis pœna,Iudic.8.16.2.Par.24.25.Prou.17.13.Ezech.16.43,Luc. 9.5.& 13.35.& 14.24.Isa.5.5.
units.tr: Ingratitude is condemned: Eccl. 9.15; Rom. 1.18; Col. 2.7, and 3.15; 1 Tim. 5.4; 2 Tim. 3.2; 1 Pet. 1.9, and 2.20. The punishment of ingratitude: Judg. 8.16; 2 Chron. 24.25; Prov. 17.13; Ezek. 16.43; Luke 9.5, and 13.35, and 14.24; Isa. 5.5.

Absalom,14.30.& 15,13: Iero-
units.tr: Examples of ingratitude: Laban, Gen. 31.1; the chief cupbearer, Gen. 40.23; the new Pharaoh, Exod. 1.8; Acts 7.18; the Israelites, Exod. 17.3, and 32.1; Num. 11.14; Judg. 2.2, and 8.35; 1 Sam. 30.6; Jer. 2.5, and 18.20; Ezek. 16.22, and 20.8; Hos. 2.8, and 8.14, and 11.3, and 13.6; the Ammonites and Moabites, Deut. 23.3–4; Saul, 1 Sam. 18.8, and 19.10; the men of Keilah, 23.11; Nabal, 25.10; Hanun, 2 Sam. 10.4; David, 11.5; Absalom, 14.30, and 15.13; Jero-
