units.tr: Jeroboam, 1 Kings 12.28; the king of Israel, 2 Kings 6.13, and 31; the Ammonites, Moabites, and Edomites, 2 Chron. 20.10; Joash king of Judah, 24.21–22; Amaziah, 25.14; Uzziah, 26.16; Hezekiah, 32.25; Israel, Neh. 9.17; the enemies of David, Ps. 35.12, and 109.4; the Hebrew nation, Ps. 38.21, and 78.11, and 106.7; the Jews, Isa. 1.2–3, and 5.4; John 1.11, and 5.43; the Tyrians, Amos 1.9; Chorazin and Bethsaida, Matt. 11.21; Luke 10.13; Capernaum, v. 15; those invited to the wedding, Matt. 22.3; the Nazarenes, Luke 4.29; the Samaritans, 9.53; the nine lepers, Luke 17.18; the tenants of the vineyard, 20.11, 14; the slave-girl with a python spirit, Acts 16.19–20; the soldiers, 27.42; the fathers in the wilderness, Heb. 3.10.

units.la: INGREDI ad Patres,Gen.15.15. aggregari ad populos suos, 25.8.Numer.27.13.& 31.2. Ingredi viam universæ terræ, Iosue 25.14.1.Reg.2.2.periphrasis est mortis, & significat idem quod mori.
units.tr: To go in to the fathers, Gen. 15.15; to be gathered to one's people, 25.8; Num. 27.13, and 31.2. To go the way of all the earth, Josh. 23.14; 1 Kings 2.2. It is a periphrasis for death, and means the same as to die.

units.la: INGREDI & egredi Hebraeis, cum de iis agitur qui publicum munus gerunt,est domi & foris, pace & bello Rem-publ.administrare,Num.27.v.17.21.Deut.31 2.1.Reg.3 7.& versari in loco aliquo,officiumque suum facere, Ier.37.4. Act.1.21 Hebraismus.
units.tr: To go in and go out, in Hebrew idiom, when speaking of those who hold public office, means to administer the commonwealth at home and abroad, in peace and in war, as in Num. 27.17, 21; Deut. 31.2; 1 Sam. 3.7; and to be active in some place and perform one's duty, Jer. 37.4; Acts 1.21. A Hebraism.

units.la: Hoc itaque dicendi genus ut plurimum declarat apud Hebræos functionis publicæ, eiusque laboriosæ administrationem :potissimum autem cum de iis agitur,qui publicum munus gerunt,ut ex Deut. 31.2. apparet: ubi Moses dicit,se propter senectutem non posse amplius ingredi & egredi,id est,muneris sui laboribus satisfacere : cum alioquin vegeta esset ipsius senectus,Deut.34 7.Item ex 2. Par.1.10. ubi Salomon prudentiam & intelligentiam petit a Domino, ut possit ingredi & egredi cum populo:id est,non ut cum populo simpliciter versari , sed ut suum officium facere possit.Item ex 1.Par.27.1. Interim tamen non nego,ad privatæ etiam vitæ officia hanc paroemiam pertinere,ut Deut.28.6.Psal.121.3.Ioan.10.9.
units.tr: This form of speech, for the most part among the Hebrews, indicates the performance of a public office and the laborious administration of it. Especially is this so when those who hold public office are in view, as appears from Deut. 31.2, where Moses says that because of his old age he can no longer go in and go out, that is, satisfy the labours of his office, although his old age was otherwise vigorous (Deut. 34.7). Likewise from 2 Chron. 1.10, where Solomon asks the Lord for wisdom and understanding so that he may go in and go out before the people, that is, not merely live among the people, but be able to perform his duty. Likewise from 1 Chron. 27.1. Meanwhile, I do not deny that this proverb also pertains to the duties of private life, as in Deut. 28.6; Ps. 121.8; John 10.9.

units.la: INGREDI ad puellam,vel virginem , vel mulierem,est rem cum ea habere , Genes.29.21.2. Sam.11.4. & 16.22. Amos 2.7.
units.tr: To go in to a girl, or a virgin, or a woman, means to have intercourse with her: Gen. 29.21; 2 Sam. 11.4, and 16.22; Amos 2.7.

units.la: INGREDI in gaudium Domini:Hebræorum more significat percipere fructum benignitatis Domini , & reipsa sentire quam gratum fuerit servi officium domino suo , Mat.25. 21.Simile dicendi genus habetur Psa.69.28.cuius dicti sensus est:ne accenseantur iustis.
units.tr: To enter into the joy of the Lord: in the manner of the Hebrews it means to receive the fruit of the Lord's kindness and to experience in actual fact how welcome the faithful service of a servant has been to his master, Matt. 25.21. A similar form of speech occurs in Ps. 69.28, whose sense is: let them not be counted among the righteous.

units.la: INGREDI in Regnum cœlorum , Matth.5.20.est,dignos esse qui in Ecclesia doceant, vt ex antecedentibus liquet. Neque enim de quorumuis piorum officio, sed de solis Doctoribus, eo loci agitur, & nomine regni coelorum, vt alibi saepe, non triumphantem, vt vulgò loquuntur, sed militantem adhuc & ministerio Pastorum egentem Ecclesiam intelligit Christus.
units.tr: To enter into the kingdom of heaven, Matt. 5.20, means to be worthy to teach in the Church, as is clear from what precedes. For the passage speaks not of the office of any godly person whatever, but only of teachers, and by the name of the kingdom of heaven Christ understands the Church, not triumphant, as people commonly speak, but still militant and in need of the ministry of pastors, as often elsewhere.

units.la: INHOSPITALITAS, Iudic.8.5.&19.18.1.Sam.25.9.14. Sap.19.13.Matth.25.43. V.Hospitalitas.
units.tr: INHOSPITALITY: Judg. 8.5, and 19.18; 1 Sam. 25.9, 14; Wisd. 19.13; Matt. 25.43. See Hospitality.

units.la: INHVMANITAS damnatur. Prou.21.13. & 28.27. Abd. v.10. Rom.1.31. Inhumanitatis exempla: Ciues Gabaa, Iudic.19.15. Saul,1.Sam.19,15. Edom, Amos 1.11. Principes Sion, 6.6. Samaritani, Luc.9.53. Sacerdos quidam, 10.31. Levita quidam v.32. Filius senior, 15.25. Vide Comitas, Humanitas.
units.tr: INHUMANITY is condemned: Prov. 21.13, and 28.27; Obad. v. 10; Rom. 1.31. Examples of inhumanity: the citizens of Gibeah, Judg. 19.15; Saul, 1 Sam. 19.15; Edom, Amos 1.11; the princes of Zion, 6.6; the Samaritans, Luke 9.53; a certain priest, 10.31; a certain Levite, v. 32; the elder son, 15.25. See Courtesy, Humanity.

units.la: INIMICITIA, ἔχθρα, Est ex odio conceptum desiderium nocendi illi, quem iam odimus. Quod si apertis signis sese declarat, apertae inimicitiae dicuntur: sin autem occultum adhuc est, & latens in animo, simultas appellatur.
units.tr: ENMITY, ἔχθρα [echthra]. It is a desire to harm one whom we already hate, conceived out of hatred. If it declares itself by open signs, it is called open enmity; but if it is still hidden and lies concealed in the mind, it is called a grudge (simultas).

units.la: INIMICITIAE damnantur, Gal.5.v.19.20. Inimicitiae aeternae inter serpentem & mulieris semen, Gen.3.15.
units.tr: ENMITIES are condemned: Gal. 5.19–20. Eternal enmity between the serpent and the seed of the woman, Gen. 3.15.

units.la: INIMICI hominis, domestici eius, Matt.10.36. Inimici non passim contemnendi, 1.Sam.14.14.&17.43. 2.Sam.21.20.1.Reg.20.1.&c.2.Reg.14.8. sed diligendi, & beneficiis supe-randi, ac deuinciendi, Exo.23.4.5. Matt.5.44. Luc.6.27. Dilectionis inimicorum exempla: Ioseph, Gen.45.3. Dauid,1.Sam.26.9.2.Sam.16.v.7.8.9.10. Elisaeus, 2.Reg.6.22. Christus, Luc.23.34. Rom.5.8. Stephanus, Act.7.60. Paulus, 2.Tim.4.16. Inimicis beneficia conferenda, Prou.25.21. Rom.12.20. Inimico reconciliato non temerè credendum, 1.Sam.24.17.&26.21.2.Sam.3.26. [Inimicus perpetuus Christi & Ecclesiae, Satan, Matt.13.v.25.28.39. Luc.10.19. Inimica, Ecclesiae Mich.7.v.8.10.1.Cor.15.26.Iac.4.4. Inimici inuisibiles & formidabiliores, Luc.1.v.71.74. Inimici filiorum Dei in genere, & in specie, Gen.22.17. Psal.9.& passim. Apoc.11.v.8.12. Inimicus homo hominis, Exod.23.4. & frequenter in Script.]
units.tr: A MAN'S ENEMIES are his own household, Matt. 10.36. Enemies are not to be despised everywhere, 1 Sam. 14.14, and 17.43; 2 Sam. 21.20; 1 Kings 20.1, etc.; 2 Kings 14.8; but are to be loved, and overcome and won over by kindnesses, Exod. 23.4–5; Matt. 5.44; Luke 6.27. Examples of loving one's enemies: Joseph, Gen. 45.3; David, 1 Sam. 26.9; 2 Sam. 16.7–10; Elisha, 2 Kings 6.22; Christ, Luke 23.34; Rom. 5.8; Stephen, Acts 7.60; Paul, 2 Tim. 4.16. Benefits are to be conferred on enemies, Prov. 25.21; Rom. 12.20. A reconciled enemy is not to be trusted rashly, 1 Sam. 24.17, and 26.21; 2 Sam. 3.26. [Satan is the perpetual enemy of Christ and the Church, Matt. 13.25, 28, 39; Luke 10.19. Enmity toward the Church, Mic. 7.8–10; 1 Cor. 15.26; James 4.4. Enemies are invisible and more formidable, Luke 1.71, 74. Enemies of the children of God in general and in particular, Gen. 22.17; Ps. 9 and passim; Rev. 11.8, 12. Man is the enemy of man, Exod. 23.4, and frequently in Scripture.]

units.la: INIQVITAS: Iniquitas pro ipsa poena, vel punitione pro iniquitate inflicta, Genes.19.15. Sic accipiunt nonnulli, & Gen.4.13.1.Sam.28.10.Psal.32.5,& 69.28. Iniquitas abundabit, Matt.24.12.1.Ioan.5.19. Iniquitas omnis peccatum, v.17. Iniquitas in Deo nulla, Psal.92.16. Rom.3.5.&9.14. Iniqui-
units.tr: INIQUITY: iniquity is sometimes put for the punishment itself, or for the punishment inflicted for iniquity, Gen. 19.15. Some understand it so also in Gen. 4.13; 1 Sam. 28.10; Ps. 32.5, and 69.28. Iniquity will abound, Matt. 24.12; 1 John 5.17 (every iniquity is sin); there is no iniquity in God, Ps. 92.16; Rom. 3.5, and 9.14. Iniqui-

units.la: [Iniquitas impiorum (Vide Impii) Iniquitatem suam portabit quisque Deut.24.16.2.Reg.14.6.2.Par.25.4.Ezech.18.20. (Reliqua vide in vocibus Op vs & Onvs) Ierem.31.29.30.]
units.tr: [The iniquity of the wicked (see Wicked): each one shall bear his own iniquity, Deut. 24.16; 2 Kings 14.6; 2 Chron. 25.4; Ezek. 18.20. (For the rest see under the words Opus and Onus.) Jer. 31.29–30.]

units.la: INIVRIA nemini facienda, Leuit.19.13.& 25.17.Psal.15.3.Mat.7.12.1.Thess.4.12.Iniuria propria non vlciscenda, sed Deo committenda, Deut.32.35.Matt.5.39.Rom.12.19. Hebr.10.30.Prou.20.22.Iniurias acceptas obliuisci iubemur, Leuit.19.18.Iniuria dissimulanda, Pro.12.16. Iniuriae condonandae, (Vide Condonatio) Col.3.13.Matt.18.21. &c. Ex animo: Matt.6.12.& 18.35. Quoties: Matt.18.21. Mature: Eph.4.26.Etiam inimicis: Mat.5.44.c. Sic Deus nobis in Christo propitius est: Col.3.13.Mat.6.14. Et contra: Mat.18.15. Iacob.2.13.Mat.7.2. Exempla, Abrahę, Gen.20 17.Iob,42.8.Christi: Col 3.13. Iniuriae illatae & passae exempla: Ioseph a fratribus, Gen.50.15. duo Hebraei, Exodi 2.14. Dauid ab Ammonitis, Syris & Semei, 2.Sam.10.6. & 19.19. 1.Paral. 19 6. Hebraeus ab Aegyptio, Act.7,24. a Corinthiis fratribus quibusdam, 1.Cor.6.8.2. Cor.7.12.]
units.tr: INJURY must be done to no one: Lev. 19.13, and 25.17; Ps. 15.3; Matt. 7.12; 1 Thess. 4.6. An injury done to oneself is not to be avenged but committed to God: Deut. 32.35; Matt. 5.39; Rom. 12.19; Heb. 10.30; Prov. 20.22. We are commanded to forget the injuries we have received, Lev. 19.18. An injury is to be overlooked, Prov. 12.16. Injuries are to be forgiven (see Forgiveness), Col. 3.13; Matt. 18.21, etc. From the heart, Matt. 6.12, and 18.35. As often as, Matt. 18.21. Promptly, Eph. 4.26. Even to enemies, Matt. 5.44, etc. Thus God is merciful to us in Christ, Col. 3.13; Matt. 6.14. And conversely, Matt. 18.15; James 2.13; Matt. 7.2. Examples: of Abraham, Gen. 20.17; of Job, 42.8; of Christ, Col. 3.13. Examples of injuries inflicted and suffered: Joseph by his brothers, Gen. 50.15; two Hebrews, Exod. 2.14; David by the Ammonites, Syrians, and Shimei, 2 Sam. 10.6, and 19.19; 1 Chron. 19.6; a Hebrew by an Egyptian, Acts 7.24; by certain brothers among the Corinthians, 1 Cor. 6.8; 2 Cor. 7.12.]

units.la: INIVSTITIA, pro falsa doctrina, 2.Thessal.2.12. Omnis iniustitia Deo abominabilis, Deuter. 25.16. Merces eius, 2. Pet.2.13.
units.tr: INJUSTICE, for false doctrine, 2 Thess. 2.12. Every injustice is abominable to God, Deut. 25.16. Its wages, 2 Pet. 2.13.

units.la: INNOCENTIA, contraria malitiae, est talis affectio animi, quae nemini noceat, ac ne nocere quidem velit. Rom.16. 18.
units.tr: INNOCENCE, the opposite of malice, is that disposition of mind which harms no one and does not even wish to harm.  Rom. 16.18.

units.la: INNOCENS nullus apud Deum, Exodi 34.7. (Vide IVSTVS)
units.tr: NO ONE is innocent before God, Exod. 34.7. (See Just.)

units.la: Innocentia Samuelis, 1. Sam.12. 3. Dauidis, 24.v 10.11 12. &c. Innocentia sua cuique tuenda, & malae suspiciones amouendae, Ios.22.22.1.Sam.1 14.1.Reg.18. 17. Ierem.37.12. Act.2 14 & 6. 4.& 7.2.& 28.17. V.Inions.
units.tr: The innocence of Samuel, 1 Sam. 12.3; of David, 24.10–12, etc. Each person must guard his own innocence and remove evil suspicions, Josh. 22.22; 1 Sam. 1.14; 1 Kings 18.17; Jer. 37.12; Acts 2.14, and 6.4, and 7.2, and 28.17. See Innocents.

units.la: INNVERE pro, signis & nutibus petere, Luc.1.62.
units.tr: TO NOD, that is, to ask by signs and gestures, Luke 1.62.

units.la: INOBEDIENTIA est, quae vel omnino negligit: vel ex parte tantum, vel perfunctorie, non autem ex animo, legitimum superioris iussum exequitur.
units.tr: DISOBEDIENCE is the failure which either altogether neglects a lawful command of a superior, or carries it out only in part, or perfunctorily, and not from the heart.

DISOBEDIENCE and its punishment: Gen. 2.16–17, and 3.17, 26; Lev. 10.1, and 26.14, etc.; Num. 14.28, 41; 16.31; 20.24; Deut. 11.16, 28; 17.12; 18.19–20; 27.16, etc.; 28.15, etc.; 1 Sam. 12.15, and 13.11, and 15.24, and 28.16; 2 Sam. 6.6; 1 Kings 11.9, and 13.15, and 14.17, and 20.35, etc.; 2 Chron. 7.19, and 6.16, 19; Isa. 24.5; Jer. 11.3, 8; 13.8, and 17.27, and 26.4, and 35.1, etc.; Jonah 1.3; Matt. 17.17; Acts 7.39; Rom. 2.8; Gal. 3.10; 2 Thess. 1.8. How great an evil disobedience is: 1 Sam. 15.23.

units.la: Inobedientia infidelitatis comes, Ephes. 2.2. eius poena Deut.30.v.17.18.2.Thess.3.14.Heb.2.v.2.3.
units.tr: Disobedience is the companion of unbelief, Eph. 2.2; its punishment, Deut. 30.17–18; 2 Thess. 3.14; Heb. 2.2–3.

units.la: Inobedientiæ & eius pœnæ exempla: Adam & Eua, Genes. 3.v.6.16.17.Roman.5.19.Pharao, Exodi 7.14. & 8.32.& 9.33.& 10.20.& 14.v.27.28. Israelitæ, 17.4. Numer.14.v.41.44.Deut.9.veri.23.24. (Quidam Israelita, 1.Reg.20.36.)2.Reg.17.14.Achan, Ios.7.1.&c. Saul, 1.Sam.13 13.& 15.19.Vir Dei, 1.Reg.13.v.21.26 Rex Israel, 20.42. Naaman, 2.Reg.5.13. Ioas Rex, 13 19. Iosias, 2.Paralip.35.22.Ionas, Ion.1.3.& 2.1. Cæci illuminati, Matth.9.31. quidam Iudæi, Tit.1.10. Inobedientia erga parentes damnatur, 2.Tim.3.2.
units.tr: Examples of disobedience and its punishment: Adam and Eve, Gen. 3.6, 16–17; Rom. 5.19; Pharaoh, Exod. 7.14, and 8.32, and 9.33, and 10.20, and 14.27–28; the Israelites, 17.4; Num. 14.41–44; Deut. 9.23–24. (A certain Israelite, 1 Kings 20.36.) 2 Kings 17.14; Achan, Josh. 7.1, etc.; Saul, 1 Sam. 13.13, and 15.19; the man of God, 1 Kings 13.21–26; the king of Israel, 20.42; Naaman, 2 Kings 5.13; King Joash, 13.19; Josiah, 2 Chron. 35.22; Jonah, Jonah 1.3, and 2.1; the blind men who were healed, Matt. 9.31; certain Jews, Titus 1.10. Disobedience toward parents is condemned, 2 Tim. 3.2.

units.la: INSANIA, morbus animi, veris Dei seruis à mundo obiicitur. Exempla: Dauidi, 2.Sam.6.20. Prophetæ Iehu vngenti.2.Reg.9.11.Christo, Marc.3.21.Ioan.10.v.19.20. Paulo, Act.26.24.V.Act.12.15.1.Cor.14 23.
units.tr: INSANITY, a disease of the mind, is thrown at the true servants of God by the world. Examples: David, 2 Sam. 6.20; the prophet who anointed Jehu, 2 Kings 9.11; Christ, Mark 3.21; John 10.19–20; Paul, Acts 26.24. See Acts 12.15; 1 Cor. 14.23.

units.la: INSATIABILIA tria, Prou.30.15. additur quartum, ibid.
units.tr: THREE things are insatiable, Prov. 30.15; a fourth is added, ibid.

units.la: INSIDIAE: Insidiarum structarum exempla: Esau Iacobo, Genes.27.42.Iosua Hai, &c. Ios.8.12. Abimelech Sichimitis & Baalitis, Iudic.9.v.25.34.42.43. Dalila Samsoni, 16 12.Israelitæ Beniamitis, 2c.v.29.36.37 38.39. Saul Amalech, 1.Sam.15.6. Dauidi, 18.v.15.16.17. & 24 v.12.13. Baasa Nadab, 1.Reg.15 27. Iezabel Eliæ, 19.2 14. Benadad Regi Israel, 2.Reg.6 8. Ozias Pekach, 15 30. Serui Amon, 21. ver.22.23. Ieroboam Abiæ, 2. Paral. 13.13. Ammonitis & Moabitis Deus, 20.22. Zadab, Ioas, 24.26. Ierusalem Amasiæ, 25.27. Bagathan & Thares Assuero, Esth.6.2. Impius pio, Psalm. 10.v.8.9. Iudæi Christo, Matt.26.4. Marc.14.1. Luc.6.7.& 11.v.53.54.& 19.47. Herodias Ioanni, Marc.6.19. Iudæi Paulo, Act.9.v.24.25.29 & 20.v.3.19. & 23.15. & 25.3.2. Cor.11.26.
units.tr: AMBUSHES: examples of laid ambushes: Esau against Jacob, Gen. 27.42; Joshua against Ai, etc., Josh. 8.12; Abimelech against the men of Shechem and the Baalites, Judg. 9.25, 34, 42–43; Delilah against Samson, 16.12; the Israelites against the Benjamites, 20.29, 36–39; Saul against Amalek, 1 Sam. 15.6; against David, 18.15–17, and 24.12–13; Baasha against Nadab, 1 Kings 15.27; Jezebel against Elijah, 19.2, 14; Ben-hadad against the king of Israel, 2 Kings 6.8; Pekah against Ozias, 15.30; the servants of Amon, 21.22–23; Jeroboam against Abijah, 2 Chron. 13.13; God against the Ammonites and Moabites, 20.22; Zabad and Jehozabad against Joash, 24.26; Amaziah against Jerusalem, 25.27; Bigthan and Teresh against Ahasuerus, Esth. 6.2. The wicked against the righteous, Ps. 10.8–9; the Jews against Christ, Matt. 26.4; Mark 14.1; Luke 6.7, and 11.53–54, and 19.47; Herodias against John, Mark 6.19; the Jews against Paul, Acts 9.24–25, 29, and 20.3, 19, and 23.15, and 25.3; 2 Cor. 11.26.

units.la: INSIPIENTIA, V. STVLTITIA.
units.tr: FOOLISHNESS, or Folly. See FOLLY.

units.la: INSONS non occidendus, Exodi 23.7. (V. Innocens.) Pro.1.11.
units.tr: The innocent is not to be killed, Exod. 23.7. (See Innocent.) Prov. 1.11.

units.la: INSTAVRATIO omnium per Christum, Eph.1.10.
units.tr: The RESTORATION of all things through Christ, Eph. 1.10.

units.la: INTEGRITAS corporis, pro valetudine, sicut & integrũ corpus pro sano & incolumi, Esai.1.6. Act.3.16. (Vide Simplicitas) Animi.1. Thess.5.23. Iac.1.4.
units.tr: INTEGRITY of body, for health, just as a "whole body" is one that is sound and unharmed, Isa. 1.6; Acts 3.16. (See Simplicity.) Of the soul: 1 Thess. 5.23; James 1.4.

units.la: INTELLECTVS à Deo est, Psal.119.v.18.34.73.125. 144.169. 2. Tim.2.7. Qualem habeamus: Eph.4.18.
units.tr: UNDERSTANDING comes from God, Ps. 119.18, 34, 73, 125, 144, 169; 2 Tim. 2.7. What kind of understanding we should have: Eph. 4.18.

units.la: INTELLIGERE Iudæos Deus optat, Deut.32.29. intelligens cor, 29.4.
units.tr: God desires the Jews to understand, Deut. 32.29; an understanding heart, Deut. 29.4.

units.la: INTELLIGENTIA nostra est verbum Dei, Deut.4.6. Intelligentia gentia vera quæ, ibid. Iob. 28. 28. Ose. 14. 9. intelligen-tia replentur artifices tabernaculi, Exodi 31.3.&35.31.Iob. 32. 8.
units.tr: Our understanding is the Word of God, Deut. 4.6. The understanding that is true wisdom for the nations, ibid.; Job 28.28; Hos. 14.9. Craftsmen were filled with understanding for the tabernacle, Exod. 31.3 and 35.31; Job 32.8.

units.la: INTEMPERANTIA, ἀκρασία, est immoderatus voluptatū corporis cùm adsunt, vel cùm haberi possunt, vsus & appetitus: Vel, Nimius, quòd ex absint iisque minimè fruamur, dolor & tristitia. V. Strach. 37.32.1. Cor. 7.5.
units.tr: INTEMPERANCE [ἀκρασία] is the immoderate use and desire of bodily pleasures, whether when they are present or when they can be had. Or it is an excessive grief and sadness when they are absent and we cannot enjoy them. See Sirach 37.32; 1 Cor. 7.5.

units.la: INTEMPERANTIA pro dapibus ex alienis interuersis facultatibus ad luxum comparatis, Matth. 23. 25. Vide GVLA.
units.tr: INTEMPERANCE, for feasts provided from the wealth of others, gathered by ruinous means for luxury, Matt. 23.25. See Gluttony.

units.la: INTENTIO: intentio nostra in Dei cultu constituendo sequenda non est, Deuter. 12.8. Prou. 14.12. & 16.25. Esa. 3.8. & 65.11. & 66.v.3.4. Ioan. 16.2.1. Tim. 4.v.1.3. Coloss. 2.v.8.23. Eorum qui suam intentionem secuti, lapsi sunt, exempla: Ioseph, Genes. 48.v.18.19. Iosua, Num. 11. v.28.29. mater Michæ, Iudic. 17.3. Saul, 1.Sam. 15.15. ducenti Viri, seu populus Absalonem secutus, 2. Samu. 15.11. Rex Israel. 1.Reg. 20.42. Giezi, 2.Reg. 4.27. Ozias, 2.Paral. 26.16. Petrus, Matth. 16. 22. Ioann. 13.8. Discipuli, Marc. 10.13. Lucæ 18.16. Ioannes, Marc. 9.v.38.39. Iacobus & Ioannes, Luc. 9. v.49.50.54.55. Iudæi, Rom. 10.2. Paulus, Gal. 1.13. (Vide ZELVS) Intentiones, quas vocant, vel ex eo satis euertuntur, quod ὑπακούειν, id est, obedire, Roman. 1.5. 1. Petr. 1.22. & κηρύσσειν, id est, prædicare (vt ex locis citatis, & ipsa verbi notatione apparet) se mutuò respiciunt. Intentiones damnantur, Deut. 12.8. Rom. 14. 7. Col. 2. v.8.23. 1. Tim. 4. v.13. (Vide Opinio.)
units.tr: INTENTION: our intention must not be followed in establishing the worship of God, Deut. 12.8; Prov. 14.12 and 16.25; Isa. 3.8; 65.11; 66.3–4; John 16.2; 1 Tim. 4.1, 3; Col. 2.8, 23. Examples of those who fell by following their own intention: Joseph, Gen. 48.18–19; Joshua, Num. 11.28–29; Micah's mother, Judg. 17.3; Saul, 1 Sam. 15.15; the two hundred men, or the people who followed Absalom, 2 Sam. 15.11; the king of Israel, 1 Kgs 20.42; Gehazi, 2 Kgs 4.27; Uzziah, 2 Chr. 26.16; Peter, Matt. 16.22; John 13.8; the disciples, Mark 10.13; Luke 18.16; John, Mark 9.38–39; James and John, Luke 9.49–50, 54–55; the Jews, Rom. 10.2; Paul, Gal. 1.13. (See Zeal.) So-called intentions are sufficiently overthrown by the fact that "to obey" [ὑπακούειν], that is, obedience, Rom. 1.5; 1 Pet. 1.22, and "to preach" [κηρύσσειν], as is clear both from the passages cited and from the very meaning of the words, refer to one another. Intentions are condemned, Deut. 12.8; Rom. 14.7; Col. 2.8, 23; 1 Tim. 4.13. (See Opinion.)

units.la: INTERIOR homo, V. HOMO.
units.tr: INNER man. See MAN.

units.la: INTERCEDIT Abraham pro Sodomitis, Gen. 18.23.
units.tr: Abraham intercedes for the Sodomites, Gen. 18.23.

units.la: INTERCESSOR noster Christus, Rom. 8.34. V. suo loco.
units.tr: Our intercessor is Christ, Rom. 8.34. See in its place.

units.la: INTERPRETATIO somniorum à Deo est, Genes. 40. 8. Dan. 2.28. Scripturæ, iuxta analogiā, proportionem fidei Rom. 12.6. Interpretatio à Spiritu Dei est, 1. Corinth. 12.10. Interpretatio Ecclesiæ necessaria est. 14.v.27.28. Dei donum est, Gen. 40.8. Dan. 2.28.1. Corinth. 12.10. & 14.13. 2. Petr. 1. 20. Eius vsus 1. Cor. 14.13.19. Abusus. v.17.
units.tr: The INTERPRETATION of dreams is from God, Gen. 40.8; Dan. 2.28. Of Scripture, according to analogy and the proportion of faith, Rom. 12.6. Interpretation is from the Spirit of God, 1 Cor. 12.10. The interpretation of the Church is necessary, 1 Cor. 14.27–28. It is God's gift, Gen. 40.8; Dan. 2.28; 1 Cor. 12.10 and 14.13; 2 Pet. 1.20. Its use, 1 Cor. 14.13, 19. Its abuse, v. 17.

units.la: INTERROGANDVS Deus in infirmitatibus, 2. Reg. 1.16.
units.tr: God is to be consulted in sicknesses, 2 Kgs 1.16.

units.la: INTROIRE & exire, Vide INGREDI & egredi.
units.tr: TO ENTER and go out. See TO ENTER and go out (INGREDI and egredi).

units.la: INVENIRI in Christo, est Christo per fidem insitos comperiri, Philip. 3.9.
units.tr: To be FOUND in Christ means to be discovered as grafted into Christ through faith, Phil. 3.9.

units.la: [Inuenire gratiam in oculis Dei, Genes. 6.8. & 19.19. Exod. 33. ver. 12.13.16. & 34.9. 2. Sam. 15.25. Luc. 1.30. Act. 7.46 Inuenire gratiam coram hominibus, Gen.18.3 & 30.27. Exempla, Ioseph. Gen.39.4. Ruth, Ruth.2.v.10.13. Anna, 1. Sam.1.18. Dauid, 1. Sam.16.22.&.20.3.& 27.5. Adad, 1.Reg. 11.19. Esther, Esther,2.v.9.]
units.tr: [To find grace in the eyes of God, Gen. 6.8; 19.19; Exod. 33.12, 13, 16; 34.9; 2 Sam. 15.25; Luke 1.30; Acts 7.46. To find grace before men, Gen. 18.3; 30.27. Examples: Joseph, Gen. 39.4; Ruth, Ruth 2.10, 13; Hannah, 1 Sam. 1.18; David, 1 Sam. 16.22; 20.3; 27.5; Hadad, 1 Kgs 11.19; Esther, Esth. 2.9.]

units.la: INVIDIA, φθόνος, Est ægritudo animi, si eo, quod concupieris, alius potiatur, ipse careas. Vel, est animi tristitia de alieno bono, quod illi vel lucrū, vel gloriam affert. Duas eius partes constituit, (Nimirum siue quis, quod ipse est, alium esse nolit siue alium videns se præstantiorem id ægre fert.) Anselmus Rom.1.
units.tr: ENVY [φθόνος] is a sickness of the mind when someone lacks what he desired while another possesses it. Or it is sadness of mind at another's good, which brings that person gain or glory. It has two parts: namely, when someone is unwilling that another should be what he himself is, or when, seeing another superior to himself, he takes it badly. Anselm, Rom. 1.

units.la: INVIDIA & odium, Genes.4.5. V.plura in exemplis. Exodi 1.8.& 20.13. Leuit.19.17. Num.35.v.20.23. Deut.19.11. Prov.10.v.12.18. Ezech.25.15. Luc.15.28. Ioann.12.4. 1.Ioan.3.13.&4.20. Invidia damnatur, Iob.5.2. Psalm.37.1.& 37.3. Prov.14.30. Rom.1.29.& 13.13.1. Cor.13.4.2. Corint.12.20. Gal.5.21. Tit.3.3. Iac.3.14.& 4.v.2.5.1. Petr.2.v.1.2. Invidia, communis omnium morbus, Eccles. 4.4. ex quæstionibus & pugnis nascitur. 1. Timoth.6.4. Invidiæ merces, Prouerb.28.22.
units.tr: ENVY and hatred, Gen. 4.5. See more in the examples: Exod. 1.8 and 20.13; Lev. 19.17; Num. 35.20, 23; Deut. 19.11; Prov. 10.12, 18; Ezek. 25.15; Luke 15.28; John 12.4; 1 John 3.13 and 4.20. Envy is condemned: Job 5.2; Ps. 37.1, 3; Prov. 14.30; Rom. 1.29 and 13.13; 1 Cor. 13.4; 2 Cor. 12.20; Gal. 5.21; Titus 3.3; James 3.14 and 4.2, 5; 1 Pet. 2.1–2. Envy, the common disease of all, Eccl. 4.4; it arises from disputes and fights, 1 Tim. 6.4. The wages of envy, Prov. 28.22.

units.la: Invidiæ exempla: Satan, Genes.3.1. Sap.2.24. Cain, Gen.4.4. Palæstini, 26.14. Esau, 27.41. Rachel, 30.1. Fratres Ioseph 37.v.4.8.11. Act.7.9. AEgyptij, Exod.1.13. Iosue, Num.11.v.28.29. Aaron & Maria, 12.v.1.2. Ephraimitæ, Iudic.8.v.1.2. Ehab frater Dauidis, 1.Sam.17.28. Saul, 18.8. Philisthæi, 29.9. Achitophel, 2.Sam.17.23. Sanaballat & Tobias, Nehem.2.10. Aman, Esth.5.13. Principes & Satrapæ Darij, Dan.6.4. Pharisæi, Matth.9.11. Ioann.12.19. Discipuli Ioannis, Matth.9.14. Ioann.3.26. Principes Sacerdotum & Scribæ, Matth.21.15. Iudæi, 27.18. Actor.13.45.& 17.5. Frater prodigi Filij, Luc.15.28. quidam Pharisæi, 19.39. Pontifices & Pharisæi, Ioan.11.47. Sacerdotes, Magistratus Templi, & Sadducæi, Actor.4.v.1.2.& 5.17. Auditores Stephani, 7.54. Corinthij, 1.Corinth.1.11. Pseudoapostoli, Philipp.1.15.
units.tr: Examples of envy: Satan, Gen. 3.1; Wis. 2.24. Cain, Gen. 4.4. The Philistines, Gen. 26.14. Esau, Gen. 27.41. Rachel, Gen. 30.1. Joseph's brothers, Gen. 37.4, 8, 11; Acts 7.9. The Egyptians, Exod. 1.13. Joshua, Num. 11.28–29. Aaron and Miriam, Num. 12.1–2. The Ephraimites, Judg. 8.1–2. Eliab, David's brother, 1 Sam. 17.28. Saul, 1 Sam. 18.8. The Philistines, 1 Sam. 29.9. Ahithophel, 2 Sam. 17.23. Sanballat and Tobiah, Neh. 2.10. Haman, Esth. 5.13. The princes and satraps of Darius, Dan. 6.4. The Pharisees, Matt. 9.11; John 12.19. The disciples of John, Matt. 9.14; John 3.26. The chief priests and scribes, Matt. 21.15. The Jews, Matt. 27.18; Acts 13.45 and 17.5. The elder brother of the prodigal son, Luke 15.28. Certain Pharisees, Luke 19.39. The high priests and Pharisees, John 11.47. The priests, the temple magistrates and the Sadducees, Acts 4.1–2 and 5.17. The hearers of Stephen, Acts 7.54. The Corinthians, 1 Cor. 1.11. The false apostles, Phil. 1.15.

units.la: INVOCATIO DEI, Est ardens affectus in Deum tendens, quo tum petimus & expectamus à solo Deo, propter Christum, dona spiritualia & corporalia, secundum ipsius mandatum & promissiones: tum pro donis acceptis gratias ipsi agimus.
units.tr: INVOCATION OF GOD is an ardent affection tending towards God, by which we ask for and expect from God alone, for Christ's sake, spiritual and bodily gifts, according to his own command and promises; and by which, for gifts received, we give him thanks.

units.la: INVOCARI nomen alicuius super aliquem, est de nomine illius vocari, Genes.48.16. Deu.28.10. 4.Esdr.4.25. Dan.9.v.18.19. Esa.4.1. Ierem.7.10. Invocare nomen Dei super aliquem, Num. 6.27. Inuocantibus Deum salus, Roman. 10.13. Inuocandus Deus corde puro, 2. Timoth. 2.22. Inuocatus Deus in tribulatione exaudit, 2. Sam. 22.7.
units.tr: To be CALLED by someone's name over someone is to be called by that person's name, Gen. 48.16; Deut. 28.10; 4 Esdras 4.25; Dan. 9.18–19; Isa. 4.1; Jer. 7.10. To invoke the name of God upon someone, Num. 6.27. Salvation belongs to those who call upon God, Rom. 10.13. God is to be invoked with a pure heart, 2 Tim. 2.22. God, when invoked in tribulation, hears, 2 Sam. 22.7.

units.la: INVOCATIO nominis Christi, pro Christi Deitatis agnitione, 1. Cor. 1.2. 2. Timot. 2.19. Inuocatio συνεκδοχικῶς pro toto Dei cultu, 2. Timoth. 2.22. Inuocatio nominis Dei præcipitur, Psal. 50.15. salutaris est, 20.8. Prou. 18.10. Ioel. 2.32. Act. 2.21. Rom. 10.13. Inuocatio nominis Dei, sacrificium Deo gratum, Psal. 116.13. Inuocatio ex fide, Roman. 10.14. Inuocatio & fides res inter se coniunctissimæ, Matt. 21.22. Marci 11.24. Iac. 1.6. 1. Ioan. 3.22. Inuocationis fructus, Philip. 4.6, 7. Inuocationis Dei exempla: Seth, Genes. 4.26. Abraham, 12.8. & 13.4. & 21.33. Isaac, 25.21. & 26.25. Iacob, 32.9. Moses, Exodi 34.9. Deut. 32.1. Samson, Iudic. 15.18. Samuel, 1. Sam. 12.17. Eccles. 40.19. Dauid, 2. Sam. 22.v. 4.7. 1. Paral. 21.26. Psalm. 17.6. & 18.4. & 31.2. & 116.13. Eccles. 47.6. Elias, 1. Reg. 17. vers. 20, 21. Esaias, 2. Regum 20.11. Ruben, Gad, & dimidia Tribus Manasse, 1. Paral. 5.v.19, 20. Asa, 2. Paral. 14.11. Iosua, Eccles. 46.6. Ezechias, 2. Paral. 32. v.20, 21, 22. Ieremias, Thren. 3.55. Stephanus, Act. 7.60. Vide Deus adorandus: &, Deus inuocandus, &c. ORATIO.
units.tr: INVOCATION of the name of Christ, for the acknowledgement of Christ's deity, 1 Cor. 1.2; 2 Tim. 2.19. Invocation, by synecdoche, for the whole worship of God, 2 Tim. 2.22. The invocation of the name of God is commanded, Ps. 50.15; it is saving, Ps. 20.8; Prov. 18.10; Joel 2.32; Acts 2.21; Rom. 10.13. The invocation of the name of God is a sacrifice pleasing to God, Ps. 116.13. Invocation from faith, Rom. 10.14. Invocation and faith are most closely joined matters, Matt. 21.22; Mark 11.24; James 1.6; 1 John 3.22. The fruit of invocation, Phil. 4.6–7. Examples of invoking God: Seth, Gen. 4.26; Abraham, Gen. 12.8; 13.4; 21.33; Isaac, Gen. 25.21; 26.25; Jacob, Gen. 32.9; Moses, Exod. 34.9; Deut. 32.1; Samson, Judg. 15.18; Samuel, 1 Sam. 12.17; Eccles. 40.19; David, 2 Sam. 22.4, 7; 1 Chr. 21.26; Ps. 17.6; 18.4; 31.2; 116.13; Eccles. 47.6; Elijah, 1 Kgs 17.20–21; Isaiah, 2 Kgs 20.11; Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, 1 Chr. 5.19–20; Asa, 2 Chr. 14.11; Joshua, Eccles. 46.6; Hezekiah, 2 Chr. 32.20–22; Jeremiah, Lam. 3.55; Stephen, Acts 7.60. See "God is to be adored" and "God is to be invoked," etc. PRAYER.

units.la: IOAB filius Sarvia, 2. Sam. 2. v. 13, 18. Princeps militiæ Davidis erat, 8.16. 1. Paral. 27.34. Abner dolo interficit, 2. Samuel. 3.27. Absalonem reducit, 14.23. eum de quercu pendentem confodit, 18.14. Amasiam clam interficit, 20.10. Davidis iussu inuitus populum numerat, 24.4. 1. Paralip. 21.6. Adoniæ regnum ambienti favet, 1. Reg. 1.7. Salomonis iussu occiditur, 2.34. iuxta mandatum Davidis, ver. 5, 6. (i. pater.)
units.tr: JOAB, son of Zeruiah, 2 Sam. 2.13, 18. He was commander of David's army, 2 Sam. 8.16; 1 Chr. 27.34. He treacherously kills Abner, 2 Sam. 3.27. He brings back Absalom, 2 Sam. 14.23. He stabs Absalom while he hangs from an oak, 2 Sam. 18.14. He secretly kills Amasa, 2 Sam. 20.10. Unwillingly, at David's command, he numbers the people, 2 Sam. 24.4; 1 Chr. 21.6. He favours Adonijah, who sought the kingdom, 1 Kgs 1.7. He is killed at Solomon's command, 1 Kgs 2.34, in accordance with David's command, vv. 5–6. (That is, the father.)

units.la: IOACHAS filius Iehu, patri in Regno Israele succedit, 2. Reg. 10.35. impius est, 13. 2. faciem Dei deprecatus exauditur, v. 4. moritur, versic. 9. (apprehendens, aut possidens, aut videns.)
units.tr: JEHOAHAZ, son of Jehu, succeeds his father in the kingdom of Israel, 2 Kgs 10.35. He is impious, 2 Kgs 13.2. Having entreated the face of God, he is heard, v. 4. He dies, v. 9. (Grasping, or possessing, or seeing.)

units.la: IOACHAS, Iosiæ filius, Rex Iuda vngitur, 2. Reg. 23.30. 2. Paral. 36.1. eius captiuitas prædicitur, Ezech. 19. vers. 4, 8. in Aegyptum abducitur, 2. Reg. 23.34. succedit ei frater, 24.8.
units.tr: JEHOAHAZ, son of Josiah, is anointed king of Judah, 2 Kgs 23.30; 2 Chr. 36.1. His captivity is foretold, Ezek. 19.4, 8. He is carried off into Egypt, 2 Kgs 23.34. His brother succeeds him, 2 Kgs 24.8.

units.la: IOACHIN, qui & Iechonias, Rex Iuda constituitur, 2. Reg. 24.6. 2. Paral. 36.8. cum matre & uxoribus Babylonem transfertur, 2. Reg. 24.15. 2. Paral. 36.10. e carcere educitur, & ad honores euehitur, 2. Reg. 25.27. Ierem. 52.31. appel-
units.tr: JEHOIACHIN, also called Jeconiah, is set up as king of Judah, 2 Kgs 24.6; 2 Chr. 36.8. He is carried to Babylon with his mother and wives, 2 Kgs 24.15; 2 Chr. 36.10. He is led out of prison and raised to honour, 2 Kgs 25.27; Jer. 52.31. He is cal-

units.la: latur Iehonias, 37.1. appellatur Neri, Lucæ 3.27. succedit ei patruus Matthanias, 2. Reg. 24.17. (Iehoiakim. 1. Domini resurrectio.)
units.tr: …is called Jehoiachin, Jer. 37.1. He is called Neri, Luke 3.27. His uncle Mattaniah succeeds him, 2 Kings 24.17. (Jehoiakim: i.e. the resurrection of the Lord.)

units.la: IOACIM, qui & Eliacim, filius Iosiæ, Rex Iuda constituitur, 2. Reg. 23.34. 2. Paral. 36.4. eius ruina prædicitur, Ierem. 22.18. Ieremiæ volumen comburi iubet, 36.23. vinctus Babylonem transportatur, 2. Paralip. 36.6. moritur, 2. Reg. 24.6. eius sepultura ignominiosa, Ieremiæ 22.19. & 36.30.
units.tr: JEHOIAKIM, also called Eliakim, son of Josiah, is made king of Judah, 2 Kings 23.34; 2 Chron. 36.4. His downfall is foretold, Jer. 22.18. He orders Jeremiah's scroll to be burned, 36.23. He is carried off to Babylon in chains, 2 Chron. 36.6. He dies, 2 Kings 24.6. His burial is shameful, Jer. 22.19 and 36.30.

units.la: IOADAN, vel (vt alij legunt) Ioiadan, Amasiæ Regis Iuda mater, 2. Reg. 14.2. 2. Paral. 25.1. (i. Domini deliciæ)
units.tr: JEHOADDAN, or (as others read) Jehoiada, mother of King Amaziah of Judah, 2 Kings 14.2; 2 Chron. 25.1. (i.e. the delight of the Lord.)

units.la: IOANNA vxor Chusæ sequitur Christum, Luc. 8.3. & 24.10.
units.tr: JOANNA, wife of Chuza, follows Christ, Luke 8.3 and 24.10.

units.la: IO ANNES, Vide IOHANNES.
units.tr: JOHANNES. See JOHN.

units.la: IOAS, Gedeonis pater, Iudic. 6.11. Cultores Baal de suo a Gedeone confracto idolo conquerentes irridet, v.31. eiúsque patronis mortem minatur, ibid.
units.tr: JOASH, father of Gideon, Judg. 6.11. He mocks the worshippers of Baal, who complain that Gideon has smashed their idol, v.31. He threatens death to their defenders, ibid.

units.la: IOAS, Ochosiæ filius, natu minimus, a Iosaphat ne interficiatur, adhuc puer a sorore absconditur, 2. Reg. 11.2. 2. Par. 22. 1. regno Iudæ inauguratur, 2. Reg. 11.12.2. paral. 23.11. eius pietas, 2. Reg. 12.2. a servis occiditur, & quare, v.21. 2. paral. 24.25. sepultura eius minimè regia: ibid.
units.tr: JOASH, son of Ahaziah, the youngest, is hidden from being killed by Jehoshaphat. While still a boy he is hidden by his sister, 2 Kings 11.2; 2 Chron. 22. He is anointed king of Judah, 2 Kings 11.12; 2 Chron. 23.11. His piety, 2 Kings 12.2. He is killed by his servants, and the reason why, v.21; 2 Chron. 24.25. His burial was by no means royal, ibid.

units.la: IOAS, filius Ioachaz, Rex Israel, patri succedit, 2. Regum 13. v. 9.10. eius impietas, v.11. insolens eius ad Amasiam regē Iuda responsum, 14.9.2. Paral. 25.18. eius in eundem victoria, 2. Regnum 14.12.2. Paral. 25.22.23. capto Amasia, Ierusalé ingreditur, expilat, & eius muri partem euertit, 2. Reg. 14, v.13 14.2 Paral. 25. v.23.24. moritur, 2 Reg. 13.13. & 14, 16. (Iehoas. 1. fundamentum Domini).
units.tr: JOASH, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, succeeds his father, 2 Kings 13.9-10. His impiety, v.11. His insolent reply to Amaziah king of Judah, 2 Kings 14.9; 2 Chron. 25.18. His victory over the same, 2 Kings 14.12; 2 Chron. 25.22-23. Having captured Amaziah, he enters Jerusalem, plunders it, and breaks down part of its walls, 2 Kings 14.13-14; 2 Chron. 25.23-24. He dies, 2 Kings 13.13 and 14.16. (Jehoash: i.e. the foundation of the Lord.)

units.la: IOATHAN, filius Gedeonis postremus, manus Abimelech euadit, Iudic. 9.5. de electo Abimelech Rege apud Sichimitas conqueritur, 9. v.7.8.9. &c. eis imprecatur, v.19.20. (Iothan. 1. Domini perfectio.)
units.tr: JOTHAM, youngest son of Gideon, escapes the hand of Abimelech, Judg. 9.5. He complains to the Shechemites about their elected king Abimelech, 9.7-9 etc. He curses them, v.19-20. (Jotham: i.e. the perfection of the Lord.)

units.la: IOATHAN, filius Hoziæ, in regno Iuda patri succedit, 2. Reg. 15.32.2. Paral. 26.23. vincit Ammonitas, 27.5. moritur, 2 Reg. 15 38.2. Paral. 27.9. Cui successit Achaz: ibid.
units.tr: JOTHAM, son of Uzziah, succeeds his father on the throne of Judah, 2 Kings 15.32; 2 Chron. 26.23. He conquers the Ammonites, 27.5. He dies, 2 Kings 15.38; 2 Chron. 27.9. Ahaz succeeded him, ibid.

units.la: IOB pius & rectus, Iob. 1.1. & 2.3. & 27.6. & 29.12. ditissimus est, 1.3. vlcere pessimo percutitur. 2.7. ab amicis inuisitur, vers. 11. miserè afflictus diei suo maledicit, 3.1. de sui mali gravitate queritur, 6.2. mortem optat, v.8.9. & 7.15. & 10. v.1.18. amicos suos temeritatis arguit, 6.25. se a fratribus & familiaribus destitutum queritur, v.13.15. & 19. v.13.14. insomniis & visionibus terretur, 7.14. blasphemiç ab amicis arguitur,15.5.& 19. 6. & 34. 37. peccatum suum agnoscit,42.6. orans pro amicis,exauditur,v.10. duplo ditior,quàm fuerat ante,redditur,v.10. moritur,v.17. eius patientia celebratur , 1ac.5 11 (.i.dolens,gemens.)
units.tr: JOB, upright and righteous, Job 1.1; 2.3; 27.6; 29.12. He is very wealthy, 1.3. He is struck with a most grievous ulcer, 2.7. He is shunned by his friends, v.11. Miserably afflicted, he curses his day, 3.1. He complains of the severity of his suffering, 6.2. He longs for death, v.8-9; 7.15; 10.1, 18. He rebukes his friends for their rashness, 6.25. He complains that he has been abandoned by brothers and familiar friends, v.13, 15, 19; 19.13-14. He is terrified by dreams and visions, 7.14. His friends accuse him of blasphemy, 15.5; 19.6; 34.37. He acknowledges his sin, 42.6. Praying for his friends, he is heard, v.10. He is restored twice as rich as before, v.10. He dies, v.17. His patience is celebrated, James 5.11. (i.e. grieving, groaning.)

units.la: OCHEBED , vxor Amram, Exod.6.20.Num.26.59.nata ex Leui in AEgypto,ibid. Mater Aaronis, Mosis & Mariae. Exodi 6.20.Numer.26 59.(i. Domini gloria vel grauitas.)
units.tr: JOCHEBED, wife of Amram, Exod. 6.20; Num. 26.59. Born of Levi in Egypt, ibid. Mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam, Exod. 6.20; Num. 26.59. (i.e. the glory or gravity of the Lord.)

units.la: IOEL , Phatuelis filius aduersus Iudam vaticinatur , Ioel.1. 1.visibilem Spiritus Sancti gratiam praedicit,2.v.28.29.adimpletur,Act.2 17.(i.Incipiens.)
units.tr: JOEL, son of Pethuel, prophesies against Judah, Joel 1.1. He foretells the visible grace of the Holy Spirit, 2.28-29. It is fulfilled, Acts 2.17. (i.e. beginning.)

units.la: IOHANNAN filius Carea Godoliam,vt sibi ab Israele caueat, in tempore mouens reiicitur , tanquam falsus accusator, Iere.40 v.13. 14. occiso Godolia ad eum reliquiae Iudaeorum confugiunt,41.14.ad Ieremiam eas adducere, vt pro illis Deum oret & consulat , rogat , 42,v.1.2.3. Ieremiam falsum loqui ait,43.2. Ieremiam cum toto populo in AEgyptum abducit,v.5.6.7.
units.tr: JOHANAN, son of Kareah, warns Gedaliah to beware of Israel (Ishmael), but since he speaks at the wrong time he is rejected as a false accuser, Jer. 40.13-14. After Gedaliah is killed, the remnant of the Jews flee to him, 41.14. They ask him to bring them to Jeremiah, so that he may pray and consult God on their behalf, 42.1-3. He says Jeremiah speaks falsely, 43.2. He leads Jeremiah away with the whole people into Egypt, v.5-7.

units.la: IOHANNA,Vide IOANNA.
units.tr: JOANNA. See JOANNA.

units.la: IOHANNES Baptista, promissus, Malach.3.1.& 4. 5.in vtero matris Spiritu S. repletus, Lucae 1. 15. in vtero matris exultat,v.41.44. nascitur,v.57.circumciditur,v.59. a Deo missus,Ioann.1.6. vocatur Angelus,Matth.11.10.Marc.1.2. Luc. 7. 27. Elias , Matth. 11.14.& 17. verf.13. Mar. 9. 13. non propheta , Ioann.1.21.ideoque negat se esse Eliam. ibid.1 Iudaei enim expectabant Eliae Thesbitae,ex loco Malach. 4. 5. sed spiritu & virtute Eliae , vt explicatur Lucae 1.17. vocatur item lucerna,Ioann.5.35. Propheta Christi , Luc.1.76. plusquam Propheta dicitur, Matth.11.9.Lucae 7.26.negat se esse Christum , Ioan.1.20. & 3. 28. (Iohanan. i. gratiosus apud Deum Graecè Ἰωάννης.)
units.tr: JOHN the Baptist, promised, Mal. 3.1 and 4.5. Filled with the Holy Spirit in his mother's womb, Luke 1.15. He leaps in the womb, v.41, 44. He is born, v.57. He is circumcised, v.59. Sent by God, John 1.6. He is called an angel, Matt. 11.10; Mark 1.2; Luke 7.27. Elijah, Matt. 11.14 and 17.12; Mark 9.13. Not a prophet, John 1.21, and therefore he denies that he is Elijah, ibid. For the Jews expected Elijah the Tishbite, from the passage in Mal. 4.5, but he came in the spirit and power of Elijah, as Luke 1.17 explains. He is also called a lamp, John 5.35. He is the prophet of Christ, Luke 1.76. He is said to be more than a prophet, Matt. 11.9; Luke 7.26. He denies that he is Christ, John 1.20; 3.28. (Johanan: i.e. gracious before God. In Greek [Ἰωάννης].)

units.la: Initium praedicationis Iohannis Baptistae , Matth. 3.1. loci in quibus ministerium suum exercuit , v. 6. Marc.1. 4.Lucae 1. 80. Ioann.3.23.in deserto habitasse,quo sensu dicatur , Vide DESERTVM. eius in cultu & victu austeritas,Matth. 3 4.Marc.1.9.nec edisse , nec bibisse dicitur, figurata ἐν ἐρήμῳ oratione , communi videlicet caeterorum hominum more , Matth.11.18.eius in arguendo Herode magnanimitas,14.4.Marc.6.18.Luc.3.19.officium, Esa.40.3.Matth.3.3.Marc.1.3,Luc.1.v.16. 76. & 3.4.& 7.27. Ioan.1.v.7.22.31.& 3.28.& 5.75. Iohannis & Christi collatio, Marc. 1.7. Luc. 3.16. Act. 13,25. & 19.4. mors, Matth. 14. 10. Marc. 6.27. sepultura, Matt. 14.12. Marc. 6.29. in Baptil-ma Iohannis baptizari quid sit Vide Baptizare.
units.tr: The beginning of John the Baptist's preaching, Matt. 3.1. The places where he exercised his ministry, v.6; Mark 1.4; Luke 1.80; John 3.23. That he dwelt in the wilderness, and in what sense this is said, see DESERT. His austerity in dress and food, Matt. 3.4; Mark 1.6. It is said that he neither ate nor drank, a figurative manner of speaking in the wilderness [ἐν ἐρήμῳ], that is, in the common way of other men, Matt. 11.18. His magnanimity in rebuking Herod, Matt. 14.4; Mark 6.18; Luke 3.19. His office, Isa. 40.3; Matt. 3.3; Mark 1.3; Luke 1.16, 76; 3.4; 7.27; John 1.7, 22, 31; 3.28; 5.33. The comparison of John and Christ, Mark 1.7; Luke 3.16; Acts 13.25; 19.4. His death, Matt. 14.10; Mark 6.27. His burial, Matt. 14.12; Mark 6.29. On what is meant by the baptism of John, see BAPTIZE.

units.la: IOHANNES Zebedei filius, vocatur à Christo, Matt. 4.21. Mar. 1.19. Luc. 5.9. Christo dilectus est, Ioan. 13:23. & 19.26. & 20.2. & 21.20. in Samariam mittitur, Act. 8.14. se Christi seruum vocat, Apoc. 1.1.
units.tr: JOHN, son of Zebedee, is called by Christ, Matt. 4.21; Mark 1.19; Luke 5.9. He is loved by Christ, John 13.23; 19.26; 20.2; 21.20. He is sent to Samaria, Acts 8.14. He calls himself a servant of Christ, Rev. 1.1.

units.la: IOHANNES, qui & Marcus, Actor. 12.12. à Paulo & Barnaba cooptatur, v. 25. & 13.5. ab iis dimissus Ierosolymam redit, vers. 13. Barnabam solum comitatur, 15. v. 37. 39.
units.tr: JOHN, who is also called Mark, Acts 12.12. He is taken on by Paul and Barnabas, v.25; 13.5. Dismissed by them, he returns to Jerusalem, v.13. He accompanies only Barnabas, 15.37, 39.

units.la: IOIDA Sacerdos cum Centurionibus & Decurionibus de liberandis religione & rege, sanctè conspirat, 2. Reg. 11. 4. 2. Paral. 23. 1. illis Dauidis arma distribuit, 2 Reg. 11. 10. 2. Paral. 23. 9. Regem in medium prolatum inungit, & impositâ corona consecrat, 2. Reg. 11. 12. 2. Paral. 22. 11. Athaliam è templo detrusam occidi iuber, 2. Reg. 11. 15. 2. Paral. 23. 14. de vero Dei cultu restituendo cum Rege & Populo pacisci tur, 2 Reg. 11. 17. 2 Paral. 23. 16. eo docente & viuente Rex pietatem colit, 2 Reg. 12. 2. 2. Paral. 24. 2. Vxorem ex stirpe regia duxerat, 2 Paral. 22. 11. moritur, 24. 15. regio sepulchro propter vitae sanctimoniam honoratur, 24. 16. eo mortuo Principes adulatores Regis mores corrumpùt, v. 17. 18. (Iehoiad a. i. scientia Domini.)
units.tr: JEHOIADA the priest, with the centurions and captains, holily conspires about freeing the religion and the king, 2 Kings 11.4; 2 Chron. 23.1. He distributes David's weapons to them, 2 Kings 11.10; 2 Chron. 23.9. He anoints the king, brought out into the open, and consecrates him by placing a crown on him, 2 Kings 11.12; 2 Chron. 22.11. He orders Athaliah thrust out of the temple and killed, 2 Kings 11.15; 2 Chron. 23.14. He makes a covenant with the king and people to restore the true worship of God, 2 Kings 11.17; 2 Chron. 23.16. While he teaches and lives, the king cultivates piety, 2 Kings 12.2; 2 Chron. 24.2. He had married a wife from the royal stock, 2 Chron. 22.11. He dies, 24.15. He is honoured with a royal tomb for the holiness of his life, 24.16. After his death the flattering princes corrupt the king's morals, v.17-18. (Jehoiada: i.e. knowledge of the Lord.)

units.la: IONADAB prudens, carnalis, & nequam, Ammonis amicus, 2 Sam. 13. 3. mali consilij Amnomi autor est, v. 5. (i. Domini munificentia.)
units.tr: JONADAB, prudent, carnal and wicked, a friend of Amnon, 2 Sam. 13.3. He is the author of Amnon's evil counsel, v.5. (i.e. the bounty of the Lord.)

units.la: IONADAB, filius Rechab, Iehu partes in delenda idololatria sequitur, 2 Reg. 10 v. 15. 16. 17.
units.tr: JONADAB, son of Rechab, follows Jehu in destroying idolatry, 2 Kings 10.15, 16, 17.

units.la: IONAS (Ionah. 1. columba) Propheta, 2 Reg. 14. 25. vocatio Ionae, Ion. 1. 1. eam vt fugiat, in Tharsim se recipit, v. 3. in mare deiicitur, v. 15. à pisce absorbetur, 2. 1. eius ventre tribus naturalibus diebus continetur, v. 2. illinc Deum orans exauditur, v. 3. & liberatur, v. 11. Niniuitis suam praedicit ruinam, 3. 4. Ionas typus Christi, Matt. 12. 39. 40. & 16. 4. Luc. 11. 30. Ionae ira, & eius oratio ob Niniuen seruatam, 4. v. 1. 2. à Deo damnatur, v. 4.
units.tr: JONAH (Jonah: i.e. a dove), prophet, 2 Kings 14.25. The call of Jonah, Jonah 1.1. To escape it, he takes ship for Tarshish, v.3. He is thrown into the sea, v.15. He is swallowed by a fish, 2.1. He remains in its belly for three natural days, v.2. From there he prays to God and is heard, v.3, and delivered, v.11. He foretells the ruin of the Ninevites, 3.4. Jonah is a type of Christ, Matt. 12.39-40; 16.4; Luke 11.30. Jonah's anger, and his prayer because Nineveh was spared, 4.1-2. He is rebuked by God, v.4.

units.la: IONATHAN, Mosis ex Gersone nepos, idoli Sacerdos, Iudic. 18. 30. (1. à Deo datus, vel Domini donum.)
units.tr: JONATHAN, grandson of Moses through Gershom, a priest of an idol, Judg. 18.30. (i.e. given by God, or the gift of the Lord.)

units.la: IONATHAN Dauidis patruus, gigantem viginti quatuor digitos in manibus, & pedibus habentem occidit, 1. Paral. 20. v. 6. 7. eius prudentia laudatur, 27. 32.
units.tr: JONATHAN, David's nephew, killed a giant who had twenty-four digits on his hands and feet, 1 Chron. 20.6-7. His prudence is praised, 27.32.

units.la: IONA-
units.tr: IONA-

units.la: NATHAS Sauli filius amabilis,2 Sam.1.26.cum Armigero Philisthæos profligat,1. Sam.14.13.propter mel gustatum à patre morte damnatur, v.44.à populo liberatur, v.45. Dauidem excusat,20.28. Dauidem profugum solatur,23.16.in prælio occumbit,31.2.2. Sam. 1. 4. plangitur à Dauide,v.17.26.
units.tr: NATHAN, Saul's beloved son (2 Sam. 1.26), defeats the Philistines with his armour-bearer (1 Sam. 14.13). He is condemned to death by his father for tasting honey (v.44), and is freed by the people (v.45). He defends David (20.28) and comforts him in his flight (23.16). He falls in battle (31.2; 2 Sam. 1.4) and is mourned by David (v.17.26).

units.la: PPE,1.pulchri tudo : Oppidum Palestinæ maritimum, in tribu Dan.Act.9.36.
units.tr: JOPPA, beauty: a maritime town of Palestine, in the tribe of Dan. Acts 9.36.

units.la: RAM, filius Iosaphat, regnum auspicatur,super Iehuda 2. Reg.8.16.2 Paral.21.1. occidit fratres suos,v.4. impietatem Achabi sequitur. v.6. Ob quam grauissime punitur v.12.ad finem vsque miserrimè moritur,v.19. ignominiosè sepelitur : v.19.20.
units.tr: JEHORAM, son of Jehoshaphat, begins his reign over Judah (2 Kings 8.16; 2 Chron. 21.1). He kills his brothers (v.4) and follows the impiety of Ahab (v.6). For this he is most severely punished (v.12). At the end he dies most miserably (v.19) and is buried dishonourably (v.19.20).

units.la: RAM Rex Israel,in locum demortui fratris vngitur, 2. Regum 1.17.impius est 3 v.2 3.àIehu occiditur,9.24.(Iehoram.1. Domino s excelsus).
units.tr: JEHORAM, king of Israel, is anointed in place of his dead brother (2 Kings 1.17). He is impious (3, v.2.3) and is killed by Jehu (9.24). (Jehoram: the Lord is exalted.)

units.la: ORDANIS fluuius, filiorum Ruben terminus, Iosue 13.23. irrigua est eius regio,Genesis 13.10.ad Leuitarum ingressum diuiditur, Ios.3.v 15.16. eum siccis pedibus transeunt Israelitæ,v.17.in eo baptizat Ioannes Baptista populum, Matthæi 3.6. Marc.1.5. Christum, Matth.3.13. Mar.1.9. Lucæ 3.21. Ioann.1.32.in Iordane lauatur Naaman,& sanatur,2 Regum 5.14. (Iarden.i.riuus iudicij.)
units.tr: JORDAN, a river, the boundary of the sons of Reuben (Josh. 13.23). Its region is well watered (Gen. 13.10). It is divided when the Levites enter (Josh. 3.15.16), and the Israelites cross it on dry feet (v.17). In it John the Baptist baptises the people (Matt. 3.6; Mark 1.5) and Christ (Matt. 3.13; Mark 1.9; Luke 3.21; John 1.32). In the Jordan Naaman washes and is healed (2 Kings 5.14). (Jarden: a river of judgement.)

units.la: OSAPHAT, filius Asæ, regnum Iuda sortitur, 1 Regum 15. 24.2. Paral.17.1. initium regni eius, 1 Regum 22 41.eius cum Achabo affinitas, 2 Paral 18.1. pietas, 2 Regum 3.11. 2.Paral 17.7. &20.v.3 5.6.31-32. quòd Achabo affinis impio opem tulerit, reprehenditur, 2 Paral.19 2.quòd cum Ochosia amicitiam inierit, reprehenditur, 20.37. moritur,1 Reg.22.51.2.Paral.21.1.(i. Domini iudicium).
units.tr: JEHOSHAPHAT, son of Asa, receives the kingdom of Judah (1 Kings 15.24; 2 Chron. 17.1). The beginning of his reign (1 Kings 22.41). His marriage alliance with Ahab (2 Chron. 18.1). His piety (2 Kings 3.11; 2 Chron. 17.7; 20.3.5.6.31-32). He is rebuked because he gave help to Ahab, an impious man (2 Chron. 19.2). He is rebuked because he made friendship with Ahaziah (20.37). He dies (1 Kings 22.51; 2 Chron. 21.1). (Jehoshaphat: the judgement of the Lord.)

units.la: IOSEPH( hoc est,addat, vel addet auferenti probrum,nimirum Iosepho nato, alterum) Iacobi filius ex Rachele, Gene. 30.v.23.24. Fratres accusat,37.2. præ fratribus a patre diligitur, v.3 4. somnia sua fratribus indicat,v.6.7. Hinc eorum sibi invidiam conflat,v.8.ab illis venditur Ismaelitis,v.28.Dei timore præditus, flagitium cum hera committere recusat, 39.9.ab ea falso accusatus, v.17.carceri includitur, v.20.formosus erat 39.6.&49.22.somnia interpretatur, 40.12.è carcere eductus, Regis somnia exponit,41.v.25.26. Saphenath Paneah appellatur,hoc est, occulta reuelans aut(vt veteri interpreti placet)Salvator mundi,v.45.
units.tr: JOSEPH (that is, "he will add", or "he will add to the one who takes away reproach", namely, another son born to Joseph), son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30.23.24). He accuses his brothers (37.2) and is loved by his father above them (v.3.4). He tells his dreams to his brothers (v.6.7), and so stirs up their envy against himself (v.8). They sell him to the Ishmaelites (v.28). Endowed with the fear of God, he refuses to commit a crime with his mistress (39.9). She falsely accuses him (v.17), and he is shut up in prison (v.20). He was handsome (39.6; 49.22). He interprets dreams (40.12). Brought out of prison, he explains the king's dreams (41.25.26). He is called Saphenath Paneah, that is, one who reveals hidden things, or (as the old translator prefers) the Saviour of the world (v.45).

units.la: vniuersæ Aegypto administrandæ præficitur, v.41.(Psal. 105. 21.) Vxorem in Aegypto ducit, v.45. Fratribus se agnoscendum præbet, 45.3. Actor.7.13. patrem accersit, Genef.45.9. ei obuiam proficiscitur, 46.29. benedicitur à patre, 49.22. Deut.33 13. primogenituræ ius assequitur, 1.Paral.5.2. sepelit patrem in terra Chanaan, Genesis 50.13.14. benignus est erga fratres, v.21. vt ossa sua ex suo arbitrio sepeliant, fratres adiurat, ver. 25. moritur, ver. 26. eius ossa Chanaan delata, in Sichem sepeliuntur, Exodi 13 19. Josue 24.32. Joseph, pro Tribu Ephrain, Apo cal.7.8. [pro omnibus tribubus Psal.78,67.&80.2.&81.6. Abd.2.18. Zach,12.6. Pro decem tribubus, Ezech 37.16.19, Amos,5.v.6.15.&6 6.] Josephi fides: Heb.11.22.
units.tr: He is placed over the whole administration of Egypt (v.41; Ps. 105.21). He takes a wife in Egypt (v.45). He makes himself known to his brothers (45.3; Acts 7.13). He summons his father (Gen. 45.9) and goes out to meet him (46.29). He is blessed by his father (49.22; Deut. 33.13). He obtains the right of the firstborn (1 Chron. 5.2). He buries his father in the land of Canaan (Gen. 50.13.14). He is kind to his brothers (v.21). He binds his brothers by oath to bury his bones at their own discretion (v.25). He dies (v.26). His bones are carried to Canaan and buried in Shechem (Exod. 13.19; Josh. 24.32). Joseph stands for the tribe of Ephraim (Apoc. 7.8). [He stands for all the tribes: Ps. 78.67; 80.2; 81.6; Obad. 18; Zech. 12.6. For the ten tribes: Ezek. 37.16.19; Amos 5.6.15; 6.6.] The faith of Joseph: Heb. 11.22.

units.la: IOSEPH, Mariæ Deiparæ Virginis maritus, vir iustus, Matth. 1.19. in somniis ab Angelo, ne repudiet vxorem Mariam, monetur, v.20. ei obtemperat, v.24. in Ægyptum fugit, eoque Filium Dei transfert, Matthæi 2.14. hinc ab Angelo reuocatur, v.19.20. dicitur Pater Christi, Luc.2.v.27.33 41.48. ex vulgi potiùs opinione, quàm quòd res erat: expresse enim additur; Eum putatiuum fuisse Christi Patrem, Lucæ 3 23. (Vbi obseruetur regula illa vsitata: Sacræ scripturæ sæpe magis loquuntur de rebus ipsis secundùm vulgi opinionem, & hominum iudicium, quàm secùdùm rei existentiam. Sic spectrum Diabolicum Sauli excitatum vocatur Samuel, 1. Sam.28.15. Herodes Antipas, qui Tetrarcha tantùm erat, Rex appellatur, Marci 6.14. Euangelium stultitia dicitur, 1 Corinth.1.18. Sic & Christus Ioseph filius dicitur, Lucæ 4.22,&c.) Ioseph faber erat, Matth.13 55. Marc.6.3.
units.tr: JOSEPH, husband of Mary the Virgin, Mother of God, a just man (Matt. 1.19). In dreams an angel warns him not to put away his wife Mary (v.20). He obeys (v.24). He flees into Egypt, and so carries the Son of God there (Matt. 2.14). Hence he is recalled by the angel (v.19.20). He is called the father of Christ (Luke 2.27.33; 41.48). This is said rather according to common opinion than because it was so, for it is expressly added that he was supposed to be the father of Christ (Luke 3.23). (Here observe the usual rule: Holy Scripture often speaks of things according to the opinion of the common people and human judgement, rather than according to their actual existence. Thus the devilish spectre raised for Saul is called Samuel (1 Sam. 28.15). Herod Antipas, who was only tetrarch, is called king (Mark 6.14). The gospel is called foolishness (1 Cor. 1.18). So also Christ is called the son of Joseph (Luke 4.22, etc.).) Joseph was a carpenter (Matt. 13.55; Mark 6.3).

units.la: IOSEPH Arimathæus, Senator prudens & honestus, Luc. 23 50. is à Pilato corpus Christi petit, Matth.27.ver.57.58. Marc.15 43 Luc.23 v.51.52. Ion.19.38.
units.tr: JOSEPH of Arimathea, a prudent and honourable senator (Luke 23.50). He asks Pilate for the body of Christ (Matt. 27.57.58; Mark 15.43; Luke 23.51.52; John 19.38).

units.la: IOSEPH, qui & Barsabas, vnà cum Matthia eligitur Apostolus, Act.1.23. Idem cognominatus est Iustus, ver.23.
units.tr: JOSEPH, also called Barsabas, is chosen apostle together with Matthias (Acts 1.23). The same man was surnamed Justus (v.23).

units.la: IOSES, Barnabas ab Apostolis cognominatur, & quare, Act.4.36. precium agri venditi Apostolis tradit, ver.37.
units.tr: JOSES: Barnabas is surnamed by the apostles, and why (Acts 4.36). He hands over the price of the field he sold to the apostles (v.37).

units.la: IOSIAS filius Amon, Rex Iuda constituitur, 2 Reg. 21.24. 2. Paral.33 25. vir pius est, 34.3. coram populo Deuteronomium legit, 2 Regum. 23.2. idola euertit, v.4.2.Paral.34. 4. Sacerdotes Baal occidit, 2. Reg.23.20. verum Dei cultum restituit, 2 Paral.34.33 Phase celebrat, 2, Reg.23.21. 2 Paral 35.1. aduersus Regem Ægypti, contra Dei verbum bum dimicare attentat, v. 22. in prælio vulnus accipit, v. 23. moritur, 2 Reg. 23. 29. 2 Paral. 35. 24. sepelitur à populo, & lugetur, ibid. (Iosiahu. 1. incensum seu thymiama Domini.)
units.tr: JOSIAH, son of Amon, is set up as king of Judah (2 Kings 21.24; 2 Chron. 33.25). He is a pious man (34.3). He reads Deuteronomy before the people (2 Kings 23.2). He overturns the idols (v.4; 2 Chron. 34.4). He kills the priests of Baal (2 Kings 23.20). He restores the true worship of God (2 Chron. 34.33). He celebrates the Passover (2 Kings 23.21; 2 Chron. 35.1). He attempts to fight against the king of Egypt, contrary to the word of God (v.22). He receives a wound in battle (v.23) and dies (2 Kings 23.29; 2 Chron. 35.24). He is buried by the people and mourned (ibid.). (Josiah: the incense of the Lord.)

units.la: IOSVA, qui & Iosue, filius Num. Exod. 33. 11. Minister Mosis, Exodi 24. 13. Iosue 1. 1. cum Caleb fideliter terram explorat, Numer. 14. 6. Dux populi loco Mosis constituitur, 27. 18. Deuter. 3. 28. & 31, 7. terram Israelitis dividere iubetur, Iosu. 13. 7. moritur, Iudic. 2. 8. Iosue à Græcis Iesus dictus, Heb. 4. 8.
units.tr: JOSHUA, also called Joshua, son of Nun (Num. 33.11; Exod. 33.11 [sic]). He is Moses' minister (Exod. 24.13; Josh. 1.1). With Caleb he faithfully spies out the land (Num. 14.6). He is appointed leader of the people in place of Moses (Num. 27.18; Deut. 3.28; 31.7). He is ordered to divide the land among the Israelites (Josh. 13.7). He dies (Judg. 2.8). Joshua is called Iesus by the Greeks (Heb. 4.8).

units.la: IOSVE, qui & Iesus, filius Iosedech, cum fratribus Altare instaurat, 1 Esdr. 3. 2. monitu Aggæi Prophetæ, Templo instaurando manum admouet, Agg. 1. v. 2. 14. typus Christi est, Zich. 3. v. 1. 2. 3.
units.tr: JESHUA, also called Jesus, son of Jehozadak. With his brothers he restores the altar (1 Esdras 3.2), at the urging of the prophet Haggai he puts his hand to the rebuilding of the Temple (Hag. 1.2.14), and he is a type of Christ (Zech. 3.1.2.3).

units.la: IPSE, pronomen, pro ipse Dominus, Hebr. 13. 3.
units.tr: IPSE, a pronoun, standing for "the Lord himself" (Heb. 13.3).

units.la: [ipse de Messia expressè dictum, Genes. 3. 15. & 49. 10. Deut. 18. 15. 2. Sam. 7. 14. Psal. 22. v. 29. 31. & 45. 12. & 72. v. 15. 17. & 89. 27. Esai. 11. 10. & 53. v. 4. 5. &c. In N. T. sæpissime de Christo pronomen hoc αὐτὸς positum legitur. Et de Spiritu S. Rom. 8. v. 16. 26.]
units.tr: [IPSE is said expressly of the Messiah: Gen. 3.15; 49.10; Deut. 18.15; 2 Sam. 7.14; Ps. 22.29.31; 45.12; 72.15.17; 89.27; Isa. 11.10; 53.4.5, etc. In the New Testament this pronoun, αὐτὸς [autos], is very often found used of Christ, and of the Holy Spirit (Rom. 8.16.26).]

units.la: IRA, pro irati Dei iudicio, & iræ diuinæ effectis: hoc est, pœnis & calamitatibus, quæ ab irato Deo peccatoribus irrogantur, seu pro iis effectis, ex quibus iratus esse Deus intelligitur: ut solet Scriptura ἀνθρωπότροπως de Deo loqui, Matth. 3. 7. Lucæ 21. 23. Rom. 2. 5 & 4. 15. & 5. 9. Ephes. 5. 6. 1 Thess. 1. 10. & 5. 9. pro vltione, seu vindicatione, qua Dominus terribiliter iratus, tandem mundum vlciscetur, Coloss. 3. 6.
units.tr: IRA (wrath) is used for the judgement of an angry God and for the effects of divine wrath, that is, the punishments and calamities which an angry God inflicts on sinners, or for those effects by which God is understood to be angry. Scripture is accustomed to speak of God in human terms (Matt. 3.7; Luke 21.23; Rom. 2.5; 4.15; 5.9; Eph. 5.6; 1 Thess. 1.10; 5.9). It is also used for vengeance or punishment, by which the Lord, terribly angry, will at last avenge the world (Col. 3.6).

units.la: Latiori significatione iræ nomen potest referri ad omnes animi offensiones, 1 Timoth. 2. 8. quæ prohibeant, quò minus bona conscientia Deum possimus invocare, ut Matth. 5. 23. sub qua specie comprehendi etiam possunt reliquæ iniuriæ, quibus affici potest proximus, de quibus Esaiæ 1. v. 15. 16.
units.tr: In a wider sense the name of wrath can refer to all offences of the mind (1 Tim. 2.8) which prevent us from calling upon God with a good conscience (Matt. 5.23). Under this heading can also be included the other injuries with which a neighbour may be affected, concerning which see Isa. 1.15.16.

units.la: Iræ Dei exempla: Contra antiquiorem mundum, diluuium, Genes. 7. 17. contra ædificatores turris Babylonicæ linguarum confusio, 11. 7. Sodoman, &c. sulphureus ignis & subuersio, 19. 24. Vxorem Loth non obedientem voci Dei, mira in statuam salis metamorphosis, ver. 26. tot & tanta prodigia in Ægypto facta, sunt manifestissima iræ diuinæ testimonia, vt latè describuntur Exodi 7. 8. 9. cap. contra Moisen, Exod. 4. 14. Deut. 3. 26. & 4. 21. Israelitas. Exodi 32. xodi 32.v.9.10.Num.11.1.& 25.3.& 32.13.Iudic.2.v.14.20.& 3.8.& 10.7.2.Sam.24.1.2. Reg.13.3 & 17.18. & 23.26. Esai, 5.25. & 47.6. Ose. 8.5. Zach.1.v.12.& 10.3. Aaronem & Mariam.Num.12.9.Aaronem.Deut.9.20.Balaam, Numer.22.22. Ozam, 2.Sam.6.v.7.8.Danidem & israelitas, 24.1.1.Par.27.24.Salomonem,1.Reg.11.9. Ierusalem & Iudam.2.Reg.24.20.1.Paral.27.24.Iosaphat.2.Par.19.2.Ierusalem, &c.propter Ioas,2.Par.24.18.Amasiam,25.15. Ezechiam,32.25.Pastores,Zach.10.3. interfectores & illusores seruorum suorum,Matt.22.7. Vide Dei ira.
units.tr: Examples of God's wrath: against the old world, the flood (Gen. 7.17); against the builders of the Tower of Babel, the confusion of tongues (11.7); against Sodom etc., sulphurous fire and overthrow (19.24); against Lot's wife, who did not obey the voice of God, a wondrous transformation into a pillar of salt (v.26). So many and such great prodigies done in Egypt are the clearest testimonies of divine wrath, as is described at length in Exod. chs. 7, 8, 9. Against Moses (Exod. 4.14; Deut. 3.26; 4.21). Against the Israelites (Exod. 32.9.10; Num. 11.1; 25.3; 32.13; Judg. 2.14.20; 3.8; 10.7; 2 Sam. 24.1; 1 Kings 13.3; 17.18; 23.26; Isa. 5.25; 47.6; Hos. 8.5; Zech. 1.12; 10.3). Against Aaron and Miriam (Num. 12.9); against Aaron (Deut. 9.20); against Balaam (Num. 22.22); against Uzzah (2 Sam. 6.7.8); against David and the Israelites (24.1; 1 Chron. 27.24); against Solomon (1 Kings 11.9); against Jerusalem and Judah (2 Kings 24.20; 1 Chron. 27.24); against Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 19.2); against Jerusalem, etc.; on account of Joash (2 Chron. 24.18); Amaziah (25.15); Hezekiah (32.25); the shepherds (Zech. 10.3); the killers and mockers of his servants (Matt. 22.7). See the wrath of God.

units.la: IRA, IRACVNDIA. ira ὀργὴ, est accensa & feruens animi ebullitio, quæ iniuriæ nobis factæ vindictam nostra æstimatione expetit & desiderat.
units.tr: ANGER, WRATH. Anger [ὀργὴ] is a hot and seething agitation of the mind, which desires and seeks vengeance for an injury done to us, according to our own estimate.

units.la: Iracundia ὀργιλότης, est animi propensio naturalis ad facile & temere, ex quauis causa, irascendum.
units.tr: Irascibility [ὀργιλότης] is a natural inclination of the mind to become angry easily and rashly, for any cause whatever.

units.la: Ira duplex est, illicita, qualis est superior descriptio, quæ inter opera carnis recensetur,Gal.5.20.
units.tr: Anger is of two kinds: unlawful, such as the description above, which is listed among the works of the flesh, Gal. 5:20.

units.la: Licita, qua quis ex amore iustitiæ,& odio peccati, cum moderatione vitiis irascitur. Nec enim Christiana religio constituit homines ἀπαθεῖς & ἀναισθήτος Bernard. Non irasci, vbi irascendum est, est peccatum emendare nolle.
units.tr: Lawful anger is when someone, out of love of righteousness and hatred of sin, is angry at vices with moderation. For the Christian religion does not require people to be without passion [ἀπαθεῖς] and without feeling [ἀναισθήτος]. Bernard: Not to be angry where anger is called for is to be unwilling to correct sin.

units.la: IRA, seu iracundia in homine damnatur, Iob.36.13.Pro.18. 14. Eccles. 7.10.Matt.5.22. Eph.4.vers.26.31. Coloss.3.8.1. Tim.2.8.Tit,1.7.Iac.1.19. non omnis tamen ira, vtpote quæ zeli nomine commendatur. (Vide ZELVS bonus) & quam Peripatetici fortitudinis cotem non temere vocarunt,sed quæ vel iniusta est, vel immoderata, Eph.4.26.Ita stulti quàm noxia,Pro.27.3. Ira seu iracundia quantum mali pariat,Gen.4.5.Iob.5.2. Pro.12.16.& 14.29.& 15.18.& 17.19.& 19.19 & 27.3.& 29.22. Eccl.7.10. Eccl.25,22. & 28.v.6.14.& 30.26.Mar.5.22. Luc.4.28. Gal.5.20. Ephes. 4.26.27.Col.3.8.Tit.1.7.Iac.1.19. Irae alterius cedendum potius,quàm resistendum & repugnandum, Gen.27.42. Prou.22.24.& 29.22.Eccl.8,19,Matt.2.13.Irae mala,Pro.15,18.& 26.21.& 29.22.Iac.1,20.
units.tr: Anger, or irascibility, is condemned in a human being: Job 36:13; Prov. 18:14; Eccl. 7:10; Matt. 5:22; Eph. 4:26, 31; Col. 3:8; 1 Tim. 2:8; Titus 1:7; James 1:19. Not every anger, however, is condemned, since it is commended under the name of zeal (see ZEAL, good). The Peripatetics rightly called it the whetstone of courage, though not every anger but only that which is unjust or immoderate (Eph. 4:26). How harmful fools are: Prov. 27:3. How much evil anger or irascibility produces: Gen. 4:5; Job 5:2; Prov. 12:16; 14:29; 15:18; 17:19; 19:19; 27:3; 29:22; Eccl. 7:10; Ecclus. 25:22; 28:6, 14; 30:26; Mark 5:22; Luke 4:28; Gal. 5:20; Eph. 4:26, 27; Col. 3:8; Titus 1:7; James 1:19. One should yield to another's anger rather than resist and fight against it: Gen. 27:42; Prov. 22:24; 29:22; Eccl. 8:19; Matt. 2:13. The evils of anger: Prov. 15:18; 26:21; 29:22; James 1:20.

units.la: Irae iniustae, seu vituperandae exempla:Cain,Genes.4.5,Balach,Numer.24.10.Eliab, 1, Sam.17.28.Saul,18.8.& 20.30. principes philistiim,29.4.Abner,2.Sam.3.8. Asa,2.par.16. 10.Achab,1.Reg,21,4,Naaman, 2.Reg 5.11. Exercitus Ephraim, 2.par.25.10. Ozias.26,19.Sanaballat, &c.Neh.4.1,Nabuchodonosor, Dan.2.12.& 3.v.13 19.Elihu, Iob.32, 2. Aman, Esth.3.5. Principes Sedechiæ, Ierem. 37.14 15. Ionas, Ion.4. v.8.9. Gentes, Ap.11.18. Herodes, Matt.2.16. Iudęi, Luc.4.28. Frater prodigi filij, 1528. Demetrius cum suis, Act.19.28. Cum iracundo amicitia non ineunda, Pro. 22.24. Iræ locum dare, Rom.12.19. est non irasci, cedere occasionibus litigandi, subterfugere materiam irascendi. Irasci dicitur Christus, Marci 3.5. sed non hominum iratorum more, in quibus ira nihil aliud est, quàm summa vindicandæ iniuriæ appetitio, ideóq. cum maleuolentia semper coniuncta est, & cum dolore quidem sed quem ex iniuria ipsis facta concipiunt, non autem ex eius vel improbitate, vel imprudentia à quo lædantur. At Christus contrà ira iratus dicitur Pharisæis, vt nihil praetermitteret, quo illos reuocaret ad officium, tantùm aberat, vt vlcisdendi rabie ferretur. Irascendum, sed non peccandum, Eph.4.26. quo in loco agit Paulus de compescendis vitiosis affectibus. Ac proinde puto iram ibi minimè præcipi, sed nos admoneri, vt si irascamur, sic saltem irascamur, vt quod ira, pessimus sanè consultor, suaserit, ne exequamur, atque adeò illi non indormiamus. Qui hoc dictum de ira laudabili accipiunt, non satis attendere evidentur ad Pauli mentem, & loci circumstantiam. Cur enim, si hoc ita esset, moneret Paulus de ira ante Solis occasum semel domanda, eodem versu, cum illam potiùs semper in nobis vigere oportear?
units.tr: Examples of unjust or blameworthy anger: Cain, Gen. 4:5; Balak, Num. 24:10; Eliab, 1 Sam. 17:28; Saul, 1 Sam. 18:8; 20:30; the princes of the Philistines, 1 Sam. 29:4; Abner, 2 Sam. 3:8; Asa, 2 Chron. 16:10; Ahab, 1 Kings 21:4; Naaman, 2 Kings 5:11; the army of Ephraim, 2 Chron. 25:10; Uzziah, 2 Chron. 26:19; Sanballat, etc., Neh. 4:1; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 2:12; 3:13, 19; Elihu, Job 32:2; Haman, Esther 3:5; the princes of Zedekiah, Jer. 37:14, 15; Jonah, Jon. 4:8, 9; the nations, Rev. 11:18; Herod, Matt. 2:16; the Jews, Luke 4:28; the brother of the prodigal son, Luke 15:28; Demetrius and his men, Acts 19:28. Do not make friendship with an angry man: Prov. 22:24. To give place to wrath: Rom. 12:19, that is, not to be angry, to yield to occasions of quarrelling, and to escape the material for anger. Christ is said to have been angry, Mark 3:5, but not in the manner of angry men, in whom anger is nothing other than the strong desire to avenge an injury; for this is always joined with ill will, and with a grief that they feel because of the injury done to them, not because of the wickedness or folly of the one by whom they are harmed. Christ, on the contrary, is said to have been angry with the Pharisees so that he might leave nothing undone that would call them back to their duty; he was far from being carried away by a fury of vengeance. Be angry, but do not sin: Eph. 4:26, where Paul treats of restraining sinful passions. I think therefore that anger is not commanded there at all, but we are admonished that if we are angry, we should at least be angry in such a way that we do not carry out what anger, a very poor counsellor indeed, suggests, and so that we do not fall asleep in it. Those who take this saying about praiseworthy anger do not seem to pay enough attention to Paul's meaning and to the context of the passage. For why, if this were so, would Paul advise that anger should be quenched before the sun goes down, in the same verse, since anger ought rather always to be alive in us?

units.la: Ira, pro zelo, seu studio rei sanctæ & iustæ. Exempla: Moses, Exo.16.20. & 32.19. Leu.10.16. Num.16.15. Deut.9.20. &c. Ionathas, 1 Sam.20.34. Phinees, Num.25.v.7.8.2. Mach.2.54. David, 2 Sa.12.5 & 13.21. Elias.1.Re.19 14. Ro. 11.3. Nehemias, Neh.5 6. Assuerus, Est.7.7. Eliacim, Sobna, & Ioahe, Esa.36 22. Ezechias, 37.1, Ieremias, Ier.6.11. Rex quidam, Matth.22.7. Christus, Mar.3.5. Paterfamilias, Luc. 14.21. Vide Zelus bonus. Iræ filij, Vide Fil ii iræ, Iræ vasa, Vide Vasa iræ.
units.tr: Anger, for zeal, or the eagerness for a holy and just cause. Examples: Moses, Exod. 16:20; 32:19; Lev. 10:16; Num. 16:15; Deut. 9:20, etc.; Jonathan, 1 Sam. 20:34; Phinehas, Num. 25:7, 8; 2 Macc. 2:54; David, 2 Sam. 12:5; 13:21; Elijah, 1 Kings 19:14; Rom. 11:3; Nehemiah, Neh. 5:6; Ahasuerus, Esther 7:7; Eliakim, Shebna and Joah, Isa. 36:22; Hezekiah, Isa. 37:1; Jeremiah, Jer. 6:11; a certain king, Matt. 22:7; Christ, Mark 3:5; the householder, Luke 14:21. See ZEAL, good. Sons of wrath: see SONS OF WRATH. Vessels of wrath: see VESSELS OF WRATH.

units.la: [Ira Satanæ & meretricis mysticæ, Apoc.12.12. & 14.8.]
units.tr: [The wrath of Satan and of the mystical harlot, Rev. 12:12; 14:8.]

units.la: IRE ad Patres, periphrasis, pro mori, Genes.15.15. Vide INGREDI.
units.tr: To go to the fathers: a periphrasis for to die, Gen. 15:15. See TO ENTER.

units.la: IRE ad Christum, pro credere ei, Ioan.6.35.
units.tr: To go to Christ: to believe in him, John 6:35.

units.la: IRIS in nubibus, Gen.9.13. (Vide ARCVS) Est tanquam dimidia quædam pars alicuius arcus variegati sublimis, & in aëre suspensi. Eccl.43.12.13.
units.tr: A RAINBOW in the clouds, Gen. 9:13. (See BOW.) It is like a kind of half of some lofty, many-coloured arc, suspended in the air. Ecclus. 43:12, 13.

units.la: IRONIA, tropus quo vox vnius dissentanei, ad oppositum dissentaneum significandum vsurpatur, in Scripturis frequens est, Deut.32.v.37.38. Iudic.10.14.2.Sam.5.6.1.Reg.18.27.& 22,15.2.Par.18.14.2.2.Reg.1.9.Esa.47.13. Ier.2.28. Osee.13.10.Matt.26.45.Mar.14.41.& 15.9.Ioan.19 14.1. Corint.4.8.2.Cor.4 12.& 11.19.& 12.v.1.3.
units.tr: IRONY, a trope by which the word of one thing is used to signify the opposite. It is frequent in Scripture: Deut. 32:37, 38; Judg. 10:14; 2 Sam. 5:6; 1 Kings 18:27; 22:15; 2 Chron. 18:14; 2 Kings 1:9; Isa. 47:13; Jer. 2:28; Hos. 13:10; Matt. 26:45; Mark 14:41; 15:9; John 19:14; 1 Cor. 4:8; 2 Cor. 4:12; 11:19; 12:1, 3.

units.la: IRRISIO, Est de malo culpae vel poenae,id est,alienae vel culpę vel afflictionis recitatio cum risu&cachimo,ad fratris contemtum,à nobis facta. Gal.6.7. Deus non irridetur : Ne fallimini.
units.tr: MOCKING is the recounting, by us, of another's fault or punishment, or of another's affliction, with laughter and scorn, to the contempt of a brother. Gal. 6:7: God is not mocked; do not be deceived.

units.la: IRRIDETVR Christus, Ioann. 19. 2. Irrisionis eiusque poenae exempla: Michol ,2.Sam.6.16. quadraginta duo pueri de Bethel.irridentes Elizæum, à duabus vrsis discinduntur 2.Re.2.v.23.24.Simei,1.Re.2.44.Milites,Ioan.19.2.
units.tr: Christ is mocked, John 19:2. Examples of mocking and its punishment: Michal, 2 Sam. 6:16; forty-two boys of Bethel mocking Elisha are torn apart by two bears, 2 Kings 2:23, 24; Shimei, 1 Kings 2:44; the soldiers, John 19:2.

units.la: IRRITATIO,(Ἐρίζεια χαρᾶς,Iacob.3 14.) Est facilis propter reuocatam in animum factam nobis iniuriam,in eum qui fecit,impetus & irae propensio.
units.tr: PROVOCATION (Ἐρίζεια χαρᾶς, James 3:14) is an easy tendency to attack the one who did the wrong, arising from the injury done to us being recalled to the mind, and an inclination to anger.

units.la: IRRITATIO abest a charitate 1.Cor.13.5.
units.tr: PROVOCATION is far from charity: 1 Cor. 13:5.

Iac. & Esau,benedicit,v.27.28.29.39.40. mortuus sepelitur,35.29.venigenitusAbrahami filius dicitur,quiaIsmael, non censetur in familia,Heb.11.17.
units.tr: ISAAC, Izehak (that is, laughter, so called from the laughter of Abraham, Gen. 17:17, 19), is promised to Abraham: Gen. 15:4; 17:16, 19; 18:10. Isaac is born of a barren mother, Gen. 16:1, and when her womb was already dead, Gen. 18:12 (Rom. 4:19); he is born, Gen. 21:2; his name is given to him, v. 3; he is circumcised on the eighth day, v. 4; Acts 7:8. Isaac is the son of promise, Gen. 21:12; Gal. 4:23, 28; the heir of Abraham, Gen. 15:4; 21:10; 24:36; 25:5; Gal. 4:30. He takes Rebekah as wife, Gen. 24:67; he sojourns in Gerar, 26:1; he is a very wealthy man, v. 13; he makes a covenant with Abimelech, v. 31; he blesses Jacob and Esau, vv. 27–29, 39, 40; he dies and is buried, 35:29. He is called the only-begotten son of Abraham, because Ishmael is not counted in the family, Heb. 11:17.

units.la: ISAI,qui & Iesse,Dauidis pater,Ruth.4.17.1.Sam.16.3.1. Par. 2.v.13.15.Matt.1.6. vnà cum filiis ad sacrificium sanctifi-catur,1.Sam.16.5. Samueli septem filios adducit,v.10.ad summam & honorabilem senectutem peruenit,17.12.(i. munus.)
units.tr: ISHAI, who is also Jesse, father of David, Ruth 4:17; 1 Sam. 16:3; 1 Chron. 2:13, 15; Matt. 1:6. Together with his sons he is consecrated for the sacrifice, 1 Sam. 16:5. He brings seven sons before Samuel, v. 10. He comes to a great and honourable old age, 1 Sam. 17:12. (That is, a gift.)

units.la: ISAIAS Propheta.(Vide ESAIAS)Isaiam legit populo, Ioannes,Luc.3.4.Christus,4.17.eum & Eunuchus Aethiops legebat,Act.8.30.
units.tr: ISAIAH the prophet (see ESAIAS). John reads Isaiah to the people, Luke 3:4; Christ read him, Luke 4:17; and the Ethiopian eunuch was reading him, Acts 8:30.

units.la: ISBOSETH, filius Saulis,Rex ab Abner constituitur,2.Sam.2. 8.9.Abnerem, quòd concubina patris defuncti abusus est,reprehendit,3.7.occidi tur,4.7.Dauidisiussu eius caput sepelitur,v.12.(Ischbosceth.i.vir confusus, ignominiosus.
units.tr: ISHBOSHETH, son of Saul, is made king by Abner, 2 Sam. 2:8, 9. He rebukes Abner because he had abused his dead father's concubine, 3:7. He is killed, 4:7. By David's command his head is buried, v. 12. (Ishbosheth, that is, a confused, dishonoured man.)

units.la: ISCHAT
units.tr: ISCHAT

units.la: CHARIOTH , gentile nomen , Vide IVDAS Icarioth.
units.tr: CHARIOTH, a gentile name. See JUDAS Iscariot.

units.la: MAEL Abrahami ex Agar ancilla filius , concipitur,Gen. 16.4.eius futura conditio, mores & nomen describuntur, v.11.12. nascitur , v.15.nomen illi ab Abrahamo imponitur,ibidem circumciditur , 17.23.persequitur Isaacum, 21.9.Gal.4.29.moritur,Gen.25.17.eius posteritas,v.12.&c. 1.Paral.1.29.Ismael,pro iis , qui ab Ismaele longo ordine & serie ortum duxerant,Genef.28 9. Familiare enim est Scripturae sacrae,ut nomina propria pro gentilibus vsurpet.
units.tr: ISHMAEL, son of Abraham by the maidservant Hagar, is conceived, Gen. 16:4. His future condition, manners and name are described, vv. 11, 12. He is born, v. 15. His name is given to him by Abraham; there he is circumcised, 17:23. He persecutes Isaac, 21:9; Gal. 4:29. He dies, Gen. 25:17. His posterity, v. 12, etc.; 1 Chron. 1:29. Ishmael is used for those who had sprung from Ishmael in a long line and succession, Gen. 28:9. For it is customary in holy Scripture to use proper names for the peoples descended from them.

units.la: MAHEL Nathaniae filius,Godoliam dolo occidit, Ier.41. 2.& Iudaeos qui cum eo erant,v.3.lacum cadaueribus eorum,quos occiderat,implet,v.9.Iohanam populi sui vindicem fugiens,ad Ammonem se recipit,v.15.
units.tr: ISHMAEL, son of Nethaniah, by treachery kills Gedaliah, Jer. 41:2, and the Jews who were with him, v. 3. He fills a pit with the corpses of those whom he had killed, v. 9. Fleeing from Johanan, the avenger of his people, he takes refuge with the Ammonites, v. 15.

units.la: ISRAEL (id est,Princeps seu victor Dei ) nuncupatur Iacob [Gen.35 10. Ab eo tempore saepius patriarcha Iacob appellatur Israel Gen 37.3.& sequentib.c.Exo.5.1. Exo.32.13. 1.Reg.18.36.1.Par.34.2.Par. 30.6.Esai.8.14.Ose.12.13.]
units.tr: ISRAEL (that is, prince or victor of God) is the name given to Jacob [Gen. 35:10]. From that time the patriarch Jacob is often called Israel: Gen. 37:3 and following chapters; Exod. 5:1; Exod. 32:13; 1 Kings 18:36; 1 Chron. 34:2; 2 Chron. 30:6; Isa. 8:14; Hos. 12:13.

Exo.12.2.ex AEgypto cum opibus egressi , v.36, Psal.105. 37.a Deo electi, Deut.7.6. & 14.2.& 10.15 foedifragi,Psal. 78.56.omnibus formidabiles,Ios.5.1. optimeinstituti,Deu. 18.14.&c.aduersus Moseu murmurant,Num.14.2.& 16.41.
