units.la: IVSTVS Deus, Deut.32.4.2. Par.12.v.5.8. Neh.9.v.15.33. Psal.11.7. &116.5.&119.137.&129.4.&145.7. Esai.45.21. Ierem.12.1. Thren.1.18. Dan.9.14. Sophon.3.5. Apoc.16.5. Iustus, Deus Pater, Ioan.17.25.1. Ioan.1.9. Iustus Christus Messias, Dei Filius, Θεάνθρωπος, &c. Esai.53.11. Ier.23.5. Zachar.9.9. Act 3. 14.& 7.52.& 22.14.2.Tim. 4,8.1.Pet.3. 18.1. Ioan.2.v.1.29.& 3.7.1.Pet.2.22.
units.tr: GOD IS JUST, Deut. 32.4, 2 Chr. 12.5, 8, Neh. 9.15, 33, Ps. 11.7, 116.5, 119.137, 129.4, 145.7, Isa. 45.21, Jer. 12.1, Lam. 1.18, Dan. 9.14, Zeph. 3.5, Rev. 16.5. The Father is just, John 17.25, 1 John 1.9. Christ the Messiah, the Son of God, is just, the God-man [Θεάνθρωπος], etc., Isa. 53.11, Jer. 23.5, Zech. 9.9, Acts 3.14, 7.52, 22.14, 2 Tim. 4.8, 1 Pet. 3.18, 1 John 2.1, 29, 3.7, 1 Pet. 2.22.

units.la: Iustus,homo dicitur,qui gratiam à Deo Patre propter Mediatorem Christum consequutus,vitam suam ad prę-scriptu legis diuinæ instituit,Ge.6.9.& 7.1.Nu 23 10.Iob. 36.7.Pf.32 11.& 33.1 & 34 v.16.18.20.22.Esai.3.10.& 26.v. 2.7.Habac.2.4.Matth.25.v.37.46.Luc.15.7.Rom.1.17.Gal. 3.11 Iustus,Innocens, probus, æquitatis & rectitudinis amans,Improbo & reo oppositus,Gen.18.23.Exo.23. v.7.8. Deut.25.1.1.Re.2.32.Iob 32.v.1.2.Prou. 17. 15, Ecci.3 17.& 7.16.Esa.5,23.Ezec.3 v.20.21.& 18.v 5.9 &c.& 33.v.12 13.18. Amos 2.6.Abac.1.4.Matt 27.v.4 19 24.Rom.5 7.1.Tim.1. 9.Iaco.5.6.Iustus,naturā Deo gratus,perfectus, sine macula,Eccl.7.20.Rom.3. 10. Iustus nomen proprium viri, Act.1.23.& 18.7.Col.4.11.Iusti,hypocritæ,qui se iustos esse somniant,& tales haberi cupiunt,Matt.9.13.& 23.28.Mar 2.17.Luc.5.32.& 18.9.& 20.20.]
units.tr: A man is called just who, having obtained grace from God the Father on account of the Mediator Christ, orders his life according to the prescription of the divine law, Gen. 6.9, 7.1, Num. 23.10, Job 36.7, Ps. 32.11, 33.1, 34.16, 18, 20, 22, Isa. 3.10, 26.2, 7, Hab. 2.4, Matt. 25.37, 46, Luke 15.7, Rom. 1.17, Gal. 3.11. Just: innocent, upright, a lover of equity and rectitude, opposed to the wicked and the guilty, Gen. 18.23, Exod. 23.7–8, Deut. 25.1, 1 Kgs. 2.32, Job 32.1–2, Prov. 17.15, Eccles. 3.17, 7.16, Isa. 5.23, Ezek. 3.20–21, 18.5, 9, etc., 33.12–13, 18, Amos 2.6, Hab. 1.4, Matt. 27.4, 19, 24, Rom. 5.7, 1 Tim. 1.9, Jas. 5.6. Just: naturally pleasing to God, perfect, without blemish, Eccles. 7.20, Rom. 3.10. Just is a proper name of a man, Acts 1.23, 18.7, Col. 4.11. The just, hypocrites, who dream that they are just and wish to be thought such, Matt. 9.13, 23.28, Mark 2.17, Luke 5.32, 18.9, 20.20.

units.la: Iustus,pro apud homines innocente ; non occidendus, Exo.23 7.(Vide P11 )Iusti apud Deum qui, Rom.2.13.1. Ioan.3.7.Iustus accusator sui , Prou. 18. 17. Iustus coram Deo nemo,Iob 4.17.& 9.2.& 25.4.Psalm.143.2.Eccl.7.15. Iustus fide sua viuit, Abac.2.4.Rom.1.17.Gal.3.11.Heb.10. 38.Iustus pronunciatur Publicanus,Luc.18.14. Iustus vix effugit tribulationes,1.Pet.4.18. Iusto auertenti se à via, mors,Ezec.18.24.& 33.12.Iusto non est lex posita , Gal.5. 23.1.Tim.1.9.Iusti & beati,Pf.32.1.Iusti iudicabunt impios, Prou.14.19.(Vide Iudicare.) Iustorum finis incognitus,Esai.57.1.Iustorum resurrectio , pro extremo iudicio, Luc.14.14.Iustorum securitas,Prou.28 1. Iustus pro summe veraci,& fideli,Roman.3.4,
units.tr: Just, for one innocent before men, not to be put to death, Exod. 23.7. (See Ps. 11.) Those who are just before God, Rom. 2.13, 1 John 3.7. A just man is his own accuser, Prov. 18.17. No one is just before God, Job 4.17, 9.2, 25.4, Ps. 143.2, Eccles. 7.15. The just lives by his faith, Hab. 2.4, Rom. 1.17, Gal. 3.11, Heb. 10.38. The publican is pronounced just, Luke 18.14. The just scarcely escape tribulations, 1 Pet. 4.18. For the just man who turns aside from the way, there is death, Ezek. 18.24, 33.12. The law is not laid down for the just, Gal. 5.23, 1 Tim. 1.9. The just and blessed, Ps. 32.1. The just shall judge the wicked, Prov. 14.19. (See to judge.) The end of the just is unknown, Isa. 57.1. The resurrection of the just, for the last judgment, Luke 14.14. The security of the just, Prov. 28.1. Just for one most true and faithful, Rom. 3.4.

units.la: Iustorum exempla.Noe,Gen.6 9.& 7.1.2.Pet.2.5.Thamar Gen.38.26.Samuel,1 Sam.12.3.4. Eccles.45.v 16.17.&c.Dauid,1 Sam.24.18.Abner & Amasa,1 Reg.2.32. Iob,Iob.1.1. Ioseph Mariæ vir, Matt.1.19. Abel & Zacharias. 23 35. Christus.27.v.4.19.Luc.23.47.Actor.3.14. & 7.52. zacharias & Elisabeth,Luc.1.6,Simeon,2.25. Cornelius,Act.10. v.1.22.Loth,2.Petr.2.7.Paulus,1 Corinth.4.v.3 4.
units.tr: Examples of the just. Noah, Gen. 6.9, 7.1, 2 Pet. 2.5; Tamar, Gen. 38.26; Samuel, 1 Sam. 12.3–4, Ecclus. 46.16–17, etc.; David, 1 Sam. 24.18; Abner and Amasa, 1 Kgs. 2.32; Job, Job 1.1; Joseph, husband of Mary, Matt. 1.19; Abel and Zechariah, Matt. 23.35; Christ, Matt. 27.4, 19, Luke 23.47, Acts 3.14, 7.52; Zechariah and Elizabeth, Luke 1.6; Simeon, Luke 2.25; Cornelius, Acts 10.1, 22; Lot, 2 Pet. 2.7; Paul, 1 Cor. 4.3–4.

units.la: IVVENES quales esse debeant, Tit.2.6.1. Pet.5.5. Iuuenum consilium secutus Roboam punitur, 1 Reg.12.10. &c.Iuuentus in timore Dei erudienda,Eccles.12.1.3. Iuuentutis cupiditates fugiendæ,2.Tim.2.22.à iuuentute benefaciendum,Eccl.11.9.& 12.1.(Vide Adolescens)Leuit.19.32. Ixoseo non vescebantur Iudæi, Deut. 14.13.
units.tr: YOUNG MEN, what they ought to be, Tit. 2.6, 1 Pet. 5.5. The counsel of the young men followed by Rehoboam was punished, 1 Kgs. 12.10, etc. Youth is to be trained in the fear of God, Eccles. 12.1, 3. The lusts of youth are to be fled, 2 Tim. 2.22. One must do good from youth, Eccles. 11.9, 12.1. (See Young man.) Lev. 19.32. The Jews did not eat Ixoseo, Deut. 14.13.

units.la: L.
units.tr: L.

units.la: ABAN filius Bathuelis, Rebeccæ frater, le-tus seruum Abrahæ hospitio excipit, Genesis 24.v.31.32. Iacobo obuius pro-ficiscitur, 29.13. tenax est & astutus, 31.15. Iacobum fugientem insequitur, v.23. fœ-dus cum Iacobo init, v.44. ( candidus, aut later.)
units.tr: LABAN, son of Bethuel and brother of Rebekah, receives Abraham's servant hospitably (Genesis 24:31-32). He goes out to meet Jacob (29:13). He is tenacious and crafty (31:15). He pursues Jacob when he flees (v. 23) and makes a covenant with Jacob (v. 44). (Meaning: white, or brick.)

units.la: [LABIA Dei : Iob.11.5. & 23.12. Psalm.17.4. Esai.30.27. Labia Christi, Psal.45.3. Cant.5.13. Esai.11.4. Ecclesiæ, Cant. 4. v.3. 11. & 7.9.
units.tr: The LIPS of God: Job 11:5; 23:12; Psalm 17:4; Isaiah 30:27. The LIPS of Christ: Psalm 45:3; Song of Songs 5:13; Isaiah 11:4. The LIPS of the Church: Song of Songs 4:3, 11; 7:9.

units.la: Labium, Labrum, pars nota oris, 1. Sam. 1.13. Iob.19.20. Esai.6.7. & 37.29. Dan.10.16. Abac.3.16. Labium, idioma, sermo, Gen.11.v.1.6.9. Labium, Labia, signif. non modò os & linguam, sed etiam loquendi facultatem & actum, Exod.6.v.12.30. Deut.23 23. Iob.1.22. Hebr.13.15 1. Petr.3.10. Labium, Limbus, Ora extrema alicuius rei, Exod.25.v.24.25 1.Reg.7.v.23 24.26 2.Par.4.v.2 3 5.] sapiens cohibet labia sua, Pro.10.19.
units.tr: Labium (lip) or labrum, the visible part of the mouth: 1 Samuel 1:13; Job 19:20; Isaiah 6:7; 37:29; Daniel 10:16; Habakkuk 3:16. Labium meaning language, speech: Genesis 11:1, 6, 9. Labium, labia, signifies not only the mouth and tongue but also the faculty and act of speaking: Exodus 6:12, 30; Deuteronomy 23:23; Job 1:22; Hebrews 13:15; 1 Peter 3:10. Labium, limbus, the outer edge of something: Exodus 25:24-25; 1 Kings 7:23-24, 26; 2 Chronicles 4:2-3, 5. "The wise man restrains his lips," Proverbs 10:19.

units.la: LABII ænei forma, Exo.30.18.
units.tr: The shape of the bronze LAVER's rim, Exodus 30:18.

units.la: LABIORVM fructus, laus Deo facta per Christum, Heb. 13.15.
units.tr: The FRUIT OF THE LIPS is praise offered to God through Christ, Hebrews 13:15.

units.la: LABOR, πόνος vel κόπος, siue diligentia, est seria corporis animæque nostri ad honestum & concessum aliquod opus aut studium applicatio, atque in eo strema occupatio: vt & Deo seruiamus, & proximo vtiles simus, ex quo etiam nobis victum quærere, si ita necesse est, possimus.
units.tr: LABOUR, πόνος or κόπος, or diligence, is the earnest application of our body and soul to some honest and lawful work or study, and the constant occupation in it, so that we serve God and are useful to our neighbour, and from it may also seek our living, if this is necessary.

units.la: LABOR manuum præcipitur, Psal.128.2. Prouerb.10.4. & 12. 11. & 13.4. & 20.4. & 28.19. & 31.27. Eccl.5.11. Ephes.4.28.1. Thess. 4.11.2. Thess.3.v.10.12. Labor & dolor omnibus communis, Gen.2.15 & 3.v.17.19. Exo 20.9. & 34,21, Deut. 5.13. Par.128.2. Prou.6.6. & 10.4. & 14.4. & 20.4. Eccles.5.11. Iob.5,7. Eccl.29 29. Ioan.21.3. Act.18.3 & 20.34.1. Cor.4.12. Eph.4.28.1. Thess.2.9. & 4.1.2. Thes. 3.v.8.12. Labor non ditat sine Dei benedictione, Gen.3.17. & 26.v.3.12. & 30.27. Deut.8.18 Iob.42.12. Psal.127.2. Prou.10.22. Eccl.11.6. Ad laborem nascitur homo, Iob 5.7. Pastoribus laborandum, 2. Tim.4.5.
units.tr: MANUAL LABOUR is commanded: Psalm 128:2; Proverbs 10:4; 12:11; 13:4; 20:4; 28:19; 31:27; Ecclesiastes 5:11; Ephesians 4:28; 1 Thessalonians 4:11; 2 Thessalonians 3:10, 12. Labour and toil are common to all: Genesis 2:15; 3:17, 19; Exodus 20:9; 34:21; Deuteronomy 5:13; Psalm 128:2; Proverbs 6:6; 10:4; 14:4; 20:4; Ecclesiastes 5:11; Job 5:7; Ecclesiastes 2:9; John 21:3; Acts 18:3; 20:34; 1 Corinthians 4:12; Ephesians 4:28; 2 Thessalonians 2:9; 3:8, 12. Labour does not enrich without God's blessing: Genesis 3:17; 26:3, 12; 30:27; Deuteronomy 8:18; Job 42:12; Psalm 127:2; Proverbs 10:22; Ecclesiastes 11:6. Man is born to labour, Job 5:7. Ministers must labour, 2 Timothy 4:5.

units.la: LABORIS manuum & agriculturæ laus & utilitas, Prou.12. II. & 13.4. & 14.23. & 24.27. & 28 19.
units.tr: The praise and usefulness of manual labour and of farming: Proverbs 12:11; 13:4; 14:23; 24:27; 28:19.

units.la: Laborantis merces debetur, Leuit.19.13. Deut.24.15. & 25.4. Ier.22.13. Malach 3.5. Matth.10.10. Luc.10.7. 1. Cor.9.v.9. 14.1. Tim.5.18. Iac.5.4.
units.tr: The wages of the labourer are due: Leviticus 19:13; Deuteronomy 24:15; 25:4; Jeremiah 22:13; Malachi 3:5; Matthew 10:10; Luke 10:7; 1 Corinthians 9:9, 14; 1 Timothy 5:18; James 5:4.

units.la: [LABOR, pro afflictione & animi cruciatu, Psal.25.18. & 88.16. Ier.20.18. Thren.3.5. Abac.1.3. pro molestia quam quis aliis molitur. Psal.10.v.7.14. & 94.20. Esai.59.4. Peruersitas, Psal.55.11.]
units.tr: LABOUR, for affliction and anguish of mind: Psalm 25:18; 88:16; Jeremiah 20:18; Lamentations 3:5; Habakkuk 1:3; for the trouble that someone causes others: Psalm 10:7, 14; 94:20; Isaiah 59:4. Perversity: Psalm 55:11.

units.la: LAC pro Dei sermone, vero vitæ spiritualis alimento, 1. Pet.2.2. Pro primis fidei rudimentis, 1. Cor.3.2. Heb.5.12. Lac & butyrum peregrinis apponitur, Gen.18.8. Lacte fluit terra Chanaan, Exodi 3.8. Lac pro victu sufficienti, Exod.3.8.17. Deut.6.3. Iof.5.6. Ier.32.22.
units.tr: MILK, for the word of God, the true spiritual food of life: 1 Peter 2:2. For the first rudiments of faith: 1 Corinthians 3:2; Hebrews 5:12. Milk and butter are set before strangers, Genesis 18:8. The land of Canaan flows with milk, Exodus 3:8. Milk for sufficient food, Exodus 3:8, 17; Deuteronomy 6:3; Joshua 5:6; Jeremiah 32:22.

units.la: [Lac, i.doctrina veritatis 1.Pet.2.2. Lac mysticum, Cant.4.11. & 5.v.1.12.]
units.tr: [Milk, that is, the teaching of truth, 1 Peter 2:2. Mystical milk, Song of Songs 4:11; 5:1, 12.]

units.la: LACHIS vrbs in Tribu Iuda, Iof.10.3. à Iosua capitur, v.32. à Roboamo muris cingitur, 2. Par.11.v.9.11
units.tr: LACHISH, a city in the tribe of Judah, Joshua 10:3. Captured by Joshua, v. 32. Walled by Rehoboam, 2 Chronicles 11:9, 11.

units.la: LACRYMAE, Vide FLETVS. Lacrymantium exempla: ibid. cum lacrymis monet Paulus fratres. Act.20.18. orat cum lacrymis pater Dæmoniaci suam à Christo incredulitatem iuuari, Marc.9.24. Lacrymis rigat peccatrix Christi pedes, Luc.7.38.
units.tr: TEARS: see WEEPING. Examples of those weeping: ibid. Paul exhorts the brothers with tears, Acts 20:18. The father of the demoniac, weeping, asks Christ to help his unbelief, Mark 9:24. The sinful woman wets Christ's feet with tears, Luke 7:38.

units.la: [LACVS Aquarum congregatio, Exod.7.19. Esai.22.11. fovea, Psalm.7.16. Dan.6.v.7.12. 16.&c. Labrum vinarium, seu amplum vas in quod mustum fluit & retinetur, Apoc.14.verf.19.20. Cisterna. 2. Sam.23.15. Esa.51.1. Sepulchrum, Psalm.28.1. Esa.38.18. Ezec.26.v.10.20. Hoc nomine designatur Babylon, quæ fuit ad tempus velut sepulchrum Ecclesiæ, Zach. 9.11. Miseria summa. Psal.88.7. Thren.3.v.53.55.]
units.tr: [POOL: a gathering of waters, Exodus 7:19; Isaiah 22:11. A pit, Psalm 7:16; Daniel 6:7, 12, 16, etc. A winepress vat, or a large vessel into which the must flows and is kept, Revelation 14:19-20. A cistern, 2 Samuel 23:15; Isaiah 51:1. A sepulchre, Psalm 28:1; Isaiah 38:18; Ezekiel 26:10, 20. Babylon is designated by this name, which for a time was like a sepulchre of the Church, Zechariah 9:11. Utmost misery, Psalm 88:7; Lamentations 3:53-55.]

units.la: LÆTITIA, de alieno bono, Est sincerum animi nostri gaudium cum gratiarum actione, quæ Deo fit à nobis, propter alterius vel novum commodum & fœlicitatem, vel recepti iam boni incrementum & accessionem.
units.tr: JOY, over another's good: it is the sincere gladness of our mind, with thanksgiving rendered to God by us, on account of another's new advantage and happiness, or the increase and addition of a good already received.

units.la: LAETITIA: Lætitiæ post victoriam exempla: Moses & populus Israeliticus, Exo.15.v.1.2. Maria cum aliis, v.20.21. Debora & Barac, Iudic.5.v.1.2. Mulieres Israelitiæ, 1.Sam.18.v.6.7. Iosaphat & omnis vir Iuda, &c. 2. Paral.20.v.27.28. vide GAVDIVM.
units.tr: JOY: Examples of joy after victory: Moses and the people of Israel, Exodus 15:1-2. Miriam with the others, v. 20-21. Deborah and Barak, Judges 5:1-2. The women of Israel, 1 Samuel 18:6-7. Jehoshaphat and all the men of Judah, etc., 2 Chronicles 20:27-28. See REJOICING.

units.la: LAGANA: eorum oblatio, Leuit.2.4.
units.tr: LAGANA: their offering, Leviticus 2:4.

units.la: [LAGENA, Amphora, Marc.14.13. Hydria, & Iudic.6.16.19. Vter, vtris, 1.Sa.10.3. & 16.20. Esai.30.14. Modius, Agg.2.17. Lagun-
units.tr: [FLASK, amphora, Mark 14:13. Pitcher, hydria, Judges 6:16, 19. Skin, a wineskin, 1 Samuel 10:3; 16:20; Isaiah 30:14. Measure, bushel, Haggai 2:17. Lagun-

units.la: Laguuncula, Bathus: Esai. 5.10. Lagona, Ierem. 19.1.10.
units.tr: Small flask, bathus, Isaiah 5:10. Lagona (jar), Jeremiah 19:1, 10.

units.la: Ramus, Esa.10.33. Vter, vtris, Iob.32.19. Ierem.13.12. & 48.12.]
units.tr: Branch, Isaiah 10:33. Skin, wineskin, Job 32:19; Jeremiah 13:12; 48:12.]

units.la: [Laicos, vt vocant, non debere se immiscere rebus Ecclesiasticis probare se posse putant Pontificij testimoniis detortis ex Leu.10.1. Num.1.51 & 3.10. nec vasa sacrata temere contingere, 1.51. & 4.v.15. 19.20. & 18.7.2. Samu.6.6.2. Par.26.18. Laici panes, 1.Sam.21.4.
units.tr: [The Papists, as they call them, think they can prove that laymen should not meddle in ecclesiastical affairs, by twisting testimonies from Leviticus 10:1; Numbers 1:51; 3:10, nor should they rashly touch the sacred vessels, Numbers 1:51; 4:15, 19-20; 18:7; 2 Samuel 6:6; 2 Chronicles 26:18. Laymen eat the loaves, 1 Samuel 21:4.]

units.la: Lais ciuitas in Tribu Afer pacatissima, Iudi.18.7. a filiis Dan capta succenditur, v.27. & appellatur Dan. v.29. & Lesen. Iof.19.47. (Lais, leo.)
units.tr: LAISH, a city in the tribe of Dan, very peaceful, Judges 18:7. Captured by the sons of Dan and burned, v. 27; and it is called Dan, v. 29, and Leshem, Joshua 19:47. (Laish means "lion".)

units.la: LAMEC, Methusaelis filius polygamus, Gen.4.18. eius de sua & Caini morte ad vxores oratio, v.23.24. (i. humiliatus.)
units.tr: LAMECH, son of Methushael, a polygamist, Genesis 4:18. His speech to his wives about his own killing and that of Cain, v. 23-24. (That is, "humbled".)

units.la: LAMEC, Methusela filius, Genes. 5.25. aetate iam provecta, Noab filium gignit, v.28. eius de filio vaticinium, v.29. Vixit 777.annos, v.31.
units.tr: LAMECH, son of Methuselah, Genesis 5:25. Though already advanced in years, he begets a son, Noah, v. 28. His prophecy about his son, v. 29. He lived 777 years, v. 31.

units.la: LAMENTATIONE sua Ioannes Baptista non pellexit Iudaeos ad poenitentiam, Matth.11.18. Vide Lamentationes Ierem. c.1. &c.
units.tr: John the Baptist did not move the Jews to repentance by his lamentation, Matthew 11:18. See the Lamentations of Jeremiah, chapter 1, etc.

units.la: LAMINAE seu bracteae sacrae forma, Exo.28.36. & 39.30. & vsus, 28.38.
units.tr: The form of the sacred plates or gold leaves, Exodus 28:36; 39:30, and their use, 28:38.

units.la: LAMPAS. Lampades virginum prudentum & fatuarum: Mat. 25.1, &c. V. Act.20.8. Lampades ardentes ante thronum: Apoc.4.5. V. Lucerna.
units.tr: LAMPS. The lamps of the wise and foolish virgins: Matthew 25:1, etc. See Acts 20:8. Burning lamps before the throne: Revelation 4:5. See LAMP.

units.la: LANGVORES inobedientibus proponuntur, Deut. 28.61. Languoribus medetur Christus, (Vide MIRACVLA.) Mat. 4.23. & 8.17.
units.tr: DISEASES are set before the disobedient, Deuteronomy 28:61. Christ heals diseases (see MIRACLES), Matthew 4:23; 8:17.

units.la: [Languores spirituales, Esai.53.4. Matt.8.17.]
units.tr: [Spiritual diseases, Isaiah 53:4; Matthew 8:17.]

units.la: LAODICAEA, vrbs Lydiae in Asia minore, prope Colossas; Col.4.13.15. Apoc.1.11. & 3.14.
units.tr: LAODICEA, a city of Lydia in Asia Minor, near Colossae, Colossians 4:13, 15; Revelation 1:11; 3:14.

units.la: LAPIS: lapides in monumentum erecti, Gen.28.18. Iof.24.26. 1.Sam.7.12. duodecim lapides e medio Iordanis sublati, Iof.4.3. eorum significatio, v.5 6.7. alteri duodecim lapides in aceruum in medio Iordane a Iosua erecti, v.9. Lapidibus pluit, 10.11. Lapis viuus Christus, Matth, 21.42.1.Pet.2.6. offensionis, Psal.118.22. Matt.21.42. Act.4 11. 1.Pet.2.7. Lapides viui Christiani, v.5. lapides quibus insculpta erant nomina Israelis Exo.28.9. &c.
units.tr: STONE: stones erected as a memorial, Genesis 28:18; Joshua 24:26; 1 Samuel 7:12. Twelve stones taken from the middle of the Jordan, Joshua 4:3; their meaning, v. 5-7. Another twelve stones, erected by Joshua in a heap in the middle of the Jordan, v. 9. It rained stones, Joshua 10:11. Christ the living stone, Matthew 21:42; 1 Peter 2:6. A stone of offence, Psalm 118:22; Matthew 21:42; Acts 4:11; 1 Peter 2:7. Living stones are Christians, v. 5. The stones on which the names of the sons of Israel were engraved, Exodus 28:9, etc.

units.la: [Lapis communis, Gen.28.v.11.18.22. preciosus a communi dist. Exo.24.10. & 39.14. 1.Reg.5.17. & 7.v.9.10.11. nomen Loci, ob insigne aliquod factum, Iosu.15.6.1.Sam.4.1.1. Reg.1.9. Pondus, Prou.16.11. Rupes, perfugium, protectio, Gen.49.24. Lapis, Christus, fundamentum Ecclesiæ, psal. 118.22. Esa.8.14. & 28.16. Dan.2.v.34.35.45. Zach.3.9. Matth. 21.v.42.44. Act.4.11. Rom.9.v.32.33. Eph.2.20. 1.Pet.2.v.4. 6.7.8. Lapis onerosus & mysticus, Zach.12.3. Lapides mystici, Ecclesiæ militantis ædificium spirituale, Esai.54.v. 11.12.1.Pet.2.5. Lapides cælestes, summam Ecclesiæ triumphantis felicitatem adumbrantes, Apoc.21.v.11.18.19.]
units.tr: [Common stone, Genesis 28:11, 18, 22; precious, distinguished from common, Exodus 24:10; 39:14; 1 Kings 5:17; 7:9-11. The name of a place, because of some notable deed, Joshua 15:6; 1 Samuel 4:1; 1 Kings 1:9. A weight, Proverbs 16:11. A rock, refuge, protection, Genesis 49:24. Stone, Christ, the foundation of the Church, Psalm 118:22; Isaiah 8:14; 28:16; Daniel 2:34-35, 45; Zechariah 3:9; Matthew 21:42, 44; Acts 4:11; Romans 9:32-33; Ephesians 2:20; 1 Peter 2:4, 6-8. A heavy and mystical stone, Zechariah 12:3. Mystical stones, the spiritual building of the Church militant, Isaiah 54:11-12; 1 Peter 2:5. Heavenly stones, foreshadowing the supreme happiness of the Church triumphant, Revelation 21:11, 18-19.]

units.la: LAPIDARE, pro lapides in aliquem conijcere, Marc.12.4. Lapidatio, genus supplicij Hebræis solenne, Leuit.20.v.2. 27.&24.14. Ioan.8.5. Lapidandus est abducens à fiducia in Deum, Deuter.13.6. blasphemus, Leuit.24.10.&c Diuinus, 20.27. Eorum qui lapidati sunt exempla: Blasphamus, Leuiti. 24.23. Colligens ligna in sabbatho, Numer.15.ver.35.36. Achan, Iosu.7.25. Aduram, 1.Regum 12.18. Naboth, 21.v. 13.14. Seruus, Matth.21.35. Stephanus, Act.7.ver.58.59. Paulus, 14.19. 2. Corinth. 11.25. (Vide MORTIS violentæ exempla.) Lapidare volunt Christum Iudæi, Ioann.8.59.& 10.31.
units.tr: To STONE, to throw stones at someone, Mark 12:4. Stoning, a kind of punishment customary among the Hebrews, Leviticus 20:2, 27; 24:14; John 8:5. One who draws away from trust in God must be stoned, Deuteronomy 13:6. The blasphemer, Leviticus 24:10, etc.; the diviner, Leviticus 20:27. Examples of those who were stoned: the blasphemer, Leviticus 24:23; the man gathering sticks on the Sabbath, Numbers 15:35-36; Achan, Joshua 7:25; Adoram, 1 Kings 12:18; Naboth, 1 Kings 21:13-14; a servant, Matthew 21:35; Stephen, Acts 7:58-59; Paul, Acts 14:19; 2 Corinthians 11:25. (See examples of violent death.) The Jews wanted to stone Christ, John 8:59; 10:31.

units.la: LAPSVS à fide, V. APOSTASIA.
units.tr: LAPSED from the faith; see APOSTASY.

units.la: LAQVEI mortis, 2.Sam.22.6. Laqueo vitam finientium, exempla: Achitophel, 2.Sam.17.23. Aman, Esth.7.10. Iudas proditor, Matth.27.5. Act.1.18. V. MORTIS violentæ exempla. Laqueus conscientiis non iniiciendus, 1.Cor.7.35.
units.tr: A NOOSE of death, 2 Sam. 22.6. Examples of those who end their lives by a noose: Ahithophel, 2 Sam. 17.23; Haman, Esth. 7.10; Judas the traitor, Matt. 27.5; Acts 1.18. See the examples of violent death. A noose is not to be cast upon consciences, 1 Cor. 7.35.

units.la: [Vide CONSCIENTIA. Laqueus aucupis, Prou.7.23. Eccles.9.12. Amos 3.5. Laqueus strangulans hom.desperabundum, Matt.27.4. Laqueus Dei, seu iudiciorum Dei in homines descriptio, ad captum nostrum accommodata, Psalm.11.6. & 69.23. Esai.8.14. Rom.11.9. 1.Timoth.6.9. Laqueus Diaboli, 1.Tim.3.7.2. Tim.2.26. Laqueus hominis, i.varia pericula, in quæ homines aliorum hominum pessimis artibus, non sine Dei permissione, incidunt vel incidere possunt, Iosu.23.13. Iob 18.9. & 22.10. Psalm. 9.16.& 10.9.& 18.6.& 25.15.& 31.5.& 124.7. & 141.9.& 142. 4. Esai.24. verf.17.18. Thren.3.47. Ose.5.1.& 9.8. Luc.21. 34.35.]
units.tr: [See CONSCIENCE. The fowler's snare, Prov. 7.23; Eccles. 9.12; Amos 3.5. A snare that strangles the desperate man, Matt. 27.4. The snare of God, that is, a description of God's judgments upon men, fitted to our understanding, Ps. 11.6; 69.23; Isa. 8.14; Rom. 11.9; 1 Tim. 6.9. The snare of the devil, 1 Tim. 3.7; 2 Tim. 2.26. The snare of man, that is, the various dangers into which men fall, or may fall, through the worst arts of other men, not without the permission of God: Josh. 23.13; Job 18.9; 22.10; Ps. 9.16; 10.9; 18.6; 25.15; 31.5; 124.7; 141.9; 142.4; Isa. 24.17-18; Lam. 3.47; Hos. 5.1; 9.8; Luke 21.34-35.]

units.la: LARVM non comedebant Iudæi, Leuit.11.16. Deut.14.15.
units.tr: The Jews did not eat the locust, Lev. 11.16; Deut. 14.15.

units.la: LASCIVIA ἀσέλγεια damnatur, Pro.7.22. Ose.4.16. Amos,6. 4.7. Marc.7.22. Rom.13.13.2. Cor.12.21. Gal.5.19. Eph.4.19. 1.Petr.4.3.2. Pet.2.18. Iudæ.v.4.
units.tr: LASCIVIOUSNESS (ἀσέλγεια) is condemned: Prov. 7.22; Hos. 4.16; Amos 6.4-7; Mark 7.22; Rom. 13.13; 2 Cor. 12.21; Gal. 5.19; Eph. 4.19; 1 Pet. 4.3; 2 Pet. 2.18; Jude 4.

units.la: [LASSVS, defessus, ab itinere, labore vario defatigatus, Gen. 25.29. Num.21.30. Deut.25.18. Iudic.8.15. 1.Sam.30.9.10.21. 2.Samu.16.14.&17.2. LASSUS, afflictus, inopia, variaque ægriægritudine pressus, Iob. 4.5. & 22.7. Esai.28.12. & 29.8. lament. 5.5. lassus, infirmus in Dei cognitione & timore, peccator resipiscens, Esai.40.29. & 50. 4. Ierem. 31.25.
units.tr: [WEARY, tired from a journey, worn out by various toil: Gen. 25.29; Num. 21.30; Deut. 25.18; Judg. 8.15; 1 Sam. 30.9-10, 21; 2 Sam. 16.14; 17.2. WEARY, afflicted by want, and oppressed by various sickness: Job 4.5; 22.7; Isa. 28.12; 29.8; Lam. 5.5. Weary, that is, weak in the knowledge and fear of God, a sinner coming to repentance: Isa. 40.29; 50.4; Jer. 31.25.]

units.la: LATINORVM quorundam vocabulorum Græcè declinatorum catalogus, V. VOCABVLA, &c.
units.tr: A catalogue of certain Latin words declined in the Greek manner; see VOCABULARY, etc.

units.la: LATITVDO cordis data Salomoni, 1.Reg.4.29. [latitudo, locus spatiosus, 2.Sam.22.20. Ps.118.5. & 119.45. Ose.4.16. latitudo mystica, Ephes.3.18.]
units.tr: A BROAD heart was given to Solomon, 1 Kings 4.29. [breadth, a spacious place: 2 Sam. 22.20; Ps. 118.5; 119.45; Hos. 4.16. Mystical breadth: Eph. 3.18.]

units.la: ἀπτεύω & δουλεύω pro eodem, Rom.1.9. & 16.18. cùm duo ista verba in illis locis inter se commutentur. λατρεύς quoque ergo & δοῦλος idem sunt. ¶ Vana itaque, imò & falsa est illa dulæ, latreæ, & hyperdulæ distinctio à Papistis excogitata. V. DVLEA.
units.tr: λατρεύω [latreuō] and δουλεύω [douleuō] are used for the same thing, Rom. 1.9; 16.18, since these two verbs are interchanged with one another in those places. So too λάτρης [latrēs] and δοῦλος [doulos] are the same. ¶ That distinction of dulia, latria and hyperdulia, devised by the Papists, is therefore vain and even false. See DULIA.

units.la: LATRINAE ex ædé Baal factæ, 2.Reg.10.27. (Mat.15.17. Dan. 3.29.
units.tr: LATRINES made from the temple of Baal, 2 Kings 10.27. (Matt. 15.17; Dan. 3.29.)

units.la: LATRONIS cum Christo pendentis fides, Luc.23.42. Latrones. (Vide FVRES.) Vide Luc.10.30.2. Cor.11.26. Matth. 21.13.
units.tr: The faith of the thief hanging with Christ, Luke 23.42. Thieves. (See THIEVES.) See Luke 10.30; 2 Cor. 11.26; Matt. 21.13.

units.la: LATVS Christi aperitur, Ioan.19.34. V.1. Ioh.5.6.
units.tr: The side of Christ is pierced, John 19.34. See John 5.6.

units.la: LAVACRVM mysticum, Ephes.5.26. Tit.3.5. V. Ioh.5.2.
units.tr: A mystical washing, Eph. 5.26; Titus 3.5. See John 5.2.

units.la: LAVABANT Iudæi mortuos, Actor. 9.37. pedes peregrinorum, Iudic. 19.21. Genes.43.24. Vide Ioh.13.8. &c. Apocal.1.5.
units.tr: The Jews washed the dead, Acts 9.37; the feet of travellers, Judg. 19.21; Gen. 43.24. See John 13.8, etc.; Rev. 1.5.

units.la: LAVS in ore proprio sordescit, Prou.27.2.
units.tr: Praise in one's own mouth grows foul, Prov. 27.2.

units.la: LAVDIS sacrificium Deo gratissimum, Psalm. 50.14. & 107. 22. Hebr.13.15. Laus nostra Deus, Exodi 15.2. Deut.10.21. Ps.22.4. & 109.1. & 118.14. Esa.12.2. Ier.17.14 Laudis hostia offerenda per Christum, Heb.13.15. in laudem suam elegit nos Deus, Deut.26.19. Eph.1.6. Laudes immodicæ suspectæ, Prou.27.21. Laudes Deo canendæ, Ps.47.2. & 147.7. & 150.1. Esa.12.4. Eph.5.19. Col.3.16. Heb.13.15. Iac.5.13. Laudandus Deus ante & post sumptum cibum, Deuter. 8.10. Laudare Deum pro merito non possumus, Ps.96.4. & 106.2. & 119.16. & 145.3. [Laus hominum, Gen.49 8 Ps.10.3. Luc. 16.8. 1.Cor.11.2. Laus Ecclesiæ, Cant.6.8. Laus idolorum, Iudic.16.24. Dan.5.v.4.23.]
units.tr: A sacrifice of praise most pleasing to God, Ps. 50.14; 107.22; Heb. 13.15. Our praise is God, Exod. 15.2; Deut. 10.21; Ps. 22.4; 109.1; 118.14; Isa. 12.2; Jer. 17.14. A sacrifice of praise to be offered through Christ, Heb. 13.15. God chose us for his own praise, Deut. 26.19; Eph. 1.6. Excessive praises are suspect, Prov. 27.21. Praises to be sung to God, Ps. 47.2; 147.7; 150.1; Isa. 12.4; Eph. 5.19; Col. 3.16; Heb. 13.15; Jas. 5.13. God is to be praised before and after eating, Deut. 8.10. We cannot praise God on account of merit, Ps. 96.4; 106.2; 119.16; 145.3. [Praise of men: Gen. 49.8; Ps. 10.3; Luke 16.8; 1 Cor. 11.2. Praise of the Church: Song 6.8. Praise of idols: Judg. 16.24; Dan. 5.4, 23.]

units.la: Laudantium Deum exempla: Moses & Israelitæ, Exodi 15.1. Turbæ, Leuit. 9. vers.23.24. Israelitæ, Iosue 22.23. Dauid, 1.Paral.29. vers.10.11. Psalm.18.4. & 22.23. & 35.18. & 51.v.16.17. & 56.5. & 59.17. & 71.23. & 116.17. & 119.v.171.
units.tr: Examples of those who praise God: Moses and the Israelites, Exod. 15.1; the crowds, Lev. 9.23-24; the Israelites, Josh. 22.23; David, 1 Chron. 29.10-11; Ps. 18.4; 22.23; 35.18; 51.16-17; 56.5; 59.17; 71.23; 116.17; 119.171;

units.la: & 145.2. & 146.2. Leuitæ & Cantores Asaph, 2.Paralip.5. v.11.12.13.Populus Israel,7.3.Sacerdotes,Leuitæ, v.6.5 20. 19.multitudo,29.v.27.28. Sacerdotes & omnis populus, 1. Esdr.3.v.10.11.Nehemias & pars Magistratus, Nehem.12. 40.Daniel,Dan.6,10.Sidrach, Misach,& Abdenago, 3.v. 24.25.26.(vide in Apocryphis.) Nabuchodonosor.4.v.34. &c, Pueri, Matth,21.15.Angeli, Luc. 2.13. Pastores,v.20. Plebs,18 43.Turba,19.v.37.38.Discipuli,24 v.53 54. Claudus sanatus à Petro,Actor.3.versi.7.8. Paulus & Silas, 16. 25.(Vide GLORIFICANTIVM exempla.) Homines ita laudandi, ut eorum vitia non probentur. Exempla: in Asa, 1,Reg.15.14. Amasia, 2.Paralipom.25 2.Ioatham, 27.2.
units.tr: and 145.2; 146.2. The Levites and the singers of Asaph, 2 Chron. 5.11-13; the people of Israel, 7.3; the priests and Levites, 5.6, 20; 19; the multitude, 29.27-28; the priests and all the people, 1 Esdr. 3.10-11; Nehemiah and part of the magistrates, Neh. 12.40; Daniel, Dan. 6.10; Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, Dan. 3.24-26 (see in the Apocrypha); Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 4.34, etc.; children, Matt. 21.15; angels, Luke 2.13; shepherds, v. 20; the people, Luke 18.43; the crowd, 19.37-38; the disciples, 24.53-54; the lame man healed by Peter, Acts 3.7-8; Paul and Silas, Acts 16.25. (See examples of those who glorify.) Men are to be praised in such a way that their faults are not approved. Examples: Asa, 1 Kings 15.14; Amaziah, 2 Chron. 25.2; Jotham, 27.2.

units.la: LAZARVS.i.à Deo adiutus, mendicus pice ,ante ostium divitis epulonis iacet, Lucæ 16.20.
units.tr: LAZARUS, that is, helped by God: a beggar lies before the gate of the rich glutton, Luke 16.20.

units.la: LAZARVS, Christi amicus, Ioan.11.5. propter Dei gloriam morbo correptus,v.4.à mortuis excitatur, v.43. excitatus persecutionem sustinet à Iudæis.12.10.
units.tr: LAZARUS, friend of Christ, John 11.5, is struck with sickness for the glory of God, v. 4; he is raised from the dead, v. 43; having been raised, he suffers persecution from the Jews, 12.10.

units.la: LEA,filia Laban,natu maior, Gen.29.16,pro sorore Rachele supponitur, v.23. præ sorore à viro contemnitur, v.29. 30. Deus eam fœcundam reddit, ver. 31. (Leah .i. laboriosa.)
units.tr: LEAH, daughter of Laban, the elder, Gen. 29.16, is substituted for her sister Rachel, v. 23; she is despised by her husband in favour of her sister, v. 29-30; God makes her fruitful, v. 31. (Leah, that is, laborious.)

units.la: LEBBAEVS, cognominatus Thadæus, discipulus Christi, Matt.10.3. appellatur Iudas Iacobi frater, Luc.6.16.
units.tr: LEBBAEUS, surnamed Thaddaeus, a disciple of Christ, Matt. 10.3, is called the brother of James Judas, Luke 6.16.

units.la: LEBNA,seu Lebadana,locus in deserto,vbi castrametati sunt Israelitæ,Num.33.20.(.i.luna,siue albedo.)
units.tr: LIBNAH, or Libnah, a place in the desert where the Israelites encamped, Num. 33.20. (That is, moon, or whiteness.)

units.la: LEBNA,ciuitas Sacerdotum in Tribu Iuda, à Iosua capitur, Ios.10.v.29 30. & 15.42.
units.tr: LIBNAH, a city of the priests in the tribe of Judah, is taken by Joshua, Josh. 10.29-30; 15.42.

units.la: LECTIO Legis præcipitur, Iosu. 1. 8. Deuter.31.11.Lectio Legis & Prophetarum visitata, Actor.13.v.15. 27. & 15.21. Lectio Scripturarum quàm vtilis,2.Petr.1.19. Apocal.1.3. Vide 2.Tim. 1.6.& 3.versi.15.16.& 4.13. 1, Cor.10. 11.Rom. 15.4.Lectio Scripturæ sacræ Pastoribus necessaria, 1.Timoth.4.13. Vide Actor. 17. 11. psalm.1.2.Col.3.16.Deuter. 6.6.
units.tr: The reading of the Law is commanded, Josh. 1.8; Deut. 31.11. The reading of the Law and the Prophets is customary, Acts 13.15, 27; 15.21. How useful the reading of Scripture is, 2 Pet. 1.19; Rev. 1.3. See 2 Tim. 1.6; 3.15-16; 4.13; 1 Cor. 10.11; Rom. 15.4. The reading of Holy Scripture is necessary for ministers, 1 Tim. 4.13. See Acts 17.11; Ps. 1.2; Col. 3.16; Deut. 6.6.

units.la: [LEGATIO sacra,2.Cor.5.20.Ephes.6.20.] Legatus Prou.13. 17.& 25.13.
units.tr: [A holy embassy, 2 Cor. 5.20; Eph. 6.20.] An ambassador, Prov. 13.17; 25.13.

units.la: [LEGIO Angelorum Sanct. Matth.26.53. Cacodæmonum, Marc.5.7. Luc. 8. v.30.36. turmæ cursorum vel satellitum principis,2.Sam.15.18.2.Reg.11.19. 1.Paral. 18. 17. Legio dicitur quibusdam cohors trium millium peditum &trecentorum equitum. Alij numerum maiorem,alij minore constituunt. LEGIS
units.tr: [A LEGION of angels, Matt. 26.53. Of demons, Mark 5.7; Luke 8.30, 36. Troops of runners or bodyguards of a prince, 2 Sam. 15.18; 2 Kings 11.19; 1 Chron. 18.17. A legion is called by some a cohort of three thousand foot soldiers and three hundred horse. Others fix a larger or smaller number.] LAW

units.la: [ 15. 40. Num. 5. 2. 2.Reg.15.5. A Deo lepra mittitur:Leuit. 14.34.
units.tr: [15.40; Num. 5.2; 2 Kings 15.5. Leprosy is sent by God: Lev. 14.34.

units.la: LEPVS: eo non vescebantur Iudæi, Leuit. 11. 6. Deut.14.7.
units.tr: LEPER: the Jews did not eat the leper, Lev. 11.6; Deut. 14.7.

units.la: LEVI (ab audiendi verbo sic dictus) Iacobi ex Lea filius nai-citur, Gen.29.34. eius benedictio, Deut.33.8. occidit cum fratre Simeone Sichimitas, Gen.34.25. punitio istius facti, 49.5. Levi in Abrahami lumbis decimatus, Heb.7.9. [Le-vi, qui & Matthæus, Marc.2.14. Luc.5.v.27.29. Alij duo ita nominati, Luc.3.v.24.29.]
units.tr: LEVI (so called from the word for hearing) was born of Leah, a son of Jacob, Gen. 29.34. His blessing: Deut. 33.8. He, with his brother Simeon, slew the men of Shechem, Gen. 34.25. The punishment for that deed, Gen. 49.5. Levi was tithed in the loins of Abraham, Heb. 7.9. [Levi, who is also Matthew, Mark 2.14; Luke 5.27-29. Two others so named, Luke 3.24, 29.]

units.la: LEVITAE Tabernaculo destinati, Numer.1.50. & 3.6. Deut. 10.8. & 18.5. & 33.10.1. Paral.15.2. 2.paral. 26.18. & 29.11. & 35.3. Leuitæ hæreditatem propriam nullam habuerunt, sed illis pro hæreditate erat Deus, Numer. 18.20. Deut. 18.1. Iosu. 13.14. Leuitæ numerantur, Numer. 3. verfic. 15 16. Leuitæ zelo Dei prediti, Exodi 32.26. quomodo purificandi, Numer. 8. versi. 6.7. 21. Leuitarum ætas, qua ad ministerium admittebantur, versi. 24. in classes distribuuntur à Dauide, 2. Paralip. 35.4. Leuitarum officia, Numer.1.50. & 3.1. &c. & 4.4. & 18.2 Paralip.6.31. & 9. 14. 2.paralip. 8.14. & 19.8. Ezech. 44. 1. pro primogenitis Israel assumit eos sibi Deus, Numer. 3. v.12,41 & 8.16. puniunt peccatum erecti vituli, Exodi 32. 26. expelluntur ex Israel, 2. paralip. 13.14. Leuitarum habenda ratio, Deuter. 12.19. & 14.27. Leuitarum vrbes, Numer.35.v. 2.3.
units.tr: LEVITES assigned to the Tabernacle, Num. 1.50; 3.6; Deut. 10.8; 18.5; 33.10; 1 Chron. 15.2; 2 Chron. 26.18; 29.11; 35.3. The Levites had no inheritance of their own, but God was their inheritance, Num. 18.20; Deut. 18.1; Josh. 13.14. The Levites are numbered, Num. 3.15-16. The Levites, endowed with zeal for God, Exod. 32.26. How they were to be purified, Num. 8.6-7, 21. The age of the Levites at which they were admitted to the ministry, v. 24. They were distributed into classes by David, 2 Chron. 35.4. The duties of the Levites, Num. 1.50; 3.1, etc.; 4.4; 18.2; 1 Chron. 6.31; 9.14; 2 Chron. 8.14; 19.8; Ezek. 44.1. God took them to himself in place of the firstborn of Israel, Num. 3.12, 41; 8.16. They punished the sin of the erected calf, Exod. 32.26. They were expelled from Israel, 2 Chron. 13.14. The care due to the Levites, Deut. 12.19; 14.27. The cities of the Levites, Num. 35.2-3.

units.la: LEVIATHAN, à varia & valida squamarū inter se connexione dicitur, est qex ceterorū genere Balena vastissima, quę tantæ est amplitudinis, vt latissima quædam rupes aut insula potius, quàm animal quoddā in mari natās appareat. Tot-tas naues vel maximas etiam oneratas facillimè cum oneribus eucrtit. Tantam aquarum copiam per fistulam capitis eructat, & vnà tantum fumum exhalat, vt naues impleat, tenebras circum inducat, ac litora ipsa & vicinia continentem natans quatiat. Ps. 104.26. Vide eius descriptionem, Iob.40.20. ad finem vsq.: & 41.4. ad finem vsq. Alij Crocodilum nomine Leuiathan intelligunt, animal ἀμφίβιον, aliquoties incredibilis magnitudinis & roboris, vt naturalis historiæ Scriptores testantur.
units.tr: LEVIATHAN, so called from the varied and strong connection of its scales with one another, is, among the other kinds, a very vast whale, of such great size that it appears not so much an animal swimming in the sea as some very broad rock or rather an island. It very easily overturns whole ships, even the largest, even laden with cargo. It spouts such a great quantity of water through the blowhole of its head, and at the same time breathes out so much smoke, that it fills ships, brings darkness around them, and, swimming, shakes the shores and the neighbouring land. Ps. 104.26. See its description, Job 40.20 to the end, and 41.4 to the end. Others understand by the name Leviathan the crocodile, an amphibious animal, at times of incredible size and strength, as writers of natural history attest.

units.la: LEVIATHAN: eius fortitudo, Iob. 40. versf. 20. 24. [figuratè intelligitur hac voce sublimitas omnis spiritualis & corporalis, quæ vi vel fraude se aduersus Deum effert, Esai. 27. 1. JV. Balæna.
units.tr: LEVIATHAN: its strength, Job 40.20-24. [By this word is figuratively understood all lofty pride, both spiritual and bodily, which exalts itself against God by force or fraud, Isa. 27.1.] See WHALE.

units.la: EVITAS, Vide Inconstantia, & Fidelitas.
units.tr: LIGHTNESS. See Inconstancy, and Faithfulness.

units.la: EX: Lex primò pro vniuersali doctrina, Iac.1.25. Secundo, in genere, pro doctrina omni, quæ aliquid aut præscribit, aut interdicit, Rom.3.v.20.27. qua ratione Euangelium vocatur Lex fidei, ibid.hoc ést, doctrina, quæ salutem proponit sub conditione, Si crediderit, quam & ipsam conditionem gratis dat Dominus, vt implere possimus. Tertio, synecdochicæ pro ceremoniis legalibus, 1 Cor.9.20. Quarto, pro secunda Legis Tabula, Rom.13.8. Quinto, pro præceptis secundæ Tabulæ, Gal. 5.14. Sexto, pro toto veteri Testamento, Ioan.10.34. &.15.25.Ps.1.2.& 19.8.Rom.3.19.Gal.4.21. pro doctrinæ sacræ libris, 1 Cor. 14.21. Septimo, pro quinque libris Mosis, Gal.3.21. Octavo, pro Mosis & reliquorum Prophetarũ scriptis, Rom.3.21. in posteriore versus parte. Nono, pro ordinatione Aaronica Heb.7.v.12.
units.tr: LAW (Lex): first, for universal doctrine, James 1:25. Second, in general, for any doctrine that either prescribes or forbids something, Rom. 3:20, 27; in this sense the Gospel is called "the law of faith," ibid., that is, a doctrine that offers salvation under the condition "If he believes," a condition which the Lord himself gives freely so that we may be able to fulfil it. Third, by synecdoche, for the legal ceremonies, 1 Cor. 9:20. Fourth, for the second Table, Rom. 13:8. Fifth, for the precepts of the second Table, Gal. 5:14. Sixth, for the whole Old Testament, John 10:34 and 15:25; Ps. 1:2 and 19:8; Rom. 3:19; Gal. 4:21; for the books of sacred doctrine, 1 Cor. 14:21. Seventh, for the five books of Moses, Gal. 3:21. Eighth, for the writings of Moses and the other prophets, Rom. 3:21, in the latter part of the verse. Ninth, for the Aaronic priesthood, Heb. 7:12.

units.la: Lex appellatur Liber Domini, Esa.34,16. Litera, 2 Corinth.3,7. quia lapideis tabulis insculpta fuit, & audientium respectu non maiorem vim habet, quam scriptum aliquod per se omnis virtutis expers, nisi apud eos à quibus præstari possit. Eiusmodi vero facultatem cùm Lex in nobis non inueniat, sed contrarias potius tenebras, & animum prorsus ei repugnatem, ideò nihil aliud, quàm externa prædicatione docet, quid flagitet, quid prohibeat Deus: nostrum autem illud vitium non modò non emendat, sed etiam irritat, vnde præceps est ad mortem saltus, nisi aliunde remedium petatur. At Euangelium, seu nouum fœdus, quatenus Legi opponitur, per se & in se consideratum, dicitur Spiritus: primo propter veteres ceremonias, temporarias, & in rebus, crassis & corporeis positas: secundo, quia materia, argumentum, Minister denique Euangelij est Iesvs Christus, non iam docens quid fugere, quid facere oporteat (quod Legis officium est) sed seipsum in æternam vitam gratis offerens credentibus, nec offerens modò, sed etiam reipsa insinuans. (Vide LITERAM vocare solet Paulus.) Neque enim sicut Lex benedictionem, addita operum conditione, ita Euangelium iustitiam sub fidei conditione offert: (ita enim & Lex & Euangelium non vitam, sed mortem offerrent: cùm nec facere, nec credere per nos possimus) sed diuerso prorsus modo. Lex quippe opera & quidem perfecta exigit, nec facultatem operandi præbere potest, ideóque in morte iacentes damnat. Euangelium verò per Spiritum Christi, quem secum habet adiunctum, fidem quam à nobis exigit, etiam donat electis, vt in Christo per eam apprehensi iustificati ac sanctificati vitam æternam adipiscantur. Itaque Euangelium viuificum, iustitiæ, vitæ, salutis, pacis, æternum denique dicitur. Vnde illud quoque liquet, literæ appellatione expositionem, quam vocant literalem; spiritus autem nomine allegorias intelligi non debere, vt nonnulli autumant. Vide LITERA:&,EVANGELIVM spiritus dicitur.
units.tr: The Law is called the Book of the Lord, Isa. 34:16, and the letter, 2 Cor. 3:7, because it was engraved on stone tablets; and with respect to those who hear it, it has no greater power than any writing which, in itself, lacks all virtue, unless it is applied by those who can put it into practice. But since the Law does not find such ability in us, but rather darkness and a mind wholly opposed to it, it teaches nothing more than what God requires and what he forbids, by outward proclamation. Our vice, however, it not only fails to correct but even provokes, so that the leap into death is headlong unless a remedy is sought elsewhere. The Gospel, or the new covenant, insofar as it is set against the Law, considered in itself and by itself, is called Spirit: first, because of the old ceremonies, which were temporary and rested on gross and bodily things; second, because its matter, its subject, and finally its minister is Jesus Christ, who no longer teaches what must be avoided or what must be done (which is the office of the Law), but offers himself freely to believers for eternal life, and not only offers himself but actually bestows himself. (Paul is accustomed to call this the letter.) For the Law does not offer blessing on the condition of works, and the Gospel likewise offer righteousness on the condition of faith (for in that way both Law and Gospel would offer not life but death, since we are able neither to do nor to believe by our own power); rather, it does so in an entirely different way. The Law demands works, and indeed perfect ones, and cannot provide the power to perform them, so it condemns those lying in death. The Gospel, however, through the Spirit of Christ, whom it has joined to itself, also gives to the elect the faith it requires from us, so that those apprehended by it in Christ, being justified and sanctified, may obtain eternal life. Hence the Gospel is called life-giving, of righteousness, of life, of salvation, of peace, and finally eternal. From this it is also clear that by the name letter we should not understand what they call the literal exposition, nor by the name spirit should we understand allegories, as some suppose. See LETTER; and the Gospel is called Spirit.

units.la: Appellatur item Lex Ministerium mortis, 2 Cor.3.7. extra Christū scilicet consideratā: vel, quatenus facit, vt ex agnitione peccati intelligamus non esse morte dignos. Vide LITERA, Pactū Domini, 2.Par.6.11. Pædagogus noster, Gal.3.24. Vocatur autem Lex ceremonialis pædagogus, non quatenus opponitur Christo, vt chirographum mortis, Coloss.2.14. sed quatenus Christum expectatum adumbrabat: Aut, si de toto Decalogo interpretari malimus, Decalogus dicetur Pædagogus ad Christum: quia postquam nos ad agnitionem peccatorum nostrorum adduxit, simul etiam stimulum addit, vt de remedio seriò cogitemus, & ad medicum Iesum Christum plena fide & fiducia confugiamus. Dicitur item Verbum vitæ, Actor.7.38. virtus peccati, 1.Corinth.15.56. extra Christum scilicet considerata: vel quia illius aduentu peccatum, quod antè sopitum & pene mortuum iacebat, in nobis reuiuiscit, vt explicat idem Apostolus, Rom.7.9.
units.tr: The Law is also called the ministry of death, 2 Cor. 3:7, that is, considered apart from Christ; or insofar as it brings it about that, from the recognition of sin, we understand that we are not worthy of death. See LETTER. The covenant of the Lord, 2 Chron. 6:11. Our tutor, Gal. 3:24. The ceremonial Law is called a tutor, not insofar as it is opposed to Christ, like the handwriting of death, Col. 2:14, but insofar as it foreshadowed the expected Christ. Or, if we prefer to interpret it of the whole Decalogue, the Decalogue will be called a tutor to Christ, because after it has led us to the recognition of our sins, it at the same time adds a goad, so that we think seriously about the remedy and flee with full faith and trust to the physician Jesus Christ. It is also called the word of life, Acts 7:38; the power of sin, 1 Cor. 15:56, that is, considered apart from Christ; or because at his coming sin, which had lain dormant and nearly dead, is revived in us, as the same apostle explains, Rom. 7:9.

units.la: Lex quomodo per Christum Abrogata, Ephes.2.15. Coloss. 2.14. nempe implendo illam, Matth.5.18. delendo chirographum, quod aduersus nos erat, Coloss.2.14. ac à damnatoria Legis sententia & maledictione suos liberando, Rom.6.14. &c. Lex quibus Bona, 1 Tim.1.8. Lex *Ceremonialis quo sensu vocetur ab Apostolo mortis chirographum, Coloss.2.14. Vide CEREMONIA. Lex ceremonialis synecdochicè, per Circumcisionem, vt illius insitionem, intellecta, Rom.2.15. Lex quorsum Data, 3.20.&5.20. &7.7. Galat.3.19.1. Tim.1.9. Lex quorsum, & quem in finem propositá sit, explicat Apostolus, Galat.3.19. Sensuseft: Legem positam esse hominibus arguendis, vt ad promissionem tantò cupidius respicerent, & intelligerent, ligerent, patefactis transgressionibus, se sola Dei gratia quam Abrahamo patefecerat & promiserat, seruari, ac proinde omnes in Christum respicerent
units.tr: How the Law was abrogated through Christ, Eph. 2:15; Col. 2:14: namely, by fulfilling it, Matt. 5:18; by blotting out the handwriting that stood against us, Col. 2:14; and by freeing his own from the condemning sentence and curse of the Law, Rom. 6:14, etc. The Law is good for whom, 1 Tim. 1:8. In what sense the ceremonial Law is called by the Apostle the handwriting of death, Col. 2:14. See CEREMONY. The ceremonial Law is understood synecdochically, through circumcision, as its sign, Rom. 2:15. For what purpose the Law was given, 3:20; 5:20; 7:7; Gal. 3:19; 1 Tim. 1:9. For what purpose and to what end the Law was set forth, the Apostle explains, Gal. 3:19. The sense is this: the Law was laid down to convict men, so that they might look to the promise all the more eagerly and understand that, once their transgressions were laid open, they are saved by the grace of God alone, which he had revealed and promised to Abraham, and therefore that all should look to Christ.

units.la: Lex iusto posita non est, 1. Timot. 1. 9. hoc est, Lex non lata est aduersus eum, qui ad ipsius normam mores suos sponte componat, quales sunt ij soli, quos Dominus vera doctrina & Spiritu Sancto imbuit. Alij sic explicant, vt sit sensus (quae tamen explicatio cum priore pene coincidit) Iusti non egent Lege, quia Spiritus in ipsis inhabitans eos gubernat, & ipsi sua sponte ad bonum opus efficiendum se inclinant. Nonnulli dicunt, verbum κεῖται in Graeco textu positum esse pro ἵσταται, vt sit sensus: Lex non premit, non vrget iustos, quum ij qui sunt in Christo, sint extra condemnationem, Rom. 8. 1. Sunt qui locum hunc a consideratione duorum Legis terminorum, obligationis scilicet, vel ad obedientiam, vel ad poenam, explicandum censeant, vt sit sensus: Iusto Lex posita non est, scilicet ad condemnationem, intelligendo locum de altero Legis termino, quo obligat ad condemnationem & poenas aeternas inobedientes.
units.tr: The Law is not laid down for the righteous man, 1 Tim. 1:9; that is, the Law has not been enacted against the one who of his own accord shapes his conduct by its rule. Such are those alone whom the Lord has imbued with true doctrine and the Holy Spirit. Others explain it in such a way that the sense (though this explanation nearly coincides with the former) is: the righteous have no need of the Law, because the Spirit dwelling in them governs them, and they themselves are inclined of their own accord to perform good works. Some say that the verb keitai [κεῖται], used in the Greek text, stands for histatai [ἵσταται], so that the sense is: the Law does not press or urge the righteous, since those who are in Christ are outside condemnation, Rom. 8:1. Some think this passage should be explained by considering the two terms of the Law, namely its obligation either to obedience or to punishment, so that the sense is: the Law has not been laid down for the righteous, that is, for condemnation; the passage being understood of the other term of the Law, by which it binds the disobedient to condemnation and to eternal punishments.

units.la: Praeter has pias & veras explicationes, simplicissima huius loci sententia petenda videtur ex Galat. 5. 23. vt sit sententia: Iusto non est Lex posita, hoc est aduersus iustum, id est aduersus eum, qui fructus illos Spiritus in se habet, quos ibidem ponit Apostolus, non est Lex posita. Lex iram efficit, Rom. 4. 15. non sua, sed nostra culpa: quia cum iam inde a nostro exortu simus irae Dei obnoxij, superuenit postea lex, quae nostra culpa, non sua, damnationem cumulet, ac veluti coeptum opus absoluat. Lex per Mosen data, Ioan. 1. 17. Act. 7. 38. per dispositionem Angelorum accepta, Exod. 19. 1. Act. 7. 53. Gal 2. 19. ex Sione Egressa, Mich. 4. 2. Internuntij opera lata est, Galat. 3. 20. quia Deum vt terribilem ac formidabilem Legislatorem ferre non poterat Israel.
units.tr: Setting aside these pious and true explanations, the simplest sense of this passage seems to be sought from Gal. 5:23, so that the meaning is: the Law has not been laid down against the righteous, that is, against the one who has in himself those fruits of the Spirit which the Apostle lists in that place. The Law works wrath, Rom. 4:15, not by its own fault but by ours: since we are liable to the wrath of God from the moment of our coming into being, the Law comes upon us afterwards, and by our fault, not its own, it piles up condemnation and, as it were, completes a work already begun. The Law was given through Moses, John 1:17; Acts 7:38; it was received through the arrangement of angels, Exod. 19:1; Acts 7:53; Gal. 2:19; it went forth from Zion, Mic. 4:2; it was given through the agency of a mediator, Gal. 3:20, because Israel could not bear God as a terrible and formidable Lawgiver.

units.la: Leuis dicitur, 1 Ioan. 5. 3. illis scilicet, qui nouas vires coelitus acceperunt, adeo quidem, vt nulla re aeque, ac Lege Dei delectentur, nedum vt illis sit grauis & onerosa, quamuis superfit adhuc grauissimum & asperrimum spiritus cum carne certamen, id quod suo exemplo docet Apostolus, Rom. 7. 21. Sed gravis est eorum respectu, qui in carne sunt: sunt autem omnes homines in carne, qui non sunt renati ex Spiritu, adeo quidem, vt eos non modò nihil alleuet, sed etiam opprimat Legis pondus, non suo tamen, sed illorum vitio. Lex ergo per se considerata, nec grauis nec leuis dici potest, sed comparatè duntaxat, pro varia eorum conditione, quorum respectus habetur, vt explicatum est.
units.tr: It is called light, 1 John 5:3, namely for those who have received new strength from heaven, so truly that nothing delights them as much as the Law of God; much less is it burdensome and oppressive to them, although the most grievous and bitter struggle of spirit with flesh still remains, as the Apostle teaches by his own example, Rom. 7:21. But it is heavy with respect to those who are in the flesh; and all men are in the flesh who have not been born again of the Spirit, so that the weight of the Law not only does not relieve them but even crushes them, yet not by its own fault but by theirs. Therefore the Law, considered in itself, can be called neither heavy nor light, but only comparatively, according to the varied condition of those with whose situation it is concerned, as has been explained.

units.la: Lex iugiter Meditanda est, Psalm.1.2. Vide DEI Lex. perquam Pura est, 12.7. & 19.v.8.9. & 119. vers.72.127. Lex Regia est, Iac.2.8. hoc est, sine villis diuerticulis, & quasi viæ regiæ instar omnibus patens: Spiritualis, Rom.7.14. hoc est, non tantum ipsas exteriores actiones, sed inprimis intimas etiā cogitationes arguens, vt explicat Christus, Matt.5.v.21.22. Lex dicitur non esse ex fide, Gal.3.2. hoc est, non pronuntiare iustum eum, qui credit, sed qui fecerit quod ipsa præcipit. Lex Viua, ac viuifica est, si à Christo inspiretur, 2.Cor.3.17.
units.tr: The Law is to be meditated on continually, Ps. 1.2. See GOD'S LAW. It is most pure, Ps. 12.7 and 19.8-9 and 119.72, 127. It is the royal law, Jas. 2.8, that is, without crooked byways, open to all like the king's highway. It is spiritual, Rom. 7.14, that is, it condemns not only outward actions but above all the inward thoughts, as Christ explains, Matt. 5.21-22. The Law is said not to be of faith, Gal. 3.2, that is, it does not pronounce just the one who believes, but the one who does what it commands. The Law is living and life-giving if it is breathed into by Christ, 2 Cor. 3.17.

units.la: LEx Christi, pro præcepto Charitatis, Ioann.13.v.15.34.35. & 15.12. Galat.6 2. vbi mutua charitas vocatur Christi Lex, quæ etiam noua dicitur, & consistit in charitate, Matth.5.44 & 7.12.& 22.36. Ioan.13.34. Roman.13.10. Galat.5.14. & 6.2 1. Timoth.1.5. Lex Dei, Lex veritatis, Nehem.9.13. piorum oblectamentum, Psal.1 2. Vide VERBVM Dei. Lex Fidei, Rom.3.27. Vide Lex & eius significata. Lex Hominis somnio polluti, Deut.23.10. Lex Iustitiæ, Rom.9 31. Lex Libertatis, Iac.1.25. & 2.12. sic dicta, non quòd nos liberet Lex à maledictione, sed quia non nisi per Filium liberatis conuenit, quibus iam non est onus seu iugum impositum ceremonialis illius legis, Actor.15.10. imò quos ne moralis quidem lex, vt seruos sub metu retinet, sed Spiritus Dei ad voluntariam obedientiam formar. Lex Mandatorum in decretis sita, Ephe.2.15. hoc est, in ritibus ceremoniarum. Lex Operum, Roman. 3.27. sic dicta à Paulo, omnis doctrina, quæ salutem promittit cum conditione hac, Si omnia feceris: quam vnus Christus pro nobis impleuit. Lex Peccati & mortis Roman.8.2. Lex Spiritus, pro Spiritu Dei, ibid.
units.tr: THE law of Christ: the commandment of love, John 13.15, 34-35; 15.12; Gal. 6.2, where mutual love is called the law of Christ, which is also called new, and consists in love, Matt. 5.44; 7.12; 22.36; John 13.34; Rom. 13.10; Gal. 5.14; 6.2; 1 Tim. 1.5. The law of God, the law of truth, Neh. 9.13; the delight of the godly, Ps. 1.2. See WORD of God. The law of faith, Rom. 3.27. See Law and its meanings. The law of the man polluted by a dream, Deut. 23.10. The law of righteousness, Rom. 9.31. The law of liberty, Jas. 1.25; 2.12. It is so called not because the Law sets us free from the curse, but because it belongs only to those freed through the Son, on whom the yoke of that ceremonial law is no longer laid, Acts 15.10; indeed, the moral law itself does not keep them under fear as slaves, but the Spirit of God forms them to voluntary obedience. The law of commandments set in ordinances, Eph. 2.15, that is, in the rites of the ceremonies. The law of works, Rom. 3.27, so called by Paul: every doctrine that promises salvation on this condition, "If you do all these things," which Christ alone fulfilled for us. The law of sin and death, Rom. 8.2. The law of the Spirit, that is, of the Spirit of God, ibid.

units.la: LEx Dei animas conuertit, & corda exhilarat, Psal.19.v.8.9. Lex iugum intolerabile neminem iustificat, quemadmodum nec præstatur ab vllo mortalium, Act.13.38.& 15.10. Gal.2 16.& 3.10. Lex omnibus legenda, Deut.31,12. Lex legitur, 15. & 31.v.9.11. Iof.8.33.2 Reg.23.2. Nehem.8.8.8 9.3. Iram operatur, Rom.4.15. Vide supra. Per fidem stabilitur. litur,3 31.in Sacerdotū ore versetur oportet, Deut.33.v, 9.10.Malach.2.7.Lex & Prophetæ ad Ioannem vsque durant,Matth.11.13. Luc.16.16.
units.tr: THE law of God converts souls and gladdens hearts, Ps. 19.8-9. The law, as an intolerable yoke, justifies no one, and indeed no mortal performs it, Acts 13.38; 15.10; Gal. 2.16; 3.10. The law is to be read by all, Deut. 31.12. The law is read, Deut. 15; 31.9, 11; Josh. 8.33; 2 Kings 23.2; Neh. 8.8; 9.3. It works wrath, Rom. 4.15. See above. It is established through faith. It must be in the mouth of the priests, Deut. 33.9-10; Mal. 2.7. The Law and the Prophets last until John, Matt. 11.13; Luke 16.16.

units.la: LEGIS Absolutio in proximi dilectione sita, Rom.13.v. 8.10. (Galat.5.14.) cuius di&i sensus est: Qui diligit alterum, non vnicum aliquod præceptum obiit, sed in genere præstitit quod Lex iubet. Itaque non agit eo loco Apostolus de perfecta vel imperfecta Legis obseruatione, vt nugantur Sophistæ, sed charitatem vt Legis summam commendat, sicut apparet ex ratione, quæ subiicitur, & conclusione, quæ attexitur, nec est aliter intelligenda. Legis Ceremoniæ abrogantur per Christum, Mat.11.13.Marc.15.38.Act.13.38.39.& 15.11.Rom.6.14.& 7.4 & 8.3.Galat.3 13.& 4.5.Eph.2,13.Col.2 14.1 Petr.1.v.11.18. Legis contemtus valde noxius,Prov.28.9.Ierem.11.3.Vide VERBI Dei contemtus.
units.tr: OF THE LAW: The fulfilling of the Law consists in love of one's neighbour, Rom. 13.8-10 (Gal. 5.14). The sense of this saying is: whoever loves another has not performed some single commandment, but has in general done what the Law commands. So the Apostle in that place does not treat of the perfect or imperfect observance of the Law, as the sophists trifle, but commends love as the sum of the Law, as is clear from the reason that follows and the conclusion that is added; nor is it to be understood otherwise. The ceremonies of the Law are abrogated through Christ, Matt. 11.13; Mark 15.38; Acts 13.38-39; 15.11; Rom. 6.14; 7.4; 8.3; Gal. 3.13; 4.5; Eph. 2.13; Col. 2.14; 1 Pet. 1.11, 18. Contempt of the Law is very harmful, Prov. 28.9; Jer. 11.3. See contempt of the WORD of God.

units.la: Legis Finis Christus, Romanⁱ.10.4.hoc est, quicunque credit in Christum, habet quod Lex requirit: videlicet perfectam erga Legem obedientiam & iustitiam,quam Christus credenti imputat.Finis enim Legis, est iustificare illos, qui perfectè eam implent & obseruant:quem finem quò minús assequamur, non vlla Legis ipsius qualitas, sed carnis nostræ vitiofitas impedit, cui demum ita medetur Christus,vt in eo vno gratis per fidem imputato,sinem Legis consequamur,per illum scilicet iustificati, qui pro nobis Legem impleuit, factus pro nobis iustitia, sanctificatio,&c.1.Cor.1,30.
units.tr: The end of the Law is Christ, Rom. 10.4, that is, whoever believes in Christ has what the Law requires, namely perfect obedience and righteousness toward the Law, which Christ imputes to the believer. For the end of the Law is to justify those who fully fulfil and keep it. What prevents us from attaining this end is not any quality of the Law itself, but the sinfulness of our flesh; Christ heals this so that, in him alone, imputed freely through faith, we attain the end of the Law, being justified through him who fulfilled the Law for us, made for us wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, etc., 1 Cor. 1.30.

units.la: Legis Impletio sine Spiritu Dei fieri & præstari à nobis non potest,Deut.5.29.Psal.118.24.Luc.18.22.Actor.15. 10. Rom.8.2. Legis infirmitas, Rom.8.3. Hebr.7.19.& 10. 1. Legis iustitia, Rom.10.5. Legis liber in templo repertus,2 Reg.22.8.2. Par.34.14. Legis natura,officium & operatio, Rom.3.20. & 4.15. & 5.20,& 7.v.1.7.Galat.3.19.1. Tim.1.8. Heb.7.v.1827. Legis obseruatio commendatur, Proverb.28.7. Eccles.12.15.Malach.4.4.Matth.19.17. Legis obseruatores vltroneos esse oportet, Psal.112.1. Legis obseruatio vitā adfert, Leuit.18.5.Ezech.20.11.Rom.10.5. Legis partes: Lex in tres partes ab Apostolo distribuitur Rom.9 4.in διαθηκας, seu Legem,quam vocant, moralem νομοθεσιαν, seu Legem iudicialem:& λατρειαν, seu Legem ceremonialem: vbi διαθηκων nomine intelligendæ sunt Tabulæ fœderis, vt vocantur Deut. 9.v.11.15. Heb.9.4. vtitur autem plurali numero, quod duæ essent Tabulæ: quæ interpretatio commodior esse videtur, quàm si ad fœdus cum Abrahamo & eius posteris initium referas: Primùm, quia non nisi vnum fuit hoc fœdus, quamuis sæpius renouatum: secundò, quia paulò post meminit ibidem promissionum, quæ ab illo fœdere vix possunt secerni: postremò, quia sic videtur distinxisse Legem Paulus commodissimè in suas illas partes, Moralem, Iudicialem, & Ceremonialem, de qua ante. Vide & ἐντολή. Legis summa, Matth.7.12 & 22.40. Luc.10.27. Legis transgressores maledicti, Deu.27.26. Gal.3.10. (Vide OBEDIENDVM Legi Dei.) Legis in vno capite transgressor efficitur omnium reus, Iac.2.10. Quia vnus & idem est Legislator, & corpus Legis indiuiduum: v.11. Legis Tabulæ dantur scriptæ digito Dei, Exodi 31.18. Deut. 5.22. franguntur, Exodi 32.19. Deut.9.17. dantur aliæ Tabulæ, Exod.34.27. Deut. 10.1.
units.tr: The fulfilling of the Law cannot be done or performed by us without the Spirit of God, Deut. 5.29; Ps. 118.24; Luke 18.22; Acts 15.10; Rom. 8.2. The weakness of the Law, Rom. 8.3; Heb. 7.19; 10.1. The righteousness of the Law, Rom. 10.5. The book of the Law found in the temple, 2 Kings 22.8; 2 Chr. 34.14. The nature, office and working of the Law, Rom. 3.20; 4.15; 5.20; 7.1, 7; Gal. 3.19; 1 Tim. 1.8; Heb. 7.18-27. The observance of the Law is commended, Prov. 28.7; Eccl. 12.13; Mal. 4.4; Matt. 19.17. The observers of the Law ought to be willing, Ps. 112.1. The observance of the Law brings life, Lev. 18.5; Ezek. 20.11; Rom. 10.5. The parts of the Law: the Apostle divides the Law into three parts, Rom. 9.4, in the covenants [διαθῆκαι], or what they call the moral Law, the legislation [νομοθεσία], or the judicial Law, and the worship [λατρεία], or the ceremonial Law. Here "covenants" is to be understood of the tablets of the covenant, as they are called in Deut. 9.11, 15; Heb. 9.4. He uses the plural because there were two tables. This interpretation seems more suitable than referring the beginning to the covenant with Abraham and his posterity: first, because there was only one covenant, though often renewed; second, because a little later in the same passage he mentions promises, which can hardly be separated from that covenant; lastly, because Paul seems to have divided the Law most conveniently into those parts, moral, judicial and ceremonial, mentioned above. See also commandment [ἐντολή]. The sum of the Law, Matt. 7.12; 22.40; Luke 10.27. The transgressors of the Law are cursed, Deut. 27.26; Gal. 3.10. (See OBEYING the Law of God.) Whoever offends in one point of the Law is made guilty of all, Jas. 2.10, because one and the same is the Lawgiver, and the body of the Law is indivisible, v. 11. The tables of the Law were given written with the finger of God, Exod. 31.18; Deut. 5.22; they were broken, Exod. 32.19; Deut. 9.17; other tables were given, Exod. 34.27; Deut. 10.1.

units.la: Legis & Euangelij discrimé, 2.Cor.3.v.7.8. (Vide EVANGELIVM & Legi discrimen.) Legis & fidei repugnantia qualis Gal.3.12.
units.tr: The distinction between Law and Gospel, 2 Cor. 3.7-8. (See GOSPEL and distinction of Law.) The opposition between Law and faith, as in Gal. 3.12.

units.la: LEGVM iniquarum conditores reprehenduntur, Esai. 10.1. LIA, Vide LEA.
units.tr: The makers of unjust laws are rebuked, Isa. 10.1. LIA: see LEA.

units.tr: [LEBANON, a noble mountain in Syria, abounding in trees, cedars, etc., Judg. 3.3; 1 Kings 5.6, etc. Mystical Lebanon, Song 4.8, etc.; Isa. 2.13; 60.13.] (i.e. white, or frankincense.)

units.tr: The bill of divorce and its law, Deut. 24.1-4; Isa. 50.1; Jer. 3.3; Mal. 2.16; Matt. 5.31; why it was permitted by Moses, 19.8; Mark 10.5. Those who maintain that after divorce there is no place for a second marriage abuse the saying in Luke 16.18.

Liber ἀντίθρωπος Deo tribuitur, qui vocatur Liber vitæ, & viuentium, Exod.32.32. Psal.69.29. Dan.12.1. Phil.4.3. Apoc.3.5. & 20.12.27. Liber volans Zachariæ ostensus, Zachar. 5.2. Libri curiosi combusti, Actor. 19.19. Librorum lectio vtilissima, Dan.9.2. [Liber mysticus, Apoc.5.v.1,2,&c. Liber Dei, seu Gratiæ, Sapientiæ & Gubernationis diuinæ Exod.32.33.34.Psal.139.16.Esai.34.16.Dan.7.10. Malac. 3.16. Apoc. 20.12.]
units.tr: BOOK, in the sense of a register, Matt. 1.1; in the sense of law, Ps. 40.8; Heb. 10.7. The book of the living, 2 Chr. 9.29; 12.15; 13.22. See the catalogue of certain books, etc. The book of life is attributed to God, which is called the book of life and of the living, Exod. 32.32; Ps. 69.29; Dan. 12.1; Phil. 4.3; Rev. 3.5; 20.12, 27. See also Luke 10.20, where the names of the godly are said to be written in heaven. The scroll sent to Ezekiel, Ezek. 2.9, eaten by Ezekiel, 3.3, and by John, Rev. 10.10. The flying scroll shown to Zechariah, Zech. 5.2. Curious books burned, Acts 19.19. The reading of books is most useful, Dan. 9.2. [The mystical book, Rev. 5.1-2, etc. The book of God, or of grace, of wisdom and of divine government, Exod. 32.33-34; Ps. 139.16; Isa. 34.16; Dan. 7.10; Mal. 3.16; Rev. 20.12.]

units.tr: [Book, contract, bond, deeds of purchase, Jer. 32.10, etc. Letter, epistle, Isa. 37.14; 39.1; Jer. 29.25, 29. The liberal arts and sciences, Dan. 1.17.]

units.la: LIBRORVM quorundam sacrorum catalogus, qui interciderunt. Liber bellorum Domini, Numer.21.14. Liber Iusti, Ios.10.13. alij librum recti interpretantur, hoc est, librum forensium annalium, siue actorum publicorum, qui interciderunt, vt alij multi forenses, quorum Scriptura meminit. Liber Nathan, 2. Paral. 9.29. 1. Par.29.29. liber Gad, ibid. liber Semeiæ. 2. Par. 12. 15. liber Haddo, 9.29. & 12.15. liber Ahiæ, 9.29. liber Iehu filij Hanani, 20.34.
units.tr: A catalogue of certain sacred books that have perished. The Book of the Wars of the Lord, Num. 21.14. The Book of the Upright, Josh. 10.13. Others interpret "the book of the upright" as the book of the public annals or official records, which have perished, as did many other public records that Scripture mentions. The Book of Nathan, 2 Chr. 9.29; 1 Chr. 29.29. The Book of Gad, ibid. The Book of Shemaiah, 2 Chr. 12.15. The Book of Iddo, 9.29; 12.15. The Book of Ahijah, 9.29. The Book of Jehu son of Hanani, 20.34.

units.la: LIBERI recte, & ex Dei verbo instituendi, Exod.12.24. & 13.14. Daniel 4.9.& 6.3.10.&9.3.&c. Liberi castigandi, Prou. 22.15.& 23.v.13.14. Ephes.6.4. humaniter fouendi, ibidem. Idolis non sacrificādi, Leuit.20.2.& 18.21. Deu.18.10. in vtero sanctificati, 1. Co.7.14. Liberi non ex æquo à parentibus dilecti. Exempla: Esau & Iacob, Gen.25.28. Ioseph & alij fratres, 37.3.
units.tr: CHILDREN are rightly and from the Word of God to be instructed, Exod. 12.24; 13.14; Dan. 4.9; 6.3, 10; 9.3, etc. Children are to be disciplined, Prov. 22.15; 23.13-14; Eph. 6.4, and kindly cherished, ibid. They are not to be sacrificed to idols, Lev. 20.2; 18.21; Deut. 18.10. They are sanctified in the womb, 1 Cor. 7.14. Children are not loved equally by their parents. Examples: Esau and Jacob, Gen. 25.28; Joseph and the other brothers, 37.3.

units.la: LIBERORVM erga parentes officium. Ephes. 6.1.2.3. Primum debent amorem. Exempla: Ioseph, Genesis 46.29 Elisæus, 1. Regum 19.20. Discipulus quidam, Matth.8.21. Secundo honorem. Exod.20.12. Exempla: Sem & Iapheth, Genes. 9.23. Ioseph, 46.29. & 48.12. Salomon, 1. Regum 2.19. Patlus & Hebraei, Hebr.12.9. Tertio, obedientiam. Col.3.20. Pro.23.22. Exempla: Isaac, Genes.22.v.6.&c. Iacob. 28.v.1.2. Ioseph, 37.v.13.14. Filia Iephte, Iudic.11.v.36.37. Samuel. 1. Sam.1,24.& 2.26. Salomon, 1. Reg.2.20. Rechabitę, Ierem. 35.v.18.19. Christus, Luc.2,51. Idem præcipit & Paulus fieri, Ephes.6.1. Coloss.3.20. Quarto, nutritionem. 1. Tim.5.4. Pro.28.24. Exemplum: Ioseph. Genes.45.v.9.10.11. Christus, Ioh.19.26.27. Minæ in contumaces, Deut.21.18. Exod.21, 15.& 17. Matth.15.4. Prou.19 26.& 30.17.
units.tr: The duty of children toward their parents, Eph. 6.1-3. First, they owe love. Examples: Joseph, Gen. 46.29; Elisha, 1 Kings 19.20; a certain disciple, Matt. 8.21. Secondly, honour, Exod. 20.12. Examples: Shem and Japheth, Gen. 9.23; Joseph, 46.29; 48.12; Solomon, 1 Kings 2.19; Paul and the Hebrews, Heb. 12.9. Thirdly, obedience, Col. 3.20; Prov. 23.22. Examples: Isaac, Gen. 22.6, etc.; Jacob, 28.1-2; Joseph, 37.13-14; the daughter of Jephthah, Judg. 11.36-37; Samuel, 1 Sam. 1.24; 2.26; Solomon, 1 Kings 2.20; the Rechabites, Jer. 35.18-19; Christ, Luke 2.51. Paul likewise commands this to be done, Eph. 6.1; Col. 3.20. Fourthly, support, 1 Tim. 5.4; Prov. 28.24. Example: Joseph, Gen. 45.9-11; Christ, John 19.26-27. Threats against the disobedient, Deut. 21.18; Exod. 21.15, 17; Matt. 15.4; Prov. 19.26; 30.17.
