units.la: MALEDICENTIA infidelium vitæ nostræ sanctimonia co-hibenda, 1.Petr.2.v.12.15. Maledici fugiendi: (Vide OB-TRECTATORES.)
units.tr: EVIL-SPEAKING: the slander of unbelievers is to be restrained by the holiness of our life, 1 Pet. 2.12, 15. Evil-speakers are to be avoided. (See DETRACTORS.)

units.la: MALEDICENS nomini Dei lapidatur, Leuit.24.10. &c. non maledicendum persecutoribus, Rom.12.14.
units.tr: A BLASPHEMER of God's name is stoned, Lev. 24.10, etc. One must not curse persecutors, Rom. 12.14.

units.la: Maledicit Deus hominibus peccatoribus, & propter eos reliquis creaturis, vel gratiam suam iustè subtrahens vel etiam pœnas temporales aut æternas peccatori-bus infligens. 2. maledicit impius Deo, vel piis. 3. Aliquoties pius in impios maledictiones Dei pronun-tiat. 4. Maledicit homo, seu maledictionem effert & optat creaturis.
units.tr: God curses sinful men, and for their sake the other creatures, either justly withdrawing his grace or inflicting temporal or eternal punishments on sinners. 2. The impious man curses God or the pious. 3. Sometimes the pious pronounce God's curses on the impious. 4. A man curses, that is, utters and wishes curses upon creatures.

units.la: Maledictio duplex consideratur. 1. Dei gratiam iustè subtrahit, & pœnis temporariis vel æternis punit pecca-tores. 2. Hominis iusti vel iniusti, maledictionem in alios efferentis.
units.tr: A curse is considered in two ways. 1. God justly withdraws his grace and punishes sinners with temporal or eternal punishments. 2. The curse of a righteous or unrighteous man, uttered against others.

units.la: MALEDICTIONIS, quā Deus homini & rebus creatis maledi-cit, exempla: Serpenti, Gen.3.14: terræ, v.17. Cain, 4.11: Po-pulo suo, Thren.2.7: impiis & reprobis, Matth.25.41. Male-dictiones in monte Hebal. Deut. 27.13. maledictiones & benedictiones, Genes.3.v.14.17. & 8.21. & 9.25. & 24.41.& 27.28. 48.v.15 20. & 49.7. Numer.5.21. Deuter. 11.26.& 27.15. Ios.8.34. Iudic.9.20. 1 Sam.17.43. 2 Sam, 2.5. & 16.7. 2 Reg.2.24. Nehem.5.13. Prouerb.26.2. Ierem. 29.2. & 49.13. Zach.8,13.
units.tr: CURSES with which God curses man and created things. Examples: the serpent, Gen. 3.14; the earth, v. 17; Cain, 4.11; his people, Lam. 2.7; the impious and reprobate, Matt. 25.41. Curses on Mount Ebal, Deut. 27.13; curses and blessings, Gen. 3.14, 17; 8.21; 9.25; 24.41; 27.28; 48.15, 20; 49.7; Num. 5.21; Deut. 11.26, 27.15; Josh. 8.34; Judg. 9.20; 1 Sam. 17.43; 2 Sam. 2.5, 16.7; 2 Kings 2.24; Neh. 5.13; Prov. 26.2; Jer. 29.2, 49.13; Zech. 8.13.

units.la: MALEDICTIONES hominum, quæ Christi causā fiunt. Vide
units.tr: CURSES of men which are done for Christ's sake. See

units.la: HOMO. Maledictionis hominis in hominem, ex vocatione ra-men concepta, exempla: Noë in Cham, Genef.9.25. Isaac in ofores Iacobi,27,29. Iacob Simeoni & Leui, 49.7. Moses transgressoribus Legis, Deuter.27.13. &c. Iosue in Ieri-chuntis instauratores,Ios.6.26. Sichimitæ in Abimelech, Iudic.9.27. Vir Dei in habitatores Meroz, 5.23. Dauid in Ioab,2 Sam.3.29. Semei in Dauidem, 16.5 & 19.21. 1 Reg. 2.8. Dauid in hostes suos,1 Samuel 26.19. Elisæus in pueros,2.Reg.2,24. Christus in ficum. Matth.21.19. in Iudam, 26.24. in diuites, Luc.6.24. in Chorazin & Bethsaida, 10.13. in Pharisæos,11.42. Pharisæi in Christum & in cœcum natum, Ioan.9.28. &c. Paulus in pseudoprophetas, Gal.5.12. Impij in Paulum,1 Cor.4.12. 1 Tim.4.10. Maledicenti non maledicit Christus, 1 Pet.2.23. maledicentibus non maledicendum,1.Pet.3.9. Paulus benedicit,1 Cor.4.12.
units.tr: MAN. Examples of a man's curse on a man, conceived though from a calling: Noah on Ham, Gen. 9.25; Isaac on the sons of Jacob, 27.29; Jacob on Simeon and Levi, 49.7; Moses on the transgressors of the Law, Deut. 27.13, etc.; Joshua on the restorers of Jericho, Josh. 6.26; the Shechemites on Abimelech, Judg. 9.27; the man of God on the inhabitants of Meroz, 5.23; David on Joab, 2 Sam. 3.29; Shimei on David, 16.5 and 19.21; 1 Kings 2.8; David on his enemies, 1 Sam. 26.19; Elisha on the boys, 2 Kings 2.24; Christ on the fig tree, Matt. 21.19; on Judas, 26.24; on the rich, Luke 6.24; on Chorazin and Bethsaida, 10.13; on the Pharisees, 11.42. The Pharisees on Christ and on the man born blind, John 9.28, etc. Paul on false prophets, Gal. 5.12. The impious on Paul, 1 Cor. 4.12; 1 Tim. 4.10. Christ did not curse the one who cursed him, 1 Pet. 2.23; one must not curse those who curse, 1 Pet. 3.9. Paul blesses, 1 Cor. 4.12.

units.la: MALEDICTVM pro maledicto non reddendum, 1 Petr.3.9. Maledictus qui pendet è ligno, Deuter.21.23. Christus pro nobis maledictum, Galat.3.13. & peccatum, id est, oblatio propitiatoria pro peccato,2. Cor.5.21. Maledictus qui Legem non implet, Deuter.27.26. Gal.3.10. Maledicti hædi, Matth. 25.41. maledicti non possidebunt Regnum, 1 Corinth.6.10. non maledicendum surdo, Leuitic.19.14.
units.tr: MALEDICTUM: a curse is not to be repaid with a curse, 1 Pet. 3.9. Cursed is he who hangs on a tree, Deut. 21.23. Christ was made a curse for us, Gal. 3.13, and sin, that is, a propitiatory offering for sin, 2 Cor. 5.21. Cursed is he who does not fulfil the Law, Deut. 27.26; Gal. 3.10. Cursed goats, Matt. 25.41. The cursed will not possess the kingdom, 1 Cor. 6.10. One must not curse the deaf, Lev. 19.14.

units.la: MALEFACTA beneficiis vincenda, Rom.12.20.
units.tr: Evil deeds are to be overcome with kindnesses, Rom. 12.20.

units.la: MALEFICI à Deo exterminandi, Malach.3,5. Malefici morte digni (Vide INCANTATORES.) Exod.22.18. 1 Petr. 2.14. Luc.23.35.39.
units.tr: EVILDOERS are to be destroyed by God, Mal. 3.5. Evildoers deserving death (see SORCERERS), Exod. 22.18; 1 Pet. 2.14; Luke 23.35, 39.

units.la: Maleficium, Incantatio, Esai. 47.9.12. Mich.5.12. Nahum.3.4. Maleficus, Incantator, Magus, Præstigiator, Exod. 7.11.22. 8.7. &c.9.11. Deuter.18.10. Iere.27.9. Mal.3.5. Exo. 22.18.
units.tr: Sorcery, enchantment, Isa. 47.9, 12; Mic. 5.12; Nah. 3.4. Sorcerer, enchanter, magician, trickster, Exod. 7.11, 22; 8.7, etc.; 9.11; Deut. 18.10; Jer. 27.9; Mal. 3.5; Exod. 22.18.

units.la: MALIGNITAS, est ipsius malitiæ & cogitationis nostræ in proximum noxiæ effectum, quòd vel opere, vel voto fit & demonstratur. Neque enim intra solius cogitationis fines se continet is, qui malignus est vel nequam vel improbus. Anselm.in Rom.c.1.
units.tr: MALICE is the harmful effect, against a neighbour, of wickedness itself and of our thought, which is done and shown either by deed or by wish. For the one who is malignant, wicked or depraved does not keep himself within the bounds of thought alone. Anselm on Rom. ch. 1.

units.la: [MALIGN Vs homo Iob. 5.12. psal.5.5. & 15.4. & 119.115. Malignus Satan 1.Ioan.2.v.13.14, & 3.12. & 5.v.18.19. Maligni Spiritus Luc.8.2.
units.tr: [MALIGNANT: a man, Job 5.12; Ps. 5.5; 15.4; 119.115. The malignant Satan, 1 John 2.13, 14; 3.12; 5.18, 19. Malignant spirits, Luke 8.2.

units.la: MALITIA, est mens & cogitatio nostra, machinans alterum quocunq; modo lædere. Huic contraria est Innocentia: de qua suo loco.
units.tr: MALICE is our mind and thought, plotting to harm another in any way. Its opposite is innocence, of which in its place.

units.la: MALITIA damnatur, Rom.1.29. Ephes.4.31. Col.3,8. Iac.1.21.1.Petr.2.1.malitia hominis multa, Gen.6.5. malitia omnis auferenda, Ephes.4.31. Col.3.8. malitiae veteris fermentum,1. Corint.5.8. In malitia perseuerantes pereunt, 1 Sam.12.25.malitia vt pueri efficiamur,studere debemus, 1.Cor.14.20.
units.tr: MALICE is condemned, Rom. 1.29; Eph. 4.31; Col. 3.8; Jas. 1.21; 1 Pet. 2.1. The malice of man is great, Gen. 6.5. All malice is to be put away, Eph. 4.31; Col. 3.8. The leaven of old malice, 1 Cor. 5.8. Those who persist in malice perish, 1 Sam. 12.25. We ought to strive to be children in malice, 1 Cor. 14.20.

units.la: MALVM omne fugiendum, Psal.34.15.& 37.27. & 119,v.101. 128.Prouerb.3.29.Esa.1.16.Ezech.18.21.Amos.5.15.Rom.12.9.1.Ioan.3.v.4.3 Ioan.3.v.11.Malum dicens bonum punie tur. Esa.5.20. Malach.2.17. Prou.24.24. Malum pro malo non reddendum, Prouerb. 17.13. & 20.22. & 24.29. Rom.12.v.14.17.1.Corint.4.12.1.Thess.5.15.1.Petr.3.9 (Vide VINDICTA) Malum bono vincendum, Rom.12.21.A malo ita abstinendum, vt quod bonum est facias,Psal.34.15. & 37.27. Esa. I.v.16.17, & 55.7. Ephes.4.28.1.Petr.3.11.
units.tr: EVIL every evil is to be shunned, Ps. 34.15; 37.27; 119.101; 128; Prov. 3.29; Isa. 1.16; Ezek. 18.21; Amos 5.15; Rom. 12.9; 1 John 3.4, 11. He who calls evil good is punished, Isa. 5.20; Mal. 2.17; Prov. 24.24. Evil is not to be repaid with evil, Prov. 17.13; 20.22; 24.29; Rom. 12.14, 17; 1 Cor. 4.12; 1 Thess. 5.15; 1 Pet. 3.9 (see REVENGE). Evil is to be overcome with good, Rom. 12.21. One must abstain from evil so that one does what is good, Ps. 34.15; 37.27; Isa. 1.16-17; 55.7; Eph. 4.28; 1 Pet. 3.11.

units.la: Malum poenae a Deo est,Deut.32.23 1.Reg.9.6 & 21.29. Esa.45.7.Ier.11.11.& 32.42.Amos,3.6. Ionae.3.10,Mich,1.12 & 2.3. malum culpae summe auertsatur Deus, tantum abest, vt eum autorem habeat, Exod.23, 7.2. Paral. 19.7. Iob.34.10. Psalm.5.v.5.7, & 45.8, Prou.15. v.8.9, Osee. 13, 9: Roman. 9,14,2, Cor.6.15, Iac.1.13, Malos Rectores & Praepositos permittit Deus ob peccata populi.2. Reg,12, 20,Iob 34.30,Esa.29.10,Ezech,14.6,Osee 13.11,2,Thess.2. 11.(Vide MAGISTRATAS:malus) Iubetque obedientiam illis praestare,Matt,23,3, malorum etiam ministrorum opera vtitur Deus,Matt.7.22. Marc.9,9,38. Luc.49.[malorum confortiu vitandum, vide SOCIETAS mali species fugienda.1, Thess,5.22, malo consentire quam noxium,Rom.1.32, malorum inuentores miseri, Prou,11,27.
units.tr: Evil of punishment comes from God, Deut. 32.23; 1 Kgs. 9.6; 21.29; Isa. 45.7; Jer. 11.11; 32.42; Amos 3.6; Jonah 3.10; Mic. 1.12; 2.3. But the evil of fault God utterly averts; so far is he from being its author, Exod. 23.7; 2 Chr. 19.7; Job 34.10; Ps. 5.5, 7; 45.8; Prov. 15.8-9; Hos. 13.9; Rom. 9.14; 2 Cor. 6.15; Jas. 1.13. God permits wicked rulers and governors on account of the sins of the people, 2 Kgs. 12.20; Job 34.30; Isa. 29.10; Ezek. 14.6; Hos. 13.11; 2 Thess. 2.11 (see MAGISTRATE: wicked). He also bids obedience to be rendered to them, Matt. 23.3. God also makes use of the works of wicked ministers, Matt. 7.22; Mark 9.9, 38; Luc.49. [Evil company is to be avoided, see SOCIETY. The appearance of evil is to be shunned, 1 Thess. 5.22. To consent to evil is harmful, Rom. 1.32. The inventors of evils are wretched, Prov. 11.27.]

units.la: MAMBRE Locus, siue vrbs, quae etiam dicitur Hebron, Genef.13,18.& 23.19.
units.tr: MAMRE: a place, or town, also called Hebron, Gen. 13.18; 23.19.

units.la: MAMMONA iniquo parandi amici, Luc.16.9. estque vox Syra,idem significans quod Graecis μαμωνᾶς, diuitiae,& quaecunque ad rem pecuniariam pertinent, Matth,6,24,dicitur autē sic,quasi dicat,diuitiae fraudulentę,fallaces, fraudatrices,quòd (experientia teste) nihil iis incertius.
units.tr: MAMMON: "make friends by unrighteous mammon," Luke 16.9. It is a Syriac word meaning the same as the Greek mammōnas, riches, and whatever pertains to money matters, Matt. 6.24. It is so called as if to say deceitful, fallacious, defrauding riches, because (as experience attests) nothing is more uncertain than they.

units.la: MANNAE & aquae ex petra profluentis coena,fuit sacramentum V. T. quo Israelitae cibo coelitus demisso alebantur, ad significandam spiritualem alimoniam carnis Christi, & aquâ ex rupe profluente potabantur, ad significandum spiritualem potum sanguinis Christi:1 Cor.10.3.4.Exod. 16.14. 15.Ioh.7.37.c.
units.tr: MANNA and the water flowing from the rock were a sacrament of the Old Testament: by the food sent down from heaven the Israelites were nourished, signifying the spiritual nourishment of the flesh of Christ, and by the water flowing from the rock they were given drink, signifying the spiritual drink of the blood of Christ: 1 Cor. 10.3-4; Exod. 16.14-15; John 7.37, etc.

units.la: MAN cibus quadraginta annis è cœlo Israelitis datus, Exodi 16.15. Deut.8.3. Ps.105.40. Man quale, Exodi 16.31. Numer. 11.7. Man reseruatur, & quare, Exodi 16.32. Man spernunt Israelitæ, Numer.11.6. Mannæ & Christi collatio Ioan.6. v.31.32.49.58. Man figura & symbolum Christi, 1 Cor.10. v.3.6. panis cœlestis & esca spiritualis dicitur Ioan.6.31. 1 Cor.10.3. hoc est, spirituale aliquid significans. Man dicitur panis Angelorum seu robustissimorum, quia illi ipsum administrabant. Ps.78.25.
units.tr: MANNA: food given to the Israelites from heaven for forty years, Exod. 16.15; Deut. 8.3; Ps. 105.40. What manna was like, Exod. 16.31; Num. 11.7. Manna is kept, and why, Exod. 16.32. The Israelites despise manna, Num. 11.6. Comparison of manna and Christ, John 6.31-32, 49, 58. Manna is a figure and symbol of Christ, 1 Cor. 10.3, 6. It is called heavenly bread and spiritual food, John 6.31; 1 Cor. 10.3, that is, signifying something spiritual. Manna is called the bread of angels, or of the most mighty, because they themselves administered it, Ps. 78.25.

units.la: MANAHEN, Rex Israel, 2 Reg.15.v.14.17. impius est.v.18. tributa potentibus & diuitibus Israelitis imperat, v.20. moritur, v.22. (i.consolans.)
units.tr: MANAHEN, king of Israel, 2 Kgs. 15.14, 17. He is impious, v. 18. He imposes tribute on the powerful and rich Israelites, v. 20. He dies, v. 22. (i.e. comforting.)

units.la: MANAHEN, Christianus Propheta, Act.13.1.
units.tr: MANAHEN, a Christian prophet, Acts 13.1.

units.la: MANASSES Iosephi primogenitus: eius nominis ratio. Gen. 41.51. a Iacobo benedicitur 48.v.14.15. 16. postponitur fratri natu minori, v.19.20. (i.obliuiosus.)
units.tr: MANASSEH, firstborn son of Joseph: the reason for the name, Gen. 41.51. Blessed by Jacob, 48.14-16; placed after his younger brother, vv. 19-20. (i.e. forgetful.)

units.la: MANASSES filius Ezechiæ, Rex Iuda constituitur, 2 Reg.20. 21.2. Paral.32.33. eius idololatria 2 Reg.21.v.3.6.2 Par.33.v. 3.6. cruore innocenti Ierusalem implet, 2.Reg.21.v.16. & 24.4: vinctus in Babylonem ducitur, 2 Par.33.11: ad Deum orans conuertitur, v.12. in regnum reducitur, v.13. moritur, 2 Reg.21.18. 2 Paral. 33.20. eius impietas Iudæorum excidij causa, Ierem.15.4.
units.tr: MANASSEH, son of Hezekiah, is made king of Judah, 2 Kgs. 20; 21.2; 2 Chr. 32.33. His idolatry, 2 Kgs. 21.3, 6; 2 Chr. 33.3, 6. He fills Jerusalem with innocent blood, 2 Kgs. 21.16; 24.4. He is led bound to Babylon, 2 Chr. 33.11. He turns to God in prayer, v. 12. He is restored to the kingdom, v. 13. He dies, 2 Kgs. 21.18; 2 Chr. 33.20. His impiety was the cause of the destruction of the Jews, Jer. 15.4.

units.la: MANDATVM magnum seu primum quod, Matthæi 22.v.37.38. Marc.12.ver.29.30. Mandatum nouum, Ioann.13.34. 1.Ioann.2.8. Mandatum vetus, v.7.2. Ioann.v.5. Mandatum carnale, pro externis ceremoniis, Hebr.7.16. Mandata Legis, Exodi 20.1.&c. Deuteron.5.6. Matth.19.18. Marc.10.19. Luc.18.28. obseruanda sunt, Exodi 24.3. Deut 6.1.&8.1.&11.1.1. Sam.15.22. Matth.19.17. Luc 10.28.1 Corinth.7.19. 1.Ioann.2.4.&3.23.&5.3. Mandata Dei citra eius gratiam præstari non possunt, Ezechiel.36.27. Mandata Dei ob traditiones humanas transgredi non licet, Matthæi 15.v 3. Mandatum Dei irritum fecisse dicuntur impij, v.6. quod ad ipsorum conatus attinet. Nam quod ad rem ipsam spectat, inuito Satana & ipsius organis frustra laborantibus stant Dei præcepta. Mandata seruat, qui diligit, Ioan. 14.v.15.23. Mandata seruantibus benedictio, Leuit.26.3. Deut.28.1. &c. mandatis hominum aduersantium Deo, non attendum, Act.4.19 & 5.29. Tit.1.14.
units.tr: COMMANDMENT: the great or first, Matt. 22.37-38; Mark 12.29-30. The new commandment, John 13.34; 1 John 2.8. The old commandment, 1 John 2.7; John 5. The carnal commandment, concerning external ceremonies, Heb. 7.16. The commandments of the Law, Exod. 20.1, etc.; Deut. 5.6; Matt. 19.18; Mark 10.19; Luke 18.20; are to be observed, Exod. 24.3; Deut. 6.1; 8.1; 11.1; 1 Sam. 15.22; Matt. 19.17; Luke 10.28; 1 Cor. 7.19; 1 John 2.4; 3.23; 5.3. God's commandments cannot be performed without his grace, Ezek. 36.27. God's commandments are not to be transgressed for the sake of human traditions, Matt. 15.3. The impious are said to have made God's commandment void, v. 6, as far as their own efforts go; but as regards the thing itself, God's precepts stand, though Satan is unwilling and his instruments labour in vain. He who loves keeps the commandments, John 14.15, 23. Blessing is promised to those who keep the commandments, Lev. 26.3; Deut. 28.1, etc. One should not attend to the commandments of men who oppose God, Acts 4.19; 5.29; Titus 1.14.

units.la: mandatis impiis & inhonestis non esse parendum Exem-
units.tr: Examples that impious and dishonourable commands are not to be obeyed:

units.la: pla: Obstetrices AEgyptiacæ, Exodi 1 17. Serui Saul, 1. Sam. 22.17 Socij Danielis, Dan. 3.18. Daniel, 6. v. 10 11. Petrus & Ioannes, Act. 4. v. 18. 9 33. Apostoli, 5. v. 8.29.40.41. Mandatis impiis & inhonestis parentium exempla: Satellites & nuncij Saulis. 1. Sam. 19 11.15.16. Doeg Idumæus, 22.18, Subdi.ti Nabuchodonosor, Daniel 3.4. (Vide PRAECEPTIONIS iniquissimæ, & servorum in re mala facile obtemperantium, exempla.)
units.tr: Examples: the Egyptian midwives, Exod. 1.17. The servants of Saul, 1 Sam. 22.17. The companions of Daniel, Dan. 3.18. Daniel, 6.10-11. Peter and John, Acts 4.18, 19, 33. The apostles, Acts 5.8, 29, 40, 41. Examples of impious and dishonourable commands of the powerful: the attendants and messengers of Saul, 1 Sam. 19.11, 15, 16. Doeg the Edomite, 22.18. The subjects of Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3.4. (See examples of most unjust commands, and of servants readily obeying in an evil matter.)

units.la: MANDRAGORAS Leæ matri affert Ruben, Gen. 30.14. earum partem ab ea emit Rachel, v.15.
units.tr: MANDRAKES: Reuben brings them to his mother Leah, Gen. 30.14; Rachel buys part of them from her, v. 15.

units.la: [MANDVCARE spirituali modo, & ore fidei, Ioann. 6, v. 50.51. 53 &c. 1. Cor. 10. 3.]
units.tr: [To eat spiritually and with the mouth of faith, John 6.50-51, 53, etc.; 1 Cor. 10.3.]

units.la: MANENDVM est nobis in Christo, Ioan. 15. 4. Rom. 8. 1. 1. Corinth. 4. 15. & 13. Coloss. 2. 6. 1. Ioann. 2. v. 6. 28. & 3. 24. & 4. 13.
units.tr: We must abide in Christ, John 15.4; Rom. 8.1; 1 Cor. 4.15; 13; Col. 2.6; 1 John 2.6, 28; 3.24; 4.13.

units.la: [MANEO, I. De summo mysterio dicitur, Ioan. 14. 10. & 15. 10. 11. II. De divina, gratiosa, beata, vel Dei inter suos & cum suis, vel electorum cum Capite suo Christo, præsentia, habitatione, & coniunctione mystica dictum, Exo. 29.46. Num. 9 19. 1 Sam. 7. 2 1 Par. 17. v. 5. 6. Ioan. 5.38. & 6, 56, & 8 31. & 14. v. 16, 17, 25 & 15. v. 4. 6. 7. 9. 10. 1. Ioan. 1. 8. & 2. v. 6. 10. 4. 24. 27. & 3. v. 6. 9. 15. 17. 24. & 4. v. 12. 13. 15. 16.
units.tr: [MANEO. I. Said of the highest mystery, John 14.10; 15.10-11. II. Said of the divine, gracious, blessed presence and dwelling of God among his own and with them, or of the elect with their Head, Christ, and their mystical union, Exod. 29.46; Num. 9.19; 1 Sam. 7.2; 1 Chr. 17.5-6; John 5.38; 6.56; 8.31; 14.16-17, 25; 15.4, 6-7, 9-10; 1 John 1.8; 2.6, 10; 4.24, 27; 3.6, 9, 15, 17, 24; 4.12-13, 15-16.

units.la: III. De Spiritu S. sub columbæ specie viso dictu, Marc. 1. 10. Ioan. 1, v. 32, 33. IV. Dicitur etiam de immota certitudine consiliorum & verbi Dei, piorum item benedictione, Ps. 33 11, & 89. 37. & 111. v. 3. 10. & 112. v. 3 9. & 117. 2. Esa. 40. 8. Ro. 9. 11. 2. Cor. 3 11. & 9. 9 1. Pet. 1 25, 1. Ioan. 2. 17. V. De affectibus pravis aut laudatis, item de consequentibus dictum: Iob. 11. 14. Ioan. 3 36 & 9. 41. & 12 46. 1. Cor. 13, 13. Heb. 13. 1, 1. Ioan. 3. 14. Alias minoris momenti significationes prætermittimus.]
units.tr: III. Said of the Holy Spirit seen under the appearance of a dove, Mark 1.10; John 1.32-33. IV. It is also said of the unchanging certainty of God's counsels and word, and likewise of the blessing of the pious, Ps. 33.11; 89.37; 111.3, 10; 112.3, 9; 117.2; Isa. 40.8; Rom. 9.11; 2 Cor. 3.11; 9.9; 1 Pet. 1.25; 1 John 2.17. V. Said of wicked or praiseworthy affections, and likewise of their consequences: Job 11.14; John 3.36; 9.41; 12.46; 1 Cor. 13.13; Heb. 13.1; 1 John 3.14. Other meanings of lesser importance we pass over.]

units.la: MANSIONES filiorum Israel, Num. 33. 1. &c. mansiones paratæ fidelibus, Ioan. 14. 2, 1. diversæ in vita æt, dignitates.
units.tr: MANSIONS of the sons of Israel, Num. 33. 1, etc. Mansions prepared for the faithful, John 14. 2. Various in this life: dignities.

units.la: MANSVETVDO, πραότης, est ea animi virtus, quæ iram concitationémque animi nostri temperat & moderatur, ne sit nimia. Ἀοργησία quidem non inducit. (Nam Paulus ait: Irascimini, & nolite peccare: Ephes. 4 26. Nec Spiritus S. ἐπιεικείαν in homine Christiano requirit. Unde Christus ipse omnis virtutis exemplar perfectissimum interdum iratus est: Mat. 21. 12.) Sed peccatum cavet.
units.tr: MEEKNESS, [πραότης], is that virtue of the mind which tempers and moderates the anger and agitation of our spirit, so that it does not become excessive. Freedom from anger [ἀοργησία] it does not bring about. (For Paul says: "Be angry, and do not sin," Eph. 4. 26. Nor does the Holy Spirit require in a Christian man [ἐπιείκεια], reasonableness. Hence Christ himself, the most perfect pattern of every virtue, was sometimes angry: Matt. 21. 12.) But it guards against sin.

units.la: MANSVETVDO commendatur, Ios. 7. 19, 1. sam. 25. 1. &c. 2. Sam.16, 10. Prou.5.1. Eccles.1.29. Matt.5.5. & 11.29. Gal.5. 23. & 6.1. Ephes.4.2. Col.3.12.1. Tim.6.11.2. Timoth. 2.25. Tit.3.2. units.tr: MEEKNESS is commended: Josh. 7. 19; 1 Sam. 25. 1, etc.; 2 Sam. 16. 10; Prov. 5. 1; Eccles. 1. 29; Matt. 5. 5 and 11. 29; Gal. 5. 23 and 6. 1; Eph. 4. 2; Col. 3. 12; 1 Tim. 6. 11; 2 Tim. 2. 25; Titus 3. 2. Examples of meekness: Moses, Num. 12. 3; Ahasuerus, Esth. 19. 11; Christ, Jer. 11. 19; Matt. 11. 29 and 21. 6; Zech. 9. 9; John 12. 15; 1 Cor. 4. 21; 2 Cor. 10. 1. (See the examples of HUMILITY and PATIENCE.)

units.tr: The MEEK, the heirs of the earth, Ps. 37. 11; Matt. 5. 5. (See MILD.)

units.la: MANVE pater Samsonis, eius genus. Iudic.13.2. ei deprecanti apparet Angelus, v.9. sacrificaturus Angelo reprehenditur, & Deo sacrificare iubetur, v.16. (1. requies, aut munus.)
units.tr: MANOAH, father of Samson, his family. Judg. 13. 2. An angel appears to him as he prays, v. 9. About to sacrifice, he is rebuked by the angel and bidden to sacrifice to God, v. 16. (1. rest, or gift.)

units.tr: A HAND to be cut off from a false witness, Deut. 19. 21. A withered hand is healed, Matt. 12. 10. (See MIRACLES.)

units.la: MANUS, commune multarum actionum instrumentum, saepe adhibetur ad instrumentum significandum, etiam ubi nihil opus est administratione manus. & significat idem quod ministerium, aut ductus, per synecdochen, aut metonymiam, ut Exodi 4.11. & 9.35. Num.4.37. & 7.8. & 33.1. Levit.8.36. & 10.11. Ios.22.9.1. Sam.11.7. 2. Sam.11.14. & 12.25. & 14.19 1. Reg.14.18. & 16.12.2. Paralip.12.7. & 33.8. & 34.14. & 35.6. Esth.1.v.11.15. Psalm.77.21. & 95.7. Esa.20. 2. Ierem.39.17. & 50.1. Ezech.38.17. Agg.1.1. & 2. 1. Zach.7. 12. Malach.1.1. Actor.7.35. Imo per catachresin tribuitur etiam bestiis, Gen.9.5. Psalm.22.21. Dan.6.27. sepulchro, Psal.49.16. Osea 13.14. gladio, Psalm.63.11. Ierem.18.21. lagueo, Psalm.141.9. malo. Abac.2.9. vsurpatur praeterea pro opere, Exodi 14.31. pro adiumento, 2. Reg.15.19. pro plaga μεταφυμικῶς, Iudic.2.15. Iob 23.2. & 27.11. pro opera & virtute, Marc 6.1. Actor.13.11. Hebraismus, pro singulari fauore & virtute Dei, Luc.1.66. pro spiritu prophetiae, Ezec.1.3. manus Dei esse dicitur super aliquem, cum percutit, Iudic.2.15. facta esse dicitur super aliquem, qui spiritu Dei & fortitudine sit accensus, 1. Reg. 18.46. manus Ieroboam aresc it, 13.4. manus non contrahenda pauperi, Deut.15.7. manus nos scandalizans abscindenda, Matth.5.30. manum Dei nemo euadit, Deut.32.39. Psal.139.7, &c. Amos 9.2. Manum sub femore ponere, Genes.24.v.2.9. qui ritus vsitatus olim erat in iuramentis, quae superiores a domesticis exigebant. Idem & Iosephum fecisse legimus, Genes.47.29.
units.tr: HAND, the common instrument of many actions, is often used to signify an instrument, even where no action of the hand is needed; and it means the same as ministry or guidance, by synecdoche or metonymy, as in Exod. 4. 11 and 9. 35; Num. 4. 37, 7. 8 and 33. 1; Lev. 8. 36 and 10. 11; Josh. 22. 9; 1 Sam. 11. 7; 2 Sam. 11. 14, 12. 25 and 14. 19; 1 Kings 14. 18 and 16. 12; 2 Chron. 12. 7, 33. 8, 34. 14 and 35. 6; Esth. 1. 11, 15; Ps. 77. 21 and 95. 7; Isa. 20. 2; Jer. 39. 17 and 50. 1; Ezek. 38. 17; Hag. 1. 1 and 2. 1; Zech. 7. 12; Mal. 1. 1; Acts 7. 35. Moreover, by catachresis it is also attributed to beasts, Gen. 9. 5; Ps. 22. 21; Dan. 6. 27; to the grave, Ps. 49. 16; Hos. 13. 14; to the sword, Ps. 63. 11; Jer. 18. 21; to a snare, Ps. 141. 9; to evil, Hab. 2. 9. It is further used for work, Exod. 14. 31; for help, 2 Kings 15. 19; metaphorically for a plague, Judg. 2. 15; Job 23. 2 and 27. 11; for work and power, Mark 6. 1; Acts 13. 11. By a Hebraism, it means the singular favour and power of God, Luke 1. 66; for the spirit of prophecy, Ezek. 1. 3. The hand of God is said to be upon someone when he strikes, Judg. 2. 15; it is said to have come upon someone who has been kindled with the Spirit of God and strength, 1 Kings 18. 46. The hand of Jeroboam withered, 1 Kings 13. 4. The hand is not to be withdrawn from the poor, Deut. 15. 7. A hand that causes us to stumble is to be cut off, Matt. 5. 30. No one escapes the hand of God, Deut. 32. 39; Ps. 139. 7, etc.; Amos 9. 2. To put the hand under the thigh, Gen. 24. 2, 9: a rite customary of old in oaths which superiors required of their servants. We read that Joseph also did this, Gen. 47. 29.

units.la: MANVVM expansio in precibus vsitata Exod.17.11.1. Reg.
units.tr: The EXTENDING of hands, used in prayers, Exod. 17. 11; 1 Kings 8. 22; 2 Chron. 6. 13; Ezra 9. 8.

units.la: 8.22.2, Paralip.6.13.1 Esdr.9.8. manuum impositio varia in veteri & novo Testamento, Genes.48.14. Exod.29.30. Leuit.1.4.&3.2. Num.27.23, Marci 10.16. Actor.6.6. &8.17.&13,3.&19.6.1.Tim.4.14,&5.22.2. Timot.1.6. manuum impositio,pro ad ministerium Ecclesiasticum ordinatione,1 Tim,5.22. manuum impositionis usus, 4,14.2 Tim.1.6,formula, (Act.6.6.) sicut & ritus ipse qui peeam significatur, ab Hebraeis fluxit, qui hac ceremonia solebant uti, partim in precibus & benedictionibus privatis, Genesis 48,14. partim etiam in publicis & solennibus victimarum consecrationibus,Leuit.1.4.&c.Quem ritum deinde seruauit Ecclesia Christiana,tum in Ministris ordinandis & constituendis,Act.6.6.1.Tim.5.22.tum in conferendis Spiritus S.donis Actor.8.16.1 Tim.4.14. tum etiam in faustis precationibus, Matth.19,13.sed nullo prorsus fit in hislocis mentio chrismatis Papistici,rasurae crucis,vestis linae,cereorum, & aliorum huiusmodi portentorum.
units.tr: The LAYING ON of hands, various in the Old and New Testaments: Gen. 48. 14; Exod. 29. 30; Lev. 1. 4 and 3. 2; Num. 27. 23; Mark 10. 16; Acts 6. 6, 8. 17, 13. 3 and 19. 6; 1 Tim. 4. 14 and 5. 22; 2 Tim. 1. 6. The laying on of hands signifies ordination to the ecclesiastical ministry, 1 Tim. 5. 22. The use of the laying on of hands: 1 Tim. 4. 14; 2 Tim. 1. 6. The formula: Acts 6. 6. Just as the rite itself, which is signified by this name, flowed from the Hebrews, who used this ceremony partly in private prayers and blessings, Gen. 48. 14, and partly also in public and solemn consecrations of victims, Lev. 1. 4, etc. The Christian Church then kept this rite, both in ordaining and appointing ministers, Acts 6. 6; 1 Tim. 5. 22, and in conferring the gifts of the Holy Spirit, Acts 8. 16; 1 Tim. 4. 14, and also in pious prayers of blessing, Matt. 19. 13. Yet in these places there is no mention at all of the Papistic chrism, the shaving of the cross, the linen vestment, the candles, and other such monstrosities of this kind.

Moses Iosuae, Deut.34.9.Christus infantibus, Matth.19.15. aegrotis, Mar.10,16.8.6.5.&8,23.Luc.4,40.Apostoli septem Diaconis & fidelibus,Actor.6.6. & 8.17.&13.3.Saulo & Barnabae 13.3.Paulus duodecim viris, 19.5.&c. units.tr: Examples of the laying on of hands. Jacob on the heads of Ephraim and Manasseh, Gen. 48. 14. Moses on Joshua, Deut. 34. 9. Christ on infants, Matt. 19. 15; on the sick, Mark 10. 16; 8. 6, 5, and 8. 23; Luke 4. 40. The apostles on the seven deacons and on the faithful, Acts 6. 6 and 8. 17 and 13. 3. On Saul and Barnabas, 13. 3. Paul on twelve men, 19. 5, etc. On the father of Publius, 28. 8. Ananias on Saul, 9. 12, 17. ¶ The Papists twist these passages (Acts 6. 6, 8. 17, 13. 3 and 19. 6; 1 Tim. 4. 14 and 5. 22; 2 Tim. 1. 6) to support the imposition of hands in what they call the sacrament of Order and of Confirmation.

Exempla Apostoli, Actor.8.17.&19.6. manuum lotio Pharisaeis frequens,(Vide IVDAEORVM superstitiones) manuum ablutio olim expiationis causa in usu fuit, Deut.21.6. Matth.27.24.Unde & Pilatus lauat manus Christu damnaturus, ibid.manus lauare ante cibum, 15.2.non lauat Christus, Luc.11.38.manus tendere ad coelum, agnoscendo peccatum, & orando, Exod.9.29. &17.11.1.Reg.8.38. manuum opera fructificare facit Deus obedientibus sibi, Deut.30.9. manuum inpositione replentur Spiritu Sancto Christiani,Act.19.6.1. Tim,4,14, repletur Spiritu Iosue, Deut.34.9. sanat Christus ægros, Luc.4.40.
units.tr: HANDS to be laid on the sick, Mark 16. 18. Examples: Christ, Mark 6. 5; Paul, Acts 28. 8. The laying on of hands for communicating the visible gifts of the Holy Spirit. Examples of the apostles: Acts 8. 17 and 19. 6. The washing of hands was frequent among the Pharisees. (See the superstitions of the Jews.) The washing of hands was once in use for the sake of expiation, Deut. 21. 6; Matt. 27. 24. Hence Pilate washes his hands when about to condemn Christ, ibid. Washing the hands before a meal: Matt. 15. 2. Christ does not wash, Luke 11. 38. Stretching out the hands to heaven, acknowledging sin and praying: Exod. 9. 29 and 17. 11; 1 Kings 8. 38. God makes the works of the hands fruitful for those obedient to him, Deut. 30. 9. Christians are filled with the Holy Spirit by the laying on of hands, Acts 19. 6; 1 Tim. 4. 14. Joshua was filled with the Spirit, Deut. 34. 9. Christ heals the sick, Luke 4. 40.

units.la: MANUS paulò apertius consideratur, sequentibus distinctionibus, proprias & figuratas significationes ostendentibus.
units.tr: HAND is considered a little more openly, with the following distinctions, showing its proper and figurative meanings.

units.la: 1. Proprie igitur indicat membrum illud notissimum corporis humani, sive dextram sive manum sinistram intelligas, prout contextus fert.
units.tr: 1. Properly, therefore, it denotes that best-known member of the human body, whether you understand the right hand or the left, as the context requires.

units.la: 2. Est cogitatio, actio, sive opus hominis, Genef.20.5, Exod.23.1 1.Sam.26.18. Iob.16 17.&31.7. Psal.7.4.&18.21. & 24.4. Esai.1.15. Ezech.18.8. Mich.2.1.&5.12. Iacob.4.8.
units.tr: 2. It means a thought, action, or work of a man: Gen. 20. 5; Exod. 23. 1; 1 Sam. 26. 18; Job 16. 17 and 31. 7; Ps. 7. 4, 18. 21 and 24. 4; Isa. 1. 15; Ezek. 18. 8; Mic. 2. 1 and 5. 12; James 4. 8.

units.la: 3. Administratio, Cura, Gubernatio, Inspectio, &c. Gen.30,39. Exod.38.28. Iudic.9.29 1.Sam.28,17, Esther.2.3, 14.Esai.3.6.Ierem.6.3.
units.tr: 3. Administration, care, government, oversight, etc.: Gen. 30. 39; Exod. 38. 28; Judg. 9. 29; 1 Sam. 28. 17; Esth. 2. 3, 14; Isa. 3. 6; Jer. 6. 3.

units.la: 4. Animus, metaphora a vigore externo, qui in manibus apparet, ad internum ducta. 1.Sam.23.16. Nehem.2, 18, & 6.9. Iob.4.3. Esai 35.3. Ierem.38.4. & 50.43. zach. 8 v 9.13.
units.tr: 4. The mind, a metaphor drawn from external strength, which appears in the hands, transferred to the inner man: 1 Sam. 23. 16; Neh. 2. 18 and 6. 9; Job 4. 3; Isa. 35. 3; Jer. 38. 4 and 50. 43; Zech. 8. 9, 13.

units.la: 5. Consilia, conatus fauor. 2.Sam.3.12.&14.19, Esdr.9.2, Prou.11.21.&16.5.
units.tr: 5. Counsels, endeavours, favour: 2 Sam. 3. 12 and 14. 19; Ezra 9. 2; Prov. 11. 21 and 16. 5.

units.la: 6. Manus, Exercitus, 2.Reg.18.17. Esai.36.2.
units.tr: 6. Hand means an army: 2 Kings 18. 17; Isa. 36. 2.

units.la: 8. Fides stans promissis, fidelitas, Gen.42,37,&43.9.1. Par.29.24.
units.tr: 8. Faith keeping to promises, faithfulness: Gen. 42. 37 and 43. 9; 1 Chron. 29. 24.

units.la: 9. Fortitudo bellica & politica, Deut.33.7 2.Sam.3, 18.1.Par.14.11.2.Par.15 7, Esdr.4.4. & 6.22. Exod.15 9.
units.tr: 9. Military and political strength: Deut. 33. 7; 2 Sam. 3. 18; 1 Chron. 14. 11; 2 Chron. 15. 7; Ezra 4. 4 and 6. 22; Exod. 15. 9.

units.la: 10. Fulcra manuaria, 1.Reg.19.19
units.tr: 10. Handles of tools: 1 Kings 19. 19.

units.tr: 12. The political ministry: 2 Kings 19. 23; 1 Chron. 6. 15; 2 Chron. 12. 7 and 17. 19.

units.tr: 13. Obedience: Ps. 68. 32. Work: Ezek. 23 (verse garbled in the scan), 24. 45.

units.la: 14. Manus nomine indicatur potestas a Deo hominibus in res creatas, vel in alios homines, variis de causis modis certis & rationibus apertis aut arcanis concessa. Genes.9.2.& 14.20. & 16.v.6.9. Num.21.v.2.34 Deut.2.v. 24.30. Ioh.1.14. Iudic.1.v.2.4.1. Sam.14.v.10.12 37.2. Sam. 5.v.19 1. Reg.20. 13. Ierem 26.14. & 38. v. 5. 16. Dan.2. 38.&3 15.17.
units.tr: 14. By the name of hand is indicated power granted by God to men over created things, or over other men, granted for various reasons, by fixed measures and by plans either open or hidden: Gen. 9. 2 and 14. 20; Gen. 16. 6, 9; Num. 21. 2, 34; Deut. 2. 24, 30; John 1. 14; Judg. 1. 2, 4; 1 Sam. 14. 10, 12; 2 Sam. 3. 7 and 5. 19; 1 Kings 20. 13; Jer. 26. 14 and 38. 5, 16; Dan. 2. 38, 3. 15, 17.

15. Hand: a formidable and violent power which someone, not without God's permission, assumes over others: Gen. 16. 12, 32. 11 and 37. 21; Exod. 2. 12 and 18. 9, 10; Lev. 26. 25; Deut. 1. 27, 3. 8, 7. 8; Judg. 3. 8, 4. 2, 6. 13, 14, etc.; 1 Sam. 7. 3, 8. 14 and 12. 9, 10, 15; 2 Sam. 12. 7; Ezra 5. 12, 8. 31 and 9. 7; Neh. 9. 27, 28; Job 5. 15 and 9. 24; Ps. 18. 1, 78. 42, 106. 10, 41, 42, 107. 2, 140. 5 and 144. 7, 11. It is a frequent expression among the prophets: Mark 9. 31 and 14. 41; Luke 1. 71, 74 and 9. 44; Acts 12. 1, 11 and 19. 11.
16. Hand: prophetic power from God: 2 Kings 3. 15; 2 Chron. 30. 12; Isa. 8. 11; Ezek. 1. 3, 3. 14, 22, 8. 1, 33. 22, 37. 1 and 40. 1.

units.tr: 17. By catachresis, a hand is attributed to beasts and inanimate creatures: Gen. 9. 5; 1 Sam. 17. 37; Ps. 22. 21 and 98. 8; Isa. 55. 12; Dan. 8. 7; Hab. 3. 10.

units.tr: 18. By the name of hand is designated a branch, Job 15. 32; support, Ezek. 16. 49; the faculty of talent, Ezra 7. 25; misery, Job 15. 23; the most grievous blow, Job 23. 2 and 27. 11.

The HAND of God, as it is regarded as kind and merciful towards his own: Exod. 33. 23; Deut. 33. 2; 2 Sam. 24. 14, 17; Ezra 7. 6, 9, 28; Neh. 2. 8, 18; Job 2. 10 and 5. 18; Ps. 31. 6, 37. 24, 78. 42, 80. 18, 95. 7, 119. 73 and 138. 7, 8; Isa. 59. 1; Jer. 22. 24; Zech. 13. 7; Rom. 10. 21; Heb. 2. 7; 1 Pet. 5. 6.
