units.la: 10. Manus, pro mandato Dei expresso. 1. Paral. 8.19.]
units.tr: 10. The hand, for an express command of God: 1 Chron. 8.19.

units.la: RA (id est, amarum) quinta Israelitarum mansio, Exodi 15.24. illic miraculo dulcescunt aquæ, v.25.
units.tr: MARAH (that is, bitter), the fifth station of the Israelites: Exod. 15.24. There the waters were made sweet by a miracle, v. 25.

units.la: MARCVS Barnabæ consobrinus, Colos. 4.10. Petri spiritualis filius, 1 Petr.5.13. pauli adiutor. (Vide IOHANNES Marcus.)
units.tr: MARK, cousin of Barnabas: Col. 4.10. Spiritual son of Peter: 1 Pet. 5.13. Helper of Paul. (See JOHN MARK.)

units.la: MARANATHA, 1 Cor.16.22. [1. Dominus noster venit] est species extremi anathematis.
units.tr: MARANATHA, 1 Cor. 16.22. [Our Lord comes.] It is a kind of extreme anathema.

units.la: MARDOCHAEVS, tutor & defensor Esther, captiuus in Babylonem abductus, Esth.2.5. iussu Regis honoratur.6.11. a proceribus regni metuitur,9.3. Vide HAMAN. ] Amara contritio.]
units.tr: MORDECAI, guardian and defender of Esther, carried captive to Babylon: Esth. 2.5. Honoured by the king's command: 6.11. Feared by the nobles of the kingdom: 9.3. See HAMAN. [Bitter crushing.]

units.la: MARE creatur, Genes.1.9. concluditur suis terminis, ibid. Iob,26 10. & 38.8. prouerb.8.29, Ierem.5.22. cedit Israelitis, Exodi 14.14. &c. sedatur verbis Christi. Matth.8. 26. mare pro lacu Hebraismus.4.18. mare Galilææ, Ioan.6 1. mare æneum fabricatur, 2 paral.4.2 mare Dei imperio paret, Iob 38.8. Psalm.89.10. mare vitreum. Apocal. 15.2. mare vltra fines à Deo positos non transilit, psalm.104.9. V.Psal.33.7.
units.tr: THE SEA is created: Gen. 1.9. It is confined within its bounds: ibid.; Job 26.10; 38.8; Prov. 8.29; Jer. 5.22. It yields to the Israelites: Exod. 14.14, etc. It is calmed by the words of Christ: Matt. 8.26. "Sea" is used for a lake, a Hebraism: 4.18. Sea of Galilee: John 6.1. A bronze sea is made: 2 Chron. 4.2. The sea obeys God's command: Job 38.8; Ps. 89.10. A glassy sea: Rev. 15.2. The sea does not cross the bounds set by God: Ps. 104.9. See Ps. 33.7.

units.la: De Mari sequentes distinctiones obseruent Theologiæ studiosi. 1. Mare est ingens illa collectio & congregatio seu moles aquæ, cuius fons & receptaculum profundissimum, in quod innumera flumina decurrunt, & cuius brachia & sinus etiam maximo sunt numero, Oceanus dicitur. 2. Mare magnum Iudæis dicebatur, mare mediterraneum, quod & AEgyptium, Phenicium Syriacum cognominatur. 3. Mare Cenereth, seu Cinnereth, apud Euangelistas, mare Galilaea, mare Tiberiadis, & lacus Genesarethanus, praesentia Christi decoratus.
units.tr: Theology students should observe the following distinctions concerning the sea. 1. The sea is that vast collection and gathering or mass of water, whose source and receptacle is very deep, into which countless rivers flow, and whose arms and bays are also very numerous; this is called the ocean. 2. The Jews called the Mediterranean the Great Sea; it is also named the Egyptian, Phoenician or Syrian sea. 3. The Sea of Cenereth, or Cinnereth, in the Evangelists is the Sea of Galilee, the Sea of Tiberias, and the lake of Gennesaret, made glorious by the presence of Christ.

units.la: 4. Mare mortuum, dictum & mare Salsum siue Salis, ma-re item deserti seu solitudinis.
units.tr: 4. The Dead Sea, also called the Salt Sea or Sea of Salt; likewise the sea of the desert or wilderness.

units.la: 5. Mare rubrum, vel algosum, seu sinus Arabicus, ( Mare, Occidens, Orienti appositus, seu pars Occidentalis, & mare magnum respiciens. 7. Paludum & aquarum ingens collectio, vt Esai.21.1. & Ierem.51.36. Figurate significat, aestuarium fluctuans huius seculi, Esai.27.1. Gentium colluuiem, Esai.60.5.9. & 66.19. Mare aeneum fusile, multae aquae capax, in vsum sacerdotum &c. 1. Reg.7. verf.23.24.25. &c. Ierem.52.17.20. IV. Baptismus Nubis.
units.tr: 5. The Red Sea, or weedy sea, or the Arabian Gulf. 6. The sea lying to the west, set over against the east, or the western part, looking toward the great sea. 7. A vast collection of marshes and waters, as in Isa. 21.1 and Jer. 51.36. Figuratively it signifies the surging tumult of this age, Isa. 27.1; the filth of the Gentiles, Isa. 60.5, 9; 66.19. The cast bronze sea, capable of holding much water, for the use of the priests, etc.: 1 Kings 7.23–25, etc.; Jer. 52.17, 20. IV. The baptism of the cloud.

units.la: MRRIA, aquae Dei verbo in vnum collectae appellantur, Genef.1.10.
units.tr: MARIA: the waters gathered together into one by God's word are called (seas): Gen. 1.10.

units.la: MARGARITAE parabola, Matth. 13.v.45.46. Vide PARABOLA. Dicitur autem margarites Graecis, a nitor splendente, Latinis Vnio, quod in conchis nulli duo reperiantur indiscreti.
units.tr: PARABLE OF THE PEARL: Matt. 13.45, 46. See PARABLE. The Greeks call a pearl margarites from its splendid shine; the Latins call it unio, because no two found in shells are ever alike.

units.la: MARIA soror Mosis Prophetissa, Exodi 15.21. i. Mosen murmurat, Numer.12. verf. 1.2. lepra fertur, verf.10. precibus Mosis sanitatem recuperat, vel 13.14.15. moritur 20.1. (Miriam.i.gutta maris, doctrix populi.)
units.tr: MARY, sister of Moses, prophetess: Exod. 15.21. She murmurs against Moses: Num. 12.1, 2. She is said to be struck with leprosy: v. 10. She recovers her health by Moses' prayers: or 13–15. She dies: 20.1. (Miriam: drop of the sea, teacher of the people.)

units.la: MARIA Virgo Deipara, Iosepho desponsa, Luc. 1.27. ad cilla Domini, v 38. Elizabetha cognatam inuisit, v.40. ut beata v.45.48. prae reliquis mulieribus benedicta, v.28.4. verbi Dei custos 2.19. prae gaudio Deo canit, 1.v.46.& Christum Filium ad mortem vsque sequitur, Ioann.19.25. cum Apostolis orat, Actor.1.14. eius fides variis tentationibus agitatur, Luc 2.35. Iohanni commendatur. 19.27.
units.tr: MARY the Virgin, Mother of God, betrothed to Joseph: Luke 1.27. The handmaid of the Lord: v. 38. She visits her kinswoman Elizabeth: v. 40. She is called blessed: v. 45–48; blessed above other women: v. 28. The guardian of God's word: 2.19. She sings to God for joy: 1.46. She follows Christ her Son even to death: John 19.25. She prays with the apostles: Acts 1.14. Her faith is shaken by various temptations: Luke 2.35. She is commended to John: John 19.27.

units.la: MARIA soror Marthae, Christo dilecta, Ioan.11.5. eius sermonem auidissime auscultat, Lucae 10.39. Christum vnxit, Matt 26.7. Ioan.11.2.& 12.3.
units.tr: MARY, sister of Martha, beloved by Christ: John 11.5. She listens most eagerly to his word: Luke 10.39. She anoints Christ: Matt. 26.7; John 11.2; 12.3.

units.la: MARIA Magdalene a possessione Daemoniorum liberatur, Christo, marc 16.9. Luc 8.2. Christo crucifixo adest, Matth. 27.56. marc 15.40. Luc 23.49. Ioan.19.25. Christi monumentum inuisit, Matth.28.1. marc 16.1. Ioan. 20.1. surrexisse Discipulis annunciat, Matt.28.9. Mar.16.10. Luc.24.10. Ioan.20.18.
units.tr: MARY MAGDALENE, freed from possession by demons by Christ: Mark 16.9; Luke 8.2. She is present at Christ's crucifixion: Matt. 27.56; Mark 15.40; Luke 23.49; John 19.25. She visits Christ's tomb: Matt. 28.1; Mark 16.1; John 20.1. She announces to the disciples that he has risen: Matt. 28.9; Mark 16.10; Luke 24.10; John 20.18.

units.la: ia Cleophæ, aut, (vt alij legunt) Cleopæ vxor, Christo crucifixo adest, Luc 24.10. Ioan.19.25.
units.tr: MARY, wife of Cleophas, or (as others read) Cleopas. She is present at Christ's crucifixion: Luke 24.10; John 19.25.

units.la: MARIA, Iacobi minoris mater Christo crucifixo adest, Matth.27.56. Marc 15.40. Christi sepulchrum inuisit, Marc 16.1.2.
units.tr: MARY, mother of James the Younger. She is present at Christ's crucifixion: Matt. 27.56; Mark 15.40. She visits Christ's sepulchre: Mark 16.1, 2.

units.la: MARIA, Ioannis Marci mater, Act. 12.12. sacri conuentus noctu ad eam conueniunt, Petro in carcere detento: ibid.
units.tr: MARY, mother of John Mark: Acts 12.12. The holy assembly gathers at her house by night while Peter is held in prison: ibid.

units.la: MARITI, maritorum erga vxores officium & authoritas, Ge.3.16. Num.5.v.12.18. & 30.v.7.13. Deut.2.1.v.11.13.&24. Prou.5.18.&18.22. &31.10. Eccles.9.9. Malac.2.v.14.16. 1. Cor.7.3.&c.11.v.3.10. Ephes.5.22.&c. Colos.3.18. Tit.2.4.1. Tim.2.11.1 Petri.3.1. Exempla: Abraham Dominus vocatur à Sara vxore sua, Genes.18.12.1 Petr.3.6. Isaac Rebeccam vnicè amat. Genes.24.67. orat pro ea 25.v.20.21. Iacob amat Rachelem, 29.18, Dauid captiuas duas vxores suas liberat, 1 Sam.30. v.17.18. Bethsabeam consolatur, 2. Sam.12.24 Iob errantem vxorem moderatè corrigit, ac reprehédit, Iob 2.10. de maritorum in vxores dominatione Assueri edictum. Esth.1.19. eò pertinet & Ge.3.16.
units.tr: HUSBANDS: the duty and authority of husbands toward their wives: Gen. 3.16; Num. 5.12, 18; 30.7, 13; Deut. 21.11, 13, 14, 24; Prov. 5.18; 18.22; 31.10; Eccles. 9.9; Mal. 2.14, 16; 1 Cor. 7.3, etc.; 11.3, 10; Eph. 5.22, etc.; Col. 3.18; Titus 2.4; 1 Tim. 2.11; 1 Pet. 3.1. Examples: Abraham is called lord by his wife Sarah: Gen. 18.12; 1 Pet. 3.6. Isaac loves Rebekah alone: Gen. 24.67; he prays for her: 25.20, 21. Jacob loves Rachel: 29.18. David frees his two captive wives: 1 Sam. 30.17, 18. He comforts Bathsheba: 2 Sam. 12.24. Job moderately corrects and rebukes his wandering wife: Job 2.10. The edict of Ahasuerus on the lordship of husbands over wives: Esth. 1.19. Gen. 3.16 belongs here too.

units.la: MARTHA Lazari soror, Ioann.11.1. diligitur à Christo, v.5. Christum hospitio excipit, Luc.10.38. & parat coenā, Ioan. 12.2. ostendit suam fidem, 11.27. (1. prouocans, domina) Taxatur à Christo: Luc.10.41. Matth.5.11.2. Tim.2.13. Phil. 1.29.30. Act.5.41.
units.tr: MARTHA, sister of Lazarus: John 11.1. Loved by Christ: v. 5. She receives Christ into her house: Luke 10.38, and prepares supper: John 12.2. She shows her faith: 11.27. (1. Provoking, mistress.) Rebuked by Christ: Luke 10.41. Matt. 5.11; 2 Tim. 2.13; Phil. 1.29, 30; Acts 5.41.

units.la: MARTYRES (1. testes) eorum felicitas, 1. Pet. 4.14. Apocal. 14,15.
units.tr: MARTYRS (that is, witnesses): their happiness, 1 Pet. 4.14; Rev. 14, 15.

units.la: MASSA & Meriba, hoc est, tentatio & contentio, locus castrorum, in deserto: Exod.17.7.
units.tr: MASSAH and Meribah, that is, temptation and strife, the place of the camp in the wilderness: Exod. 17.7.

units.la: MASCVLVS & fœmina, homo creatus, Gen.5.2. Matt.19.4. qui cum masculis concumbunt, 1. Reg 14.24. à regno Dei excludendi, 1.Cor.6.9. Vide COITVS illiciti.]
units.tr: MALE and female, man created: Gen. 5.2; Matt. 19.4. Those who lie with males: 1 Kings 14.24. To be excluded from the kingdom of God: 1 Cor. 6.9. See UNLAWFUL INTERCOURSE.

units.la: [MASPHA: ibi congregantur Israelitæ, Iudic.20.1. Misphah.1. specula]
units.tr: [MIZPAH: there the Israelites gather, Judg. 20.1. Mizpah, a watchtower.]

units.la: MATER: eius in filios intimus & vehemens affectus, Esai. 49.15. Exempla: Respha,2, Sam.21.10. Mulierum meretricum altera, 1.Reg.3.26. Matrem qui non honorat, maledictus. Deut. 27.16. matrem suam commendat Christus Ioanni, Ioan.19.27.
units.tr: MOTHER: her intimate and vehement affection toward her sons: Isa. 49.15. Examples: Rizpah: 2 Sam. 21.10. The other of the two harlots: 1 Kings 3.26. Cursed is he who does not honour his mother: Deut. 27.16. Christ commends his mother to John: John 19.27.

units.la: MATERNVM officium non solo partu, sed & lactatione ac pia educatione definitur, Luc.11.27. quod sanctarum matrum exemplis confirmatur : Saræ, Gen.21.7. Annæ, Sam.1.23.v.2.Tim.1.5.
units.tr: The maternal office is defined not only by bearing a child but also by nursing and pious upbringing: Luke 11.27. This is confirmed by the examples of holy mothers: Sarah, Gen. 21.7; Hannah, 1 Sam. 1.23, 2; Timothy's mother and grandmother, 2 Tim. 1.5.

units.la: MATER spiritualis Christi quæ, Matt.12.50. Marc. 3.35. Luc 8.21. Vide Luc 2.19.
units.tr: SPIRITUAL MOTHER of Christ, who: Matt. 12.50; Mark 3.35; Luke 8.21. See Luke 2.19.

units.la: MATERIA Tabernaculi, Exodi 25.v.3.4.5 6.
units.tr: MATERIALS of the Tabernacle: Exod. 25.3, 4, 5, 6.

units.la: MATHAN, Sacerdos Baal, interficitur, 2.Reg.11.18.2. Paralip. 23.17. (i.donum.)
units.tr: MATTHAN, priest of Baal, is slain: 2 Kings 11.18; 2 Chron. 23.17. (That is, gift.)

units.la: MATHATHIAS, patruus Ioachim Regis Iuda, regno praficitur, 2.Reg.24.17. Sedechias nuncupatur, ibidem, 1.Paral.3.15 (p.donum Dei.)
units.tr: MATTHANIAH, uncle of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, is set over the kingdom: 2 Kings 24.17. He is named Zedekiah, ibid.; 1 Chron. 3.15. (That is, gift of God.)

units.la: MATRIMONIUM a Deo institutum, Genes.2.24. Prouer.2.17. Malachiæ 2.15. matrimonium marem & fœminam eadem Tribu oriundos apud Iudæos iungebat, Num.37. (¶ Ad matrimonium damnandum impudenter inscitè detortus locus à Syricio Papa Rom. 8.8. vbi Et in carne, quid significet Paulo, Vide in CARNE esse.) V de CONIVGIVM.
units.tr: MARRIAGE, instituted by God: Gen. 2.24; Prov. 2.17; Mal. 2.15. Among the Jews, marriage joined a man and a woman born of the same tribe: Num. 37. (¶ A passage wrongly and unlearnedly twisted by Pope Siricius to condemn marriage: Rom. 8.8. On what "in the flesh" means to Paul, see BEING IN THE FLESH.) See also CONJUGAL UNION.

units.la: MATRIMONIUM consensu parentum & cognatorum contrahendum est, Col.3.20. Mat.15.4.1.ad Cor.7.38. Exempla: Agar ex consensu Sarae fit vxor Abrahæ, Genesis 16.v.1. Ismael ex consensu matris ducit vxorem, 21.21. Isaac cum Rebecca ex consensu parentum contrahit matrimonium, 24.v.2.3.50.51. Iacob cum Rachel, 28.v.1.2.&29. 18.19.20. Sichem cum Dina, 34.4. Her cum Thamar, 38. Samson cum Dalila, Iudicium 14.3. Dauid cum Michol 1.Sam.18.v.20.21.27. Adonias, petit à Salomone Abisag Reg.2.17.
units.tr: MARRIAGE is to be contracted with the consent of parents and relatives: Col. 3.20; Matt. 15.4; 1 Cor. 7.38. Examples: Hagar becomes Abraham's wife with Sarai's consent: Gen. 16.1. Ishmael takes a wife with his mother's consent: 21.21. Isaac contracts marriage with Rebekah with the consent of his parents: 24.2, 3, 50, 51. Jacob with Rachel: 28.1, 2; 29.18, 19, 20. Shechem with Dinah: 34.4. Er with Tamar: 38. Samson with Delilah: Judg. 14.3. David with Michal: 1 Sam. 18.20, 21, 27. Adonijah asks Solomon for Abishag: 1 Kings 2.17.

units.la: MATRIMONIUM requirit consensum Sponsi & Sponsæ. Exempla: Isaac & Rebecca, Gen.24.v.56. 57.58. 67. Dauid & Abigail, 1.Sam.25.v.40.41.42.
units.tr: MARRIAGE requires the consent of bridegroom and bride. Examples: Isaac and Rebekah: Gen. 24.56, 57, 58, 67. David and Abigail: 1 Sam. 25.40, 41, 42.

units.la: MATRIMONIORVM inter Iudæos & Gentiles contractum Dei contractorum exempla: Esau, Genesis 2 verf. 34.35. & 28.9. Iudas, 38 vers.1 2. Ioseph, 41.45. Moses Exodi 2.21. Samson, Iudic.14.3, Salomon, 1.Reg. 3.1.& 1 v.1 2.
units.tr: Examples of marriages contracted between Jews and Gentiles, of which God disapproved: Esau, Gen. 26.34, 35; 28.9. Judah, Gen. 38.1, 2. Joseph, Gen. 41.45. Moses, Exod. 2.21. Samson, Judg. 14.3. Solomon, 1 Kings 3.1; 11.1, 2.

units.la: in MATRIMONIO contrahendo externorum quorundam rituum in veteri Testamento annotatorum & observatorum exempla: In connubio Isaac & Rebeccæ servus Abrahæ ablegatus ad Bathuelem, Rebeccam petit uxorem, parentes explorata filiæ voluntate consentiunt, servus loco arrhæ tradit Rebeccæ vasa aurea & argentea & vestes, & fratribus eius ac matri dona offert, & celebrat. tur conuiuium: Ac tandem Rebecca cum nutrice", seruo Abrahæ & comitibus eius ad Sponsum abit: qui eam introducit ad tabernaculum Sarę matris, & accipit vxorem, Genes.24.2.&c. Iacob septem annis seruit pro Rachel, &c.29.18.&c. Sichem quum compressisset Dinam, Patrem ablegat ad Iacobum, vt petat nuptias, &c.34.4. &c. Samson ambiens nuptias Dalilæ, re cum parentibus communicata, matrimonium cum ea contrahit, & conuiuium nuptiale agitat, &c.Iudic.14.v.1. &c. Saul per consiliarios agit cum Dauide de nuptiis Filiæ, & dotis loco postulat centum præputia Philisthæorum, 1.Sam.18.25. Dauid ablegat nuncios ad Abigail petitum nuptias eius,25.v.39. 40.41.
units.tr: In contracting marriage, examples of certain external customs noted and observed in the Old Testament: In the marriage of Isaac and Rebekah, Abraham's servant, sent to Bethuel, asks for Rebekah as a wife. Her parents, after exploring their daughter's willingness, consent. In place of a pledge, the servant gives Rebekah gold and silver vessels and garments, offers gifts to her brothers and mother, and a feast is held. At last Rebekah goes with her nurse, with Abraham's servant and his companions, to the bridegroom, who brings her into the tent of his mother Sarah and takes her as his wife, Gen. 24.2 etc. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, etc., 29.18 etc. Shechem, having lain with Dinah, sends her father to Jacob to ask for the marriage, etc., 34.4 etc. Samson, seeking marriage with Delilah, tells his parents, contracts marriage with her and holds a wedding feast, etc., Judg. 14.1 etc. Saul, through his counsellors, deals with David about the marriage of his daughter, and as dowry demands a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, 1 Sam. 18.25. David sends messengers to Abigail to ask for her in marriage, 25.39, 40, 41.

units.la: MATRIMONIVM inter Sacramenta numeratur à Pontificiis, idque probare nituntur ex epistola ad Ephesios 5. 32. Sed refutantur vel ex epistola ad Colost.1.27. vbi Gentium vocatio dicitur mysterium, vel, vt vetus Interpres vertit, Sacramentum. Vide & Ephes.1.9.& coniugium.
units.tr: MARRIAGE is counted among the sacraments by the Papists, and they try to prove this from Ephesians 5.32. But it is refuted from Colossians 1.27, where the calling of the Gentiles is called a mystery, or, as the old translator renders it, a sacrament. See also Ephesians 1.9, and the entry on marriage (coniugium).

units.la: MATTHAEVS, qui & Leui, Publicanus, à Christo vocatur, Matthæi 9.9. Marci 2.14. Lucæ 5.27. conuiuio amplissimo Christum excipit, Matth.9 10. Marci 2.15. Lucæ 5 28. (i. Donatus) fuit Apostolus & Euangelista.
units.tr: MATTHEW, who is also called Levi, a tax collector, was called by Christ, Matt. 9.9; Mark 2.14; Luke 5.27. He received Christ at a very large banquet, Matt. 9.10; Mark 2.15; Luke 5.28. (i.e. Donatus.) He was an Apostle and Evangelist.

units.la: MATTHIAS Discipulus, in loco Iudæ Apostatæ sufficiendus designatur, Actor.1.23.sorte eligitur, versi.26. (i. donum Dei.)
units.tr: MATTHIAS, a disciple, is designated to be chosen in place of the apostate Judas, Acts 1.23. He is chosen by lot, v. 26. (i.e. gift of God.)

units.la: MATHVSALA filius Henoch, Genesis 5.21. nongentos sexaginta nouem annos vixit.v.27. (Methuselah. i. mortis missio.)
units.tr: METHUSELAH, son of Enoch, Gen. 5.21, lived nine hundred and sixty-nine years, v. 27. (Methuselah: i.e. the sending forth of death.)

units.la: MAXILLAM percutienti, altera obuertenda, Matth.5.39. Luc.6.29. maxilla asini occiduntur mille Philisthæi, Iudic.15.15.
units.tr: Whoever strikes you on the cheek, turn the other to him, Matt. 5.39; Luke 6.29. With the jawbone of an ass a thousand Philistines are slain, Judg. 15.15.

units.la: IEDAD in castris Mosis prophetat, Num.11.26. (mensurans.)
units.tr: ELDAD prophesies in the camp of Moses, Num. 11.26. (measuring.)

units.la: MEDIATOR, inter Deum & populum Moses, Deut.5.5. (qui internuntius dicitur Gal.3.19. & seruus in domo Dei, & typus Christi.)
units.tr: MEDIATOR between God and the people: Moses, Deut. 5.5. (He is called an intermediary, Gal. 3.19, and a servant in the house of God, and a type of Christ.)

units.la: MEDIATOR vnus Christus, (Vide CHRISTVS.) 1. Tim.2.5. Heb. 11. 24. per quem & in quo nos D. elegit ab æterno, Eph.14.
units.tr: The one MEDIATOR is Christ (see CHRIST), 1 Tim. 2.5; Heb. 11.24, through whom and in whom God chose us from eternity, Eph. 1.4.

units.la: MEDICINA à Deo creata, Eccles.38.1.ad 16.vsque V. Prou.68. 15.& Esa.38.21.
units.tr: MEDICINE was created by God, Ecclus. 38.1 to 16; Prov. 68.15; and Isa. 38.21.

units.la: quibus necessarius, Matt. 9. 11. Marc. 2. 17. Luc. 5. 31. medico honos tribuendus, Eccles. 38. 1. Locus dandus v. 12. medicinæ magis quàm Deo fidere perniciosum. Exemplum Asa, 2. Paral. 16. 12. medice cura teipsum, Luc. 4. 13. Verum medicus Christus: Mat. 11. 28. V. Col. 4. 14. Lucas medicus Col. 4. 14.
units.tr: Those who are in need of it, Matt. 9.11; Mark 2.17; Luke 5.31. Honour is to be given to the physician, Ecclus. 38.1. A place is to be given (v. 12). It is harmful to trust in physicians more than in God. Example: Asa, 2 Chron. 16.12. "Physician, heal yourself," Luke 4.13. But the true physician is Christ, Matt. 11.28. See Col. 4.14: Luke the physician, Col. 4.14.

units.la: inconcessa quærentium exempla: Saul, 1. Sam. 28. v. 6. 7. 8. Ochosias, 2. Reg. 1. v. 2. 3. 4. Rex Moabitarum, 3. 27. Zambri, 1. Reg. 16. 18. Asa plus fidit medicis, quam Deo, 2. Para. 16. 13. Achaz, 28. v. 3. 4. Ephraim, Oseæ 5. 13. mediis (quas vocant) legitimis utentes iuuat Deus, 2. Sam. 10. 12. 2. Para. 32. v. 6. 8. Nehem. 4. 9. 21.
units.tr: Examples of those who seek forbidden things: Saul, 1 Sam. 28.6, 7, 8; Ahaziah, 2 Kings 1.2, 3, 4; the king of Moab, 3.27; Zimri, 1 Kings 16.18; Asa, who trusted physicians more than God, 2 Chron. 16.13; Ahaz, 28.3, 4; Ephraim, Hos. 5.13. God helps those who use the lawful means (as they call them): 2 Sam. 10.12; 2 Chron. 32.6, 8; Neh. 4.9, 21.

units.la: verbum Dei, Deut. 11. verf. 18. 19. Iosu. 1. 8. Psalm. 1. 2. Psalm. 18. 15. sit meditatio animi mei coram te.
units.tr: The word of God: Deut. 11.18, 19; Josh. 1.8; Ps. 1.2; Ps. 18.15: "let the meditation of my heart be before you."

units.la: ad vastandam Babyloniam à Deo excitati, Esai. 13. v. 17. 18. Dan. 5. 28. occupant eam. v. 31. V. Act. 2. 9. Media autem regio est Asiæ maioris.
units.tr: Stirred up by God to lay waste Babylon, Isa. 13.17, 18; Dan. 5.28. They will seize it, v. 31. See Acts 2.9. Now the middle region is of Asia Major.

units.la: in corpore leonis, Iudic. 14. 8. sit mel de petra surgerent, constituit Deus Israelitas super excelsam terram, Deut. 32. 13. mel gustat Ionathas, edicti paterni ignarus, 1. Sam. 14. 27. Mel agreste alimentum I. I. Matt. 3. 4.
units.tr: In the lion's body, Judg. 14.8. "Honey out of the rock" (Deut. 32.13), God set Israel over the high earth. Jonathan tastes honey, ignorant of his father's command, 1 Sam. 14.27. Wild honey as food, Matt. 3.4.

units.la: Rex & Sacerdos, Gen. 14. 18. Ps. 110. 4. Heb. 7. 1. Christus typus: Primùm in coniunctione Regni & Sacerdotij, Heb. 7. 1. Secundò, in adiunctis Regni, pace, & iustitia, v. 2. Tertiò, quia principio & fine careat, v. 3. Quartò, quia Abrahamo superior, v. 4. 5. 6. 7. Melchisedechi lacerdotium præstantius est quàm Leviticum, 7. v. 6. 7. (1. Rex iustus sue iustitiæ.)
units.tr: King and priest, Gen. 14.18; Ps. 110.4; Heb. 7.1. Christ as the type: First, in the joining of kingdom and priesthood, Heb. 7.1. Second, in the attributes of the kingdom, peace and righteousness, v. 2. Third, because he has no beginning and no end, v. 3. Fourth, because he is superior to Abraham, vv. 4–7. The priesthood of Melchizedek is more excellent than the Levitical, 7.6, 7. (1. A king just in his own righteousness.)

units.la: ambitus montis Sion interior, in quem populus conuenire solebat, ædificatur à Salomone, 1. Reg. 9. 24. Iud. 9. 6.
units.tr: The inner circuit of Mount Zion, where the people used to gather, is built by Solomon, 1 Kings 9.24; Judg. 9.6.

units.la: , pro omnibus hominis partibus, Iac. 4. 1. ea sunt mortificanda, Coloss. 3. 5. Membrorum vocabulo Paulus eleganter vocat pravos illos motus, & cupiditates spiritui repugnantes, atque adeò totam hominis non regeneratam partem, Coloss. 3. 5. (Vide CARO : & HOMO) Membra nostra Templum Spiritus Sancti, 1. Corinth. 6. 19. V. Eph. 4. 16. Sumus alii aliorum membra, v. 25. V. Cor. 12. 25.
units.tr: For all the parts of man, James 4.1. These are to be mortified, Col. 3.5. Paul elegantly calls those wicked motions and desires that resist the Spirit by the word "members," and so the whole unregenerate part of man, Col. 3.5. (See FLESH and MAN.) Our members are the temple of the Holy Spirit, 1 Cor. 6.19. See Eph. 4.16. We are members of one another, v. 25. See 1 Cor. 12.25.

units.la: adferri sibi cupit Paulus, 2. Tim. 4. 13.
units.tr: Paul wishes to have it brought to him, 2 Tim. 4.13.

units.la: MEMORIA beneficiorum acceptorum necessaria est, Deut.24. v.18.22.& 26.5. Psal. 71.6.& 78.6. memoria praeteritarum miseriarum utilis est, Exodi 22.21.& 23.9. Leu.19.34. Deu. 10.19.& 15.15.& 16.12. (memoria impiorum, Vide Impii. memoria piorum, V. Pii.)
units.tr: Remembrance of the benefits received is necessary: Deut. 24.18, 22; 26.5; Ps. 71.6; 78.6. Remembrance of past miseries is useful: Exod. 22.21; 23.9; Lev. 19.34; Deut. 10.19; 15.15; 16.12. (Memory of the wicked: see IMPII. Memory of the pious: see PII.)

units.la: SIMPHIS, urbs Agypti regia, quam Prophetae NO vocant, ubi Iudaei cum Ieremia de Hierosolymis profugi habitarunt. Isa.19.13. Ierem. 44.1.& 46.14.19. Ezech.30.13. 16 Ose.9.6.
units.tr: SIMPHIS (Memphis), the royal city of Egypt, which the prophets call NOPH, where the Jews who fled from Jerusalem with Jeremiah lived. Isa. 19.13; Jer. 44.1; 46.14, 19; Ezek. 30.13, 16; Hos. 9.6.

units.la: MENANDRI Poetae testimonium, 1.Cor.15.33.
units.tr: The testimony of the poet Menander, 1 Cor. 15.33.

units.la: MENDACIVM fugiendum, Gen.38.23: Exodi 20 16. & 23.v.1. 7.Leuit.19.11: Psalm.4.3.& 15 2. Prou.6.17.& 12.22.& 19.v. 5.22.& 30.v.6.8: Ier.5.31. Zach.8.17. Ephes.4.25. Coloss.3.9. Apocal.21.27. mendacium a Principe alienum esse debet, Prouer.17 7. ab impiis facile arripitur, 2 Thess. 2.11. mendacij poena, Apo.21.& 22.15. mendacium passim regnat, Ps. 12.2.3.4 5.
units.tr: Lying is to be avoided: Gen. 38.23; Exod. 20.16; 23.1, 7; Lev. 19.11; Ps. 4.3; 15.2; Prov. 6.17; 12.22; 19.5, 22; 30.6, 8; Jer. 5.31; Zech. 8.17; Eph. 4.25; Col. 3.9; Rev. 21.27. A lie ought to be alien to a prince, Prov. 17.7. It is readily seized upon by the impious, 2 Thess. 2.11. The punishment of lying: Rev. 21 and 22.15. Lying reigns everywhere, Ps. 12.2–5.

units.la: Mendacij vulgo duas constituunt species: Honestum, seu officiosum, quod cum proximi commodo est coniunctum: & perniciosum, quae distinctio sumta videtur ex Augustini Enchiridio ad Laurentium, cap.22: Sed refellitur.
units.tr: Commonly, people set up two kinds of lie: the honest, or dutiful, which is joined with the advantage of a neighbour, and harmful. This distinction seems to be taken from Augustine's Enchiridion to Laurentius, ch. 22. But it is refuted.

units.la: Primo, quia etiam mendacium honestum seu officiosum, peccat (sed venialis) rationem habere, quod beneuolentia excusat, asserit ibidem Augustinus, nec vllo modo a culpa eximit. Secundo, quia ab omni mali specie, qua mendacium officiosum non caret, abstinendum est, 1 Thessal.5.22. Tertio, quia ne in Dei quidem gloriam & fauorem mentiendum est, Iob, 13. v.7.10. Prou. 13.17: multo minus ergo in hominis vllius gratiam & salutem. Nec obstat quod mendacij huius patroni obiiciunt, homines saepe ea ratione iuuari, idque ut faciamus, charitatem a nobis postulare: charitas enim non gaudet iniustitia, 1 Corin.13.6. a veritate autem discedere, iniustitiae pars est. Deinde homines non iuuantur proprie mendacio, imo potius laeduntur, quia ira Dei prouocatur: sed quod mendacium nonnunquam cedit in proximi emolumentum & commodum, fit summa Dei misericordia, qui factum hominis malum ipse pro mira sua sapientia in bonum conuertere nouit: Quarto, quia Prophetae grauissime inuehebatur in mendaces, & mendacia inter maxima scelera abiis sunt numerata, non adhibita perniciosi aut officiosi distinctione, Psalm. 5.7. Osee 4.2: Zachar. 8.16. Quinto, quod repugnat etiam manifestè cum Decalogi præcepto, Exod. 20.16. Non dices falsum testimonium: quod omnis generis mendacia vetat, & prohibet. Sexto, quia verum fateri, mendacio autem abstinere iubemur, Matt. 5.37. 1 Cor. 1.18.19. Ephes. 4.25. 1 Ioan. 2.21. Quare hæc distinctio ita non potest, nisi velimus illi locum dare, ut neutram in illius speciem culpæ eximamus, sed dissimiliter: Hoc enim illo gravius longè est peccatum, unde & Augustinus illud Veniale vocat, hominum scilicet respectu, quod excusat benevolentia.
units.tr: First, because even a dutiful or honest lie is a sin (though a venial one). Augustine says that goodwill excuses it, yet it is in no way free from fault. Second, because one must abstain from every kind of evil, and the dutiful lie is not free of it, 1 Thess. 5.22. Third, because one must not lie even for the glory and favour of God, Job 13.7, 10; Prov. 13.17. Much less, then, for the favour and salvation of any man. Nor does it help that the defenders of this lie object that people are often helped by such a reason, and that charity demands that we do it, for charity does not rejoice in injustice, 1 Cor. 13.6, and to depart from the truth is part of injustice. Moreover, people are not truly helped by a lie; rather they are harmed, because the wrath of God is provoked. But that a lie sometimes turns to the profit and advantage of a neighbour is the great mercy of God, who by his wondrous wisdom knows how to turn the evil deed of man to good. Fourth, because the prophets inveighed most gravely against liars, and lies have been counted among the greatest crimes, without any distinction of harmful or dutiful, Ps. 5.7; Hos. 4.2; Zech. 8.16. Fifth, because it clearly contradicts the precept of the Decalogue, Exod. 20.16: "You shall not bear false witness," which forbids and prohibits every kind of lie. Sixth, because we are commanded to tell the truth and to abstain from lying, Matt. 5.37; 1 Cor. 1.18, 19; Eph. 4.25; 1 John 2.21. Therefore this distinction cannot stand, unless we wish to give it a place, so that we do not exempt either kind from the category of fault, but treat them unequally. For this is by far the graver sin, whence Augustine also calls that one venial, namely with respect to men, which goodwill excuses.

units.la: MENDACII honesti, seu officiosi hęc dantur exempla: Ioseph Gen. 43.18. & 44. v.1.2. & Obstetrices piæ, Exodi 1 v.19. Rahab Iosue 2. v.4.5 6. Michol 1 Sam. 19. v.16 17. David 20. v.1 2.3 4 5 6.7 & 21. v 9 10.11 13. Chusai 2 Sam. 16.17. Elizæus 2 Reg. 6. v.16.19.20.
units.tr: Examples of honest or dutiful lying are these: Joseph, Gen. 43.18 and 44.1,2; the pious midwives, Exod. 1.19; Rahab, Josh. 2.4,5,6; Michal, 1 Sam. 19.16,17; David, 1 Sam. 20.1–7 and 21.9,10,11,13; Hushai, 2 Sam. 16.17; Elisha, 2 Kings 6.16,19,20.

units.la: MENDACII, (ut vocant) perniciosi & vitiosi exempla: Serpens, Gene. 3 4. Sara 18.15. Huc referunt etiam Abraham exemplum, Gen 12 13. & 20.2. Vbi petit ab uxore sua Sara ut se sororem ipsi esse fateatur: quum illis locis non peteret ab uxore Abraham, ut mentiatur, falsum aliens, aut non agens verum: sed tantum ut veri partem reticens (aut enim communem habuerunt, Genesis 20.12.) ipsum a periculo liberet. Quod autem Sara filia patris Abrahæ dicitur, Genesis 20.12. Ex Hebræorum idiotismo fit, quod nepotes & neptes, avorum filios & filias vocare solent, & Exodi 2. v.18.20 Idem & de Isaaco, Genesis 26.7, dixit. Iacob 27.v.19.24. Rachel 31 35. Patriarchæ 37. v.32. Vxor Putiphari 39.14 Gibaonitæ, Ioso 9. v.8 9 Simeon, Iudic. 16. v.13 14.15. Fama de Absalone, 2 Sam.13 3 mulier quædam, 17 20. altera meretricum, 1 Reg 3. v 22. falsi testes, 21 13. Prophēta quidam 13 18. Gezi, 2 Reg. 5.22. Hazael 8. v.14 15. Aman, Esth 3 8. Principes & residua pars populi a captivitate. Ieremiæ 42 v 5 21 Iudæi, Scribæ & Pharisæi, Marc. 11 19. Petrus 26 v.70.71. Iudæi seniores & milites custodes sepulchri, 28. v.11.1..13. Parentes conjugati, Ioan. 9.v.20 21 22. Ananias & Sapphira, Act 5.v.2. Falsi testes, 6 14. Quæstuarii, 16.v.19.20. Athenienses 18. Demetrius, 19 27. Iudæi quidam, 21.28. Tertullus Orator, 24 5. Cretenses, Tit.1.12. Pseudoapostoli, Ap.2.2. Pseudo Iudæi, v 9.& 59 [?].
units.tr: Examples of what they call pernicious and vicious lying: the serpent, Gen. 3.4; Sarah, Gen. 18.15. To these they also refer the example of Abraham, Gen. 12.13 and 20.2, where he asks his wife Sarah to admit that she is his sister. Yet in those passages he did not ask Abraham's wife to lie, to say something false, or to act untruthfully. He only asked her to conceal part of the truth, so that he would be freed from danger (for they had a common father, Gen. 20.12). That Sarah is called the daughter of Abraham's father, Gen. 20.12, is a Hebrew idiom: they usually call grandsons and granddaughters sons and daughters of their grandfathers. Exod. 2.18,20. The same is said of Isaac, Gen. 26.7. Jacob, Gen. 27.19,24; Rachel, Gen. 31.35; the patriarchs, Gen. 37.32; the wife of Potiphar, Gen. 39.14; the Gibeonites, Josh. 9.8,9; Simeon, Judg. 16.13,14,15; the report about Absalom, 2 Sam. 13.3; a certain woman, 2 Sam. 17.20; the other of the harlots, 1 Kings 3.22; false witnesses, 1 Kings 21.13; a certain prophet, 1 Kings 13.18; Gehazi, 2 Kings 5.22; Hazael, 2 Kings 8.14,15; Haman, Esth. 3.8; the princes and the remnant of the people after the captivity, Jer. 42.5,21; the Jews, the scribes and the Pharisees, Mark 11.19; Peter, Matt. 26.70,71; the Jewish elders and the soldiers guarding the sepulchre, Matt. 28.11–13; the parents of the blind man, John 9.20,21,22; Ananias and Sapphira, Acts 5.2; false witnesses, Acts 6.14; the moneymakers, Acts 16.19,20; the Athenians, Acts 18; Demetrius, Acts 19.27; certain Jews, Acts 21.28; the orator Tertullus, Acts 24.5; the Cretans, Titus 1.12; the pseudo-apostles, Rev. 2.2; the pseudo-Jews, Rev. 2.9 and 59 [?].

units.la: Mendacium non suscipiendum à Iudice, Exodi 23 v.1.
units.tr: A lie must not be accepted from a judge, Exod. 23.1.

units.la: Mendax omnis homo, Psal.116.11. Esa.9.16. Rom.3.4. mendax est, qui negat Christum, 1.Ioan.2.22. mendax spiritus in Prophetis, 1 Reg.22.22. mendax Spiritui Sancto Ananias & Sapphira moritur, Act.5. v.3.5.&c.
units.tr: Every man is a liar, Ps. 116.11; Isa. 9.16; Rom. 3.4. Whoever denies Christ is a liar, 1 John 2.22. A lying spirit was in the prophets, 1 Kings 22.22. Ananias and Sapphira die for lying to the Holy Spirit, Acts 5.3,5, etc.

units.la: VENDICI nulli in Ecclesia esse debent, Deut.15.4. Dauid etiam asserit, se non vidisse iustum derelictum, & semen eius quærens panem, Psalm.37.25. multi tamen erant Christi tempore, quod illius temporis corruptelam arguit, Lucæ 16.20.& 18.35.Ioan.9.8. Act.3.2.
units.tr: Beggars ought not to exist in the Church, Deut. 15.4. David also affirms that he has never seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging for bread, Ps. 37.25. Yet there were many beggars at Christ's time, which shows the corruption of that age: Luke 16.20; 18.35; John 9.8; Acts 3.2.

units.la: IDOLUM. V. IDOLORUM catalogus.
units.tr: IDOL. See the catalogue of idols.

units.la: MENSA Tabernaculi, & eius forma, Exod.25. v.23.24.25.26. 27.28.& 37.v.10.11.12.13.14.15. mensæ decem in Templo fabricantur, 2 Paral.4.8. Mensa Domini, 1 Cor.10.21. dæmoniorum: ibid.
units.tr: The table of the tabernacle and its form, Exod. 25.23,24,25,26,27,28 and 37.10–15. Ten tables were made in the Temple, 2 Chron. 4.8. The table of the Lord, 1 Cor. 10.21. The table of demons, ibid.

units.la: MENS, pro intelligentia, νοῦς, duntaxat, Tit.1.15. mens sive ratio in non renatis, caput est naturæ corruptionis, Col.1.21: ideoque carnis etiam nomine sæpe comprehenditur, Rom.8.7. Eph.4.v.17.18.& 2.3. Colos.2.18. mentis renovatio necessaria, Rom.12.2. Eph.4.22.23. Vide REGENERATIO. (V.Anima.)
units.tr: MIND, for understanding, νοῦς only, Titus 1.15. The mind or reason of unregenerate people is the head of corrupt nature, Col. 1.21, and so it is often included under the name of the flesh, Rom. 8.7; Eph. 4.17,18; 2.3; Col. 2.18. Renewal of the mind is necessary, Rom. 12.2; Eph. 4.22,23. See REGENERATION. (See SOUL.)

units.la: MENSIS primus, Exodi 12.2. mensis novorum fructuum, 13.4. mensium observatio ceremonialis & Iudaica damnatur: Gal.4.10. V. Col.2.16. i. Mensis Nisan, Hebraicè, Ester,3.7. id est, Martius.2. Iiaz, Aprilis.3. Sivan, maius.4. Tamuz, Iunius.5, Abib Iulius.6, Elul, Augustus.7, Tisri, September.8, Mar, hes, van, October, 9. Casleu, November.10. Tebeth, December.11. Sebath. Ianuarius.12, Adar, Februarius. (Beroaldus in suis Chronic.
units.tr: The first month, Exod. 12.2. The month of new fruits, Exod. 13.4. The ceremonial and Jewish observance of months is condemned, Gal. 4.10; see Col. 2.16. The Hebrew names of the months (Esther 3.7) are: (1) Nisan, that is, March; (2) Iyyar, April; (3) Sivan, May; (4) Tammuz, June; (5) Av, July; (6) Elul, August; (7) Tishri, September; (8) Marheshvan, October; (9) Kislev, November; (10) Tevet, December; (11) Shevat, January; (12) Adar, February. (Beroaldus in his Chronicles.)

units.la: MENSTRUOSA mulier, & eius lex, Leu.15.v.19.20.21.&c. Vide Isa.64 6.
units.tr: The menstruous woman and her law, Lev. 15.19,20,21, etc. See Isa. 64.6.

units.la: MENSURA iusta esse debet, Leui.19.35 36. Deut.25. v.13.14.15. 16. Ezech.45.10. Mich.6 11. Amos 8.5. &c. Prou.16.11.& 20: 10. mensura iniqua Deo abominabilis, Prou.20.10. Mich. 6.11 mensura qua mensi fuerimus remetietur nobis, Exo. 21.23. Iudic.1.7.1 Sam.15.33.2 Sam.2.25. Psal.18. 21. Prov.22. 23. Esa.33.1.& 65.6.& 66.4. Ier.50.v.15 29.& 51.49. Ezec.16: 59. Ioel.3. 7. Matth.7.2. Marc.4.24, Luc.6 38. Mensura pro mensura Hebræis idem est quod Latini dicunt, Par pari referre, Matt.7.2.
units.tr: A just measure must be used, Lev. 19.35,36; Deut. 25.13,14,15,16; Ezek. 45.10; Mic. 6.11; Amos 8.5, etc.; Prov. 16.11 and 20.10. An unjust measure is abominable to God, Prov. 20.10; Mic. 6.11. "By what measure you measure, it will be measured back to you," Exod. 21.23; Judg. 1.7; 1 Sam. 15.33; 2 Sam. 2.25; Ps. 18.21; Prov. 22.23; Isa. 33.1; 65.6; 66.4; Jer. 50.15,29; 51.49; Ezek. 16.59; Joel 3.7; Matt. 7.2; Mark 4.24; Luke 6.38. "Measure for measure" among the Hebrews means the same as what the Latins say, "like for like," Matt. 7.2.

units.la: Mensuram Patrum complere Hebræis dicuntur, qui maiores suos imitari pergunt, ut tandem ipsorum improbitas ad summum gradum peruenia t,Mat.23.32. Huc pertinent illa dicendi genera Hebreis vsitata: Complere iniquitates suas,Gen.15.16. Complere sua peccata, 1 Theff. 16, quibus significatur hæreditaria improbitas : quia nimirum Dominus non statim ad iram prorumpit, sed expleto demum iniquitatis cumulo, vt reprobi suo ipsorum iudicio millies conuicti teneantur.
units.tr: The Hebrews say that people "fill up the measure of their fathers" when they continue to imitate their elders, so that at last their wickedness reaches its highest degree, Matt. 23.32. To this belong those forms of speech common among the Hebrews: "to fill up their iniquities," Gen. 15.16; "to fill up their sins," 1 Thess. 2.16. By these is signified hereditary wickedness: the Lord does not at once break out in anger, but when the heap of iniquity is complete, the reprobate are held convicted a thousand times by their own judgment.

units.la: MENTIRI non potest Deus, Tit.1.2, Hebr.6.18.
units.tr: God cannot lie, Titus 1.2; Heb. 6.18.

units.la: MERARI filius Leui,Numer.3.17. Meraritarum officium ve 33.& 4.42. (1.amarus.)
units.tr: MERARI, son of Levi, Num. 3.17. The duty of the Merarites, Num. 3.33 and 4.42. (See 1. Amarus.)

units.la: MERCES mercenarij statim reddenda,Leuit.19.13. Deut.24. v.14.15. Tob.4.15. Eccles.34. Iac.5.4. Malac.3.5.&c. Merces nomen passim in Scripturis accipitur pro constituto quidem præmio, sed eo tamen gratuito: vt Scholastici mutui meriti & mercedis relationem somniant, Matth.6.1. & quod ita esse patet: quod enim à Luca, Luc.6.32. χάρις est, gratia dicitur, id à Matthæo dicitur μισθός, id est, merces, Matth.6.1.
units.tr: A hireling's wages must be paid at once, Lev. 19.13; Deut. 24.14,15; Tob. 4.15; Ecclus. 34; James 5.4; Mal. 3.5, etc. In Scripture, "reward" is everywhere taken for a prize that has indeed been appointed, but is nevertheless free. The Schoolmen dream of a relation of mutual merit and reward, Matt. 6.1; and that this is so is plain, for what Luke calls grace [χάρις] (Luke 6.32), Matthew calls reward [μισθός] (Matt. 6.1).

units.la: ¶ Hoc non animaduertentes Pontificij, suorum operum fiducia turgentes, aut saltem animaduertere nolentes, pro operum meritis tanquam pro aris & focis dimicant, & mercedem deberi operibus probare se posse somniant. Gen.4.7.&15.1. Psal.119.112. Prou.11.18. Sap.5.16.&10.17. Eccles.2.8.&11.24.&18.22.&36.18.&51.v.30.38. Esa.3.10. Ierem.31.16. Mat.5.12.&6.1.&10.v.32.41.&20.8. Marc.9.41. Luc.6.35.&10.7. Ioann.4.36. Rom.4.4.1 Cor.3.8.1 Timo.5.18. Ap.22.12. V. MERITA Operum: & OPERVM merita.
units.tr: Papists, not noticing this, swollen with confidence in their own works, or at least unwilling to notice, fight for the merits of works as for their altars and hearths, and dream that they can prove that a reward is owed to works. Gen. 4.7; 15.1; Ps. 119.112; Prov. 11.18; Wisd. 5.16; 10.17; Ecclus. 2.8; 11.24; 18.22; 36.18; 51.30,38; Isa. 3.10; Jer. 31.16; Matt. 5.12; 6.1; 10.32,41; 20.8; Mark 9.41; Luke 6.35; 10.7; John 4.36; Rom. 4.4; 1 Cor. 3.8; 1 Tim. 5.18; Rev. 22.12. See MERITS OF WORKS and WORKS, merits of.

units.la: Sed notandum est contra istos hypocritas, Legis obseruationem, vel perfectissimam, vllius mercedis meritorian non esse, Luc.17.10. & tamen ad subleuandam solatio al quo carnis nostræ infirmitatem & debilitatem, non ad inflandos gloria animos mercedem bonis operibus promitti à Deo, Psalm.19.2. Matth.10.42. Marc 9.41 11.Cor 3 8.2 Cor.5.10. Gal.6.8. Merces piorum amplissima, Matth. 5.11.12.&10.41. Luc.6.23.35. 2 Tim.1.v.16.18. Hebr.6.10. 10.35.&11.26. Merces scorti non offerenda Deuter.23.18. Merces Abrahæ & omnium nostrum, Deus, Gen.15.1. merces persecutionem passis, Matt.5.12. Merces secundum opus, 1 Corinth.3.v.8.14. merces vinitoribus ex æquo data. Matth.20.8. (V.Merita) merces retenta vindicatur: Malac.3.5.&c.
units.tr: But it must be noted against these hypocrites that the observance of the Law, even the most perfect, deserves no reward, Luke 17.10. Yet God promises a reward for good works not to puff up minds with glory, but to lift up the weakness and feebleness of our flesh with some comfort, Ps. 19.2; Matt. 10.42; Mark 9.41; 1 Cor. 3.8; 2 Cor. 5.10; Gal. 6.8. The reward of the godly is very great, Matt. 5.11,12; 10.41; Luke 6.23,35; 2 Tim. 1.16,18; Heb. 6.10; 10.35; 11.26. The wages of a whore are not to be offered, Deut. 23.18. God is the reward of Abraham and of all of us, Gen. 15.1. A reward for those who suffer persecution, Matt. 5.12. A reward according to work, 1 Cor. 3.8,14. Wages given equally to vinedressers, Matt. 20.8. (See MERITS.) A reward withheld is avenged, Mal. 3.5, etc.

units.la: MERCENARIVS Pastor, Ioan.10.12. Mercenarij & Pastori ver eri ac boni discrimen, ibid. v. 10. u. &c. Mercenarij notan-tur, Phil. 2. 21.
units.tr: MERCENARY shepherd, John 10.12. The difference between a mercenary and a true good shepherd, ibid. v. 10 etc. Mercenaries are censured, Phil. 2.21.

units.la: ARCVRIVS, Nuntius & interpres deorum poeticorum: sic Lystrenses Paulum nominarunt : Actor. 14. 12. G. Ἑρμῆς.
units.tr: MERCURY, messenger and interpreter of the poetic gods. So the Lycaonians called Paul, Acts 14.12: Hermes [Ἑρμῆς].

units.la: MERETRIX & scortator in populo Dei non tolerandi, Deu. 23. 17. meretrix fugienda, Prou. 23. 27. 28.
units.tr: A harlot and fornicator must not be tolerated among God's people, Deut. 23.17. A harlot is to be fled from, Prov. 23.27,28.

units.la: MERETRICIS mores describuntur, Prou. 2. v. 16. 17. & 5. v. 3. 4. & 7. v. 5. ad finem vsq; & 9. v. 13. 14. 15. & 22. 14. Ecc. 7. 27. meretricis præmium quale, Prou. 6. 26. &c. Meretrix magna, Apocal. 17. 1. eius descriptio, ver. 3. 4. 5. sanguine Martyrum ebria est, v. 6. meretrici adhærens vnum cum ea est corpus, 1. Cor. 6. 16. meretrices & Publicani Euangelio credentes, Regnum Dei ingrediuntur, Matth. 21. v. 31. 32. Meretricum exempla: Thamar, Gen. 38 24. Madianitis, Numer. 25. 6. Rahab, Ios. 2. v. 1. 2. & 6 23. Hebr. 11. 31, mater Iephthe, Iudic. 11. 1, meretrix Gazæ, Iudic. 16. 1. duæ meretrices, 1. Reg. 3. 16. Peccatrix, Luc. 7. 37. mulier in adulterio deprehensa, Ioan. 8. 3.
units.tr: The manners of a harlot are described: Prov. 2.16,17; 5.3,4; 7.5 to the end; 9.13,14,15; 22.14; Ecclus. 7.27. What the reward of a harlot is like, Prov. 6.26, etc. The great harlot, Rev. 17.1; her description, vv. 3,4,5; she is drunk with the blood of the martyrs, v. 6. Whoever cleaves to a harlot is one body with her, 1 Cor. 6.16. Harlots and publicans who believe the Gospel enter the kingdom of God, Matt. 21.31,32. Examples of harlots: Tamar, Gen. 38.24; the Midianite women, Num. 25.6; Rahab, Josh. 2.1,2 and 6.23; Heb. 11.31; the mother of Jephthah, Judg. 11.1; the harlot of Gaza, Judg. 16.1; the two harlots, 1 Kings 3.16; the sinful woman, Luke 7.37; the woman taken in adultery, John 8.3.

units.la: MERIBA (i. iurgium, contentio) nomen loci, qui etiam tentatio dicitur, & cur, Exod. 17. 7. Ps. 95 8.
units.tr: MERIBAH (that is, strife, contention), the name of a place, which is also called temptation, and why: Exod. 17.7; Ps. 95.8.

units.la: MERITA operum euertuntur, Psalm. 51. 12. Esa. 55. 1. & 64. 6. Thren. 5. 21. Ezech. 36. v. 22. 32. Agg. 2. 14. Matt. 7. 11. Luc. 17. 10. units.la: MERITORIA Opera nostra non esse meritoria probatur : 1. Quia sunt imperfecte bona. 2. Quia sunt debita. 3. Quia quatenus sunt bona, non sunt proprie nostra, sed sunt gratuita Dei dona. 4. Quia nulla quicquam sua natura de Deo mereri possunt, & eum obligare ad præmium dandum. 5. Quia inter bona opera nostra & vitam æternam nulla est proportio. 6. Quia si meritoria essent, sequerentur multa absurda. 1°. Esset de quo gloriari iure possemus apud Deum. 2. Turbaretur certitudo Christiana de iustificatione & salute nostra per Christum. 3. Christus frustra esset mortuus. 4. Irrita esset promissio. 5. Christus non esset perfectus Seruator. 6. Diuersi modi iustificandi, & salutem consequendi introducerentur: Aliter enim iustificatus & seruatus esset Abraham, aliter nos iustificaremur & seruaremur.
units.tr: That our works are not meritorious is proved as follows: (1) because they are imperfectly good; (2) because they are owed; (3) because, insofar as they are good, they are not properly ours but are free gifts of God; (4) because by their own nature they cannot merit anything from God or oblige him to give a reward; (5) because there is no proportion between our good works and eternal life; (6) because, if they were meritorious, many absurd consequences would follow. First, we could boast of something before God by right. Second, the Christian certainty of our justification and salvation through Christ would be disturbed. Third, Christ would have died in vain. Fourth, the promise would be void. Fifth, Christ would not be a perfect Saviour. Sixth, different ways of being justified and obtaining salvation would be introduced: for Abraham would have been justified and saved in one way, and we in another.

units.la: MESOPOTAMIA Syriæ regio, Actor.2.9. V. SYRIA. Græcis duobus fluuiis nomen habet, quia inter Tygrim & Euphratem sita est, Gen.24.10. Accipitur etiam generaliùs & latiùs, ut complectatur sub se non eam modò regionem quæ duobus annibus, Euphrate & Tygri includitur, sed etiam Babyloniam, cuius pars est Chaldæa, Act.7.2. Indeè gressum fuisse legimus Abrahamum, Gen.11.31. Hebræi Aram Naharaim.i. Syria fluuiorum.
units.tr: MESOPOTAMIA, a region of Syria, Acts 2:9. See SYRIA. It has a name in Greek meaning "two rivers", because it lies between the Tigris and the Euphrates, Gen. 24:10. It is also taken more generally and broadly, so as to include under it not only that region enclosed by the two rivers Euphrates and Tigris, but also Babylonia, of which Chaldea is a part, Acts 7:2. We read that Abraham set out from there, Gen. 11:31. The Hebrews call it Aram Naharaim [ארם נהרים], that is, Syria of the rivers.

units.tr: The sacred or ecclesiastical MINISTRY, both before and after Christ was manifested in the flesh: Exod. 28.35. Levit. 21.18. Numer. 1.50. Deut. 10.8. 1 Par. 6, v. 32, 48. 2 Par. 5.11. Esdr. 7.19. Nehem. 13.30. Ierem. 52.18. Ezech. 45.4. Act. 1, vv. 17, 25, 6.1, 4, 11.29, 12.25, 13.5, 20.24, 21.1, 9. Rom. 11.13, 12.7, 16.1. 1 Cor. 16.15. 2 Cor. 3.9, 5.18, 6.3, 8.4, 9.1, 12–13, 11.8. Eph. 4.12. Col. 4.17. 1 Tim. 1.12. 2 Tim. 4.5, 11. Heb. 9.21. Apoc. 2.19. A ministry subordinate to the Levitical, and altogether servile: Ios. 9.27. A secular ministry, private or public: Gen. 40.13, 44.33. 1 Par. 26, vv. 30, 32. Esth. 7.9. Esai. 22.19. Luc. 10.40. The ministry of the stars, serving man: Deut. 4.19.

units.la: Ministeri opera in veteri & nouo Testamento. Primo, Docere verbum Dei,& administrare Sacramenta. Exempla: Leuitae & Sacerdotes, 2 Paralip. 17. 9, Ezech, 44,23, Petrus & Apostoli concionantur poenitentiam & remissionem peccatorum, Actor.2.38.baptizant credentes,ver. 41. perseuerant in factione panis, v.46 Paulus summam sui officij recitat, Actor. 20. v.20. 21 & 26. v. 19, 20. Secundo, Refutat impia Pseudoprophetarum & falsorum Doctorum dogmata. Exempla: Elias, 1 Reg.18.v. 21. 22. Ieremias iussu Dei refutat Pseudoprophetarum vaticinia, qui asserebant Deum non punituru m g'adio & fame Ierosolymam, Ierem. 14 v.1.2 &c.Hananiam grauiter refutat, 28 v. 15 16. Ezechiel similiter refutat Pseudoprophetas, & Pseudoprophetissas, Ezechiel.13.v. 3.18.Stephanus Scholasticos Libertinorum, Cyrenensium, Cilicum,&c.refutat, Actor.6 9 &c,Paulus confundit Iudeos,& refutat Graecos & demonstrat Christum esse Filium Dei,9.22. Idem cum Barnaba & aliis Antiochiae refutat Pseudoapostolos, 15 2 quod ipsum in Epistolis etiam suis strenue & terio agit.Apollos vehementer reuincebat Iudaeos, ostendens per Scripturas, quod Iesus esset Christus, Act.18.28 Petrus refutat Pseudodoctores, 2.Petri 2.v.1.12.&c.& 3.3.&c.4.v.2.3. Ioannes refutat Antichristi doctrinam 1 Ioan.4 2.3 & 2.Ioh.v.7. Tertio Hortari ad conversionem & poenitentiam. Exempla:Prophetae,Ieremiam 35.15. Oseas,Ose,5 1.& 6.1.&14.2.Baruch,2.v.13.14 15. Ioel,Ioel 2.12. Ioannes Baptista, Matt.3.v.1.7. Vide POENITENTIA. Ministerium Euangelicum a ciuili iurisdictione distinguitur, & ministrorum potestas quousque extendatur,ostenditur, Matt.20.v.25.26,
units.tr: The works of the ministry in the Old and New Testaments. First, to teach the Word of God and administer the sacraments. Examples: the Levites and priests, 2 Par. 17.9; Ezech. 44.23; Peter and the apostles preach repentance and the forgiveness of sins, Act. 2.38; they baptize believers, v. 41; they persevere in the breaking of bread, v. 46; Paul recites the sum of his office, Act. 20.20, 21, and 26.19, 20. Second, to refute the impious doctrines of false prophets and false teachers. Examples: Elijah, 1 Reg. 18, vv. 21–22. Jeremiah, at God's command, refutes the prophecies of false prophets who asserted that God would not punish Jerusalem with sword and famine, Ierem. 14, vv. 1–2, etc. He sharply refutes Hananiah, 28, vv. 15–16. Ezekiel likewise refutes false prophets and false prophetesses, Ezech. 13, vv. 3, 18. Stephen refutes the scholars of the Freedmen, the Cyrenians, the Cilicians, etc., Act. 6.9, etc. Paul confounds the Jews, refutes the Greeks and demonstrates that Christ is the Son of God, Act. 9.22. The same man, with Barnabas and others at Antioch, refutes the false apostles, Act. 15.2; which he also does vigorously and frequently in his Epistles. Apollos vigorously convinced the Jews, showing from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ, Act. 18.28. Peter refutes false teachers, 2 Petr. 2, vv. 1, 12, etc., and 3.3, etc., 4, vv. 2–3. John refutes the doctrine of Antichrist, 1 Ioan. 4.2–3 and 2 Ioan. v. 7. Third, to exhort to conversion and repentance. Examples: the prophets, Ieremiam 35.15. Hosea, Hos. 5.1, 6.1, 14.2. Baruch, 2, vv. 13–15. Joel, Ioel 2.12. John the Baptist, Matth. 3, vv. 1–7. See REPENTANCE. The Gospel ministry is distinguished from civil jurisdiction, and the extent of the power of ministers is shown, Matth. 20, vv. 25–26.

units.la: MINISTRI quales in mundo habentur, Act.26.24. (Vide INSANIA). Patrisfamilias comparantur, Matth. 13.52. Filios Dei gigni dicuntur, quatenus Dei sunt instrumenta,1 Cor. 4. 15. Gal.4. 19. Philem.v.10. Minister noster Christus, Matth.20.28. Marci 10.45. Hebr.8.2. minister sit,qui primatum quaerit, Matth 20 26.ministri Dei sunt Paulus, Apollos,& huiusmodi Praedicatores, 1 Cor. 35.&c.4.1. ministri Dei quales, Leuit.21.17. ministri verbi a Deo pretendi, matt.9 38. diligendi sunt, 1 Thess.5. v.12.13.
units.tr: MINISTERS, as they are regarded in the world, Act. 26.24 (see MADNESS). They are compared to a householder, Matth. 13.52. They are said to beget sons of God, inasmuch as they are God's instruments, 1 Cor. 4.15, Gal. 4.19, Philem. v. 10. Our minister is Christ, Matth. 20.28, Marc. 10.45, Heb. 8.2. Whoever seeks the first place is to be the minister, Matth. 20.26. Paul, Apollos and such preachers are ministers of God, 1 Cor. 3.5, etc., 4.1. What sort of people God's ministers should be: Levit. 21.17. Ministers of the Word are to be asked of God, Matth. 9.38. They are to be loved, 1 Thess. 5, vv. 12–13.

units.la: MINISTRORUM elogia: In veteri Testamento appellati sunt Prophetae, Gen.20.7. Deut.18.18. & passim alibi. Dij, Exodi 4.16. & 7.1. Videntes, 1 Sam. 9.9. Pastores, Ephes. 4.11. Plantores, 1 Cor. 3.6. Rigatores, ibid. Sal terræ, Matt. 5.13. συνεργοί, i. cooperarij Dei, 1 Cor. 3.v. 5.9. Serui Dei, Tit. 1.1, Dei & Christi, Iacob. 1.1, Apostoli, Eph. 1.1, & 4.11,2, Cor. 1.1, Coloss. 1.1, Gal. 1.1. Christi, serui: Rom. 1.1; Phil. 1.1.
units.tr: THE TITLES of ministers. In the Old Testament they are called prophets, Gen. 20.7, Deut. 18.18, and elsewhere; gods, Exod. 4.16 and 7.1; seers, 1 Sam. 9.9; men of God, 1 Sam. 9.6, 1 Reg. 13.1–2; 2 Petr. 1.20–21; watchmen, Esai. 56.10, Ezech. 3.17 and 33.7. In the New Testament: angels, Apoc. 3.1; stewards of the mysteries of God, 1 Cor. 4.1, Tit. 1.7; teachers, Eph. 4.11; bishops, 1 Tim. 3.2, Tit. 1.7; evangelists, Eph. 4.11; leaven, Matth. 13.33, Luc. 13.21; light of the world, Matth. 5.14; ministers of God, Tit. 1.1; pastors, Eph. 4.11; planters, 1 Cor. 3.6; waterers, ibid.; salt of the earth, Matth. 5.13; συνεργοί [synergoi], fellow workers of God, 1 Cor. 3, vv. 5, 9; servants of God, Tit. 1.1; servants of God and of Christ, Iac. 1.1; apostles, Eph. 1.1, 4.11, 2 Cor. 1.1, Col. 1.1, Gal. 1.1; servants of Christ, Rom. 1.1, Phil. 1.1.

units.la: Ministri quo icco habendi, 1 Corint. 3 4. &c. & 4.1,1 Thess. 5,12,1, Tim. 5 17, Hebr. 13,17, Ministrorum officium, seu munus, est vera ædificandi ratio, 1 Corinth. 3. ver. 6.9, 10, Ministrorum sermo qualis esse debeat, 1.17. & 2 13.1, Petr. 4 11,2 Petr. 1,16, Ephes. 4.29,2, Tim. 2,v,15,25, & 1,13, Colos. 4.6, Tit. 1,9, Duces sunt & pastores animarum, Hebr. 13,17, Vide Apostoli. ideòque illis parendum, v. 17. Supremus eorum & aliarum omnium pastor Christus, v. 20.
units.tr: How ministers are to be regarded: 1 Cor. 3.4, etc., 4.1; 1 Thess. 5.12; 1 Tim. 5.17; Heb. 13.17. The office or duty of ministers is the true method of building: 1 Cor. 3, vv. 6, 9, 10. What the speech of ministers should be like: 1 Cor. 1.17, 2.13; 1 Petr. 4.11; 2 Petr. 1.16; Eph. 4.29; 2 Tim. 2, vv. 15, 25, and 1.13; Col. 4.6; Tit. 1.9. They are leaders and shepherds of souls, Heb. 13.17. See APOSTLES. Therefore they are to be obeyed, v. 17. Their supreme shepherd, and that of all others, is Christ, v. 20.

Timoth. 5, v 1,2 3,20. probandi sunt prius, quàm ministrent, 1, Tim. 3,10.
units.tr: They are allowed to live from the Gospel: Deut. 24, vv. 14–15, and 25.4. Matth. 10.10. Luc. 10.7. Rom. 15.27. 1 Cor. 9.7, etc. Gal. 6.6. 1 Tim. 5, vv. 17–18. From these passages it is clear that the ministers of the Word are owed sustenance. The Philippians supplied Paul with it, Philipp. 4, vv. 14–16. Ministers are to be held dear, and to be anticipated with honour, respect and obedience, 1 Thess. 5.12; 1 Tim. 5.17; Heb. 13.17. What sort of men are to be chosen: 1 Tim. 3.13; Tit. 1, vv. 5–8. The perfect pattern of ministers is set forth: 1 Tim. 3, vv. 1–2, etc.; Tit. 1, vv. 5–8. The duty and prudence in rebuking men and women of different ages: 1 Tim. 5, vv. 1–3, 20. They are to be tested before they minister: 1 Tim. 3.10.

units.la: Ministrorum etiam malorum operâ dignatur uti Deus bonitas, Matth. 7,22, Marci 9,38, Lucæ 9,49, quos & audiri iubet, Matt. 23 3, Ministri Verbi dicuntur in Scriptura alios saluare, Abdiæ 1,21, seruare, 1 Timoth. 4,16, quia sunt Ministri salutis per Euangelij doctrinam. Sic dicuntur peccata remittere, Ioannis 20. 23. quod alioqui solus Dei est, Marc. 2.7, Minister Circumcisionis quo sensu dicatur Christus, Rom. 15,8, quum eam suo aduentu abrogârit. Vide CIRCVMCISIO. Contra Ministros Dei murmurans, murmurat contra Deum, Exodi 16.7, ministerium reconciliationis accepit paulus Euangelium nuncians, 2 Corinth. 5.18. ministerium Verbi, prædicatio Euangelij, Actor. 20.24. ministeria varia Christianis data, Ephes. 4.7. &c. ministrationes Spiritus diuersæ, 1 Corinth. 12.5.
units.tr: God deigns to use the work even of evil ministers: Matth. 7.22, Marc. 9.38, Luc. 9.49. He also commands that they be heard, Matth. 23.3. Ministers of the Word are said in Scripture to save others, Obad. 1.21, and to preserve them, 1 Tim. 4.16, because they are ministers of salvation through the doctrine of the Gospel. So they are said to forgive sins, Ioann. 20.23, which otherwise belongs to God alone, Marc. 2.7. In what sense Christ is called the minister of the circumcision, Rom. 15.8, since by his coming he abrogated it. See CIRCUMCISION. Whoever murmurs against God's ministers murmurs against God, Exod. 16.7. Paul received the ministry of reconciliation by announcing the Gospel, 2 Cor. 5.18. The ministry of the Word is the preaching of the Gospel, Act. 20.24. Various ministries are given to Christians, Eph. 4.7, etc. There are diverse ministrations of the Spirit, 1 Cor. 12.5.

units.la: MIPHIBOSETH, Ionathæ filius, casu claudus efficitur. 2. Sam. 4. 4. omnes Saulis agri [illi restituuntur, 9. 9. inuenit gratiam coram Dauide, 9.7. parcit ei Dauid, 21.7. appellatur Meribbaal, 1. Paral. 9.40. (i. de ore ignominia.)
units.tr: MEPHIBOSHETH, son of Jonathan, is made lame by an accident, 2 Sam. 4.4. All the fields of Saul are restored to him, 9.9. He finds grace before David, 9.7. David spares him, 21.7. He is called Meribbaal, 1 Par. 9.40 (that is, out of the mouth of shame).

units.la: MIPHIBOSETH filius Saulis suspenditur, 2. Sam. 21. 8. &c.
units.tr: MEPHIBOSHETH, son of Saul, is hanged, 2 Sam. 21.8, etc.

units.tr: The wonderful name of God, Iudic. 13.18.

units.la: MIRACVLA: Miraculis à fide abducens occidendus, Deut. 13.1. &c. miraculum Christi primum, Ioan. 2. 11. miracula Christi non omnia scripta, 20.30.31. doctrinam sequuntur perinde ac tabulas sigilla, Matth. 10.8. Marc. 16. 20. Actor. 4. v. 29 30. Rom. 15 19. Heb. 2.4. miracula tempore Christi futura prædicuntur, Esaiæ 35. v. 5. 6. miracula sunt confirmatio verbi, Marc. 16.17. Pseudoprophetarum, Ierem. 23.32. miracula fidem in Christum comitantur, Marc. 16.17.
units.tr: MIRACLES. One who draws people away from faith by miracles is to be put to death, Deut. 13.1, etc. The first miracle of Christ, Ioann. 2.11. Not all the miracles of Christ are written, 20.30–31. They accompany doctrine just as seals accompany documents, Matth. 10.8, Marc. 16.20, Act. 4.29–30, Rom. 15.19, Heb. 2.4. Miracles were foretold as future at the time of Christ, Esai. 35, vv. 5–6. Miracles are the confirmation of the Word, Marc. 16.17; the miracles of false prophets, Ierem. 23.32. Miracles accompany faith in Christ, Marc. 16.17.

units.la: MIRACVLORVM finis legitimus, Matth. 9.8. & 15.31. Mar. 2.12. & 7.37. Ioan. 6.14. & 11. 45. & 12. 11. Actor. 9. v. 35. 42. & 14. 15 & 19. 17. Miracula dicuntur signa, Heb. 2. 4. eò quòd aliud repræsentent, quàm quod cernitur, ut quæ nihil aliud sint, quàm veræ doctrinæ sigilla. Dicuntur item prodigia, quòd nouum & insuetum aliquid exhibeant. Et virtutes, quòd excellentis illius diuinæ virtutis extraordinarium specimen edant, miracula edere etiam impiis interdum concessum. Matth. 7. v. 22. 23. & 24. 24. Marci 13.22. Apocal. 13. 13. & 16.14. & 19.20. miracula falsa Antichristi imperio stabiliendo concessa, Matth. 24.24. Marc. 13.22.2. Thessal. 2.9. Vide SIGNA: & PRODIGIA.
units.tr: The lawful end of miracles: Matth. 9.8; 15.31; Mark 2.12; 7.37; John 6.14; 11.45; 12.11; Acts 9.35, 42; 14.15; 19.17. Miracles are called signs (Heb. 2.4) because they point to something other than what is seen, since they are nothing other than seals of true doctrine. They are also called prodigies because they display something new and unusual. And they are called powers because they make manifest an extraordinary example of that excellent divine power. It has also sometimes been granted even to the wicked to work miracles: Matth. 7.22, 23; 24.24; Mark 13.22; Rev. 13.13; 16.14; 19.20. These are the false miracles of Antichrist, permitted for establishing his rule: Matth. 24.24; Mark 13.22; 2 Thess. 2.9. See SIGNS and PRODIGIES.

units.la: Miraculorum exempla: Creatio mundi, Genesis 1.1. Diluuium, 7. v. 19. 21. in diluuio seruata familia Noe. 8.18. Linguarum confusio, 11. 7. Sodomæ & Gomorrhæ excidium, 19.24. Vxoris Loth in salis statuam mutatio, v. 26. Rubus ardens, Exodi 3.2. Virga Mosis in colubrum versa 4. v. 3. 4. Mosis manus leprosa, v. 6. 7. Virga Aaronis in colubrum versa, 7.10. aquæ in sanguinem mutatæ, v. 20. Ranæ, 8.6. Muscæ, v. 24. Vesicarum vlcera, 9.10. Fulgur, grando & ignis, v. 23. 24. 25. Locustæ, 10. v. 12. 13. 14. Tenebræ, v. 22. 23. Psalm. 105. 28. Primogenitorum clades, Exod. 12. 29.
units.tr: Examples of miracles: the creation of the world, Gen. 1.1; the Flood, 7.19, 21; the family of Noah preserved in the Flood, 8.18; the confusion of tongues, 11.7; the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, 19.24; the transformation of Lot's wife into a pillar of salt, v. 26; the burning bush, Exod. 3.2; Moses' rod turned into a serpent, 4.3, 4; Moses' leprous hand, vv. 6, 7; Aaron's rod turned into a serpent, 7.10; the waters turned into blood, v. 20; the frogs, 8.6; the flies, v. 24; the boils and ulcers, 9.10; the lightning, hail and fire, vv. 23–25; the locusts, 10.12–14; the darkness, vv. 22, 23; Ps. 105.28; the slaughter of the firstborn, Exod. 12.29.

Aqua è Petra manans, 17.6. promulgatio Legis, 19. & 20. c. in qua multa concurrunt mirabilia Dei opera, vt sunt, tonitrua, fulgura, nubes, ignis, insolitus tubarum clangor, vox Dei, montis tremor, &c. 19. v. 16.18.
units.tr: The pillar of fire and cloud, Exod. 13.21; the Red Sea divided, 14.21, 22, 26; the bitter waters made sweet, 15.25; the quails, 16.13; Num. 11.31; the manna, Exod. 16.14, 15; water flowing from the rock, 17.6; the giving of the Law, Exod. 19 and 20, in which many wondrous works of God come together: thunders, lightnings, clouds, fire, the unusual blast of trumpets, the voice of God, the trembling of the mountain, and so on, 19.16, 18.

Reg. 13.1. &c. arefacta manus Ieroboam, & eiusdem restitutio, v.4. 6. propheta à leone occisus, v.24. Elias à coruis pastus, 1. Reg. 17. 6. ab
units.tr: Also having the force of miracles: Moses' stay with the Lord on the mountain for forty days, Exod. 19.19 etc.; the stone tablets written with the finger of God, containing the Law, 31.18; the breaking and restoring of the same, 32.19 and 34.1; the appearance of the glory of the Lord and the covering of the Tabernacle, 40.34; fire going out from the Lord and consuming the burnt offering, Lev. 9.24; a cloud covering the Tabernacle, Num. 9.15; the prophesying of Eldad and Medad, 11.26; the leprosy of Miriam, who murmured against Moses, 12.10; the death of the spies of the land of Canaan, 14.27–30; the destruction of Korah, Dathan and Abiram, and their being swallowed up by the earth, 16.32, 33; the fiery serpents, whose antidote was the sight of the bronze serpent, 21.6–8; Balaam's ass speaking, 22.30; the garments of the Israelites not worn out during forty years, Deut. 8.4; the old age of Moses, vigorous, 34.7; the Jordan turned back, Josh. 3.16; the fall of the walls of Jericho, 6.20; stones falling from heaven, 10.11; the sun standing still in the middle of heaven for the space of one day, vv. 12, 13; Samson and his miraculous birth, Judg. 13.3; the killing of the lion by him, 14.6; the slaughter of a thousand men with a single jawbone of an ass, struck by him, 15.15; the water flowing from the ass's jaw, v. 19; the carrying of the gates of Gaza to the mountain, 16.3; the collapse of the house and the death (of the Philistines), v. 30; Dagon falling before the ark, 1 Sam. 5.2, 3; the striking of the Philistines in their hinder parts, 5.9; the return of the ark, 6.7; the call of Saul to the kingdom, 10.1 etc.; the stratagem of Jonathan with his armour-bearer and the rout of the Philistines, 14.14; the slaying of Goliath by David, 17.49; David's deliverance from Saul and other most bitter enemies, 1 Sam. 18, 19, 24, 25 etc.; a famine of three years on account of the violated faith of the Gibeonites, 2 Sam. 21.1, which was averted when seven men of Saul's family had been hanged, vv. 6, 7 etc.; the plague, 24.15; the cloud in the house of God, 1 Kings 8.10; fire from heaven consuming the sacrifices, 2 Chron. 7.1; the altar at Bethel split at the word of the man of God, 1 Kings 13.1 etc.; the hand of Jeroboam withered and restored, vv. 4, 6; the prophet killed by a lion, v. 24; Elijah fed by ravens, 1 Kings 17.6; by an angel, 19.5 etc.

Hospitæ sterili filius impetratus, 4.17. eiusdem refuscitatio, ver.34. Aquę lethales salubres redditæ,2.v.20.21. Pulmentum amarum dulce redditum, 4.41. Panes famis tempore multiplicati, v. 43. Hazaeli præsenti, eorum quæ facturus erat, prædiction,8.12. Cadauer mortui Elisæi,13.21.Samariæ obsidio soluta,& Syri profligati, 7. v. 6. 7. Ab Angelo centum & octoginta quinque hominum millia interfecta,19.35.(Esai 37.36.2. Paral. 31.21.) Horologium Achaz 2.Reg.20.v.10.11. Æthiopum profligatio,1.Paral.14.12.Moabitæ,Ammonitæ, &c.mutuis vulneribus cõcidentes, 20.v.15.16.17.18.19.20. 23.Oziæ lepra.26.19.
units.tr: The meal of the widow, 17.15, 16; the raising of the widow's son, v. 22; the burnt offering kindled and consumed by fire from heaven, 18.38; the strength of the food given to Elijah, 19.7, 8; the waters of Elijah's mantle divided, 2 Kings 2.8; the taking up of Elijah into heaven, v. 11. Miracles performed through Elisha: the division of the waters, 2 Kings 2.14; water obtained for the army, 3.20; the widow's oil, 4.3–5; the cleansing of Naaman the Syrian from leprosy, 5.14; Gehazi struck at the word of Elisha, v. 27; the iron floating, 6.6; the blinding of the enemies, v. 18; a son obtained for the barren hostess, 4.17; his raising of the same, v. 34; the deadly waters made wholesome, 2.20, 21; the bitter pottage made sweet, 4.41; the loaves multiplied in time of famine, v. 43; the prediction to Hazael of what he was going to do, 8.12; the corpse of the dead Elisha, 13.21; the siege of Samaria lifted and the Syrians routed, 7.6, 7; a hundred and eighty-five thousand men slain by an angel, 19.35 (Isa. 37.36; 2 Chron. 31.21); the sundial of Ahaz, 2 Kings 20.10, 11; the rout of the Ethiopians, 1 Chron. 14.12; the Moabites and Ammonites falling by mutual wounds, 2 Chron. 20.15–20, 23; the leprosy of Uzziah, 26.19.

units.la: Tempore captiuitatis Babylonicæ multa etiam acciderunt admiratione digna:vt sunt, Somnium Nabuchodonosor de statua,Dan.2.1. &c.eius per Danielem repetitio & interpretatio, v. 16. 29. Sidrach, Misach, & Abdenagonis liberatio, 3.v.25.26. 27.28. Nabuchodonosor ex hominibus & humana societate expulsio,4.v.21.22.25. Danielis ex lacu leonum liberatio,6.22. Visiones miraculosæ Danieli factæ de futuris euentibus, Danielis 7. 8.9.10.11.capitibus.Ionas à pisce absorptus, & iterum liberatus, Ionæ 2. vers. 1. 11. Miraculosæ etiam res sunt, quòd Mardochæus ab Assuero honoratur, Esther 6. 10. Aman Iudæorum hostis suspenditur,7.10. mandatum crudele in Iudæos abrogatur,7. 10. & 8.8. Miracula item sunt. Populi Iudaici ex captiuitate dimissio, & Templi ac ciuitatis reædificatio,1.Esdræ 1.2.3.4. 5.6. 7.capitibus:& Nehemiæ 2.3.4 6.capitib. Catalogum miraculorũ Dei, Dauid etiam passim in Psalmis suis texit, vt Psalm.44.1.& 76.1. & 78.1.& 89.1.& 105.1.106.1.& 114. 1.& 115.1.& 135.1.& 136.1.& 145.4.Et Nehemias.9Nehem. v.5.6 &c.
units.tr: In the time of the Babylonian captivity many things also happened worthy of admiration, such as: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue, Dan. 2.1 etc., and its repetition and interpretation by Daniel, vv. 16, 29; the deliverance of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, 3.25–28; Nebuchadnezzar's expulsion from men and human society, 4.21, 22, 25; Daniel's deliverance from the den of lions, 6.22; the miraculous visions shown to Daniel of future events, Daniel chapters 7–11; Jonah swallowed by a fish and again set free, Jonah 2.1–11. There are also wondrous things in that Mordecai is honoured by Ahasuerus, Esther 6.10; Haman, the enemy of the Jews, is hanged, 7.10; the cruel decree against the Jews is revoked, 7.10 and 8.8. Miracles also are the release of the Jewish people from captivity, and the rebuilding of the Temple and the city, Ezra chapters 1–7, and Nehemiah chapters 2–4, 6. David also, throughout his Psalms, recounts the catalogue of God's miracles: Ps. 44.1; 76.1; 78.1; 89.1; 105.1; 106.1; 114.1; 115.1; 135.1; 136.1; 145.4. And Nehemiah, Neh. 9.5, 6 etc.

units.tr: Aqua flowing from the rock, Exod. 17.6; bitter waters made sweet, 15.25; wholesome made, 2 Kings 2.20, 21; the mantle of Elijah divided, v. 14; water turned into wine, John 2.9. Ear of Malchus restored, Luke 22.51. Blind: the Sodomites struck with blindness, Gen. 19.11; the Syrians, 2 Kings 6.18; Saul, Acts 9.9; Elymas, 13.11. The blind receive sight, Matth. 9.30; 12.22; 15.30; 20.34; Mark 8.25; Luke 7.21; John 9.7. The lame walk, Matth. 15.30; 21.14; Acts 3.7; 14.10. The bent woman is made upright, Luke 13.12, 13. Demons cast out, Matth. 8.16; 9.33; 12.22; 15.28; 17.18; Mark 1.26, 34, 39; 3.11; 5.8; 7.29; 9.25; 6.9; Luke 4.35, 41; 6.18; 8.2; 9.42; 11.14; 13.32; Acts 16.18; also by wicked men, Matth. 7.22; Mark 9.39; Luke 9.49; Acts 19.13. Fevers cured, Matth. 8.15; Mark 1.31; Luke 4.39; John 4.52; Acts 28.8. The fig tree withered, Matth. 21.18; Mark 11.13. The dropsical cured, Luke 14.4. The river Jordan divided, Josh. 3.16; 2 Kings 2.14. Lepers cleansed: Miriam, sister of Moses, Num. 12.15; Naaman the Syrian, 2 Kings 5.14; lepers, Matth. 8.3; Mark 1.42; Luke 5.13; 17.14. Those afflicted with diseases are restored, Matth. 4.23, 24; 9.25; 12.15; 19.2; Mark 1.34; 3.10, 56; Luke 4.40; 6.18; 7.21; 9.? ; John 5.8; Acts 5.16. The withered hand healed, Matth. 12.13; Mark 3.1 etc.; Luke 6.10. The sea divided, Exod. 14.21; the sea walked on as solid ground by Christ, Matth. 14.25; Mark 6.48; John 6.19. The dead called back to life, 1 Kings 17.22; 2 Kings 4.34, 35; 13.21; Matth. 9.25; 27.52; Mark 5.41, 42; Luke 7.14; 8.54, 55; John 11.44; Acts 9.40; 10.10. Loaves multiplied, Matth. 14.19, 20; 15.36, 37; Mark 6.43; 8.6, 7; Luke 9.16; John 6.11. The paralytics healed, Matth. 8.13; 9.6; Mark 2.11; Luke 5.24; John 5.8; Acts 9.33. Fish innumerable caught, Luke 5.6; John 21.6. The doors of the prison opened, Acts 5.19; 12.10; 16.26. The flux stopped, Matth. 9.20; Mark 5.29; Luke 8.48. The deaf hear, Mark 7.32. A stater found in the mouth of a fish, Matth. 17.27.

units.la: MIRACVLA per se fieri orant Apostoli, Act. 4 30. miraculis Christi glorificatur Deus, Matth. 15. 31. miraculis mentientes se Christum, Matth. 24 24. miraculis nostram fidem tentat Deus, Deut. 13. 3. miraculis potuit cognosci Christus, Ioan. 10 25. miraculis probatus est Christus a Deo esse missus, Act. 2. 22.
units.tr: The apostles pray that miracles may be done through themselves (Acts 4:30). God is glorified by the miracles of Christ (Matt. 15:31). Those who falsely claim to be Christ do so by miracles (Matt. 24:24). God tests our faith by miracles (Deut. 13:3). Christ could be known by miracles (John 10:25). Christ was proved by miracles to have been sent by God (Acts 2:22).

units.la: MIRACVLORVM Diabolicorum catalogus: Malefici & incantatores apud Pharaonem virgas in draconem commutant, Exodi 7.12. aquas in cruorem, v.20. &c. Pythonissa mulier Samuelem producit, 1.Sam.28.11. &c. ¶ Miracula operari Deum per Sanctos & eorum reliquias, quas magno cumulo ostentant, quibus testimoniis probent idololatriae Pontifici, Vide SANCTI: & RELIQVIAE.
units.tr: MIRACLES: a catalogue of diabolical miracles. Sorcerers and enchanters at Pharaoh's court turn rods into serpents (Exod. 7:12) and water into blood (v. 20), etc. The woman who was a medium brings up Samuel (1 Sam. 28:11), etc. ¶ That God works miracles through the saints and their relics, which they display in great heaps, and by which the Papists prove their idolatry. See SAINTS and RELICS.

units.la: MISACH, (Vide SIDRACH.) Mesach.1. preciosus, vel tendens arcum.
units.tr: MISACH (see SHADRACH). Meshach: "precious" or "stretching the bow."

units.tr: MERCY, kindness, namely of God: Exod. 34:5-6; Neh. 9:17 and 13:14, 22; Isa. 63:7; Jonah 4:2. Mercy is the benefit which God kindly bestows on a man: Gen. 32:10. The mercies of God: 1 Chron. 21:13; Neh. 9:27, 31; Ps. 25:6; 40:12; 51:3; 69:17; 103:8; 119:77; 145:9; Isa. 54:7; 63:15; Jer. 16:5; Lam. 3:22; Dan. 9:18; Hos. 2:18. (See COMPASSION.)

units.tr: Mercy, the mercy of man toward man: Job 31:18; Zech. 7:9; Phil. 2:1; Heb. 10:28.

units.tr: A miserable man: Judg. 5:27; Eccl. 5:15; 1 Cor. 15:19; Rev. 3:17.

units.tr: God shows mercy, that is, is favourable to men: Gen. 39:21; Deut. 8:16; 2 Sam. 24:16; 2 Kings 13:23; Ps. 30:11; 60:3; 103:13; Isa. 54:8; 60:10; Amos 7:3, 6; Jonah 3:10; Rom. 9:15, 16, 18; 11:32; Phil. 2:27. Christ, God and man, dwelling among men, shows mercy: Matt. 9:36; 14:14; 20:34; Mark 1:41; 5:19; 6:34. A man shows mercy to a man: Exod. 2:6; Ruth 2:19, etc.; Ps. 37:21, 26; 103:13; 112:5; Prov. 14:21, 31; 19:17; Matt. 18:33; Rom. 12:8; Jude 22.]

units.la: MISERETVR Deus cuius vult, Exodi 33.19. Roman.9.15. miseretur Deus propter promissiones suas, 2.Reg.13.23. vt misereatur nostri Deus orandum, Numer.6.25. misereatur tui Deus, benedictionis formula, Gen.43.29.
units.tr: God shows mercy to whom he wills: Exod. 33:19; Rom. 9:15. God shows mercy for the sake of his promises: 2 Kings 13:23. That God may show mercy to us is to be prayed for: Num. 6:25. "May God show mercy to you" is a formula of blessing: Gen. 43:29.

units.la: MISERI sumus, vt felices efficiamur, Iac.4.9.
units.tr: We are wretched so that we may be made happy: Jas. 4:9.

units.la: MISERICORDIA, est alienae miseriae in corde nostro, ex sensu charitatis, compassio, cui vtique si possumus, subvenire uenire cupimus. Misericors igitur succurrit, si potest, omni petenti atque afflicto, siue noto nobis, siue ignoto: ex praecepto Christi, Luc. 6. 30. 36.
units.tr: MERCY is, from a sense of love, the feeling of another's misery in our heart, a compassion, to which we desire, if we can, to bring help. The merciful therefore come to the aid, if they can, of every petitioner and afflicted person, whether known or unknown to us, by the precept of Christ: Luke 6:30, 36.

Ierem. 12. 15. & 36. 3. Ezech. 16. v. 63. & 18. 30. misericordia misericordi promittitur, Matth. 5. 7. misericordia commendatur, Prou. 11. 17. Mich. 6. 8. Zachar. 7. 9. Luc. 6. 36. Ephes. 4. 32. Iac. 2. 13. 1 Petr. 3. 8. misericordia sacrificiis anteferenda Ose. 6. 6. Matt. 9. 13. & 12. 7.
units.tr: MERCY: mercy is used for the duties of humanity, Matt. 9:13 and 12:7; by synecdoche, for grace: Jude v. 2; mercy promised to the repentant: Deut. 30:2-3; Isa. 55:7; Jer. 12:15 and 36:3; Ezek. 16:63 and 18:30. Mercy is promised to the merciful: Matt. 5:7. Mercy is commended: Prov. 11:17; Mic. 6:8; Zech. 7:9; Luke 6:36; Eph. 4:32; Jas. 2:13; 1 Pet. 3:8. Mercy is to be preferred to sacrifices: Hos. 6:6; Matt. 9:13 and 12:7.

units.tr: The good things of mercy: Prov. 21:21. The works of mercy to be shown to a neighbour: 1 Sam. 15:6; 2 Chron. 28:9, 15; Ps. 112:5, 9; Prov. 11:17; 14:21, etc.; 15:27; 24:21, 31; 19:7; 25:21; Eccl. 4:2, 29; 35:18; Isa. 59:7; Hos. 6:11; Mic. 6:8; Zech. 7:9; Matt. 5:7; 9:13; 10:41; 18:33; 25:41; Mark 9:41; Luke 6:35; 10:33; Rom. 12:13; Gal. 6:11; Col. 3:12; 1 Tim. 5:10. Israelitas, Exodi 15.13. erga populum suum, 2 Reg.13.23. Vide Dei misericordiam. Filiæ Pharaonis erga Mosen, Exodi 2.6. Rahab erga exploratores, Iosu 2.12. Cinæi erga Israelitas, 1 Sam.15.6. Galaaditarum erga Saulem, 2 Samu.2.5. Dauidis erga Miphiboseth, 2 Samu.9.7. Christi erga turbas & languidos, Matth. 9.36. & 14.14. & 15.32. & 20.34. Marc.1 41. Samaritani erga faucium, Luc.10.33. Misericordiæ vasa quinam ab Hebræis dicantur, Vide VASA misericordiæ.
units.tr: [Merciful God: Exod. 22:27 and 34:6; Neh. 9:17; Ps. 78:38; 86:5; 103:8. See "God the Merciful One." Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2; Luke 6:36; Jas. 5:11. Merciful Christ: Heb. 2:17. Merciful man: Prov. 11:17 and 13:13; Matt. 5:7; Luke 6:36; Eph. 4:32; 1 Pet. 3:8.] Examples of mercy: God's toward Joseph, Gen. 39:21; toward the Israelites, Exod. 15:13; toward his own people, 2 Kings 13:23. See God's mercy. Pharaoh's daughter toward Moses, Exod. 2:6; Rahab toward the spies, Josh. 2:12; the Kenizzites toward the Israelites, 1 Sam. 15:6; the men of Gilead toward Saul, 2 Sam. 2:5; David toward Mephibosheth, 2 Sam. 9:7; Christ toward the crowds and the sick, Matt. 9:36; 14:14; 15:32; 20:34; Mark 1:41; the Samaritan toward the wounded man, Luke 10:33. What are the vessels of mercy, as the Hebrews call them: see VESSELS of mercy.
