Malach.1. ver.10.11. ¶ Per varias veteris Testamenti figuras significatum esse nugantur, Genes. 14 18 & 16.6. & 22.13. Exodi 12.v.5.24. & 25.30. & 29 v.2.15. Leuit.2. verf.13. & 3.12 & 4.23. & 5.ver.7.11 & 6.15. & 9 8. & 14.4. & 16 3 & 19.21. Numer.15.24. & 18.17.1 Sam. 21 4. 1 Regum 19.6 2. Reg. 4 41. Dan. 8. 12. appellari illud iuge Sacrificium, eúsque offerentem non interire, Ierem.33 11.31. & 12 11. eúsque offerentem non interire, Ierem.33 verf.18.21. à Christo esse institutum, Luc. 22. 19. & Discipulis eius institutum, Actor.13. 2. vbi λειτουργούντων meminit Lucas. Fieri eius mentionem apud Paulum etiam 1 Cor. 10.16. & 11.23. celebrari illud donec veniat Dominus, v.26.
units.tr: ¶ That the sacrifice of the Mass was foretold and announced long ago, the Papist sacrificers try to prove by these testimonies: Lev. 26:9-12; Ps. 23:5 and 110:4; Isa. 2:2-3 and 19:19-20; 56:7; 61:6; 66:15, 20-21; Jer. 31:31; 33:16-18; Dan. 12:11; Amos 9:11; Mal. 1:10-11. ¶ They trifle that it was signified through various figures of the Old Testament: Gen. 14:18; 16:6; 22:13; Exod. 12:5, 24; 25:30; 29:2, 15; Lev. 2:13; 3:12; 4:23; 5:7, 11; 6:15; 9:8; 14:4; 16:3; 19:21; Num. 15:24; 18:17; 1 Sam. 21:4; 1 Kings 19:6; 2 Kings 4:41; Dan. 8:12. That this perpetual sacrifice is so called, and that its offerer does not perish: Jer. 33:11, 31; 12:11; Jer. 33:18, 21. That it was instituted by Christ: Luke 22:19, and instituted for his disciples: Acts 13:2, where Luke mentions their ministering [λειτουργούντων]. Its mention is also made by Paul: 1 Cor. 10:16 and 11:23. That it is to be celebrated "until the Lord comes": v. 26.

units.la: MITES, (V.mansuetudo) beati, Matt.5.5. Diriguntur à Deo Psal.25.9. & clementer tractatantur, 86. 5. & 147.6. & euehuntur, Eccles.10.17. Vero gaudio recreantur, Esa.29.19. Præstant diuite superbo, Prou.16 19. sedant litem, 15.v.18. Hæreditatis iure terram possident: Matth 5.5. Psal.37. 11. exempl. Moses, Num.12 3. Christus, Matt.11.29.
units.tr: The meek (V. mansuetudo) are blessed, Matt. 5:5. God guides them, Ps. 25:9, and treats them gently, Ps. 86:5 and 147:6, and lifts them up, Eccles. 10:17. They are refreshed with true joy, Isa. 29:19. They surpass the proud rich, Prov. 16:19, and they settle quarrels, Prov. 15:18. By right of inheritance they possess the land, Matt. 5:5; Ps. 37:11. Examples: Moses, Num. 12:3; Christ, Matt. 11:29.

units.la: MNA, vel Mina Hebræorum, & eius æstimatio, Ezech.45.12. Mina Græcorum, cuius pretium aureorum circiter decem fuit, Luc.19.13. Est genus ponderis continens certum numerum vnciarum.
units.tr: MINA, or mina among the Hebrews, and its value, Ezek. 45:12. The Greek mina, whose price was about ten gold pieces, Luke 19:13. It is a kind of weight containing a fixed number of ounces.

units.la: MNASON Cyprius, Pauli hospes, Act.21.16. (Consolatio.)
units.tr: MNASON of Cyprus, Paul's host, Acts 21:16. (Consolation.)

units.la: MOAB ex incestu Lothi & eius filiæ natu maioris commercio nascitur, Genes. 19.37. hinc Moabitæ originem ducunt, ibid. Ab Ecclesia Iudaica arcebantur, Deut.23.3. Nehem.13.1 Moabitæ tributarij fiunt Dauidi, 2 Sam. 8.2. 1 Paral.11.
units.tr: MOAB was born from the incest of Lot with his elder daughter, Gen. 19:37; from him the Moabites trace their origin, ibid. They were excluded from the Jewish Church, Deut. 23:3; Neh. 13:1. The Moabites became tributaries to David, 2 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chron. 18:2.

units.la: ral.18.2.2 Reg.3 4.(.i.De patre.)
units.tr: …Chron. 18:2; 2 Kings 3:4. (i.e., concerning the father.)

units.la: MOABITARVM excidium prædicitur, Esa.15.1 & 25.10. Ierem. 48.v.2.4. Amos 2.v.1.2. Soph.2.v.8.9. Moabitarum idolum, Chamos, 1 Reg.11.7. contra Moabitas pugnare prohibetur Israel, Deut.2.8.9.
units.tr: The destruction of the Moabites is foretold, Isa. 15:1 and 25:10; Jer. 48:2, 4; Amos 2:1–2; Zeph. 2:8–9. The idol of the Moabites was Chemosh, 1 Kings 11:7. Israel is forbidden to make war against the Moabites, Deut. 2:8–9.

units.la: MODERATIO in rebus omnibus tenenda, 1 Cor.7.35.& 14.40.1 Tim.5.1. Iac.5.13. Moderationis exemplum: Paulus, 1 Cor. 3.2.& 9.22.
units.tr: Moderation is to be observed in all things, 1 Cor. 7:35; 14:40; 1 Tim. 5:1; James 5:13. An example of moderation: Paul, 1 Cor. 3:2 and 9:22.

units.la: MODESTIA, vt piis necessaria, commendatur, Rom. 12. v.3. 16. Galat.5.23. Philipp.4.5. Coloss.3.12. Tit.3.2.1 Petr.3.8.v. Prou.22.4. modestia pastoribus in primis necessaria. Vide PASTORES. Modestiæ exempla: Abraham, Genef. 23.7. Fratres Ierosolymitani, Actor. 11.18. & 15.12. Paulus, 26. 25.1 Cor.7.35.2 Corinr.12.2.&c.1 Thess.4.1 Tit.1.5. Philem. v.14.
units.tr: Modesty is commended as necessary for the godly, Rom. 12:3, 16; Gal. 5:23; Phil. 4:5; Col. 3:12; Titus 3:2; 1 Pet. 3:8; Prov. 22:4. Modesty is especially necessary for ministers; see MINISTERS. Examples of modesty: Abraham, Gen. 23:7; the brethren at Jerusalem, Acts 11:18 and 15:12; Paul, Acts 26:25; 1 Cor. 7:35; 2 Cor. 12:2, etc.; 1 Thess. 4:1; Titus 1:5; Philem. 14.

units.la: MODIVS (mensura quædam) iustus & æqualis sit, Leuit.19.36. Deut.25 14. Candela non ponenda subter modium: Matt. 5.15.
units.tr: The bushel (a certain measure) must be just and equal, Lev. 19:36; Deut. 25:14. A lamp is not to be put under a bushel, Matt. 5:15.

units.la: MOECHANDVM non est, Exodi 20.14. Deut.5.18.
units.tr: You shall not commit adultery, Exod. 20:14; Deut. 5:18.

units.la: MOECHVS moriatur, Leuit.20.10.
units.tr: The adulterer shall die, Lev. 20:10.

units.la: MOERORE consumitur inobediens, Deut.28 65.
units.tr: The disobedient are consumed with sorrow, Deut. 28:65.

units.la: MOLA, nec superior, nec inferior, pignori accipienda, Deut. 24.6. mola appensa collo paruos offendentis, Matth. 18.6.
units.tr: A millstone, neither upper nor lower, is not to be taken in pledge, Deut. 24:6. A millstone hung about the neck of one who causes little ones to stumble, Matt. 18:6.

units.la: MOLLITIES animi est, cum quid ingratum & insuave sensibus ferimus quidem, sed mollius, quàm viros graves & patientes deceat. Itaque eiulamus, conquerimur, impre-camur iis, qui nos affligunt, & fœminarum more ploramus. 1 Thess.4.13.
units.tr: Softness of spirit is when we bear something unpleasant and unpalatable to our senses, but more softly than befits serious and patient men. Thus we wail, complain, curse those who afflict us, and weep in the manner of women. 1 Thess. 4:13.

units.la: MOLLES à regno Dei excludendi, 1 Cor.6.v.10.11.
units.tr: The effeminate are to be excluded from the kingdom of God, 1 Cor. 6:10–11.

units.la: MOLOCH siue Milcom, idolum Ammonitarum, 1 Reg.11.5.2. Reg 23.10. illi suos liberos immolare prohibentur Iudæi, Leuit.20.2.&c.2. Reg.23.10. Ierem.32.35. Amos 5.26. Soph. 1.5. (Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.) Act.7.34.
units.tr: Moloch, or Milcom, the idol of the Ammonites, 1 Kings 11:5; 2 Kings 23:10. The Jews are forbidden to sacrifice their children to him, Lev. 20:2 etc.; 2 Kings 23:10; Jer. 32:35; Amos 5:26; Zeph. 1:5. (See the catalogue of IDOLS.) Acts 7:43.

units.la: MOMENTANEA leuitas oppressionum, 2 Cor.4.17.
units.tr: The momentary lightness of oppressions, 2 Cor. 4:17.

units.la: MONITIONES in Ecclesia necessariæ, Coloss.3.16.1 Thess.5.14. 1 Timoth.5.7.2 Timoth. 4.2. Hebr. 10.24. Monitionis exempla: Paulus, Act.20.28. Petrus, 2 Petr.1.13.&3.1. Iudas Iacobi frater, Iud.v.5. Monitiones temperandæ, 1 Tim.5.v.1.2. Iac. 3 1. Vide Admonitio.
units.tr: Admonitions are necessary in the Church, Col. 3:16; 1 Thess. 5:14; 1 Tim. 5:1; 2 Tim. 4:2; Heb. 10:24. Examples of admonition: Paul, Acts 20:28; Peter, 2 Pet. 1:13 and 3:1; Jude, the brother of James, Jude 5. Admonitions are to be tempered, 1 Tim. 5:1–2; James 3:1. See Admonition.

units.la: [MONS, montes communiter dicti frequenter, in Scripturis Sacris. Mons Sina, vel Sinai, cuius partes Horeb & Pha-ran, mons Dei dictus, Exod. 3.1. & 4.27. & 18.5 propter apparitiones illustres, & colloquia diuinæ maiestatis cum Mose, cui lex ibi data est. Mons Sion, qui & olim mons moria ab Abrahamo appellatus, mons Domini, mons Sanctus, mons domus Domini, cognominatur, quod in eo Ierosolyma & templum extructum fuerit. Genes. 22.v.2. 14.2 Reg. 19.31.2 Par 33.15. Psalm. 2.6. & 68.16. Esai. 2. v. 2. 3. Dan. 9.20. Zach. 8.3 Mons Sion, typus Ecclesiæ militantis & triumphantis, Heb. 12.22. Apoc. 14.1. mons Babylon, typus colluuiei Satanicæ quæ Ecclesiam Dei persequitur Ierem. 51.25. Zach. 4.7.
units.tr: [MOUNT: mountains are commonly so called frequently in Holy Scripture. Mount Sinai, or Sina, whose parts are Horeb and Paran, called the mount of God, Exod. 3:1; 4:27; 18:5, because of the illustrious appearances and the conversations of the divine majesty with Moses, to whom the law was given there. Mount Zion, which was also formerly called Moriah by Abraham, is named the mount of the Lord, the holy mount, the mount of the house of the Lord, because Jerusalem and the temple were built on it. Gen. 22:2; 2 Kings 19:31; 2 Chron. 33:15; Ps. 2:6 and 68:16; Isa. 2:2–3; Dan. 9:20; Zech. 8:3. Mount Zion is a type of the militant and triumphant Church, Heb. 12:22; Rev. 14:1. Mount Babylon is a type of the Satanic filth that persecutes the Church of God, Jer. 51:25; Zech. 4:7.]

units.la: MONTES mystici, Cant. 2.8. & 4.8. & 8.14. Daniel. 2. ver. 34. 35. 45.
units.tr: Mystical mountains, Song 2:8; 4:8; 8:14; Dan. 2:34–35, 45.

units.la: MONTES à Deo erecti, Psal. 104. 8. Dei contactu fumant, v. 32. & 144.5.
units.tr: Mountains raised up by God, Ps. 104:8. They smoke at God's touch, Ps. 104:32 and 144:5.

units.la: MORBI, ex peccato vt plurimùm proficiscuntur, Matth. 9.2. Mar. 2.5. Luc. 5.20. Ioan. 5.14. 1 Cor. 11.30. (V. AFFLICTIONES, & ÆGRITVDO.)
units.tr: Diseases for the most part proceed from sin, Matt. 9:2; Mark 2:5; Luke 5:20; John 5:14; 1 Cor. 11:30. (See AFFLICTIONS and SICKNESS.)

units.la: MORI, interdum quàm viuere, beatius: Exempla: Iosia, 2 Paral. 34.28. Israelitæ, Osee 10.8. Iudæi, Luc. 23.30. mori Paulo lucrum, Phil. 1.21. mori pro liberari, Col. 2.20. pro affligi & crucem ferre, Roman. 8.35. 2 Tim. 2.11. morte mori, phrasi Hebraica est, absque vlla spe veniæ impetrandæ morte multari, Mar. 7.10. & alibi passim in Veteri & Nouo Testamento. Mori in peccato dicuntur, quos undique peccato constrictos mors absorbet, Ioan. 8.21.
units.tr: Dying is sometimes more blessed than living. Examples: Josiah, 2 Chron. 34:28; the Israelites, Hos. 10:8; the Jews, Luke 23:30. To die is gain for Paul, Phil. 1:21; to die to be freed, Col. 2:20; to die for being afflicted and bearing the cross, Rom. 8:35; 2 Tim. 2:11. "To die the death" is a Hebrew phrase meaning to be punished with death without any hope of obtaining pardon, Mark 7:10, and elsewhere throughout the Old and New Testaments. They are said to die in sin who, bound on every side by sin, are swallowed up by death, John 8:21.

units.la: Mori peccato, tertio casu is dicitur, Roman. 6.2. in quo vis illa peccati extincta est per Christi virtutem, qui cum per fidem coaluit, adeò vt mutuò inter se respondeant, Mori peccato, & Viuere Deo, seu iustitiæ, seu Christo. Inde mortuus peccato, ibid. dicitur is, qui virtutis Christi particeps ita factus est, vt natiua illa corruptio sit in eo emortua, id est, vigore illo suo (qui transit titiè vita peccati dicitur) extincto, fructus illos amarissimos non edat: contrà verò, Viuere peccato & iniustitiæ, dicitur quisquis est in carne, id est, quemcunque Spiritus Dei à naturæ corruptionis seruitute non asseruit. Contraria verò illi priori significatione, mortuus peccatis, sexto casu, Ephes. 2.5. aut mortuus in peccatis, Col. 2.13. phrasi Paulina is dicitur, qui peccatis magis immortuus tenetur, qui & mortuus absolutè dicitur, Roman. 6.13. & 7.10. Eph. 5.14. 1 Tim. 5. Tim.5.6.qui etiam dicitur in umbra mortis habitare, Esa. 9.1.&qui non est renatus: quia sicut immortalitas damnatorum non est vita, sed mors quaedam perennis, sic etiam haec animi & corporis coniunctio, vita proprie non est, sed mors, in iis qui Christi Spiritu non aguntur, ut Esa. 9.1.Ioan.5.28.Ro.6.v.2.13.& 7.10.1 Tim.5.6. Mori in peccatis suis, Num.27.3.dicitur, qui propter peccata sua moritur. Mortuum peccatum, Paulo Rom.7.9.est, quod in nobis quidem est, sed non agnoscitur pro peccato, neque ita furit, ut solet post Legis cognitionem, ut apparet ex antithesi superioris versiculi, & ex iis quae sequuntur. Mortua opera dicuntur, Heb.9.14.peccata, quae a morte proficiscuntur, & nihil aliud quam mortem generant.
units.tr: To die to sin is said in the dative case, Rom. 6:2, in which that power of sin is extinguished through the virtue of Christ, who has grown together with us through faith, so that these correspond mutually: to die to sin and to live to God, whether to righteousness or to Christ. Hence he is said to be dead to sin, ibid., who has been made a partaker of the virtue of Christ, so that that native corruption is dead in him; that is, with its force (which is called the life of sin in the body) extinguished, he does not bear those most bitter fruits. On the contrary, he is said to live to sin and unrighteousness who is in the flesh, that is, whomever the Spirit of God has not rescued from the bondage of corrupt nature. But with the opposite meaning to that former one, "dead to sins" in the sixth case, Eph. 2:5, or "dead in sins," Col. 2:13, is the Pauline phrase for one who is held more dead to sins; he is also called simply dead, Rom. 6:13; 7:10; Eph. 5:14; 1 Tim. 5:6, and is said to dwell in the shadow of death, Isa. 9:1, and who is not reborn. For just as the immortality of the damned is not life but a kind of perpetual death, so also this union of soul and body is properly not life but death in those who are not driven by the Spirit of Christ, as in Isa. 9:1; John 5:28; Rom. 6:2, 13; 7:10; 1 Tim. 5:6. "To die in one's sins," Num. 27:3, is said of one who dies on account of his own sins. "Sin is dead," in Paul, Rom. 7:9, is that which is indeed in us but is not recognised as sin, nor does it rage as it usually does after the knowledge of the Law, as appears from the antithesis of the preceding verse and from what follows. "Dead works," Heb. 9:14, are sins which proceed from death and generate nothing but death.

units.la: Mors pro naturali animae & corporis solutione, ex peccato est, Gen.2,17 & 3.9. Rom.5.12.& 6.23. Cor.15.21. Col. 2.13.1 Tim.5.6.Eph.2.1.Iac.1.15.pro pelle, Apocal.6.8. per auxesin, pro ingentibus periculis, 2.Cor.1.10.& pro praesentibus mortis periculis, 1 Cor.15.31.2.Corin.1.9.& 11.23.mors, peccati finis, Rom.6.21, mors peccati stipendia, v.23.mors certa & mortis dies omnibus hominibus constitutus, Deut.31.14.1.Sam.26.10.Iob.14.5.Psalm.89.49. Eccles.3.2.& 8.8.& 9.5.Eccles.17.3.& 41.1.Icann.7.30.& 8.20. Rom.5.12.& 6.23. Hebr.9.27.mortis hora incertissima, Eccles.9.12. Matth.24.43.Luc.12.40.1.Thess.5.2.2. Thess.2.2. Iac.4.13.14. mors per Christum destructa, 2. Tim.1.10.1.Pet.3.22.mors prorsus delenda est, 1. Cor.15.v.26.54.Apoc.20.14.mors aeterna impiis apparata, 2.Thess.1.9.Mors duplex: prima corporum, secunda animorum, Apoc.20.14.mors secunda, 2.11.& 21.8. mors omnibus communis, Rom.5.12.Heb.9.27. mors piis non timenda, Mat. 10.28.Ioan.12.25.2.Ro.14.8.& 8.28.Cor.5.v.12. Phil.1.23.& 2.17.Heb.2.15.2, Pet.1.14. mors piis est quasi somnus & dormitio quaedam, Deut.31.16,2. Sam.7.12.1.Reg.2.10.& 11.v.21,43.& 14.20. Matt.9.24.Ioan.11.11,25.Act.7.60.& 13.36.1 Cor.11.29 1.Thess.4.13. mors quorundam olim praedicta. Exempla: Filij Davidis, 2.Sam.12.14. Filij Ieroboam, 1.Reg 14.12.domus Baasae, 16,3. Ochosiae, 2.Reg.1.16. Hananiae Pseudoprophetae, Ier.2.8.16. Amasiae & eius familiae, Amos 7.17.Petri, Ioan.21.18.2.Pet.1,14.
units.tr: Death, for the natural separation of soul and body, comes from sin, Gen. 2:17 and 3:19; Rom. 5:12 and 6:23; 1 Cor. 15:21; Col. 2:13; 1 Tim. 5:6; Eph. 2:1; James 1:15. For skin, Rev. 6:8. By amplification, for great dangers, 2 Cor. 1:10; and for present dangers of death, 1 Cor. 15:31; 2 Cor. 1:9 and 11:23. Death is the end of sin, Rom. 6:21; the wages of sin is death, v. 23. Death is certain and the day of death is appointed for all men, Deut. 31:14; 1 Sam. 26:10; Job 14:5; Ps. 89:48; Eccles. 3:2; 8:8; 9:5; Ecclus. 17:3 and 41:1; John 7:30 and 8:20; Rom. 5:12 and 6:23; Heb. 9:27. The hour of death is most uncertain, Eccles. 9:12; Matt. 24:43; Luke 12:40; 1 Thess. 5:2; 2 Thess. 2:2; James 4:13–14. Death has been destroyed through Christ, 2 Tim. 1:10; 1 Pet. 3:22. Death must utterly be destroyed, 1 Cor. 15:26, 54; Rev. 20:14. Eternal death is prepared for the impious, 2 Thess. 1:9. Death is twofold: the first of bodies, the second of souls, Rev. 20:14; the second death, Rev. 2:11 and 21:8. Death is common to all, Rom. 5:12; Heb. 9:27. Death is not to be feared by the godly, Matt. 10:28; John 12:25; Rom. 14:8; 8:28; 2 Cor. 5:12; Phil. 1:23 and 2:17; Heb. 2:15; 2 Pet. 1:14. For the godly, death is like a sleep and a kind of slumber, Deut. 31:16; 2 Sam. 7:12; 1 Kings 2:10 and 11:21, 43 and 14:20; Matt. 9:24; John 11:11, 25; Acts 7:60 and 13:36; 1 Cor. 11:30; 1 Thess. 4:13. The deaths of certain persons were foretold in former times. Examples: the sons of David, 2 Sam. 12:14; the sons of Jeroboam, 1 Kings 14:12; the house of Baasha, 16:3; Ahaziah, 2 Kings 1:16; Hananiah the false prophet, Jer. 28:16; Amasiah and his family, Amos 7:17; Peter, John 21:18; 2 Pet. 1:14.

units.la: MORS AETERNA, est ineffabilis & miserrima reproborum conditio divinitus destinata, qua tum anima tum corpus aeternis poenis iustissime addicuntur.
units.tr: DEATH ETERNAL is the ineffable and most miserable condition of the reprobate, decreed by God, in which both soul and body are most justly consigned to eternal punishments.

units.tr: The different kinds of violent death. ¶ Examples of those drowned in water: the ancient world, Gen. 7.21; Matt. 24.37; Luke 17.27; 2 Pet. 2.5. Pharaoh with his army, Exod. 14.28. Those killed by animals: by lions, examples: the disobedient prophet, 1 Kgs. 13.24; the companion of the prophet, 20.36; the men of Babylon, 2 Kgs. 17.25. By serpents, examples: the Israelites, Num. 21.6; 1 Cor. 10.9. By worms, examples: Herod Agrippa, Acts 12.23. By bears, examples: the forty-two boys, 2 Kgs. 2.24. Examples of those killed by deceit and treachery: the Shechemites, Gen. 34.25; Abner, 2 Sam. 3.27; Ishbosheth, 4.6; Amasa, 20.10; Elah, 1 Kgs. 16.10; Sennacherib, 2 Kgs. 19.37; 2 Chron. 32.21; Isa. 37.38; Amon, 2 Kgs. 21.23; 2 Chron. 33.24; Joash, 24.25; Gedaliah, Jer. 41.2. Examples of those destroyed by haemorrhoids: the men of Ashdod, 1 Sam. 5.6. Examples of those consumed by fire: the Sodomites, Gen. 19.24, 25; Nadab and Abihu, Lev. 10.2; the people murmuring, Num. 11.1; a thousand men, Judg. 9.45, 49; Samson's wife, 15.6; Zimri, 1 Kgs. 16.18; two captains of fifty, 2 Kgs. 1.10, 12; the son of Ahaz, 16.3; 2 Chron. 28.3; the sons of Israel, 2 Kgs. 17.17; the son of Manasseh, 21.6; Jer. 29.22; the sons of Sepharvaim, 2 Kgs. 17.31. Of those crushed by stones: the blasphemer, Lev. 24.23; the one gathering wood on the Sabbath, Num. 15.35; Achan taking the devoted thing, Josh. 7.25; Adoram, who was over the king's tribute, 1 Kgs. 12.18; 2 Chron. 10.18; Naboth, 1 Kgs. 21.13; 2 Chron. 24.21; St Stephen, the first martyr, Acts 7.58. See the examples of those stoned. Example of one overwhelmed by the multitude of people: the unbelieving captain, 2 Kgs. 7.17.

units.tr: The shadow of death for deathly and gloomy death, a Hebraism, Matt. 4.16; Luke 1.79. Christ has conquered our death by his death, Isa. 25.8; Hos. 13.14; Rom. 6.9; 1 Cor. 15.54; 2 Tim. 1.10; Heb. 2.14; Acts 2.24. To taste death, for to die, Matt. 16.28; John 8.52; Heb. 2.9. To die a death, see DIE. To kill with death, a Hebrew pleonasm, for to destroy by utter slaughter, Rev. 2.23. The body of death (see BODY of death).

Luc. 9. 6. 2. Corinth. 5. 15. Ephes. 2. 1. mortuis quo sensu dicatur Euangelium praedicatum fuisse, 1 Petr. 4. 6. (Vide EVANGELIVM mortuis, &c.) Mortui non consulendi, Deut. 18. 11. Esaiae. 8. 19. mortui in fide, in Christo obdormiunt, Actor. 7. 60. mortui non lugendi, Philip. 2. 27. 1 Thess. 4. 13. &c. Mortui quatenus lugendi, aut non lugendi, Levit. 19. 28. (Vide MIRACVLA: Et, RESVRRECTIO. Mortui ad vitam reuocari, Vide MIRACVLA. & Lugere.)
units.tr: DEAD, for a brief time and one about to die at once, Gen. 20.3; 2 Kgs. 20.1; Isa. 38.1. The dead, for people who are "psychical" [ψυχικοῖς], as Paul calls them, 1 Cor. 2.14, or for those not yet regenerated, who are strangers to life and are in no way concerned about the doctrine of the Gospel and eternal life; indeed they stubbornly resist it, Matt. 8.22; Luke 9.60; 2 Cor. 5.15; Eph. 2.1. In what sense the Gospel is said to have been preached to the dead, 1 Pet. 4.6. (See GOSPEL to the dead, etc.) The dead are not to be consulted, Deut. 18.11; Isa. 8.19. The dead in faith fall asleep in Christ, Acts 7.60. The dead are not to be mourned, Phil. 2.27; 1 Thess. 4.13, etc. The dead, as to whether they are to be mourned or not, Lev. 19.28; Deut. 14.1; 34.8; 2 Sam. 1.11; 3.32; 10.2; 12.16; 14.2; 18.33; 21.10; Matt. 9.23; Luke 7.13; John 11.13, etc.; Acts 8.2; 9.39; 1 Thess. 4.13. The dead do not praise God as the living do, Ps. 6.5; 30.9; 88.10-11; 115.17; Isa. 38.18. The dead rise again, Matt. 27.53. (See MIRACLES and RESURRECTION. The dead restored to life: see MIRACLES; and MOURN.)

units.la: MORTVORVM Dominus dicitur Deus, Roman. 14. 9 quod negat Christus, Matt. 22. 32. Sed non pugnant hi duo loci inter se: Christus enim ex Sadducaeorum hypothesi negat Dominum esse Deum mortuorum, qui (Sadducaei) mortuos nunquam resurrecturos, nec vnquam exituros dicebant. Paulus autem ex alia hypothesi idem affirmat, quae nimirum hypothesis Christi resurrectione nititur, & hoc modo Deus est & dicitur Deus mortuorum: quoniam corpora ne mortua quidem sunt in nihilum redacta, & suo tempore tandem sunt resurrectura. Mortuorum sepultura. V. SEPVLTVRA. Mortuorum suffragia. Vide PVRGATORIVM & Iob. 14. 21. Eccles. 9. Esa. 63. 16. 2 Reg. 22. 20.
units.tr: The LORD of the dead is called God, Rom. 14.9, which Christ denies, Matt. 22.32. But these two passages do not contradict each other. For Christ, on the hypothesis of the Sadducees, denies that God is God of the dead, since the Sadducees said the dead would never rise nor ever come out of their state. Paul, however, affirms the same from another hypothesis, which rests on the resurrection of Christ; and in this way God is, and is called, God of the dead, since bodies, even when dead, are not reduced to nothing, and will at their appointed time rise again. The burial of the dead: see BURIAL. The suffrages for the dead: see PURGATORY; and Job 14.21; Eccl. 9; Isa. 63.16; 2 Kgs. 22.20.

units.la: MORTICINA caro non comedenda, Deut.14.21.

units.tr: MORTIFICATION, as the wretched condition of the faithful in this life, 2 Corinth.4.10. Mortification prefigured in Baptism, 1 Petr.3.21. Mortification is necessary for the godly. See ABNEGATION, Col.3.5.

Legis litera, carnis minister, ex aliorum tamen hypothesi, & habita corruptionis hominum ratione, non autem lege in scipia, vel ex recto visu considerata, quatenus nimirum ad Christum ducit, & quatenus Paedagogus vocatur ad Christum, Galat.3,24. vocatur item Princeps & Liberator Israel. Actor.7.35.
units.tr: MOSES (that is, drawn out) is born, Exod.2.2; Acts 7.20. The reason for his name, Exod.2.10. Moses is liberally educated, Acts 7.22. He kills an Egyptian, Exod.2.12; Acts 7.24. He marries Zipporah in Sephoram, Exod.2.21. He is sent to Pharaoh, Exod.3.10; Acts 7.34. He sees God in the bush, Exod.3.2. He judges the people, Exod.18.13. He builds an altar, Exod.24.4. Stirred by just anger, he breaks the tablets, Exod.32.19. He pleads for the idolatrous people, v.32. He is God's friend and intimate, Exod.33.11. He hears God speaking in the Tabernacle, Num.7.89. He complains to God about the people's stubbornness, Num.11.11. He desires that all should prophesy, v.29. He is the meekest and most gentle of all men, Num.12.3, and the most faithful servant in God's house, v.7; Heb.3.5. He prays for Miriam, who was leprous, Num.12.13; for the rebellious and seditious people, Num.14.19 and 16.46; and for Aaron, Deut.9.20. He is permitted to see the land but not to enter it, Deut.32.52. He dies, Deut.34.5. He is buried, v.6. What sort of prophet he is, v.10. He speaks of Christ, Luke 24.44; John 5.46; Acts 26.22. He converses with Christ, Matt.17.3; Mark 9.4; Luke 9.30. He is called the accuser of the Jews, John 5.45; the herald of the Gospel, Deut.30.12; Rom.10.5-6; the messenger of the Law, John 1.17; Gal.3.19. The letter of the Law, the minister of the flesh, is so called according to the view of others, and with regard to the corruption of men, but not when the Law is considered in itself or from a right view, namely insofar as it leads to Christ, and insofar as it is called a schoolmaster leading to Christ, Gal.3.24. He is also called the Prince and Deliverer of Israel, Acts 7.35.

units.tr: An adulterous woman is to be avoided, Prov.2.16 (see HARLOT). A woman who seizes a man's private parts is to be punished by cutting off her hand, Deut.25.11-12. A good woman is praised, Prov.11.16; 12.4; 14.1; 18.22; 31.10, 30. A captive woman, Deut.21.11. A woman should take care of the household, Prov.31.15; Titus 2.5. A beautiful woman who has become proud is condemned, Prov.11.22; 14.1. A quarrelsome woman is condemned, Prov.19.13; 21.9; 25.24; 21.19; 27.15. A woman is a weak vessel, to whom honour is to be given, 1 Pet.3.7. A woman must not wear men's clothing, Deut.22.5. A woman openly praises Christ, Luke 11.27. The Samaritan woman recognizes Christ and, having recognized him, proclaims him, John 4.29. A woman taken in adultery is brought to Christ, John 8.3. The beautiful and prudent Abigail, 1 Sam.25.3. A woman suffering from a flow of blood is healed, Matt.9.20. The woman sitting upon the scarlet beast, Rev.17.3. A woman who makes a vow, Num.30.4.

units.la: MVLIERIS poena ob peccatum. Genesis. 3.16. mulieris prudentis consilium, 2 Samuel.20.16.mulieri Christus evangelizat, Ioan. 4. 7. &c. mulieri non dandus primatus, 1. Timoth.2.12, mulierem non tangere, bonum.1. Corint. 7.1, Sed propter fornicationes suam quisque vxorem habeat.v.2.
units.tr: The punishment of woman for sin, Gen.3.16. The counsel of a prudent woman, 2 Sam.20.16. Christ preaches the gospel to a woman, John 4.7 etc. Primacy is not to be given to a woman, 1 Tim.2.12. It is good not to touch a woman, 1 Cor.7.1; but because of fornication, let each man have his own wife, v.2.

units.la: MVLIERES in vrbium expugnatione non necandae, Deut. 20.14. mulieres iure belli captae, quibus conditionibus vxores ducendae, Deuter.21.v.11,13. mulieres prae fame filios comedunt, 2 Reg.6. ver.28.29. mulieres cantant canticum cum Mag cum Maria, Exodi.15.20. cohaeredes sunt gratiae, 1 Petr.3.7. Christo ministrant. (Vide MARIA.) plangunt Adonidem in Templo, Ezec.8.14. Christum, Luc.23.27. Christum fuisse resurrexisse praedicant, Matth.28.v.8.11. mulieres Pseudoprophetissae damnantur, Ezec.13.17. mulieres saluantur per liberorum generationem si maneant in fide &c.1. Tim.2.15.
units.tr: Women are not to be killed when cities are stormed, Deut.20.14. Women taken as spoils of war, and the conditions under which they may be taken as wives, Deut.21.11, 13. Women eat their sons from famine, 2 Kings 6.28-29. Women sing the song with the Magnificat, with Mary, Exod.15.20. Women are fellow heirs of grace, 1 Pet.3.7. They minister to Christ (see MARY). They lament Adonis in the Temple, Ezek.8.14. They weep for Christ, Luke 23.27. They proclaim that Christ has risen, Matt.28.8, 11. Women who are false prophetesses are condemned, Ezek.13.17. Women are saved through bearing children, if they remain in faith, etc., 1 Tim.2.15.

Marc.16.7. Ioan.20.v.17.18.
units.tr: Barren women made fruitful. Examples: Sarah, wife of Abraham, Gen.16.1; 21.1. Rebekah, Gen.25.21. Rachel, Gen.30.1, 22-23. The wife of Manoah, Judg.13.24. Hannah, 1 Sam.1.5, 20. Elizabeth, Luke 1.7, 57. (See EXAMPLES OF BARRENNESS.) Women are subject to their husbands: Gen.3.16; Eph.5.22; Col.3.18; 1 Pet.3.1. Women cannot exercise the public office of teaching, 1 Cor.14.34; 1 Tim.2.11-12. Women must pray with their heads covered, 1 Cor.11.5. Women are the first to announce Christ's resurrection, even to the Apostles themselves, Matt.28.7; Mark 16.7; John 20.17-18.

Cuius filiae sunt imitatrices eius, ibid.
units.tr: The chastity of women is required, 1 Tim.2.9; 3.11. The consolation of women, 1 Tim.2.15; 1 Pet.3.7. The elaborate adornment of women is condemned, Eccl.9.8; Isa.3.16-18 etc.; 1 Tim.2.9 to the end, and 3.11; Eph.5.22; Col.3.18; 1 Pet.3.3. Examples: Tamar, Gen.38.14; Jezebel, 2 Kings 9.30. See ADORNMENT. The modesty of women is commended, 1 Cor.11.13. Good women are few in number, Eccl.7.29. The duty of women, 1 Tim.5.14; Titus 2.3 etc. With what clothing and modesty they ought to conduct themselves in the sacred assembly, 1 Tim.2.9-11; and what their true adornment is, ibid., and 1 Pet.3.3. The manner of rebuking elderly women, 1 Tim.5.2. An example of holy women: Sarah, 1 Pet.3.6. Her daughters are her imitators, ibid.

Exempla: Michol, 1.Sam.18.28. Secundò, Monere de pietate Exempla: Sunamitis, 2.Reg 4.v.9.10. Esther, Esth. 7.v.1.2. &c. Tertiò, illi parere & honorem deferre. Exempla: Sara, iuxta mandatum Abrahæ mariti subticet se esse vxorem Abrahæ, Genes. 12.14 &c. & dominum eum vocat, 1 Petri 3.6. Sunamitis veniam petit à marito eundi ad Elisæum, 2.Reg.4.22.
