Sephora similiter sequitur Moysen, Exodi 4.20. Dauidem exulem in terra Geth, vxores, 1.Sam.27.3. Mulieribus etiam legendum Deuteronomium, Deut.31.11.12.13. mulieribus præ-dicat Paulus, Act.16.13.
units.tr: Examples of covetousness and lust in women: Eve, Gen. 3.6; Sarai, 16.1, 2; Lot's daughters, 19.31, etc.; Rebecca, 24.58; Rachel, 30.1; Dinah, 34.1; Potiphar's wife, 39.11; Achsah, Josh. 15.17, 18, 19; Hannah, 1 Sam. 1.7, 8; the Shunammite, 2 Kings 4.22, 23, 24; Athaliah, 11.13, etc.; Esther, Esth. 9.12, 13; Rhoda, Acts 12.13, 14. The duties of women. First, to embrace their husbands with love. Examples: Michal, 1 Sam. 18.28. Second, to advise them concerning piety. Examples: the Shunammite, 2 Kings 4.9, 10; Esther, Esth. 7.1, 2, etc. Third, to obey them and show them honour. Examples: Sarah, who, at her husband Abraham's command, kept silent that she was Abraham's wife, Gen. 12.14, etc., and called him lord, 1 Pet. 3.6; the Shunammite asked her husband's permission to go to Elisha, 2 Kings 4.22. Fourth, to relieve their husbands' miseries by patience and consolation. Examples: Zipporah, Exod. 4.25; Michal, 1 Sam. 19.11, 12; the wife of Jeroboam consults Ahijah, 1 Kings 14.4; Jezebel, 21.7. Fifth, to follow their husbands wherever they go. Examples: Sarah, Gen. 12.5, 6, and 20.1, 2; Rebecca came from Mesopotamia to Isaac in Canaan, 24.61; Leah and Rachel willingly followed Jacob in flight, 31.14; Zipporah likewise followed Moses, Exod. 4.20; the wives followed David into exile in the land of Gath, 1 Sam. 27.3. Women should also read Deuteronomy, Deut. 31.11, 12, 13; Paul preached to women, Acts 16.13.

units.la: MVLTILOQVIVM vitiosum, Prou.10.19. Matt.6.7. (Vide Loquacitas damnatur.)
units.tr: Talkativeness is sinful, Prov. 10.19; Matt. 6.7. (See: Talkativeness is condemned.)

units.la: MVLTITVDO Dei auxilio non anteponenda, Psalm.3.7.&27. v.1.5.6. Deo non semper melior, & Deo probatior, 1 Reg. 22.6. Matth.7.13. 2.Tim.4.3. 2.Petr.2. v.2.5. Multitudo ob vnius peccatum interdum plectitur. Exempla: Propter peccatum Achan Israelitæ puniuntur, Ios.7.v.1.4. ob peccatum Dauidis septuaginta millia peste pereunt, 2 Sam.24. v.15.17. Baasa, 1 Reg 16.v.11.12 (Vide MAGISTRATVS peccata puniuntur in subditis.)
units.tr: A multitude must not be preferred to the help of God, Ps. 3.7; 27.1, 5, 6. A multitude is not always better, nor more acceptable to God, 1 Kings 22.6; Matt. 7.13; 2 Tim. 4.3; 2 Pet. 2.2, 5. A multitude is sometimes punished on account of one man's sin. Examples: on account of Achan's sin the Israelites are punished, Josh. 7.1, 4; on account of David's sin seventy thousand die by pestilence, 2 Sam. 24.15, 17; Baasha, 1 Kings 16.11, 12. (See: the sins of rulers are punished in their subjects.)

units.la: Multitudo non semper vincit. Exempla, Iabin cum confœderatis regibus à Iosua vincitur, Ios.11.8. Gedeonis exercitus paucus numero, Iudic.7.2. Asæ exercitus, 2 Paral. 14.v.9.10.11.12. Iosaphat oratione ieiunio iuncta, & soli Deo fidens, vincit Moabitas & Ammonitas, 2 Paral. 20.v.21.&c. Syri, 24.24. Ezechias, 32.v.7.8
units.tr: A multitude does not always conquer. Examples: Jabin with his allied kings is conquered by Joshua, Josh. 11.8; Gideon's army is small in number, Judg. 7.2; Asa's army, 2 Chron. 14.9, 10, 11, 12; Jehoshaphat, joining prayer with fasting and trusting in God alone, conquers the Moabites and Ammonites, 2 Chron. 20.21, etc.; the Syrians, 24.24; Hezekiah, 32.7, 8.

units.la: MVLTITVDINIS malorum exempla: Antiquior mun-dus, Gen.7.21. Sodoma, Gomorrha.&c.19 14. Fratres Io-seph, inter quos duo tantùm inuenti sunt, Ruben & Iuda, qui laborarent pro liberando Iosepho, sed præualuerunt mali, Genes.37.ver.22.26. Ismaël filij plures fuerūt, quàm filij Isaaci, Genes.25.13. &c. Israëlitarum ingens fuit nu-merus, sed ex illis tantùm, (qui quidem ex Ægypto e-greßi erant) Iosue & Caleb, in promissam terram Cha-naan sunt ingressi, Num.1.46.& 14.30. Plures fuerunt cum Absalone regnum patris inuadente, quàm cum Dauide, 2 Sam.15.21. Multitudini non semper fidendum, Exo.23.2. 2 Paralip.14.11.& 20.15.& 24 24.& 32.7. Matth. 24.v.5.10. 11.2 Pet.2.2.
units.tr: Examples of the multitude of evils: the old world, Gen. 7.21; Sodom, Gomorrah, etc., 19.14; Joseph's brothers, among whom only two were found, Reuben and Judah, who laboured to free Joseph, but the wicked prevailed, Gen. 37.22, 26; Ishmael had more sons than Isaac, Gen. 25.13, etc.; the number of the Israelites was huge, but of them only Joshua and Caleb entered the promised land of Canaan, Num. 1.46 and 14.30; there were more with Absalom, who invaded his father's kingdom, than with David, 2 Sam. 15.21. One must not always trust in a multitude, Exod. 23.2; 2 Chron. 14.11, and 20.15, and 24.24, and 32.7; Matt. 24.5, 10, 11; 2 Pet. 2.2.

units.la: MVLTI, pro omnibus, Psal.97.1. Dan.12.2.
units.tr: MANY, for all, Ps. 97.1; Dan. 12.2.

units.la: MVNDVS, pro toto humano genere, 1. Ioann. 5.19. pro omni quod spirituali Christi Regno aduersatur, Ioann.14.17.&15.19.&16.20.&17 9. Galat.6.14.&à Lege Dei nos abducit, 1.Ioan.5 4. Secundo, pro vitæ terrenæ conditione, 1.Cor.7.33. Tertio, pro fidelibus, qui mundum incolunt, 2 Cor.5.19.1.Ioan.2.2. Quarto, pro hominibus metonymicè, 2 Pet.1.4. Quinto, pro quibusuis indefinitè, Ioann.18 20. Sic potest accipi & Ioan.3.17. in posteriori versus parte, vt habet versus precedens: hoc est, pro quibusuis creditu-ris, siue ij sint Iudæi, siue Gentiles. Sexto, pro hominibus quales sunt in sese, in malo veluti sepulti, 1 Ioann.2.15. Septimo, pro gentibus per vniuersum mundum dispersis, Roman.11.12. pro vniuersa Ecclesia, 2.Corinth.5.19. Octauo, pro omnibus omnium ætatum, ordinum, locorum, electis, 1 Ioan.2.2. pro omni hominum, cæterarumque rerum splendore, Galat.6.14. Nono, pro iis omnibus, quæ nobis hîc viuentibus vtenda concediuntur, 1 Cor.7.31. pro iis quæ ad vitam in coniugio transigendam necessariò requiruntur, 1.Cor.7.34.
units.tr: WORLD, for the whole human race, 1 John 5.19; for everything that opposes the spiritual kingdom of Christ, John 14.17, and 15.19, and 16.20, and 17.9; Gal. 6.14; and that draws us away from the law of God, 1 John 5.4. Second, for the condition of earthly life, 1 Cor. 7.33. Third, for the faithful who dwell in the world, 2 Cor. 5.19; 1 John 2.2. Fourth, for men, by metonymy, 2 Pet. 1.4. Fifth, for whomever, indefinitely, John 18.20. In this sense John 3.17 may also be understood, in its latter part, as the preceding verse has it: that is, for whoever believes, whether they are Jews or Gentiles. Sixth, for men as they are in themselves, as if buried in evil, 1 John 2.15. Seventh, for the nations scattered throughout the whole world, Rom. 11.12; for the whole Church, 2 Cor. 5.19. Eighth, for all the elect of every age, rank and place, 1 John 2.2; for all the splendour of men and of other things, Gal. 6.14. Ninth, for all those things which are granted us to use while we live here, 1 Cor. 7.31; for those things which are necessarily required for passing life in marriage, 1 Cor. 7.34.

units.la: Breuiùs, præcipua mundi significata sic concipi possunt: Mundus tripliciter potissimùm vsurpatur: Primo, pro rebus ipsis creatis, quibus tota hæc machina visibilis constat, Ioan.1.10.2.Pet.3 6. Secundo, pro vitiosa ea & miserâ conditione, quæ ex peccato hominis contracta, omnibus hisce rebus communiter nunc inhæret, in qua manifestissima ἀταξία inest, summáque rerum perturbatio, 1 Ioan.2.16.& 5 19. Tertio, pro vna quadam parte, eáque nobilissima & præstantissima: nimirum pro hominibus tantùm, iisque primò vel omnibus, Ioan.3.16. Rom.5.12. Secundò, vel solis renatis,1 Ioan.2.2. Tertiò, vel reprobis & infidelibus, Ioan.14.v.17.22 1 Ioan.3.13.
units.tr: More briefly, the chief meanings of the world may be conceived thus: the world is used in three main ways. First, for the created things themselves, of which this whole visible machine consists, John 1.10; 2 Pet. 3.6. Second, for that vicious and wretched condition which, contracted through man's sin, now clings in common to all these things, in which there is most manifest disorder [ἀταξία] and the greatest confusion of things, 1 John 2.16; 5.19. Third, for one particular part, and that the most noble and excellent: namely, for men only, and these either first, or all, John 3.16; Rom. 5.12; secondly, or only the reborn, 1 John 2.2; thirdly, or the reprobate and unbelieving, John 14.17, 22; 1 John 3.13.

units.la: Deinde mundi nomine primò nunc intelligitur ipse locus: secundò, nunc ipsa rerum substantia : tertiò, nunc homines, vt præcipua mundi pars: quartò, nunc eiusdem partis, id est, hominum depravatio & corruptio, Mundus ex nulla præexistente materia conditus est, Hebr. 11.3.
units.tr: Next, by the name "world" is understood, first, the place itself; second, the substance of things; third, men, as the chief part of the world; fourth, the depravity and corruption of that same part, that is, of men. The world was created out of no pre-existing matter, Heb. 11.3.

units.la: Mundus ex aquis emersit, 1 Petri 3.5. agro similis est, Matthæi 13.38. Divinitatis Dei speculum est, Rom.1.20. à Spiritu Sancto arguendus, Ioan. 16.8. Spiritus Sancti minimè capax, Ioann.14.17. Piis contemnendus, 15.18. & 16.33. Romanorum 12.2. Galat.6.14. Coloss.3 v 1.2. Iac.1.10. & 4.4. 1 Ioann.2.15. (Mundus per Christum factus, Vide CHRISTVS Deus.) Mundus piorum præsentia indignus, Heb. 11.38. nequam & malignus, Galat.1.4.1 Ioann.5.19. mundus prisçus diluuio à Deo punitus, 2 Petr.2 5. mundus Deo reconciliatus, 2 Corinth.5.19. à Christo superatus, Ioann. 16.33. Dei cognitione vacuus, v.3. & 17.25. Christum non agnoscit.1 10,& 8.19. Christum odit, & quare, 7.7.
units.tr: The world rose out of the waters, 1 Pet. 3.5. It is like a field, Matt. 13.38. It is a mirror of the divinity of God, Rom. 1.20. It is to be convicted by the Holy Spirit, John 16.8. It is in no way able to receive the Holy Spirit, John 14.17. It is to be despised by the pious, 15.18; 16.33; Rom. 12.2; Gal. 6.14; Col. 3.1, 2; James 1.27; 4.4; 1 John 2.15. (The world made through Christ: see CHRIST, God.) The world is unworthy of the presence of the pious, Heb. 11.38. It is wicked and malignant, Gal. 1.4; 1 John 5.19. The old world was punished by God with the flood, 2 Pet. 2.5. The world was reconciled to God, 2 Cor. 5.19. It was overcome by Christ, John 16.33. It is empty of the knowledge of God, v. 3, and 17.25. It does not acknowledge Christ, 1.10, and 8.19. It hates Christ, and why, 7.7.

units.la: MVNDVS iniquitatis, pro congerie & cumulo quodam omnium scelerum, Iac.3.6.
units.tr: The world of iniquity: a heap and mass of all sins, James 3.6.

units.la: MVNDI amor quàm noxius,2 Timot.4.10. Iac.4.4. 1 Ioannis 2.15. quatenus scilicet cum Dei voluntate non consentit,& eum amorem damnat, qui nos à Deo abducit. Alioquin dicitur Deus ipse mundum infinito quodam amore dilexisse, Ion.3.16. id est, eos, quos ex mundo elegit. Mundi finis, messi confertur, Matth.3.12.& 13.39. mundi opera mala, Ioan.7.7. mundi sapientia,1 Cor.3.19. mundi status corruptioni obnoxius,2 Pet.3.v.7.10. mundi vanitas quanta, Rom.8.20. 1 Cor.7.31. mundi ætas ultima, 1 Cor.10.11.
units.tr: How harmful is the love of the world, 2 Tim. 4.10; James 4.4; 1 John 2.15, namely insofar as it does not agree with the will of God, and condemns that love which draws us away from God. Otherwise it is said that God himself loved the world with an infinite love, John 3.16, that is, those whom he chose out of the world. The end of the world is compared to harvest, Matt. 3.12, and 13.39. The works of the world are evil, John 7.7. The wisdom of the world, 1 Cor. 3.19. The state of the world is liable to corruption, 2 Pet. 3.7, 10. How great is the vanity of the world, Rom. 8.20; 1 Cor. 7.31. The last age of the world, 1 Cor. 10.11.

units.la: MVNDO crucifigi dicitur, qui mundum despicit: & mundus crucifixus dicitur ei, qui mundum vicissim nihili facit, Galat.6.14. mundo renunciandum est, vt Deo seruiamus, Rom.12 2.2. Pet.1.4. 1 Ioan.2.15. Vide VITAE sanctitati studendum. Mundum iudicabunt fideles, Vide IVDICARE. Pro mundo non orat Christus, Ioan.17.9.
units.tr: It is said to be crucified to the world by one who despises the world, and the world is said to be crucified to one who in turn makes nothing of the world, Gal. 6.14. We must renounce the world so that we may serve God, Rom. 12.2; 1 Pet. 1.4; 1 John 2.15. See: the sanctity of life must be pursued. The faithful will judge the world, see JUDGE. Christ does not pray for the world, John 17.9.

units.la: MVNDVS nemo coram Deo, Iob.25.4. mundi corde, Psal. 24 4.& 51.12.& 73.1. Matth.5.8. 1. Pet.1.22.
units.tr: No one in the world is clean before God, Job 25.4; clean of heart, Ps. 24.4; 51.12; 73.1; Matt. 5.8; 1 Pet. 1.22.

units.la: [MVNDVS substantiuè, seu in subiecto consideratus, sequentes acceptiones & significationes habere videtur, quas ad classes captu faciles reuocauimus in gratiam iuuenum studiosorum.
units.tr: WORLD, taken as a noun or considered as a substantive, seems to have the following senses and meanings, which I have grouped into classes for the benefit of studious young people.

units.la: 1. Est igitur Mundus, ingens illa machina, cælum & terram, & omnia quæ in eis continentur, comprehendens.
units.tr: 1. The world is that vast machine which comprises heaven and earth and all that is contained in them.

units.la: 2. Orbis & ambitus terrarum: Terra in qua filij Adæ viuunt ad tempus.
units.tr: 2. The orb and circuit of the lands: the earth in which the sons of Adam live for a time.

units.la: 3. Quicquid extra veri Dei in Christo notitiam & reverentiam homines in mundo, vt pretiosum & sibi conducibile, ambiunt, cupidè retinent, & deflent amissum.
units.tr: 3. Whatever lies outside the knowledge and reverence of the true God in Christ, which men in the world seek out, greedily keep as precious and useful to themselves, and lament when lost.

units.la: 4. Electi Dei, ex genere humano & mundo collecti.
units.tr: 4. The elect of God, gathered out of the human race and the world.

units.la: 5. Homines omnes, tum Iudæi, tum Gentiles, non regenerati.
units.tr: 5. All men, both Jews and Gentiles, who are not regenerate.

units.la: 6. Impij qui ante diluuium vixerunt, vt Apostolus Heb. 11.7. & Petrus, c.2. ep.2. v.5. testantur.
units.tr: 6. The wicked who lived before the Flood, as the Apostle attests in Heb. 11.7, and Peter in 2 Pet. 2.5.
7. The Jewish nation, often in John 7.4, 8.26, 12.19, 14.19, 22, and 18.20.

units.la: 8. Mundi elementa dicuntur Ceremoniæ legales Iudeis traditæ, Gal.4.3. Coloss.2.v.8 20.
units.tr: 8. The elements of the world are said to be the legal ceremonies delivered to the Jews, Gal. 4.3; Col. 2.8, 20.

units.la: 9. Mundus muliebris, Esther 2. v.3. 9. Ezec. 16 7.8. 23.40.
units.tr: 9. A woman's adornment: Esth. 2.3, 9; Ezek. 16.7, 8; 23.40.

units.la: MVNDVS adiectiuè, seu in adiecto consideratus, habet sequentes notationes.
units.tr: WORLD, taken as an adjective, or considered adjectivally, that is CLEAN, has the following senses.

units.la: mundus Deus, Abac.1.13.
units.tr: Clean as an attribute of God: Hab. 1.13.

units.la: Mundus, munda, mundum, artificialiter, & in superlatiuo mundiss. Exo.25.v.11 17 31. & 37.29. Leuitic.24.4.2. Par. 13.11. Dan.7.9. Matth.23 26. & 27.59.
units.tr: Clean, cleanly, artificially clean, and in the superlative most clean: Exod. 25.11, 17, 31; 37.29; Lev. 24.4; 2 Chr. 13.11; Dan. 7.9; Matt. 23.26; 27.59.

units.la: Mundus, supernaturaliter, Iob.15.15. & 25.5. mundus cælesti quadam & plane mystica ratione, Apoc.15.6. & 19. 14. & 21.v.18.21.]
units.tr: Clean supernaturally: Job 15.15; 25.5. Clean in a certain heavenly and quite mystical sense: Rev. 15.6; 19.14; 21.18, 21.

units.la: MVNDITIES interior & exterior commendatur, Matthæ 23.25. 23.25.Luc.11.39.2 Cor.7.1.(V.Gen.17.1. Exod.20.17.Leuit. 19.2.Deut.30.6.Ier.4.4.Isa.1.16.1 Thess.4.3.Heb.12.14.Ioh. 13.9 10. A Deo est, Pf.51 12. per Spiritum S.in Filio, Act.15. 9. 1 Cor.6.11. nos semine sui Verbi per S. S. regenerante, Ioh.15 3.Gal.6.15.1 Pet.1 23.)
units.tr: CLEANNESS, inward and outward, is commended: Matt. 23.25; Luke 11.39; 2 Cor. 7.1 (see Gen. 17.1; Exod. 20.17; Lev. 19.2; Deut. 30.6; Jer. 4.4; Isa. 1.16; 1 Thess. 4.3; Heb. 12.14; John 13.9, 10). It is from God, Ps. 51.12; through the Holy Spirit in the Son, Acts 15.9; 1 Cor. 6.11; the Spirit regenerates us by the seed of his Word, John 15.3; Gal. 6.15; 1 Pet. 1.23.

units.la: MVNVS: Munera accipiunt filij Israel Iudices, & male iudicant,1 Samu.8.3. munera accipiens Giezi, leprosus fit, 2 Reg 5.verfic.21.27. munera accipiens vt occidat innocentem, maledictus, Deuter.27.25. munera non accipit Deus, Deut.10 7. munera non accepit Elisæus à Naaman gentili, quem sanauerat, 2 Regum 5.16. munera non accipienda, Exodi 23.8. Deut.16.19.& 27.25.1 Sam.8.3 & 12.3.1 Reg. 13.7.2.Reg.5 16.Psalm.15.5.Prou.15.27. & 17.23. Eccles.8.3. & 20 10.Esaiæ 1.23.& 5.23.Ezech.13.19.& 22.12.Amos 5.12. Mich.3.11.
units.tr: GIFTS: the judges of the sons of Israel take gifts and judge badly, 1 Sam. 8.3. Gehazi, taking gifts, becomes a leper, 2 Kings 5.21, 27. One who takes gifts to kill the innocent is cursed, Deut. 27.25. God does not take gifts, Deut. 10.17. Elisha did not take gifts from the Gentile Naaman whom he had healed, 2 Kings 5.16. Gifts are not to be accepted: Exod. 23.8; Deut. 16.19; 27.25; 1 Sam. 8.3; 12.3; 1 Kings 13.7; 2 Kings 5.16; Ps. 15.5; Prov. 15.27; 17.23; Eccl. 8.3; 20.10; Isa. 1.23; 5.23; Ezek. 13.19; 22.12; Amos 5.12; Mic. 3.11.

units.la: MVNERVM acceptio periculosa,Gen.14.23.Exodi 23 8.Num. 22.v.7.8 17.Deut.16.19.& 27.25.Iudic.16 5. 1.Sam.8.3 & 12. v.3 4. 2 Sam. 16. 1 Iob.15.34.& 36.18. Psalm.15.5.& 26 10. Prou. 15. 27. & 17.23. & 22.9. Esaiæ 1 23.& 33.15.Mich.3.11. Eccl.4 36.& 7.6.& 20.31. Matt.28.v.12 15. Act.24.v.26 27. Iudæ v.16 Munerum oblationis & exhibitionis exempla: Rex Sodomorum Abrahæ, Gene.14.v.21.22.Iacob Esau fratri, 33.v.9.10.Iosepho,43.11.Israelitæ ad Tabernaculum,Exodi 35.v.20.21 22.Ahud Regi Eglon,Iudic.3.17. Regina Saba Salomoni,1 Reg.10.10.Salomon Reginę Sabæ,v.13.Tohi rex Hemath Dauidi, 2 Samu.8 9. Asa Regi Benadad, 1 Reg.15.18.Rex Babyloniorum Ezechię Regi,2 Reg.20.12. Achaz Regi Assyriorum, 2 Paral.28.21. Magister militiæ Ieremiæ, Ierem.40.5. Nabuchodonosor Danieli,Dan.2. 48.Magi Christo,Matt.2.11.
units.tr: TAKING BRIBES is dangerous: Gen. 14.23; Exod. 23.8; Num. 22.7, 8, 17; Deut. 16.19; 27.25; Judg. 16.5; 1 Sam. 8.3; 12.3, 4; 2 Sam. 16; Job 15.34; 36.18; Ps. 15.5; 26.10; Prov. 15.27; 17.23; 22.9; Isa. 1.23; 33.15; Mic. 3.11; Eccl. 4.36; 7.6; 20.31; Matt. 28.12, 15; Acts 24.26, 27; Jude 16. Examples of offering and presenting gifts: the king of Sodom to Abraham, Gen. 14.21, 22; Jacob to his brother Esau, 33.9, 10; to Joseph, 43.11; the Israelites to the Tabernacle, Exod. 35.20, 21, 22; Ehud to King Eglon, Judg. 3.17; the Queen of Sheba to Solomon, 1 Kings 10.10; Solomon to the Queen of Sheba, v. 13; Toi, king of Hamath, to David, 2 Sam. 8.9; Asa to King Ben-hadad, 1 Kings 15.18; the king of the Babylonians to King Hezekiah, 2 Kings 20.12; Ahaz to the king of Assyria, 2 Chr. 28.21; the captain of the guard to Jeremiah, Jer. 40.5; Nebuchadnezzar to Daniel, Dan. 2.48; the Magi to Christ, Matt. 2.11.

units.la: Munerum recusationis in tempore à piis factæ exempla: Abraham, Genes.14.22. Vir Dei,1 Reg.13.8. Elisæus, 2.Reg.5. v.15.16. Dauid, 2 Sam.22.24. Daniel, Dan.5.17.Petrus,Actor. 8 20. Muneribus multa obtineri. Muneribus inhibitum exempla: Filij Samuelis,1 Sam.8.3.Giezi,7.2.Reg.5.v.20. 21.Custodes sepulcri Christi,Matth.28.12.Felix,Actor.24. 26 27.
units.tr: Examples of gifts refused in time by the pious: Abraham, Gen. 14.22; the man of God, 1 Kings 13.8; Elisha, 2 Kings 5.15, 16; David, 2 Sam. 22.24; Daniel, Dan. 5.17; Peter, Acts 8.20. Many things are obtained by gifts. Examples of those restrained by gifts: the sons of Samuel, 1 Sam. 8.3; Gehazi, 2 Kings 5.20, 21; the guards of Christ's sepulchre, Matt. 28.12; Felix, Acts 24.26, 27.

units.la: VRES aurei Philistinorum, 1 Sam.6,5.
units.tr: EMERODS: the golden emerods of the Philistines, 1 Sam. 6.5.

units.la: VRMVRATIO cauenda, 1 Corint.10.10 Philipp.2.14.1 Pet. 4.9. Murmurationis exempla: Cain, Genes.4.14.Israelitæ, Exod.15.21.& 15.24.& 16.2.& 17.3.Num.11.1. & 13.31.& 14.2. & 16.41.& 20.3,& 21.5.Deut. 1.26.Pharisæi, Matth.9.11.& 12.2. & 15.2. Mar.2.6. Luc.5.30 Mercenarij, Mat.20.11. Discipuli Christi,26 v.8.9. Scribæ & Pharisæi, Mar.2.24. & 7.5. Lucæ 6.2. & 15 2. & 19.7. Iudæi, Ioan 6. v.41.52. Discipuli quidam,v.60. Turba 7.32. Iudas Iscariotes,12.v 4.5. Græci aduersus Hebræos,Act.6.1. Vide IMPATIENTIAE & murmuris exempla.
units.tr: MURMURING is to be avoided: 1 Cor. 10.10; Phil. 2.14; 1 Pet. 4.9. Examples of murmuring: Cain, Gen. 4.14; the Israelites, Exod. 15.21, 24; 16.2; 17.3; Num. 11.1; 13.31; 14.2; 16.41; 20.3; 21.5; Deut. 1.26; the Pharisees, Matt. 9.11; 12.2; 15.2; Mark 2.6; Luke 5.30; the hired workers, Matt. 20.11; the disciples of Christ, Matt. 26.8, 9; the scribes and Pharisees, Mark 2.24; 7.5; Luke 6.2; 15.2; 19.7; the Jews, John 6.41, 52; certain disciples, v. 60; the crowd, 7.32; Judas Iscariot, John 12.4, 5; the Greeks against the Hebrews, Acts 6.1. See the examples under IMPATIENCE and murmuring.

units.la: Murmurationis pœnæ exempla: Israelitæ, Num.11.1. & 14. 36 37. & 16 49. Maria soror Mosis,12.10. Vide IMPATIEN-TIA.
units.tr: Examples of punishments for murmuring: the Israelites, Num. 11.1; 14.36, 37; 16.49; Miriam, sister of Moses, Num. 12.10. See IMPATIENCE.

units.la: MVRVS pro mœniis. Muri Ierichuntis corruunt. V. MIRACVLA. Muri Ierusalem instaurantur, Nehem.3.1.&c. & 12. 27. murus pro præsidio,1 Sam.25 16. Ier.1.18. Murus æneus Ieremias ipse.15.20.
units.tr: WALLS: the walls of Jericho fall; see MIRACLES. The walls of Jerusalem are restored, Neh. 3.1, etc., and 12.27. A wall as a defence: 1 Sam. 25.16; Jer. 1.18. A brazen wall: Jeremiah himself, Jer. 15.20.

units.la: MVSICA instrumenta, vt Ecclesiæ ruditati & pueritiæ convenientia, diuinis olim celebrandis laudibus adhibita, 2 Sam.6.5.1 Paral.15.16.&25.1.2.Paral.5.12.& 29.25.Psalmo 33.2.& 43 4.& 57.9. & 71.22.& 81.3.& 92.4, & 98.5. & 108. 3.& 144.9.& 147.7.& 149.3. & 150. versic.3 4. Musicorum instrumentorum sumta comparatione docetur vsus interpretandi Scripturas,1 Cor.14.7. abusus tollitur, versic. 10.&c.
units.tr: MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS, suited to the immaturity and childhood of the Church, were formerly used in celebrating divine praises: 2 Sam. 6.5; 1 Chr. 15.16; 25.1, 2; 2 Chr. 5.12; 29.25; Ps. 33.2; 43.4; 57.9; 71.22; 81.3; 92.4; 98.5; 108.3; 144.9; 147.7; 149.3; 150.3, 4. By the comparison of musical instruments the use of interpreting Scripture is taught, 1 Cor. 14.7; the abuse is removed, vv. 10 etc.

units.la: MVTARE gloriam Dei quid sit, V.DEI gloriam mutare, Mutatur homo in alium virum à Spiritu Dei,1 Sam.10.6. Mutatio status in Israel prædicitur, Amos 8.10.
units.tr: CHANGING God's glory: what it is; see GOD. A man is changed into another man by the Spirit of God, 1 Sam. 10.6. A change of state in Israel is foretold, Amos 8.10.

units.la: MVTVS Deum authorem habet, Exodi 4.11. Muti extraordinarij exemplum Zacharias, Lucæ 1.22, sanatur v.64.&c. Mutus surdus sanatur, Marci 7.32.&c. Mutus Dæmoniacus sanatur,Matt.9.32. V.MIRACVLA. Mutus Spiritus, pro Spiritu qui mutum reddit eum, quem tenet ab effectu sic dictus:metonymia,Marc.9.v.17.sanatur 25.
units.tr: DUMB: God is the author of dumbness, Exod. 4.11. An example of an extraordinary dumbness: Zechariah, Luke 1.22; he is healed, v. 64, etc. A dumb and deaf man is healed, Mark 7.32, etc. A dumb demoniac is healed, Matt. 9.32; see MIRACLES. "Dumb spirit" is used for the spirit that makes the one it holds dumb, put by metonymy for its effect: Mark 9.17; he is healed, v. 25.

units.la: MVTVVM dandum proximo,Deut.15.8.Mat.5.42. Lucæ 6.35. mutui lex, Exodi 22.14.
units.tr: A LOAN must be given to a neighbour: Deut. 15.8; Matt. 5.42; Luke 6.35. The law of loans: Exod. 22.14.

units.la: MVTVA dilectio commendatur à Christo, Ioan. 15. v.12.17. adhortatio ad eam, 1 Thess.4.9. (Vide CHARITAS, DILECTIO. Mutua fides quid vocetur à Paulo, Vide FIDES mutua.)
units.tr: MUTUAL LOVE is commended by Christ, John 15.12, 17; exhortation to it, 1 Thess. 4.9. (See CHARITY, LOVE. For what Paul calls mutual faith, see FAITH, mutual.)

units.la: Μύαγρος, idolum Græcorum, V.BEELZEBVB.
units.tr: Myagrus [Μύαγρος], an idol of the Greeks; see BEELZEBUB.

units.la: MYRRHA, arbuscula est in Arabia nascens, cuius cortice inciso defluit lacryma etiam myrrha dicta: Eius præcipua virtus est vt mortuorum cadauera incorrupta conseruet. Magi Christo recens nato myrrham offerunt. Matt. 2.11. V.Ioh.19.39.
units.tr: MYRRH is a small shrub growing in Arabia, from whose cut bark flows a tear, also called myrrh. Its chief property is to preserve the bodies of the dead from corruption. The Magi offer myrrh to the newly born Christ, Matt. 2.11. See John 19.39.

units.la: Mysterium: Primò, hoc vocabulo arcana non quæuis, sed sacra & profanis hominibus minimè committenda significabantur, Matth.13.11. Quamobrem etiam Græcis ita sunt vocati sacri symbolici & figurati Christianorum ritus, quos Latini Sacramenta, à solenni (vt docti autumant) iureiurando vocârunt. Secundò, Mysterium fidei, pro Euangelico munere, 1 Timoth.3 9. Tertiò Mysterium pro Euangelio, Vide Evangelivm. Quartò, non tam pro Euangelica doctrina, quàm Gentium vocatione, Roman.16.25. vt explicatur Ephes.3. vers.4.5. Quintò, Mysterium iniquitatis pro Antichristianismo, 2 Thessalon.2.7. mysterij nomen in fronte Meretricis magnæ inscriptum Apoc.17.5. Sextò, mysterium pro arcano. Vide Arcanvm. Mysteria reuelat Deus. Vide Devs. Septimò, Ecclesiæ & Christi coniunctio, mysterium, Eph.5 32. Magnum est pietatis mysterium, Deus conspicuus factus in carne, 1 Timoth.3.16. Octauò, mysterium in malam partem, 1 Cor.14.2.
units.tr: Mystery: First, by this word were meant not any secrets, but sacred things which are not to be entrusted to profane people, Matt. 13.11. For this reason the Greeks also called the sacred, symbolic and figurative rites of the Christians by this name, which the Latins called sacraments, from a solemn oath (as learned men think). Second, the mystery of faith, for the evangelical office, 1 Tim. 3.9. Third, mystery for the Gospel; see GOSPEL. Fourth, not so much for evangelical doctrine as for the calling of the Gentiles, Rom. 16.25, as explained in Eph. 3, vv. 4, 5. Fifth, the mystery of iniquity for Antichristianism, 2 Thess. 2.7; the name of mystery written on the forehead of the great harlot, Rev. 17.5. Sixth, mystery for a secret; see SECRET. God reveals mysteries; see GOD. Seventh, the union of the Church and Christ is a mystery, Eph. 5.32. Great is the mystery of godliness: God made manifest in the flesh, 1 Tim. 3.16. Eighth, mystery in a bad sense, 1 Cor. 14.2.

units.la: N
units.tr: N

units.la: AAMA vxor Solomonis, mater Roboam.
units.tr: AAMA, wife of Solomon and mother of Rehoboam.

units.la: NAAMAN princeps militiæ leprosus, 2 Reg. 5. 1. curatur, v. 14. eius in Deum & ministrum Dei Elisæum gratitudo, v.15.17. (i. iucundus pulcher.)
units.tr: NAAMAN, captain of the army and a leper, is cured, 2 Reg. 5. 1. His gratitude toward God and toward God's minister Elisha, v.14, 15, 17. (i.e. pleasant, beautiful.)

units.la: AAS pater Abigail, 2 Sam.17.25. (i. Augur, vel serpens.)
units.tr: AAS, father of Abigail, 2 Sam. 17.25. (i.e. augur, or serpent.)

units.la: AAS rex Ammonitarum, Iabes Galaad obsidet, 1 Sam.11.1. eius ferocitas, & in Israel odium, v.2. vincitur, v.11. moritur, 2 Sam.10.1. Amicus Dauidis.v.2.
units.tr: AAS, king of the Ammonites, besieges Jabesh Gilead, 1 Sam. 11.1. His ferocity and hatred toward Israel, v.2. He is defeated, v.11, and dies, 2 Sam. 10.1. A friend of David, v.2.

units.la: AASSON V. Nahasson.
units.tr: AASSON: see Nahasson.

units.la: ABAL (id est stultus, 1 Sam.25 26.) vir ditissimus, ibid.v.2. ferox & inhumanus, v. 3. Dauidis seruis victum denegat, v.10 à Deo percussus moritur, v.38.
units.tr: ABAL (that is, foolish, 1 Sam. 25.26), a very wealthy man, ibid. v.2, fierce and inhuman, v.3. He denies food to David's servants, v.10, and is struck down by God and dies, v.38.

units.la: ABAAM idolum. V. Idolorvm catalogus.
units.tr: ABAAM, an idol. See the Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: ABO, Babyloniorum idolum, Esaiæ 46.1. Vide Idolorvm catalogus.
units.tr: ABO, an idol of the Babylonians, Isaiah 46.1. See the Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: ABOTH, vineam suam Regi Achab dare recusat, 1 Reg 21.3. Leuit. 25. 23. &c. ob id suppositio crimine lapidatur, v.13. mors eius vindicata 1 Reg,22.38. (i. Prophetia.) V.cap.21. 19.2.Reg.9.36.
units.tr: ABOTH refuses to give his vineyard to King Ahab, 1 Kings 21.3; Lev. 25.23, etc. On account of this he is stoned on a false charge, v.13. His death is avenged, 1 Kings 22.38. (i.e. prophecy.) See chap. 21.19; 2 Kings 9.36.

units.la: ABVCHODONOZOR potentissimus Rex Babylonis, Ierem. 27.6. invadit Ægyptum.2 Reg.24.7. Ieremiæ 46.2. contra Iudam ascendit,2 Paralip.36.6. Ierusalem obsidionem cingit,2 Reg.25.1. Ierem.39.1. Dan.1.1 iuxta prophetiam, Ierem.25.8.&32.28. servus Dei appellatur, 27.6.&43.10. Ezech.29.v.18.20. erigit auream statuam, Daniel.3. 1 Regno pulsus bestiarum more vivit,4.30.&c. ingens eius superbia dominij amplitudo & crudelitas explicatur, Esaiæ 14. vers.28. Nabucadnezar. i. prophetans eiusmodi angustiam.
units.tr: NEBUCHADNEZZAR, most powerful king of Babylon, Jer. 27.6. He invades Egypt, 2 Kings 24.7; Jer. 46.2. He marches against Judah, 2 Chron. 36.6, and lays siege to Jerusalem, 2 Kings 25.1; Jer. 39.1; Dan. 1.1, in accordance with prophecy, Jer. 25.8 and 32.28. He is called God's servant, Jer. 27.6 and 43.10; Ezek. 29.18, 20. He erects a golden statue, Dan. 3. Driven from his kingdom, he lives like a beast, Dan. 4.30, etc. His great pride, the extent of his dominion and his cruelty are described in Isaiah 14.28. (Nebuchadnezzar, i.e. prophesying such distress.)

units.la: NABVZARDAN, Dux militiæ Regis Babylonis, destruit domum Dei, muros Ierusalem, & populum qui remanserat, transportat cum omnibus vasis Templi in Babylonem, 2. Reg.25.8. Ier.39.v.9.11.&52.12. liberat Ieremiam ex carcere 39.11. (i. prophetans gladium iudicij.)
units.tr: NABUZARADAN, commander of the army of the king of Babylon, destroys the house of God, the walls of Jerusalem, and the people who remained. He carries them to Babylon with all the vessels of the Temple, 2 Kings 25.8; Jer. 39.9, 11; 52.12. He frees Jeremiah from prison, Jer. 39.11. (i.e. prophesying the sword of judgment.)

units.la: NACHOR, avus Abrahæ, Gen.11.v.24.25. (requies lucis.)
units.tr: NACHOR, grandfather of Abraham, Gen. 11.24, 25. (rest of light.)

units.la: NACHOR, Abrahæ frater nascitur, Gen.11.26. Melcha vxorem ducit,v.29.
units.tr: NACHOR, brother of Abraham, is born, Gen. 11.26. He takes Milcah as his wife, v.29.

units.la: NADAB, Aaronis filius, nascitur, Exo.6.23. hic cum fratre Abihu alienum ignem Deo offert, Levit.10.1. igne cœlitus immisso vorantur, vers.2. Num.3.4.&26.61. 1 Paral.24.2. (i. spontaneus.)
units.tr: NADAB, son of Aaron, is born, Ex. 6.23. He, with his brother Abihu, offers strange fire to God, Lev. 10.1. They are consumed by fire sent down from heaven, v.2; Num. 3.4; 26.61; 1 Chron. 24.2. (i.e. voluntary.)

units.la: NADAB Ieroboami filius, Rex Israel constituitur, 1 Reg.14.20. quo tempore regnavit, 15.25. patris impij impia vestigia sequitur, v.26. à Baasa occiditur, v.27.28.
units.tr: NADAB, son of Jeroboam, is set up as king of Israel, 1 Kings 14.20. The length of his reign, 15.25. He follows the ungodly footsteps of his ungodly father, v.26. He is killed by Baasha, v.27, 28.

units.la: NAHASSON filius Aminadab, Princeps & Dux Tribus Iuda, Numer.1.7.&2.3.&7.12. Matth.1.4. Luc.3.32. (i. augurium.)
units.tr: NAHASSON, son of Amminadab, prince and leader of the tribe of Judah, Num. 1.7; 2.3; 7.12; Matt. 1.4; Luke 3.32. (i.e. augury.)

units.la: NAHVM Propheta eius contra Assyrios vaticinium, Nah.1.1. prædicat in Niniuem, 1.2.3. capitibus. (Consolator.)
units.tr: NAHUM, prophet. His prophecy against the Assyrians, Nah. 1.1. He preaches against Nineveh, 1.2, 3 chapters. (Consoler.)

units.la: NAIN vrbs Galileæ, vbi suscitatur filius viduæ, Luc.7.11.
units.tr: NAIN, a town of Galilee, where the son of a widow is raised, Luke 7.11.

units.la: NANAEA idolum. V. IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: NANAEA, an idol. See the Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: NARCISSVS Claudij Libertus, insigne Ecclesiæ Romanæ membrum, Rom.16.11.
units.tr: NARCISSUS, freedman of Claudius, a distinguished member of the Church at Rome, Rom. 16.11.

units.la: NARDVS pro vnguento nardino, Marc.14.3.
units.tr: NARDUS, for nard ointment, Mark 14.3.

units.la: NATALIS sui convivium celebrat Herodes, Marc.6.21.
units.tr: NATALIS: Herod celebrates his birthday feast, Mark 6.21.

units.la: NATHAN filius Dauidis, 2 Sam.5.14. (Donatus.)
units.tr: NATHAN, son of David, 2 Sam. 5.14. (Given.)

units.la: NATHAN Propheta, Dauid, ne Templum ædificet, Deo authore suadet, 2 Sam.7.5. ad Dauidem, vt eum de adulterio & homicidio coarguat, mittitur, 12.v.1.9. Dauidi peccatum agnoscenti veniam à Deo denunciat, v.13, &c.
units.tr: NATHAN, the prophet, on God's authority advises David not to build the Temple, 2 Sam. 7.5. He is sent to David to rebuke him for adultery and murder, 12.1, 9. He announces God's pardon to David, who acknowledges his sin, v.13, etc.

units.la: NATHANAEL Suar filius, Numer.1.8. Tribus Isachar Princeps fuit, 2.5.&10.15. (i. Donum Dei, vel à Deo datus.)
units.tr: NATHANAEL, son of Zuar, Num. 1.8. He was prince of the tribe of Issachar, 2.5; 10.15. (i.e. gift of God, or given by God.)

units.la: NATHANAEL Galilæus, verus Israelita, in quo dolus non est, Ioan.1.47. Christum pro Messia agnoscit, & illi credit v.49 50. videtur à Christo, v.48. manifestat se illi Christus. cap.21.2.
units.tr: NATHANAEL of Galilee, a true Israelite, in whom there is no guile, John 1.47. He acknowledges Christ as the Messiah and believes in him, v.49, 50. He is seen by Christ, v.48, and Christ reveals himself to him, chap. 21.2.

units.la: NATIVITAS Christi, qua ex virgine Maria Bethlemi in lucem edit editus: Luc.2.4 Mat.2.1.2. Eius fines & visus Heb.2. 14.& 8 3 & 2.17.& 4.15.& 1 Ioh.3 5. Rom.8.3.
units.tr: NATIVITY of Christ, who was brought into the light from the Virgin Mary at Bethlehem, Luke 2.4; Matt. 2.1, 2. Its ends and purpose: Heb. 2.14; 8.3; 2.17; 4.15; 1 John 3.5; Rom. 8.3.

units.la: [NATIVITAS Christi hominis spiritualis seu regenerati. Natiuitas hominis naturalis. natiuitas, seu potius ortus animantium & rerum variarum. De his multa occurrunt dicta in scripturis S. ]
units.tr: [The spiritual or regenerate nativity of man. The natural nativity of man; the nativity, or rather the origin, of living creatures and various things. Many statements about these occur in the Holy Scriptures.]

units.la: NATVRA: Primò, pro re ipsa, seu verè, Gal. 4.8. Secundò, pro sensualitate, vt vocant, 2 Petr.2.12. Tertiò, pro ea quæ nascendo nobis comparatur, prærogatiua, Gala.2.15. Quartò, pro qualitate naturaliter essentiæ inhærenti, 2 Pet.1.4. Vocat enim eo loci Petrus naturam, non ipsam σοίαν, sed certas (vt ita loquar) qualitates: quas Dei virtus in nobis efficit, vt hactenus Dei imago fimus, veluti cùm nos coelesti sapientia, boni amore, vitij odio, & veris virtutibus imbuit: vt etiam accipi ferè consueuit naturæ nomen pro naturæ rerum dispositione & efficacitate.
units.tr: NATURE: First, for the thing itself, or truly, Gal. 4.8. Second, for sensuality, as they call it, 2 Pet. 2.12. Third, for that which is acquired for us by birth, a prerogative, Gal. 2.15. Fourth, for a quality inherent in the essence by nature, 2 Pet. 1.4. For Peter there calls nature not the substance itself [οὐσίαν], but certain qualities (so to speak) which the power of God produces in us, so that we may thus be the image of God, when he imbues us with heavenly wisdom, love of good, hatred of vice and true virtues. In the same way the word nature is commonly taken for the disposition and efficacy of the natures of things.

units.la: Sic imago illa fuit hominis, ante lapsum naturæ: & post lapsum contrà, vitiosa omnis illa totius hominis qualitas, quæ Vetus homo dicitur, & caro, cui opponitur, quod Spiritus Dei in nobis efficit, ideóque tum Nouus homo, tum Spiritus vocatur. Pro corruptione per peccatum in naturam inuecta, seu pro natuta non qualis est ab initio creata, sed vt est in Adamo corrupta & ab eo in posteros deriuata, Rom.11.24. Ephes.2.3. Naturæ impuritas, Iob.25.4.
units.tr: Thus that image belonged to man before the fall of nature. After the fall, on the contrary, that whole quality of the whole man is vicious, which is called the Old Man and the flesh, to which the Spirit of God, which he produces in us, is opposed; and therefore the latter is called both the New Man and the Spirit. Nature also means the corruption introduced into nature through sin, or nature not as it was created at the beginning, but as it is corrupted in Adam and derived from him into his posterity, Rom. 11.24; Eph. 2.3. Impurity of nature, Job 25.4.

units.la: NATVS ex Deo, Ioan.1.13.1. Ioan.5.4. peccatum non facit, 3 9.
units.tr: Born of God, John 1.13; 1 John 5.4. Does not commit sin, 1 John 3.9.

units.la: NAVFRAGIVM Pauli, Act.27.59.2. Cor.11.25. Quorumdam circa fidem. 1 Tim.1.19.
units.tr: SHIPWRECK of Paul, Acts 27.59; 2 Cor. 11.25. Of certain men concerning the faith, 1 Tim. 1.19.

units.la: NAVIGIVM cathedra Christi docentis Luc.5.1.&c.
units.tr: BOAT: the chair of Christ teaching, Luke 5.1, etc.

units.la: NAZARETH viculus Galilææ Christum aliquantisper alit, Mat.2.23. Luc.4 16. & ob id Nazarenus vocatur, Mat.2.23. Nazareni Christum spernentes, 13. 54. Marc. 6. 2. Luc. 4. 22. præcipitare eum conantur è supercilio montis, 4 29.
units.tr: NAZARETH, a little village of Galilee, which for a while nourished Christ, Matt. 2.23; Luke 4.16. On this account he is called the Nazarene, Matt. 2.23. The Nazarenes, despising Christ, Matt. 13.54; Mark 6.2; Luke 4.22, try to throw him down from the brow of the mountain, Luke 4.29.

units.la: NAZARAEORVM secta, Act.24.5. Nazaræorum lex, Numer. 6.2. &c. Samson Nazaræus, Iudic.13.5. & Samuel.1.Sam. II. & Christus, qui ex toto genere humano segregatus est, & consecratus Deo, vt nos propter eum consecremur. Ioh.17.19. Ego pro eis sanctifico meipsum, vt sint & ipsi sanctificati per veritatem. Nazaraei autem dicebantur, qui votum ad tempus habebant in Lege: Augustr.
units.tr: SECT of the Nazarenes, Acts 24.5. The law of the Nazarites, Num. 6.2, etc. Samson the Nazarite, Judg. 13.5; and Samuel, 1 Sam. 1.11; and Christ, who was set apart from the whole human race and consecrated to God, so that we might be consecrated because of him, John 17.19: "For their sake I sanctify myself, that they also may be sanctified through the truth." Those were called Nazarites who had a vow for a time under the Law. Augustine.

units.la: NEBO mons, quem Moses conscendere iubetur, ibidem moriturus, post aspectam terram promissam. Deut. 32.49. & 34.1.
units.tr: NEBO, a mountain which Moses is commanded to climb, there to die, after seeing the promised land, Deut. 32.49; 34.1.

units.la: NEBVLA impletur Templum, 1 Reg.8.10. V. Nubes.
units.tr: A CLOUD fills the Temple, 1 Kings 8.10. See Clouds.

units.la: NECESSITAS Es Pauli 2 Cor. 6. 4. Dauidis, 1 Sam.21.1. &c. Sanctorum, Rom. 12 13.
units.tr: NECESSITY: of Paul, 2 Cor. 6.4; of David, 1 Sam. 21.1, etc.; of the saints, Rom. 12.13.

units.la: NECHAO Rex Ægypti, 2 Reg.23.29 2 Par.35.20. & 36.3.
units.tr: NECHO, king of Egypt, 2 Kings 23.29; 2 Chron. 35.20; 36.3.

units.la: NEGARE Christum, Vide ABNEGATIO. Negaturus est & Christus illum, qui ipsum negauerit, Matt. 10.33. Marc.8. 38. Luc.9.26. & 12.9.2 Tim.2.12.
units.tr: To DENY Christ: see DENIAL. Christ also will deny the one who has denied him, Matt. 10.33; Mark 8.38; Luke 9.26; 12.9; 2 Tim. 2.12.

units.la: NEGLIGENTIA: Negligentiae & acediae exempla: Filij Iacob, Gen.42.v.1.2. Israelitae, Num.21.v.4.5. Abner, 1 Sam.26,v. 13.14.15.16. Isboseth, 2 Sam.4.v.5.6. Pontifex & Sacerdotes, 2 Reg.12.7. Ionas, Ion.1.5. Operarij, Matth.20.v.3.6. Fatuae Virgines, 25.5. (V. Pigritia & Acedia.)
units.tr: NEGLIGENCE: Examples of negligence and sloth: the sons of Jacob, Gen. 42.1, 2; the Israelites, Num. 21.4, 5; Abner, 1 Sam. 26.13–16; Ish-bosheth, 2 Sam. 4.5, 6; the High Priest and the priests, 2 Kings 12.7; Jonah, Jon. 1.5; the labourers, Matt. 20.3, 6; the foolish virgins, Matt. 25.5. (See Laziness and Sloth.)

units.la: NEGOTIATIO, Vide EMERE & vendere. Negotiantium exempla: Patriarchae, Gen.34.21. Madianitae, 37.28. Negotiatores Regis Solomonis, 2 Paral.1 v.16.17, alij Negotiatores, Nehem.13.20. Principes Tyri, Esa.23.8. Negotiatores Tarsicienses, &c. Ezech.27.v.12.13. Profanantes. Templum Dei, Matth.21.12. Mar.11.15. Luc.19.45. Ioan.2.14.15. Negotiatores Babylonis, Apoc.18.11.
units.tr: TRADING: see BUYING and selling. Examples of traders: the patriarchs, Gen. 34.21; the Midianites, Gen. 37.28; the merchants of King Solomon, 2 Chron. 1.16, 17; other merchants, Neh. 13.20; the princes of Tyre, Isa. 23.8; the merchants of Tarshish, etc., Ezek. 27.12, 13. Those who profane the Temple of God, Matt. 21.12; Mark 11.15; Luke 19.45; John 2.14, 15. The merchants of Babylon, Rev. 18.11.

units.la: NEHEMIAS (i.consolatio Domini) Hecheliae filius, Neh.1.1. orat pro suo populo, v.5.6. Pincerna est Artaxerxis, v.11. mittitur in Iudaeam ad aedificandum quae erant destructa, 2.9. coram populo verba Legis recitat, 8.4. appellatur Atherfata, v.9.
units.tr: NEHEMIAH (i.e. consolation of the Lord), son of Hachaliah, Neh. 1.1. He prays for his people, v.5, 6. He is cupbearer to Artaxerxes, v.11. He is sent to Judea to rebuild what had been destroyed, 2.9. He reads the words of the Law before the people, 8.4. He is called Athersatha, v.9.

units.la: [NEHVSTAN, idolum. Vide Idolorum Catalogus.]
units.tr: [NEHUSHTAN, an idol. See the Catalogue of Idols.]

units.la: NEMROD, (Vide NIMROD, 1. Auarus dominator.)
units.tr: NIMROD (see NIMROD, 1. A greedy lord.)

units.la: NEMESIS inhumana, siue ἀσορΐα (quam intellexisse videtur Paulus, 2 Tim. 3.3.) est quae de alieno commodo & felicitate cruciatur, aliena autem calamitate & damno delectatur.
units.tr: NEMESIS, inhuman, or unfeeling [ἀστοργία], which Paul seems to have understood (2 Tim. 3.3), is that which is tormented by another's advantage and happiness, and takes pleasure in another's calamity and loss.

units.la: NEMO, pro perpaucis, qui penè nulli videri possunt cum caeteris collati, Ioan.3.32.
units.tr: NO ONE, for very few, who can scarcely be seen when compared with the rest, John 3.32.

units.la: NEMVS plantat Abraham in Berfabee, Gen.21.33.
units.tr: A GROVE: Abraham plants a grove at Beersheba, Gen. 21.33.

units.la: Nephthali, (id est, luctatio, vel luctatio mea est) Iacobi ex Bala (ancilla Rachelis) filius nascitur, Gen.30.v.6.7.8. ratio nominis, ibid. benedicitur.49.21. Deut.33.23. eius filij, Gen.46.24. sors, Ioh.19.32.
units.tr: Naphtali (that is, a wrestling, or my wrestling is) is born to Jacob from Bilhah, Rachel's maidservant, Gen. 30.6–8. The reason for the name, ibid. He is blessed, Gen. 49.21; Deut. 33.23. His sons, Gen. 46.24. Lot, Josh. 19.32.

units.la: [NEQVAM, homo malus, Gen.38.7. Luc.19.22. Malus Spiritus. Matth.13.38. Act.19.v.12.15. Mundus corruptus, Gal. 1.4. Nequitia, Vide MALITIA.]
units.tr: [WICKED: a bad man, Gen. 38.7; Luke 19.22. An evil spirit, Matt. 13.38; Acts 19.12–15. A corrupt world, Gal. 1.4. Wickedness: see MALICE.]

units.la: NEQVITIA damnatur, Rom.1.29. Nequitiæ extremæ exempla. Hostes Dauidis, Psal.35.12. &38.21.
units.tr: WICKEDNESS is condemned, Rom. 1.29. Examples of extreme wickedness. The enemies of David, Ps. 35.12; 38.21.

units.la: NERGEL, idolum Cuthæorum, 2 Reg.17.30. Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: NERGAL, the idol of the Cuthites, 2 Kings 17.30. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: NERI (i. lucerna mea) pater Salathiel in Christi genealogia Luc.3.27.
units.tr: NERI (that is, my lamp), father of Salathiel in Christ's genealogy, Luke 3.27.

units.la: NERO, quem leonem vocat Paulus: 2. Tim.4.17. De cuius misero exitu V. Persecutorum Ecclesiæ, &c.
units.tr: NERO, whom Paul calls a lion, 2 Tim. 4.17. On his wretched end see Persecutors of the Church, etc.

units.la: NERVVM femoris non comedunt Iudæi, Gen.32.32.
units.tr: The Jews do not eat the sinew of the thigh, Gen. 32.32.

units.la: NICANOR, Diaconus eligitur, Act 6.5 (victor.)
units.tr: NICANOR is chosen as deacon, Acts 6.5 (victor).

units.la: NICODEMVS, Iudæorum Princeps, Ioan.3.1, noctu ad IESVM venit, & in ipsis Christianæ religionis fundamentis à Christo instituitur, v.2.3. & 7.5c. eius constantia & magnanimitas,19.39 (victoria populi).
units.tr: NICODEMUS, a ruler of the Jews, came to Jesus by night, John 3.1, and in the very foundations of the Christian religion is instructed by Christ, vv. 2–3 and 7. His steadfastness and magnanimity, 19.39 (victory of the people).

units.la: NICOLAVS Antiochenus Diaconus eligitur, Actor.6.5. (Victoria plebis)
units.tr: NICOLAUS of Antioch is chosen as deacon, Acts 6.5 (victory of the common people).

units.la: NICOLAITAE hæretici, Apoc.2.v.6.15. Vxores communes habuerunt, & vagis libidinibus se polluerunt, tegentes suum scelus praua imitatione Nicolai: Euseb.l.3 cap.29.
units.tr: NICOLAITANS, heretics, Rev. 2.6, 15. They had wives in common and defiled themselves with promiscuous lusts, covering their crime with a perverse imitation of Nicolaus. Eusebius, bk 3, ch. 29.

units.la: NIDVS, pro receptaculo aut mansione quauis: metaphora, Gen.6.14. Iob.29.18. Abd.v.4. de Nido inuento lex, Deut. 22.v.6.7.
units.tr: NEST, used for any receptacle or dwelling, as a metaphor, Gen. 6.14; Job 29.18; Obad. v. 4. The law concerning finding a nest, Deut. 22.6–7.

units.la: NIGER, Propheta Christianus, Act.13.1.
units.tr: NIGER, a Christian prophet, Acts 13.1.

units.la: NIGRA, Ecclesia mysticè ita cognominatur propter afflictionum & tentationum, varium æstum, Cantic.1.5.&5.11.
units.tr: NIGRA: the Church is mystically so named because of the varying heat of afflictions and temptations, Song 1.5; 5.11.

units.la: NILVS Ægypti fluuius, celeberrimus, septem ostijs in mare mediterraneum influens: Esa.23.3.
units.tr: NILE, the river of Egypt, most famous, flowing into the Mediterranean through seven mouths, Isa. 23.3.

units.la: NIMROD, filius Chus, Gen.10.8. potens & robustus venator, v.8.9. eius Regni principium Babylon, v.10. quod autem additur in textu, fuisse robustissimum venatorem coram Iehoua, per Hebraismum, significatur eo singularis quædam eius præstantia. Sic & de Ioanne dicitur, Luc.1.15. Vide DORAM Deo.
units.tr: NIMROD, son of Cush, Gen. 10.8, a mighty and strong hunter, vv. 8–9. The beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, v. 10. What is added in the text, that he was a very strong hunter before the LORD, signifies by a Hebraism a certain singular excellence of his. So also it is said of John, Luke 1.15. See DORAM Deo.

units.la: NINIVE ab Assur extructa, Gen.10.11. nuncupatur ciuitas magna, ver.12. & ciuitas sanguinum, Nah.3.1. malitia vrbis Niniue, Ion. 1.2. poenitentia, 3.5. Matth. 12.41. quantitas, Ionæ.3.3. ruina prædicitur v.4. Nah.1.1. & 2.1. & 3.1. &c. Soph.2.13. Niniue stabit in iudicio, & condemnabit obcæcatos Iudæos, Mat.12.41. (1. pulchra, seu habitata.)
units.tr: NINEVEH, built by Asshur, Gen. 10.11; it is called a great city, v. 12, and a city of bloods, Nah. 3.1. The wickedness of the city of Nineveh, Jonah 1.2; its repentance, 3.5; Matt. 12.41; its size, Jonah 3.3; its ruin is foretold, v. 4; Nah. 1.1; 2.1; 3.1, etc.; Zeph. 2.13. Nineveh will stand in judgment and condemn the blinded Jews, Matt. 12.41. (1. beautiful, or inhabited.)

units.la: NISAN mensis nomen, Esth.3.7. (V.Mensis.
units.tr: NISAN, the name of a month, Esth. 3.7. (See MONTH.)

units.la: NIX, est nubis dissolutio, quæ in guttas quidem propter nimium frigus eam cōstringens eliquari non potest, sed in floccos & densiores quasdam partes à figure compactas, & albicantes, à Deo rumpitur, & in terram decidit Iob.38.22. Pro.26.1. Ignis, grando, nix, ventus turbineus, efficiens verbum eius: Psal.148.8. Fœcundat terram: Isa.55.10. Psal.147.16.
units.tr: SNOW is a dissolution of cloud which, because of excessive cold, binds itself not into drops, which cannot melt, but is broken by God into flakes and denser parts, compacted and whitish, and falls to the earth, Job 38.22; Prov. 26.1. Fire, hail, snow and stormy wind effect his word, Ps. 148.8. It makes the earth fruitful, Isa. 55.10; Ps. 147.16.

units.la: No vide Heliopolis
units.tr: See HELIOPOLIS.

units.la: NOADIA Pseudoprophetissa, Neh.6.14.
units.tr: NOADIAH, a false prophetess, Neh. 6.14.

units.la: NOBE ciuitas, Sacerdotum in terra Beniamin, unde sic dicta, Num.32.42. à Saule deletur, 1 Sam. 22.19. Neboh. 1. Propheta).
units.tr: NOB, a city of priests in the land of Benjamin, so called, Num. 32.42; destroyed by Saul, 1 Sam. 22.19. Neboh, 1 (a prophet).

units.la: NOBILES pauci in Ecclesia Corinthiorum, 1 Cor. 1.26.
units.tr: Few nobles in the Corinthian Church, 1 Cor. 1.26.

units.la: NOBILITATIS ratio vtcunque habenda. Exemplum: Iehu,2. Reg.9.34. V.Iacob.2.1 2.3.4.
units.tr: The consideration of nobility is to be held in whatever way. Example: Jehu, 2 Kings 9.34. See James 2.1–4.

units.la: NOCTVA: eam non comedunt Iudæi, Deut.14.15.
units.tr: The Jews do not eat the night-owl (noctua), Deut. 14.15.

units.la: NOE (id est quietus, vel quiete recreans & consolationem afferens, Gen.5.29.) filius Lamech, nascitur, v.28. nominis ratio, v.29. Deo gratus est, 6.8. iustus & pius, v.9. arcam construere iubetur, v.14. eam fide ædificat, Hebr 11 7. ingreditur illuc, Genes. 7.7. egredi ex ea iubetur, 8.16. integrum annum commoratus est in arca, vt patet ex collatione horum duorum locorum, 7.11. & 8.14. Altare Deo erigit, 8.20. benedicitur à Deo, 9 1. accipit signum fœderis, arcum cœlestem in nubibus, v.8.14. terram colit, vitemque serit, v.20. ebrius à filio deridetur, v.21.22. iustitiæ præco fuit, 2 Petr. 2 5. eius vitæ tempus, Gen.9.28. commendatur, 2. Pet 2.5. Noë tempora, Matt.24.37.
units.tr: NOAH (that is, rest, or one who refreshes with quiet and brings consolation, Gen. 5.29), son of Lamech, is born, v. 28; the reason for the name, v. 29. He is pleasing to God, 6.8; just and pious, v. 9. He is commanded to build an ark, v. 14, and builds it by faith, Heb. 11.7. He goes into it, Gen. 7.7; he is commanded to come out of it, 8.16. He stayed a whole year in the ark, as appears from comparing 7.11 with 8.14. He erects an altar to God, 8.20; is blessed by God, 9.1; receives the sign of the covenant, the rainbow in the clouds, vv. 8–14; tills the land and plants a vine, v. 20; is mocked by his son when drunk, vv. 21–22. He was a herald of righteousness, 2 Pet. 2.5. The length of his life, Gen. 9.28. He is commended, 2 Pet. 2.5. The days of Noah, Matt. 24.37.

units.la: NOEMI vxor Elimelech. Ruth.1.2. nuribus suis piè consulit, v.8. & 2.22. & 3.1 (Naami.1 pulchra, suauis).
units.tr: NAOMI, wife of Elimelech, Ruth 1.2; she advises her daughters-in-law piously, v. 8; 2.22; 3.1. (Naomi: beautiful, sweet.)

units.la: NOLIM vos ignorare, Rom.1.13.1.Cor.10.1.1.Thess.4.13. Hebraica μείωσις pro, velim vos hoc in primis expendere.
units.tr: "I would not have you ignorant," Rom. 1.13; 1 Cor. 10.1; 1 Thess. 4.13. A Hebraic understatement [μείωσις] for "I would have you weigh this especially carefully."

units.la: [NOMEN, sequentibus distinctionibus explicatur.
units.tr: [NAME is explained by the following distinctions.

units.la: 1. Nomen Dei, Iehouæ, seu Domini, 1. quicquid de Dei maiestate cogitari vel enuntiari potest, quingenties occurrit in Scripturis. 2. No-
units.tr: 1. The name of God, Jehovah, or of the Lord: 1. whatever can be thought or said of God's majesty, occurs five hundred times in Scripture. 2. No-

units.la: 3. Nomen Filij Dei, qui patribus olim apparuit & tandem in carne manifestatus est, Gen.32.29. Iudic.13 v. 6.17 18. Psal.72.17.Prou.30.4. Cantic 1.3. Esai.7 14. & 9 5. & 49.1. Ierem.23.6. Zach.6 12. Matt. 1.v.21.23.25. & 7.22. & 10.22.& 12.21.& 28.19. Ioan.1.12. & 14 13.& 16.23.Act.2. 38,&c.læpiss. in N.T.
units.tr: 3. The name of the Son of God, who once appeared to the fathers and at last was manifested in the flesh, Gen. 32.29; Judg. 13.6, 17, 18; Ps. 72.17; Prov. 30.4; Song 1.3; Isa. 7.14; 9.5; 49.1; Jer. 23.6; Zech. 6.12; Matt. 1.21, 23, 25; 7.22; 10.22; 12.21; 28.19; John 1.12; 14.13; 16.23; Acts 2.38, etc.

units.la: 4. Nomen Spiritus S.Matth.28 19.
units.tr: 4. The name of the Holy Spirit, Matt. 28.19.

units.la: 5. Nomen Angeli,Ephes.1.21.Philip.2.9.
units.tr: 5. The name of an angel, Eph. 1.21; Phil. 2.9.

units.la: 6. Nomen Diaboli, Marc.5.9. Apoc.9.11.V. Abaddon.
units.tr: 6. The name of the devil, Mark 5.9; Rev. 9.11. See ABADDON.

units.la: 7. Nomen hominum,vel proprium, vel indefinitum, aut correlatum & vocationes respiciens.
units.tr: 7. The name of men, either proper, or indefinite, or correlative and having regard to their callings.

units.la: 9. Nomen idolorum, Exod.23.13.Deut.18.10.Ios.23.7. 1 Reg.18.v.24.26. Psal.16.4: Ose.2 17. zach.13 2. V.Idolo- lorum Catalog.
units.tr: 9. The name of idols, Exod. 23.13; Deut. 18.10; Josh. 23.7; 1 Kings 18.24, 26; Ps. 16.4; Hos. 2.17; Zech. 13.2. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: 10. Nomen variorum locorum.
units.tr: 10. The name of various places.

units.la: 11. Nomen Mortis,Apoc 6 8.
units.tr: 11. The name of Death, Rev. 6.8.

units.la: 13. Nomen rei vel creatæ & naturalis, vel artificio factæ, Gen.2.11. &c.20. Exod.16 31 & 17 15. & 33.7 1 Reg. 7.21.52.Reg.18 4.
units.tr: 13. The name of a thing or creature, natural, or made by art, Gen. 2.11, etc.; Exod. 16.31; 17.15; 33.7; 1 Kings 7.21, 52; 2 Kings 18.4.

units.la: 14. Nomen Stellæ, Psal.147.4. Esai.40.26. Apoc.8.11.]
units.tr: 14. The name of a star, Ps. 147.4; Isa. 40.26; Rev. 8.11.]

units.la: NOMEN: Nomen pro amplitudine, vel excellentia, sed cum re ipsa coniuncta, Ephes.1.21. Philip. 2 9. Pro dignitate ac præstantia, Hebr. 1.4. pro notitia, Rom. 1. 5. Nomen nouum electis datum, Apoc.2.17. Nomen Domini, (Vide DEI nomen.) Nomen Domini IESV,ex Hebraeorum idiotismo idem declarat quod Dominus Iesus,1 Corin. 1.10. Nomem Christi nominare dicitur,qui colit Christum, & tanquam fidelis ab eo cognominatur, 2 Tim.2.19. Nomine Christi aliquem recipere, est Christi causa excipere,quòd ipsi hunc honorem habeat receptor,Mar.9.37.Nomen pro celebri illa virtute Dei,quam testatur quisquis Deum appellat,Mat.7.22. Nomen Dei auditū vbique,1 Reg.8.42.non assumendum frustra, Exod.20.7. polluitur periurio, Leuit. 19. 12. Nomen Dei, Sum qui sum, Exodi 3. 14. Nomen Dei inuocare sūper aliquem, Numer.6.27. in nomine Domini benedicit Dauid populo,2. Sam.6.18.sic maledicit Elisæus liberis peruersis,2.Reg.2.24.
units.tr: NAME: a name for greatness or excellence, but joined with the thing itself, Eph. 1.21; Phil. 2.9. For dignity and eminence, Heb. 1.4. For knowledge, Rom. 1.5. A new name given to the elect, Rev. 2.17. The name of the Lord (see NAME of God). The name of the Lord Jesus, by a Hebrew idiom, means the same as the Lord Jesus, 1 Cor. 1.10. To name the name of Christ is said of one who worships Christ and, as a faithful man, is named by him, 2 Tim. 2.19. To receive someone in the name of Christ is to receive him for Christ's sake, because the recipient has this honour for him, Mark 9.37. A name is also used for that celebrated power of God which everyone who calls upon God attests, Matt. 7.22. The name of God is heard everywhere, 1 Kings 8.42. It is not to be taken up in vain, Exod. 20.7; it is polluted by perjury, Lev. 19.12. The name of God: "I am who I am," Exod. 3.14. To invoke the name of God upon someone, Num. 6.27. David blesses the people in the name of the Lord, 2 Sam. 6.18; so Elisha curses the perverse boys, 2 Kings 2.24.

units.la: Nomen patris inuocatum super Ephraim & Manassem, Genef. 48. 16. vbi, nomen patris & maiorum vocari super Ephraim & Manassen, est nominari vel vocari nomine patris & maiorum, vt & reliqui Filij Iacob. ¶Frustrà ergò, imò impie ex hoc loco Sanctorum inuocatio à Papistis stabilitur. Similes Phrases extant, Genes.48.16. Deut.28.10. Esajæ.4.1.4. Eldr.4.25. Dan.9 v.18.19. In nomine Domini venire quid sit, Vide VENIRE. Nomen facere, Vide FACERE nomen. In nomen alicuius baptizari quid sit, Vide BAPTIZARI.
units.tr: "The name of the father invoked upon Ephraim and Manasseh," Gen. 48.16, where to have the name of the father and the forefathers called upon Ephraim and Manasseh means to be named or called by the name of the father and the forefathers, as were the rest of the sons of Jacob. ¶ Therefore the invocation of the saints is established by the Papists from this passage in vain, nay, impiously. Similar phrases occur: Gen. 48.16; Deut. 28.10; Isa. 4.1; Eldr. 4.25; Dan. 9.18, 19. For what it is to come in the name of the Lord, see COME. For to make a name, see MAKE NAME. For what it is to be baptized into the name of someone, see BAPTIZED.

units.la: Nominum impositionis exempla: Eua, Gen.3.20. Seth,4.25.Noe,5.29. Ismael,16 11. Sara.17.15.Isaac.v.19.Moab.19.37.Ammon. v.38. Esau.25.25.Iacob.v.26.Ruben.29.32.Simeon.v.33. Levi.ver.34. Iuda.35.Ioseph.30.24.Beniamin,35.18. Manasses.41.51. Ephraim. v.52. Moses, Exodi. 2.10. Gerson & Eliezer, v 22 & 18.ver.3.4. Samuel,1 Sam.1.20. Loruhama, Ose.1.6.Loammi,v.9.Ioannes,Luc.1.v.60.61. 62.IESVS.2.21.
units.tr: Examples of the giving of names: Eve, Gen. 3.20; Seth, 4.25; Noah, 5.29; Ishmael, 16.11; Sarai, 17.15; Isaac, v. 19; Moab, 19.37; Ammon, v. 38; Esau, 25.25; Jacob, v. 26; Reuben, 29.32; Simeon, v. 33; Levi, v. 34; Judah, 35; Joseph, 30.24; Benjamin, 35.18; Manasseh, 41.51; Ephraim, v. 52; Moses, Exod. 2.10; Gershom and Eliezer, Exod. 2.22 and 18.3–4; Samuel, 1 Sam. 1.20; Lo-ruhamah, Hos. 1.6; Lo-ammi, v. 9; John, Luke 1.60–62; Jesus, 2.21.

units.la: NOMINA Filiorum Israel in Sacerdotis pectore insculpta, Exodi. 28.29. nomina blasphemiæ, Apocalypsis 13.1.
units.tr: NAMES of the sons of Israel engraved on the breast of the priest, Exod. 28.29; names of blasphemy, Rev. 13.1.

units.la: NON posse, pro nolle, Marc. 6.5. hoc enim est Dei velle, quod posse, teste Tertuliano. Vide POSSE.
units.tr: NOT able, for unwilling, Mark 6.5; for this is God's willing, which is his being able, as Tertullian attests. See ABLE.

units.la: NOSSE, pro agnoscere, approbare, gratum & sibi coniunctissimum habere, Hebraismus, Psal.1.6. & 37.18.Ioan.10. 14.2. Timot. 2.19. Apocal. 2.24. Non nosse, contrà, pro displicere, non approbare, gratum non habere, repellere, Psal.1.6.& 37.18.&c.Matth.7.23.& 25.12.
units.tr: KNOW, for acknowledge, approve, hold as pleasing and most closely joined: a Hebraism, Ps. 1.6; 37.18; John 10.14; 2 Tim. 2.19; Rev. 2.24. Not to know, on the contrary, means to displease, not approve, not hold as pleasing, to reject: Ps. 1.6; 37.18, etc.; Matt. 7.23; 25.12.

units.la: NOTA vniuersalis, pro signo (vt vocant) indifferentiæ & indefinitæ, 2 Reg.8.9.Rom.12.3.1. Corinth.12.6 Col.1.23. 1 Timoth.2.v.1.4.6. Hebr.13.4.Iac.1 5.1. Ioan.2.2.Nota vniversalis restringenda ad filios Ecclesiæ, Ioann.6.45.vt diserte additur Esa.54.13. id est, ad eos, qui ordinati sunt ad vitam æternam, Act.13.48. Sic restringenda est, Matt. 23.3.vt patet ex Matt 16.6. Sic particula Omnis non complectitur singulos homines, sed omnia Christi membra in vnum corpus conjungit, vt restringitur illa ad solos fideles, Heb.2.9. Iolam Ecclesiam etiam complectitur, Col.1.20. quam alibi Apostolus Mundum simili dicédi genere appellat,2 Cor.5.19. Restringenda item est ad id de quo agitur, vt 1 Cor.8.1, & 10 v.23.33. & 11 2. & 15.28.
units.tr: The UNIVERSAL NOTE (nota universalis) is used for the sign, as they call it, of indifference and indefiniteness: 2 Kings 8.9; Rom. 12.3; 1 Cor. 12.6; Col. 1.23; 1 Tim. 2.1, 4, 6; Heb. 13.4; James 1.5; John 2.2. The universal note must be restricted to the children of the Church, John 6.45, as is expressly added at Isa. 54.13; that is, to those who are ordained to eternal life, Acts 13.48. It is so to be restricted in Matt. 23.3, as appears from Matt. 16.6. So the particle "all" does not embrace single men, but joins all Christ's members into one body, and is restricted in this way to the faithful alone, Heb. 2.9. It also embraces the whole Church, Col. 1.20, which elsewhere the Apostle calls the world by a similar manner of speaking, 2 Cor. 5.19. It is likewise to be restricted to the matter in hand, as in 1 Cor. 8.1; 10.23, 33; 11.2; 15.28.

units.la: Tollit praeterea eadem nota vniuersalis discrimen ordinum & aetatum, 1 Cor.11.4, personarum, Gal.3.26.&c. gentium, Rom.11.32. Col.1.28. (V.omnis).
units.tr: Moreover, this same universal sign removes the distinction of orders and ages (1 Cor. 11.4), of persons (Gal. 3.26, etc.), and of nations (Rom. 11.32; Col. 1.28). (The word is omnis.)

units.la: NOVACYLA non raduntur pili Nazaraeorum, Num.6.5.
units.tr: NEW MOON: the locks of the Nazarites are not shaved (Num. 6.5).

units.la: NOVISSIMA praeuidenda, Deuter.32.29 nouissima tempora, 1.Timoth.4.1.2. Timoth.3.1.2. Petr.3.3. Nouissimi primi, Matth.19.30.&20 16, Marc.10 31. Lucae.13.30,
units.tr: LATTER THINGS to be foreseen: Deut. 32.29, the last times (1 Tim. 4.1, 2; 2 Tim. 3.1, 2; 2 Pet. 3.3). The last will be first: Matt. 19.30; 20.16; Mark 10.31; Luke 13.30.

units.la: NOVITAS vitae ex Hebraeorum idiotismo, pro noua vita, Roman. 6.4. in ea ambulandum est. ibid. Vide REGENERATIO.
units.tr: NEWNESS of life, by a Hebrew idiom, for a new life: Rom. 6.4, "that we should walk in it." See REGENERATION.

units.la: NOVAE linguae pro peregrinis, & quibus nunquam antea vsi essent, qui singulari Spiritus munere repente euadebant earum periti, non autem pro recenter fabricatis, alioquin nullus earum inter homines visus esset, nisi & intelligerentur ab eis, Marc. 16.17. alibi dicuntur aliae & diuersae linguae, Act. 2.4. noua creatura in Christo, Gal. 6.15. nouus homo, Ephes. 4. 24. nouum coelum & noua terra post mundi inuocationem, Esai. 65.17. & 66.22.2. Petr.3.13. Apocal.21.1. nouum Testamentum, Ierem.31.31. Matth,26.28. Mar.14.24. Luc.22.20.1. Corinth.11.24. Heb. 8.8. & 9.15. & 10.16. & 13.20. nouum nihil sub coelo, Eccles.1.10.
units.tr: NEW TONGUES are those of foreigners, and of languages never before used by those who, by the singular gift of the Spirit, suddenly became skilled in them. They are not languages recently invented, for otherwise no one would have been seen speaking them among men, unless they were understood by them (Mark 16.17). Elsewhere they are called other and diverse tongues (Acts 2.4). A new creature in Christ (Gal. 6.15); the new man (Eph. 4.24); a new heaven and a new earth after the invocation of the world (Isa. 65.17; 66.22; 2 Pet. 3.13; Rev. 21.1); the new Testament (Jer. 31.31; Matt. 26.28; Mark 14.24; Luke 22.20; 1 Cor. 11.24; Heb. 8.8; 9.15; 10.16; 13.20). Nothing new under the sun (Eccl. 1.10).

units.la: NOX Dei verbo creata, Genes.1.5. Psalm.104.20. sint tenebrae dies vicissim succedentes; Gen.8.22. Finis Psalm. 104.20. nox pro Dei ignoratione, Rom 13.12.1. Thess.5.5. Nox pro afflictione grauissima, Mich.3.6. (Ioan.9 4. pro tenebris.)
units.tr: NIGHT, created by the word of God (Gen. 1.5; Ps. 104.20); let there be darkness, days succeeding one another in turn (Gen. 8.22; end of Ps. 104.20). Night for ignorance of God (Rom. 13.12; 1 Thess. 5.5). Night for the most grievous affliction (Mic. 3.6). (In John 9.4 it stands for darkness.)

units.la: NVBES, est corpus quoddam vel ex vapore in sublime exhalato & sublato concretum, vel ex aquis illis caelestibus in expansione constitutis condensatum & compactum. Nubium autem aliae steriles sunt & pluuia carent, aliae foecundae, quae pluuiam effundunt Iob. 36 29.30. Iud.v.12. pro.25.14. Iob.38 27.&37.11.
units.tr: CLOUD is a certain body, either condensed from vapour exhaled and lifted up on high, or thickened and compacted from those heavenly waters set in the firmament. Some clouds are barren and lack rain, others are fruitful and pour out rain (Job 36.29, 30; Judg. 5.12; Prov. 25.14; Job 38.27; 37.11).

units.la: NVBES Tabernaculum operit, Exodi. 40. vers.34.35. Num. 9 15. Deus in nube apparet Mosi, Exodi.19.v.9.16.&24. v.15.16. Deus in nube super oraculo apparituros, Leuit. 16.2. nubes rore concrescunt, Proverb. 3.20. nubes in occasu orta, pluuiae signum, Lucae.12.54. in nubis columna apparet Deus Mosi, Deuter.31.15. in nube loquitur Deus Mosi, Exod.33.9. Numer. 11.25.&12.10. nubes discurrunt magnificentia Dei, Deut.33.26. nubis candidæ visio, Apoc.14.14.
units.tr: A CLOUD covers the Tabernacle (Exod. 40.34, 35; Num. 9.15). God appears to Moses in a cloud (Exod. 19.9, 16, 24; 24.15, 16). God will appear in a cloud above the oracle (Lev. 16.2). Clouds gather in dew (Prov. 3.20). A cloud rising in the west is a sign of rain (Luke 12.54). God appears to Moses in a pillar of cloud (Deut. 31.15). God speaks to Moses in a cloud (Exod. 33.9; Num. 11.25; 12.10). Clouds move along in the majesty of God (Deut. 33.26). A vision of a white cloud (Rev. 14.14).

units.la: Nvbunt priores, quæ maiores sunt ætate sorores, Genes.29.26. prohibere ne quis nubat, doctrina est Dæmoniorum, 1. Tim.4.3. nubant qui se continere non possunt, 1 Cor.7.9. in resurrectione neque vxores ducunt, neque nuptum dantur, Matth.22.30.
units.tr: The former will marry, those who are the elder sisters (Gen. 29.26). To forbid anyone to marry is a doctrine of demons (1 Tim. 4.3). Those who cannot contain themselves let them marry (1 Cor. 7.9). In the resurrection they neither take wives nor are given in marriage (Matt. 22.30).

units.la: Nvditas inobedientibus, Deut.28.48. nudus Israel inter hostes, Exodi 32 25. nudi Adam & Eua, Genes.2.25. nudi vestiendi, Esa 58.7. Ezech.18.7. Matth.25.v.36.43. (Nuditas spiritualis, Ierem.2.25. Nahum.3.5. Apocalip.3.18. 2. Cor.5.3.) Nudus vt in terram veni, sic nudus abibo: Iob.1.21.
units.tr: Nakedness is for the disobedient (Deut. 28.48). Israel naked among its enemies (Exod. 32.25). Adam and Eve naked (Gen. 2.25). Clothe the naked (Isa. 58.7; Ezek. 18.7; Matt. 25.36, 43). (Spiritual nakedness: Jer. 2.25; Nah. 3.5; Rev. 3.18; 2 Cor. 5.3.) "Naked I came into the earth, and naked I shall go" (Job 1.21).

units.la: Nvdivs tertius, Vide Heri.
units.tr: NUDIUS TERTIUS: see Heri (the day before yesterday, i.e. three days ago).

units.la: [Nvdvs spirituali quadam ratione, Ezech.16.v.7.22.39.& 23.29. Ose.2.3. Apoc.3.17.& 16.15.]
units.tr: [Naked in a certain spiritual sense: Ezek. 16.7, 22, 39; 23.29; Hos. 2.3; Rev. 3.17; 16.15.]

units.la: Nvmervs septenarius, pro multo, Psalm.119.164. numerus finitus, pro infinito, Genes.31.7. Numer.14.22. numerus ternarius, pro extremo, 2 Corinth.12.8. numerus singularis pro plurali, 1 Timoth.2.15. numerus bestiæ, Apoc.13.18.
units.tr: Number: the number seven stands for many (Ps. 119.164). A finite number stands for the infinite (Gen. 31.7; Num. 14.22). The number three stands for the extreme (2 Cor. 12.8). The singular number stands for the plural (1 Tim. 2.15). The number of the beast (Rev. 13.18).

units.la: Nvnc interdum est particula συλλογιστικὴ, id est, illatiua, Ioan.8.40.& 18.36. 1.Cor.7.14.& 12.v.18.20. interdum σωμα-τικὴ, qua in assumptionibus argumentorum vtimur, & significat idem quod Atqui, Heb.11.16.
units.tr: Now is sometimes an illative particle [συλλογιστικὴ], that is, inferential (John 8.40; 18.36; 1 Cor. 7.14; 12.18, 20). Sometimes it is an assumptive particle [σωματικὴ], which we use in the assumptions of arguments, and it means the same as But (Heb. 11.16).

units.la: Nvntivs fidelis laudatur, Prouerb.25.v.13.26. Nuntio stulto vti ridiculum, 26.6. Nuntij Saulis prophetant, 1 Sam.19.21. Nuntij boni exempla: Rebecca, Gen.24.28 Rachel, 29.12. Fil j Iacob.45 26. Iuda, 46.28. Vxor Manue, Iudic.13.10. Ionatha & Achimaas, 2 Sam.17.21. Nuntius Elisæi, 2 Reg.5.10. Leprosi, 7.10. Nuntius Ezechiæ, 2 Paral.30.6. Mulieres resurrectionem Christi nuntiantes, Matth.28.8. Angelus, Lucæ 2.10. Septuaginta Discipuli, 10.17. Rhode, Act.12.14. Petrus, v.16.&c.
units.tr: A messenger who is faithful is praised (Prov. 25.13; 26.6 is cited in the sense of a foolish messenger being ridiculous to use). Saul's messengers prophesy (1 Sam. 19.21). Examples of good messengers: Rebekah (Gen. 24.28); Rachel (Gen. 29.12); the sons of Jacob (Gen. 45.26); Judah (Gen. 46.28); the wife of Manoah (Judg. 13.10); Jonathan and Ahimaaz (2 Sam. 17.21); Elisha's messenger (2 Kings 5.10); the lepers (2 Kings 7.10); Hezekiah's messengers (2 Chron. 30.6); the women announcing Christ's resurrection (Matt. 28.8); the angel (Luke 2.10); the seventy disciples (Luke 10.17); Rhoda (Acts 12.14); Peter (Acts 12.16, etc.).

units.la: Nuntij mali, tristis, & infelicis exempla: Cham, Genes.9.22. Rebeccæ, 27.42. Iudæ 38.24. Iacobo, 37.32. Iosepho, 48.1. Pharaoni, Exodi 14.5. Regi Ierichuntis, Iof.2.2. Sisaræ, Iudic.4.12. Ioathan, 9.7. Viri de Beniamin, 1 Sam.4.12. Vxori Phinees, v.19. Samueli, 15.12. Item Ionathas, Dauid, 19.2. Sauli, 24.2. vnus de pueris Nabal, 25.14. Amalechita, 2 Sam.1.16. Ioab, 3.23. units.tr: Examples of evil, sad and unhappy messengers: Ham (Gen. 9.22); Rebekah (Gen. 27.42); Judah (Gen. 38.24); to Jacob (Gen. 37.32); to Joseph (Gen. 48.1); to Pharaoh (Exod. 14.5); the king of Jericho (Josh. 2.2); Sisera (Judg. 4.12); Jotham (Judg. 9.7); the men of Benjamin (1 Sam. 4.12); the wife of Phinehas (1 Sam. 4.19); to Samuel (1 Sam. 15.12); likewise Jonathan to David (1 Sam. 19.2); to Saul (1 Sam. 24.2); one of Nabal's servants (1 Sam. 25.14); the Amalekite (2 Sam. 1.16); Joab (2 Sam. 3.23); the sons of Rimmon (2 Sam. 4.8); to David (2 Sam. 10.5; 12.18; 24.13); Hushai (2 Sam. 18.32); Gad (2 Sam. 24.13); to Solomon (1 Kings 2.29; 2.29, 41); Ahab (1 Kings 19.1); the servants of the man of God (2 Kings 6.15); to the king of Assyria (2 Kings 17.26); Eliakim, etc. (2 Kings 18.37); the messengers of Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 20.2); the captives who were left (Neh. 1.3); the eunuchs (Esth. 4.4); Job's messengers (Job 1.14, 15, etc.); Isaiah (Isa. 38.8); the disciples of John (Matt. 14.12); the ruler of the synagogue (Luke 8.49).

units.la: NVPTIAE, pro conuiuio nuptiali, Matth.22.8. pro loco nuptiis celebrandis destinato,25.10. allegoricè, pro vita beata & immortali, ibid. Apoc.19.9. Nuptię celebrantur, Gen. 29.22. Iudic.14.10. Ioan.2.v.1.2.
units.tr: WEDDINGS, for the wedding feast (Matt. 22.8); for the place appointed for celebrating a wedding (Matt. 25.10); allegorically, for the blessed and immortal life (ibid.; Rev. 19.9). Weddings are celebrated (Gen. 29.22; Judg. 14.10; John 2.1, 2).

units.la: Nuptiarum Secundarum exempla: Abraham, Gen.25.1. Abigail, 1 Sam.25.42. Assuerus, Esth.2.17. Nuptiis interfuit Christus, Ioann.2.2. Nuptiarum parabola, Matth.22.11. Nuptialis vestis fides, ibid. ad nuptias Agni vocati, beati, Apoc.19.9. Nuptias benedicendi formula, Gen.24.60. Ruth.4.11.
units.tr: Examples of second marriages: Abraham (Gen. 25.1); Abigail (1 Sam. 25.42); Ahasuerus (Esth. 2.17). Christ was present at a wedding (John 2.2). The parable of the wedding (Matt. 22.11). The wedding garment is faith (ibid.). Called, blessed, to the marriage of the Lamb (Rev. 19.9). Formula for blessing a marriage (Gen. 24.60; Ruth 4.11).

units.la: NVTRIX vt fouet suos liberos, sic Paulus Theßalonicenses, nihil ab eis exigens, 1 Thess.2.7. [Nux mystica, Cantic. 6.7.]
units.tr: A NURSE, as she cherishes her own children, so Paul (dealt with) the Thessalonians, demanding nothing from them (1 Thess. 2.7). [Mystical nut, Song of Songs 6.7.]

units.la: NYCTICORAX: eo non vescuntur Iudæi, Deuter. 14.7.
units.tr: NIGHT HERON: the Jews do not eat it (Deut. 14.7).

units.la: BED, filius Booz ex Ruth, nascitur, Ruth. 4.13. suscipitur à Noemi, ver.16. nomen illi imponunt vicinæ, verf.17. Obed Dauidis auus, v.17.18. (i. seruiens.)
units.tr: Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth, is born (Ruth 4:13). Noemi takes him up (v. 16). The neighbour women give him his name (v. 17). He is grandfather of David (v. 17, 18). (That is, serving.)

units.la: OBED-EDOM Gethæus, Arcam domo excipit, 2 Samu. 6.11. ob id à Deo benedicitur, ibid. & verf. 12. (id est seruiens terræ.)
units.tr: Obed-Edom the Gittite receives the ark into his house (2 Sam. 6:11), and for this reason is blessed by God (ibid., and v. 12). (That is, serving the land.)

units.la: OBEDIENTIA ὑπακοὴ [?], est fidelis & prompta iussus & mandati à magistratu, & ab eo qui præest, facti executio & præstatio à nobis exhibita, quantum in nobis situm est. Eph. 6.1.
units.tr: OBEDIENCE [ὑπακοὴ]: the faithful and prompt carrying out and performance, by us, of what is commanded and ordered by the magistrate and by the one who is set over us, as far as lies in us. Eph. 6:1.

units.la: OBEDIENTIA pro nouitate, 1 Pet.1.2. Obedientia ex fide nascitur, Rom. 1.5. & 16.26. Heb.11.7. Iudæ v.5. obedientia electionis effectus, 1 Petri 1.2. Sacrificiis præstantior est, 1 Sam.15.23. Eccl.4.17. obedientia commendatur, Ierem.35. v.18.19. Rom.16.26. 2. Cor.9.13. & 10.6. Eph.5. v.8.10. Heb. 3.8. & 10.7. Iac.4.7. 1 Petri 1.22. 1 Ioan.2.3. & 4.6. (obedientia potior Deo quàm hominibus debetur. Vide MAGISTRATVS.) Obedientia parentibus debetur, Exod.20.12. Deut.5.16. Leuit.19.3. Ephes.6.1. Col. 3.20. obedientia erga Pastores & reliquos Ecclesiæ Ministros commendatur, Heb.13.17. obedientia dominis carnalib. debita, Eph.6.5. Col.3.22. 1 Pet.2.18. Obedientiæ bona, Gen.26.v.4.5. 1 Reg.9.v.4.5. 2 Paral.7.18.
units.tr: OBEDIENCE for newness (1 Pet. 1:2). Obedience is born of faith (Rom. 1:5; 16:26; Heb. 11:7; Jude v. 5). Obedience is the effect of election (1 Pet. 1:2). Obedience is better than sacrifices (1 Sam. 15:23; Eccl. 4:17). Obedience is commended (Jer. 35:18, 19; Rom. 16:26; 2 Cor. 9:13; 10:6; Eph. 5:8, 10; Heb. 3:8; 10:7; James 4:7; 1 Pet. 1:22; 1 John 2:3; 4:6). (Obedience is owed to God rather than to men. See MAGISTRATE.) Obedience is owed to parents (Exod. 20:12; Deut. 5:16; Lev. 19:3; Eph. 6:1; Col. 3:20). Obedience towards pastors and the other ministers of the Church is commended (Heb. 13:17). Obedience owed to earthly masters (Eph. 6:5; Col. 3:22; 1 Pet. 2:18). Blessings of obedience (Gen. 26:4, 5; 1 Kings 9:4, 5; 2 Chron. 7:18).

units.tr: OBLATION, see SACRIFICE. [Christ's offering, Eph. 5.2; Heb. 10.10, 14, 18. Legal or ceremonial offering, often repeated, in the books of Moses and among the Prophets: Acts 21.26 & 24.17; Heb. 10.5, 8; Mal. 1.11; Rom. 15.16. Ministry, Rom. 15.3.] Offerings of one's own children: Lev. 18.21 & 20.2; Deut. 12.31 & 18.10; Judg. 11.39; 2 Kings 3.27 & 16.3 & 17.17 & 21.6; 2 Chr. 28.3; Ps. 106.37; Isa. 57.5; Jer. 5.31 & 15.5; Ezek. 16.20, 36 & 20.31 & 23.37. An offering must be without blemish or spot: Lev. 1.3 & 3.1 & 22.19; Num. 28.3, 31; Deut. 15.21; Ecclus. 35.14; Ezek. 43; Mal. 1.8, 14. Many offerings pleasing to God were set alight from heaven: Gen. 4.4 & 8.20 & 15.17; Lev. 9.24; Judg. 6.21 & 13.19; 1 Kings 18.38; 1 Chr. 21.26; 2 Chr. 7.1, 2; 1 Macc. 1.22 & 2.10. Daily offerings: Exod. 29.39; Num. 28.3; 1 Esd. 3.2. Feasts of the offerings were celebrated with joy: Gen. 31.46; Exod. 18.12 & 32.6; Num. 25.2; Deut. 12.5 etc. & 27.7; 1 Sam. 1.4 & 9.12 etc. & 16.5; 2 Sam. 15.12; 1 Kings 1.9 & 3.15; 1 Chr. 29.21. Offerings of the impious: Gen. 4.3, 5; 1 Sam. 15.21; Ps. 40.7 & 50.7 etc. & 51.18; Prov. 15.8 & 21.27; Ecclus. 35.15; Isa. 1.10 etc. & 43.23 & 61.8 & 66.3; Jer. 6.20 & 7.20, 21 & 14.12; Hos. 5.6 & 8.13 & 9.4; Amos 5.22; Mic. 6.7; Mal. 1.7, 13; Matt. 9.13 & 12.7; Mark 12.33; Heb. 10.5. ¶ The Papists gather from 2 Macc. 12.13 etc. that there is an offering for the dead. See PURGATORY. OBLIVION of benefits, see BENEFITS. See Isa. 1.1 etc.

units.la: OBLIVISCENDVM non est Dei in diuitiis, Deut.6.21.&c.&8.11. V.Prou.30.8.9. Nec Legis.3.v.1 Iacob.1.25.

units.tr: Israel, forgetting God, is afflicted: Deut. 32.18; Judg. 3.7. Those who forget God will perish: Deut. 9.19, 20.
