Phil.3 15. tum quod omnium verarum virtutum semina sint ipsis a Dei Spiritu insita, quamuis nondum plene adoleuerint, & opponantur rudibus, Phil.3.15. tales ut euadamus enitendum est, Matt.5.48. 1. Corinth.1 19. & 14.20. & 15.1. Ephe1.6.12. phil.3.15. Col.1,28.1 Pet.1.13 [ Perfecta Ecclesia, Canti.6.9. nempe imputatione perfectæ iustitiæ sponsi sui. Col.1 28. Perfecta lex & voluntas Dei, Rom.12.1.2. Iacob.1.25. perfecta Charitas, i.adimplerta, 1.Ioan.2.5. & 4.v.12.17.
units.tr: PERFECT: in faith and the other gifts of regeneration, confirmed, Heb. 5.14. This does not mean those who have now attained full and complete wisdom, but comparatively, those who in comparison with the rest have made progress in knowledge of divine things and have sound and uncorrupted judgment, 1 Cor. 2.6; Phil. 3.15; 2 Tim. 3.17. Christians are called perfect both because they are confirmed and certain in faith and the other gifts of regeneration, and because they strive toward that future perfection, Eph. 4.13; Phil. 3.15; and because the seeds of all true virtues have been implanted in them by God's Spirit, although they have not yet fully grown, and they are set against the raw and untrained, Phil. 3.15. We must strive to become such, Matt. 5.48; 1 Cor. 1.19; 14.20; 15.1; Eph. 1.6, 12; Phil. 3.15; Col. 1.28; 1 Pet. 1.13. [Perfect Church, Song 6.9, namely by the imputation of the perfect righteousness of her bridegroom, Col. 1.28. Perfect law and will of God, Rom. 12.1–2; James 1.25. Perfect love, that is, fulfilled, 1 John 2.5; 4.12, 17.]

units.la: Perfecta plebs i.edocta, bene instructa, Luc.1.17.
units.tr: A perfect people, that is, taught and well instructed, Luke 1.17.

units.la: Perfectus Deus, Pater cælestis, Matth. 5, 48. homo 1 Tim.3.16.17. Iacob.1.4. & 3.2.] Opera Dei perfecta, Deut. 32.4.
units.tr: Perfect is God, the heavenly Father, Matt. 5.48; man, 1 Tim. 3.16–17; James 1.4; 3.2. The works of God are perfect, Deut. 32.4.

units.la: Perfectus, pro eo qualem se hypocrita iactat, Matth.19. 21. verba enim illa Christi non in quo posita sit per se vita æterna declarant, sed huc spectant, ut hypocritam illum falsæ suæ iustitiæ spe deiectum redarguant. Perfectus est, qui est sicut Magister Christus, Luc.6.40. ad perfectionem exhortatio, Genes.17.1. Deuteron.18.13. Matth.5. 48.1 Cor.1.10. & 14.20.2. Corint.13 11. Ephes. 6.13.1. Petr. 1.13.
units.tr: Perfect, in the sense of what a hypocrite boasts of being, Matt. 19.21. For those words of Christ do not declare where eternal life itself is found, but aim at this: that they refute that hypocrite, cast down from his hope in his false righteousness. He is perfect who is like his Master, Christ, Luke 6.40. Exhortation to perfection, Gen. 17.1; Deut. 18.13; Matt. 5.48; 1 Cor. 1.10; 14.20; 2 Cor. 13.11; Eph. 6.13; 1 Pet. 1.13.

units.la: PERICVLVM piis non lethale, Exod.14.13. &c. V. Act.27. 22. &c. Marc.16.18.
units.tr: DANGER that is not deadly for the pious, Exod. 14.13, etc. See Acts 27.22, etc.; Mark 16.18.

units.la: PERIPSEMA omnium, Paulus, 1 Corinth. 4.13. (id est sordes.)
units.tr: The off-scouring of all things, Paul, 1 Cor. 4.13 (that is, filth).

units.la: PERIVRIVM est, quando quis sciens & volens per iuramentum fallit, vel legitimum non seruat. Peierare enim est, vel rem falsam iurare, puta te non esse reum cædis cùm interfeceris: vel rem licitè iuratam non præstare.
units.tr: PERJURY is when someone knowingly and deliberately deceives by an oath, or does not keep a lawful one. For to perjure oneself is either to swear to a false thing, for example that you are not guilty of murder when you have killed someone, or not to perform a thing lawfully sworn.

units.la: V.Iuramentum.
units.tr: See Oath.

units.la: PERIVRIVM: periurium prohibetur, Exod.20.7. Leuit.19.12. Deut.5.11. Matth.5.33. periurij & falsi crimen, Exod.8.v.15. 28. Leuit.5.4.1 Sam.19.6.1 Reg.8.31. Ier.7.9. Zach.5.3. Malach.3.5.1. Mach.6.62. & 7.v.15.18. & 11.53. & 13 ver.16.19. Machab.4.34. & 12.3. Matth.26.72.1 Tim.1.10. periurij poena, Malach.3.5. V.2 Sam.21.1. &c.
units.tr: PERJURY: perjury is forbidden, Exod. 20.7; Lev. 19.12; Deut. 5.11; Matt. 5.33. The crime of perjury and falsehood, Exod. 8.15, 28; Lev. 5.4; 1 Sam. 19.6; 1 Kings 8.31; Jer. 7.9; Zech. 5.3; Mal. 3.5; 1 Macc. 6.62; 7.15, 18; 11.53; 13.16, 19; 4 Macc. 4.34; 12.3; Matt. 26.72; 1 Tim. 1.10. The penalty for perjury, Mal. 3.5. See 2 Sam. 21.1, etc.

units.la: PERSECVTIONES ex Dei ignoratione, Ioann.16.3. à Satana excitantur, 8.44. Apoc.2.9. & 12.v.13 17. persecutionum vtilitas, Actor.8.4. & 11.20. Vide AFFLICTIONVM vtilitas. Persecutionis magnæ exemplum in Ecclesia Ierosolymitana Act.8.1. Persecutiones internæ interdum sunt: Exemplum in Isaac, Genes.21.9. Galat.4.29. Persecutionis piorum exempla: Cain persecutus est Abelem, Genes.4.8. Tyrannus Lothum in captiuitatem abductum, 14.12. Ismael Isaac cum, 21.9. Galat.4.29. Esau Iacobum, Genesis 27.v.42.4. Ægyptij Israelitas, Exod.14.8. Deut.26.6. Saul Dauidem 1 Sam.23.v.14.15.16. & 24.v.1.2.3. &c. 25.1. & 26.v.1.2.&c. Abalon
units.tr: PERSECUTIONS arise from ignorance of God, John 16.3; they are stirred up by Satan, John 8.44; Rev. 2.9; 12.13, 17. The usefulness of persecutions, Acts 8.4; 11.20. See Usefulness of afflictions. An example of great persecution in the Jerusalem church, Acts 8.1. Persecutions are sometimes internal; example in Isaac, Gen. 21.9; Gal. 4.29. Examples of the persecution of the pious: Cain persecuted Abel, Gen. 4.8. A tyrant led Lot away into captivity, Gen. 14.12. Ishmael [persecuted] Isaac, Gen. 21.9; Gal. 4.29. Esau [persecuted] Jacob, Gen. 27.42. The Egyptians [persecuted] the Israelites, Exod. 14.8; Deut. 26.6. Saul [persecuted] David, 1 Sam. 23.14–16; 24.1–3, etc.; 25.1; 26.1–2, etc. Absalom

units.la: Absalom Dauidem,2 Sam.15.14.& 17.21. Iezabel Eliam,1 Reg.16.v.1.2.&c. Achab Michæam,22.verf.26.27. Aman Iudæos,Esth.3.v.8.9.10.
units.tr: persecuted David, 2 Sam. 15.14; 17.21. Jezebel [persecuted] Elijah, 1 Kings 16.1–2, etc. Ahab [persecuted] Micaiah, 22.26–27. Haman [persecuted] the Jews, Esth. 3.8–10.

units.la: Persecutionis piorum verbi diuini Ministrorum & aliorum fidelium insignia exempla extant in Ieremia,quem Sedechias & Principes eius ad mortem deposcunt, & miris modis vexant,ac persequuntur, Ierem. 37.15.& 38.v.4.5.6. Tribus iuuenibus idolum erectum adorare detractantibus, quos Nabuchodonosor & Satrapæ eius persequuntur, Dan. 3.v.16.17.&c. Daniele,Dan.6.16.& 14 30.
units.tr: Remarkable examples of the persecution of the pious ministers of the divine Word and of other faithful people are found in Jeremiah, whom Zedekiah and his princes demand to death and whom they harass and persecute in marvellous ways, Jer. 37.15; 38.4–6. Three young men who refused to worship the erected idol, whom Nebuchadnezzar and his satraps persecute, Dan. 3.16–17, etc. Daniel, Dan. 6.16; 14.30.

units.la: In Christo,quem multiplex excepit & vexauit persecutio:Primùm enim simulac in lucem editur, fit exul,Matth. 2.14.Deinde Satan immediatè eum adoritur, idque insidiis,Matt.4.v.1.2.&c. Tertiò,Sacerdotes summi atque infimi,Scribæ, Pharisæi,eorum Ministri, Seniores populi, ac reliqua turba superiorum exempla secuta, interitum Christo minantur,Matt.12.14.& alibi passim.Quartò, Herodes Galilæę Tetrarcha Baptistæ carnitex,cum suis Ministris tendit Christo insidias,timens aliquam vulgi concitationem,malè sibi de Ioanne conscius,Luc.13.31. Quinto,Iudas Iscariotes,vnus ex duodecim, cum hostibus colludens,& præmia aucupans, tradit in manum carnificum Christum,Matt.26.47.Sexto,Magistratus politicus ex urbe Roma in Iudæam missus,partim Ecclesiæ gubernatoribus gratificans,partim suis commodis metuens, iniquis sententiis & violentia IESVM opprimit,& morti tradit, Matth. 27.v.1.2.&c. Mar. 15.v.1.2.& Luc. 22.66.& 23.1. Ioan.18.v.28.29.&c.Septimo, milites & turba suis dominis studens placere & commoda quædam captans, omnem in eum rabiem exercet,vt historia passionis Christi abundè declarat.
units.tr: In Christ, whom manifold persecution received and afflicted. First, as soon as he is brought into the light he becomes an exile, Matt. 2.14. Second, Satan immediately attacks him, and that by snares, Matt. 4.1–2, etc. Third, the chief priests and the lowest priests, the scribes, the Pharisees, their ministers, the elders of the people and the rest of the crowd, following the example of their superiors, threaten Christ with death, Matt. 12.14, and elsewhere throughout. Fourth, Herod, tetrarch of Galilee, the executioner of the Baptist, together with his ministers lays snares for Christ, fearing some stirring up of the common people and conscious of wrongdoing regarding John, Luke 13.31. Fifth, Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, colluding with the enemies and seeking rewards, hands Christ over into the hands of the executioners, Matt. 26.47. Sixth, the political magistrate sent into Judea from the city of Rome, partly to gratify the governors of the Church and partly fearing for his own advantage, oppresses Jesus with unjust sentences and violence and hands him over to death, Matt. 27.1–2, etc.; Mark 15.1–2; Luke 22.66; 23.1; John 18.28–29, etc. Seventh, soldiers and the crowd, eager to please their masters and seizing some advantage for themselves, vent all their rage upon him, as the history of Christ's passion fully declares.

units.la: Herodes persequitur & necat pueros bimulos, Matth. 2.16 Herodes Agrippa Ioannem Baptistam,14.10. Pharisæi cœcum natum,Ioan.9.v.23.24 Lazarum,12.10.Gubernatores politici & Ecclesiastici primitiuam & nouellam Apostolorum Ecclesiam,Acto.4.3.&c.5.v.18.19.&c.Synagogici falsi testes,& Concilium Stephanum, 6.v.12.13.14. & 7.v.1.2.&c. Persecutio in Ierosolymitana Ecclesia,8.1. Saulus persequitur Christianos,ibid.&c. Iudæi Paulum ad fidem Christi conuersum, 9.23. Herodes Iacobum, 12.v.1.2 Petrum, v.3 4.Iudæi Paulum & Barnabam,13.50. Philippenses Magistratus & totus populus, 16. v. 21.22. Demetrius Paulum, Gaium, Aristarchum, Alexandrum Actor.19.v.24.&c. Denique tota Actorum Apostolicorum historia plena est persecutionibus Pauli. Inter alios autem Pauli persecutores non postremus fuit Nero, qui Leonem appellat, 2 Tim.4.17. Alexander faber ærarius cuius etiam meminit v.14.
units.tr: Herod pursues and kills the boys of two years old, Matt. 2.16. Herod Agrippa (kills) John the Baptist, 14.10. The Pharisees (cast out) the man born blind, John 9.23-24; (they plot against) Lazarus, 12.10. Political and ecclesiastical rulers (persecute) the primitive and newly founded Church of the Apostles, Acts 4.3ff., 5.18-19ff. False witnesses and the Sanhedrin (act against) Stephen, 6.12-14 and 7.1-2ff. Persecution in the Jerusalem Church, 8.1. Saul persecutes the Christians, ibid. ff. The Jews (seek to kill) Paul after his conversion to the faith of Christ, 9.23. Herod (kills) James, 12.1-2, and (imprisons) Peter, 3-4. The Jews (persecute) Paul and Barnabas, 13.50. The magistrates and the whole populace of the Philippians (beat Paul and Silas), 16.21-22. Demetrius (stirs up trouble against) Paul, Gaius, Aristarchus and Alexander, Acts 19.24ff. In short, the whole history of the Acts of the Apostles is full of persecutions of Paul. Among Paul's other persecutors, Nero, whom he calls a lion, 2 Tim. 4.17, was not the least. Alexander the coppersmith, whom he also mentions in v. 14.

units.la: PERSECVTORVM Ecclesiæ Dei & piorum eius civium poenæ exempla:
units.tr: EXAMPLES OF THE PUNISHMENTS OF THE PERSECUTORS OF THE CHURCH OF GOD AND OF HIS PIOUS CITIZENS:

units.la: Pharao, quem decem plagis afflixit Dominus, Exodi 7.19. & 8.1. &c. 9.17. & 10.4. ac tandem submersit in mari cum omni exercitu, 14.28. Achab, 2 Paral. 18.v.33.34. iuxta illud, 1 Regum 21.21.2 Regum 9.7. Iezabel, 9 v.33.36. Aman, Esth.7.10. Sennacherib, 2 Regum 19.v.35.37. Hostes Danielis & sociorum eius, Dan.3 22.& 6.24. Ioacim, Ietem.36 v.29.30.&c. Ammonitæ, 49.v.1.2.&c. Idumæi, v.9.10.17.18.19. Chaldæi, 51.v.20.21. Montis Seir & Idumæorum destructio, quod populum Dei afflixerint, Ezechielis 35.v.3.4.5. Edom, Amos 1.11. Abd.v.18. Aegyptus Toel.3.19. Hostes Ecclesiæ, Soph.3.19. Hostes Davidis, Psal. 57.v.4.7.& 79.v.10.11. Herodes Ascalonita Christum occidere tentans, plurimosque pueros neci tradens, Matth.2. 16. propter tyrannidem graviter punitur a Deo, ut legitur apud Iosephum lib.17.Antiq.Iudaic.cap.7.item lib.1. de Bello Iudaico, cap.21. Herodes Antipas præstantissimum virum, ac peculiarem Messiæ præconem, præter fas & æquum, capite truncans, & ipsi Christo insidias tendens, Matthæi 14.10. in perpetuum exilium Lugdunum in Galliam relegatur, teste eodem Iosepho lib.18.Antiq. cap.9. & Eusebio libro 2. cap. 4. Pontius Pilatus Christum innocentem in gratiam Iudæorum condemnans, & alia multa in Iudæos tyrannice faciens, tandem multis coactus angoribus, manus sibi conscuit, vt Iosephus lib.18.Antiq.capit.5.& Eutropius lib.7. narrant. Herodes Agrippa fratrem Ioannis gladio feriens, iusto Dei iudicio horribili morte periit. Act.12.v.2.22.23. Legatur prolixius illa historia apud Iosephum lib.19.Antiq.c.7. De Neronis quoque exitu, quem Paulus Leonem vocat 2 Tim.4.17. scribit Eutropius lib.8. Senatus sententia constitutum fuisse, vt nudus per publicum ductus, furca collo eius inserta, virgis usque ad mortem caederetur, atque ité e saxo praecipitaretur. Quam sententiam etsi euasit, tamen violentas sibi inferre manus tandem coactus est Domitianus. Domitianus persecutor Ioannis Euangelistæ, non sine sanguine occubuit: nam in cubiculo à suis propriis ministris, conscia etiam vxore Domitia, multis vulneribus trucidatus est. Senatus autem Romanus cadauer eius popularibus Vespillones contumeliosè more gladiatoris efferri iussit, teste Suetonio & Eutropio. Vide Afflictio.
units.tr: Pharaoh, whom the Lord afflicted with ten plagues, Exod. 7.19; 8.1ff.; 9.17; 10.4, and at last drowned in the sea with his whole army, 14.28. Ahab, 2 Chron. 18.33-34, according to that passage, 1 Kings 21.21; 2 Kings 9.7. (Punished) Jezebel, 9.33-36. Haman, Esther 7.10. Sennacherib, 2 Kings 19.35-37. The enemies of Daniel and his companions, Dan. 3.22 and 6.24. Jehoiakim, Jer. 36.29-30ff. The Ammonites, 49.1-2ff. The Edomites, vv. 9-10, 17-19. The Chaldeans, 51.20-21. The destruction of Mount Seir and of the Edomites, because they afflicted the people of God, Ezek. 35.3-5. Edom, Amos 1.11; Obad. v. 18. Egypt, Joel 3.19. The enemies of the Church, Zeph. 3.19. The enemies of David, Ps. 57.4, 7; 79.10-11. Herod the Ascalonite, who tried to kill Christ and handed over very many boys to death, Matt. 2.16, was severely punished by God for his tyranny, as is read in Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, book 17, chapter 7; likewise The Jewish War, book 1, chapter 21. Herod Antipas, who beheaded the most outstanding man, and a special herald of the Messiah, contrary to right and justice, and laid snares for Christ himself, Matt. 14.10, was relegated to perpetual exile in Lyons in Gaul, as the same Josephus testifies, Antiquities book 18, chapter 9, and Eusebius, book 2, chapter 4. Pontius Pilate, who condemned the innocent Christ to please the Jews, and who did many other tyrannical things against the Jews, at last, forced by many distresses, fell upon his own sword, as Josephus, Antiquities book 18, chapter 5, and Eutropius, book 7, relate. Herod Agrippa, who struck the brother of John with the sword, perished by a dreadful death through the just judgment of God, Acts 12.2, 22-23. That story is to be read at greater length in Josephus, Antiquities book 19, chapter 7. Concerning the end of Nero also, whom Paul calls a lion, 2 Tim. 4.17, Eutropius, book 8, writes that by a decree of the Senate it was ordained that he be led naked through the public place, with a forked stick fixed to his neck, be beaten with rods until death, and then be thrown down from the rock. Though he escaped this sentence, Domitian was at last forced to lay violent hands on himself. Domitian, the persecutor of John the Evangelist, did not die without bloodshed: for he was butchered with many wounds in his bedchamber by his own servants, his wife Domitia also being privy to it. The Roman Senate, moreover, ordered his corpse to be carried out by the common undertakers, dragged out in the manner of a gladiator with insult, as Suetonius and Eutropius testify. See Affliction.

units.la: ERSECVTIO nòminatur aqua, Vide AQVA.
units.tr: PERSECUTION is called water. See WATER.

units.la: ERSEVERANTIA in fide, Est beneficium Dei, quo gratiam Christi per Spiritum sanctum sic in electis obsignat, vt in ea, & vera Christi professione, contra omnia aduersa, permaneant, ad gloriam Dei, proximi ædificationem, & animæ salutem.
units.tr: PERSEVERANCE in faith is a benefit of God, by which he seals the grace of Christ in the elect through the Holy Spirit, so that they remain in it and in the true profession of Christ against all adversities, to the glory of God, the edification of their neighbour and the salvation of their souls.

units.la: Causa efficiens, Spiritus S. Ier. 32.40. Timorem meum eis dabo in corde eorum, vt non recedant à me. Adiuuas, oratio. Iudæ v.20.21.22. Materia, Heb.3.14. Col.2.6 2 Tim. 3.14.1 Ioh.2.24 Contra omnia aduersa: Rom.8.38.c. Finalis, salus nostra: &c. Matt.10.22. & 24.13. Contrarium, est Apostasia, & pertinacia in superstitionibus.
units.tr: Efficient cause: the Holy Spirit, Jer. 32.40: "I will put my fear in their hearts, so that they do not depart from me." Helps: prayer, Jude vv. 20-22. Matter: Heb. 3.14; Col. 2.6; 2 Tim. 3.14; 1 John 2.24. Against all adversities: Rom. 8.38ff. Final cause: our salvation, Matt. 10.22 and 24.13. The contrary is apostasy and obstinacy in superstitions.

units.la: Licet Renati interdum grauissimè peccent, tamen eos à gratia Dei & fide, nec omni, nec in perpetuum excidere probatur, Ps.125.1. Iesf.48.4. & 54.10. & 42.1 Matth.12. 20.Matt.7.24.25. & 24.24 Luc.22.23.Ioh.17.15 17.20.Rom. 8.34. Ioh. 6. 39. 37.Rom.11.29.Eph.1.13 14.1 Pet.1.2.3 4.1 Ioh.2.19 & 3.19.Ro.8.16.1 Ioh.3.24.2 Tim.2.12.Gal.2.20.
units.tr: Although the regenerate sometimes sin very grievously, yet it is proved that they do not fall from the grace of God and from faith, neither completely nor for ever: Ps. 125.1; Isa. 48.4; 54.10; 42.1; Matt. 12.20; Matt. 7.24-25; 24.24; Luke 22.32; John 17.15, 20; Rom. 8.34; John 6.39, 37; Rom. 11.29; Eph. 1.13-14; 1 Pet. 1.2-4; 1 John 2.19 and 3.19; Rom. 8.16; 1 John 3.24; 2 Tim. 2.12; Gal. 2.20.

units.la: Perseuerantia cuíque sua certa constare debet, Psal.138. 7.Rom.8 v 38.39.1 Cor.1 9. & 15.58.1 Pet.1.v.3.4.5. & 5.12. 1 Ioan.2.19.Perseuerantia in Sanctis necessaria est, Matth. 10 22. & 24 10.13. Marci 13.13. Luc.22,32. Romanor.2.7.& Coloss.1 23.& 2.5.1 Thess.2.v.3,10. & 3,8.2 Thess.3.13 1 Ti. 2 15.2 Tim.2. v.5.10.& 3.14.Heb.3 v.6.14 & 6.v.11.15. & 10. 23.Iacob.1.4.2 Pet.3.17.2 Ioan 9.Apoc.2.10.
units.tr: Each person's perseverance ought to be constant: Ps. 138.7; Rom. 8.38-39; 1 Cor. 1.9; 15.58; 1 Pet. 1.3-5; 5.12; 1 John 2.19. Perseverance is necessary in the saints: Matt. 10.22; 24.10, 13; Mark 13.13; Luke 22.32; Rom. 2.7; Col. 1.23; 2.5; 1 Thess. 2.3, 10; 3.8; 2 Thess. 3.13; 1 Tim. 2.15; 2 Tim. 2.5, 10; 3.14; Heb. 3.6, 14; 6.11, 15; 10.23; James 1.4; 2 Pet. 3.17; 2 John 9; Rev. 2.10.

units.la: Perseuerantiæ exempla: Dauid.,1 Sam.17.32. Psalm.119. 51.Nehemias cum reducibus à captiuitate, Nehem.4 21. & 6.v.11.15.& 9.10.Mardochæus,Esth.3.2.&5.9.Daniel & socij eius,Dan.3.18.&6.10.Cæcus natus, Ioan.9.v.17.31. Apostoli,Actor.4.13.&5.24.Antiochena Ecclesia,11.23.Iudæi,13.43 paulus,20.23.Rom.8.38. Vide CONSTANTIA. Perseuerantia in precibus commendatur,Lucæ 11.v.5.8 9. & 18.1.&21.19.Rom.12.12.Ephes.6.18.1 Thess.5 17.2 Thess.3.1.Coloss.4 v 2.3.1 Petri 4.7.&5 9.Iudæ v.20. Perseuerantiæ in precibus exempla : Elias, 1 Reg.18.42. Dauid, Psalm.77.3.& 88.vers.2.10.Vidua,Luc.18.3. Cæcus, v.39 Apostoli,Act.1.14.& 2.42. (Vide ORATIO.) Ecclesiæ Act.12.5.
units.tr: Examples of perseverance: David, 1 Sam. 17.32; Psalm 119.51. Nehemiah with those returning from captivity, Neh. 4.21; 6.11, 15; 9.10. Mordecai, Esther 3.2; 5.9. Daniel and his companions, Dan. 3.18; 6.10. The man born blind, John 9.17, 31. The Apostles, Acts 4.13; 5.24. The Church of Antioch, 11.23. The Jews, 13.43. Paul, 20.23; Rom. 8.38. See CONSTANCY. Perseverance in prayer is commended: Luke 11.5-9; 18.1; 21.19; Rom. 12.12; Eph. 6.18; 1 Thess. 5.17; 2 Thess. 3.1; Col. 4.2-3; 1 Pet. 4.7; 5.9; Jude v. 20. Examples of perseverance in prayer: Elijah, 1 Kings 18.42. David, Ps. 77.3; 88.2, 10. The widow, Luke 18.3. The blind man, v. 39. The Apostles, Acts 1.14; 2.42. (See PRAYER.) The Church, Acts 12.5.

units.la: PERSIA, (quæ & Elam vocatur) est regio Asiæ maioris. Ezech.27.10 & 38.5.
units.tr: PERSIA (which is also called Elam) is a region of Asia Minor. Ezek. 27.10; 38.5.

units.la: PERSONA : pro externa hominum specie, sine videlicet quispiam dives, aut pauper, &c. vt ad eius voluntatem flectas: Et pro externis, vt vocant, circumstantiis, quas si quis respiciat, paria de paribus non constituat, ac denique pro toto habitu, Matt.22.16. Marci 12.14. Luc. 20.21. πρόσωπον [?], Latinis superficies terræ, V.Gen.7.4.Exod.10.3.
units.tr: PERSON: for the external appearance of men, that is, whether someone is rich or poor, etc., so that you may bend him to your will; and for external circumstances, as they call them, which if one takes into account, one will not judge equals as equals; and finally for the whole outward bearing: Matt. 22.16; Mark 12.14; Luke 20.21. [prosopon]. In Latin, the surface of the earth; see Gen. 7.4; Exod. 10.3.

units.la: PERSONA Deitatis, est subsistentia totam essentiam diuinam naturâ habens, sed proprietate incommunicabili ab aliis personis distincta. 1.Ioh.5.7.
units.tr: PERSON of the Godhead is a subsistence having the whole divine essence by nature, yet distinguished from the other persons by an incommunicable property. 1 John 5.7.

units.la: personæ in Deo plures, Gen.1.26.&3.22.&11.7. Matth.3.16.17.&28.19.Luc.3.22. ¶ Personarum acceptio illicita nec Deus personam respicit, Leuit.19.15. Deut.1.17.&16.19.1 Sam.16.7.2 Par.19.7. Iob.34.19. Prou.18.5.24.23.&28.21. Sap.6.8. Eccl.35.v.15.16. Esaiæ 11.3. Malac.9. Matt.22.16. Marci 12.14. Lucæ 20.21. Act.10.34. Rom.11. Gal.2.6. Eph.6.9. Col.3.25.1 pet.1.17.Iac.2.v.1.9 (V.ACCEPTIO personarum damnatur:&, DEVS acceptor personarum non est.)
units.tr: There are several persons in God: Gen. 1.26; 3.22; 11.7; Matt. 3.16-17; 28.19; Luke 3.22. ¶ Unlawful acceptance of persons: God does not regard persons, Lev. 19.15; Deut. 1.17; 16.19; 1 Sam. 16.7; 2 Chron. 19.7; Job 34.19; Prov. 18.5; 24.23; 28.21; Wisd. 6.8; Ecclus. 35.15-16; Isa. 11.3; Mal. 1.9; Matt. 22.16; Mark 12.14; Luke 20.21; Acts 10.34; Rom. 2.11; Gal. 2.6; Eph. 6.9; Col. 3.25; 1 Pet. 1.17; James 2.1, 9. (See ACCEPTANCE of persons is condemned, and GOD is not an acceptor of persons.)

units.la: PERTINACIA (αὐθάδεια Tit.1.7.2. Pet.2.10.) est vel priuati animi sententiæ, vel speciali vitæ generis & ab aliis eiusdem vocationis hominibus differentis obstinata ἄλογος defensio atque retentio. Qui tales sunt, proprio sensui (vt loquuntur) addicti sunt, homines sibi plurimum arrogantes & superbi.
units.tr: PERTINACITY (αὐθάδεια [authadeia], Titus 1.7; 2 Pet. 2.10) is either the obstinate and unreasoning defence and retention of a private opinion of the mind, or of a special manner of life that differs from other men of the same calling. Those who are such are given over to their own sense (as they say), men who are very arrogant and proud of themselves.

units.la: [PES, pedes Dei, Exod.24.10.2 Sam.22.10. 1 Par.28.2.Ps.132. Esai.60.13.&66.1. Thren.2.1.&3.34.Ezech.43.7.Nahum 1.3.Abac.3.5.Matt.5.35.Act.7.49. (Vi pedes.)
units.tr: FEET, the feet of God: Exod. 24.10; 2 Sam. 22.10; 1 Chron. 28.2; Ps. 132; Isa. 60.13; 66.1; Lam. 2.1; 3.34; Ezek. 43.7; Nahum 1.3; Hab. 3.5; Matt. 5.35; Acts 7.49. (See Feet.)

units.la: Pedes Christi, quando de scabello pedum eius agitur omnipotentiam significant. Pedes vero eiusdem inter homines versantis, pars sunt veri illius corporis quod pro nobis. Assumsit pedes Christi glorificati, in Apocalypsi praesertim, maiestatis eiusdem sunt indicium. (Matttth.22. 44.Psal.110.1.
units.tr: The feet of Christ, when they are spoken of as his footstool, signify omnipotence. The feet of the same one while he dwelt among men are part of that true body which was given for us. The feet of Christ glorified, especially in the Apocalypse, are an indication of his majesty. (Matt. 22.44; Ps. 110.1.)

units.la: Pedes Angelorum, Esai.62. Ezech.1.7. Apocal.19.10.& 22.8.
units.tr: The feet of angels: Isa. 62; Ezek. 1.7; Rev. 19.10; 22.8.

units.la: Pedes Ecclesiae, Cantic.5.3. Esai. 68.14. Apocal. 3. 9. & 12. 1.
units.tr: The feet of the Church: Song of Songs 5.3; Isa. 68.14; Rev. 3.9; 12.1.

units.la: Pedibus hominis proprie tribuuntur bases & fulcra corporis, quorum frequens in Scripturis mentio.
units.tr: Properly, the bases and supports of the body are attributed to the feet of a man, and these are frequently mentioned in Scripture.

units.la: Pedes, affectus, cogitationes, consilia, opera, & progressus hominum tum piorum, tum impiorum, in hac vita, figurate significant, 1 Sam.2.9. Iob.13.27. Psalm.9.16. & 25. 15. & 119.105. & 121.3. Mar.9.45. Luc.1.79. Rom.16.20. Eph. 6.15. Heb.12.13.
units.tr: The feet, that is, the affections, thoughts, counsels, works and progress of men, both pious and impious, in this life, are figuratively signified: 1 Sam. 2.9; Job 13.27; Ps. 9.16; 25.15; 119.105; 121.3; Mark 9.45; Luke 1.79; Rom. 16.20; Eph. 6.15; Heb. 12.13.

units.la: Pedes, potentia hominis, cui alij subiiciuntur, 2 Sam.22. 39. Psal.47.4. Ier.38.22. Malac.4.3.
units.tr: The feet: the power of a man, to whom others are subjected: 2 Sam. 22.39; Ps. 47.4; Jer. 38.22; Mal. 4.3.

units.la: Pedes, in corpore Reipublicae, vulgus, Esai.1.6. & 7.20.
units.tr: The feet, in the body of the commonwealth: the common people, Isa. 1.6; 7.20.

units.la: Pedes bestiae mysticae, Dan.7.4.19. idolorum Psal. 115.7. quadrupedum, Gen.24.32. Exo.12.9. Esai.32.20. Ezec.32.2. Reptilium, Leuit.11.v.20.21.22.42. Statuae mysticae, Dan. 2.33.&c. Pes fulcrum, praesidium, Iob.29.15.]
units.tr: The feet of the mystical beast: Dan. 7.4, 19; of idols: Ps. 115.7; of quadrupeds: Gen. 24.32; Exod. 12.9; Isa. 32.20; Ezek. 32.2; of reptiles: Lev. 11.20-22, 42; the mystical statue: Dan. 2.33ff.; the foot as support and protection: Job 29.15.

units.la: PESTILENTIA ob Dei contemtum immittitur, Leuitici 26. 25. Deut.28.21. 1 Reg.8.37. pestilentia in Israele ob Dauidis facinus saevit, 2 Sam.24.15 1 Paral.21.14. V.Exod.9.3. Ier.14. 12. & 21.9. & 24.10. Ezech.6.11. Mat.24.7.
units.tr: PESTILENCE is sent on account of contempt for God: Lev. 26:25; Deut. 28:21; 1 Kings 8:37. A pestilence raged in Israel because of David's deed: 2 Sam. 24:15; 1 Chron. 21:14. See Exod. 9:3; Jer. 14:12; Jer. 21:9; Jer. 24:10; Ezek. 6:11; Matt. 24:7.

PETITIONS, or our requests to God, ought to be framed according to his will, as revealed in his word: 1 John 5:14. The petitions and prayers of believers are not in vain: 1 Sam. 7:8; 1 Kings 17:1-2; 2 Kings 1:10; 2 Kings 4:32-33, 35; 2 Kings 19:4, 20; Job 42:8; Ps. 3:5; Ps. 4:2, 4; Ps. 10:17; Ps. 18:7; Ps. 22:25; Ps. 30:3; Ps. 31:30; Ps. 34:5, 18; Ps. 38:16; Ps. 40:2; Ps. 55:17; Ps. 69:34; Ps. 77:2-3; Ps. 79:8; Ps. 80:3; Ps. 86:6; Ps. 91:15; Ps. 99:6; Ps. 102:18; Ps. 118:5; Ps. 120:1; Ps. 138:3; Ps. 141:1; Ps. 145:19; Prov. 15:29; Isa. 30:19; Isa. 37:2, 21; Isa. 38:5; Isa. 49:8; Isa. 58:9; Isa. 65:24; Jer. 29:12; Jer. 33:3; Dan. 2:19; Joel 2:3; Zech. 10:6; Zech. 12:10; Matt. 7:8; Matt. 18:19; Matt. 21:22; Mark 11:24; Luke 18:7; John 9:31; John 14:13-14; John 15:7; John 16:23; Acts 4:31; Acts 7:34; Acts 10:4; Acts 16:25-26; 1 Pet. 3:11; James 1:5; James 5:17-18; 1 John 3:22; 1 John 5:14-15. Examples: Moses, Exod. 17:11-13; Samuel, 1 Sam. 7:8-10; Elijah, 1 Kings 17:1-2; 2 Kings 1:10-11; Ecclus. 48:3; James 5:16-17; Elisha, 2 Kings 4:33; Hezekiah, 2 Kings 19:3-4, etc.; Job, Job 42:8; David, Ps. 3:5; Ps. 4:2; Ps. 10:17; Ps. 18:7; Ps. 22:25; Ps. 30:3; Ps. 31:21; Ps. 34:5; Ps. 40:2; Ps. 77:2; Ps. 86:7; Ps. 118:5; Ps. 120:1; the Israelites, Ps. 99:7; Jonah, Jonah 2:3; Paul and Silas, Acts 16:25-26.

units.la: Petitiones iustæ esse debent. exempla: Samson, Iudic. 15.verf.18.19. Anna,1 Sam.1.ver.10 11.17.Salomon,1 Reg.3. v.10.11.12.Elias,2 Reg.2.v.9.10.Zacharias, Lucæ 1.13.Petitionum iniustarum exempla:Naas,1 Sam.11.2.Adonias, 1 Reg. 2.Filij Zebedæi,Matth.20.21.Marci 10.37. Herodiadis filia,Marci 6.25.Petitiones iniustæ poena, 1 Reg.2.25. Vide Iac.4.3.
units.tr: Petitions ought to be just. Examples: Samson, Judg. 15:18-19; Hannah, 1 Sam. 1:10-11, 17; Solomon, 1 Kings 3:10-12; Elijah, 2 Kings 2:9-10; Zechariah, Luke 1:13. Examples of unjust petitions: Nahash, 1 Sam. 11:2; Adonijah, 1 Kings 2; the sons of Zebedee, Matt. 20:21; Mark 10:37; Herodias' daughter, Mark 6:25. The penalty for unjust petitions: 1 Kings 2:25. See James 4:3.

units.la: [PETRA, Arabiæ Petræ metropolis,2 Reg.14.7.Arx,Iudic.6.20.26. culter lapideus, Exod.4.25. Lapis Iob.8.17.Pf. 137.9.Esai.50.7.Ier.23.29.Ezech.24.7.&c.Matt.27.51. Luc. 8. v.6.13.
units.tr: [PETRA, the metropolis of Arabia Petraea, 2 Kings 14:7. A citadel, Judg. 6:20, 26. A stone knife, Exod. 4:25. Stone, Job 8:17; Ps. 137:9; Isa. 50:7; Jer. 23:29; Ezek. 24:7, etc.; Matt. 27:51; Luke 8:6, 13.]

units.la: Petra,locus tutissimus,protectio Dei,Psalm.27.5.& 40.3.& 61.3.Cantic.2.14 Petra,rupes,Exod.17.6.& 33.21.22 Num. 20.v.8.10.11.Deut.8.15.& 32.13.Matt.7.v.24.25.& 27 60.Apo.6.v.15.16.
units.tr: Petra: a most secure place, the protection of God, Ps. 27:5; Ps. 40:3; Ps. 61:3; Song 2:14. Petra: rock, Exod. 17:6; Exod. 33:21-22; Num. 20:8, 10-11; Deut. 8:15; Deut. 32:13; Matt. 7:24-25; Matt. 27:60; Rev. 6:15-16.

units.la: Petra,Deus,2 Sam.22.2. Psal.18.3.]
units.tr: Petra: God, 2 Sam. 22:2; Ps. 18:3.]

units.la: PETRA Christus, de qua hauserunt fideles Iudæi, 1 Cor.10.4.Petra scandali,1 Petr.2.7. V. CHRISTVS. Super petram Christum fundata est Ecclesia,Mat.16.18. V.FVNDAMEN-TVM:&,ECCLESIA.
units.tr: PETRA: Christ, from whom the faithful Jews drank, 1 Cor. 10:4. A rock of offence, 1 Pet. 2:7. See CHRIST. The Church was founded upon the rock Christ, Matt. 16:18. See FOUNDATION and CHURCH.

units.la: PETRVS ad Christum adducitur,Ioann.1.42. à Christo vocatur,Matt.4 18.futuræ vocationis admonetur,Lucæ 5.10. Apostolus Christi est,1 Petr.1.1.2.Pet.1.1.Iudæorum Apostolus,Gal.2.v.7.8 fide super aquas ambulat,Matth.14.29. Christum interrogat,18 21.Christum verum Messiam agnoscit,& confitetur,16 16.Luc 9 20.Ioan.6.69. à Christo Satan vocatur,& cur,Mat.16.23.Marci 8 33 Cæsari tributum pendit,Mat 17.27.Malcho auriculam amputat,26. 51.Marc.14.47.Luc.22.50.Ioan.18.10. Christum sequitur, Mat.26.58.Marci 14 54.Christum negat, Mat.26.v.70.72. 74.Marci 14.v.69.70.Luc.22.v.57 58.60. Ioann.18.v.17.25. 27.eum turpis facti poenitet.Mat.26.75.Marc.14.72,Lucæ 22.62.pro terna abnegatione, ternam confessionem edit, Ioan.21.v.17.25. Christi monumentum inuisit,Lucæ 24. 12.Ioan.20.4.
units.tr: PETER is brought to Christ, John 1:42; is called by Christ, Matt. 4:18; is warned of his future calling, Luke 5:10. He is an apostle of Christ, 1 Pet. 1:1-2. He is the apostle of the Jews, Gal. 2:7-8. By faith he walks on the water, Matt. 14:29. He questions Christ, Matt. 18:21. He acknowledges and confesses Christ as the true Messiah, Matt. 16:16; Luke 9:20; John 6:69. He is called Satan by Christ, and why, Matt. 16:23; Mark 8:33. He pays tribute to Caesar, Matt. 17:27. He cuts off Malchus' ear, Matt. 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:50; John 18:10. He follows Christ, Matt. 26:58; Mark 14:54. He denies Christ, Matt. 26:70-72, 74; Mark 14:69-70; Luke 22:57-58, 60; John 18:17, 25-27. He repents of his shameful deed, Matt. 26:75; Mark 14:72; Luke 22:62. After his threefold denial he makes a threefold confession, John 21:17, 25. He visits Christ's tomb, Luke 24:12; John 20:4.

units.la: Petrus in carcerem ter coniicitur, Act.4.3.& 5.18.& 12. 4.liberatur, cap.4.v.21.& 5.19 & 12.v.5.&c. in Samariam missus,illic Euangelium annuntiat,8,14. à Paulo reprehenditur, ditur, Galat.2.v.11.14. [Æneam paralyticum sanat, Actor. 9.v.33.34.] Thabitham ex mortuis excitat, Actor.9.40.visionem videt, 10. v.11.12. Petrus morte violenta moriturus, Ioann.21.v.18.19.2 Petr.1.14. passionum Christi testis est, 1 Pet.5.1. Petri conciones, Actor.1.16. & 2.14. & 4.8. & 10.34. & 15.7. curiositas coercetur, Ioann.21. v.21.22. Eius socrus sanatur, Matt.8.14. Lucae 4.v.38.39. umbra, infirmos sanat, Actor.5.15. uxor, 1 Corinth.9.5. Petrum primum Apostolorum esse asseritur à Pontificiis, ut primatum pontificis Romani adstruere possint, ex Matth.10.2. & 16. v.18.24.&c. Luc.22.v.31.&c. Ioann.21.17.&c. V. PRIMATVS Petri. (1 Petr.5.v.1.2.3. Se aliorum collegam fatetur, dominantes cleris condemnans.)
units.tr: Peter is thrice cast into prison, Acts 4:3; 5:18; 12:4; he is freed, Acts 4:21; 5:19; 12:5, etc. He is sent into Samaria, and there preaches the gospel, Acts 8:14. He is rebuked by Paul, Gal. 2:11-14. [He heals Aeneas the paralytic, Acts 9:33-34.] He raises Tabitha from the dead, Acts 9:40; he sees a vision, Acts 10:11-12. Peter is to die a violent death, John 21:18-19; 2 Pet. 1:14. He is a witness of Christ's sufferings, 1 Pet. 5:1. Peter's sermons: Acts 1:16; 2:14; 4:8; 10:34; 15:7. His curiosity is checked, John 21:21-22. His mother-in-law is healed, Matt. 8:14; Luke 4:38-39. His shadow heals the sick, Acts 5:15. His wife, 1 Cor. 9:5. The Papists assert that Peter was the first of the apostles, so that they may establish the primacy of the Roman bishop, from Matt. 10:2; Matt. 16:18, 24, etc.; Luke 22:31, etc.; John 21:17, etc. See PRIMACY of Peter. (1 Pet. 5:1-3: he acknowledges himself a colleague of the others, condemning those who lord it over the clergy.)

units.la: PHACEIA, Manahen filius in Israel regnat, 2 Reg.15.23. impius est, ver.24. à Phacee interficitur, v.25. (aperiens dominus.)
units.tr: PHACEIAH: the son of Menahem, reigns over Israel, 2 Kings 15:23. He is impious, v.24. He is killed by Pekah, v.25 (the Lord opening).

units.la: PHACEE, filius Romeliae, postquam occidit Phaceiam, regnum Israel usurpat, 2 Reg.15.27. impie regnat, v.28. pugnat contra Ierusalem, Esa.7.1. occidit de Iuda centum viginti millia virorum uno die, 2 Paral.28.6. ab Osee interficitur, 2 Reg.15.30.
units.tr: PEKAH, son of Remaliah, after he killed Pekahiah, seizes the kingdom of Israel, 2 Kings 15:27. He reigns impiously, v.28. He makes war against Jerusalem, Isa. 7:1. He killed of Judah a hundred and twenty thousand men in one day, 2 Chron. 28:6. He is slain by Hoshea, 2 Kings 15:30.

units.la: PHALEG, filius Heber, cur sic dictus, Genesis 10.25. eius anni & posteritas, 11.v.18.19. (peleg.i.diuisio.)
units.tr: PELEG, son of Eber: why he was so called, Gen. 10:25. His years and posterity, Gen. 11:18-19. (Peleg: division.)

units.la: PHANVEL, id est aspectus, vel facies Dei: sic vocatur locus, vbi Angeli visi sunt Iacobo, Gen.32.30. V. Penuel.
units.tr: PENUEL, that is, the face or presence of God: so the place is called where angels appeared to Jacob, Gen. 32:30. See PENIEL.

units.la: PHANVEL ex tribu Aseris, pater Annae prophetissae: Luc.2.36. Phantasma. V. Spectrum.
units.tr: PENUEL, of the tribe of Asher, father of the prophetess Anna, Luke 2:36. Phantasm. See SPECTRE.

units.la: PHANVEL turris subuertitur à Gedeone occisis habitatoribus ciuitatis, Iudic.8.v.8.13.17.
units.tr: The tower of PENUEL is overthrown by Gideon, and the inhabitants of the city are killed, Judg. 8:8, 13, 17.

units.la: PHARAO: Ægyptiorum Regum nomen commune. ¶ Primus, de quo sacra Biblia verba faciunt, Sarai Abrahae vxorem sibi adduci imperat, Gen.12.15. ob id à Deo percutitur, v.17. cum Abrahamo, quòd sibi Sarai vxorem esse dissimulasset, expostulat, v.18. eam illi restituit, v.19. liberaliter eos dimittit, v.20. (Dissipans.)
units.tr: PHARAOH: the common name of the kings of Egypt. The first, of whom Holy Scripture speaks, orders Sarai to be brought to him as Abraham's wife, Gen. 12:15. For this he is struck by God, v.17. He reproaches Abraham for having pretended that Sarai was his wife, v.18. He restores her to him, v.19. He liberally dismisses them, v.20. (Scattering.)

units.la: PHARAO, in his, de quibus Biblia loquuntur, secundus, somnium videt, Gene. 41.ver.1 2,3,4. Somniis perterritus, coniectores, qui ea interpretentur, accersit, sed frustrà, v.8. Iosephum super somniis consulit, v.14.15.17. Iosephi cōsiliis acquiescit, v.37. eum vniuersæ Aegypto præficit, v.39.40. Act.7.10. Iacobū Iosephi patre liberaliter excipit, Gen.47. v.7.8. eius mandato terra patriarchis habitanda & excolenda tradiditur, v.11.
units.tr: PHARAOH: among those of whom the Bible speaks, the second, sees a dream, Gen. 41:1-4. Terrified by his dreams, he summons interpreters to explain them, but in vain, v.8. He consults Joseph about the dreams, vv.14-15, 17. He yields to Joseph's counsels, v.37. He sets him over all the land of Egypt, vv.39-40; Acts 7:10. He receives Jacob, Joseph's father, graciously, Gen. 47:7-8. By his command the land is handed over to the patriarchs to dwell in and cultivate, v.11.

units.la: PHARAO, in his, de quibus Biblia, tertius, Iosephi in Ægyptum beneficiorum immemor, Exodi 1.8. Act. 7.18. hic adversus Israel ingeniosus est, Exod. 1. v. 9.10.15.22. Act. 7.19. [Pharaonem quartum in historia sacra,] aggrediuntur Moses & Aaron, Exod. 5.1. blasphemat, v.2. impium se confitetur, 9.27. & 10.16. indurator, 9.v 34.35. & 10. v.1.20.27.8 14. v.4.8.17. eius indurationis finis, Rom. 9.17. 18. fluctibus cum toto exercitu obruitur, Exod. 14.28.
units.tr: PHARAOH: among those of whom the Bible speaks, the third, forgetful of the benefits Joseph bestowed on Egypt, Exod. 1:8; Acts 7:18. He is crafty against Israel, Exod. 1:9-10, 15, 22; Acts 7:19. [The fourth Pharaoh in sacred history.] Moses and Aaron confront him, Exod. 5:1. He blasphemes, v.2. He confesses himself impious, Exod. 9:27; 10:16. He is hardened, Exod. 9:34-35; 10:1, 20, 27; 8:14; 8:4, 8, 17. The end of this hardening: Rom. 9:17-18. He is overwhelmed in the waves with his whole army, Exod. 14:28.

units.la: [Pharao in S. historia, quintus, Salomonis Socer, 1 Reg. 3.1. &c.
units.tr: [Pharaoh in sacred history, the fifth, Solomon's father-in-law, 1 Kings 3:1, etc.]

units.la: Pharao, sextus, Ezechiæ tempore, 2 Reg. 18.21.
units.tr: Pharaoh, the sixth, in the time of Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18:21.

units.la: Pharao, septimus,] cognomine Nechao, Ioachas Iudæ Regem in vincula coniicit, 2 Regum 23.33. in eius locum Eliacim, eius fratrem, Regem constituit, v. 34. 2. Paral. 36. v. 3.4.
units.tr: Pharaoh, the seventh, surnamed Necho, throws King Jehoahaz of Judah into chains, 2 Kings 23:33. In his place he appoints Eliakim, his brother, as king, v.34; 2 Chron. 36:3-4.

units.la: [Pharao octavus, cogn. Ephroe, seu Ophra, vel Apryes, qui paulò ante Sedeciam captum & deportatos in Chaldæam Iudæos regnauit, Ierem. 44.30.]
units.tr: [Pharaoh the eighth, surnamed Ephroe, or Ophra, or Apries, who reigned shortly before Zedekiah was taken and the Jews were carried off to Chaldea, Jer. 44:30.]

units.la: PHARAONIS, id est Regis, & regni Ægyptiaci excidium prædicitur, Ezech. 29. v.2.3. & 31.13.
units.tr: The overthrow of PHARAOH, that is, of the king and of the Egyptian kingdom, is foretold, Ezek. 29:2-3; 31:13.

units.la: PHARES (id est ruptura) Iuda ex Thamar filius, nascitur, & re nata nomen sortitur, Gen. 38.29. eius filij, 46.12.1 Paral. 2 5.
units.tr: PHARES (that is, breach), son of Judah by Tamar, is born, and receives his name at his birth, Gen. 38:29. His sons: Gen. 46:12; 1 Chron. 2:5.

units.la: PHARETRA Dei, Thren. 3.13. Esai. 49 2.
units.tr: The QUIVER of God: Lam. 3:13; Isa. 49:2.

units.la: Pharetra hominis, Genes. 27.3.1 Paral. 18.7. Esai. 22.6. Ierem. 51.11. Iob 39.26. Psalm. 11.2. Ierem. 5.16. Ezech. 27.11.
units.tr: The quiver of man: Gen. 27:3; 1 Chron. 18:7; Isa. 22:6; Jer. 51:11; Job 39:26; Ps. 11:2; Jer. 5:16; Ezek. 27:11.

units.la: PHARISAEVS quidam Christum convivio excipit, Lucæ 36. (1. Diuisus.)
units.tr: A PHARISEE invites Christ to a meal, Luke 7:36. (1. Divided.)

units.la: PHARISAEI (à seiungendo dicti, quòd ab aliis affectata vitæ sanctimonia seiuncti essent. Idem testatur & Tertullianus libro de Præscript.) Pharisæi maledicti, Matth. 2 versicul. 13.14.15. Luc. 11.42.43.44. Ioannem Baptistam accedunt, & ab eo grauiter increpantur, Matth. 3.7. Ioan. 1. ver. 19.24. à Christo insciti arguuntur, Matth. 12.2. & in Christum conspirant, & illi insidiantur, Marc. 3.6. & 13. murmurant in Christum, Matth. 9.11. Marc. 2.16. Luc. 30. & 15.2, & in eius Discipulos, Matth. 12.2. & 15.2. Marc. 24. & 7.5. Luc. 6.2. signum postulant, Matt. 12, 38. confiliu Dei spernunt, Lucæ 7.30. Christum tentant, Vide CHRI STVS. Vt Christum capiant, ministros mittunt, Ioann. 32.
units.tr: PHARISEES (named from separating, because they were set apart from others by a self-affected sanctity of life; Tertullian also testifies to this in his book De Praescriptione). The Pharisees are cursed, Matt. 23:13-15; Luke 11:42-44. They approach John the Baptist and are severely rebuked by him, Matt. 3:7; John 1:19-24. Questioned by Christ, they are refuted, Matt. 12:2. They conspire against Christ and lie in wait for him, Mark 3:6; 13. They murmur against Christ, Matt. 9:11; Mark 2:16; Luke 5:30; 15:2, and against his disciples, Matt. 12:2; 15:2; Mark 2:24; 7:5; Luke 6:2. They demand a sign, Matt. 12:38. They despise God's counsel, Luke 7:30. They tempt Christ: see CHRIST. To catch Christ they send ministers, John 7:32.

units.la: 32. eorum doctrina noxia, ideoque cauenda, Matth.16.6. Pharisæi & Scribæ intelligentes & sapientes dicuntur à Christo, per concessionem. (Tales enim eos esse oportuerat,) cum fuerint omnium maximè rudes, Matth.11.25. Pharisæi nomen sectæ: Scribæ verò, nomen publici muneris, vt apparet ex Act.23.9. Pharisæorum mores notantur, Matth.23.v.7.8. Luc.16.14. Pharisæus & publicanus orant, 18,10.
units.tr: 32. Their teaching is harmful and therefore to be avoided, Matt. 16:6. The Pharisees and scribes are called intelligent and wise by Christ, by concession (for they ought to have been such), though they were most ignorant, Matt. 11:25. "Pharisee" is the name of a sect; "scribe," however, is the name of a public office, as appears from Acts 23:9. The manners of the Pharisees are noted: Matt. 23:7-8; Luke 16:14. The Pharisee and the publican pray, Luke 18:10.

units.la: PHARISAISMVS paulo exquisitissima secta, Actor. 26.5. partim ex aduersariorum hypothesi, qui sectam pharisaicam pro sanctissima & religiosissima habebant: partim collatione cum reliquis facta, cum pharisæi resurrectionem futuram crederent, Sadducæi verò eandem negarent, Act.23.8.
units.tr: PHARISAISM, a rather exquisite sect, Actor. 26.5. Partly this is according to the view of its opponents, who held the Pharisaic sect to be most holy and most religious; partly it is by comparison with the rest, since the Pharisees believed in a future resurrection, while the Sadducees denied it, Act. 23.8.

units.la: PHASE Domini præcipitur, Exodi 12.18. Leuitic.23.5. Deuteron.16.2. ritu perpetuo celebrandum, Exodi 12.17. Vide PASCHA.
units.tr: The Passover of the Lord is commanded, Exod. 12.18, Lev. 23.5, Deut. 16.2, to be celebrated with a perpetual rite, Exod. 12.17. See PASCHA.

units.la: PHASSVR Sacerdos, filius Emmer, Iere.20.1. Ieremiam percutit, v.2. ab eo reprehenditur, v.3. eíque Dei iudicium denuntiat: v.4. &c.
units.tr: PHASSUR the priest, son of Immer, strikes Jeremiah, Jer. 20.2. He is rebuked by him, v.3, and Jeremiah announces God's judgment to him, v.4, etc.

units.la: PHEGIEL, dux Tribus Aser, Num.1.13.
units.tr: PHEGIEL, leader of the tribe of Asher, Num. 1.13.

units.la: PHELTIAS filius Benaiæ moritur, Ezech.11.13. (i. liberatio Domini.)
units.tr: PHELTIAS, son of Benaiah, dies, Ezek. 11.13. (i.e. deliverance of the Lord.)

units.la: PHENENNA, altera Eleanæ vxor, 1 Sam.1.2. fœcunda est, v.2. insolescit, & sterilitatem Annæ exprobrat. v.6. (gemma, siue facies nostra.)
units.tr: PHENENNA, the second wife of Elkanah, 1 Sam. 1.2. She is fruitful, v.2, and grows insolent and reproaches Hannah for her barrenness, v.6. (A gem, or our face.)

units.la: PHERESAEI, funditus deleri præcipiuntur, Deut.2017. à Iuda vincuntur, Iud.1.4 eorum reliquiæ Salomoni tributum pendunt, 2 Paral.8.7. (i. Rurales.)
units.tr: The Perizzites are commanded to be utterly destroyed, Deut. 20.17. They are conquered by Judah, Judg. 1.4, and their remnants pay tribute to Solomon, 2 Chron. 8.7. (i.e. rustics.)

units.la: PHIALARVM Templi fabricatio, 2 Paralip. 4.8. sunt crateres.
units.tr: The making of the phials of the Temple, 2 Chron. 4.8; they are bowls.

units.la: Phialæ aureæ cœlestes. Apo.5.8. phialæ iudiciorum Dei, Apo.15.7, & 16.v.1.2.&c.& 17.1.& 21.9. phialæ tabernaculi, Exod.25.29.1 Reg.7.50. phialæ à principibus datæ, Num. 7.v.13.19.&c. seu crateres.
units.tr: Heavenly golden phials, Rev. 5.8; the phials of God's judgments, Rev. 15.7, 16.1, 2, etc., 17.1, 21.9; the phials of the tabernacle, Exod. 25.29, 1 Kings 7.50; phials given by the princes, Num. 7.13, 19, etc.; or bowls.

units.la: PHILADELPHIA, vrbs Lydiæ in Asia, proxima Sardibus, Apoc.1. 11.&3.7. (i. fraternitatis affectus.)
units.tr: PHILADELPHIA, a city of Lydia in Asia, next to Sardis, Rev. 1.11, 3.7. (i.e. the affection of brotherhood.)

units.la: PHIGIEL, V. PHEGIEL.
units.tr: PHIGIEL, see PHEGIEL.

units.la: PHILANTIA, 2 Tim.3.2. V. Amor sui.
units.tr: PHILAUTIA, 2 Tim. 3.2. See Self-love.

units.la: PHILEMON, pauli adiutor, Philem. versic.1. eius charitas & fides laudatur, versic. 5. 6.7. Ad eum scripsit paulus. (i. Deosculans.)
units.tr: PHILEMON, Paul's helper, Philem. v.1. His love and faith are praised, vv.5, 6, 7. Paul wrote to him. (i.e. kissing him.)

units.la: PHILETVS,(.i.amabilis.)vel,vt alij legunt,Phygellus,Apostata,2 Tim.1.15.seductor est,2.17. docens resurrectionem iam esse factam.
units.tr: PHILETUS (i.e. beloved), or, as others read, Phygellus, an apostate, 2 Tim. 1.15. He is a seducer, 2.17, teaching that the resurrection has already taken place.

units.la: PHILIPPI,prima Macedoniæ ciuitas, Act.16.12. eius ciues Euangelium recipiunt,v.13.14.15.
units.tr: PHILIPPI, the first city of Macedonia, Acts 16.12. Its citizens receive the Gospel, vv.13, 14, 15.

units.la: PHILIPPVS Apostolus à Christo vocatur, Ioann.1.43. à Christo Deum patrem sibi ostendi petit,14.8. (amator eorum.)
units.tr: PHILIP the Apostle is called by Christ, John 1.43. He asks Christ to show him God the Father, 14.8. (Lover of horses.)

units.la: PHILIPPVS Diaconus eligitur,Act.6.5. Euangelistæ munus obit, 8.v.5 38.&21.8. eius filiæ prophetant,v.9. Paulum & eius comites hospitio excipit,v.8. Eunuchum Aethiopem conuertit. Act.8.27.
units.tr: PHILIP the Deacon is chosen, Acts 6.5. He performs the office of evangelist, Acts 8.5, 38 and 21.8. His daughters prophesy, v.9. He receives Paul and his companions into his hospitality, v.8. He converts the Ethiopian eunuch, Acts 8.27.

units.la: Philippus frater Herodis Tetrarchæ, Matth.14.3.Luc.3.19.
units.tr: Philip, brother of Herod the Tetrarch, Matt. 14.3, Luke 3.19.

units.la: PHILISTHAEI unde oriundi, Gen.10.14.1 Paral.1.12.Philisthæi sexcenti vomere à Samgare occiduntur, Iudic.3.31. cæduntur,1 Sam.7.11.&14.14.&19.8.&23.5.2 Sam.5.20.1 Paral.14.11.2.Sam.21.22.1 Paral.18.1.&20.4. Dauidi tributarij fiunt,2 Sam.8.1.2.cædunt Israelitas,1 Sam.31.1.terram Iuda inuadunt,&vastant,2 Par.21.17.&28.18. vincuntur,2 Reg.18.8.Para.26.7.Philisthæorum excidium prædicitur, Esaiæ 14.29.Ierem.47.1.Ezech.25.15.&c. Amos 1.8.Soph.2.5.zach.9.6.(.i.Coniperfi,scilicet cinere aut puluere.)
units.tr: PHILISTINES, whence they sprang, Gen. 10.14, 1 Chron. 1.12. Six hundred Philistines are killed by Shamgar with an ox-goad, Judg. 3.31. They are struck down, 1 Sam. 7.11, 14.14, 19.8, 23.5; 2 Sam. 5.20; 1 Chron. 14.11; 2 Sam. 21.22; 1 Chron. 18.1, 20.4. They become tributary to David, 2 Sam. 8.1, 2. They slay Israelites, 1 Sam. 31.1. They invade and lay waste the land of Judah, 2 Chron. 21.17, 28.18. They are conquered, 2 Kings 18.8, 1 Chron. 26.7. The destruction of the Philistines is foretold, Isa. 14.29, Jer. 47.1, Ezek. 25.15, etc., Amos 1.8, Zeph. 2.5, Zech. 9.6. (i.e. dusted over, namely with ashes or dust.)

units.la: PHILOSOPHIA in rebus Dei fallax, Coloss.2.8. ideóque damnatur ab Apostolo non simpliciter,(vt qui principiis cum vera philosophia communibus sæpe vtatur, methodum quàm accuratissime obseruet, philosophiam veram Dei donum esse sciat,&Episcopum velit esse ὀρθοτομοῦντα τὸν λόγον τῆς ἀληθείας, id est, qui recte sermonem veritatis secet,2 Tim.2.15. quod sine mediocri liberalium artium & philosophiæ cognitione fieri non potest): sed καθ' ὅ quatenus nimirum illa sese intra fines suos non continet, nec ad gloriam Dei fertur, sese denique verbo Dei, cui ancillari,non dominari debebat,regi non finit,(V.Act.17.18.1 Cor.2.4.)
units.tr: PHILOSOPHY is deceptive in the things of God, Col. 2.8. Therefore it is condemned by the Apostle, not simply (since he often uses the principles common to true philosophy, observes method as accurately as possible, knows that true philosophy is a gift of God, and wishes the bishop to be [orthotomounta ton logon tēs alētheias], that is, one who rightly divides the word of truth, 2 Tim. 2.15, which cannot be done without a moderate knowledge of the liberal arts and philosophy), but in so far as it does not keep itself within its own bounds, nor is directed to the glory of God, and finally does not let itself be ruled by the Word of God, to which it ought to be a handmaid, not a master [kath' ho] (see Acts 17.18, 1 Cor. 2.4).

units.la: PHINEES,Eleazari filius,Exodi 6.25. Iudic.20.28. scortantes occidit,Num.25.7.eius zelus,Ps.106.30. mittitur in terram Galaad,Iosh.22.13. (Pinehas, os confidens.)
units.tr: PHINEHAS, son of Eleazar, Exod. 6.25, Judg. 20.28. He killed the fornicators, Num. 25.7. His zeal, Ps. 106.30. He is sent into the land of Gilead, Josh. 22.13. (Pinehas, a confident mouth.)

units.la: PHINEES, Heli Sacerdotis filius,1 Sam.1.3.impius est,2.12. moritur.4 11.vt prædictum fuerat.2.34.
units.tr: PHINEHAS, son of Eli the priest, 1 Sam. 1.3. He is impious, 2.12. He dies, 4.11, as had been foretold, 2.34.

units.la: PHISON,Edenis fluuius, Genes.2.11.eius præstantia, verfic. 12.(.i.oris mutatio.)
units.tr: PISON, a river of Eden, Gen. 2.11. Its excellence, v.12. (i.e. change of mouth.)

units.la: PHITHON vibs, ædificatur à filiis Israël in AEgypto, Regi Pharaoni, Exod. 1.11.
units.tr: PITHOM, a city built by the sons of Israel in Egypt for Pharaoh the king, Exod. 1.11.

units.la: PHOEBE, 1. Lucida Diaconissa, Ecclesiæ piorum in Cenchreis, suburbio Cor.1.Rom 16.1.
units.tr: PHOEBE, 1. Bright, deaconess of the church of the pious at Cenchreae, a suburb of Corinth, Rom. 16.1.

units.la: PHOENICIA, Syriæ pars est, in qua Sidon & Tyrus amplissimæ vibes sitæ sunt. Act.11.19 & 15.3.& 21 2 & 27.12.
units.tr: PHOENICIA, a part of Syria, in which the very great cities of Sidon and Tyre are situated, Acts 11.19, 15.3, 21.2, 27.12.

units.la: PHRYGIA provincia, Asiæ minoris: Act.2.10.
units.tr: PHRYGIA, a province of Asia Minor, Acts 2.10.

units.la: PHUL, una ex Obstetricibus Hebræis, Exodi 1.15.
units.tr: PHUL, one of the Hebrew midwives, Exod. 1.15.

units.la: PHUL, Rex Assyriorum, copias adducit contra Israelem, 1 Reg.15 19.(i.ruina.aut faba.)
units.tr: PHUL, king of the Assyrians, leads forces against Israel, 1 Kings 15.19. (i.e. ruin, or bean.)

units.la: PHYGELLUS & Hermogenes amici perfidi deserentes Paulum captiuum Romæ 2. Tim.1.15.
units.tr: PHYGELLUS and Hermogenes, faithless friends who deserted Paul when he was a prisoner at Rome, 2 Tim. 1.15.

units.la: PHYLACTERIA, [Matt.23.5] Vide φυλακτήριον in litera Fy.
units.tr: PHYLACTERIES, [Matt. 23.5]. See φυλακτήριον under the letter Ph.

units.la: PIETAS: Pietas, pro legitimo & spirituali Dei cultu, 2 pet.3. 11. cum quo comparatur corporis exercitatio, 1 Tim.4.v. 7.8. commendatur, 4.v.7.8. & 6.v.6.11. Tit.2.12.2 per. 1,6 7. & 3.11 (pietas Reges dicat, prou.25 5.) V. 1 Tim.2.2. & 3. 16. Simulata damnatur: 2 Tim.3 5.
units.tr: PIETY: piety, for the lawful and spiritual worship of God, 2 Pet. 3.11; bodily exercise is compared with it, 1 Tim. 4.7, 8. It is commended, 1 Tim. 4.7, 8, 6.6, 11; Titus 2.12; 2 Pet. 1.6, 7, 3.11. (Piety exalts kings, Prov. 25.5.) See 1 Tim. 2.2, 3, 3.16. Feigned piety is condemned, 2 Tim. 3.5.

units.la: Pietatis exempla: Abel, Gen.4.4. Henoch, 5 22. Noah.6. 9.& 7.1.& 8.20 Abraham.12.v.7 8 & 13. ver.4.18.& 18.v.18. 19.& 21 33. Abrahæ famulus.24.12. Isaac,26.25. Iacob,28.18. & 33 20.&35.7 Ioseph,42 18. Moses, Exodi 17.15. Iosias,2 Reg.22.13.& 23 2. Dauid,1 paral,21.26. Asa, 2 paral,14.11. Iosaphat, 17.3. Ezechias,29.20. Esa.37.1. Nehemias, Nehem.8.7. Iob, Iob.1.v.5.20. quidam Ierosolymitani, Act.8. 2. Cornelius,10 2 Barnabas,11.24, Lydia,16.4. Iustus, 18.7. Lois & Eunice,2 Tim.1.5. Onesiphorus, v.16. electa illa Domina, ad quam Iohannes suam secundam scripsit Epistolam, 2 Ioan v.1.4. Vide Adorationis, & eorum qui altaria ædificaverunt, exempla: & Invocationis exempla. (Deus omnia nobis ad pietatem pertinentia donauit: 2 Pet.1.3.
units.tr: Examples of piety: Abel, Gen. 4.4; Enoch, 5.22; Noah, 6.9, 7.1, 8.20; Abraham, 12.7, 8, 13.4, 18, 18.18, 19, 21.33; Abraham's servant, 24.12; Isaac, 26.25; Jacob, 28.18, 33.20, 35.7; Joseph, 42.18; Moses, Exod. 17.15; Josiah, 2 Kings 22.13, 23.2; David, 1 Chron. 21.26; Asa, 2 Chron. 14.11; Jehoshaphat, 17.3; Hezekiah, 29.20, Isa. 37.1; Nehemiah, Neh. 8.7; Job, Job 1.5, 20; certain Jerusalemites, Acts 8.2; Cornelius, 10.2; Barnabas, 11.24; Lydia, 16.4; Justus, 18.7; Lois and Eunice, 2 Tim. 1.5; Onesiphorus, v.16; that chosen lady to whom John wrote his second epistle, 2 John vv.1, 4. See the examples of Adoration, and of those who built altars, and the examples of Invocation. (God has given us everything pertaining to piety, 2 Pet. 1.3.)

units.la: pietas sperat vitam æternam, Tit.1.v.1.2. pietas, vel impietas, non Deo, sed homini prodest, vel nocet, Iob.35.v.6, &c. in pietate assidui esse debemus, 2 pet.3.11. pietas, magnus quæstus est, 1 Tim.6.6. pie volentes viuere in Christo, persecutionem patientur, 2 Tim.3.12.
units.tr: Piety hopes for eternal life, Titus 1.1, 2. Piety or impiety benefits or harms not God but man, Job 35.6, etc. We ought to be constant in piety, 2 Pet. 3.11. Piety is great gain, 1 Tim. 6.6. Those who wish to live piously in Christ will suffer persecution, 2 Tim. 3.12.

units.la: PIETAS erga parentes species & quedam στοργὴς generalis & naturalis affectionis, ea nimirum, quæ ipsos parentes (qui nos genuerunt) amplectitur summo atq; sincero affectu & quatum decet. 1 Ti.5.4. Si qua vidua liberos aut nepotes habet, discant prius in propriam domum ευσεβειν pietatem exercere, & vicem rependere parentibus, LI 4
units.tr: PIETY towards parents is a kind of general and natural affection (στοργή), namely that which embraces the parents themselves, who begot us, with the highest and sincere affection and as far as is fitting. 1 Tim. 5.4: If any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to exercise piety [eusebein] in their own house, and to repay their parents in return.

units.la: PIGER excitatur ad laborem, Prouer.6.6. laborem fugiens in egestate erit, 20.4. & 21.5. cui similis, 26.14. in pigrum, prou.21.v.25.26.& 22.13.&26.15.
units.tr: The sluggard is roused to labour, Prov. 6.6. The one who flees labour will be in want, 20.4, 21.5. Like him, 26.14. Against the sluggard, Prov. 21.25, 26, 22.13, 26.15.

units.la: PIGRITIA (ὀκνότης siue ἀτονία 2. Thess.3.) est operis, studiique, ad quod vocati vel apti sumus, vel in totum praetermissio, vel illius negligens & perfunctoria siue remissa functio & aggressio. Et est labori contrarium vitium.
units.tr: SLOTH (ὀκνότης or ἀτονία, 2 Thess. 3) is the complete omission of the work or study to which we are called or fit, or a negligent, perfunctory or lax performance and undertaking of it. It is a vice contrary to labour.

units.la: PIGRITIA damnatur, Prou. 13.4.& 19.v.15.24.& 20.13. & 21.25.&22.13.& 26.13.14. Eccles.11.4. Rom.12.11. pigritiae mala, prouer.20.4.&21.5.&24 30.&c.28.19. Matth.13.25. Vide ACEDIA. Pigritiae exempla: Israelitae, Num. 11.4.& 21.4. reduces à captiuitate, Agg.1.2. Operarij, Matth.2 c3. Seruus nequam, 25.26. Apostoli, Mar.14.40. Vide NEGLIGENTIAE exempla, & Acedia.
units.tr: SLOTH is condemned, Prov. 13.4, 19.15, 24, 20.13, 21.25, 22.13, 26.13, 14; Eccl. 11.4; Rom. 12.11. The evils of sloth, Prov. 20.4, 21.5, 24.30, etc., 28.19; Matt. 13.25. See ACEDIA. Examples of sloth: the Israelites, Num. 11.4, 21.4; those returned from captivity, Hag. 1.2; labourers, Matt. 20.3; the wicked servant, Matt. 25.26; the Apostles, Mark 14.40. See the examples of NEGLIGENCE, and Acedia.

units.la: PIGNVS à Iuda Thamar nurui suae datur, Gen.38.18. pignoris loco non quiduis accipiendum, Deut.24.6. reddedum v.12. pignora quando reddeda proximo, Exo.22.26. Deuter.24.13 pignora non vi auferenda ab iis, quibus mutuaverimus aliquid, v.10. pignus promissae felicitatis & salutis nostrae Spiritus Sanctus, Rom.8.15.16.2 Cor.1.22.& 5.5. Ephes.1.13.& 4.30. Vide ARRHABO: & SPIRITVS Sanctus. (Vide Iob. 22.6. & 24.3. Prou. 20.16.& 27.13. Ezech.18.7.&33 15.)
units.tr: PLEDGE: given by Judah to his daughter-in-law Tamar, Gen. 38.18. Nothing whatever is to be taken as a pledge, Deut. 24.6, and it is to be returned, v.12. Pledges are to be returned to a neighbour when, Exod. 22.26, Deut. 24.13. Pledges are not to be taken by force from those to whom we have lent something, v.10. The Holy Spirit is the pledge of the promised happiness and our salvation, Rom. 8.15, 16; 2 Cor. 1.22, 5.5; Eph. 1.13, 4.30. See ARRHABO and HOLY SPIRIT. (See Job 22.6, 24.3; Prov. 20.16, 27.13; Ezek. 18.7, 33.15.)

units.la: PILATVS, Christum innocentem pronūtiat. Vide CHRISTVS innocens ac integer. Pilatus Christum flagellari iubet, Ioan.19.1 Pilatus inexcusabilis, Matth.27.23. Marci 15.14. Lucę 23.22. Christum morti adiudicat, Matt.27.26. Marci.15.15. Lucę.23.25. Ioh.19.16. hostis est veritatis, Act. 4.27. Pilatus & Herodes amici, & qua occasione, Lucae 23.12. eius vxor Christum à morte liberare conatur, Matthaei 27.19. Pilati peccatum Iudae summi Sacerdotis peccato minus est, Ioan.19 11. misere periit. V.persecutorum Ecclesiae &c.
units.tr: PILATE declares Christ innocent. See CHRIST, innocent and blameless. Pilate orders Christ to be scourged, John 19.1. Pilate is inexcusable, Matt. 27.23, Mark 15.14, Luke 23.22. He adjudges Christ to death, Matt. 27.26, Mark 15.15, Luke 23.25, John 19.16. He is an enemy of the truth, Acts 4.27. Pilate and Herod became friends, and on what occasion, Luke 23.12. His wife tries to free Christ from death, Matt. 27.19. Pilate's sin is less than the sin of Judas and of the high priest, John 19.11. He perished wretchedly. See the persecutors of the Church, etc.

units.la: PILOSVS Elias, 2. Reg.1.8. (V. Capilli) Esau: Genes.27 11. PINGVIS Israel, derelinquit Deum, Deut.32.15.
units.tr: PILOSE Elijah, 2 Kings 1.8 (see Hair). Esau, Gen. 27.11. FAT Israel forsakes God, Deut. 32.15.

units.la: PINNAE (siue pinnaculum) erat ambitus, quo planū templi tectum âbiebatur, ne quis inde posset decidere, prout cautum erat, Deut.22.8. Mat.4 5. Luc.4 9.
units.tr: PINNACLE (or pinnaculum) was the parapet by which the flat roof of the temple was surrounded, so that no one could fall from it, as was provided, Deut. 22.8; Matt. 4.5; Luke 4.9.

units.la: PISCINA in Ierusalem quinque porticus habens, Ioann. 5.2. In quam quisquis infirmorum primus descendebat, post aquam ab angelo turbatam, sanabatur.v.3.4. scēs à Deo conditi, Genes.1.21. pisces multi ad Christi nutū capiuntur, Lucæ 5.6. Ioann. 21.v.6.11. (pisces multiplicantur, Vide Miracvla) piscium caro qualis, 1. Cor. 15.39. pisces mundi & immundi, Levit.11.9. Deut. 14.9. piscibus dominatur homo: Gen.1.26. & 9.2. Ps.8.9. Pisces in aquis Aegyptiacis perëunt: Exod. 7.18.21. Ps.105.29. Nullius piscis forma colenda, Deut.4.18. pisces doctores, Iob.12.8. Deus piscem ad excipiendum Ionam parat: Ion. 2.1. &c. Petrus piscem cum staterē capit, Mat.17.27. Et piscator hominum constituitur, Mat.4.19.
units.tr: POOL in Jerusalem, having five porticoes, John 5.2. Whoever of the sick went down into it first, after the water was stirred by an angel, was healed, vv.3, 4. Fish created by God, Gen. 1.21. Many fish are caught at Christ's nod, Luke 5.6, John 21.6, 11 (fish multiplied, see Miracles). What kind of flesh fish have, 1 Cor. 15.39. Clean and unclean fish, Lev. 11.9, Deut. 14.9. Man rules over the fish, Gen. 1.26, 9.2, Ps. 8.9. Fish perish in the Egyptian waters, Exod. 7.18, 21, Ps. 105.29. The form of no fish is to be worshipped, Deut. 4.18. Fish as teachers, Job 12.8. God prepares a fish to swallow Jonah, Jonah 2.1, etc. Peter takes a coin from a fish, Matt. 17.27. And a fisher of men is appointed, Matt. 4.19.

units.la: Pisidia. Minoris Asiæ provincia: Act.13.14. & 14.24.
units.tr: Pisidia, a province of Asia Minor: Acts 13.14 and 14.24.

units.la: Pius solus Deus, Apoc.15.4. seu sanctus.
units.tr: God alone is holy (pius), Rev. 15.4, or sanctus.

units.la: Pii, Aduenæ, hospites & peregrini in hoc mundo, 2. Corinth.5.6. Hebr.13.14. 1 Petr.2.11.2. Petr.1. vers.13.14. pij amici Christi, Ioannis.15.14. Angelis similes futuri, Matt. 22.30. Marc. 12.25. Benefici & misericordes, Psalm.37.21. Ciues Regni cœlestis, Ephes.2.19. Hebr.12.v.22.23. & 13.14. cohæredes Christi, Roman.8.17. consortes diuinæ naturæ, 2 Petri.1.4. corpus vnum cum Christo, Roman.12.5. 1 Corinth.10.17. & 12.v.13.27. Ephes.4.v.4.25. Coloss.3.15. Hebr.13.3. creaturæ nouæ, 1 Cor.5.7. Gal.6.15. Ephes.2.10. Diuites in fide Iac.2.5. Filij lucis, Ioan.12.36. Ephes.5.8.1. Thess.5.5. Vide Filii. filij obedientiæ, 1 petr.1.14. forma, seu exemplar debent esse aliis, 1 Thessa.1.7. Fratres Christi sunt, Vide Christus frater piorum. Hæreditas Domini, psalm.28.9. Vide Hæreditas Hæredes Dei, Roman.8.17. hæredes regni, Iacob.2.5. hæredes terræ, Ps.37.v.11.22. Prou.2.21. hæredes vitæ æternæ, Tit.3.7.1 Pet.3.22. Hic consule Vet. versionem.
units.tr: The godly are sojourners, guests and strangers in this world: 2 Cor. 5.6; Heb. 13.14; 1 Pet. 2.11; 2 Pet. 1, vers. 13–14. They are friends of Christ, John 15.14; are to be like the angels, Matt. 22.30; Mark 12.25; are beneficent and merciful, Ps. 37.21; are citizens of the heavenly kingdom, Eph. 2.19; Heb. 12.22–23 and 13.14; are co-heirs with Christ, Rom. 8.17; are partakers of the divine nature, 2 Pet. 1.4; are one body with Christ, Rom. 12.5; 1 Cor. 10.17; 12.13, 27; Eph. 4.4, 25; Col. 3.15; Heb. 13.3; are new creatures, 1 Cor. 5.7; Gal. 6.15; Eph. 2.10; are rich in faith, James 2.5; are sons of light, John 12.36; Eph. 5.8; 1 Thess. 5.5 (see Sons); are sons of obedience, 1 Pet. 1.14; ought to be a pattern to others, 1 Thess. 1.7. For the brothers of Christ, see Christ, brother of the godly. The godly are the inheritance of the Lord, Ps. 28.9 (see Inheritance); heirs of God, Rom. 8.17; heirs of the kingdom, James 2.5; heirs of the land, Ps. 37.11, 22; Prov. 2.21; heirs of eternal life, Titus 3.7; 1 Pet. 3.22. Consult the Old Version here.

units.la: Pij infantibus quomodo similes, 1 Petr.2.2. inopes esse nequeunt, psal. 34.10. Lapides viui sunt, 1 petri.2.5. Misericordes, Proverb.21.26. Quibus similes, Vide Deus suorum pastor. piscibus bonis similes, Matthæi.13.48. velut portenta in mundo habentur, Esa.8.18. purgamenta mundi. 1 Corint.4.13. Reges sunt, Apoc.1.6. & 5.10. & regale Sacerdotium, 1 pet.2.9. quomodo Sacerdotes, Ef.61.6.& 66, 21.Hebr.13.15. Rom.15. Rom.12.1. Apoc.1.6. & 5.10. & 20.6. spectaculum facti sunt mundo, Angelis & hominibus, 1 Cor. 4.9. stulti habentur, versi.10.serui sunt iustitiæ, Rom.6.18. conferuntur semini, Matthæ.13.38. superiores futuri sunt hostibus suis, psalm.149.vers.5.6.7. Esa.41.15. & 54.17. Terræ bonæ similes, Matt.13.22.23 Marci.4.20.Luc.8.5.&c. Hebr. 6. verf.5.7. tritico conferuntur, Matth.3.12. Lucæ. 3.17.
units.tr: The godly are like infants, 1 Pet. 2.2; they cannot be in want, Ps. 34.10; they are living stones, 1 Pet. 2.5; they are merciful, Prov. 21.26; for those they resemble, see God the shepherd of his people. They are like good fish, Matt. 13.48; they are regarded as portents in the world, Isa. 8.18; they are the filth of the world, 1 Cor. 4.13. They are kings, Rev. 1.6; 5.10, and a royal priesthood, 1 Pet. 2.9; they are priests, Isa. 61.6; 66.21; Heb. 13.15; Rom. 15; Rom. 12.1; Rev. 1.6; 5.10; 20.6. They have been made a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men, 1 Cor. 4.9; they are held to be fools, ibid. vers. 10. They are servants of righteousness, Rom. 6.18; they are compared to seed, Matt. 13.38; they will be superior to their enemies, Ps. 149.5–7; Isa. 41.15; 54.17. They are like good ground, Matt. 13.22–23; Mark 4.20; Luke 8.5, etc.; Heb. 6, vers. 5, 7. They are compared to wheat, Matt. 3.12; Luke 3.17.

units.la: PII Deo chari & pretiosi, Esa. 43.4.& 49.16.Deuter.32.10. psalm. 17.8. Zac.2.8.Matth 10.31.Luc.12.6.Ioan.4.v.21.23. &16.27. & 17.23.Ephes.1.6 cur Deo chari, Ioann.16.27.à Deo cogniti,1 Cor.8.3.2. Tim.2.19.Christo dilecti,Ioan. 14.21.& 15,v.9.14.in mundo contemti, psalm.123.4.1Cor. 4.v.9.10.13.Vide FIDELES.PIJ vno ac solo Deo contenti, Psal.73.28. in Deilaudem creati, Esa. 43.v.7.21. interdum à Deo reliĉi, & omni consolatione destituti videntur, psal.22.2. & 88.v.9 19. & 142.5. Esa.51.18. Matt.27 46.Marc 15.34. & 37. Luc. 22.45 pij omnes à Deo edocti, Esaiæ 54.13.Ierem.31.34.Ioann.6.45. mundo exosi,15.19.&17.14 1 Ioann.3.13.propter mundi odium non n iseri, Matt.5.11. Luc.6.22.Ioan.7.7.& 15.18.pij imitandi,Philip.3 17 pecca to mortui, Rom. 6.v.2.11.1. Petr.2.24. Vide ELECTI:& MORI peccato, opprobriis & ludibriis obnoxij, Psal.79. 4.variis ærumnis expositi,Pro.11.31.Eccles.5 12. Vide AF FLICTIO.
units.tr: The godly are dear and precious to God, Isa. 43.4; 49.16; Deut. 32.10; Ps. 17.8; Zech. 2.8; Matt. 10.31; Luke 12.6; John 4.21–23; 16.27; 17.23; Eph. 1.6. Why they are dear to God: John 16.27. They are known by God, 1 Cor. 8.3; 2 Tim. 2.19. They are beloved of Christ, John 14.21; 15.9, 14. They are despised in the world, Ps. 123.4; 1 Cor. 4.9–10, 13 (see Faithful). The godly are content with the one and only God, Ps. 73.28. They were created for the praise of God, Isa. 43.7, 21. At times they seem to be forsaken by God and deprived of all comfort, Ps. 22.2; 88.9, 19; 142.5; Isa. 51.18; Matt. 27.46; Mark 15.34, 37; Luke 22.45. All the godly are taught by God, Isa. 54.13; Jer. 31.34; John 6.45. They are hated by the world, John 15.19; 17.14; 1 John 3.13. They are not to be pitied for the world's hatred, Matt. 5.11; Luke 6.22; John 7.7; 15.18. The godly are to be imitated, Phil. 3.17. They are dead to sin, Rom. 6.2, 11; 1 Pet. 2.24 (see Elect and Dead to sin). They are liable to sin, reproach and mockery, Ps. 79.4; they are exposed to various troubles, Prov. 11.31; Eccl. 5.12. See Affliction.

units.la: Pij à Deo plantati, Esa.61 3. pij cum impiis non puniendi,2 Reg. 10.23.pij in cœlestibus sedentes, Eph.2.6.è mundo selecti, Ioan.15.19.& 17.v.6 14.16.à Deo per Spiritum Sanctum signati & uncti,2 Cor. 2.22.Ephes.1.13.& 4. 30.pij aliis utiles ac fructuosi, Prou.11.11.Ioan.15.4.pij nihil aggrediuntur ex se, Ps.119 24.Act.20 22.Spiritu Dei aguntur,Rom.8.v.9 14.inChristo manent, Ioa.6.56.&15. 4.pij seipsos probăt,2 Cor.13.5.pij indies proficiunt,Ioan. 13.10.&15.2. Ephes 3 19.&4 15. Phil.3.12.Col.1.v.9.10.&2. 7.1 Thess.1.v.3 10.& 4.1 2 Thess.1.11.& 2.17.1 Pet.2.2 2Pet. 1.v.5.12.& 3.1.1 Ioan.2.12.
units.tr: The godly are planted by God, Isa. 61.3. The godly are not to be punished along with the wicked, 2 Kings 10.23. The godly sit in heavenly places, Eph. 2.6. They are chosen out of the world, John 15.19; 17.6, 14, 16. They are sealed and anointed by God through the Holy Spirit, 2 Cor. 1.22; Eph. 1.13; 4.30. The godly are useful and fruitful to others, Prov. 11.11; John 15.4. The godly undertake nothing of themselves, Ps. 119.24; Acts 20.22. They are led by the Spirit of God, Rom. 8.9–14. They remain in Christ, John 6.56; 15.4. The godly test themselves, 2 Cor. 13.5. The godly make progress day by day, John 13.10; 15.2; Eph. 3.19; 4.15; Phil. 3.12; Col. 1.9–10; 2.7; 1 Thess. 1.3, 10; 4.1; 2 Thess. 1.11; 2.17; 1 Pet. 2.2; 2 Pet. 1.5, 12; 3.1; 1 John 2.12.

units.la: PIORVM Conditio in hoc seculo misera, Psalm.11.109.Esaiai.41.14.& 51 v.21.23.Abac.1.v.3.4.13. Matth.11.18. Lucæ 2.7,& 6,23,Ioan.15 20.Rom.8,36,1 Cor.4.v.9.11.& 15,19, 2 Corint. 4. 10, Hebr.10,33, &11,35,piorum conditio post vitam præsentem beata, Matt.13. 43.& 22 30,Marc.12,25, Luc.18,30, Apoc.3,21.&7,verf.16.17.&14.13,piorum coniunctio,ar tissima, Ioann.17, verl.11.22,consilia optima,Pro. 12, 20, consolatio, Psalm. 119.verl. 52. 76. Matth.5,v.5,12, Luc.6.23,& 12.31,2. Corinth.1,v.5.7.1 Timoth. 4.10.1 Pet. 4.13.constantia in bono, Psal.119.v.51.69,consortia,vtilia, Prou.13.20.corpora gloriosa futura,1 Cor.15.53.Philipp.3, 21.piorum
units.tr: The condition of the godly in this age is wretched: Ps. 119.109; Isa. 41.14; 51.21–23; Hab. 1.3–4, 13; Matt. 11.18; Luke 2.7; 6.23; John 15.20; Rom. 8.36; 1 Cor. 4.9–11; 15.19; 2 Cor. 4.10; Heb. 10.33; 11.35. The condition of the godly after this present life is blessed: Matt. 13.43; 22.30; Mark 12.25; Luke 18.30; Rev. 3.21; 7.16–17; 14.13. The fellowship of the godly is most close, John 17.11, 22. Their counsels are the best, Prov. 12.20. Comfort: Ps. 119.52, 76; Matt. 5.5, 12; Luke 6.23; 12.31; 2 Cor. 1.5, 7; 1 Tim. 4.10; 1 Pet. 4.13. Constancy in good: Ps. 119.51, 69. Companionships are useful, Prov. 13.20. The bodies of the godly will be glorious in the future, 1 Cor. 15.53; Phil. 3.21.

units.la: 2. Piorũ desiderium, Psalm.119 174. Apoc.22.17. dignitas ac praestantia, Matth.10.31. Luc.8.21. Ioan.1.12. & 12. 1 Cor. 1.9 & 3.22. & 7.23. Ephes.1.19. 1 Pet.2.9. 1 Ioan.3 v.1 2. domus benedicta, Prov.14.11. & 15. 7: domus coelestis, 2 Cor.5.1. Exercitium, Psal.119 v.15. 27.48.78. Eph.5.19. Col.3.16. 1 Thes. 5.11.1. Tim.4.8. 2 Tim.2.22. Tit.2.12. Fortitudo, Mich.4.13.
units.tr: The longing of the godly: Ps. 119.174; Rev. 22.17. Their dignity and excellence: Matt. 10.31; Luke 8.21; John 1.12; 12; 1 Cor. 1.9; 3.22; 7.23; Eph. 1.19; 1 Pet. 2.9; 1 John 3.1–2. A blessed house, Prov. 14.11; 15.7. A heavenly house, 2 Cor. 5.1. Exercise: Ps. 119, vers. 15, 27, 48, 78; Eph. 5.19; Col. 3.16; 1 Thess. 5.11; 1 Tim. 4.8; 2 Tim. 2.22; Titus 2.12. Strength: Mic. 4.13.

units.la: Piorum gemitus, Rom. 8,23.2 Cor.5,v.2,4 gloria,1,12. piorum gloria in futuro seculo, Matth. 13, 43. Philipp.3, 21, Col.3,4,2 Thess. 1,7, gloriatio. Vide FIDELES. Piorum Hæreditas, Deus, psalm. 73.26, Piorum Hæreditas praeclara, Vide FIDELES. Piorum hostes perdendi, psalm. 37,22. Piorum Iustitia qualis esse debeat, Matt.5,20. piorum Labor minime inanis. 1 Cor.15,58. Galat.6.9. Heb.6, 10. Apoc.14,13. laus Deus, Ier.17,14. Liberi, sancti. 1 Cor.7, 14. Vide infra, PIORVM semen. Piorum liberationis fructus & finis, psalm 30,v.12.13. & 40.v.2.4. & 56. verf.43.45. & 106,47. & 118,17. Esa.37.20. Ierem.31,9. piorum libertas. 1 Petr.2.16. lingua quod rectum est, loquitur, psalm. 37.30.
units.tr: The groanings of the godly: Rom. 8.23; 2 Cor. 5.2, 4. Glory: 1.12. The glory of the godly in the future age: Matt. 13.43; Phil. 3.21; Col. 3.4; 2 Thess. 1.7. Boasting: see Faithful. The inheritance of the godly is God: Ps. 73.26. The excellent inheritance of the godly: see Faithful. The enemies of the godly are to be destroyed, Ps. 37.22. What the righteousness of the godly ought to be: Matt. 5.20. The labour of the godly is by no means in vain: 1 Cor. 15.58; Gal. 6.9; Heb. 6.10; Rev. 14.13. Praise of God: Jer. 17.14. Free and holy: 1 Cor. 7.14. See below, Seed of the godly. The fruit and end of the deliverance of the godly: Ps. 30.12–13; 40.2, 4; 56.43, 45; 106.47; 118.17; Isa. 37.20; Jer. 31.9. The liberty of the godly: 1 Pet. 2.16. The tongue of the godly speaks what is right, Ps. 37.30.

units.la: Piorum Meditatio,1,2 & 119.v 143,147,174.&143.5. Prouerb.15, 28. piorum membra, Spiritus Sancti templa,1, Corin.6,19. piorum memoria aeterna, psal.112.6. laudabilis, prou.10,7. Mar.14.9. piorum militia qualis, & quanta,
units.tr: The meditation of the godly: Ps. 1.2; 119.143, 147, 174; 143.5; Prov. 15.28. The members of the godly are temples of the Holy Spirit, 1 Cor. 6.19. The eternal memory of the godly: Ps. 112.6; they are praiseworthy, Prov. 10.7; Mark 14.9. What the warfare of the godly is like, and how great:

units.la: Vide FIDELIVM militia , & MILITIA. piorum mors, quieta,Gen.15 14.& 25.8.Vide, FIDELIVM mors piorum mors,interdum præmatura,Esa.57.1. piorum multitudo, 49.20.Hebr.12.1.mundities,in quo sita , Ioan.15.3.Act.15. 9.piorum * Nomina in cœlis scripta, Vide ELECTI: & LIBER.piorum nota,Esa.66.5. Ezech.9. 6. Ioann.8.47.& 10.27.& 13.25. & 18.37. 2 Tim. 2.19. 1 Ioan.4.7.Apoc.7.3. Vide SIGNATI.
units.tr: See Faithful, warfare, and Warfare. The death of the godly is peaceful: Gen. 15.14; 25.8. See Faithful, death of. The death of the godly is sometimes premature: Isa. 57.1. The multitude of the godly: Gen. 49.20; Heb. 12.1. Their cleanness, and where it lies: John 15.3; Acts 15.9. The names of the godly are written in heaven: see Elect and Book. The marks of the godly: Isa. 66.5; Ezek. 9.6; John 8.47; 10.27; 13.25; 18.37; 2 Tim. 2.19; 1 John 4.7; Rev. 7.3. See Marked.

units.la: Piorum Opera,Deo præunte facta , Ioan.3.21.piorum orationes,Vide ORATIO:&, PETITIONES. Piorum paucitas,impiorum multitudinis respectu , Esa.8.16. & 53.1. Ioan.12.8.Mich.7.14.Mat.20.16.&22.14.Luc.12.32.& 13.23. Rom.9.27.1 Pet.3.10.piorum Pax,Esai.57.19. Agg.2.10.po- steritas , Psal.34.11. & 92.13. Esaiæ 54.17. & 58.11.& 65.14. Zach.8.12.piorum in primis habenda ratio , Rom.12.13. Galat.6.10.Ephe.1.15.Col.1.4.Heb.6.10,Piorum ruina lethalis non est,Prouer.24.16. Piorum salus æterna,Esa.45. 17.gratuita est,Ephes.2.v.5.8.
units.tr: The works of the godly are done with God going before them, John 3.21. The prayers of the godly: see Prayer and Petitions. The fewness of the godly, in comparison with the multitude of the wicked: Isa. 8.16; 53.1; John 12.38; Mic. 7.14; Matt. 20.16; 22.14; Luke 12.32; 13.23; Rom. 9.27; 1 Pet. 3.10. The peace of the godly: Isa. 57.19; Hag. 2.10. Their posterity: Ps. 34.11; 92.13; Isa. 54.17; 58.11; 65.14; Zech. 8.12. The godly are to be held in regard first of all: Rom. 12.13; Gal. 6.10; Eph. 1.15; Col. 1.4; Heb. 6.10. The ruin of the godly is not deadly, Prov. 24.16. The eternal salvation of the godly is in Isa. 45.17; it is a free gift, Eph. 2.5, 8.

The blessed seed of the godly. Job 42.16; Ps. 18.51; 25.13; 37.25, 29; 102.29; 112.2; Prov. 11.21; 14.26; 20.7; Isa. 44.3; 48.19; 54.13; 60.21; 65.23; Jer. 32.39; Zech. 10.7; Acts 2.39. The separation of the godly from the wicked, Matt. 13.41, 49; 25.32. The godly's words: see FAITHFUL. The simplicity of the godly: see the SIMPLICITY of the FAITHFUL. The honourable fellowship of the godly, 1 John 1.3. The hope of the godly is God, Ps. 39.8; 40.5; 91.2, 9; 142.6; Joel 3.16. The one hope of the godly, Eph. 4.4. The hope of the godly is by no means vain, Ps. 9.19; 17.7; 21.7; 25.2, 20; 28.7; 31.2; 71.1, 5; 32.10; 34.6, 9; 37.9, 40; 62.7; 71.5; 86.2; 91.2; 112.7; 119; 119.116; 125.1; 142.6; 143.8; Prov. 10.28; Isa. 26.3; 30.8; 40.31; 45.17; 49.23; 50.7; 57.13; Jer. 31.17; Rom. 5.2, 5; 8.24; 9.33; 12.12; Heb. 6.19. The godly, on account of the prosperity of the wicked.

units.la: Piorum Tentatio, Psal.73.v.12.13.Esaiae 49.14. Piorum ob populi calamitatem,tristitia,Esa.22.4.in laetitiam vertitur,Psal.30.12.& 68.14.Esa.61.3.& 65.20.Ier. 31. 13. Ioan. 16.20. Piorum victoria, Psalm. 149.6.Esai.41.15.& 54.17. Daniel. 7.22. Mich 4. 13.& 5.9.Malach.4.3.Matth.16.18. Luc. 1.71.Roman.8.37.& 16.20. 1 Corinth.15.57. 1 Ioann. 2.14. & 4. 4. & 5. 4. Apoc.12.11. Piorum victoriae fructus, Apoc. 2. 11. & 3. v.5.12. 21.& 21.7.Piorum vita,Deo consecrata,Rom.14.7.8.Col.33.Piorum vitae finis, Psalm. 118.17.& 119.175 Esai.43.7.& 60.21.& 61.3. piorum vnanimitas, Act.4.32.& 5.12.& 15.12.Rom.15.6. piorum cum Christo vnitas,Ioan. 17. 11. piorum vocatio praestantissima, 1 Thess.2.12.& 4.7.1 Petr.2.21.& 3 9.& 5.10. piorum voluptas in Deo sita,Psf.37.4. piorum zelus,119.139.Rom. 12.11.
units.tr: The temptation of the godly, Ps. 73.12, 13; Isa. 49.14. The sorrow of the godly over the calamity of the people is turned into joy, Isa. 22.4; Ps. 30.12; 68.14; Isa. 61.3; 65.20; Jer. 31.13; John 16.20. The victory of the godly, Ps. 149.6; Isa. 41.15; 54.17; Dan. 7.22; Mic. 4.13; 5.9; Mal. 4.3; Matt. 16.18; Luke 1.71; Rom. 8.37; 16.20; 1 Cor. 15.57; 1 John 2.14; 4.4; 5.4; Rev. 12.11. The fruits of the godly's victory, Rev. 2.11; 3.5, 12; 21.7. The life of the godly, consecrated to God, Rom. 14.7, 8; Col. 3.3. The end of the godly's life, Ps. 118.17; 119.175; Isa. 43.7; 60.21; 61.3. The unanimity of the godly, Acts 4.32; 5.12; 15.12; Rom. 15.6. The union of the godly with Christ, John 17.11. The most excellent calling of the godly, 1 Thess. 2.12; 4.7; 1 Pet. 2.21; 3.9; 5.10. The delight of the godly lies in God, Ps. 37.4. The zeal of the godly, Ps. 119.139; Rom. 12.11.

units.la: Piorum sub Magistratu impio & ethnico degentium exempla:Abraham sub Pharaone in Aegypto,Gen.12.10.Israelitae sub Pharaone, Exod. 12. 40. Iudaei sub Philisthaeis Iudic.15.11.parentes Dauidis sub Achis,1 Sam.22.3. Dauid cum suis sub Achis, 27.v.2.3. Elias cum septem millibus piorum, qui non flexerunt genua ipsi Baal cum Achabo & Iezabele,1 Reg.19.18. [Daniel & Iudei sub Babyloniis Daniel. 1. 2. &c. capitibus. vide libros Esdrae & Nehemie.]
units.tr: Examples of the godly living under an impious and heathen magistrate: Abraham under Pharaoh in Egypt, Gen. 12.10; the Israelites under Pharaoh, Exod. 12.40; the Jews under the Philistines, Judg. 15.11; the parents of David under Achish, 1 Sam. 22.3; David with his men under Achish, 27.2, 3; Elijah with seven thousand godly men, who had not bowed their knees to Baal, along with Ahab and Jezebel, 1 Kings 19.18. [Daniel and the Jews under the Babylonians, Dan. 1.2 etc., chapters. See the books of Ezra and Nehemiah.]

units.la: Piis male esse non potest, Esa. 3. 10. piis benefaciendum Iudic.5.23.Psalm. 16. 3. piis fauendum, & eorum innocentia tuenda. Exempla: Ionathas,1 Sam.20.32.Abimelech,22.14.piis liberatis interdum impij affliguntur, Esa. 43.v.3.4.
units.tr: It cannot go ill with the godly, Isa. 3.10. Good should be done to the godly, Judg. 5.23; Ps. 16.3. The godly are to be favoured and their innocence defended. Examples: Jonathan, 1 Sam. 20.32; Abimelech, 22.14. When the godly are delivered, the wicked are sometimes afflicted, Isa. 43.3, 4.

units.la: Pios eripit Dominus e tentatione, 2 Pet.2.9.nec finit eos vltra tentari,quam quod possunt ferre, 1 Corint.10.13.sola Dei misericordia fidunt, Psal.52.10.
units.tr: The Lord rescues the godly from temptation, 2 Pet. 2.9, and does not allow them to be tempted beyond what they can bear, 1 Cor. 10.13. They trust in God's mercy alone, Ps. 52.10.

units.la: PLACABILITAS, Καταλλαξις, συγγνωμη, est offensæ atque iniuriæ nobis factæ facilis & ex animo delectio & obliuio propter Dei præceptum, & in pristinam cum eo, qui nos offendit, amicitiam reditio atque redintegratio (Implacabilis autem animus illi contrarius est, & ab homine Christiano prorsus alienus.) 1 Cor.7.11. Vide Prouer.15.4.26.
units.tr: PLACABILITY, reconciliation [καταλλαξις], forgiveness [συγγνωμη], is the ready and heartfelt release and forgetting of an offence and injury done to us, for the sake of God's command, and the return and restoration of former friendship with the one who has wronged us. (An implacable mind is the opposite of this and wholly foreign to a Christian man.) 1 Cor. 7.11. See Prov. 15.4; 15.26.
