units.la: PLACATUR Deus oratione Mosis, Exo.32.14. Placatur Rex à viro sapiente, Prou.16.14. Esau.muneribus Gen.32.20.
units.tr: God is appeased by the prayer of Moses, Exod. 32.14. A king is appeased by a wise man, Prov. 16.14. Esau [is appeased] by gifts, Gen. 32.20.

units.la: PLACEAMVS ut Meo, orat Paulus, Rom.12.1.2. non ut placeret hominibus, prædicauit Paulus, sed Deo, Gala.1.10.1 Thess.2.4. non placendum sibi ob cognitam libertatem per Christum nobis partam, Rom.15.v.1.2. Carnales Deo non placent.8.8.
units.tr: Let us please, as I do, Paul prays, Rom. 12.1, 2. Paul preached not to please men but God, Gal. 1.10; 1 Thess. 2.4. We should not please ourselves on account of the knowledge of the freedom won for us through Christ, Rom. 15.1, 2. The carnal do not please God, Rom. 8.8.

units.la: PLAGAE Ægyptiorum, Exo.7.8.9.10.11.&c. & 12.29. Vide Ægyptvs, plagæ corporis Christi, Psal.22.18. plagæ quoé verberando inferendæ, Deut.25.v.2.3. qui plagis multis vapulabunt à Deo, Luc.12.47. Pauli plagæ 2 Cor.6.5. lauantur, Act.16.33.
units.tr: The plagues of the Egyptians, Exod. 7.8–11, etc.; 12.29. See EGYPT. The plagues of Christ's body, Ps. 22.18. Plagues to be inflicted by beating, Deut. 25.2, 3. Those who are beaten with many stripes by God, Luke 12.47. Paul's stripes, 2 Cor. 6.5. Are washed, Acts 16.33.

units.la: Plagæ morbi grauiss. Dar.3.10.& 5.v.19.34. Luc.7.21.
units.tr: Plagues of grievous disease, Dan. 3.10; 5.19, 34; Luke 7.21.

units.la: Plagæ eorum, qui verbo M.adiiciunt: Apoc.22.18. Iehova curans plagæ Ecclesiæ suæ: Esa.30.26.
units.tr: The plagues of those who add to the Word, Rev. 22.18. Jehovah heals the plagues of his Church, Isa. 30.26.

units.la: Plaga, tractus seu pars orbis summi vel infimi, Genes.4.16.&13.1. Exod.26.22.&38.9.11.12.13. Esai.11.12. Ierem.49.36. Plagæ quatuor, orientem, occidentem, aquilonem & austrum versus, 1.Par.9.24. Gen.18.14.
units.tr: A plague, a region or part of the highest or lowest quarter of the world, Gen. 4.16; 13.1; Exod. 26.22; 38.9, 11, 12, 13; Isa. 11.12; Jer. 49.36. The four quarters, toward east, west, north and south, 1 Chron. 9.24; Gen. 18.14.

units.la: PLAGIVM est, cum homines, siue liberi, siue serui surripiuntur, quod furti genus damnatur appertissimè tam iure humano, vt lege Fabia de Plagearis, quàm diuino: Deut.24.7.1 Tim.1.10. Vide Raptus.
units.tr: KIDNAPPING is when men, whether free or slaves, are seized. This kind of theft is condemned most plainly both by human law, as by the Fabian law concerning kidnappers, and by divine law: Deut. 24.7; 1 Tim. 1.10. See RAPE.

units.la: PLAGIARIIS lex posita, 1 Tim.1.10.
units.tr: A law laid down against kidnappers, 1 Tim. 1.10.

units.la: PLANGITVR Iacob ab Ægyptiis, Genes.50.10. Moses ab Israelitis, Deut.34.8. Propheta mortuus ab altero Propheta, 1 Reg.13.30. planctus super mortuum, 2 Sam.3.31 1 Thess.4.13. Vide FLERE. Stephanus, Act.8.2. V.Apoc.18.9.
units.tr: Jacob was mourned by the Egyptians, Gen. 50.10; Moses by the Israelites, Deut. 34.8. A dead prophet was mourned by another prophet, 1 Kings 13.30. Lamentation over the dead, 2 Sam. 3.31; 1 Thess. 4.13. See WEEP. Stephen, Acts 8.2. See Rev. 18.9.

units.la: PLANTA, est corpus mixtum, quod & primùm & nunc quoque, sed nunc ordinarie è terra nascitur, Dei iussu, & ad ipsius gloriam manifestandam, tamen sensu carens, terræ autem inseparabiliter adhærens: cuius Terræ succo velut lacte alitur, virescens ac facultate vegetante duntaxat præditum.
units.tr: A PLANT is a mixed body, which both first and now also, but now ordinarily, arises from the earth by God's command and to make his glory known. Yet it lacks sense and clings inseparably to the earth, from whose juice, as if from milk, it is nourished, and it is endowed only with a power of growing and flourishing.

units.la: Fines, Gloria Dei: Prou.16.4. Pf.148.9. Vsus: Gen.1 29.30 Pf.104.14.1 Tim.4.4.
units.tr: Ends: the glory of God, Prov. 16.4; Ps. 148.9. Use: Gen. 1.29, 30; Ps. 104.14; 1 Tim. 4.4.

units.la: PLANTAVIT Deus Israelem, Exo.15.17. paulus Christianos, 1 Cor.3.6. plantatio quam non plantauit Deus, eradicabitur, Matth.15.13. seu reprobi peribunt.
units.tr: God planted Israel, Exod. 15.17. Paul [planted] the Christians, 1 Cor. 3.6. Every plant that God did not plant will be uprooted, Matt. 15.13; or the reprobate will perish.
[The planting of God, Gen. 2.8; Ps. 94.9; 104.16; Isa. 60.21; 61.3.]

units.la: Plantatio plane mystica, Ezech.17.v.22.23.
units.tr: A planting wholly mystical, Ezek. 17.22, 23.

units.la: plantatio Christi Esai.51.16. Ezech.36.36.
units.tr: The planting of Christ, Isa. 51.16; Ezek. 36.36.

units.la: Plantatio per ministerium verbi, Ier.1.10. & 31.5.1 Cor. 3.v.6.7.8.
units.tr: Planting through the ministry of the Word, Jer. 1.10; 31.5; 1 Cor. 3.6–8.

units.la: Plantati à Deo misericordę, Exo.15 17. Psal.44.3. & 80.v.9. 10.16. & 92.14. Hi vineæ comparantur, Esai.5.2. Ier.2.21. & 11.17. & 24.6.
units.tr: Planted by God's mercy, Exod. 15.17; Ps. 44.3; 80.9, 10, 16; 92.14. These are compared to a vine, Isa. 5.2; Jer. 2.21; 11.17; 24.6.

units.la: Plantat Deus hypocritas, ad tempus, Ier. 12. 2. & 45.4. Ezech.17.v.8.10. & 19.10.]
units.tr: God plants hypocrites for a time, Jer. 12.2; 45.4; Ezek. 17.8, 10; 19.10.

units.la: PLEBS Dei Israel, Rom.11.2.
units.tr: The people of God, Israel, Rom. 11.2.

units.la: PLEIADES stellæ solo Dei nutu impediri possunt, Iob. 38.31.
units.tr: The Pleiades, stars which can be held back only by the nod of God, Job 38.31.

units.la: PLENITVDO Christi, Ecclesia, Ephes.1.13. Vide ECCLESIA.
units.tr: The fullness of Christ, the Church, Eph. 1.13. See CHURCH.

units.la: [plenitudo Christi, Ioan.1.16. Col.1.19.]
units.tr: [The fullness of Christ, John 1.16; Col. 1.19.]

units.la: PLENITVDO temporum, Galat. 4.4. Ephes.1.10. vbi per temporum plenitudinem, aut tempus plenum, intelligit Apostolus illud tempus, quo exhibitus est Christus mundo, hoc est, tempus illud, quod reuolutis seculis tam diu expectatum, tandem aduenerit. plenitudo terræ Dauidi Psal.24.1. & paulo, 1 Cor.10.26. significat infinitam illam rerum omnium copiam, quibus plena est terra. plenitudo, Coloss.1.19. non pro ipsâ Deitate, vt Coloss.2.9. sed pro cumulatissima omnium rerum diuinarum copia, (quam Scholastici gratiam habitualem, à gratia vnionis distinctam, appellant,) ex qua in Christo, tanquam inexhausto fonte omnis gratiæ, in nos pro cuiusque membri modulo, deriuentur: vt hic locus comparetur cum Ioan.1.16. & 3.v.34 35.
units.tr: The fullness of time, Gal. 4.4; Eph. 1.10, where by "the fullness of time" or "a full time" the Apostle understands that time at which Christ was revealed to the world, that is, the time which, after the ages had turned, at last arrived after being so long awaited. "The fullness of the earth" (Ps. 24.1; and, in Paul, 1 Cor. 10.26) signifies that infinite abundance of all things with which the earth is full. "Fullness" in Col. 1.19 is not used of the Deity itself, as in Col. 2.9, but of the most abundant store of all divine things, which the Schoolmen call habitual grace, distinct from the grace of union, and which flows from Christ, as from an inexhaustible fount of all grace, into us, according to the measure of each member. Thus this passage is to be compared with John 1.16 and 3.34, 35.

units.tr: RAIN is the dissolving of a cloud, which hung aloft, into drops of water, that is, the melting of the cloud, which for many reasons is brought about by God, by the force of an arriving heat which softens and melts that cloud, Job 37.6; 28.26.

units.tr: Rain from God alone, Gen. 2.5; Deut. 28.12; 1 Kings 8.36; 2 Chron. 6.26; 1 Kings 18.1; Job 5.10; 38.26, 28; Ps. 68.10; 65.10, 11; 147.8; Jer. 5.24; 10.13; 14.22; 51.16; Hos. 2.23; Amos 4.7; Zech. 8.12; 10.1; Matt. 5.45; Acts 14.17. A rain at the time of the flood, Gen. 7.12. Abundant rain at the voice of Elijah, 1 Kings 18.45. Morning and evening rain is looked for by the farmer, James 5.7. Rain was given from heaven to the land of promise, Deut. 11.11, 12. Rains are sometimes withheld on account of sin, 1 Kings 8.35; 17.1. Seasonal rains are given to the obedient, Lev. 26.4; Deut. 11.14; 28.12.

units.la: Πνεῦμα, id est spiritus,pro phantasmate,seu spectro,Luc.24.37.vt explicatur Matt.24.26. Hebræorum more pro impulsu,seu afflatu Dei, interdum per Spiritum suum agentis,Dan.4.v.5.6. & 5.v.11.14. (unde Spiritus intelligentiæ sapientiæ, pietatis, consilij, & alij eiusmodi Spiritus in Scripturis commemorati) interdum per Spiritus malos sua iudicia exercendis,unde Spiritus fornicationum,auaritiæ,vertiginis,soporis,& alij similes afflatus, 2 Paralip. 18.22.Rom.11.8.& alibi sæpe pro impulsu,seu afflatu Diabolico, Luc.4.33. quamuis & pro Diabolo ipso accipere possimus,vt sit Hebraica geminatio,Spiritus Diabolicus pro Diabolo ipso, quales geminationes reperire est Psal.40.lutum cœni, pro luto cœnoso, hoc est, cœno profundissimo,Dan.12.2.terra pulueris,pro pulvere terrestri, id est humo.Vide Apoc.16.14. πνεῦμα, id est spiritus, idem declarans quod ψυχή.1 Cor.6 20.& 7.34.Act.7.59.Heb.12.9.Vide Spiritus.
units.tr: Spirit [πνεῦμα, pneuma], that is, spirit, is used for a phantasm or apparition, Luke 24.37, as is explained at Matt. 24.26. In the manner of the Hebrews it is used for the impulse or breath of God, who at times acts through his own Spirit, Dan. 4.5, 6; 5.11, 14 (whence the Spirit of understanding, wisdom, piety, counsel, and other such spirits mentioned in Scripture). At times it is used for evil spirits by which God executes his judgements, whence the spirit of fornication, of avarice, of giddiness, of stupor, and other similar impulses: 2 Chron. 18.22; Rom. 11.8; and often elsewhere for a diabolical impulse or breath, Luke 4.33; although we may also take it for the Devil himself, so that it is a Hebrew doubling, "a diabolical spirit" for the Devil himself. Such doublings are found at Ps. 40 ("mire of mud" for muddy mire, that is, the deepest mud); Dan. 12.2 ("dust of earth" for earthly dust, that is, the ground). See Rev. 16.14. Pneuma [πνεῦμα], that is, spirit, declaring the same thing as psyche [ψυχή]: 1 Cor. 6.20; 7.34; Acts 7.59; Heb. 12.9. See SPIRIT.

units.la: POCVLVM metonymicè, pro eo quòd poculo continetur. Matth.20.22. Lucæ 22.20. 1 Corinth.11.25. (Vide CALIX.) Hebræorum more, pro modo vel iræ Dei ac pœnæ peccatis nostris inflictæ, Psalm.11.6. Matth.26.39. (vbi Dominus nostram personam sustinet) vel afflictionis, quæ ad nos probandos & confirmandos immittitur à Deo, Mat. 20.22. vel lætitiæ qua cumulantur fideles, Psalm.23.5. significat denique cuiusque sortem & conditionem, 16.5.
units.tr: POCULUM, by metonymy, for what is contained in the cup: Matt. 20.22; Luke 22.20; 1 Cor. 11.25. (See CALIX.) In the Hebrew manner it means the measure or wrath of God and the punishment inflicted on our sins, Ps. 11.6; Matt. 26.39 (where the Lord bears our person); or the affliction which God sends upon us to test and confirm us, Matt. 20.22; or the joy with which the faithful are filled, Ps. 23.5. Finally, it signifies anyone's lot and condition, Ps. 16.5.

units.la: POENA: Pœnæ impiorum in thesauris reconditæ, Deut.32.34. delinquentibus pœna à Iudicibus irroganda, 25.1. pœna singulorum peccatorum, Vide PECCATA, pœna damni facti, Exodi 22.5. furis, v.1. &c. homicidij, 21.12. idololatriæ, 22.20. per superbiam peccantis, Numer.15.30. talionis, Genes.9.6. Exodi 21.23. Leuit.24.17. Deuter.19.19. pœnarum tria genera Dauidi proposita, 1 Paral.21.9. pœna Heli, 1 Sam.2.29.c.
units.tr: PUNISHMENT: The punishments of the wicked are laid up in treasuries, Deut. 32.34. Offenders are to be punished by judges, Deut. 25.1. The punishment of individual sins: see SINS. Punishment for damage done: Exod. 22.5; for theft, v. 1, etc.; for homicide, Exod. 21.12; for idolatry, Exod. 22.20; for sin committed through pride, Num. 15.30; retaliation (lex talionis): Gen. 9.6; Exod. 21.23; Lev. 24.17; Deut. 19.19. The three kinds of punishment set before David: 1 Chron. 21.9. The punishment of Eli: 1 Sam. 2.29, etc.

units.la: POENITERE pro dolorem capere, 2 Cor.7.8.
units.tr: TO REPENT, meaning to feel grief: 2 Cor. 7.8.

units.la: POENITENTIA, est vera ad Deum vitæ nostræ conuersio, à sincero & serio Dei timore profecta, quæ carnis nostræ veterisque hominis mortificatione, & noui viuificatione constat. Ps.34.13. Rom.12.9. Ier.4.4. Causa efficiens, Deus per Spiritū S. Ier.31.18. Deut.30.16. Act.11.6. Quam efficit in nobis per prædicationem Legis & Euangelij: Luc.3.3. & 24.46.47. Act.2.37. & 26.17. Materialis in qua, est mens, cor, voluntas, & omnes effectus hominis, in quibus fit mutatio per conuersionem: Rom.12.2. Gal.5.24. Formalis, est renouatio mentis humanæ, vt probet quæ sit bona Dei voluntas, secundum quam cor affectus & actiones totâ vitâ dirigantur. Finalis, Gloria Dei, Mat.5.16. proximi ædificatio, Luc.22.32. Salus nostra, Act.11.18. de qua nobis per nouâ obedientiâ constet: 2 Pet.1.10.11. Effectus, Vita Christiana, seu officia pietatis erga Deum, charitatis erga proximum, & in tota vita sanctimonia, Mat.3.8. Luc.1.75. &c.
units.tr: REPENTANCE is the true conversion of our life to God, proceeding from a sincere and earnest fear of God, and consisting in the mortification of our flesh and old man and the quickening of the new. Ps. 34.13; Rom. 12.9; Jer. 4.4. Efficient cause: God, through the Holy Spirit, Jer. 31.18; Deut. 30.16; Acts 11.6. He brings it about in us through the preaching of the Law and the Gospel: Luke 3.3; 24.46-47; Acts 2.37; 26.17. Material cause: the mind, heart, will and all the faculties of man, in which the change takes place through conversion: Rom. 12.2; Gal. 5.24. Formal cause: the renewal of the human mind, so that it may prove what is the good will of God, according to which the heart, affections and actions are directed throughout life. Final cause: the glory of God, Matt. 5.16; the edification of our neighbour, Luke 22.32; our salvation, Acts 11.18, of which we are assured through new obedience: 2 Pet. 1.10-11. Effect: the Christian life, or the duties of piety towards God and of charity towards our neighbour, and holiness in the whole of life: Matt. 3.8; Luke 1.75, etc.

units.la: Poenitentiam agentes, etiam poenarum corporalium mitigationem impetrant. exempla: Abimelech, Gen.20.1. &c. Maria poenitentiam agens liberatur à lepra, Num.12.11. Israelitæ poenitentiam agentes, impetrant remedium contra serpentes ignitos, 21.7. poenitentiam agentibus promittitur liberatio à fame, peste, locusta, morbis, hostibus, captiuitate, &c. 1 Regum 8.28. &c. 2 Paral.6.1. &c. Achab, 1 Reg.21.v.4.5. Iosias, 2 Reg.22. verl.19.20. Dauid, 2 Sam.24.v.16.17. 1 Paral.21. v.16.17. Roboam & principes eius, 2 Paral.12.v.7.8. Ezechias, 32.26. Vide Ierem.25.5. Dan. 4.24.27.
units.tr: Those who repent also obtain a mitigation of bodily punishments. Examples: Abimelech, Gen. 20.1, etc. Miriam, repenting, is freed from leprosy, Num. 12.11. The Israelites, repenting, obtain a remedy against the fiery serpents, 21.7. To those repenting is promised deliverance from famine, pestilence, locusts, diseases, enemies, captivity, etc., 1 Kings 8.28, etc.; 2 Chron. 6.1, etc. Ahab, 1 Kings 21 vv. 4, 5. Josiah, 2 Kings 22 vv. 19, 20. David, 2 Sam. 24 vv. 16, 17; 1 Chron. 21 vv. 16, 17. Rehoboam and his princes, 2 Chron. 12 vv. 7, 8. Hezekiah, 32.26. See Jer. 25.5; Dan. 4.24, 27.

units.tr: POLLUTE: to hold as polluted and unclean, Acts 10.15. They polluted the name of God by sacrificing to the idol Moloch, Lev. 18.21 and 21.3. The name of God is polluted by perjury, 19.12.

Tit.1.6. nominatim Regibus, Deuteron.17. 17. polygamiæ exempla: Lamech, Genes.4.19. Abraham, 16. versi.2.3. Esau, 26.34.& 28.9. Iacob, 29.29.& 30.verfic.4.5. Gedeon, Iudic.8.30. Elcana, 1 Samuel.1.2. Dauid, 25.ver.42. 43.44.2 Samu.5.13. Roboam, 1 Paral.11.v.18 19.20. Abia, 13. 21. Ioas, 24.3. Solomoni fœminæ erant 700. concubinæ 300.1 Reg.11.3.
units.tr: POLYGAMY is forbidden to all in general, Gen. 2.24; Mal. 2 vv. 14, 15; Matt. 19.5; 1 Cor. 7 vv. 2, 3; 1 Tim. 3.2; Titus 1.6; and expressly to kings, Deut. 17.17. Examples of polygamy: Lamech, Gen. 4.19; Abraham, 16 vv. 2, 3; Esau, 26.34 and 28.9; Jacob, 29.29 and 30 vv. 4, 5; Gideon, Judg. 8.30; Elkanah, 1 Sam. 1.2; David, 25 vv. 42, 43, 44; 2 Sam. 5.13; Rehoboam, 1 Chron. 11 vv. 18, 19, 20; Abijah, 13, 21; Joash, 24.3. Solomon had 700 wives and 300 concubines, 1 Kings 11.3.

units.tr: FRUITS, mystical: Song 4 vv. 13, 16; 6.11; 7.13. Fruits, precious things, Deut. 33 vv. 13, 14, 15; orchards, gardens, Eccl. 2.5. See Lev. 26.4; Joel 1.12.

units.la: PONERE, ex Hebraeorum idiotismo, pro facere vt sint; Matth.22.44. seu reddere & efficere, Actor.2.35. ponere verba in ore, Numer.23.12. 2 Corinth.5.19. dicitur, qui aliquius opera vtitur in re quapiam significanda: sed cum de Deo agitur, peculiaris est huius formulae emphasis, qua significatur & cor loquentis à Domino impelli, & linguam regi, Numer.23.16.& alibi saepe, apud prophetas maximè.
units.tr: PUT, in the Hebrew idiom, means to make that they be, Matt. 22.44; or to render and bring about, Acts 2.35; to put words in the mouth, Num. 23.12; 2 Cor. 5.19. It is said of one who uses another's work in signifying something; but when it concerns God, the emphasis of this formula is peculiar, signifying both that the heart of the speaker is impelled by the Lord and that the tongue is governed, Num. 23.16, and often elsewhere, especially among the prophets.

units.la: PONTIFEX à Deo vocatur, & ad quid, Heb.5.v.1.2.3.& 8.3.a mortuum ingredi prohibetur, Leu.21.1.&c. pontifex non ster Christus, Hebr.2.17.& 3.1.& 4.14.& 5.5.& 6.20.& 8.
