units.tr: PONTUS, a region of Asia Minor: Acts 2:9; 1 Pet. 1:1.

units.la: POPVLVS vere beatus, Psalm.33.12. Prou.29.18. populus Dei qualis, Esa.62.12. populus Dei, Christiani, 1 Petr.2.9 in pe pulum assumti Israelitæ, Exo.6 7.&19.v.5.6. Deut.4.20. 7.7.&27 9.&29.13. Dauid 2 Sam.6.21. & 7.8. 1 Reg.8.16. populus Israel maris arenæ par, 1 Reg.4.20. à Deo redem tus, Psal.77.16.
units.tr: PEOPLE truly blessed: Ps. 33:12; Prov. 29:18. What kind of people is God's people: Isa. 62:12. The people of God, Christians: 1 Pet. 2:9. The Israelites taken as a people: Exod. 6:7; 19:5-6; Deut. 4:20; 7:7; 27:9; 29:13. David: 2 Sam. 6:21; 7:8; 1 Kings 8:16. The people of Israel as numerous as the sand of the sea: 1 Kings 4:20. Redeemed by God: Ps. 77:16.

units.la: POPVLI dissipatio unde, Prouer.29.18. populi inconstantia.
units.tr: THE SCATTERING OF A PEOPLE, whence it comes: Prov. 29:18. The inconstancy of a people.

units.la: Vide INCONSTANTIA. Populi seniores, Vide SENIORES. populis omnibus missus Christus, Luc.2.31.
units.tr: See INCONSTANCY. The elders of the people: see ELDERS. Christ sent to all peoples: Luke 2:31.

units.la: [POPVLVS Latinis proprie significat cœtum hominū unius civitatis, Reipublicæ, monarchiæ, iure & communione officiorum, societatum, à quodam magistratu gubernatum. Præterea Hebræis etiam significat paucos homines vel multitudinem incompositam, aliquando etiam familiam amplam. 2. Speciatim populus Israelis, est numerosa Iacobi Patriarchæ posteritas 12. tribuum, sub Mosè Iudicibus, Regibus & post captivitatem.
units.tr: [In Latin, POPULUS properly means an assembly of men of one city or commonwealth or monarchy, bound by law and by common duties and associations, and governed by a certain magistrate. Among the Hebrews it also means a few men or a disorderly multitude, and sometimes even a large household. 2. Specifically, the people of Israel is the numerous posterity of the patriarch Jacob in the twelve tribes, under Moses, the judges, the kings, and after the captivity.

units.la: 3. Populi seu populorum nomine frequenter etiam apud Prophetas incircuncisi, hostes Ecclesiæ, & Gentiles ad Christum convertendi intelliguntur. 4. Nonnunquam, præsertim quum de Deo & Christo agitur, & pro nomen suus, meus, tuus, vel nomen Dei appositum occurrit Ecclesiam, vel ex Iudæis tantùm, vel ex Iudæis & Gentilibus constitutam indicat, quas significationes ex contextus circumstantiis quùm facile dignosce e possint studiosi, non distinguimus amplius.]
units.tr: 3. By the name of peoples or nations, the Prophets often also understand the uncircumcised, enemies of the Church, and Gentiles to be converted to Christ. 4. Sometimes, especially when God and Christ are spoken of, and the words "his," "my," "your," or the name of God occur in apposition, the Church is indicated, composed either of Jews only or of Jews and Gentiles. Students can easily distinguish these meanings from the circumstances of the context, so we do not distinguish them further.]

units.la: PORCVS: porcum non comedunt Iudæi, Leu.11. v.7.8. Deut.14.8. porci, quos Dæmones inualerunt, mortui sunt, Matth.8.v.32.33. Marc.5.13. Luc.8.33. porci infideles, impij, homines desperatæ malitiæ & impuritatis, quibus sordet Dei verbum. Matt.7.6. V.Sus.
units.tr: PIG: The Jews do not eat pork: Lev. 11:7-8; Deut. 14:8. The pigs into which the demons entered died: Matt. 8:32-33; Mark 5:13; Luke 8:33. Pigs are unbelievers, the impious, men of hopeless malice and impurity, to whom God's word is repugnant: Matt. 7:6. See SWINE.

units.la: PORPHYRIO auis, quæ non vescuntur Iudæi, Leu.11.19. Deut.14.17.
units.tr: PORPHYRION, a bird which the Jews do not eat: Lev. 11:19; Deut. 14:17.

units.la: PORTÆ, pro loco ante portam, ubi conuentus fiebant, iudicia agitabantur, Gen.23.10.& 34.20. Psal.9.15. quia at vrbiū munitiones & propugnacula in portis earum co locabantur veteribus: hinc factum est, ut portę accipiantur subinde pro vrbibus & consilio & propugnaculis muni-tis. Gen. 22. 17. & 24. 60. ratio Phraseos est (vt iam dixi) quia propugnacula in portis collocari, & Magistratus ibi ius dicere solebant, Deut. 22. 15. inde illud quoque liquet, quid apud Matthæum: (cap. 16. 18. portæ inferorum nihil nocituræ Ecclesiæ Christi.) Portarum inferorum nomine sit intelligendum, nempe tota Satanæ potentia: hoc est, quicquid vel consilio, vel viribus & machinationibus, ac mille technis potest, id denique quod Paulus ἐχυρώματα, hoc est, munitiones vocat. 2 Corinth. 10. 4. Seruo, qui perpetuæ ieruituti se addicebat, in portis perforari solebat auris subulâ, Exo. 21. 6. Deut. 15. 7. Vide Psalm. 40. 7. Hebr. 10. 7. portæ vrbis Gaza à Samsone sublatæ, Iudic. 16. 3.
units.tr: GATES: for the place before the gate where assemblies were held and judgments pronounced: Gen. 23:10; 34:20; Ps. 9:15. Because in ancient times the fortifications and bulwarks of cities were placed at their gates, gates came to be taken from time to time for cities, for counsel, and for fortified defences: Gen. 22:17; 24:60. The reason for this phrase (as I have already said) is that bulwarks were set up at the gates and magistrates customarily pronounced justice there: Deut. 22:15. From this it is also clear what is meant in Matthew (16:18), that the gates of hell will not prevail against the Church of Christ. By the name "gates of hell" must be understood the whole power of Satan, that is, whatever can be accomplished by counsel, by force, by machinations, and by a thousand devices; in short, what Paul calls ἐχυρώματα [echyrōmata], that is, fortifications: 2 Cor. 10:4. A servant who bound himself to perpetual servitude used to have his ear pierced with an awl at the gate: Exod. 21:6; Deut. 15:17. See Ps. 40:7; Heb. 10:7. The gates of the city of Gaza were carried off by Samson: Judg. 16:3.

units.la: [porta, portæ Castrorum, Ciuitatum, Tabernaculi, templi, &c. palatij. portæ græcæ carceris. porta angusta & lata, Matth. 7. 13. 14. porta cœli Gen. 28. 17. portæ ciuitatis cœlestis, Apoc. 21. 12. &c. portæ inimicorum, Genes. 22. 17. & 24. 60. portæ mortis, inferi, Iob 38. 17. Psalm. 9. 14. & 107. 18. Esai. 38. 10. portæ mysticæ, Cantic. 7. 13. Esai. 54. 12. & 60. 11.]
units.tr: [gate, gates of camps, cities, the tabernacle, the temple, etc., of a palace; the Greek gates of a prison; the narrow and the wide gate: Matt. 7:13-14; the gate of heaven: Gen. 28:17; the gates of the heavenly city: Rev. 21:12, etc.; the gates of enemies: Gen. 22:17; 24:60; the gates of death, of hell: Job 38:17; Ps. 9:14; 107:18; Isa. 38:10; the mystical gates: Song 7:13; Isa. 54:12; 60:11.]

units.la: PORTARE, pro tueri, Heb. 1. 3. portauit Deus filios Israel, Exodi 19. 4. Deut. 32. 11. V. Psal. 91. 11. 12.
units.tr: TO BEAR, in the sense of to protect: Heb. 1:3. God bore the sons of Israel: Exod. 19:4; Deut. 32:11. See Ps. 91:11-12.

units.la: [PORTENTA, extraordinaria Dei opera, tum in cœlo, tum in terris, Deut. 4. 34. Iosh. 24. 5. &c. 2 par. 32. 31. Esa. 20. 3. Marc. 13. 22. Hebr. 2. 4.]
units.tr: [PORTENTS, the extraordinary works of God, both in heaven and on earth: Deut. 4:34; Josh. 24:5, etc.; 2 Chron. 32:31; Isa. 20:3; Mark 13:22; Heb. 2:4.]

units.la: [PORTICVS templi, 1 Reg. 6. 3. & 7. v. 6. &c. Bethesda, Ioan. 5. 2. Salomonis, Ioan. 10. 23. Act. 5. 12.]
units.tr: [PORCHES of the temple: 1 Kings 6:3; 7:6, etc.; of Bethesda: John 5:2; of Solomon: John 10:23; Acts 5:12.]

units.la: PORTIVS Festus Iudææ præses, Act. 24. 28.
units.tr: PORCIUS Festus, governor of Judea: Acts 24:27.

units.la: POSSE, pro velle positum, Atticorum more, Marc. 6. 5. sed tamen notandum est hoc dicendi genus, quo significatur homines incredulos & ingratos, quasi Deo manus vincire, ne ipsis opem ferat, quò spectant illa Dei verba ad Moysen, Exodi 32. 10. &, Non posse, pro, non velle: Hoc enim est Dei, velle quod posse, vt loquitur Tertullianus.
units.tr: TO BE ABLE, used for to be willing, after the manner of the Attic writers: Mark 6:5. But it must be noted that this way of speaking, by which unbelieving and ungrateful men are signified, is as if they bound God's hands so that he cannot bring them help; to this refer those words of God to Moses: Exod. 32:10. And "not to be able" means "not to be willing." For it is characteristic of God to will what he can, as Tertullian puts it.

units.la: POSSIDERE animas per patientiam, iubentur Apostoli, Luc. 21. 19. hoc est, vt quamuis multa eos und que mala circumstent, fruantur nihilominus virtute sua, illa omnia fortitèr sustinendo. possidere vas suum cum honore, 1 Thes. 4. 4. est corpus suum ab omni labe purum conseruare. 2 V 1 Cor. 7. 29. &c. Qui regnum D. non possidebunt. Cor. 6. 9. &c.
units.tr: The Apostles are commanded to possess their souls through patience: Luke 21:19; that is, although many evils surround them on every side, they nevertheless enjoy their own strength by bearing all these things bravely. To possess one's vessel in honour: 1 Thess. 4:4, is to keep one's body pure from every stain. 1 Cor. 7:29, etc.: those who will not possess the kingdom of God: 1 Cor. 6:9, etc.
1 Cor. 6:9, etc.

units.la: Possessio Leuitarum Deus, Numer.18.20. Deut.10.9. & 18. Iof.13.v.14. 33. Ezech.44.28. Iobi, Iob.1.3. Vide Apoc.21.7. Cor.3.22.
units.tr: God is the possession of the Levites: Num. 18:20; Deut. 10:9; 18; Josh. 13:14, 33; Ezek. 44:28. Job's possession: Job 1:3. See Rev. 21:7; 1 Cor. 3:22.

units.la: Posterior a Dei videt Moses, Exodi 33.23.
units.tr: Moses sees God's back: Exod. 33:23.

units.la: Potentia, pro eximiis & excellentibus donis Spiritus sancti, Act.6.8. potentia Dei. Hebraismus, pro, potens Deus. Mat.26.64. vt patet ex Luc.22.69. potentia Dei est Euangelium, Rom.1.16. hoc est, organum Dei vere potens et efficax ad seruandum. V. Deus.
units.tr: Power, for the outstanding and excellent gifts of the Holy Spirit: Acts 6:8. The power of God is a Hebraism for the powerful God: Matt. 26:64, as is clear from Luke 22:69. The power of God is the Gospel: Rom. 1:16; that is, an instrument of God truly powerful and effective for saving. See God.

units.la: Potestas, μετωνυμικῶς, non pro ipso iure imperandi, sed pro regionibus imperio subditis, Lucae 4.6. pro potestatis & dominij symbolo, 1 Corinth.11.10 potestas Dei, V. Deus. Potestas omnis a Deo, Ioan.19.11. Rom.13.1. Potestatis abusus exemplum: Pilatus, Ioann.19.10. potestates in Ecclesia. Cor.12.28. potestas & principatus tribuitur etiam regno tenebrarum, Coloss.2.15. Vide Diabolus. Potestates coelorum, Hebraismus, pro potentibus coelis, Mat.24.29. Dicuntur autem coeli potentes, tum ob illorum corporum inenarrabilem firmitatem, tum etiam ob illorum minimam, in moderanda inferiorum corporum temperie facultatem.
units.tr: Power, by metonymy, not for the right of ruling itself but for the regions subject to rule: Luke 4:6; as a symbol of power and lordship: 1 Cor. 11:10. The power of God: see God. All power is from God: John 19:11; Rom. 13:1. An example of the abuse of power: Pilate, John 19:10. Powers in the Church: 1 Cor. 12:28. Power and dominion are also ascribed to the kingdom of darkness: Col. 2:15. See Devil. The powers of heaven: a Hebraism for the powerful heavens, Matt. 24:29. The heavens are called powerful both because of the inexpressible firmness of those bodies and because of their least power in moderating the temperature of the lower bodies.

units.la: Potionem vnam potare in vnum Spiritum, 1 Corinth.13.est, vno viuifico sanguinis Domini potu participes fieri vnius Spiritus ipsius, qui per omnia membra permeans singula viuificet, reddatque suis functionibus idonea. Vide Isai.51.17. Ierem.25.15. &c. Psalm.75.9. Apocal.14.8. & 16.19.
units.tr: To drink one drink into one Spirit: 1 Cor. 12:13, means to become partakers, by drinking the one life-giving blood of the Lord, of the one Spirit himself, who penetrates all the members, gives life to each, and renders them fit for their functions. See Isa. 51:17; Jer. 25:15, etc.; Ps. 75:9; Rev. 14:8; 16:19.

units.la: Potus spiritualis, Ioann.6.55. 1 Cor.10.4. potus pro tota coena, 12.13. potus immundus, Leuit.11.34. V. Matth.10.42. & 25.37.
units.tr: Spiritual drink: John 6:55; 1 Cor. 10:4. Drink for the whole supper: 1 Cor. 10:4 (cf. 12:13). Unclean drink: Lev. 11:34. See Matt. 10:42; 25:37.

units.la: Praeceptum magnum. Vide Mandatum magnum.
units.tr: The great commandment. See the Great Commandment.

units.la: Praecepta Dei filiis inculcanda, Deut.6.20. Vide Parentes. praecepta non bona, quomodo Israelitis data. Ezech.20.25. praecepta Decalogi, Exodi.20.1. &c. Deut.5.6 &c. in duabus Tabulis scripta, v.22. praecepta de charitate, prouerb.3.27. &c. Vide Charitas. praecepta fiant in agnitione Dei, & charitate, 1 Ioan.2.3.
units.tr: The precepts of God to be impressed on children: Deut. 6:20. See Parents. Precepts that are not good, how they were given to the Israelites: Ezek. 20:25. The precepts of the Decalogue: Exod. 20:1, etc.; Deut. 5:6, etc., written on two tables: v. 22. Precepts about love: Prov. 3:27, etc. See Charity. Precepts are to be carried out in the knowledge of God and in love: 1 John 2:3.

units.la: Praeceptio diuersorum. Exempla, optimi Manasses, 2 Paral.33.16. iniquissimi: Saul, 1 Sam.19. Achab, 1 Reg.21.8. 9.10. Ioas, 2 paral.24.21. Nabuchodonosor, Dan.3.19. Claudius, Actor.18.2. princeps Sacerdotum, 23.2. Vide PRAE-
units.tr: A variety of examples. Examples of the best: Manasseh, 2 Chron. 33:16. Of the most wicked: Saul, 1 Sam. 19; Ahab, 1 Kings 21:8-10; Joash, 2 Chron. 24:21; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3:19; Claudius, Acts 18:2; the high priest, Acts 23:2. See PRAE-

units.la: PRECEPTA custodientibus Deus misericors, Deut.7.9. seruantibus, benedictio: non seruantibus, maledictio, Exodi 20.v.5.6. Leuit.26.v.3 14, Deut.7.11. &c.
units.tr: PRECEPTS: God is merciful to those who keep them: Deut. 7:9; blessing to those who keep them, curse to those who do not: Exod. 20:5-6; Lev. 26:3, 14; Deut. 7:11, etc.

units.la: PRAECVRSOR noster Christus, Heb.6.20. Vide Ioh.14. 1. &c.
units.tr: FORERUNNER: our Christ: Heb. 6:20. See John 14:1, etc.

units.la: PRAEDA æquo dividenda, Deut.20.14. Num.31.v.26.27. Iosue 22.8 1 Sam.30.24. Exempla: Moses, Num.31.27. Iosuah, Ios.8.v.2.27. & 11.14. & 22.8. Israelitæ, 1 Sam.14.v.31. 32. Dauid, 30.verf.22.24.25. Iosaphat, 2 Paral.20.25. Viri Israel, 28.14. qui prædatur, etiam ipse prædabitur, Esa.33.1. Vide SPOLIVM.
units.tr: BOOTY to be divided equally: Deut. 20:14; Num. 31:26-27; Josh. 22:8; 1 Sam. 30:24. Examples: Moses, Num. 31:27; Joshua, Josh. 8:2, 27; 11:14; 22:8. The Israelites, 1 Sam. 14:31-32. David, 30:22, 24-25. Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 20:25. The men of Israel, 28:14. He who plunders shall himself also be plundered: Isa. 33:1. See SPOIL.

units.la: PRAEDESTINATIO æterna vocationis fidei causa est, Ro. 8.30. Eph.1.v.4.5 11.2 Tim.1.9.1 Pet.1.2. ob prædestinationem non disputandum cum Deo, Rom.9.20.
units.tr: PREDESTINATION is the eternal cause of calling and of faith: Rom. 8:30; Eph. 1:4-5; 2 Tim. 1:9; 1 Pet. 1:2. One must not dispute with God about predestination: Rom. 9:20.

units.la: PRAEDESTINATIO, est actus diuini beneplaciti, quo Deus ab æterno proposuit in sese de universitate creaturarum, certas aliquas, gratiæ & gloriæ suæ, participes efficere, in Christo, ad laudem suam, & salutem ipsarum. Eph 1,5, Deus prædestinauit nos, quos adoptaret in filios per Iesum Christum in sese, pro beneuolo affectu voluntatis suæ: ad laudem gloriosæ suæ gratiæ, qua nos gratis effecit sibi gratos in illo dilecto, &c. V. Electio.
units.tr: PREDESTINATION is the act of the divine good pleasure by which God purposed from eternity, in himself, concerning the whole universe of creatures, to make certain of them partakers of his grace and glory in Christ, to his own praise and their salvation. Eph. 1:5: God predestined us, whom he would adopt as sons through Jesus Christ in himself, according to the kindly disposition of his will, to the praise of the glory of his grace, by which he made us acceptable to himself in the Beloved, etc. See Election.

units.la: PRAEIRE, improprie etiam de iis dicitur, quos nemo sequitur, Matth. 21.31. sensus dicti est: Cessantibus & recusantibus vobis, properant ad regnum Dei, ut vos oportuerit saltem eorum exemplum imitari.
units.tr: To go before is also said, improperly, of those whom no one follows (Matt. 21.31). The sense of the saying is: while you hold back and refuse, they hasten into the kingdom of God, so you ought at least to imitate their example.

units.la: PRAEIVDICIA cauenda sunt, ne, quos damnauerimus, absoluere cogamur, Act.16 35.
units.tr: Prejudgements must be guarded against, lest we be compelled to absolve those whom we have condemned (Acts 16.35).

units.la: PRAEDICATIO, prius ministerij Apostolici pensum, Matth. 28.v.19.20. Marc,16.15. prædicationis Apostolicæ summa, Matth.10.7. Mar.6.12. finis eius, 1 Ioan.1.5. prædicatio pauli qualis, 1 Cor.2.4 1 Thess.2.3.
units.tr: PREACHING: the first part of the apostolic ministry (Matt. 28.19-20; Mark 16.15). The sum of apostolic preaching (Matt. 10.7; Mark 6.12). Its end (1 John 1.5). What Paul's preaching was like (1 Cor. 2.4; 1 Thess. 2.3).

units.la: PRAEDICAT Christus in nau i, Matth. 13.2. Marc. 4.1. qui prædicat, prædicet Dei sermones, 1 Pet.4.11. prædicauit Christus semper palam, Ioann.18.20. prædicare non possunt, nisi sint missi, Roman.10.15. prædicantibus Apostolis Deus dat incrementum, Actor.2.47,1 Cor.3.6.
units.tr: PREACHES: Christ preaches in a ship (Matt. 13.2; Mark 4.1). Whoever preaches should preach the words of God (1 Pet. 4.11). Christ always preached openly (John 18.20). They cannot preach unless they are sent (Rom. 10.15). When the apostles preach, God gives the increase (Acts 2.47; 1 Cor. 3.6).

units.la: PRAEDICTIONES, Vide PROPHETIAE.
units.tr: PREDICTIONS: see PROPHECIES.

units.la: [prædictio Dei, 2 Sam.7.11. Christi, Marc.13.23. Angeli, Matt. 28.7. prophetæ Dei, Gen. 41.54.1 Reg.13 32. Act, 1.16. Rom.9.29. Iud.verf.17. pseudoprophetæ, Deut.13.1, & 18.22.]
units.tr: [Prediction of God (2 Sam. 7.11); of Christ (Mark 13.23); of an angel (Matt. 28.7); of prophets of God (Gen. 41.54; 1 Kings 13.32; Acts 1.16; Rom. 9.29; Jude v. 17); of false prophets (Deut. 13.1 and 18.22).]

units.la: Praedo vendens hominem moriatur, Deut. 24. 7. Exo. 21.16.
units.tr: A kidnapper who sells a man shall die (Deut. 24.7; Exod. 21.16).

units.la: Praegnantem percutiens rixando, Exodi. 21. v. 22. 23. prægnantes scinduntur à Manahem, 2 Reg. 15.16. Vide 8.12.
units.tr: One who strikes a pregnant woman in a quarrel (Exod. 21.22-23). Pregnant women are ripped open by Menahem (2 Kings 15.16). See 8.12.

units.la: Praelivm Deus docet, 2 Sam. 22.35. Psal. 18, 35, & 8.144.
units.tr: God teaches the battle (2 Sam. 22.35; Ps. 18.35; and 8.144).

units.la: Praepositis obediendum, Heb. 13 7.17
units.tr: Those in authority are to be obeyed (Heb. 13.7, 17).

units.la: Præputivm, pro circumcisis, seu præputiatis, metonymice, sive pro Gentibus. Rom. 2, v. 26, 27, & 3, 7, centurio Philisthæorum præputiis vxorem sibi comparauit D. Iuid, 1 Sam. 18, 25. 27. 2. Sam. 3. 14, præputium, pro statu et conditione præputiati, Roman. 2, 26. in posteriore parte versus: hoc est, pro incircumcisum esse, sive, vt ita dicam, pro gentilissimo, Nam in priore versus parte, præputium, pro præputiato, id est, circumciso accipitur, per metonymiam. Præputij Euangelium quid vocet Paulus, Vide Evangelium. Præputium nihil prodest Christiano, aut circumcisio, sed obseruatio mandatorum Dei, 1 Corinth. 7, 19, præputia lignorum auferenda Levit. 19, 23.
units.tr: FORESKIN (praeputium) stands for the circumcised, or uncircumcised, by metonymy, or for the Gentiles (Rom. 2.26-27; 3.7). The Philistine's foreskins bought David a wife (1 Sam. 18.25, 27; 2 Sam. 3.14). Foreskin stands for the state and condition of the uncircumcised (Rom. 2.26). In the latter part of the verse it means being uncircumcised, or, as I may say, the state of a Gentile. For in the former part of the verse, foreskin is taken for the one who has a foreskin, that is, the circumcised, by metonymy. For what Paul calls the Gospel of the foreskin, see GOSPEL. Neither foreskin nor circumcision profits a Christian, but the keeping of God's commandments (1 Cor. 7.19). Foreskins of trees are to be removed (Lev. 19.23).

units.la: Praescitj, qui & prædestinati. Rom. 8.29. & 11.2.
units.tr: Those foreknown, who are also predestined (Rom. 8.29; 11.2).

units.la: Praesepe Christi, Luc. 2, 7, (V. 1, Reg. 4.26.
units.tr: The manger of Christ (Luke 2.7; see 1 Kings 4.26).

units.la: Præsumptio vitiosa, est: eius gratiæ, quam non habes, falsa & mendax iactatio & vindicatio. Est contraria verae humilitati. Siquis sibi videtur aliquid, cum nihil sit, hunc suus ipsius animus fallit. Gal 6.3.
units.tr: Vicious presumption is a false and lying boast and claim to a grace one does not have. It is the opposite of true humility. If anyone thinks himself to be something when he is nothing, his own mind deceives him (Gal. 6.3).

units.la: Praesumptio sancta, Eph. 3.12. præsumptio inanis damnatur, Prou. 26.12. & 28, v. 25, 26, Galat. 6.3, Præsumptionis exempla: Quidam Apostatæ, 1 Timoth. 1.7, Ecclesia Laodicensium, Apoc. 3, v. 16, 17, Vide Iactantia.
units.tr: Holy presumption (Eph. 3.12). Empty presumption is condemned (Prov. 26.12; 28.25-26; Gal. 6.3). Examples of presumption: certain apostates (1 Tim. 1.7); the Church of the Laodiceans (Rev. 3.16-17). See BOASTING.

units.la: Precatio, Vide Oratio. & Inuocatio.
units.tr: Prayer: see PRAYER and INVOCATION.

units.la: Precationum varie formulæ: Nuptiis benedicendi, Genes. 24 60. Ruth. 4, 11, populo benedicendi, Nume. 6. v. 23. 24. 25. Regem consecrandi, 1 Reg. 1, 37, salutandi & benedicendi precādi, Rut. 2, 4, Mat. 21, 9, & 28, 9, Marc. 11. 9, Ioa. 12. 13.
units.tr: Various formulas of prayer: blessing at weddings (Gen. 24.60; Ruth 4.11); blessing the people (Num. 6.23-25); anointing a king (1 Kings 1.37); greeting and blessing with prayer (Ruth 2.4; Matt. 21.9; 28.9; Mark 11.9; John 12.13).

units.la: Precibvs precari, repetitio est Hebraica, pro deuote & religiose precari, Iac. 5 17. ¶ Ad preces, pro defunctis extruendas, detortus locus, Matt. 12.32.
units.tr: To pray with prayers is a Hebrew repetition, meaning to pray devoutly and religiously (James 5.17). ¶ A passage about building prayers for the dead is twisted (Matt. 12.32).

units.la: [Presbyter Ecclesiæ pastor, Act. 14. 23. 1 Tim. 5. v. 17, 19 Tit. 1. 5, Iacob. 5, 14.]
units.tr: [The presbyter is the pastor of the Church (Acts 14.23; 1 Tim. 5.17, 19; Titus 1.5; James 5.14).]

units.la: Presbyteri, id est, pastores, Diaconi, & alij Ecclesiæ gubernatores, in Ecclesia in singulis vrbibus constituti, Actor.14.23. Tit.1,5. Vide SENIORES. & EPISCOPI. presbyteri seduli habenda ratio, 1 Tim.5,17. (vide presbyterium dicitur, 4,14. totus ille coetus, qui in Verbo laborant) Presbyteri & Episcopi paulo, pro iisdem, Act.20,28. Tit.1,5. ad Presbyteros exhortatio, 1 Petr.5,1. &c. presbyteros quales esse oporteat, Tit.1,6. &c. Nemo tuam iuuent. desp.1.Tim. 4.12.
units.tr: Elders, that is, pastors, deacons, and other governors of the Church, appointed in the Church in each city (Acts 14.23; Titus 1.5). See ELDERS and BISHOPS. Diligent elders are to be honoured (1 Tim. 5.17; see presbytery at 4.14, meaning the whole company who labour in the Word). Paul uses elders and bishops for the same persons (Acts 20.28; Titus 1.5). Exhortation to the elders (1 Pet. 5.1, etc.). What elders ought to be like (Titus 1.6, etc.). Let no one despise your youth (1 Tim. 4.12).

units.la: PRETIO mortis Christi redemti sumus, Act. 20.28. 1 Cor. 6.20. & 7,23. 1 Petr.1.19.
units.tr: We have been redeemed by the price of Christ's death (Acts 20.28; 1 Cor. 6.20; 7.23; 1 Pet. 1.19).

units.la: PRIMATVS primatum tenet Christus, Colos.1,18. ¶pro primatu Petri, vt Antichristi Romani primatu & indomitā tyrānidem stabilire quoquo modo possint, allegat pontificij locum Mat.10.2, eò quòd primo loco collocetur Petrus. Atqui nihil in ordine latere mysterij apparet ex Mar. 3.17. &c. Luc.6.14. &c. Gal.2,9. vbi hic ordo tollitur & inuertitur. Cōceditur Petro primatus inter Apostolos, sed ordinis inter pares, non gradus super inferiores. Apostoli enim omnes pari erat dignitate, 2 Cor. 1,5. ¶ Adducūt itē locum Mat.16.9. sed frustrā, & insciter refellūt autem Antichristi Romani primatū & tyrannidē hi loci, Mar.9,2, v.34,35.36. Luc.22.v.25.26. 2 Cor.11.5 (de primatu cōtendūt Apostoli, Mat.18,1. &c.) V. Matt.14.31. & 6.23. & 17.4. (marc 9.6) Mat.18,21. & 19,27, & 26,33.35,40,51,56,69,70,72,74. Gal.2,11.
units.tr: PRIMACY: Christ holds the primacy (Col. 1.18). ¶ To establish the primacy of Peter, by which they might in any way secure the primacy and unbridled tyranny of the Roman Antichrist, the Papists cite Matt. 10.2, because Peter is placed first. But nothing hidden in the order appears from Mark 3.17 etc., Luke 6.14 etc., and Gal. 2.9, where this order is removed and reversed. Peter is granted primacy among the apostles, but it is primacy of order among equals, not of rank over inferiors, for all the apostles had equal dignity (2 Cor. 1.5). ¶ They also cite Matt. 16.9, but in vain. These passages, rightly understood, refute the primacy and tyranny of the Roman Antichrist: Mark 9.2, vv. 34-36; Luke 22.25-26; 2 Cor. 11.5 (the apostles contend about primacy, Matt. 18.1 etc.). See Matt. 14.31; 6.23; 17.4 (Mark 9.6); Matt. 18.21; 19.27; 26.33, 35, 40, 51, 56, 69, 70, 72, 74; Gal. 2.11.

units.la: PRIMITIAE praecipiuntur, Exo.22,29, &34.26, &35.5. Deut.12, 17. Vide & Leuit.23.10, Num.18,13, Deut.18.4, &26,v.2,10 2, paralip 31.5, Nehem.10, v.35,37, prou.3,9, primitiae triennales quibus dandae, Deut.26,2 primitiae Sacerdotum & Leuitarum erant, Num.5,9, & 18, verf.8,11, primitias Spiritus vocat Paulus, Roman.8,23, particulam, quae spem certam nobis facit, fore vt quod in nobis coepit Deus, perficiat: sicut olim primitiarum oblatio, vsum totius acerui sanctificabat. primitiae resurgentium Christus, 1 Corinth.15,23. Colos.1.18. De primitiis Ezec.45.13. &c.
units.tr: FIRSTFRUITS are commanded (Exod. 22.29; 34.26; 35.5; Deut. 12.17). See also Lev. 23.10; Num. 18.13; Deut. 18.4; 26.2, 10; 2 Chron. 31.5; Neh. 10.35, 37; Prov. 3.9. Triennial firstfruits, to be given (Deut. 26.2). The firstfruits were those of the priests and Levites (Num. 5.9; 18.8, 11). Paul calls the Spirit the firstfruits (Rom. 8.23), a pledge that makes us certain that God will complete what he has begun in us, just as the offering of firstfruits once sanctified the use of the whole heap. Christ is the firstfruits of those who rise (1 Cor. 15.23; Col. 1.18). On the firstfruits, see Ezek. 45.13 etc.

units.la: PRIMOGENITVRAE vis & praerogatiua, Genesis. 25.31, & 49.32 paral,21,3. cui danda, Deut,21.v.15.16.
units.tr: The force and prerogative of the firstborn (Gen. 25.31; 49.3; 2 Chron. 21.3). To whom it is to be given (Deut. 21.15-16).

units.la: PRIMOGENITA Ægyptiorum omnia occiduntur media nocte, Exodi.12.29, psal.78,51, & 105.36. & 135,8. & 136.10. primogenita Deo sanctificanda, Exodi.13.2 & 22.29. & 34,v.19.20, Leuit,27.26. Num.3.13. & 8.17. Deut.12.17. & 14. 23. & 15.19.1 Sam.1.24. Luc.2.23. Asini redemptio Exo.13.primogenitus dicitur ante quem nullus alius est editus ab ijsdem parentibus, etiam si nullus post eum vnquam procreatus fuerit. Luc.2.7.
units.tr: All the firstborn of the Egyptians are killed at midnight (Exod. 12.29; Ps. 78.51; 105.36; 135.8; 136.10). Firstborn are to be sanctified to God (Exod. 13.2; 22.29; 34.19-20; Lev. 27.26; Num. 3.13; 8.17; Deut. 12.17; 14.23; 15.19; 1 Sam. 1.24; Luke 2.23). The redemption of the donkey (Exod. 13). A firstborn is called the one before whom no other was born to the same parents, even if no child was ever born after him (Luke 2.7).

units.la: RIMOGENITVS vniuersæ creaturæ, seu omnis rei creatæ, dicitur Christus, Phil. 1.15. id est, ante res vllas conditas genitus. Primogenitus inter multos fratres, Rom.8.29. Coloss. 1.15. primogenitus mortuum, vel ex mortuis, 1.18. id est, qui à mortuis primus ad vitæ æternæ possessionem resurrexit, quod est noui seculi, in quo Filii Dei reuera simus, reale (vt vulgo loquuntur) initium. Vide CHRISTVS. Primogenitorum prærogatiua, 2 Paralip. 21.3 primogeniti nonnunquam à Deo reiiciuntur. Gen. 48.19. & 49.4. Rom. 9.13. Horum redemptio: Ex. 13.13. Num. 18.16.
units.tr: FIRSTBORN: Christ is called the firstborn of every creature, or of every created thing (Phil. 1.15), that is, begotten before any things were made. Firstborn among many brethren (Rom. 8.29; Col. 1.15). Firstborn of the dead, or from the dead (1.18), that is, the one who first rose from the dead to the possession of eternal life, which is the real beginning (as people commonly say) of the new age, in which we are truly sons of God. See CHRIST. The prerogative of the firstborn (2 Chron. 21.3). Firstborn are sometimes rejected by God (Gen. 48.19; 49.4; Rom. 9.13). Their redemption (Exod. 13.13; Num. 18.16).

units.la: [Primogenitus Dei, populus Israel, Exod. 4.22. Jerem. 31.9. Primogeniti hominum & pecudum, sæpius occurrunt in V.T. Primogenitus, Psalm. 89. 28. summus, aliorum principum caput & princeps Salomon nominatur, quatenus fuit typus Christi, in quo solo perfectè hæc impleta sunt.]
units.tr: [The firstborn of God is the people of Israel (Exod. 4.22; Jer. 31.9). Firstborn of men and of beasts occur very often in the Old Testament. Firstborn (Ps. 89.28): the highest, the head and prince of other princes. Solomon is named as far as he was a type of Christ, in whom alone these things were perfectly fulfilled.]

units.la: PRIMVM, pro precipuè, vel præsertim, Rom.3.2.
units.tr: FIRST, meaning chiefly or especially (Rom. 3.2).

units.la: PRIMI nouissimi, Matthæi 19. 30. Marci. 10. 31. Lucæ 13.30
units.tr: FIRST and LAST (Matt. 19.30; Mark 10.31; Luke 13.30).

units.la: [PRIMVS, Iehoua, AEternus, Deus pater, Filius, Spiritus S. Esai. 41. 4. & 44.6. & 48.12. Primus, Iesus Christus, Deus æternus & æterni Dei patris Filius, Apocal. 1.17. & 22.13. Primus, numeri, ordinis, temporis ratione dicitur de die, mense, homine nato, &c.]
units.tr: [FIRST: Jehovah, the Eternal, God the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit (Isa. 41.4; 44.6; 48.12). First: Jesus Christ, the eternal God and Son of the eternal God the Father (Rev. 1.17; 22.13). "First," in terms of number, order, or time, is said of a day, a month, a man who is born, and so on.]

units.la: PRINCEPS Pastorum. Vide CHRISTVS.
units.tr: PRINCE of the pastors. See CHRIST.

units.la: PRINCEPS Christus, nempe exercitus Dei, Ios. 5.14. Ecclesiæ, Ezech. 34.24. pacis, Esai. 9.5. Seruator electorum, Act. 5.31 pastorum, 1.Petr. 5.4. Regum terræ, Apoc. 1.5.
units.tr: PRINCE: Christ, namely of the army of God (Josh. 5.14); of the Church (Ezek. 34.24); of peace (Isa. 9.5); Saviour of the elect (Acts 5.31); of the pastors (1 Pet. 5.4); of the kings of the earth (Rev. 1.5).

units.la: princeps, vir omnium præstantiss, Genes. 23, 6, pius quisque, cuius cor veluti porta est, qua Christus intromittitur, Psal. 24, ver. 7,9 princeps vir magnificus, Iudic. 5, 25, princeps Dæmoniorum, Mat. 9.34. & 12. 24. Marc. 3. 22. Luc. 11.15
units.tr: Prince: a man most excellent of all (Gen. 23.6); any pious man whose heart is like a gate through which Christ enters (Ps. 24.7, 9); a magnificent prince (Judg. 5.25); prince of demons (Matt. 9.34; 12.24; Mark 3.22; Luke 11.15).

units.la: PRINCEPS aëris, huius & mundi, Diabolus, Ioan. 12,31. & 14.30. & 16.11. Ephes. 2.2. & 6.12. Col. 2.15. princeps impius cui similis, Prouerb. 28.15. Ezech. 22.27.2. Tim. 4,17.
units.tr: PRINCE of the air, of this world: the Devil, John 12:31, 14:30, 16:11; Eph. 2:2, 6:12; Col. 2:15. An impious prince, like whom there is none: Prov. 28:15; Ezek. 22:27; 2 Tim. 4:17.

units.la: PRINCIPIS peccatū quomodo expiādum, Leuit. 4.v.22. &c.
units.tr: How the sin of a prince is to be atoned for: Lev. 4:22, etc.

units.la: PRINCIPES & Reges in populo Iudaico inaugurandi ritus exempla: In Iosua, Numer.27. v.18,19, Saule,1 Sam.10. verf.1,2, Dauide,16, verf.11,12,13.2 Sam.2,4,& 5,3, Salomone,1 Reg,1,v.38,39, Iehu.2 Reg.9, ver.1,2,3, Ioa.11, v.10, 11,12, Ioachaz, 23.30, Dij cur dicantur, Vide REX, principes non irritandi, Prou. 25. 15, principes Dauidi ministrantes, 1. paral. 27.1. principes Sacerdotum, Matth.2, 4.&c. vocabantur, qui ex posteris Aaronis (nam ij soli Sacerdotes dicebantur) erant familiarum suarum capita, sicuti post captiuitatem fuerat earum distributio instaurata, vt refertur Nehem. 11, & 12. cap. quamobrem etiam vocantur principes Sanctuarij, 2 Paralip. 24. 5.& Principes Sacerdotum. 36. 14. principes Salomonis, 1 Regum.4, 2. principes mali, ob peccata populi, Prouer. 28.2. principes quomodo à Deo demententur, Psalm. 76. 13. Prouerb. 29.12. Ministri Dei sunt, Roman.13.4. quales esse oporteat Deut. 1. 13. principes ignorantes crucifixerunt Christum, Actor.3.17.1 Corinth.2 8.multi ex Iudæis credunt Christo, non audentes tamen confiteri, Ioann.12, 42. ad principes exhortatio Ezech.45.9 in principes pauperum oppressores, Amos 4. 1. & 6. 1. Sophon.3.1.
units.tr: Examples of the rite of inaugurating princes and kings among the Jewish people: in Joshua, Num. 27:18-19; Saul, 1 Sam. 10:1-2; David, 1 Sam. 16:11-13, 2 Sam. 2:4 and 5:3; Solomon, 1 Kings 1:38-39; Jehu, 2 Kings 9:1-3; Joash, 11:10-12; Jehoahaz, 23:30. Why they are called so, see KING. Princes are not to be provoked, Prov. 25:15. Princes ministered to David, 1 Chron. 27:1. Those called chief priests, Matt. 2:4, etc., were those who were of the posterity of Aaron (for these alone were called priests) and were the heads of their families, just as their distribution was restored after the captivity, as is related in Neh. 11 and 12. For this reason they are also called princes of the sanctuary, 2 Chron. 24:5, and chief priests, 36:14. Princes of Solomon, 1 Kings 4:2. Evil princes, on account of the people's sins, Prov. 28:2. How princes are deposed by God, Ps. 76:13 (Vulgate 75:12); Prov. 29:12. They are ministers of God, Rom. 13:4. What sort they ought to be, Deut. 1:13. The princes, in ignorance, crucified Christ, Acts 3:17; 1 Cor. 2:8. Many of the Jews believed in Christ but did not dare to confess it, John 12:42. An exhortation to princes, Ezek. 45:9; against princes who oppress the poor, Amos 4:1, 6:1; Zeph. 3:1.

units.la: PRINCIPVM & Regum corda in manu Dei sunt, proverb.21.1. principum officium, Vide MAGISTRATVS. Principum scelera minimè dissimulanda. Exempla: Esaias, Esa. 1.23. Ioannes Baptista, Matth.14.4. Marc.6.18. principum placandorum expedita ratio, proverb. 25.15 principum status mutantur, Iob. 12.18. Principum & praelatorum malorum exempla: Aaron, Exodi 32. 21. Filij Israelitarum, Num. 25 4. Filij Heli,1 Sam. 2.v.12.22. Ieroboam, 1 Reg.12.v.19.20.28.30. Achab, 18.18. Manasses, 2 paralip.33.9. Nabuchodonosor,Esai.14.20. Reges Aegypti,19.13. Sobna,22.16. Sedechias, Ierem.38.5 Pilatus,Mat. 27.v.18.24. Ioan.19.15. principes Sacerdotum, Actor.4. 8 Magistratus Templi, 5.v.18. 26.40. Iudaeorum Clerus,6. 12. Magistratus Phillippensis, 16. 22. Ananias,23.verf.2.3. Felix,24.28. Festus, 25. v. 9.12. principes mali malos ministros habent, proverb.29.12. Eccles.10.2.
units.tr: The hearts of princes and kings are in the hand of God, Prov. 21:1. The duty of princes: see MAGISTRATE. The crimes of princes are by no means to be overlooked. Examples: Isaiah, Isa. 1:23; John the Baptist, Matt. 14:4; Mark 6:18. A ready method of placating princes, Prov. 25:15. The positions of princes are changed, Job 12:18. Examples of evil princes and prelates: Aaron, Exod. 32:21; the sons of Israel, Num. 25:4; the sons of Eli, 1 Sam. 2:12, 22; Jeroboam, 1 Kings 12:19-20, 28, 30; Ahab, 18:18; Manasseh, 2 Chron. 33:9; Nebuchadnezzar, Isa. 14:20; the kings of Egypt, 19:13; Shebna, 22:16; Zedekiah, Jer. 38:5; Pilate, Matt. 27:18, 24; John 19:15; the chief priests, Acts 4:8; the temple magistrates, 5:18, 26; the clergy of the Jews, 6:12; the magistrates of Philippi, 16:22; Ananias, 23:2-3; Felix, 24:28; Festus, 25:9, 12. Evil princes have evil ministers, Prov. 29:12; Eccles. 10:2.

units.la: PRINCIPIBVS non maledicendum, Exodi. 22. 28. Eccles. 10.20. Act.23.5. (principibus magnis subiici, non semper est tutum, Esa.8.6.) V.2 Pet.2.10. Iudæ.v.8.9.10.
units.tr: Princes are not to be reviled: Exod. 22:28; Eccles. 10:20; Acts 23:5. (It is not always safe to submit to great princes, Isa. 8:6.) 2 Pet. 2:10; Jude 8-10.

units.la: PRINCIPATVS omnis caput Christus, Col.2.10.
units.tr: Christ is the head of every principality: Col. 2:10.

units.la: PRINCIPATVS tribuitur & regno tenebrarum, Col.2.15. DIABOLVS.
units.tr: Dominion is ascribed also to the kingdom of darkness: Col. 2:15. See DEVIL.

units.la: PRISCILLA, vxor Aquilæ, quæ &Prisca, Act.18.2. Priscilla adiutrix Pauli, Rom.16.3. (i. agnoscens, Hierony.)
units.tr: Priscilla, wife of Aquila, who is also called Prisca: Acts 18:2. Priscilla, a helper of Paul: Rom. 16:3 (that is, acknowledging, according to Jerome).

units.la: PROBANDA omnia, 1 Thess.5.21. Spiritus unde sint, 1 Ioh.4.1.
units.tr: All things are to be proved: 1 Thess. 5:21. Whence the spirits come: 1 John 4:1.

units.la: PROBEMUS an simus in fide, 1 Corinth.11.28. 2 Corinth.13.5.
units.tr: Let us examine whether we are in the faith: 1 Cor. 11:28; 2 Cor. 13:5.

units.la: PROBATI, pro iis, qui opponuntur hypocritis, 1 Corinth.11.19.
units.tr: Approved, in contrast to hypocrites: 1 Cor. 11:19.

units.la: PROBATIO, spem auget, Rom.5.4. Parit patientiam. Iac.1.3.
units.tr: Proof increases hope, Rom. 5:4; it produces patience, James 1:3.

units.la: PROBLEMA Samsonis, Iudic.14.12. soluitur, v.18. V.1 Reg. IC.1.
units.tr: Samson's riddle, Judg. 14:12, is solved at v. 18. 1 Kings 10:1.

units.la: PRODIGALITAS, ἀσωτία, est nimia & inconsiderata pecuniæ profusio, quæ funestum bonorum suorum exitum tandem facit & furiosum. Eph.5.18. Tit.1.6. 1 Pet.4.4.
units.tr: Prodigality, [ἀσωτία], is an excessive and thoughtless squandering of money, which at last brings a ruinous and frenzied end to one's goods. Eph. 5:18; Titus 1:6; 1 Pet. 4:4.

units.la: PRODIGALITAS damnatur, Prouer.5.9, &c. Prodigalitatis exemplum: Prodigus filius, Luc.15.13.
units.tr: Prodigality is condemned, Prov. 5:9, etc. Example of prodigality: the prodigal son, Luke 15:13.

units.la: PRODIGIA, per Mosen edita, Actor.7.36. prodigia in morte Christi, Matth.27.45.51. prodigia vt fiant, orant Apostoli, Actor.4.30. prodigia per Apostolos edita, 43. & 5.12. prodigia a Stephano edita, 6.8. Vide MIRACVLA.
units.tr: Portents, wrought through Moses, Acts 7:36. Portents at the death of Christ, Matt. 27:45, 51. The apostles pray that portents may be done, Acts 4:30. Portents wrought through the apostles, 4:43; 5:12. Portents wrought by Stephen, 6:8. See MIRACLES.

units.la: PROCHORVS Diaconus eligitur, Act.6.5. πρόχειρος, promptus.
units.tr: Prochorus is chosen as deacon, Acts 6:5. [πρόχειρος], ready, prompt.

units.la: PRODITIO damnatur, 2 Tim.3.4. proditio Euangelij causa Luc.21.16. proditionis poena, 2. Paral.25.3. & 33.25. Esth.22. Proditio exempla: Cain, Genes.4.8. Simeon & Leui 34.v.25, 27. Vxor Samsonis Philisthæa, Iudic.14.17. Dalila 16.9. Saul, 1 Sam.18.v.11, 17, 25. Doeg 22.9. Viri Ceilæ, 23. 5.7.12. Ziphæi, v.19 & 26.1. Ioab, 2 Sam.3.27. & 20.10. v. 2 Reg.2.5. Rechab, Iosf.2.4.6. Dauid, 2 Sam.11.v.14, 15. Ammon, 13.v.10.11. Absalom, v.28. & 15.v.7.10.11. Zambri, 1 Reg.16.10. Serui Ioas, 2 Reg.12.20. 2 Paral.24.25. Pekach Reg.15.25. Sennacherib filij, 19.37. Serui Amon, 21.23. 2 Paral.33.24. Ismael filius Nathaniæ, 2 Reg.25.25. Ierem.41.1, 2.6.7. Ciues Ierosolymitani, 2 Par.25.27. Iudæorum hostes, 1 Esdr.4.2. Neh.6.2. duo Eunuchi, Esth.2.21. Dauid hostes, Psalm.35.23. & 41.10. Hostes Danielis, Dan 6.v.12. Scribæ & Pharisæi, Matth.12.10. Marc.3.2. Luc.6.7. Iudæ
units.tr: Betrayal is condemned, 2 Tim. 3:4. Betrayal for the sake of the gospel, Luke 21:16. The punishment of betrayal, 2 Chron. 25:3; 33:25; Esth. 2:2. Examples of betrayal: Cain, Gen. 4:8; Simeon and Levi, 34:25, 27; the Philistine wife of Samson, Judg. 14:17; Delilah, 16:9; Saul, 1 Sam. 18:11, 17, 25; Doeg, 22:9; the men of Keilah, 23:5, 7, 12; the Ziphites, 23:19; 26:1; Joab, 2 Sam. 3:27; 20:10; 1 Kings 2:5; Rechab, Josh. 2:4, 6; David, 2 Sam. 11:14-15; Ammon, 13:10-11; Absalom, 13:28; 15:7, 10-11; Zimri, 1 Kings 16:10; the servants of Joash, 2 Kings 12:20; 2 Chron. 24:25; Pekah, 2 Kings 15:25; the sons of Sennacherib, 19:37; the servants of Amon, 21:23; 2 Chron. 33:24; Ishmael son of Nethaniah, 2 Kings 25:25; Jer. 41:1-2, 6-7; the citizens of Jerusalem, 2 Chron. 25:27; the enemies of the Jews, 1 Esd. 4:2; Neh. 6:2; the two eunuchs, Esth. 2:21; the enemies of David, Ps. 35:23; 41:10; the enemies of Daniel, Dan. 6:12; the scribes and Pharisees, Matt. 12:10; Mark 3:2; Luke 6:7; Judah...

units.la: Iudas Iscariotes, Matth. 26. 49. Marc. 14. 45. Luc. 22. v. 47. 48. Ioan. 18.5. Iudæi, Actor.7.52. & 23.15. Vide DOLI exempla. Proditionis pœnæ exempla: Serui Ioas.2 Paral. 25.3. Serui Amon, 33. 25. duo Eunuchi Regis Assueri, Esth.2.22. Iudas proditor, Matt.27.5. Actor. 1.18.
units.tr: Judas Iscariot, Matt. 26:49; Mark 14:45; Luke 22:47-48; John 18:5. The Jews, Acts 7:52; 23:15. See examples of guile. Examples of the punishment of betrayal: the servants of Joash, 2 Chron. 25:3; the servants of Amon, 33:25; the two eunuchs of King Ahasuerus, Esth. 2:22. Judas the traitor, Matt. 27:5; Acts 1:18.

units.la: PROFESSIO religionis externa requiritur, Esa.44.5. & 45.23. Rom.10 10.1 Pet.3.15. V. Confessio.
units.tr: Outward profession of religion is required: Isa. 44:5; 45:23; Rom. 10:10; 1 Pet. 3:15. See CONFESSION.

units.la: PROFVNDITAS diuitiarum ex Hæbræorum idiotismo, profundæ diuitiæ, Roman.11.33. pro rebus profundis, 8. 39. Satius est in profundum maris demergi &c. Matth. 18.6.
units.tr: The depth of riches, by the Hebrew idiom: "the depths of riches," Rom. 11:33; for deep things, 8:39. It is better to be drowned in the depth of the sea, etc., Matt. 18:6.

units.la: PROHIBENDI non sint, quomodocunque verbum Dei annuntiantes, Marc.9.39. Luc.9.50. Nec pueruli, Matth. 19 14.
units.tr: Those who proclaim the word of God in whatever manner are not to be hindered, Mark 9:39; Luke 9:50. Nor are little children, Matt. 19:14.

units.la: PROHIBENTIVM contrahere matrimonium, doctrina diabolica, 1 Tim.4.3. Qui arcent alios à cognitione D. Luc. 11.52.
units.tr: Forbidding people to marry is a diabolical doctrine, 1 Tim. 4:3. Those who keep others from the knowledge of God, Luke 11:52.

units.la: PROMITTERE, facilius est, quàm præstare, Exo.19.8. quod promiserimus Deo, reddendum, Deut.23.21.
units.tr: To promise is easier than to perform, Exod. 19:8. What we have promised to God is to be paid, Deut. 23:21.

units.la: PROMISSIO μετωνυμικῶς, pro, promissionis præstatione, seu, vt alij volunt, pro re ipsa promissa, per metonymiam. Hebr. 11. 39. Sic accipitur iuxta quosdam & Galat.3.22. Vide PATRIS non adepti promissa. promissio Patris, Spiritus Sanctus, Actor.1.4. & 2.33. promissio salutis ab æterno, Eph.1.13. & 2.12. promissio Abrahæ facta, Rom.4.13. & 9.9.
units.tr: Promise, [μετωνυμικῶς], metonymically, for the fulfilment of the promise, or, as others prefer, for the very thing promised, by metonymy. Heb. 11:39. According to some, Gal. 3:22 is also understood this way. See the promises not obtained by the fathers. The Father's promise, the Holy Spirit, Acts 1:4; 2:33. The promise of salvation from eternity, Eph. 1:13; 2:12. The promise made to Abraham, Rom. 4:13; 9:9.

units.la: PROMISSIONIS Filij qui, Rom. 9.8. Vide FILII promissionis. Promissionis terra qualis, Deut.8.7. promissionis Spiritus quid significet, Vide SPIRITVS promissionis.
units.tr: Who are the children of promise, Rom. 9:8. See CHILDREN OF PROMISE. What the land of promise is like, Deut. 8:7. What the promised Spirit signifies, see SPIRIT OF PROMISE.

units.la: PROMISSIONES vitæ præsentis, 1 Timoth. 4.8. 2. Petr.3.13. promissiones Dei cum conditione fiunt, Deut. 19.2. & 28.1. &c.33. 4. Leuit.26.1. &c.1 Reg. 2.30. Ezech.18.1. &c.33. v.15.19. Mar.16.16. Ioan.3 v. 1. 16.36. & 6.47. & 8.31. & 13.17. & 15.v.7.14. Rom. 8. 17. Col.1.23. Hebr.3 14.2. Pet 1.4. Apo. 2.3.cap. & 21.7. promissiones Dei in Christo sunt. Etiam & Amen 2 Cor.1.20. Vide DEI promissiones. Promissiones Dei obiicit Moses, orans pro peccato populi Israel, Exod.32.13. Deut.9.27. promissiones omnes adimpleuit Deus Iudæis, Iol. 21. 43, & 23. 15. propter promissiones suas ad Abraham &c. factas, omnia egit Deus erga Iudæos, Exod.2.24.& 6.v.5.6. Leuit.26.42.Deut.4 20.& 8.1 Sam.12.22.2 Sam.7.v.24 25.2 Reg.13.23.&19.34.& 6. promissiones suas adimpleuit Deus, misso suo Filio Act.3.18.&13.33.promissionum Dei memor Iacob, Gen.32.9.
units.tr: Promises of the present life, 1 Tim. 4:8; 2 Pet. 3:13. God's promises are made with a condition: Deut. 19:2; 28:1, etc.; 33:4; Lev. 26:1, etc.; 1 Kings 2:30; Ezek. 18:1, etc.; 33:15, 19; Mark 16:16; John 3:1, 16; 6:47; 8:31; 13:17; 15:7, 14; Rom. 8:17; Col. 1:23; Heb. 3:14; 1 Pet. 1:4; Rev. 2:3; 21:7. The promises of God are in Christ, and Amen: 2 Cor. 1:20. See PROMISES OF GOD. Moses, praying for the sin of the people of Israel, sets before God the promises: Exod. 32:13; Deut. 9:27. God fulfilled all his promises to the Jews: Josh. 21:43; 23:15. For his promises made to Abraham, etc., God did everything for the Jews: Exod. 2:24; 6:5-6; Lev. 26:42; Deut. 4:20; 8:1; 1 Sam. 12:22; 2 Sam. 7:24-25; 2 Kings 13:23; 19:34; 6. God fulfilled his promises by sending his Son: Acts 3:18; 13:33. Jacob, mindful of God's promises: Gen. 32:9.

units.la: PROMISSIS standum, Prou.25.t4. Pf.15.4. Exemplum: Donec Ioseph, Iudic.1.25.
units.tr: One must stand by promises: Prov. 25:14; Ps. 15:4. Example: until Joseph, Judg. 1:25.

units.la: PROPHANA vitet Episcopus, 2 Tim.2.16. Nequis fit profanus, Heb.12.16.
units.tr: The bishop is to avoid profane things, 2 Tim. 2:16. Lest anyone be profane, Heb. 12:16.

units.la: PROPHANORVM hominum testimonio vti aliquando licet, modò id parcè, & in tempore fiat, Act.17.28. 1 Cor.15. Tit 1.12. V. Mat.12.42. 1 Reg.10.1.
units.tr: It is sometimes lawful to use the testimony of profane men, provided it is done sparingly and at the right time: Acts 17:28; 1 Cor. 15:33; Titus 1:12. See Matt. 12:42; 1 Kings 10:1.

units.la: PROPHETA: Propheta in propria patria contemnitur, Matth. 13.57. Luc.4.24. Ioan.4.44.
units.tr: A prophet is despised in his own country: Matt. 13:57; Luke 4:24; John 4:44.

units.la: PROPHETAE triplex genus. Primum eorum, qui in Ecclesia gubernatione extraordinariè suscitati, de communibus eius necessitatibus Deum è re nata consulebant. Hi Videntes dicuntur, 1 Sam.9. 9.1 Paral.21.9. & 26 28.& 29.2 Paral. 9 29.& 12.15.& 16.10.& 19.2 & 26.5.& 29.v.2 30. Secundum genus Prophetarum eos complectitur, qui cessantibus Sacerdotibus ad Legem interpretandam extraordinariè à Deo mittebantur, sua cuique assignata prouincia, Esa.1.1. Ier.1.3. Ezech.1.3. Ose.1.1. Amos 1. Abdias v.1. Abac.1.1. Zach 1.1. Malach.1.1. horum xii. minores volumen efficiunt, Act.7.42. Omnium huius generis Prophetarum doctrinæ summa, Matth.22.40. Tertium Prophetarum genus eorum est, qui doctrinæ diuinæ explicandæ & applicandæ dono insigniuntur. Act.13.1. 1 Cor.12.28. Ephes.4.11. hinc prophetare, pro, doctrinæ sum ædificationi, exhortationi & consolationi applicare. 1 Cor.14.13 & Prophetia, pro huiusmodi exercitio, Rom.12.6.1. Thess.5.20. huius forma describitur 1 Cor.14. v.29.30.&c. Prophetarum duæ species à Paulo constituuntur, Vide DIACONIA: &, ECCLESIASTICAE functione. Prophetæ variis afflictionibus expositi, Matth.5.12. non seipsis loquuntur. 2 Paral.36.12. Ierem.26.13. Matth.12.17. Actor.3.v 18 21.& 28.23. Heb.1.1.& 3.7.& 10. 15.1 Petr. 1.11. Petr.1.21. de Christo loquuti sunt omnes, Luc.24 27. Ioan. 5.39. & 12.41. Actor 3.24 & 10.43.& 26.22. 1 Pet. 1 11. à Deo missi, Ierem.7.25. ab Israelitis occisi, Neh.9.26. Matth.5.12. & 23.37. Luc.11.49.& 13 34. Act.7.v.51.52.1 Thess.2.15. non bis in exemplar proponuntur. Iac. 5.10. Spiritum Dei habuerunt, Vide Apostoli & prophetæ habuerunt Spiritum Dei. [Horum omnium prophetarum caput & princeps Christus qui propheta appellatur, Deut. 18. v. 15. &c. Matt. 21. 11. Luc. 7. 16. Ioan. 4. 19. & 6. 14. & 9. 17. Act. 3. v. 22. 23. & 7. 37.]
units.tr: There are three kinds of prophets. First, those who were raised up extraordinarily in the governing of the Church and consulted God, as the occasion arose, on its common needs. These are called Seers: 1 Sam. 9:9; 1 Chron. 21:9; 26:28; 29:29; 2 Chron. 9:29; 12:15; 16:10; 19:2; 26:5; 29:25; 30:2. Second, the kind of prophets who, when the priests were failing, were sent extraordinarily by God to interpret the Law, each with his own assigned province: Isa. 1:1; Jer. 1:3; Ezek. 1:3; Hos. 1:1; Amos 1:1; Obad. 1; Hab. 1:1; Zech. 1:1; Mal. 1:1. Of these, the twelve minor prophets make up one volume: Acts 7:42. The sum of the teaching of all prophets of this kind: Matt. 22:40. Third, the kind of prophets are those who are distinguished by the gift of explaining and applying divine teaching: Acts 13:1; 1 Cor. 12:28; Eph. 4:11. Hence "to prophesy" means to apply teaching to edification, exhortation and consolation: 1 Cor. 14:3; and "prophecy" for such an exercise, Rom. 12:6; 1 Thess. 5:20. Its form is described in 1 Cor. 14:29-30, etc. Paul establishes two species of prophets: see DIACONATE and ECCLESIASTICAL function. Prophets were exposed to various afflictions: Matt. 5:12. They did not speak of themselves: 2 Chron. 36:12; Jer. 26:13; Matt. 12:17; Acts 3:18, 21; 28:23; Heb. 1:1; 3:7; 10:15; 1 Pet. 1:11; 2 Pet. 1:21. All of them spoke of Christ: Luke 24:27; John 5:39; 12:41; Acts 3:24; 10:43; 26:22; 1 Pet. 1:11. They were sent by God: Jer. 7:25. They were killed by the Israelites: Neh. 9:26; Matt. 5:12; 23:37; Luke 11:49; 13:34; Acts 7:51-52; 1 Thess. 2:15. They are not set forth twice as examples: James 5:10. They had the Spirit of God: see Apostles and prophets had the Spirit of God. [Christ, who is called the Prophet, is the head and prince of all these prophets: Deut. 18:15, etc.; Matt. 21:11; Luke 7:16; John 4:19; 6:14; 9:17; Acts 3:22-23; 7:37.]

units.la: Prophetæ primo, omnium non solùm subditorum, & infimi subsellij hominum, sed Regum etiam & principum, ac summorum potentúmque virorum peccata magno zelo & acri sermone coarguerunt. exempla: Moses graviter obiurgat Aaronem & populum ob vitulum conflatum, Exod. 32. 21. populum, Num. 14. v. 41. 42. Deut. 9. v. 7. 8. Rubenitas, si non iuuent Fratres suos, Num. 32. v. 6. 7. Vir Dei graviter obiurgat Heli Sacerdotem, 1 Sam. 2. v. 27. 28. Samuel populum, ob præposteram Regis petitionem, 12. v. 12. 13. &c. Saulem ob neglectum Dei mandatum 13. v. 13. 14. Nathan Dauidem propter adulterium & caedem, 2 Sam. 12. 7. &c. Gal. Dauidem, ob numerationem populi, 24. 13. Vir Dei, Ieroboamum, 1 Reg. 13. v. 12. 3. Ahias Silonites Ieroboamum, 14. 9. Iehu Propheta, Baasa, Regem, 16. v. 2 3. Elias populum ob idololatriam Baal, 18. v. 21. 22. & 19. 10. Achabum ob Naboth interfectum, 21. 19. Ochosiam, 2 Reg. 1. 16. Ioram Regem per literas, 2 par. 21. v. 12. 13. 14. Elisæus Ioram Regem Israel, 2 Regū 3. 13. prophetæ populum, 21. v. 10. 11. Hanani propheta Asa Regem Iudæ, 2 par. 16. v. 7. 8. Iehu prophetaIosaphatum, 19. 2. Zacharias populum, 24. 20. Azarias Oziam, 26. 18. Dauid impios, Ps. 75. 35. Oseas diuersos ordines populi, Ose. 5. 1. Esaias populum, Esa. 1. 4. & 58. Ieremias, omnium ordinum homines, Ier. 1. 18. & 2. v. 8. 9. 36. & 23. 11. V. Impii & peccatores quomodo tractandi.
units.tr: First, the prophets rebuked the sins of all people, not only of subjects and the lowest rank of men, but also of kings, princes, and the most powerful men, with great zeal and sharp speech. Examples: Moses sharply rebukes Aaron and the people over the calf that was made, Exod. 32. 21; the people, Num. 14. 41, 42; Deut. 9. 7, 8; the Reubenites, if they do not help their brothers, Num. 32. 6, 7. The man of God sharply rebukes Eli the priest, 1 Sam. 2. 27, 28. Samuel rebukes the people for their rash request for a king, 1 Sam. 12. 12, 13, etc.; Saul for neglecting God's command, 13. 13, 14. Nathan rebukes David for adultery and murder, 2 Sam. 12. 7, etc.; Gad rebukes David for the numbering of the people, 2 Sam. 24. 13. The man of God rebukes Jeroboam, 1 Kings 13. 1, 2, 3; Ahijah the Shilonite rebukes Jeroboam, 1 Kings 14. 9; the prophet Jehu rebukes Baasha the king, 1 Kings 16. 2, 3. Elijah rebukes the people for the idolatry of Baal, 1 Kings 18. 21, 22, and 19. 10; he rebukes Ahab for the killing of Naboth, 1 Kings 21. 19; Ahaziah, 2 Kings 1. 16; King Jehoram by letter, 2 Chron. 21. 12, 13, 14. Elisha rebukes Jehoram king of Israel, 2 Kings 3. 13; the prophet rebukes the people, 2 Chron. 21. 10, 11. Hanani the prophet rebukes Asa king of Judah, 2 Chron. 16. 7, 8; Jehu the prophet rebukes Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 19. 2; Zechariah rebukes the people, 2 Chron. 24. 20; Azariah rebukes Uzziah, 2 Chron. 26. 18. David rebukes the wicked, Ps. 75. 35 [Ps. 75.5 in the Vulgate numbering]; Hosea rebukes the various ranks of the people, Hos. 5. 1; Isaiah rebukes the people, Isa. 1. 4 and ch. 58; Jeremiah rebukes men of every rank, Jer. 1. 18, and 2. 8, 9, 36, and 23. 11. See: How the impious and sinners are to be treated.

units.la: Secundo; Quinetiam prophetæ & Sacerdotes interdum etiam corporali exercuerunt vindictam erga contumaces & rebelles. V. VINDICTA.
units.tr: Second, the prophets and priests sometimes also carried out bodily punishment against the stubborn and rebellious. See VENGEANCE.

units.la: Tertio, De mutationibus Imperiorum prænomuerunt suos. exempla: Samuel indicat regnum à Saule esse transferendum, 1 Sam. 15. 23. Ahias prædicit Ieroboamo, quòd scissurus sit Deus regnum in duas partes, 1 Reg. 11. v. 30. 31. Elisæus prædicit Iosaphato regi Iuda victoriam contra Moabitas, 2 Reg. 3. 18. &c. vaticinatur item Ioas Regi, quòd tribus vicibus sit percussurus Syriam, 2 Reg 13. 18. Propheta Domini indicat Deū propter peccara Manassis deletūrum Ierosolymam & in captiuitate abducturum populum per Assyrios, 21.v.11.12.13. Daniel multa prænunciat de Monarchiarum mutationibus, Dan.2.4.5.7.8.9.10.11. capitibus.
units.tr: Third, they foretold to their people changes of empires. Examples: Samuel declares that the kingdom is to be transferred from Saul, 1 Sam. 15. 23. Ahijah predicts to Jeroboam that God will tear the kingdom into two parts, 1 Kings 11. 30, 31. Elisha predicts to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, victory against the Moabites, 2 Kings 3. 18, etc. Likewise Joash prophesies to the king that he will strike Syria three times, 2 Kings 13. 18. The prophet of the Lord declares that God, because of the sins of Manasseh, will destroy Jerusalem and lead the people away into captivity by the Assyrians, 2 Kings 21. 11, 12, 13. Daniel foretells many things about changes of monarchies, Dan. 2. 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 chapters.

units.la: Quartò, Docuerunt de pœnis peccatorum. exempla: Vt Dei prædicit Heli Sacerdoti, quibus pœnis esset affligendus à Deo propter nimiam erga liberos indulgentiam, 1 Sam.2.v.31.32. eadem repetit 3. v.17.18. quæ etiam exitum comprobauit, 4.17. Samuel prædicit Sauli pœnas ob neglectum Dei mandatum, 1 Sam.15.28. Nathan Dauidi denunciat calamitates secuturas, 2 Sam.12.11. Gad similiter 1 Par.21.10. Salomoni denuntiatur ira Dei ob idololatriam, 1 Reg.11.11. Ahias prædicit Ieroboamo mortem filij, & excidium totius familiæ, 14.10. Iehu prædicit Baasæ interitum cum tota familia 16.v.2.3. Elias famem, propter idololatriam, Achabo, 17.1, & ob homicidium mortem 21.19. ob dimissionem Benadad Achabum cum tota familia pœnas daturum prædicit, 20.42. prænunciat Ochoziæ mortem, 2 Reg.1.16. eadem mala ventura prænunciat Iosiæ, Hulda prophetissa, 2 Reg.22.15. &c. Ezechiel vaticinatur contra ciuitatem sanguinariam Ezech. v.3.4.
units.tr: Fourth, they taught about the punishments of sins. Examples: Eli the priest is told in advance by God what punishments he would be afflicted with for his excessive indulgence toward his sons, 1 Sam. 2. 31, 32; he repeats the same in 3. 17, 18, and the outcome confirmed it, 4. 17. Samuel predicts to Saul the punishments for neglecting God's command, 1 Sam. 15. 28. Nathan announces to David the calamities that would follow, 2 Sam. 12. 11; Gad likewise, 1 Chron. 21. 10. God's wrath for idolatry is announced to Solomon, 1 Kings 11. 11. Ahijah predicts to Jeroboam the death of his son and the destruction of his whole family, 1 Kings 14. 10. Jehu predicts to Baasha his destruction together with his whole family, 1 Kings 16. 2, 3. Elijah predicts famine to Ahab because of idolatry, 1 Kings 17. 1, and death because of murder, 1 Kings 21. 19; he predicts that Ahab with his whole family will pay the penalty for sending away Ben-hadad, 1 Kings 20. 42. He foretells Ahaziah's death, 2 Kings 1. 16. Huldah the prophetess foretells the same evils to come upon Josiah, 2 Kings 22. 15, etc. Ezekiel prophesies against the bloody city, Ezek. 22. 3, 4.

units.la: Quintò De speciālibus euentibus vaticinati sunt, & prædixerunt. exempla: Moses Exo.16.v.12.13. Num.14.vet.39.40.41.42. Vir Dei, 1 Reg.13.v.2.3. 2 Regum 23.v.20. Elias, 1 Reg.17.v.13.14. Propheta Dei, 20.13. Michæas, 28. Elisæus.2 Reg.7.v.1.2. & 8.v.1.11.12. Esaias, 2 Para.32.2. Esa.20.1 & 38.1.
units.tr: Fifth, they prophesied and foretold particular events. Examples: Moses, Exod. 16. 12, 13; Num. 14. 39, 40, 41, 42. The man of God, 1 Kings 13. 2, 3; 2 Kings 23. 20. Elijah, 1 Kings 17. 13, 14. A prophet of God, 1 Kings 20. 13. Micaiah, 1 Kings 22. 28. Elisha, 2 Kings 7. 1, 2, and 8. 1, 11, 12. Isaiah, 2 Chron. 32. 2; Isa. 20. 1 and 38. 1.

units.la: Sextò, Liberationes prædixerunt. exempla: Elisæus, 2 Esd. 19.19. &c. 2 Par.20.v.15.16. Ieremias, Ier.29.v.8.9.
units.tr: Sixth, they foretold deliverances. Examples: Elisha, 2 Esd. [Neh.] 19. 19, etc.; 2 Chron. 20. 15, 16. Jeremiah, Jer. 29. 8, 9.

units.la: Septimò, Vnà cum aliis policitis viris consiliis iuuerunt externam etiam politiam. exempla: Moses, Exodi 18. vers. 13.14. Osee.12.13. Samuel, Eccles.46.ver.17.18. Elias, 2 Reg.12. Elisæus, 4.13. & 6.versi.9.12. & 13.14. Ioiada, 11. versic. 16. &c. 2 Paralip.23.9.10. &c. Sacerdotes Leuitæ, 19.v.5.7.8.9.10.11.
units.tr: Seventh, together with other men of prudence they helped also with counsel in the external government. Examples: Moses, Exod. 18. 13, 14; Hos. 12. 13. Samuel, Ecclus. 46. 17, 18. Elijah, 2 Kings 12. Elisha, 4. 13, and 6. 9, 12, and 13, 14. Jehoiada, 2 Kings 11. 16, etc.; 2 Chron. 23. 9, 10, etc. The priests and Levites, 2 Chron. 19. 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.

units.la: Octauò, Hortati sunt homines ad bona opera. exempla: Sacerdos Regi exemplar libri Legis dare iubetur, vt sciat sui officij esse illum ad pietatem & bona opera cohortari, Deut.17.18. V.1 Sam.14.v.36.37. Azarias, 2 Paral.15.v.1. Ieremias, Ier.17.v.20.21.& 35.v.14.15. Ezechiel, Ezech.3.17.18. &c. Osee, Ose.10.12. Nonò, Prophetæ & Sacerdotes, Dei iussa & mandata populo retulerunt. exempla: Iethro, Exodi 18.19. Samuel, 1 Sam.15.ver.16.17. Semeia, 2 Paral.11.v.2.3.4. Gad, 2 Sam. 24.v.19.20. Ieremias, Ier.1.17. & 17.v.15.16, Ezechiel, Ezec. 2.8. & 3.17.
units.tr: Eighth, they exhorted men to good works. Examples: The priest is ordered to give the king a copy of the book of the Law, so that he may know that it is part of his office to urge him to piety and good works, Deut. 17. 18. 1 Sam. 14. 36, 37. Azariah, 2 Chron. 15. 1. Jeremiah, Jer. 17. 20, 21, and 35. 14, 15. Ezekiel, Ezek. 3. 17, 18, etc. Hosea, Hos. 10. 12. Ninth, the prophets and priests reported God's commands and orders to the people. Examples: Jethro, Exod. 18. 19. Samuel, 1 Sam. 15. 16, 17. Shemaiah, 2 Chron. 11. 2, 3, 4. Gad, 2 Sam. 24. 19, 20. Jeremiah, Jer. 1. 17, and 17. 15, 16. Ezekiel, Ezek. 2. 8, and 3. 17.

units.la: PROPHETAE & Sacerdotes sinceri ac fideles, ab impiis afflicti & interfecti sunt. Exempla: Abimelech, vna cum octoginta septem Sacerdotibus, 1 Sam.22.18. Iehu, 1 Regum 16.7. Prophetæ à Iezabel, Elia excepto, 19 14 Michæas, 22. verfic.24.25.2 Paralip.18.26 Zacharias, 24.21. Hanani 16. 10. Prophetæ, 4 Esdr.1 32. Matth.23.37. Lucæ 13.34 1 Thess. 2.15. Ieremias, Iere.20.2. Daniel, & socij eius, Dan.3.20. & 6.16.
units.tr: The prophets and priests who were sincere and faithful were afflicted and killed by the impious. Examples: Abimelech, together with eighty-seven priests, 1 Sam. 22. 18. Jehu, 1 Kings 16. 7. The prophets, by Jezebel, except Elijah, 1 Kings 18. 14. Micaiah, 1 Kings 22. 24, 25; 2 Chron. 18. 26. Zechariah, 2 Chron. 24. 21. Hanani, 2 Chron. 16. 10. The prophets, 4 Esd. [2 Esd.] 1. 32; Matt. 23. 37; Luke 13. 34; 1 Thess. 2. 15. Jeremiah, Jer. 20. 2. Daniel and his companions, Dan. 3. 20, and 6. 16.

units.la: PROPHETIS & Ministris omnia mala & calamitates imputantur, exempla: in Mose & Aarone, Exodi 5.21. & 14.v.11. 12. Elia, 1 Reg.18.17. Elisæo, 2 Reg.6.v.30.31. Ieremia, Iere. 44.v.15.16.17. Prophetis propter vaticinia gratitudinis ergo munuscula dabantur. exempla: Saul Samuelis, 1 Sam.9. 7.8. Ieroboam Ahiç, 1 Reg.14.13. Benadad Elisæo, 2 Regum 4.42. Rex Syriæ Elisæo, 8.8. Magister militiæ Ieremiæ, Ier.40.v.4.5.
units.tr: All evils and calamities are imputed to the prophets and ministers. Examples: in Moses and Aaron, Exod. 5. 21, and 14. 11, 12. Elijah, 1 Kings 18. 17. Elisha, 2 Kings 6. 30, 31. Jeremiah, Jer. 44. 15, 16, 17. Small gifts were given to prophets as a mark of thanks. Examples: Saul to Samuel, 1 Sam. 9. 7, 8. Jeroboam to Ahijah, 1 Kings 14. 13. Ben-hadad to Elisha, 2 Kings 8. 9 [4.42 in the Latin text]. The king of Syria to Elisha, 2 Kings 8. 8. The commander of the army to Jeremiah, Jer. 40. 4, 5.

units.la: PROPTETARVM contemtus, 2 Paral. 24.19. & 25.16. & 36.v. 12.16. Ier. 7.25. Prophetarum filij, pro eorum discipulis, 2 Reg.4.38. & 6.1. Prophetarum mos, gestu aut habitu alienam personam exprimere, Ose.1.2. Mic.1.8. exempla: Esaias, Esa.5.1. & 21.v.3.4. Oseas, Ose.1.3. & 2.23. Rom.9.25. Prophetarum verorum & falsorum discrimen, Deut.13.2. & 18.22. Ier.28.9. Prophetarum penuria, irae Dei signum est, Psal.74.9. Ezech.7.26. Vulpi similes, 13.4.
units.tr: The contempt of the prophets: 2 Chron. 24. 19; 25. 16; 36. 12, 16; Jer. 7. 25. The sons of the prophets, as the disciples of the prophets, 2 Kings 4. 38, and 6. 1. It was the custom of the prophets to express another person by gesture or dress: Hos. 1. 2; Mic. 1. 8. Examples: Isaiah, Isa. 5. 1, and 21. 3, 4. Hosea, Hos. 1. 3, and 2. 23; Rom. 9. 25. The distinction between true and false prophets: Deut. 13. 2, and 18. 22; Jer. 28. 9. A shortage of prophets is a sign of God's wrath, Ps. 74. 9; Ezek. 7. 26. They are like foxes, Ezek. 13. 4.

units.la: Prophetarum & Ministrorum verbi Dei in hoc mundo præmia: Primò, Accusatio. exemplum: Oseas, Ose.4.4. Amos, Am.7.10.] Secundò, Carcer. exempla: Michæas, 1 Reg.22. 27. Ieremias, Ierem.20.2. & 32. verfic. 3.4. & 37.15 & 38.6. Hanani, 2 Paral.16.10. Tertiò, Condemnatio. exemplum: Ieremias, Ierem.26.11. Quartò, Conuitia. Exempla: Elisæus, 2 Regum 2.23. Prophetæ qui viri rixarum & discordiæ appellantur in vniuersa terra, Ierem.15.10. Quintò, Criminatio, quòd sint seditiosi, turbulenti & blaphemi. exempla: Elias, 1 Reg.18.17. Ieremias, Ierem.5.13. & 37. 13. & 43.v.2.3. Sextò, Fames. exempla: Elias à corui s & à Sareptana tenuiter pastus, 1 Reg.17.versi.6.7.&c. Centum Prophetæ ab Abdia absconditi, pane, & aqua pasti, 18. ver. 4.13. Septimò, Insidiæ, exemplum: Elias, qui conqueritur se esse in insidias, 1 Regum 19.v.10. 14. Octauo, Mors. exempla: Prophetæ Domini, 1 Reg.18.4. & 19.10.4. Esdr.1.32. Matth. 5.1. & 23.37. Luc.13.34. 1 Thessal.2.15. Vrias, Ieremiæ.26.v.20.26. Ioannes Baptista, Matth.14.10. Marci 6.27. Dauid Psal.109.5. Decimò, Proditio. exempla: Ieremias, qui proditur a Semeia, ob librum Babylonem missum, Ierem.29.v.24.&c. Amos, Amos 7. Vndecimò Subsannatio. Exempla: Prophetæ, & nuntij Dei, 2 Paral.36.v.14.15. V.Ezech.12.6.&24.24. 1 Cor.4.v.9. Duodecimò, Verbera. exempla: Michæas, 1 Reg 22.24. Ieremias, Ierem.20.2.
units.tr: The rewards of prophets and ministers of the Word of God in this world: (1) accusation, example: Hosea, Hos. 4. 4; Amos, Amos 7. 10. (2) Prison, examples: Micaiah, 1 Kings 22. 27; Jeremiah, Jer. 20. 2, and 32. 3, 4, and 37. 15, and 38. 6; Hanani, 2 Chron. 16. 10. (3) Condemnation, example: Jeremiah, Jer. 26. 11. (4) Insults, examples: Elisha, 2 Kings 2. 23; the prophets who are called men of strife and discord in the whole land, Jer. 15. 10. (5) Accusation that they are seditious, troublemakers and blasphemers, examples: Elijah, 1 Kings 18. 17; Jeremiah, Jer. 5. 13, and 37. 13, and 43. 2, 3. (6) Hunger, examples: Elijah, fed meagrely by the ravens and by the woman of Zarephath, 1 Kings 17. 6, 7, etc.; one hundred prophets hidden by Obadiah and fed with bread and water, 1 Kings 18. 4, 13. (7) Ambushes, example: Elijah, who complains that he is in ambushes, 1 Kings 19. 10, 14. (8) Death, examples: the prophets of the Lord, 1 Kings 18. 4, and 19. 10; 4 Esd. [2 Esd.] 1. 32; Matt. 5. 12, and 23. 37; Luke 13. 34; 1 Thess. 2. 15. Uriah, Jer. 26. 20, 23. John the Baptist, Matt. 14. 10; Mark 6. 27. The householders in the parable, Matt. 21. 35; Mark 12. 3, 4, 5; Luke 20. 9, 10, 11, 12. James, the brother of John, Acts 12. 2, etc. Stephen, the first martyr, Acts 7. 59. (9) Hatred, examples: Micaiah, 2 Chron. 18. 7; David, Ps. 109. 5. (10) Betrayal, examples: Jeremiah, who is betrayed by Shemaiah because of the book sent to Babylon, Jer. 29. 24, etc.; Amos, Amos 7. (11) Mockery, examples: the prophets and messengers of God, 2 Chron. 36. 14, 15. See Ezek. 12. 6, and 24. 24; 1 Cor. 4. 9. (12) Beatings, examples: Micaiah, 1 Kings 22. 24; Jeremiah, Jer. 20. 2.

units.la: PROPHETAE falsi, lupis similes, Matth.7.15. falsi Prophetæ habi temporibus, 1 Regum 18.20. ad sanguinem usque seipsos lacerant, ibid. occiduntur, versic.40. falsi Prophetæ reprehendi debent, Ezech.13.2.&22.versic.25.28. Sophon. 3.4.
units.tr: False prophets, like wolves, Matt. 7:15. False prophets were present in the times of 1 Kings 18:20. They lacerate themselves even to blood, ibid. They are slain, v. 40. False prophets ought to be rebuked, Ezek. 13:2; 22:25, 28; Zeph. 3:4.

units.la: In PROPHETIS loqui dicitur Deus, Hebr.1.1. peculiari Hebraeorum id otismo, quo significatur Deum quasi Prophetis ipsis insidentem & animum & linguam eorum statu quodam peculiari fuisse moderatum, vt explicatione. 2 Petr.1.21. Dicitur etiam Deus locutus esse in Filio, Hebr.1.1. vbi Filij nomine totum Christum intellige, qui Deus & homo, vnus est Filius. Sed illud notandum est, aliter locutum fuisse Deum in Filio, quàm in prophetis. Fuit enim Filius, &est vere & σωματικώς, siue κατασας. De Prophetæ verò duntaxat diuino spiritu acti, vt scribi. 2 Petri 1.21. Prophetarum spiritus, quid vocet Paulus Cor.14.32. Vide SPIRITVS Prophetarum. Prophetæ de futura, tanquam de præsenti loquuntur, Malac.3.1. Mat. 1.2. & vt plurimum tempore præterito vtuntur, etiam de re futura loquantur, propter rei certitudinem, Esaiæ 6.& alibi sæpe.
units.tr: God is said to speak through the Prophets, Heb. 1:1, by a peculiarly Hebrew idiom, by which it is signified that God, as it were resting upon the Prophets themselves, so governed both their mind and their tongue by a certain special condition, as the explanation in 2 Pet. 1:21 shows. It is also said that God spoke in the Son, Heb. 1:1, where by the name of the Son you should understand the whole Christ, who is God and man, one Son. But it must be noted that God spoke in the Son otherwise than in the Prophets. For the Son was, and is, truly and bodily [σωματικώς], or essentially [κατ' οὐσίαν]. But of the Prophets only, moved by the divine Spirit, it is written, 2 Pet. 1:21. What Paul calls the spirits of the Prophets, 1 Cor. 14:32. See SPIRIT of the Prophets. The Prophets speak of the future as if of the present, Mal. 3:1; Matt. 1:2, and for the most part they use the past tense even when speaking of future things, on account of the certainty of the event, Isa. 6, and often elsewhere.

units.la: PROPHETAM in nomine Prophetæ recipere, est recipere Prophetam, & eo quod est Propheta, Matt.10.41. vt expectatur Marci 9.41.
units.tr: To receive a Prophet in the name of a Prophet is to receive the Prophet, and because he is a Prophet, Matt. 10:41, as is expected in Mark 9:41.

units.la: PROPHETAE, pro prædicationibus propheticiis, Matth.5. pro librorum libris, Marc. 1.2. pro Apostolis, Ministris, Matth.23.34.
units.tr: PROPHETS: for prophetic preachings, Matt. 5; for the books of the prophets, Mark 1:2; for Apostles and ministers, Matt. 23:34.

units.la: PROPHETARE, pro futura vaticinari, Mat.II.13. pro prophetias interpretari, I Cor.II.v.4 5. & 14 3.
units.tr: TO PROPHESY: to foretell the future, Matt. 11:13; to interpret prophecies, 1 Cor. 11:4–5 and 14:3.

units.la: PROPHETIA, Dei donum, Rom.12.6.1 Cor.12.10. Prophetæ donum optandum, 14.1.&c.interpretatio à Deo, 2 Petr.1. v.20.21.
units.tr: PROPHECY: a gift of God, Rom. 12:6; 1 Cor. 12:10. The gift of prophecy is to be desired, 1 Cor. 14:1, etc. Interpretation comes from God, 2 Pet. 1:20–21.

units.la: PROPINQVITATIS iuri quomodo cesserint Iudæi, Ruth 4. 7.(V. Calceamentum.)
units.tr: KINSHIP RIGHT: how the Jews yielded to it, Ruth 4:7. (See SHOE.)

units.la: PROPITIATIO pro peccatis Christus, 1 Iohann. 2. 2. & 4. 10.
units.tr: PROPITIATION: Christ is the propitiation for sins, 1 John 2:2 and 4:10.

units.la: PROPITIATORIVM & eius forma, Exod. 25. 17. & 37. 6. Hebr.9.5.eius situs, Exodi 26.34. eius antitypus Christus, Roman. 3. 25. Inde Deus Moiem alloquebatur: Exod. 25.22.
units.tr: MERCY SEAT and its form, Exod. 25:17 and 37:6; Heb. 9:5. Its position, Exod. 26:34. Its antitype is Christ, Rom. 3:25. Hence God spoke to Moses, Exod. 25:22.

units.la: PROPOSITIONIS panes, Leuit.24.5. &c. comedit Dauid necessitate coactus, 1 Sam.21.6, Matth.12.3. Marc.2.25. Luc.6.3. V.PANIS.
units.tr: SHOWBREAD: Leviticus 24:5, etc. David, compelled by necessity, ate it, 1 Sam. 21:6; Matt. 12:3; Mark 2:25; Luke 6:3. See BREAD.

units.la: PROPOSITVM vocat Paulus, Rom. 8.27. id quod Deus ab æterno apud se pro bona sua voluntate constituit, ut id plane fit, quòd dicitur, definitum consilium, Acto.2. 23 & beneplacitum Dei, quod proposuit in seipso, Ephes.1.9. & consilium voluntatis Dei, v.11.
units.tr: Paul calls PURPOSE Rom. 8:27 that which God from eternity has determined within himself according to his good pleasure, so that it is plainly what is called the definite counsel, Acts 2:23, and the good pleasure of God, which he purposed in himself, Eph. 1:9, and the counsel of the will of God, v. 11.

units.la: PROSELYTI à sacris Scriptoribus vocantur, genere quidem profani, religione verò Iudæi facti, seu qui ex profanis Gentibus ad Iudaismum erant conuersi, id quod ostendit manifesta Iudæorum & Proselytorum antithesis Act.2.10. siue sint circumcisi, de quibus agere videtur Lucas Act.13.43. siue incircumcisi, qualis fuit Cornelius, què σεβόμενος, hoc est, pium & timentem Deum appellat Lucas, Actor.10.2. reipsa videlicet & corde, quamuis nondum aperto & externo cultu Iudæum. A Græcis vocabantur Proselyti, qui patria relicta superstitione, Iudaismum eamplexi, quasi aduentitios dicas, Matth.23.15. Scribæ, & Pharisæi auebant Proselytos multos facere, & ad Iudaismum conuertere, Matth.23.15. quos se deteriores faciebant.
units.tr: PROSELYTES are called by the sacred writers those who were indeed Gentiles by birth but became Jews in religion, that is, those who from the Gentiles were converted to Judaism. This is shown by the clear contrast between Jews and proselytes, Acts 2:10, whether they were circumcised, of whom Luke seems to speak, Acts 13:43, or uncircumcised, such as Cornelius, whom Luke calls σεβόμενος [God-fearing], that is, pious and fearing God, Acts 10:2, truly indeed in deed and heart, although not yet a Jew by open and outward worship. The Greeks called proselytes those who, having left their native superstition, embraced Judaism; you might call them newcomers. The scribes and Pharisees, Matt. 23:15, sought to make many proselytes and convert them to Judaism, Matt. 23:15, whom they made worse than themselves.
