Prosperitas superbiæ occasio, Roman. 2. 4.Exempla: Israelitæ, Deuter.32.15. Prosperitas Christi tempore, Mich. 4.4. Impiorum prosper.non inuidendum: Psalm.37.1.7.
units.tr: PROSPERITY comes from God, Gen. 39:2; 1 Sam. 18:14; 2 Sam. 5:10; 2 Kings 18:7; 1 Chron. 11:9; 17:8; 18:6; 22:11; 2 Chron. 1:1; 14:6; 15:9; 17:3; 20:30; Ps. 23:5; 90:17; Prov. 3:33; Eccl. 3:13; Isa. 14:3; 26:12; Joel 2:20; Zech. 8:12. The prosperity of the wicked and their sudden destruction, Job 21:7, etc.; Ps. 37:10, 35–36; Isa. 41:12. Prosperity promised to those who fear God, 1 Chron. 22:13; 2 Chron. 19:11; 20:20; 26:5; 27:6; 31:21; 32:30; Ezra 8:22–23; Ps. 25:13–14; Isa. 1:19; 30:23; 48:18; 58:8; Jer. 7:23; 22:4; 31:39; Hos. 2:21. Prosperity restored in the Church, Jer. 31:12, 14. Prosperity is sometimes dangerous, 1 Tim. 6:17. Prosperity is an occasion of pride, Rom. 2:4. Example: the Israelites, Deut. 32:15. Prosperity in the time of Christ, Mic. 4:4. The prosperity of the wicked is not to be envied, Ps. 37:1, 7.

units.la: PROSPERITATIS mala, Proverb.30.9. Ierem.5.7. Ezech.16.49. Oseæ 13.6.Prosperitatis temporalis abusus exempla: Israelitæ,Deuteron.32.15. Gedeon cùm paruus esset homo, & in area frumentum excuteret, bonus fuit, Angelúsque Domini visitauit eum,Iudi.6.12.post obtentam autem & peractam victoriam prospera fortuna abusus est. Fecit enim ex inauribus aureis Ephod, & posuit illud in ciuitate sua Ephra, fornicatúsque est omnis Israel in eo,& factum est Gedeoni & omni eius domui in ruinam, Iudi.8. v.13 14.27.
units.tr: EVILS OF PROSPERITY: Prov. 30:9; Jer. 5:7; Ezek. 16:49; Hos. 13:6. Abuse of temporal prosperity, examples: the Israelites, Deut. 32:15. Gideon, when he was a small man and threshed wheat in the threshing floor, was good, and the Angel of the Lord visited him, Judg. 6:12; but after the victory was won and completed, he abused his prosperous fortune. For he made an ephod from golden earrings and placed it in his city Ophrah, and all Israel played the harlot with it, and it became a ruin to Gideon and to all his house, Judg. 8:13–14, 27.

units.la: Dauid post bella multa & victorias multas, remanens quietus in Ierusalem,committit adulterium, 2 Sam.11.4. post adulterium etiam homicidium, v.15. Occasione multitudinis subditorum in superbiam effertur,& populum numerandum curauit,24. ver.1.2.Salomon,1 Regum 10.vers.26.27.& 11,versi.1.2. 4. Ieroboam antequam consequeretur dominium super decem Tribus, non legitur fuisse malus,sed post fecit vitulos aureos, &c. 1 Reg.12.v. 20.28.Amasias postquam debellauit Edom, eleuatum est cor eius, & voluit contra Ioas Regem Israel pugnare, 2 Reg.14.v.7.8 9.&c.Roboam, 2 Paral.12.v.13 14. Ozias,26 v.16.17. Manasses,33.9.Israelitæ,Nehem.9.v.25.26. Nabuchodonosor,Dan.4.21. Adolescens quidam,Matth.19.22 Diues stolidus,Lucæ 12. v.16.17.18. 19. Villæ emptor,14.v 18.19.Diues epulo,16 19.Herodes,Act.12.v.21.22. Diuites huius seculi,1 Timoth.6.17. Sodoma: Ezech.19 49. Vide Abusus.
units.tr: David, after many wars and many victories, remaining quiet in Jerusalem, committed adultery, 2 Sam. 11:4; after the adultery, also murder, v. 15. Through the multitude of his subjects he was lifted up in pride and had the people numbered, 2 Sam. 24:1–2. Solomon, 1 Kings 10:26–27 and 11:1–2, 4. Jeroboam, before he obtained dominion over the ten tribes, is not read to have been wicked, but afterwards made golden calves, etc., 1 Kings 12:20, 28. Amaziah, after he had defeated Edom, his heart was lifted up and he wished to fight against Joash king of Israel, 2 Kings 14:7–9, etc. Rehoboam, 2 Chron. 12:13–14. Uzziah, 26:16–17. Manasseh, 33:9. The Israelites, Neh. 9:25–26. Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 4:21. A certain young man, Matt. 19:22. The foolish rich man, Luke 12:16–19. The buyer of a farm, Luke 14:18–19. Dives the feaster, Luke 16:19. Herod, Acts 12:21–22. The rich of this age, 1 Tim. 6:17. Sodom, Ezek. 16:49. See ABUSE.

units.la: Prosperitas multos habet amicos.exempla: Fratres, sorores,& amici Iobi,Iob 42.v.10.11.12.
units.tr: Prosperity has many friends. Examples: the brothers, sisters and friends of Job, Job 42:10–12.

units.la: PROSPERIS in rebus exultatio nimia reprehensa, Iac. 4. 9
units.tr: Excessive exultation in prosperous circumstances is rebuked, James 4:9.

units.la: PROSTIBVLI merces non offerenda, Deute.23.18.V.Levit 21.7.
units.tr: The wages of a prostitute are not to be offered, Deut. 23:18. See Lev. 21:7.

units.la: PROTERVIA, ἀσωλγία, est cum aliquid ad inhonestam venerem excitandam, vel ad excitatam fouendam dicimus, facinúsq;lùbentes. Dolor(ait Bernard.)continuus est cordi meo,quòd nonnullos tam pravos ad leuitatè, ad risū,& ad scurrilia verba tam faciles video.Marc.7.22.Rom.13.13.2 Cor.12.21.Gal.5.19.Eph.4.19.1 Pet.4.3. 2.Pet.4.3.2 Pet.2.18.
units.tr: WANTONNESS, ἀσωλγία [licentiousness], is when we speak of anything that stirs up or fosters dishonourable lust, and we delight in deeds. "Continual grief," says Bernard, "is in my heart, because I see some so depraved, so easily given to levity, to laughter, and to scurrilous words." Mark 7:22; Rom. 13:13; 2 Cor. 12:21; Gal. 5:19; Eph. 4:19; 1 Pet. 4:3; 2 Pet. 2:18.

units.la: PROVERBIA,in sacris Scripturis passim occurrunt, Gen.10. 9.1 Sam.10.12.& 19.24.2 Sam.5.8.& 20 18.Pro.22.6. Eze.12. 22.& 18.2.Luc.4.23.Prouerbia Salomonis,&eorum numerus, 1 Reg.4. 32. in prouerbium facti Iudæi, Deut.28.37.1 Reg.9.7.&c.Ab improbis prodit improbitas:1 Sam. 24.14.
units.tr: PROVERBS occur everywhere in the Holy Scriptures: Gen. 10:9; 1 Sam. 10:12; 19:24; 2 Sam. 5:8; 20:18; Prov. 22:6; Ezek. 12:22; 18:2; Luke 4:23. The proverbs of Solomon and their number, 1 Kings 4:32. The Jews became a proverb, Deut. 28:37; 1 Kings 9:7, etc. Wickedness comes forth from the wicked, 1 Sam. 24:14.

units.la: PROVIDENTIA Dei.(V.Dei prouidentia.) Est æternum,sapientissimum iustissimum atque immutabile a consilium siue decretum Dei,quo res b singulas à se cõditas ad suam ipsius c gloriam & electorum d salutem liberrimè gubernat & conseruat.
units.tr: PROVIDENCE of God. (See God's providence.) It is the eternal, most wise, most just and unchangeable counsel or decree of God, by which he most freely governs and preserves each single thing created by him, for his own glory and the salvation of the elect.

units.la: PROXIMVS qui habendus,Luc.10. versi.36.37. proximus non temerè à nobis iudicandus Rom. 14. 4.Iac.4.11.12 proximi dilectio,Legis est complementum,Rom.13.ver.8.9.10. Gal.5.14. (Vide Charitas.)Inimicus etiam, est proximus: Ex.23.4 5.
units.tr: Who is to be regarded as NEIGHBOUR, Luke 10:36–37. A neighbour is not to be judged rashly by us, Rom. 14:4; James 4:11–12. The love of neighbour is the fulfilment of the Law, Rom. 13:8–10; Gal. 5:14. (See Love.) Even an enemy is a neighbour, Exod. 23:4–5.

units.la: PROXIMVS est omnis homo, cuiuscunq; sit sexus, nationis, cognationis,religionis,& erga nos affectionis : quem diligere & cui benefacere iubemur.Rom.12.18. Gal.6.10. Luc. 10.30.&c.
units.tr: Every person is a NEIGHBOUR, whatever his sex, nation, kindred, religion, and his disposition towards us, whom we are commanded to love and to do good to, Rom. 12:18; Gal. 6:10; Luke 10:30, etc.

units.la: PROXIMI dilectio præcipitur,Leu.19.18.Mat.22.39.Marc.12. 31.Luc.10.27. Iac. 2.8. proximi dilectio sacrificiis præfertur,Marci 12.33. V.Mât.5 43. &c.
units.tr: The love of neighbour is commanded, Lev. 19:18; Matt. 22:39; Mark 12:31; Luke 10:27; James 2:8. The love of neighbour is preferred to sacrifices, Mark 12:33. See Matt. 5:43, etc.

units.la: PROXIMORVM contemtores, Malach. 2. 10. damnantur, ibid.
units.tr: Contemners of neighbours are condemned, Mal. 2:10, ibid.

units.la: PROXIMO placendum ad ædificationem, Rom.15.2.
units.tr: We must please our neighbour for edification, Rom. 15:2.

units.la: PROXIMIS etiam ignotis benefaciendum. exemplum: Moses, Exodi 2. 17.
units.tr: We must do good even to neighbours unknown to us. Example: Moses, Exod. 2:17.

units.la: PRVDENTIA, est per quam dirigimus vnamquanq; actionẽ, & præuidemus quid agamus,quando, quo loco,quo tempore,coram quibus,vt omnia conueniente loco,tempore, & modo fiant,secundum voluntatem Dei.Eph.5.15.16.17.
units.tr: PRUDENCE is that by which we direct each single action, and foresee what we are doing, when, in what place, at what time, before whom, so that all things are done in a suitable place, time and manner, according to the will of God, Eph. 5:15–17.

units.la: PRVDENTIA à Deo est, 1 par. 22.12. Luc.1.17. Rom.8.6. piis omnibus necessaria, Matt.10.16. 1 petr.4 7. sed pastoribus maximè, 1 Tim. 3. 2. & senibus, Tit. 2. v.2.5. in loquendo necessaria, prouerb. 13.3 & 17.27. units.tr: Prudence comes from God, 1 Chron. 22:12; Luke 1:17; Rom. 8:6. It is necessary for all the pious, Matt. 10:16; 1 Pet. 4:7, but above all for ministers, 1 Tim. 3:2, and for elders, Titus 2:2, 5. It is necessary in speaking, Prov. 13:3 and 17:27. Examples of prudence and discretion: Abraham, Gen. 13:9 and 25:5–6; Jacob, 30:32 and 32:3, 7; Joseph, 40:14 and 41:33–38; Jethro, Exod. 18:19; Rahab, Josh. 2:4; Joshua, 8:15; Jotham, Judg. 9:7; the Gileadites, 12:6; the eleven tribes, 20:32; Saul, 1 Sam. 10:27; Abigail, 25:18, 36; the woman of Tekoa, 2 Sam. 14:2; the woman of Abel, 20:16; Bathsheba, 1 Kings 1:15; Solomon, 3:9, 25–28; the old counsellors of Rehoboam, 12:7; Jehoiada, 2 Kings 11:4; 2 Chron. 23:1; the people of Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18:36; Hezekiah, Isa. 36:21; 2 Chron. 32:3; Nehemiah, Neh. 2:12; Esther, Esther 4:11; Mordecai, v. 12; Tobit; Job, 4:19; Judith, Judith 4:10 and 11:19; Christ, Matt. 21:24; Mark 11:29; Luke 20:3; the Virgin Mother of God, Luke 1:29; the unjust steward, Luke 16:8; Christ, Luke 2:47 and 20:24; John 8:7; Paul, Acts 16:37; a certain prince of Asia, 19:31; Paul, 22:25 and 23:6, 17; and 25:11; the tribune, 23:23.

units.la: PRVDENTIA carnis & mundi damnatur, prou.3.5. Esai.29. 14.1 Cor.1.19. Rom.8.6. &12.16. prudentię carnis argumenta,2 Pet.3.4. Prudentiæ carnalis exempla: Esau, Gen. 25.32. Pilatus, Luc.23.v,16 22. Ioann.19.1. Nicodemus, Ioan.3.4. Pharisæi,7.48. Iudæi,8,52. prudentiæ propriæ non inni-tendum, prouer.12.v.2.15. & 17.12. Esa.5.21.& 30.1. Abd.v.8. Prudentia spiritus, Rom.8 6.
units.tr: Prudence of the flesh and of the world is condemned, Prov. 3.5; Isa. 29.14; 1 Cor. 1.19; Rom. 8.6; and 12.16. Arguments of fleshly prudence, 2 Pet. 3.4. Examples of fleshly prudence: Esau, Gen. 25.32; Pilate, Luke 23.16, 22; John 19.1; Nicodemus, John 3.4; the Pharisees, 7.48; the Jews, 8.52. One must not rely on one's own prudence, Prov. 12.2, 15; 17.12; Isa. 5.21; 30.1; Obad. v. 8. The prudence of the Spirit, Rom. 8.6.

units.la: PRVDENS Dauid in omnibus, 1 Sam.18.14. & 21.13. prudētes & simplices simus, Matth.10.16.
units.tr: PRUDENT: David was prudent in all things, 1 Sam. 18.14; 21.13. We should be prudent and simple, Matt. 10.16.

units.la: PRVRIGINE percutiuntur inobedientes, Deut.28.27.
units.tr: ITCH: the disobedient are struck with the itch, Deut. 28.27.

units.la: PSALLENDVM Deo, & quomodo, Eph.5.19. Col.3.16. spiritu, & mente, id est, gratiæ agendæ, Iudic.5.3.1 Corint.14.15 psallendum tempore lætitiæ Iac.5.13. V. Cantandum.
units.tr: SINGING: God is to be sung to, and how, Eph. 5.19; Col. 3.16; with the spirit and with the mind, that is, to give thanks, Judg. 5.3; 1 Cor. 14.15. Singing is to be done in a time of joy, James 5.13. See Cantandum.

units.la: PSALTES egregius Dauid, 2 Sam.23.1.
units.tr: PSALMIST: the outstanding David, 2 Sam. 23.1.

units.la: PSEVDOAPOSTOLI, operarij subdoli, describuntur, 2 Corinth.11.13. phil.3.v.2.18.19. Tit.1.10. ab illis cauendum, phil.3.2.18. pseudoapostoli crucis Christi inimici, Gal.6. 12. phil.3.18.
units.tr: FALSE APOSTLES, deceitful workers, are described: 2 Cor. 11.13; Phil. 3.2, 18, 19; Titus 1.10. One must beware of them, Phil. 3.2, 18. False apostles are enemies of the cross of Christ, Gal. 6.12; Phil. 3.18.

units.la: PSEVDOAPOSTOLORVM erroris præcipuum caput, Act. 15.1. interitus.2 Cor.11.15.
units.tr: FALSE APOSTLES: the chief head of their error, Acts 15.1. Their destruction, 2 Cor. 11.15.

units.la: PSEVDOCHRISTI in Ecclesia futuri, Matthæi 24.24. Mar.13. 6. Luc.21.8.
units.tr: FALSE CHRISTS who will arise in the Church, Matt. 24.24; Mark 13.6; Luke 21.8.

units.la: PSEVDOPROPHETAE & eorum punitio, & quòd non sint audiend, Deut. 3.1. & 18 20. Regum. 13. 1. & 18.40. & 22.v.6 10.2. Reg.10.19 Prou.28 10. Esa.3.11, & 28,7,& 56. o.lerem.14 v. 3. 5.& 23 1.&c.27.9,& 28.1 &c 29.v.8.21 25.Ezech 13,ver.1, &c.14 9. & 22,25, & 34 v 2,8 18, Amos 7, o. Mich.3,5 Zachar.13,2, Matt.7,15, & 24,11, Marc.8,15, & 13,6, Luc.12,1 & 17,23. Actor.20,29,1 Cor. 15,32, Phil.3,2, Col.2,8,1 Tim.4,1, 2 Timot.2.17. & 3.1 2 pet. 2,1, &c.Iudæ v.4,8, &c. Pseudoprophetæ habentur, qui antequam mittantur,currunt, Ierem.14, 14, & 23 32,& 27,15, Ezech. 13 4 6,
units.tr: FALSE PROPHETS, their punishment, and that they are not to be heard: Deut. 13.1; 18.20; 1 Kings 13.1; 18.40; 22.6; 2 Kings 10.2, 19; Prov. 28.10; Isa. 3.11; 28.7; 56.10; Jer. 14.3; 5.31; 23.1, etc.; 27.9; 28.1, etc.; 29.8, 21; 25; Ezek. 13.1, etc.; 14.9; 22.25; 34.2, 8, 18; Amos 7.10; Mic. 3.5; Zech. 13.2; Matt. 7.15; 24.11; Mark 8.15; 13.6; Luke 12.1; 17.23; Acts 20.29; 1 Cor. 15.32; Phil. 3.2; Col. 2.8; 1 Tim. 4.1; 2 Tim. 2.17; 3.1; 2 Pet. 2.1, etc.; Jude v. 4, 8, etc. Those are regarded as false prophets who run before they are sent, Jer. 14.14; 23.32; 27.15; Ezek. 13.4, 6.

units.la: pseudoprophetarum merces ab impiis: Primò, auditorum frequentia & applausus, Psal.73.9. Ier.5.31.
units.tr: The wages of false prophets from the impious. First, the crowd of hearers and their applause, Ps. 73.9; Jer. 5.31.

units.la: Secundo, Fauor & honor, Quadringenti quinquaginta Prophetæ Baal, de mensa Iezabel comedunt, 1 Reg.18,19, Elias verò in maximis periculis versatur, 19.10 & cum fame conflictatur, 17. 4, &c. Illi in precio habentur Achabuni, 22.6. Micheas verò odio est illi v.8 2 Par.18.7. ideóqj in custodiam traditur, 1.Reg. 22. 27. Tertiò munera & ampla commoda: Pseudoprophetæ Israel, Esa 56 v. 10.11.Ezec.13 v.18.19.& 34.v 3.4. Pseudoprophetarum notæ duæ: Falsa doctrina,& mali mores, Mat.7.v.15.16. ideóque vitandi, v.15. Mar.8.15, Luc.17.23.
units.tr: Secondly, favour and honour: the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal eat at Jezebel's table, 1 Kings 18.19; but Elijah is in the greatest dangers and struggles with famine, 17.4, etc. The former are held in high esteem by Ahab, 22.6; but Micaiah is hated by him, v. 8; 2 Chron. 18.7, and therefore is handed over to custody, 1 Kings 22.27. Thirdly, gifts and ample advantages: the false prophets of Israel, Isa. 56.10–11; Ezek. 13.18–19; 34.3–4. Two marks of false prophets: false doctrine and evil morals, Matt. 7.15–16; therefore they are to be avoided, v. 15; Mark 8.15; Luke 17.23.

units.la: PTOLEMAIS, (antea Achum dicta) civitas in Iudea: Act.21.7.
units.tr: PTOLEMAIS (formerly called Accho), a city in Judea: Acts 21.7.

units.la: PUBLICANI. Publicani, qui vectigalia publica redimebant, sic vocati, Iudæis exosi, Matth.9.11. Marc.2.16. Luc.5.30. tum quòd profanis hominibus, id est, equitibus Romanis operam suam, quasi ad opprimendam populi Dei libertatem locassent: tum quòd hoc hominum genus, avaritiæ nomine pessimè semper audiverit: tum postremò quòd Iudæi iniquissimè ferrent Romanorum iugum, Matth.9.10. Publicani autem vt plurimum prouinciales erant, & quia hi, Iudæa in prouinciam redacta, operam suam ad exactionem tributorum Romanis locabant. & cum iis plerumque versabantur, à cæteris Iudæis inter profanos censebantur, illisque odiosi erant, vt dictum est, & peccatores ac scelerati vocabantur, nec in synedria recipiebantur, rel gionis quidem obtentu, quòd cum circumcisis communem vitæ consuetudinem haberent, sed reuera Romanorum iugum exosi, quibus isti operam locabant, Publicani Deum iustificant, Luc.7.29. Publicani & meretrices Euangelio credunt. Matth. 21.32. Publicani & Pharisæi parabola, Luc. 18.10. publicanorum officium describitur Luc. 3. ver. 12.13. videlicet ne plus exigant, quàm constitutum est eis, ibid.
units.tr: PUBLICANS. The publicans, who farmed the public revenues, were so called. They were hated by the Jews, Matt. 9.11; Mark 2.16; Luke 5.30: partly because they had let out their services to profane men, that is, to Roman knights, as if to crush the freedom of God's people; partly because this class of men has always been spoken of very badly under the name of greed; and finally because the Jews took very ill the yoke of the Romans, Matt. 9.10. Publicans, however, were for the most part provincials, and since Judea had been reduced to a province, they let out their services to the Romans for the collection of tributes. They generally associated with them, and were counted among the profane by the other Jews and were hated by them, as has been said. They were called sinners and wicked, and were not received into the synedria, ostensibly on the ground of religion, because they had common social life with the circumcised, but in truth because they were hated for the Roman yoke to which these men let out their services. Publicans justify God, Luke 7.29. Publicans and harlots believe the gospel, Matt. 21.32. Publicans and Pharisees, a parable, Luke 18.10. The duty of publicans is described, Luke 3.12–13, namely that they should not exact more than what was appointed for them, ibid.

units.la: Publius Melitæ insulæ primarius, Paulum & eius comites hospitio excipit, Actor. 28. 7. pater febre à Paulo leuatur, 8.
units.tr: Publius, the chief man of the island of Malta, receives Paul and his companions hospitably, Acts 28.7. His father is relieved of fever by Paul, 8.

units.la: Pudor interdum vtilis est, 1 Cor. 15. 34. Ephes. 5. 12. 2. Thess. 3. 14. pudor ex peccato, Gen. 3. 7. V. 2. v. 25.
units.tr: Shame is sometimes useful, 1 Cor. 15.34; Eph. 5.12; 2 Thess. 3.14. Shame arising from sin, Gen. 3.7; cf. 2.25.

units.la: Puella vouens, quatenus voto teneatur, Num. 30. v. 4.5.
units.tr: Girl making a vow, insofar as she is bound by the vow, Num. 30.4–5.

units.la: [Puer ætate, nempe ad infantia vsque ad iuuentutem, Genes. 21. v. 8.14. Luc. 1. v. 59. 80. Puer iuuenis, Genes. 19. 4. & 37. 2. Exod. 33. 11. 1. Samuel. 2. 18. & 17. 42. Puer discipulus, Esai. 8. 18. puer, miles, 1 Sam. 25. 9. &c. 26. 22. 2 Sam. 2. 14. Puer, seruus, minister, vario munere fungens, domi & foris, Gen. 18. 7. 2 Sam. 9. 9. Luc. 7. 7. puer, seruus honorarius, Gen. 19. 2. 1 Sam. 25. 8. puer nomen, quo amicos, aut familiares & notos, blandè quis compellat, Ioan. 21. 5. puer qui iudicio non pollet, Eccl. 10. 16. Esai. 3. 4. Ierem. 1. v. 6. 7. 1 Cor. 14. 20. puer, seruus Dei Patris nempe Christus Mediator, Ecclesiæ caput, & seruorum Dei Princeps, Matt. 12. 18. Act. 4. 27. puer, seruus Dei, Abrahamus, Israelis populus, Dauid, Leuitarum grex, Psal. 105. 42. & 113. 1. & 134. 1. Luc. 1. 54. 69. Act. 4. 25.]
units.tr: [Boy by age, namely from infancy up to youth, Gen. 21.8, 14; Luke 1.59, 80. Boy as young man, Gen. 19.4; 37.2; Exod. 33.11; 1 Sam. 2.18; 17.42. Boy as disciple, Isa. 8.18. Boy as soldier, 1 Sam. 25.9, etc.; 26.22; 2 Sam. 2.14. Boy as servant, minister, performing various duties at home and abroad, Gen. 18.7; 2 Sam. 9.9; Luke 7.7. Boy as a servant of honour, Gen. 19.2; 1 Sam. 25.8. Boy as a name by which someone affectionately addresses friends, intimates or acquaintances, John 21.5. Boy who lacks judgment, Eccl. 10.16; Isa. 3.4; Jer. 1.6–7; 1 Cor. 14.20. Boy, the servant of God the Father, namely Christ the Mediator, head of the Church and prince of God's servants, Matt. 12.18; Acts 4.27. Boy, the servant of God: Abraham, the people of Israel, David, the flock of the Levites, Ps. 105.42; 113.1; 134.1; Luke 1.54, 69; Acts 4.25.]

units.la: Pueri Elisæo illudentes, ab vrsis lacerantur, 2 Regum. 2. 24. puer efficiatur, qui vult ingredi regnum Dei, Matt. 18. 3. puerum amplectitur Christus, Marc. 9. 36. & 10. 16. Pueri adducuntur ad Christum, Mat. 19. 13. Luc. 18. 15. non scandalizandi, Mat. 18. 6. precantur Christo salutem, 21, 15. Puerorum est regnum cœlorum, 19. 14. Vide PARVVLI. pueris Angeli custodes adhibiti, 18. 10.
units.tr: Boys mocking Elisha are torn by bears, 2 Kings 2.24. One must become a child to enter the kingdom of God, Matt. 18.3. Christ embraces a child, Mark 9.36; 10.16. Children are brought to Christ, Matt. 19.13; Luke 18.15. They are not to be made to stumble, Matt. 18.6. They cry out to Christ for salvation, 21.15. Of such is the kingdom of heaven, 19.14. See PARVULI. Guardian angels are assigned to children, 18.10.

units.la: Puericia amanda, Matth. 18. v. 3, 4. 5. 1 Cor. 14. 20. puericia quæ fugienda, ibid. puericia virgis coercenda, Prou. 13. 24. & 22. 15. & 23. 13. Hebr. 12. 7.
units.tr: Childhood is to be loved, Matt. 18.3–5; 1 Cor. 14.20. Childishness is to be shunned, ibid. Childhood is to be restrained with the rod, Prov. 13.24; 22.15; 23.13; Heb. 12.7.

units.la: Pugnat pro Israelitis Deus, Exod. 14. 14. Deut. 3. 22.
units.tr: God fights for the Israelites, Exod. 14.14; Deut. 3.22.

units.la: Pugnator noster Deus, Exodi 15. 3.
units.tr: Our God is a warrior, Exod. 15.3.

units.la: Pugnae legis vitandæ, Tit. 3. 9. V. 1. Tim. 1. 4. 2. Tim. 2. 23.
units.tr: Quarrels of the law are to be avoided, Titus 3.9; cf. 1 Tim. 1.4; 2 Tim. 2.23.

units.la: Pulchritudo meretricis periculosa, Prou. 6. 25. 26. & 11. 22. & 31. 30. pulchritudinis exempla: Sarai, Gen. 12. v. 11. 14. Filiæ hominum, 6. 2. Rebecca. 24. 16. & 26. 7. Rachel, 29. 17. Ioseph, 39. 6. & 49. 22. Moses Exod. 2. 2. Noemi (hoc est, pulchra) Ruth 1. 20. Saul, 1 Sam. 9. 2. & 10. 24. Dauid. 16. v. 12. 18. & 17.42. Abigail, 25.3. Saul & Ionathas, 2. Sam. 1. 23. Ionathas, v.26. Bethsabee, 11.2. Thamar Absalonis soror 13.1. Thamar Absalonis filia, 14.27. Absalom, v.25.26. Abilag, 1 Regum 1.4. Adonias, v.6. Vasthi, Esth. 1.11. Esther, Esther 2.7. Filiae Iob. Iob 42.15. Daniel & socij eius, Dan. 1.4. homo, Gen. 3.19. & 18.27. puluere caput aspergebant Hebraei dolentes, Ios. 7.6. puluis pedum excutien-dus in contemtores Euangelij, Matth. 10.14. Luc. 6.5. Exempla: Paulus & Barnabas: Act. 13.51 & 18.6.
units.tr: Beauty of a harlot is dangerous, Prov. 6.25–26; 11.22; 31.30. Examples of beauty: Sarai, Gen. 12.11, 14; the daughters of men, 6.2; Rebekah, 24.16; 26.7; Rachel, 29.17; Joseph, 39.6; 49.22; Moses, Exod. 2.2; Naomi (that is, pleasant), Ruth 1.20; Saul, 1 Sam. 9.2; 10.24; David, 16.12, 18; 17.42; Abigail, 25.3; Saul and Jonathan, 2 Sam. 1.23; Jonathan, v. 26; Bathsheba, 11.2; Tamar, sister of Absalom, 13.1; Tamar, daughter of Absalom, 14.27; Absalom, vv. 25–26; Abishag, 1 Kings 1.4; Adonijah, v. 6; Vashti, Esth. 1.11; Esther, Esth. 2.7; the daughters of Job, Job 42.15; Daniel and his companions, Dan. 1.4. Man: Gen. 3.19; 18.27. The Hebrews, grieving, sprinkled dust on their heads, Josh. 7.6. Dust is to be shaken from the feet against the despisers of the gospel, Matt. 10.14; Luke 9.5. Examples: Paul and Barnabas, Acts 13.51; 18.6.

units.la: se dicit Dauid, 1 Sam. 24.15. & 26.20.
units.tr: David calls himself (a dead dog, a flea), 1 Sam. 24.15; 26.20.

units.la: commendatur, Exod. 22. 22. Deut. 24. v. 17.26. & 27.19. Psal. 82.3. Zach. 7.10. Iac. 1.27 (V. Orphanus) Decimis alendi, Deut. 14.29. His Deus iudicium facit: 10.18. oculi, custoditus Israel, Deuteron. 32.10. pupillam oculi Dei tangit, qui tangit, Christos suos, Zachar. 2.8. V. Psal. 17.8. pro. 7.2.
units.tr: The fatherless is commended, Exod. 22.22; Deut. 24.17; 26; 27.19; Ps. 82.3; Zech. 7.10; James 1.27 (see Orphan). They are to be fed from the tithes, Deut. 14.29. God executes judgment for them, Deut. 10.18. Israel is kept as the apple of God's eye, Deut. 32.10. He who touches the pupil of God's eye touches his anointed ones, Zech. 2.8. See Ps. 17.8; Prov. 7.2.

units.la: peccatorum per Christum, Heb. 1.3. purgatio-nis nostrae finis, Cultus: 9.14. V.2 Pet. 1.9.
units.tr: The purging of sins through Christ, Heb. 1.3. The end of our purification (worship), Heb. 9.14; see 2 Pet. 1.9.

units.la: (id est locus, vbi animas defunctorum esse, & virorum precibus ac bonis operibus iuuari & purgari contendunt) Pontificij confirmare niruntur ex Mat. 5.v.23 24.25 & 12 32. Luc. 12.59. 1. Cor. 3.16. Phil. 2.10. 2 Tim. 1.18 1. Ioan. 5.15. Apoc. 5.v 3 13.
units.tr: (That is, the place where they contend that the souls of the dead are, and are helped and purged by the prayers and good works of the living.) The Papists try to confirm this from Matt. 5:23, 24, 25 and 12:32; Luke 12:59; 1 Cor. 3:16; Phil. 2:10; 2 Tim. 1:18; 1 John 5:15; Rev. 5:3, 13.

units.la: Sed & commentitius Romanensium purgatoriusignis & omnes humanae satisfactiones destruuntur his locis, Psalm. 32.1. & 51.9. & 103.12 Esa. 1.18. & 43.25. & 44.22. & 53.5 Ierem. 50.20. Mich. 7.19. Matt. 20.28. Luc. 16.22. & 23.43. Ioan. 19.30 Actor. 15.9. Rom. 5 v.1.10. & 8.v.1.33 1 Corint. 1.30. 2 Cor. 4.17.18. Fallum est ergo, poenam temporalem in purgatorio purgari, & 5 v.1.18.21. Ephes. 1.7. & 5.25.26. Col. 1 v.14.19.20. & 2.13. Phil. 1.23. 1 Thess. 4.7.18. 1. Tim. 2.5.6.2. Tim. 4. v.6 7.8. Hebr. 1.3. & 9.14. & 12. v.22 23.24 & 10 v. 14.17. 8.1 Petr. 2.24 & 5.10. 1. Ioann. 1. v.7.9. & 2.1.2. & 4.10. Apoc. 1.5.6. & 7.14. & 14.13. Ex quibus omnibus liquido constat, Christum pertulisse poenas peccatis nostris debitas, nobis non amplius perferendas, & suo sanguine semel in ara crucis effuso nos emundasse ab omni peccato, ac proinde non opus habere nos noua purgatione. Vide Culpa: & Satisfactiones.
units.tr: But the made-up purgatorial fire of the Romanists and all human satisfactions are also overthrown by these passages: Ps. 32:1; 51:9; 103:12; Isa. 1:18; 43:25; 44:22; 53:5; Jer. 50:20; Mic. 7:19; Matt. 20:28; Luke 16:22; 23:43; John 19:30; Acts 15:9; Rom. 5:1, 10; 8:1, 33; 1 Cor. 1:30; 2 Cor. 4:17, 18; Eph. 1:7; 5:25, 26; Col. 1:14, 19, 20; 2:13; Phil. 1:23; 1 Thess. 4:7, 18; 1 Tim. 2:5, 6; 2 Tim. 4:6, 7, 8; Heb. 1:3; 9:14; 12:22, 23, 24; 10:14, 17; 1 Pet. 2:24; 5:10; 1 John 1:7, 9; 2:1, 2; 4:10; Rev. 1:5, 6; 7:14; 14:13. Therefore it is false that the temporal punishment is purged in purgatory. From all these passages it is clear that Christ bore the punishments owed to our sins, which we need no longer bear, and that by his blood, once shed on the altar of the cross, he has cleansed us from all sin; therefore we have no need of any new purgation. See Culpa and Satisfactions.

units.la: PVRIM, fuerunt imperatiuae feriae Iudaeorum, a regina Esther & Mardochaeo institutae, quae 14. & 15. diebus mensis Adar celebrabatur, ad memoriam crudelissimi consilij Hamanis,
units.tr: PURIM, the imperative festival days of the Jews, instituted by Queen Esther and Mordecai, which were celebrated on the 14th and 15th days of the month Adar, in memory of the most cruel plan of Haman,

units.la: de Iudæis vbique trucidandis, diuinitus impediti. Esther 9.17.
units.tr: to slaughter the Jews everywhere, which was divinely prevented. Esth. 9:17.

units.la: PVRIFICATIO leuitarum, Num.8.7.& 9.9. Purificationes Iudæorum, V.IVDAEVS.
units.tr: PURIFICATION of the Levites, Num. 8:7; 9:9. The purifications of the Jews: see JEW.

units.la: PVSILLANIMITAS, est timor honoris egregij vel adipiscendi, vel adepti administratio regnis, quę mollities animi appellatur.
units.tr: PUSILLANIMITY is fear of either obtaining or administering a distinguished honour, or of an office once obtained; it is called softness of spirit.

units.la: PVSILLANIMES confirmandi & consolandi sunt, Isa.35.4.1 Thes.5.14. Pusillanimitatis exempla: Loth, Gen.19 19 Filij Israel, Exod.14.10.& 20.19. Exploratores terrae Chanaan, Num.13 29. Israelitae, Ios.7. v.4 5. Saul & Israelitae,1 Sam.17.11.& 28.5. Roboam,2 Paral.13 7. Achaz & populus eius, Esa.7.2. Apostoli, Mat.8 26. Petrus, 14.30.& 26 58. Discipuli Christi, v.56. quidam iuuenis, Marc.14.52. Nicodemus, Ioan.3.2. Coeci nati parentes,9 22. quidam Principes Iudaeorum,12.42. V.Iudic.6.13 4.
units.tr: The PUSILLANIMOUS are to be strengthened and comforted: Isa. 35:4; 1 Thess. 5:14. Examples of pusillanimity: Lot, Gen. 19:19; the sons of Israel, Exod. 14:10; 20:19; the spies of the land of Canaan, Num. 13:29; the Israelites, Josh. 7:4, 5; Saul and the Israelites, 1 Sam. 17:11; 28:5; Rehoboam, 2 Chr. 13:7; Ahaz and his people, Isa. 7:2; the apostles, Matt. 8:26; Peter, 14:30; 26:58; the disciples of Christ, v. 56; a certain young man, Mark 14:52; Nicodemus, John 3:2; the parents of the man born blind, 9:22; certain rulers of the Jews, 12:42. See Judg. 6:13; 4.

units.la: PVTEI Abrahae obstruuntur a Philistaeis, Gen.26.5. V.Exo.21.3.3.
units.tr: The WELLS of Abraham were stopped up by the Philistines, Gen. 26:15. See Exod. 21:3, 3.

units.la: PYGARGVM non comedebant Iudaei, Deu.14.5.
units.tr: The Jews did not eat the PYGARG, Deut. 14:5.

units.la: PYTHONES non consulendi, Deut.18 11. Levit.19.31. Esa 8.19. morte moriantur, Levit.20.27. Pyrhones aufert Iosias,2 Reg.23.24. Saul,1 Sam.28 9. Pythonissam consulit Saul,1 Sam.28 8 &c. Unde partim mortuus fuisse dicitur: 1 Par.10.13. Pythonis testimonium aegre fert paulus, Act.16.18. vt & Christus Diaboli. Vide DIABOLIS non permittitur, &c. V.Diuini, Manasses,2 Reg 21.8.
units.tr: PYTHONS are not to be consulted, Deut. 18:11; Lev. 19:31; Isa. 8:19; they are to be put to death, Lev. 20:27. Josiah removed the pythons, 2 Kings 23:24. Saul, 1 Sam. 28:9. Saul consults the Pythoness, 1 Sam. 28:8, etc. Hence he is said to have partly died, 1 Chr. 10:13. Paul was displeased with the testimony of the python, Acts 16:18, as also with Christ's (testimony of the) devil. See DEVILS are not permitted, etc. See DIVINERS: Manasseh, 2 Kings 21:8.

units.la: PVTEOLI, civitas Campaniae: vbi 7.dies mansit Paulus: Act.28.13.
units.tr: PUTEOLI, a city of Campania, where Paul stayed seven days, Acts 28:13.

units.la: Q.
units.tr: Q.

units.la: Q[?]VADRAGESIMALIS ieiunij exempla: Vide IEIVNIVM miraculosum.
units.tr: QUADRAGESIMAL examples of fasting: see FASTING, miraculous.

units.la: QVADRANTEM vsque ad vltimum soluere, dicitur proverbialiter is, qui cum summo iure agitur. Mat.5 26.
units.tr: To pay the last farthing is proverbially said of one who is dealt with under the strictest law. Matt. 5:26.

units.la: QVADRIGARVM visio, vide CVRRVS.
units.tr: The vision of the chariots: see CHARIOT.

units.la: [Quadrigarum bellicarum vsus frequens, Iudic 5.28.1 Paral.18.4. Esai.36 9.& 37.24. Mich.5.10. Quadrigae, ad luxum. Esai 2.7.& 22.7. Quadrigae mysticae, Zacharch.6.v.1.2.3. Quadrigis & equis non fidendum, Esa.31.1 Ps.20.8.]
units.tr: [Frequent use of war chariots: Judg. 5:28; 1 Chr. 18:4; Isa. 36:9; 37:24; Mic. 5:10. Chariots for luxury: Isa. 2:7; 22:7. Mystical chariots: Zech. 6:1, 2, 3. Do not trust in chariots and horses: Isa. 31:1; Ps. 20:8.]

units.la: QVADRVPEDES, pro iis duntaxat animantibus, quæ ad communem hominum vsum ah solent, Act.10.12. Rom. 13.
units.tr: QUADRUPEDS, meaning only those animals which are commonly used by men, Acts 10:12; Rom. 13.

units.la: QVADRVPLVM, 2 Sam.12.6. Luc.19.8. Exod.22 1.]
units.tr: QUADRUPLE: 2 Sam. 12:6; Luke 19:8; Exod. 22:1.]

units.la: QVAERENDVS Deus, Deut.4.29. Vide Devs.
units.tr: GOD is to be sought, Deut. 4:29. See GOD.

units.la: Quærit Ecclesia Christum sponsum, Cant.3.v.1.2. & 5. v.6. & 6.1.
units.tr: The Church seeks Christ her bridegroom, Song 3:1, 2, and 5:6; 6:1.

units.la: Quærit homo hominem, aliam rem creatam vel arte factam, negotium, &c. Genes.37. v 15.16. Exod. 4. 19. 1 Sam.9.3 2 Sam.17.3.1 Reg.v 1.2. Esther.2.v.2.15. &c. Psalm. 37.v.10.25.32.36. Proverb 2 4. Quærit homo salutaria sibi & meliorem vitam spectantia Matth. 6.33. & 7.vers.7.8. Col.3.1.
units.tr: Man seeks another man, or another created or manufactured thing, or business, etc.: Gen. 37:15, 16; Exod. 4:19; 1 Sam. 9:3; 2 Sam. 17:3; 1 Kings 1:2; Esth. 2:2, 15, etc.; Ps. 37:10, 25, 32, 36; Prov. 2:4. Man seeks what is salutary for himself and pertains to a better life: Matt. 6:33; 7:7, 8; Col. 3:1.

units.la: Quærit Christus, Luc.13.v.6.7.& 19.10. Ioan.5 30.
units.tr: Christ seeks: Luke 13:6, 7; 19:10; John 5:30.

units.la: Quærit Deus Pater, Ioan.4 23.
units.tr: God the Father seeks: John 4:23.

units.la: Quærunt animalia escam sibi à Deo, Psal.104.21 27.
units.tr: Animals seek their food from God: Ps. 104:21, 27.

units.la: Quærit Diabolus, Matth.12.43. Luc.11.24.1 Petr.5 8.]
units.tr: The Devil seeks: Matt. 12:43; Luke 11:24; 1 Pet. 5:8.]
See Luke 22:31.

units.la: QVÆSTIONES variæ, & earum solutiones: Quæstio de vera Dei adoratione, Ioan.4.ver.20.21.22.23. de cuiusdam cæcitatis causa 9.v.2.3. de modo, quo fit Christum concep-tura Maria, Luc.1.v.34 35. An Iesus sit Christus, 22.v.67, 69.70. Ioan.10.v.24.25, 26.27. An sit Filius Dei, Matth. 22.v.42 43.44 45. Marci 12. 35. Luc. 20.v. 42.43.44. de Christi discessu, Ioann.13 36. de carnis Christi manducatione, Ioan.6.ver.52. 61.62 63. de vulgi opinione de Christo, Matth.16.v.13.14.15.16.17. Marc. 8.27. Luc.9.18. De Christi potestate; Matth 21. 23. Marc.11.v.28.29.30.33. Luc.20.v.1.3.4.7.8. De Elia venturo, Marc.9.v.11.12.13. de gentibus, Act.11.v.3.4.17. de ieiunio, Matt.9.v.14.15. Marc, 2.v.18.19. Luc.5.v.33.34. de Ioannis baptismate, Matt.21.v. 25.27. Mar.11.v.30 32. Luc.20.4. de Ioannis persona, Ioan, 1.v.19.20.21.22. de libertate, 8.v.33.34.36. de præcipuo Legis mandato, Matth.22.v.36.37.38. Marc.12.v.28.29.30. de numero saluandorum, Luc.13.v.23.24. &c. de operibus Dei, Ioan.6.v.28.29. de potestate Apostolis collata, Act.4.v.7.8.
units.tr: VARIOUS QUESTIONS and their solutions: a question about the true worship of God, John 4:20, 21, 22, 23; about the cause of a certain man's blindness, 9:2, 3; about the manner in which Mary was to conceive Christ, Luke 1:34, 35; whether Jesus is the Christ, 22:67, 69, 70; John 10:24, 25, 26, 27; whether he is the Son of God, Matt. 22:42, 43, 44, 45; Mark 12:35; Luke 20:42, 43, 44; about Christ's departure, John 13:36; about eating Christ's flesh, John 6:52, 61, 62, 63; about the common opinion concerning Christ, Matt. 16:13, 14, 15, 16, 17; Mark 8:27; Luke 9:18; about Christ's power, Matt. 21:23; Mark 11:28, 29, 30, 33; Luke 20:1, 3, 4, 7, 8; about Elijah's coming, Mark 9:11, 12, 13; about the Gentiles, Acts 11:3, 4, 17; about fasting, Matt. 9:14, 15; Mark 2:18, 19; Luke 5:33, 34; about the baptism of John, Matt. 21:25, 27; Mark 11:30, 32; Luke 20:4; about the person of John, John 1:19, 20, 21, 22; about liberty, John 8:33, 34, 36; about the chief commandment of the Law, Matt. 22:36, 37, 38; Mark 12:28, 29, 30; about the number of those to be saved, Luke 13:23, 24, etc.; about the works of God, John 6:28, 29; about the power conferred on the apostles, Acts 4:7, 8.

units.la: 10.de præmio discipulorum Christi, Matth.19.27.28. 2 Marc.10.v.28.29.30.de Iudæorum purificatione,Ioan.3. 25.26.27.de hominis regeneratione,Ioan.3.v.4.5.6.de restituendo Israelis regno, Act.1.v.6.7 de primatu Apostolorum,Matth.18.1.&c.de futuro resurrectionis statu,22. 28.29.30.Mar.12.23.Luc.20.33. quomodo resurgant mortui,1 Cor.15.v.35.36.num sabbatis benefacere liceat,Luc.6.v 9.10.&14.v.3 4.5.de templi destructione, Matth.24. 2.3.4.Mar.13.v.4.5.de tributo petendo & soluendo, Matth. 22.v.17.18.20.21. Luc.20.22. de instituenda vitæ ratione Luc.3.v.10.11.de vita æterna possidenda,Matth.19.v.16.17. Mar.10.v.17.18.19.20.21. Luc.20.v.25.26.27.28. de vxore relinquenda,Matth.19.3.Marc.10.v.2.3.4.5.10.11.12.
units.tr: 10. About the reward of Christ's disciples, Matt. 19:27, 28; 2 Mark 10:28, 29, 30. About the purification of the Jews, John 3:25, 26, 27. About the regeneration of man, John 3:4, 5, 6. About restoring the kingdom to Israel, Acts 1:6, 7. About the primacy of the apostles, Matt. 18:1, etc. About the future state of the resurrection, Matt. 22:28, 29, 30; Mark 12:23; Luke 20:33. How the dead rise, 1 Cor. 15:35, 36. Whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath, Luke 6:9, 10; 14:3, 4, 5. About the destruction of the temple, Matt. 24:2, 3, 4; Mark 13:4, 5. About paying and rendering tribute, Matt. 22:17, 18, 20, 21; Luke 20:22. About ordering the course of life, Luke 3:10, 11. About obtaining eternal life, Matt. 19:16, 17; Mark 10:17, 18, 19, 20, 21; Luke 20:25, 26, 27, 28. About leaving a wife, Matt. 19:3; Mark 10:2, 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12.

units.la: QVÆSTIONES contentiosæ, vanæ, ac inutiles vitandæ, Rom.14.1.1 Cor.15.33.Phil.2.14.1 Tim.1.4.&6.4.2 Tim.2.v.14.23.Tit.3.9.Vide & Gen.3 v.1.6.Prou.25.27.Eccle.7.10.Eccle.3.2.Matt.24.3.4.Ioan.6.52.&21.21.Act.1.6.7.
units.tr: CONTENTIOUS, vain and useless QUESTIONS are to be avoided: Rom. 14:1; 1 Cor. 15:33; Phil. 2:14; 1 Tim. 1:4; 6:4; 2 Tim. 2:14, 23; Titus 3:9. See also Gen. 3:1, 6; Prov. 25:27; Eccles. 7:10; 3:2; Matt. 24:3, 4; John 6:52; 21:21; Acts 1:6, 7.

units.la: QVÆSTIONARII quæstum ex Dei doctrina facientes,1 Tim.6.5.
units.tr: QUESTIONERS who make gain from the doctrine of God: 1 Tim. 6:5.

units.la: QVÆSTVS magnus est pietas,1 Tim.6.6.7.8.
units.tr: Godliness is great gain: 1 Tim. 6:6, 7, 8.

units.la: QVERIMONIA,συκοφαντία,Iacob.5.9.est probrosa & vagè à nobis sparsa apud quoslibet de fratre nobis iniurioso fama querela.
units.tr: COMPLAINT, [συκοφαντία], James 5:9, is a shameful and vaguely spread report or accusation, made by us against a brother who has wronged us, among anyone at all.

units.la: QVERIMONIA,Num.17.5.Querimoniæ exempla: Elias,1 Reg.19.14. Rom.11.3. Ieremias ob destructam Ierusalem Thren.1.1.querimoniæ iustæ exempla: Moses, Exod.5.22.Iosuah,Ios.7.7.Gedeon,Iudic.6.13.14.populus, Nehem.5. Christus,Matt.27.46.Marc.15.34. sine QVERELA vivimus,Philip.2.14.15.1 Thess.3 13.Col.3.13.1 Pet.4.9.
units.tr: COMPLAINT, Num. 17:5. Examples of complaint: Elijah, 1 Kings 19:14; Rom. 11:3; Jeremiah, over the destroyed Jerusalem, Lam. 1:1. Examples of just complaint: Moses, Exod. 5:22; Joshua, Josh. 7:7; Gideon, Judg. 6:13, 14; the people, Neh. 5; Christ, Matt. 27:46; Mark 15:34. We live without COMPLAINT: Phil. 2:14, 15; 1 Thess. 3:13; Col. 3:13; 1 Pet. 4:9.

units.la: QVIES continget populo Dei,Heb.4.9. Quietem & pacem certam consequentur iusti,Sap.3.3.&4.1.Esa.57.2.Luc.22.Apoc.14 13. Vide PIORVM securitas. Quietem inuenire animæ suæ,Ier.6.16.Matt.11.29.
units.tr: REST remains for the people of God, Heb. 4:9. The righteous will obtain rest and certain peace, Wisd. 3:3; 4:1; Isa. 57:2; Luke 22; Rev. 14:13. See SECURITY of the pious. To find rest for one's soul, Jer. 6:16; Matt. 11:29.

units.la: QVIESCENDVM à peccatis,Rom.6.6.&c.Gal.2.18.
units.tr: We must REST from sins, Rom. 6:6, etc.; Gal. 2:18.

units.la: QVIETI simus,1 Thess.4.11.
units.tr: Let us be QUIET, 1 Thess. 4:11.

units.la: QVINQVAGENARII ad Eliam ab Achazia missi, igne consumti ,2 Reg.1.10. Tertius verò præseruatus, vide 13.&c.
units.tr: The fifty men sent by Ahaziah to Elijah were consumed by fire, 2 Kings 1:10. The third, however, was spared; see 13, etc.

units.la: QVOVSQVE,Vide DONEC.QVIVIS,V.Nota.
units.tr: UNTIL: see UNTIL (DONEC). WHOEVER: see NOTE.

units.la: R.
units.tr: R.

units.la: ABBA, vel Rabbath, regia Ammonitarum ciuitas, ab Israelitis obsidetur, 2.Sam.11. 1. 1 Paral.20.1.in eius obsidione Vrias occiditur,2Sam.11. 17.expilatur,12.29.1 paral.20.2.(Rabb.i.magna,copiosa.)
units.tr: Abba, or Rabbath, the royal city of the Ammonites, is besieged by the Israelites (2 Sam. 11:1; 1 Chron. 20:1). Uriah is killed during the siege (2 Sam. 11:17), and the city is plundered (2 Sam. 12:29; 1 Chron. 20:2). (Rabbah: great, abundant.)

units.la: RABBI.1.Magister, Ioann. 1.38. Rabbi cognomen Doctoribus diuini verbi ordinariis, Christo ῥαββί attribuitur, Ioan.1.38. Rabbi seu magister noster, Pharisaei vocari gaudent,Matth.23.v. 6.7.id fugiant fideles,hortatur eos Christus,v.8.Rabboni. i.magister,Ioh.20.16.
units.tr: RABBI: Teacher (John 1:38). The title "rabbi" is given to the ordinary teachers of the divine word, and to Christ as [ῥαββί] (John 1:38). The Pharisees like to be called "rabbi" or "our teacher" (Matt. 23:6-7), and Christ urges the faithful to flee from this (v. 8). Rabboni, that is, Master (John 20:16).

units.la: ABSACES, archipincerna Sennacherib, ad Ezechiam mittitur,2 Regum 18.17.Esa.36.2.eius blasphemia, 2 Reg.18. 19.20 &c.(Rabsace.i.princeps deosculatus.)
units.tr: RABSHAKEH, chief cupbearer of Sennacherib, is sent to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17; Isa. 36:2). His blasphemy (2 Kings 18:19-20, etc.). (Rabsaris: chief who kisses.)

units.la: ACA, Matt.5.22.qua voce significatur homo imprudens, & quasi cerebro vacuus, vt Hebraicae linguae periti ex vocis etymo affirmant. Alij malunt pro incondita homines indignantis vocula accipere, & tres eo loci eorum gradus constituunt,qui contra hominum opinionem pro homicidis apud Deum censentur,de quibus vide HOMICIDA. Culpaeius, qui vocula illa visus in fratrem fuerit, Matth. 5.22.& poena,ibid.(V.Supplicium.)
units.tr: ACA (Matt. 5:22): a word by which a man is signified who is imprudent and, as it were, empty-headed, as those skilled in Hebrew affirm from the etymology of the word. Others prefer to take it as the inarticulate cry of an indignant man. They establish three grades of such men, who, contrary to human opinion, are counted as murderers before God; on these see MURDERER. The guilt of one who has uttered that little word against a brother (Matt. 5:22), and the punishment (ibid.). (See PUNISHMENT.)

units.la: RACHEL,filia Laban,Genes.29.6.patris oues pascit, verf.9. formosa est,v.17.Traditur Iacobo in vxorem, v.29.patris idola furatur,31.19.Rachel, pro toto illo tractu & vicinia Bethlehemitica, Matth.2 18.nam in via ducente in oppidum Bethlehem (cuius & Ephrata nomen habet, à soli fertilitate,& frugum copia)Rachel Iacobi coniux in partu mortua sepultaque fuit,Gen.35.19.&48.7.(i.quies mitis ac placida.)
units.tr: RACHEL, daughter of Laban (Gen. 29:6). She pastures her father's sheep (v. 9). She is beautiful (v. 17). She is given to Jacob as his wife (v. 29). She steals her father's idols (31:19). Rachel stands for that whole district and neighbourhood of Bethlehem (Matt. 2:18). For on the road leading to the town of Bethlehem (which also bears the name Ephrath, from the fertility of the soil and abundance of crops), Rachel, Jacob's wife, died in childbirth and was buried (Gen. 35:19; 48:7). (That is, gentle and peaceful rest.)

units.la: RADIX arboris,herbae.Radix, ima pars montis, similitudine à plantis ducta, quarum radices infimae sunt. Radix causa & origo, vel etiam effectum & consequens rei alicuius,potentia item vis,dignitas, & praestantia humana, Deut.29.18.Iob.5.3.Psal.52.7.&80.10.Prou.12.v.3.12 1 Tim. 6.10.Heb.12.15.Radix,fides,Matth.13.21. Radix, stirps aut genus alicuius post eum, Esai.11.v.1.10.Ezech.16.3.Rom. 11.16.&15.12.Apoc.5.5.&22.16.Radix, ratio & fundamentum rei seu negotij alicuius,Iob.19.28.&29.19.]
units.tr: ROOT of a tree or herb. Radix: the lowest part of a mountain, a term drawn by likeness from plants, whose roots lie lowest. Root: the cause and origin, or also the effect and consequence of something; likewise the power, strength, dignity and excellence of a man (Deut. 29:18; Job 5:3; Ps. 52:7; 80:10; Prov. 12:3, 12; 1 Tim. 6:10; Heb. 12:15). Root: faith (Matt. 13:21). Root: the stock or family of someone, his descendants (Isa. 11:1, 10; Ezek. 16:3; Rom. 11:16; 15:12; Rev. 5:5; 22:16). Root: the reason and foundation of a matter or business (Job 19:28; 29:19).

units.la: RADIX Dauid, & Iesse, (Vide CHRISTVS.) Roman. 12. Apoc. 22. 16. radix Iudæorum, sancti Patres, Roma. 11. 16.
units.tr: ROOT of David and of Jesse (see CHRIST). Rom. 12; Rev. 22:16: "the root of David". The root of the Jews: the holy Fathers (Rom. 11:16).

units.la: RAGVEL Sacerdos Madian, pater Iethro soceri Mosis: Ex. 2. 18. (Reuël, pastor Dei.)
units.tr: REUEL, priest of Midian, father of Jethro, Moses' father-in-law (Ex. 2:18). (Reuel: shepherd of God.)

units.la: RAHAB, Ierichuntina meretrix, exploratores hospitio ex cepit, Iof. 2. 1. eos occultat, v. 4. fides illius, vers. 8. 9. 10. 11. Hebr. 11. 31. operibus iustificata est, Iac. 2. 25. hoc est, fides non mortuam, sed per charitatem operantem (vt Paulus loquitur Gal. 5. 6.) habere declarata est. Cum suis in Iericho ntis deuastatione seruatur, Iof. 6. 25. (i. dilitatio.)
units.tr: RAHAB, the harlot of Jericho, received the spies into her house as guests (Josh. 2:1). She hid them (v. 4). Her faith (vv. 8-11; Heb. 11:31). She was justified by works (Jas. 2:25), that is, it was shown that she had a faith that was not dead but working through love (as Paul puts it, Gal. 5:6). She was saved with her family when Jericho was destroyed (Josh. 6:25). (That is, enlargement.)

units.la: RAHAB vxor Salmon, Mat. 1. 5 genuit Booz maritum Rut proauum regis Dauidis: ibid.
units.tr: RAHAB, wife of Salmon, who bore Boaz, husband of Ruth, great-grandfather of King David (Matt. 1:5). Ibid.

units.la: RAMA in Tribu Beniamin ciuitas, Iof. 18. 25. à Baasa instau ratur, 1 Reg. 15. 17. destruitur, v. 22. (i. altitudo, excelsa.)
units.tr: RAMAH, a city in the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 18:25). It was built up by Baasha (1 Kings 15:17) and destroyed (v. 22). (That is, height, lofty.)

units.la: RAMESSES, Ægypti vrbs ab Hebræis ædificatur, Exo. 1. 11. Hinc ab Ægypto discessum auspicantur Israelitis, Num. 33. v. 3 5. (i. tonitruum gaudij.)
units.tr: RAMESES, a city of Egypt built by the Hebrews (Ex. 1:11). From there the Israelites began their departure from Egypt (Num. 33:3, 5). (That is, thunder of joy.)

units.la: RAMI naturalis oleæ Iudæi, Rom. 11. 17.
units.tr: The branches of the natural olive, the Jews (Rom. 11:17).

units.la: RAMOTH Galaad obsidetur, 1 Reg. 22 3. à rege Achabo (i. excelsum signum.)
units.tr: RAMOTH GILEAD is besieged by King Ahab (1 Kings 22:3). (That is, high sign.)

units.la: RANAE super terram Ægypti, Exo. 8. 2. Ps. 78. 45. Apoc. 16. 1.
units.tr: FROGS over the land of Egypt (Ex. 8:2; Ps. 78:45; Rev. 16:1).

units.la: RAPINA damnatur, Prou. 21 7. & 22. 16. Esa. 33. 1 Ezech. 22. 25. Rapinæ & intemperantiæ nomine intelliguntur, Mal. 23. 25. dapes ex alienis interuersis facultatibus ad luxum comparatæ: Rapinæ & spoliationis exempla: Simeon & Leui Gen. 34. 28. Israelitæ, Exo. 12. v. 35. 36. Deut. 2. v. 32. 35. Amalechitæ, 1 Sam. 30. 16. &c. Dauid, v. 18. 20. populus Israel 2 Sam. 23. 10. Achab. 1 Reg. 21. v. 15. 16. Nabuchodonosor 2 Reg. 24. 13. Philisthæi, 1 Par. 10. 8. exercitus Assiræ regis Par. 14. 13. &c. Iosaphat & populus, 20. 25. Filij Israel, 28. Achaz, v. 21. V. Zacchæus, Luc. 19. 8. Pharisæi, 11. v. 39.
units.tr: ROBBERY is condemned (Prov. 21:7; 22:16; Isa. 33:1; Ezek. 22:25). Under the name of robbery and intemperance are understood (Matt. 23:25) the feasts prepared for luxury from the goods of others, seized by violence. Examples of robbery and plunder: Simeon and Levi (Gen. 34:28); the Israelites (Ex. 12:35-36; Deut. 2:32, 35); the Amalekites (1 Sam. 30:16, etc.); David (vv. 18, 20); the people of Israel (2 Sam. 23:10); Ahab (1 Kings 21:15-16); Nebuchadnezzar (2 Kings 24:13); the Philistines (1 Chron. 10:8); the army of the king of Assyria (2 Chron. 14:13, etc.); Jehoshaphat and the people (20:25); the sons of Israel (28); Ahaz (v. 21). See ZACCHAEUS (Luke 19:8); the Pharisees (11:39).

units.la: RAPACES fugiendi, 1 Cor. 5. 11. eorum merces, Prou. 28. 10. 21. 7. Esa. 33. 1. 1 Cor. 5. 11. & 6. 10. V. Deut. 28. 31. 58. Nahum 3. 1. Iob. 20. 19. Gen. 6. 11.
units.tr: ROBBERS are to be shunned (1 Cor. 5:11). Their wares (Prov. 28:10; 21:7; Isa. 33:1; 1 Cor. 5:11; 6:10). See Deut. 28:31, 58; Nah. 3:1; Job 20:19; Gen. 6:11.

units.la: RAPTVS est, cùm puellæ, nuptæ, viduæ, libertinæ, necnon pueri rapiuntur à custodia vel parentis, vel tutoris, vel curatoris, vel patroni, vel domini: vt illigitimi coitus habeantur, siue sequatur matrimonium, siue nosgressus habeantur, siue sequatur matrimonium, siue no Qui furatus fuerit hominem, morte multetur: Exo. 21. 16. Raptus infaustus Gen. 6. 2. 7. & 34. 25. V. Plagium.
units.tr: RAPE occurs when girls, married women, widows, freedwomen, and also boys, are seized from the custody of a parent, guardian, curator, patron or master, so that illicit intercourse takes place, whether or not marriage follows. "Whoever has stolen a man shall be put to death" (Ex. 21:16). Ill-omened rape (Gen. 6:2, 7; 34:25). See KIDNAPPING.

units.la: RASIN, rex Syriæ, à rege Assyriorum interficitur, 2 Reg. 16.9.
units.tr: RASIN, king of Syria, is killed by the king of the Assyrians (2 Kings 16:9).

units.la: RATIO humana, in rebus spiritualib. cœca, Vide LIBERUM arbitrium. Rationi propriæ non fidendum, Deut.12.8.Prov.3.5.&14.12. Rationem reddat Deo quisque pro se oportet, Matth.12.36.&18.23.&25.14. &c. Rom.14.12. 2 Cor.5.10. rationem spei nostræ cuilibet reddere parati esse debemus. 1 Pet.3.15. A Pastoribus reddenda Deo ratio pro anima Heb.13.17. Eze.13.18.
units.tr: HUMAN REASON, in spiritual matters, is blind. See FREE WILL. One must not trust one's own reason (Deut. 12:8; Prov. 3:5; 14:12). Each person must render account to God for himself (Matt. 12:36; 18:23; 25:14, etc.; Rom. 14:12; 2 Cor. 5:10). We ought to be ready to give an account of our hope to anyone (1 Pet. 3:15). Ministers must render account to God for souls (Heb. 13:17; Ezek. 13:18).

units.la: RATIONALE seu pectorile iudicij quale, Exod.28.15.&39.8.
units.tr: The RATIONAL, or breastpiece of judgment (Ex. 28:15; 39:8).

units.la: RAZON, Eliada filius, Salomonis & Israelis aduersarius, 1 Reg.11.23. princeps latronum constituitur, ver.24. (voluntas.)
units.tr: REZON, son of Eliada, an adversary of Solomon and Israel (1 Kings 11:23), is made chief of robbers (v. 24). (Will.)

units.la: REBECCA, filia Bathuelis, Gen.22.23. formosa est, 24.16.&26.7. vxor fit Isaaci, 24.50. sterilis elt, ideo in eius gratiam Deum orat Isaac, 25.21. concipit gemellos, v.22.23. parit, v.24. Roman.9.10. Iacobum filium minorem natu, loco Esau primogeniti ad eripiendam illi benedictionem paternam, ad patrem intromittit, Genes.27.v.8.&c. Iacobo, ut ad Labanem fratrem concedat, author est, v.43. (Ribekah.1. multum expectata, vel patiens.)
units.tr: REBEKAH, daughter of Bethuel (Gen. 22:23), is beautiful (24:16; 26:7). She becomes the wife of Isaac (24:50). She was barren, so Isaac prays to God on her behalf (25:21). She conceives twins (vv. 22-23) and bears them (v. 24; Rom. 9:10). She sends the younger son Jacob into his father's presence, in place of the firstborn Esau, to snatch the paternal blessing from him (Gen. 27:8, etc.). She advises Jacob to go to her brother Laban (v. 43). (Rebekah: much expected, or patient.)

units.la: REBELLIO, est apertus & manifestus subditorum aduersus legitimum Magistratus aut Superioris iussum ausus, & inceptio, siue factis, siue verbis sese prodens.
units.tr: REBELLION is the open and manifest daring of subjects against the lawful magistrate or a superior's command, and its beginning, showing itself either in deeds or in words.

units.la: REBELLIO damnatur, Deut.21.17.1 Sam.15.23. Rebellionis merces, Esa.45.24. Rebellionis exempla: Israelitæ, Exo.16,20. Num.14.4.&26.9. Deut.9.v.23.24. Core, Dathan & Abiron Num.16.v.12.14. Ieroboam, 1 Reg.11.26. Zabri, 16.v.9.16. Serui Benadad.20.32. Oiec, 2 Reg.17.4. Ioacim, 24.v.8.9.10. Iudei, 1 Esdr.4.12. Minatur etiam Deus se fame, peste & gladio perditurum Sedeciam & populum Iudaicum, aliaque omnes gentes quæ detrectent seruire regi Babel, Ier.27.8. Vide Ezec.17.15. Alter Hebræorum lit gantium, Actor.7.27. Israelitæ, Rom.10.20. Vide
units.tr: REBELLION is condemned (Deut. 21:17; 1 Sam. 15:23). The reward of rebellion (Isa. 45:24). Examples of rebellion: the Israelites (Ex. 16:20; Num. 14:4; 26:9; Deut. 9:23-24); Korah, Dathan and Abiram (Num. 16:12-14); Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:26); Zimri (16:9, 16); the servants of Ben-hadad (20:32); Hoshea (2 Kings 17:4); Jehoiakim (24:8-10); the Jews (1 Esdras 4:12). God also threatens to destroy Zedekiah and the Jewish people, and all other nations that refuse to serve the king of Babylon, by sword, famine and pestilence (Jer. 27:8). See Ezek. 17:15. Another of the Hebrews quarrelling (Acts 7:27). The Israelites (Rom. 10:20). See SEDITION.

units.la: SEDITIO.
units.tr: SEDITION.

units.la: REBELLES in Mosen comburuntur, Numer.16.35. rebelles Israelitæ, Deut.9.24.&31.27. Core, &c. Numen 16.2.
units.tr: REBELS against Moses are burned (Num. 16:35). Rebellious Israelites (Deut. 9:24; 31:27). Korah, etc. (Num. 16:2).

units.la: RECALCITRAVIT Israel, Deut.32.15.
units.tr: Israel kicked out (Deut. 32:15).

units.la: RECEDERE à tergo Dei, 1 Sam. 12. 20. Non recedendum à Deo, Deut. 11. 16. v. 8, 9. Sed à malo : Prouerb. 3.7.
units.tr: To depart from behind God (1 Sam. 12:20). One must not depart from God (Deut. 11:16; vv. 8-9), but from evil (Prov. 3:7).

units.la: RECHAB & Baana, fratres, Isboseth occiderunt, 2 Sam. 4. ver. 6. 7. eius caput Dauidi afferunt, ver. 8. Dauidis in eos sententia v. 9. 10. 11. 12. qua impia congratulatio plectitur.
units.tr: Rechab and Baanah, brothers, killed Ish-bosheth (2 Sam. 4:6-7). They brought his head to David (v. 8). David's sentence against them (vv. 9-12), by which impious rejoicing is punished.

units.la: RECHAB, pater Ionadab, amici Iehu regis Israel, 2 Reg. 10. 15. (i. quadriga, vel equitans.)
units.tr: REKAB, father of Jehonadab, friend of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 10:15). (That is, chariot, or riding.)

units.la: RECHABITAE paternæ constitutionis obseruantissimi, Ier. 35.6.
units.tr: The RECHABITES, most observant of their father's ordinance (Jer. 35:6).

units.la: RECIPERE Christum, Ioan. 1.12. salutare est, ibid.
units.tr: To receive Christ (John 1:12). It is salutary (ibid.).

units.la: RECONCILIARE est. 1. Intercedere pro eo, qui offendit, apud offensum. 2. satisfacere pro iniuria illata. 3. promittere & efficere, vt pars offendens non amplius offendat. Est igitur Christus pacificator inter Deum & homines, placans iram Dei, & restituens homines in gratiam Dei, intercedendo & satisfaciendo pro eorum peccatis & faciens vt Deus amet homines & homines Deum ament, sitque inter Deum & homines constans & æterna pax atque concordia.
units.tr: To RECONCILE is: 1. to intercede for the one who has offended, with the offended party; 2. to make satisfaction for the injury inflicted; 3. to promise and bring about that the offending party no longer offends. Christ, therefore, is the peacemaker between God and men, appeasing the wrath of God and restoring men into God's favour, by interceding for and making satisfaction for their sins, and by causing God to love men and men to love God, so that between God and men there is a constant and eternal peace and concord.

units.la: RECONCILIATIO cum Deo per Christum, Rom. 5. v. 10. 11. Cor. 5. v. 18. 19. Col. 1. v. 20. 22. reconciliatio cum fratre præcipitur, Matt. 5. 24. Iac. 5. 16. Reconciliationis seu expiationis dies, Leuit. 23. 27. Reconciliationis cum proximo offenso exempla: Iudas, Genes. 38. 2. Fratres Ioseph 50, v. 17. 18. 19. 20. Pharao, Exo. 10. 6. 16. 17. Israelitæ, 1 Sam. 12. v. 18. 19. Semei 2 Sam. 19. 19. V. Iob. 42. 7. 8. 9. Prouer. 16. 7.
units.tr: RECONCILIATION with God through Christ (Rom. 5:10-11; 2 Cor. 5:18-19; Col. 1:20-22). Reconciliation with a brother is commanded (Matt. 5:24; Jas. 5:16). The day of reconciliation or atonement (Lev. 23:27). Examples of reconciliation with an offended neighbour: Judah (Gen. 38:2). The brothers of Joseph (50:17-20). Pharaoh (Ex. 10:6, 16-17). The Israelites (1 Sam. 12:18-19). Shimei (2 Sam. 19:19). See Job 42:7-9; Prov. 16:7.

units.la: RECORDEMVR beneficiorum Dei, exhortatio, Deuteron. 8. 2. & vers. 10. 11. 1 Corinth. 11. 26. Et præteritorum : I 32.7.
units.tr: WE ARE TO REMEMBER GOD'S BENEFITS: an exhortation, Deut. 8:2, and vv. 10, 11; 1 Cor. 11:26. And past things: I 32.7.

units.la: RECORDATVR Deus nostri, cùm nos liberat aut aliquid donat, Genes. 30.22 1 Sam. 1.11. Vide Genes. 9.15. 19.29.
units.tr: GOD REMEMBERS US when he delivers us or grants us something: Gen. 30:22; 1 Sam. 1:11. See Gen. 9:15; 19:29.

units.la: RECTVS est Deus, Deut. 32. 4. rectum coram Deo faciendum, Exo. 15. 26. quod rectum videtur nobis, non faciendum, Deut. 12.8.
units.tr: GOD IS RIGHT, Deut. 32:4. What is right is to be done before God, Exod. 15:26. What seems right to us is not to be done, Deut. 12:8.

units.la: REDARGVO. Ne commercium habete cum operibus infructuosis tenebrarum: sed potius redarguite: Eph. 5. 11. Tit. 1. 11. Iac. 2. 9. (Vide Correptio.) 2 Timoth. 4. 2. Leuit. 19.17.
units.tr: I REBUKE. "Have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them," Eph. 5:11; Titus 1:11; James 2:9. (See Correction.) 2 Tim. 4:2; Lev. 19:17.

units.la: REDEMTIO, pro redemtionis signo aut indicio, Exod. 8.23. Redeu
units.tr: REDEMPTION, for a sign or token of redemption, Exod. 8:23. Redeu

units.la: Redemtio per Christum facta, Matth.20, 28. Marc.10 45. Act.28.28.Rom.3.23.24.& 4.25.& 5.v.6.9.& 8.1.1 Cor.1.30. Eph.1 7.Col.1.14.1 Thess.1.10.1 Tim.2.6.Heb.9 12.1 Pet.1 v.18 19. 2 Pet. 2.1. Apoc.5.9. redemtionis nostræ finis, Luc. 1.v.74.75.Eph,1.v.4.5.6.Tit.2.14.Hebr.9.14. redemtio corporis nostri, vocatur liberatio à corpore(id est dissolutio) Rom.8.22.qua fit, vt spiritus à corpore liberatus, à Christo recipiatur, vt Rom.7.24. Phil.1.23. vel illa corporis ipsius instauratio, quæ futura est nostræ adoptionis consummatio, Luc.21.28.
units.tr: Redemption made through Christ: Matt. 20:28; Mark 10:45; Acts 28:28; Rom. 3:23, 24; 4:25; 5:6, 9; 8:1; 1 Cor. 1:30; Eph. 1:7; Col. 1:14; 1 Thess. 1:10; 1 Tim. 2:6; Heb. 9:12; 1 Pet. 1:18, 19; 2 Pet. 2:1; Rev. 5:9. The end of our redemption: Luke 1:74, 75; Eph. 1:4–6; Titus 2:14; Heb. 9:14. The redemption of our body is called deliverance from the body (that is, dissolution), Rom. 8:22. By this, the spirit, freed from the body, is received by Christ, as in Rom. 7:24 and Phil. 1:23. Or it is that restoration of the body itself, which will be the completion of our adoption, Luke 21:28.

units.la: REDEMTOR noster Christus (1 Corin.1.30.1 Tim.2.6.) quia immediate opus redemtionis perfecit. Nam solus filius factus est λυτρον pro peccatis nostris, & pro nobis pretium soluit in cruce. Sed pater dicitur etiam redemtor noster, quia filium suum dedit nobis: item Spiritus sanctus, quia nos Christo adunit, & eius beneficiorum participes facit. V. Salvator.
units.tr: OUR REDEEMER is Christ (1 Cor. 1:30; 1 Tim. 2:6), because he alone accomplished the work of redemption immediately. For the Son alone was made a ransom [λύτρον] for our sins, and paid the price for us on the cross. But the Father is also called our Redeemer, because he gave his Son to us. Likewise the Holy Spirit, because he unites us to Christ and makes us partakers of his benefits. See Saviour.

units.la: REDIMERE novit Deus suos multis modis ex angustia, Genes.19.1.&c. Exod.14.1.&c.18.8.1 Sam.23.v.14 26. 2. Reg.7, 1.&c. 2 Paralipom. 18, 31. & 20. 24.1 Eidr. 6.22. Esth. 7.5. Psalm.91.9.&c. Esai.41.10 & 43.1 Dan.3.29. & 6. versi. 21. &c.2 Pet. 2.9.
units.tr: GOD KNOWS HOW to redeem his people from distress in many ways: Gen. 19:1 etc.; Exod. 14:1 etc.; 18:8; 1 Sam. 23:14, 26; 2 Kings 7:1 etc.; 2 Chron. 18:31; 20:24; 1 Esd. 6:22; Esth. 7:5; Ps. 91:9 etc.; Isa. 41:10; 43:1; Dan. 3:29; 6:21 etc.; 2 Pet. 2:9.

units.la: REDVNDANTIA gratiæ, pro redundante gratia, Hebraismus Rom.5.17.
units.tr: ABUNDANCE OF GRACE, for abounding grace, a Hebraism: Rom. 5:17.

units.la: REFVGII civitates, Exod.21.13. Num.35.11. Deut.4 41.& 19.v. 2.7. Ios.20.1.&c.1 Reg.1.50. & 2.28.
units.tr: CITIES OF REFUGE: Exod. 21:13; Num. 35:11; Deut. 4:41; 19:2, 7; Josh. 20:1 etc.; 1 Kings 1:50; 2:28.

units.la: REGENERATIO, est beneficium Dei, per quod corrupta nostra natura ad imaginem Dei per Spiritum sanctum renovatur: duabus præcipuis partibus constat: Veteris hominis, i. prauitatis nobis ingenitæ depositione, & noui hominis, i. puriratis nobis per gratiam collatæ instauratione: quarum vtraque in nobis nunc incohata suis gradibus absoluitur, illo quidem sensim moriente, isto vero sensim ad perfectionem alterius vitæ perueniente.
units.tr: REGENERATION is God's benefit, by which our corrupt nature is renewed through the Holy Spirit to the image of God. It consists of two main parts: the putting off of the old man, that is, the laying aside of the depravity born in us, and the putting on of the new man, that is, the restoration of the purity bestowed on us by grace. Both of these, begun in us now, are carried forward by their stages: the one gradually dying, the other gradually reaching perfection in the other life.

units.la: REGENERATIO, Dei opus est, Esa.19.25. & 43.1.& 44.v.2.3. 4.21.Ioh.1.13.Eph.1.19.&2.10.1 Pet.1.3 interdum tamen ad ministerij commendationem hominibus tribuitur, 1 Cor. 4.15.Philem.v.10. Paulatim fit, Ioan.13.10.Ephes.4.15. regeneratio necessaria est, Gal.6.15.Eph.4 22.23. Iac.1.18. 1 Pet.
units.tr: REGENERATION is the work of God: Isa. 19:25; 43:1; 44:2, 3, 4; 21; John 1:13; Eph. 1:19; 2:10; 1 Pet. 1:3. Yet at times it is attributed to men for the commendation of the ministry: 1 Cor. 4:15; Philem. 10. It happens gradually: John 13:10; Eph. 4:15. Regeneration is necessary: Gal. 6:15; Eph. 4:22, 23; James 1:18; 1 Pet. 1:23; 2:24.

units.la: Oo 1.23.&2.24. Regeneratio est immutatio carnis in spiritū Ioan.3.5. carnalium affectionum in spiritualem affectum Rom.8.v.5.13.infidelitatis in fidem, Ioan.1.12. Gala.3.26. Ioan.5.1.renouatio mentis per Spiritum sanctum, Tit.3.5 Gal.4.6. atque adeo carnalis naturae in diuinam naturam 2 Pet.1.4.Col.2.11.12.qui mali fuimus sanctificamur,1 Cor. 6.11.Eph.5.8.
units.tr: Oo 1.23.&2.24. Regeneration is the change of the flesh into spirit (John 3.5), of carnal affections into spiritual affection (Rom. 8.5, 13), of unbelief into faith (John 1.12; Gal. 3.26; John 5.1), and the renewal of the mind through the Holy Spirit (Titus 3.5; Gal. 4.6). Indeed, it is the change of our carnal nature into the divine nature (2 Pet. 1.4; Col. 2.11, 12), so that we who were evil are sanctified (1 Cor. 6.11; Eph. 5.8).

units.la: Capitur regenerationis vocabulum, & pro illa iudicio extremi die,qua incipient electi nouam vitam viuere, id est, cum animo & corpore fruentur haereditate illa coelesti,Matth.19.28.in futuro seculo. Aut,si cum verbo, secutis, coniungatur regenerationis vocabulum, apud Matthaeum,Matt.19.28. regenerationis nomine ipsa Euangelij praedicatio erit intelligenda, quia tum veluti de integro conditus est mundus, cum illud Christus ipse in terras attulit. REGENERATIONIS nostrae finis,Col.3.10.1 Ioan 3.9. REGENERATI interius, etiam exterius in nouitate vitae ambulare debent,Rom.6.1.&c.& 7.6. & 12.1. Ephes.4.22. &c.Col.3.9.1 Cor.5.7.2 Cor.5.15.1 Pet.4.2.&c. REGES, V.REX. [REGINA coeli,Sol,seu Luna,Ier.7.18.& 44.17.&c. Regina,Ecclesia Dei,Psa.45.10.&c.Cantic.6.v.7.8. Regina mystica,Babylon Apocalyptica, Esa.47.7.Apocal. 18. 7. Regina Sabaea,1 Reg.10.(1.Matt.12.42.) Aegypti 11.19.Vasthi,Ester 1.9.Esther,Esther 5.v.2.3.5.cap. sequentibus. Reginae nutrices Ecclesiae,Esai.49 23. Candaces reginae Aethiopiae,Act.8.27.] REGIONES orbis a quibus diuisae, Gene. 10.3. regiones albae ad messem,Ioan.4 35.V.Deut.32.8. Matt.4.16. REGNABAT Deus super Israele n,antequam regem peteret, 1 Sam.12.12.regnabit Deus in perpetuum, Exod.15.18. regnare nolentes Christum,occiduntur coram ipso,Luc.19. 27.ne regnet peccatum in nobis,Rom.6.12. [REGNAT Deus, Exod.15.18.1 Sam.8.7.1 Para.16 31. Psa.9.36 & 47.9.& 93.1.& 96.10.& 97.1.& 99.1.& 146.10. Regnat Christus,Ecclesiae princeps,Deus-homo,Psa.45.5. &c.Esa.32.1.& 52.7.Ier.23.5 Mich.4.7. Luc.1.33. & 19. v.14. 27.1 Cor.15.25.Apoc.11.v.15 17. & 19.6. Regnât Christi membra, Rom.5.17. Apo.1.6. & 5.10. & 20. v.4.6.&22.5.
units.tr: The word regeneration is also taken for that state at the last day of judgment, when the elect will begin to live a new life, that is, when they enjoy that heavenly inheritance with both soul and body in the age to come (Matt. 19.28). Or, if the word regeneration is joined with the word "when" (as in Matthew 19.28), then by the name regeneration the preaching of the Gospel itself is to be understood, because then the world was, as it were, created afresh, when Christ himself brought this into the earth. The end of our regeneration (Col. 3.10; 1 John 3.9). Those who have been regenerated inwardly ought also to walk outwardly in newness of life (Rom. 6.1ff.; 7.6; 12.1; Eph. 4.22ff.; Col. 3.9; 1 Cor. 5.7; 2 Cor. 5.15; 1 Pet. 4.2ff.). KINGS; see KING. [QUEEN of heaven, the sun or moon (Jer. 7.18; 44.17, etc.). The queen, the Church of God (Ps. 45.10, etc.; Song 6.7, 8). The mystical queen, Babylon in the Apocalypse (Isa. 47.7; Rev. 18.7). The Queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10; Matt. 12.42). The queen of Egypt (Exod. 11.19?). Vashti (Esther 1.9). Esther (Esther 5.2, 3, 5 and the following chapters). Nursing queens of the Church (Isa. 49.23). Candace, queen of the Ethiopians (Acts 8.27).] REGIONS of the world, by which they are divided (Gen. 10.3); the regions are white for harvest (John 4.35); see Deut. 32.8; Matt. 4.16. GOD REIGNED over Israel before it asked for a king (1 Sam. 12.12). God will reign forever (Exod. 15.18). Those who are unwilling for Christ to reign are slain before him (Luke 19.27), so that sin may not reign in us (Rom. 6.12). [GOD REIGNS (Exod. 15.18; 1 Sam. 8.7; 1 Chron. 16.31; Ps. 9.36; 47.9; 93.1; 96.10; 97.1; 99.1; 146.10). CHRIST REIGNS, the Prince of the Church, God-man (Ps. 45.5, etc.; Isa. 32.1; 52.7; Jer. 23.5; Mic. 4.7; Luke 1.33; 19.14, 27; 1 Cor. 15.25; Rev. 11.15, 17; 19.6). The members of Christ reign (Rom. 5.17; Rev. 1.6; 5.10; 20.4, 6; 22.5).

units.la: Regnant homines, vt reges Ægypti, Cananæorum, Phi- listhæorum, Israelitarum, Iudæorum, &c. de quibus men- tio frequens apud Mosen, Iosuam, priores & posteriores Prophetas.
units.tr: Men reign, as the kings of Egypt, of the Canaanites, of the Philistines, of the Israelites, of the Jews, etc., of whom there is frequent mention in Moses, Joshua, and the earlier and later Prophets.

units.la: Regnat gratia, mors, peccatum, Rom.5.v.14. 17.21. & 6.12.
units.tr: Grace, death, and sin reign (Rom. 5.14, 17, 21; 6.12).

units.la: <bl>REGNVM</bl> significat, i. ditionem, regionem vel amplissimam, vel minorem locorum certis interuallis & limitibus di- stinctam atque conclusam, in qua super alios princeps re- gnat, vt Iudę, Israelis, &c. regnum. 2. Dominatio ipsa prin- cipis & regni ipsius in subditos bona vel mala adminis- stratio. 3. Subditi regni, siue populus in regno consistens & viuens. Multa in scripturis de triplici hac significatio- ne, humani regni respectu testimonia occurrunt, quæ de- scribere haud necesse est.
units.tr: KINGDOM signifies: (1) a dominion or region, either very large or smaller, distinguished and enclosed by fixed intervals and boundaries, in which a prince reigns over others, as the kingdom of Judah, of Israel, etc.; (2) the very rule of the prince and of the kingdom itself, its good or bad administration over its subjects; (3) the subjects of the kingdom, or the people living and dwelling in the kingdom. Many testimonies in Scripture concerning this threefold meaning, with respect to a human kingdom, occur, which it is not necessary to describe.

units.la: REGNVM potentiæ Deo tributum, dicitur gubernatio illa cœ- lestis, qua omnia potenter administrat, moderatur & disponit Deus, hostes quoscunque sibi quum libet subii- ciens, contumaces puniens, suos subditos conseruans, 1 Para.29.10. &c. Psal.22.29. & 103.19. & 145.v.11.12.13. Dan. 4 31. & 6.26.
units.tr: KINGDOM OF POWER is the name given to God, for that heavenly government by which God mightily administers, moderates, and disposes all things, subduing whatever enemies he pleases, punishing the stubborn, and preserving his subjects (1 Chron. 29.10, etc.; Ps. 22.29; 103.19; 145.11–13; Dan. 4.31; 6.26).

units.la: REGNVM Gratiæ, quod & regnum cœlorum, regnum Dei, & simpliciter regnum nominatur. Appellatione autem re- gni cœlorum, seu gratiæ, intelligitur prædicatio Euangelij, per quam Christus regnum suum spirituale exercet in e- lectis & eosdem ad regnum cœleste seu gloriæ præparat. Et cœlorum dicitur hoc regnum spirituale, quia plenitu- do illius continget demum electis, quando translati erunt in cœlum, Matth.3.v.2. & 4.17.23. & 9.35. & 13.11. &c. Rom. 14.17. 1 Cor.4.20. Col.4.11.
units.tr: KINGDOM OF GRACE, which is also called the kingdom of heaven, the kingdom of God, and simply the kingdom. By the name of the kingdom of heaven, or of grace, is understood the preaching of the Gospel, through which Christ exercises his spiritual kingdom in the elect and prepares them for the heavenly kingdom of glory. And this spiritual kingdom is called "of heaven" because its fullness will at last fall to the elect, when they are carried up into heaven (Matt. 3.2; 4.17, 23; 9.35; 13.11, etc.; Rom. 14.17; 1 Cor. 4.20; Col. 4.11).

units.la: <bl>REGNVM</bl> potentiæ, gloriæ, gratiæ Dei, Matth.6.10. Lucæ 11.2.
units.tr: KINGDOM of power, of glory, and of the grace of God (Matt. 6.10; Luke 11.2).

units.la: REGNVM Christi in Ecclesia, cuius Iudæ regnum fuit typus, 2 Sam.7.v.12.13.16. Psal.45.7. Dan.2.44. & 7.ver.24.27. Luc 1.33. Ioan.18.36. Col.1.13. Apoc.1.9.
units.tr: KINGDOM OF CHRIST in the Church, of which the kingdom of Judah was a type (2 Sam. 7.12, 13, 16; Ps. 45.7; Dan. 2.44; 7.24, 27; Luke 1.33; John 18.36; Col. 1.13; Rev. 1.9).

units.la: Regnum Christi, Dei, & Patris, dicitur gloria illa quæ in Christo post resurrectionem eluxit, Matt.16.28.&26.29. Luc.22.v.16.18. Regnum cælorum, Ecclesia Dei, post Christi plenam manifestationem sub Euangelio, Matt.5.19. & 11.11. & 13.24.& 18.4. Luc.7.28.
units.tr: The kingdom of Christ, of God, and of the Father, is the name given to that glory which shone forth in Christ after the resurrection (Matt. 16.28; 26.29; Luke 22.16, 18). The kingdom of heaven is the Church of God after the full manifestation of Christ under the Gospel (Matt. 5.19; 11.11; 13.24; 18.4; Luke 7.28).

units.la: REGNVM Antichristi, temporale, 2 Thess.2.7. regnum bestiae, & meretricis magnæ Apo.17.v.18. regnum Satanæ, Matth.12.26 Luc.11.18. Alias significationes videmus quæ ad superiores commodè referri possunt, nec tamen omittuntur, ne quid lector desideret, imò repetitione necessaria gaudeat & delectetur.]
units.tr: KINGDOM OF ANTICHRIST, temporal (2 Thess. 2.7); the kingdom of the beast and of the great harlot (Rev. 17.18); the kingdom of Satan (Matt. 12.26; Luke 11.18). We see other meanings which can conveniently be referred to the above, and yet they are not omitted, lest the reader should lack anything, but rather may rejoice and take delight in the necessary repetition.]

units.la: REGNVM cœlorum, pro publica Euangelij prædicatione, Matth.13.v.24.44.47.52. & 16.38. & 20.1. Secundò pro Ecclesiæ renouatione: Matth.3.2. & 4.17. & 5.19. & 19.7. & 11.11, & 18.23. & 22.2. Tertiò, pro rebus spiritualibus & cœlestibus. Matth. 13.11. Quartò, pro vita cœlesti ac æterna, Matth.16.19. & 18.v.1.3 & 19 v.14.23.&23 13.& 25.34 & 26.29. Luc.22.30. Quintò, pro officiis pietatis, Matth.19 12. Sexto, pro Ecclesia militante, & ministerio pastorum egente, Matth.5.ver.19.20. quæ bonis iuxtà ac malis mixta est, quod adumbrauit Christus similitudinibus, Matth.13.24.&c. agri scatentis lolio, reticuli dominici, in quo cum bonis piscibus sordes sunt mixtæ, versi.47. Dicitur autem Ecclesia in his terris militans, regnum cœlorum, primò, quia à Deo cœlesti modo regitur & administratur. Secundò, quia eius cives, contemtis rebus mundanis, ad cœlestia aspirant, illa meditantur & docent alios. Septimo, pro ipsa Dei cognitione thesauri abscondíti nomine significata, Matth.13.44. Octauo, pro externa professione Christianismi, Rom.14.17. Nono, pro cœlo ipso & beatorum statu in cœlo post hanc vitam, Matth.19.24. Luc.13.29.
units.tr: KINGDOM OF HEAVEN, for the public preaching of the Gospel (Matt. 13.24, 44, 47, 52; 16.18; 20.1). Secondly, for the renewal of the Church (Matt. 3.2; 4.17; 5.19; 9.7; 11.11; 18.23; 22.2). Thirdly, for spiritual and heavenly things (Matt. 13.11). Fourthly, for the heavenly and eternal life (Matt. 16.19; 18.1, 3; 19.14, 23; 23.13; 25.34; 26.29; Luke 22.30). Fifthly, for the duties of piety (Matt. 19.12). Sixthly, for the Church militant, which lacks the ministry of ministers, and which is mixed with good and bad alike (Matt. 5.19, 20), as Christ shadowed forth in parables: the field full of tares (Matt. 13.24, etc.), the Lord's net, in which filth is mixed with good fish (v. 47). The Church in this earthly warfare is called the kingdom of heaven, first, because it is ruled and administered by God in a heavenly manner; secondly, because its citizens, despising worldly things, aspire to heavenly things, meditate upon them, and teach them to others. Seventhly, for the very knowledge of God, signified under the name of the hidden treasure (Matt. 13.44). Eighthly, for the outward profession of Christianity (Rom. 14.17). Ninthly, for heaven itself and the state of the blessed in heaven after this life (Matt. 19.24; Luke 13.29).

units.la: <bl>REGNVM</bl> Christi æternum. 1 Paral.17.v.12.14. Psalm.45.8. & 89.v.4.35.36.37. Esa.9.5.6. Dan.2.44 Luc.1 33. Heb.1.8. Traditurus ergo est Christus regnum Deo & patri, 1 Cor.15.24. vltimo illo die, quo profligatis omnibus ad vnum hostibus, omnes quos à patre gubernandos accepit, illi veluti in manus tradet, æterna gloria coronandos. Non quòd abdicet se regno, sicut nec pater se abdicauit regno, cùm illud traderet Filio. Psal.n.2.versi.6.8.9. &c. nec quòd resignet imperium ipsum, quod accepit à patre in perpetuum, sed officia tantum ista regis, quæ accepit ad tempus, vt est pugnare pro Ecclesia, eripere eam è manibus hostium, hostes debellare, Ecclesiam denique regere, gere, ea ratione, qua regitur & regetur ad finem vsque mundi, quæ officia, quia post hostes debellatos & Ecclesiam coronandam ad patrem adductam, pro ea regiminis forma, qua Christus in hoc mundo vius est, cessabunt, nemini mirum videri debet, quòd Christus regnum Deo & patri traditurus dicatur. regni itaque vox, eo loco non pro ipsa (vt ita dicam) regni, aut imperij substantia, qua nunquam Christus caruturus est, sed pro administratione, aut administrandi forma, qua vtitur Christus in colligenda & conseruanda Ecclesia sua in hoc mundo, capitur.
units.tr: KINGDOM of Christ, eternal. 1 Chron. 17.12, 14; Ps. 45.8; 89.4, 35–37; Isa. 9.5, 6; Dan. 2.44; Luke 1.33; Heb. 1.8. Christ will therefore hand over the kingdom to God and the Father (1 Cor. 15.24) on that last day, when all enemies have been overthrown and he has delivered to the Father, as if into his hands, all whom he received to govern, to be crowned with eternal glory. This does not mean that he will abdicate the kingdom, just as the Father did not abdicate his kingdom when he handed it over to the Son (Ps. 2.6, 8, 9, etc.). Nor does it mean that he will give up the sovereignty itself, which he received from the Father for ever. It means only the offices of king which he received for a time: to fight for the Church, to snatch her from the hands of her enemies, to subdue those enemies, and finally to rule the Church. He will rule her in the manner in which she is ruled and will be ruled until the end of the world. These offices will cease once the enemies are subdued and the Church has been brought to the Father to be crowned, so that the form of government by which Christ has ruled in this world will come to an end. No one should be surprised that Christ is said to hand over the kingdom to God and the Father. So the word "kingdom" in that place is taken not for the substance (so to speak) of the kingdom or sovereignty, which Christ will never lose, but for the administration, or the manner of administering, which Christ uses in gathering and preserving his Church in this world.

units.la: REGNUM Israel calamitosum futurum, 2 Para.15.3.
units.tr: KINGDOM of Israel to be disastrous, 2 Chron. 15.3.

units.la: REGNUM Salomonis: Regni Salomonis diuisio prædicitur. 1 Reg.11.v.11.31.V.SALOMON.
units.tr: KINGDOM of Solomon. The division of Solomon's kingdom is foretold. 1 Kings 11.11, 31. See SOLOMON.

units.la: REGNI bene instituti descriptio, Esa.32 1. regni invasio infinita, e úsque pœna: Absalom,2 Sam.15.4.& 18.9.Adonias, 1 Reg.2. v.22 23.24.25.
units.tr: Description of a well-ordered kingdom, Isa. 32.1. Endless invasion of a kingdom, and punishment reaching even to: Absalom, 2 Sam. 15.4; 18.9. Adonijah, 1 Kings 2.22–25.

units.la: REGNA & imperia omnia in manu Dei, 1 Reg. 11.31. Iob.12. 18.& 34.18. Dan.4. v.14.22. Regna & imperia Deus transfert.& mutat,Iob.34.24.Dan.2.21.& 4. v.14.29.Ier.27.5.6. Exempla,Regnum Saulis ad Davidem, 1 Sam. 16. v. 1.13. 1 Par.10.v.13.14. Regni Roboami pars ad Ieroboamum: A Roboamo enim filio Salomonis decem tribus avelluntur, & Ieroboamo committuntur, & ex Monarchia fit Dyarchia,1 Reg.11.13. & 12.v.21.22.23.24. regnum Iuda ad Nabuchodonosorem Ierem. 27 v.4.5 6.7.8. regnum Nabuchodonosor ad Balthasarem,Dan.2.v,20.21.&4.v.31.32. & 5.1. regnum Balthasaris ad Darium Medum,5.31. De quatuor regnis mundi,Dan.7.1 &c.
units.tr: All kingdoms and empires are in God's hand: 1 Kings 11.31; Job 12.18; 34.18; Dan. 4.14, 22. God transfers and changes kingdoms: Job 34.24; Dan. 2.21; 4.14, 29; Jer. 27.5, 6. Examples: the kingdom of Saul passes to David, 1 Sam. 16.1, 13; 1 Chron. 10.13, 14. Part of Rehoboam's kingdom passes to Jeroboam. For ten tribes are torn away from Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and committed to Jeroboam, and monarchy becomes dyarchy: 1 Kings 11.13; 12.21–24. The kingdom of Judah passes to Nebuchadnezzar, Jer. 27.4–8. The kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar passes to Belshazzar, Dan. 2.20, 21; 4.31, 32; 5.1. The kingdom of Belshazzar passes to Darius the Mede, Dan. 5.31. On the four kingdoms of the world, Dan. 7.1ff.

units.la: [REGO. Regit Deus suos, Psal.23.1.& 48.15.& 80. 2 Regit Christus Ecclesiam suam,Esa.49.10.Matth.2.6.Rom.15.12 Apo. 7.17. regit Christus Gentes, seu potenter coercet hostes suos, Psal.2.9. Apoc.2.27 & 12.5. & 19.15. regit homo seipsum vel alios, Iud.16.26 2 Sam.3.6.1 Reg.4.12. & 21.7. 1 Par.12. 12. & 24.7. Act.20.28.]
units.tr: [RULE. God rules his own, Ps. 23.1; 48.15; 80. Christ rules his Church, Isa. 49.10; Matt. 2.6; Rom. 15.12; Rev. 7.17. Christ rules the nations, or powerfully restrains his enemies, Ps. 2.9; Rev. 2.27; 12.5; 19.15. A man rules himself or others, Judg. 16.26; 2 Sam. 3.6; 1 Kings 4.12; 21.7; 1 Chron. 12.12; 24.7; Acts 20.28.]

units.la: REGULA aequa, Levi.19.35 regula Euanglij, Gal.6.16. Phil.3. 16 ea sequenda & in ea permanendum, ibid.
units.tr: RULE, equal: Lev. 19.35. The rule of the Gospel, Gal. 6.16; Phil. 3.16. It is to be followed and persevered in, ibid.

units.la: REGULUS, Christum adit pro filij sanitate, Ioan.4.47.
units.tr: A petty king (regulus) approaches Christ for his son's health, John 4.47.

units.la: Vera RELIGIO, est purus Dei cultus, à vero Deo instituus, & ad verũ illũ Deum relatus, eò spectans, ut Deus sanctè & piè ab hominibus ametur & observetur, homines vero Deum amando & colendo vitam aeternam consequantur: Rom.12.2. Ioh.4.25.
units.tr: True RELIGION is the pure worship of God, instituted by the true God and directed to that true God. Its aim is that God be loved and worshipped holily and piously by people, and that people, by loving and worshipping God, attain eternal life. Rom. 12.2; John 4.25.

units.la: RELIGIO munda & immaculata quae, Iac.1.27.
units.tr: RELIGION that is pure and undefiled: Jas. 1.27.

units.la: RELIGIONIS contemtae exempla: Gallio, Act.18.15. simulatae, Absalom, 2 Sam.15.7. religionis Christianae rudimenta, Heb.6.1. religionis semen humanis mentibus inditum, 2 Reg.17.v.26.27. religionis externa professio requiritur, Esa.44.5, & 45.23. religioni Iudaicae multi adiunguntur, Esth.8.17.
units.tr: Examples of despised religion: Gallio, Acts 18.15. Of feigned religion: Absalom, 2 Sam. 15.7. The rudiments of the Christian religion: Heb. 6.1. The seed of religion placed in human minds: 2 Kings 17.26, 27. An external profession of religion is required: Isa. 44.5; 45.23. Many join themselves to the Jewish religion: Esth. 8.17.
