units.la: Religiosi viri, erant conversi ex Gentibus ad Iudaeos, & doctrinam ac promissiones Dei amplexi: sed non circumcisi, nec observantes ceremonias: quia Gentibus liberum erat servare circumcisionem & ceremonias, Tales fuerunt Naaman Syrus, Eunuchus, & alij de quibus Act.2.5.
units.tr: Religious men were converts from the Gentiles to the Jews who embraced the teaching and promises of God, but were not circumcised and did not observe the ceremonies, since it was free for Gentiles to keep circumcision and the ceremonies. Such were Naaman the Syrian, the eunuch, and others mentioned in Acts 2.5.

units.la: RELINQUERE patrem. &c. propter Christum, Matth.19.29. Mar.10.29. Luc.18.29. relinqui, pro deseri periturum, Mat.24.41. Relinquentes Deum affliguntur, Iosh.24.20. Iudi.10.6.7. non relinquit eos Deus, Deut.4.30.31.
units.tr: To LEAVE father, etc., for Christ's sake: Matt. 19.29; Mark 10.29; Luke 18.29. To be left means to be deserted and to perish: Matt. 24.41. Those who forsake God are afflicted: Josh. 24.20; Judg. 10.6, 7. God does not leave them: Deut. 4.30, 31.

units.la: RELIQUIAE servatae, Esa.19. & 10. versi 21.22. & 21.17. Ierem.23.3. Ezec.14.22. & 17.ver.22.23. Roman.9.29 & 11.5. Reliquias & vestes sanctorum magnam vim habere, & Deum per eas operari, ac proinde venerandas & adorandas esse eas, nituntur Pontifici Idololatrae confirmare: ut, Pa-lium Eliae, 2 Reg 2.14. Ossa Elisaei, 13.21. Fimbria Christi, Matt.9.20. & 14.36. Sudaria Pauli, Act.19.12. Umbra Petri, Act.5.15. miracula edidisse leguntur. Vide solutionem, Act.19.10.
units.tr: REMNANTS preserved: Isa. 10.21, 22; 19; 21.17; Jer. 23.3; Ezek. 14.22; 17.22, 23; Rom. 9.29; 11.5. The Idolatrous Pontiff strives to confirm that relics and garments of the saints have great power, and that God works through them, and that therefore they are to be venerated and adored. Thus we read that the mantle of Elijah (2 Kings 2.14), the bones of Elisha (13.21), the hem of Christ (Matt. 9.20; 14.36), the handkerchiefs of Paul (Acts 19.12), and the shadow of Peter (Acts 5.15) performed miracles. See the answer in Acts 19.10.

units.la: REMISSIO, sive libertas anno Iubilaeo. Vide IVBILAEVS. Remissio debitorum anno septimo, Deut.15.v.1 2. remissio peccatorum in Ecclesia, Esa.33.24 gratuita est, Psal.19.13. 14. Act.2.38. Col.1.20. à poenitentia seiungi non potest, Esa.55.7. Ezec.18.v.27.31. & 33.11. 1 Ioan.1.7. sanguine Christi par-ti
units.tr: REMISSION, or liberty, in the Jubilee year. See JUBILEE. Remission of debts in the seventh year: Deut. 15.1, 2. The remission of sins in the Church, Isa. 33.24, is free: Ps. 19.13, 14; Acts 2.38; Col. 1.20. It cannot be separated from repentance: Isa. 55.7; Ezek. 18.27, 31; 33.11; 1 John 1.7. It is obtained by the blood of Christ

units.la: sti parta, Matth.26 28. V. PECCATA.
units.tr: obtained, Matt. 26.28. See SINS.

units.la: REMISSIO peccatorum, quid sit, & quo sensu in futurum seculum reiiciatur. Vide PECCATORVM remissio. Remissio peccatorum, solius Dei opus. Vide DEVS Remissionis peccatorum praedicatio in Christi nomine, Luc.24. 47. remittendum ex corde fratribus, Eccles.28.8. Matth.5. 23. & 6.12. & 18.v.22.35. Luc.11.4. & 17.v.3.4. Ephes.4.32. Col.3.13. ¶ Quod nos de remissione peccatorum & vita aeterna consequenda semper dubitare debeamus, quib. testimoniis stabiliant Papistae. Vide CERTI & Psal.103. integrum. Esa.1.18. Mich.7.18. 1 Ioh.1.7. Eph.5.25. Col.2.13. Rom.8.1.31. ad finem usque Esa.53.5.1 Pet.2.24. Matth.26. 28. Act.10.43. Apoc.1.5.1 Corin.6.9.10.11. Heb.1.3.1 Ioh.4. 10. & similia permulta, quibus impium dogma evertitur.
units.tr: The REMISSION of sins: what it is, and in what sense it is denied in the age to come. See REMISSION OF SINS. The remission of sins is the work of God alone. See GOD. The preaching of remission of sins in the name of Christ: Luke 24.47. We must forgive our brothers from the heart: Ecclus. 28.2; Matt. 5.23; 6.12; 18.22, 35; Luke 11.4; 17.3, 4; Eph. 4.32; Col. 3.13. ¶ That we must always doubt the remission of sins and the attainment of eternal life: the Papists confirm this by what testimonies? See CERTAIN. And Ps. 103 entire; Isa. 1.18; Mic. 7.18; 1 John 1.7; Eph. 5.25; Col. 2.13; Rom. 8.1, 31 to the end; Isa. 53.5; 1 Pet. 2.24; Matt. 26.28; Acts 10.43; Rev. 1.5; 1 Cor. 6.9–11; Heb. 1.3; 1 John 4.10, and very many similar passages, by which the impious doctrine is overthrown.

units.la: REMPHAN idolum, vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: REMPHAN, an idol: see the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: RENASCI, vide REGENERATIO. Renascimur per verbum Dei, 1 Petr.1.23. Renatus ex aqua & spiritu sancto, Ioan.3.5.
units.tr: To be REBORN: see REGENERATION. We are reborn through the word of God, 1 Pet. 1.23. Born again of water and the Holy Spirit, John 3.5.

units.la: RENES accincti in agno paschali, Exodi 12.11.(1 Pet. 1 13.)
units.tr: LOINS girded in the paschal lamb, Exod. 12.11 (1 Pet. 1.13).

units.la: RENOVATIO nostra Christus, Tit.3.5.
units.tr: Christ is our RENEWAL, Titus 3.5.

units.la: RENVNTIANDVM omnibus quae possidemus, Luc.14.26.
units.tr: All that we possess must be RENOUNCED, Luke 14.26.

units.la: REPREHENSIONES, necessariae & utiles, 1 Corint.4.21.2 Corinth.2.4. Ephes.5.v.11.13.2 Tim.3.16.& 4.2. Vide OBIVRGATIO,
units.tr: REPROOFS, necessary and useful: 1 Cor. 4.21; 2 Cor. 2.4; Eph. 5.11, 13; 2 Tim. 3.16; 4.2. See REBUKE.

units.la: REPROBATIO, est Actus divini placiti, quo Deus ab aeterno propositit in se de vniuersitate creaturarum maiorem partem praeterire, quo ad gratiae & gloriae suae salutaris & supernaturalis communionem, & eadem integritate originis suae non perstituras, secundum iustitiam suam propter peccata ipsorum, praedamnare, ad illustrationem gloriae suae.
units.tr: REPROBATION is an act of the divine purpose, by which God decided from eternity to pass over in himself the greater part of the universe of creatures, as regards the saving and supernatural fellowship of his grace and glory, and, condemning them according to his justice on account of their sins, to consign them to the same condition of origin in which they will not persist, to the illustration of his glory.

units.la: REPROBATIO: Reprobatio aeterna est, Psal.58.3. Rom.9.v.11. 12.13.17.18.20.21.22. Reprobationis signum, Psal.36.v.4.5.2 Cor.4.3.4.1 Ioan.3.12.& 4.6.
units.tr: REPROBATION: eternal reprobation is Ps. 58.3; Rom. 9.11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 20, 21, 22. The sign of reprobation: Ps. 36.4, 5; 2 Cor. 4.3, 4; John 3.12; 4.6.

units.la: REPROBI, vasa contumeliae, interitui destinata, Roman. 9.verf.21.22.1 Thess.2.16. 2 Thess.2. verf. 11.12.2 Timoth. 2.v.16.20.1 Pet.2.8. Reprob: Deo exosi, Malach.1.3. a patre non plantati, Matth.15.13. corrigi nequeunt, Eccles.7. 14. Reproborum interitus, Apoc.20.15. Vide IMPII. De
units.tr: REPROBATES, vessels of dishonour, destined for destruction: Rom. 9.21, 22; 1 Thess. 2.16; 2 Thess. 2.11, 12; 2 Tim. 2.16, 20; 1 Pet. 2.8. Reprobates are hated by God, Mal. 1.3; not planted by the Father, Matt. 15.13; cannot be corrected, Eccles. 7.14. The destruction of the reprobate: Rev. 20.15. See the IMPIOUS. Concerning

units.la: reprobis, Matt.13.13. Marc.4.12. Luc. 8.10. Reprobum non esse certò scit Paulus, 2 Cor.13.3.6.
units.tr: the reprobate: Matt. 13.13; Mark 4.12; Luke 8.10. Paul knows for certain that he is not a reprobate: 2 Cor. 13.3, 6.

units.la: REPTILIA Dei verbo creantur, Genes. 1.24. Reptilia immunda, Leuit. 11.v.41.42.43.&c.
units.tr: REPTILES are created by the word of God, Gen. 1.24. Unclean reptiles: Lev. 11.41–43, etc.

units.la: REPVDIVM, (vide Libellus repudij,) Deut.24.1.Esa.5.1.Ierem. 3.3.Malac.2.16.Matt.5,30,& 19,7, Marc.10.4. Repudiatam à viro Sacerdotes ne accipiunto, Leuit.21.7.
units.tr: DIVORCE (see Bill of divorce): Deut. 24.1; Isa. 5.1; Jer. 3.3; Mal. 2.16; Matt. 5.30; 19.7; Mark 10.4. Priests shall not take a woman put away by her husband: Lev. 21.7.

units.la: REPVLERVNT Deum Israelitæ, Num.11, 20,1 Sam.10,19.
units.tr: The Israelites REJECTED God: Num. 11.20; 1 Sam. 10.19.

units.la: REQVIES vera in Christo quærenda, Matth. 11,29. requies pijs apparata, 2 Thess.1.7. Hebr. 4.3, requies nulla inobedientibus, Deut.28,65, Quies eorum qui in Domino moriuntur Apoc.14.13.
units.tr: True REST is to be sought in Christ, Matt. 11.29. Rest is prepared for the godly, 2 Thess. 1.7; Heb. 4.3. There is no rest for the disobedient, Deut. 28.65. The rest of those who die in the Lord: Rev. 14.13.

units.la: REQVIEVIT Deus die septimo, Genes.2,2.
units.tr: God RESTED on the seventh day, Gen. 2.2.

units.la: RERVM temporalium & spiritualium discrimen, 2 Cor.4.18.
units.tr: The difference between temporal and spiritual things: 2 Cor. 4.18.

units.la: RES ipsa non parum afficit, Iudic. 9. 19. res propius expedenda, priusquam damnetur, Iosu.22,v.13 30, res proximi perdita restituenda, Deut.22.1.
units.tr: The matter itself touches us no little: Judges 9:19. The matter must be examined more closely before anyone is condemned: Joshua 22:13, 30. A neighbour's lost property must be restored: Deuteronomy 22:1.

units.la: RESIPISCENTIA, Vide POENITENTIA. Resipiscentes consolandi, 2 Corint. 2,v.7.8. Resipiscentia donum Dei, Thren.5.21. Resipiscentia Israelis, Ierem. 3,22, &c. resipiscere omnes desiderat Deus, 2 Pet.3.9.
units.tr: REPENTANCE: see REPENTANCE. Those who repent are to be comforted: 2 Corinthians 2:7-8. Repentance is a gift of God: Lamentations 5:21. The repentance of Israel: Jeremiah 3:22, etc. God desires that all should repent: 2 Peter 3:9.

units.la: RESPHA, concubina Saulis, 2 Sam. 21.11. eius filij cruci affiguntur, v. 8, eius in illos materna charitas & affectus, v. 10. ingreditur ad eam Abner, 2 Sam.3.7.
units.tr: RESPHA, Saul's concubine: 2 Samuel 21:11. Her sons are fastened to the cross: v. 8. Her maternal love and feeling towards them: v. 10. Abner goes in to her: 2 Samuel 3:7.

units.la: RESPICERE, pro diligere & gratuito fauore completi, Luc.1.48. Respicit Deus super obedientes, Leu.26,9. vt respiciat ipsum Deus, orat Israel, Deut.26,15.
units.tr: TO LOOK UPON (RESPICERE), meaning to love and to be filled with free favour: Luke 1:48. God looks upon those who obey: Leviticus 26:9. Israel prays that God would look upon him: Deuteronomy 26:15.

units.la: RESTITVTIO rei ablatæ: Exod. 22.3. Num.5.7, Luc.19,8, Ezech.33.19.1, Cor.6.11, Rei amissæ, Deut.22.1.
units.tr: RESTITUTION of a thing taken away: Exodus 22:3; Numbers 5:7; Luke 19:8; Ezekiel 33:19. (1 Corinthians 6:11 also.) Of a thing lost: Deuteronomy 22:1.

units.la: RESPONSIONES variæ duræ, Iudic. 8.7. 2 Reg. 9.22. 2 Par. 10.13. ironicæ, Dan. 3 16.
units.tr: RESPONSES, various: harsh, Judges 8:7; 2 Kings 9:22; 2 Chronicles 10:13. Ironic, Daniel 3:16.

units.la: Responsio præmeditanda: pro.18.13. & 15.28. Quomodo stulto sit respondendum: Pro.26 4.5. Responsio mollis vtilis: Pro.15.1. & 25.15. Exempla, Sedatur Esau à fratre: Gen. 33.3. Ioseph à fratribus: G. 5c.16. Saul à Dauide. 1. Sam.24.9. Dauid ab Abigail, 1 Sam.25.23. Ephraemitæ à Gedeone, Iudic.8.1. Responsio dura & temeraria exitialis: Pro.15.1. 28. Exempla: Caino, Ge.4.9. ait Deus, maledictus esto. Nabal Dauidem ad cædem provocauit, 1 Sam.25. Roboam populum ad defectionem, 1 Reg. 12.
units.tr: A response to be premeditated: Proverbs 18:13 and 15:28. How a fool is to be answered: Proverbs 26:4-5. A soft response is useful: Proverbs 15:1 and 25:15. Examples: Esau is calmed by his brother, Genesis 33:3; Joseph by his brothers, Genesis 50:16; Saul by David, 1 Samuel 24:9; David by Abigail, 1 Samuel 25:23; the Ephraimites by Gideon, Judges 8:1. A harsh and rash response is destructive: Proverbs 15:1, 28. Examples: Cain, Genesis 4:9, to whom God said, "Cursed be you"; Nabal provoked David to slaughter, 1 Samuel 25; Rehoboam drove the people to revolt, 1 Kings 12.

units.la: RESPONDER Hebraica præsi, is etiam dicitur, qui non est rogatus, Matth. 17, 4, & est idem quod sermonem innem incipere aut ordiri, vt patet ex Marc.11.14.hoc po- nitur pro sermonem inchoare, nec semper præsupponit interrogationem, Sic Matth.28.5. Luc.8.40. respondere dicitur Christus, cùm tacitas hominum cogitationes compellat.
units.tr: TO ANSWER (RESPONDERE). In Hebrew idiom it is also said of one who has not been asked: Matthew 17:4. It is the same as beginning or opening a speech, as is clear from Mark 11:14. It is used for beginning to speak, and does not always presuppose a question: so Matthew 28:5; Luke 8:40. Christ is said to answer when he addresses the silent thoughts of men.

units.la: [respondet Deus. 2. Deus Pater. 3 Christus Deus, Filius Dei, Angelus Patris, Ecclesiæ sponsus, Deus in carne manifestans. 4. respondet vox è cœlo. 5. Angelus bonus.6.Angelus malus.7.Homo.]
units.tr: [God answers. (1) God the Father. (2) Christ, God, Son of God, Angel of the Father, Bridegroom of the Church, God manifest in the flesh. (3) A voice from heaven. (4) A good angel. (5) An evil angel. (6) A man.]

units.la: RESPUBLICA, iustis regnantibus floret, Prouerb.28.12.& 29.2. Reipublicæ destructionis vera effigies, Esa.3.v.1.2.&c.
units.tr: THE COMMONWEALTH flourishes when the just rule: Proverbs 28:12 and 29:2. The true picture of the ruin of a commonwealth: Isaiah 3:1-2, etc.

units.la: RESURRECTIO carnis, Est iterata & individua animæ cum corpore copulatio, facta potente Dei virtute, vt morte victa, homines immortales facti, perpetuò viuant alij in gloria, alij in pœnis, Ioan.5.29.
units.tr: RESURRECTION OF THE FLESH is the renewed and indivisible joining of the soul with the body, brought about by the mighty power of God, so that, with death overcome, men made immortal may live forever, some in glory and others in punishments: John 5:29.

units.la: RESVRRECTIO, pro ipsa redemptione, aut vita immortali, quæ resurrectionem sanctorum consequetur, phil.3.10. Nam alioquin etiam infideles resurgent, sed in perpetuas pœnas, quæ vocatur mors æterna μεταφυμικὸς, pro iis, qui à mortis somno sunt excitati, Actor 26.23. non secus ac circumcisi Iudæi, appellantur Circumcisio, Tit.1.10 Resurrectio, fidelium scopus, 2 Cor. 4.14. Resurrectio generalis prædicitur, Dan. 12. 2 certissima est, Iob.19.v.25.26.27. Esaiæ.26.19 & 65.18.& 66.14. Ion.2.11. Soph.3.8. Luc.14.14. & 20 35. Rom.8.v.11 21.1. Cor.15 12. per totum caput.2. Tabita Ioppensis à Petro excitata,Actor.9.40. Eutychus à Paulo excitatus, 20. 10. Vide ANIMARV immortalitas.
units.tr: RESURRECTION is used for redemption itself, or for the immortal life that will follow the resurrection of the saints: Philippians 3:10. For otherwise unbelievers too will rise, but to everlasting punishments, which is called eternal death (μεταφυμικὸς). It is used for those who have been woken from the sleep of death: Acts 26:23; just as the circumcised Jews are called "the Circumcision": Titus 1:10. Resurrection is the goal of believers: 2 Corinthians 4:14. The general resurrection is foretold: Daniel 12:2; it is most certain: Job 19:25-27; Isaiah 26:19, 65:18, 66:14; Jonah 2:11; Zephaniah 3:8; Luke 14:14, 20:35; Romans 8:11, 21:1; 1 Corinthians 15:12 throughout the chapter; 2 Corinthians 4:10-11; Colossians 3:4; Galatians 6:7-8; Philippians 3:11, 21, 4:3; 2 Timothy 2:11; Revelation 20:12. Many testimonies to the general resurrection are added: Job 19:25; Ezekiel 37:1; Daniel 12:2; Isaiah 26:19; Matthew 22:30-31; John 5:28, 6:40, 11:24; Acts 24:15, 26:6-8; 1 Corinthians 15:12; Philippians 3:11, 21; 1 Thessalonians 4:14. The particular instances contained in the singular resurrections are: the taking up of Enoch into heaven, which is a most certain and infallible proof of the resurrection, Genesis 5:24; Hebrews 11:5; the taking up of Elijah, 2 Kings 2:9-11; the son of the widow of Zarephath, 1 Kings 17:22; the son of the Shunammite woman, 2 Kings 4:33; a man raised by touching the bones of Elisha, 2 Kings 13:21; the dry bones raised, Ezekiel 37:1, etc.; the daughter of Jairus, Matthew 9:25; Mark 5:42; the son of the widow at Nain, Luke 7:15; Lazarus, John 11:43-44; Christ himself, Matthew 28:6; Mark 16:6; Luke 24:5; John 20:8-12, 13, 21:14; Romans 1:4, 4:24-25, 6:4, 8:11, 10:9; 1 Corinthians 6:14, 15:4, 20; 2 Corinthians 4:14, 5:15; Galatians 1:1; Ephesians 1:20; Philippians 2:9; Colossians 2:12, 3:1; 1 Thessalonians 1:10, 4:14; Hebrews 11:20; 1 Peter 1:20. Those raised at the time of Christ's passion: Matthew 27:52-53. Tabitha of Joppa, raised by Peter: Acts 9:40. Eutychus, raised by Paul: Acts 20:10. See IMMORTALITY OF THE SOULS.

units.la: Resurrectio piis ac impiis communis est, Matt.25.31. Act.24.15.Etsi autem resurrectio generalis est, & piis atque impiis communis, tamen restringitur ad pios, Luc. 20.36.quia sicut ij deinde dicuntur victuri,qui aeterna illa felicitate perfruentur, ita ij vere censentur resurgere qui in vitam aeternam resurgunt. ¶ Nonnulli male sani homines,praeter hunc Lucae locum, negantes impiorum resurrectionem, abuntur & illo Christi dicto, Luc. 20.38, vbi Deus dicitur esse non autem fore Deus mortuorum. Et quo dicto consequi videtur (vt illi colligunt) aut iam illos resurrexisse,aut haec verba non pertinere ad corporum resurrectionem, sed ad animi vitam. Sed respondet ibidem Christus huic obiectioni, vt dicat Deo iam viventes qui suo tempore sint resurrecturi. ¶ Ad haec arripiunt etiam illud,Luc.21.36. & Psal.1.5. vbi dicuntur impij non consistere,aut,vt Graecus interpres, & eum sequuti matuerunt,non resurgere,hoc est, non apparere confidenter & intrepide coram Iudice Christo.
units.tr: The resurrection is common to the godly and the ungodly: Matthew 25:31; Acts 24:15. Although the general resurrection is indeed common to the godly and the ungodly, it is nonetheless restricted to the godly: Luke 20:36. For just as those are said to live hereafter who enjoy that eternal happiness, so those are truly considered to rise who rise to eternal life. Some men of unsound mind, apart from this passage of Luke, deny the resurrection of the wicked, and they also misuse that saying of Christ, Luke 20:38, where God is said to be the God not of the dead but of the living. From this saying, as they gather, it seems to follow either that they have already risen, or that these words do not pertain to the resurrection of bodies but to the life of the soul. But Christ answers this objection in the same place, saying that those who are to rise at their appointed time are living to God already. They also seize upon Luke 21:36 and Psalm 1:5, where the wicked are said not to stand, or, as the Greek translator and those who followed him rendered it, not to rise, that is, not to appear boldly and fearlessly before the Judge, Christ.

units.la: De resurrectione duo primarij Christi Discipuli dubitant,Marci 9.10. Illa autem quaestio eo loci mota, non est simpliciter accipienda, quasi de futura resurrectione dubitarent.Nam etsi erant admodum rudes, tamen non ita erant. opinor, imperiti, vt hominis felicitatem huius vitae spatio terminari putarent (alioqui pij omnium hominum miserrimi essent,1 Corinth.15.19.) sed quum nullam corporum resurrectionem, praeter illam vniuersalem, intelligerent, & de terrestri Messiae regno & Eliae aduentu Pharisaicis opinionibus essent imbuti, non poterant capere, quod Christus dixerat de singulari illa & peculiari sua resurrectione, tertio die futura. Quamobrem etiam, cùm Dominus iam esset in coelum conscensurus, non verentur ex eo quaerere, an illo tempore esset regnum Israelis restituturus, Actor.1.6.vt intelligamus, quam necesse sit Christum corporeà nobis abesse, vt eum non in terra, sed in coelo quaerere discamus. Resurrectio carnis creditu difficilis Actor.17.v.18.32, resurrectio quando futura, Iob.14.12.
units.tr: Concerning the resurrection, two chief disciples of Christ doubted: Mark 9:10. That question raised in that place is not to be taken simply, as if they doubted the future resurrection. For although they were quite rude, I think they were not so unlearned as to suppose that the happiness of man ends within the span of this life (otherwise the godly would be the most wretched of all men, 1 Corinthians 15:19). But since they understood no resurrection of bodies except that general one, and since they had been steeped in Pharisaic opinions about the earthly kingdom of the Messiah and the coming of Elijah, they could not grasp what Christ had said about his own unique and singular resurrection, to take place on the third day. Therefore too, when the Lord was about to ascend into heaven, they do not hesitate to ask him whether at that time he would restore the kingdom of Israel: Acts 1:6. So that we may understand how necessary it is that Christ be physically absent from us, so that we learn to seek him not on earth but in heaven. The resurrection of the flesh is hard to believe: Acts 17:18, 32. When the resurrection will take place: Job 14:12.

units.la: ESVRRECTIO Christi, Vide CHRIST vs. resurrectio Iudicij, Ioan.5.29. resurrectio iustorum, Lucæ 14.14. resurrectio Christo tanquam fundamento nititur,1 Corin. 15.21. Resurrectio vitæ, pro ea resurrectione, quam perennis vita comitatur, quasi dicas, vitalis, Hebraismus, Ioan.5.29.
units.tr: RESURRECTION of Christ: see CHRIST. Resurrection of judgment: John 5:29. Resurrection of the just: Luke 14:14. The resurrection rests on Christ as its foundation: 1 Corinthians 15:21. Resurrection of life, meaning that resurrection which is accompanied by perpetual life, as if you were to say "vital"; a Hebraism: John 5:29.

units.la: Resurrectio duplex est. Prior, Apoc.20.v.5.6. quæ animorum est, Rom.6 v.4.5.11. Coloss. 1. 12. in qua qui partem habuerint, secunda mors in eos potestatem non habebit, Apoc.20.76. Posterior, Apoc.20 13. quæ carnis est, de qua supra, [Est & resurrectio quædam gratiæ, quando Deus suis benigne adest, ne in lapsu pereant quotidiano, Prov 34.16.]
units.tr: The resurrection is twofold. The first is in Revelation 20:5-6; it belongs to souls: Romans 6:4-5, 11; Colossians 1:12. Those who have a share in it, the second death will have no power over them: Revelation 20:6. The second is in Revelation 20:13; it belongs to the flesh, concerning which see above. [There is also a resurrection of grace, when God kindly stands by his own, lest they perish in their daily fall: Proverbs 24:16.]

units.la: RESURRECTIONIS filij, Luc. 20. 36. Vide FILII.de resurrectione erronea opinio,2 Timot.2.18.
units.tr: SONS OF THE RESURRECTION: Luke 20:36. See SONS. A mistaken opinion about the resurrection: 2 Timothy 2:18.

units.tr: Examples of those raised up: see RESURRECTION, particular; and MIRACLES.

units.tr: Bodies rose at the death of Christ: Matthew 27:52. Christ rose, 28:1, etc., for our justification: Romans 4:25. To rise with Christ: 6:5. The Apostles testify that Christ rose: Acts 4:33. The resurrection of Christ was foretold by David: Acts 2:25. The power of Christ's resurrection: Hosea 13:14. In Christ's resurrection, eternal life: 1 Peter 1:3-4. Concerning the resurrection of Christ: 1 Corinthians 15:12, etc. Christ is the resurrection and the life: John 11:25. The resurrection of the dead and the change of the flesh into glory: Exodus 6:4; Ezra 2:16, 14:25; Job 14:13, 19:26, 21:30; Isaiah 6:19, 66:14; Ezekiel 37:1, 9; Daniel 12:12; Jonah 2:11; Zephaniah 3:8; Matthew 22:23, 31; Luke 20:35; John 5:21, 28, 5:39, 1:24; Acts 24:15; 1 Corinthians 15:1, etc.; 2 Corinthians 4:14, 5:1, etc.; Colossians 3:4; Philippians 3:21, 4:3; 1 Thessalonians 4:13-16; 2 Timothy 2:11; Revelation 20:12.

units.tr: God judges according to righteousness, 1 Sam. 26.23; Prov. 13.21; Ps. 18.21, and according to unrighteousness, Deut. 32.41, 43; Ps. 137.8; Rom. 12.19. Those who repay evil for good: Ps. 35.12. And against them, Matt. 5.44.

units.tr: Phaleg, son of Eber, Gen. 11.18; his posterity, vv. 20, 24. (ascent)

units.tr: To whisper in someone's ear: to tell them something. 1 Sam. 19.13; 2 Sam. 7.27; 1 Sam. 9.15; Matt. 13.35.

units.la: REVELATIO Antichristi, pro aperto eius tyrannidis exercitio,2 Thess.2.3.8. reuelatio secundi aduentus Christi à fidelibus expectatur,1 Corinth.1.7. reuelationes & visiones,Iosu.5.13.1 Reg.17.9.2 Machab.3.24. & 5.2.& 10.& 11.8. Reuelationum Dei peculiarium exempla, Vide APARITIONVM Dei, &c. Reuelationum genera peculiaria olim duo fuerunt,Num.12.6.V. Act.2.17.& 2 Corinth.12.7.
units.tr: The revelation of Antichrist, that is, the open exercise of his tyranny, 2 Thess. 2.3, 8. The revelation of the second coming of Christ is awaited by the faithful, 1 Cor. 1.7. Revelations and visions: Josh. 5.13; 1 Kings 17.9; 2 Macc. 3.24; 5.2; 10; 11.8. Examples of God's particular revelations: see APPEARANCES of God, etc. Of particular kinds of revelation there were formerly two: Num. 12.6; cf. Acts 2.17 and 2 Cor. 12.7.

units.la: REVERENTIA, est dignitatis superiorisque potestatis agnitio & veneratio, quam & animo & corpore exhibere inferiores debent,Leuit.19.3.V.Liberorum,& aliorum officium.
units.tr: REVERENCE is the recognition and honouring of dignity and superior power, which inferiors ought to show both in mind and in body, Lev. 19.3; it is the duty of children and of others.

units.la: REVERENTIA erga alios praecipitur, Rom.12.10. Phil.2. 1 Pet.5.5. Vide HONOS. Reuerentiae exempla: Rex Israel Reg.6.v.21.22. Discipuli,Marci 9.32.Elizabeth, Luc.1. populus,9.45.Actor.5.13. Ecclesia Gentium,20.37.& 21. Paulus,26.25.V.HONOR.
units.tr: Reverence towards others is enjoined, Rom. 12.10; Phil. 2; 1 Pet. 5.5. See HONOUR. Examples of reverence: the king of Israel, 1 Kings 6.21, 22; the disciples, Mark 9.32; Elizabeth, Luke 1; the people, Luke 9.45; Acts 5.13; the church of the Gentiles, Acts 20.37; 21; Paul, Acts 26.25. See HONOUR.

units.la: REX:Rex qualis,& quorsum constituendus,Deut.17.15. Rex iustus,regni stabilimentum,Prou.29.4. à Deo est,1 Sam.12.13.1 Reg.10.9. honore afficiendus, Rom 13.1.&c.1 Pet.2.17. Legem legere debet,Deut.17.v.18.19.equos sibi multiplicare non debet, v.16. Rex seculorum immortalis,1 Tim.1.17.
units.tr: KING: what sort of king is to be appointed, and to what end, Deut. 17.15. A just king is the establishment of a kingdom, Prov. 29.4; he is from God, 1 Sam. 12.13; 1 Kings 10.9; he is to be honoured, Rom. 13.1, etc.; 1 Pet. 2.17. He ought to read the law, Deut. 17.18, 19; he ought not to multiply horses for himself, v. 16. The King of the ages is immortal, 1 Tim. 1.17.

units.la: REGIS cor in manu Domini,Prou.21.1.Regis ira periculosa,16.14.& 19.12. Regis irae exempla:Ioas,2 Paral.24.21.. Nebuchodonosor,Dan.2.v.5.12. Reges inaugurandi & concrandi formula,Vide PRECATIONVM formulae:&,PRINCIPES inaugurandi.
units.tr: The king's heart is in the hand of the Lord, Prov. 21.1. The king's wrath is dangerous, Prov. 16.14; 19.12. Examples of the wrath of kings: Joash, 2 Chron. 24.21; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 2.5, 12. The form of inaugurating and crowning kings: see the PRAYER formulas, and PRINCES, inauguration of.

units.la: Reges ac Principes religionis curam suscipere debent. Exempla:Dauid, 2 Sam.6.2.& 72. Iosaphat,2 Par.17.7. 19.3.Ezechias,29.5. Iosia,34.8. (Vide MAGISTRATUS & eorum officia.) Reges mortalis suae conditionis monefieri debent, Psalm.82.7. Reges ac Principes non facile cedunt. Exempla: Dauid 2 Sam.19.29.1 Paral.21. Roboam,2 Paral 10.8.Asa.16.10. Amasias,25.16. Ozias,26.19.Iosias,35.22.Sedechias,36.v.12.13. Ioacim, Iere.36. Herodes, Mar.6.17. Reges interdum clientum suorum metu indigna committunt. Exempla: Darius,Dan.6. Reges ob populi peccata mutantur,Prou.28.2. reges qui facere quidve fugere debeant,Deut.17.19.1 Sam.8.1.&c. regum 2.2.&c.&10.9.2 Paral.9.1.&19.5.Iob.34.30. Psal.10.&40. 10. & 101. &c. Prou.14.28. & 19.12. & 20.v.8.26. & 28.15. & 29.v.4.14. & 31.4. Sap.6.9. Ierem.22.2.3. (V. Magistra- tvvm officia.)
units.tr: Kings and princes ought to take up the care of religion. Examples: David, 2 Sam. 6.2; 7.2; Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 17.7; 19.3; Hezekiah, 29.5; Josiah, 34.8. (See MAGISTRATE and the duties of magistrates.) Kings ought to be reminded of their mortal condition, Ps. 82.7. Kings and princes do not readily yield. Examples: David, 2 Sam. 19.29; 1 Chron. 21; Rehoboam, 2 Chron. 10.8; Asa, 16.10; Amaziah, 25.16; Uzziah, 26.19; Josiah, 35.22; Zedekiah, 36.12, 13; Jehoiakim, Jer. 36; Herod, Mark 6.17. Kings sometimes commit unworthy acts out of fear of their own clients. Examples: Darius, Dan. 6. Kings are changed on account of the sins of the people, Prov. 28.2. Which things kings ought to do or avoid: Deut. 17.19; 1 Sam. 8.1, etc.; 2 Kings 2.2, etc.; 10.9; 2 Chron. 9.1; 19.5; Job 34.30; Ps. 10; 40; 101, etc.; Prov. 14.28; 19.12; 20.8, 26; 28.15; 29.4, 14; 31.4; Wis. 6.9; Jer. 22.2, 3. (See the duties of magistrates.)

units.la: EGVM corda inscrutabilia, Prou.25.3. Regum & bonorum Principum officia, 1 Reg.2.3. Ps.2.v.10.11. Prou.20.v.26.28. Esa.49.23. Regum salus & victoria à Deo Ps. 144. 16. Regum ac Principum vitia non sunt dissimulanda. Exempla: Elias, 1 Reg.18.18. Elisæus, 2 Reg.3.13. Ioannes Baptista, Matth. 14.v.3.4. (V. Principum vitia non dissimulanda: & Prophetae.)
units.tr: The hearts of kings are unsearchable, Prov. 25.3. The duties of kings and of good princes: 1 Kings 2.3; Ps. 2.10, 11; Prov. 20.26, 28; Isa. 49.23. The safety and victory of kings are from God, Ps. 144.16. The vices of kings and princes are not to be concealed. Examples: Elijah, 1 Kings 18.18; Elisha, 2 Kings 3.13; John the Baptist, Matt. 14.3, 4. (See The vices of princes are not to be concealed; and the Prophets.)

units.la: IGIBVS quod debetur reddendum, Matth.22.21. Rom. 13.7. Regibus & Principibus Deorum nomen attribuitur, Ps.82.6. Ioan.10.v.34.35. Primo, eò quòd iudicia Dei exerceant inter homines, 2 Paral.19.6. hoc est ratione officij, bona & iusta promouendo, mala puniendo & tollendo. Ideóque naturam Dei imitari debent, qui Magos & Ariolos, Leuit.20.6. Deut.18.10. Blasphemos, Leuit.24.v.16. inducentes ad idolol. Deut.13.v.9.10. Parentibus honorem non deferentes, Leuit.20.9. illegitimi concubitus reos, v.11.12.13.14. &c. & alios insigni facinore pollutos, vt sunt Idololatræ, Exod.22.20. Deut.17.ver.5.6.7. & similes, solli è medio, & capitali supplicio affici iubet. Secundo, Dij dicuntur, quia notas aliquas sui Spiritus Deus iis impri- mit, id est, dona quædam pene diuina illis communi- cat, vt patet ex Num.11.17. 1 Sam.16.v.13.14. Dauid etiam petit se Spiritu principali confirmari, Psalm.51.14. Zoro- abalis quoque Spiritum à Deo excitatum legimus, Hagg. 1.14. Etsi autem non semper nec omnes Principes & Reges regenerat Spiritus, tamen aliqua etiam excellentia Spiritus Dei dona in Ethnicis reperiuntur, su- ra aliorum hominum sortem, quamobrem Dij vocentur. Finem, in quem constituti sunt Reges & Magistratus, exprimit Paulus, 1 Tim. 2.2. pro Regibus oran- um, ibid.
units.tr: Honour is to be rendered to whom it is due, Matt. 22.21; Rom. 13.7. The name of gods is attributed to kings and princes, Ps. 82.6; John 10.34, 35. First, because they exercise the judgements of God among men, 2 Chron. 19.6; that is, by reason of their office, promoting good and just things, punishing and removing evil ones. Therefore they ought to imitate the nature of God, who orders that magicians and soothsayers, Lev. 20.6; Deut. 18.10, blasphemers, Lev. 24.16, those who induce to idolatry, Deut. 13.9, 10, those who do not render honour to parents, Lev. 20.9, those guilty of illegitimate intercourse, vv. 11–14, etc., and others defiled by notable crimes, such as idolaters, Exod. 22.20; Deut. 17.5–7, and similar persons, be cut off from the midst and put to capital punishment. Second, they are called gods because God imprints certain marks of his Spirit upon them, that is, he imparts to them certain almost divine gifts, as is clear from Num. 11.17; 1 Sam. 16.13, 14. David also asks to be confirmed by a princely Spirit, Ps. 51.14. We also read that Zerubbabel was stirred up by the Spirit of God, Hag. 1.14. Although the Spirit does not always, nor in all, regenerate princes and kings, yet even among the heathen some excellent gifts of the Spirit of God are found, above the lot of other men, and for this reason they are called gods. Paul expresses the end for which kings and magistrates are appointed: 1 Tim. 2.2, prayer for kings, etc., in the same place.

units.la: temptum ita nominatus sæpe apud Euangelistas; Matt. 2. & 27. 11. &c. Ioan. 1.49. & 19.3. &c. Act. 17.7.
units.tr: tempt, so named often by the Evangelists: Matt. 2; 27.11, etc.; John 1.49; 19.3, etc.; Acts 17.7.]

units.la: Rex interitus, seu terrorum, 1. mortis, Iob. 18.14.
units.tr: King of destruction, or of terrors, that is, of death, Job 18.14.

units.la: Rex filiorum superbiæ, 1. ferarum, Leuiathan, Iob 41.25.
units.tr: King of the children of pride, that is, of wild beasts: Leviathan, Job 41.25.

units.la: Rex locustarum mysticarum; Apoc. 9.11. Apollyon.
units.tr: King of the mystical locusts, Rev. 9.11: Apollyon.

units.la: RHAMNI arboris parabola, Iudic. 9. v. 8.14. seu Oliuæ.
units.tr: Parable of the bramble tree, Judg. 9.8, 14, or of the olive.

units.la: RHINOCEROS: eius natura describitur, Iob 39. v. 12.13.
units.tr: RHINOCEROS: its nature is described, Job 39.12, 13.

units.la: RHODE famula, Ecclesiæ clandestino conuentui intey est, Act. 12.13. RHODVS: insula in Lycio mari. Act. 21.1.
units.tr: RHODA, a maidservant, is the clandestine assembly of the Church, Acts 12.13. RHODES: an island in the Lycian sea, Acts 21.1.

units.la: RISVS, pro deliciis, Iac. 4. 9. risus impiorum maledictus, Iob 6.25. risus Saræ votiosus, Gen. 18.13. Abrahæ, 17.17.
units.tr: LAUGHTER, for pleasures, James 4.9. The laughter of the wicked is cursed, Job 6.25. The laughter of Sarah was doubtful, Gen. 18.13; of Abraham, 17.17.

units.la: RIGAVIT Apollos, 1 Cor. 3.6. Qui rigat nihil est. v.7.
units.tr: Apollos watered, 1 Cor. 3.6. He who waters is nothing, v. 7.

units.la: RIMNON idolum, Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: RIMMON, an idol: see the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: RIXAE damnantur, Vide DISCORDIA: opus carnis sunt, Gal. 5.20. de rixarum suscitatione, Pro. 10.12. & 15.18. & 17.19. 18.6. & 23.29. & 26.17. & 29.22. de Rixantibus lex, Exod. 18. &c. V. Lites.
units.tr: QUARRELS are condemned: see DISCORD. They are works of the flesh, Gal. 5.20. On stirring up quarrels: Prov. 10.12; 15.18; 17.19; 18.6; 23.29; 26.17; 29.22. The law concerning those who quarrel: Exod. 18, etc. See LAWSUITS.

units.la: ROBOAM, filius Salomonis, rex Iuda & Israelis, 1 Reg. 11.4 dura populo respondet, 12.13. Regno Israelis priuatur v.20. 2 Paral. 10.19. præcipit ei Deus, ne pugnet contra Israel, 11.2. urbes munitas in Iuda ædificat, v.5. Legem Dei obliuiscitur, ut & Israel, 12.1. oppugnatur à Sesac rege Ægypti, vers. 2.9. meticulosus est, 13.7. moritur, 1 Reg. 14. 31. regnat Abiam filius eius pro eo, 15.1. (Rehabeam. i. dilatatio populi.)
units.tr: REHOBOAM, son of Solomon, king of Judah and Israel, answers the people harshly, 1 Kings 12.13; he is deprived of the kingdom of Israel, v. 20; 2 Chron. 10.19; God commands him not to fight against Israel, 11.2; he builds fortified cities in Judah, v. 5; he forgets the law of God, as does Israel, 12.1; he is attacked by Shishak king of Egypt, vv. 2, 9; he is timid, 13.7; he dies, 1 Kings 14.31; his son Abijah reigns in his place, 15.1. (Rehoboam, i.e. enlargement of the people.)

units.la: ROBORATVR homo, sed non in fortitudine sua, 1 Sam. 2. V. Iosue. 1.6. Prou. 12.3. Isa. 35.3. Ier. 9.23.
units.tr: A man is strengthened, but not in his own strength, 1 Sam. 2. See Josh. 1.6; Prov. 12.3; Isa. 35.3; Jer. 9.23.

units.la: ROBVSTORVM exempla: Nemrod, Gen. 10.9. Moabitæ, Iudic. 3.29. Samson, 14. v.5.6. Israelitæ & Beniamitæ, 20.4.
units.tr: Examples of the strong: Nimrod, Gen. 10.9; the Moabites, Judg. 3.29; Samson, 14.5, 6; the Israelites and the Benjaminites, 20.4.

units.la: Cis pater Saulis, 1 Sam. 9.1. Dauid, 16.18. & 17. ver. 34.35.36.37. Cusçai 2 Sam. 16.18. Goliath, 1 Sam. 17. v.4.5 &c. Abisai 2 Sam. 23.18.1 Paral. 11.20. Ioiada & Bananias, 2 Sam. 23.20.22.1 Par. 11.22. Filij Vlam, 1 Par. 8.40. & 9.13. Iesbaam 11.11 Eleazar, v.12. Viri de Gadditis 12.8 Filij Mesclemi 26.9. Robusti Ierusalem, 2 Paral. 17. v.13.14. Robusti Israel, 25 6. V. FORTES Dauidis.
units.tr: Kish, father of Saul, 1 Sam. 9.1; David, 16.18; 17.34–37; Cushai, 2 Sam. 16.18; Goliath, 1 Sam. 17.4, 5, etc.; Abishai, 2 Sam. 23.18; 1 Chron. 11.20; Jehoiada and Benaiah, 2 Sam. 23.20, 22; 1 Chron. 11.22; the sons of Ulam, 1 Chron. 8.40; 9.13; Ishbaal, 11.11; Eleazar, v. 12; the men of Gad, 12.8; the sons of Meshelemiah, 26.9; the mighty men of Jerusalem, 2 Chron. 17.13, 14; the mighty men of Israel, 25.6. See the STRONG MEN of David.

units.la: ROMA, concubina Nachor, Gen. 22.24. (i. sublimis)
units.tr: ROMA, concubine of Nahor, Gen. 22.24. (i.e. lofty)

units.la: ROMA, vrbs olim propemodum totius orbis domina. Rom. 1.8. (i. robusta.) ROMANVM ciuem se dic Paulus, Actor.16.37. & 22.25. Vide PAVLVS Romam appellit, 28.16. Romanorum Christia-norum laus, Rom.1.8. Romanos destructuros Ierusa-lem & Templum Domini praedicitur, Num.24.24. Esa.5.26. & 6.11. Dan.9.26. & 11.v.30.31. Luc.19.41.&21.20. Ioann.11.48. Romani neminem indicta causa condem-nabant, Actor.25.16. Romanos timebant Iudaei, Ioan.11.48. Paulus dicitur de Christo testaturus Rom. Act.23.11.&28.30.
units.tr: ROME, a city once almost the mistress of the whole world, Rom. 1.8. (i.e. strong.) Paul declares himself a Roman citizen, Acts 16.37; 22.25. See PAUL. Paul comes to Rome, Acts 28.16. The praise of the Christians at Rome, Rom. 1.8. It is foretold that the Romans will destroy Jerusalem and the Temple of the Lord, Num. 24.24; Isa. 5.26; 6.11; Dan. 9.26; 11.30, 31; Luke 19.41; 21.20; John 11.48. The Romans condemned no one without a hearing of the case, Acts 25.16. The Jews feared the Romans, John 11.48. Paul is said to bear witness of Christ at Rome, Acts 23.11; 28.30.

units.la: ROS in solitudine, qui & man, Exod.16.13. ros & pluuia non data est tribus annis tempore Achab, 1 Regum 17.1 Roris, imbri, nivi, & pluuiae comparatur Dei verbum, Esa.55.10. Vide Deuteron.32.2. Ioseph rore benedicendus, 33.v.13.
units.tr: DEW in the wilderness, which is also manna, Exod. 16.13. Dew and rain were not given for three years in the time of Ahab, 1 Kings 17.1. The word of God is compared to dew, rain, snow and showers, Isa. 55.10. See Deut. 32.2. Joseph is to be blessed with dew, Deut. 33.13.

units.la: ROTA, Orbis, Aëris media regio Psalm.77.19. Rota, aliquid admodum volubile, consistere nesciens, si vel tantillum impellatur, Psalm.83.14. Rota in corpore humano figura-tè sumitur pro perpetua illa vaporum ex pectore & venriculo sursum ascendentium, & ex cerebro in partes in-seriores quasi cisternam descendentium rotatione, Eccle.2.6. Rota nativitatis, curriculum vitae nobis praescriptum, Iacob.3.6.]
units.tr: WHEEL: the orb, the middle region of the air, Ps. 77.19. A wheel, something very rolling, unable to stand still if it is pushed even a little, Ps. 83.14. In the human body the wheel is taken figuratively for that perpetual rotation of vapours rising upward from the chest and stomach, and descending from the brain into the inner parts as into a cistern, Eccles. 2.6. The wheel of birth is the course of life prescribed to us, James 3.6.]

units.la: RVBARVM visio, Ezech.10.v.2.6.9.10.12.
units.tr: The vision of the wheels, Ezek. 10.2, 6, 9, 10, 12.

units.la: RVBEN (id est, filius videntis afflictionem) Iacobi ex Lea filius, nascitur, Gen 29.32. ratio appellationis, ibid. patris ubile polluit, 35.22. & 49.4. dantur ob id primogenita eius filiis Ioseph. 1 Paralipom. 51. eius benedictio, Deuteronom.33.6. nititur fratrem suum Ioseph liberare, Genef.37.vers.21.22.29. Beniaminem ut in AEgyptum a-portare liceat, contendit apud patrem, 42.27. Filius Ru-ben primo requies datur, Numer.32.1. &c. Deuteron. 12.&29.8. Iosue.1 vers.12. & 13.23. caeduntur, 2 Regum. 33. transferuntur ad terram Assyriorum, 15.39.1 Paral.5. secundum prophetiam, Genesis 49.4. aedificat Altare, Iosu.22.10. dimicaverunt contra Agarenos, 1 Paral.5.19. innuente Deo precibus eorum. v.20.
units.tr: Reuben (that is, a son who sees affliction), son of Jacob by Leah, is born, Gen. 29.32. The reason for the name is given there. He defiled his father's bed, 35.22, and 49.4. Because of this his firstborn rights were given to the sons of Joseph, 1 Chron. 5.1. His blessing is in Deut. 33.6. He tries to free his brother Joseph, Gen. 37.21, 22, 29. He presses his father to let Benjamin go to Egypt, 42.27. The son of Reuben is first given rest, Num. 32.1, etc.; Deut. 12 and 29.8; Josh. 1.12 and 13.23. They are slain, 2 Kings 33. They are carried off to the land of the Assyrians, 15.39; 1 Chron. 5. This is according to the prophecy in Gen. 49.4. He builds an altar, Josh. 22.10. They fought against the Hagarites, 1 Chron. 5.19, God answering their prayers, v. 20.

units.la: IVS ardens, qui non consumebatur: Exo.3.2. Deut.33.16. Mar.12.26. Luc.20.37. Act.7.30.
units.tr: The fire that burned and was not consumed: Exod. 3.2; Deut. 33.16; Mark 12.26; Luke 20.37; Acts 7.30.

units.la: RUINAM praecedit exaltatio, Prou.18.12. in ruinam reliquit eus Iudaeis Chananeos, Iudic.2.3. ruituros multos Iu-deos praedicit Simeon, Luc.2.34. Qualis ruina contemto-rum Legis: Deut.28.48.
units.tr: Ruin is preceded by exaltation, Prov. 18.12. He left the Canaanites to the Jews for their ruin, Judg. 2.3. Simeon foretells that many Jews will fall, Luke 2.34. Such is the ruin of those who despise the Law: Deut. 28.48.

units.la: RVMOR falsus. Exempla: De Filiorum Dauidis strage, 2 Sa.1 30.de corpore Christi surrepto, Matth. 28.13. &c. de Ioan ne non morituro, Ioan. 21.23.
units.tr: A false rumour. Examples: the slaughter of David's sons, 2 Sam. 1.30; the stolen body of Christ, Matt. 28.13, etc.; concerning John, that he would not die, John 21.23.

units.la: RVTH Moabitis, nurus Noemi, Ruth 1.4 veram religione deserere nō vult, v.16. spicas in agro Booz legit, 2.3. Booz grata & accepta est, v.13. sex hordei modios ad socrum defert, 3.16. Booz nubit, 4.13. 11. Paral. 2.12. Matth. 1.5. concepit, & parit Obed, Ruth. 4.13.17. qui fuit pater Iesai, patris Dauidis, ibid. (i. irrigata.)
units.tr: Ruth the Moabitess, daughter-in-law of Naomi, does not want to abandon the true religion, v. 16. She gathers ears of corn in the field of Boaz, 2.3. Boaz is pleased with her and receives her, v. 13. She carries six measures of barley to her mother-in-law, 3.16. Boaz marries her, 4.13; 1 Chron. 2.12; Matt. 1.5. She conceives and bears Obed, Ruth 4.13, 17, who was the father of Jesse, the father of David, ibid. (that is, watered).

units.tr: S.

units.la: ABA Regina inuisit Salomonem, 1 Reg. 10.1. Matt. 12.42. (i. ebrietas.) [Saba siue Sceba regio Arabiæ Iob. 19. Ps. 72. 10. Esai. 60.6. Sabæi populi Arabiæ, Iob. 1.15.
units.tr: The queen of Sheba visited Solomon, 1 Kings 10.1; Matt. 12.42. (That is, drunkenness.) [Sheba or Seba, a region of Arabia, Job 1.15; Ps. 72.10; Isa. 60.6, the Sabeans, a people of Arabia, Job 1.15.

units.la: SABAOTH, epitheton Dei, [qui Deus exercituum appellatur Iere. 11.20.] Rom. 9.29. Iac. 5.4. significans idem quod Exercituum, quo epitheto summa Deo potentia attribuitur.
units.tr: SABAOTH, an epithet of God, [who is called the God of hosts, Jer. 11.20.] Rom. 9.29; James 5.4. It signifies the same as "of hosts", an epithet by which supreme power is attributed to God.

units.la: SABBATHVM à Deo benedicitur, Genes. 2.3. propter hominem constitutum est, Mar. 2.27. Sabbathum perpetuum Esa. 66.23. Heb. 4.9. Sabbathum terræ septimo quoque anno, Exo. 23.11. Leuit. 25.4. Sabbathum alterum primum pro festi plurium dierum vltimo, Lucæ 6.1. Sabbathi observatio præcipitur, Exo. 16.29. & 20.v.8.9. & 23.12. & 31.14.16. & 34.21. & 35.2. Leuit. 19.v.3.30. & 23.3. & 26.2. Deut. 5.12. Esa. 56.2. & 58.13. Ierem. 17.21. Ezec. 20.20. (i. Quies et vacatio.)
units.tr: The Sabbath was blessed by God, Gen. 2.3. It was instituted for the sake of man, Mark 2.27. A perpetual Sabbath, Isa. 66.23; Heb. 4.9. A Sabbath for the land every seventh year, Exod. 23.11; Lev. 25.4. The first Sabbath, and the second, for the last of several festival days, Luke 6.1. The observance of the Sabbath is commanded, Exod. 16.29; 20.8, 9; 23.12; 31.14, 16; 34.21; 35.2; Lev. 19.3, 30; 23.3; 26.2; Deut. 5.12; Isa. 56.2; 58.13; Jer. 17.21; Ezek. 20.20. (That is, rest and cessation.)

units.la: Causæ præcipuæ sanctificationis Sabbathi sunt quatuor. Prima, vt dies ille impendatur cultui diuino, quo die potissimum solebant agi conuentus publici, Lucæ 4.16 quæ consuetudo agendi conuentus, in diem Dominicum translata est, vt colligitur ex Actor. 20.7. 1 Corinth. 16. Vide DIES Dominicus. Secunda, vt ne continuis laboribus te aut tuos fatiges, & conficias, Exod. 23.12. Deut. 5.14. Tertia, vt perpetuo recorderis operum Dei creationis, Gen. 2.v.1.2. Exod. 20.v.10.11. Vltima causa est, perpetua memoria liberationis à seruitute Ægyptiaca, Deut. 5.
units.tr: There are four chief causes for sanctifying the Sabbath. The first is that the day be devoted to divine worship; on that day especially public assemblies used to be held, Luke 4.16. This custom of holding assemblies was transferred to the Lord's day, as is gathered from Acts 20.7 and 1 Cor. 16. See LORD'S DAY. The second is that you should not wear yourself or yours out with continual labours, Exod. 23.12; Deut. 5.14. The third is that you should constantly remember the works of God's creation, Gen. 2.1, 2; Exod. 20.10, 11. The last cause is the perpetual memory of liberation from Egyptian bondage, Deut. 5.

units.la: Deut. 5. 15. Addi his potest & liberalitas Dei in sexto, & cessatio Man in septimo die, quam causam attingit Moses, Exod. 16.29. Sabbathi obseruatio, quod ad sabbathi diem, & ritus legales, fuit ceremoniale: quod ad Dei cultum attinet, est legis moralis, immotæ, & in hac vita perpetuæ præceptum: & stetit ille sabbathi dies à creatione mundi ad Domini resurrectionem, propter cuius memoriam & alias nonnullas causas longè grauissimas in diem Dominicum transfertur, Apo. 1. 10. Vide Deus Dominicus. Sabbathi obseruati exempla: Israelitæ, Exod. 16.30. Christus studiosè coluit sabbathum, ita vt plerunque sabbatho in synagogis doceret, & miraculis se patefaceret, Luc. 4. v. 16. 17. &c. Paulus & Barnabas, Acto. 13. v. 14. 15. 42. & 16. 13. Paulus & Silas, 20. 7. Sabbathi violationis, siue profanationis, eiusque pœnæ exempla: Homo colligens ligna, Numer. 15. 32. &c. Israelitæ, Nehem. 13. 15. &c. Ierem. 17. 27. Sabbathi Dominus Christus, Marc. 2. 28. hoc est, in sua potestate habet sabbathum, vt possit pro suo imperio moderari. Sabbathum magnum vocabatur Iudæis, Ioann. 19. 31. cum in sabbathum dies Paschæ incideret: hoc est, valde solenne & celebre: concurrente videlicet duplici celebritate. Sabbathum profanare dicuntur Sacerdotes, Matth. 12. 5. non ipsorum, sed Legis sabbathi respectu, si absque exceptione accipiatur, vt Pharisæi velle videbantur, qui nempe Christi opera à quotidianis quorumuis, neque Christum à communi hominum sorte discernebant. Sabbathi sacrificia, Ezech. 46. 4.
units.tr: Deut. 5.15. To these may be added God's generosity on the sixth day and the cessation of the manna on the seventh day, which Moses touches on, Exod. 16.29. The observance of the Sabbath day, and the legal rites that go with it, was ceremonial; as far as the worship of God is concerned, it belongs to the moral law, a precept unchanging and perpetual in this life. That Sabbath day stood from the creation of the world until the Lord's resurrection, and because of its memory and some other far weightier causes it was transferred to the Lord's day, Rev. 1.10. See LORD'S DAY. Examples of observing the Sabbath: the Israelites, Exod. 16.30. Christ diligently kept the Sabbath, so that for the most part on the Sabbath he taught in the synagogues and revealed himself by miracles, Luke 4.16, 17, etc. Paul and Barnabas, Acts 13.14, 15, 42; and 16.13. Paul and Silas, 20.7. Examples of violation or profanation of the Sabbath, and its punishment: a man gathering sticks, Num. 15.32, etc.; the Israelites, Neh. 13.15, etc.; Jer. 17.27. The Lord Christ is Lord of the Sabbath, Mark 2.28; that is, he has the Sabbath in his power, so that he may regulate it by his own authority. The Jews called the Sabbath "great", John 19.31, when the day of the Passover fell on the Sabbath; that is, very solemn and celebrated, the two celebrations coinciding. Priests are said to profane the Sabbath, Matt. 12.5; not with respect to themselves, but with respect to the Sabbath law, if it is taken without exception, as the Pharisees seemed to want, who did not distinguish Christ's works from those of anyone else, nor Christ from the common lot of men. Sabbath sacrifices, Ezek. 46.4.

units.la: SABBATHA, non pro septimo die, vt alias sæpe, nec pro singulis hebdomadis diebus, quos vulgò Ferias vocant, sed potius pro ipsis septimanis, Leuit. 25. 8. & pro septimana ipsa, Mat. 28. 1. per synecdochen.
units.tr: SABBATHS: not for the seventh day, as often elsewhere, nor for the single days of the week, which are commonly called weekdays, but rather for the weeks themselves, Lev. 25.8, and for the week itself, Matt. 28.1, by synecdoche.

units.la: Sabbathismus, Heb. 4. 9 sempiternus seu vita æt. Isai. 66. 22.
units.tr: Sabbatism, Heb. 4.9: everlasting, or eternal life, Isa. 66.22.

units.la: Sabbathizare Exo. 16. 30 Leui. 25. 2. & 26. 34.]
units.tr: To keep the Sabbath, Exod. 16.30; Lev. 25.2; and 26.34.]

units.la: Sacculus, i. crumena, loculus, mantica, pera, Prou. 7. 20. Esai. 46. 6. Luc. 10. 4. & 12. 33. & 22. v. 35. 36.]
units.tr: A little bag, that is, a purse, pouch, wallet or scrip, Prov. 7.20; Isa. 46.6; Luke 10.4; 12.33; 22.35, 36.]

units.la: SACCVS: eius in pœnitentiæ & humilitatis signum, vsus, Ioel. 1. ver. 8. 13. Saccis indutorum, lugentium, & pœnitentium exempla: Iacob, Genef. 37. 34. Israelitæ, Exod. 33. 4. Dauid cum populo, 2 Sam. 3. 31. Syrij, 1 Reg. 20. 32. Achab, 21. 27. Ezechias, 2 Reg. 19. 1. Esa. 37. 1. Iob, Iob. 16. ver. 15. 16. Dauid, Psalm. 35. ver. 13. 14. & 69. ver. 11, 12. Israelitæ, Nehem.
units.tr: SACKCLOTH: its use as a sign of penitence and humility, Joel 1.8, 13. Examples of those clothed in sackcloth, mourning and penitent: Jacob, Gen. 37.34; the Israelites, Exod. 33.4; David with the people, 2 Sam. 3.31; the Syrians, 1 Kings 20.32; Ahab, 21.27; Hezekiah, 2 Kings 19.1; Isa. 37.1; Job, Job 16.15, 16; David, Ps. 35.13, 14, and 69.11, 12; the Israelites, Neh.

units.la: 9.1. Mardochæus & Iudæi, Esth.4. v.1.2.3.4. Esther, v.16. Daniel, Dan.9.3. Iuda, Ioel.1.8.12.13. Ninivitæ, & Rex Ninivitæ, Ion.3.5. duo Testes, Apocal.11.3. Saccus in lumbis, Reg.20.31.&21.27.
units.tr: 9.1. Mordecai and the Jews, Esth. 4.1, 2, 3, 4; Esther, v. 16; Daniel, Dan. 9.3; Judah, Joel 1.8, 12, 13; the Ninevites and the king of Nineveh, Jonah 3.5; the two witnesses, Rev. 11.3. Sackcloth on the loins, 1 Kings 20.31, and 21.27.

units.la: SACERDOS pro se & populo orat, Leuitic.9.7.&16.6.17.18. à mortuorum exequiis abstinet, 21.1. barbam non radit, ver.5. Virginem vxorem ducit, v.13. Ezech.44.22. Sacerdos noster Christus, Hebr.5.6.&7.1.&c. Vide CHRISTVS.
units.tr: The priest prays for himself and for the people, Lev. 9.7; 16.6, 17, 18; he abstains from the funeral rites of the dead, 21.1; he does not shave his beard, v. 5; he takes a virgin as his wife, v. 13; Ezek. 44.22. Our priest is Christ, Heb. 5.6; 7.1, etc. See CHRIST.

units.la: SACERDOTIS ad populum præliaturum exhortatio, Deuteron.20. verfic.2.3. Sacerdotis filia fornicans, comburenda, Leuitic.21.9. Sacerdotis peccatum, quomodo expiandum, Sadum, 4 3.
units.tr: The priest's exhortation to the people about to go to battle, Deut. 20.2, 3. A priest's daughter who commits fornication is to be burned, Lev. 21.9. How a priest's sin is to be expiated: Sadum, 4.3.

units.la: SACERDOTI rebellis, morte plectendus, Deut.17.12. Sacerdoti, antequam Sanctuarium ingrediatur, observanda, Leuit.16.v.2 3.
units.tr: A priest who rebels is to be punished with death, Deut. 17.12. What is to be observed by a priest before he enters the sanctuary, Lev. 16.2, 3.

units.la: SACERDOTES oblationis reliquias comedunt, Leuiti.10.12. Sacerdotes quando à vino abstineant, verfic.8.9. Ezech.44.20. Sacerdotes mali arguuntur, 22.26. Oseæ 5. Soph.3.4. Malach.1.6. &2.1. Sacerdotes mali, & eorum punitio, Numer.16.1.&c. 1 Samuel 2.22. &c. 3.13.1 Reg.2 26. Esaiæ 1 11.&28 7. Ierem.2.8.&8.10. Ose.4.6. Malach.2 ver.1.8. 1 Machab.7. verfic.5.9. Sacerdotes multi Christi credunt, Act 6.7. Sacerdotes veritatis hostes, 4.1.6. Sacerdotes & Principes Sacerdotum qui dicti fuerint, Vide PRINCIPES Sacerdotum. Sacerdotes & Prophetæ, interdum vi corporali exercuerunt vindictam in sceleratos. Vide VINDICTA. Sacerdotes Baal occiduntur, 1 Regum 18.40. 2 Regum 10.18.19.&23.5. Sacerdotum avaritia, Malach.1.10. Autoritas, Deuteron.17.9. in populum benedictio, Numer.6.24. eius efficacia, Genes.14.19. Num. 6.26.
units.tr: Priests eat the remains of the offering, Lev. 10.12. When priests abstain from wine, v. 8, 9; Ezek. 44.20. Evil priests are rebuked, 22.26; Hos. 5; Zeph. 3.4; Mal. 1.6 and 2.1. Evil priests and their punishment: Num. 16.1, etc.; 1 Sam. 2.22, etc.; 3.13; 1 Kings 2.26; Isa. 1.11 and 28.7; Jer. 2.8 and 8.10; Hos. 4.6; Mal. 2.1, 8; 1 Macc. 7.5, 9. Many priests believed in Christ, Acts 6.7. Priests were enemies of the truth, 4.1, 6. For the priests and chief priests so named, see CHIEF PRIESTS. Priests and prophets sometimes carried out vengeance on the wicked by bodily force. See VENGEANCE. The priests of Baal are slain, 1 Kings 18.40; 2 Kings 10.18, 19, and 23.5. The covetousness of priests, Mal. 1.10. Their authority, Deut. 17.9. The blessing upon the people, Num. 6.24; its efficacy, Gen. 14.19; Num. 6.26.

units.la: Sacerdotum benedictionis exempla: Heli, 1 Sam.2.20. Sacerdotum Regis Ezechiæ, 2 Paralip.30.27. Sacerdotum consecratio, Exod.28.41.&29 1. coquinæ, Ezech.46.20. Hæreditas Deus ipse, Deuteron.18.2. Vide LEVITAE. Ignorantia, Ezech.22.26. inuidia, Matth.27.18. multitudo & numerus in veteri Testamento. 1 Paral.23.3. vbi numerantur 38000. officium, Exo.29.44.&30.7. Leu.10. v.1.6.9.10. &21.1.&c.22.1.&c.24.3. Num.3.10.&4.v.5.21.&10.8.&18. v.1.7. Deut.20.2 & 21.5.1 Sam.2.v.28 35. 1 Par.6.49.2. Para. 26.17. Ezech.44.20.23. Malach.2.verf.4.7. Hebr.5.7.&10.1. ornamenta vestium & ordinatio, Ezod. 28.1. &c. 29.1. & 39.1.& 40.12. Leuitici 8.verf.8.terra eorum fame grassante minimè vendita, Genef.47.22.victus unde sumendus, Vide de PRIMITIAE. Sacerdotum defunctorum viduæ Sacerdotum vxores esse possunt, Ezech.44.22. non autem vlla repudiata, ibid.
units.tr: Examples of the priestly blessing: Eli, 1 Sam. 2.20; the priests of King Hezekiah, 2 Chron. 30.27. The consecration of priests, Exod. 28.41; 29.1. The kitchen, Ezek. 46.20. Their inheritance is God himself, Deut. 18.2. See LEVITES. Ignorance, Ezek. 22.26. Envy, Matt. 27.18. Multitude and number in the Old Testament, 1 Chron. 23.3, where 38,000 are numbered. Office, Exod. 29.44; 30.7; Lev. 10.1, 6, 9, 10; 21.1, etc.; 22.1, etc.; 24.3; Num. 3.10; 4.5, 21; 10.8; 18.1, 7; Deut. 20.2 and 21.5; 1 Sam. 2.28, 35; 1 Chron. 6.49; 2 Chron. 26.17; Ezek. 44.20, 23; Mal. 2.4, 7; Heb. 5.7; 10.1. The ornaments of their garments and their ordination, Exod. 28.1, etc.; 29.1; 39.1; 40.12; Lev. 8.8. Their land, when famine raged, was not sold at all, Gen. 47.22. For where their food was to be taken from, see FIRSTFRUITS. Widows of deceased priests may be wives of priests, Ezek. 44.22, but no divorced woman may be, ibid.

units.la: SACERDOTVM Leuiticorum & Christi discrimen, Heb.9.25. & 10.v.11.12.
units.tr: The difference between the Levitical priests and Christ, Heb. 9.25; 10.11, 12.

units.la: SACERDOTIBVS dabantur decimæ & primitiæ, Numer. 5.versi.9.10.& 18.versi.8.11. Deuteron.18.3 &c. vt liberi à solicitudine comparandi victum, possent vacare Legi Dei, 2 Paralip.31.verf.4.&c. Vide DECIMAE: & PRIMITIAE. Necessaria vitæ sustentatio iis assignabatur, Exod. 29.26. Levit.2.verf.3.10.& 5.13.& 6.verf.9.19.& 7.v 6 3.& 10.13.& 24.9. Numer.3.48.& 5.9.& 18.ver.8.11.28. Deuter. 18.1.1 Sam.2 28 2 Reg.12.16.1 Paral.6.54. 2 Paralip.31.4.2. Esdr.10.36. à Sacerdotibus Legem accipiat Rex, Deuter. 17.18.
units.tr: Tithes and firstfruits were given to the priests, Num. 5.9, 10; 18.8, 11; Deut. 18.3 etc., so that, free from the care of obtaining a living, they might have leisure for the Law of God, 2 Chron. 31.4 etc. See TITHES and FIRSTFRUITS. The necessities of life were assigned to them: Exod. 29.26; Lev. 2.3, 10; 5.13; 6.9, 19; 7.3, 6; 10.13; 24.9; Num. 3.48; 5.9; 18.8, 11, 28; Deut. 18.1; 1 Sam. 2.28; 2 Kings 12.16; 1 Chron. 6.54; 2 Chron. 31.4; Ezra 10.36. The king receives the Law from the priests, Deut. 17.18.

units.la: SACERDOTIVM Leuiticum abrogatū, Hebr.7.v.11.12. Christianum, quo spirituales hostiæ offeruntur per Christum, Esa.66.21. Rom.15.16. 1 Pet.2.5.
units.tr: The Levitical priesthood abrogated, Heb. 7.11, 12; the Christian priesthood, by which spiritual sacrifices are offered through Christ, Isa. 66.21; Rom. 15.16; 1 Pet. 2.5.

units.la: [Sacerdotium Christi, Hebr.7.24. Christiani, 1 Petr. 2.5.]
units.tr: [The priesthood of Christ, Heb. 7.24. The Christian priesthood, 1 Pet. 2.5.]

units.la: SACERDOS à nobis hoc ordine descriptus consideratur.
units.tr: The priest is considered here as described by us in the following order.

units.la: 1. Sacerdos ante legem datam & Leuitici ministerij institutionem, Genes.14.18. Psalm. 110. 4. Hebr. 7. versicul. 3.
units.tr: 1. The priest before the Law was given and the Levitical ministry instituted: Gen. 14.18; Ps. 110.4; Heb. 7.3.

units.la: 2. Sacerdotes sub lege vsque ad plenam Christi sub Evangelio manifestationem. Inter eos, ex tribu Leuitica, summus sacerdos, deinde alij Sacerdotes: quorum ille, Christum, inferiores, Ecclesiæ Christianæ pastores, deinde Christianos sacerdotes Spirituales figurabant.
units.tr: 2. The priests under the Law, until the full manifestation of Christ under the gospel. Among them, from the tribe of Levi, there was the high priest and then the other priests; of these, the high priest prefigured Christ, the lesser priests prefigured the ministers of the Christian Church, and then the Christian priests, the spiritual ones.

units.la: 3. Sacerdos summus, & Ecclesiæ Pontifex æternus Iesus Christus: cuius typi fuerant summi sacerdotes ante legem sub lege. Ps. 110.4. Zach.6.13. Hebr.5 6. & 7. v.3.11.15.17. 1.& 8.4.& 10 21.
units.tr: 3. The high priest and eternal Pontiff of the Church, Jesus Christ, whose types were the high priests before the Law and under the Law: Ps. 110.4; Zech. 6.13; Heb. 5.6; 7.3, 11, 15, 17; 1.8; 4; 10.21.

units.la: 4. Sacerdotes idolorum tum intra, tum extra Iudæam.
units.tr: 4. The priests of idols, both within Judaea and outside it.

units.la: 5. Sacerdotes qui victimas spirituales offerunt. Esai 1.6.& 66.21. Apo.1 6.& 5.10.& 20.6.1 Pet.2.5. Heb.13.5.
units.tr: 5. The priests who offer spiritual sacrifices: Isa. 1.6; 66.21; Rev. 1.6; 5.10; 20.6; 1 Pet. 2.5; Heb. 13.5.

units.la: 6. Sacerdotes, curatores rerum ad Ecclesiæ & politiæ conseruationem pertinentium, Gen.41.45.& 47.22. Exod. 16.& 3.1.& 18.1.]
units.tr: 6. The stewards of matters pertaining to the preservation of the Church and the commonwealth: Gen. 41.45; 47.22; Exod. 16; 31; 18.

units.la: SACERDOTALE Dei regnum, Israelitæ. Exod.19. 6. 1 Pet. 2.9.
units.tr: The kingdom of God as a priestly kingdom: the Israelites, Exod. 19.6; 1 Pet. 2.9.

units.la: SACRAMENTVM, est actio sacra, diuinitus instituta, in qua Deus, secundùm promissionem, gratiam suam in Christo, conueniente signorum & rerum significatarum analogia, obsignat, & nos mutuam erga ipsum fidem & pietatem testamur.
units.tr: A sacrament is a sacred action, divinely instituted, in which God, according to his promise, seals his grace in Christ, by a fitting analogy between the signs and the things signified, and we testify our mutual faith and piety towards him.

units.la: SACRAMENTA. Græcis μυστήρια dicta, Vide MYSTERIA à solis Pastoribus & Ecclesiæ ministris administranda. Matth. 28. 19. 1 Corin. 4. 1. à Christo separata, quid valeant. Hebr. 9. v. 9. 10. &c. Sacramenta & alia externa in Ecclesiis piis & impiis communia, 1 Cor. 11. v. 27. 29. exempla: Abraham & domestici, Genes. 17. 23. Sichem & Hemor, 34. 2. Absalom, Achitophel, & populus, 2 Sam. 15. 12. Iudas, Luc. 22. 21. Simon, Act. 8. 13. Sacramenta vetera typi fuerunt novorum, 1 Cor. 10. 16.
units.tr: Sacraments, called mysteries [μυστήρια] by the Greeks; see MYSTERIES. They are to be administered only by pastors and ministers of the Church: Matt. 28.19; 1 Cor. 4.1. What they are worth when separated from Christ: Heb. 9.9, 10, etc. Sacraments and other external things are common to the pious and the impious in the churches: 1 Cor. 11.27, 29. Examples: Abraham and his household, Gen. 17.23; Shechem and Hamor, Gen. 34.2; Absalom, Ahithophel, and the people, 2 Sam. 15.12; Judas, Luke 22.21; Simon, Acts 8.13. The old sacraments were types of the new: 1 Cor. 10.16.

units.la: SACRAMENTORVM partes, Vide BAPTISMVS, CIRCVNCISIO, COENA.
units.tr: The parts of the sacraments: see BAPTISM, CIRCUMCISION, SUPPER.

units.la: [Sacrarium, 1 Cor. 9. 13. scilicet templum, metonymice pro iis quæ in templo offeruntur.
units.tr: [Sanctuary, 1 Cor. 9.13, namely the temple, by metonymy for the things offered in the temple.]

units.la: SACRIFICANDI ritus, Leuit. 1. 2. Deo non vbique sacrificandum, Deut. 12. 5, 6.
units.tr: The rites of sacrificing: Lev. 1.2. God is not to be sacrificed to everywhere: Deut. 12.5, 6.

units.la: SACRIFICIVM quale esse debet, Exod. 29. 38. Leuit. 1. 3. & 1. & 22. v. 19 20. Numer. 28. 3. Deut. 15. 21. & 17. 1. Eccles. 35. 1. Ezec. 43. 23. Malach. 1. vers. 8. 14. Sacrificium matutinum vespertinum. Exod. 29. v. 38. 39. Num. 28. 4. Esdr. 3. 3. sacrificium pacificum, Leuitic. 3. 1. & 7. versic. 11. 12. 13. sacrificium pro peccato, Exod. 29 36. Leu. 7. 1. 2. &c. Num. 28. 22. Sacrificium quando spernat Deus, Psalm. 51. 18. sacrificium laudis Deo gratissimum, 50. 14. & 69. v. 31. 32. & 107. 22. Osee. 14. Heb. 13. 15. sacrificium verum & Deo acceptissimum, Prov. 21. 3. Mich. 6. v. 6. 7. 8. sacrificium fidelium, Rom. 12. 1. Phil. 2. 17. Hebr. 13. v. 15. 16. 1 Petr. 2. 5. sacrificium noui Testamenti, vt vocant, V. MISSA.
units.tr: What a sacrifice ought to be: Exod. 29.38; Lev. 1.3; 1; 22.19, 20; Num. 28.3; Deut. 15.21; 17.1; Eccl. 35.1; Ezek. 43.23; Mal. 1.8, 14. The morning and evening sacrifice: Exod. 29.38, 39; Num. 28.4; Ezra 3.3. The peace offering: Lev. 3.1; 7.11, 12, 13. The sin offering: Exod. 29.36; Lev. 7.1, 2, etc.; Num. 28.22. When God rejects a sacrifice: Ps. 51.18. The sacrifice of praise, most acceptable to God: Ps. 50.14; 69.31, 32; 107.22; Hos. 14; Heb. 13.15. The true sacrifice, most acceptable to God: Prov. 21.3; Mic. 6.6, 7, 8. The sacrifice of the faithful: Rom. 12.1; Phil. 2.17; Heb. 13.15, 16; 1 Pet. 2.5. The sacrifice of the New Testament, as they call it: see MASS.

units.la: SACRIFICII lex, Leuit. 6. 14, Deut. 18. 3.
units.tr: The law of sacrifice: Lev. 6.14; Deut. 18.3.

units.la: SACRIFICIO manus imponenda, Leuit. 1. 4. sacrificio misericordia potior, Osee. 6. 6. Matt. 9. 13. & 12. 7. sacrificio dilectio maior, Mar. 12. 33.
units.tr: Hands are to be laid on the sacrifice: Lev. 1.4. Mercy is preferable to sacrifice: Hos. 6.6; Matt. 9.13; 12.7. Love is greater than sacrifice: Mark 12.33.

units.la: SACRIFICIA ad quid instituta, Heb. 10. 3. sacrificia cum sale Leuitic. 2. 13. Marc. 9. 49. sacrificia priuata à Deo prohibita Leuiti. 17. v. 3. 4. sacrificia igni cœlesti consumta, Gen. 4. & 8. 20. & 15. 17. Leuit. 9. 24. Iudic. 6. 21. & 13. 19. 1 Reg. 18. 3.
units.tr: For what purpose sacrifices were instituted: Heb. 10.3. Sacrifices with salt: Lev. 2.13; Mark 9.49. Private sacrifices forbidden by God: Lev. 17.3, 4. Sacrifices consumed by heavenly fire: Gen. 4; 8.20; 15.17; Lev. 9.24; Judg. 6.21; 13.19; 1 Kings 18.38.

units.la: 1 Paralp.21 26. 2 Paralip. 7. 1. sacrificia quomodo à Deo respuantur, Psalm.40.7. & 50.versi.8.9. Esai.1.11. Ierem.7. 21.Malach.2.12.Matth.9.13.& 12.7.Hebr.10. ver.5.6.sacrificia carnalium subIannantur, Ose.5.6. sacrificia fidelium, Psalm.51.18.19.Malach.3.16. Iudæorum polluta, Agg.2.13. sacrificia quæ requirat Dominus, Mich.6.6. sacrificia veteris Legis reiicit Deus, Psalm.50.8. Ierem.6.20. Malach. 2.13. Sacrificia impiorum, Vide IMPIORVM sacrificia. Sacrificia expiatoria non habuerunt vim purificandi, alioquin desiissent offerri, Hebr.10.v,1.2. dicuntur tamen expiare, Leuit.16.30.non ipsorum symbolorum, sed vnicæ illius futuræ Christi oblationis respectu, quæ per illa quotannis, atq. adeò singulis diebus per omnes ceremonias adumbrabatur. Sacrificia, seu, vt Græci vocant, Θυσίας, qualia sacrificia vocent Iudæi, Vide HOLOCAVTOMATA.
units.tr: 1 Chron. 21.26; 2 Chron. 7.1. How sacrifices are rejected by God: Ps. 40.7; 50.8, 9; Isa. 1.11; Jer. 7.21; Mal. 2.12; Matt. 9.13; 12.7; Heb. 10.5, 6. The sacrifices of the carnal are overthrown: Hos. 5.6. The sacrifices of the faithful: Ps. 51.18, 19; Mal. 3.16. The sacrifices of the Jews are polluted: Hag. 2.13. The sacrifices which the Lord requires: Mic. 6.6. God rejects the sacrifices of the old Law: Ps. 50.8; Jer. 6.20; Mal. 2.13. The sacrifices of the wicked: see WICKED, sacrifices of. Expiatory sacrifices did not have the power to purify, otherwise they would have ceased to be offered: Heb. 10.1, 2. Yet they are said to expiate, Lev. 16.30, not with respect to the symbols themselves but with respect to that one future oblation of Christ, which was foreshadowed by them every year, and indeed every day through all the ceremonies. Sacrifices, or, as the Greeks call them, thusiai [Θυσίαι], which the Jews call by such names: see HOLOCAUSTS.

units.la: SACRIFICIORVM conuiuia cum gaudio celebrabantur, Vide OBLATIONES.
units.tr: The sacrificial feasts were celebrated with joy. See OBLATIONES.

units.la: SACRIFICIORVM & oblationum vocabula metaphoricè à Paulo vsurpata, significant ipsos fideles, Deo devotos, & quicquid est in fidelibus, vel proficiscitur à fidelibus, Deo gratum, & eorum fides ac bona opera, vt Roma.12.1.& 15. 16.Phil.2.17. & 4.18.1 Petri 2.5.
units.tr: Paul uses the words "sacrifice" and "offering" metaphorically to mean the faithful themselves, devoted to God, and whatever is in the faithful or comes from them that is pleasing to God, including their faith and good works: Rom. 12.1; 15.16; Phil. 2.17; 4.18; 1 Pet. 2.5.

units.la: SACRIFICIVM vnicum expiatorium, seu propitiatorium, quod Iesus Christus Ecclesiæ summus & æternus Sacerdos semel in area crucis pro peccatorum nostrorum satisfactione, & Electorum omnium redemptione Deo Patri obtulit.
units.tr: The one expiatory or propitiatory sacrifice is the one that Jesus Christ, the eternal High Priest of the Church, offered to God the Father once and for all on the altar of the cross, to satisfy for our sins and to redeem all the elect.

units.la: Typos habuit ante Legem & sub Lege
units.tr: It had types before the Law and under the Law.

units.la: Sacrificia omnia ab Adamo & posteris in Ecclesia veteri usque ad plenam Christi manifestationem sub Euangelio, per fidem oblata, nempe holocausta, sacrificia pro peccato & reatu, apud Mosem in Leuitico & Numeris descripta.
units.tr: All sacrifices offered in faith from Adam and his posterity in the old Church, until the full manifestation of Christ under the Gospel, namely the burnt offerings and the sacrifices for sin and guilt, are described by Moses in Leviticus and Numbers.

units.la: Eucharistica autem sacrificia sub lege tria fuerunt, nempe Mynha seu oblatio, Sacrificia pacifica, & laudis. Horum veritas, remotis ceremoniis legalibus, toti Ecclesiæ communis fuit, & erit ab initio usque ad finem mundi: & sub Euangelio sacrificia spiritualia, nempe laudis, fidei, confessionis, charitatis, commendantur. Hæc autem in reali & expiatorio Christi sacrificio sacrificantur, & Patri cælesti accepta sunt. }
units.tr: There were three eucharistic sacrifices under the Law: the meal offering (minhah), the peace offerings, and the offerings of praise. The truth of these, once the legal ceremonies are set aside, has been common to the whole Church, and will be from the beginning until the end of the world. Under the Gospel, spiritual sacrifices are commended: those of praise, faith, confession and charity. These are offered in the real and expiatory sacrifice of Christ, and are acceptable to the heavenly Father.

units.la: SACRILEGIVM, est earum rerum furtum, quæ diuinæ vo- cantur: non quòd hisce Deus egeat, sed ex víu & fine, ad quem destinatæ sunt, ad Dei videlicet cultum. Rom.2.22. Qui abominaris idola, sacrilegium admittis? Vide Ios.22. 16. Ananias & vxor eius Saphira partem pretij Domino consecrati interuertentes, animam efflarunt: Act.5.1.&c. Ephesi scriba negat Paulum & socios eius esse sacrilegos, 19.v.36.&c. Vide.1.Reg.14.25.&c.
units.tr: SACRILEGE is the theft of things that are called sacred. It is not that God needs them, but it is theft from the use and purpose for which they are destined, namely the worship of God. Rom. 2.22: "You who abhor idols, do you commit sacrilege?" See Josh. 22.16. Ananias and his wife Sapphira, by embezzling part of the price consecrated to the Lord, gave up the ghost: Acts 5.1 etc. At Ephesus the town clerk denies that Paul and his companions are sacrilegious: 19.36 etc. See 1 Kings 14.25 etc.

units.la: SADDVCAEI (secta inter Iudæos) ad Ioannem Baptistam venium, Mat.3.7. negant mortuorum resurrectionem, 22.23 Mar.12.18.Luc.20.27. Act.4.2.&23.8. veritatis hostes sunt, 5.17. Christum tentant, V. CHRISTVS tentatur à Saddu-cæis. (i. Iusti aut iustificati.)
units.tr: The SADDUCEES, a sect among the Jews, came to John the Baptist (Matt. 3.7). They deny the resurrection of the dead (Matt. 22.23; Mark 12.18; Luke 20.27; Acts 4.2; 23.8). They are enemies of the truth (Acts 5.17) and they tempt Christ. See CHRIST tempted by the Sadducees. (i.e. just or justified.)

units.la: SADDVCAEORVM exitialis doctrina, Mat.16.6. præcipua heresēon illorum capita, Act.23.8.
units.tr: The pernicious teaching of the Sadducees: Matt. 16.6. Their chief heresies: Acts 23.8.

units.la: SADOC sacerdos, 1 Rex.2.35. 1 Paral.29.22. afflictum. Dauidem sequitur, 2 Sam.15.24. (i. iustus aut iustificatus.)
units.tr: ZADOK the priest: 1 Kings 2.35; 1 Chron. 29.22. He was afflicted and followed David: 2 Sam. 15.24. (i.e. just or justified.)

units.la: [Sadoci alij plures, 2 Regum 15.33. 1 Paralipomen.12. 28.2 Paralipom.27.1 Nehem.3.versic.4.24. & 13.13. Matth. 1.14.]
units.tr: [Other Zadoks: 2 Kings 15.33; 1 Chron. 12.28; 2 Chron. 27.1; Neh. 3.4, 24; 13.13; Matt. 1.14.]

units.la: SAGA, i. aulæa Tabernaculi, Exodi 26.7.&36.12.
units.tr: SAGA, i.e. the curtains of the Tabernacle: Exod. 26.7; 36.12.

units.la: SAGENAE parabola, Matth.13.47. V. Recte.
units.tr: The parable of the DRAGNET: Matt. 13.47. See Recte.

units.la: [Sagena Dei, Ezech.12.13. & 17.20.&32.3. Hominis, Abac.1.v.15.16.17.]
units.tr: [The dragnet of God: Ezek. 12.13; 17.20; 32.3. Of man: Hab. 1.15–17.]

units.la: SAGITTAE Dei, Deut.32.v.23.42. 2 Sam.22.15. Iob.6.4. Psal. 7.14 & 38.3.&77.18.&91.5.&144.6. Ezec.5.16. Ionatæ sagittæ, indices iræ Saulis: 1 Sam.20.20.
units.tr: The ARROWS of God: Deut. 32.23, 42; 2 Sam. 22.15; Job 6.4; Ps. 7.14; 38.3; 77.18; 91.5; 144.6; Ezek. 5.16. Jonathan's arrows were signs of Saul's anger: 1 Sam. 20.20.

units.la: sagittæ Christi, regis Ecclesiæ, Psal.45.6.
units.tr: The arrows of Christ, the King of the Church: Ps. 45.6.

units.la: sagitta salutis Domini, 2 Reg. 13.17.
units.tr: The arrow of the Lord's salvation: 2 Kings 13.17.

units.la: Sagittæ hominis, pacis & belli tempore, frequenter occurrunt in script. ] V. Funditor.
units.tr: The arrows of man, in times of peace and of war, often occur in Scripture. See Funditor.

units.la: SAGITTARIORVM exempla: Ismael, Gen.21.20. Philisthæi sagittarij, 1 Sam.31.3.1 Para.10.3. sagittarij vrbis Raba, 2 Sam. 11 v.23.24. Beniamitæ, 2 Paral. 14.8. Nechao Regis sagittarij, 35 23. Filij Cedar, Esa.21.17. Lydij.Ier.46.9.
units.tr: Examples of ARCHERS: Ishmael, Gen. 21.20. The Philistine archers, 1 Sam. 31.3; 1 Chron. 10.3. The archers of the city of Rabbah, 2 Sam. 11.23–24. The Benjaminites, 2 Chron. 14.8. King Necho's archers, 2 Chron. 35.23. The sons of Kedar, Isa. 21.17. The Lydians, Jer. 46.9.

units.la: SAL, vrbe Sichem destructa, diiperium ab Abimelech, Iudic. 9.45. sal sacrificiis adhibitum, Leui.2.13. Ezech 43.24. Marci 9.49. sal terræ, Apostoli, Matth.3.13. Marc 9.50.
units.tr: SALT: the city of Shechem, destroyed, was sown with salt by Abimelech: Judg. 9.45. Salt was used in sacrifices: Lev. 2.13; Ezek. 43.24; Mark 9.49. "Salt of the earth": the Apostles, Matt. 5.13; Mark 9.50.

units.la: SAL is statua facta est vxor Loth, Genes.19.26. salis pactum, stabile, Numer.18.19. 2 Par.13.5. vsus, Luc.14.35. sale conditus sit sermo, Coloss.4.6. sale condita victima, Marc.9.49. con-
units.tr: SALT: Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt: Gen. 19.26. A covenant of salt, lasting forever: Num. 18.19; 2 Chron. 13.5. Its use: Luke 14.35. "Let your speech be seasoned with salt": Col. 4.6. A victim seasoned with salt: Mark 9.49. Con-

units.la: conditum sacrificium, Leuit.2.13.
units.tr: A sacrifice seasoned with salt: Lev. 2.13.
