units.la: SALTATIO: saltationis fit mentio in scriptura sacra, Exo.15.20. & 32.6.1 sam.18.6.2 sam.6.16. Eccles.3.4. Matth.11.17.&14.6. Marci 6 22. Luc.7.32.
units.tr: DANCING: Scripture mentions dancing: Exod. 15.20; 32.6; 1 Sam. 18.6; 2 Sam. 6.16; Eccl. 3.4; Matt. 11.17; 14.6; Mark 6.22; Luke 7.32.

units.la: Ex quibus duo colligi possunt: Primus: Saltationum duo genera reperiri in Scriptura.
units.tr: Two points can be drawn from these passages. First, there are two kinds of dancing to be found in Scripture.

units.la: I. Aliae enim sunt honestae. Exempla: Maria submerso Pharaone, organis ludens & choreas agens cum aliis mulieribus, Exo.15.20. Dauid Ephod lineo cinctus totis viribus saltans coram Domino, 2 Sam.6.v.14.16. Mulieres occiso Goliatho paeana canentes Dauidi, & saltantes, 1 Sam. 18.7.
units.tr: I. Some dances are honourable. Examples: Miriam, after Pharaoh had been drowned, played the instrument and led dances with the other women (Exod. 15.20). David, girded with a linen ephod, danced with all his might before the Lord (2 Sam. 6.14–16). Women sang a paean to David after Goliath was killed, and danced (1 Sam. 18.7).

units.la: II. Aliae vero turpes. Exempla: populus coram vitulo conflato ludens & saltans, Exod.32.6. Filia Herodiadis in natalitiis Herodis saltans, Matthaei.14.6 Marci 6.22. Ideoque damnantur: Quia non moechandum: Exod.20. Ab oi mali specie abstinendum: 1 Thess.5.22. Diligenda non sunt quae sunt in mundo, vt cupiditas carnis, libido oculorum, fastus vitae: 1 Ioh.2.16. Sermonis otiosi, in die iudicij, ratio reddenda: Mat. 12.36. Tempus redimé- dum: Eph. 5.16. Vide raptum Dinæ, Gen. 34.1. Et filiarum Israel: Iudicum, 21.23. Posterius: Choreas diuisas fuisse ratione sexus: hoc est, aliæ fuerunt mulierum, aliæ virorum choreæ. Nam Dauid solus saltat, non cum matronis aut puellis. Sic Maria inter mulieres & cum mulieribus saltat. Mulieres item pæana Dauidi canentes. Huiusmodi choreæ, aptè, decenter, honestè, piè, suo loco & tempore, sine aliorum damno & scandalo actæ, tolerari à piis possunt.
units.tr: II. Others are shameful. Examples: the people played and danced before the molten calf (Exod. 32.6). Herodias's daughter danced at Herod's birthday feast (Matt. 14.6; Mark 6.22). Such dances are condemned: because one must not commit adultery (Exod. 20); one must abstain from every appearance of evil (1 Thess. 5.22); the things of the world are not to be loved, such as the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life (1 John 2.16); an account must be given on the day of judgment for every idle word (Matt. 12.36); and time must be redeemed (Eph. 5.16). See the rape of Dinah (Gen. 34.1) and the daughters of Israel (Judg. 21.23). Second, dances were separated by sex: some were dances of women, others of men. For David danced alone, not with matrons or girls; so Miriam danced among women and with women; likewise the women who sang a paean to David. Dances of this kind may be tolerated by the godly when they are done fittingly, decently, honourably and piously, in their proper place and time, and without harm or scandal to others.

units.la: [SALVATOR, Seruator. 1. Deus Saluator, qui suos ex omnibus periculis clementer seruat, 1 Sam. 10.19. & 14.39. 2 Sam. 22.v.3.1 Par. 16.35. Iob. 13.16. Psal. 25.5. & 62.67. Esa. 17.10. 43.verf. 3.11. & 45.15. & 63.8. Ierem. 14.8. Dan. 6.27. Ose. 13.4. Mich. 7.7. V. Redemptor.
units.tr: [SAVIOUR, Preserver. 1. God the Saviour, who graciously preserves his own from all dangers: 1 Sam. 10.19; 14.39; 2 Sam. 22.3; 1 Chron. 16.35; Job 13.16; Ps. 25.5; 62.7; Isa. 17.10; 43.3, 11; 45.15; 63.8; Jer. 14.8; Dan. 6.27; Hos. 13.4; Mic. 7.7. See Redeemer.]

units.la: 2. Saluator, Seruator Ecclesiæ, cui redemptionem æternam acquisiuit, Messias patribus promissus, in plenitudine temporum exhibitus Iesus Christus, æternus æterni Patris Filius, conceptus de Spiritu S. natus ex Maria Virgine, Deus-homo, Esai. 12.2. & 19.20. & 62.11. Zachar. 9.9. Luc. 2.11. Ioann. 4.42 Act. 5 31. & 13.23. Ephes. 5.23. Phil 3.20. 1 Timot. 1.1. & 2.5. & 4.10 2 Timot. 1.10. Tit. 1.v.3 4.8. 2.v.10.13. & 3 v.4 6.2. Petr. 1.1. & 2.20. & 3.v.2.18. 1 Ioann. 4 14. Iud. v.25.
units.tr: 2. The Saviour, the Preserver of the Church, for whom he obtained eternal redemption: the Messiah promised to the fathers and revealed in the fullness of time, Jesus Christ, the eternal Son of the eternal Father, conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, God-man: Isa. 12.2; 19.20; 62.11; Zech. 9.9; Luke 2.11; John 4.42; Acts 5.31; 13.23; Eph. 5.23; Phil. 3.20; 1 Tim. 1.1; 2.5; 4.10; 2 Tim. 1.10; Titus 1.3; 2.10, 13; 3.4, 6; 1 Pet. 1.1; 2.20; 3.2, 18; 1 John 4.14; Jude v. 25.

units.la: 3. Saluator, i. Saulus per Messiam Ecclesiæ parta: Esai. 12.2. & 26.1. & 45 8. & 51.5. & 62.1.
units.tr: 3. Saviour, i.e. salvation won for the Church through the Messiah: Isa. 12.2; 26.1; 45.8; 51.5; 62.1.

units.la: 4. Saluator, homo à Deo excitatus, qui alios à periculis liberet: Genes. 41.47. Iudic. 2.16. & 3.v.15.19.2. Reg. 13.5. Nehem. 9.27.
units.tr: 4. Saviour: a man raised up by God to free others from dangers: Gen. 41.47; Judg. 2.16; 3.9, 15, 19; 2 Kings 13.5; Neh. 9.27.

units.la: 5. Saluatores vocantur fideles serui Iesu Christi, qui homines ad participationem gratiæ Dei per Euangelij prædicationem vocant & pertrahunt: Abd. verf. 1.21. 1 Tim. 4.16.
units.tr: 5. The faithful servants of Jesus Christ are called saviours, since they call and draw men to share in God's grace through the preaching of the Gospel: Obad. v. 21; 1 Tim. 4.16.

units.la: 6. Seruatores etiam, dicuntur quicunque pij in vocatione Ecclesiastica, politica, priuata variis modis, ne ruât in æternum exitium conseruant, iuuant consiliis, exhortationibus, opibus, aliisque legitimis auxiliis. Vide Iudæ epistolam. v.23. & Iac. 5.19.20.
units.tr: 6. Those who are godly in their ecclesiastical, civil or private calling are also called saviours, since in various ways they keep others from rushing into eternal destruction, helping them with counsel, exhortation, resources and other lawful aid. See Jude v. 23 and James 5.19–20.

units.la: SALVS pro auxilio, 2 Samuel. 10.11. psalm. 60. 13. pro eo, qui seruandis electis destinatus est, 50.23. hoc est, pro Messiæ, vnico salutis organo, à Deo, non, vni duntaxat Iudæorum genti, sed toti mundo exhibito. Lucæ 3.6. Sicut accipiunt vulgò & Genes. 49.18. pro doctrina Euangelij, Hebr. 2.3. pro iustificatione quæ in hac vita contingit, Mat. 9.22. Luc. 19.9. Ephes. 2.8. 2. Timoth. 1.9. Tit. 3.4. pro æterna illa gloria, quæ post hanc vitam datur. Roman. 8.23. Hebr. 1.14. & 5.9. 1 Petr. 1.9. quam Paulus gloriam appellat. Rom. 8.18. Salus à solo Deo, Psalm. 3.9. & 18 ver. 3.4, & 27.1 & 33.16. & 44. v. 4.5. & 73.25. Esa. 27.3 & 43. v. 3. Ieremiæ 3.3. Oseæ 13.4. Iacob. 4.12. (Vide Deus) Salus in solo Christi nomine, per solam Christi gratiam confertur. Actor. 4.12. & 15.14. Neque tamen pugnant cum his loci: Abd. 1.22. 1 Timoth. 4.16. Iacob. 5.20. Vbi Ministri Verbi dicuntur saluare, & seruare suos auditores, quatenus scilicet sunt administri salutis per doctrinam Euangelij. Sic etiam dicuntur peccata remittere. Ioannis 20.23. tribuendo scilicet id instrumento, quod efficientis causæ est proprium. Non multum absimiliter dicuntur ij etiam recipere in æterna tabernacula, qui ex iniusto mammona amici facti sunt aliis, Lucæ 16.9. nempe implorando illis benedictionem & misericordiam: quo etiam sensu dicuntur parentes prolongare (vt nonnulli interpretantur) vitam suorum filiorum, qui quidem morigeri erga ipsos fuerint, Exod. 20.12. nimirum honorem sibi ex Dei mandato à liberis suis delatum approbantes, ac d uinam benedictionem longævamque vitam illis implorantes.
units.tr: SALVATION, meaning help: 2 Samuel 10.11; Psalm 60.13. Of that which is appointed for the saving of the elect: 50.23, that is, of the Messiah, the only means of salvation, offered by God not merely to the one nation of the Jews but to the whole world: Luke 3.6. It is commonly taken also as the doctrine of the Gospel: Genesis 49.18. Of the justification that takes place in this life: Hebrews 2.3; Matthew 9.22; Luke 19.9; Ephesians 2.8; 2 Timothy 1.9; Titus 3.4. Of that eternal glory which is given after this life: Romans 8.23; Hebrews 1.14 and 5.9; 1 Peter 1.9, which Paul calls glory, Romans 8.18. Salvation comes from God alone: Psalm 3.9; 18.3, 4; 27.1; 33.16; 44.4, 5; 73.25; Isaiah 27.3; 43.3; Jeremiah 3.3; Hosea 13.4; James 4.12 (See GOD). Salvation is conferred in the name of Christ alone, through Christ's grace alone: Acts 4.12; 15.14. Nor do the following passages conflict with these: Obadiah 1.22; 1 Timothy 4.16; James 5.20. Here ministers of the Word are said to save and preserve their hearers, insofar as they are servants of salvation through the teaching of the Gospel. So too they are said to forgive sins, John 20.23, the act being attributed to the instrument, which is proper to the efficient cause. Not very differently, those are also said to receive others into the eternal tabernacles who have made friends for themselves by unrighteous mammon, Luke 16.9, namely by invoking blessing and mercy upon them. In the same sense parents are said to prolong (as some interpret) the life of those sons who have been obedient to them, Exodus 20.12, namely by approving the honour owed to them by their children under God's command, and by invoking upon them the divine blessing and a long life.

units.la: Salus ex Dei gratia & misericordia, Eph. 2. v. 5.8. Tit. 2.11. Heb. 7.25. & 8.8. & 10.14. in Christo perfecta. Vide CHRISTVS. Salus in Ecclesia, Esa. 46.13. Ioel. 2.32. Abd. vers. 17. salus ex Iudæis, Ioan. 4.22. salus per Euangelium confertur, Rom. 1.16. 1 Cor. 15.2. Iac. 1.11. in spe posita, Rom. 8.24. (vide significata salutis) Heb. 4.8. 1 Petr. 1.3. salus minimè negligenda, Hebr. 2.3. salus eadem nobis & Patribus communis. 1. Pet. 1.10. salus animarum, fidei finis, 1.9. salus piorum æterna, Esa. 45.17. Heb. 7.25. salus piorum quomodo promoveatur, Rom. 8.27.28.29 30. &c.
units.tr: Salvation comes from the grace and mercy of God, Ephesians 2.5, 8; Titus 2.11; Hebrews 7.25; 8.8; 10.14, and is perfected in Christ (See CHRIST). Salvation is in the Church: Isaiah 46.13; Joel 2.32; Obadiah verse 17. Salvation is from the Jews: John 4.22. Salvation is conferred through the Gospel: Romans 1.16; 1 Corinthians 15.2; James 1.21. It is placed in hope: Romans 8.24 (see the meanings of salvation); Hebrews 4.8; 1 Peter 1.3. Salvation is by no means to be neglected: Hebrews 2.3. Salvation is the same for us and the Fathers, common to both: 1 Peter 1.10. The salvation of souls is the end of faith: 1 Peter 1.9. The eternal salvation of the godly: Isaiah 45.17; Hebrews 7.25. How the salvation of the godly is advanced: Romans 8.27–30, etc.

units.la: ALVTIS. fidelium certitudo, 1 Thessal. 5.9. Hebr. 12.13. salutis cornu erigere quid sit, Vide CORNV salutis galea, Eph. 6.17. salutis partes omnes in Christo continentur, Col. 1.v 13 14. salutis via, cognitio veritatis; 1. Timot. 2.4.1 Cor. 1.30.31. V. Certos non esse.
units.tr: SAFETY. The certainty of the faithful: 1 Thessalonians 5.9; Hebrews 12.13. What it is to raise the horn of salvation (See HORN). The helmet of salvation: Ephesians 6.17. All parts of salvation are contained in Christ: Colossians 1.13, 14. The way of salvation is the knowledge of the truth: 1 Timothy 2.4; 1 Corinthians 1.30, 31. (See: not to be certain.)

units.la: SALVTEM nostram cum timore & tremore conficere iu-bemur,Philip.2.12.ex quo dicto salutem nostram ex operibus nostris pendere quis autumare posset:sed id quidem minime verum est,quum ne Abraham quidem in se habeat, de quo glorietur apud Deum, Rom.4.2.Confecre tamen salutem dicitur , qui in iustitiæ stadio currit. Quamuis enim gratis in vno Christo per fidem apprehenso seruemur ( vt supra visum est ) tamen per viam iustitiæ ad salutem contendere nos oportet:quum Filij Dei, eius Spiritu ducantur, per quem sunt iustificati, vt in bonis operibus ambulent, Roman.8.14.Coniungit autem Apostolus, Philip.2.12.timorem ac tremorem, sicut & 1 Cor. 2.3.tanquam veræ modestiæ comites, non quidom illos quibus perterrefiat conscientia, aut dubitatio quędam animis piorum ingeratur,vt Pontificij sophistæ impiè docent, sed qui vanitati & arrogantiæ opponuntur.
units.tr: SALVATION: we are bidden to work out our salvation with fear and trembling, Philippians 2.12. From this saying someone might suppose that our salvation depends on our works; but this is by no means true, since not even Abraham has anything in himself of which to glory before God, Romans 4.2. Yet he is said to work out his salvation who runs in the race of righteousness. For although we are saved freely, through faith apprehended in Christ alone (as was shown above), nevertheless we ought to strive toward salvation by the way of righteousness, since the sons of God are led by his Spirit, through whom they have been justified, so that they may walk in good works, Romans 8.14. Moreover, the Apostle joins fear and trembling in Philippians 2.12, as also in 1 Corinthians 2.3, as companions of true modesty. He does not mean those by which the conscience is terrified, or some doubt is cast into the minds of the godly, as the Papist sophists impiously teach, but those which are opposed to vanity and arrogance.

units.la: SALVTARE in pace, 1 Sam.10.4. in sancto osculo,Roman.16.16.1 Corint.16.20.2 Cor.13.12.1 Pet.5.14.(Vide Oscvaʟᴜᴍ) Salutare in via prohibetur Apostoli,Luc.10.4.qua locutione hyperbolica vtuntur Hebræi, cùm alicui præcipitur, vt celeriter & nulla prorsus interieƈta mora aliquid obeat, vt 2. Reg. 4.29.alioquin comes & humanas salutationes inter Christiana quoque officia numerantur passim. Nonnulli per synecdochen interpretantur,vt sit species pro genere posita, salutatio, pro colloquio, aut collocutione, q.d.cum nemine colloquimini, quod sit vobis in moram.Sic & 2 Reg.4.29.
units.tr: TO GREET: in peace, 1 Samuel 10.4; with a holy kiss, Romans 16.16; 1 Corinthians 16.20; 2 Corinthians 13.12; 1 Peter 5.14 (See KISS). To greet on the way is forbidden to the Apostles, Luke 10.4. This is a hyperbolic expression, which the Hebrews use when someone is commanded to carry out something quickly and without any delay at all, as in 2 Kings 4.29. Otherwise, the courtesy of human greetings is numbered among Christian duties everywhere. Some interpret by synecdoche, so that the species is put for the genus: "greeting" for "conversation" or "talk", as if to say: "Speak with no one, lest it delay you." So also 2 Kings 4.29.

units.tr: GREETING: the angel's greeting to Mary, Luke 1.28. The form of apostolic and Christian greeting: Matthew 10.12, 13; Luke 10.5. Examples of greeting: Moses and Jethro, Exodus 18.7. The angel greets Gideon, Judges 6.12. The scouts of the tribe of Dan, Judges 18.15. Saul greets Samuel, 1 Samuel 13.10. David's young men greet Nabal, 1 Samuel 25.5. David greets the people, 2 Samuel 30.2. Tohu greets David, 2 Samuel 8.10. The people greet Absalom, 2 Samuel 15.5. The Apostles greet the household they are about to enter, Matthew 10.12; Luke 10.5. Christ greets the disciples, Matthew 28.9; Luke 24.36. The people greet Christ, Mark 9.15. The angel greets Mary, Luke 1.28. Mary greets Elizabeth, v. 40. Paul greets the Church of Caesarea, Acts 18.22. Paul greets the brothers, Acts 21.7, 18, 19. Agrippa and Bernice greet Festus, Acts 25.13. Paul greets Priscilla, Aquila, the remaining brothers and saints, Romans 16.3, etc.; the Church of Asia, etc.; the Corinthians, 1 Corinthians 16.19, etc.

Pauli comites Titum, Tit. 3.15. Epaphras, &c. Philemonem, Philem.v.23. Hebræi suos præpositos, Hebr. 13.24. & Itali Hebræos, ibid. Ecclesia Babylone collecta sanctos 1 Pe. 5.13. Amici Caij, Caium, 3 Ioan. v.15.
units.tr: 16.19, etc. The Corinthians greet one another, 2 Corinthians 13.12. The saints of Philippi, Philippians 4.21, etc. Aristarchus, Mark, etc. The Colossians, Colossians 4.10, etc. Eubulus, etc. Timothy, 2 Timothy 4.21. Paul's companions greet Titus, Titus 3.15. Epaphras, etc. Philemon, Philemon verse 23. The Hebrews greet their leaders, Hebrews 13.24, and the Italians greet the Hebrews, ibid. The Church gathered at Babylon greets the saints, 1 Peter 5.13. The friends of Gaius greet Gaius, 3 John verse 15.

units.la: Salutandi superiores ritus: Exempla: Abraham, Gen. 23. 7 Ruth, Ruth. 2.10. Abigail, 1 Sam. 25.v 23.24. Miphibosheth, 2 Sam. 9.6. Iob. 14.22. Absalom, veri 33. Bethsabee, 1 Reg. 1.16. Filij prophetarum. 2 Reg. 2.15. Salutationes in foro amabant Pharisæi & Scribæ, Matth 23.7. Luc. 20.46.
units.tr: Rites of greeting superiors. Examples: Abraham, Genesis 23.7; Ruth, Ruth 2.10; Abigail, 1 Samuel 25.23, 24; Mephibosheth, 2 Samuel 9.6; Job 14.22 (?); Absalom, ibid. 33; Bathsheba, 1 Kings 1.16; the sons of the prophets, 2 Kings 2.15. The Pharisees and scribes loved greetings in the marketplace, Matthew 23.7; Luke 20.46.

units.la: [SALVVS dicitur, qui à Deo immediatè vel mediatè ex variis periculis recipitur: Genesios, 19 17. Iudic. 6 36. 2 Sam. 19.5. & 22. versic. 4. 28. 2 Reg. 16. 6. & 19. 19. Iob. 5. 15. units.tr: [SAFE is said of one who is rescued by God, immediately or through means, from various dangers: Genesis 19.17; Judges 6.36; 2 Samuel 19.5; 22.4, 28; 2 Kings 16.6; 19.19; Job 5.15; Psalm 3.8; 6.5; 7.2, 3, 11, and very often in what follows; Matthew 14.30; 27.42; Acts 23.24; 27.31; 1 Peter 3.20.]

Tim. 1.15. & 2.4. & 4.16. 2 Tim. 4.18. Tit. 3.4.]
units.tr: [Saved: freed from sins, and in this life a sharer by faith and hope in eternal life, and after this life in reality: Matthew 1.21; Mark 16.16; Luke 8.12; John 5.34; Acts 2.21, 47; 4.12; 11.14; 14.9; 16.30, 31; Romans 5.9, 10; 8.23; 9.27; 10.9, 13; 11.4, 26; 1 Corinthians 1.18, 21; 2 Corinthians 2.15; 1 Thessalonians 2.16; 2 Thessalonians 1.10; 1 Timothy 1.15; 2.4; 4.16; 2 Timothy 4.18; Titus 3.4.]

units.la: SAMARIA, quæ postea metropolis fuit decem tribuum Israel, extruitur, 1 Regum 16. 24. obsidetur à Syris, 2 Reg 6 24. obsidetur ab Assyrus vique in tertium annum, capitur, abducitur populus, & habitatur ab extraneis 17. 5.24. samaria quando capta ab Assyriis, v.6. &c. & 18.v.9. o samaria nolebat recipere verbum Dei. Luc. 9.53. recipit illud, Actor. 8.5. (1 Custodia Domini).
units.tr: SAMARIA, which afterwards was the metropolis of the ten tribes of Israel, is built, 1 Kings 16.24; is besieged by the Syrians, 2 Kings 6.24; is besieged by the Assyrians even to the third year, is taken, and the people are led away and the land is inhabited by foreigners, 17.5, 24. When Samaria was taken by the Assyrians, verse 6, etc.; and 18.9. Samaria was unwilling to receive the Word of God, Luke 9.53; it receives it, Acts 8.5. (1 The Lord's watch.)

units.la: SAMARIAE excidium prædicitur, Esa. 7.9. & 9.7.8. Ezech. 23. &c. Oe. 14.1 Amos. 3.2. Mich. 1.6. samariæ idololatria, zech. 23.v. 4. 5. iniquitas, Amos 3.9. Mich. 1.3. samariæ mala. Ose. 13.16. & 14. v. 1. &c. samariæ mons emtus ab Gimri rege Israel, 1 Reg. 16,24.
units.tr: The destruction of Samaria is foretold: Isaiah 7.9; 9.7, 8; Ezekiel 23, etc.; Hosea 14.1; Amos 3.2; Micah 1.6. The idolatry of Samaria: Zechariah 23.4, 5. The iniquity of Samaria: Amos 3.9; Micah 1.3. The evils of Samaria: Hosea 13.16; 14.1, etc. The mountain of Samaria was bought by Omri, king of Israel, 1 Kings 16.24.

units.la: SAMARITAE Deo & dæmonibus seruiunt, 2 Reg. 17. 5 &c.
units.tr: The Samaritans serve God and demons, 2 Kings 17.5 etc.

units.la: SAMARITANAE historia, Ioannis 4. 7. &c. Vide Mulier samaritana. samaritanis Christū prædicat Philippus, Act. 8.5.
units.tr: The history of the Samaritans, John 4.7 etc. See "Samaritan woman". Philip preaches Christ to the Samaritans, Acts 8.5.

units.la: Samaritanum blasphemant Iudæi esse Christum, Ioan. 8.48. Samaritani multi credunt in Christum, Ioan 4. ver. 39.41. Act.8. v.12.14. Samaritani Christum reliciunt &quaere Luc.9.53. Samaritani parabola docens quis sit proximus, Luc.10.29. &c.
units.tr: The Jews blaspheme, saying that the Samaritan is Christ, John 8.48. Many Samaritans believe in Christ, John 4.39, 41; Acts 8.12, 14. The Samaritans reject Christ; see also Luke 9.53. The parable of the Samaritan, teaching who is our neighbour, Luke 10.29 etc.

units.la: Samgar Iudex Israel profligat Philisthæos Iudic. 3.31.
units.tr: Shamgar, judge of Israel, defeats the Philistines, Judges 3.31.

units.la: Samothrace, Insula vicina Thraciæ, sic dicta, quòd eam Samij & Thraces incoluerunt: Act.16.11.
units.tr: Samothrace, an island near Thrace, so called because the Samians and the Thracians inhabited it, Acts 16.11.

units.la: [Samma, proprium nomen variorum, Gen.36.13.17.1 Par.1. 43.&7.37.1 Sam.16.9.1 Par.11.44. Sammai, 1 Par.2.44.&4. 1 Sammoth, 1 Par.11.27. Sammua, Num.13.5. Samri,1 Par.1. 45.&2 Par.29.13.]
units.tr: [Samma, a proper name of various men: Gen. 36.13, 17; 1 Chr. 1.43; 7.37; 1 Sam. 16.9; 1 Chr. 11.44. Sammai, 1 Chr. 2.44 and 4. Sammoth, 1 Chr. 11.27. Sammua, Num. 13.5. Samri, 1 Chr. 1.45 and 2 Chr. 29.13.]

units.la: Samsai scriba, Esdr.4.v.8.6.17.23.
units.tr: Samsai the scribe, Ezra 4.8; 6.17; 23.

units.la: Samson nascitur, cui benedicit Deus, Iudic.13.24. iuxta praemissionem Angeli v.3. leonem lacerat 14.6. uxorem Philisthæam ducit, v.7.8. problema convivius proponit, v.14. id uxori exponit, v. 17. accensis vulpium caudis segetes Philisthæorum exurit, 15.4. eius socer & uxor comburuntur, v.6. maxilla asini mille Philisthæos occidit, v.15. portas Gazæ in montem transfert, 16.3. à Dalila decipitur, v.19. Philistæis excæcatur, ver.21. cum principib. Philisthiim reliqua multitudine moritur, ædificiorum ruina obruti v.30 (Simsou.i.sol eorum.)
units.tr: Samson is born, and God blesses him, Judges 13.24; according to the angel's promise, v. 3. He tears a lion, 14.6. He takes a Philistine wife, vv. 7–8. He proposes a riddle at the feast, v. 14. He explains it to his wife, v. 17. With foxes' tails set alight, he burns the Philistines' crops, 15.4. His father-in-law and his wife are burned, v. 6. With the jawbone of an ass he kills a thousand Philistines, v. 15. He carries the gates of Gaza up to the mountain, 16.3. He is deceived by Delilah, v. 19. He is blinded by the Philistines, v. 21. He dies with the princes of the Philistines and the rest of the crowd, buried under the collapse of the buildings, v. 30. (Shimshon, that is, their sun.)

units.la: Samuel (.i.petitus à Deo) nascitur, 1 Sam.1.20. Domino ministrat 2.11 & 3.1. Deo & hominibus gratus est, 2.26. à Deo quater vocatur, 3.v.4.7.8.10. fidelis Dei propheta est, v.20. Deum pro populo orat, 7.9. Israelem in Maspha iudicat, v.15. altare Deo extruit, v.17. filios iudices Israelis constituit, 8.1. Saulem regem ungit, 10.1. innocens & integer est, 12.3. Saulem luget, 15.35. Unde desistere iubetur, 16.1. Davidem Regem ungit, 16.13. moritur, 25.1. (eius præstantia Psal.99.6.) eum excitari Saulus optat, 28.11. post mortem prophetare dicitur, Eccles.46.21. quod prudenter discendum est, laudatur v.14.&c.
units.tr: Samuel (that is, asked of God) is born, 1 Sam. 1.20. He ministers to the Lord, 2.11 and 3.1. He is pleasing to God and to men, 2.26. He is called by God four times, 3.4, 7, 8, 10. He is a faithful prophet of God, v. 20. He prays to God for the people, 7.9. He judges Israel at Mizpah, v. 15. He builds an altar to God, v. 17. He appoints his sons judges of Israel, 8.1. He anoints Saul king, 10.1. He is innocent and upright, 12.3. He mourns for Saul, 15.35. Hence he is ordered to stop, 16.1. He anoints David king, 16.13. He dies, 25.1 (his excellence, Ps. 99.6). Saul wishes him to be raised up, 28.11. He is said to have prophesied after his death, Ecclus. 46.21. That one should learn prudently is praised, v. 14, etc.

units.la: [Samuel, Amihudi F. Num.34.20. Issacharis nepos, 1 Par. 7.2.]
units.tr: [Samuel, son of Ammihud, Num. 34.20. Grandson of Issachar, 1 Chr. 7.2.]

units.la: Sanaballat, præfectus Samariæ, conatur impedire templi ædificationem, Nehem.2.10. (i. Rubus in abscondito.)
units.tr: Sanballat, governor of Samaria, tries to hinder the building of the temple, Neh. 2.10. (That is, a bush in hiding.)

units.la: Sanator, curator Deus, Exod.15.26. Sanatio, Act.4.22. Sanat. nati à peccatis, Esai.53.5. 1 Petr.2.24. Vide Ægrotorum mu-nus.
units.tr: Sanator, the God who heals, Exod. 15.26. Healing, Acts 4.22. Healed from sins, Isa. 53.5; 1 Pet. 2.24. See "The office of caring for the sick".

units.la: SANCTIFICARE, pro purgare, 2 Sam. 11. 4. pro consecrare, Leu.25.10. pro laudé & gloriā tribuere, 1 Pet.3.15. sanctifi-cat seipsum patri Christus pro nobis & immolat, Ioan. 17.19. vt sanctificet Pater Apostolos, orat Christus, Ioan. 17.17. sanctificemus nos, 1 Ioan.3.3. sanctificare Dominum coram populo, Num.20.12. & 27.14. sanctificare festum, Leu.25.10. sanctificari vult Deus, Leu.10.3. sanctificari, pro sanctum haberi & coli, Matth.6.9.
units.tr: TO SANCTIFY: for to purge, 2 Sam. 11.4; for to consecrate, Lev. 25.10; for to ascribe praise and glory, 1 Pet. 3.15. Christ sanctifies himself to the Father for us, and offers himself, John 17.19. Christ prays that the Father sanctify the apostles, John 17.17. Let us sanctify ourselves, 1 John 3.3. To sanctify the Lord before the people, Num. 20.12; 27.14. To sanctify the feast, Lev. 25.10. God wills to be sanctified, Lev. 10.3. To be sanctified, that is, to be held and worshipped as holy, Matt. 6.9.

units.la: sanctificare, verbum, paulò distinctius, descriptum, cum deriuatis.
units.tr: The verb "to sanctify", described somewhat more precisely, with its derivatives.

units.la: 1. Sanctificat Deus homines, dies, res, &c. Gen.2.3. Exo. 20.11. & 29.44. & 31.13. 1 Reg 9.v.3.7. Ierem.1.5. Ezech.20. 12. & 36.23. 1 Thess.5.23.
units.tr: 1. God sanctifies men, days, things, etc.: Gen. 2.3; Exod. 20.11; 29.44; 31.13; 1 Kings 9.3, 7; Jer. 1.5; Ezek. 20.12; 36.23; 1 Thess. 5.23.

units.la: 2. Sanctificat Deus Pater, Ioan.10.36. & 17.17.
units.tr: 2. God the Father sanctifies: John 10.36; 17.17.

units.la: 3. Sanctificat Deus Filius, Ioan.17.19. Eph.5.26. Hebr.2. 11. & 3.12.
units.tr: 3. God the Son sanctifies: John 17.19; Eph. 5.26; Heb. 2.11; 3.12.

units.la: 4. Sanctificat Spiritus Sanctus cuius virtute sanctificantur homines, & res, Ioan.17.19. Actor.20.32. Roman.15.16. 1 Cor.1.2. & 6.11. & 7.14. 1 Tim.4.4. 5.2 Tim.2.21. Heb.10. v.10.14.29. Apoc.22.11.
units.tr: 4. The Holy Spirit sanctifies, by whose power men and things are sanctified: John 17.19; Acts 20.32; Rom. 15.16; 1 Cor. 1.2; 6.11; 7.14; 1 Tim. 4.4; 5.2 [sic]; 2 Tim. 2.21; Heb. 10.10, 14, 29; Rev. 22.11.

units.la: 5. Sanctificat Deus, i. præparat, Ierem.12.3. & 22.7. & 51. v.27.28. Soph.1.7. Sanctificati, i. apparati, instructi, ad aliquid exequendum, Dei iudicis prouidentia, Esai.13. 3. Verbum illud etiam, fere eodem sensu idem est ac Indico, Proclamo, Ierem.6.4. Ioel.1.14. & 2.v.15. 16. & 3.9. Mich.3.5.
units.tr: 5. God sanctifies, that is, prepares: Jer. 12.3; 22.7; 51.27–28; Zeph. 1.7. Those are sanctified, that is, made ready and equipped to carry out something, by the providence of God the judge: Isa. 13.3. This word also, in almost the same sense, means the same as "to proclaim" or "to announce": Jer. 6.4; Joel 1.14; 2.15–16; 3.9; Mic. 3.5.

units.la: 6. Sanctificatur Deus, Leuit.10.3. Num.20.v.12.13. Deut. 32.51. Esai.5.16. Ezech.20.41. Matth.6.9.
units.tr: 6. God is sanctified: Lev. 10.3; Num. 20.12–13; Deut. 32.51; Isa. 5.16; Ezek. 20.41; Matt. 6.9.

units.la: 7. Sanctifico, Sanctificor, idem significat, ac Præparo me, vel præparo alios homines, dies aut res varias, ad sacram, ex Dei mandato, peragendam, Exod.13.2. & 16.23. & 19.ver.10.14. 22. & 20.8. & frequentissime apud Moysem, & Prophetas: Matth.23.v.17.19. Actorum 21.24. Hebræor.9.13. vbi Sanctificari, sanctificati & homines, & res sanctificatæ dicuntur, id est, in sacros vsus comparati vel comparatæ. Porrò sanctificationes seu consecrationes legales typi fuerunt huius sanctificationis quæ ex Christo Ecclesiæ capite in membra corporis mystici virtute Sancti Spiritus quotidie defluunt.
units.tr: 7. "To sanctify" and "to be sanctified" mean the same as to prepare myself, or to prepare other people, days, or various things, for a sacred task according to God's command: Exod. 13.2; 16.23; 19.10, 14, 22; 20.8; and very frequently in Moses and the Prophets; Matt. 23.17, 19; Acts 21.24; Heb. 9.13. There men and things are said to be sanctified, that is, fitted or prepared for sacred use. Moreover, the legal sanctifications or consecrations were types of that sanctification which daily flows from Christ, the head of the Church, into the members of his mystical body by the power of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 8. Sanctificare, i. glorificare, Esai.8.13 1 Petr.3.15. Purificare ratione externa, Ioan.11.55. Act.21.24. Hebr.9 13. Itus purificare, 1 Ioan.3 3.]
units.tr: 8. To sanctify, that is, to glorify: Isa. 8.13; 1 Pet. 3.15. To purify by an external reckoning: John 11.55; Acts 21.24; Heb. 9.13. To purify rites: 1 John 3.3.

units.la: SANCTIFICATIO, electionis testimonium, 1 Pet.1.2. sanctificatio, altera Christi in nos beneficij pars, (vide CHRISTVS) sanctificatio nostra Christus, 1 Cor.1 30.
units.tr: SANCTIFICATION is a testimony of election, 1 Pet. 1.2. Sanctification is the second part of Christ's benefit to us (see CHRIST). Christ is our sanctification, 1 Cor. 1.30.

units.la: SANCTIFICATI Christiani per Christum, 1 Corinth. 6.11.
units.tr: Christians are sanctified through Christ, 1 Cor. 6.11.

units.la: SANCTIFICATOR noster Deus, Leuit. 20. 8. Ezech. 37.28.
units.tr: Our sanctifier is God, Lev. 20.8; Ezek. 37.28.

units.la: SANCTIFICATA à quibus edi debeant, Leuit.22.10.11.12. [Sanctificatio externa, Legalis, Sanctificationis internae typus, Exod.29.39. & 30 35. & 37.29. Leui.8.9 & 25.12. Num. 6.v.12.21.
units.tr: THINGS SANCTIFIED, and by whom they ought to be eaten, Lev. 22.10–12. [External sanctification, legal, a type of internal sanctification: Exod. 29.39; 30.35; 37.29; Lev. 8.9; 25.12; Num. 6.12, 21.]

units.la: Sanctificatio interna, Iustificationis electorum Dei consequens & effectus, Rom.6.v.19.22.32 Cor.7.1 Thess.4.1 3.4.7.2 Thess.2.13.1 Tim.2.15. 1 Petr.1.2. Sanctificationis Spiritus, Rom.14. Sanctificatio Ecclesiae Christus, Esa.8 14.1 Cor.1.30.
units.tr: Internal sanctification is the consequence and effect of the justification of God's elect: Rom. 6.19, 22; 2 Cor. 7.1; 1 Thess. 4.1, 3, 4, 7; 2 Thess. 2.13; 1 Tim. 2.15; 1 Pet. 1.2. Sanctification of the Spirit: Rom. 14. Christ is the sanctification of the Church: Isa. 8.14; 1 Cor. 1.30.

units.la: Sanctificatio, res sancta, Ezech.20.40. Robur Dei, Psal. 132.8. Sanctitas Dei, Ps.97.12 & 114.2. Esai.63.18. Malac.3 11. Heb.12 10. Sanctuarium, i. tabernaculum, in quo Sancta Dei praesentia signum pij habuerunt, Ps.78.54. & 96 6. Esai.60.13. & 64 11. Ierem.17.12. & 51.51 Thren.2.7. Dan.8.1. Sanctuarium κατασκευαστὸν dictum, ab hominibus, suo arbitrio, non Dei iussu erectum, Amos.7.v.9.13.]
units.tr: Sanctification, a holy thing: Ezek. 20.40. The strength of God: Ps. 132.8. The holiness of God: Ps. 97.12; 114.2; Isa. 63.18; Mal. 3.11; Heb. 12.10. Sanctuary, that is, the tabernacle, in which the godly had the sign of God's holy presence: Ps. 78.54; 96.6; Isa. 60.13; 64.11; Jer. 17.12; 51.51; Lam. 2.7; Dan. 8.11. A sanctuary is called "made with hands" [κατασκευαστόν] by men, erected by their own choice and not by God's command: Amos 7.9, 13.

units.la: SANCTITAS vera quae, 1 Cor.7.34.2 Cor.7.1. sanctitas est electionis fructus, Eph.1.4.
units.tr: True holiness: 1 Cor. 7.34; 2 Cor. 7.1. Holiness is the fruit of election: Eph. 1.4.

units.la: SANCTVARIVM, Vide, TABERNACVLVM, aut Templum.
units.tr: SANCTUARY: see TABERNACLE or TEMPLE.

units.la: SANCTVM canibus non dandum, Matth.7.6. sanctum Domini, Exod.35.2. Leu.16.1. &c. Psalm.114.2. Matth.7.6. Luc. 1.37.
units.tr: "Do not give what is holy to the dogs," Matt. 7.6. The holy things of the Lord, Exod. 35.2; Lev. 16.1, etc.; Ps. 114.2; Matt. 7.6; Luke 1.37.

units.la: [Sanctum, sancta sanctorum, Sanctum Sanctorum, Adytum locus sanctissimus tabernaculi & templi Salomonis, ad
units.tr: [Sanctum, the holy of holies, the Most Holy Place: the most holy place of the tabernacle and of Solomon's temple, to which

units.tr: no entrance lay open except to the high priest, and that

units.la: semel quotannis,Hebr.9.v.3.24.25.
units.tr: once a year: Heb. 9.3, 24, 25.

units.la: Sanctum sanctorum, sanctitas sanctissima, Exod.29.37.
units.tr: Holy of holies, most holy holiness: Exod. 29.37;

units.la: & 30. v. 10. 20.36. Sanctum, Sancta, Sanctuarium, Exod.
units.tr: 30.10, 20; 36. Holy (sanctum), the sanctuary: Exod.

units.tr: heaven: Ps. 20.3; Isa. 57.15; Heb. 9.8, 12; 10.19. Holy (sanctum),

units.la: ctum,res sancta, Leuitic.10.10.& 12.4.Ezech.44.13. San-
units.tr: a holy thing: Lev. 10.10; 12.4; Ezek. 44.13. Holy

units.la: cta Sanctorum, res sanctissimæ, Numer. 4.19. & 18.9.San-
units.tr: of holies, most holy things: Num. 4.19; 18.9. Holy (sanctum),

units.la: ctum, sanctificatum, sacrum: sancta, sanctificata, sacra E-
units.tr: sanctified, sacred; holy things (sancta), sanctified things, sacred things: Exod.

units.la: xod.40.11.Leu.19.8. Matth. 7.6,Sanctum,Sanctitas,Exod.
units.tr: 40.11; Lev. 19.8; Matt. 7.6. Holy (sanctum), holiness: Exod.

units.la: SANCTVS est Deus, Esa.6.3. Apocal.4.8. sancti appellatio
units.tr: GOD is holy, Isa. 6.3; Rev. 4.8. The title "holy" is

units.la: Christo tributa, 1 Ioan. 2.20. qui sanctus peculiariter di-
units.tr: ascribed to Christ, 1 John 2.20, who is also called holy in a special way,

units.la: citur etiam, Luc.1.35. imò verò peculiariter sanctus san-
units.tr: as in Luke 1.35; indeed, in a special way, holy of the holy,

units.la: ctorum, id est, sanctus sanctissimus,Dan.9.24.sed & Deo
units.tr: that is, most holy, Dan. 9.24. But this can also be attributed to God,

units.la: hoc tribui potest, qui nos vngit in filio,vel etiam spiri-
units.tr: who anoints us in the Son, or even to the Holy Spirit,

units.la: tui sancto, qui sanctus proprie dicitur ab effectu isto,
units.tr: who is properly called holy from this effect.

units.la: Est enim Dei virtus essentialis, vt qui & ipse sit patri &
units.tr: For he is God's essential power, so that he himself is [homoousios] with the Father and the Son, and equal to them in all things,

units.la: filio ὁμοούσιος & æqualis per omnia, qua nos patet vngit
units.tr: by whom we are anointed and sanctified in the Son.

units.la: & sanctificat in filio. Sanctus Dei populus, Israelitæ,
units.tr: God's holy people, the Israelites, and in the Son he sanctifies them. Deut. 14.21. [Holy people]

units.la: Deut. 14. 21. sanctus panis,1 Sam.21.4. sanctus pro suo de-
units.tr: Deut. 14.21. Holy bread, 1 Sam. 21.4. The holy one prays for his own dedication,

units.la: dicto orat, Psal.32.6. Qui sanctus est, santificetur adhuc,
units.tr: Ps. 32.6. Let him who is holy be sanctified still,

units.la: SANCTI & mundi esse debemus, Levit.11.44.&19.2.&20,
units.tr: We ought to be holy and clean, Lev. 11.44, and 19.2, and 20.7, 26, and 21.6; Num. 15.40; Deut. 26.19; Eph. 5.26; 1 Thess.
4.3; 1 Pet. 1.16: holy, dedicated to God; unclean, Job 15.15.

units.la: 4.3.1 Petr. 1. 16.sancti Deo collati, immundi, Iob.15.15.
units.tr: Holy, as dedicated to God; unclean, Job 15.15.

units.la: sancti quatenus imitandi,1 Cor.4.16. Gal.4.12.Phil.3.17.
units.tr: Holy, insofar as they are to be imitated: 1 Cor. 4.16; Gal. 4.12; Phil. 3.17.

units.la: 1 Thess.1.6.2.Thess.3.7. sancti,in charitate exercenda re-
units.tr: 1 Thess. 1.6; 2 Thess. 3.7. Holy, in exercising charity, to be preferred to other men:

Ephes.1.15. Hebr.6.10. sancti pro iis qui absolutè in Dei
units.tr: Eph. 1.15; Heb. 6.10. Holy are those who are absolutely in God's house,

units.la: ædere sunt, etiamsi vera, id est interiori sanctitate ca-
units.tr: even if they lack true inner holiness.

units.la: eant,Rom.11.16.1 Cor. 7.14.sancti mundum indicabunt,
units.tr: Rom. 11.16; 1 Cor. 7.14. The saints will judge the world:

units.la: Matth. 19. 28. 1 Corint.6.2. Iudæ.v.14. Vide IVDICARE.
units.tr: Matt. 19.28; 1 Cor. 6.2; Jude 14. See JUDGE.

units.la: sancti cum Christo in cœlis regnantes, Ioan. 12. 26.
units.tr: Saints reigning with Christ in heaven: John 12.26;

units.la: 17.24. 2 Corinth.5.8. Philip.1.23. Apocal.3.21.&7.
& 14.13.sancti faciunt miracula.Vide MIRACVLA.
units.tr: Saints work miracles. See MIRACLES.

units.la: SANCTORVM communio Vide Communio, 2 Cor.8.14.
units.tr: COMMUNION OF SAINTS. See Communion; 2 Cor. 8.14.

units.la: sanctorum ministerio aliquando tribuitur,quod soli Deo
units.tr: The ministry of the saints is sometimes ascribed to what belongs chiefly to God alone:

units.la: sacipuè conuenit, Matth. 18.v.16.18. Ioan.20.23.Rom.

units.tr: 1 Cor. 6.20–21; 1 Tim. 4.16; James 5.19–20. See ABOVE.

units.la: SVPRA
units.tr: See ABOVE.

units.la: SANCTIS[?] suis Deus laudatur, Psalm.150.1, pro sanctis Christianis semper orandum, Eph.6.18.
units.tr: SAINTS: God is praised in his saints, Ps. 150.1; one must always pray for Christian saints, Eph. 6.18.

units.la: SANCTOS vt nos faceret & mundos, misit Deus Filium suum, Coloss.1.22.
units.tr: SAINTS: God sent his Son to make us holy and clean, Col. 1.22.

units.la: ¶ SANCTOS pro nobis orare, hisce testimoniis probare conantur pontifici, Ierem.15.1 Baruch 3.4.2.Mach.15.14. Apocal.5.8.& 8.3.propter eorum preces & merita, multo Deum nobis largiri, quamuis illi mortui sint, Genes.2 v.5.24.Exod.32.v.13.14.1Reg.11.v.12.13.32.34.& 15.v.4.5. Reg.19.34.& 20.6.Esai.37.35 Eccles 44.24. ¶ Nos pro eosdem invocare & orare sine iniuria Mediatoris, vt pro nobis orent, sicut & petimus ab aliis hominibus preces pro nobis fieri: vt Paulus, Rom.15.30.Coloss.4.3.Ephes.6.19.1 Thess.5.25.2 Thess.3.1.Hebr.13.18. ¶ nec mirum esse, quod sancti preces nostras cognoscant, quia sunt sicut Angeli Dei, Matth.22.30.Luc 15.10. Sed Esaias diversum quam hi docet, qui Abrahamum nescire nos, & Iacobum ignorare nos dicit, Esa. 63.16. ¶ Eos offerre Deo preces nostras, Tob.12.12.Apocal 5.8.& 8.3, nec huic contrarium esse, quod Deus solus est cordis inspector, quia & homines cognoverunt secreta cordium. Deo eis revelante, 2 Reg. 5.26.& 6.12. Dan. 2.29. recte eos a nobis laudari. Eccles 44.1.&c.Ioan 12.26.& in eorum memoriam Deum orandum esse, Genes.32.9.& 48.16.Exod.32.13.Deut.9.27.1 Reg. 18.36.1 Paral.29.18.2 Paral.5.42. Tob.7.15.Esther.13.15. 14.18.Esai.63.17.Dan.3.35. Sanctorum praepositis cultoribus commode obiici potest, Ioan 5.45. Item diabolum impios, cultum Deo debitum sibi vendicare: Matth.4. (vt Darius, Dan.6.8.Haman, Esther.3.2. sapientes huius mundi, Rom.1.23.) Angelos bonos id abhorrere: Apoc. 19.10.& 22.9.Col.2.18. Itemque fideles (vt Petrus & Iohannes sanato claudo Ierosolymis: Act.3.12. Et Petrus Cornelium se adorantem increpans: Act.10.25. Paulus Barnabas sanato Lystris claudo ab omni sacrilegio cavens: Act. 14.8. Iacob obiurgans uxorem quod a Deo, prolem peteret. Genes.30.1. Vide 2. Reg. 5.7.)
units.tr: ¶ SAINTS PRAY FOR US: The Papists try to prove this from these testimonies: Jer. 15.1; Bar. 3.4; 2 Macc. 15.14; Rev. 5.8 and 8.3; that, because of their prayers and merits, God bestows many things on us, although they are dead: Gen. 2.5, 24; Exod. 32.13–14; 1 Kings 11.12–13, 32, 34 and 15.4–5; 2 Kings 19.34 and 20.6; Isa. 37.35; Ecclus. 44.24. ¶ We may invoke and pray to them without injury to the Mediator, that they may pray for us, just as we ask other men to pray for us: as Paul does, Rom. 15.30; Col. 4.3; Eph. 6.19; 1 Thess. 5.25; 2 Thess. 3.1; Heb. 13.18. ¶ Nor is it strange that the saints know our prayers, since they are like the angels of God, Matt. 22.30; Luke 15.10. But Isaiah teaches otherwise, who says that Abraham does not know us and Israel is ignorant of us, Isa. 63.16. ¶ They offer our prayers to God, Tob. 12.12; Rev. 5.8 and 8.3; nor is it contrary to this that God alone is the searcher of hearts, since men too have known the secrets of hearts, God revealing them to them: 2 Kings 5.26 and 6.12; Dan. 2.29. Rightly they are praised by us, Ecclus. 44.1ff.; John 12.26; and God is to be prayed to in their memory: Gen. 32.9 and 48.16; Exod. 32.13; Deut. 9.27; 1 Kings 18.36; 1 Chron. 29.18; 2 Chron. 5.42; Tob. 7.15; Esther 13.15 and 14.18; Isa. 63.17; Dan. 3.35. Against the worship of saints one can fairly object: John 5.45. Likewise, the devil claims for himself the worship due to God, Matt. 4 (as Darius did, Dan. 6.8; Haman, Esther 3.2; the wise men of this world, Rom. 1.23). Good angels abhor this, Rev. 19.10 and 22.9; Col. 2.18. Likewise the faithful (as Peter and John at Jerusalem, when the lame man was healed, Acts 3.12; and Peter, rebuking Cornelius who was worshipping him, Acts 10.25; Paul and Barnabas at Lystra, when the lame man was healed, Acts 14.8, guarding against every sacrilege; Jacob rebuking his wife for asking God for offspring, Gen. 30.1). See 2 Kings 5.7.

units.la: Quia Deus gloriam suam aliis tribui non vult: Esa.42. Quicquid sine fide fit, peccatum est: Rom.14.23. Esi autem Deus solus Schadlai, sibi, suisque sufficiens, omnipotens, ubique praesens: Ps.139.7. Cuius oculis omnia patent, Heb.4.13. Cordium scrutator: 1 Reg.8.39.
units.tr: Because God does not wish his glory given to others, Isa. 42. Whatever is done without faith is sin, Rom. 14.23. God alone is Shaddai, self-sufficient, sufficient for his own, omnipotent, present everywhere, Ps. 139.7; to whose eyes all things lie open, Heb. 4.13; the searcher of hearts, 1 Kings 8.39.

units.la: Homo vero ea tantum videt, quae oculis eius obiiciuntur. 1 S tur.1.Sam.16.7. Defuncti ignorant quæ in terris geruntur:Eccle.9.5.vt Abraham & Israel:Esa.63.16. Psal.27.9.2 Reg 22.20. Vide Act.13.36.quid de Dauide dicatur & Iob. 14.21.
units.tr: Man, however, sees only what is placed before his eyes, 1 Sam. 16.7. The dead do not know what happens on earth, Eccl. 9.5, as Abraham and Israel do not, Isa. 63.16; Ps. 27.9; 2 Kings 22.20. See Acts 13.36 on what is said of David, and Job 14.21.

units.la: Quia nefas est Christum θεανθρωπον suo honore spoliare:Qui vnicus est Dei & hominum mediator: 1 Tim.2.5. Dilectus patri,Mat.3.17.Sacerdos in æternum: Psal.110.4. Ad dextram Dei Patris postulans pro nobis: Rom.8.34. Semen,in quo omnes nationes benedicuntur: Gen.12.3. Per quem solum ad Patrem itur Ioh. 14.6. Ephe.2.17. Quem Apostoli suum etiam vnicum Aduocatum agnouerunt:1.Ioh.2.1. Qui probè nostras infirmitates nouit: Hebr. 4.15. Vbique præsens veris adoratoribus: Matth. 18.20. Qui cùm in æternum maneat, Hebr.7.24.perpetuum habet sacerdotium: Vnde prorsus seruare potest eos,qui per ipsum ad Deum accedunt, semper viuens vt pro eis interpellet.Quia non datum est aliud nomen hominibus,in quo oporteat nos saluos fieri, quàm nomen Iesu:Act.4. Qui sic nos compellat: Venite ad me omnes qui fatigati estis,&c.Matt.11.28.
units.tr: Because it is wrong to strip Christ, the God-man (θεάνθρωπος) [theanthrōpos], of his honour: he alone is the mediator between God and men, 1 Tim. 2.5; beloved of the Father, Matt. 3.17; priest forever, Ps. 110.4; at the right hand of God the Father, interceding for us, Rom. 8.34; the seed in whom all nations are blessed, Gen. 12.3; through whom alone we go to the Father, John 14.6; Eph. 2.17; whom the apostles acknowledged as their only Advocate, 1 John 2.1; who knows our infirmities well, Heb. 4.15; present everywhere to true worshippers, Matt. 18.20. Since he remains forever, Heb. 7.24, he has a perpetual priesthood; hence he is wholly able to save those who come to God through him, living always to intercede for them. For no other name has been given to men by which we must be saved than the name of Jesus, Acts 4. He calls us thus: "Come to me, all you who are weary," etc., Matt. 11.28.

units.la: Quid maledictio iis denuntiatur,qui secus fecerint.Ier. 17.5. Ierem. 2,13. Matth. 10.33. Roman. 1.23. &c. Galat. 5.20.

units.la: ANGVIS pro homine occiso,Iosu.20.5.pro cædis causa, Leuitic.20.9.Iosu.2 10.Iudic.9.24.2 Sam.1.16. 1 Reg.2.38.Ezech.18.13. & 31.4. Actor.18.6 : quibus in locis sanguinis appellatione cum cædis, tum omne exitij genus intelligitur,cuius causa is esse dicitur Hebraeis,cuius (vt ita loquar) capiti imponitur, id est, cui imputatur,quasi ipse suû ipsius sanguiné fundat,& quasi ipse sibi mortem conscisçat.vnde est illa acclamatio Iudæorû, Mat.27.25.cuius sensus est,si quid peccabitur in eo occidendo, nos & posteritas nostra pœnas luamus. Eadem formula, species quædam obtestationis est,apud Lucam, Actor.18.6. quasi dicat Paulus, video vos in perniciem vestram ruere: ego igitur hic Deum coram vobis testor,non me, sed vos vobis ipsis causam esse exitij:vt & Dauid loquitur,2 Samu.16.pro cæde,1 Reg.2.5.2 Reg 9.7.Psalm.106.38.Esa.1 15.& 9.4.& 26.21. & 33.15. Ezech. 5.17. & 14 19. Ose.1.4.& 4.2. Mich.7.2.Abac.2.v.8.12.pro suppliciis capitalibus,Psalm. 51.16 pro impura naicentis hominis origine, Ioann. 1.13. pro cognatione, Actor.17. 26. Præterea sanguinis & carnis appellatione, in scriptura sacra interdum intelligitur solum corpus, idque non nudum, sed cum infirmitate adiuncta, 1 Corinth.15.50. ut apparet ex eo quod subiicitur de corruptione: interdum vero totus homo, corpore & anima constans, quatenus est corruptus peccato, Matth.16.17. Galat.1.16. sanguis omnis bruti anima est, Leuit.17. ver.11. 14. sanguis innoxius ex Hebraeorum idiotismo dicitur, homo insons, Matth.27.4. sanguis innoxius ad Deum clamare dicitur, Genes.4.10. 4. Esdr.15.8. Hebr.12.4. Apocalyp.6.10. sanguis iustus cum venire super caput aliquorum dicitur, nihil aliud est, quam reos & obnoxios esse, vel in caput eorum redundare sanguinem iustum, Matth.23.35. sanguis non comedendus ante Messiae regnum Genes.9.4. Leuit.3.17. & 7.26. & 17.10. & 19.26. Deuteron.12. vers.16.23. & 15.23.1 Sam.14.32. eius vi Christi adventu concessus, propter fratrum infirmitatem ad tempus prohibetur, Act.15.v.20.29. & 21.25. sanguinis Achab a canibus lingitur, 1 Reg.22.38. sanguis foederis, Exod.24.8. Hebr.9.20. sanguis & aqua, e Christi latere fluunt, Ioan.19.34. sanguis Christi, Vide CHRISTVS. & Ioh.5.6.
units.tr: BLOOD for a man slain: Josh. 20.5; for the cause of a killing: Lev. 20.9; Josh. 2.10; Judg. 9.24; 2 Sam. 1.16; 1 Kings 2.38; Ezek. 18.13 and 31.4; Acts 18.6. In these places, by the term "blood" is understood both the killing and every kind of destruction, of which the one who is guilty is said by the Hebrews to be the cause; and upon whose head (so to speak) it is laid, that is, to whom it is imputed, as though he himself shed his own blood and as though he himself brought about his own death. Hence that cry of the Jews, Matt. 27.25, whose sense is: if anything is wrongly done in killing him, we and our posterity will bear the punishment. The same formula is a kind of solemn appeal in Luke, Acts 18.6, as if Paul were saying: I see you rushing to your own destruction; therefore I here call God to witness before you that I am not the cause of your ruin, but you are yourselves; as David also speaks, 2 Sam. 1.16. For the murder: 1 Kings 2.5; 2 Kings 9.7; Ps. 106.38; Isa. 1.15 and 9.4 and 26.21 and 33.15; Ezek. 5.17 and 14.19; Hos. 1.4 and 4.2; Mic. 7.2; Hab. 2.8, 12. For capital punishments: Ps. 51.16. For the impure origin of the man being born: John 1.13. For kinship: Acts 17.26. Moreover, by the terms "flesh and blood" in Holy Scripture is sometimes understood only the body, and that not bare but with its infirmity joined to it, 1 Cor. 15.50, as appears from what follows about corruption; but sometimes the whole man, consisting of body and soul, insofar as he is corrupted by sin, Matt. 16.17; Gal. 1.16. "The blood of every beast is its life," Lev. 17.11, 14. "Innocent blood" is said, by the Hebrew idiom, of an innocent man, Matt. 27.4. "Innocent blood" is said to cry out to God, Gen. 4.10; 4 Ezra 15.8; Heb. 12.24; Rev. 6.10. When "righteous blood" is said to come upon the head of some, it means nothing other than that they are guilty and liable, or that the righteous blood returns upon their head, Matt. 23.35. Blood was not to be eaten before the kingdom of the Messiah, Gen. 9.4; Lev. 3.17 and 7.26 and 17.10 and 19.26; Deut. 12.16, 23 and 15.23; 1 Sam. 14.32. By the power of Christ's coming, this was permitted, but for the time being it is forbidden on account of the weakness of the brethren, Acts 15.20, 29 and 21.25. The blood of Ahab was licked by dogs, 1 Kings 22.38. "The blood of the covenant," Exod. 24.8; Heb. 9.20. Blood and water flowed from the side of Christ, John 19.34. For the blood of Christ, see CHRIST; and John 5.6.

units.tr: SPRINKLING OF BLOOD: Exod. 24.6 and 29.20; Lev. 1.5, 11; 3.2, 8, 13; 4.6, 16; 7.2; 8.19, 30; 9.18; 16.14, 18; 17.6; 2 Chron. 30.16; Ezek. 43.20; Heb. 9.14, 19, 21, 22. Sprinkling of the blood of Christ: Heb. 9.14, 19; 12.24; 1 Pet. 1.2. The shedding of innocent blood: Deut. 19.5, 11; 27.24; 2 Sam. 20.9; 1 Kings 21.13; 2 Kings 21.16; 24.4; 2 Chron. 24.22; Prov. 6.17; 28.17; Isa. 26.21; Jer. 7.6 and 22.3; Ezek. 22.4; 4 Ezra 1.32; Matt. 23.34–35; Luke 11.50; Rev. 6.10 and 18.24. It cries out for vengeance before God, Gen. 4.10; 4 Ezra 15.8; Heb. 12.24; Rev. 10. The flow of blood is stopped, Matt. 9.20. See MIRACLES.

units.tr: WE ARE BOUGHT WITH THE BLOOD OF CHRIST: 1 Cor. 6.20 and 7.23; Acts 20.28; 1 Pet. 1.18–19; Rev. 5.9.

units.tr: SAPH: the giant was slain, 1 Chron. 2 Sam. 21.18 (i.e., a basin, a bowl).

units.la: SAPHAN, templi scriba, 2 Reg.12.3. a Iosia ad Helciam pontificem mittitur, v.4. legis librum, ab Helcia repertum, legit, v.8.
units.tr: SAPHAN, scribe of the temple, 2 Kings 12.3, was sent by Josiah to the high priest Hilkiah, v. 4; he read the book of the law, found by Hilkiah, v. 8.

units.tr: [WISE] God is wise. See GOD. Christ is wise, Jer. 23. See CHRIST. A wise man, that is, prudent, Gen. 41; Deut. 1.13. Wise, a wisdom falsely so called, endowed with...

units.tr: Exod. 7.22; Esther 6.13; Isa. 9.11–12. A wise teacher, Eccl. 8.16. Industrious, Exod. 35.10. Intelligent, Prov. 17.2. Just, Prov. 10.11. Skilled, 1 Cor. 3.10. Elders, Exod. 18.21–22; 2 Sam. 23.8.

units.la: Sapientes, Apostoli, Matt.23 34.
units.tr: Wise men, the apostles, Matt. 23.34.

units.la: Sapientia Æterna, Filius Dei, Prou.8.v.1 12.& 9. 1.Matt. 11.19. Luc.11.49. 1 Cor 1 v.24 30.
units.tr: Eternal Wisdom, the Son of God, Prov. 8.1–12 and 9.1; Matt. 11.19; Luke 11.49; 1 Cor. 1.24, 30.

units.la: Sapientia Dei, Iob 12 13. Psal.m.104.24. & 147.5. Esai.40, 28 Ierem.10.12. Roman.11.33. 1 Corinth.1.21. & 2.7. Ephes. 3.10.

Sapientia, à Deo hominibus gratiosè collata, quæ circa vitæ præsentis vsum & æternæ felicitatis apprehensionem versatur. Cui opposita est falsò nominata Sapientia mundi, quæ humana etiam & sensualis nominatur; Deut.4.6.1 Reg.2.6.&4.29. Iob.12.2, Psal.107.27. Prou.17. verf.6 24. Eccles.1.16. &c. Esai.10 13. & 47.10. Ierem.8.9. Dan.1.4 &c. Matth.12.42. Actor.7.10; Coloss.2.23. 1 Cor. 1.17.
units.tr: Wisdom, graciously bestowed by God on human beings, which is concerned with the use of the present life and the grasping of eternal happiness. Opposed to it is the falsely named wisdom of the world, which is also called human and sensual. Deut. 4:6; 1 Kings 2:6; 4:29; Job 12:2; Ps. 107:27; Prov. 17:6, 24; Eccles. 1:16, etc.; Isa. 10:13; 47:10; Jer. 8:9; Dan. 1:4, etc.; Matt. 12:42; Acts 7:10; Col. 2:23; 1 Cor. 1:17.

units.la: Sapientia carnis, mundi, humana, sensualis, terrena: quo nomine proprie intellig tur acumen illud ingenij humani, Vanitati & corruptioni suæ relicti, diuinæque sap entiæ & voluntati superbè reluctantis, Esai.29 14. Ierem.49. 7. Ezec.28.v.4 5 &c. Rom.8.7. 1 Cor.1.19 & 2.4. 2 Cor.1.12, Iacob.3.15.
units.tr: Wisdom of the flesh, of the world, human, sensual, earthly. By this name is properly understood that keenness of human intellect which is left to its own vanity and corruption and proudly resists divine wisdom and will. Isa. 29:14; Jer. 49:7; Ezek. 28:4-5, etc.; Rom. 8:7; 1 Cor. 1:19; 2:4; 2 Cor. 1:12; James 3:15.

units.la: Sapientia Christi, i.quæ in Christo vero homine eluxit, qua eius anima prædita est, Matth.3.54. Marc 6 2. Luc.2. v.40.52. Sapientia Christo glorificato tributa, Coloss.2.3. Apoc.5.12.
units.tr: Wisdom of Christ, that is, which shone forth in Christ the true man, with which his soul was endowed. Matt. 3:54; Mark 6:2; Luke 2:40, 52. Wisdom ascribed to Christ in his glorified state. Col. 2:3; Rev. 5:12.

units.la: Sapientia, membris & Christi ministris sub Euangelio gratis concessa, Luc.21.15 Act.6.v.3. 10.1 Corin.2.6.&12.8. Eph 1.v.8 17. Iacob.3.17. 2 Per.3.15. Apoc.17.9.
units.tr: Wisdom, freely granted under the Gospel to the members of Christ and to his ministers. Luke 21:15; Acts 6:3; 10:1; 1 Cor. 2:6; 12:8; Eph. 1:8, 17; James 3:17; 2 Pet. 3:15; Rev. 17:9.

units.la: Sapientia, peritia, Exo.cap.31.3.6. 1 Reg.7.14.]
units.tr: Wisdom, skill. Exod. 31:3, 6; 1 Kings 7:14.

units.la: SAPIENS pro astuto, 2 Sam. 14.2. sapientis & stulti collatio, Eccles.6.8. sapiens audit consilia & gaudet argui, Prou.13. & 25.12. sapiens vir artificiosus, Exo.28.3.& 35.10. sapientes in bono, Rom.16.19: sui amantes, Prou.26.12.
units.tr: WISE, meaning shrewd. A comparison of the wise and the foolish. 2 Sam. 14:2; Eccles. 6:8. The wise man hears counsels and rejoices to be reproved, Prov. 13; 25:12. A wise man, skilled in craft, Exod. 28:3; 35:10. Wise in what is good, Rom. 16:19. Lovers of themselves, Prov. 26:12.

units.la: SAPIAMVS, sed non alta, Rom.11.25. quomodo sapiendum, 2.3 vt sapiant Iudæi, optat Deus, Deut.32.29.
units.tr: Let us be wise, but not high-minded, Rom. 11:25. How one ought to be wise. God desires that the Jews be wise, Deut. 32:29.

units.la: SAPIENTIA vera quæ, Iob.28.28. Psalm.107.47.1.10. Prouerb.1.7.&28.7. Ierem.9.23.1 Corin h.1.31.2. Corint. 2.11. Roman.16.19. Ephes.5.15. Philipp.1.9.10. Coloss.1. 3.& 4.5. Hebr.8.11, Iac.1.5. & 3.17. sapientia vera, donum
units.tr: True wisdom, which is... Job 28:28; Ps. 107:47; 1:10; Prov. 1:7; 28:7; Jer. 9:23; 1 Cor. 1:31; 2 Cor. 2:11; Rom. 16:19; Eph. 5:15; Phil. 1:9-10; Col. 1:3; 4:5; Heb. 8:11; James 1:5; 3:17. True wisdom is the gift of God.

Iac.1.5. sapientia iustificata,& à quibus,Luc.7. 35.Vide IVSTIFICARE. sapientia fortitudini praestat, Ec-clesi 9.v.16.17.18.sapientia nulla contra Dominum, Prou. 21 30.sapientia carnis damnatur,Rom.8.7. sapientia fidelium. Vide FIDELIVM sapientia. sapientia mundi huius vana & mera stultitia,idóque fugienda, Iob.5.13 Prouerb. 3 7.Esai.44.25.Ierem.4.22.Roma.1.22.& 11.25.& 12.v.3.16. 1 Cor.1.v.19.20.& 2.v.5.6.& 3.19.20 2 Corint.1.12.Iac.3.15. sapientia mulierum,Vide MVLIERVM sapientia. sapientia sermonis,pro eloquentia,1 Corint 1.17.sapientia terrena, animalis & diabolica,Iac.3.15.
units.tr: The gift of God, 1 Kings 3:9, 12; 4:29; 2 Chron. 9:23; Prov. 2:6; Dan. 2:20-21; James 1:5. Wisdom justified, and by whom, Luke 7:35. See JUSTIFY. Wisdom is better than strength, Eccles. 9:16-18. No wisdom against the Lord, Prov. 21:30. The wisdom of the flesh is condemned, Rom. 8:7. The wisdom of believers. See FAITHFUL, wisdom. The wisdom of this world is vanity and sheer folly, and so is to be shunned: Job 5:13; Prov. 3:7; Isa. 44:25; Jer. 4:22; Rom. 1:22; 11:25; 12:3, 16; 1 Cor. 1:19-20; 2:5-6; 3:19-20; 2 Cor. 1:12; James 3:15. The wisdom of women. See WOMEN, wisdom of. Wisdom of speech, that is, eloquence, 1 Cor. 1:17. Earthly, animal and diabolical wisdom, James 3:15.

units.la: SAPIENTIAE verae praestantia,Prouerb.3.v.13. 14. & 8. 12. & 16.16 Iac.3.17.sapientiae contemptus,mors est,Prouerb.8. versi.36.sapientiae diuinae origo,proprietas, laus, & vtilitas.Deut.4.6. & 29. 9. Prouerb. 1.7. sapientiae & stultitiae discrimen, Eccles 2 13.
units.tr: WISDOM The excellence of true wisdom, Prov. 3:13-14; 8:12; 16:16; James 3:17. The contempt of wisdom is death, Prov. 8:36. The origin, property, praise and usefulness of divine wisdom: Deut. 4:6; 29:9; Job 28:20; 32:7; Eccles. 7:12; 9:13; Luke 21:15; Rom. 11:33; 1 Cor. 1:17; 2:6; 3:19; Col. 2:3; James 1:5; 3:15. The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, Ps. 111:10; Prov. 1:7. The distinction between wisdom and folly, Eccles. 2:13.

units.la: SAPPHIRA,mendacij mariti conscia,Act.5.1.2.mendacium iterat,v.7.8.9.Ob id Petri voce obiurgata expirat, ver.10. (Syriace,1.formosa.)
units.tr: SAPPHIRA, party to her husband's lie, Acts 5:1-2. She repeats the lie, v. 7-9. For this, rebuked by Peter's word, she expires, v. 10. (In Syriac, beautiful.)

units.la: SARAI vxor Abraham,Genef.11.29.pulchra mulier est, 12.v. 11.14.nominatur Sara, 17.15. negat se risisse, 18. 15. eripitur Abrahae,20.2.quomodo Abrahae soror sit,v 12. sterilis, fide concepit,Hebr.11.11.filium Isaac lactat, Genef.21.7. fidelium mulierum mater est,1 Pet.3.6.Vixit 127.ann.& obiit,Gen.23.1.2.marito suo obediens,Dominum eum vocabat.1 Pet.3.6.(Sarah.i.domina,princeps.)
units.tr: SARAI, wife of Abraham, Gen. 11:29. She is a beautiful woman, 12:11, 14. She is named Sarah, 17:15. She denies that she laughed, 18:15. She is snatched from Abraham, 20:2. How she is Abraham's sister, v. 12. Barren, she conceived by faith, Heb. 11:11. She nursed Isaac, Gen. 21:7. She is the mother of believing women, 1 Pet. 3:6. She lived 127 years and died, Gen. 23:1-2. She was obedient to her husband and called him lord, 1 Pet. 3:6. (Sarah means lady, princess.)

units.la: SARAIAS,princeps Prophetiae,Ier.51.59.sacerdos occiditur, 52.27.(.i. Canticum Domini.)
units.tr: SARAIAH, chief of the prophecy, Jer. 51:59. A priest is slain, 52:27. (That is, the Song of the Lord.)

units.la: SARVIA filia Isai,soror Dauidis,genuit Abisai, Ioab, & Asahel,2 Sam 2.18,1 Paral.2.16.quos timet Dauid,2 Sam.3 39 & 16.10. &19.22. Tseruja legitur.
units.tr: SERUIAH, daughter of Jesse, sister of David, bore Abishai, Joab and Asahel, 2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chron. 2:16. David feared them, 2 Sam. 3:39; 16:10; 19:22. Zeruiah is the form read.

units.la: SATANAS, Vide DIABOLVS satanae nomen etiam hominibus accommodatur,qui Dei voluntati aduersantur, vel obstinata malitia, (vt Iudas,diabolus,Ioan.6,70.) vel in cogitantia quadam aut arrogantia,vt Petrus Matth.16.23 sasanae tradi,1 Cor.5.3.1 Tim.1.20. nihil aliud est, quam fieri sicut ethnicum & publicanum , Matt.18.17.id est, in Christianae ciuitatis vsque ad resipiscentiam amittere, ue excommunicari, satanæ denique mancipari, qui extra Ecclesiam regnat. satanas, Deus huius seculi dicitur, 2 Corint. 4. 4. quia sese illi veluti Deo mancipárunt homines huius seculi. A Deo impetrata facultate, percutit Iobum, Iob. 1. 12. est spiritus mendax in ore omnium Prophetarum Achab, 1 Reguni 22.22. Apostolos appetiverat, &c. Luc 22.31. in Iudam proditorem ingreditur, 22.3. vt fulgur è cœlo cadit, Luc. 10.18. in Angelum lucis transformatur, 2 Cor. 11.14. Colaphis cædit Paulum, 12.7. impedit Paulũ, 1 Thess. 2 18 (satan. i. aduersarius, 1 Pet. 5.8.)
units.tr: SATAN. See DEVIL. The name of Satan is also applied to men who oppose the will of God, either through obstinate malice (as Judas, the devil, John 6:70), or through some presumption or arrogance (as Peter, Matt. 16:23). To be delivered to Satan, 1 Cor. 5:3; 1 Tim. 1:20, means nothing other than to be treated as a heathen and a tax collector, Matt. 18:17, that is, to lose the status of a Christian commonwealth until repentance, or to be excommunicated, and finally to be handed over to Satan, who reigns outside the Church. Satan is called the god of this age, 2 Cor. 4:4, because men of this age have given themselves over to him as to a god. With permission obtained from God he struck Job, Job 1:12. He is a lying spirit in the mouth of all the prophets of Ahab, 1 Kings 22:22. He had sought to have the apostles, Luke 22:31, etc. He entered into Judas the betrayer, 22:3. He fell like lightning from heaven, Luke 10:18. He is transformed into an angel of light, 2 Cor. 11:14. He struck Paul with blows, 12:7. He hindered Paul, 1 Thess. 2:18. (Satan means adversary, 1 Pet. 5:8.)

units.la: SATIATI, ne obliuiscamur Dei, Deuter. 8. v. 10 11. 1 Corinth. 10.30.
units.tr: SATIATED, lest we forget God, Deut. 8:10-11; 1 Cor. 10:30.

units.la: Satietas piorum, & impiorum dissimilis: Psal. 17.14 15. & 107.8.9. satiatur terrae cultor Pro. 12.11.
units.tr: The satiety of the pious and of the impious is unlike. Ps. 17:14-15; 107:8-9. The tiller of the land is satisfied, Prov. 12:11.

units.la: SATIETAS à Deo impiis negatur, Iob. 20.7. Hos. 28. Mich. 6. 14. Agg. 1.6. satietas vitanda. Prouerb. 25.16. V. Mat. 5.6. Luc. 1.53.
units.tr: SATIETY is denied by God to the impious, Job 20:7; Hos. 2:8; Mic. 6:14; Hag. 1:6. Satiety is to be avoided, Prov. 25:16. See Matt. 5:6; Luke 1:53.

units.la: SATISFACTIONES Papisticæ stabiliuntur, vt satisfactores isti putant, Col. 1.24. (Vide PVRGATORIVM) evertuntur, Roman. 4.5. & 14.6. 2 Corinth. 5. v. 20. 21. Galat. 1.4. Coloss. 1.14. 1 Tim. 2.6. 1 Ioan. 4.10. (V. GRATIA: & REDEMTOR: & PVRGATORIVM.)
units.tr: PAPAL SATISFACTIONS are upheld, as these satisfiers suppose, Col. 1:24. (See PURGATORY.) They are overthrown, Rom. 4:5; 14:6; 2 Cor. 5:20-21; Gal. 1:4; Col. 1:14; 1 Tim. 2:6; 1 John 4:10. (See GRACE, REDEEMER and PURGATORY.)

units.la: SATVRAT Deus obedientes, Deut. 11. 15. saturati ne Dei obliuiscamur, Deu. 6. vers. 11. 12. saturatus Israel relinquit Deum, 32.15. (saturis væ, & quare, Luc. 6.25.) V. Ier. 5.7.
units.tr: God satisfies the obedient, Deut. 11:15. Lest we forget God when we are satisfied, Deut. 6:11-12. Israel satiated forsakes God, 32:15. (Woe to the full, and why, Luke 6:25.) See Jer. 5:7.

units.la: SATVARI, Phil. 4.12. & inebriari, Gen. 43.34. Esa. 55.10. Iere. 31.25. Hebraeorum more non significat ingurgitare, sed tantum sumere, quantum satis est.
units.tr: To be satisfied, Phil. 4:12, and to be drunk, Gen. 43:34; Isa. 55:10; Jer. 31:25. In the Hebrew manner, this does not mean to gorge oneself, but only to take as much as is enough.

units.la: SAVL filius Cis, quærit asinas patris, 1 Sam. 9.3. vngitur in regem, 10.1. prophetat, 10,10. & 19.23. percutit Philistheos, 13.4. offerens holocaustum peccat, v. 11. Domino altare extruit, 14.35. reseruato Agag, in Deum peccat, 15.8. regno expellitur, v. 23. à spiritu nequam exagitatur, 16 14. & 18. 10. Dauidem timet, ver. 12. eum occidi iuber, 19.1. in Ionathan filium, Dauidis causa excandescit, 20 30. sacerdotes occisi iubet, 22.18. in desertum Maon Dauidem persequitur, 23.25. Pythonissam adit, 28 8 seipsum interficit, 31.4. 1 Parali. 10.4. cur à Deo occisus, v. 13. eius ossa à viris Iabes Galaad sepeliuntur, 1 Sam. 31.13. à Dauide fletur, 2 Sam. 1. v. 12 17. filij eius in crucem aguntur, 2 Sam. 21.9.
units.tr: SAUL, son of Kish, seeks his father's donkeys, 1 Sam. 9:3. He is anointed king, 10:1. He prophesies, 10:10; 19:23. He strikes the Philistines, 13:4. Offering a burnt offering, he sins, v. 11. He builds an altar to the Lord, 14:35. Sparing Agag, he sins against God, 15:8. He is expelled from the kingship, v. 23. He is troubled by an evil spirit, 16:14; 18:10. He fears David, v. 12. He orders him killed, 19:1. He grows furious against Jonathan his son, because of David, 20:30. He orders the priests slain, 22:18. He pursues David into the wilderness of Maon, 23:25. He consults a medium, 28:8. He kills himself, 31:4; 1 Chron. 10:4. Why he was slain by God, 1 Chron. 10:13. His bones are buried by the men of Jabesh Gilead, 1 Sam. 31:13. He is mourned by David, 2 Sam. 1:12-17. His sons are hanged on a gibbet, 2 Sam. 21:9.

units.la: SAVL de Rehoboth, rex Edom. [Gen. 36.37 31. Par. 1. v. 48.49
units.tr: SAUL of Rehoboth, king of Edom. [Gen. 36:37; 1 Chron. 1:48-49.]

units.la: [Nepos Caathi, 1 Parali. 6.24. Nepos Iacobi ex Simeone. G n.46.10 Exo.6 15.Num 26.13.1 Par.4.24 Saulitæ,Num. 26.33 ..postulatus,vocatus.
units.tr: [Grandson of Kohath, 1 Chron. 6:24. Grandson of Jacob through Simeon, Gen. 46:10; Exod. 6:15; Num. 26:13; 1 Chron. 4:24. Saulites, Num. 26:33. Asked for, called.]

units.la: SAVLVS qui & Paulus, Act.7 58 & 9 1 &c. (Vide PAVLVS.)
units.tr: SAUL, who is also Paul, Acts 7:58; 9:1, etc. (See PAUL.)

units.la: [SCABELLVM pedum Dei,1 Par.28.2 Psal.99 5. Esa.66 1.Thre. 2.1 Matt.5 5 Act.7 49.Scabellum pedum Christi,Ecclesiæ regis,Psal.110 1 Matt.22 44. Act.2.35 Hcb.1 13. & 10.13. Scabellum pedum hominis,2 Para.9.18. Iacob.2 3.]
units.tr: [The footstool of God's feet, 1 Chron. 28:2; Ps. 99:5; Isa. 66:1; Lam. 2:1; Matt. 5:35; Acts 7:49. The footstool of Christ, King of the Church, Ps. 110:1; Matt. 22:44; Acts 2:35; Heb. 1:13; 10:13. The footstool of man, 2 Chron. 9:18; James 2:3.]

units.la: SCABIE percutiuntur inobedientes,Deut.28.27. [V.Leu.13. 6 & 21.20.Exod.9.9.10.11.Ioh.2.7.]
units.tr: With scab the disobedient are struck, Deut. 28:27. [See Lev. 13:6; 21:20; Exod. 9:9-11; John 2:7.]

units.la: SCALA vita Iacobo,Gen.28.12. V.Ioh.1.51.
units.tr: A LADDER, life to Jacob, Gen. 28:12. See John 1:51.

units.la: SCANDALVM acceptum, est actio, qua alius inducitur ad peccandum,vel in ruinam,praeter intentionem operantis & naturam ipsius actionis. Datum offendiculum est omne,quod opere vel dicto fit,praeter Legem Dei, per quod alius vel ad male agendum inducitur,vel ab officio retardatur.Mar.6 23 Scandala pro reprobis.Matt.13 41.42.
units.tr: SCANDAL taken is an action by which another is led into sin or into ruin, beyond the intention of the agent and the nature of the action itself. An offence given is anything done by deed or word, contrary to the Law of God, by which another is either induced to do evil or is held back from his duty. Mark 6:23. Scandals for the reprobate, Matt. 13:41-42.

units.la: SCANDALVM seu offendiculum proximo nec in vita, nec in doctrina ponendum.Leuit.4 3.Num.3 .16. 2 Sam.2.14.1 Esdr.8.22. Prov.28 10.2 Mach.6 24. Matth.17.27.& 18.6. Marc 9.43. Luc.17.1 Ioan.16.1 Rom.14.v.1.15.1 Cor.8,9.10. 32.2.Cor.6.3. 1 Thess.5.22.
units.tr: Scandal or offence to a neighbour is to be given neither in life nor in doctrine. Lev. 4:3; Num. 3:16; 2 Sam. 2:14; 1 Esd. 8:22; Prov. 28:10; 2 Macc. 6:24; Matt. 17:27; 18:6; Mark 9:43; Luke 17:1; John 16:1; Rom. 14:1, 15; 1 Cor. 8:9-10, 32; 2 Cor. 6:3; 1 Thess. 5:22.

units.la: SCANDALI ex Christo occasionem capere, valde noxium. Luc.7.23 scandali Pharisaici sive accepti exempla: Quidam scribæ,Matth 9.v 2 3. Pharisæi,v.10.11.& 15 12.Ioan.7,ver. 45.52. Act 9.14:Iudæi,Marc.6 3 Ioan.5.v.17 18.& 6. verfic. 51.52.& 7.v.41.46 & 8.v 44 48.56.57 58 59. Act.11. ver.2.3. quidam Iudæi,Act.13 v.44.43 44.45 & 28.v.28 29: Nazareni, Matth 13.57. Marc.6 3.Pharisæi & Scribæ,Luc.15.2: quidam ex discipulis,Ioan 6.60. Concilium Ierosolymitanum,Actor.4. v 2 3.4 5. Scandali dati exempla:Petrus, Matth.16.23.Gal.2.11 Zimri,Nob.25 6.Dauid, 2 Sam.11,2. & 12 14.sin Heli, 1 Samu. 2. 24. Scandali vitati Exempla: Christus & Petrus,Matt.17.27.Paulus,Act.16.3 & 21. ver. 24.26.quicunque scandalo esse nobis possunt, vitandi. Exodus 34.12 Deuter.7.v.2 16.& 13.1.&c.Matth.5.20 & 16.22. Marc.9 42.Rom 16.17.V.Mat.5 29 30.
units.tr: To take occasion of scandal from Christ is very harmful, Luke 7:23. Examples of Pharisaic scandal, or of scandal taken: Certain scribes, Matt. 9:2-3. Pharisees, v. 10-11; 15:12; John 7:45-52; Acts 9:14. Jews, Mark 6:3; John 5:17-18; 6:51-52; 7:41-46; 8:44-59; Acts 11:2-3. Certain Jews, Acts 13:44-45; 28:28-29. The Nazarenes, Matt. 13:57; Mark 6:3. Pharisees and scribes, Luke 15:2. Certain of the disciples, John 6:60. The Council of Jerusalem, Acts 4:2-5. Examples of scandal given: Peter, Matt. 16:23; Gal. 2:11. Zimri, Num. 25:6. David, 2 Sam. 11:2; 12:14. The sins of Eli, 1 Sam. 2:24. Examples of scandal avoided: Christ and Peter, Matt. 17:27. Paul, Acts 16:3; 21:24, 26. Whoever can be a scandal to us is to be avoided. Exod. 34:12; Deut. 7:2, 16; 13:1, etc.; Matt. 5:20; 16:22; Mark 9:42; Rom. 16:17. See Matt. 5:29-30.

units.la: SCELERVM praeteritorum memoria,Iosu.22.17.
units.tr: The memory of past crimes, Josh. 22.17.

units.la: SCENOPEGIÆ solennitas,Ioan.7.2. scenopegiæ oblationes, Ezech.45.25. Erat dies festus, qui die 15. mensis septimi celebrabatur,ad memoriam conseruationis populi in tabernaculis deserti commemorantis, & gratiarum actionem pro terra promissa ipsis tradita, & pro annuis frugibus bus colle&tis:Deut.16. (Σκηνοπηγία. i. tabernaculorum struc-tura.)
units.tr: The solemnity of Scenopegia, John 7.2. Scenopegia offerings, Ezek. 45.25. This was a festival day, celebrated on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, in memory of the preservation of the people who dwelt in tabernacles in the wilderness, and in thanksgiving for the promised land given to them and for the annual harvest gathered in, Deut. 16. (Scenopegia [Σκηνοπηγία], that is, the building of tabernacles.)

units.la: ΣΚΕΝΟΦΑCTORIAM artem exercet Paulus, Actor.18.3. Sceptrum, metonymice dominatio, Gen.49.10.Ier.51.19. Abac.3.14, Zach.10.11.]
units.tr: Paul practised the craft of tent-making [σκηνοποιία], Acts 18.3. Sceptre, by metonymy, dominion, Gen. 49.10, Jer. 51.19, Hab. 3.14, Zech. 10.11.

units.la: EVA Iudæus, Actor.19.14. Cuius filij exorcistæ à satana venerati sunt: ibid.&c.
units.tr: Sceva the Jew, Acts 19.14. Whose sons, exorcists, were assailed by Satan, ibid., etc.

units.la: HADDAI (i.qui à seipso sufficiens sit) dicitur Deus,17.1.& 35.11.
units.tr: HADDAI (that is, the one who is self-sufficient) is said of God, Gen. 17.1 and 35.11.

units.la: SHIBBOLETH (i.est, fluxus fluminis) ut accipitur Iudic.12. 6.Psal.69.3 & Esa.27.12. Sibboleth verò, est vox corrupta e blæsa Ephraimitarum pronuntiatione, nihil per se significans, ex cuius vocis pronuntiatione deprehenduntur & cæduntur Ephraimitæ, Iosu.12.6.
units.tr: SHIBBOLETH (that is, a flowing of a river), as it is taken in Judg. 12.6, Ps. 69.3 and Isa. 27.12. Sibboleth, however, is a word corrupted by the lisping pronunciation of the Ephraimites, meaning nothing in itself; by the pronunciation of this word the Ephraimites were detected and slain, Josh. 12.6.

units.la: SCHISMATA cauenda, 1 Cor.10.& 33.& 11.18.& 12.v.25.Heb. 10.25. schismaticus arguitur, Prouer.6.12. Est autem Schisma, cum qui in doctrina alioqui consentiunt, tamen sese ab aliis seiungunt: 1 Cor.1.12.13. V. Secta Ioh.7.43.
units.tr: SCHISMS are to be avoided, 1 Cor. 10 and 33, 11.18, 12.25, Heb. 10.25. A schismatic is condemned in Prov. 6.12. A schism is when people who otherwise agree in doctrine nevertheless separate themselves from others, 1 Cor. 1.12, 13. See SECT, John 7.43.

units.la: SCHOLA: Scholarum & Academiarum institutarum exemplar in veteri testamento. I. Samuel Heli discipulus, Samuel apud Heli sacerdotem versabatur, 1 Sam.3.1.
units.tr: SCHOOL: the pattern of established schools and academies in the Old Testament. I. Samuel, a disciple of Eli: Samuel lived with Eli the priest, 1 Sam. 3.1.

units.la: II. grex Prophetarum, 10.5, & 19.20. III. puer Elisæi, 2 Reg.9.1. Ex quibus patet, in veteri etiam testamento fuisse locum quendam publicum & personas, à quibus iuuentus in vera fide & pietate informaretur. In novo testamento: IV. duodecim Apostoli, Luc.6.13. Christus enim, vnicus generis humani saluator & Doctor, non abrogauit scholas alias visitatas, in quibus iuuentus rudimenta artium didicit, sed Theologicam scholam ipse tamen penes se habuit, distinctam ab auditoribus, quibus aliàs sinceram Dei doctrinam tradebat: peculiariter enim vocabat duodecim, quos & Apostolos, propter officium quod gesturi erant, nominabat, Luc.6.13. aliàs etiam passim discipuli dicantur. Eos verò non habebat in vno loco, sicut nec ipse in vno loco commorabatur, nam per totam Iudæam innotescere debebat: sed quocunque iter faciebat, secum ducebat, ita vt neglectis suis vocationibus prioribus, Christo tantùm adhærere cogerentur. V. septuaginta discipuli, Luc.10.1. Præter duodecim Apostolos, etiam septuaginta eligebat Christus discipulos, qui in sua schola enutriri, & donis miraculorum ornati & instructi, ablegabantur, Luc. 10.1. vt passim in IudæaEuangelium Christi prædicarent.
units.tr: II. The company of prophets, 1 Sam. 10.5 and 19.20. III. The servant of Elisha, 2 Kings 9.1. From these it is clear that in the Old Testament too there was a certain public place and certain persons by whom young people were instructed in the true faith and piety. In the New Testament: IV. The twelve apostles, Luke 6.13. For Christ, the only Saviour and Teacher of the human race, did not abolish the other schools in use, in which young people learned the rudiments of the arts; but he himself kept a theological school with himself, distinct from the hearers to whom he otherwise taught the sound doctrine of God. For he specially called the twelve, whom he also named apostles because of the office they were to hold, Luke 6.13, and elsewhere they are called disciples in general. He did not keep them in one place, just as he himself did not stay in one place, for he was to become known throughout all Judea. Rather, wherever he went he took them with him, so that, neglecting their former callings, they were compelled to cling to Christ alone. V. The seventy disciples, Luke 10.1. Besides the twelve apostles, Christ also chose seventy disciples, who were trained in his school, adorned and equipped with gifts of miracles, and sent out, Luke 10.1, to preach the gospel of Christ throughout Judea.

units.la: VI. discipuli Ioannis, Ioann. 1. 28. Ioannes Baptist quoque habuit schölam, in qua præ aliis quosdam discipulos habuit, quos in vera doctrina instituit. Patet ex Ioan. 1.28. vbi duobus discipulis, quorum vnus erat Andreas, frater Simonis Petri, Ioannes concionatur de Christo: Ecce agnus Dei: idem testatur historia, quòd duo Ioannis discipuli sint ad Christum missi, quæsitum an Iesus esset Messias Matth. 11. 2. VII. Schola Ierosolymitana, verf. 15. Scholam aliquam fuisse Ierosolymis, in qua iuuentus in studiis præsertim sacrarum literarum informabatur, vel inde colligi promtum est, quòd Pharisæi etiam suos habuerint discipulos, Matth. 22. verf. 15. 16. VIII. Paulus Gamalielis discipulus, Actor. 22.3. vbi commemorat ipsemet Paulus, se ad pedes Gamalielis Legis doctoris diligenter in patria lege institutum esse. IX. Synagoga Libertinorum, Actor. 6, 9. vbi fit mentio eorum qui fuerunt ex synagoga Libertinorum, & Cyrenensium, & Alexandrinorum, & Ciliciam, & Asianorum, disputantium cum Stephano. Vnde apparet, diuersa scholarum genera fuisse Ierosolymis. X. Schola Athenien-sium, Actor. 17. 18. Gentes etiam suas habuisse Academias, in quibus artes & Philosophiam tradiderunt, præter profanorum authorum monimenta, constat etiam ex Actor. 17. 18. vbi Atheniensium Philosophorum cum Paulo disputantium fit mentio. XI. Schola Corinthiaca Actor. 18. 8. &c. Et Tyrannus quidam Ephesi schölam habuisse dicitur, Actor. 19. 8. 9. XII. Domesticæ scholæ: Paulus, Rom. 16. & 1 Corint. 16. 19. meminit congregationis quæ fit in domo Aquilæ & Priscillæ, & Coloss. 4. 15. quæ fit in domo Nymphæ. XIII. Timotheus Pauli discipulus, 2 Timoth. 3. v. 10. 14. Scholas Ecclesiasticas singulos Apostolos, vbicunque locorum egerint, aperuisse, non tantum eo videntur, quòd passim in synagogis docuerunt, Actor. 13. v. 14. 15. 42. sed etiam quòd suos semper habuerunt discipulos, quos in sacris literis instituerunt, & ad ministerium præpararunt. Paulus enim se Timotheum docuisse testatur, 2 Timoth. 2. 2. & 3. v. 14. XIV. Schola Alexandrina. Alexandriæ ab antiquo fuisse scholam, testatur Eusebius lib. 5. cap. 9. Forte cùm Marcus ibi Ecclesiam colligit, philosophis & Iudæis ad Christianismum conueruersus, schola illa Ethnica seu Philosophica in Christianam est commutata.
units.tr: VI. The disciples of John, John 1.28. John the Baptist also had a school, in which he trained certain disciples above the others in true doctrine. This is clear from John 1.28, where John, preaching about Christ to two disciples, one of whom was Andrew, brother of Simon Peter, says: "Behold the Lamb of God." History also attests that two disciples of John were sent to Christ to ask whether Jesus was the Messiah, Matt. 11.2. VII. The school of Jerusalem, v. 15. That there was some school at Jerusalem, in which young people were instructed especially in the study of the sacred letters, can readily be gathered from this, that the Pharisees too had their disciples, Matt. 22.15, 16. VIII. Paul, a disciple of Gamaliel, Acts 22.3, where Paul himself records that he was diligently trained at the feet of Gamaliel, a teacher of the Law, in the law of his fathers. IX. The synagogue of the Freedmen, Acts 6.9, where mention is made of those who were of the synagogue of the Freedmen, and of the Cyrenians, the Alexandrians, and those of Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen. From this it appears that there were different kinds of schools at Jerusalem. X. The school of the Athenians, Acts 17.18. That the Gentiles too had their own academies, in which they taught the arts and philosophy, apart from the writings of profane authors, is also clear from Acts 17.18, where mention is made of the Athenian philosophers disputing with Paul. XI. The Corinthian school, Acts 18.8, etc. And a certain Tyrannus is said to have kept a school at Ephesus, Acts 19.8, 9. XII. Domestic schools: Paul, Rom. 16 and 1 Cor. 16.19, mentions the congregation that met in the house of Aquila and Priscilla, and Col. 4.15, which met in the house of Nymphas. XIII. Timothy, a disciple of Paul, 2 Tim. 3.10, 14. The apostles, wherever they worked, seem to have opened ecclesiastical schools, not only because they taught in the synagogues everywhere, Acts 13.14, 15, 42, but also because they always had their own disciples, whom they trained in the sacred letters and prepared for the ministry. For Paul testifies that he taught Timothy, 2 Tim. 2.2 and 3.14. XIV. The school of Alexandria. Eusebius, book 5, chapter 9, testifies that there was a school at Alexandria from ancient times. Perhaps, when Mark gathered a church there, converting philosophers and Jews to Christianity, that Gentile or philosophical school was changed into a Christian one.

units.la: SCIENTIA, pro doctrinæ diuinæ cognitione, 2 Cor.11.16. pro vsu & peritia, 8.7. scientia vera quæ, 1 Cor.2.2. Col.2.v.2.3 1 Timot.6.20. 1 Ioan.5.20. scientia à Deo, 1 Sam.2.3. Dan.1.17. scientia inflat, 1 Cor.8.1. scientiam labor comitatur, Eccles.1.18. scientia particularis in piis requiritur, Ioan.11.22. 2 Corint.5.1.1. Ioan.2.v.3.18. & 5.19. scientia veritatis, 2 Tim.3.7.
units.tr: SCIENCE, for the knowledge of divine doctrine, 2 Cor. 11.16; for practice and skill, 8.7; true knowledge, which..., 1 Cor. 2.2, Col. 2.2, 3, 1 Tim. 6.20, 1 John 5.20; knowledge from God, 1 Sam. 2.3, Dan. 1.17; knowledge puffs up, 1 Cor. 8.1; labour accompanies knowledge, Eccles. 1.18; a particular knowledge is required in the godly, John 11.22, 2 Cor. 5.1, 1 John 2.3, 18, and 5.19; knowledge of the truth, 2 Tim. 3.7.

units.la: SCIENTIAM ita distinguimus.
units.tr: We distinguish knowledge thus.

units.la: 1. Scientia Dei, 1 Sam.2.3. Psal.73.11. & 139.6, Rom.11.33
units.tr: 1. The knowledge of God, 1 Sam. 2.3, Ps. 73.11 and 139.6, Rom. 11.33.

units.la: 2. Scientia de Deo, id est, Cognitio quam hominthey de Deo Deiqz voluntate, ex eius beneplacito obtinent. Prou.2.5. Esai.11.1.9. Ose.4.1. & 6.6, 2 Cor.10.5. Col.1.10.
units.tr: 2. Knowledge about God, that is, the knowledge which men obtain of God and of God's will from his good pleasure, Prov. 2.5, Isa. 11.1, 9, Hos. 4.1 and 6.6, 2 Cor. 10.5, Col. 1.10.

units.la: 3. Scientia, Christi, id est, Cognitio omnium mysteriorum Dei, in Christo absolutissima, Colos.2.3. V.Isa.11.2.
units.tr: 3. Knowledge of Christ, that is, the knowledge of all the mysteries of God, most perfect in Christ, Col. 2.3. See Isa. 11.2.

units.la: 4. Scientia de Christo, i. Cognitio salutaris quam electi Dei de Christo seruatore suo per Spiritum S. obtinent, Esai.53.11.
units.tr: 4. Knowledge of Christ, that is, the saving knowledge which the elect of God obtain of Christ their Saviour through the Holy Spirit, Isa. 53.11.

units.la: 5. Scientia Sanctorum, Prou.9.10. & 30.3.
units.tr: 5. The knowledge of the saints, Prov. 9.10 and 30.3.
