units.la: 6. Scientia hominis, i. Cognitio illa rerum, quæ tum ad rectum vitæ præsentis vsum, tum ad salutem æternam pertinent, hominibus à Deo concessa: Genes.2.v.9.17. & 44.15. Exod.31.3 & 35.31. Iob 36.v.3 4.26. Psa.94.10 Prou.1.v.4.22. Esai.11.2 Ierem.3.15. Dan.5.11. & 12.4. Ose.4.6. Malach.2.7. Luc.1.77. Roman.10.2. & 15.4. Ephes.3.19. Phil.1.9. & 3.8.2. Tim.3.7.2 Pet.1.v.5.6.
units.tr: 6. Human knowledge, that is, that knowledge of things which, both for the right use of the present life and for eternal salvation, is granted to men by God: Gen. 2.9, 17, and 44.15. Exod. 31.3 and 35.31. Job 36.3, 4, 26. Ps. 94.10. Prov. 1.4, 22. Isa. 11.2. Jer. 3.15. Dan. 5.11 and 12.4. Hos. 4.6. Mal. 2.7. Luke 1.77. Rom. 10.2 and 15.4. Eph. 3.19. Phil. 1.9 and 3.8. 2 Tim. 3.7. 2 Pet. 1.5, 6.

units.la: 7. Scientia, falsò sic nominata, Esai.44.25. Ierem.16. [4.1 Tim.6.20.]
units.tr: 7. Knowledge falsely so called, Isa. 44.25, Jer. 16, 1 Tim. 6.20.

units.la: PINTILLAM suam vocat, filium suum vnicum vidua, 2 Sam.14.7.
units.tr: PINTILLA: the widow calls her only son by this name, 2 Sam. 14.7.

units.la: FORTATIO damnatur Exod.20.14. Deut.23.v.17.18. Pro.5. & 6.ver.24.25. & 7.5. & 9.ver.13.19. & 31.3. Matth.5.v.27.28. Act.15.20. Rom.1.v.28.29. & 13.13.1 Cor.6.v.15.16.18. & 10.8.2 Corinth.12.21. Galat.5.19. Ephes.5.3. Coloss.3.5.1. Thess.4.v.3.4.5. Hebr.13.4 Iac.2.11. Apoc.2.14. non solum in opere externo, sed & in affectu, Exod.20.17. Matth.5.28. scortatio spiritualis, Vide IDOLOLATRIA.
units.tr: FORNICATION is condemned, Exod. 20.14, Deut. 23.17, 18, Prov. 5, 6.24, 25, 7.5, 9.13, 19, 31.3, Matt. 5.27, 28, Acts 15.20, Rom. 1.28, 29, 13.13, 1 Cor. 6.15, 16, 18, 10.8, 2 Cor. 12.21, Gal. 5.19, Eph. 5.3, Col. 3.5, 1 Thess. 4.3, 4, 5, Heb. 13.4, James 2.11, Rev. 2.14, not only in the outward act but also in the desire, Exod. 20.17, Matt. 5.28. Spiritual fornication: see IDOLATRY.

units.la: FORTATIONIS variæ species, Matth.5.28. scortationis mala: Primo, iram Dei provocat, Deut.22.21. Proverb.23.27. Eccles.19.3. Ierem.5.7. Ose.4.14.1 Corint.6.v.9.13.15. Coloss.3.5. Hebr.13.4. Secundo, corpus euertat & facultates absumit, Iob.31.12. Prou.23.27. & 29.3. & 31.3. Eccles.9. 6. Tertio, infamiam adfert, Eccles. 9.10. & 41.21. scortationis etiam occasiones vitandæ, Eccles. 9. v. 4.12. & 42.11. Scortationis pœna, Deut.22.21. Ieren.29.23. Ezech.23. 11.1 Corinth. 5.9. & 6.ver. 9.10. & 10.8. Ephef.5.5. Apoc. 21.8. Scortationis punitæ exempla: Sodomitæ, Gene.19.24. Sichemitæ,34.25. Israelitæ,Numer.25.1 &c. Israelita quidam v.6. Beniamitæ,Iudic.20.44. Filij Heli, Ophni & Phinees 1.Sam.2.v.22.25. & 4.17. Israelitæ. Ierem. 5.v.7.8.9. scortatores impuri, Apoc.21.8. Vide ADULTERIUM. Scortationis & furti collatio, Prou.6.v.30.32.&c.
units.tr: The various kinds of fornication, Matt. 5.28. The evils of whoredom: first, it provokes the wrath of God, Deut. 22.21, Prov. 23.27, Eccles. 19.3, Jer. 5.7, Hos. 4.14, 1 Cor. 6.9, 13, 15, Col. 3.5, Heb. 13.4. Second, it ruins the body and consumes one's substance, Job 31.12, Prov. 23.27, 29.3, 31.3, Eccles. 9.6. Third, it brings infamy, Eccles. 9.10 and 41.21. Occasions of whoredom are also to be avoided, Eccles. 9.4, 12, 42.11. The punishment of whoredom, Deut. 22.21, Jer. 29.23, Ezek. 23.11, 1 Cor. 5.9, 6.9, 10, 10.8, Eph. 5.5, Rev. 21.8. Examples of punished whoredom: the Sodomites, Gen. 19.24; the Shechemites, 34.25; the Israelites, Num. 25.1 etc.; a certain Israelite, v. 6; the Benjamites, Judg. 20.44; the sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, 1 Sam. 2.22–25 and 4.17; the Israelites, Jer. 5.7–9; impure whoremongers, Rev. 21.8. See ADULTERY. A comparison of whoredom and theft, Prov. 6.30–32, etc.

units.la: SCRIBA quidam Christum sequi instituit, Matth.8.19. Scriba tumultum sedat, Act.19.35. Scribæ nomen, publici muneris, Pharisæi autem, sectæ nomen est, vt apparet e Acto.23.9. Scriba, in genere pro doctore, Matt.13.52. comparatur prudenti patrifamilias, ibid. Scribæ aduersus Christum murmurant, Luc.5.30. & 15.2. & discipulos Matth.15.2. Marc.7.v.1.2. signum petunt, Matt.12.38. Scribæ, quo sensu dicantur à Christo intelligentes, Vide PHARISAEI.
units.tr: A certain scribe resolved to follow Christ, Matt. 8.19. A scribe calms a tumult, Acts 19.35. The name "scribe" is that of a public office, whereas "Pharisee" is the name of a sect, as appears from Acts 23.9. "Scribe," in general, means a teacher, Matt. 13.52, and is compared to a prudent householder, ibid. The scribes murmur against Christ, Luke 5.30 and 15.2, and against his disciples, Matt. 15.2, Mark 7.1, 2. They seek a sign, Matt. 12.38. In what sense the scribes are called understanding by Christ, see PHARISEES.

units.la: Scribarum genera tria reperiuntur in scriptura sacra. Vnum eorum, qui regibus apparebant, quodcunque tandem eorū munus fuerit, 2 Sam.8.17. & 9.3. & 20.25. 2 Reg. 12.10. & 22.3. Alterum eorum, qui priuatorum contractus & instrumenta videntur descripsisse, quos notarios vocamus, cui rei operam solitos fuisse nauare Cinæos nullam alioquin hæreditatem cum tribubus sortitos, liquere potest ex 1 Paral.2 55. Eiusmodi etiam cotractuum quis fuerit mos colligi potest ex Ierem. 32.11. quò videtur allusisse Propheta, Psalm. 45.2. Tertiò, denique scribæ dicti sunt, iuris diuini, periti inter cæreros (quo nomine laudatur Esdras, cap.7. & 11.) quorum munus fuit, tum in synagogis, tum in templo legem docere (qua de causa γραμματεῖς appellati sunt) vt constare potest ex Mat.7.29. & 10.&23.13. Marc.12.28. Luc.7.30.&11.46.1.Corint.1.20. Eorum horum pręterea numero selecti erant nonnulli, qui scribæ populi vocabantur, quorum fit mentio. Matth.2.4. Scribas ex eo sic dictos fuisse, quòd legi scribendæ & interpretandæ vacarent, quasi sacrarum tabularum custodes, constare potest ex Ierem.8.8. Scribarum mores notantur, Matth.23.v.3.4. Marc.12.v.38.39.40.
units.tr: There are three kinds of scribes in Holy Scripture: (1) those who attended on kings, whatever their precise office was (2 Sam. 8:17; 9:3; 20:25; 2 Kings 12:10; 22:3); (2) those who seem to have drawn up private contracts and documents, whom we call notaries. That the Kenites, who otherwise received no inheritance among the tribes, were accustomed to devote themselves to this work can be seen from 1 Chron. 2:55. The custom of such contracts can also be gathered from Jer. 32:11, to which the Prophet seems to allude at Ps. 45:2; (3) finally, scribes were called those learned in the divine law, among the others (this is the title by which Ezra is praised, Ezra 7 and 11). Their task was to teach the law both in the synagogues and in the temple, which is why they were called γραμματεῖς [grammateis]. This is clear from Matt. 7:29; 10:23; 23:13; Mark 12:28; Luke 7:30; 11:46; 1 Cor. 1:20. Among these, some were chosen who were called scribes of the people, as in Matt. 2:4. That scribes were so named because they devoted themselves to writing and interpreting the law, as custodians of the sacred tablets, can be gathered from Jer. 8:8. The manners of the scribes are noted at Matt. 23:3–4 and Mark 12:38–40.

units.la: SCRIBA IBIT Deus legem ac mandata, Exod. 24.12. scribatur in corde Dei in oribus. Deut. 6.9. & 11.20.
units.tr: THE LORD WILL WRITE the law and the commandments (Exod. 24:12), that they be written on the heart of God, in the mouth (Deut. 6:9; 11:20).

units.la: Scribit Iesus Christus Deus homo, Ioann. 8. v. 6. 8. Apo- cal. 3.12.
units.tr: Jesus Christ, God and man, writes (John 8:6, 8; Rev. 3:12).

units.la: Scribit homo, vel Dei iussu & instinctu quae ad institutionem & salutem Ecclesiae pertinent, vel quae alius homo uber, vel quae mens & voluntas ei dictat. Scripta autem a Dei Spiritu profecta, ea sunt, quae in libris Canonicis veteris & Novi Testamenti leguntur, a Dei servis consignata, & toti Ecclesiae fideliter tradita. De his occurrunt sexcenta testimonia.]
units.tr: A man writes either by the command and impulse of God those things which pertain to the instruction and salvation of the Church, or those things which another man dictates, or which his own mind and will dictates. Those writings, however, which proceed from the Spirit of God, are those which are read in the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments, which were committed to writing by the servants of God and faithfully handed down to the whole Church. Countless testimonies to these occur.

units.la: SCRIPTORES profani, quatenus utiles, Act. 17.28. citantur, Corinth. 15.33. Tit. 1.12.
units.tr: Secular writers, insofar as they are useful, are cited (Acts 17:28; 1 Cor. 15:33; Titus 1:12).

units.la: SCRIPTURA sacra ὡς τονομαστικῶς: pro scripturis sacris Propheticis & Apostolicis, Ioann. 20.9. pro lege, Galat. 3.22. Scriptura sacra unde sit, & quis eius usus, Exod. 17.14. & 34.27. Deut. 4.1 & 17.8. & 31.9. Iosu 1.8. Ierem 36.v.2.10. 45.1. Daniel. 10.21. Matthaei 4.4. & 22.29. Lucae 4.4. & 29. Ioan. 5.39. & 10.34.35. & 20.30. Actor. 15.21. & 17.11. Rom. 1.2. & 4.2. & 15.4.1. Corinth. 9.9. & 10.11. & 15.3.2. Timoth. 3.15.2. Petr. 1.20. & 3.12. Apoc. 1.19. scriptura sacra a Spiritu Deo tradita, Exod. 20.1. & 34.1. data Angelorum ministerio, Actor. 7.53. Galat. 3.19. Hebr. 2.2. per Spiritum sanctum data, Actor. 2.4.2. Petr. 1.21. scriptura sacra, omnia ad salutem cognitu necessaria continet, Lucae 16. Ioanni 20.31. Ephes. 2.20. 2 Timoth. 3.v.15.17. Scriptura sacra, Satanae & hominum tentationibus opponenda, Matthaei 4.v.4.7.10. & 5.18. & 9.13. & 12.v.3.5.7. & 15.4. & 21.13. Lucae 9.46. Matthaei 21.42. & 22.v.31.32. & 35. Marci 7.10. & 10.5.7. & 12.10. Lucae 4.4. & 10.26. & 17.v.17.42. & 21.33. Ioan. 10.v.34.35. Actor. 2.25. & 8.30. & 15. & 17.11. & 18.v.24.28. (V. Verbum Dei).
units.tr: SCRIPTURE, sacred, [ὡς ὀνομαστικῶς] as a proper name: for the sacred Prophetic and Apostolic Scriptures (John 20:9); for the law (Gal. 3:22). Where sacred Scripture comes from, and what its use is: Exod. 17:14; 34:27; Deut. 4:1; 17:8; 31:9; Josh. 1:8; Jer. 36:2, 10; 45:1; Dan. 10:21; Matt. 4:4; 22:29; Luke 4:4, 21; John 5:39; 10:34–35; 20:30; Acts 15:21; 17:11; Rom. 1:2; 4:2; 15:4; 1 Cor. 9:9; 10:11; 15:3; 2 Tim. 3:15; 2 Pet. 1:20; 3:12; Rev. 1:19. Sacred Scripture was delivered by God through the Spirit (Exod. 20:1; 34:1), given through the ministry of angels (Acts 7:53; Gal. 3:19; Heb. 2:2), and given through the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:4; 2 Pet. 1:21). Sacred Scripture contains everything necessary to know for salvation (Luke 16; John 20:31; Eph. 2:20; 2 Tim. 3:15, 17). Sacred Scripture is to be set against the temptations of Satan and of men (Matt. 4:4, 7, 10; 5:18; 9:13; 12:3, 5, 7; 15:4; 21:13; Luke 9:46; Matt. 21:42; 22:31–32, 35; Mark 7:10; 10:5, 7; 12:10; Luke 4:4; 10:26; 17:17, 42; 21:33; John 10:34–35; Acts 2:25; 8:30, 15; 17:11; 18:24, 28). (See Word of God.)

units.la: SCRIPTURAE abusus, Lucae 4.10. scripturae certitudo. Vide verbi certitudo. scripturae cognitio a Christo, Lucae verf. 45.46. scripturae corruptores puniendi, 2 Petr. 3. scripturae expositio, plebi quam necessaria, Proverb. 8. scripturae finis praecipuus, Roman. 15.4. scripturae integritas, errorum causa, Matth. 22.29. Marc. 12.24. 5. scripturae lectio piis necessaria est, Ioan. 5.39. Rom. 15.4. 1. Thess. 5. 1. Tim. 4.13. Hebr. 5.14.2. Petr. 1.19. & 3.v.16. Col. 3.16. Iut. 17.18. Ps. 1.2. Deut. 6.6. Exempla: Moses, Exod. 31.18. Israelitæ, Nehemiæ 9.3. Daniel, Dan.9. 2. Ionathas & maiores Iudæorum, 1 Macha.12.9. Christus, Lucæ 4.v.16. qui scripturæ sacræ autoritate confudit Satanam, Matt. v.4.7.10. Pharisæos 12.v.1.2.3. &c. & sæpiùs eius lectionem commendat, Ioan.5.39. Eunuchus Candaces reginæ, Act. 8.28. Beroenses, 17.v.10.11. Apollos, 18.v.24.25. Timotheus, 1 Tim.4.13.2 Tim.3.v.14.15.16.
units.tr: Abuse of Scripture (Luke 4:10). The certainty of Scripture: see certainty of the Word. The knowledge of Scripture from Christ (Luke 24:45–46). Corrupters of Scripture are to be punished (2 Pet. 3). The exposition of Scripture, how necessary it is for the common people (Prov. 8). The principal end of Scripture (Rom. 15:4). The integrity of Scripture, the cause of errors (Matt. 22:29; Mark 12:24). The reading of Scripture is necessary for the pious (John 5:39; Rom. 15:4; 1 Thess. 5; 1 Tim. 4:13; Heb. 5:14; 2 Pet. 1:19; 3:16; Col. 3:16; Josh. 1:7–8; Ps. 1:2; Deut. 6:6). Examples: Moses (Exod. 31:18); the Israelites (Neh. 9:3); Daniel (Dan. 9:2); Jonathan and the elders of the Jews (1 Macc. 12:9); Christ (Luke 4:16), who by the authority of Holy Scripture confounded Satan (Matt. 4:4, 7, 10) and the Pharisees (Matt. 12:1–3, etc.), and often commended its reading (John 5:39). The eunuch of Queen Candace (Acts 8:28); the Bereans (Acts 17:10–11); Apollos (Acts 18:24–25); Timothy (1 Tim. 4:13; 2 Tim. 3:14–16).

units.la: Scripturæ præstatio seu adimpletio, necessaria, Matt. 18.& 24.34.& 26.v.54 56. Luc.21.22.& 22,37.& 24.v.44. Ioan.10.35.& 12.ver.16.38. & 13.18.& 15.25.& 17.12.& 19. 24.28.36 37. Actor.1.16.& 3 18. & 13. 27. Scripturarum lectioni ipsam quoque plebem olim interfuisse, & scripturas vernaculo sermone explicari solitas fuisse apud Iudæos, non obscurè colligitur ex Luc. 4. 22. vt quiuis omnia intelligere, quiuis etiam rogare & respondere posset, ritè tamen & certo ordine constituto, vt liquet ex Actor.13.15. Quem morem cùm Satan iam coepisset Patrum tempore deprauare, restituit eum pro viribus Apostolorum 1 Cor.14.16. &c.
units.tr: The fulfilment or accomplishment of Scripture is necessary (Matt. 18; 24:34; 26:54–56; Luke 21:22; 22:37; 24:44; John 10:35; 12:16, 38; 13:18; 15:25; 17:12; 19:24, 28, 36–37; Acts 1:16; 3:18; 13:27). It is clearly gathered from Luke 4:22 that the common people also were once present at the reading of the Scriptures, and that among the Jews the Scriptures were usually explained in the vernacular language, so that anyone could understand everything, and anyone could even ask and answer, yet properly and in a settled order, as is clear from Acts 13:15. When Satan had begun to corrupt this custom already in the time of the Fathers, the Apostles restored it as far as they could (1 Cor. 14:16, etc.).

units.la: [Scriptura Dei, immediatè, Exod.32.16.Ezech.13.9. Mediatè, sed medio planè miraculoso, Dan.5.v.7.8.15.8. Mediatè per sanctos Dei homines, ductu Spiritus S. in libris Canonicis V. & N. T. consignata, q Scriptura & Scriptura ΓΡΑΦΗ dicitur, & nu.pl. Scripturæ.
units.tr: [Scripture of God: immediately (Exod. 32:16; Ezek. 13:9); mediately, but by a plainly miraculous means (Dan. 5:7–8, 15; 8:1); mediately, through holy men of God, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, committed to writing in the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments. It is called Scriptura and γραφή [graphē], and in the plural, Scripturae.]

units.la: Scriptura veritatis, decretum Dei de rebus futuris Dan.10.21. Scriptura hominis, & de homine, seu ad hominem proprie pertinens, 2 Paralip. 36.22. Esd.1.1.& 2. Neh.7.64.]
units.tr: [Scripture of truth: the decree of God concerning future things (Dan. 10:21). Scripture of man, and concerning man, or pertaining properly to man (2 Chron. 36:22; Ezra 1:1–2; Neh. 7:64).]

units.la: ¶ SCRIPTVRAM sacram obscuram & intellectu difficilem esse cauillantur Pontificij ex 2 Pet.3.16. nec omnia scripta mandata esse ab Apostolis, Ioan.20.30.& 21.25. 1 Cor. 14.2 Thess.2.15 2 Ioan.v.12.3 Ioan.v.13.14. Idque ideo faciunt, vt suis commentis autoritatem concilient. Contra quos vide supra: scriptura sacra omnia ad salutem, &c.
units.tr: ¶ The Papists cavil that Holy Scripture is obscure and difficult to understand, from 2 Pet. 3:16, and that not everything was commanded in writing by the Apostles (John 20:30; 21:25; 1 Cor. 14:2; 2 Thess. 2:15; 2 John 12; 3 John 13–14). They do this so that they may win authority for their own inventions. Against them see above: Scripture is sufficient for salvation, etc.

units.la: ¶ Præterea, nec scripturam, nec legem, esse iudicem, sed sacerdotem, contendunt ex Deut.17.18.Ezech.44.24.Malach.2.7. V. SACERDOS.
units.tr: ¶ Moreover, they contend that neither Scripture nor the law is the judge, but the priest, from Deut. 17:18; Ezek. 44:24; Mal. 2:7. See PRIEST.

units.la: [SCRUPULUS, Offensio, 1 Sam.25.31.]
units.tr: [SCRUPLE, offence, 1 Sam. 25:31.]

units.la: [SCRUTATOR cordium Deus, Rom. 8. 26. (Vide Deus.) Scrutator Cordium Iesus Christus, Apoc. 2.23.
units.tr: [GOD, the searcher of hearts, Rom. 8:26 (see God). Jesus Christ, the searcher of hearts, Rev. 2:23.]

units.la: Scrutator cordium Spiritus S. 1 Cor.2.10.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit, the searcher of hearts (1 Cor. 2:10).

units.la: Scrutator homo, qui vel externa & temporalia, vel spiritualia & coelestia meditatur Ge.31. v.32.34.37.1 Reg.20.6. Pf.119.v.2,34.69 115,129. Thren.3.40.Ioan.5.39. Act.17.11.1 Petr.1.v.10.11.]
units.tr: A man who searches, who meditates either on external and temporal things, or on spiritual and heavenly things (Gen. 31:32, 34, 37; 1 Sam. 20:6; Ps. 119:2, 34, 69, 115, 129; Lam. 3:40; John 5:39; Acts 17:11; 1 Pet. 1:10–11).

units.la: SCVLPTILE, V. IDOLVM. Sculptile qui facit maledictus, Deut.27.15. Et totius populus dicet, Amen.
units.tr: GRAVEN IMAGE: see IDOL. "Cursed is the man who makes a graven image" (Deut. 27:15). And all the people shall say, Amen.

units.la: VRRILITAS (vitanda, Ephes.5.4.) Est risus iocisque aliis movendi intempestivum & immoderatum studium & affectatio.
units.tr: LEVITY (to be avoided, Eph. 5:4) is an untimely and immoderate eagerness and affectation for provoking laughter and other jests.

units.la: VTVM auxilij Deus, Deut.33.29. 2 Sam.22.3. scutum fidei, Eph.6.16. scuta aurea Salomonis iussu facta, 1 Reg.10.16. & 14.v.26.27.
units.tr: USE, as a help: God (Deut. 33:29; 2 Sam. 22:3). The shield of faith (Eph. 6:16). Golden shields made at the command of Solomon (1 Kings 10:16; 14:26–27).

units.la: Oreb & Oreb duo principes Madianitarum interficiuntur, Iudi.7.25.
units.tr: Oreb and Zeeb, two princes of the Midianites, are killed (Judg. 7:25).

units.la: Bochri filius, coniurationis princeps, 2 Sam.20.1. eum eo in Dauidem omnis Israel conspirat vers.2. obtinetur, ver.13.15. eius caput amputatum Ioabo traditur, vers.22.
units.tr: Sheba, son of Bichri, leader of a conspiracy (2 Sam. 20:1). With him all Israel conspires against David (v. 2); he is overcome (vv. 13–15). His head is cut off and handed over to Joab (v. 22).

units.la: IA vxor Ochosiae, mater Ioas regis Israel 2 Reg.11.1.
units.tr: Athaliah, wife of Ahaziah, mother of Joash, king of Israel (2 Kings 11:1).

units.la: RETA mirum in modum patefiunt, Eccles.10.20. V. ARCANVM: & MYSTERIVM.
units.tr: Secrets are revealed in a wonderful manner (Eccl. 10:20). See MYSTERY and SECRET.

units.la: TA Christianorum, Act.28.22. secta Nazarenorum, pro Christianismi professione, Actor.24.5. sectae. i. in religione factiones, damnantur. 1 Cor.1.v.10.13. Galat.5.20. sectae pernitiosae praedicatae, 2 Pet.2.1. sectae iam olim ab Apostolorum tempore exortae, 1 Cor.1.12. & 3.4. & 11.18. Heb.10.25. Ioan.2.18.19.
units.tr: SECT of the Christians (Acts 28:22); the sect of the Nazarenes, for the profession of Christianity (Acts 24:5). Sects, that is, factions in religion, are condemned (1 Cor. 1:10, 13; Gal. 5:20). Pernicious sects are preached (2 Pet. 2:1). Sects already arose long ago, from the time of the Apostles (1 Cor. 1:12; 3:4; 11:18; Heb. 10:25; John 2:18–19).

units.la: SÆCVLVM, seculum Graecis αἰὼν, Hebraeis עולם, Primo, interdum idem declarat, quod a condito mundo, Actor. 3.21. Secundo, interdum ab aeterno, seu tempus perpetuum & aeternum, Genes.9.12. Psal.89.3. Tertio, interdum non perpetuum, sed longum temporis spatium significat, aut usque ad annum Iubilaeum, ut patet ex Levit. 25.v.39.40. & Ierem.2.20. V. AETERNVM. Quarto, interdum tempus vitae alicuius, Psal.89.2. & 119.52. capitur etiam seculi vox pro deprauatissima illa hominum vita & miserrima conditione extra Christum, 2 Cor.4.4. qua significatione saepe solet mundi & tenebrarum nomen vsurpari. Pro hominibus etiam non renatis capitur, Rom.12.2. ad domum seculi, Eccles.12.7.1. ad sepulchrum, quod est domus quo habitat in seculum.
units.tr: AGE, world; in Greek αἰών [aiōn], in Hebrew olam [עולם]. First, it sometimes denotes the same as from the creation of the world (Acts 3:21). Second, sometimes from eternity, or perpetual and eternal time (Gen. 9:12; Ps. 89:3). Third, sometimes it signifies not a perpetual but a long span of time, or even up to the year of Jubilee, as is clear from Lev. 25:39–40 and Jer. 2:20 (see ETERNAL). Fourth, sometimes the lifetime of someone (Ps. 89:2; 119:52). The word age is also taken for that most depraved human life and most wretched condition outside Christ (2 Cor. 4:4), in which sense the name of the world and of darkness is often used. It is also taken for men not yet reborn (Rom. 12:2). To the house of the age (Eccl. 12:5), that is, to the grave, which is the house in which he dwells for ever.

units.la: SECVLA V. MVNDVS.
units.tr: SECULA. V. MUNDUS (AGES; WORLD)

units.la: [Seculi varias acceptiones ita distinguimus.
units.tr: [We distinguish the various senses of seculum as follows.

units.la: 1. Tempus elapsum & praeteritum significat.
units.tr: 1. It denotes past and bygone time.

units.la: 2. Futurum, ad multos annos, sed finitum & determinatum.
units.tr: 2. The future, lasting many years but finite and determined.

units.la: 3. Perpetuum, nunquam finiendum, aeternum.
units.tr: 3. Perpetual, never to be ended, eternal.

units.la: 4. Continuum, sed incrementa sua habens;
units.tr: 4. Continuous, yet having its own successive periods.

units.la: 5. Seculum Mundus nominatur, Matth.13.v.19. & 28. 20.1 Cor.2.8.
units.tr: 5. Seculum is called the World: Matt. 13:19; 28:20; 1 Cor. 2:8.

units.la: 6. Mundus, & res omnes visibiles & invisibiles creatae, Heb.1.2. & 11.3.
units.tr: 6. The world, and all things created, visible and invisible: Heb. 1:2; 11:3.

units.la: 7. Vita praesens, Eccl.9.6 Matth.12.32. Marc.4.19.1 Cor.3.18.1 Tim.6.17.2 Tim.4.10. Tit.2.12.
units.tr: 7. The present life: Eccl. 9:6; Matt. 12:32; Mark 4:19; 1 Cor. 3:18; 1 Tim. 6:17; 2 Tim. 4:10; Titus 2:12.

units.la: 8. Vitae nostrae ratio P.90.8.
units.tr: 8. The manner of our life: Ps. 90:8.

units.la: 9. Corruptio cordis & morum, ad quam sese componunt & accommodant homines praesenti vitae addicti, futurae contemptores.
units.tr: 9. The corruption of heart and morals, to which men devoted to the present life and despisers of the future conform and accommodate themselves.

units.la: 10. Seculum futurum, vel venturum, regnum caeleste, locus supra omnes coelos electis Dei paratus. Marc.10.30. Luc.18.30. Heb.6.5.]
units.tr: 10. The future or coming age, the heavenly kingdom, the place above all the heavens prepared for the elect of God: Mark 10:30; Luke 18:30; Heb. 6:5.]

units.la: SECVRITAS laudibilis ea est, quae recumbit in Dei promissionibus: eo quod statuit pia conscientia Deum nunquam sibi defuturum, & inuicta persuasione facta satanae & petulanti cato audacter & intrepide insultat: nihilo tamen minus suae infirmitatis memor cum timore & humiliter sese Deum reiicit, seque illi studiose & solicite commendat. Ps.91.1.c. Heb.13.5. Rom.8.31.c.1 Cor.10.12. Phil.2.12.13 Matth.6.9.1 Pet.5.4.c.
units.tr: Security is praiseworthy when it rests on God's promises, since the pious conscience holds that God will never fail it. Trusting this with unconquered confidence, it boldly and fearlessly mocks Satan and his impudent assaults. Yet, mindful of its own weakness, it humbly and fearfully casts itself upon God and commends itself to him earnestly and anxiously: Ps. 91:1; Heb. 13:5; Rom. 8:31; 1 Cor. 10:12; Phil. 2:12–13; Matt. 6:9; 1 Pet. 5:4.

units.la: Vituperanda est, quae ex socordia oritur, dum hoc in mundi donis praesentibus, perinde ac si extra teli iactum essent, nihil curant, sed acquiescunt in sua conditione: quo fit ut omnibus satanae incursionibus sint expositi. Ergo haec curas remittit ubi non oportet, quando, & quatum non oportet.1 Corinth.10.12. Luc.17.26 c. Pro.28. Ierem.5.12.1 Thess.5.3. Remedium, 1 Pet.5.8. Eph.11.c.
units.tr: Security is to be blamed when it arises from carelessness, when men care nothing for the present gifts of the world, as if they were out of range of the missile, and acquiesce in their condition. The result is that they are exposed to all the assaults of Satan. Such security relaxes care where it should not, when it should not, and to the degree it should not: 1 Cor. 10:12; Luke 17:26; Prov. 28; Jer. 5:12; 1 Thess. 5:3. Remedy: 1 Pet. 5:8; Eph. 11.

units.la: SECVRITAS nimia cavenda, Prov.28.14. securitas Satanae ditum patefacit, Matth.12.44. Ezech.16.49. ubi securitas otium ocium videntur allegorice designari, quorum illa aditum Satanæ patefacit, illud autem eum etiam ad se vltrò alli- cit. Securitas vera ex Legis obedientia, Exod. 34. 24. 2 Para. 20. 20. Securitas mentis optima, Prou. 15. 15. Iecuritas quibus promissa, Leuit. 25. 18. & 26. 6. Iecuritas piorum, Vide Psal. [Securitas falsa, 1 Thess. 5. 3.] Securitatem perfectam de peccatorum remissione, aut salute consequenda, non haberi in hac vita, probare conantur Pontificij ex Eccles. 19. v. 12. & aliis nonnullis locis. ( V. CERTI. & Remissio peccat.)
units.tr: Excessive security is to be avoided: Prov. 28:14. Security opens the way for Satan: Matt. 12:44; Ezek. 16:49, where security and idleness seem to be allegorically designated. The former opens the way for Satan, while the latter even draws him on of its own accord. True security comes from obedience to the Law: Exod. 34:24; 2 Chr. 20:20. The best security of mind: Prov. 15:15. Security promised to those who… : Lev. 25:18; 26:6. Security of the pious: see Ps. [...]. False security: 1 Thess. 5:3. The Papists try to prove from Eccl. 19:12 and some other passages that perfect certainty of the forgiveness of sins, or of obtaining salvation, cannot be had in this life. (See CERTAINTY and REMISSION OF SINS.)

units.la: SECVRIS Esai. 10. 15. Securis Dei, vindicta in hypocritas, Matth. 3. 10.] Enatans: 2 Reg. 6. 5. V. Deut. 19. 5. Isa. 10. 15.
units.tr: AXE: Isa. 10:15. The axe of God is vengeance on hypocrites: Matt. 3:10. Enatans: 2 Kings 6:5. See Deut. 19:5; Isa. 10:15.

units.la: DECIAS, qui & Matthanias, seu Matthathias, Rex Iuda constituitur, 2 Reg. 24. 17. Babylonis Regi rebellat, ver. 20. Ierosolymam obsessam deserit, 25. 4. Ieremiae 39. 4. fugiens Chaldaeis capitur, v. 5. 2 Reg. 25. 5. Babylonem non erat visurus, licet ibi moriturus, Ezech. 12. 13. oculis effossis illuc perductus est. 2 Reg. 25. 7. eius calamitas & mors praedicuntur, Ierem. 21. 7. & 24. 8. & 34. v. 3. 4. Ezech. 12. 13. & 17. 16. & 21. 25. eius filij occiduntur, 2 Reg. 25. 7. Ierem. 39. 6.
units.tr: ZEDEKIAH, also called Mattaniah or Mattathias, is made king of Judah: 2 Kings 24:17. He rebels against the king of Babylon: v. 20. He abandons Jerusalem while it is besieged: 25:4; Jer. 39:4. Fleeing from the Chaldeans, he is captured: v. 5; 2 Kings 25:5. He was not going to see Babylon, though he was to die there: Ezek. 12:13. He was led there with his eyes put out: 2 Kings 25:7. His calamity and death are foretold: Jer. 21:7; 24:8; 34:3–4; Ezek. 12:13; 17:16; 21:25. His sons are slain: 2 Kings 25:7; Jer. 39:6.

units.la: DECIAS Pseudopropheta, 1 Reg. 22. 11. 2 Paral. 18. 10. eius in Michaeam violentia, 1 Reg. 22. 24.
units.tr: ZEDEKIAH, a false prophet: 1 Kings 22:11; 2 Chr. 18:10. His violence against Micaiah: 1 Kings 22:24.

units.la: DECIAS alter Pseudopropheta, Ierem. 29. 21. comburitur, 22. (Zidekiah. i. iustitia Domini.)
units.tr: ZEDEKIAH, another false prophet, is burned: Jer. 29:21–22. (Zedekiah, i.e. the righteousness of the Lord.)

units.la: HERE, Hebraeis idem significat nonnunquam quod habitare, commorari, versari, Mat. 4. 16. Actor. 18. 11. (quod verum postea veteres Episcopi suum fecerunt, unde est phrasis, Sedisse aliquem tot aut tot annos: hoc est praefuisse Ecclesiae, & rexisse eam) sicut contrà, surgere idem declarat, quod proficisci, Marc. 10. 1. capitur & pro consilium capere, Luc. 14. 28.
units.tr: SIT. Among the Hebrews this sometimes means the same as to dwell, sojourn, or live: Matt. 4:16; Acts 18:11. (The ancient bishops later made this their own, whence the phrase "to have sat" someone so many or so many years, that is, to have presided over and governed the Church.) Conversely, to rise means the same as to set out: Mark 10:1. It is also taken to mean to take counsel: Luke 14:28.

units.la: Sedere ad dextram Patris in coelis, Ephes. 1. 20. significat consortem esse imperij illius summi: cuius etiam rectu Dei maiestatem dicimus esse in coelis, non quòd illic inclusa, sed quòd illic potissimum emineat. Quanquam quòd ad humanitatem Christi attinet, certum sit in coelis esse, non in terra, quòd aliquin imaginaria sit ipsius ascensio, & imaginarium corpus. Sessione itaque ad dextram Patris, Heb. 1. 13 significatur imperij in omnes res creatas attributa homini etiã Christo potestas: tempe quia qui idem homo est, etiam Deus est. Patre alioquin gloriam suam alteri non daturo. Neque ha- sessio essentialia naturæ humanæ idiomata tollit, quibus sublatis natura humana non glorificaretur, sed abolë- retur.
units.tr: To sit at the right hand of the Father in heaven (Eph. 1:20) signifies to share in that supreme dominion. We likewise say that the majesty of God is in heaven at his right hand, not because it is enclosed there, but because it chiefly shines forth there. As far as the humanity of Christ is concerned, however, it is certain that he is in heaven and not on earth; otherwise his ascension would be imaginary and his body imaginary. Therefore the session at the right hand of the Father (Heb. 1:13) signifies the power over all created things granted to man, even to Christ: because he who is the same man is also God, the Father not otherwise giving his glory to another. Nor does this session abolish the essential properties of human nature; without them human nature would not be glorified but would be abolished.

units.la: Deinde illud quoque obseruandum est, sessionem quidem hanc vnius esse Christi propriam, quatenus eminet super omnia creata, & caput etiam est Ecclesiæ suæ: sed tamen admittit membra pro suo modulo ad huius æternæ gloriæ consortium. Nam & cum Christo regnaturi dicuntur, Apoc.3 21. & Angelos iudicaturi, 1 Cor.6.v.2.3. Christo in cœlis assessores futuri, Matth.19.28. V.Sessio Sedes, V.Sessio.
units.tr: Next, it must also be observed that this session belongs to Christ alone, insofar as he is exalted above all created things and is also the head of his Church. Yet it admits members, each according to his measure, to the fellowship of this eternal glory. For they are said to reign with Christ (Rev. 3:21), to judge the angels (1 Cor. 6:2–3), and to be future assessors with Christ in heaven (Matt. 19:28). See SESSION, SEAT.

units.la: SEDITIO, est inter eiusdem imperij & potestatis multitudinem & subditos, contra legitimum & patefactum magistratus iussum & mandatum, orta discordia, spectans arma.
units.tr: SEDITION is the discord that arises among the multitude and subjects of the same realm and power, against the lawful and published command and mandate of the magistrate, and that looks toward arms.

units.la: SEDITIO : Seditiones vitandæ sunt, 2 Cor.12.20. Seditio exempla: Core, Dathan & Abiron, Numer.16.vers.12. Israelitæ, v.41.42. & 2c 3. Ephraimitæ, Iud.12.1.&c. Abi-lom, 2 Sam.15.v.10.11. Semei.16.v.5.&c. Seba filius Bochri 20.v.1 2. Adad Idumæus, 1. Reg,11.14. Rasón.v.23. Ieroboam, v.26. Zimbri.16.v.9,16 Barrabes, Marc.15.7. Lu-23.v.18.19. Theudas, Actor.5.v.35.36. Iudas Galilæus, v.37. quidam Iudæi, 15. v.1.2. Demetrius cum suis, 19.vers. &c. Vide REBELLIO.
units.tr: SEDITION. Seditions are to be avoided: 2 Cor. 12:20. Examples of sedition: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, Num. 16:12; the Israelites, vv. 41–42; and 2 and 3. The Ephraimites, Judg. 12:1 etc. Absalom, 2 Sam. 15:10–11. Shimei, 16:5 etc. Sheba son of Bichri, 20:1–2. Adad the Edomite, 1 Kings 11:14. Rezon, v. 23. Jeroboam, v. 26. Zimri, 16:9, 16. Barabbas, Mark 15:7; Luke 23:18–19. Theudas, Acts 5:35–36. Judas the Galilean, v. 37. Certain Jews, 15:1–2. Demetrius with his men, 19 etc. See REBELLION.

units.la: Seditionis crimen Prophetis, & Apostolis aliisque plurimis hominibus publico docendi munere fungentibus, falsò ab impiis est obiectum. Exempla: Achab Elias Reg.18.v.17.18. Consiliarij Artaxerxis Iudæis, 1 Esdræ.4.12.13. Artaxerxes Ierusalem, v.18.19. Aman. Iudæis, Esth.3.8.&9.24. Amasias Prophetæ, Amos 7,10. Iudæi Christo: Christus enim duorum atrocissimorum criminum reus peragitur, Blasphemiæ, Mat.6.5.26.64. Luc.22.70.71.& seditionis, 23.2. cum tamen omni culpa vacaret adeo ut non vereretur omnium conscientias provocare Igan.8.46.& cum videret turbam ipsum correpturam in Regem creaturam, secesserit, Ioann.6.15. Pontifices & Idæi Apostolis, Actor.4.18.&5.28. Tertullus, 24.5. Seditiosi punitæ exempla: Core, Dathan, & Abiron, cum 250.viris Num.16.31.&c. Absalom, 2 Sam.18.9. &c. Seba Bochrius.2 Sam.20.21. Semei, 1 Reg.2.v.41.&c. Zimbri, 16.18. dechias,2 Reg.24.20.& 25.v.6.7. Theudas cum suis, Act.5.36.Iudas Galilæus cum suis. v.37.
units.tr: The charge of sedition was falsely brought by the impious against the prophets, the apostles, and many others who performed the public office of teaching. Examples: Ahab against Elijah, 1 Kings 18:17–18. The counsellors of Artaxerxes against the Jews, 1 Esdras 4:12–13. Artaxerxes against Jerusalem, vv. 18–19. Haman against the Jews, Esth. 3:8–9; 9:24. Amaziah against the prophet, Amos 7:10. The Jews against Christ: Christ was accused of two most atrocious crimes, blasphemy (Matt. 26:65; Luke 22:70–71) and sedition (Luke 23:2), although he was free of all fault, so much so that he did not fear to challenge the consciences of all (John 8:46). When he saw the crowd about to seize him and make him king, he withdrew (John 6:15). The priests and Jews against the apostles: Acts 4:18; 5:28. Tertullus: Acts 24:5. Examples of seditious people punished: Korah, Dathan, and Abiram with 250 men, Num. 16:31 etc. Absalom, 2 Sam. 18:9 etc. Sheba son of Bichri, 2 Sam. 20:21. Shimei, 1 Kings 2:41 etc. Zimri, 16:18. Zedekiah, 2 Kings 24:20; 25:6–7. Theudas with his men, Acts 5:36. Judas the Galilean with his men, v. 37.

units.la: Sublato seditionis autore, seditio aufertur, exempla: Absalom, 2 Samuel.18.16. Seba, 20.22. Vide CONIVRATIO.
units.tr: When the author of the sedition is removed, the sedition is removed. Examples: Absalom, 2 Sam. 18:16. Sheba, 20:22. See CONSPIRACY.

units.la: SEDITIOSI puniuntur, Numer.16.31. Vide MVRMVRATORES.
units.tr: Seditious people are punished: Num. 16:31. See MURMURERS.

units.la: DVCTOR quis dicendus,2 Ioan.v.7.Iudæ v. 12. &c. Ioh.7.12. Alij dicebant,Vir bonus est,scilicet Christus: Alij autem dicebant,Non:sed turbam seducit. Si seducere decipere est, nec Christus seductor,nec Apostoli eius, nec quisquam seductor debet esse Christianus.Si autem seducere aliunde aliquem ad aliud persuadendo deducere est, quærendum est vnde,& quo.Si à mala ad bonum, bonus seductor est,si à bono ad malum,malus seductor est. August.in Tract.29. in Iohan.
units.tr: Who is to be called a deceiver? (2 John 7; Jude 12 etc.; John 7:12.) Some said, "He is a good man," namely Christ; others said, "No, he leads the crowd astray." If to seduce is to deceive, then neither Christ nor his apostles nor anyone else should be a Christian. But if to seduce is to lead someone from one thing to another by persuasion, it must be asked from where and to where. If one leads from bad to good, the seducer is good; if from good to bad, he is a bad seducer. Augustine, Tractate 29 on John.

units.la: DVCTORES in peius proficiunt,2 Tim.3.13. seductores cauendi,Mat.7.15.& 24.4.23.Marc.13.5.Act.20.28. &c. Rom.16.17.2 Cor.11.3.Philipp.3.2.2 Pet.3.17.1 Ioan.2.26.& 3.7.2 Ioan.v.7 10.Iudæ, v. 4.à seductoribus decepti puniuntur, Ose.4.9.Mat.15,14. Luc 6.39.
units.tr: Deceivers grow worse: 2 Tim. 3:13. Seducers are to be avoided: Matt. 7:15; 24:4, 23; Mark 13:5; Acts 20:28 etc.; Rom. 16:17; 2 Cor. 11:3; Phil. 3:2; 2 Pet. 3:17; 1 John 2:26; 3:7; 2 John 7, 10; Jude 4. Those deceived by seducers are punished: Hos. 4:9; Matt. 15:14; Luke 6:39.

units.la: DVLITAS,est virtus, suam cuique functionem in vita attribuens,& diligenter,constanter ac fideliter,propter Deum & communem salutem, faciens labores suæ functionis proprios ac necessarios.
units.tr: DILIGENCE is a virtue that assigns to each person his own function in life and, for the sake of God and the common good, carries out diligently, constantly, and faithfully the labours that are proper and necessary to that function.

units.la: DVLITAS commendatur, Prou.22.29. Sedulitatis exempla: Iudæorum reducum aduersarij ,1 Esdr.4.23. Iudæi reduces,Nehem.4.23.Ioseph & Maria,Mat.2.14. Iudas proditor,26.47. Principes sacerdotum & seniores populi, 27.1. Mulieres piæ,Maria Magdalena,& aliæ Mariæ, Luc.24.1. duo Discipuli euntes Emaus,v.32.33. Christus, Lucæ 4.v.42.43.Ioan.8.2.Pharisæi,7, v.30.31.32. Maria Magdalena, 20.1.Petrus & alter Discipulus, v. 33. credentes, Actor.2.44.sacerdotes & Magistratus,4.1.&c.Apostoli,5.21.Iudæi, 9.v.23.24.Petrus,10 9.Paulus,15.ver.35.36.40.41. & 20.16, &c.sedulitas patrisfamiliâs,Prou.20.13.& matrisfamiliâs, Pro.31.10. &c.
units.tr: DILIGENCE is commended: Prov. 22:29. Examples of diligence: the adversaries of the returning Jews, 1 Esdras 4:23; the returning Jews, Neh. 4:23; Joseph and Mary, Matt. 2:14; Judas the traitor, 26:47; the chief priests and elders of the people, 27:1; the pious women, Mary Magdalene and the other Marys, Luke 24:1; the two disciples going to Emmaus, vv. 32–33; Christ, Luke 4:42–43; John 8:2; the Pharisees, John 7:30–32; Mary Magdalene, 20:1; Peter and the other disciple, v. 33; believers, Acts 2:44; priests and magistrates, 4:1 etc.; the apostles, 5:21; the Jews, 9:23–24; Peter, 10:9; Paul, 15:35–36, 40–41, and 20:16 etc.; the diligence of the head of the household, Prov. 20:13, and of the mistress of the household, Prov. 31:10 etc.

units.la: GOR,seu Tsoar,quæ & Bela ciuitas est,Genes.14.2. Lothi precibus è communi Sodomæ & Gomorrhæ incendio liberatur,19.v.20.21.22.23. (ipsa vox significat idem quod parua aut exigua, quo significato alluditur ad Loth vetba, 19.20.)
units.tr: GOR, or Tsoar, which is also the city Bela, Gen. 14.2. Through Lot's prayers he is saved from the common burning of Sodom and Gomorrah, Gen. 19.20-23. (The word itself means the same as small or little, an allusion to Lot's words, 19.20.)

units.la: SEHON. Rex Amorrhæorum, Num.21.21. commeatum Israëlitis denegat, bellóque eos lacessit, ver.23. Deut.2.30. vincitur, Num.21.24. Deut.2.33. (i. Eradicatio.)
units.tr: SEHON. King of the Amorites, Num. 21.21. He refuses passage to the Israelites and attacks them in war, v.23; Deut. 2.30. He is defeated, Num. 21.24; Deut. 2.33. (i.e. eradication.)

units.la: SEIR mons Idumæa: illic habitauit Esau, Genes.36.8. Iosu 2.4. eius desolatio prædicitur, Ezech.35.3. (Hispidus, pilosus.)
units.tr: SEIR, a mountain of Edom, where Esau dwelt, Gen. 36.8; Josh. 2.4. Its desolation is foretold, Ezek. 35.3. (Bristly, hairy.)

units.la: SELA filius Iudæ tertius, Gen.38.5. (i. dissolvens.)
units.tr: SELA, third son of Judah, Gen. 38.5. (i.e. dissolving.)

units.la: SELLA, altera vxor Lamech, Gen.4.19. Tubal-Cain mater, v. 22. (Zillah, i. umbra eius.)
units.tr: SELLA, the second wife of Lamech, Gen. 4.19, and mother of Tubal-Cain, v.22. (Zillah, i.e. his shadow.)

units.la: SELLVM Israelis regnum, Zacharia interfecto, vsurpat, 2 Reg.15.10. à Manahen interficitur, v.14.
units.tr: SELLUM, king of Israel, seizes the kingdom after Zechariah is killed, 2 Kings 15.10. He is killed by Menahem, v.14.

units.la: SELLVN. Iosiæ filius, 1 Paral.3.15. eius mors prædicitur, Ierem. 22.11. (Schallum, i. retributor.)
units.tr: SHALLUM, son of Josiah, 1 Chr. 3.15. His death is foretold, Jer. 22.11. (Shallum, i.e. the one who repays.)

units.la: SELEVCIA, ciuitas Syriæ, quam Paulus peragrauit: Act. 13.4.
units.tr: SELEUCIA, a city of Syria, which Paul travelled through, Acts 13.4.

units.la: SEM, filius Noah, Gen.5.32. eius benedictio. 9.26. (i. nomen.)
units.tr: SHEM, son of Noah, Gen. 5.32. His blessing, Gen. 9.26. (i.e. name.)

units.la: SEMAIAS Pseudopropheta: eius turpe factum, Nehem.6.v. 10.12.13. (i. obedrens Domino.)
units.tr: SHEMAIAH the false prophet: his shameful deed, Neh. 6.10, 12, 13. (i.e. disobedient to the Lord.)

units.la: SEMEI maledicit Dauid, 2 Sam.16.v.5.7. veniam deprecatur, 19.19. Salomonis iussu interficitur, 1 Reg.2.46. ex præcepto Dauid, v.9. (simei, i. fama, auditus.)
units.tr: SHIMEI cursed David, 2 Sam. 16.5, 7. He begged pardon, 19.19. He was put to death at Solomon's command, 1 Kings 2.46, by David's order, v.9. (Shimei, i.e. report, hearing.)

units.la: SEMEIA, vir Dei, 1 Reg.12.22. 2 Paral.11.2. Roboamum à bello gerendo contra Israel dehortatur, 2 Reg.12.24. eius bri, 2 Par.12.15. (Audiens Dominum.)
units.tr: SHEMAIAH, a man of God, 1 Kings 12.22; 2 Chr. 11.2. He dissuaded Rehoboam from waging war against Israel, 2 Chr. 11.4. His book, 2 Chr. 12.15. (Hearing the Lord.)

units.la: SEMEIA, Pseudopropheta, Ieremiæ 29.31. eius punitio, 32.
units.tr: SHEMAIAH, a false prophet, Jer. 29.31. His punishment, Jer. 32.

units.la: SEMEN. pro posteritate, Luc.1.55. pro sobole. 2 Corinth 11.1 semen fratri mortuo, ex Legis præcepto, olim suscitandum, Ge.38.8. Deu.25.5. Ruth.4.5. semen Abrahæ verum qui ex Isaac nati, & filij promissionis sunt, Gen.21.12. V de ABRAHAE filij, semen Dauidis Christus, 2 Sam.7. v.12. &c. semen ex Iudæis, Apostoli, Roman.9.29. semen fructificans, Marc.4.27. semen paucum inobedientibus, Deut. 28.38. semen piorum benedictum, Psal.102.29. & 112.2. V de Pii. semen impiorum, V de IMPII semen, Dei verbum Luc.8.11. Vide VERBVM Dei. semini suo dat corpus suum Deus, 1 Cor.15.38.
units.tr: SEED: for posterity, Luke 1.55; for offspring, 2 Cor. 11.1. The seed of a brother who had died was to be raised up according to the precept of the Law, as in former times, Gen. 38.8; Deut. 25.5; Ruth 4.5. The true seed of Abraham are those born of Isaac, who are children of the promise, Gen. 21.12. See SONS OF ABRAHAM. The seed of David is Christ, 2 Sam. 7.12, etc. The seed from the Jews, the Apostles, Rom. 9.29. Fruitful seed, Mark 4.27. Little seed for the disobedient, Deut. 28.38. The seed of the pious is blessed, Ps. 102.29 and 112.2. See PIOUS. The seed of the impious: see IMPIOUS. The seed is the word of God, Luke 8.11. See WORD OF GOD. God gives to the seed its own body, 1 Cor. 15.38.

units.la: SEMENTIS & messis non cessant, Genes.8.22. existente terra.
units.tr: Sowing and harvest do not cease, Gen. 8.22, while the earth endures.

units.la: SEMINARE in benedictionibus, pro, liberaliter & hilari fronte, ac animo donare, 2 Corinth.9.6. &c. quæ seminatur etitus, Gal.6.7. &c. seminare carni, pro, huius vitæ cor modis inseruire, v.8. Quod qui facit, interitura metet.
units.tr: To sow in blessings: to give liberally and with a cheerful face and mind, 2 Cor. 9.6, etc. What a man sows, that he will also reap, Gal. 6.7, etc. To sow to the flesh: to serve the desires of this life in various ways, v.8. He who does so will reap corruption.

units.la: SEMINAN
units.tr: SOWER

units.la: EMINANTIS parabola, Matthæi 13.3. (Vide PARABOLA.) impari successu semen vitæ seri ostendens.
units.tr: PARABLE OF THE SOWER, Matt. 13.3. (See PARABLE.) Showing the seed of life sown with unequal success.

units.la: EMINIFLVVS vir, Leuit.15.2. De quo lex, versibus seq.
units.tr: MAN WITH A FLUX, Lev. 15.2. The law concerning him is in the following verses.

units.la: EMMA, vel samma, vir fortissimus, 2 Samu.23 11. magnam Philistheorum multitudinem interfecit, v.12.
units.tr: SHAMMAH, or Shamma, a very valiant man, 2 Sam. 23.11. He killed a great multitude of the Philistines, v.12.

units.la: NES quomodo admonendi, 1 Timoth 5 1. quales esse debeant, Tit.2.2. honorandi sunt, Leuit.19 32. Iob.32.6. Prou. 16.31. sensibus florebunt, Esa.65.20. senum consilium non aspernandum, 1 Reg.12.8. senex peccator maledictus, Esai. 65.20.
units.tr: OLD MEN: how they are to be admonished, 1 Tim. 5.1; what sort they ought to be, Titus 2.2; they are to be honoured, Lev. 19.32; Job 32.6; Prov. 16.31. They will flourish in their faculties, Isa. 65.20. The counsel of the elderly is not to be scorned, 1 Kings 12.8. An old sinner is cursed, Isa. 65.20.

units.la: NECTVTIS exempla: Abraham, Sara, Genes.18.11. & 24.1. Loth.19.31. Isaac,27.1. & 35.29. Iacob,44.20. & 48.10. Iosua, Ios.23.v.1.2. Gedeon Iudic.8.32. senex in Gabaa,19 16. &c. Noemi, Ruth.1.12. Eli,1 sam.2.22. & 4.18 Samuel,8 1 & 12, 2:Isai.17.12. Berzellai,2 Sam.19.v.31.32. Dauid, 1 Reg.1.1. 1 Paral.23.1 Salomon,1 Reg.11.4. Propheta quidam,13 11. Asa, Isa,15.23. Ioiada,2 Paral.24.15. Iob, Iob 42. v.16. 17. Zacharias,Luc.1.18. Paulus Philem.v.9 Ioannes, 2 Ioan. v.1.& 3, Ioan.v.1. (Vide LONGAEVITATIS exempla.) senectutis incommoda, Psal.90.v.10.11. V.Eccl.12.3.&c. commendatio, Prou. 16.31.
units.tr: Examples of old age and grey hair: Abraham and Sarah, Gen. 18.11 and 24.1. Lot, 19.31. Isaac, 27.1 and 35.29. Jacob, 44.20 and 48.10. Joshua, Josh. 23.1, 2. Gideon, Judg. 8.32. The old man in Gibeah, 19.16, etc. Naomi, Ruth 1.12. Eli, 1 Sam. 2.22 and 4.18. Samuel, 8.1 and 12. Isaiah 17.12. Barzillai, 2 Sam. 19.31, 32. David, 1 Kings 1.1; 1 Chr. 23.1. Solomon, 1 Kings 11.4. A certain prophet, 13.11. Asa, Isa. 15.23. Jehoiada, 2 Chr. 24.15. Job, Job 42.16, 17. Zechariah, Luke 1.18. Paul, Philem. v.9. John, 2 John v.1, and 3 John v.1. (See examples of longevity.) The inconveniences of old age, Ps. 90.10, 11; Eccl. 12.3, etc. Commendation: Prov. 16.31.

units.la: SENIORES: seniorum vocabulum, non tam ætatis, quàm dignitatis est, & eos designat, qui adiecto nonnunquam epitheto, potissimum in novo Testamento, dicuntur seniores populi, penes quos, sacerdotibus & scribis selectis adiunctis, erant iudicia, quæ Hebræi Græco vocabulo Sanhedrin, id est, συνέδρια vocant, ut ij plane sint, πρεσβύτεροι quos Latine eadem ratione senatores vocant, Matth. 16.21. & 27.41. Deut.21.2. seniores pro maioribus, Matt.15. Marc.7.3. seniores septuaginta sibi allegit Moses, Num. 11.16. V. Synedrium.
units.tr: ELDERS: the word "seniores" refers less to age than to dignity, and designates those who, sometimes with an added epithet, especially in the New Testament, are called elders of the people. With the chief priests and selected scribes joined to them, they held the judgments, which the Hebrews call by the Greek word Sanhedrin, that is, synedria [συνέδρια]. So they are plainly presbyters [πρεσβύτεροι], whom Latin writers for the same reason call senators, Matt. 16.21 and 27.41; Deut. 21.2. "Seniores" also means ancestors, Matt. 15; Mark 7.3. Moses chose seventy elders for himself, Num. 11.16. See SYNEDRIUM.

units.la: SENIORVM præcepta, Act.16 4 visio, Apo.4.4.
units.tr: PRECEPTS OF THE ELDERS, Acts 16.4. VISION OF THE ELDERS, Rev. 4.4.

units.la: SENIORIBVS traditur Deuteronomium, Deut.31 9.
units.tr: Deuteronomy was handed over to the elders, Deut. 31.9.

units.la: SENNACHERIB, Assyriorum rex, civitates Iuda obsidet, 2 Reg.18.13 2 Paral 32.1, eas expugnat, 2 Reg.18.13. Ezechiæ omnia dira minatur, v 20. blasphemat, v.35. Esai.36.1 &c. à filiis interficitur,2 Reg.19.37.2 Paral 32. 21. Esai.37.37. secundum verba Esaiæ, Esa.10.23.& 31.8. & 33.1. (1. Rubus destructionis.)
units.tr: Sennacherib, king of the Assyrians, besieges the cities of Judah, 2 Kings 18.13; 2 Chr. 32.1, and captures them, 2 Kings 18.13. He threatens Hezekiah with every dreadful thing, v.20. He blasphemes, v.35; Isa. 36.1, etc. He is killed by his sons, 2 Kings 19.37; 2 Chr. 32.21; Isa. 37.37, according to the words of Isaiah, Isa. 10.23; 31.8; 33.1. (1. A bramble of destruction.)

units.la: SENSVS carnis, pro humano iudicio, Coloss.2.18 sensus carnalis, 1 Ioan 5.20. sensum Christi tenet Paulus, Corint.2 16.sensum Dei nemo nouit, Rom.11.34. non sen- su, sed multitia pueri simus, 1 Corint.14.20, in sensu abun- det vnusquisque, seu certus sit, Roman. 14. 5. sensuum hu- manorum imbecillitas, Luc. 24.16. In sensum reprobum tradit D. impios, Rom.1 28.
units.tr: The sense of the flesh is human judgment, Col. 2.18. Carnal sense, 1 John 5.20. Paul holds the sense of Christ, 1 Cor. 2.16. No one knows the mind of God, Rom. 11.34. Let us be children not in understanding but in malice, 1 Cor. 14.20. Let each abound in his own sense, whether he is certain, Rom. 14.5. The weakness of human senses, Luke 24.16. God gives the impious over to a reprobate mind, Rom. 1.28.

units.la: SEPVLTVRA antiqua est: sepultorum honorifice exempla: Sara, Genes.23.v.4.15. Abraham 25.8.9. Debora nutrix Rebecca, 35.8. Rachel, v.19.& 48.7. Iacob, 49.v.29. &c. 50.5. &c. Ioseph, v.24.25.26. Exod.13.19. Iosue 24.32. Rebecca, Lia, Gen.49.v.30.31. Maria, Num.20.1. Aaron, v.28. Deut.10,6. Moses a Deo, 34.v.5.6. Eleazar, Iosua 24.33. Iosua, 24. v.29.30. Iud.2.v.8 9. Gedeon.8.32. Thola, 10.v.1.2. Iair, v.5. Iephte 12.7. Abesan, v.10. Aialon, v.12. Abdon, v.15. Samson, 16.31. Samuel, 1 Sam 25.1. & 28.3. Saul, & Ionathas, 31.12.13. Sam.2.5 &c. Abel, 2 Sam.2, v.31.32. Abner, 3.31. Isboieth, 4. 12. Achitophel, 17.23. Saul, Ionathas, & septem filij eius, 21. 12. Dauid, 1 Reg.2.10. Ioab, v.34. Salomon 11.43: Prophet verbo Dei inobediens, 13.v.29.30. Filius Ieroboam, 14.ver. 17.18. Roboam, v.31. Abia, 15.8. Asa, v.24.2. Paral.16.v.13.14. 3 Esd.1 v.30.31. Baasa, 1 Reg 16.6. Amri, v.28. Achab, 22.37. Iosaphat, v.51. Ioram.2 Reg.8.24, Ochosias, 9. 28. Iehu.10. 35. Ioas.12.21.& 14 16. Ioachas, 13 9. Elisæus, v.20. Amasias, 14.v.19.20. Azarias, 15.7. Ioatham, v.38. Achas, 16 20.2 Paral.28.27. Manasses 2 Reg.21.18. Amon, v.26. Iosias 23.v.25. 30.2 Chron.35.24. Ioiada, 2 Paral.24.16. Ozas, 26.23. Ezechias,32.33. Ioannes Baptista, Matth.14.12. Iesus, Marc.1. 46,Ioan.19.v.38.39 40. Ananias, Act.5.5. vxor eius, v.9. Stephanus, 8.2.
units.tr: BURIAL is ancient. Examples of honourable burial of the dead: Sarah, Gen. 23.4, 15. Abraham, 25.8, 9. Deborah, nurse of Rebekah, 35.8. Rachel, v.19; 48.7. Jacob, 49.29, etc.; 50.5, etc. Joseph, v.24-26; Exod. 13.19; Josh. 24.32. Rebekah and Leah, Gen. 49.30, 31. Miriam, Num. 20.1. Aaron, v.28; Deut. 10.6. Moses, buried by God, Deut. 34.5, 6. Eleazar, Josh. 24.33. Joshua, 24.29, 30; Judg. 2.8, 9. Gideon, 8.32. Tola, 10.1, 2. Jair, v.5. Jephthah, 12.7. Ibzan, v.10. Elon, v.12. Abdon, v.15. Samson, 16.31. Samuel, 1 Sam. 25.1; 28.3. Saul and Jonathan, 31.12, 13; 2 Sam. 2.5, etc. Abner, 2 Sam. 3.31, 32. Ishbosheth, 4.12. Ahithophel, 17.23. Saul, Jonathan and his seven sons, 21.12. David, 1 Kings 2.10. Joab, v.34. Solomon, 11.43. A prophet disobedient to the word of God, 13.29, 30. The son of Jeroboam, 14.17, 18. Rehoboam, v.31. Abijah, 15.8. Asa, v.24; 2 Chr. 16.13, 14; 1 Esd. 1.30, 31. Baasha, 1 Kings 16.6. Omri, v.28. Ahab, 22.37. Jehoshaphat, v.51. Joram, 2 Kings 8.24. Ahaziah, 9.28. Jehu, 10.35. Joash, 12.21 and 14.16. Jehoahaz, 13.9. Elisha, v.20. Amaziah, 14.19, 20. Azariah, 15.7. Jotham, v.38. Ahaz, 16.20; 2 Chr. 28.27. Manasseh, 2 Kings 21.18. Amon, v.26. Josiah, 23.25, 30; 2 Chr. 35.24. Jehoiada, 2 Chr. 24.16. Uzziah, 26.23. Hezekiah, 32.33. John the Baptist, Matt. 14.12. Jesus, Mark 15.46; John 19.38-40. Ananias, Acts 5.5; his wife, v.9. Stephen, 8.2.

units.la: Sepultura honorifica carere, afflictio est, & iræ diuinæ ac vindictæ signum. Exempla: Iezabel, 2 Reg.9.33. Israel, Psalm.79 3. Ioram, 2 Paralipom.21.19. Iudæi, Ierem. 16. ver.1.2.& 4.16 & 16.v.4.5.6.7.& 25.23. Ioachim, 22. ver.19. Sedecias.34.5. Prophetæ Euangelici, Apocal.11.9. Sepultorum ossa ex sepulchris eiici,& ad Solem expandi, iræ diuinæ aduersus peccatores accensæ signum, Ierem.
units.tr: To lack honourable burial is an affliction and a sign of divine wrath and vengeance. Examples: Jezebel, 2 Kings 9.33. Israel, Ps. 79.3. Joram, 2 Chr. 21.19. The Jews, Jer. 16.1, 2; 4.16; 16.4-7; 25.23. Jehoiakim, 22.19. Zedekiah, 34.5. The prophets of the Gospel, Rev. 11.9. For the bones of the dead to be cast out of their tombs and spread out to the sun is a sign of divine wrath kindled against sinners, Jer.

units.la: SEPHARVAIM incolæ, idolo Adramelech filios suos adolebant, 2 Reg. 17.31. Vide Idolorum catalogus.
units.tr: SEPHARVAIM, inhabitants, who burned their sons to the idol Adrammelech, 2 Kings 17.31. See the catalogue of idols.

units.la: SEPHORA, vna ex piis Hebræorum Obstetricibus, Exodi 1.15. (i. pulchra.)
units.tr: SHIPHRAH, one of the pious Hebrew midwives, Exod. 1.15. (i.e. beautiful.)

units.la: SEPHORA, vxor Mosis, Exod. 2.21 : filium Gerson circumcidit, 4.25.
units.tr: ZIPPORAH, wife of Moses, Exod. 2.21; she circumcised her son Gershom, 4.25.

units.la: SEPTENARIVS numerus, V. Nvmerus septenarius.
units.tr: SEPTENARY NUMBER. See SEPTENARY NUMBER.

units.la: SEPTVAGINTA Discipuli prædicant, Luc. 10.1.17. &c.
units.tr: The seventy disciples preach, Luke 10.1, 17, etc.

units.la: SEPVLCHRA concupiscentiæ, Num. 11.34. sepulchrum Mosis ignoratur, Deut. 34.6. sepulchra dealbata, Matth. 23.27. sepulchrum Christi, 27.57. &c. in sepulchra Prophetarum extruentes, 23.29. In morte Christi sepulchra aperta sunt: Mat. 27.52.
units.tr: Sepulchres of lust, Num. 11.34. The sepulchre of Moses is unknown, Deut. 34.6. Whitewashed sepulchres, Matt. 23.27. The sepulchre of Christ, 27.57, etc. Building the sepulchres of the prophets, 23.29. At the death of Christ the sepulchres were opened, Matt. 27.52.

units.la: SEQVITVR Caleb Deum, Numer. 14.24. Deuter. 1.36. sequi Christum, crux, Mat. 10.38. sequi vestigia Christi, 1 Petr. 2.21. sequens Christum, immobilis fit, Matth. 8.22. sequens Christum propter temporalia, 8.19. sequentibus Christum nihil deest, 14.15. sequendus Deus, Deut. 13.4. 1 Sam. 12.14. Exempl. Iosue & Caleb. Num. 32.12. Tubæ, Matth. 12.15. Væ horrendum sectatoribus deorum alienorum. Deutero. 28.14. &c.
units.tr: Caleb follows God, Num. 14.24; Deut. 1.36. To follow Christ is the cross, Matt. 10.38. To follow the footsteps of Christ, 1 Pet. 2.21. One who follows Christ becomes unmoved, Matt. 8.22. Following Christ for temporal things, 8.19. Nothing is lacking to those who follow Christ, 14.15. God is to be followed, Deut. 13.4; 1 Sam. 12.14. Example: Joshua and Caleb, Num. 32.12. Trumpets, Matt. 12.15. Dreadful woe to the followers of foreign gods, Deut. 28.14, etc.

units.la: SERAPHIN, Angelici ordinis nomen, q.d. ardentes, quia sunt naturæ lucidæ, Ps. 104.4. Vel quia ardent amore Dei & Ecclesiæ: Isa. 6.v.2.3.
units.tr: SERAPHIM, the name of an angelic order, that is, "burning ones," because they are of a luminous nature, Ps. 104.4. Or because they burn with love for God and the Church, Isa. 6.2, 3.

units.la: SERGIVS Paulus Proconsul, Actor. 13.7. Paulum & Barnabam audire cupit, ibidem. eorum sermonibus credit, versicul. 12. quem Elymas a fide quærebat avertere: ver. 8.
units.tr: SERGIUS Paulus, the proconsul, Acts 13.7. He desired to hear Paul and Barnabas, ibid. He believed their words, verse 12, whom Elymas sought to turn away from the faith, verse 8.

units.la: SERIT Israel, perdit omnia, & quare, Iudic. 6. versicu. 1.2.3. &c.
units.tr: ISRAEL sows and loses everything, and why, Judg. 6, verses 1, 2, 3, etc.

units.la: SERMO prudens sale conditus Col. 4.6. in quo lingua non præcurrit, sed contra mens linguam, qui cum ædificatione aliquid admissæ honestæ vrbanitatis habet & sapit. Denique moderatio linguæ dici debet tota hæc virtus: de qua Iac. 3.1 Petr. 3.10. & in Prouerb. agitur. Ephes. 4.29.
units.tr: A prudent speech, seasoned with salt, Col. 4.6, in which the tongue does not run ahead of the mind but the mind governs the tongue. Such speech, with edification, has and savours of some admissible decent wit. In short, this whole virtue ought to be called the moderation of the tongue, which is treated of in James 3.1, 1 Pet. 3.10, and in Proverbs. See Eph. 4.29.

units.la: Sermo putris σαπρὸς Eph. 4.29. qui cordis nostri fœtorem, & in blasphemiis, vel obscœnis cogitationibus nequitiam ore ipso & verbis prodit. Mat. 12.36.
units.tr: Corrupt speech, σαπρὸς, Eph. 4.29, which betrays the stench of our heart and the wickedness of blasphemies or obscene thoughts by the mouth and its words, Matt. 12.36.

units.la: SERMO, aut verbum, ex Hebræorum idiotismo : Prio ò, pro re quauis aut indefinita particula. Vide VERBVM. Secundo, pro viua voce, aut libris conscriptis, 2 Thess. 1. 2.2, pro sponsione, seu promissione, Tit.1,3. κατ' ἐξοχὴν, pro doctrina Euangelica, Actor.16 6. Philip.1.14. quæ dicitur sermo Christi, Coloss.3 16. sermo vitæ, Philip.2.15. sermo veritatis, 2 Cor.6.7. sermo iustitiæ, quo docetur iustitia, hoc est, Euangelium, Heb.5.13. quam significationem obtinet iustitiæ vox, Rom.1. v.17. 18. sermo vnus omnibus, ante extructam turrim Babel, Genes.11.1.
units.tr: SPEECH, or word, in the Hebrew idiom: first, for any thing whatever, or as an indefinite particle. See WORD. Second, for the living voice or for written books, 2 Thess. 2.2; for a promise or pledge, Titus 1.3; par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν], for the Gospel doctrine, Acts 16.6, Phil. 1.14, which is called the word of Christ, Col. 3.16; the word of life, Phil. 2.15; the word of truth, 2 Cor. 6.7; the word of righteousness, by which righteousness, that is, the Gospel, is taught, Heb. 5.13, a meaning which the word "righteousness" also bears, Rom. 1.17, 18; one speech for all, before the tower of Babel was built, Gen. 11.1.

units.la: Sermo pro fucata dicendi ratione, 2 Corint. 11. 6. pro pietatis doctrina Gal.6.6. sermo damnandus, Eph.4. 29. Col.3.8. sermo laudandus, Prou.15.v.1.23.& 16.21.& 25.15. sermo piorum qualis, Matth.5.37.& 12.36.37. Eph.4.19. & 5.3 Col.3 8. 1 Petr.3.10. (Vide Pn) Sermo caro factus est, Ioan.1.14. hoc est, homo factus est, per synecdochen, vt Esa.40 5, Ioel.2 28.(V. Caro) Sermo auditionis Hebraeis, pro sermone auribus percepto 1, Thessal.3.13. Sermonem Dei quaerere, 1 Reg.22.5. Vt in sermone confirmet nos Deus, orat Paulus, 2 Thessal.2.17. sermones Dei loquatur, qui loquitur, 1 Petr. 4.11. sermo Dei & eius natura, Vide Deus. sermones Dei proiicere, 1 Sam.15.26.
units.tr: Speech for a varnished manner of speaking, 2 Cor. 11.6; for the doctrine of piety, Gal. 6.6; damnable speech, Eph. 4.29, Col. 3.8; praiseworthy speech, Prov. 15.1, 23; 16.21; 25.15; what sort of speech the pious use, Matt. 5.37; 12.36, 37; Eph. 4.19; 5.3; Col. 3.8; 1 Pet. 3.10 (See Pn). The Word was made flesh, John 1.14, that is, man was made, by synecdoche, as in Isa. 40.5 and Joel 2.28 (See FLESH). Speech of hearing, in the Hebrew sense, for speech perceived by the ears, 1 Thess. 3.13. To seek the word of God, 1 Kings 22.5. That God may confirm us in word, Paul prays, 2 Thess. 2.17. Let him who speaks, speak the words of God, 1 Pet. 4.11. The word of God and its nature: see God. To cast off the words of God, 1 Sam. 15.26.

units.la: [SERMO, sermones, Verbum, Verba Domini Dei, quibus mediate vel immediate voluntatem suam hominibus piis, aut etiam impiis manifestat. Gen.15.1 Exo.17.1. Leuitic.8.5. Numer.4.37. Deut.1.26. 1 Sam.3.11. 1.7.17.18.19. 2 Sam.7.4.1 Reg.2.4. 2 Reg.1.17 Psal.50 17. & 119. v.9.16.17.42.131. Esai.66.2 Dan.9 2.&c. Ioan.17.17. Rom.3 4. 2 Thessal.3.1. Heb.4.12. 1 Petr.4.11.
units.tr: [WORD, words, the Word, the words of the Lord God, by which he makes his will known to pious men, or even to impious men, mediately or immediately: Gen. 15.1; Exod. 17.1; Lev. 8.5; Num. 4.37; Deut. 1.26; 1 Sam. 3.11; 1.7, 17, 18, 19; 2 Sam. 7.4; 1 Kings 2.4; 2 Kings 1.17; Ps. 50.17; 119.9, 16, 17, 42, 131; Isa. 66.2; Dan. 9.2, etc.; John 17.17; Rom. 3.4; 2 Thess. 3.1; Heb. 4.12; 1 Pet. 4.11.

units.la: Sermo hominis ad hominem, Gen.4.23. Exo.2.15. Num. 23.2. Deut.4.21. Psal.55.22. Eccl.5.v.1.2 5.6. Mat.6.37 Col. 4.5. sermo, nempe internus, cogitatio, visio, Dan.2.v.5.8. 10.11.23. Ezec.38 10. Fama, Luc.5.15.& 7.17. Negotium, in quo vltro citroque varia dicta & facta concurrunt. Gene. 24.50.1 Sam.10.16. Prou.25.2. scriptura, scriptum rem aliquam continens, Esd.5.7. Dan.5.v.15.:6.
units.tr: The speech of man to man, Gen. 4.23; Exod. 2.15; Num. 23.2; Deut. 4.21; Ps. 55.22; Eccl. 5.1, 2, 5, 6; Matt. 6.37; Col. 4.5. Speech, namely inward speech, thought, or vision, Dan. 2.5, 8; 10.11, 23; Ezek. 38.10. Report, Luke 5.15; 7.17. Business, in which various sayings and deeds run back and forth, Gen. 24.50; 1 Sam. 10.16; Prov. 25.2. Writing, a document containing some matter, Ezra 5.7; Dan. 5.15; 6.

units.la: Sermones gesta, res gestae, 1 Reg.14.29.& 15. ver.7.23.31.& 16.versi.5.14.20.27. sermones dierum, Diaria, Chronica, 1 Reg.22.39. 2 Reg.1.18. &c.]
units.tr: Speeches, that is, deeds, things done, 1 Kings 14.29; 15.7, 23, 31; 16.5, 14, 20, 27. Speeches of days, diaries, chronicles, 1 Kings 22.39; 2 Kings 1.18, etc.]

units.la: SERPENS attutum animal, Genes.3.1. Euam decipit, 3.v.4.5.1 Tim.2 14. a Deo maledicitur, Gen.3.14. Initio familiare homini v.1. sed quia satan eius ministerio vsus est ad decipiendum hominem, truces inimicitiae ortae sunt: v.15. Isai. 59.5. Iob.20.16. foeminae oblonga ova pariunt, Isai. 59. 5. Dracones volantes, Isai.14.29 & 30 6. Magorum sibilis incantari antari potest: Pf.58 4 Hier. 8 17. Ita vt tunc nocere non possit: Eccl. 10.11. V. Marc. 16 18.
units.tr: The SERPENT, a subtle animal, Gen. 3.1. It deceives Eve, Gen. 3.4, 5; 2 Tim. 2.14. It is cursed by God, Gen. 3.14. At first it was familiar to man, v. 1; but because Satan used its service to deceive man, fierce enmities arose, v. 15. Isa. 59.5; Job 20.16. Female serpents lay long eggs, Isa. 59.5. Flying serpents, Isa. 14.29 and 30.6. A serpent can be charmed by the hissing of magicians, Ps. 58.4; Jer. 8.17, so that it cannot then do harm, Eccl. 10.11. See Mark 16.18.

units.la: SERPENS æneus à Moïse erigitur, Num. 21.9. Figura Christi est, Ioan. 3.14. ab Ezechia frangitur, 2 Reg. 18.4. & appellatur Nehustan. ibid. [Serpens, antiquus, Diabolus, Satan, Gen. 3. v. 13. 14. Esa. 27.1.2 Cor. 11 3. Apoc. 12. v. 9. 14. 15. & 20 2.]
units.tr: The bronze serpent is raised up by Moses, Num. 21.9. It is a figure of Christ, John 3.14. It is broken by Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18.4, and is called Nehushtan, ibid. [Serpent, the ancient one, the Devil, Satan, Gen. 3.13, 14; Isa. 27.1, 2; 2 Cor. 11.3; Rev. 12.9, 14, 15; 20.2.]

units.la: SERPENTIS figura hæc erat, vt ex populo pestilerum morituri moribundi, peccata confitentes, & in serpentem æneum perticæ impositum intuentes, sanitatem reciperent: Num. 21.5. 6 7. &c.
units.tr: This was the figure of the serpent: that from among the people, those dying of the plague, confessing their sins and looking upon the bronze serpent set on a pole, would receive health, Num. 21.5, 6, 7, etc.

units.la: Significatio erat fideles diaboli morsu in æternum morituros, peccata confitentes, ex fide in Christum crucifixum intuitu, sanitatem ad vitam æternam recipere. Ioh. 3.14 15. & 12. 32.
units.tr: The meaning was that believers, destined to die eternally from the bite of the devil, confessing their sins and looking by faith upon Christ crucified, receive health unto eternal life, John 3.14, 15; 12.32.

units.la: SERPENTES igniti puniendis Israelitis mittuntur, Numer. 21 6. serpentes vocantur Pharisæi Matth. 23 33. serpentina prudentia commendatur, 10. 16. [serpentes, aperti & operti Ecclesiæ hostes, squamæ satanæ, Esai. 27.1. Matth. 23.33.]
units.tr: Fiery serpents are sent to punish the Israelites, Num. 21.6. The Pharisees are called serpents, Matt. 23.33. Serpentine prudence is commended, Matt. 10.16. [Serpents, open and hidden enemies of the Church, the scales of Satan, Isa. 27.1; Matt. 23.33.]

units.la: SERVATORIS nomen etiam Patri tribuitur, 1 Timoth. 1.1. V. saluator.
units.tr: The name of Saviour is also given to the Father, 1 Tim. 1.1. See SAVIOUR.

units.la: SERVIRE duobus dominis impossibile, Matth. 6.24. servire Deo, Ios. 22.27. Deo & Dæmonibus, 2 Regum. 17.25. &c. serviendum soli Deo, Exod. 23.25 Deut. 6 13 & 10.12. & 11. 13 & 13.4. Matt. 4.10. Luc. 4 8 1 Tim. 1 9.17. vt serviremus, redemit nos Christus, 1 Thess. 1.9. serviamus invicem, Gal. 5 13.
units.tr: It is impossible to serve two masters, Matt. 6.24. To serve God, Josh. 22.27; to serve God and demons, 2 Kings 17.25, etc. One must serve God alone, Exod. 23.25; Deut. 6.13; 10.12; 11.13; 13.4; Matt. 4.10; Luke 4.8; 1 Tim. 1.9, 17. Christ redeemed us that we might serve, 1 Thess. 1.9. Let us serve one another, Gal. 5.13.

units.la: SERVITVS ex peccato Genes. 9.25. seruitus peccati, Ioan. 8. 34 Rom. 6.20, seruitus sanctimoniae, v. 18. 19. 22. Gal. 5. 13. 1 Petr. 2.16. seruitus pro coniugalis vinculi obligat one, 1 Corinth. 7.15. seruitutis & adoptionis Spiritus, vocatur à Paulo ipse spiritus sanctus, Roman. 8.15. seruitus est circumcidi, Galat. 2. 4. seruitium Dei quale, Luc. 1.74 75. à seruitute Diaboli liberati, Deut. 5. 6. 15. Legis, Hebr. 2.15. (V. Ophthalmodulia) à iugo seruitutis, Gal. 5. 1.
units.tr: Servitude from sin, Gen. 9.25; the servitude of sin, John 8.34; Rom. 6.20; the servitude of holiness, v. 18, 19, 22; Gal. 5.13; 1 Pet. 2.16; the servitude that the bond of marriage imposes, 1 Cor. 7.15; the Spirit of servitude and of adoption, which Paul calls the Holy Spirit himself, Rom. 8.15; it is servitude to be circumcised, Gal. 2.4; what kind of service to God, Luke 1.74, 75; freed from servitude to the Devil, Deut. 5.6, 15; of the Law, Heb. 2.15 (See Ophthalmodulia); from the yoke of servitude, Gal. 5.1.

units.la: SERVVS, quomodo à pueritia tractandus, Prou. 39. vers. 21. seruus Hebræus quousque detinendus, & quomodo tractandus, Exo. 21.2. &c. Leuit. 25.39. Deut. 15 12. Ierem. 34. 14. serui, qui perpetuæ se addixit seruituti, subula auris est perforanda, Exod. 21.6, Deut. 15.17. (vide Psalm. 40. 7. Hebr. 10.5.) Vide PORTAE & SECVLVM. Seruus sugiens, Deuterom.23.15. seruus damnatur,14. 35, seruus laudandus. v.35. & 17.2. & 27.18.Serui nomen tribuitur etiam Christo,Esa.42.1 Matth.12.18. iuxta illud Philipp. 2.7.quatenus fuit Minister, & quidem Prophetarum caput. Per serui formam autem quid intelligat Paulus, Vide FORMA.Seruus Dei, κατ' ἐξοχὴν[?], pro Mose, Apocal.15.3. vt describitur Deut.34.10. Num.12.7.serui fidelis descriptio,Matth.24.45.mali,vers.48. seruus Christianorum, 20. v.26.27. seruus Dei esse nequit, qui quærit hominibus placere,Galat.1.10. seruus Abrahami,Genes.24.2.&c. seruus omnium,Paulus,1 Corinth.9.19. seruus probus Iacob.Genes.31.38.seruus non est maior domino suo, Ioan.15.20.
units.tr: The servant: how he is to be treated from childhood, Prov. 39.21. How long a Hebrew servant is to be kept, and how he is to be treated, Exod. 21.2, etc.; Lev. 25.39; Deut. 15.12; Jer. 34.14. A servant who has bound himself to perpetual servitude: his ear is to be pierced with an awl, Exod. 21.6; Deut. 15.17 (see Ps. 40.7; Heb. 10.5). See GATES and AGE. A fugitive servant, Deut. 23.15. A servant is condemned, 14.35; a servant is praised, v. 35; 17.2; 27.18. The name of servant is also given to Christ, Isa. 42.1; Matt. 12.18, in accordance with Phil. 2.7, inasmuch as he was a minister, and indeed the head of the prophets. For what Paul understands by the form of a servant, see FORM. The servant of God, par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν], is Moses, Rev. 15.3, as he is described in Deut. 34.10 and Num. 12.7. Description of the faithful servant, Matt. 24.45; of the wicked, v. 48. A servant of Christians, 20.26, 27. He cannot be a servant of God who seeks to please men, Gal. 1.10. Servant of Abraham, Gen. 24.2, etc. A servant of all: Paul, 1 Cor. 9.19. A good servant: Jacob, Gen. 31.38. A servant is not greater than his lord, John 15.20.

units.la: SERVI Dei Israelitæ, Leui.25.42. seruri Dei omnes nos, quibus taleta data sunt,Matt.25.14. seruus Dei sumus inutiles, Luc.17.10. seruri Dei sumus, liberati à peccato, Ioan.8.36. Roman.6.22. serui Diaboli, liberati per Christum,Deut.6.12. serui Iudæorum, peregrini, Leui.25.44. serui peccati Ioan.8.34. serui Regis omnes,1 Sam.8.17. serui quales esse debeant, Ephes.6.5. Col.3.22.1 Tim.6.1. Tit.2.9.1.Petri 2.18. serui sumus iustitiæ, Rom.6.18. de seruis emendis Exod.21.2.Deut.15.12.
units.tr: SERVANTS of God: the Israelites, Lev. 25.42. We are all servants of God, to whom talents have been given, Matt. 25.14. We are unprofitable servants of God, Luke 17.10. We are servants of God, freed from sin, John 8.36; Rom. 6.22. Servants of the Devil, freed through Christ, Deut. 6.12. Servants of the Jews, foreigners, Lev. 25.44. Servants of sin, John 8.34. All are servants of the King, 1 Sam. 8.17. What sort of servants they ought to be, Eph. 6.5; Col. 3.22; 1 Tim. 6.1; Titus 2.9; 1 Pet. 2.18. We are servants of righteousness, Rom. 6.18. On buying servants, Exod. 21.2; Deut. 15.12.

units.la: [SERVI Dei & Iesu Christi peculiari quadam ratione dicuntur Patriarchæ, Prophetæ, Apostoli,& alij in V.& NT. vocatione magnifica in domo Dei & insignibus donis ad Ecclesiæ ædificationem vocati. Serui Dei etiam vocantur Principes & Heroes, quorum opera Deus vsus est,vt pios conseruaret & impios coerceret. Nominatim verò Messias,nempe Iesus Christus,mediator noster,ratione intercessionis & redemptionis, quam in statu humiliationis impleuit,Seruus Dei,& Dauid(qui typus Messiæ fuit)apud Prophetas appellatur. Dauid autem,typus Christi,promissiones regni æterni, in Messia fundati,adeptus,speciali quadam prærogatiua seruus Dei vocatur & propter illum,nempe ratione promissionis in Christo stabilitæ,Ecclesia liberanda dicitur.]
units.tr: [SERVANTS of God and of Jesus Christ are called, in a certain peculiar sense, the Patriarchs, the Prophets, the Apostles, and others in the Old and New Testaments who were called to a glorious ministry in the house of God and with distinguished gifts for the building up of the Church. Servants of God are also called princes and heroes, through whose works God made use to preserve the pious and restrain the impious. Specifically, the Messiah, namely Jesus Christ, our mediator, by reason of the intercession and redemption which he accomplished in the state of humiliation, is called, among the Prophets, servant of God, as is David (who was a type of the Messiah). David, however, a type of Christ, who obtained the promises of an eternal kingdom founded in the Messiah, is called servant of God by a special prerogative; and on account of him, namely by reason of the promise established in Christ, the Church is said to be delivered.]

units.la: SERVORVM conditio, Exod. 21. 20. 1 Corint.7.21,1.Timot.6.1.Seruorum & famularum consolatio, & erga dominos ac dominas suas officium, Genes.16.v.4 6.9. & 24.v.1 2 &c.& 30.25.& 31.4. & 39.v.1.6.Exodi 2.v.20.1 Reg.5.ver. 20.25.Prouerb.14.35. & 17.2.&19.10. &. 29.19. Ecclef.2.7. Ecclef.7.22,& 10.28. Ieremiæ 34.8. Ioel.2.29.Luc.12.v.37 45. Act. 12. 13. 1 Cor. 7. 22. Ephes. 6. v. 5. 6 8. Coloss. 3. 22. 1 Timoth. 6. v. 1. 2. Tit. 2. 9. 1 Petr. 2, v. 18. 19. Serui Dei fides habenda, Exod. 4. 1 Deuter. 18. 15. 2. Paral. 26. 20. Serui Dei confirmatio necessaria. Exempla: Elias, 2. Reg. 1. 15. Paulus, Actor. 27. 24. Seruorum frugi exempla: Seruus Abrahae, Genes. 24. v. 10. 12. Iacob. 30. 29. Ioseph. 39. 8. serui Dauidis, 2 Sam. 15. 15. Ethai, & qui cum eo erant, v. 22. serui hominis peregrè profecti, Matth. 25. v. 16. 17. Nobilis cuiusdam serui, minas habentes, Luc. 19. v. 16. 18. serui Cornelij, Actor. 10. 7.
units.tr: SERVANTS: the condition of servants, Exod. 21. 20; 1 Cor. 7. 21; 1 Tim. 6. 1. The consolation of male and female servants, and their duty toward their masters and mistresses, Gen. 16. 4, 6, 9; 24. 1, 2, etc.; 30. 25; 31. 4; 39. 1, 6; Exod. 2. 20; 1 Kings 5. 20, 25; Prov. 14. 35; 17. 2; 19. 10; 29. 19; Eccl. 2. 7; Eccl. 7. 22; 10. 28; Jer. 34. 8; Joel 2. 29; Luke 12. 37, 45; Acts 12. 13; 1 Cor. 7. 22; Eph. 6. 5, 6, 8; Col. 3. 22; 1 Tim. 6. 1, 2; Titus 2. 9; 1 Pet. 2. 18, 19. Faith is to be placed in the servant of God, Exod. 4. 1; Deut. 18. 15; 2 Chron. 26. 20. The confirmation of the servant of God is necessary. Examples: Elijah, 2 Kings 1. 15; Paul, Acts 27. 24. Examples of worthy servants: Abraham's servant, Gen. 24. 10, 12; Jacob, 30. 29; Joseph, 39. 8; the servants of David, 2 Sam. 15. 15; Ittai, and those who were with him, v. 22; the servants of a man travelling abroad, Matt. 25. 16, 17; the servants of a certain nobleman, having minas, Luke 19. 16, 18; the servants of Cornelius, Acts 10. 7.

units.la: Seruorum in remala facilius obtemperantium exempla: Serui Pharaonis, Exodi. 9. verf. 34. 35. & 14. 5. serui Saulis, 1 Sam. 18. v. 22. 23. & 19. 11. & 28. v. 6. 7. Doeg Idumeus, 22. v. 17. 18. serui Dauidis, 2 Sam. 11. 4. Ioab. v. 15. 16. & 24. 4. serui Absalonis, 13. 28. & 14. v. 29. 30. Seniores Israel, 1 Reg. 21. ver. 9. 10. 11. Vrias Sacerdos, 2 Reg. 16. v. 10. 11. serui Ioas, 2. Paral. 24. 21. Nabuchodonosor, Dan. 3. verf. 19. 20. &c. Cursores Assueri, Esth. 3. 13. Satellites Herodis, Marc. 6. 17. Custodes carceris, Act. 16. 24. Vide MANDATIS impiis & inhonestis parentium exempla. Seruorum maiorum exempla: Pincerna & Pistor Pharaonis, Genes. 40. 1. serui Semei, 1 Reg. 2. 39. Giezi, 2. Reg. 5. v. 21. 22. serui Ioas Regis Iuda, 12. v. 20. 21. 2. Paral. 24. 25. serui Amon Regis Iuda, 21. v. 22. 23. serui Assueri, Esther 2. 21. seruorum malorum descriptio, Matt. 24. 48. Luc. 12. 45.
units.tr: Examples of servants who more readily obeyed in evil: the servants of Pharaoh, Exod. 9. 34, 35; 14. 5; the servants of Saul, 1 Sam. 18. 22, 23; 19. 11; 28. 6, 7; Doeg the Edomite, 22. 17, 18; the servants of David, 2 Sam. 11. 4; Joab, v. 15, 16; 24. 4; the servants of Absalom, 13. 28; 14. 29, 30; the elders of Israel, 1 Kings 21. 9, 10, 11; Uriah the priest, 2 Kings 16. 10, 11; the servants of Joash, 2 Chron. 24. 21; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3. 19, 20, etc.; the couriers of Ahasuerus, Esther 3. 13; Herod's guards, Mark 6. 17; the jailers, Acts 16. 24. See MANDATES: examples of impious and dishonourable commands of parents. Examples of the worst servants: Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker, Gen. 40. 1; the servants of Shimei, 1 Kings 2. 39; Gehazi, 2 Kings 5. 21, 22; the servants of Joash, king of Judah, 12. 20, 21; 2 Chron. 24. 25; the servants of Amon, king of Judah, 2 Kings 21. 22, 23; the servants of Ahasuerus, Esther 2. 21. A description of evil servants, Matt. 24. 48; Luke 12. 45.

units.la: SAC, Ægypti Rex, Ierosolymam obsidet, 1 Reg. 14. 25. Templum diripit, v. 26. 2. Paral. 12. 9. (1. byssus laxeus). Sesach, Dea Babyloniorum, Cuius respectu Caldaeorum monarcha rex Sesach nominatur, Ierem. 25. 26. & 51. 41.
units.tr: SAC: the king of Egypt besieges Jerusalem, 1 Kings 14. 25; he plunders the Temple, v. 26; 2 Chron. 12. 9 (1. fine linen). Sesach, goddess of the Babylonians, in view of whom the monarch of the Chaldeans is called king Sesach, Jer. 25. 26; 51. 41.

units.la: Sessio, sedes, 1 Sam. 20. 18. Esther. 5. 9. Psalm. 139. 2 Thren. 3. 63.
units.tr: Sitting, seat, 1 Sam. 20. 18; Esther 5. 9; Ps. 139. 2; Lam. 3. 63.

units.la: Sessio, Sedere, Sedes, Deo, Patri, Filio, Spiritui S. Angelis, Ecclesiae, homini, &c. tribuuntur. De his ergo distincte quaedam annotanda videntur. (Vide Sedere).
units.tr: Sitting, to sit, seat are attributed to God, the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit, the angels, the Church, man, etc. Certain points about these therefore seem worth noting separately. (See "to sit.")

units.la: 1. Sedere igitur, humano more loquendo, Deus dicitur, 1 sam. 4. 4. 2. sam. 6 2 1. Reg. 22. 19 2. Reg. 19 15 Psalm. 9. 5 & 29. 10. & 47. 9. & 89 2. & 99. 1. Esai. 6. 1. & 37. 16. & 40. 22. Dan. 7. 9. Ioel. 3. 12. Matt. 23. 22. Apoc. 21. 5.
units.tr: 1. To sit, then, is said of God in human manner of speaking: 1 Sam. 4. 4; 2 Sam. 6. 2; 1 Kings 22. 19; 2 Kings 19. 15; Ps. 9. 5; 29. 10; 47. 9; 89. 2; 99. 1; Isa. 6. 1; 37. 16; 40. 22; Dan. 7. 9; Joel 3. 12; Matt. 23. 22; Rev. 21. 5.

units.la: 3. Deus Filius, Iesus Christus, Mediatoris partes adimplens in terris, Iudic. 6.11. Isai.16.5. Malac.3.3. Act.2.30. Conuersans in statu humiliationis inter homines, Matth. 5.1. & 13.ver.12. &.15.29. & 21.v.5.7. & 24.3. & 26.55. Luc.2. 46. & 4.20. &5.v 3 17. Ioan.4.6. & 6.3. & 8.2. & 12.v.14.15. In statu gloriæ Psalm.110.1. Zach.6.13. Matth.19.28. & 20.23. & 22.44. & 25.31. & 26.64. Marc.16.19. Luc.22.69. Coloss.3. 1. Hebr.1.v 3,13,& 10,12. & 12,2, Apocal.3,21,& 19.v 11,19, 21,& 20,11.
units.tr: 3. God the Son, Jesus Christ, fulfilling the office of Mediator on earth, Judg. 6. 11; Isa. 16. 5; Mal. 3. 3; Acts 2. 30. Living among men in the state of humiliation, Matt. 5. 1; 13. 12; 15. 29; 21. 5, 7; 24. 3; 26. 55; Luke 2. 46; 4. 20; 5. 3, 17; John 4. 6; 6. 3; 8. 2; 12. 14, 15. In the state of glory, Ps. 110. 1; Zech. 6. 13; Matt. 19. 28; 20. 23; 22. 44; 25. 31; 26. 64; Mark 16. 19; Luke 22. 69; Col. 3. 1; Heb. 1. 3, 13; 10. 12; 12. 2; Rev. 3. 21; 19. 11, 19, 21; 20. 11.

units.la: Sessio Christi ad d. D. P. est summus gradus exaltationis Christi, dum evectus in sacerdotio & regno suo in cœlesti sacrario est perpetuus noster Pontifex, & omnem potestatem in res creatas universas in cœlo & in terra possidet, ut per ipsum pater omnia immediate agat & gubernet. (Vide Sedere).
units.tr: The sitting of Christ at the right hand of the Father is the highest degree of Christ's exaltation, while, raised up in his priesthood and kingdom, he is our perpetual High Priest in the heavenly sanctuary and possesses all power over all created things in heaven and on earth, so that the Father acts and governs all things through him immediately. (See "to sit.")

units.la: 4. Spiritus S. Deus sedere dicitur Act.2.3.
units.tr: 4. God the Holy Spirit is said to sit, Acts 2. 3.

units.la: 5. Sedet Angelus S. Matth.28.2 Marc.16 5. Ioann.20. 12, Apoc.6.2. & 14.v.14,15.16.
units.tr: 5. The holy angel sits, Matt. 28. 2; Mark 16. 5; John 20. 12; Rev. 6. 2; 14. 14, 15, 16.

units.la: 6. Ecclesia militans, Cantic. 2. 3. Esai. 52.2. Mich. 7,8, Zach.14,11, Matth.4,16, Luc.1.79, Triumphans, Matth.19, 28. Luc.22.30. Apoc.3.21. & 4.4. & 11.16, & 20,4.
units.tr: 6. The Church militant, Song 2. 3; Isa. 52. 2; Mic. 7. 8; Zech. 14. 11; Matt. 4. 16; Luke 1. 79. Triumphant, Matt. 19. 28; Luke 22. 30; Rev. 3. 21; 4. 4; 11. 16; 20. 4.

units.la: 7. Sedent homines mortales in terra, provocationum suarum ratione, ut patresfamilias, hospitales viri, convivæ, peregrini, quiescentes, iudices, principes, reges, subditi, pauperes, divites, afflicti, senes, viri, fœminæ: de quibus ducenta testimonia in Scripturis occurrunt.
units.tr: 7. Mortal men sit on earth, according to the circumstances of their activities: as heads of households, hospitable men, guests, travellers, those at rest, judges, princes, kings, subjects, the poor, the rich, the afflicted, the aged, men, women. Some two hundred testimonies of these occur in the Scriptures.

units.la: 8. Sedet Angelus malus, summi iudicis Lictor & carnifex, Apoc.6.v.4 5. & 9,17.
units.tr: 8. The evil angel sits, the lictor and executioner of the supreme Judge, Rev. 6. 4, 5; 9. 17.

units.la: 9. Sedet Antichristus, qui & meretrix mystica, 2, Thess.2,4 Apoc.17.v.1.9,15,& 18,7.
units.tr: 9. Antichrist sits, who is also the mystical harlot, 2 Thess. 2. 4; Rev. 17. 1, 9, 15; 18. 7.

Sedes Dei Patris, Hebr. 8. 1, & 12 2, Apocal. 4. verfic. 2. &c. & 14. 3. 3. Dei filij, nempe Christi, regis Ecclesiæ Psal.45. 7. & 89. 5. & 97. 2 Matth.19.28. & 25.31. 4.
