units.tr: "Seat" is said of God, likewise of the Father, of God the Son, of men, of the beast, and of Satan. 1. Of God: Ps. 11. 4; 47. 9; 89. 15; 93. 2; 103. 19; Isa. 66. 1; Acts 7. 49; Rev. 22. 1, 2. The seat of God the Father: Heb. 8. 1; 12. 2; Rev. 4, verse 2, etc.; 14. 3. 3. Of the Son of God, namely Christ, King of the Church: Ps. 45. 7; 89. 5; 97. 2; Matt. 19. 28; 25. 31. 4. Of man: Josh. 22. 8; Judg. 9. 15; Ps. 94. 20; 122. 5; 132. 11; Luke 1. 32, 52; Acts 2. 30. 5. Of the pious in heaven: Matt. 19. 28; Rev. 11. 16; 20. 4, 6.

units.la: [?]20, 4, 6, Sedes bestiæ mysticæ, Apoc. 16. 10. & meretricis magnæ, Apoc. 17. versic.1,3,9, Sedes satanæ, Apoc. 12,13.],
units.tr: [?]20, 4, 6. The seat of the mystical beast, Rev. 16. 10; and of the great harlot, Rev. 17, verses 1, 3, 9. The seat of Satan, Rev. 12, 13.

units.la: SETH, filius Adæ, nascitur, Genesis 41 25. nascitur illi Enos, religionémque restituit, ver 26. eius ætas 5.8. positio, seu fundamentum Ecclesiæ & promissionis de Christo)
units.tr: SETH, son of Adam, is born, Gen. 4. 25. Enos is born to him, and he restored religion, ver. 26. His age, 5. 8. A position, or foundation, of the Church and of the promise concerning Christ.

units.la: ETIM, locus in deserto. Num. 25.1 Iof.2.1 & 3.1. Ligni species, apud Moisem frequenter occurrens, Exod.cap.25.5. 10.23,28.1.(Sittim.1.pinus,vel spina).
units.tr: ETIM, a place in the desert, Num. 25. 1; Josh. 2. 1; 3. 1. A kind of wood, frequently occurring in Moses, Exod. 25. 5, 10; 23, 28; 1. (Sittim: 1. pine, or thorn.)

units.la: VERITAS interdum necessaria, 2 Corinth.7.8. & 13.2. Tit.2.15. Iudæ.v.23. Seueritas Dei in Iudæos, Roman.11. 22. Seueritatis Dei iustissimi erga delinquentes exempla: Erga Euam, Genes.3.16. Adamum,v.17. Amalechitas, Exodi.17. 18.9. &c. Israelitas, vitulum aureum adorantes.32.v.26. &c.blasphemum, Leuit.24.10.&c populum Israeliticum, Numer. 11. ver.32.33. Mariam, 12. versi.9.10. Israelitas, 14. v.28. 29. 30. & 21. v. 5.6.colligentem ligna sabbatho, 15. 32. &c. Moisen & Aaronem, 20. v. 11. 12. Tribum Beniamin, quæ iubente Domino tota, exceptis sexcentis viris, est deleta, Iudic.20.46.47. Saulem.1Sam.13.13.&c. Filios Saulis, 2. Sam.21.9. Oziam, 2 Paral. 26.19. Ezechiam, 2 Regum 20. v. 16. 17. Saraiam, Sophoniam, & ianitores, 25.v.18.19. Ierosolymitanos, Esai.3.6.&c. Babylonem, Ierem.51.1. &c.seruum nequam, Matt. 8.34. seruum inutilem.25.30, Ananiam, Act.5, v.5 6, Sapphiram, 7.10, Herodem,12,23, Vide Deus.
units.tr: TRUTH sometimes necessary, 2 Cor. 7. 8; 13. 2; Titus 2. 15; Jude 23. The severity of God toward the Jews, Rom. 11. 22. Examples of the most just severity of God toward offenders: toward Eve, Gen. 3. 16; Adam, v. 17; the Amalekites, Exod. 17. 18; 9, etc.; the Israelites adoring the golden calf, 32. 26, etc.; the blasphemer, Lev. 24. 10, etc.; the Israelite people, Num. 11. 32, 33; Miriam, 12. 9, 10; the Israelites, 14. 28, 29, 30; and 21. 5, 6; the man gathering wood on the Sabbath, 15. 32, etc.; Moses and Aaron, 20. 11, 12; the tribe of Benjamin, which at the Lord's command was utterly destroyed, except six hundred men, Judg. 20. 46, 47; Saul, 1 Sam. 13. 13, etc.; the sons of Saul, 2 Sam. 21. 9; Uzziah, 2 Chron. 26. 19; Hezekiah, 2 Kings 20. 16, 17; Seraiah, Zephaniah, and the doorkeepers, 25. 18, 19; the Jerusalemites, Isa. 3. 6, etc.; Babylon, Jer. 51. 1, etc.; the wicked servant, Matt. 8. 34; the unprofitable servant, 25. 30; Ananias, Acts 5. 5, 6; Sapphira, 7. 10; Herod, 12. 23. See God.

units.la: [?]A, seruus saulis, à Dauide vocatur, 2 sam.9.2, dominum also accusat, 16.3, procedit obuiam Regi Dauidi,19,17,(1. miles præliator)
units.tr: ZIBA, a servant of Saul, is summoned by David, 2 Sam. 9:2; he slanders his master, 16:3; he meets King David, 19:17. (i.e. a soldier, a fighter.)

units.la: CITAS in Iudæa Ierem.14.1,&c. Aggæ.1,11,V.Deut,28.23.
units.tr: SITIS (thirst) in Judea, Jer. 14:1, etc.; Hag. 1:11; see Deut. 28:23.

units.la: ELEG, ciuitas in Tribu Iuda, simeonitis adscripta,Ios. 9,v.5, donatur Dauidi.1 sam. 27, 6, ab Amalechitis exuritur,30 1(Zikelag.1,cortex,mucolucrum).
units.tr: ZIKLAG, a city in the tribe of Judah, assigned to the Simeonites, Josh. 19:5; given to David, 1 Sam. 27:6; burned by the Amalekites, 30:1. (Ziklag: bark, sap.)

units.la: ERA, quibus & quando non bibenda, Num. 6.v.1.2. Iudic.13.v.4.7.14. Luc.1.15. siceram in deserto non biberunt Israelitæ, Deut. 29. 6. sicera quibus danda, Prouer.31.6, significat sechar id omne quod inebriare potest)V.v.4.5.
units.tr: STRONG DRINK: by whom and when it is not to be drunk, Num. 6:1-2; Judg. 13:4, 7, 14; Luke 1:15. The Israelites did not drink strong drink in the wilderness, Deut. 29:6. To whom strong drink is to be given, Prov. 31:6. It signifies sechar [שכר], that is, everything that can intoxicate; see vv. 4-5.

units.la: HEM, Filius Hemor, violat Dinam. Gen.34. v.1.2.eam ibi vxorem petit,v.4, occiditur cum viris omnib.v.25.26.
units.tr: HEMOR's son Shechem violates Dinah, Gen. 34:1-2; he asks for her there as his wife, v. 4; he is killed with all his men, vv. 25-26.

units.la: HEM turris cum mille hominibus comburitur, Iudic.49,(sechem.1,humerus)
units.tr: The tower of Shechem with a thousand men is burned, Judg. 9:49. (Shechem: shoulder [שכם].)

units.la: SICHEM vrbs ab Amalech destituitur. Iudic. 9. 45. à Ieroboa mo instauratur, 1 Reg. 12. 25.
units.tr: The city of Shechem is destroyed by Abimelech, Judg. 9:45; it is rebuilt by Jeroboam, 1 Kings 12:25.

units.la: SICHIMITAE destruuntur, Iudic. 9. 57. ob facinus a trox.
units.tr: The Shechemites are destroyed, Judg. 9:57, on account of their atrocious crime.

units.la: SICHVTH idolum. V. IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: SIKKUTH, an idol. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: SICLVS, & eius precium, Exod. 30. 13. Ezech. 45. 12. Siclus i Lege est duplex: communis, iam ante latam Legem in re bus politicis receptus, qui valebat quadrantem talerii sacer, ad res sacras institutus Lege, duplo maior altero, qu valebat dimidium talerum. De illo fit mentio Genef. 2. 16. & alibi saepe, vbi de rebus politicis & communibus a gitur: de hoc, Exod. 30. 13. Ezech. 45. 12.
units.tr: SHEKEL and its price, Exod. 30:13; Ezek. 45:12. The shekel in the Law is of two kinds. The common shekel was already in use in civil affairs before the Law was given; it was worth a quarter of a sacred talent. The sacred shekel, appointed by the Law for holy things, was twice as large as the other and was worth half a talent. The former is mentioned in Gen. 2:16 and often elsewhere, where civil and common matters are treated; the latter in Exod. 30:13 and Ezek. 45:12.

units.la: SIDERA, Vide SYDERA.
units.tr: SIDERA: see SYDERA.

units.la: SIDON, Phoeniciae ciuitas, Iosue 11. 8. Esa. 23. 4. Ezech. 28. ver 21. 22. Sidoniorum idolum, 1 Reg. 11. 5. 2 Reg. 23. 13. i Sidonem sermo Domini, Ezech. 28. 21. Sidonis & Ty ri conditio tolerabilior futura, incolarum Corazin Bethsaida conditione, Matt. 11. 22. Luc. 10. 14. (Zidon. i. v natór.)
units.tr: SIDON, a city of Phoenicia, Josh. 11:8; Isa. 23:4; Ezek. 28:21-22. The idol of the Sidonians, 1 Kings 11:5; 2 Kings 23:13. The word of the Lord against Sidon, Ezek. 28:21. The condition of Tyre and Sidon will be more tolerable, like that of the inhabitants of Chorazin and Bethsaida, Matt. 11:22; Luke 10:14. (Zidon, i.e. hunter [ציד].)

units.la: SIDRACH (.i. decorus meus, Philo.) cum duobus sociis i fornacem ardentem coniicitur, & quare, Dan. 3. 21. hit illaesus vna cum iisdem egreditur, quòd in vnius Dei cu tu perstiterint, laudantur, à Rege in summum honore euehuntur, Dan. 3. 30.
units.tr: SHADRACH (i.e. my delight, as Philo says) is thrown with two companions into a burning furnace, and why, Dan. 3:21. He comes out unharmed together with them, because they persisted in the worship of the one God; they are praised and raised by the King to the highest honour, Dan. 3:30.

units.la: SIGNATI litera Thau seruantur, Ezech. 9. 6. Apoc. 7. 3. Vi PIORVM nota.
units.tr: The marked, who bear the letter Tau, are preserved, Ezek. 9:6; Rev. 7:3. See the mark of the PIOUS.

units.la: SIGNA varia à Deo hominibus data: Noacho arcus coel stis in nubibus, Gen. 9. v. 12. 13. Abrahae clibanus sumam & lampas ignis, 15. 17. Abrahae & toti posteritati, Circun cisio, 17. v. 9. 10. Mosi virga, Exo. 4. v. 2. 3. &c. Aaroni vir germinans, Num. 17. 8. Israelitis serpens aeneus, 21. v. 6. &c. Gedeoni, Iudic. 6. v. 17. 18. eidem vellus, v. 36. Ezechi omnimoda rerum copia sine cultura, 2 Reg. 19. 29. eide horologium, 20. 9. Esa. 38. 7. Achaz Regi, promissio Me fiae, 8. v. 11. 12. 13. 14. Domini Israel, later & sartago fe rea, Ezech. 4. v. 1. 2. 3. Viris gementibus, Thau in front bus, 9. v. 6. 7. Scribis, Pharisaeis, & aliis incredulis & obce catis, signum Ionae Prophetae, Matth. 12. 39. & 16. 4. Mar 8. 11. Luc. 11. 29. Signum Ionae Prophetae, pro, simile sig Ionae Prophetae. Sic peccata Manassis, 2 Reg. 24. 3. mun vel collecta Mosis, 2 Paral. 24. 6. iniquitas Patrum, Exo 34. 7. 34.7.contradictio Core, & error Balaam, Iudæ v.11.aliá-que plurima τροπικῶς, quasi eádem essent, eodem modo appellantur.
units.tr: Signs given by God to men: to Noah the rainbow in the clouds, Gen. 9:12-13; to Abraham the smoking furnace and the lamp of fire, 15:17; to Abraham and all his posterity, circumcision, 17:9-10; to Moses the rod, Exod. 4:2-3, etc.; to Aaron the budding staff, Num. 17:8; to the Israelites the bronze serpent, Num. 21:6, etc.; to Gideon, Judg. 6:17-18, and to him the fleece, v. 36; to Hezekiah an abundance of all things without cultivation, 2 Kings 19:29, and to him the sundial, 20:9; Isa. 38:7; to King Ahaz the promise of Immanuel, Isa. 8:11-14; the sign of the Lord to Israel, the brick and the frying pan, Ezek. 4:1-3; for the men who groan, the Tau on their foreheads, Ezek. 9:6-7; to the scribes, Pharisees and other unbelieving and obstinate people, the sign of the prophet Jonah, Matt. 12:39; 16:4; Mark 8:11; Luke 11:29. "The sign of the prophet Jonah" means "a sign like that of the prophet Jonah." Thus the sins of Manasseh, 2 Kings 24:3; the gift or collection of Moses, 2 Chron. 24:6; the iniquity of the fathers, Exod. 34:7; the contradiction of Korah and the error of Balaam, Jude v. 11; and very many other things are called by the same name tropically, as if they were the same.

units.la: Signa è cœlo, Matth.16.1. vocantur, quale edidit Iosue, Solem sistens Iof.10.13. Samuel, tonitrua eliciens, 1 Sam. 12.17. Esaias umbrā regredi iubens in solario, 2 Reg.20.11. vel potiùs Moses, cùm mannam Deus cœlitùs plueret, quòd esse virisimilius, videtur ex Ioan. 6.30.31.32.33. colligi posse. Signum pro insigni aliquo Domini facto, siue quo consoletur, siue etiam quo puniat, vt Deut.28.37. 1 Cor.14.22. Signum Circumcisionis, pro ipsa Circumcisione, Rom.4.11. Vide CIRCVMCISIONIS signum. Signum Filij hominis, Matth.24.30. signa Diuinorum quàm vana, Esai.44.25. signa mœroris, Esth.4.v.1.3. signa appellatione à rebus, quas significant, mutuantur, Genes.17.13. Exod.12. 11. Ezech.5.v.1.5. Matth.26. ver. 26.28. Ioan.15.1.1 Corinth. 5.7. & 10.4. & 11.v.24.25. signa fidem in Christum subsequentia, Mar.16.v.17. 18. signa vt fiant, optant Apostoli, Vide PRODIGIA. Signa multò plura à Christo edita, quàm literarum monumentis commendata, Ioan.20.30.
units.tr: Signs from heaven, Matt. 16:1, are so called, such as Joshua produced when he stopped the sun, Josh. 10:13; Samuel when he brought forth thunder, 1 Sam. 12:17; Isaiah when he bade the shadow go back on the dial, 2 Kings 20:11; or rather Moses, when God rained manna from heaven, which seems more likely from John 6:30-33. A sign is also a notable deed of the Lord, whether to comfort or to punish, as in Deut. 28:37 and 1 Cor. 14:22. The sign of circumcision is circumcision itself, Rom. 4:11; see the sign of CIRCUMCISION. The sign of the Son of Man, Matt. 24:30. The signs of diviners, how vain they are, Isa. 44:25. Signs of mourning, Esth. 4:1, 3. Signs borrow their names from the things they signify: Gen. 17:13; Exod. 12:11; Ezek. 5:1, 5; Matt. 26:26, 28; John 15:1; 1 Cor. 5:7; 10:4; 11:24-25. Signs that follow faith in Christ, Mark 16:17-18. Signs that they may come to be, the apostles desire; see PRODIGIES. Signs performed by Christ were far more numerous than those commended in the written records, John 20:30.

units.la: V. MIRACVLA.
units.tr: V. MIRACLES.

units.la: Signa externa ad quid prosint, Ier.51.63. Ezec.4.1. Mat. 10.14. Lucæ.10.11. signorum eiusmodi visus, Marci.9.verf. 36.37. Actor. 4.31. & 13.51. & 16.26. & 18.6. & 21.11. signa, adventus Christi diem præcessura, Matth.24.v.4.5. Marci.13.verf.4.5.6. Lucæ.21.verf.8.9. signa futurorum, Genes. 9.12. Exodi. 31.13. Iosu. 2.18. 1 Samuel, 2.34. & 10.2.2. Samuel. 5. 24. 2. Regum. 19. 20. Esai. 38. 7. Lucæ. 2. 12. signa in memoriam præteritorum, Exodi.12. verf.3.8. Num. 15 38. & 16.v.38.40. & 10.Iosue, 4.v.6.&c. signa & miracula fiunt, vt per illa, omnipotentia, veritas, iustitia, & bonitas Dei innotescat Exodi. 4.verf.2.6.&.7.17.&16. 12. Iosu. 3.v.10.14.1. Regum. 13.4. & 17.14.& 18.38.& 20. v.13.38.2. Reg.5.14.& 20.9. Mat.8.26.& 9.2.& 14.28. Signo certificatur Ionathas, 1 Sam. 14.10. confirmatur Saul.10.1. HON Rex Amorrhæorum, Vide SEHON.
units.tr: For what purpose external signs serve: Jer. 51:63; Ezek. 4:1; Matt. 10:14; Luke 10:11. The sight of such signs: Mark 9:36–37; Acts 4:31; 13:51; 16:26; 18:6; 21:11. Signs that will precede the coming of Christ's day: Matt. 24:4–5; Mark 13:4–6; Luke 21:8–9. Signs of future things: Gen. 9:12; Exod. 31:13; Josh. 2:18; 1 Sam. 2:34; 10:2; 2 Sam. 5:24; 2 Kings 19:20; Isa. 38:7; Luke 2:12. Signs as a memorial of past things: Exod. 12:3, 8; Num. 15:38; 16:38–40; Josh. 4:6, etc. Signs and miracles are wrought so that by them God's omnipotence, truth, justice and goodness may become known: Exod. 4:2, 6–7; 7:17; 16:12; Josh. 3:10, 14; 1 Kings 13:4; 17:14; 18:38; 20:13, 38; 2 Kings 5:14; 20:9; Matt. 8:26; 9:2; 14:28. Jonathan is assured by a sign, 1 Sam. 14:10; Saul is confirmed, 1 Sam. 10:1. HON, king of the Amorites: see SEHON.

units.la: AS Propheta, vnà cum Barsaba, Antiochiam mittitur, Act. 15.v.22.27. illic vnà cum collega adhortatur Fratres, v.32. Paulo comes adiungitur v.40. virgis cum Paulo cæditur, 16.22. in carcerem coniicitur, v.23. illic Deum contenta voce orant & laudant, v.25. eorum liberatio, v.26. &c. Vide PAVLVS.
units.tr: As a prophet, together with Barsabas, he is sent to Antioch, Acts 15:22, 27. There, together with a colleague, he exhorts the brethren, v. 32. He is joined as a companion to Paul, v. 40. He is beaten with rods along with Paul, 16:22; thrown into prison, v. 23; there they pray and praise God with a loud voice, v. 25; their deliverance, v. 26, etc. See PAUL.

units.la: SILENTIVM, pro sedata expectatione, &, vt ita dicam, prae conquiescientia, Esaiae 30. 15. sic accipiunt nonnulli & Psalmo 65.2. Silentium suo tempore seruandum, Prou.25.28. Iac.1.19. Silere utile est, Prou.17.28. Eccles.3.7. Eccl.20.6. & 32.12. Silentij & taciturnitatis exempla: Aaron, Leuit.10.3. Anna, 1 Sam.1.13. Samuel, 3.15. Saul, 10.ver.16.27. Abigail, 25.36. Elisaeus, 2 Reg.2.3. populus Iudaicus, 18.39. Neh.5.8. Esther, Esth.2.ver.10.20. Iob, Iob.39.37. Dauid, Psalm.32.3. Sobna cum collegis, Esa.36.21. Dominus 42.14. Christus, Matt.26.63. & 27.12.14. Marci 15.5. Deipara Virgo, Luc.2, v.19.48. &c. Petrus, Iacobus & Ioannes Apostoli, 9.36. Iudaei, Act.13.16. & 21.4c. Sororis Pauli filius, 23.21.22.
units.tr: SILENCE, for a calmed expectation, and, as I may say, a quiet rest: Isa. 30:15; some also take Psalm 65:2 in this way. Silence is to be kept at its proper time: Prov. 25:28; James 1:19. It is useful to be silent: Prov. 17:28; Eccles. 3:7; Ecclus. 20:6; 32:12. Examples of silence and taciturnity: Aaron, Lev. 10:3; Hannah, 1 Sam. 1:13; Samuel, 3:15; Saul, 10:16; 27; Abigail, 25:36; Elisha, 2 Kings 2:3; the Jewish people, 18:39; Neh. 5:8; Esther, Esth. 2:10, 20; Job, Job 39:37; David, Psalm 32:3; Shebna with his colleagues, Isa. 36:21; the Lord, 42:14; Christ, Matt. 26:63; 27:12, 14; Mark 15:5; the Virgin Mother of God, Luke 2:19, 48, etc.; Peter, James and John the apostles, 9:36; the Jews, Acts 13:16; 21:40; the son of Paul's sister, 23:21–22.

units.la: SILO, locus vbi Iosua cum suis copiis castra metatus est. Ios. 18.1. Domus Dei illic est. verf. 8. Iudic. 18.31.& 20.1 Sam.1.3. Illic forte terra in septem partes diuiditur. Ios.18.v.9.10. in Silo virgines capiuntur, vt filiorum Beniamin vxores fiant, Iudic.21.verf.21.23. de Silo affertur arca, 1 Sam.4.4. Ierem.7.12.& 26.6. (Siloh.i. pacificus, Gen.49.10. Ezech.21.27. Psal.Lxix.)
units.tr: SHILOH, the place where Joshua pitched his camp with his forces, Josh. 18:1. The house of God is there, v. 8; Judg. 18:31; 1 Sam. 1:3. There, perhaps, the land is divided into seven parts, Josh. 18:9–10. At Shiloh virgins are seized so that they may become wives of the sons of Benjamin, Judg. 21:21–23. The ark is brought from Shiloh, 1 Sam. 4:4; Jer. 7:12; 26:6. (Shiloh, i.e. peaceable, Gen. 49:10; Ezek. 21:27; Psalm 69.)

units.la: SILOE fons scaturiens in vrbe Hierosolyma ad radices montis Sion, vnde emanans riuus piscinam efficit: Ioh.9.7. (Siloah.i. missus) Esa.8.6. Ibi turris erat exstructa ad aquae ductum, quae repente prostrata decem & octo homines interemit: Luc.13.4.
units.tr: SILOAM, a spring welling up in the city of Jerusalem at the foot of Mount Zion, from which the stream flowing out forms a pool: John 9:7. (Siloah, i.e. sent.) Isa. 8:6. There was a tower built over the water conduit, which suddenly collapsed and killed eighteen men: Luke 13:4.

units.la: SIMEON (ab audiendo verbo sic dictus) secundus Iacobi ex Lea filius nascitur, Gen.29.33. hic cum fratre Leui, crudeliter sororis stuprum vlciscitur, 34.v.25.26. hinc patris sententiam incurrit, v.30.& 49.v.5.6.7.
units.tr: SIMEON (so called from hearing the word), the second son of Jacob by Leah, is born, Gen. 29:33. He, with his brother Levi, cruelly avenges the rape of their sister, 34:25–26. Hence he incurs his father's condemnation, v. 30; and 49:5–7.

units.la: SIMEON vir iustus, & donis Spiritus Sancti instructus, Luc. 2.25. de Christo ante mortem videndo promissionem accipit, v. 26. ea fruitur cum cantico, v.28.29.30. Israelis magna ex parte reiectionem, & Gentium vocationem praedicit, v 34.
units.tr: SIMEON, a just man, instructed by the gifts of the Holy Spirit, receives the promise that he will see the Christ before his death, Luke 2:25–26. He enjoys it with a canticle, vv. 28–30. He foretells, v. 34, the rejection of Israel for the most part and the calling of the Gentiles.

units.la: SIMILAE oblatio, Leuit.2.v 1 2 3.
units.tr: The SIMILAR offering, Lev. 2:1–3.

units.la: SIMILITVDINIS & figurę vocabulis interdum ipsa rei veritas significatur, Philip.2.7. (V.parabola.)
units.tr: Sometimes the very truth of a thing is signified by words of likeness and figure: Phil. 2:7. (See PARABLE.)

units.la: SIMON Petrus, Vide PETRVS. {1.audiens,obedientia.}
units.tr: SIMON PETER, see PETER. {1. hearing, obedience.}

units.la: SIMON Cananites inter Apostolos recensetur, Mat.10.v.2.4.
units.tr: SIMON the Canaanite is listed among the apostles, Matt. 10:2, 4.

units.la: SIMON Cyrenaeus, crucem post Christum ferre iubetur, Mar.15.21.
units.tr: SIMON of Cyrene is ordered to carry the cross after Christ, Mark 15:21.

units.la: SIMON Leprosus in Bethania excipit Dominum, Matth.26. Marc.14.3.Ioan.12.1.
units.tr: SIMON the leper in Bethany receives the Lord, Matt. 26; Mark 14:3; John 12:1.

units.la: SIMON Magus, Act.8.9. omnes magicis suis artibus demen-tat.v.10 11.Philippo Euangelium praedicanti credit,& bap-tizatur, v.13:pecunia sibi Spiritus S.dona cõparare vult, v.18.19.à Petro seuerissimè obiurgatur,v.20.resipiscere vi-detur,v.24.
units.tr: SIMON MAGUS, Acts 8:9. He astonishes everyone with his magical arts, vv. 10–11. He believes Philip preaching the gospel and is baptized, v. 13. He wishes to acquire for himself, for money, the gifts of the Holy Spirit, vv. 18–19. He is most severely rebuked by Peter, v. 20; he seems to repent, v. 24.

units.la: SIMONIA,(Vide VENDI dona Dei.)Est,cum fauore vel pre-tio,vel non legitimo modo, quis ecclesiasticam digni-tatem est consecutus. Gratis enim illa est accipienda:& huiusmodi pretium in perniciem dantibus, & in lepram accipientibus: vti Giezi seruo Elizæi cessit. Act.8.20.2 Reg.5.27.
units.tr: SIMONY (see SELL, the gifts of God). It is when someone obtains an ecclesiastical dignity through favour or price, or in some illegitimate manner. For it is to be received freely; and such a price brings ruin on those who give it and leprosy on those who receive it, as happened to Gehazi, the servant of Elisha: Acts 8:20; 2 Kings 5:27.

units.la: SIMON Coriarius Petrum hospitio accipit,Actor.9.43.&10. v.6.17.32.
units.tr: SIMON the tanner receives Peter into his house, Acts 9:43; 10:6, 17, 32.

units.la: SIMON seu Simeon Niger,Propheta Actor.13.1.
units.tr: SIMON, or Simeon Niger, a prophet, Acts 13:1.

units.la: SIMPLICITAS seu Integritas est virtus illa,qua mens homi-nis aliena redditur ab omni versutia,malitia & duplicita-te. Vel est iustitia illa, qua cor tum erga Deum, tum erga proximum recte est,& competenter animatum, & ab omnis generis malitia alienum. V. Duplicitas.
units.tr: SIMPLICITY or integrity is that virtue by which the mind of a man is made free from all craftiness, malice and duplicity. Or it is that righteousness by which the heart, both towards God and towards neighbour, is rightly and fittingly disposed, and kept free from every kind of malice. See Duplicity.

units.la: SIMPLICITAS laudatur ; Pro.28 v.6.18.simplicitas vera quae, Matt.10 16.Act.2.46 Rom.16 19.2 Cor.1 12.Phil.2.15.Co-loss.3.22.Simplicitas omnibus piis necessaria est,vt ex su-perioribus constar,& se 1.Matt.5.v.837. & 6 4.22.& 12.33. Act.13.10.1 Cor.3.4.&14.20.2 Cor.8.2.& 9.11. & 11.v.3. In simplicitate tribuendum,Rom.12 8.Simplicitas Fi-delium,V.FIDELES.Simplicitatis exempla:Abimelech. Gen.20.v 4.5.6 Iacob,25.27.& 29.v.25 28.Populus,2 Sam.15 12. Dauid,1 Reg 9.4.1 Par.29.23.Naaman.2 Regum 5.23.Iob, Iob 1.1.& 31.v.5.6 Iudaei, 1.Mach.2 37. Daniel,Dan.6.22. Godolias , Ierem.40. 16 Nathanael,Ioan.1.48.Fideles, Act.2 46.Paulus ,in simplicitate conuersatus est,2 Corin.1.12.
units.tr: SIMPLICITY is praised: Prov. 28:6, 18; true simplicity, Matt. 10:16; Acts 2:46; Rom. 16:19; 2 Cor. 1:12; Phil. 2:15; Col. 3:22. Simplicity is necessary for all the godly, as is clear from what has been said above, and see Matt. 5:8, 37; 6:4, 22; 12:33; Acts 13:10; 1 Cor. 3:4; 14:20; 2 Cor. 8:2; 9:11; 11:3. Giving is to be done in simplicity, Rom. 12:8. The simplicity of the faithful: see FAITHFUL. Examples of simplicity: Abimelech, Gen. 20:4–6; Jacob, 25:27; 29:25, 28; the people, 2 Sam. 15:12; David, 1 Kings 9:4; 1 Chron. 29:23; Naaman, 2 Kings 5:23; Job, Job 1:1; 31:5–6; the Jews, 1 Macc. 2:37; Daniel, Dan. 6:22; Gedaliah, Jer. 40:16; Nathanael, John 1:48; the faithful, Acts 2:46; Paul, who lived in simplicity, 2 Cor. 1:12.

units.la: SIMPLEX & rectus,Genes.20 6.& 25 27.Iob.1.v.1.8.Matt.10. 16.Rom.16 18.simplici corde diligendum,1 Pet.1.22. simplices in malo, Rom. 16.19. simplicibus & humilibus re-sistentes,Deus,quod abscondit iis, qui sibi videntur sapientes,Esa.29.v 18.24.& 32.4.Eccles.9. 15. Matth.11.25. Luc.2.9.&5.8.&10.21.Act.4.13.1. Cor.1. 4.&2.1. ad simplicitatem hortatur suos Christus,Matt.10.16.
units.tr: SIMPLE and upright: Gen. 20:6; 25:27; Job 1:1, 8; Matt. 10:16; Rom. 16:18. One must love with a simple heart, 1 Pet. 1:22. Simple in evil: Rom. 16:19. God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble, hiding from those who seem wise to themselves what he reveals to the simple: Isa. 29:18, 24; 32:4; Eccles. 9:15; Matt. 11:25; Luke 2:9; 5:8; 10:21; Acts 4:13; 1 Cor. 1:4; 2:1. Christ exhorts his people to simplicity, Matt. 10:16.

units.la: SIMULACHRA cauenda, Vide IDOLOLATRIA.Simulachrorum seruitus,auaritia,Coloss.3.5.cultus eorum fugiendus Act.15.20.
units.tr: IMAGES are to be avoided, see IDOLATRY. The servitude of images is covetousness, Col. 3:5; their worship is to be shunned, Acts 15:20.

units.la: SIMVLAT Dauid insaniam, 1 Sam.21.13. Vnde irrisu est.
units.tr: DAVID feigns madness, 1 Sam. 21:13. Hence he is a laughing-stock.

units.la: SIMVLATIO & hypocrisis cauenda, Iob.15.34.Esa.32.6. Ierem.9.6 Matth.23.1.&c.abesse debet à Christianis, 1 Petri 2.1. (Vide HYPOCRISIS.) Est autem simulatio rei quam habes,quasi eam non habeas, occultatio & immi nutio.
units.tr: SIMULATION and hypocrisy are to be avoided: Job 15:34; Isa. 32:6; Jer. 9:6; Matt. 23:1, etc. They ought to be absent from Christians, 1 Pet. 2:1. (See HYPOCRISY.) Simulation, moreover, is the concealment and pretence of a thing you have, as if you did not have it.

units.la: SINA,mons in Arabia, Galat.4.25.illic Mosi Lex data est Exo.19.20.&20.1. anagogicè delineat legalem pactionem,Gal.4.24.(Sina.i.spinetum.)
units.tr: SINAI, a mountain in Arabia, Gal. 4:25. There the Law was given to Moses, Exod. 19:20; 20:1. Allegorically it portrays the legal covenant, Gal. 4:24. (Sina, i.e. a thorn-bush.)

units.la: SINAPIS granum prouerbialiter pro re minima,Luc.17.6.Sinapis parabola, Matt.13.31.
units.tr: The MUSTARD seed, proverbially for a very small thing, Luke 17:6. The parable of the mustard seed, Matt. 13:31.

units.la: SINDONE,tenuissima linea veste (à Sidone ciuitate, in qua texi illa consueuerat, vocata) inuoluitur Christi corpus Matth. 27.59. simili veste erat indutus iuuenis quidam Marc.14.51.
units.tr: SINDON, a very fine linen cloth (so called from the city of Sidon, where it was customarily woven), in which the body of Christ was wrapped, Matt. 27:59. A young man was dressed in a similar cloth, Mark 14:51.

units.la: SINVS:in sinu esse,pro, non solùm intimum & coniunctissimum amoris charitate, sed & naturæ vnione planè eundem esse,Ioan.1.18. In sinum dantur Dauidi vxores Domini sui,hoc est,ad animum:Metonymia, 2 sam.12.8.Sinus Abrahæ, pro loco electis destinato, Luc.16.v.22.23.
units.tr: BOSOM: to be in the bosom means not only to be most intimate and closely joined by the bond of love, but also to be altogether one by unity of nature: John 1:18. The wives of his lord are given into David's bosom, that is, to his mind: a metonymy, 2 Sam. 12:8. The bosom of Abraham is a place destined for the elect, Luke 16:22–23.

units.la: SION, mons sanctus in parte meridionali vrbis Ierosolymæ Psal.2 6.Esa.65.10.Ioel 3.17.Soph.3.11.à Deo dilectus, Psal.68.&78.2.à Deo fundatus,Esa.14 32.Dei habitatio est,Psal.132.v.13.14.illic arx,quæ Dauidis ciuitas dicitur, (1 Par.15.)erat.2 Sam.5.7.1 Reg.8.1.Sionis excidium prædicitum Mich.3.12.
units.tr: ZION, the holy mountain on the southern side of the city of Jerusalem: Psalm 2:6; Isa. 65:10; Joel 3:17; Zeph. 3:11. Beloved by God, Psalm 68; 78:2. Founded by God, Isa. 14:32. It is the dwelling of God, Psalm 132:13–14. There the citadel, which is called the city of David (1 Chron. 15), stood: 2 Sam. 5:7; 1 Kings 8:1. The destruction of Zion is foretold: Mic. 3:12.

units.la: Figuratè verò significat Ecclesiam Dei quę sub lege cultum externum habuit in templo Ierosolymitano, quod in monte Sionis exstructum erat, & sub Evangelio per orbem vniuersum plantatum veritatem exhibuit in typo demonstratam. (Sion.i. titulus, vel signum, vel specula.)
units.tr: Figuratively, however, it signifies the Church of God, which under the law had external worship in the temple of Jerusalem, built on Mount Zion, and under the gospel, planted throughout the whole world, has given forth the truth demonstrated in the type. (Zion, i.e. a title, or a sign, or a watchtower.)

units.la: SIONIS filia,Ecclesiam Iudaicam designat, quę militantis triumphantis Ecclesię Christi typus fuit.
units.tr: The DAUGHTER OF ZION designates the Jewish Church, which was a type of the militant and triumphant Church of Christ.

units.la: Sionis filię mulieres & puellę Ierosolymitanę. Threni 1.6. Aliquoties incolę vrbis ipsius & regionis circumiacentis significantur.Item verę Ecclesiæ ciues,vt Cantic.1.& alibi. [illegible, ~20 letters] ARA, Iabin regis exercitui praest, Iudi. 4.2. viso Baracho, [illegible, ~10 letters] ugam pedibus arripit, vt 15. fugiens occiditur à Iahele, v. 11. 1 Sam.12.9. Ps.83.10. (i. equi visio.)
units.tr: The daughters of Zion are the women and girls of Jerusalem: Lam. 1:6. Sometimes the inhabitants of the city itself and of the surrounding region are signified. Likewise the true citizens of the Church, as in Song 1 and elsewhere. [illegible] SISERA, who commanded the army of King Jabin, Judg. 4:2. When he sees Barak, [illegible] he takes to flight on foot, and, fleeing, as in v. 15, he is killed by Jael, v. 11; 1 Sam. 12:9; Psalm 83:10. (i.e. vision of a horse.)

units.la: IENS Christus potatur à ceto, Ioan.19.29. sitienti Dauidi [illegible, ~8 letters] ootus adfertur, 2 Sam.17.27. sitientes vitam æternam, Ioh. 7.37. sitiens, Auarus rapax, Iob 5.5. & 24.11.
units.tr: THIRSTING: Christ, thirsting, is given vinegar by a sponge, John 19:29. To David, thirsty, [illegible] drink is brought, 2 Sam. 17:27. Those who thirst for eternal life: John 7:37. Thirsting: the greedy and rapacious, Job 5:5; 24:11.

units.la: [illegible, ~6 letters] IS inobedientibus, Deut.28.48. Sitis exempla: Agar & eius filius, Gen.21.v.14.15. Israelitæ, Exod.17.v.1.2. Nehe. 9.20. Num.20.2. Sisara, Iudic.4.19. Samson, 15.18. Exercitus regum Israelis & Iuda & Edom. 2. Reg.3.9. Iudæi, Esa.5.13. sactantes paruuli, Thren.4.4. Christus, Psa.69.22. Ioan.19. 8. Apostoli, 1 Cor.4.11. Paulus, 2 Cor.11.27.
units.tr: [illegible] thirst for the disobedient, Deut. 28:48. Examples of thirst: Hagar and her son, Gen. 21:14–15; the Israelites, Exod. 17:1–2; Neh. 9:20; Num. 20:2; Sisera, Judg. 4:19; Samson, 15:18; the army of the kings of Israel, Judah and Edom, 2 Kings 3:9; the Jews, Isa. 5:13; sucklings who thirst, Lam. 4:4; Christ, Psalm 69:22; John 19:28; the apostles, 1 Cor. 4:11; Paul, 2 Cor. 11:27.
Spiritual thirst, most worthy of praise: Psalm 42:3; 63:2; Isa. 35:7; 44:3; 55:1; 65:13; Matt. 5:6; John 4:13–14; 6:35; 7:37; Rev. 21:6; 22:17.

units.la: SMARAGDVS typicus Exod.28.17. & 39.10. Smaragdus my-sticus Apoc.21.19.
units.tr: SMARAGDUS, typical: Exod. 28.17 and 39.10. Smaragdus, mystical: Apoc. 21.19.

units.la: SYRNA, vrbs in qua olim Christi Ecclesia celebris, Apo. 2.11. & 2.8. (vrbs Ioniæ in Asia minore.)
units.tr: SYRNA (Smyrna), a city where the Church of Christ once flourished: Apoc. 2.11 and 2.8. (A city of Ionia in Asia Minor.)

units.la: TAN mensis tertij nomen, Esth.8.9. V. Mensis.
units.tr: TAN, the name of the third month: Esth. 8.9. See MONTH.

units.la: ACH, regis Syriorum militiæ princeps, 2 Samu.10.16. in obsedio prælio à Dauide occiditur, v.18. (i. conuertens te.)
units.tr: ACH, commander of the army of the Syrian king, is slain by David in battle, 2 Sam. 10.16; v. 18. (I.e. turning yourself.)

units.la: NA, regis Ezechiæ scriba, 2 Reg.18.18. eius ruina prædi-catur, Esa.22.15. (Sobnas, sedens vel reuertens.)
units.tr: NA, scribe of King Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18.18. His downfall is foretold, Isa. 22.15. (Shebna, sitting or returning.)

units.la: SOBRIETAS, etsi generaliter accipi potest, tamen quando di-stinguitur ab Abstinentia, dicitur esse moderatio vini in-briantis, mentem turbantis & ad lasciuiam nos vocantis.
units.tr: SOBRIETY, although it can be taken in a general sense, when it is distinguished from abstinence it is said to be moderation in wine, which intoxicates, disturbs the mind and calls us to lasciviousness.

units.la: SOBRIETAS commendatur, Luc.21.34. Roma.13.13. 4.1 Thess. 5.6. 1 Tim.3.2. Tit.1.8. & 2.ver.2.3.5.12. 1 Petr.5.8. Sobrietatis abstinentiæ exempla: Moses, Exod.24.18. vxor Manoah, Iudic.1.3.4. Israelitæ, 20.26. 1 Sam.7.6. & 14.26. Nehem.9. Dauid, 2 Sam.23.16. Achab, 1 Reg.21.27. Rechabitæ, Ie-rem.35.v.6.14. Ezechiel, Ezec.4.9. Daniel, Dan.1.8. & 9.3. & 10.3. Esdras, 1 Esd.8.21. Nehemias, Nehem.1.4. Josaphat, 2 Chron. 20.3. Ioannes Baptista, Matthæi 3.4. & 11.18. Anna prophetissa, Luc.2.37. Apostoli, Luc.10.7. & 24.42. Ioan.21. Iesus Christus, Matth.4.2. Luc.4.2. Paulus & Barnabas, Actor.14.23. Vide ABSTINENTIA, & IEIVNIVM. Sobrie-tas animi commendatur, Roman.12.3. 2 Timoth 2. v.9.15. 1 Timoth.1.7. 1 Petr.1.13. & 4.7. & 5.8. Exemplum, Paulus. Act.26.25.
units.tr: SOBRIETY is commended: Luke 21.34; Rom. 13.13; 1 Thess. 5.6; 1 Tim. 3.2; Tit. 1.8; 2.2, 3, 5, 12; 1 Pet. 5.8. Examples of sobriety as abstinence: Moses, Exod. 24.18; the wife of Manoah, Judg. 13.3, 4; the Israelites, Judg. 20.26; 1 Sam. 7.6 and 14.26; Neh. 9; David, 2 Sam. 23.16; Ahab, 1 Kings 21.27; the Rechabites, Jer. 35.6, 14; Ezekiel, Ezek. 4.9; Daniel, Dan. 1.8, 9.3, 10.3; Ezra, 1 Esd. 8.21; Nehemiah, Neh. 1.4; Jehoshaphat, 2 Chron. 20.3; John the Baptist, Matt. 3.4, 11.18; Anna the prophetess, Luke 2.37; the Apostles, Luke 10.7, 24.42, John 21; Jesus Christ, Matt. 4.2, Luke 4.2; Paul and Barnabas, Acts 14.23. See ABSTINENCE and FASTING. Sobriety of mind is commended: Rom. 12.3; 2 Tim. 2.9, 15; 1 Tim. 1.7; 1 Pet. 1.13, 4.7, 5.8. Example: Paul, Acts 26.25.

units.la: SOBRIVS, Temperans, qui suis affectibus imperat, tum ebrio speciatim, tum intemperanti in genere, oppositus, Cor. 5. 13. 1 Thess. 5. v. 6. 8. 1 Tim. 3. v. 2. 11. Tit. 1. 8. & 2. v. 2. 5. 1 Pet. 1. 13. & 5. 8.]
units.tr: SOBER: temperate, one who rules his own passions; opposed especially to the drunkard, and to intemperance in general: 1 Cor. 5.13; 1 Thess. 5.6, 8; 1 Tim. 3.2, 11; Tit. 1.8, 2.2, 5; 1 Pet. 1.13, 5.8.

units.la: SOCIETAS bona consectanda, mala fugienda, Genes. 19. 1 Levit. 7. 19. Num. 16. 25. 26. & 25. 4. Ios. 23. 12. 2 Sam. 22. 27. Paral. 19. 2 Iob. 31. 1. Psalm. 18. ver. 26. 27. & 26. v. 4. 8. & 37. Prou. 1. v. 10. 15. & 4. 14. & 6. 25. & 13. 20. & 22. v. 5. 24. & 24. & 29. v. 27. Ier. 16. 8. Eccl. 6. 35. & 8. v. 1. 18. & 9. 21. & 12. 10. 13. v. 1. 20. Tob. 1. 5. Matt. 7. 15. Act. 19. 9. 2 Cor. 6. 14. Eph. 5. 1 2 Tim. 4. 14. Apoc. 18. 4. societatis commoda, Eccl. 4. 9. societas spiritualis, quam pij cum Deo habent, 2 Corinth. 6. v. 17. & 1 Cor. 6. 17. 1 Ioann. 1. 6. societatis bonae fructus Genes. 18. 32. & 30. 30. & 35. 3. & 39. 5. Iudic. 5. 15. 2 Reg. 3. versic. 14. 15. Dan. 2. versic. 17. 18. Act. 2. versic. 1. 44. & 9. 26. 27. 24.
units.tr: SOCIETY: good company is to be sought, bad company to be fled: Gen. 19; Lev. 7.19; Num. 16.25, 26, 25.4; Josh. 23.12; 2 Sam. 22.27; 1 Chron. 19.2; Job 31.1; Ps. 18.26, 27, 26.4, 8, 37; Prov. 1.10, 15, 4.14, 6.25, 13.20, 22.5, 24, 24.29, 29.27; Jer. 16.8; Eccl. 6.35, 8.1, 18, 9.21, 12.10, 13.1, 20; Tob. 1.5; Matt. 7.15; Acts 19.9; 2 Cor. 6.14; Eph. 5.1, 2; 2 Tim. 4.14; Rev. 18.4. The advantages of society: Eccl. 4.9. Spiritual society, which the godly have with God: 2 Cor. 6.17; 1 Cor. 6.17; 1 John 1.6. The good fruits of good society: Gen. 18.32, 30.30, 35.3, 39.5; Judg. 5.15; 2 Kings 3.14, 15; Dan. 2.17, 18; Acts 2.1, 44, 9.26, 27, 24.

units.la: Societatis bonorum & eius fructus exempla: Si decem iusti inuenti fuissent in quinque peccatricib. ciuitatibus, perciffet Deus vniuersis, propter illos, Gen. 18. 32. Laban cum Iacobo, Gen. 30. 30. Dei cum Iacobo, 35. v. 2. 3. Iosephi cum Putiphare, 39. 5. Israelitarum cum Deo, Ios. 24. 31. Du cum Issachar cum Debora, Iudic 5. 15. Saulis cum Samuele & Prophetis, 1 Sam 19. v. 20. 21. &c. Elisaei cum Iosaphate propter quem impetrauit aquas dari exercitui, in quo cum rant alij duo reges, 2 Reg. 3. v. 14. 17. propter Danielem bene fit Magis, &c. Dan. 2. v. 24. 25. propter praesentiam spiritus sancti, cum fidelibus, Act. 2. v. 3. &c. Panli, Apostolis, 26. nauigantibus cum Paulo, bene est, propter Paulum, 2 24. V. CONVERSATIO.
units.tr: Examples of the fellowship of good people and its fruits: If ten righteous men had been found in the five sinful cities, God would have spared all of them for their sake, Gen. 18.32. Laban with Jacob, Gen. 30.30. God with Jacob, 35.2, 3. Joseph with Potiphar, 39.5. The Israelites with God, Josh. 24.31. Issachar with Deborah, Judg. 5.15. Saul with Samuel and the prophets, 1 Sam. 19.20, 21, etc. Elisha with Jehoshaphat, for whose sake he obtained water for the army, in which two other kings also were, 2 Kings 3.14, 17. For Daniel's sake good came to the Magi, etc., Dan. 2.24, 25. Because of the presence of the Holy Spirit with the faithful, Acts 2.3, etc. Of Paul: the Apostles and those sailing with Paul fared well because of Paul, Acts 27.24. See CONVERSATION.

units.la: Societatis malae fructus, Genes. 4. 8. & 11. 31. & 15. 7. 19 4. Num. 16. 26. & 33. 55. Ios. 7. 1. 15. Iudi. 1. 28. & 2. v. 1. 2. 3. Sam. 13. versic. 3. 5. & 15. 13. & 21. 1. 1 Reg. 22. 32. 2 Paral. 19. 2. 25. 7. Iob. 30. 29. Psalm. 120. 5. Esa. 6. 5. & 7. 2. Ezech. 2. 6. Luc. 23. 12. Act. 2. 40. & 13. 8. & 14. v. 18. 19. Phil. 2. 15. Societatis malae fructuum Exempla: Cain Abel, Gene. 4. 8. Thare, Abraham, Chaldaei, 11. 31. & 15. 7. Sodomitae, Loth. 19. 4. Ismael, Isaac. 21. 9 Esau, Iacob: Iacob non voluit vna progredi cum fratre suo Esau, 33. v. 12. 13. Israelitae, Dathan, & Numer. 16. 24. &c. Israelitae, Chananaei, 33. versic. 51. 5. Propter Achan Israelitae percutiuntur, Iosu. 7. 5. Ammon à Ionadab amico suo corrumpitur, 2 Samuel 13. ver. 3. 4. Iosaphat, reprehenditur à Propheta ob societatem cum Ochosia initam, 2 Para. 20. 37. Vide Iob 30. 29. Psalm. 120. 5. §.Esa.6.5. Ezech.2.6. cœcus natus non fuit inter Christi fideles, donec eiectus fuit ex Pharisæorum synagoga, Ioan.9.34. Iubemur etiam nos seruare à generatione mala, Act.2.40.Phil.2.15. societatem habere cum Deo. 1 Ioan. 1.3.
units.tr: Fruits of bad society: Gen. 4.8, 11.31, 15.7, 19.4; Num. 16.26, 33.55; Josh. 7.1, 15; Judg. 1.28, 2.1, 2, 3; 1 Sam. 13.3, 5, 15.13, 21.1; 1 Kings 22.32; 2 Chron. 19.2, 25.7; Job 30.29; Ps. 120.5; Isa. 6.5, 7.2; Ezek. 2.6; Luke 23.12; Acts 2.40, 13.8, 14.18, 19; Phil. 2.15. Examples of the fruits of bad society: Cain and Abel, Gen. 4.8. Terah, Abraham, the Chaldeans, 11.31, 15.7. The Sodomites and Lot, Gen. 19.4. Ishmael and Isaac, 21.9. Esau and Jacob: Jacob was unwilling to go on together with his brother Esau, 33.12, 13. The Israelites and Dathan, Num. 16.24, etc. The Israelites and the Canaanites, Num. 33.51, 55. Because of Achan the Israelites are struck down, Josh. 7.5. Amnon is corrupted by his friend Jonadab, 2 Sam. 13.3, 4. Jehoshaphat is rebuked by the prophet for the alliance he entered into with Ahaziah, 2 Chron. 20.37. See Job 30.29, Ps. 120.5, Isa. 6.5, Ezek. 2.6. The man born blind was not among the faithful of Christ until he was cast out of the synagogue of the Pharisees, John 9.34. We are also commanded to be saved from this evil generation, Acts 2.40; Phil. 2.15. We are commanded to have fellowship with God, 1 John 1.3.

units.la: Socius qui nobis adhæret in itinere, labore, studio, opere, externo, vel interno & spirituali. Gen.14.15. & 33. v.12.15. & 35.5.6.Exod.31.6. Ios.8.10.& 10.v.18.27.Iudi.3.8.& 9.41. 1 Sam.23.25.2 Samu.16.13.1 Reg.20.35.2 Reg.4.40.Esai.1. 23.Ierem.40.7.Dan.2.13. Matth.23.30.Luc.5.v.7.9.1 Cor. 10.20.2 Cor.1.7.& 8.23. Philipp.1.7.Philem.vers.17,Hebr. 10.33.]
units.tr: A companion who clings to us on the road, in toil, study, or work, whether external or internal and spiritual: Gen. 14.15, 33.12, 15, 35.5, 6; Exod. 31.6; Josh. 8.10, 10.18, 27; Judg. 3.8, 9.41; 1 Sam. 23.25; 2 Sam. 16.13; 1 Kings 20.35; 2 Kings 4.40; Isa. 1.23; Jer. 40.7; Dan. 2.13; Matt. 23.30; Luke 5.7, 9; 1 Cor. 10.20; 2 Cor. 1.7, 8.23; Phil. 1.7; Philem. 17; Heb. 10.33.

units.la: SOCRVS Petri sanatur, Matth.8.15, Vide PETRVS. socrus non est vxor ducenda, vide AFFINITAS.
units.tr: MOTHER-IN-LAW: Peter's mother-in-law is healed, Matt. 8.15. See PETER. A mother-in-law is not to be taken as a wife. See AFFINITY.

units.la: SOCOTH (à tuguriis nomen habens, Genes.33.17.) ciuitas in tribu Gad munitissima, Ios.13.27 Socoth principes Gedeoni inhumani, Iud.8.v.5,6. suæ inhumanitatis pœnas luunt, v.15.16.(Succoth.i. tabernacula.)
units.tr: SUCCOTH (named from tents, Gen. 33.17), a very well fortified city in the tribe of Gad, Josh. 13.27. The princes of Succoth, inhospitable to Gideon, Judg. 8.5, 6, paid the penalty for their inhumanity, v. 15, 16. (Succoth, i.e. tabernacles.)

units.la: SOCOTH-benoth Babyloniorum idolum, 2 Reg.17.30. Vide IDOLORVM Catalogus. (tabernacula filiarum.)
units.tr: SUCCOTH-BENOTH, an idol of the Babylonians, 2 Kings 17.30. See the Catalogue of IDOLS. (Tabernacles of the daughters.)

units.la: SODOMA & Gomorrha amœnissimo loco sita, Genes.13.10. sodomitæ, homines pessimi, Genes.13.13. spoliantur, 14.11. 23.Sap.10.6.Esa.13.19.Iere.50.40.Amos 4.11. Luc.17.29.6. Petr.2.6. Iudæ vers.7. causæ subuersionis, Ezech.16.49. sodomitarum peccata quæ fuerint, Genes.19.4.&c.Ezech. 16.49.Eorum conditio tolerabilior futura est, quàm incolarum Corazim & Bethsaidæ conditio, Matt.11.24. doma spiritualis, Apoc.11.8. sodomitæ, Genef.13.13. (Sedomah. secretum eorum.)
units.tr: SODOM and Gomorrah, situated in a most pleasant place, Gen. 13.10. The Sodomites, most wicked men, Gen. 13.13, are plundered, 14.11. Isa. 13.19; Jer. 50.40; Amos 4.11; Luke 17.29; 2 Pet. 2.6; Jude 7. The causes of their overthrow: Ezek. 16.49. What the sins of the Sodomites were: Gen. 19.4, etc.; Ezek. 16.49. Their condition will be more tolerable than that of the inhabitants of Chorazin and Bethsaida, Matt. 11.24. Spiritual Sodom: Rev. 11.8. Sodomites: Gen. 13.13. (Sedomah, their secret.)

units.la: SODOMIA, crimen contra naturam & damnabile: Leui.18.22. cum mare ne concubito concubitu muliebri: abominatio est. cap.20.13. Qui cubuerit cum mare concubitu muliebri: rem abominandam fecerunt ambo: omnino morte afficiuntor, cædis ipsorum causa est in ipsis. 1 Tim.1.10. regno Dei excluduntur. ἀρσενοκοῖται: 1 Cor.6.9. In sensum reprobum traditi: Rom.1.26. Eph.4.19. sodomitæ hoc genere sceleris peccarunt, qui sulphure & igne deleti sunt. Genef.19.24.
units.tr: SODOMY, a crime against nature and damnable: Lev. 18.22, "A man shall not lie with a male as with a woman; it is an abomination." Lev. 20.13, "If a man lies with a male as with a woman, both have done an abominable thing; they shall surely be put to death; their blood is upon them." 1 Tim. 1.10: they are excluded from the kingdom of God. Greek [ἀρσενοκοῖται], men who lie with males: 1 Cor. 6.9. Given over to a reprobate mind: Rom. 1.26; Eph. 4.19. The Sodomites sinned by this kind of wickedness, and were destroyed by brimstone and fire, Gen. 19.24.

units.la: SOL, Dei verbo creatus, Gen.1.16. nouit suum occasum: Psal.104.19. Cedit nocti ibid. Et nox soli, 22. ad vocem Iosue stitur, Ios.10.13. retrocedit decem gradibus ad petitionem Ezechiæ & preces Esaiæ, 2 Reg.20.11. obscuratur, Matth.27.45. Marc.15.33. Luc.23.45. Deus facit vt sol oriatur super iustos & iniustos: Mat.5.
units.tr: SUN, created by God's word (Gen. 1.16), knows its setting (Ps. 104.19). "Cedit nocti," ibid. And night to the sun, 22. At Joshua's word it stood still (Josh. 10.13). It went back ten steps at Hezekiah's petition and Isaiah's prayer (2 Kings 20.11). It was darkened (Matt. 27.45; Mark 15.33; Luke 23.45). God makes the sun rise on the just and the unjust (Matt. 5).

units.la: SOLIS ardor, piis non noxius, Psalm.121.6. Apo.7.16. solis ortus, & cursus magnificentia, Psal.19. v 5.6.7.16. soli & Lunæ seruientes, à Iosia occiduntur, 2 Reg 23.5. V. Deut.4.19.) reprehenduntur à Ieremia, Ier.44.v.1.&c. solis nomen pro oppressione, vel persecutione, qua tanquam sole torrefiunt hypocritæ, Matt.13.6. solis & lunæ equi. 2 Reg.23.11. Deus est sol suis, Ps.84.12.
units.tr: The heat of the sun is not harmful to the pious (Ps. 121.6; Rev. 7.16). The rising of the sun and the magnificence of its course (Ps. 19.5–7, 16). Those who served the sun and moon were slain by Josiah (2 Kings 23.5; see Deut. 4.19) and rebuked by Jeremiah (Jer. 44.1ff). "Sun" is a name for oppression or persecution, by which hypocrites are scorched as by the sun (Matt. 13.6). The horses of the sun and moon (2 Kings 23.11). God is a sun to his own people (Ps. 84.12).

units.la: [Sol ecclesiæ & Christus, Esai.60.19.20. Malac.4.2. V. Mat.17.2. sol afflictionum & persecutionum æstus, Cant.1.6. sol gloriæ qua quis fruitur, Ier.15.9. sol, spes laborationis, Amos.8.9.) Visio veritatis: Mich.3.6. sol ad opificem suum laudandum inuitatur: Ps.148.3.4.&136.5.7.8.9.&104.v.22.
units.tr: [The sun of the Church and Christ (Isa. 60.19–20; Mal. 4.2; see Matt. 17.2). The sun of afflictions and persecutions, its heat (Song 1.6). The sun of glory, which a man enjoys (Jer. 15.9). The sun as the hope of labour (Amos 8.9). Vision of truth (Mic. 3.6). The sun is invited to praise its maker (Ps. 148.3–4; 136.5, 7–9; 104.22).]

units.la: SOLEAS portare, prouerbialiter vsurpatur, Ps.60.10. Matthei 3.11. quo vilissimum ministerium significatur.
units.tr: To carry sandals is used proverbially (Ps. 60.10; Matt. 3.11), signifying the most menial ministry.

units.la: SOLENNITATES anniuersariæ erant, quæ quotannis recurrebant, & plurium dierum erant, in quibus primus & ultimus dies pari ceremonia celebrandi erant: Leui.21. propterea vltimus ille dies commodè vocatur à Luca Sabbathum ἀντιπεγαῖον cap.6.v.1. solennitas post plures annos recurrens, erat sabbathum terræ, septimo quoque anno, quo à cultu agrorum & vinearum cessandum fuit, recurrens, Leu.25.1.&c. Itè annus Iubilæus, quinquagesimo quoque anno recurrens, quo omnes possessiones ad suos dominos redibant, & serui Hebræi manumittebantur: Leui.25.8.&c.
units.tr: Solemnities were annual observances that recurred each year and lasted several days, the first and last of which were to be celebrated with the same ceremony (Lev. 21). For this reason Luke fittingly calls that last day the Sabbath [δευτεροπρώτῳ] (Luke 6.1). A solemnity recurring after several years was the sabbath of the land, which came every seventh year, when work in the fields and vineyards was to cease (Lev. 25.1ff). Likewise the Jubilee year, recurring every fiftieth year, when all possessions returned to their owners and Hebrew slaves were set free (Lev. 25.8ff).

units.la: SOLENNITATES Hebrœorum præcipuè tres, Exodi 23.v.14. 17.Leuit.23.1.&c.Deuter.16.1.&c. solennitas Azymorum, Ezod.23.15.& 34.18.Leu.23.v.5.6.Num.28.17.Deut.16.ver. 1.2.5.solennitas Expiationum, Leu.16.30.&23.27.Numer. 29.v.7.8.solennitas Hebdomadarum, Exod.34.22. solen- nitas Messis, seu Pentecostes, Exod.23.16.Num.28.26.Leu. 23.v.15.16.Deut.16.v 9.10.Ioan.5.1.Act.2.1.& 20.16.1 Cor. 16.8.solennitas Primitiarum, Leu.23.10. solennitas Epu- larum Esth.9.18. solennitas Tabernaculorum, Exo.23.16. Leu.23.v.39.&c.Deut.16.13.& 31.10.1 Esdr.3.4. Nehem.8. 18.Ioan.7.2. solennitas Tubarum, Leui.23.24. Num.29.1.2. Par.5.3.solennitas Neomeniæ (seu noui lunij) Colos.2.16. Num.28.11.1 Sam.20.5. Ezech. 45.18. solennitas sabbathi, V.SABBATHVM solennitatum seu festorum violatio, quare graviter puniatur, Numer.15.32. In solennitate diei festi quare non captus Christus, Matt.5.
units.tr: The Hebrews had three chief solemnities (Exod. 23.14, 17; Lev. 23.1ff; Deut. 16.1ff): (1) the Solemnity of Unleavened Bread (Exod. 23.15; 34.18; Lev. 23.5–6; Num. 28.17; Deut. 16.1–2, 5); (2) the Solemnity of Atonement (Lev. 16.30; 23.27; Num. 29.7–8); (3) the Solemnity of Weeks (Exod. 34.22); (4) the Solemnity of Harvest, or Pentecost (Exod. 23.16; Num. 28.26; Lev. 23.15–16; Deut. 16.9–10; John 5.1; Acts 2.1; 20.16; 1 Cor. 16.8); (5) the Solemnity of Firstfruits (Lev. 23.10); (6) the Solemnity of Feasts (Esth. 9.18); (7) the Solemnity of Tabernacles (Exod. 23.16; Lev. 23.39ff; Deut. 16.13; 31.10; 1 Esd. 3.4; Neh. 8.18; John 7.2); (8) the Solemnity of Trumpets (Lev. 23.24; Num. 29.1–2; 1 Chr. 5.3); (9) the Solemnity of the New Moon (Col. 2.16; Num. 28.11; 1 Sam. 20.5; Ezek. 45.18); (10) the Solemnity of the Sabbath (see SABBATH). The violation of solemnities or feasts, why it is grievously punished (Num. 15.32). Why Christ was not seized on the day of the feast (Matt. 5).

units.la: SOLICITVDO nimia, Exod.34.21. Leuit.25.20.21. Deut.8.3. Iob 7.16 Psal.55.23.& 145.v.15.16. Prou.10.3. & 13.23. Matth. 6. 25.ad finem usque & 10.v.9.10.& 13.22.& 16.5. Luc.8.14 & 12.11.22.& 14.18.& 21.34.1 Corint.7.32.Phil.4.6. Hebr.13. 5.6. solicitudo diffidentiæ coniuncta damnatur, cùm licet homo sine fide & spe auxilij diuini, animo angitur de futuris euentis, cùm priuatis tum publicis, vt superiora & seq.docent. Marc.4.19.1 Tim.6.8.1 Pet.5.7. Psal.55.23. hæc Græcis μέριμνα dicitur.
units.tr: Excessive anxiety (Exod. 34.21; Lev. 25.20–21; Deut. 8.3; Job 7.16; Ps. 55.23; 145.15–16; Prov. 10.3; 13.23; Matt. 6.25 to the end; 10.9–10; 13.22; 16.5; Luke 8.14; 12.11, 22; 14.18; 21.34; 1 Cor. 7.32; Phil. 4.6; Heb. 13.5–6). Solicitude joined with diffidence is condemned, when a man, without faith and hope of divine help, is troubled in mind about future events, both private and public, as the passages above and below teach (Mark 4.19; 1 Tim. 6.8; 1 Pet. 5.7; Ps. 55.23). In Greek this is called merimna [μέριμνα].

units.la: Solicitudo vocationis, Græcis φροντίς dicta, præcipitur, cùm scilicet quis euenta quæcunque Deo commendat, interim tamen labores sibi mandatos suo loco & tempore pro sua vocatione sedulò v g. t, Rom.12.11.(Vide ANXIETAS: & SOCORDIA excutienda.) solicitudo Pauli pro Ecclesia, 2 Corinth.7.12.& 11.v.28.pro proximo, Ephes.4.28.1 Cor. 12.26.
units.tr: Solicitude about one's calling, called phrontis [φροντίς] in Greek, is enjoined, namely when a man commends all events whatsoever to God, yet meanwhile diligently performs the labours entrusted to him in their place and time, according to his calling (e.g. Rom. 12.11). (See ANXIETY; and carelessness is to be shaken off.) Paul's solicitude for the Church (2 Cor. 7.12; 11.28); for his neighbour (Eph. 4.28; 1 Cor. 12.26).

units.la: SOLICITVS Deus pro Abrahamo, Genes.12.17.soliciti simus seruare vnitatem spiritus vinculo pacis, Eph.4.3.
units.tr: God was solicitous for Abraham (Gen. 12.17). Let us be solicitous to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace (Eph. 4.3).

units.la: SOLITARII molestia vana, Eccl.4.v.7.8.
units.tr: The vain trouble of the solitary man (Eccl. 4.7–8).

units.la: [SOLITVDO desertum sæpissimè, pro animi anxietate sinimitur, Ezech.12.19.& pro desolatione, Esai.24.12.Ezech.29.9 Ose.13.5.Ioel.2.3.]
units.tr: [SOLITUDE, a desert, is very often used for anxiety of mind (Ezek. 12.19), and for desolation (Isa. 24.12; Ezek. 29.9; Hos. 13.5; Joel 2.3).]

units.la: SOLIVM regium iustitia confirmatur, Pro.16.12. & 25.5.& 29. 14.solium Salomonis, V.SOLOMON.
units.tr: A royal throne is confirmed by righteousness (Prov. 16.12; 25.5; 29.14). The throne of Solomon: see SOLOMON.

units.la: SOLIVM Dei, 1 Reg.8.13.49. Esai.6.1.& 63.15. Ierem.3.17. Thren.5.19.Solium Christi filij Dauidis, Esai.9.6.& 16.5.& 22.23. Zac.6.13. folium Regum, Ægypti, Iudæ, Israelis, Chaldæorum, &c. folium iniquitatis. Amos 6.5.]
units.tr: [The throne of God (1 Kings 8.13, 49; Isa. 6.1; 63.15; Jer. 3.17; Lam. 5.19). The throne of Christ the son of David (Isa. 9.6; 16.5; 22.23; Zech. 6.13). The thrones of kings: of Egypt, Judah, Israel, the Chaldeans, etc. The throne of iniquity (Amos 6.5).]

units.la: SOLOMON, Dauidis ex Bethlabee filius nascitur, 2 Sam.12.24. à Deo diligitur, ibidem Solomon Deriussu, cur sic dictus, 1 Par.22.9. Prophetæ Nathan erudiendus & educandus traditur, 2 Sam.12.25. Patris iussu, rex Israelis vngitur, 1 Reg.1.38. &c. 1 Paral.23.1. & 29.22. mille hostias offert, 2 Paral.1.6. typus Christi est Psal.45.8. & 72.5. Pharaonis filiam vxorem ducit, 1 Reg.3.1. sapientiam à Deo petit, v.9. & Paral.1.10. Sapient. 9.4. ligna templo extruendo necessaria ab Hiram petit. 1. Reg. 56.2. Par. 2.3. templum ædificat 1 Regum 6.1. 2 Paralipp. 3.1 Actor. 7.47. Ecclesiæ Israel benedicit, 1 Reg.8.v.14.55. 56. ciuitates extruit 9.17.2 Par.8.2. populos sibi tributarios reddit v.7. 8. Hiram regi viginti oppida largitur, 1.Reg.9 11. auri habendi causa in Ophir nuntios mittit, 2.Paral.8.18. alienigenas mulieres amat, 1 Regum 11.1. Deos alienos sequitur, v.4. 2 Reg.23.13. moritur, 2 Par.9.31. (Solomoh.1.pacificus.)
units.tr: Solomon was born to David by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 12.24) and was loved by God (ibid.). By God's command, why he was so called (1 Chr. 22.9). He was handed over to the prophet Nathan to be taught and brought up (2 Sam. 12.25). By his father's command he was anointed king of Israel (1 Kings 1.38, etc.; 1 Chr. 23.1; 29.22). He offered a thousand sacrifices (2 Chr. 1.6). He is a type of Christ (Ps. 45.8; 72.5). He took Pharaoh's daughter as his wife (1 Kings 3.1). He asked wisdom of God (v. 9; 2 Chr. 1.10; Wisd. 9.4). He asked Hiram for the timber needed to build the temple (1 Kings 5.6; 2 Chr. 2.3). He built the temple (1 Kings 6.1; 2 Chr. 3.1; Acts 7.47). He blessed the Church of Israel (1 Kings 8.14, 55–56). He built cities (1 Kings 9.17; 2 Chr. 8.2). He made peoples tributary to himself (1 Kings 9.7–8). He gave Hiram twenty towns (1 Kings 9.11). He sent messengers to Ophir to get gold (2 Chr. 8.18). He loved foreign women (1 Kings 11.1). He followed foreign gods (v. 4; 2 Kings 23.13). He died (2 Chr. 9.31). (Solomon: peaceable.)

units.la: SOLOMONIS regni anni, 1 Reg. 11. 42. artificum numerus, 1 Reg.5.13.2 Paral.2.v.17.18. Aduersarij.1 Reg.11.25. 26. carmina, 1 Reg. 4. 32. census annuus, 10.14. cibus quotidianus, 4.verf.22.23. de rebus variis disputationes. v.33. Equi & currus, v.26.2. Par.1.14. gloria quanta, 1 Par.29.25. 2 Par.1.12. & 9.22. de duabus meretricibus iudicium, 1 Regum 3.27. orationes, ver.11.&8.23. parabolæ, 4 32 principes, v.2.3. prosperitas, 2 Par.7.11. regni eius fines, 1 Regum 4.21.2 Para.9.26. sapientia quanta, v.6.23. Mat.12.42. Templi Salomonis forma, 1 Reg.6 2. thronus, 10.18. vxores & concubinæ. 11,3.
units.tr: The years of Solomon's reign (1 Kings 11.42). The number of his craftsmen (1 Kings 5.13; 2 Chr. 2.17–18). His adversaries (1 Kings 11.25–26). His songs (1 Kings 4.32). His annual revenue (1 Kings 10.14). His daily food (1 Kings 4.22–23). His disputations on various matters (v. 33). His horses and chariots (v. 26; 2 Chr. 1.14). How great his glory was (1 Chr. 29.25; 2 Chr. 1.12; 9.22). The judgment concerning the two harlots (1 Kings 3.27). His prayers (1 Kings 8.11, 23). His parables (1 Kings 4.32). His princes (1 Kings 4.2–3). His prosperity (2 Chr. 7.11). The borders of his kingdom (1 Kings 4.21; 2 Chr. 9.26). How great his wisdom was (1 Kings 4.6, 23; Matt. 12.42). The form of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6.2). His throne (1 Kings 10.18). His wives and concubines (1 Kings 11.3).

units.la: SOLVERE ad extremum quadrantem, Matth. 5. 26. proverbialiter is dicitur, qui cum summo iure agitur. Soluere, pro sua interpretatione, quasi enervare, Matth.5,19 soluti, pro violari aut irrita fieri, Matth.5.v.17.19. Ioan.10.35. aut destrui, 7.23 soluere peccata quid, Matth.16 19. Ioann. 20.23.
units.tr: To pay to the last farthing (Matt. 5.26) is said proverbially of one who is dealt with by the strictest law. To loosen, in the sense of interpreting, as if to weaken (Matt. 5.19). Loosed, for violated or made void (Matt. 5.17, 19; John 10.35), or destroyed (John 7.23). What it is to loose sins (Matt. 16.19; John 20.23).

units.la: SOMNIA, olim seruis Dei familiaria, Num.12.6. somnia & visiones, in quibus Deus nonnunquam suam voluntatem aperiebat, Gen.20.3. & 28.12. & 31.24 & 37.v.5.9. & 40.8. & 41.1. & 46.2 Num.12.6. Iudic.7.v.13.15 1 Sam 3.versi.4.8 10. & 28.6.2 Samu.7.4.1 Reg.3.verfic.5.15. Iob.7.13.14. & 33.15. Daniel 2.1. & 7.1 Matth.1.20. & 2. ver.12.13. Act.16.9 & 18. 9. & 23.
units.tr: Dreams, once familiar to God's servants (Num. 12.6). Dreams and visions, in which God sometimes revealed his will (Gen. 20.3; 28.12; 31.24; 37.5, 9; 40.8; 41.1; 46.2; Num. 12.6; Judg. 7.13, 15; 1 Sam. 3.4, 8, 10; 28.6; 2 Sam. 7.4; 1 Kings 3.5, 15; Job 7.13–14; 33.15; Dan. 2.1; 7.1; Matt. 1.20; 2.12–13; Acts 16.9; 18.9; 23.11; 27.23).

units.la: 9. & 23. 11. & 27. 23, somnia & visiones quæ non conue-niunt cum verbo Dei & doctrina Ecclesiæ, sunt contem-nenda, Deut.13.Eccles.5 3.Eccles34.1.&c.Iere. 23. v.16.25. & 27.9.& 29.8.Somniorum interpretatio à Deo est, Gen. 41.v.16 39. Dan.1.17. & 2, 23. somniis non inhærendum, Eccles.5.v 2,6. Somniorum & revelationum per illa factarum exempla Abimelech, Genes.20.3.Iacob,28.12.& 31.11. Laban, v.24.Ioseph 37. v. 5. 9. Vide Ios EPH.Pincernæ & pistoris cum interpretatione,40.5.Pharaonis item cum interpretatione,41.1.cuiusdam Madianitæ, Iudic. 7.13.Nabuchodonosor,Dan.7.1. Vide Dan. Vide VISION VM exempla.[Somniator, Gen. 37.19.Deut.13.3.Iere.27.9.Zac. 10.2.]
units.tr: 9. & 23. 11. & 27. 23. Dreams and visions that do not agree with God's Word and the doctrine of the Church are to be despised (Deut. 13; Eccl. 5.3; Ecclus. 34.1ff; Jer. 23.16, 25; 27.9; 29.8). The interpretation of dreams is from God (Gen. 41.16, 39; Dan. 1.17; 2.23). One must not cling to dreams (Eccl. 5.2, 6). Examples of dreams and of revelations made through them: Abimelech (Gen. 20.3); Jacob (28.12; 31.11); Laban (v. 24); Joseph (37.5, 9); see JOSEPH. The cupbearer and the baker, with their interpretation (40.5); Pharaoh likewise, with interpretation (41.1); a certain Midianite (Judg. 7.13); Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 7.1); see DANIEL; see the examples under VISION. [A dreamer (Gen. 37.19; Deut. 13.3; Jer. 27.9; Zech. 10.2).]

units.la: OMNVS quibus suavis, Eccles. 5. 11. somno non indulgendum,Prou.20.13 & 24.22.& 6.4.Act.20.9.
units.tr: SLEEP is sweet to some (Eccl. 5.11). One must not indulge in sleep (Prov. 20.13; 24.33; 6.4; Acts 20.9).

units.la: [Somnus Spiritualis,Rom.13.11.Somnus, mors corporis, Ioan.11.11.]
units.tr: [Spiritual sleep (Rom. 13.11). Sleep, the death of the body (John 11.11).]

units.la: SOPATER,vel ut alij legunt,Sosipater , Pauli comes & cognatus , Actor. 20. 4. Rom.16,21. (σωσίπατρος, seruans patrem.)
units.tr: SOSIPATER, or as others read, Sosipater, companion and kinsman of Paul (Acts 20.4; Rom. 16.21). [σωσίπατρος], saving the father.

units.la: SOPHAR Naamathites amicus Iobi, Iob.11.1. eius in Iobum vehemens obiurgatio,v.2.3.(i.speculator eius.)
units.tr: SOPHAR the Naamathite, friend of Job (Job 11.1). His vehement rebuke of Job (v. 2–3). (That is, his watchman.)

units.la: SOPHONIAS propheta:eius prophetiæ tempus , Soph.1.1. prophetiæ eius argumentum, v.2.3. (Abiconsio Domini.)
units.tr: SOPHONIAS the prophet: the time of his prophecy (Zeph. 1.1); the subject of his prophecy (v. 2–3). (That is, the hiding of the Lord.)

units.la: SORDES animæ,Prou.30.12.Esai.4.4. Thren.1. 9. Ezech.24. 13. Ose.5.11. I Petr.3.21. Apoc.22.11. Sordes corporis Iob.7.5.Esai. 28.13. Est nimia in honesto,& qui nos decet.
units.tr: Filth of the soul (Prov. 30.12; Isa. 4.4; Lam. 1.9; Ezek. 24.13; Hos. 5.11; 1 Pet. 3.21; Rev. 22.11). Filth of the body (Job 7.5; Isa. 28.13). It is an excess in what is honourable, and what befits us.

units.la: SOROR, Græcis ἀδελφή, idem declarans quod אחות fidelis seu Christiana,1 Cor.9.5.sorores,pro cognatis, Hebraismus, Mar.6.3.soroes Christi, V.FRATRES:&, CHRISTI sorores.Soror Abrahæ Sara,Gen.20.12.
units.tr: SISTER, in Greek adelphē, the same as the Hebrew [אחות], a faithful or Christian sister (1 Cor. 9.5). "Sisters" for kinswomen, a Hebraism (Mark 6.3). The sisters of Christ: see BROTHERS and SISTERS OF CHRIST. Abraham's sister Sarah (Gen. 20.12).

units.la: SOROR,afflictio carni adhærens.Iob.17.14. Soror mystica, Prou.7.4.Soror Ecclesia Christi, propter Spiritum adoptionis,& ex immensa quadam charitate, à Christo deo homine,fratre & sponso,soror compellatur. Cantic.4.v. 9.10.12.& 5.v.1.2.Soror Ecclesiæ Iudaicæ est Ecclesia Gentium,Cantic.8.8.Soror consanguinea, Matth.13 56. Soror spiritualis,Matth.12.50.Rom.16.1.1 Cor.7.15.Iac.2.15. Sorores dicuntur Iuda & Israel, quod tribus 12. ex quibus regna illa constabant ab eodem patre duxissent originem. Harum Soror Sodoma dicitur, propter morum similitudinem.]
units.tr: SISTER: affliction clinging to the flesh (Job 17.14). A mystical sister (Prov. 7.4). The sister of the Church of Christ: because of the Spirit of adoption, and out of an immense charity, the Church is addressed as sister by Christ, God-man, brother and bridegroom (Song 4.9–10, 12; 5.1–2). The sister of the Jewish Church is the Church of the Gentiles (Song 8.8). A blood sister (Matt. 13.56). A spiritual sister (Matt. 12.50; Rom. 16.1; 1 Cor. 7.15; Jas. 2.15). Judah and Israel are called sisters, because the twelve tribes of which those kingdoms consisted had originated from the same father. Of these, Sodom is called the sister, because of the similarity of their morals.

units.la: SORS est medium à Deo constitutum, quo ipse controuersias, quæ aliter ab hominibus dirimi non possunt, componit. pro. 18.18. Num. 26.55. Iosh. 14.2. Leuit. 16.8.
units.tr: A lot (sors) is a means set up by God by which he himself settles controversies that cannot otherwise be resolved by men. Prov. 18.18; Num. 26.55; Josh. 14.2; Lev. 16.8.

units.la: SORS: sortes à Deo reguntur, Prouerb. 16.33. fortium missionis praxis, Iosu. 18.10. 1. Samuel 10.20. & 14.42. Esth. 3.7. Psal. 22.19. Matth. 27.35. Ionæ. 1.7. Act. 1.26.
units.tr: LOT: lots are governed by God, Prov. 16.33. The practice of casting lots: Josh. 18.10; 1 Sam. 10.20; 14.42; Esth. 3.7; Ps. 22.19; Matt. 27.35; Jonah 1.7; Acts 1.26.

units.la: Sortilegy siue sortium missionis exempla: super duobus hircis, Leuit. 16.8. in diuidenda terra, Num. 26.v.54.55.56. & 33.54. & 36.2. units.tr: Examples of divination by lot, or of casting lots: over the two goats, Lev. 16.8; in dividing the land, Num. 26.54, 55, 56; 33.54; 36.2; Deut. 1.38; 31.7; in discovering the theft of the accursed thing, Josh. 7.14; the lot of the sons of Judah and Caleb, 15.1, etc.; of the sons of Joseph, 16.1; of the tribe of Manasseh, 17.1; of the seven tribes, 18.10; of the sons of Aaron, etc., 21.4; in choosing a king for the people of Israel, 1 Sam. 10.20, 21; the lot between Saul and Jonathan, 14.41, 42; the lots of the sons of Aaron, etc., in assigning duties, 1 Chr. 24.5; in appointing singers, etc., 25.8; in appointing the gatekeepers of the temple, 26.13; in slaying the Jews, Esth. 3.7; the lot of the sailors, Jonah 1.7; in dividing Christ's garment, Ps. 22.19; Matt. 27.35; Mark 15.24; John 19.23; for performing the priesthood, Luke 1.9; in choosing Matthias in the place of Judas, Acts 1.26.

units.tr: [A spiritual lot, pertaining to eternal life: Acts 26.18; Eph. 1.11; Col. 1.12.]

units.la: SOSIPATER, Vide SOPATER.
units.tr: SOSIPATER: See SOPATER.

units.la: SOSTHENES synagogæ princeps percutitur, Act. 18.17, Paulo collega adiungitur, 1. Corin. 1.1. (σωσθένης, saluator potens.)
units.tr: SOSTHENES, ruler of the synagogue, is beaten, Acts 18.17; he is joined as a colleague to Paul, 1 Cor. 1.1. (σωσθένης [Sōsthenēs], strong saviour.)

units.la: SPECIES pro eo quod videtur & apparet, non autem reuera est. Ab omni specie mali abstinete. 1. Thes. 5.22. Producat terra animantia in speciebus ipsorum: Genes. 1.24.
units.tr: SPECIES: that which is seen and appears, but is not in fact real. Abstain from every appearance of evil, 1 Thess. 5.22. Let the earth bring forth living creatures in their kinds, Gen. 1.24.

units.la: SPECTACVLVM facti mundo Apostoli, 1 Cor. 4.9. Heb. 10.33.
units.tr: A SPECTACLE: the apostles were made a spectacle to the world, 1 Cor. 4.9; Heb. 10.33.

units.la: SPECTRA, phantasmata, seu visiones, sunt imagines dormientibus vigilantibus obiectæ diuersa specie & aspectu vario, incerto interdum etiam fine. Mat. 14.26. Marc. 6.49. V. Ioh. 6.19. 1 Sam. 28.8. &c.
units.tr: SPECTRES, phantasms or visions, are images presented to those sleeping or waking, of various forms and varying appearance, sometimes also of uncertain end. Matt. 14.26; Mark 6.49. See John 6.19; 1 Sam. 28.8, etc.

units.la: SPECVLATOR, 1. Sam. 4.16.2. Sam. 13.34. & 1.8.v.24.26.27. 2. Reg. 9.17. & 18.20. Speculator Ecclesiasticus & spiritualis, Esai. 52.8.& 56.10. Ierem. 6.17. Ezech. 3.17, & 33.v.2.6.7. Speculator cœlestis, qui maiestatem Christi Dei hominis oculis corporeis aspexit, 2. Petr. 1.16.]
units.tr: SCOUT: 1 Sam. 4.16; 2 Sam. 13.34; 1 Sam. 8.24, 26, 27; 2 Kings 9.17; 18.20. An ecclesiastical and spiritual scout: Isa. 52.8; 56.10; Jer. 6.17; Ezek. 3.17; 33.2, 6, 7. A heavenly scout: he who with his bodily eyes beheld the majesty of Christ, God and man, 2 Pet. 1.16.

units.tr: MIRROR: Paul used the likeness of a mirror in two ways. First

units.la: Primo vocat speculum, 2. Corinth. 3. 18. Filium Dei in carne manifestatum, qui nobis in ipsius Euangelio spectandus proponitur, & Mosi velato opponitur: Et simul notitiam nostram per Euangelium, non per partes, sed semel totam considerans, conferensque cum cognitione ex lege, quod limpidissimum Christi speculum velatae Mosis faciei opponit, 2 Corinth. 3. 18. Secundo, speculum vocat, notitiam Dei quam nunc habemus, illámque cum futura longe perfectiore comparat, 1 Corinth. 13 12, & dicit, nos in hac vita mortali non plene Deum ipsum, qualis est, sed quasi in speculo imaginem eius quandam conspicere. Specula filiarum Sionis peritura, Isa. 3. 23. Vid. Iac. 1. 23.
units.tr: First, he calls it a mirror, 2 Cor. 3.18: the Son of God manifested in the flesh, who is set before us to be beheld in his Gospel, and set over against the veiled face of Moses. At the same time, considering our knowledge gained through the Gospel not in parts but all at once, and comparing it with the knowledge from the law, he sets the most clear mirror of Christ against the veiled face of Moses, 2 Cor. 3.18. Second, he calls the knowledge of God which we now have a mirror, and compares it with the far more perfect knowledge to come, 1 Cor. 13.12, saying that in this mortal life we do not see God himself fully as he is, but see his image in a mirror, as it were. The mirrors of the daughters of Zion, which will perish, Isa. 3.23. See James 1.23.

units.la: SPELUNCAM latronum fecerant Dei donum Iudei, Matth. 21. 13. Speluncae fidelium, Heb. 11. 38. Centum Prophetarum, 1. Reg. 18. 4.
units.tr: The Jews had made God's gift a den of robbers, Matt. 21.13. The caves of the faithful, Heb. 11.38. A hundred prophets, 1 Kings 18.4.

units.tr: HOPE is a gift of God, Rom. 15.13. It is a patient expectation of the full enjoyment of the things which we believe by faith. It comes from faith as a daughter from her mother: Gal. 5.5, "We through the Spirit wait for the hope of righteousness by faith." HOPE is used for faith, Heb. 6.11; 1 Pet. 3.15; and for the thing hoped for, by metonymy, Rom. 8.24; Gal. 5.5; Phil. 1.20; Eph. 1.18; Col. 1.5; Titus 2.13. Hope arises from proof, Rom. 5.4. Hope is like an anchor, Heb. 6.19. It is a gift of God, Rom. 15.13; 2 Thess. 2.16. It is the helmet of salvation, 1 Thess. 5.8. It is necessary for all the godly, Rom. 12.12; Titus 3.7; 1 Pet. 1.3, 15; 1 John 3.3. Hope is to be conceived from past and already known benefits. Examples: Jacob, Gen. 32.10, 11; the Israelites, Deut. 7.18; 20.1; David, 1 Sam. 17.34, 37; Jehoshaphat, 2 Chr. 20.7; David, Ps. 3.8; 22.10; 32.5; 34.7, 8; 71.6, 17; 77.12; 86.7; 142.8; 143.5; Paul, 1 Cor. 1.8, 9; Col. 1.10; Phil. 1.6; 1 Thess. 5.24; 2 Tim. 4.18; Peter, 1 Pet. 1.3.

units.tr: Good hope is to be conceived concerning the godly. Examples: Paul, Rom. 15.14; 2 Thess. 3.4; the apostle, Heb. 6.9. Hope is to be drawn from the Scriptures, Rom. 15.4. Example: David, Ps. 119.42, 74. Hope is to be placed neither in men nor in other creatures: 2 Chr. 16.7; 25.8; Ps. 20.8, 9; 73.28; 118.8, 9; 127.1, 2; 146.3, 5; 147.10; Prov. 11.28; 21.31; 28.25; Isa. 20.6; 30.2; 31.3; 36.6; 40.7; Jer. 7.4; 17.5; 48.7; Ezek. 29.6; Hos. 5.13; 7.11; 9.3; 12.1; Amos 6.1; Mic. 5.10; Hab. 1.17; 2.3; Mark 10.24; 1 Tim. 6.17.
