units.tr: Hope that is deferred is grievous, Prov. 13.12. Hope is to be retained to the end, Heb. 3.6. Hope does not disappoint, Ps. 22.5, 6; 37.9; Rom. 5.5. Hope drives out fear, Ps. 56.4, 5, 12. Hope makes a man blessed, Ps. 2.12; 34.9; 84.13. The hope of the righteous is founded not on temporal things but on God and his promises, Gen. 26.5; Judg. 7.2, 4; 1 Sam. 4.3; 17.45; 22.1; 1 Kings 20.28; 1 Chr. 19.13; 2 Chr. 25.7; 16.7; 20.15, 20; Judith 9.13; Ps. 9.11; 14.6; 22.5, 10; 25.2; 31.2; 40.5; 62.1, etc., 7; 91.2; 15.9, 10, 11; 142.6; 146.5; Prov. 3.5; 22.9; 28.25; 30.9; Isa. 26.4; 29.9; 30.1, 15; 31.1; 36.7; 40.30; Jer. 2.33; 7.4; 9.22; 17.7; 30.8; Lam. 3.24; Ezek. 29.6; Hos. 12.6; Mic. 7.5, 7; Nah. 1.7; Matt. 10.37; 12.21; Rom. 5.2; 8.24; 2 Cor. 5.2; Col. 1.27; 1 Thess. 2.3; 1 Tim. 1.1; 6.17; Heb. 3.6; 1 Pet. 1.13. Christ is the hope of believers, 1 Tim. 1.1. The hope of the pious: see Pii. Examples of hope in God: Hezekiah, 2 Kings 18.5; the sons of Judah, 2 Chr. 13.18; Jehoshaphat, 17.3, 4; 20.13; David, 2 Sam. 22.2; Ps. 3.4; 7.2; 13.5, 6; 16.1; 18.1, 2; 22.10; 25.20; 27.1, 2; 28.8; 11.1, 2; 38.16; 52.10; 55.24; 56.11; 57.1; 69.4; 71.1; 72.10; 91.9; 130.5; 141.5; 142.6; 144.2. The fathers, Ps. 22.5; the house of Israel and Aaron, Ps. 115.9, 10. Job, Job 13.15; 19.25, 26, 27. Jeremiah, Jer. 17.17; Lam. 3.21. Paul, Acts 24.14, 15; 1 Tim. 4.10; Eph. 1.12; Phil. 2.10; 1 Pet. 1.13. See FAITH. The hope of the wicked will vanish, and all things in which they trust are vain: 2 Kings 18.21; Job 8.13; 11.20; 14.19; 20.4; 27.8; Prov. 10.28; 11.7, 23; 25.19; Isa. 28.15, 18; 30.2, 12; 37.11; Jer. 9.12; 17.7. See WICKED. The ground of hope must be given to anyone who asks. See FAITH. ¶ Hope does not make us secure about the certain forgiveness of sins and eternal life, nor does it exclude fear, as the Papists prove by their testimonies. See FEAR and CERTAINTY.

units.la: SPICAS licebat colligere in segete proximi, Deut.23.25. spicas colligit Ruth in agro Booz, unde nutriat Noemi socrum rum suam, Ruth 2.i. &c. Spicas vellunt Apostoli, Matth. 12.1.
units.tr: It was permitted to gather ears of grain in a neighbour's field, Deut. 23.25. Ruth gathers ears in the field of Boaz, by which she feeds her mother-in-law Naomi, Ruth 2.1, etc. The apostles pluck ears, Matt. 12.1.

units.la: NAE appellantur solicitudines huius mundi, diuitiæ & voluptates vitæ mundanæ, Matt. 13.v.7.22. & 19.22. Marc. 4.v.7.18. & 10.22. Luc. 8.v. 7. 14. & 18. 22. spinæ & tribuli propter peccatum Adæ, Genes. 3.18. (spinea corona donatur Christus, Matth. 27.28.29. Vide Prou. 15.19. & 4.31.
units.tr: THORNS are the cares of this world, the riches and pleasures of worldly life, Matt. 13.7, 22; 19.22; Mark 4.7, 18; 10.22; Luke 8.7, 14; 18.22. Thorns and briars came because of Adam's sin, Gen. 3.18. (Christ is given a crown of thorns, Matt. 27.28, 29.) See Prov. 15.19 and 4.31.

units.la: SPIRITVS Primo, pro affectu, impulsu seu afflatu, & animi motu sive bono qui à spiritu sancto proficiscitur, sive diabolo excitatur, Dan. 4. vers. 5.6. & 5 vers. 11.14. Luc. 4.33. & 9.55. Eph. 2.2. unde factum est, ut dona Dei vocentur spiritus, & e contrario, vitia quoque spiritus nomen sortiantur: ut spiritus auaritiæ, superbiæ, furoris, & quæ sequuntur. Secundo, pro animo, Paral. 5.26. Luc. 10.21. Ioan. 13.21. Tertio pro anima immortali, Eccles. 12.7. Matth. 27.50. Ioann. 19.30. Actor. 7.59. 1. Corinth. 2.11. & 6.20. 2. Cor. 7.1. Heb. 12.9. Spiritus, id est anima, in morte Deo commendandus. Exempla: Dauid, Psal. 31.6. Christus, Luc. 23.46. Stephanus, Actor. 7.59. Quarto, spiritus per mimesin, pro commentis & somnis hominum, quibus spiritus præterexitur, 2. Thessal. 2.2. Quinto pro spirituali Dei cultu, Phil. 3.3. sexto, in genere, pro omnibus spiritus S. donis & gratiis spiritualibus, 2. Corinth. 1.4. quibus prædicati Christi vis ac potentia in animis credentium, testibus etiam in fidelibus obsignabatur, Mar. 16.20. Act. 8.15. & 18.2.1. Corinth. 1.v.3.7. & 14.12. Gal. 3.2. Septimo pro Euangelio, 2. Corinth. 3.6. & spirituali Euangelii efficacia, Galat. 3.3. Octauo, pro hominis parte regenerata, Roman. 7.6. Ioann. 3.6. in posteriori parte versus, hoc est pro toto homine spirituali. Spiritus sancti gratia Christo insito, ac proinde in eo renovato, qui & ipse spiritus dicitur, ut natura eius perennis, pura ac immortalis significetur, quamuis adhuc superstes incta carnis, adeo, ut vnus & idem homo fidelis, quandiu ita versatur, & caro & spiritus diuersis respectibus dici possit, ut suo exemplo elegantissime describit Paulus, Roman. 7.21.&c. spiritum quid vocet Paulus, cum opponitur carni, Vide CARO: item cum opponitur literæ, Vide LITERA. Nono, pro altera parte hominis regenerati, vide cet anima, Rom. 8.10. Decimo, pro cœlesti & integra, terrenæ siue peccati iugo mancipatæ naturæ opposita, v.14. Vndecimo, pro mente seu rationis sede, & πνευματικὰ Corinth. 11. & 16. 8. 2 Cor. 2. 12. & 7. v. 1. 13. 1 Thess. 5. 2. Heb. 4. 12. Duodecimo, pro diuina Christi potentia, & efficacia Deitatis in humanitate assumta. Matth. 12. 28. Rom. 1. 4. 1. Tim. 3. 16. Heb. 9. 14. 1 Petr. 3. verf. 18. 19. sic accipiunt nonnulli & 1. Ioannis 5. 8. Decimotertio, pro Deitate Christi, Ioan. 6. 63. in posteriore parte versus, 1 Petr. 2. 18. Decimoquarto, pro iis qui se spiritu prœditos dicunt ad obeundum prophetiæ munus μετωνυμικῶς, 1 Tim. 4. 1. 1. Ioan. 4. Decimoquinto, pro spiritualibus exercitiis, Gal. 6. 8. spiritu mandato oppositus, Ioan. 4. 23. quod carnale dicitur, Heb. 7. 16. in sese videlicet consideratum, & à signo reipsa iunctum.
units.tr: SPIRIT. First, it means an affection, impulse or inspiration, and a movement of the mind, whether good, coming from the Holy Spirit, or stirred up by the devil, Dan. 4.5, 6; 5.11, 14; Luke 4.33; 9.55; Eph. 2.2. Hence it has come about that God's gifts are called spirits, and conversely, vices also take the name of spirit, such as the spirit of covetousness, of pride, of fury, and so on. Second, it means the mind, 1 Chron. 5.26; Luke 10.21; John 13.21. Third, it means the immortal soul, Eccles. 12.7; Matt. 27.50; John 19.30; Acts 7.59; 1 Cor. 2.11; 6.20; 2 Cor. 7.1; Heb. 12.9. The spirit, that is the soul, is to be committed to God at death. Examples: David, Ps. 31.6; Christ, Luke 23.46; Stephen, Acts 7.59. Fourth, by metonymy, spirit means the fancies and dreams of men, by which the Spirit is pretended, 2 Thess. 2.2. Fifth, it means the spiritual worship of God, Phil. 3.3. Sixth, in general, it means all the gifts and spiritual graces of the Holy Spirit, 2 Cor. 1.4, by which the power and might of the preached Christ was also sealed in the hearts of believers, as a witness even among the faithful, Mark 16.20; Acts 8.15; 18.2; 1 Cor. 1.3, 7; 14.12; Gal. 3.2. Seventh, it means the Gospel, 2 Cor. 3.6, and the spiritual efficacy of the Gospel, Gal. 3.3. Eighth, it means the regenerate part of man, Rom. 7.6; John 3.6, in the latter part of the verse, that is, the whole spiritual man. It means the grace of the Holy Spirit implanted in Christ, and therefore renewed in him, who is himself also called spirit, so that his nature is signified as enduring, pure and immortal, although still in the flesh of the body; so that one and the same faithful man, as long as he is so disposed, can be called both flesh and spirit under different aspects, as Paul describes most elegantly by his own example, Rom. 7.21ff. For what Paul calls spirit when it is opposed to flesh, see FLESH; likewise when it is opposed to letter, see LETTER. Ninth, it means the other part of the regenerate man, that is, the soul, Rom. 8.10. Tenth, it means the heavenly and whole nature, opposed to the earthly nature, or the nature enslaved to the yoke of sin, v. 14. Eleventh, it means the mind or seat of reason, and spiritual things [πνευματικὰ], 1 Cor. 11 and 16; 2 Cor. 2.12; 7.1, 13; 1 Thess. 5.2; Heb. 4.12. Twelfth, it means the divine power of Christ and the efficacy of the Godhead in the assumed humanity, Matt. 12.28; Rom. 1.4; 1 Tim. 3.16; Heb. 9.14; 1 Pet. 3.18, 19. Some also take 1 John 5.8 in this sense. Thirteenth, it means the Godhead of Christ, John 6.63, in the latter part of the verse; 1 Pet. 2.18. Fourteenth, it means those who say they are endowed with the Spirit to perform the office of prophecy, by metonymy [μετωνυμικῶς], 1 Tim. 4.1; 1 John 4. Fifteenth, it means spiritual exercises, Gal. 6.8, opposed to the command of the Spirit, John 4.23, which is called carnal, Heb. 7.16, namely when considered in itself and joined by the sign to the thing itself.

units.la: Spiritus adoptionis, Rom. 8. 15. spiritus adoptionis qui vocetur à Paulo. Vide Servitutis spiritus. Spiritus compunctionis, 11. 8. dæmonij aut dæmoniacus, pro Diabolus, Hebraismus, Luc. 4. 33. dilectionis, 2 Tim. 1. 7. erroris. ibidem Filij, Gal. 4. 6.
units.tr: The spirit of adoption, Rom. 8.15. It is called the spirit of adoption by Paul. See spirit of bondage. The spirit of compunction, Zech. 12.10. A demon, or demoniac, for the devil, a Hebraism, Luke 4.33. Of love, 2 Tim. 1.7. Of error, ibid. Of sons, Gal. 4.6.

units.la: Dicitur autem spiritus sancti peculiariter Filij spiritus, cùm & patris & filij sit spiritus eo quòd per eum obsignatur nostra in Christum adoptio. Spiritus ex fide, Galat. 4. 5. dicitur spiritus, qui fidem generat, seu qui fidelibus datur. Spiritus gratiæ, Hebr. 10. 29. gratiæ & precum, Zach. 12. 10. infirmitatis, pro morbo Satana inflicto, Luc. 13. 11. vt explicatur vers. 16. sapientiæ intelligentiæ, consilij, fortitudinis, scientiæ & timoris. Isa. 11. 2. spiritus sapientiæ, pro dono sapientiæ per spiritum sanctum infuso, Eph. 1. 17. spiritus lenitatis, pro spiritu leniter affecto, Hebraismus, 1 Cor. 5. 2. spiritus sanctificationis, Roman. 1. 4. dicitur autem sic spiritus sanctus, aut potius spiritus sancti virtus, qua perfusa est Ecclesia, cùm iam Christus in cœlos ascendisset, ex quo optime videlicet intelligitur, Christum non modò non esse mortuum, sed plane Deum esse cum Patre regnante. At tertiò altera Christi natura, nempe diuina, quod antithesis carnis, qua humana natura significatur, & spiritus particulare videtur.
units.tr: The Spirit of the Holy Spirit is called peculiarly the Spirit of the Son, since he is the Spirit both of the Father and of the Son, because through him our adoption in Christ is sealed. The spirit of faith, Gal. 4.5, is the Spirit who begets faith, or who is given to believers. The spirit of grace, Heb. 10.29; of grace and supplications, Zech. 12.10; of infirmity, for the sickness inflicted by Satan, Luke 13.11, as is explained in v. 16; of wisdom, understanding, counsel, strength, knowledge and fear, Isa. 11.2. The spirit of wisdom, for the gift of wisdom poured into us through the Holy Spirit, Eph. 1.17. The spirit of gentleness, for a spirit gently disposed, a Hebraism, 1 Cor. 4.21. The spirit of sanctification, Rom. 1.4. The Holy Spirit, or rather the power of the Holy Spirit, is called thus, by which the Church was endowed when Christ had already ascended into heaven. From this it is very clearly understood that Christ is not only not dead, but plainly is God, reigning with the Father. But thirdly, the other nature of Christ, namely the divine, which is the antithesis of the flesh, by which the human nature is signified, seems to be a particular spirit.

units.la: Spiritus seruitutis, Rom. 8. 15. Vide Servitus: sobrietatis, 1 Timoth. 1. 7. promissionis, Ephes. 1. 13. sic dicitur, quod non adfert legis & seruitutis terrorem, sed promissionem gratuitæ adoptionis suis donis obsignat in credentium animis. Spiritus mundi, Cor. 1. 2. 12. sic dictus à Paulo, qui d... [?]eat quæ mundus curat, & quorum capaces sunt homi-nes quadam naturæ sponte. Prophetarum, hoc est, pro doctrina quam adferunt Prophetæ spiritu Dei afflati, quia in sese verax est, vtpote Deus æternus, quàm ab effectu, quòd veritatem inspiret, Ioan.16.13. Prophetæ etiam & doctores vocantur spiritus veritatis, 1 Ioan.4.6. quasi dicat, spiritus veridici, sicut contrà spiritus erroris, vocantur spiritus errantes, & alios in errorem adducen-tes. Spiritus virtutis, 2 Tim.1.7. vitæ, pro, vita animalis Apoc.11.11.
units.tr: The spirit of bondage, Rom. 8.15. See Bondage. Of sobriety, 2 Tim. 1.7. Of promise, Eph. 1.13. It is so called because it does not bring the terror of the law and of bondage, but seals the promise of gratuitous adoption by its gifts in the minds of believers. The spirit of the world, 1 Cor. 2.12, so called by Paul, who despises what the world cares for and what men by a certain natural impulse are capable of. Of the prophets: that is, for the teaching which the prophets, inspired by the Spirit of God, bring. It is named by its effect (that it inspires truth) rather than by its own nature, since it is true in itself as the eternal God, John 16.13. The prophets and teachers are also called spirits of truth, 1 John 4.6, as if to say, spirits speaking truth, just as on the contrary spirits of error are called wandering spirits, leading others into error. Spirit of power, 2 Tim. 1.7. Of life, for animal life, Rev. 11.11.

units.la: SPIRITVS, numero multitudinis, pro interioribus animi conceptionibus & motibus, 1 Cor.12.10. spiritus septem Dei maiestati adiunguntur quasi stipatores, Apo.1.4. non quasi illos Ioannes vlla ex parte, vel Deo exæquet, vel cum Christo conferat: sicut etiam Paulus testes vnà citat Deum, Christum & Angelos, 1 Rim.5.21. Nam quòd septem hos spiritus nonnulli pro spiritu sancto accepe-runt, cuius septiformis (vt loquuntur) sit gratia, quibus-dam minimè placet: & refellunt illam interpretationem ex Apoc.5.6. vbi iidem spiritus, agni cornua & oculi, hoc est ministri dicuntur.
units.tr: SPIRIT, in the plural, means the inward conceptions and movements of the mind, 1 Cor. 12.10. The seven spirits are joined to the majesty of God as attendants, Rev. 1.4. John does not in any way make them equal to God or compare them with Christ, just as Paul also cites God, Christ and the angels together, 1 Tim. 5.21. For some have taken these seven spirits to be the Holy Spirit, whose grace is (as they say) sevenfold; this interpretation does not please some at all, and they refute it from Rev. 5.6, where the same spirits are called the horns and eyes of the Lamb, that is, ministers.

units.la: SPIRITVS sanctus: Spiritus sanctus pro spiritualibus eius donis [illegible, ~12 letters], Luc.2.25. Ioan.7.39. Actor.8.v.15.17. & 10.4 & 11.15. & 15.8. & 19.v.2 6.1.Cor.14.12. pro vi & efficacia Christi, quam per spiritum sanctum exerit in nobis viuificandis & sanctificandis, Matt.3.11. spiritus S. pro tertia in sancta Triade persona, qui vnà cum Patre & Filio, essentia & Deitate idem est: Deus disertè appellatur, Esaiæ 6.v.8.9. Actor.28.v.25.26. & 5.v.3.4.1 Cor.3.16. & 6.19. Ioan.2 Cor.6.16.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit: the Holy Spirit, for his spiritual gifts [illegible], Luke 2.25; John 7.39; Acts 8.15, 17; 10.4; 11.15; 15.8; 19.2, 6; 1 Cor. 14.12. For the power and efficacy of Christ, which he exerts through the Holy Spirit in quickening and sanctifying us, Matt. 3.11. The Holy Spirit, for the third person in the holy Trinity, who together with the Father and the Son is the same in essence and Godhead. He is expressly called God, Isa. 6.8, 9; Acts 28.25, 26; 5.3, 4; 1 Cor. 3.16; 6.19; 2 Cor. 6.16.

units.la: Deus probatur: quia æternus est, Gen.1.2. Heb.9.14. quia cum in solius Dei nomen sit baptizandum, (V. BAPTIZARE in nomen) in spiritus S. nomen baptizare iubemur, Matt.28.19. Mar.16.15. quia cùm nemo sit bonus nisi Deus, Matt.19.17. Marc.10.18. Lucæ 18.19. Spiritus bonus dicitur, Ps.143.10. quia Ecclesiæ præest, dat illis Apostolos & doctores, omniúmque bonorum fons atq. autor est, Esa.48.16. Act.13.2. & 20.28. Rom.15.13.1 Cor.12.v.6.11. quia illa sua bona pro liberrima sua voluntate omnibus prout vult dividit, & communicat, 1 Cor. 12. v.4 5.7.8.9.10. 11.vbi etiam manifestè à suis donis discernitur, quia creator est, Iob.26.13.&33.4.Pf.33.6.&vitā in rebusquibus libet creat Psal.104. 30. quia arcanæ Dei patris voluntatis conscius 1.Cor.2.v.10 11. quia cùm omnis cōsolationis autorDeus fit,Rom.15.5.2. Corinth. 1.3. spiritus sanctus consolatur corda credentium,unde & consolator appellatur,Ioann 14. v.16.26. & 15.26. & 16.7.quia cum Patre & Filio conjungitur. Matthæi.28.19.2. Corinth.13.13.quia cum nisi a Deo doceantur fideles intrinsecus,Esa.54.13. Ioann 6.45. spiritus sanctus docere dicitur, Luc.12.12,Ioann.14 26.& 16.13.1.Ioan.2.27. quia Dominus dicitur & Deus, Corinth.12. ver.4.5. Atqui si donum tantum aut motus esset,Dominus minime diceretur: motus enim & donum Dominus appellari non potest. quia cùm solus Iehovah verus Deus eduxerit populum ex Ægypto, Exod.20. Spiritus sanctus ductor populi ex AEgypto dicitur,Esai 63.14. quia mouet corda intrinsecus vt oremus,Rom. 26. quia cùm liberos facere sit Dei opus,Spiritus sancti liberos facit,2.Corinth.3.17. quia cùm solius Dei sit iustificare. Roman.4. 5. spiritus sanctus iustificare dicitur, Corinth.6 11. quia nostræ regenerationis tanquam pars est.Ioan.3.ver.6.8.quia peccatum in eum admissum,blasphemia,id est, impium in diuinitatem delictum dicitur Matthæi.12.31. quia cùm populi Israelitici rebellio cōtra solum verum & æternum Deum facta fuisse legatur passim in scriptura populus Israeliticus in Spiritum sanctum rebellis fuisse dicitur, Psalm.78. 40. Esa. 63. 10 quia cum sanctificare sit solius Dei proprium,spiritus S.dicitur spiritus sanctificationis,id est, sanctificans, Rom.1.4.quia omnis sapientia & loquendi facultas sit solius veri Dei ac proinde ab ipso petenda, Exodi. 4.11.Iac.1.v.5.17.Spiritus S.& sapientiam & loquendi facultatem conferre citur,Matt.10.v.19.20. Marc.13.11. Luc.12 v.14.15.Ioan 14.26.Act.2.4.1. Corinth.2.13. & 12,8. quia cùm præcipitur ne Deum tentemus, Deut.6.16. Matth.4.7.ne spiritus S.tentetur,iubetur, Act. 5.9. sicut nec Christus tentandus est,1.Corinth.10.9. quia cum solius Dei verbum sit,audiendum,& in præceptis ipsius ambulandum, Ezech.20.v.19.Luc.11.28 verba spiritus S.audienda præcipiuntur, poc.2.v.7.17.29. quia Christus virtute spiritus Dei edidit miracula dicitur,Roman.5.19.quia veritas est,1.Ioan 5.6.non secus ac Filius, Ioan.14.6.eiusdem ergo essent cum Filio.quia verba illa quæ prophetæ palam Deo exc cituum attribuunt, Leu.26 v.12.13. Psal.95.v.7.8.Esa.6.v. 7.9. spiritui S. attribuuntur, Act.28.v.25.26.1.Cor.3.16.&6 19 2.Cor.9.16.Hebr.3.v.7.8.9.
units.tr: That God he is, is proved: because he is eternal, Gen. 1.2; Heb. 9.14. Because, although baptism is to be performed in the name of God alone (see BAPTIZE INTO THE NAME), we are commanded to baptize in the name of the Holy Spirit, Matt. 28.19; Mark 16.15. Because, since no one is good but God, Matt. 19.17; Mark 10.18; Luke 18.19, he is called good, Ps. 143.10. Because he presides over the Church, gives it apostles and teachers, and is the fountain and author of all good things, Isa. 48.16; Acts 13.2; 20.28; Rom. 15.13; 1 Cor. 12.6, 11. Because he divides and communicates his good things to all as he wills, by his most free will, 1 Cor. 12.4, 5, 7–11, where he is also plainly distinguished from his gifts. Because he is the creator, Job 26.13; 33.4; Ps. 33.6; and he creates life in whatever things he pleases, Ps. 104.30. Because he is conscious of the secret will of God the Father, 1 Cor. 2.10, 11. Because, since God is the author of all consolation, Rom. 15.5; 2 Cor. 1.3, the Holy Spirit comforts the hearts of believers, whence he is also called the Comforter, John 14.16, 26; 15.26; 16.7. Because he is joined with the Father and the Son, Matt. 28.19; 2 Cor. 13.13. Because, unless the faithful are taught inwardly by God, Isa. 54.13; John 6.45, the Holy Spirit is said to teach, Luke 12.12; John 14.26; 16.13; 1 John 2.27. Because the Lord is called also God, 1 Cor. 12.4, 5. And yet if he were only a gift or a motion, he would by no means be called Lord, for a motion or a gift cannot be called Lord. Because, since only Jehovah, the true God, led the people out of Egypt, Exod. 20, the Holy Spirit is called the leader of the people out of Egypt, Isa. 63.14. Because he moves hearts inwardly that we may pray, Rom. 8.26. Because, since making free is the work of God, the Holy Spirit makes free, 2 Cor. 3.17. Because, since justifying belongs to God alone, Rom. 4.5, the Holy Spirit is said to justify, 1 Cor. 6.11. Because he is, as it were, a part of our regeneration, John 3.6, 8. Because sin committed against him is called blasphemy, that is, an impious offence against the divinity, Matt. 12.31. Because, since the rebellion of the Israelite people against the only true and eternal God is recorded everywhere in Scripture, the Israelite people are said to have rebelled against the Holy Spirit, Ps. 78.40; Isa. 63.10. Because, since sanctifying is the proper work of God alone, the Holy Spirit is called the Spirit of sanctification, that is, sanctifying, Rom. 1.4. Because all wisdom and the faculty of speech belong to the true God alone and must therefore be sought from him, Exod. 4.11; James 1.5, 17, the Holy Spirit is said to confer both wisdom and the faculty of speech, Matt. 10.19, 20; Mark 13.11; Luke 12.11, 12; John 14.26; Acts 2.4; 1 Cor. 2.13; 12.8. Because, when we are commanded not to tempt God, Deut. 6.16; Matt. 4.7, the Holy Spirit is likewise commanded not to be tempted, Acts 5.9, just as Christ himself is not to be tempted, 1 Cor. 10.9. Because, since it is the word of God alone that is to be heard and that we are to walk in his precepts, Ezek. 20.19; Luke 11.28, the words of the Holy Spirit are commanded to be heard, Rev. 2.7, 17, 29. Because Christ is said to have performed miracles by the power of the Spirit of God, Rom. 15.19. Because he is the truth, 1 John 5.6, no differently from the Son, John 14.6; therefore he would be of the same substance as the Son. Because those words which the prophets openly attribute to God, Lev. 26.12, 13; Ps. 95.7, 8; Isa. 6.7, 9, are attributed to the Holy Spirit, Acts 28.25, 26; 1 Cor. 3.16; 6.19; 2 Cor. 6.16; Heb. 3.7, 8, 9.

units.la: Quòd autem creatura non sit, probatur: quia omnis creatura vanitati subiecta est, Roman.8.20.ergo idem & de spiritu S. dicendum foret, si creatura esset, quod est ατον prorsus & absurdum, cùm vbi spiritus, ibi sit libertas.2. Corinth.3.17.& spiritus S. sit æternus, Hebr.9.14. quia cùm ab increato procedat, Ioan. 15.26. increatus vt sit, necesse est. Quòd autem spiritus S. vltimo loco ponitur, Mat.28.19.2. Corint. 13.13. neminem conturbet, nam & primo loco positus legitur, 1. Corinth.12.4. Quia etiam profunditates Dei inuestigat, 1. Corinth.2.10. Atqui id creaturæ non competit. quia habitat in nobis. Roman.8.9 1.Cor.3.16. & 6.19 2. Cor. 6.16.2. Timot. 1.14. quod est solius veri Dei proprium, Leu.26.12.2. Cor.16. quia filios Dei facit eos in quibus habitat, Rom.8.14. quod creatura efficere non potest. quia viuificat, Rom.8.12. atqui viuificare nulla creatura potest. quia Christum in desertum & in Galilæam abduxit, Lucæ.4. ver.1,14. atqui Christus vn genitus Dei filius, non fuit ita imbecillis, vt creati spiritus virtute indigeret. quia renascimur per spiritum S.Io 3 5.1.Per.1.23. quod creaturæ tribui non potest.
units.tr: That the Spirit is not a creature is proved thus: because every creature is subject to vanity, Rom. 8:20. If the Spirit were a creature, the same would have to be said of him, which is utterly absurd, since where the Spirit is, there is liberty, 2 Cor. 3:17. The Spirit is also eternal, Heb. 9:14. Because, since he proceeds from the uncreated one, John 15:26, he must himself be uncreated. That the Spirit is placed last, Matt. 28:19; 2 Cor. 13:13, should disturb no one, for he is also read as placed first, 1 Cor. 12:4. Because he searches even the depths of God, 1 Cor. 2:10, which does not belong to a creature. Because he dwells in us, Rom. 8:9; 1 Cor. 3:16; 6:19; 2 Cor. 6:16; 2 Tim. 1:14, which is the proper property of the one true God alone, Lev. 26:12; 2 Cor. 6:16. Because he makes sons of God those in whom he dwells, Rom. 8:14, which a creature cannot do. Because he quickens, Rom. 8:12, and no creature can quicken. Because he led Christ into the desert and into Galilee, Luke 4:1, 14; but Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, was not so weak that he needed the power of a created spirit. Because we are born again through the Spirit, John 3:5; 1 Pet. 1:23, which cannot be attributed to a creature.

units.la: Quòd aut motus aut donum tantum non sit, sed vera hypostasis seu persona, probatur à proprietatibus personæ subsistenti competentibus: quia tribuitur illi vox, Act.13.2. Apocal. 2.ver.7.17.29. libera voluntas, 1. Corinth.12.11.vbi etiam manifestè distinguitur à suis donis, v.4.5.6. &c. Vide SPIRITVS sancti personæ propria attributa.
units.tr: Because a voice is attributed to him, Acts 13:2; Rev. 2:7, 17, 29, and free will, 1 Cor. 12:11, where he is also clearly distinguished from his gifts, vv. 4–6, etc. That he is not merely a motion or a gift but a true hypostasis or person is proved from the properties that belong to a subsisting person. See SPIRIT, the proper attributes of the person of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: SPIRITVS sanctus aquæ nomine significatus, Esaiæ.44.3. Ioan.3.5. Heb.10.22. Vide AQVAE) & ignis, Matth.3.11. ab ipsius in nobis effectu Spiritus sanctus Arrhabo, 2. Corinth.1.22.&55. Gal.4.6. Ephes.1.v.13 14. quia in cordibus nostris futuræ hæreditatis certitudinem suo testimonio stabilit, confirmat & obsignat, Rom.8.15. Spiritus sanctus, diuinorum donorum distributor, 1. Corinth.12.11. Digitus Dei, Luc.11.20. ipiorum doctor, Matth.10.20. Ioan.14.26. Actor. 6.10. 1. Corinth. 2. 12.1. Ioan. 2.27. pio-rum dux, Rom.8.9. semen dicitur, 1. Ioan.3.9. ab effectu, quòd eius virtute tanquam ex semine quodam noui homines efficiamur, id est, corruptæ nostræ qualitates instaurentur per Christum, cui per fidem sumus coniuncti, vt peccato mortui, viuamus Deo. Sigillum, 2 Corint.1.21. Eph.4.30 Παρόχυντος quod & Christo tribuitur, sed diuersa prorsus quam Spiritu S. ratione. V. Παράκλητος, Testis Christi, Ioan.15.26.1 Ioan.5.7. virtus ex alto, Luc.24.49. vnctio, 1 Ioan.2.v.20.27.
units.tr: The Holy Spirit is signified by the name of water, Isa. 44:3; John 3:5; Heb. 10:22 (see WATER), and of fire, Matt. 3:11. From his effect in us, the Holy Spirit is a pledge, 2 Cor. 1:22; 5:5; Gal. 4:6; Eph. 1:13–14, because he establishes, confirms and seals in our hearts the certainty of the future inheritance by his testimony, Rom. 8:15. He is the distributor of divine gifts, 1 Cor. 12:11; the finger of God, Luke 11:20; the teacher of the pious, Matt. 10:20; John 14:26; Acts 6:10; 1 Cor. 2:12; 1 John 2:27; the leader of the pious, Rom. 8:9. He is called seed, 1 John 3:9, from his effect: by his power we are made new men, as if from a certain seed, that is, our corrupt qualities are restored through Christ, to whom we are joined by faith, so that, dead to sin, we live to God. He is a seal, 2 Cor. 1:21; Eph. 4:30. He is the Paraclete, a title also given to Christ, but in a completely different way from the Holy Spirit. See PARACLETE. He is the witness of Christ, John 15:26; 1 John 5:7; the power from on high, Luke 24:49; and the anointing, 1 John 2:20, 27.

units.la: <bl>SPIRITVS</bl> sanctus minime contristandus, Eph.4.30. Spiritus S. Apostolis datus, Ioan. 20. 22. Act.2.v.3.4.33. in fideles copiosè effusus est, Tit 3.6. Spiritus (i. lumen & afflatus Dei in mentibus refulgens) minimè extinguendus, 1 Thess.5.19. Sed dicat quis: Cum is in electis nunquam extinguatur, frustra id ab Apostolo praecipi videtur. Minime vero, imo ideo non extinguitur in electis, quia eum fouent, vt autem foueant, ittiusmodi exhortationib. adducuntur. Nam qui constituit Spiritum in electis suis nunquam extinguere, simul patefecit quibus rationibus illum velit fouere, suo videlicet in pietate progressu. Petos Dauidis locutus est, 2 Sam.23.2. Actor.1.16. in Prophetis locutus dicitur, 28.25. Heb.3.7. & 10.15. 1 Petr.1.11.2 Petr.1.21. Spiritus Sanctus, Ecclesiae promissus, Esa.44.v.13.E. zech. 11.19. & 36.ver.26.27.& 39.29. Ioel.2.28. Zach.2.10 Matth.3.11. Luc.11.13.& 24.49. Ioan.7.39. & 14.v.16.26.8 15.26.& 16.7. Act.1.4.& 2.17. Spiritus sanctus non tentandus. 5.9. quomodo agnoscitur 1 Iohan.4.2. super Christum descendit, Matt.3.16. Ioan.1. verfic.32.33. in piis habitat, Roman.8.9. 1 Corin.3.16. Ephes.3.16. 2 Timot.1.14. Ioann. 3.24.& 4.13 interpellat pro nobis, Roman.8.26. non quòd apud Patrem vel Filium ipse sit Mediator, sed quia nos ad preces instigat, atque adeò velut verba & suspiria nobis intus dictat. Sic dicitur clamare Galat. 4.6. quoniam facit ipse vt clamemus, quemadmodum explicatur Rom.8.15. Spiritus vivificat, Ioan. 6.63.
units.tr: <bl>SPIRIT</bl>: the Holy Spirit is by no means to be grieved, Eph. 4:30. The Holy Spirit was given to the apostles, John 20:22; Acts 2:3, 4, 33, and poured out abundantly upon the faithful, Titus 3:6. The Spirit (that is, the light and breath of God shining in minds) is by no means to be extinguished, 1 Thess. 5:19. But someone may say: since he is never extinguished in the elect, it seems in vain for the Apostle to command this. Not at all; rather he is not extinguished in the elect precisely because they foster him, and to foster him they are urged by exhortations of this kind. For he who determined that he would never extinguish the Spirit in his elect has at the same time revealed by what means he wishes him to be fostered, namely by progress in piety. He spoke through the mouth of David, 2 Sam. 23:2; Acts 1:16; he is said to have spoken through the prophets, Acts 28:25; Heb. 3:7 and 10:15; 1 Pet. 1:11; 2 Pet. 1:21. The Holy Spirit was promised to the Church, Isa. 44:3; Ezek. 11:19; 36:26–27; 39:29; Joel 2:28; Zech. 2:10; Matt. 3:11; Luke 11:13; 24:49; John 7:39; 14:16, 26; 15:26; 16:7; Acts 1:4; 2:17. The Holy Spirit is not to be tempted, Acts 5:9. He is recognised by this, 1 John 4:2. He descended upon Christ, Matt. 3:16; John 1:32–33. He dwells in the pious, Rom. 8:9; 1 Cor. 3:16; Eph. 3:16; 2 Tim. 1:14; John 3:24; 4:13. He intercedes for us, Rom. 8:26, not because he is himself a mediator with the Father or the Son, but because he stirs us up to prayer, and so, as it were, dictates words and sighs within us. So he is said to cry out, Gal. 4:6, because he himself makes us cry out, as Rom. 8:15 explains. The Spirit gives life, John 6:63.

Iac.1.25.& 4.5.1.Ioan.2.27. 5.8.Spiritus fructus, Galat.5.22. Spiritus nouitas, Rom.6.Spiritus prudentia,8.6.Spiritus cum carne pugna, Galat.5.17.Spiritus sancti virtus,V.SPIRITVS Deus & Dns. Spiritus vis. Spiritus vnitas seruanda, Ephes.4.vers.1.3.
units.tr: <bl>SPIRIT</bl>: the proper attributes of the person of the Holy Spirit: John 15:26; 16:7, 8, 13, 14; 1 Cor. 12:3, 4; 2 Cor. 1:21, 22; 13:13; Eph. 1:13, 14; 1 Thess. 5:19; Titus 3:5; James 1:25; 4:5; 1 John 2:27; 5:8. The fruit of the Spirit, Gal. 5:22. The newness of the Spirit, Rom. 6. The prudence of the Spirit, Rom. 8:6. The struggle of the Spirit with the flesh, Gal. 5:17. The power of the Holy Spirit. See SPIRIT: God and Lord; the power of the Spirit. The unity of the Spirit is to be kept, Eph. 4:1, 3.

units.la: <bl>SPIRITV</bl> ambulare, Gal.5.16. IRITVS immundus, Vide SATAN. Spiritus mutus & surdus,(V.MVTVS spiritus)ab effectu, pro eo qui mutum & surdum reddit, Marci 9. v.17.25. Spiritus probandi sunt, Ioan.4.1.1 Corint. 14.29. 1 Thess.5.21.
units.tr: <bl>SPIRIT</bl>: to walk in the Spirit, Gal. 5:16. Unclean spirit: see SATAN. Dumb and deaf spirit (see DUMB SPIRIT), named from its effect, since it makes a man dumb and deaf, Mark 9:17, 25. Spirits are to be tested, John 4:1; 1 Cor. 14:29; 1 Thess. 5:21.

units.la: SPIRITVS significationes varias sequentibus sectionibus includere visum est, quae praecedentium erunt epitome.
units.tr: It has seemed good to set out the various meanings of SPIRIT in the following sections, which will be an epitome of what has gone before.

units.la: 1. Spiritus igitur, essentialiter acceptus, Deus est, Pater, filius, Spiritus S. incorporeus, spiritualis essentiae, indivisibilis, simplex, Ioann.4.24. Spiritus, personaliter acceptus, est tertia persona in essentia divina, Spiritus Domini & Dei, nempe Patris & filij, verus etiam & unus cum utroque Deus aeternus, consubstantialis, Omnipotens &c.
units.tr: 1. Spirit, taken essentially, is God: Father, Son and Holy Spirit; incorporeal, of spiritual essence, indivisible, simple, John 4:24. Spirit, taken personally, is the third person in the divine essence, the Spirit of the Lord and of God, namely of the Father and of the Son, true and one God with each, eternal, consubstantial, almighty, etc.

units.la: 2. Spiritus, Divina Christi natura, Roman.1.4. 1 Corint. 15. 45. 1 Timoth. 3. 16. 1 Petr. 3. 18. Spiritus mysticus, 1 Corinth. 6. 17. Ephes. 4. 4. Spiritus, sapientia in Deo, Malach.2.15. Spiritus, affectus Deo humanitus tributi, Exod.15.8.2 Samu. 22.16. Iob.4.9. & 15.30. Psalm.33.6. Esai. 30.28.
units.tr: 2. Spirit: the divine nature of Christ, Rom. 1:4; 1 Cor. 15:45; 1 Tim. 3:16; 1 Pet. 3:18. Spirit, mystical, 1 Cor. 6:17; Eph. 4:4. Spirit: wisdom in God, Mal. 2:15. Spirit: affection attributed to God in human terms, Exod. 15:8; 2 Sam. 22:16; Job 4:9; 15:30; Ps. 33:6; Isa. 30:28.

units.la: 3. Spiritus Deorum, eximius & divinus quidam Spiritus, mortali homini concessus, Dan. 4.v.5.8.9.18 & 5.ver. 11.14. Spiritus: is qui Spiritus S. dono peculiari se praeditum esse dicit, 1 Ioann. 4.v.1.2.5 6. Spiritus, Organum per quod Spiritus S. vitam infundit & operatur in electis Dei Ioan. 5.63, spiritus, pars regenerationi electis, Rom. 8. v.6.9.10. Galat.5.17.
units.tr: 3. Spirits of gods: an extraordinary and divine sort of spirit granted to a mortal man, Dan. 4:5, 8, 9, 18; 5:11, 14. Spirit: one who says he is endowed with a special gift of the Holy Spirit, 1 John 4:1, 2, 5, 6. Spirit: the instrument through which the Holy Spirit pours in life and works in the elect of God, John 6:63. Spirit: the part of the elect that is regenerated, Rom. 8:6, 9, 10; Gal. 5:17.

units.la: 4. Spiritus, pietatis studium à spiritu S. profectum: Galat. 1.8. revelatio à spiritu S. prolata, 2 Thessal.2.2. spirituale donum, 1 Cor.14.12. Is qui adoptionis gratia donatus est, Ioan.3.6. spiritualis modus, legali & externo ritui opposit us, Ioann.4.23.24. Phil.3.3. spiritualis ratio & vis fidei, quae divinae promissioni immittitur, Galat.4.29. Verbum Christi, Esa.11.v.4. 2.Thess.2.8.
units.tr: 4. Spirit: zeal for piety arising from the Holy Spirit, Gal. 1:8. A revelation brought forth by the Holy Spirit, 2 Thess. 2:2. A spiritual gift, 1 Cor. 14:12. One who has been granted the grace of adoption, John 3:6. A spiritual mode, opposed to the legal and external rite, John 4:23, 24; Phil. 3:3. The spiritual reason and power of faith, which is directed to the divine promise, Gal. 4:29. The word of Christ, Isa. 11:4; 2 Thess. 2:8.

units.la: 5. Spiritus, Angeli boni, Iob.4.15. Act.23.9. Heb.1.14. Angeli mali, Iudi.9.23.1 Sam.16.14.1 Regum,22.v.21.22. Matth.16.Eph.2.2. Apoc.16.13. & 18.2.
units.tr: 5. Spirits: good angels, Job 4:15; Acts 23:9; Heb. 1:14. Evil angels, Judg. 9:23; 1 Sam. 16:14; 1 Kings 22:21, 22; Matt. 16; Eph. 2:2; Rev. 16:13; 18:2.

units.la: 6. Spiritus, Anima rationalis & immortalis, Psalm 31. Zach.12.1 Matth.27.50. Act.23.8. 1 Cor.5.5. 1 Petr.3.19. Animus humanus, in quo sedes voluntatis & affectuum, Genes.45.27. Luc.1.47. Ioann.11.33. Actor.17.16.1
units.tr: 6. Spirit: the rational and immortal soul, Ps. 31; Zech. 12:1; Matt. 27:50; Acts 23:8; 1 Cor. 5:5; 1 Pet. 3:19. Human mind, in which is the seat of the will and the affections, Gen. 45:27; Luke 1:47; John 11:33; Acts 17:16; 2 Cor. 7:13; 1 Pet. 3:4.

units.la: 2 Corinth.7.13.1 Petr.3.4.Affectus & spirituales, boni vel mali, Num.5.14. Ose.4.12. Luc.9.55. Rom.11.8.Spiritus vitalis, in animantibus halitus,Genes.6.17. Psalm.78.39. & 104.29. Apocalyp.11.11. & 13.15.
units.tr: Affections and spiritual dispositions, good or bad, Num. 5:14; Hos. 4:12; Luke 9:55; Rom. 11:8. The vital spirit, the breath in living things, Gen. 6:17; Ps. 78:39; 104:29; Rev. 11:11; 13:15.

units.la: 7. Spiritus, visio in mente,Ezech.37.1. Apocalyp.1.10 & 4.2.& 17.3. & 21.10. Spiritus, Creatura omnis Spiritu vitali & habitu praedita, Psalm.150.6.Spiritus mundi 1 Corinth.2.12. spiritus erroris, 1 Timoth.4.1.spiritus Spectrum,Luc.24.v.37.39. Concentus, strepitus, Ezech.26.13.
units.tr: 7. Spirit: a vision in the mind, Ezek. 37:1; Rev. 1:10; 4:2; 17:3; 21:10. Spirit: every creature endowed with a vital spirit and disposition, Ps. 150:6. The spirit of the world, 1 Cor. 2:12. Spirit of error, 1 Tim. 4:1. Spirit, a ghost or apparition, Luke 24:37, 39. Sound, noise, Ezek. 26:13.

units.la: 8. Spiritus Oris,Rex, cuius beneficio subditi respirare & vitam trahere videntur, Thren.4.20.spiritus ventus Genes.8.1. Psalm.104 4.&147.18. spiritus, afflictio gravis, Psalm.55.9. Ezech.13.13. Spiritus, Vanitas, Mich 2.11.
units.tr: 8. Spirit of the mouth: a king by whose benefit his subjects seem to breathe and draw life, Lam. 4:20. Spirit: wind, Gen. 8:1; Ps. 104:4; 147:18. Spirit: heavy affliction, Ps. 55:9; Ezek. 13:13. Spirit: vanity, Mic. 2:11.

units.la: SPIRITVALES qui,1 Cor.2.15.Gal.6.1.Domus,1 Petr.2.5. Oblatio. v.5.
units.tr: SPIRITUAL, who, 1 Cor. 2:15; Gal. 6:1. House, 1 Pet. 2:5. Offering, v. 5.

units.la: SPOLIA ex aequo diuidenda,Num.31.27. Deut.20.14.spolia renuit Abraham,Gen.14.23. (Vide PRAEDA ex aequo diuidenda:&, RAPINAE ac spoliationis exempla.) 1 Sam.30.24.
units.tr: SPOILS to be divided equally, Num. 31:27; Deut. 20:14. Abraham refused spoils, Gen. 14:23. (See PLUNDER to be divided equally, and examples of robbery and spoliation.) 1 Sam. 30:24.

units.la: SPONDERE alieno nomine leuiter,temerarium, Prou.6.1. 11.15.&22.26.Sponsionis temerariae exemplum:Ruben,Gen.4 37.[Sponsor, Christus,Hebr.7.22.]V.Fideiussio.
units.tr: To give surety for another's name lightly is rash, Prov. 6:1; 11:15; 22:26. Example of rash suretyship: Reuben, Gen. 42:37. [Surety: Christ, Heb. 7:22.] See SURETYSHIP.

units.la: SPONSA Christi Ecclesia,V.ECCLESIA.
units.tr: SPOUSE of Christ: the Church. See CHURCH.

units.la: SPONSVS Ecclesiae Christus,Esa.54.5.&62.4.Iere.31.22.Ezec.16.8. Matth.9.15. &25 1.Marc.2.19.&Luc.5.34.Ioan.3.29. Corint.11.2 Ephes.5.24.Apoc.19.7.&21.2.V.CHRISTVS CONIVGIVM spirituale.
units.tr: SPOUSE of the Church: Christ, Isa. 54:5; 62:4; Jer. 31:22; Ezek. 16:8; Matt. 9:15; 25:1; Mark 2:19; Luke 5:34; John 3:29; 2 Cor. 11:2; Eph. 5:24; Rev. 19:7; 21:2. See CHRIST, spiritual marriage.

units.la: SPONSAM ambiendi & tradendi ritus exempla:Seruus Abrahae Isaaco,Gen.24.49.Hemor Sichem filio suo,34.8. Tobiae Saram,Tob.6.v.11.12.13. Raguel filiam suam Tobiae 7.v.13.14.15.Dauid Abigail.1 Sam.25.v.39.40. Sponsis decedentibus bene precandi formula: Parentes & cognati Rebeccae bene precantur ipsi, Gen.24.60. totus populus & Seniores ipsi Ruth,Ruth.4.11.Seruitutis propter sponsas exemplum:Iacob pro Lia & Rachel,Gen.29.v.17.&c. Fortitudinis & insignis facinoris,propter sponsas praestiti exempla:Othoniel,Iudic.1.13.Dauid 1 Sam.18.27.
units.tr: Examples of the rites of courting and giving a bride: Abraham's servant for Isaac, Gen. 24:49; Hamor of Shechem for his son, Gen. 34:8; Tobias for Sarah, Tob. 6:11–13; Raguel giving his daughter to Tobias, Tob. 7:13–15; David for Abigail, 1 Sam. 25:39–40. A formula of blessing for brides departing: the parents and kinsfolk of Rebecca bless her, Gen. 24:60; the whole people and the elders bless Ruth, Ruth 4:11. Example of servitude on account of brides: Jacob for Leah and Rachel, Gen. 29:17, etc. Examples of courage and remarkable deeds performed on account of brides: Othniel, Judg. 1:13; David, 1 Sam. 18:27.

units.la: SPVRIVS, ac etiam decima eius generatio, ab Ecclesiae suctione arcendus,ne propter infamiam, impiis detur occasio deridendi Ecclesiam: Deut.23.2. Iephthacum quide[?] corruptis temporibus extra ordinem vocavit Deus, Iudic.11.(sed qui ordinariae vocationis leges indixit hominibus, nullam sibi necessitatem imposuit.
units.tr: A bastard, and even his tenth generation, must be kept out of the assembly of the Church, so that the impious are not given an occasion, through his infamy, to mock the Church: Deut. 23.2. God called Jephthah out of the ordinary order when the times were corrupt, Judg. 11. But he who laid down the laws of ordinary calling for men did not impose any such necessity on himself.

units.la: [Stagnum ignis, Locus damnatorum. Apo.19.20.& 20. v.10.14.15. & 21.8.]
units.tr: [Lake of fire, the place of the damned. Rev. 19.20 & 20.10, 14, 15 & 21.8.]

units.la: [?]ANS videat ne cadat,1 Cor.10.12.
units.tr: Let him who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall, 1 Cor. 10.12.

units.la: [?]ARE,pro,versari,Ioan.1.26.V.Sto.
units.tr: STARE, in the sense of to dwell or to be, John 1.26. See STO.

units.la: [?]TATER,numi species,quatuor drachmarum, 1 Samu.9.8. Ier.32.9. Mat.17.27.]
units.tr: STATER, a kind of coin worth four drachmas, 1 Sam. 9.8; Jer. 32.9; Matt. 17.27.

units.la: [?]ATERA seu trutina aequa esse debet,Leu.19 36. Prou.11.1. & 16.11.& 20.23.vide Ierem.32.10.Ezech.45.10.Ose.12.7.8. Am.8.5.Mic.6.11 statera mystica, Apo.6.5.
units.tr: A balance, or statera, ought to be even, Lev. 19.36; Prov. 11.1, 16.11, 20.23. See Jer. 32.10; Ezek. 45.10; Hos. 12.7-8; Amos 8.5; Mic. 6.11. The statera of the mystical vision, Rev. 6.5.

units.la: [?]ATVAE religionis causa non erigendae,Deute.16.22.Vide IDOLVM. Statua,iussu Nabuchodonosor erecta.Daniel.3. I.ei divinos cultus exhiberi edicit,versi.4.5.poenam recusanti statuit, v.6. eam tres Iudaei adolescentes incurrunt, V.SIDRACH.
units.tr: Statues are not to be erected for the sake of religion, Deut. 16.22. See IDOL. A statue erected by the command of Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 3. He commands that divine worship be rendered to it, vv. 4-5, and sets a penalty for those who refuse, v. 6, which the three young Jews incur. See SHADRACH.

units.la: [?]ATVRAE magnae & procerae homines: Filij Enac,Nume. 334.Saul, 1 Samu.10.23. & 16.7. Goliath,17.4.ad statuam suam cubitum unum nemo addere potest, Matt.6 27. Luc.12.25.
units.tr: Men great and tall in stature: the sons of Anak, Num. 13.34; Saul, 1 Sam. 10.23 & 16.7; Goliath, 17.4. No one can add one cubit to his stature, Matt. 6.27; Luke 12.25.

units.la: [?]ELLA matutina 2 Pet.1.19.Apo.2.28. & 22.16. stella Maiorum dux, Matt.2.v.2.9.
units.tr: STAR, the morning star, 2 Pet. 1.19; Rev. 2.28 & 22.16. A star, the leader of the Magi, Matt. 2.2, 9.

units.la: [?]ELLAE verbo Dei creatae,Gen.1.17.Ps.8.4.Singulis nomina D.imposuit:Iob.38.31.32.Ps.147.4. singularum cursum regit:ps.136.78.9.Isa.40.26. Aliae aliis lucis gradu differunt: 1 Cor.15.41.coram Deo immundae,Iob 25.5. stellae,Ecclesiarum pastores, Apo.1.20.
units.tr: The stars, created by God's word, Gen. 1.17; Ps. 8.4. God gave a name to each of them, Job 38.31-32; Ps. 147.4. He governs the course of each, Ps. 136.7-9; Isa. 40.26. Some differ from others in degree of brightness, 1 Cor. 15.41; before God they are unclean, Job 25.5. Stars are the ministers of the Churches, Rev. 1.20.

units.la: [Stellae mysticae, Apo.6.13.& 8. v.10.11.12. & 12.1. stella figuratè dicitur regnum populi Dei coeptum in Davide, completum in Christo, Num. 24.17.]
units.tr: [Mystical stars, Rev. 6.13 & 8.10-12 & 12.1. A star is figuratively said of the kingdom of God's people, begun in David and completed in Christ, Num. 24.17.]

units.la: [?]ELLIONE non vescuntur Iudaei.Leuit.11.v.30.31.
units.tr: STELLIO: the Jews do not eat it, Lev. 11.30-31.

units.la: [?]PHANVS Diaconus eligitur, Actor.6.5.signa ac miracula edit, v.8. Gymnasiorum Ierosolymitanorum impetum sustinet,v.9.eum verbo & doctrina retundit,v.10.in concilium rapitur,v.12.13.vultu, animi fidem & constantiam prodit,v.15. apologia viro fortissimo digna, se suamque doctrinam defendit,7.v.2.3.4. dicendo adversariorum vlus tangit, ita ut apertius insaniant, v. 53. mortem praentiens,propiusChristum intuetur,& in coelum assurgit, 55.lapidatur,v.58. Christum invocat, v.59. pro inimicis orat.v.60.Sepelitur,8.v.2.
units.tr: STEPHEN is chosen as deacon, Acts 6.5. He does signs and great miracles, v. 8. He withstands the assault of the Jerusalem synagogues, v. 9. He overcomes them by his word and teaching, v. 10. He is dragged before the council, vv. 12-13. By his countenance he shows the faith and constancy of his spirit, v. 15. With a defence worthy of a most courageous man, he defends himself and his teaching, 7.2-4. In speaking he touches the wrongs of his opponents, so that they rage more openly, v. 53. Foreseeing his death, he looks more closely at Christ and rises toward heaven, v. 55. He is stoned, v. 58. He calls on Christ, v. 59. He prays for his enemies, v. 60. He is buried, 8.2.

units.la: ST HEPHANAE familia, primitiæ Achaiæ, 1 Corinth. 16.15. A Paulo baptizatur, 1.16. Stephanæ præsentia Paulus recreatur 16.17.
units.tr: The household of STEPHANAS, the firstfruits of Achaia, 1 Cor. 16.15. He is baptized by Paul, 1.16. Paul is refreshed by the presence of Stephanas, 16.17-18.

units.la: STERCVS inimici Dei, Psalmo. 83. 11. omnia præ Christo, Phil. 3.8. stercus solennitatum, Malac. 2.3.
units.tr: DUNG: the enemy of God, Ps. 83.11; all things for the sake of Christ, Phil. 3.8; the dung of your solemn feasts, Mal. 2.3.

units.la: [Conditio abiectiff. 1 Sam. 2.8. Psal. 113.7.]
units.tr: [Lowly condition. 1 Sam. 2.8. Ps. 113.7.]

units.la: Deus ex stercorilino extollit pauperem: 1 Sam. 2.8. Ps. 113. 7. Excrementa sua qui comedent: 2 Reg. 18.27. Indignè de Deo loquentis domus in stercorilinium redigatur. Dan. 3.29.
units.tr: God lifts the poor man up from the dunghill, 1 Sam. 2.8; Ps. 113.7. Those who eat their own dung, 2 Kings 18.27. The house of one who speaks unworthily of God is reduced to a dunghill, Dan. 3.29.

units.la: STERILIS nulla obedientibus, Exodi 23 26. Deut. 7.14.
units.tr: STERILE: no one among those who obey, Exod. 23.26; Deut. 7.14.

units.la: STERILITAS olim opprobrij nota Iudæis, Gen. 30.23. 1 Sam. 1.6. Lucæ 1.36. Sterilitatis exempla: Sara, Gen. 11.30. Hebr. 11. 11. Rebecca, 25.21. Rachel, 29 31. Vxor Manuę, Iud. 13.2. Anna, 1 Sam. 1.2. Michol. 2 Sam. 6.23. Sunamitis, 2 Regum. 4.14. Elizabeth, Luc. 1.37. Vide MVLIBRES steriles fœcundæ redditæ. V. Isa. 54 1.
units.tr: STERILITY was formerly a mark of disgrace among the Jews, Gen. 30.23; 1 Sam. 1.6; Luke 1.36. Examples of sterility: Sarah, Gen. 11.30; Heb. 11.11. Rebekah, Gen. 25.21. Rachel, Gen. 29.31. Manoah's wife, Judg. 13.2. Hannah, 1 Sam. 1.2. Michal, 2 Sam. 6.23. The Shunammite, 2 Kings 4.14. Elizabeth, Luke 1.36. See BARREN WOMEN made fruitful; see Isa. 54.1.

units.la: STIGMATA Christi, id est, iniustas notas, se portare inquit Apostolus, Gal. 6.17. quales inuri seruis solebant, magna quidem cum ipsorum infamia, unde & stigmatiæ dicti sunt. Stigmata sibi inurere fideles non debent. Leui. 19.28. V. 1 Reg. 18.28.
units.tr: STIGMATA of Christ, that is, unjust marks, which the Apostle says he bears, Gal. 6.17, such as were customarily branded on slaves, indeed with great disgrace to them, whence they were also called stigmata. The faithful ought not to brand marks on themselves, Lev. 19.28. See 1 Kings 18.28.

units.la: STIMVLVS carnis cur perfectioribus relictus, 2 Cor. 12.7. stimulus mortis, 1 Cor. 15.56. V. Act. 9 5. 1 Sam. 13.21.
units.tr: STIMULUS of the flesh, why it was left to the more perfect, 2 Cor. 12.7; the sting of death, 1 Cor. 15.56. See Acts 9.5; 1 Sam. 13.21.

units.la: STIPENDIA militibus debentur. 1 Corinth. 9.7. iis contenti viuant oportet, Luc. 3.14. stipendia peccati mors, Rom. 6.23. V. Mors.
units.tr: Wages are owed to soldiers, 1 Cor. 9.7; they ought to be content with them, Luke 3.14. The wages of sin is death, Rom. 6.23. See DEATH.

units.la: [STO, Verbum, multa in Scripturis respicit, obseruanda digna paucis descripta.
units.tr: [STARE, the word; it refers to many things in the Scriptures; the points worth observing are described briefly.]

units.la: 1. Stare dicitur Deus, 1 Sam. 3.10. Psal. 82.1. Esa. 3.13. Ezech. 10.18. Amos 7.7. Abac. 3 6. Zach. 14 4.
units.tr: 1. God is said to stand, 1 Sam. 3.10; Ps. 82.1; Isa. 3.13; Ezek. 10.18; Amos 7.7; Hab. 3.6; Zech. 14.4.

units.la: 2. Stat filius Dei, Angelus Iehoua, Angelus Iehouę, &c. Exo. 14.19. Ios 5 13. Cantic. 2.9. Zach. 1.8. &c. & 3.v.1.5. etiam filius Dei in carne manifestatus, inter Iudæos tempus, Matth. 20.32 & 27.11. Ioan. 7.37. stat post resurrectionem inter suos, Lucæ 24.36. Ioan. 19.26. & 21.4. stat in cælis, Act. 7.v.55 56. Apoc. 5.6. & 14.1. stat spiritualiter circa suos, Apo. 3 20.
units.tr: 2. The Son of God stands: the Angel of Jehovah, the Angel of Jehovah, etc., Exod. 14.19; Josh. 5.13; Song 2.9; Zech. 1.8, etc., and 3.1, 5. Also the Son of God, manifested in the flesh, stood among the Jews at the time, Matt. 20.32 & 27.11; John 7.37. He stands after the resurrection among his own, Luke 24.36; John 19.26 & 21.4. He stands in heaven, Acts 7.55-56; Rev. 5.6 & 14.1. He stands spiritually around his own, Rev. 3.20.

units.la: 3. Stant Angeli Electi, vt varia ministeria exequantur, Nume. 22. verf. 22. 23. &c. 1 Para. 21. verf. 15. 16. Esai. 6.1. Ezech. 1. verf. 21. &c. Dan. 10.16. & 12.5. &c. Luc. 1.11. & 24. Act. 10.30. & 11.13. Apoc. 7. verf. 1.11. & 8. v. 2.3. & 10. verf. 5. & 19.17. 4. Stat, malus Angelus, Iob. 2. 1. Zach. 3. 1. Apoc. 12. v. 4. 17.
units.tr: 3. Elect angels stand, so that they may carry out various ministries, Num. 22.22-23, etc.; 1 Chr. 21.15-16; Isa. 6.1; Ezek. 1.21, etc.; Dan. 10.16 & 12.5, etc.; Luke 1.11 & 24; Acts 10.30 & 11.13; Rev. 7.1, 11 & 8.2-3 & 10.5 & 19.17. 4. An evil angel stands, Job 2.1; Zech. 3.1; Rev. 12.4, 17.

units.la: 5. Stat de homine aliisque creaturis & variis rebus tum natura tum arte factis, ad usus varios pertinentibus, frequenter dictum.
units.tr: 5. Stand is often said of man and of other creatures and of various things, whether made by nature or by art, which serve various uses.

units.la: 6. Praesertim vero de beata sorte piorum in vita praesenti, quatenus fide, spe, patientia, &c. gratiose donantur a Deo, verbum illud summa cum piorum laetitia dicitur occurrit, Rom. 5. 2. & 11. 20. & 4. 4. 1. Cor. 10. 12. & 15. 16. 13. 2. Cor. 1. 24. Galat. 5. 1. Ephes. 6. ver. 11. 14. Philip. 1. 7. & 4. 1. Coloss. 4. 12. 1. Thess. 3. 8. 2. Thess. 2. 15. 1. Petr. 5. 12.
units.tr: 6. Especially of the blessed lot of the godly in the present life, insofar as they are graciously granted by God through faith, hope, patience, etc., that word occurs, to the great joy of the godly: Rom. 5.2 & 11.20 & 4.4; 1 Cor. 10.12 & 15.16; 13.2; 2 Cor. 1.24; Gal. 5.1; Eph. 6.11, 14; Phil. 1.7 & 4.1; Col. 4.12; 1 Thess. 3.8; 2 Thess. 2.15; 1 Pet. 5.12.

units.la: 7. Item, de statu mystico & glorioso electorum Deiditur, Apoc. 7. 9. & 11. v. 4. 11. & 15. 2.
units.tr: 7. Likewise, it is said of the mystical and glorious state of the elect, Rev. 7.9; 11.4, 11; 15.2.

units.la: 8. Stabunt omnes homines coram Christo iudice, Rom. 14. 10. Apoc. 20. 12.]
units.tr: 8. All men will stand before Christ the judge, Rom. 14.10; Rev. 20.12.]

units.la: STOICI philosophi cum Paulo disputant. & Athenis: Act. 17. 18.
units.tr: The STOIC philosophers dispute with Paul, also at Athens, Acts 17.18.

units.la: STORGE, sive affectio naturalis est is animi impetus & propensio naturalis, per quam vere & ex animo, sicut oportet diligimus eos omnes & charos habemus, quos nobis natura vel propter commune sanguinis vinculum, vel propter communem vitae ipsius humanae societatem conciliavit. Sic affectus hic ad parentes, & vicissim ad liberos, ad vxorem, ad domesticos, ad cognatos, affines, late diffunditur, non ad patriam, concives & conterraneos. Vide Asiorgia
units.tr: STORGE, or natural affection, is that impulse and natural inclination of the mind through which we truly and from the heart love, as we ought, and hold dear all those whom nature has bound to us, either through the common bond of blood or through the common society of human life itself. Thus this affection extends widely toward parents, and in turn toward children, wife, household members, relatives and in-laws, but not toward country, fellow citizens and fellow countrymen. See ASTORGIA

units.la: CIDOR detium, insignis doloris signum. Matt. 8. 12. & 13. 22. 13. & 24. 51 & 25. 30. Marc. 9. 18. Luc. 23. 28. 7. Act. 7. 54.
units.tr: Gnashing of teeth (STRIDOR DENTIVM), a sign of deep grief: Matt. 8.12 & 13.22; 13.42 & 24.51 & 25.30; Mark 9.18; Luke 13.28; Acts 7.54.

units.la: VTHIO: eius natura describitur, Iob. 39. 16. eius esus. Iureis prohibetur Levit. 11. 16.
units.tr: OSTRICH (STRVTHIO): its nature is described, Job 39.16; its eating is forbidden by the Law, Lev. 11.16.

units.la: ILTILOQVIVM damnatur, Rom. 1, 30. Ephes. 5. 4. Est enim tantum inanis sive inutilis, sed peruersi, & quo quis inscrito offenditur, sermonis a sciente facta prolatio.
units.tr: FOOLISH TALK (STVLTILOQVIVM) is condemned, Rom. 1.30; Eph. 5.4. For it is merely vain or useless, but perverse, the utterance of speech by which someone is offended, spoken knowingly.

units.la: LTITIA, Prov. 14. 29. & 20. 3. & 26. 1. & 27. 22. Eccles. 10. 2. Eccles. 33. 5. Baruch 3. 23. Matth. 7. 26. & 25. 2. Marc. 7. 22. Ephes. 5. 4. stultitia quae laudanda, 1 Corinth. 3. 18 stultitiae & sapientiae discrimen, Vide SAPIENTIA. Stultitia veris Dei ministris a mundo nonnunquam obiicitur, Vide IN-IANIA.
units.tr: JOY (LAETITIA): Prov. 14.29 & 20.3 & 26.1 & 27.22; Eccl. 10.2; Ecclus 33.5; Bar. 3.23; Matt. 7.26 & 25.2; Mark 7.22; Eph. 5.4. Folly that is to be praised, 1 Cor. 3.18. The difference between folly and wisdom: see WISDOM. Folly is sometimes objected to the true ministers of God by the world: see MADNESS.

units.la: STVLTVS stultitiam deserere non potest, Prou.27.22. stultus felicitate vti non potest,26.1,
units.tr: A fool cannot abandon his folly, Prov. 27:22. A fool cannot bear prosperity, 26:1.

units.la: STVLTI ira quàm noxia,27.3. stulti & sapientis collatio, VIDE Sapiens.
units.tr: How harmful the anger of fools is, 27:3. For the comparison of the fool and the wise man, see WISE MAN.

units.la: STVLTO quando respondendum,Prou.26 4.5.
units.tr: When one should answer a fool, Prov. 26:4-5.

units.la: STVLTO nihil prosunt diuitiæ,seu pretium,17.16.
units.tr: Riches do not profit a fool, or the price (of wisdom), 17:16.

units.la: STVLTI contentionum authores, Prou.18. 6. sapientes sibi videntur,26.16. itaque castigatione vix emendantur,17.10. & tamen castigandi sunt,10.13. & 26.3. stulta mundi cur à Deo eliguntur, 1 Cor.1.27.
units.tr: Fools are the authors of quarrels, Prov. 18:6. They seem wise to themselves, 26:16, and so they are scarcely corrected by chastisement, 17:10, yet they must be chastised, 10:13 and 26:3. Why God chooses the foolish things of the world, 1 Cor. 1:27.

units.la: STVLTORVM corda,in ore eorum sunt : sapientum ora è contrario in corde sunt. Ecclef.21.26. 27. sultorum infinitus numerus est,Ecclef.1.15. Stultorum & stultitiæ,seu stultæ factorum exempla: Aaron & Maria,Num.12.11. Israelitæ, Deute 32.6. Saul, 1 Sam.13 13. & 26.21. Dauid,2.13.2 Sam.24.10. Nabal,1 Sam.25.25. Asa, 2 Paral. 16.9. Vxor,Iob,Iob 2.10. Princeps,Saon,Esa 19.11. Iudei Iere.4.22.& 5.21. Pharifæi Matth.23.v.16.17. Diues quidam,Luc.12. 20. duo Discipuli,24.25. Gentes, Rom.1.21. Gal.3.1.
units.tr: The hearts of fools are in their mouths; on the contrary, the mouths of the wise are in their hearts, Ecclus. 21:26-27. The number of fools is infinite, Eccles. 1:15. Examples of fools and of foolish deeds: Aaron and Miriam, Num. 12:11; the Israelites, Deut. 32:6; Saul, 1 Sam. 13:13 and 26:21; David, 2 Sam. 13:13 and 24:10; Nabal, 1 Sam. 25:25; Asa, 2 Chron. 16:9; Job's wife, Job 2:10; the prince Saction (?), Isa. 19:11; the Jews, Jer. 4:22 and 5:21; the Pharisees, Matt. 23:16-17; a certain rich man, Luke 12:20; two disciples, Luke 24:25; the Gentiles, Rom. 1:21 and Gal. 3:1.

units.la: STVLTIS silentium imponendum, Prouerb. 26.10. 1 Petri 2.15.
units.tr: Fools must be silenced, Prov. 26:10; 1 Pet. 2:15.

units.la: STVPOR,est alienatio quædam sensuum,quòd sensus constituentur.
units.tr: Stupor is a certain alienation of the senses, by which the senses are benumbed.

units.la: STVPORIS exempla. Iaac: Genef.27.33. Regina Saba,2 Paralip 9.v.3.4. Israelitæ, Esai.28.10.& 29.11. Ieremiæ 5.3. Daniel. Dan.8.27. Turba,Matth.12,23. Lucæ 9.43. Ioan.12.37. Capharnaitæ,Marc.1 22. Pilatus & Iudæi,Matth.27 13.14. &c. Discipuli,Marc.6.v.49.52. Luc.18.34. Petrus,5.9. Actor.12. 6. Pharifæi & legis Doctores,Luc.2.47.& 5 26. Paulus, Actor.9.6. Comites Pauli,v.7. impij, Ephes.4.18. Vide ADMIRATIONIS exempla.
units.tr: Examples of stupor. Isaac, Gen. 27:33; the queen of Sheba, 2 Chron. 9:3-4; the Israelites, Isa. 28:10 and 29:11; Jer. 5:3; Daniel, Dan. 8:27; the crowd, Matt. 12:23, Luke 9:43, John 12:37; the Capernaites, Mark 1:22; Pilate and the Jews, Matt. 27:13-14, etc.; the disciples, Mark 6:49-52, Luke 18:34; Peter, Luke 5:9 and Acts 12:6; the Pharisees and the doctors of the law, Luke 2:47 and 5:26; Paul, Acts 9:6; Paul's companions, v. 7; the impious, Eph. 4:18. See examples of ADMIRATION.

units.la: STVPRVM, committitur quando solutus quispiam seu nondum coniugatus extra matrimonium cum virgine aut viduam rem habet. Deut.22.28. Gen.34.13.27. Leuit.39.10. 2 Samu. 13.12. V. Scortatio.
units.tr: Fornication is committed when an unmarried man, that is, one not yet married, has relations outside marriage with a virgin or a widow. Deut. 22:28; Gen. 34:13, 27; Lev. 19:20; 2 Sam. 13:12. See FORNICATION.

units.la: SVA,vir Chananæus,Iudæ vxoris pater,Gen.38.2.
units.tr: Shua, a Canaanite man, father of Judah's wife, Gen. 38:2.

units.la: SVA, Rex Aegypti ,2 Reg.17.2. (Schua.1. clamor vel opulentus.)
units.tr: Shua, king of Egypt, 2 Kings 17:2 (Shua: 1. a cry, or wealthy).

units.la: SVBCINERITII panes. Exodi 12. 39. 1 Reg. 17. 12. 13. Osee. 7. 8.
units.tr: Unleavened cakes baked in ashes: Exod. 12:39; 1 Kings 17:12-13; Hos. 7:8.

units.la: SVBDITI Principem facilè imitantur, Prou.29.2. Ecclef.10. Exempla:Populus Saulis, 1 Sam.15.9. subditi Ieroboam,
units.tr: Subjects readily imitate their prince, Prov. 29:2; Eccles. 10. Examples: the people of Saul, 1 Sam. 15:9; the subjects of Jeroboam,

units.la: 1 Reg. 12, v. 28. 30, & 14, 16. Maiores natu Israel, 2 Regum 10, 5. subditi Manassis, 21, v. 9, 22.
units.tr: 1 Kings 12:28, 30 and 14:16; the elders of Israel, 2 Kings 10:5; the subjects of Manasseh, 21:9, 22.

units.la: SUBDITORUM erga Regem amor & reuerentia.
units.tr: The love and reverence of subjects toward the king.

units.la: Exempla: Dauidis milites, 2 Sam. 21, 17. Subditorum erga Magistratum officia: I. Agnoscere gubernatores suos, non casu, sed Dei consilio praefectos esse. Exempla: Dauid agnoscit Saulem pro Christo Domini, 1 Sam. 24, v. 5, 6, 7, & 26, 9, Abisai similiter Dauidem, 2 Sam. 19, 21. Miphiboseth, v. 26, 27. Adonias, 1 Regum 2, 15. Populus Israel, 3. 28. Daniel, Dan. 2. 37. II. Fauore & amore eos prosequi. Exempla: Iacob, Gen. 47, v. 7, 10, Mulier Thecuitis, 2 Sam. 14. 5, &c. Ioab. ver. 22, Echai, 15, 21, Chusai. v. 31, 32, 33, Berzellai, 19, v. 31, 32, Esaias, 2 Reg. 19, 6, & 20, 7, Mardochaeus, Esth. 2, verf. 21, 22, Daniel, Dan. 6, 21. III. Praestare legibus & mandatis eorum pietati & honestati consentaneis debitam obedientiam. Exempla: Rubenitae & Gaditae, Ios. 13, 8, & 22, ver. 1, 2, subditi Saulis, 1 Sam. 11. v. 14, 15, exercitus saulis, 14, 24, Isai, 16, v. 17, &c. serui Dauidis, 2 sam. 15, v. 13, 14, Banaias, 1 Reg. 2, 25, Nuntius Asae 15. 22, Milites Iehu, 2 Reg. 10, 25.
units.tr: Examples: David's soldiers, 2 Sam. 21:17. The duties of subjects toward the magistrate: (I) to acknowledge their rulers as set over them not by chance but by the counsel of God. Examples: David acknowledges Saul as the Lord's anointed, 1 Sam. 24:5-7 and 26:9; Abishai likewise regards David, 2 Sam. 19:21; Mephibosheth, v. 26-27; Adonijah, 1 Kings 2:15; the people of Israel, 3:28; Daniel, Dan. 2:37. (II) to pursue them with favour and affection. Examples: Jacob, Gen. 47:7, 10; the woman of Tekoa, 2 Sam. 14:5, etc.; Joab, v. 22; Ittai, 15:21; Hushai, v. 31-33; Barzillai, 19:31-32; Isaiah, 2 Kings 19:6 and 20:7; Mordecai, Esth. 2:21-22; Daniel, Dan. 6:21. (III) to render due obedience to their laws and commands, insofar as these agree with piety and honesty. Examples: the Reubenites and Gadites, Josh. 13:8 and 22:1-2; the subjects of Saul, 1 Sam. 11:14-15; Saul's army, 14:24; Isaiah, 16:17, etc.; the servants of David, 2 Sam. 15:13-14; Benaiah, 1 Kings 2:25; the messenger of Asa, 15:22; the soldiers of Jehu, 2 Kings 10:25.

units.la: IV. Conferre sumtus ad gubernationem necessarios, tributum, vectigal, census, decimas, & similia, pro diuersa politiarum ratione, i. Sam. 8, v. 11, &c. Matt. 22, 21. Roman. 13. 7.
units.tr: (IV) to contribute the expenses necessary for government: tribute, customs, taxes, tithes and the like, according to the different constitutions of states. 1 Sam. 8:11, etc.; Matt. 22:21; Rom. 13:7.

units.la: V. Æquo animo accipere eorum sententiam, & iustas poenas propter violatas leges. Exempla: Semei, 2. Sam. 19. 19. Miphiboset, verf. 27. 28.
units.tr: (V) to accept the sentence of the magistrate with an equable mind, and just punishments for violated laws. Examples: Shimei, 2 Sam. 19:19; Mephibosheth, v. 27-28.

units.la: VI. Timere eos, & leui ora quaedam errata iis condonare, ac tolerare eorum iniurias, & sibi temperare ab eorum caede. Exempla: Israel, Iosue 4, 14, populus saulus, 1 sam. 12, 7. Dauid, 24, verf. 9. 10. 11. & 26. 9. Gentes, 1 Paral. 14, 17.
units.tr: (VI) to fear them, to pardon them certain light errors, and to tolerate their injuries, and to refrain from their slaughter. Examples: Israel, Josh. 4:14; the people of Saul, 1 Sam. 12:7; David, 24:9-11 and 26:9; the nations, 1 Chron. 14:17.

units.la: VII. Petere a Magistratu auxilium & defensionem. Exempla: Mulier Thecuitis, 2 sam. 14. 4. Mulier quaedam, 2. Regum. 6. 26. Sunamitis, 8. 3.
units.tr: (VII) to seek help and protection from the magistrate. Examples: the woman of Tekoa, 2 Sam. 14:4; a certain woman, 2 Kings 6:26; the Shunammite, 8:3.

units.la: VIII. Eternis gestibus suam erga Magistratum declarare reuerentiam Exempla: Iacob, Genes. 28. 4. & 47. 7. Fratres Ioseph, 50. 18, Nathan & Bethsheba submisso in terram vultu, adorauit Dauidem, 1 Reg. 1, v. 23, 31.
units.tr: (VIII) to declare their reverence toward the magistrate by outward gestures. Examples: Jacob, Gen. 28:4 and 47:7; the brothers of Joseph, 50:18; Nathan and Bathsheba, with face bowed to the earth, worshipped David, 1 Kings 1:23, 31.

units.la: IX. Imitari pietatem & caeteras virtutes bonorum gubernatorum. Exempla: Israelitae, Ios. 24. 31. Subditi, Iosiae, 2 Paral. 34. 33. Vide Eccles. 10. 2. X. Orare pro Magistratu, & felicissima quaeque ei precari. Exempla: Subditi saulis, 1 sam. 10. 24. Banaias, 1 Reg. 1. 47. subditi salomonis, verf. 39. subditi Ioas, 2 Regum 11, v. 11, 12, Chaldaei, Ierem. 29.
units.tr: (IX) to imitate the piety and other virtues of good rulers. Examples: the Israelites, Josh. 24:31; the subjects of Josiah, 2 Chron. 34:33. See Eccles. 10:2. (X) to pray for the magistrate and wish him every happiness. Examples: the subjects of Saul, 1 Sam. 10:24; Benaiah, 1 Kings 1:47; the subjects of Solomon, v. 39; the subjects of Joash, 2 Kings 11:11-12; the Chaldeans, Jer. 29:7.

units.la: 7.Satrapæ Regis,Dan 3 9. Regina Balfafar, 5.10.Satrap
units.tr: 7. The satraps of the king, Dan. 3:9. The queen (of Belshazzar), 5:10. The satrap

units.la: Darij,6 6.Daniel verfic.21.Vide.1.Timoth.2.ver.1.2.3.
units.tr: of Darius, 6:6; Daniel, verse 21. See 1 Tim. 2:1-3.

units.la: SVBIECTIO ὑποταγὴ [?] est voluntaria & ex ferio diuinæ ordi nationis sensu facta animi summissio ei, qui etsi simili & eiusdem tecum naturæ quidem,tibi tamen præfectus est à Deo,& in sublimiori gradu & potestate collocatus Rom.13.1.Col.3 22.
units.tr: SUBJECTION [ὑποταγή] is a voluntary submission of the mind, made from a sense of the divine order, to one who, though of the same nature as yourself and like you, has nevertheless been set over you by God and placed in a higher rank and power. Rom. 13:1; Col. 3:22.

units.la: SVBIECTIO mutua commendatur, Ephef.5.21.1.Petr.5.5.
units.tr: Mutual subjection is commended, Eph. 5:21; 1 Pet. 5:5.

units.la: SVBSANNATIONIS Exempla,V. DERISIONIS: & IRRISIO NIS:& ILLVSIONIS exempla.
units.tr: Examples of MOCKERY, DERISION, and ILLUSION. See also SCORN.

units.la: SVCHOTH - BENOTH idolum , Vide IDOLORVM catalogus.
units.tr: SUCCOTH-BENOTH, an idol. See the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: SVFFICIENTIA omnis ex Deo, 2.Cor.3.5.& 9.v.7.8 Sufficentia commendatur,1.Tim.6.v.6.8.Hebr.13.5.eam didicerat Paulus, 2 Corinth.3.5. Philip.4.11. Sufficientiæ exemplum Paulus,Philip.4.11.12.V.αὐτάρκεια.
units.tr: All sufficiency is from God, 2 Cor. 3:5 and 9:7-8. Sufficiency is commended, 1 Tim. 6:6, 8; Heb. 13:5. Paul had learned it, 2 Cor. 3:5; Phil. 4:11. Paul is an example of sufficiency, Phil. 4:11-12. See SELF-SUFFICIENCY [αὐτάρκεια].

units.la: SVFFITVS sacri confectura, Exod. 30. v. 34. ad finem vsque Vsus.v.7.8.9.Altare thymiaterium suffitus,V.1.Figurabat Christi mediationem & Spiritus gratiam, qua sacrificii nostra,seu cultus,Deo accepta reddutur:Psal.141.2.Romanos 8.33.
units.tr: The incense of the sacred compound, Exod. 30:34 to the end, and the use, v. 7-8. The altar of incense, v. 1. It prefigured Christ's mediation and the grace of the Spirit, by which our sacrifice, or worship, is rendered acceptable to God. Ps. 141:2; Rom. 8:33.

units.la: SVFFOCATVM, ante Legem Patribus prohibitum, Gen. 9.4.Fideles etiam Euangelij luce illustrati, ab eo ad temperantiam abstinent, propter Iudæorum fratrum infirmitatem in rebus medijs concessoris eis discendi spatio Act. 15.v.20.29. (V.Leuit.17.v.14.15.)
units.tr: Things strangled were forbidden to the fathers before the Law, Gen. 9:4. The faithful, also illumined by the light of the Gospel, abstain from them in moderation, because of the weakness of their Jewish brethren, and in things indifferent they were allowed a period for learning. Acts 15:20, 29. (See Lev. 17:14-15.)

units.la: SVNAM, ciuitas in tribu Isachar in qua Helisæus suæ hospitæ filium mortuum in vitam reuocauit. 2. Reg. 4. 32.c.
units.tr: Shunem, a city in the tribe of Issachar, in which Elisha restored to life the dead son of his hostess, 2 Kings 4:32, etc.

units.la: SVPERBIA, est propriæ gloriæ & laudis, propter gratiam & donum quod quis habet à Deo, insolens arrogatio Vel vt Augustinus ait, Est amor propriæ excellentiæ, nimirum cum quis à se habere ea putat quæ bona habet, aut eorum bonorum laudem in se transfert.
units.tr: Pride is an insolent arrogation of one's own glory and praise, on account of the grace and gift which one has from God; or, as Augustine says, it is the love of one's own excellence, namely when someone thinks he has from himself the good things he possesses, or transfers to himself the praise of those goods.

units.la: Superbiæ punitæ exempla: In Adamo & Eua, Genes.3.16. &c.Eccles.10.14. Aedificatoribus turris Babylonicæ, Gen. 11.5, &c.Agar.16.v.5.7 Sodoma.19.24.Ezech.16.49.Maria, Num.12.v.8.9.Core, Dathan,& Abiron.16.v.31 32.Israelitis, Deut.1.v.43 44. Babylone,v.11.12 Ier.50.31.& 51.v.1.2.52.53.Moabitę.Esa.16, v.6.7. Tyro.23 8 Ezechiel. 28.v.12, &c,Ephraim,Esaiæ, 28.Israel Ezech. 24.21. Pharaone Rege Aegypti, 29. v.3. 4.& 31.v.10.11.12. Nabuchodonosor Dan.4.v.19.&c.Balsasar Chaldæorum Rege. 5.1.2.22.&c.Israelitis,Ose.5.5.& 7.10. Capharnaitis, Matt.11 23. Luc.10 15.Pharisæo,18.14.
units.tr: Examples of punished pride: in Adam and Eve, Gen. 3:16, etc.; Eccles. 10:14. The builders of the Tower of Babel, Gen. 11:5, etc.; Hagar, 16:5, 7; Sodom, 19:24; Ezek. 16:49; Miriam, Num. 12:8-9; Korah, Dathan and Abiram, 16:31-32; the Israelites, Deut. 1:43-44; Gaal son of Obed, Judg. 9:37-38; Goliath, 1 Sam. 17:50; Nabal, 25:37; Saul, 31:4; Sheba son of Bichri, 2 Sam. 20:1, 22; the people of David, because of the proud numbering of the people, 24:5; Adonijah, 1 Kings 1:5, etc.; Ben-hadad, 20:19-20; Rabshakeh and Sennacherib, 2 Kings 19:28, 35; Amaziah, who was notably humbled, 2 Chron. 25:19-23; Uzziah, who arrogantly usurped the priestly office contrary to God's calling, 26:16, 19; Hezekiah, 32:24-26; Haman, Esth. 7:10; Damascus, Isa. 8:4 and 17:1; Assur, 10:12, 23, etc.; the king of Babylon, 14:13-15; Babylon, v. 11-12; Jer. 50:31 and 51:1-2, 52-53; Moab, Isa. 16:6-7; Tyre, 23:8; Ezek. 28:12, etc.; Ephraim, Isa. 28; Israel, Ezek. 24:21; Pharaoh, king of Egypt, 29:3-4 and 31:10-12; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 4:19, etc.; Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, 5:1-2, 22, etc.; the Israelites, Hos. 5:5 and 7:10; the Capernaites, Matt. 11:23; Luke 10:15; the Pharisee, 18:14.

units.la: Superbiæ exempla: Adam & Eua. Duabus enim potissimum rebus moti delinquunt: prima, quòd se deos fore crederent:secunda,quæ impulit eos & pellexit,fuit gula, & formosa pomorum species, Genes.3.v.5.6. Ecclesiæ.10. 14. Aedificatores turris Babylonicæ, Genes.11.4. Agar.16. 4.Fratres Ioseph, 37.8. Aaron,& Maria. Num.12.ver.1.2. Core,Dathan.& Abiron,Num.16.1.Gaal,filius Obed,Iudic.9. 28. Abimelech. v. 30. 45.Saul,1 Sam.13.2.& 15.ver. 19.20.30. Goliath.17.42. Nabal.25 v.10.11.Abialon,2.Sam. 15.4.Sebafilius.Bochri,20.1.Dauid.24.1.Adonias,1 Regum 1.5.Roboam,12.14. Ieroboam.13.4. Benadad. 20 18.Rabsaces,2 Reg. 18.24. Pharao & Ierui eius, Nehem. 9.v.10. Patres & Israelitę,v.29.Nabuchodonosor,Iudith.1.7.& 11 1.&c. Dan. 4.27. Aman, Esth.3.6.&.5.13.Filiæ Sion, Esaiæ. 3. 16.
