Amos,6.8.Idumæi,Abd. verf.3, Pharisæus, Lucæ.18.11,Pharisæi,Ioan.5,44.Iudęi,9, 34.Simon Magus, Act.8,9, Herodes,12,21.Agrippa & Berenice,25,23,Babylonica Meretrix, Apoc.17,1,& 18,7,Superbiæ mala,Prou.11,2,& 22,5,
units.tr: Examples of pride: Adam and Eve. For they sinned moved chiefly by two things: first, because they believed they would become gods; second, what drove and enticed them was gluttony and the attractive appearance of the fruit, Gen. 3.5, 6. Eccles. 10.14. The builders of the Tower of Babel, Gen. 11.4. Hagar, 16.4. The brothers of Joseph, 37.8. Aaron and Miriam, Num. 12.1, 2. Korah, Dathan and Abiram, Num. 16.1. Gaal, son of Ebed, Judg. 9.28. Abimelech, v. 30, 45. Saul, 1 Sam. 13.2; 15.19, 20, 30. Goliath, 17.42. Nabal, 25.10, 11. Absalom, 2 Sam. 15.4. Sheba, son of Bichri, 20.1. David, 24.1. Adonijah, 1 Kings 1.5. Rehoboam, 12.14. Jeroboam, 13.4. Ben-hadad, 20.18. Rabshakeh, 2 Kings 18.24. Pharaoh and his people, Neh. 9.10. The fathers and the Israelites, v. 29. Nebuchadnezzar, Judith 1.7; 11.1, etc.; Dan. 4.27. Haman, Esth. 3.6; 5.13. The daughters of Zion, Isa. 3.16. The king of the Assyrians, 47.7. Azariah and Johanan, Jer. 43.2. Tyre, Isa. 23.8, 9; Ezek. 27.3; 28.2. Belshazzar, Dan. 5.20, 22; 8.25. The Antichrist, 11.36; 2 Thess. 2.4. Israel, Hos. 7.10; 13.6. Amos 6.8. The Edomites, Obad. v. 3. The Pharisee, Luke 18.11. The Pharisees, John 5.44. The Jews, 9.34. Simon Magus, Acts 8.9. Herod, 12.21. Agrippa and Bernice, 25.23. The Babylonian harlot, Rev. 17.1; 18.7. The evils of pride, Prov. 11.2; 22.5.

units.la: SVPERROGATIO refellitur, 1. Ioan. 1,8, unde eius merita manarint, Col.2,23, V. merita.
units.tr: SUPEREROGATION is refuted, 1 John 1.8; whence its merits flowed, Col. 2.23. See MERITS.

units.la: SVPERHVMERALE quale, Exodi.28.6.
units.tr: THE SUPERHUMERAL, what kind it was, Exod. 28.6.

units.la: SVPERSTITIO, est peccatum, cum affectus diuinae gratiae vel vis aliqua naturalis, rei aut gestui tribuitur sine mandato diuino, aut sine causis physicis.
units.tr: SUPERSTITION is a sin when the grace of the divine affection or some natural power is attributed to a thing or a gesture, without a divine command or without physical causes.

units.la: SVPERSTITIO damnatur, Coloss.2,23, Superstitionis exempla: Filij Israel, Gen. 32, 32, Cives Ephrae & cognati Gedeon, Iudic.8, 27. Vide EPHOD, Sacerdotes Dagon, 1.Sam.5.5. Athenienses, Act.17,22. Vide IDOLORVM catalogus V. Act.25,19.
units.tr: SUPERSTITION is condemned, Col. 2.23. Examples of superstition: the sons of Israel, Gen. 32.32; the citizens of Ephrah and the kinsmen of Gideon, Judg. 8.27. See EPHOD. The priests of Dagon, 1 Sam. 5.5. The Athenians, Acts 17.22. See the catalogue of IDOLS. Acts 25.19.

units.la: SVPPLANTATIO summi iudicis, Iob. 12.19, Psalm. 17.13.& 18,40, Supplantatio hominis, Gen.27,36, Osee.12.3.4. Impiorum, Psal.140.5, Esa.29,21, Ierem.9.4. Impiorum miseria, Prou.13.6. & 19.3 & 22.12. & 11.v.3.
units.tr: SUPPLANTING by the supreme judge, Job 12.19; Ps. 17.13; 18.40. Supplanting of a man, Gen. 27.36; Hos. 12.3, 4. Of the wicked, Ps. 140.5; Isa. 29.21; Jer. 9.4. The misery of the wicked, Prov. 13.6; 19.3; 22.12; 11.3.

units.la: SVPPLICIORVM genera quadruplicia fuerunt apud Iudeos: Strangulatio, gladius, lapidatio, & combustio, antequam Herodes, & post Herodem Romani, totum hunc ordinem perturbassent, quorum postremum non dubium est quin fuerit grauissimum. Inde etiam factum, ut aeternas illas poenas cum ignis supplicio passim Scriptores comparent. Vide Math.5.22.
units.tr: There were four kinds of capital punishment among the Jews: strangling, the sword, stoning and burning, until Herod and, after Herod, the Romans upset this whole order; of these the last was undoubtedly the most severe. Hence also it came about that writers everywhere compare those eternal punishments with the torment of fire. See Matt. 5.22.

units.la: SVPPORTEMVS nos inuicem, Ephes.4.2. Col.3.13.
units.tr: Let us bear with one another, Eph. 4.2; Col. 3.13.

units.la: SVRDVS a Deo factus, Exod. 4.11. surdo non maledicendum. Leu.19.14, surdi sanatur (V. MIRACVLA) Audituri. Isa.35.5.
units.tr: DEAF, made so by God, Exod. 4.11. The deaf are not to be cursed, Lev. 19.14. The deaf are healed (see MIRACLES). Hearers. Isa. 35.5.

units.la: SVRGERE, pro proficisci, (Vide SEDERE.) Surgere, de Deo humanitus dictum, Num.10,35, Psal.82,8, & 132.8, Esai.2.v.19.21.
units.tr: To rise, meaning to set out (see TO SIT). To rise, said of God in human terms, Num. 10.35; Ps. 82.8; 132.8; Isa. 2.19, 21.

units.la: SVRGENTES verbum Dei meditentur, Deut.11.19.& 6.7.
units.tr: Rising up, let them meditate on the word of God, Deut. 11.19; 6.7.

units.la: SVS immundum animal: Eo vesci Iudeis non licebat, Levit.11.7. Deut.14.7. Suis immundities describitur, 2.Pet.2.22. V. porcus.
units.tr: THE SWINE is an unclean animal; the Jews were not permitted to eat it, Lev. 11.7; Deut. 14.7. The uncleanness of swine is described in 2 Pet. 2.22. See PIG.

units.la: SVSAN civitas, regni Persici metropolis, Esth.1.2. (lilium aut rosa)
units.tr: SUSA, a city, the metropolis of the Persian kingdom, Esth. 1.2. (lily or rose)

units.la: SVSANNA Christum sequitur, Luc.8.3. (lilium aut rosa vel laetitia)
units.tr: SUSANNA follows Christ, Luke 8.3. (lily or rose, or joy)

units.la: SVSCITABIT nos Deus.1. Cor.6,14,2, Cor.1.9. Hebr.11,19, [Suscitat Deus quos vult ad diversa opera, 2,Sam.12,11. 1.Regum.11.v.14.23. Zach.11.14. Agg.1,14, Suscitat, 1.Erigit. 1 Sam.2.8, Psal.113.7. Esai.44.26. Iere.50,32, Amos 2.11.v. de DEVS.& CHRISTVS, innumera paene sunt huius verbi, ad Dei Omnipotentiam & Sapientiam relati, significata.]
units.tr: GOD WILL RAISE US UP, 1 Cor. 6.14; 2 Cor. 1.9; Heb. 11.19. [God raises up whom he wills for various works, 2 Sam. 12.11; 1 Kings 11.14, 23; Zech. 11.14; Hag. 1.14. To raise up, i.e. to erect, 1 Sam. 2.8; Ps. 113.7; Isa. 44.26; Jer. 50.32; Amos 2.11. Concerning God and Christ, the meanings of this word, related to God's omnipotence and wisdom, are almost innumerable.]

units.la: SVSPENSVS ipso die sepeliebatur, Deut.21.23. V. Esth.7.10.
units.tr: A hanged man was buried on the same day, Deut. 21.23. See Esth. 7.10.

units.la: SVSPICIONES male ex pugnis & logomachiis proficiscuntur, 1. Timoth. 6. 4. Suspicionis exempla, Abraham, Genes. 20,11, Laban,31,20. Iacob,37,33, Putiphar, 39.19, Fratres Ioseph, 43, 18. Filij Israel, Ios. 22.v.11 12. socer samsonis, Iudic. 15.2. Eli,1. sam. 1.13. Saul.20.30.& 22.8. Principes Philistheorum, 29,4, Principes filiorum Ammon,2.sam. 10.3.1, Paralip.19,3, Rex Syriae,2, Regum 5.5, Assuerus, Esth 3.11.& 7.8. Ierias, portae custos, Ierem.37,13. Azarias, 43,v,2,3, Discipuli, Matt. 14. v.25.26. Actor. 9.26. simon Pharisaeus, Lucae.7,39, Iudei, Act. 2.12.& 21.29. Plebs & Magistratus,16.22. Lysias,21.38. Barbari.4.19.
units.tr: SUSPICIONS arise badly from quarrels and word-battles, 1 Tim. 6.4. Examples of suspicion: Abraham, Gen. 20.11; Laban, 31.20; Jacob, 37.33; Potiphar, 39.19; the brothers of Joseph, 43.18; the sons of Israel, Josh. 22.11, 12; the father-in-law of Samson, Judg. 15.2; Eli, 1 Sam. 1.13; Saul, 20.30; 22.8; the princes of the Philistines, 29.4; the princes of the sons of Ammon, 2 Sam. 10.3; 1 Chron. 19.3; the king of Syria, 2 Kings 5.5; Ahasuerus, Esth. 3.11; 7.8; Irijah, the gatekeeper, Jer. 37.13; Azariah, 43.2, 3; the disciples, Matt. 14.25, 26; Acts 9.26; Simon the Pharisee, Luke 7.39; the Jews, Acts 2.12; 21.29; the people and the magistrates, 16.22; Lysias, 21.38; the barbarians, Barbari 4.19.

units.la: SVSVRRATIO ... Rom.1.30. Est de altero absente in alterius aurem occulta & clandestina detractio, ut malum illi nomen conciliemus, sive apud eos quibus iam honeste innotuit, sive apud alios quoslibet. Quae sane ratio a Christiana Charitate alienissima est.
units.tr: DETRACTION ... Rom. 1.30. It is the secret and clandestine whispering into another's ear to disparage someone absent, so that we fix a bad name upon him, whether among those to whom he is already honourably known or among any others at all. This practice is certainly most alien to Christian charity.

units.la: SVSVRRONES damnantur, Levit.19.16, Proverb.26.v.20. 22. Rom.1.29.2, Cor.12.20. Exod.23,1, Ecclesiae.5.16.& 28.15.&c.
units.tr: WHISPERERS are condemned, Lev. 19.16; Prov. 26.20, 22; Rom. 1.29; 2 Cor. 12.20; Exod. 23.1; Eccles. 5.16; 28.15, etc.

units.la: SVDERA in manu Dei, Iob. 38.31, syderum constellationes non metuendae, Ierem. 10.2. Astrologia, & Stella.
units.tr: THE STARS are in the hand of God, Job 38.31; the constellations of the stars are not to be feared, Jer. 10.2. Astrology, and Star.

units.la: SYDVS, idoli, Amos.5.26. Act.7.43, sydera, Esai.47.13. abd.v.4. sydera errantia, Iud.v.13.
units.tr: STAR, of an idol, Amos 5.26; Acts 7.43. The stars, Isa. 47.13; Obad. 4. Wandering stars, Jude 13.

units.la: SYLVANVS Pauli adiutor, 1 Thess. 1.1. eius fidelitas commen-datur, 1 Pet. 5.12. (nomen est à sylua.)
units.tr: SILVANUS, Paul's helper, 1 Thess. 1.1. His faithfulness is commended, 1 Pet. 5.12. (The name is from silva, a forest.)

units.la: SYMPATHIA, Vide COMMISERATIO: &, COMPAS-SIO.
units.tr: SYMPATHY. See COMMISERATION; and COMPASSION.

units.la: SYNAGOGA, proprie conuentus est & locus inter Iudæos, Legi & Prophetis legendis consecratus, Matth. 4.23. & 6. verf. 2. 5. 23. 6. Act. 13. 14. & 15.21. eius moderatores Archisynagogi, vel synagogæ Principes appellabantur, Numer. 4.34. & 16.2. Matth. 9.18. Marc. 5.22. Luc. 8 41. & 13.14. Act. 18.8. Synagogæ plures in vna ciuitate, Academiarum instar. 6.9 Synagoga impia, Osee 2.1. Synagoga Satanæ, Apoc. 2.9.
units.tr: SYNAGOGUE properly means an assembly and place among the Jews, consecrated to the reading of the Law and the Prophets, Matt. 4.23; 6.2, 5; 23.6; Acts 13.14; 15.21. Its leaders were called archisynagogi, or rulers of the synagogue, Num. 4.34; 16.2; Matt. 9.18; Mark 5.22; Luke 8.41; 13.14; Acts 18.8. There were several synagogues in one city, like academies. An impious synagogue, Hos. 2.1. The synagogue of Satan, Rev. 2.9.

units.la: SYNEDRIVM, vel concessus duplex: Minus, quod ex XXIII. constabat Iudicibus, qui in vrbium frequentiorum portis eius dicebant: Maius, quod ex tribus constabat ordinibus: Sacerdotibus nimirum, Legisperitis, seu Scribis, & Senioribus populi, seu qui ex populo legebantur, & hoc erat Iudicium LXXI. ac de grauissimis causis decernebat, vtpote de certa aliqua Tribu, de summo Sacerdote, de Pseudoprophēta, de pace vel bello, &c. V. SENIORES, & Matt. 5.22.
units.tr: THE SANHEDRIN, or double assembly: the lesser, which consisted of twenty-three judges, who sat at the gates of the more populous cities; the greater, which consisted of three orders: namely, the priests, the lawyers or scribes, and the elders of the people, or those chosen from the people; and this was the court of seventy-one, which decided the most serious cases, such as those concerning a particular tribe, the high priest, a false prophet, peace or war, etc. See ELDERS, and Matt. 5.22.

units.la: SYNODORVM à malis conuocatarum & celebratarum exempla: Achab, 1 Reg. 22.6. Herodes, Matth. 2. verf. 3.4. Pharisæi, Scribæ, &c. Ioan. 1. verf. 19 22. & 9.22. & 12.42. Pontifices & Pharisæi, 11. v. 46. 47. Matth. 26. v. 3.4.58. & 28. v. 11. 12. Annas Princeps Sacerdotum, Caiaphas, Ioannes, Alexander, &c, Actor. 4. v. 5.6 & 5.21. &c. Vide CONVENTVM impiorum exempla. Synodorum à Bonis conuocatarum exempla: Vide CONVENTVM piorum exempla.
units.tr: EXAMPLES OF SYNODS convened and held by wicked men: Ahab, 1 Kings 22.6; Herod, Matt. 2.3, 4; the Pharisees, scribes, etc., John 1.19, 22; 9.22; 12.42; the chief priests and Pharisees, 11.46, 47; Matt. 26.3, 4, 58; 28.11, 12; Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, etc., Acts 4.5, 6; 5.21, etc. See the CONVENTION of the wicked, examples. Examples of synods convened by the good: see the CONVENTION of the pious, examples.

units.la: SYRACVSA, metropolis Siciliæ: Act. 28.12. vbi Paulus triduum mansit.
units.tr: SYRACUSE, the metropolis of Sicily: Acts 28.12, where Paul stayed three days.

units.la: SYRIA, quondam terrarum maxima, & pluribus nominibus distincta, 2 Sam. 10.6. 1 Par. 18.5. Syria Damasci Dauidi tributaria est, 2 Sam. 8.6.
units.tr: SYRIA, once the greatest of lands, distinguished by many names, 2 Sam. 10.6; 1 Chron. 18.5. Syria of Damascus was tributary to David, 2 Sam. 8.6.

units.la: SYRI imperant Israeli, Iudic. 3.8. opprimuntur ab Othoniel, v. 10. ab Israelitis profligantur, 2 Sam. 10.13. 1 Para. 19. 18. Syri numero pauci, Iudam & Ierusalem expugnant, 2 Par. 24.23. caecitate percutiuntur, 2 Reg. 6.18. ex Ierosolymitana obsidione miraculo fugantur, 7. v. 6.7. vastantur à Rege Assyriorum, & transferuntur Cyrenen, 16.9. desolatio eotio eorum prænuntiatur, Esa.17.1 Ierem.49.23.Amos. 1.3.
units.tr: THE SYRIANS ruled over Israel, Judg. 3.8; were oppressed by Othniel, v. 10; were routed by the Israelites, 2 Sam. 10.13; 1 Chron. 19.18. The Syrians, few in number, attacked Judah and Jerusalem, 2 Chron. 24.23; were struck with blindness, 2 Kings 6.18; were put to flight by a miracle from the siege of Jerusalem, 7.6, 7; were laid waste by the king of the Assyrians and carried away to Kir, 16.9. Their desolation is foretold, Isa. 17.1; Jer. 49.23; Amos 1.3.

units.la: Syrophoenissa mulier Græca, ex cuius filia dæmonium Christus eiecit:Marc.7.26.c.
units.tr: The Syrophoenician woman, a Greek, from whose daughter Christ cast out a demon: Mark 7.26.

units.la: Syrtis sinus in mari Lybico nauigantibus periculosissimus. Act.27.17.
units.tr: The Syrtis, a bay in the Libyan Sea, most dangerous to sailors. Acts 27.17.

units.la: T.
units.tr: T.

units.la: ABERNACVLA [ab Israelitis ex frondentibus arborum ramis componebantur septimo mense, in quibus festos dies agebant Leuitic.23.v.34.42.Nehem.8.14. &c. Tabernacula, hominum tentoria,Genes.9.21.& 33.17.cant.1.8.Ierem. 49.29.
units.tr: TABERNACLES: Among the Israelites these were made from the leafy branches of trees in the seventh month, and in them they kept the festal days (Lev. 23:34, 42; Neh. 8:14, etc.). Tabernacles are the tents of men (Gen. 9:21; 33:17; Song 1:8; Jer. 49:29).

units.la: TABERNACVLI erectio præcipitur, Exod.40.2. præstatur, 36.8 &40.v.16.&c. Tabernaculi exemplar e cœlo in monte Mosi ostenditur,25.40.Acto.7.44.Heb.8.5. Tabernaculi materia, V. Materia Tabernaculi. Tabernaculum pro corpore nostr. 2 Corint.5.4. 2 Pet.1.v.13.14. pro Christi corpore,Heb.8.2.& 9.11.idque dicitur manu factum, nec humanæ structuræ,ut opponatur structuræ Tabernaculi, quod ex rebus mortuis,puta auro, argento, ligno, pellibus,&c.non naturali fabrica,sed artificiosa,structum erat. In Tabernaculis habitat Abraham, Gen.12.8.
units.tr: The erection of the tabernacle is commanded (Exod. 40:2) and carried out (36:8; 40:16, etc.). A pattern of the tabernacle is shown to Moses from heaven on the mountain (25:40; Acts 7:44; Heb. 8:5). For the material of the tabernacle, see MATERIAL OF THE TABERNACLE. The tabernacle stands for our body (2 Cor. 5:4; 2 Pet. 1:13-14) and for the body of Christ (Heb. 8:2; 9:11). The latter is said to be not made with hands, nor of human construction, in contrast to the structure of the tabernacle, which was built of dead materials, such as gold, silver, wood and skins, by artificial rather than natural workmanship. Abraham dwelt in tabernacles (Gen. 12:8).

units.la: TABERNACVLVM,huius intima pars Sanctuarium,in quod non omni tempore Sacerdoti,ingredi permittitur,etiam summo Sacerdoti, sed semel quotannis, Leuit.16.2.&c. Heb.9.7. corporis Christi typus fuit, Hebr.9.11. eius expiatio,Leuit.16.16.forma,Exo.25.9. eius reuerentia commendatur,Leuit.19.30.& 26.2.Sanctuarium Domini,terra Chanaan appellatur,Exod.15.17.18.
units.tr: THE TABERNACLE: its innermost part, the sanctuary, into which the priest was not permitted to enter at all times, not even the high priest, but only once a year (Lev. 16:2, etc.; Heb. 9:7). It was a type of the body of Christ (Heb. 9:11). Its atonement (Lev. 16:16), its form (Exod. 25:9), and its reverence are commended (Lev. 19:30; 26:2). The land of Canaan is called the sanctuary of the Lord (Exod. 15:17-18).

units.la: [Tabernaculum,quod Dauid,instinctu Spiritus S.arcę erexit, 2 Sam.6.17.1 Par.15.1.2 Par.1.4.Tabernaculum Dei,Nubes, regio ætherea, in qua gloriosæ potentiæ radij elucent, Psalm.18.12.Tabernaculum Dauidis,regnum eius, in Christo æternum,Esai.16.5.Amos 9.11.Act.15.16.Tabernaculum mysticum,nempe Ecclesia Dei, Esa.54.2 Iere.30.18.Apoc. 13.6.Tabernaculum cœleste & æternum, Luc.16.9.Heb.8.2. & 9.11.Apo.15.5.& 21.3.T.Idoli tabernaculum,Amos 5.26. Solis tabernaculum,Psal.19.5.]
units.tr: [The tabernacle which David, moved by the Spirit, erected for the ark (2 Sam. 6:17; 1 Chron. 15:1; 2 Chron. 1:4). The tabernacle of God: the clouds, the ethereal region in which the rays of glorious power shine (Ps. 18:12). The tabernacle of David: his kingdom, eternal in Christ (Isa. 16:5; Amos 9:11; Acts 15:16). The mystical tabernacle, namely the Church of God (Isa. 54:2; Jer. 30:18; Rev. 13:6). The heavenly and eternal tabernacle (Luke 16:9; Heb. 8:2; 9:11; Rev. 15:5; 21:3). T. The tabernacle of an idol (Amos 5:26). The tabernacle of the sun (Ps. 19:5).]

units.la: TABITHA, quæ & Dorcas, mulier pia & sancta, Act.9.36. moratur,v.37.excitatur à Petro,v.40. 41. eius resurrectionis fructus,v.42.(Tabitha, id est,Caprea, Græcè Dorcas.)
units.tr: TABITHA, also called Dorcas, a pious and holy woman (Acts 9:36). She died (v. 37), was raised by Peter (vv. 40-41). The fruit of her resurrection (v. 42). (Tabitha, that is, a roe; in Greek, Dorcas.)

units.la: TABVLÆ testimonij Mosi datæ, Exod.31.18.& 32.15. lapideæ erant,& digito Dei scriptæ,31.18.& 32.16. Deut.9.10. Tabulæ lapideæ,2 Cor.3.3. adumbrabant humani ingenii summam duritiem,à qua cor hominis non regenerati lapideum denominatur,Ezech.11.19.& 36.26. cui opponitur cor carneum,non quod in carne versatur, sed e contrario, quod vi Spiritus Dei factum est mollius, vt in eo tanquam nouis tabulis Euangelij gratia possit insculpi, vt prædictum fuit Ierem.31.31.&c.
units.tr: THE TABLES of the testimony given to Moses (Exod. 31:18; 32:15) were of stone and written by the finger of God (31:18; 32:16; Deut. 9:10). The stone tables (2 Cor. 3:3) represented the greatest hardness of the human mind, from which the heart of a man not yet regenerated is called stony (Ezek. 11:19; 36:26). A heart of flesh is set against it, not because it dwells in the flesh but, on the contrary, because by the power of God's Spirit it has been made softer, so that grace might be engraved on it, as on new tablets of the Gospel, as was foretold (Jer. 31:31, etc.).

units.la: TABVLÆ testimonij franguntur,Exod.,32.19. Deut.9.17. Dei iussu alteræ fiunt,Exod.34.v.1.4. in quibus Deus eadem verba,quæ in prioribus,scripsit, ibid.in arca reconduntur,Deut.10.5.Hebr.9.4.
units.tr: THE TABLES of the testimony were broken (Exod. 32:19; Deut. 9:17). By God's command two others were made (Exod. 34:1, 4), on which God wrote the same words as on the former ones (ibid.). They were kept in the ark (Deut. 10:5; Heb. 9:4).

units.la: Tabulæ cordis Prou.3.3 & 7.3. Tabulæ mysticæ,Cant.8.9.
units.tr: Tables of the heart (Prov. 3:3; 7:3). Mystical tables (Song 8:9).

units.la: [Tabulata tabernaculi, Exod. 26. 29. & 35.11.&c. Templi, Reg 6.v.5.6.10.15.16.] TACENDVM vbi opus est, V.SILENTIVM. TACITVRNITAS laudatur,Prou.11.12. & 17.27. Ecclef.20.1. Taciturnitatis exempla: V.SILENTIVM.
units.tr: [The floors of the tabernacle (Exod. 26, 29; 35:11, etc.); of the temple (1 Kings 6:5-6, 10, 15-16).] KEEPING SILENCE is to be practised where it is needed; see SILENCE. Taciturnity is commended (Prov. 11:12; 17:27; Ecclus. 20:1). Examples of taciturnity: see SILENCE.

units.la: TALENTVM multiplex est,pro diuersitate regionum.Valebat autem talentum Atticum minus sex millia drachmarum,hoc est,(si ad Gallicæ pecuniæ æstimationem redigas)coronatos sexcentos,singulis coronatis solidis Turonensibus 35.æstimatis. TALENTORVM parabola,Matt.25.14. V.PARABOLA.
units.tr: THE TALENT varied according to the region. The Attic talent was worth less than six thousand drachmas, that is (if you reduce it to the value of French money) six hundred crowns, each crown valued at 35 Tours shillings. For the parable of the talents, see PARABLE (Matt. 25:14).

units.la: TALIO,& eius lex,Gen.9.6.Exod.21.24.Leuit.24.20. Deut.19.21.Matt.5.38.& 7.2.Psal.137.7.Esa.33.1.& 55.7. Talionis pœnâ multatorum exempla: Adonibezec,Iudic.1.7.Agag.1 Sam.15.33.Babylon,Ierem.50.v.14.15.& 51. v.6.49. Idumæi,Ezech.35.11.Edom,Abd.v.15. Vide Esa.33.1.Abac.2.8. Accusatores Dan.Dan.6.24.Aman,Esther.7.10.
units.tr: THE LAW OF TALION (retaliation): Gen. 9:6; Exod. 21:24; Lev. 24:20; Deut. 19:21; Matt. 5:38; 7:2; Ps. 137:7; Isa. 33:1; 55:7. Examples of those punished by talion: Adoni-bezek (Judg. 1:7); Agag (1 Sam. 15:33); Babylon (Jer. 50:14-15; 51:6, 49); the Idumeans (Ezek. 35:11); Edom (Obad. 15). See Isa. 33:1; Hab. 2:8. Accusers of Daniel (Dan. 6:24); Haman (Esther 7:10).

units.la: TARSVS ciuitas metropolis Ciciliæ:Act.9.30.& 11.25.& 21.39.& 22.3. TAV,V.PIORVM nota:&,SIGNATI seruantur.
units.tr: TARSUS, the metropolis city of Cilicia (Acts 9:30; 11:25; 21:39; 22:3). TAV: see MARK OF THE PIOUS. And the marked ones are preserved.

units.la: TECTVM domus muniendum,Deut.22.8. Vide Matth.8.8. Marc.2.4.
units.tr: A ROOF must be fenced for the house (Deut. 22:8). See Matt. 8:8; Mark 2:4.

units.la: TEGERE pedes,pro purgare aluum,periphrasis honesta hebraeis,purgantis aluum,Iudic.3.24.1 Sam.24.4.
units.tr: TO COVER THE FEET, a decent periphrasis among the Hebrews for relieving the bowels (Judg. 3:24; 1 Sam. 24:4).

units.la: TEMERITAS in iudicando(2 Tim.3.4. ) est nullo iusto fundamento fulta animi nostri de alio sententia & pronunciatio,qua quid illi vel addimus vel detrahimus. Vtroque enim modo fieri potest.
units.tr: RASHNESS in judging (2 Tim. 3:4) is a judgment and pronouncement of our mind about another, supported by no just foundation, by which we either add to or take away from that person. For it can happen in either way.

units.la: TEMERITAS damnatur,Prou.15.22. Temeritatis exempla : Israelitæ,Num.14.v.40.41.Deut.1.v.42.43.Iosaphat,2 Par. 20.22.Ioseph & Azarias,1 Mach.5.v.56.&c.Iosias,2 Paral. 35.22.Petrus,Matt.26.51.Thomas, Ioann.11.16.Exorcistæ, Act.19.v.13.16. Temeritatis pœnæ exempla : Israelitæ,Nu.14. 45.Deut.1.44.Iosaphat.2 Paral.20.37.Iosias, 35.23.Ioseph & Azarias,1.Macch.5.v.59.60.
units.tr: RASHNESS is condemned (Prov. 15:22). Examples of rashness: the Israelites (Num. 14:40-41; Deut. 1:42-43); Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 20:22); Joseph and Azariah (1 Macc. 5:56, etc.); Josiah (2 Chron. 35:22); Peter (Matt. 26:51); Thomas (John 11:16); the exorcists (Acts 19:13-16). Examples of the punishments of rashness: the Israelites (Num. 14:45; Deut. 1:44); Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 20:37); Josiah (2 Chron. 35:23); Joseph and Azariah (1 Macc. 5:59-60).

units.la: TEMPERANTIA,est virtus quæ animi nostri notum & affectionem in voluptatibus corporis appetendis , fugiendisque quantum Dei præceptum iubet, regit & moderatur:ne illæ precationem, meditationem ac vocationem nostram impediant.&c.
units.tr: TEMPERANCE is the virtue which governs and moderates the inclination and affection of our mind in desiring and avoiding bodily pleasures, as far as God's precept requires, so that these do not hinder our prayer, meditation and calling, etc.

units.la: TEMPERANTIA in cibo,potu & concubitu , Tob. 6.15.&c. Eccl.3.5.Eccles.31.18. & 32.7.Dan.1.v.8.11.Rom.13.13. & 14. 17.1.Cor.7.v.4.5.&c.Galat.5.23.1 Tim.3.2.2 Tim. 1.7.Tit. 1.8.& 2.v.6.12.1 Pet.1.13.& 5.8.2 Petr.1.6.
units.tr: TEMPERANCE in food, drink and sexual intercourse (Tob. 6:15, etc.; Eccles. 3:5; Ecclus. 31:18; 32:7; Dan. 1:8, 11; Rom. 13:13-14; 1 Cor. 7:4-5, etc.; Gal. 5:23; 1 Tim. 3:2; 2 Tim. 1:7; Titus 1:8; 2:6, 12; 1 Pet. 1:13; 5:8; 2 Pet. 1:6).

units.tr: TEMPEST: a violent change of the air, a very strong whirlwind; a storm; thunder (Prov. 10:25; Isa. 5:28; 17:13; 29:6; Ps. 50:2; 81:8; Jer. 4:13; Dan. 11:40; Jonah 1:4, 12; Nah. 1:3; Matt. 16:3; Luke 8:24; Acts 27:18, 20). A tempest also means a season of the year (1 Chron. 21:29; 2 Chron. 28:9; Gen. 8:22). A tempest also means the most grievous affliction by which someone is overwhelmed (Job 27:20; 36:14; 37:9; Ps. 55:9; 69:3, 16; 83:16; Isa. 54:11; Jer. 23:19; Ezek. 13:13; 27:35).
