Amos 9.1 Mich.3.12.Zach.1.12.
units.tr: TEMPLE: that court of the temple called the court of the people (Matt. 21:12). See COURT. The temple is clearly distinguished from the court (Luke 1:9). Construction of the Lord's temple begins (1 Kings 6:1-2; 1 Chron. 3:1-2): when, how long, and in what form it was built (1 Kings 6:1, etc.; 7:1, etc.; 2 Chron. 3:1, etc.; 4:1, etc.). Its construction is dedicated (1 Kings 6:19); it is completed in the reign of Solomon (1 Kings 8:63); it is filled with cloud (v. 11); it is plundered by Joash king of Israel (2 Kings 14:14); it is restored by command of Joash king of Judah (2 Chron. 24:5); it is profaned by Ahaz (28:21); consecrated by Hezekiah (29:1, etc.); profaned and again consecrated by Manasseh (33:7, 15); burned (2 Kings 25:9), as had been foretold (2 Chron. 7:20); built again (Ezra 1:3-5; chapters 5 and 6, vv. 3, 7). Its desolation (Dan. 9:26; Matt. 24:2; Mark 13:2; Luke 19:41, etc.). Prophecies against the temple (Lev. 26:31; 1 Kings 9:7; 2 Kings 21:12; 2 Chron. 7:20; Ps. 74:6; Isa. 66:1; Jer. 7:3-4, 17; 26:6, 12; Amos 9:1; Mic. 3:12; Zech. 1:12).

units.la: TEMPLVM, orationis domus,2 Par.6.21.Esa.56.7. Matth.21.13.bi oratur & exaudit Deus, 1 Reg.8.29.& 9.3.2 Par.6.19.Matth.21.13. Templum Dei, Patris domus,Ioan.2.16. Templum spirituale,& domus Dei,2 Sam.7.13. Prou.9.1. Agg.2.8.Matt.7.24.& 16.18.Ioan.2.19 1 Cor.3.16.& 6.19. 2 Cor.6.16.Eph.2.20.21.1 Tim.3.15.Hebr.3.6 1 Pet.2.5.V.
units.tr: THE TEMPLE, a house of prayer (2 Chron. 6:21; Isa. 56:7; Matt. 21:13), where God is prayed to and hears (1 Kings 8:29; 9:3; 2 Chron. 6:19; Matt. 21:13). The temple of God, the house of the Father (John 2:16). The spiritual temple and house of God (2 Sam. 7:13; Prov. 9:1; Hag. 2:8; Matt. 7:24; 16:18; John 2:19; 1 Cor. 3:16; 6:19; 2 Cor. 6:16; Eph. 2:20-21; 1 Tim. 3:15; Heb. 3:6; 1 Pet. 2:5). See CHURCH.

units.la: ECCLESIA.
units.tr: THE CHURCH.

units.la: Templum Dei, singuli fideles dicuntur, 1 Cor.3.16.& 6.19.2 Corint.6.16. ideo quod Deus per Spiritum Sanctum ipsos in Christo sanctificârit, & quasi apud eos domicilium delegerit. Eadem ratione Ecclesiae etiam idem nomen tribuitur,Eph.2.21.cum fideles omnes in vnum quasi aedificium compingantur. Templum Dei violare.i.vt rem sacram polluere ac contaminare dicuntur Paulo, 1 Cor.3.17.qui carnali facundia puritatemEuangelij inquinabant, quique factionibus scindebant Ecclesiam, quod neque sunt impune laturi. Templum sacrificiorum domus,2 Par.7.12. vestigiorum locus,Ezech.43.7. locus sanctus,Genes.28.17.Exo.3.5. spelunca latronum fit, Ier.7.11. Marc.11.17.a Chaldaeis succenditur, 2 Reg.25.9.Psal.74.7. Ierem.52.13.
units.tr: Individual believers are called the temple of God (1 Cor. 3:16; 6:19; 2 Cor. 6:16), because God has sanctified them in Christ through the Holy Spirit and, as it were, chosen them as his dwelling place. For the same reason the same name is given to the Church (Eph. 2:21), since all believers are joined together into one building. Those who pollute and defile the holy thing are said to violate the temple of God (1 Cor. 3:17). Paul means those who corrupted the purity of the Gospel with fleshly eloquence and who divided the Church into factions, and they will not escape unpunished. The temple is the house of sacrifices (2 Chr. 7:12), the place of God's footsteps (Ezek. 43:7), a holy place (Gen. 28:17; Ex. 3:5). It becomes a den of robbers (Jer. 7:11; Mark 11:17), and it is set on fire by the Chaldeans (2 Kings 25:9; Ps. 74:7; Jer. 52:13).

units.la: TEMPLI instaurandi dispositio, Ezech. 41.1. instauratio 1 Esdr.3.9. impeditur.4. ver. 4.24. continuatur, 6.14. dedicatur, ver. 16. eius destructio praecidutur, 2. Paral. 7.20.Luc.21.6. Templi secundi gloria gloriae prioris praestat, Agg. 2.3. Vide HAGGAEVS gloriam,&c. Templi profanatio,Ioan.2.14.profanatores a Deo puniuntur,Esa.56.5.Matt.21.12. Ioan.2.15. Templi religio & sanctitas.2 Reg.11.15.Marci.11.16.
units.tr: The plan for rebuilding the temple (Ezek. 41:1) and its restoration (1 Esd. 3:9) are hindered (Ezra 4:4, 24), continued (Ezra 6:14), and dedicated (Ezra 6:16). Its destruction is foretold (2 Chr. 7:20; Luke 21:6). The glory of the second temple surpasses the glory of the first (Hag. 2:3). See HAGGAI, glory, etc. The profanation of the temple (John 2:14) and its profaners are punished by God (Isa. 56:5; Matt. 21:12; John 2:15). The reverence and holiness of the temple (2 Kings 11:15; Mark 11:16).

units.la: TEMPLA manu facta non inhabitat Deus, quasi iis concludi possit, vel illis indigeat, vt homo aedibus, 1 Reg 8.27. 2 Par.6.18.Esa.66.1.Ierem.23.24. Act.7.48.& 17.24. alioquin Deus in templis materialibus habitare dicitur. 1 Reg 6.13.& 8.12.1 Par.23.25.Psalm.78.60.& 132.13.Ier.7.v.3.7. Mat.23.21.Act.7.46. Templa idolorum.1 Sam.5.2.& 31.9. 1 Reg.11.7.2 Reg.10.21.& 17.32.& 19.37.1 Par.11.10. Esa.37.38.Ier.43.12.Dan.14.1.&c. Act.19.27.
units.tr: God does not dwell in temples made by hands, as if he could be confined in them or needed them, as a man needs a house (1 Kings 8:27; 2 Chr. 6:18; Isa. 66:1; Jer. 23:24; Acts 7:48; 17:24). Otherwise God is said to dwell in material temples (1 Kings 6:13; 8:12; 1 Chr. 23:25; Ps. 78:60; 132:13; Jer. 7:3, 7; Matt. 23:21; Acts 7:46). Temples of idols (1 Sam. 5:2; 31:9; 1 Kings 11:7; 2 Kings 10:21; 17:32; 19:37; 1 Chr. 11:10; Isa. 37:38; Jer. 43:12; Dan. 14:1, etc.; Acts 19:27).

units.la: TEMPLORVM vsus,Esa.56.7.sanctus,V.Eccles.5.1. in TEMPLO frequenter versabantur Christus & fideles. Marth. Matt.24.1 Marc.11.11.& 13.45. Luc.2.37.& 19.45. Act.2.46.& 3.1 & 5.v.20.21.& 21.26.& 22.17.
units.tr: The use of temples (Isa. 56:7) and their holiness (see Eccl. 5:1). Christ and the faithful frequently spent time in the temple (Matt. 24:1; Mark 11:11; 13:1; Luke 2:37; 19:45; Acts 2:46; 3:1; 5:20-21; 21:26; 22:17).

units.la: TEMPVS, pro certo temporis articulo. Matth.16.3. rebus omnibus constitutum, Eccles.3.1. &c. tempus redimendum, Ephes.5.16. Coloss.4.5. tempus Euangelij,2 Cor.6.2. tempus extremum,1 Corint.10.11. Hebr.1.v.1.2.& 9.26.1 Petr. 1.v.5.20.1 Ioan. 2.18. tempus extremum periculosum, & Antichristi seductionibus obnoxium,2 Timo.3.1.2 Pet.2. 2.Iudae v.17.18. Tempus horae, pro exiguo temporis interuallo, 1 Thessal.2.17. tempus plenitudinis,pro pleno tempore,& eo cuius sunt omnia peracta spacia, Galat.4. 4. Ephes.1.10. Vide PLENITVDO temporum. Tempus praesens pro praeterito,1 Ioan.2.8. tempus praesens pro futuro,Coloss.3.6.1 Thessal. 4.15. praeteritum pro praesenti, Roman.8.29.30.praeteritum pro futuro,Esa.65.1 Rom.10. 21.Iudae v.14.
units.tr: TIME, for a certain moment of time (Matt. 16:3); the appointed time for all things (Eccl. 3:1, etc.); to redeem the time (Eph. 5:16; Col. 4:5); the time of the Gospel (2 Cor. 6:2); the last time (1 Cor. 10:11; Heb. 1:1-2; 9:26; 1 Pet. 1:5, 20; 1 John 2:18); the last time is dangerous and exposed to the seductions of the Antichrist (2 Tim. 3:1; 2 Pet. 2:2; Jude 17-18). Time of an hour, for a brief interval of time (1 Thess. 2:17). The fullness of time, for the full time and for that by which all the spans of time were completed (Gal. 4:4; Eph. 1:10). See FULNESS of times. The present time for the past (1 John 2:8); the present time for the future (Col. 3:6; 1 Thess. 4:15); the past for the present (Rom. 8:29-30); the past for the future (Isa. 65:1; Rom. 10:21; Jude 14).

units.la: TEMPORIS habenda ratio, Gal.6.10. Exemplum: Gedeon,Iudi. 6.27.tempore vtendum, & temporis opportunitas in omnibus seruanda,Eccl.3.1.& 8.5.Eccl.20.6.& 32.20.Rom. 12.11.V. OCCASIO arripienda.
units.tr: TIME, taking account of time (Gal. 6:10). Example: Gideon (Judg. 6:27). One must make use of time, and the opportunity of the moment must be kept in all things (Eccl. 3:1; 8:5; Eccl. 20:6; 32:20; Rom. 12:11). See OPPORTUNITY, to be seized.

units.la: TEMPORA secularia, 2 Tim. 1.9.Tit.1.2. ita vocari existimatur à plerisque annorum series, qui à seculorum origine fluxerunt,vt idem prorsus significet.(Ante tempora seculorum) atque, Ante iacta mundi fundamenta: si quidem tempus cum mundo coepit. temporum ciulis obseruatio non vituperanda,Gen.1.14. superstitiosa obseruatio damnatur,Galat.4 10.Coloss.2.16. vicissitudo à Deo, Genes.8, 22. tempora distincta,1.14.& 8.22. nosse non est nostrum. Act. 1.7.
units.tr: TIMES, secular times (2 Tim. 1:9; Titus 1:2). By many people this is thought to mean the succession of years which have flowed from the beginning of the ages, so that the phrase means exactly the same as "before the foundations of the world were laid," since time began together with the world. The observance of seasons is not to be condemned (Gen. 1:14); superstitious observance is condemned (Gal. 4:10; Col. 2:16). The changing of seasons comes from God (Gen. 8:22). The times are distinct (Gen. 1:14; 8:22). To know them is not our business (Acts 1:7).

units.la: TENACITAS φειδωλία, Est metus vel dolor vllius omnino pecuniae in re honesta & necessaria effundendae: vel quantum satis est conferendae: qualis est quam damnat Paulus 2, Cor.9 6.Qui parce serit,parce metet. TENACITAS, V. AVARITIA.
units.tr: TENACITY (φειδωλία) [pheidōlia]. It is a fear or grief at spending any money at all, whether in an honourable and necessary matter, or beyond what is enough to contribute. Such is the tenacity that Paul condemns (2 Cor. 9:6): "He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly." See TENACITY, and AVARICE.

units.la: TENEBRAE,Gen.1.4.sunt merè priuatio lucis creatae.
units.tr: DARKNESS (Gen. 1:4) is merely the privation of created light.

units.la: TENEBRAE palpabiles in Ægypto, Vide MIRACVLA, tenebrae exteriores, Matth. 8.12. & 22.13.& 25.30. super terram vniuersam, Vide MIRACVLA. tenebrae Gentes, Ephes.5.8.nullae sunt in Deo,1 Ioan.1.5.tenebrarum appellatione in genere apud Hebraeos intelligitur calamitas, 2 Sam.22.29.Eccl.5.17.& 6.4 Esai.45.7.Sophon.1.15. Lucis nomine vicissim liberatio ex ea, & felicitas, quae illam consequitur. V. Luc.1.79. item regnum cœleste & gloriosum. Phi.1.12. Ponitur etiam tenebrarum nomen pro hominis mente, qualis post lapsum euasit, Ioan.1.5. Luc.1.79. Act.26.18. Eph.4.18. & 5.v.8.11. tenebræ, Sepulchrum, Iob 10.22. Psalm.88.13. tenebræ, Luci æternæ & beatissimæ, quae Deus est, opponuntur, 1 Ioan.1.5. Item tenebræ sumuntur pro pœnis illis æternæ felicitati oppositis, Matth. 8.12.8. 22.13. & 25.30. 2 Petr.2.17. Iud.v.13. tenebrarum opera quae sint, Roman.13.12. Vide Opera tenebrarum in tenebris, in impietate, in iniustitia, in intemperantia, versatur mundus, & amat eas, Esa.9.1. & 59.9. & 60.2. Ioan.1.5. & 3.19. & 8.12. & 12.35. Act.26.17. 1 Thess.5.7.1 Ioan.2.11. Vide Caligo.
units.tr: DARKNESS: palpable darkness in Egypt, see MIRACLES; outer darkness (Matt. 8:12; 22:13; 25:30); over the whole earth, see MIRACLES. The Gentiles are darkness (Eph. 5:8). There is no darkness in God (1 John 1:5). By the name of darkness, among the Hebrews, calamity is generally understood (2 Sam. 22:29; Eccl. 5:17; 6:4; Isa. 45:7; Zeph. 1:15). By the name of light, in turn, deliverance from it and the happiness that follows it (see Luke 1:79), and also the heavenly and glorious kingdom (Phil. 1:12). The name of darkness is also used for the mind of man, such as it became after the fall (John 1:5; Luke 1:79; Acts 26:18; Eph. 4:18; 5:8, 11). Darkness: the sepulchre (Job 10:22; Ps. 88:13). Darkness is opposed to eternal and most blessed light, which God is (1 John 1:5). Likewise darkness is taken for those punishments set against eternal happiness (Matt. 8:12; 22:13; 25:30; 2 Pet. 2:17; Jude 13). What the works of darkness are (Rom. 13:12); see Works of darkness. The world is occupied in darkness, in impiety, in injustice, in intemperance, and loves them (Isa. 9:1; 59:9; 60:2; John 1:5; 3:19; 8:12; 12:35; Acts 26:17; 1 Thess. 5:7; 1 John 2:11). See Caligo [gloom].

units.la: TENTARE Deum quid, Act.15.10.
units.tr: WHAT IT IS TO TEMPT GOD

units.la: tentare Deum non licet. Exod.14.11. & 17.2. Deut.6.16. Iudith.8.11. Matt.4.7. 1 Cor.10.9. tentare Christum, 1 Corinth.10.9. est, eum velut ad certamen provocare, ut explicatur ibidem, vers.22. tentat seu verius probat & explorat Deus suos variis modis, Gen.22.1. &c. Exodi 15.25. & 16.4. & 20.20. Deut.8.2. & 13.3. Iud.c.2.22. & 3.1.2. Paral 32.31. Iob.1.12. Zach.13.9. Roma.5.4. Iac.1.2.2 Petr.2.9. Vide Deus neminem, ut malum operetur, tentat. tentari non patitur Deus suos supra quod possunt, 1 Cor.10.13. 2 Petr.2.9. Apocal.2.10. tentat Satan. i. ad malum solicitat: unde & tentator dicitur. Mat.4.3.
units.tr: It is not lawful to tempt God (Ex. 14:11; 17:2; Deut. 6:16; Judith 8:11; Matt. 4:7; 1 Cor. 10:9). To tempt Christ (1 Cor. 10:9) is to provoke him, as it were, to a contest, as is explained in the same place, verse 22. God tests, or rather proves and examines, his people in various ways (Gen. 22:1, etc.; Ex. 15:25; 16:4; 20:20; Deut. 8:2; 13:3; Judg. 2:22; 3:1-2; 2 Chr. 32:31; Job 1:12; Zech. 13:9; Rom. 5:4; James 1:2; 2 Pet. 2:9). See that God tempts no one to do evil. God does not allow his people to be tempted beyond what they can bear (1 Cor. 10:13; 2 Pet. 2:9; Rev. 2:10). Satan tempts, that is, solicits to evil, and hence he is called the tempter (Matt. 4:3).

units.la: TENTATIO, pro eo omni quod nos solicitat, 1 Cor.10.13.
units.tr: TENTATION, used for anything that stirs us up to sin, 1 Cor. 10:13.

units.la: pro ad malum solicitare, Iacob.1.13. pro afflictione & rebus aduersis, quibus exploratur fides, 1 vers.2.3.12. 2 Petr.2.9. pro experimento, vel probatione, Heb.2.18. pro irritamento, 3. vers.8.9. tentatio mala à Satana proficiscitur. Matth.26.41. Act.5.3. tentationis diabolicæ Exempla: in Eua, Gene.3. vers.1.3.4. 2 Cor.11.3. Dauide, 1 Paralip.21.1. Iobo, Iob.1.11. & 2.7. Christo. Matth.4.3. Petro, Luc.22.31. Iuda proditore, Ioan.13.2. Ananias, Actor.5.3. tentare iubemur nos ipsos, num simus in fide, 2 Corinth.13.5. tentationes ad malum non esse à Deo, Iac.1.13. tentatio humana, 1 Cor.10.13. dicitur illa, quæ ab imbecillitate humana proficiscitur. tentationes pro lucro ducendæ, Iac.1.2. nouit Dominus pios ex tentationibus eripere. 2 Petr.2.9. nec sint eos supra modum tentari, 1 Cor.10.13. 2 Petr.2.9. Apoc.2.10.
units.tr: Used for stirring someone to evil, James 1:13; for affliction and adversity, by which faith is tested, James 1:2, 3, 12; 1 Pet. 2:9; for an experiment or trial, Heb. 2:18; for an incitement, James 1:8, 9. Evil temptation comes from Satan: Matt. 26:41; Acts 5:3. Examples of diabolical temptation: in Eve, Gen. 3:1, 3, 4; 2 Cor. 11:3; in David, 1 Chron. 21:1; in Job, Job 1:11 and 2:7; in Christ, Matt. 4:3; in Peter, Luke 22:31; in Judas the traitor, John 13:2; in Ananias, Acts 5:3. We are commanded to test ourselves, whether we are in the faith, 2 Cor. 13:5. Temptations to evil do not come from God, James 1:13. Human temptation, 1 Cor. 10:13, is the name for that which arises from human weakness. Temptations are to be counted as gain, James 1:2. The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from temptations, 2 Pet. 2:9, and does not allow them to be tempted beyond what they can bear, 1 Cor. 10:13; 2 Pet. 2:9; Rev. 2:10.

units.la: Tentat Deus homines, ut Abrahamum Israelitas, suos vavariis modis. 2. tentat Christus hominem, Ioann.6.6. 3. Homo tentat Deum, vt populus Israeliticus sæpiß. in deserto,4. Christus sæpius tentatus legitur à suis aduersariis, Pharisæis nempe, Sadducæis, & aliis.5. tentat homo hominem, vt Salomon tentatus est à regina Sabæ. 1 Reg.10. 1.6. Homo tentat seipsum, 2 Corint.13.5. 7.tentatur à lua concupiscentia,Iacob 1.v.13.14. 8. Diabolus tentat Christum,& homines,Matt.4.1.Act.5.3.1 Cor.7.5.1 Thessal.3.5. Apoc.3.10.
units.tr: God tempts men, as he tempted Abraham and the Israelites, in various ways. (2) Christ tempts a man, John 6:6. (3) A man tempts God, as the Israelite people often did in the desert. (4) Christ is read of as tempted often by his adversaries, namely the Pharisees, the Sadducees and others. (5) A man tempts a man, as Solomon was tempted by the queen of Sheba, 1 Kings 10:1. (6) A man tempts himself, 2 Cor. 13:5. (7) A man is tempted by his own concupiscence, James 1:13, 14. (8) The devil tempts Christ and men, Matt. 4:1; Acts 5:3; 1 Cor. 7:5; 1 Thess. 3:5; Rev. 3:10.

units.la: Tentatus est Christus,Hebr.2.18.& 4.15. tentantur fideles,1 Cor.10.13.Galat.6.1 Hebr.2.18.& 11.v.16.37.]
units.tr: Christ was tempted, Heb. 2:18 and 4:15. The faithful are tempted, 1 Cor. 10:13; Gal. 6:1; Heb. 2:18 and 11:16, 37.

units.la: TENTATORVM,déque fructu tentationis. exempla: Abraham,Gen.22.1.Hebr.11.17.Iacob : lucta Iacobi fuit quædam tentatio, Genes.32.24. Israelitæ, Exodi 15.25.& 16.4. Deut.8.v.2.16.& 13.3.Iudic.2.22. & 3.1. Ezechias, 2 Paral. 32.31.Dauid,Psal.26.2.&119.71.Paulum quoque expertum esse spirituales tentationes,& ignita Diaboli tela, promtum est colligere ex his locis,2 Cor.2.11.& 7.5. & 10. 4. & 12.7.Eph.6.12. 1 Thess.2.18.
units.tr: OF THOSE WHO ARE TEMPTED, and on the fruit of temptation. Examples: Abraham, Gen. 22:1; Heb. 11:17. Jacob: his wrestling was a kind of temptation, Gen. 32:24. The Israelites, Exod. 15:25 and 16:4; Deut. 8:2, 16 and 13:3; Judg. 2:22 and 3:1. Hezekiah, 2 Chron. 32:31. David, Ps. 26:2 and 119:71. It is easy to gather from these passages that Paul too experienced spiritual temptations and the fiery darts of the devil: 2 Cor. 2:11; 7:5; 10:4; 12:7; Eph. 6:12; 1 Thess. 2:18.

units.la: TENTORIVM pro Ecclesia aspectabili,Psal.15.1.tentorij forma, Exod. 26.36.
units.tr: TENT, used for the visible Church, Ps. 15:1. The form of the tent, Exod. 26:36.

units.la: [Tentorium Dei,Iob.36.29.tentorium mysticum,Esai. 54.2 Ierem.10.20. Thren.2.6.]
units.tr: [The tent of God, Job 36:29. The mystical tent, Isa. 54:2; Jer. 10:20; Lam. 2:6.]

units.la: TEPIDOS Deus euomit,Apo.3.v.15.16.
units.tr: God vomits the lukewarm, Rev. 3:15, 16.

units.la: TER,pro,sæpe,2 Cor.12.8.
units.tr: TIMES, that is, often, 2 Cor. 12:8.

units.la: TERMINI agrorum non transferendi, Deuter.19.14.&27.17. Prou.22.28.& 23.10.
units.tr: Boundary-stones of fields not to be moved, Deut. 19:14 and 27:17; Prov. 22:28 and 23:10.

units.la: TERNARIVS numerus,Vide NVMERVS ternarius.
units.tr: TERNARY number. See the entry NUMBER, the ternary.

units.la: TERRA,à Deo creata,Genes.1.1.Iob.38.4.5.6. Esai.40.12. super aquas fundata.Psal.24.2. & 136.6. 2 Petr.3.5. quorsum creata,Exod.9.29.& 19.5.Deuter.10 14.Psalm.24.1.Esa.45. 18 Psam. 115.16. ob peccatum hominis maledicta, Genes. 3.17.& 5.29.pedum Dei scabellum,Esa.66.1.Matth.5.35. Actor.7,49.stabilis & firma, Psalm.104.5.Eccles.1.4. D.suspendit terram super nihilum, Iob.26.7.terra exurenda,2 Petr.3,10.terra nova expectanda, Esai.65.17. 2 Petr. 3.13.Apocalyp.21.1. Terra Chanaan, Vide CHANAAN. terra pro ipsis incolis metonymicè,Genes.6.11. & 9.13.& 41.57.2 Samu.15.23.Esai.37.18. pro proventu, Genes.3 17. terra,Græcis γῆ, pro regione,Matth.9.26.Luc.4.25. Marc. 15.33.terra bibens imbrem, Hebr.6.7.terra Dei, (Psalm. 85.1.) peculiariter dicta, terra Israeli à Deo tradita. terra omnis Dei, Exod. 9.29. & 19.5. Psalm.24.1. 1 Corinth. 10.26.
units.tr: EARTH, created by God, Gen. 1:1; Job 38:4, 5, 6; Isa. 40:12. Founded upon the waters, Ps. 24:2 and 136:6; 2 Pet. 3:5. Why it was created: Exod. 9:29 and 19:5; Deut. 10:14; Ps. 24:1; Isa. 45:18; Ps. 115:16. Cursed on account of man's sin, Gen. 3:17 and 5:29. God's footstool, Isa. 66:1; Matt. 5:35; Acts 7:49. Stable and firm, Ps. 104:5; Eccles. 1:4. God hangs the earth upon nothing, Job 26:7. The earth is to be burned, 2 Pet. 3:10. A new earth is to be expected, Isa. 65:17; 2 Pet. 3:13; Rev. 21:1. The land of Canaan, see CANAAN. Earth is put by metonymy for its inhabitants, Gen. 6:11; 9:13; 41:57; 2 Sam. 15:23; Isa. 37:18. For produce, Gen. 3:17. Earth, in Greek [γῆ], for a region, Matt. 9:26; Luke 4:25; Mark 15:33. The earth that drinks in rain, Heb. 6:7. The land of God (Ps. 85:1) is spoken of in a special sense: the land given by God to Israel. All the earth is God's, Exod. 9:29 and 19:5; Ps. 24:1; 1 Cor. 10:26.

units.la: Terræ motus exempla: tempore Ozię regis, Amos 1.1 Zac. 14.5. tempore passionis & expirationis Christi, Matth.27. 54. tempore resurrectionis Christi, 28.2. tempore Pauli & Silæ incarceratorum, Actor. 16.26. Vide & Apoc. 6.12. & 8. 5. & 11.13. & 16.18. terræ transitus, Matth. 5.18. Luc. 21.33. terræ venditio, quomodo facienda, Leuit. 25.v.23.24. a terra esse dicitur is (Ioan. 3.31.) qui nihil aliud est, quàm homo terræ videlicet fœcis opificium. in terram reuertetur homo, Gen. 3.19.
units.tr: Examples of earthquakes: in the time of King Uzziah, Amos 1:1; Zech. 14:5. At the time of Christ's passion and death, Matt. 27:54. At the time of Christ's resurrection, Matt. 28:2. At the time of Paul and Silas being in prison, Acts 16:26. See also Rev. 6:12; 8:5; 11:13; 16:18. The passing of the earth, Matt. 5:18; Luke 21:33. The sale of land, how it is to be done, Lev. 25:23, 24. He who is of the earth (John 3:31) is said to be from the earth, that is, nothing but a man, a creature of earthly dregs. Man shall return to the earth, Gen. 3:19.

units.la: <bl>TERRAE</bl> à quibus diuisæ, Gen. 10.5.
units.tr: TERRAE (lands) from which they were divided, Gen. 10:5.

units.la: [TERRAE varias acceptiones ita distinctè enumeramus.
units.tr: [We set out the various meanings of TERRA as follows.

units.la: 1. Terra generaliter significat totam hanc inferiorem & elementarem regionem. 2. Proprie, istud terræ elementum, quod partim aquis alluitur & rigatur, partim ab hominibus incolitur. 3. Specialius accipitur pro regione vel provincia aliqua, seu terræ particula, vt terra Ægypti, Chanaam, Ammonitarum, Chaldæorum, &c. 4 Nonnunquam pro infimo loco, sicut cælum pro summo. 5. Aliquando illam proprie regionem designat, de qua in contextu sermo habetur, vt Genes. 13.6. & 34.10. & 36.7.2 Paral. 22.12. & alibi. Circumiacentes regiones denotat, vt 2.Par. 9 v.22.23. &c. 7. Sumitur pro exigua quadam portione & breui spatio in regione aliqua, vt Genes. 23.15. & alibi passim. Item signif. paululum terræ ex qua aliquid compingitur, vt Exod. 20.24. & alibi. 8. Superficies terræ, in qua quis agit aut patitur aliquid, vt Gen. 33.3. Exod. 34.8. &c.
units.tr: 1. Terra generally means this whole lower, elemental region. 2. Properly, that element of earth which is partly washed and watered by waters and partly inhabited by men. 3. More specifically, it is taken for some particular region or province, or a part of the earth, as the land of Egypt, of Canaan, of the Ammonites, of the Chaldeans, etc. 4. Sometimes it means the lowest place, as heaven means the highest. 5. Sometimes it designates that particular region of which the discussion in the context speaks, as Gen. 13:6; 34:10; 36:7; 2 Chron. 22:12, and elsewhere. It denotes the neighbouring regions, as 2 Chron. 9:22, 23, etc. 7. It is taken for a small portion and brief space in some region, as Gen. 23:15 and elsewhere everywhere. Likewise it signifies a little piece of earth from which something is put together, as Exod. 20:24 and elsewhere. 8. The surface of the earth on which someone acts or suffers something, as Gen. 33:3; Exod. 34:8, etc.]

units.la: Terra, metonymicè sumitur pro hominibus terram incolentibus, Iosu. 14.15. & 23.14. Iudic. 5.31. 1 Samuel. 14.29. Psalm. 2.10. & 66.1. & 100. 1 Prouerb. 28. 2. Terra mystica, Ecclesia, Cantic. 2.12. Esai. 49.8. & 51.16. Terra noua, 1. instauratio & salus Ecclesiæ, Esai. 65.17. & 66.22. Apoc. 21.1.
units.tr: Earth, by metonymy, is taken for the men who inhabit the land, Josh. 14:15 and 23:14; Judg. 5:31; 1 Sam. 14:29; Ps. 2:10 and 66:1 and 100; Prov. 28:2. Mystical earth is the Church, Song 2:12; Isa. 49:8 and 51:16. New earth means: 1. the renewal and salvation of the Church, Isa. 65:17 and 66:22; Rev. 21:1.

units.la: <bl>TERRENUS</bl> primus homo, 1 Corin. 15.47. terrena dicere, est crasso & plebeio stylo uti, Ioan. 3.12.
units.tr: EARTHLY: the first man, 1 Cor. 15:47. To speak of earthly things is to use a crude and common style, John 3:12.

units.la: <bl>TERRIBILIS</bl> Deus noster, Deut. 10.17. Ps. 76.8. &c. & 96.4. & 99.3. Dan. 9.4. terribilis, formidabilis Ecclesia, Cant. 6.v.4. 10. Bestia mystica, Dan. 2.31. & 7.7. 19.
units.tr: TERRIBLE: our God, Deut. 10:17; Ps. 76:8, etc., and 96:4 and 99:3; Dan. 9:4. The terrible, formidable Church, Song 6:4, 10. The mystical beast, Dan. 2:31 and 7:7, 19.

units.la: <bl>TERTIVS</bl>, Epistolæ ad Rom. amanuensis. Rom. 16.22.
units.tr: TERTIUS, amanuensis of the Epistle to the Romans, Rom. 16:22.

units.la: <bl>TERTVLLIVS</bl> orator, Act. 24.1. eius in Paulum actio, v.2. &c.
units.tr: TERTULLUS the orator, Acts 24:1; his speech against Paul, v. 2, etc.

units.la: TESTAMENTVM, Gal.4.24. Hebr.9 1. & 13.20.
units.tr: TESTAMENT, Gal. 4:24; Heb. 9:1 and 13:20.

units.la: TESTAMENTVM vetus, Genes. 12.7. Hebr.9.verf.4.18. Exod. 24.8. Testamentum vetus, sanguine dedicatum, Exod. 24. 8. Hebr.9.18.20. Testamentum vetus corrigitur, Hebr. 8. 13. Testamentum vetus apud Hebraeos in tres ordines diuiditur: in Torah, legem, Nebiim, Prophetas, & Cherubim, hoc est, scripta siue Hagiographa. Citatur secunda illa sectio veteris Testamenti, cuius pars est Esaias, Ioann. 6.45. testamenti veteris repetitio, Iosu.24.20. &c. Testamentum nouum a Christo sancitum, Hebr.8.6. Vide Novum Testamentum testamenti veteris & noui discrimen, Ierem.31.31. Matth.26.28. 1 Corint.11.25.2 Corinth. 3.6.6. Hebr.8. verfic.8.9.10. Vide Legis & Euangelij discrimen.
units.tr: The OLD TESTAMENT, Gen. 12:7; Heb. 9:4, 18; Exod. 24:8. The Old Testament dedicated with blood, Exod. 24:8; Heb. 9:18, 20. The Old Testament is corrected, Heb. 8:13. Among the Hebrews the Old Testament is divided into three orders: the Torah, the Law; the Nebiim, the Prophets; and the Cherubim, that is, the Writings or Hagiographa. That second section of the Old Testament, of which Isaiah is a part, is cited at John 6:45. Repetition of the Old Testament covenant, Josh. 24:20, etc. The New Testament sanctioned by Christ, Heb. 8:6. See NEW TESTAMENT. The difference between the Old and New Testaments: Jer. 31:31; Matt. 26:28; 1 Cor. 11:25; 2 Cor. 3:6; Heb. 8:8, 9, 10. See the difference between Law and Gospel.

units.la: TESTICVLI attriti, Deuter.23.1. Leuitic.22.24. tum hominis, tum bestiae.
units.tr: TESTICLES crushed, Deut. 23:1; Lev. 22:24, both of man and of beast.

units.la: TESTIMONIVM verum commendatur, Proverb. 14. 5.25. falsum prohibetur, Exod.20.16. & 23.1 Deut.5.20. Proverb.6. 19. & 14.5. & 19.5. & 21.28. Luc. 18.20. Vide MENDACIVM.
units.tr: TESTIMONY: true testimony is commended, Prov. 14:5, 25; false testimony is forbidden, Exod. 20:16 and 23:1; Deut. 5:20; Prov. 6:19, 14:5, 19:5, 21:28; Luke 18:20. See LIE.

units.la: TESTIS in iudicio singulus non sufficit: teste enim vno nemo occidendus est, Numer.35.30 Deuteron.17.6. & 19.15. Matth.18.16. testis falsus, quomodo puniendus, Deuter. 19.verf.16. &c. Proverb.19.verf.5 9 testes falsi quibus similes Proverb.25.18. Testimonij falsi exempla: Doeg aduersus Dauidem, 1 Sam 22.9. Psal.35.11.12. Sibae aduersus Miphiboseth, 2 Sam.16.3. Duorum testium aduersus Naboth, 1 Reg.21.13. Ieriae aduersus Ieremiam, Ier.37.12. principum Sedechiae aduersus Ieremiam, 38.4. duorum falsorum testium aduersus Christum, Matt.26.60.&c. falsorum testium aduersus Stephanum. Act.6.v.11.13. & Paulum 24.5 9.
units.tr: A single witness is not sufficient in judgment: for no one is to be put to death on one witness, Num. 35:30; Deut. 17:6 and 19:15; Matt. 18:16. How a false witness is to be punished, Deut. 19:16, etc.; Prov. 19:5, 9. False witnesses are like those in Prov. 25:18. Examples of false testimony: Doeg against David, 1 Sam. 22:9; Ps. 35:11, 12. Ziba against Mephibosheth, 2 Sam. 16:3. Two witnesses against Naboth, 1 Kings 21:13. Jeriah against Jeremiah, Jer. 37:12. The princes of Zedekiah against Jeremiah, Jer. 38:4. Two false witnesses against Christ, Matt. 26:60, etc. False witnesses against Stephen, Acts 6:11, 13; and against Paul, Acts 24:5, 9.

units.la: THABOR, mons in medio Galilaeae campo, mira sublimis rtunditate: Psal.88.13. Vertex eius campestris 23. stadiis iacet V. Ier. 46.18. In hoc monte Saluator transfiguratus est, plerique putant. Mat.17.1.
units.tr: THABOR, a mountain in the middle of the plain of Galilee, of remarkable lofty roundness: Ps. 89:12. Its summit lies five miles (twenty-three stadia) from the plain. Jer. 46:18. Many think the Saviour was transfigured on this mountain, Matt. 17:1.

units.la: THADDAEVS, V. LEBBAEVS.
units.tr: THADDAEUS: see LEBBAEUS.

units.la: THALAMI filij, V. FILII Thalami.
units.tr: SONS OF THE BRIDE-CHAMBER: see SONS OF THE BRIDE-CHAMBER.

units.la: THAMAR, Iudae nurus, Genes.38.6. meretricem se simulat, v. 14. vt meretrix a socero de amore solicitatur, v.25. cum illo commercium habet, v.18. igni adiudicatur, v.24. absolvitur. v.25.26. gemellos parit, v.27. (i. palma arbor.)
units.tr: THAMAR, daughter-in-law of Judah, Gen. 38:6. She pretends to be a harlot, v. 14. Being solicited by her father-in-law as a harlot concerning love, v. 25. She has intercourse with him, v. 18. She is condemned to the fire, v. 24, and is acquitted, v. 25, 26. She bears twins, v. 27. (That is, palm tree.)

units.la: THAMAR Absalonis soror ab Ammon deperitur, 2 Samu.13. i. vitium ab illo oblatum recusat, v. 11. 12. eius pudor vi expugnatur. v. 14. stuprator eius trucidatur. v. 22. &c.
units.tr: THAMAR, sister of Absalom, is burned with love for Ammon, 2 Sam. 13. She refuses the vice offered by him, v. 11, 12. Her modesty is overcome by force, v. 14. Her ravisher is slain, v. 22, etc.

units.la: THAMAR Absalonis filia fortissima, 2 Sam. 14. 27.
units.tr: THAMAR, very brave daughter of Absalom, 2 Sam. 14:27.

units.la: THAMMVZ, idolum, V. IDOLORVM Catalogus.
units.tr: THAMMUZ, an idol: see the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: THARE, filios Nachor, Gen. 11. 24. Abram, Nachor, & Aram generat, v. 26. idolis seruiuit, Ios. 24. 2. eius anni, Gen. 11. 32. (Tharah, i. respiratio.)
units.tr: THARAH, the father of the sons of Nahor, Gen. 11:24. He begets Abram, Nahor and Haran, v. 26. He served idols, Josh. 24:2. The years of his life, Gen. 11:32. (Tharah, that is, breathing.)

units.la: THARSIS, filius Iauan, Gen. 10. 4. a quo Tarsus vrbs Ciciliae condita esse existimatur : unde Paulus oriundus erat Act. 21. 39. & 22. 3. Hinc naues Tharsis, i. maris mediterranei, quo plurimum Tharienses vtebantur. Saepe etiam simpliciter mare hac voce significatur. 1 Reg. 2. 22. 2 Para. 9. 21. (Tharsis, i. Chrysolithus, vel hyacinthus.)
units.tr: THARSHISH, son of Javan, Gen. 10. 4., from whom the city of Tarsus in Cilicia is thought to have been founded; Paul was a native of it, Acts 21. 39. and 22. 3. Hence "ships of Tarshish" means ships of the Mediterranean, which the Tarshishites used most. This word often signifies the sea in general, 1 Kings 2. 22.; 2 Chron. 9. 21. (Tarshish, i.e. chrysolite or hyacinth.)

units.la: THARTAK idolum, V. IDOLORVM Catalogus.
units.tr: THARTAK, an idol; see the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: THAV, Vide SIGNATI seruantur, & Piorum nota. Ezec. 9. 4.
units.tr: THAV; see MARKED, those who are preserved, and the sign of the godly. Ezek. 9. 4.

units.la: THEBES ciuitas, ab Abimelech obsidetur, Iudic. 9. 50. in eius obsidione perit Abimelech, v. 53. 2 Sam. 11. 21.
units.tr: Thebes, a city, is besieged by Abimelech, Judg. 9. 50.; in its siege Abimelech dies, v. 53.; 2 Sam. 11. 21.

units.la: TNEBIN, Gineth filius, in regno Israelitico ambiendo competitor Amri, 1 Reg. 16. 21. occubuit, v. 22.
units.tr: Tibni, son of Ginath, a rival of Omri in the contest for the kingdom of Israel, 1 Kings 16. 21.; he perished, v. 22.

units.la: THECVITIS mulier adit Regem Dauidem, 2 Samu. 14. 2. &c. (tuba canens.)
units.tr: The woman of Tekoa comes to King David, 2 Sam. 14. 2. etc. (sounding the trumpet.)

units.la: THEGLATHPILESER, rex Assur, vniuersam Nephtali terram subegit, & transtulit populum in Assyriam, 2. Reg. 15. 29. Iudam vastat, 2 Paral. 28. 20. 1 Par. 5. 6.
units.tr: Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, subdued the whole land of Naphtali and carried the people off into Assyria, 2 Kings 15. 29.; he ravaged Judah, 2 Chron. 28. 20.; 1 Chron. 5. 6.

units.la: THEOPHILVS, vir primariae nobilitatis & virtutibus insignis. Huic vtrumque suum librum inscribit Lucas, Luc. 1. 3. Act. 1. 1. (i. Deo dilectus.)
units.tr: THEOPHILUS, a man of the highest nobility and distinguished for his virtues. Luke inscribes both of his books to him, Luke 1. 3.; Acts 1. 1. (i.e. beloved of God.)

units.la: HARAPHIM idolum, V. IDOLORVM Catalogus.
units.tr: TERAPHIM, an idol; see the catalogue of IDOLS.

units.la: THESAVRVS, pro penu siue cella, Matth. 13. 52. thesaurus verus quis, Esa. 33. 6. Ierem. 9. 23. Matt. 6. 20. Luc. 6. 45. & 12. 33. & 18. 22. 1 Timo. 6. versi. 18. 19. thesaurus minus diligendus, magis diligitur, Ose. 9. 1 Matth. 6. 19. & 19. 22. Marc. 10. 22. Luc. 12. v. 22 33. & 18. 23. Ioan. 6. 26. 2 Corint. 4. 8. thesaurus Euangelij in vasis fictilibus. 2 Cor. 4. 7. thesauri parabola, Matth. 13. 44. Vide PARABOLA. thesauri sapientiae & scientiae, omnes in Christo abscondidi, Coloss. 2. 3. thesauri impietatis noxij, Mich. 6. 10. In thesaurizantes, Luc. 12. 16. &c. Deus custodientibus Legem thesaurum suum aperit. Deut. 28. 12.
units.tr: TREASURE: for a storeroom or cellar, Matt. 13. 52.; true treasure, Isa. 33. 6.; Jer. 9. 23.; Matt. 6. 20.; Luke 6. 45.; 12. 33.; 18. 22.; 1 Tim. 6. 18–19. Treasure less to be loved yet more loved, Hos. 9.; Matt. 6. 19.; 19. 22.; Mark 10. 22.; Luke 12. 22, 33.; 18. 23.; John 6. 26.; 2 Cor. 4. 8. The treasure of the gospel in earthen vessels, 2 Cor. 4. 7. The parable of the treasure, Matt. 13. 44. See PARABLE. The treasures of wisdom and knowledge are all hidden in Christ, Col. 2. 3. The treasures of harmful impiety, Mic. 6. 10. Those who store up treasure, Luke 12. 16. etc. God opens his treasure to those who keep the Law, Deut. 28. 12.

units.la: THESSALONICAE Christum annuntiat Paulus, Act. 17. 3.
units.tr: THESSALONICA: Paul proclaims Christ there, Acts 17. 3.

units.la: THESSALONICENSES Paulo charissimi, 1 Thessal. 2. 8. eorum
units.tr: THESSALONIANS, dearest to Paul, 1 Thess. 2. 8. their

units.la: rum conuersio,1 Thes.1.9.electio,v.4.laus,2 Thess.1.4. magno animo ferunt persecutiones,1.v.4.5.7.
units.tr: conversion, 1 Thess. 1. 9.; election, v. 4.; praise, 2 Thess. 1. 4.; they bear persecutions with a great spirit, 1 Thess. v. 4, 5, 7.

units.la: THEVDAS Pseudopropheta, Act.5.36.hic cum suis sectatoribus perit.ibidem.
units.tr: THEUDAS, a false prophet, Acts 5. 36.; he and his followers perished, ibid.

units.la: THOLA, dux Israelis, Iudic.10.1.(i.vermiculus.)
units.tr: TOLA, a judge of Israel, Judg. 10. 1. (i.e. a worm.)

units.la: TOLMAI, rex Gessur 2 Sam.13 37.(i.sulcus.)
units.tr: TALMAI, king of Geshur, 2 Sam. 13. 37. (i.e. a furrow.)

units.la: THOMAS Christi Apostolus, Matth. 10.3. cum Lazaro mori exoptat, Ioan.11.16. Christum, de via quae ducat ad caelos interrogat, 14.5. incredulus primum est, 20. vers.24.25. tandem vt credat, Christi lateri manum inferre permittitur, v.27.28.(Graece Didymos. i.gemellus.)
units.tr: THOMAS, an Apostle of Christ, Matt. 10. 3.; he wishes to die with Lazarus, John 11. 16.; he asks Christ about the way that leads to heaven, 14. 5.; at first he is unbelieving, 20. vv. 24, 25.; finally, that he may believe, he is allowed to put his hand into the side of Christ, v. 27, 28. (In Greek Didymos, i.e. twin [Δίδυμος].)

units.la: THOPHET destruitur, 2 Reg.23 10.(V.TOPHET.)
units.tr: TOPHET is destroyed, 2 Kings 23. 10. (See TOPHET.)

units.la: THOV rex Emath, Dauid victori congratulatur, 2 Sam.8,v. 9.10. pacem a Dauide petit.1 Par.18.9.10.(i.errans.)
units.tr: TOI, king of Hamath, congratulates David on his victory, 2 Sam. 8. vv. 9, 10.; he seeks peace from David, 1 Chron. 18. 9, 10. (i.e. wandering.)

units.la: THRONVS, vide SOLIVM. Thronus Salomonis, Vide SOLOMON. Throni pro ipsis Angelis, Coloss.1.16. Throni magni visio, Apoc.20.11. Thronus gloriae, Hebraismus, pro throno glorioso & maiestatis pleno, Marth.19.28.(Thronus Dei, Ps.9.v.5.8. Dei Patris Apoc.1,4.& 3.21.& 4. v. 5.9. 10.& 5.v.1.6.7.11.13.& 6.16.& 7.v.9.10.11.15. & 8.3. & 12.5. & 14.5.& 16.17.& 19.v.4.5. Filij Dei, Messiae. Psalm.89.v.30. 37.Heb.1.8.Apoc.3.21.& 7,17,&20.v.11.12.& 21.v.3.5. Throni Apostolorum, Luc.22.30. Throni seniorum, Apoc.4.4. Thronus Dauidis, typus regni Messiae. Aliorum regum throni.
units.tr: THRONE: see SEAT. The throne of Solomon: see SOLOMON. "Thrones" for the Angels themselves, Col. 1. 16. The vision of the great throne, Rev. 20. 11. The throne of glory, a Hebrew idiom, meaning a glorious throne full of majesty, Matt. 19. 28. (The throne of God, Ps. 9. v. 5, 8; of God the Father, Rev. 1. 4; 3. 21; 4. vv. 5, 9, 10; 5. vv. 1, 6, 7, 11, 13; 6. 16; 7. vv. 9, 10, 11, 15; 8. 3; 12. 5; 14. 5; 16. 17; 19. vv. 4, 5. Of the Son of God, the Messiah: Ps. 89. vv. 30, 37; Heb. 1. 8; Rev. 3. 21; 7. 17; 20. vv. 11, 12; 21. vv. 3, 5. Thrones of the Apostles, Luke 22. 30. Thrones of the elders, Rev. 4. 4. The throne of David, a type of the kingdom of the Messiah. The thrones of other kings.)

units.la: THVBALCAIN filius Lamech, artis fabrilis inuentor, Gen.4.22.(i.mundana possessio.)
units.tr: TUBAL-CAIN, son of Lamech, the inventor of the metalworking craft, Gen. 4. 22. (i.e. worldly possession.)

units.la: THVS offerendum, & quomodo, Leuit.2.v.1.2.&c. thus offertur Christo a Magis, Matth.2.11.
units.tr: INCENSE: what is to be offered, and how, Lev. 2. vv. 1, 2, etc. Incense is offered to Christ by the Magi, Matt. 2. 11.

units.la: THVRIBVLA Core, Dathan & Abiron in monimentum sceleris eorum conseruata, Num.16.39.40. Vide 2 Paral. 26.19.
units.tr: THE CENSERS of Korah, Dathan and Abiram, kept as a memorial of their wickedness, Num. 16. 39, 40. See 2 Chron. 26. 19.

units.la: THYATIRORVM in urbe Paulus instituit Lydiam purpuriam, Actor.16.14. Thyatirensium Ecclesia, Apoc.2.18.
units.tr: At the city of the Thyatirans Paul founded Lydia the seller of purple, Acts 16. 14. The church of the Thyatirans, Rev. 2. 18.

units.la: THYMIAMATIS confectio, Exod.30.35.&37.29. V. Suffitus.
units.tr: The compounding of the incense, Exod. 30. 35.; 37. 29. See Incense offering.

units.la: TIBERIVS Imperator Romanorum: Luc.3.1.
units.tr: TIBERIUS, Emperor of the Romans, Luke 3. 1.

units.la: TIBERIAS, vrbs Galilaeae, ab Herode rege in honorem Tiberij Caesaris condita: Ioh.6.1.23.
units.tr: TIBERIAS, a city of Galilee, founded by King Herod in honour of Tiberius Caesar, John 6. 1, 23.

units.la: TIBICINVM vsus in exequiis olim solennis, Matt.9.23.
units.tr: The use of flute-players at funerals, once a solemn custom, Matt. 9. 23.

units.la: TIBIIS cecinit Christus Iudaeis, Matth.11.16. Luc.7.32.
units.tr: Christ played the flute to the Jews, Matt. 11. 16.; Luke 7. 32.

units.la: TIGRIS fluuius. Gen.14. Dan.10.4. Hiddekel vocatur.
units.tr: TIGRIS, a river, Gen. 2. 14.; Dan. 10. 4. Called Hiddekel.

units.la: TIGRIS Eccles.24.33. (Heb.Hiddekel) est insignis Asiae fluuius, ex Paradiso nascens, & Mesopotamiam ab ortu alluens: Gen.2.14. Dan.10.4. Alias Tigris est fera sæuissi-ma. V.Iob.4.10.11.
units.tr: TIGRIS, Ecclus. 24. 33. (Hebrew Hiddekel) is a famous river of Asia, rising in Paradise and washing Mesopotamia on its eastern side, Gen. 2. 14.; Dan. 10. 4. Otherwise the tigris is a most savage wild beast; see Job 4. 10, 11.

units.la: TIMERE aliquando totum Dei cultum complectitur. Luc.1.50. Act.10.35. & significat idem quod religiosè ac reuerenter colere. Hebraismus.
units.tr: FEAR sometimes embraces the whole worship of God, Luke 1. 50.; Acts 10. 35., and it signifies the same as worshipping religiously and reverently. A Hebrew idiom.

units.la: TIMIDITAS nimia damnatur, Prou.18.8. in bello periculosa est, Deut.20.8. Iudic.7.3. Timiditatis exempla: Israelitæ, 1 Sam.13.6. Samuel, 16.2. Saul, 17.11. Israelitæ, ver.24. Roboam, 2.Par.13.7. Achaz, Esa.7.2. Nicodemus, Ioan.3.2. Parentes cæci nati, 9.22. multi principes, 12.42. Ananias, Act.9.13. timiditatis pœna, Apoc.21.8. timiditatis spiritus, 2.Tim.1.6.7.
units.tr: TIMIDITY is condemned when excessive, Prov. 18. 8.; in war it is dangerous, Deut. 20. 8.; Judg. 7. 3. Examples of timidity: the Israelites, 1 Sam. 13. 6.; Samuel, 16. 2.; Saul, 17. 11.; the Israelites, v. 24.; Rehoboam, 2 Chron. 13. 7.; Ahaz, Isa. 7. 2.; Nicodemus, John 3. 2.; the parents of the man born blind, 9. 22.; many rulers, 12. 42.; Ananias, Acts 9. 13. The punishment of timidity, Rev. 21. 8.; the spirit of timidity, 2 Tim. 1. 6, 7.

units.la: TIMON, Diaconus eligitur, Act.6.5. (Honorabilis.)
units.tr: TIMON is chosen as a deacon, Acts 6. 5. (Honourable.)

units.la: TIMOR, Hebræorum more pro toto Dei cultu, Rom.11.20. pro obedientia. Roman.13.7. pro religione, Iob.4.6. pro reuerentia, estque piis necessarius Roman. 11.20, Ephes. 5. 33. Philip. 2.12, Hebr. 4. 1. & 11. 7. & 12. 28. 1.Petr.1.17 & 2.18. & 3.v.2.15. Iudæ, v.23. nec repugnat fidei & spei, Psalm.2.11. Eccles.9 v.1.2. Eccles.5.5.1. Corinth.9.27. & 10.12. Phil.3.v.11.13. Hebr.3.14.2.Pet.3.17. ¶Timor duplex est: Alius est naturæ, quo timore timuisse legitur Christus, Matth.26.38. Alius est diffidentiæ, de quo Rom. 8.15. ille ex imbecillitatis nostræ humaneque naturæ sensu est, neque peccatum est per se hic ex incredulitatis nostræ sensu proficiscitur, ideoq; vitium est. Timor quis vitiosus, Leu.18.22. Esa.29.13.1.Pet.3,14,1,Ioan.4.18.Ap.21.8.
units.tr: FEAR, in the Hebrew manner, is used for the whole worship of God, Rom. 11. 20.; for obedience, Rom. 13. 7.; for religion, Job 4. 6.; for reverence, and it is necessary for the godly: Rom. 11. 20.; Eph. 5. 33.; Phil. 2. 12.; Heb. 4. 1.; 11. 7.; 12. 28.; 1 Pet. 1. 17.; 2. 18.; 3. vv. 2, 15.; Jude v. 23. Nor does it conflict with faith and hope, Ps. 2. 11.; Eccles. 9. vv. 1, 2.; Eccles. 5. 5.; 1 Cor. 9. 27.; 10. 12.; Phil. 3. vv. 11, 13.; Heb. 3. 14.; 2 Pet. 3. 17. ¶ Fear is twofold. One is of nature, with which Christ is read to have feared, Matt. 26. 38.; the other is of diffidence, of which Rom. 8. 15. The first arises from the feeling of our weakness and human nature, and is not in itself a sin; the second arises from the feeling of our unbelief, and so is a vice. A vicious fear: Lev. 18. 22.; Isa. 29. 13.; 1 Pet. 3. 14.; 1 John 4. 18.; Rev. 21. 8.

units.la: Timoris magni exempli: Iacob. Genes.32,7, fratres Iosephi, 43.18, Israelitæ, Exod.14,10, & 19,16, Deut.5.5.1 Sam.7,7, Saul 17,11,&28.5, Elias, 1.Reg.19,3, minister Elisæi prophetæ, 2, Reg.6, v.15,16, Achaz, Esa.7.2, discipuli, Matth.8,25. & 17,6, Marc.6,49. Luc.8.25. porcorum custodes, Marc.5,15, Petrus, 9.6. Maria Magdalena, Maria Iacobi, & Salome, 16. v. 5,8, Zacharias, Luc. 1.12. vicini Zachariæ v.65, Pastores, 2.9. Capernaitæ 4.36. Scribæ & Pharisæi, 5.26. Viri Naim, 7.16. Petrus & alij, 9.34. mulieres, 24.5. Pilatus, Ioan.19.8.
units.tr: Examples of great fear: Jacob, Gen. 32. 7.; Joseph's brothers, 43. 18.; the Israelites, Exod. 14. 10.; 19. 16.; Deut. 5. 5.; 1 Sam. 7. 7.; Saul, 17. 11.; 28. 5.; Elijah, 1 Kings 19. 3.; the servant of the prophet Elisha, 2 Kings 6. vv. 15, 16.; Ahaz, Isa. 7. 2.; the disciples, Matt. 8. 25.; 17. 6.; Mark 6. 49.; Luke 8. 25.; the keepers of the swine, Mark 5. 15.; Peter, Mark 9. 6.; Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome, Mark 16. vv. 5, 8.; Zechariah, Luke 1. 12.; the neighbours of Zechariah, v. 65.; the shepherds, Luke 2. 9.; the Capernaites, Luke 4. 36.; the scribes and Pharisees, Luke 5. 26.; the men of Nain, Luke 7. 16.; Peter and the others, Luke 9. 34.; the women, Luke 24. 5.; Pilate, John 19. 8.

units.la: Timor præposterus, Matth.10.28, Luc.12,4. Timoris, quæ mali bonos timent, exempla: Abimelech timet Abrahamum, Gen. 21, v.22,23. Aegyptij Israelitas, Exod. 14. v. 25, Saul Dauidem, 1Sam.18.v.28.29. Tertius quinquagenarius primceps
units.tr: Preposterous fear, Matt. 10. 28.; Luke 12. 4. Examples of those who are feared, being evil, by the good: Abimelech fears Abraham, Gen. 21. vv. 22, 23.; the Egyptians fear the Israelites, Exod. 14. v. 25.; Saul fears David, 1 Sam. 18. vv. 28, 29.; the third captain of fifty

units.la: ceps Eliam,2 Reg 4.ver.13.14. Gentes Israelitas,Nehem. 6. v. 15.16. Herodes Ioannem Baptistam, {Marc. 6, v. 19. 20. custos carceris Paulum & Silam, Act. 6,v. 26, &c. Quis timendus,Matth.10.28,Luc.12.5. timendus Deus,& ante oculos habendus,Genes.22.12. & 31.42. Exod. 1.17.& 20.20.Deut.4.9.& 6.v.2.13.14 & 10.v.12 20.13 4.Iosue,24. 14. Iudic.6.10.2 Reg.17.36 2. Par.22 15.4,Eldr.16.68.Iob. 1.8.& 28 28. Psalm. 27.1. & 33.8. & 34. v. 8, 10, & 111.5, & 112,1, & 128,1. Prov.1.7. & 3.7. & 9.10, & 14, v.2, 27, & 15, 16, & 16,6,& 22,4,& 24.2. Eccles.12,11, Esa 8,5,& 41,10 & 43,1. & 51, 12, Ierem.10.7 & 32.39,Matt.10.28.Luc.12,5,1. Petr.2.17,& 5.5. Apocal.14,7.
units.tr: captain, Elijah, 2 Kings 1. v. 13, 14.; the Gentiles fear the Israelites, Neh. 6. vv. 15, 16.; Herod fears John the Baptist, Mark 6. vv. 19, 20.; the jailer fears Paul and Silas, Acts 16. v. 26, etc. Who is to be feared: Matt. 10. 28.; Luke 12. 5. God is to be feared and kept before the eyes, Gen. 22. 12.; 31. 42.; Exod. 1. 17.; 20. 20.; Deut. 4. 9.; 6. vv. 2, 13, 14; 10. v. 12; 20. 13.; Josh. 24. 14.; Judg. 6. 10.; 2 Kings 17. 36.; 2 Chron. 22. 15.; 4 Ezra 16. 68.; Job 1. 8.; 28. 28.; Ps. 27. 1.; 33. 8.; 34. vv. 8, 10; 111. 5.; 112. 1.; 128. 1.; Prov. 1. 7.; 3. 7.; 9. 10.; 14. v. 2, 27; 15. 16.; 16. 6.; 22. 4.; 24. 2.; Eccles. 12. 11.; Isa. 8. 5.; 41. 10.; 43. 1.; 51. 12.; Jer. 10. 7.; 32. 39.; Matt. 10. 28.; Luke 12. 5.; 1 Pet. 2. 17.; 5. 5.; Rev. 14. 7.

units.la: Timoris Dei exempla:Abraham,Gen.21.12.Ioseph,39.v.8. 9.obstetrices Hebraeorum, Exod.1.17. Aegyptii,9.20. Hebraei.14.31.Israelitae,1 Sam.12.18. Dauid,24.v.5.6.1.Paral. 13.12.Psal.5.8. Babylonij, Cuthaei,2 Reg.17,41, Iob,Iob.1. 8,& 2.3.Simeon,Luc.2.25. Fideles, Act.8.2.Ecclesia Christi,9,31.Cornelius Centurio, 10 v.2.22.miles centurionis, v.7.(Vide Deus timendus,& Metus Dei,)Timoris Dei fructus,vtilitas & laus, Gen.20,9. Psalm.103,17,& 115 1.& &118:1.&c. Prouer.10.27.& 14.27.& 19.23. & 22.4.eius defectus est causa peccandi,Genes.20.11.timore punit Deus & terrore,Genes.33.5,Exod.23.27. Leuit.26,36.Deut.2.24 25,& 11.25.& 28.v 10.65. Iosu.2 9. & 10.10. Iudic.4 5.& 7. 21.1.Sam.7.10.2.Reg.7,6,1,Par.15,17,2,Parl.14,14,& 17.10. & 20.29.Psalm.9.20.21.Ierem.49.37.
units.tr: Examples of the fear of God: Abraham, Gen. 21. 12.; Joseph, 39. v. 8, 9.; the Hebrew midwives, Exod. 1. 17.; the Egyptians, 9. 20.; the Hebrews, 14. 31.; the Israelites, 1 Sam. 12. 18.; David, 24. vv. 5, 6.; 1 Chron. 13. 12.; Ps. 5. 8.; the Babylonians, the Cuthaeans, 2 Kings 17. 41.; Job, Job 1. 8.; 2. 3.; Simeon, Luke 2. 25.; the faithful, Acts 8. 2.; the Church of Christ, Acts 9. 31.; Cornelius the centurion, Acts 10. vv. 2, 22.; the soldier of the centurion, v. 7. (See God to be feared, and the Fear of God.) The fruit, usefulness and praise of the fear of God: Gen. 20. 9.; Ps. 103. 17.; 115. 1.; 118. 1., etc.; Prov. 10. 27.; 14. 27.; 19. 23.; 22. 4. Its lack is the cause of sinning, Gen. 20. 11. God punishes with fear and terror, Gen. 33. 5.; Exod. 23. 27.; Lev. 26. 36.; Deut. 2. 24, 25.; 11. 25.; 28. vv. 10, 65.; Josh. 2. 9.; 10. 10.; Judg. 4. 5.; 7. 21.; 1 Sam. 7. 10.; 2 Kings 7. 6.; 1 Chron. 15. 17.; 2 Chron. 14. 14.; 17. 10.; 20. 29.; Ps. 9. 20, 21.; Jer. 49. 37.

units.la: TIMOTHEVS, gentilis cuiusdam ex Hebraea fideli filius, Act. 16.1. sacras literas ab infantia didicit,2. Tim.3.15.circumcidi tur,& quare, Actor.16 3. Pauli adiutor, Roman. 6. 21. Pauli filius,& quomodo,1 Cor 4.17. Philipp. 2. 9.22.1. Timoth.1.2. pauli frater quomodo,1 Thess.3.2. Pauli minister. Act.19.22. Dei minister,1 Thess.3.2.ministerio Evangelistae fungitur,1. Tim.4.12 2. Tim.4.5. seruus Christi,Phil.1.1.a paulo relictus Ephesi,& cur,1 Tim.1.ver.3.4. commendatur Corinthiis,1. Corinth.4.17.16.10,philippensibus mittendus promittitur, phil.2. 19.ad Thessalonicenses mittitur,1 Thessal.3.2. fides eius, aviae,& matris laudatur.2 Tim.1 5(Timotheus honor Dei, vel honorans D.)
units.tr: TIMOTHY, the son of a certain Gentile and a believing Hebrew woman, Acts 16. 1.; he learned the holy letters from infancy, 2 Tim. 3. 15.; he is circumcised, and why, Acts 16. 3.; a helper of Paul, Rom. 16. 21.; a son of Paul, and how, 1 Cor. 4. 17.; Phil. 2. 9, 22.; 1 Tim. 1. 2.; a brother of Paul, how, 1 Thess. 3. 2.; a minister of Paul, Acts 19. 22.; a minister of God, 1 Thess. 3. 2.; he discharges the office of an evangelist, 1 Tim. 4. 12.; 2 Tim. 4. 5.; a servant of Christ, Phil. 1. 1.; left by Paul at Ephesus, and why, 1 Tim. 1. vv. 3, 4.; he is commended to the Corinthians, 1 Cor. 4. 17.; 16. 10.; it is promised that he will be sent to the Philippians, Phil. 2. 19.; he is sent to the Thessalonians, 1 Thess. 3. 2.; his faith, and that of his grandmother and mother, is praised, 2 Tim. 1. 5. (Timothy, the honour of God, or one who honours God.)

units.la: TINTINABVLA in tunica Aaronis, Exod. 28. 33. & 39.25.
units.tr: BELLS on Aaron's tunic, Exod. 28. 33. & 39. 25.

units.la: TITVLVS lapideus a Iacobo erigitur, Genes. 28. 18. titulus crucis Christi, Matth. 27. 37. titulos erigere religionis ergo,prohibemur,Leuit.26.1.
units.tr: TITLE: a stone title set up by Jacob, Gen. 28. 18. The title of Christ's cross, Matt. 27. 37. We are forbidden to set up titles for the sake of religion, Lev. 26. 1.

units.la: Titus gentilis, à Paulo assumitur, Galat.2. 1 non circumci-ditur,& quare,v.3.dicitur Pauli filius, Tit.1.4.frater,2 Co-rinth.2.13.socius,8.23. cur Cretæ relictus, Tit 1.5. propter collecta ad Corinthios mittitur,2 Corinth. 8.16.in Dal-matiam proficiscitur,2 Tim.4.10.(1.honorabilis.)
units.tr: Titus, a Gentile, is taken along by Paul, Gal. 2. 1. He is not circumcised, and the reason is given at v. 3. He is called Paul's son, Tit. 1. 4; his brother, 2 Cor. 2. 13; his partner, 8. 23. Why he was left in Crete, Tit. 1. 5. He is sent to the Corinthians on account of the collection, 2 Cor. 8. 16. He sets out for Dalmatia, 2 Tim. 4. 10. (1. Honourable.)

units.la: TITVM iustum hospitem habet Paulus, Act.18.7.
units.tr: Paul has Titus Justus as his host, Acts 18. 7.

units.la: [TOBIAS multorum nomen,2. Par.17.8. Esdr.2.6.Nehem.2. 10.19. &c. Zach.6.10.14. Tobias cuius liber apocryphus extat.](1.Bonus Dominus.)
units.tr: [TOBIAH, the name of many men, 2 Chr. 17. 8; Ezra 2. 6; Neh. 2. 10, 19, etc.; Zech. 6. 10, 14. Tobias, whose apocryphal book exists. (1. The Lord is good.)]

units.la: TOLERANTIA, Vide PATIENTIA:&, Perseuerantia tole-rantia mutua præcipitur, Coloss 3.13. Phil.1.8.ex fide nata commendatur,2 Tim 2.12. Hebr.10.v.36.38. Tolerantiæ, fidei & charitatis incrementa laudantur,2. Thess.1.v.1.&c tolerans spes,1 Thess.1.3.
units.tr: TOLERANCE: see PATIENCE; and perseverance. Mutual tolerance is enjoined, Col. 3. 13; Phil. 1. 8. It is commended as born of faith, 2 Tim. 2. 12; Heb. 10. 36–38. The increase of tolerance, faith and love is praised, 2 Thess. 1. 1, etc. Tolerant hope, 1 Thess. 1. 3.

units.la: TONANTE Deo, conteruntur Philisthæi ad preces Samuelis 1.Sam.7.10,&c.
units.tr: With God thundering, the Philistines are crushed at Samuel's prayers, 1 Sam. 7. 10, etc.

units.la: TONITRV Sonus, qui fit ob effractam nubem in expansione à Deo proficiscitur, Exo.9.23.1.Sam.2,10,& 7.10.Iob.38.25. Psal.29.3.eius vis maxima, v.5.6,7,8,9, Tonitrua, cùm lex promulgatur, Exod. 19.16. tonitruis percutiuntur Aegyptij.Exod.9.23.Vide Iob.37.4.5.& Ier.51.16.
units.tr: THUNDER: the sound that arises when a cloud is burst in the expanse proceeds from God, Exod. 9. 23; 1 Sam. 2. 10 & 7. 10; Job 38. 25; Ps. 29. 3. Its greatest force is described at vv. 5–9. Thunder sounds when the law is promulgated, Exod. 19. 16. The Egyptians are struck by thunderbolts, Exod. 9. 23. See Job 37. 4–5 and Jer. 51. 16.

units.la: TONSIO ouium,1 Sam. 25.7,2. Sam. 13,24, Genes.38.v.12.13.
units.tr: SHEARING of sheep, 1 Sam. 25. 7; 2 Sam. 13. 24; Gen. 38. 12–13.

units.la: TOPHET, locus in valle filij Ennon, vbi quondam parentes filios igni exustos,idolo Moloch deuouebant: A Iosia con-taminatur,2Reg.23.10,occisionis vallis nominandus præ-dicitur,Ierem.19 6.(1.tympanum.V.Gehenna.)
units.tr: TOPHET, a place in the valley of the son of Hinnom, where parents once devoted their sons, burnt in the fire, to the idol Moloch. Josiah defiled it, 2 Kings 23. 10. It is foretold that it shall be called the valley of slaughter, Jer. 19. 6. (1. Drum. See GEHENNA.)

units.la: TORRENS erumpit, dimisso accola, aquæ obliuioni traditæ à pede,exhauriuntur mortalis opera,abscedunt.Iob.28.4.
units.tr: A torrent breaks forth, the inhabitant having been dismissed; the waters, once trodden under foot, are forgotten; mortal labours are drained away and depart, Job 28. 4.

units.la: TRADERE, pro causam apud Iudicem obtinere,qui reum in carcerem ad ducendum apparitori tradat,Mat.5 25.in priore parte versiculi.
units.tr: TO HAND OVER: to win a cause before a judge, who hands the defendant over to an officer to be led to prison, Matt. 5. 25, in the first part of the verse.

units.la: [TRADIT Deus homines, regiones, ciuitates,regna aliis ho-minibus, eisque subiicit.2. Tradit homines sibi ipsis,suis affectionibus in reprobum sensum.3.Tradit,1.exponit ho-mines variis calamitatibus. deniq;morti & exitio.4. Tra-dit,1.Dat suis varia donaatque bona spiritualia & tempo-ralia 5.Tradidit morti Deus Pater filium suum vnigeni-tum pro salute Ecclesiæ.6.Tradidit Deus Pater omnia fi-lio,& filius tradet regnum Patri.
units.tr: [God hands over men, regions, cities and kingdoms to other men, and subjects them to them. 2. He hands men over to themselves, to their own affections, into a reprobate mind. 3. He hands them over, that is, exposes men to various calamities, and finally to death and destruction. 4. He hands over, that is, gives his own people various gifts and good things, both spiritual and temporal. 5. God the Father handed over his only-begotten Son to death for the salvation of the Church. 6. God the Father handed all things over to the Son, and the Son will hand the kingdom over to the Father.]

units.la: Tradit homo seipsum & res varias Satanæ,vel in homi-num potestatem.2.aliquando Satanæ traduntur homines occultis quibusdam sed iustis iudiciis.3. Traditus est Christus Iudaeis, à proditore Iuda, crucifigendus, non sine Dei Patris consilio, qui eundem filium suum pro electis morti tradidit.]
units.tr: [Man hands himself and various things over to Satan, or into the power of men. 2. Sometimes men are handed over to Satan by certain hidden yet just judgments. 3. Christ was handed over to the Jews by the traitor Judas, to be crucified, not without the counsel of God the Father, who handed over his same Son to death for the elect.]

units.la: [TRADITIONES pro doctrina ore tradita, & tandem ab insanis hominibus in blasphemos Talmudis libros relata Iudaeis Cabala dicta, Matth.15.3. Marc.7.3. pro doctrina, quę tum voce tum scriptis tradita ab Apostolis est.2.Thess.2.15. seruandę eę sunt.ibid. ¶ Tradidisse Apostolos quaedam viua tantum voce, probare conantur Pontificij ex 1 Corinth.11.34. 2.Ioan.v.12.13.3. Ioan.v.13.traditiones humanę euertutur, Esa.29.13. Matth.15.v.3.6.9. Coloss.2. v.8.22. Ezec. 20.18. Esa, 8.19. 20. Rom.12. 6.1 Cor.2.13.2. Pet.1.19.Act.17.11.Deut.4.2.&12.8.Pro.30.6.Apoc.22.18.19 vide HOMIMES. ¶ Ad traditiones humanas asserendas detortiloci, Matth. 23.23. Luc. 11.42. Act.1.3. & 16.4. Rom. 15.15.1. Corinth. 11.2.2. Tim.3.8.V. Antiquas vias.]
units.tr: [TRADITIONS: doctrine handed down by mouth and, at last, by insane men carried into the blasphemous books of the Talmud, which the Jews call Cabala, Matt. 15. 3; Mark 7. 3. It is also doctrine delivered by the Apostles both by voice and in writings, 2 Thess. 2. 15. These are to be kept, ibid. ¶ The Papists try to prove that the Apostles delivered certain things by living voice alone, from 1 Cor. 11. 34; 2 John 12–13; 3 John 13. Human traditions are overthrown: Isa. 29. 13; Matt. 15. 3, 6, 9; Col. 2. 8, 22; Ezek. 20. 18; Isa. 8. 19–20; Rom. 12. 6; 1 Cor. 2. 13; 2 Pet. 1. 19; Acts 17. 11; Deut. 4. 2 & 12. 8; Prov. 30. 6; Rev. 22. 18–19. See MEN. ¶ To assert human traditions, twisted passages are used: Matt. 23. 23; Luke 11. 42; Acts 1. 3 & 16. 4; Rom. 15. 15; 1 Cor. 11. 2; 2 Tim. 3. 8. See "Ancient paths."]

units.la: [TRAHIT Deus, Ose.11.4. Trahit Deus,pater suos electos, vt credant, Ioann. 6.44. Trahit Deusfilius, Sponsus, & Seruator ecclesiæ,Cant.1.4.Ioan.12.32. Trahit Satan draco antiquus, Cauda sua partem stellarum mysticarum, Apocal.12,4.
units.tr: [GOD draws his people, Hos. 11. 4. God the Father draws his elect, that they may believe, John 6. 44. God the Son, the Bridegroom and Saviour of the Church, draws, Song 1. 4; John 12. 32. Satan, the ancient dragon, draws with his tail a part of the mystical stars, Rev. 12. 4.]

units.la: [Traho, Trahor, de homine & aliis creaturis dictum, Iud. 5. 21.2. Sam. 17. 13. Abac. 1.15. Lus.12.58.& 21.Ioā.20. v.6.8. Act.8 3.&14.19.& 17.6 & 21.30. Iac.2.6.

units.tr: Trembling and terror are sent by God upon the impious and sinners, Exod. 23. 27; Deut. 2. 25 & 11. 25. Examples of trembling: the citizens of Bethel, Gen. 35. 5; the brothers of Joseph, 45. 3; Moab, Exod. 15. 15–16; the citizens of Jericho, Josh. 2. 9–11; the kings of the Amorites, 5. 1; the Gibeonites, 9. 24; Sisera, Judg. 4. 15; the Philistines, 1 Sam. 7. 10; Agg. 15. 32–33; the Syrians, 2 Kings 7. 6; the Gentiles, 1 Chr. 14. 17; all nations, 17. 21; Jeroboam, 2 Chr. 13. 15; the Ethiopians, 14. 12–14; the kingdoms neighbouring Judah, 17. 10 & 20. 29; the men of Judah and Benjamin, Ezra 10. 9; the enemies of the Israelites, Neh. 6. 16; the princes of the Assyrians and their whole army, Judith 14. 47; the Persians and Medes, Esth. 8. 17 & 9. 2; Job, Job 4. 13–14 & 21. 5–6; the enemies of the Church, Ps. 48. 7, 65. 9, 76. 6–8; the Egyptians, Ps. 105. 38; hypocrites, Isa. 33. 14; the Israelites, Jer. 30. 5–6; the Egyptians, 46. 5; the Ammonites, 49. 5; the Elamites, v. 37; Daniel and certain others, Dan. 10. 7, 11; the guards of Christ's tomb, Matt. 28. 4; a certain woman, Mark 5. 33; Mary Magdalene, etc., Mark 16. 8; the disciples, Luke 24. 22; Moses, Acts 7. 31–32; Paul, 9. 6; 1 Cor. 2. 3; the jailer, Acts 16. 29; Felix, 24. 25–26; the Corinthians, 2 Cor. 7. 15.

units.tr: TRIBULATION, examples of its usefulness: Joseph grew more in exile, in the land of poverty, than he would have grown in the land of his birth, Gen. 41. 40; Ps. 105. 17, etc.; Acts 7. 9–10. The Israelites afflicted by fiery serpents repent, Num. 21. 6–7. David, fleeing from the face of Absalom, was patient in bearing the reproaches of Shimei, 2 Sam. 16. 10; but after winning the victory he proudly took care to have the people counted, 24. 1; and seeing the Lord angry, he asks to be punished and the people spared, v. 17. Micaiah, 1 Kings 22. 26–27. The princes of Israel, 2 Chr. 12. 5–7. Manasseh, 33. 12–13. The Israelites, Neh. 9. 35–37. Job, variously vexed and afflicted by the Sabeans, Job 1. 15; by fire sent down from heaven, v. 16; by the Chaldeans, v. 17; by Satan, v. 18 & 2. 7; by his wife, v. 9, etc.; at last he feels relief from his evils and is set free, Job 42. 12, etc. Jeremiah, sanctified in the womb, Jer. 1. 5, nevertheless cries out to himself, 15. 10. Nebuchadnezzar, set in prosperity, was proud and arrogant, but cast out from the company of men, he lifts his eyes to heaven and blesses God, Dan. 4. 31, etc. Susanna, placed under sentence of death, weeping lifts her eyes to heaven, 13. 42. The Israelites, 1 Macc. 9. 23–24; 2 Macc. 6. 1–2. The Apostles, Acts 5. 40. The Church, 8. 1. Paul and Silas, Acts 16. 19–20. Paul, 9. 23–25 & 13. 45, 49–50 & 14. 19 & 17. 5, 18 & 18. 4, 12 & 19. 23, etc. & 20, etc. & 20. 1–3 & 21. 26, etc., 22. 22, etc., 23. 10, etc., 25. 1, etc., 27. 29, etc.; 2 Cor. 1. 8 & 6. 4–5 & 7. 23–25 & 11. 32–33.

Half the tribe of Manasseh, given over to idolatry, 1 Chron. 5:23-25. The ten tribes led into captivity, 2 Kings 17:6. The lots of the tribes, Ezek. 48:1-23. The union of the ten tribes with the remaining two, Ezek. 37:19.

units.la: Trinitas personarum in Deo V. in Deo personæ tres. Trinitatis opera extrinseca (quæ vocant) communia sunt tribus personis: vt, Vocatio ad Munus aliquod & missio nunc tribuitur Patri, à quo Christus missus dicitur, Esa. 61.1. Luc.4.18. nunc Christo, Ioan.20.21. Ephes.4.11. Gal.1.1. nunc Spiritui sancto, Actor.1.2.& 13.2.& 20.28. Trinitatis personarum peculiares actiones ad salutem electorum simul concurrentes, 1 Pet.1.2. Trinitas figurata & declarata, Gen.1.26.& 18.2. Exod.3.v.6.15.16.& 4.5. Psalm. 33 6.Esa.6.3.& 34.16.& 48.16.& 61.1 Matth.3.16. & 10.20. & 17.5. & 28.19. Luc.4.18.Ioan.3.35.& 14.v.16.26.& 15.26. 16.3.1. & Ioan.5.7.
units.tr: The Trinity of persons in God. In God there are three persons. The outward works of the Trinity (as they are called) are common to the three persons. For example, a calling to some office and a sending are now ascribed to the Father, from whom Christ is said to be sent, Isa. 61:1; Luke 4:18; now to Christ, John 20:21; Eph. 4:11; Gal. 1:1; now to the Holy Spirit, Acts 1:2; 13:2; 20:28. The peculiar actions of the persons of the Trinity concur together for the salvation of the elect, 1 Pet. 1:2. The Trinity is foreshadowed and declared in Gen. 1:26; 18:2; Exod. 3:6, 15-16; 4:5; Ps. 33:6; Isa. 6:3; 34:16; 48:16; 61:1; Matt. 3:16; 10:20; 17:5; 28:19; Luke 4:18; John 3:35; 14:16, 26; 15:26; 16:13-14; and 1 John 5:7.

units.tr: To be sad immoderately over temporal things is in no way to be praised, Prov. 12:25; 15:13; 17:22; Eccl. 30:22; 38:19; 2 Cor. 7:10; 1 Thess. 4:13. See 2 Cor. 9:7.

units.tr: Sad. Christ was sad because of the blindness of the Jews, Mark 3:5. The rich young man was sad, Luke 18:23. Let the one who is sad pray, James 5:13. Christ's soul was sorrowful unto death, Matt. 26:38. The sad are to be comforted, Prov. 31:6; 25:20; 1 Thess. 4:13, etc.; and 5:14.

units.la: TRISTITIA duplex,2 Corinth.7.10.secundum Deum, quæ à Dei spiritu manat,& Deo accepta est, quæ de peccatis admissis dolet, idque non poenæ formidine, sed hoc ipsum ægerrimè ferens, quòd Deum clementissimum patrem offenderet,cuius offensam optet sua etiam damnatione,si ita fieri posset,redemptam. At qui secundum mundum dolet, vel terrenis amissis commodis, vel alieno bono angitur, vel alicuius poenæ impendentis metu est solicitus.Tristitia quàm noxia.Prouerb.17.22.& 25.20.tristitia vitiosa,1 Thess. 4. 13. units.tr: SORROW is twofold, 2 Cor. 7:10. There is sorrow according to God, which flows from the Spirit of God and is accepted by God: it grieves over sins committed, and grieves most painfully over this very thing, that it offended God, the most merciful Father, whose offence it would wish, even at the cost of its own damnation (if that could be done), to have redeemed. But he who grieves according to the world grieves either because of lost earthly advantages, or is distressed by another's good, or is anxious through fear of some impending punishment. How harmful sorrow is: Prov. 17:22; 25:20. Sinful sorrow, 1 Thess. 4:13. Examples of sorrow: in Isaac and Rebekah, Gen. 26:35; Esau, 27:34; Rebekah, 27:46; 6:7 [sic]; Jacob, 37:34; 43:6; the baker and the cupbearer, 40:6-7; Joseph, 42:24; 43:30; Samuel, 1 Sam. 15:35; Jonathan, 2 Sam. 1:34; David, 2 Sam. 1:11; 6:8; Ps. 35:13; 38:7; 42:6; 43:2; 55:3; Tamar, sister of Absalom, 2 Sam. 13:19; Ahab, 1 Kings 21:5; Ezra, Ezra 9:3; Nehemiah, Neh. 2:1-2; the Jews, Esth. 3:15; Neh. 8:9; Mordecai, Esth. 4:1; Job, Job 1:20; Jeremiah, Jer. 8:21; Darius, Dan. 6:14; Herod, Matt. 14:9; the disciples, 17:23; 26:22; John 16:22; fellow servants, Matt. 18:31; the rich young man, 19:22; Christ, 26:37; Peter, John 21:17; Paul, Rom. 9:2; 2 Cor. 2:3; Phil. 2:27; 2 Cor. 6:10; and Acts 20:36, etc.

units.tr: WHEAT and spelt: Exod. 9:32. The disobedient is threatened, Deut. 38:5 [as printed]. See Isa. 62:8-9. The obedient is promised, Deut. 11:14; Hos. 2:22. God will gather the wheat into his barn and burn the chaff with fire, Matt. 3:12. Tares sown among the wheat, Matt. 13:25; to be separated at harvest time, v. 30.
