units.la: TYCHICVS, fidus Christi minister, Eph. 6.21. Col. 4.7. commendatur, Ibid. Ephesum mittitur, à Paulo ab urbe Roma 2. Tim. 4.12. (i. contingens.)
units.tr: TYCHICUS, a faithful minister of Christ, Eph. 6:21; Col. 4:7. Commended, ibid. Sent to Ephesus by Paul from the city of Rome, 2 Tim. 4:12. (That is, happening by chance.)

units.la: TYMPANIS celebrant Deum mulieres, Exo. 15.20. Iud. 11.34. Psal. 6.8. 26.1 Sam. 18.16. Vsus, Psal. 81.3. & 150.4. Abusus, Isa. 5.12. & 24.80.
units.tr: TIMBREL: women celebrate God with timbrels, Exod. 15:20; Judg. 11:34; Ps. 68:26; 1 Sam. 18:6. Use: Ps. 81:3; 150:4. Abuse: Isa. 5:12; 24:8.

units.la: TYRANNI schola, in qua Paulus disserit, Act. 19.8.9.
units.tr: SCHOOL of the tyrant, in which Paul disputes, Acts 19:8-9.

units.la: TYRANNVS Tyranni imago, Prou. 28.15. tyrranni, Dei voluntate præsunt, Ierem. 27.8. tyranni arguuntur, Psal. 14.4. tyranni metui volunt, Esa. 10.13. aliquando subditos timent, Matt. 14.5. tyrannorum furorem fugere licet, Exod. 2.15. tyrannorum merces, Esa. 33.1. V. Iob. 15.20. Tyrannorum nequitia & crudelitas. Exempla: Gigantes, Genef.6.4. Nemrod,10.v.8 9. Nouus Pharao,Exod.1. v.8. &c. & 5.v.2.5.6.7. Adonibezech,Iud.1 7. Abimelech,9. 5.Saul,1.Sam.22.ver.17.& 27.v.1.2.Isbibenob,2 Sam.21.16. Roboam, 1 Reg.12.4. Iezabel,19.2.Achab,22.26.Manasses,2 Reg.21 16.Nebucadnezar Dan.2.v.11.12.& 3.19. Aman,Esth.3 6.Hostes Dauidis & Ecclesiæ, Pf.2.2.& 31.14. & 69.13.& 80.14.& 1 9 23 Sedechias & principes eius, Ierem.38.v.5.6.Rex Babylonis, 39 6. Herodes Ascalonita, Matt.2.16.& 14.v.9.10.Marc.6.v.26.27.Pilatus.Matt.27.18. Herodes tetrarcha,Luc.23 8.Herodes Agrippa, Act.12.v. 1.2 magistratus impius,16.v.22.23 Festus,24.27.& 25.v.9. 12.V.Persecutor.
units.tr: TYRANT: the image of a tyrant, Prov. 28:15. Tyrants rule by the will of God, Jer. 27:8. Tyrants are rebuked, Ps. 14:4. Tyrants want to be feared, Isa. 10:13; sometimes they fear their subjects, Matt. 14:5. It is lawful to flee the fury of tyrants, Exod. 2:15. The wages of tyrants, Isa. 33:1. See Job 15:20. The wickedness and cruelty of tyrants. Examples: the giants, Gen. 6:4; Nimrod, 10:8-9; the new Pharaoh, Exod. 1:8, etc.; 5:2, 5-7; Adoni-bezek, Judg. 1:7; Abimelech, 9:5; Saul, 1 Sam. 22:17; 27:1-2; Ishbi-benob, 2 Sam. 21:16; Rehoboam, 1 Kings 12:4; Jezebel, 19:2; Ahab, 22:26; Manasseh, 2 Kings 21:16; Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 2:11-12; 3:19; Haman, Esth. 3:6; the enemies of David and of the Church, Ps. 2:2; 31:14; 69:13; 80:14; 19:23; Zedekiah and his princes, Jer. 38:5-6; the king of Babylon, 39:6; Herod the Ascalonite, Matt. 2:16; 14:9-10; Mark 6:26-27; Pilate, Matt. 27:18; Herod the tetrarch, Luke 23:8; Herod Agrippa, Acts 12:1-2; an impious magistrate, 16:22-23; Festus, 24:27; 25:9, 12. See Persecutor.

units.la: TYRUS, urbs Phœniciæ: Tyri celebritas describitur, Ezec.27. 3. Tyri conuersio prædicitur, Esa 23 17.Act. 21.3. &c. eius excidium, versi. 1. Ezec.26.3. Amos 1.9. Tyri & Sidonis tolerabilior futura est conditio, quàm Corazin & Bethsaidæ incolarum conditio, Matth. 11.22.Luc.10.14.V. Ps.45.13.
units.tr: TYRE, a city of Phoenicia: the celebrity of Tyre is described, Ezek. 27:3; the conversion of Tyre is foretold, Isa. 23:17; Acts 21:3, etc.; its destruction, Isa. 23:1; Ezek. 26:3; Amos 1:9. The condition of Tyre and Sidon will be more tolerable than that of the inhabitants of Chorazin and Bethsaida, Matt. 11:22; Luke 10:14. See Ps. 45:13.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: ACCA rufa & eius oblatio,Numer.1.9.2. Vaccæ lactantes arcam reducunt,1 Sam. 6.12. [Vacca,idola,Ose.10.5.Vaccę,furores hominis,Superbi,Tyranni,Psalm.68.31. Amos 4.1.]Vaccæ pulchrę,& deformes. Ge.41.2.3 4.
units.tr: ACCA, the red heifer and its offering, Num. 1.9. 2. Milch cows bring back the ark, 1 Sam. 6.12. [Cow: idols, Hos. 10.5. Cows: the furies of men, the proud, tyrants, Ps. 68.31; Amos 4.1.] Cows beautiful and ill-favoured, Gen. 41.2, 3, 4.

units.la: VADERE per viam vniuersæ carnis,V.INGREDI viam vniuersæ carnis.
units.tr: TO GO along the way of all flesh, see V. TO ENTER the way of all flesh.

units.la: VALEDICTIONIS ritus: Parétes & cognati Rebeccæ omnia bona precantur, Gen.24. v.59.60. Isaac Iacobo profecturo in Syriam benedicit, 28.v.1.2.3. Laban osculatur filios & filias, 31.v.27.28. 55. Iacob filiis bona precatur & optat, 43. 14. Ruth nurus suas osculatur & bene precatur eis, Ruth 1.v.9.10. Ephesii osculantur Paulum iam iam ab ipsis discessurum, Act.20.v.37.38.
units.tr: FAREWELL, the rite of: Rebekah's parents and kinsfolk bless her with every good wish, Gen. 24.59, 60. Isaac blesses Jacob as he sets out for Syria, 28.1, 2, 3. Laban kisses his sons and daughters, 31.27, 28, 55. Jacob blesses and wishes good things for his sons, 43.14. Ruth kisses her daughters-in-law and blesses them, Ruth 1.9, 10. The Ephesians kiss Paul, who is about to leave them at once, Acts 20.37, 38.

units.la: VALLIS benedictionis cur sit dicta, 2 Paral.20.26. vallis filiî Ennon à Iosia contaminata, 2 Reg.23.10. occisionis vallis nominanda prædicitur, Ier.19.6. vide TOPHET.
units.tr: VALLEY of blessing: why it was so called, 2 Chr. 20.26. The valley of the son of Hinnom was defiled by Josiah, 2 Kings 23.10. It is foretold that a valley is to be named the valley of slaughter, Jer. 19.6. See TOPHET.

units.la: Validus armatus, Luc.11,21. Mat.12.29.
units.tr: Strong and armed, Luke 11.21; Matt. 12.29.

units.la: VANILOQVENTIA damnatur, 1 Timot.1.6. 2 Tim.2.16. Tit.1.10. vaniloquis quomodo os obturandum, Tit.1.10.
units.tr: Idle talk is condemned, 1 Tim. 1.6; 2 Tim. 2.16; Titus 1.10. How the mouths of idle talkers are to be stopped, Titus 1.10.

units.la: VANITAS, per quam temerè plus de nobis, nostrísque opibus, quàm in iis est, præsumimus & pollicemur. vide Fidelitas. Corruptio etiam vanitas est. A vanitate nobis cauendum, Ps.119.37. vanitas omnis homo, 39.v.6. & 144.4. & vanitate leuior, 62.v.10.
units.tr: VANITY, by which we rashly presume and promise more about ourselves and our resources than is really there. See Faithfulness. Corruption too is vanity. We must beware of vanity, Ps. 119.37. Every man is vanity, Ps. 39.6 and 144.4, and lighter than vanity, Ps. 62.10.

units.la: VANITAS omnia Eccl.1.2. vanitatis studiosi pietatem obliviscuntur, Ion.2.9 Vanitatis exemplum: Herodes, Matt.14.6. vanitates idola nuncupantur, 1 Sam.12.21.1 Reg.16.26. vanitatis damnatur, quicquid est extra Christum, Col.2.4. vanitati subiecta creatura, Rom.8.20.
units.tr: VANITY is all things, Eccl. 1.2. Those who are zealous for vanity forget piety, Jonah 2.9. Example of vanity: Herod, Matt. 14.6. Idols are called vanities, 1 Sam. 12.21; 1 Kings 16.26. Whatever is outside Christ is condemned as vanity, Col. 2.4. The creature was subjected to vanity, Rom. 8.20.

units.la: VANAE quæstiones reiiciendæ. 1 Timoth.1.4. & 6.4. Tit.3.9.
units.tr: Vain questions are to be rejected: 1 Tim. 1.4; 6.4; Titus 3.9.

units.la: VARIA dona cui collata, 1 Corint.12 7. Eph.4.7.
units.tr: To whom various gifts were given: 1 Cor. 12.7; Eph. 4.7.

units.la: VAS, pro quauis supellectile, per Hebraismum, Ezech.12.v.3.7. Matth.12.29. pro quouis instrumento, Actor.9.15. 1 Petr.3.7. pro vtensilibus nauticis, Actor.27.17. [vasa belli, 1. militum arma & supellex castrensis, vasa mortis, Psalm.7.14.1. arma lethifera. vasa musica, muliebria. pastoris, peregrinationis, venationis, &c: pro supellectili musicorum, mulierum, pastorum, peregrinantium, venatorum, &c. Vasa domus Dei, Dan.1.2. &c. Supellex omnis sacra quæ in templo Ierosolymitano fuit, præsertim autem vasa aurea & argentea, Dan.5. verse.2 3.23. vt antea vasa tabernaculi, Num.1.50.&c. Vasa furoris Dei, 1.exercitus populorum, quibus iudicia sua formidabilia est exequutus, Esai.13.5. Ierem.50.25. vas, vnus quisque, 2 Timoth.2.21. vasa iniquitatis, Genes.49.5.] vas suum possidere cum honore quisque Christianorum iubetur, vide POSSIDERE vas, &c. vasa honoris & contumeliæ, 2 Timot. 2.20. vasa tabernaculi, Exod.27.19. vasa aurea Salomonis, 1 Reg.10.25. vasa aurea, argentea, &c. in magna domo, 2 Timoth.2.20. vasa testacea; in quibus euangelij thesaurus habetur reconditus, 1 Corinth.4.7. Vasa irae, ex Hebraeorum idiotismo dicuntur ij, in quos iram decreuit Deus exercere, Roman. 9.22. Vasa misericordiae contrà, in quos misericordiam suam exercere decreuit, ibid. 23. vasa muliebri, vt infirmiori honor tribuendus, 1 Petr. 3.7. vasa fictilia, corpora nostra, 2 Corinth. 4.7. vasa, instrumentis, 1 Sam.21.5.
units.tr: VESSEL, for any household furniture, by Hebraism, Ezek. 12.3, 7; Matt. 12.29; for any instrument, Acts 9.15; 1 Pet. 3.7; for ship's tackle, Acts 27.17. [Vessels of war: a soldier's weapons and camp equipment. Vessels of death, Ps. 7.14: deadly weapons. Musical vessels, women's vessels, shepherds' vessels, travellers' vessels, hunters' vessels, etc.: the equipment of musicians, women, shepherds, travellers, hunters, etc. Vessels of the house of God, Dan. 1.2, etc. All the sacred furniture that was in the temple at Jerusalem, especially the golden and silver vessels, Dan. 5.2, 3, 23; as formerly the vessels of the tabernacle, Num. 1.50, etc. Vessels of the wrath of God: the peoples as an army, with which he carried out his terrible judgments, Isa. 13.5; Jer. 50.25. Vessel, each one, 2 Tim. 2.21. Vessels of iniquity, Gen. 49.5.] Each of the Christians is commanded to possess his own vessel with honour; see POSSESS. Vessels of honour and of dishonour, 2 Tim. 2.20. Vessels of the tabernacle, Exod. 27.19. Solomon's golden vessels, 1 Kings 10.25. Golden and silver vessels, etc., in a great house, 2 Tim. 2.20. Earthen vessels, in which the treasure of the gospel is stored, 2 Cor. 4.7. Vessels of wrath: by Hebrew idiom, those on whom God has decreed to exercise his wrath, Rom. 9.22. Vessels of mercy, on the other hand, are those on whom he has decreed to exercise his mercy, ibid. 23. A wife as the weaker vessel, to whom honour is to be given, 1 Pet. 3.7. Earthen vessels, our bodies, 2 Cor. 4.7. Vessels, instruments, 1 Sam. 21.5.

units.la: VAST HIS Assueri regis vxor, Esth.1.9. à rege vocata superbè venire recusat, v.10.11.12. Mamuchani consilio, propter superbum facinus regno & maritali thoro mouetur, v.16. 19.20. 2. eius occasione, rex edicto publico, vt mariti summum in familia imperium teneant, cauet. v.22.
units.tr: VASHTI, wife of King Ahasuerus, Esth. 1.9. Summoned by the king, she proudly refuses to come, vv. 10, 11, 12. At the counsel of Memucan, because of her proud deed she is removed from the kingdom and from the marriage bed, v. 16, 19, 20. 2. On this occasion the king, by public edict, provides that husbands are to hold supreme authority in the household, v. 22.

units.la: Vber, vbertas, V. Huber, Hubertas.
units.tr: Fruitful, fruitfulness. See Huber, Hubertas.

units.la: VELAMEN faciei Mosis impositum, Exod.34.v.34. velamen cordi Iudaeorum impositum, 2 Cor.3.vers.13.14. per Christum tollitur, ver.14.16. velamen subiectionis symbolum 1 Corinth.11.10. vnde & ipsum velamen capiti mulieris impositum, dicitur potestas, non per se, sed quòd sit symbolum potestatis viri in eam, per metonymiam, res signata pro signo.
units.tr: VEIL placed on the face of Moses, Exod. 34.34. The veil placed on the hearts of the Jews, 2 Cor. 3.13, 14. It is taken away through Christ, vv. 14, 16. The veil as a symbol of subjection, 1 Cor. 11.10. Hence the veil itself, placed on a woman's head, is called authority; not in itself, but because it is a symbol of the husband's authority over her, by metonymy, the thing signified for the sign.

units.la: Sic Abraham dicitur velamen oculorum Sarae, hoc est maritus, Gen.20.16. esse enim velamen oculorum, est periphrasis mariti, sumpta à iure, quod in vxorem habet, & ab officio illam protegendi. Nam in subiectionis signum velatur vxor, Gen.24.65. 1 Cor.11.7. simile est, expandere alam vestimenti, Ruth.3.9. Esa.4.1.
units.tr: So Abraham is called the veil of Sarah's eyes, that is, her husband, Gen. 20.16. For to be a veil of the eyes is a periphrasis for husband, taken from the right he has over his wife and from the duty of protecting her. For a wife is veiled as a sign of subjection, Gen. 24.65; 1 Cor. 11.7. Similar is spreading the wing of a garment, Ruth 3.9; Isa. 4.1.

units.la: VELLE aliquem, est gratum ei esse, Matt.27.43. velle tribuitur etiam inanimatis rebus, Ioan.3.8. & significat liberum ac vagum impetum. Velle interdum plus est quam velle simpliciter, & significat idem quod cupere, Matt.14.5. accipitur & pro amare, 12.38. vt explicatur. 23.4. hoc est, pro summo studio expetere, & ambire. Et velle & perficere Deus operatur, Phil 2.13.
units.tr: TO WISH for someone is to be pleasing to him, Matt. 27.43. Wishing is also attributed to inanimate things, John 3.8, and signifies a free and wandering impulse. To wish is sometimes more than simply to wish, and signifies the same as to desire, Matt. 14.5. It is also taken for to love, 12.38, as is explained at 23.4: that is, to seek and strive after with the greatest zeal. And God works both to will and to perform, Phil. 2.13.

units.la: VELLVS Gedeonis. Iudic.6 37. V.Iob.31.20.
units.tr: FLEECE of Gideon, Judg. 6.37. See Job 31.20.

units.la: VELVM tabernaculi quale, Exod.26.31. velum templi scinditur, Matth.27.51. velum dicitur caro assumta, Hebr.10.20. vbi instituitur allegoria veli illius quod operiebat sacrarij arcana, per quod tamen aditus in sacrarium patebat, sic inquit Apostolus, Christi caro diuinitatem nobis quasi sub velo ostendit, cuius alioqui fulgorem non pos-semus sustinere. Per hanc igitur viam accedamus ad Deum. Sed & velo videntur significari peccata, quæ nos à cælo arcebant, & à Christo fuerunt expiata, quo respectu fuit illud velum, Christo mortuo, à summo ad imum vsque penitus laceratum. Matt. 27. 51. VENATOR Esau, Gen. 25. 27. venator robustus Nemrod, 10. 9. [Venator Hominum, Psal. 91. 3. & 124. 7. Ier. 16. Mich. 7. 2. ] V. I Pet. 5. 8. Iob. 1. 7. Venatio, Leuit. 17. 13. VENDERE & dare pauperibus, Mar. 19. 21. Luc. 12. 33. & 18. 22. Act. 2. 45. venduntur hostibus inobedientes, Deu. 32. 30. Iudic. 2. 14. Vendentes eiiciuntur, Matt. 21. 12. VENDI non debent dona Dei, 2 Reg. 5. v. 22 26. &c. Dan. 5 17. Matt. 10. 8. Act. 8. 20 & 20 35. 1 Cor. 9. 14. 15. 2 Cor. 11. 9. & 12. 13. Vide EMERE, & Simonia. VENDITOR hominis occidendus, Deut. 24 7. V. Plagium de venditionibus, Leu. 25. 14. &c. De venditione sui ipsius v. 39.
units.tr: VEIL of the tabernacle, of what kind, Exod. 26.31. The veil of the temple was torn, Matt. 27.51. The assumed flesh is called a veil, Heb. 10.20, where the allegory of that veil which covered the secrets of the sanctuary is set up, through which nevertheless access into the sanctuary lay open. So the Apostle says: Christ's flesh shows us the divinity as if under a veil, whose brightness we could not otherwise endure. Let us therefore draw near to God by this way. But also by the veil are apparently signified the sins which kept us from heaven and were expiated by Christ; in this respect that veil was utterly torn from top to bottom when Christ died, Matt. 27.51. HUNTER: Esau, Gen. 25.27; Nimrod, a mighty hunter, 10.9. [Hunter of men, Ps. 91.3; 124.7; Jer. 16; Mic. 7.2.] See 1 Pet. 5.8; Job 1.7. Hunting, Lev. 17.13. TO SELL, and to give to the poor, Mark 19.21; Luke 12.33; 18.22; Acts 2.45. The disobedient are sold to their enemies, Deut. 32.30; Judg. 2.14. Sellers are cast out, Matt. 21.12. God's gifts ought not to be sold, 2 Kings 5.22, 26, etc.; Dan. 5.17; Matt. 10.8; Acts 8.20 and 20.35; 1 Cor. 9.14, 15; 2 Cor. 11.9 and 12.13. See BUY, and Simony. The seller of a man is to be put to death, Deut. 24.7. On kidnapping, and on sales, see Lev. 25.14, etc. On the sale of oneself, v. 39.

units.la: VENEFICIVM, φαρμακεία, Est venenorum noxiorum in necem & perniciem alterius confectio: vel eorundem applicatio maleuola, & non ignara mali, quod illi inest. ( Vide Incantatio.)
units.tr: POISONING, φαρμακεία [pharmakeia]: the preparation of harmful poisons for the death and destruction of another, or their malicious application by one who is not ignorant of the harm that is in them. (See Incantation.)

units.la: VENEFICIA damnantur, Gal. 5 20. veneficij pœna, Apocal. 9. 21. & 22. 15. veneficiis Babyl. omnes gentes seductæ. 18. 23.
units.tr: Poisonings are condemned, Gal. 5.20. The penalty of poisoning, Rev. 9.21; 22.15. By the poisonings of Babylon all nations were led astray, Rev. 18.23.

units.la: VENIO, verbum, ad Deum essentialiter & personaliter connexum, refertur: item ad Angelos, deinde ad homines, res, dies, horas, tempora, eventa, & accidentia varia.
units.tr: COME, a verb, referred essentially and personally to God; also to angels, then to men, things, days, hours, times, events and various accidents.

units.la: 1. Venire Deus dicitur, in iudicium & misericordiam, variis modis, Genes. 11. 7. & 18. 10. & 20. 3. Exod. 19. 9. & 20. verfic. 20. 24. Num. 22. versi. 9. 20. Deut. 33. 2 Psalm. 50. 2. 3. & 80. 3, & 101. 2 Esai. 3. 14. & 66. 15. Dan. 7. 22. Abac. 3. 3. Zach. 2. 10. & 14 5. Malac. 4 6. Rom. 9 9. Iud. v. 14. 15. Apoc. 16. 15.
units.tr: 1. God is said to come, in judgment and in mercy, in various ways: Gen. 11.7; 18.10; 20.3; Exod. 19.9; 20.20, 24; Num. 22.9, 20; Deut. 33.2; Ps. 50.2, 3; 80.3; 101.2; Isa. 3.14; 66.15; Dan. 7.22; Hab. 3.3; Zech. 2.10; 14.5; Mal. 4.6; Rom. 9.9; Jude 14, 15; Rev. 16.15.

units.la: 2. Venire de Deo Patre, dictum, Marc. 9. 7. Ioan. 14. v. 8. 30. & 14. 23. Apoc. 1. 4.
units.tr: 2. Coming from God the Father is spoken of in Mark 9:7, John 14:8, 30 and 14:23, and Revelation 1:4.

units.la: 3. De Christo Dei F. dictum, Iudic. 6. 11. Psalm. 40. 8. & 96. 13. & 118. 26, Cantic. 4. 16. & 7. 11. Esai. 35. 4 & 59. 20. Dan. 7. 13. & 10 13. Agg. 2. 7. Zac. 9. 9. Malach. 3. 1. De eodem in carne manifestato, & inter homines in terra versante, frequens mentio apud Euangelistas. De secundo domini aduentu, occurrunt testimonia multa, ex quibus pauca sequuntur, Ioan.21.23. Act.1.11.1 Cor.11.26. Apoc.1.7. & 2.5.16.25. & 3.v.3.11 & 22.v.7.12.17.20.
units.tr: 3. The coming of God's Son is spoken of in Judges 6:11, Psalm 40:8, Psalm 96:13, Psalm 118:26, Song of Songs 4:16 and 7:11, Isaiah 35:4 and 59:20, Daniel 7:13 and 10:13, Haggai 2:7, Zechariah 9:9, and Malachi 3:1. Its manifestation in the flesh, and his dwelling among men on earth, is frequently mentioned by the Evangelists. Many testimonies concern the second coming of the Lord, of which a few follow: John 21:23, Acts 1:11, 1 Corinthians 11:26, Revelation 1:7, 2:5, 16, 25, 3:3, 11, and 22:7, 12, 17, 20.

units.la: 4. Venit Spiritus S. Matth.3.16. Ioann.15.26. & 16.v.7.13. Act 19.6.
units.tr: 4. The Holy Spirit comes: Matthew 3:16, John 15:26, 16:7, 13, and Acts 19:6.
5. The angel of the Lord comes: Genesis 19:1, Numbers 22:32, 2 Kings 19:3, Job 16, Daniel 9:23 and 10:14, 20, Revelation 8:3, 17:1, and 21.
6. Satan comes: Job 1:7 and 2:2, Matthew 12:44 and 13:19, Mark 4:15, Luke 8:12 and 11:25, John 14:30.

units.la: 7. Venio de hominibus dictum, in imperandi modo age, agite, nonnunquam significat. Aliquando idem est si diceres, Eo, Redeo. De rebus autem, temporis momento vt die, hora, &c. item de variis euentis dicitur. Quum passim occurrat, lectori considerandum relinquimus.]
units.tr: 7. "To come" said of men is sometimes used in the imperative as "go, come on." At other times it means the same as "go" or "return." Said of things, it refers to a moment of time, such as a day, an hour, and so on, and is also used of various events. Since it occurs everywhere, we leave its consideration to the reader.

units.la: VENIRE ad Christum, donum Dei est, Ioann.6.v 37.44 6.
units.tr: COMING to Christ is a gift of God: John 6:37, 44.

units.la: venire in nomine Domini, Hebraico idiotismo, dicitur qui peculiaris est Dei veluti legatus, Matth.21.9.
units.tr: To come in the name of the Lord, in a Hebrew idiom, is said of one who is, as it were, a special envoy of God: Matthew 21:9.

units.la: VENTER extra castra leuandus, Deut.23.12. venter pro Deo eligitur, Rom.16.18. Phil.3.19. ventris fructus multiplicantur obedientibus Deo, Deut.28.4. Ventris abolitio.1 Cor.6.13.
units.tr: The BELLY is to be removed outside the camp: Deuteronomy 23:12. The belly is chosen in place of God: Romans 16:18, Philippians 3:19. The fruits of the belly are multiplied for those who obey God: Deuteronomy 28:4. The abolition of the belly: 1 Corinthians 6:13.

units.la: [Venter mysticus, Cant.5 v.14.& 7.2. Ioan.7.38.]
units.tr: [The mystical belly: Song of Songs 5:14 and 7:2, John 7:38.]

units.la: VENTVS, est exhalationis in sublime eductæ motus vel dispersio, quæ in hac expansione proximiore & viciniore nubis, aere, à Deo fit. Iob.38.24. Ego sum Deus creans ventum, Amos 4.13. Iob.28.25. Ps.148.8.
units.tr: WIND is a motion or dispersion of vapour drawn up on high, which God brings about in this nearer and more neighbouring expansion of cloud and air: Job 38:24. "I am the God who creates the wind": Amos 4:13. Job 28:25, Psalm 148:8.

units.la: VENTVS: venti in manu Dei, Genes.8.1. Exod.10.13.& 14.21. Num.11.31. Psal.104.3.& 135. Ierem.10.13. Amos.4.13. Ion.4.& 4 8. venti Christo obediunt, Matt.8.26. Mar.4.39. Luc.8.24.
units.tr: WIND: winds are in the hand of God: Genesis 8:1, Exodus 10:13 and 14:21, Numbers 11:31, Psalm 104:3 and 135, Jeremiah 10:13, Amos 4:13, Jonah 4:8. Winds obey Christ: Matthew 8:26, Mark 4:39, Luke 8:24.

units.la: [VENTVS, ira Dei, Esa.41.16.& 57.13. Ezec.13.11.& 27.26. Ose.13.15. Plaga orbis terrarum, 1 Par.9.24. Ier.49.v.32.36. Ezec.5.v.10.12.& 12.14.& 17.21.& 42.v.16. ad 20. Mat.24.31. Rep. nullius momenti, Spes vana, Mendacium, Esai.41.29. Ierem.22.22. Ose.8.7.& 12.1. Ventus, Euangelij doctrina, vide Ioann.3.8. venti, Euangelici doctores, Apocal.7.1.]
units.tr: [WIND as the anger of God: Isaiah 41:16 and 57:13, Ezekiel 13:11 and 27:26, Hosea 13:15. A scourge of the whole earth: 1 Chronicles 9:24, Jeremiah 49:32, 36, Ezekiel 5:10, 12 and 12:14 and 17:21 and 42:16 to 20, Matthew 24:31. Of no account, empty hope, a lie: Isaiah 41:29, Jeremiah 22:22, Hosea 8:7 and 12:1. Wind as the doctrine of the Gospel: see John 3:8. Winds as evangelical teachers: Revelation 7:1.]

units.la: VENTILABRVM, Mat.3.12. ventilabrum Dei, Ier.15.7.
units.tr: WINNOWING FAN: Matthew 3:12. God's winnowing fan: Jeremiah 15:7.

units.la: VENVNDATVS Achab, vt faceret malum, 1 Reg.21.20.
units.tr: SOLD: Ahab was sold to do evil: 1 Kings 21:20.

units.la: VERAX Deus, Exo.34.6. Ioan.3.33.
units.tr: God is TRUTHFUL: Exodus 34:6, John 3:33.

units.la: VERBERIBVS cæduntur impii, Deut.25.2.3. Interdum pijs: Paulus, 2 Cor.11.24.25. Christus, Mat.27.26. Apostoli Act. 5.40.41.
units.tr: The wicked are beaten with STRIPES: Deuteronomy 25:2, 3. Sometimes the pious too: Paul, 2 Corinthians 11:24, 25; Christ, Matthew 27:26; the apostles, Acts 5:40, 41.

units.la: ERBVM pro re quapiam, vel negotio, aut etiam pro particula indefinita, Genes.24.50 Esa.2.1 Matth.21.24 Luc.1.37 & 2.15. pro nutu seu voluntate, Hebr.1.3. κατ' ἐξοχὴν, pro promissione gratuita, fide in Christum recepta, Eph.5.26. pro lege diuina, praeceptis, decretis Dei, & prophetis ac promissionibus Dei, Psalm.119.v.49.89. Matth.24.35. pro mandato, Luc.5.5. sicut & dicere pro iubere, Matt.8.8. verbum fidei pro ipso Euangelio, Rom.10.8. verbum otiosum quam noxium, Matth.12.36. verbum Dei manet in aeternum, Numer.23.19. Psalm.33.11. & 127.2 & 119.89. Esai. 40.8. & 51.6. & 54.10. Matt.5.18. & 24.35. Marc.13.31. Luc.16.17. & 21.32. 1 Pet.1.25.
units.tr: WORD is used for some matter or affair, or even as an indefinite particle: Genesis 24:50, Isaiah 2:1, Matthew 21:24, Luke 1:37 and 2:15. It is used for a nod or will: Hebrews 1:3. Par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν] it is used for the free promise received by faith in Christ: Ephesians 5:26. It is used for the divine law, the precepts and decrees of God, and the prophets and promises of God: Psalm 119:49, 89; Matthew 24:35. It is used for a command: Luke 5:5, just as to speak means to order: Matthew 8:8. "The word of faith" is the Gospel itself: Romans 10:8. "Idle word," more harmful than otherwise: Matthew 12:36. "The word of God abides forever": Numbers 23:19, Psalm 33:11, 127:2, 119:89; Isaiah 40:8, 51:6, 54:10; Matthew 5:18, 24:35; Mark 13:31; Luke 16:17, 21:32; 1 Peter 1:25.

units.la: [Verbum, λόγος, Dei filius, sermo, sapientia patris, seu patris interpres: ille ipse de quo locutus est Deus, & quem Ecclesiae suae seruatorem promisit atque exhibuit, Ioan.1.v.1.14. 1 Ioan.1 1.& 5.7. Apoc.19.13.
units.tr: [Word [λόγος], the Son of God, speech, the wisdom of the Father, or the interpreter of the Father: he himself, of whom God spoke and whom he promised and showed to his Church as its saviour: John 1:1, 14; 1 John 1:1 and 5:7; Revelation 19:13.]

units.la: ERBVM Dei, est instrumentum sacrum de veritate Dei ad salutem necessaria, instinctu Spiritus Sancti A, per viros sanctos B, ac in primis per Prophetas C, & Apostolos D, fideliter & perfectè in libris Canonicis V. & N. T. perscriptum, ad erudiendam Dei Ecclesiam E, de recto cultu Dei, deq; vera hominis felicitate. A. 2 Tim.3 16. 2 Pet.3.21. B.ib. C.Rom.12.2. Pet.1 19. D. 2 Pet.3 15. E. Rom.15.4. 1 Tim.4.13.16.2 Tim.3 15.Ioh.5.39.& 30.31. (V.Scriptura.)
units.tr: WORD of God is the sacred instrument of the truth of God necessary for salvation, written by the impulse of the Holy Spirit A, through holy men B, and above all through the Prophets C and Apostles D, faithfully and perfectly in the canonical books of the Old and New Testaments, to instruct the Church of God E in the right worship of God and the true happiness of man. A. 2 Timothy 3:16; 2 Peter 3:21. B. ibid. C. Romans 12:2; 1 Peter 1:19. D. 2 Peter 3:15. E. Romans 15:4; 1 Timothy 4:13, 16; 2 Timothy 3:15; John 5:39 and 30:31. (See Scripture.)

units.la: Verbum Dei non audiendum solùm & loquendum, sed & corde credendum, & factis praestandum, vide DEI verbum. Verbi Dei auditionis exempla: vide AVDITIONIS. verbi Dei, &c. verbi Dei vis & efficacia. ¶ Verbum Dei universum non esse literis proditum, unde probetur: vide, DEI verbum. verbum caro factum est, hoc est homo Ioan. 1.14. per synecdochen, sicut & Esai. 40.5. Ioel.2.28. vide CARO.
units.tr: The Word of God is not to be only heard and spoken, but also believed in the heart and carried out in deeds; see WORD OF GOD. Examples of hearing the Word of God: see HEARING. The power and efficacy of the Word of God, and so on. ¶ That the whole Word of God has not been handed down in writing, how this is proved: see WORD OF GOD. The word was made flesh, that is, man: John 1:14, by synecdoche, as also Isaiah 40:5 and Joel 2:28; see FLESH.

units.la: VERBA non leuiter effutienda, sed ponderanda sunt, Psal.12.5. Prou.15.v.2 23.& 13.3.& 20.15 & 17.27.& 21.23.& 25.11 Eccles.5.2.& 10.11.&c. Mat.13.36. Col.4 6. Iac.1 19.
units.tr: WORDS are not to be uttered lightly but weighed: Psalm 12:5; Proverbs 15:2, 23, 13:3, 20:15, 17:27, 21:23, 25:11; Ecclesiastes 5:2, 10:11, etc.; Matthew 13:36; Colossians 4:6; James 1:19.

units.la: VERECVNDIA sancta est virtus quae turpitudinem omnem temperantiae contrariam fugit. Est igitur testimonium sanae mentis & sinceri iudicij de rebus obscoenis, adhuc in nobis permanentis. Haec maximè est in adolescentibus, minùs in senibus, propter aetatis & sanguinis penuriam. V.Psal.44.r6.1 Cor 6.5.
units.tr: MODESTY is a holy virtue which flees every baseness contrary to temperance. It is therefore a testimony of a sound mind and sincere judgment about obscene things, still remaining in us. It is found most of all in young people, less in the old, because of the lack of age and of blood. See Psalm 44:16; 1 Corinthians 6:5.

units.la: SECVNDIA, in mulieribus exigitur, 1 Timorh.2.9. Verècundiæ exempla: Sem & Iapher, Gen.9.23.Sara,18.15. Mulie̅ sanguinis fluxu laborans,Matth.9.20.Marc.5.33.Elizabeth Luc.1.24. vide PVDOR.
units.tr: MODESTY is required in women: 1 Timothy 2:9. Examples of modesty: Shem and Japheth, Genesis 9:23; Sarah, Genesis 18:15; the woman suffering from a flow of blood, Matthew 9:20, Mark 5:33; Elizabeth, Luke 1:24. See SHAME.

units.la: VERITAS I. pro vera perceptione rerum ad salutem necessariarũ,Ioan.17.17. II. veritas, Ioan.4.23. non opponitur mendacio, vt a iâs sæpe, sed externis Legis ceremoniis quæ duntaxat adumbrabant id,quod reipsa præstat Christus.veritas,pro fraudis experte.Ioann.3.21. III. pro benevolentia & voluntati diuinæ congruenter viuendi regula,Roman.2.8.1.Petr.1.22. IV. veritas Euangelij, Galat.2 ver.5.14.pro vera ac sincera Euangelij doctrina. V. veritas in genere pro iustitia,Hebraeorum more,1 Cor.13.6. VI. pro integritate animi,quæ omni dissimulationi aduersatur, Philip.1.18.3.Ioan.v.3 VII. non pro prædicatione verbi Dei sed pro naturali notitia cum voluntate diuina conuenie̅te,Roman.2.8.IIX. κατ' ἐξοχὴν, pro vera religione,Ioan 17.17.Galat.3.1 Coloss.1.5.Tit.1.1.IX. pro Christo,vel doctrina eius,hoc est Euangelio, 2 Ioann.verf.1. veritas Dei Pro constantia ipsius, Roman.3.7. veritas commendatur Zach.8.v.16.19.Matt.5.37,Ephes.4.25. & 6.14. Iacob.5.12 veritas libertatem adfert,Ioan.8.32. veritas per Christum 1.17.& in Christo,Eph.4.21. veritas consensus fundamentum. v.15.
units.tr: TRUTH: I. for the true perception of things necessary for salvation: John 17:17. II. Truth, John 4:23, is not opposed to falsehood, as the Jews often think, but to the external ceremonies of the Law, which only foreshadowed what Christ in fact performs. Truth, for what is free of deceit: John 3:21. III. For the rule of living in accordance with the goodwill and will of God: Romans 2:8; 1 Peter 1:22. IV. The truth of the Gospel: Galatians 2:5, 14, for the true and sincere doctrine of the Gospel. V. Truth in general for righteousness, after the manner of the Hebrews: 1 Corinthians 13:6. VI. For integrity of mind, which opposes all pretence: Philippians 1:18; John 3:3. VII. Not for the preaching of the Word of God, but for natural knowledge agreeing with the divine will: Romans 2:8. VIII. Par excellence [κατ' ἐξοχὴν], for the true religion: John 17:17; Galatians 3:1; Colossians 1:5; Titus 1:1. IX. For Christ, or his teaching, that is, the Gospel: 2 John, verse 1. The truth of God is for his constancy: Romans 3:7. Truth is commended: Zechariah 8:16, 19; Matthew 5:37; Ephesians 4:25 and 6:14; James 5:12. Truth brings liberty: John 8:32. Truth through Christ and in Christ: John 1:17; Ephesians 4:21. Truth is the foundation of agreement: verse 15.

units.tr: Truth breeds hatred. Examples: the brothers of Joseph, Genesis 37:4, 8; Balaam, Numbers 24:10, 11; Abimelech, Judges 9:21; Saul, 1 Samuel 20:33; Baasha, 1 Kings 16:7; Ahab, 22:27; 2 Chronicles 16:10; Joash, 24:21; Uzziah, 26:19; Zedekiah, Jeremiah 32:3; Jehoiakim, 36:23; the princes of Judah, 38:4; Herod, Matthew 14:4; Luke 3:19; the chief priests and Pharisees, Matthew 21:45; the Pharisees and lawyers, Luke 11:33, 34; the chief priests and scribes, 20:19; the world, John 7:7 and 17:14; the Pharisees, 9:28; the Jews, 15:24; Luke 4:28; Acts 7:54; the chief priests, 5:33; the enemies of Paul, 9:23, 29; the Galatians, Galatians 4:16. Truth wins in the end: Proverbs 28:23. Truth is Christ: John 14:6. The Gospel: 2 Peter 1:12. Truth is the belt of the loins: Ephesians 6:14. The truth of God in promises: Genesis 32:10. Truth in judges: Exodus 18:21.

units.la: VERITATIS aduersarij quomodo tractandi, 2 Tim.2.25.veritatis agnitio,via salutis,1 Timot.2.4.veritatis contemtus quàm noxius,2 Thessal.2.10.veritatis doctrina à Deo petenda,Zach.10.1.fructus,salus hominis, 2 Thessal.2.10. vis quanquanta, Prou.28.23. Zach.13.3. Luc.21.15. Act.4.14, & 9.22. & 26.28.
units.tr: How the adversaries of the truth are to be dealt with: 2 Timothy 2:25. The knowledge of the truth is the way of salvation: 1 Timothy 2:4. How harmful contempt for the truth is: 2 Thessalonians 2:10. The doctrine of the truth is to be sought from God: Zechariah 10:1. Its fruit is the salvation of man: 2 Thessalonians 2:10. Its power is great: Proverbs 28:23; Zechariah 13:3; Luke 21:15; Acts 4:14, 9:22, 26:28.

units.la: VERITATI Euangelij resistentes, 2. Tim.2.18. & 3.8.
units.tr: Those who resist the truth of the Gospel: 2 Timothy 2:18 and 3:8.

units.la: VERITATEM vocat Paulus, Roman. 1.18. quicquid lucis ad Dei notitiam in homine relictum est: non, ut hac duce in Dei gratia redeant (quod solius Christi opus est) sed ut suo ipsorum iudicio sceleris conuincantur. Veritatem omnem dicere, est rem totam, ita ut gesta erat, narrare, Marc.5.33. contra veritatem ne propinquissimus quidem acquiescendum, Mich.7.5. Veritatem facere, pro sincere agere, Ioan.3.21. 1 Ioan.1.6. pro veritatem sectari. Ephes.4.15. In veritate ambulandum, 1 Reg.2.4. 1 Ioan.2.27. in veritate seruiendum Deo, Ios.24.14.
units.tr: Paul calls TRUTH whatever light of knowledge of God remains in man: Romans 1:18. Not that by this guide they return to the grace of God, which is the work of Christ alone, but that they are convicted of their wickedness by their own judgment. To tell the whole truth is to narrate the whole matter just as it was done: Mark 5:33. One must not agree even with the closest friend against the truth: Micah 7:5. To do the truth, that is, to act sincerely: John 3:21; 1 John 1:6, for to pursue the truth: Ephesians 4:15. One must walk in truth: 1 Kings 2:4; 1 John 2:27. To serve God in truth: Joshua 24:14.

units.la: VERA adoratio, & veri adoratores qui, Ioan.4.21. veri pare-tes Christi qui, Matth.12.48. Marc.3.33. Luc.8.19. veri Apostoli descriptio, 1 Corinth.4.1. veri Pastoris exemplar absolutum proponitur, 1 Timot.1. &c. Tit.1.1. &c. verus usus interpretandi Scripturas traditur, 1 Cor.14.12. &c. abusus tollitur, v.17. V. interpretatio.
units.tr: TRUE worship, and true worshippers who: John 4:21. The true brothers of Christ who: Matthew 12:48; Mark 3:33; Luke 8:19. Description of a true apostle: 1 Corinthians 4:1. The complete model of a true minister is set forth: 1 Timothy 1, etc.; Titus 1:1, etc. The true use of interpreting Scripture is taught: 1 Corinthians 14:12, etc. Abuse is removed: verse 17. See V. interpretation.

units.tr: WORM that gnaws: Isa. 66.24; Mark 9.44, 46, 48. [Worm; afflicted man, Ps. 22.7; Isa. 41.14; frail man, Job 25.6.

units.tr: TOP (vertex) of a man, Gen. 49.26; Deut. 28.35 and 33.16; 2 Sam. 14.25; Job 2.7; Ps. 17 and 68.22. Top, or summit, of a mountain, Exod. 19.20 and 24.17. Top of the stars, Job 22.12. Top of the body politic, Isa. 1.6. Top of a tree, Ezek. 17.22.

units.la: VERTIGINIS Spiritus, Esa.19.14.] v. Gal.3.1.
units.tr: SPIRIT OF GIDDINESS, Isa. 19.14. [See Gal. 3.1.]

units.tr: BATS: the Jews do not eat them, Lev. 11.19; Deut. 14.18. See Isa. 2.20.

SACERDOS.
units.tr: GARMENTS which are unlawful: Deut. 21.13. A widow's garment is not to be taken in pledge, 24.17. A man's garment is unlawful for a woman, and the reverse, 22.5. To one who takes your coat, the tunic is to be given too, Luke 6.29. To one who has no garment, let him who has two give one, Luke 3.11. Wedding garment, Matt. 22.11. Garments of Christ: see CHRIST. Soldiers divide them, Matt. 27.35. The garments of the Israelites in the desert did not wear out, Deut. 29.5. Garments of Adam and Eve, of skins, Gen. 3.21. Garments of the priest: see PRIEST.

On the abuse of garments, see Abuse of garments, and ornament. See 1 Tim. 6.8; Gen. 28.20.

units.tr: THE NAKED are to be clothed: see The naked are to be clothed.

units.tr: FRINGE of a garment, Matt. 14.36. [A garment, whether sacred, public, political or domestic, is easily distinguished by the circumstances of the places where it occurs.]

units.tr: CLOTHING of women: what it ought to be, 1 Tim. 2.9; 1 Pet. 3.3-4; Isa. 3.15-17. See Ornament.

units.la: VETVS homo vocatur à Paulo, Roman. 6. 6. Coloss.3.9. vniuersa hominis natura,itavt cum iniquitate conceptus est,& in hanc lucem editus. vide Caro:&,Homo exterior,vetus homo exuendus, Eph. 4.22. cum Christo crucifixus dicitur, Roman. 6. 6. quod non sic accipiendum est, quasi corrupta hæc natura Christo aliter quàm per imputationem tribuatur. Nam iam inde ab ipso conceptionis momento carnem nostram in sese ita sanctificauit nobis, vt omnis peccati expers fuerit. Itaque nobis veterem hominem crucifixit: sicut mortuus dicitur peccato, Roman.6.10. non vt peccare desineret, sed vt peccatum destrueret.Vetus testamentum corrigitur,Heb.8.13.Veteris testamenti diuisio,Vide Testamentum vetus.
units.tr: The OLD MAN is what Paul calls the whole nature of man, as it was conceived in iniquity and brought forth into this light: Rom. 6.6; Col. 3.9. See Flesh, and Outward man. The old man is to be put off, Eph. 4.22. He is said to be crucified with Christ, Rom. 6.6. This is not to be understood as if this corrupt nature were attributed to Christ in any other way than by imputation. For from the very moment of conception he sanctified our flesh in himself, so that it was free of all sin. Thus he crucified the old man for us, just as he is said to have died to sin, Rom. 6.10: not so that he might cease to sin, but so that he might destroy sin. The Old Testament is set aside, Heb. 8.13. On the division of the Old Testament, see Testament, Old.

units.la: VETVSTAS literæ,Rom.7.6.vide Litera.
units.tr: The ANTIQUITY of the letter, Rom. 7.6. See Letter.

units.la: VITVLARVM officium quod,Tit.2.3 &c.4.5.
units.tr: The DUTY of young women, Titus 2.3 etc.; 4.5.
