Quarto, pro doctrina Euangelica, Actor.9.2. & 22.4. Via arcta & spaciosa,Matth.7.13,Luc.13.24.via Balaam, Vide Balaam. Via Christus,Iohã.14.6.via per quam iusti ambulant,quæ & qualis sit,Psal.119.5.Prouer.3.v.6.17.&16.v.7.17.Eccles.12.Esa.26.7.& 30.21.& 35.8.& 40.3.Ier.31.25.Osea.14.9. 1 Thess.4.1.Hebr.12.13. via gentium, pro profanis & impiis gentium moribus, Matth.10.5. Quinto, pro aperta & simplici professione religionis Christianæ, Actor. 24,14. Via Dei,18.26,id est via ad Deum ducens.
units.tr: WAY: First, for a settled manner and rule of life, Rom. 11.33. Second, for life and conduct, Matt. 21.32; Acts 14.16. Third, by antonomasia, for Christianity, Acts 19.9. Fourth, for evangelical doctrine, Acts 9.2; 22.4. The narrow and broad way, Matt. 7.13; Luke 13.24. The way of Balaam: see Balaam. The Way is Christ, John 14.6. The way in which the just walk, and what kind it is, Ps. 119.5; Prov. 3.6, 17; 16.7, 17; Eccles. 12; Isa. 26.7; 30.21; 35.8; 40.3; Jer. 31.25; Hos. 14.9; 1 Thess. 4.1; Heb. 12.13. The way of the Gentiles, meaning the profane and impious customs of the Gentiles, Matt. 10.5. Fifth, for the open and simple profession of the Christian religion, Acts 24.14. The way of God, Acts 18.26, that is, the way leading to God.

units.la: Viam Dei docere, Matt. 22. 16. est docere, quid fis fit, aut minus, ex Dei voluntate, siue qua via sit hominibus incedendum, ita vt Deum non offendant, via impiorum qualis, Psalm. 119. 3. Prou. 4. 19. & 12. 15. & 21. 2. & 22. 5. & 29. 27. Esaiae. 57. 10. Viae impiorum exitus & finis, Iob 6. 18. Prou. 14. 12. & 28. 18. Ierem. 2. 36. & 4. 18. Via iusto- rum a Domino dirigitur, Psalm. 17. 5. & 25. 4. & 119. 35. Pro. 4. ver. 12. 18. & 13. 6. & 16. 9. & 20. 24. Esai. 48. 17. Ierem. 10. 23. Mich. 4. 2. via iustorum, remunerationem expectat a Deo, Psal. 24. 12. &c. Prou. 12. 28. Ierem. 6. 16. & 7. 3. Via pacis, Hebraeorum more, pro ea via, quae ad veram pacem & felicitatem ducit, Luc. 1. 79. pro vita pacifica & innocente, Rom. 3. 17.
units.tr: To teach the way of God, Matt. 22.16, is to teach what is fitting or unfitting according to God's will, or by what way men ought to walk so as not to offend God. The way of the impious, what kind it is: Ps. 119.3; Prov. 4.19; 12.15; 21.2; 22.5; 29.27; Isa. 57.10. The end and outcome of the ways of the impious: Job 6.18; Prov. 14.12; 28.18; Jer. 2.36; 4.18. The way of the just is directed by the Lord: Ps. 17.5; 25.4; 119.35; Prov. 4.12, 18; 13.6; 16.9; 20.24; Isa. 48.17; Jer. 10.23; Mic. 4.2. The way of the just awaits reward from God: Ps. 24.12 etc.; Prov. 12.28; Jer. 6.16; 7.3. The way of peace, in the Hebrew manner, is the way that leads to true peace and happiness, Luke 1.79; or a peaceable and innocent life, Rom. 3.17.

units.la: VIAE, pro rebus gestis. Apoc. 15. 3.
units.tr: WAYS, for deeds done: Rev. 15.3.

units.la: [VIA, vt distincte procedamus, I. Significat Iter, vel spatium illud quod metiuntur homines, & animalia, pedib? vehiculis, aliis modis variis, temporis momento longo vel breuiori, terminoq; a quo incipitur, vsq; ad terminū ad quē perficitur. II. via, vitae humanae rationem, institutum cogitationes, consilia, & hominum actiones denotat, Genes. 6. 12. Num. 22. 32. Deut. 28. 29. Iosu. 1. 8. Iudic. 2. 19. 1. Sam. 9. 3. 1. Reg. 15. 26. 2. Reg. 8. 16. Psal. 1. 1. Rom. 3. 16. 1. Cor. 4. 17. & 12. 31. Iacob. 1. 8. & 5. 20. 2. Pet. 2. 15. Iud. v. 11. viae Domini, 1. Praecepta eius, siue voluntas, signi, patefacta in Dei verbo seu doctrina Mosis, Prophetarum & Apostolorum. Haec via autem variis epithetis a viis aliis distinguitur. Nam appellatur bona, lucida, immaculata, vitae iustitia, pacis, sapientiae, &c. via recte, aequae, pulchrae viae dicuntur. Vide 1. Sam. 12. 2. 11. Reg. 8. 36. Eldr. 8. 2 1. Iob. 21. 14. Psal. 2. 12. & 16. 11. & 101. v. 2. 6. & 119. v. 30. 151. Prou. 2. 20. & 3. 17. & 4. 11. & 6. 23. & 8. 20. & 16. 31. Ier. 21. 8. Ezech. 18. v. 25. 29. & 33. 17. Ose. 14. 18. Roman. 3. 17. 2. Pet. 2. v. 2 15. 20. 21.
units.tr: [WAY. To proceed clearly: I. It signifies a journey, or that distance which men and animals cover on foot, by vehicles or in other ways, over a longer or shorter span of time, from the starting point to the point reached. II. Way denotes the manner of human life, custom, thoughts, plans and human actions: Gen. 6.12; Num. 22.32; Deut. 28.29; Josh. 1.8; Judg. 2.19; 1 Sam. 9.3; 1 Kings 15.26; 2 Kings 8.16; Ps. 1.1; Rom. 3.16; 1 Cor. 4.17 and 12.31; James 1.8 and 5.20; 2 Pet. 2.15; Jude v.11. The ways of the Lord: 1. His precepts, or will, revealed in God's word, or in the doctrine of Moses, the Prophets and the Apostles. This way is distinguished from other ways by various epithets: it is called good, bright, unspotted, the way of righteousness of life, of peace, of wisdom, and so on. Ways are called right, equal, beautiful. See 1 Sam. 12.2; 1 Kings 8.36; Eccles. 8.12; Job 21.14; Ps. 2.12; 16.11; 101.2, 6; 119.30, 151; Prov. 2.20; 3.17; 4.11; 6.23; 8.20; 16.31; Jer. 21.8; Ezek. 18.25, 29; 33.17; Hos. 14.18; Rom. 3.17; 2 Pet. 2.2, 15, 20, 21.

units.la: IV. Via, viae Domini 1. Sapientissima agendi ratio, voluntas beneplaciti in Deo, quo omnia recte disponit & exequitur. Deut. 32. 4. 2. Sa. 22. 31. Psal. 19. 151. & 145. 17. Esai. 40. 14. & 55. v. 8. 9. Rom. 11. 33. Apoc. 15. 3 v. via vitae aeternae Christus, Ioan. 14. 6. VI. Via Christi, Esai. 2. v. 3. 4. & 42. 16. Malac. 3. 1. Matt. 3. 3. & 11. 10. Ioan. 1. 23. VII. Religionis verae confitans professio, Iudic. 2. 17. Act. 9. 2. & 19. v. 9. 23. & 22. 4. & 24. 23. VII. Modus, Esai. 10. v. 24. 26. IX. via vniuersae terrae, Mors omnibus constituta, Iosu. 23. 14. 1. Reg. 2. 2. X. ad statum beatum vel miserum via, Matth. 7. v. 13. 14. Ioan. 14. v. 4. 5. Hebr. 9. 8. & 10. 20.
units.tr: IV. Way: the ways of the Lord. 1. The most wise manner of acting, the will of good pleasure in God, by which he rightly orders and carries out all things: Deut. 32.4; 2 Sam. 22.31; Ps. 19.151 and 145.17; Isa. 40.14 and 55.8-9; Rom. 11.33; Rev. 15.3. The way of eternal life is Christ, John 14.6. V. The way of Christ: Isa. 2.3-4 and 42.16; Mal. 3.1; Matt. 3.3 and 11.10; John 1.23. VI. The constant profession of the true religion: Judg. 2.17; Acts 9.2 and 19.9, 23; 22.4 and 24.23. VII. The manner: Isa. 10.24, 26. VIII. The way of the whole earth, death appointed for all: Josh. 23.14; 1 Kings 2.2. IX. The way to a blessed or a wretched state: Matt. 7.13-14; John 14.4-5; Heb. 9.8 and 10.20.

units.la: VICINVS bonus Prouerb. 27. 10. Vicini Iudæam infestantur delendi: Ier. 12. 14.
units.tr: A GOOD NEIGHBOUR: Prov. 27.10. Neighbours who harass Judea are to be destroyed: Jer. 12.14.

units.la: VICISSITVDO, 2 Thess. 1. ver. 6. 7. 1 Ioan. 3. 14. Vicissitudinis praxis, Iudic. 1, 7, Esth. 9, 1, Esa. 14, 2, & 33, 1, & 34, v. 12, 13, 14 Thren. 4. v. 5. 7 8. Soph. 2, 14. Zach. 8. 13, Luc. 10, 15. & 12. 2. & 16. 15. Act. 9. 21 & 14. v. 18, 19. Gal. 1. 23. Phil. 3. 7, Coloss. 1. 13. 1. Petre. 2. 25. V. Talio. & Pro. 1. 24. &c.
units.tr: CHANGE of fortune: 2 Thess. 1.6-7; 1 John 3.14. The practice of retribution: Judg. 1.7; Esth. 9.1; Isa. 14.2; 33.1; 34.12-14; Lam. 4.5, 7-8; Zeph. 2.14; Zech. 8.13; Luke 10.15; 12.2; 16.15; Acts 9.21 and 14.18-19; Gal. 1.23; Phil. 3.7; Col. 1.13; 1 Pet. 2.25. V. Retaliation (talio): Prov. 1.24 etc.

units.la: VICTIMA: Vide SACRIFICIVM Victimæ nomen μεταφορικῶν vsurparum, Vide SACRIFICIORVM & oblationum nomina μεταφορικῶν vsurpata. Victima omnis sale salitur in Lege Mosis, Marci. 9. 49. victimæ & ieiunia, obstinatis, non prosunt, Ierem. 14, 12, victimas iustitiæ immolare, Deut. 33. 16. V. Esa. 1, 11.
units.tr: VICTIM: See SACRIFICE, on the victim name used metaphorically. See also the names of sacrifices and offerings used metaphorically. Every victim is salted with salt in the Law of Moses, Mark 9:49. Victims and fasts do not profit the obstinate, Jer. 14:12. To offer the victims of righteousness, Deut. 33:16. See Isa. 1:11.

units.la: VICTORIAE exempla: Vide BELLORVM diuina virtute confectorum exempla. Victoriæ genus præstantissimum, Rom. 12. 21. 1 Ioh. 5. 4. Pro. 16, 32, victorie fiducia vincenda sunt omnia aduersa, 2 Timoth. 3. v. 9, 10, victoria Agni, Apoc. 17. 14, victoriam consecuti laudant Deum, 19. 6. victoria potiuntur pauci contra multos, Genes. 14. 14. Iudic. 7. v. 2, 4 Iosu. 11, v. 1. 17, 1, Sa. 14. v. 6, 14. 2. Par. 13. 14. & 14. v. 11. 12. & 2. 4. 24. Post victoriam parta triumphus constituitur. Num. 3. 13.
units.tr: Examples of VICTORY: see the examples of wars waged by divine power. The most excellent kind of victory, Rom. 12:21; 1 John 5:4; Prov. 16:32. By the confidence of victory all adversities are to be overcome, 2 Tim. 3:9, 10. The victory of the Lamb, Rev. 17:14. Those who have obtained victory praise God, Rev. 19:6. A few gain victory over many, Gen. 14:14; Judg. 7:2, 4; Josh. 11:1, 17; 1 Sam. 14:6, 14; 2 Chron. 13:14; 14:11, 12; 24:4. After victory is won, a triumph is held, Num. 31:13.

units.la: VICTVS in vultus sudore parandus, Genes.3.19.2, Thess.3.10. victum Deus largitur homini & bestiis, in genere,1.verf. 29.30. Psalm. 145.v.15.6, & 147,v.8,9, sed viduae, pupillo & peregrino peculiariter, Deuter.10.18, de victu non debemus esse soliciti, Matth 6.25, Luc.12,22.v. Pro.10.3.& 13,25,& 15,16,17,& 16.8,& 17,1,& 30.8.9, V. Cibus.
units.tr: FOOD is to be obtained by the sweat of one's face, Gen. 3:19; 2 Thess. 3:10. God gives food to man and beasts in general, Gen. 1:29, 30; Ps. 145:15; 147:8, 9; but to the widow, the orphan and the stranger in particular, Deut. 10:18. We ought not be anxious about food, Matt. 6:25; Luke 12:22. See Prov. 10:3; 13:25; 15:16, 17; 16:8; 17:1; 30:8, 9. See Food.

units.la: VIDERE interdum pro sentire, Hebraeis. Actor,2.27.pro cognoscere, Lucae.5.20. pro pati, Ioan.8.51. Videre mortem pro sentire mortem, Lucae. 2.26, videre vitam,pro vita frui. Non videre vitam,pro non frui vita, Ioan.3.36. videre regnum Dei, pro intrare in regnum Dei,3.3.vt explicatur v.5. Videre, interdum ad animum transfertur, & significat:ex manifesto signo aliquid colligere, Exodi.20.18.Matth. 9. v. 2. 4. pro cognoscere,Luc.5.20.pro intelligere,9.47. Ioan 5.19. pro cauere, Marc.12.38. videre Deum nemo potest, Exod.33.20. vidit Deum Iacob, Gen.32.30. Moses,Exodi.24.17.
units.tr: VIDERE (to see) sometimes means "to perceive" among the Hebrews: Acts 2:27. It means "to know," Luke 5:20; "to suffer," John 8:51. To see death means to perceive death, Luke 2:26. To see life means to enjoy life; not to see life means not to enjoy life, John 3:36. To see the kingdom of God means to enter the kingdom of God, John 3:3, as v. 5 explains. Videre is sometimes transferred to the mind and signifies to gather something from a clear sign, Exod. 20:18; Matt. 9:2, 4, "to know," Luke 5:20; "to understand," Luke 9:47; John 5:19; "to beware," Mark 12:38. No one can see God, Exod. 33:20. Jacob saw God, Gen. 32:30; Moses, Exod. 24:17.

units.la: VIDENS,pro Propheta,1. Sam.9.9. &c.2. Sam.15.27.1.Par.21. 9.& 25.5.& 27.28.& 29.29. Esai.30.10.videntes oculi obedientibus,Deut.29.4.
units.tr: VIDENS (seeing), for a prophet, 1 Sam. 9:9, etc.; 2 Sam. 15:27; 1 Chron. 21:9; 25:5; 27:28; 29:29; Isa. 30:10. Seeing eyes belong to the obedient, Deut. 29:4.

units.la: VIDVA, in deliciis viuens, mortua,1 Tim.5.6.
units.tr: A widow who lives in pleasure is dead, 1 Tim. 5:6.

units.la: VIDVAE munusculum à Christo laudatur, Lucae.21.3. Viduae Deus facit iudicium, & ipsi dat victum, Deuter.10.18.viduae vestimentum pignori non accipiendum, Vide Vestis. Viduae parabola, quae crebis precibus iudicium aequum obtinuit, ab iniquo iudice, Lucae. 18.2.&c. Viduae filius suscitatur,Lucae.7.11.
units.tr: The widow's little gift is praised by Christ, Luke 21:3. God executes judgement for the widow and gives her food, Deut. 10:18. A widow's garment is not to be taken as a pledge; see Garment. The parable of the widow who, by her frequent prayers, obtained a fair judgement from an unjust judge, Luke 18:2, etc. The son of the widow is raised, Luke 7:11.

units.la: VIDVAE quales in Ecclesiae ministerium, seu in Diaconissarum collegium recipiendae, 1 Timoth. 5.3. quot annorum recipiendae,v.9. Viduae iuniores lasciuiunt, ideoque deuitandae sunt,v.11. vbi non reiiciuntur viduae iuniores ab Ecclesia,sed ad numerum Diaconissarum non admittuntur. Viduae verae quae, 1 Tim. 5.3. quae videlicet solae sunt, & omni humano praesidio destitutae & vera pietate ornatae.
units.tr: What kind of widows are to be received into the ministry of the Church, or into the college of deaconesses, 1 Tim. 5:3; of what age they are to be received, v. 9. Younger widows wax wanton and so are to be avoided, v. 11, where younger widows are not rejected by the Church but are not admitted to the number of deaconesses. True widows are those who, 1 Tim. 5:3, are, that is, alone and destitute of all human help, and adorned with true piety.

units.la: VIDVARVM domos comedere,Matthaei.23.14. Viduarum officium,1.Corint.7.v.8.9.1. Timot.5.2. Viduarum habenda ratio,& benefaciendum illis, Exodi.22.22. Deut.16.14.& 24. v. 17. 19. 20. 21. & 26. v.12.13.& 27 19.Iob.24.3.&31.16. Eccles.4.10. Esai.1.17. Ieremiae.22,3, Zach.7,v.10 Malach. 3,5,Matth.23,14,1,Timoth.5.3,Iacobi.1,27.
units.tr: To devour widows' houses, Matt. 23:14. The duty of widows, 1 Cor. 7:8, 9; 1 Tim. 5:2. Regard is to be had for widows, and good is to be done to them, Exod. 22:22; Deut. 16:14; 24:17, 19, 20, 21; 26:12, 13; 27:19; Job 24:3; 31:16; Eccles. 4:10; Isa. 1:17; Jer. 22:3; Zech. 7:10; Mal. 3:5; Matt. 23:14; 1 Tim. 5:3; James 1:27.

units.la: VIDVAS pias quid deceat,Luc.2.37.1. Timoth.5,v.3.5,Tit '3. VIGILANTIA piis omnibus, sed Pastoribus imprimis necessaria, Matth.24. ver. 42.43. & 25 13. & 26.41. Marc.11.33. Luc.12.37. & 21.36. Rom.13.11. 1 Cor.15.34. 2 Tim.4.5. 1 Pet. 4.7. & 5.v.8.9.
units.tr: What befits pious widows, Luke 2:37; 1 Tim. 5:3, 5; Titus 2:3. VIGILANCE is necessary for all the pious, but for ministers above all, Matt. 24:42, 43; 25:13; 26:41; Mark 11:33; Luke 12:37; 21:36; Rom. 13:11; 1 Cor. 15:34; 2 Tim. 4:5; 1 Pet. 4:7; 5:8, 9.

units.la: [VIGILARE 1. De Deo dicitur, & significat, in id quod proposuit sedulò eum incumbere, vel in misericordia, vel in iudicio, Ierem.1.verl.11.12. & 31.28. & 44.27. Dan. 9.14.
units.tr: [VIGILARE. 1. Said of God, and means to apply oneself diligently to what he has proposed, either in mercy or in judgement: Jer. 1:11, 12; 31:28; 44:27; Dan. 9:14.

units.la: II. Quando de hominibus dicitur, significat solicitè & attente custodire & observare aliquid, Esdr. 8.29. Iob.24.5. Psal.127.1 Matt.24 43 & 26.38.
units.tr: II. When said of men, it means to guard and observe something carefully and attentively: Ezra 8:29; Job 24:5; Ps. 127:1; Matt. 24:43; 26:38.

units.la: III. Ad vigiliam seu vigilantiam internam & spiritualem refertur, atque significat piè, iustè, sobriè viuere in verae religionis exercitu, 10. Psalm.63.2. Prou.8.v.17.34. Cantic.5.2. Esai.26.9. Marci v.13.37. Luc.12.37. & 21.36. Act. 20.31. 1 Cor.16.13. Ephes.6.18. Coloss.4.1. 2 Thess.v.6.10. 2 Tim.4.5. 1 Petr.4.7. & 5.8. Apoc.3.v.2.3. & 16.15.]
units.tr: III. It refers to inner and spiritual watchfulness, and means to live piously, justly and soberly in the exercise of true religion: Ps. 63:2; Prov. 8:17, 34; Song 5:2; Isa. 26:9; Mark 13:37; Luke 12:37; 21:36; Acts 20:31; 1 Cor. 16:13; Eph. 6:18; Col. 4:1; 2 Thess. 5:6, 10; 2 Tim. 4:5; 1 Pet. 4:7; 5:8; Rev. 3:2, 3; 16:15.]

units.la: VIGILEMVS, & sobrij simus, 1 Thess.5.6. vigilemus in orationibus, Coloss.4.2. (V. Aduentus Domini.) VILLICI parabola, Luc.16 1. &c. VIM patitur regnum caelorum, Matt.11.12. VINCTORVM memineri mus, Heb.10 34. & 13 3. Ex. Act.12.5. Amos 6.6.
units.tr: Let us watch and be sober, 1 Thess. 5:6. Let us watch in prayers, Col. 4:2. (See Advent of the Lord.) The parable of the steward, Luke 16:1, etc. The kingdom of heaven suffers violence, Matt. 11:12. Let us remember the prisoners, Heb. 10:34 and 13:3. From Acts 12:5; Amos 6:6.

units.la: [VINCVLVM, instrumentum quodcunque in carcere, vel extra carcerem, quo homo vel aliud quidpiam detinetur & trahitur. 2. Metonymicè significat captiuitatem vel seruitutem ipsam. 3. Metaphoricè, leges, iura, doctrinam, ut Psal.2.3. Ierem. 2.20. & 5.5. Item obligationem coniugij, Ruth.1.2. & foederis, Ezech.20.37.] VINCVLA Pauli vsui sunt Sanctis, 2 Tim.2.9 10.
units.tr: [VINCULUM: any instrument, in prison or outside it, by which a man or some other thing is held and dragged. 2. Metonymically, it signifies captivity or servitude itself. 3. Metaphorically, laws, rights and doctrine: Ps. 2:3; Jer. 2:20; 5:5. Likewise the bond of marriage, Ruth 1:2, and of covenant, Ezek. 20:37.] The bonds of Paul are useful to the saints, 2 Tim. 2:9, 10.

units.la: VINDICTA non appendeda, sed Deo soli, eiusque Ministris ac Magistratui legitimo relinquenda: vnde & prohibita aliis est, Genesis 15.14. Leuit.19.18. Deut.32.35. Iudic.8.19. & 16.20. Psalm.7.7 & 9.13. & 94.1 Prou. 17. 19.13. & 20.22. & 24.29, Ieremiae 51.36. Ezech.25.12,13. Nahum.1.2. Matth.5, 39. & 6.14. & 18.v.22.35. & 26.52. Marci 11.26. Lucae 6.v.27. 28. & 9.55. & 17.3 29. & 18.7. Rom.12.19.1 Cor.6.7. Galat.5. 10.1 Thess.5 15.2 Tim.4.14. Heb.10.30. Iac.5. v.4.9.1 Pet.3. 9. Apoc.6.10.
units.tr: REVENGE is not to be taken into one's own hands but left to God alone, and to his ministers and the lawful magistrate; whence it is also forbidden to others: Gen. 15:14; Lev. 19:18; Deut. 32:35; Judg. 8:19; 16:20; Ps. 7:7; 9:13; 94:1; Prov. 17:19; 13:19; 20:22; 24:29; Jer. 51:36; Ezek. 25:12, 13; Nah. 1:2; Matt. 5:39; 6:14; 18:22, 35; 26:52; Mark 11:26; Luke 6:27, 28; 9:55; 17:3, 4; 18:7; Rom. 12:19; 1 Cor. 6:7; Gal. 5:10; 1 Thess. 5:15; 2 Tim. 4:14; Heb. 10:30; James 5:4, 9; 1 Pet. 3:9; Rev. 6:10.

units.la: vindicta acceptae iniuriae, Deo committenda. exempla: Ioseph, Genes.50 19. Saul,1 Sam. 11.13. & 24.12. Dauid,2 Sam.16.10. & 19.v.22.23. Rex Israel,2 Reg.6.23. Dauid, Psal. 7,5. Chri-
units.tr: Vengeance for an injury received is to be committed to God. Examples: Joseph, Gen. 50:19; Saul, 1 Sam. 11:13; 24:12; David, 2 Sam. 16:10; 19:22, 23; the king of Israel, 2 Kings 6:23; David, Ps. 7:5. Chri-

units.la: 7.5. Christus, Esa.53.7.1 Pet.2.21.&c. Luc.23.34. Stephanus, Act.7.60.
units.tr: 7.5. Christus, Esa.53.7. 1 Pet.2.21.&c. Luc.23.34. Stephanus, Act.7.60.

units.la: VINDICTAE expetitae, & eorum quae inde consecuta sunt exempla: Filij Iacob, Genef.34.v.25.26. Samson, Iudic.16.v.28.&c. Abner,2 Sam.3.9. Absalonis, 14.30. Aman, Esth.3.6.&c.
units.tr: Examples of vengeance sought and of what followed from it: the sons of Jacob, Genef.34.v.25.26. Samson, Iudic.16.v.28.&c. Abner, 2 Sam.3.9. Absalom, 14.30. Haman, Esth.3.6.&c.

units.la: VINDICTAM interdum Sacerdotes & Prophetae vi corporali exercuerunt. Exempla: Moses per filios Leui iubet occidi idololatras, Exod.32.v.26.27. Phinees occidit Zambri & Cozbi, Nu.25.v.7.8.14.15.1 Machab.2.54. Samuel Agagum, 1 Sam.15.32.33. Elias Propheta Prophetas Baal, 1 Regum 18.40. Vindictae propriae punitae exempla: Idumaei, Ezech.25.v.12.13. Palaesthini, v.15.16.
units.tr: Sometimes priests and prophets carried out vengeance by physical force. Examples: Moses orders the sons of Levi to kill the idolaters, Exod.32.v.26.27. Phinehas kills Zimri and Cozbi, Num.25.v.7.8.14.15. 1 Macc.2.54. Samuel (kills) Agag, 1 Sam.15.32.33. Elijah, the prophet, (kills) the prophets of Baal, 1 Kings 18.40. Examples of one's own vengeance being punished: the Edomites, Ezek.25.v.12.13. The Philistines, v.15.16.

units.la: VINDEMIA vber obedientibus, Leuit.26.5. vindemiae leges, 19.10.
units.tr: The vintage is abundant for the obedient, Lev.26.5. The laws of the vintage, 19.10.

units.la: VINDEMIAE interdum, ad Ecclesiae calamitates referetur, Ps. 80.13. Thren.1.12.&2.20. ad excidium impiorum, Thren.1.21. Apoc.14.v.18.19. Vindemiatores, persecutores Ecclesiae, Ierem.49.9. Abd.v.5.]
units.tr: The vintage is sometimes applied to the calamities of the Church, Ps.80.13. Lam.1.12 & 2.20; to the destruction of the wicked, Lam.1.21. Rev.14.v.18.19. Vintagers are the persecutors of the Church, Jer.49.9. Obad. v.5.]

units.la: VINDEX Deus, 1 Thess.4.6. [Apoc.6.10.&19.20. vindex magistratus, Rom.13.4.]
units.tr: God is the avenger, 1 Thess.4.6. [Rev.6.10 & 19.20. The magistrate is the avenger, Rom.13.4.]

units.la: VINEA, Salomonis, Cantic.8.11. Dei L. Esa.5.1 Matth.20.1. &21.33. vinea a Noe plantatur, Genef.9.20. diuersis generibus non serenda, Deuter.22.9. vinea proximi non laedenda, Exodi 22.5. Deuter 23.24. licet ex eius vuis decerpere & comedere, ibid. vinea Dei, Iudaei, Matt.21.33. Mar.12.1. vineae parabola, vide PARABOLA. vineae & Agricolarum similitudine notata impietas Sacerdotum, Luc.20.9. Inobedientes suis vineis non fruuntur: Deut.28.30.39. Isa 66.21.
units.tr: VINEYARD: of Solomon, Cant.8.11. The vineyard of the Lord, Isa.5.1. Matt.20.1 & 21.33. The vineyard is planted by Noah, Gen.9.20. Not to be sown with diverse kinds, Deut.22.9. A neighbour's vineyard not to be harmed, Exod.22.5. Deut.23.24: it is lawful to pluck and eat its grapes, ibid. The vineyard of God, the Jews, Matt.21.33. Mark 12.1. For the parable of the vineyard, see PARABLE. The impiety of the priests is marked by the likeness of the vineyard and the husbandmen, Luke 20.9. Those who disobey do not enjoy their vineyards: Deut.28.30.39. Isa.66.21.

units.la: [Vinea mystica, allegorica, parabolica, 1. sub cuius descriptione status Ecclesiae proponitur, Cant. 1.6. & 2.13. Ezec.17. verf. 6. 8.&19.10. Matth.20.1. &c. & 21.v.28.33.39. 41, Vinea Sodomea, vinea Iudae 12. Deut.32.32.
units.tr: [Mystical, allegorical, parabolical vineyard: 1. under whose description the state of the Church is set forth, Cant.1.6 & 2.13. Ezek.17 v.6.8 & 19.10. Matt.20.1 &c. & 21.v.28.33.39.41. The vineyard of Sodom, the vineyard of Judah, Deut.32.32.]

units.la: VINVM, hominis cor recreat ac reficit. Iudic.9.13. Psalm.104.15. vinum quibus & quando prohibitum: nempe Leuitis intrantibus Tabernaculum, & Israelitis facientibus votum, Leuit.10.9. Num.6.3. Exempla: Vxor Manue, Iudic.13, v.13.14. Ioannes Baptista, Luc. 1.15. vinum in diserto Israelitae non biberunt annis x L. Deut.29.6. vinum dat Deus obedientibus, 11.14.&28.39. vnum myrrhatum, id est, myrrha conditum, Christo crucifixo exhibetur, Marci 15. 23. vinum Coenę Dominicæ, dicitur fœdus nouum, per metonymiam Scripturæ familiarem, Luc. 21. 20. vinum nouum in vtres nouos infundendum, Matth. 9.17. Luc. 5. 36. &c. Vini abusus quàm noxius, Prou. 20. 1. & 23.30. & 31. v. 4.5. Esa. 5.11. Ephes. 5. 18. Tit. 1.7. & 2.3. pauculo & modico vino vtendum, 1 Tim. 5.23. vini potatorem esse Christum, criminantur Iudæi, Matt. 11.19.
units.tr: Wine refreshes and cheers the heart. Judg. 9.13. Ps. 104.15. On which occasions and to whom wine was forbidden: namely to the Levites when they entered the Tabernacle, and to Israelites making a vow, Lev. 10.9. Num. 6.3. Examples: the wife of Manoah, Judg. 13.13-14; John the Baptist, Luke 1.15. The Israelites in the desert did not drink wine for forty years, Deut. 29.6. God gives wine to the obedient, Deut. 11.14 and 28.39. Myrrhed wine, that is wine mixed with myrrh, was offered to Christ on the cross, Mark 15.23. The wine of the Lord's Supper is called the new covenant, by a metonymy familiar in Scripture, Luke 22.20. New wine must be poured into new wineskins, Matt. 9.17; Luke 5.36, etc. How harmful the abuse of wine is: Prov. 20.1; 23.30; 31.4-5; Isa. 5.11; Eph. 5.18; Titus 1.7; 2.3. Wine is to be used in small and moderate amounts, 1 Tim. 5.23. The Jews accuse Christ of being a winebibber, Matt. 11.19.

units.la: [vinum mysticum, Cantic. 5.1. & 8.2. Esai. 55.1. vinum iræ Dei, Ps. 75.9. & Ierem. 25.15. Apoc. 14. v. 8.10. & 16.19. & 17. 2. & 18. v. 3.13. & 19.15. vinum figuratè sumitur pro actionibus humanis. Deut. 32.33. Prouerb. 4.17. Esai. 1.22. vinum compunct. 1. vertiginis spiritus, Ps. 60 5.
units.tr: Mystical wine, Song 5.1; 8.2; Isa. 55.1. The wine of God's wrath, Ps. 75.9; Jer. 25.15; Rev. 14.8, 10; 16.19; 17.2; 18.3, 13; 19.15. Wine is taken figuratively for human actions, Deut. 32.33; Prov. 4.17; Isa. 1.22. Wine of compunction, that is, of a spirit of giddiness, Ps. 60.5.

units.la: VIOLENTIA damnatur, Leuit. 25.53. Prou. 22.22. 28. ver. 15. 16. 17. 18. Ezech. 46.18. Mich. 2.1. &c. & 3. v. 2.34. violentię merces, Prou. 11.24. Iob. 27.13. &c. A violentis vindicandi pauperes: Iob. 5.15. violenti rapiunt regnum Dei: Matth. 11.12. Luc. 16.16.
units.tr: VIOLENCE is condemned, Lev. 25.53; Prov. 22.22; 28.15-18; Ezek. 46.18; Mic. 2.1; 3.2-3, etc. The wages of violence, Prov. 11.24; Job 27.13, etc. The poor are to be defended against the violent, Job 5.15. The violent take the kingdom of God by force, Matt. 11.12; Luke 16.16.

units.la: VIPERA, cuius familia semper funesta est, & dirus ortus. formina marem necat in coeundo, & dentibus caput ei abscindit. Fœtus matrem in vindictam patris exeundo lacerant, & trucidant aluum eius erodentes. Vide Iob. 20. 16. Esa. 30.6.
units.tr: The VIPER, whose brood is always deadly and whose birth is dire. The female kills the male in mating and bites off his head with her teeth. The young, coming out to avenge their father, tear their mother apart and gnaw through her belly to kill her. See Job 20.16; Isa. 30.6.

units.la: VIPERAE morsus Act. 28 3. viperarum genimina, Matth. 3. 7 & 12.34. & 23.33 V. Marc. 16.18. Luc. 10.19.
units.tr: The VIPER's bite, Acts 28.3. Brood of vipers, Matt. 3.7; 12.34; 23.33. Mark 16.18; Luke 10.19.

units.la: VIR pro indefinita particula, quidam, Act. 8.27. pro quovis homine, Gen. 49.6. Vide HOMO. Vir à muliere seductu, 3. v. 6. 12. 1 Timot. 2.14. vir mulieris caput est, 1 Cor. 11.3. Ephes. 5.23. & dominus, Gen. 3.16. & 18.12. 1 Petri 3. v. 5.6. vir imago & gloria Dei est, 1 Cor. 11.7. hoc est, imago gloriæ Dei, in qua nimirum elucet Dei maiestas & imperiū. Est enim vir in supremo gradu collocatus in hoc mundo, & tanquam secundarius aliquis Deus, vt ita dicam, ipsius etiam mulieris respectu: alioquin si mulierem cum cæteris creaturis conferas, est & ipsa Dei imago: nam illis dominatur, & vsum earum habet: sed hoc loco mulier cum viro collata, non dicitur imago Dei, quia viro non dominatur, sed potius ei paret. Viri gloria mulier, 1 Cor. 11.7. Non vir ex muliere, sed mulier ex viro: neque vir propter mulierem, sed mulier propter virum condita est, 1 Cor. 11. v. 8.9.
units.tr: VIR, used as an indefinite particle, "someone", Acts 8.27; for any man, Gen. 49.6. See HOMO. Man was not deceived by woman, but woman by the serpent, and the woman was deceived, 1 Tim. 2.14. The man is the head of the woman, 1 Cor. 11.3; Eph. 5.23, and her lord, Gen. 3.16; 18.12; 1 Pet. 3.5-6. Man is the image and glory of God, 1 Cor. 11.7, that is, the image of the glory of God, in which indeed God's majesty and rule shine forth. For man is placed in the highest rank in this world, and is as it were a secondary god, so to speak, even in relation to woman herself. Otherwise, if you compare woman with the other creatures, she too is God's image, for she rules over them and has their use; but in this place woman, compared with man, is not called the image of God, because she does not rule over man but rather obeys him. Woman is the glory of man, 1 Cor. 11.7. Man was not made from woman, but woman from man; nor was man created for woman, but woman for man, 1 Cor. 11.8-9.

units.la: VIRE
units.tr: MEN

units.la: VIRI vxores suas diligere debent, Ephes. 5. v. 25. 28. 29. 33. Col. 3. 19. Viri quomodo orare debeant, 1 Cor. 11. 14. 1 Tim. 2. 8. Virorum erga vxores officium, 1 Pet. 3. 7. Ephes. 5. 25. Col. 3. 19. vide MARITI.
units.tr: Husbands ought to love their wives, Eph.5 v.25.28.29.33. Col.3.19. How men ought to pray, 1 Cor.11.14. 1 Tim.2.8. The duty of husbands toward their wives, 1 Pet.3.7. Eph.5.25. Col.3.19. See HUSBANDS.

units.la: VIR belli, id est, magnus bellator, vel bellicosissimus, Exodi 15. 3. 1 Reg. 5. 3. Esa. 42. 13. Ierem. 49. v. 26. 30. & 52. 7. Ezech. 27. v. 10, 27. Osee 2. 7. Ioel. 3. 9. Viri belli, pro viri ad bellum apti & idonei. Deut. 2. 14. viri Belial, pro hominibus nequam, 1 Reg. 2. 10. vir mortis, id est reus mortis, 2. 2 6. viri nominis, id est celeberrimi, Genes. 6, 4. Numer. 16. 2. 1 Paral. 5. 24. viri roboris, id est, strenui, 2 Sam. 24. 9. Es. 5. 22. Vir sanguinum, id est, sanguinarius, 2 Sam. 16. 7. Psalm. 26. 9. & 55. 24. Vir Dei, Propheta, 1 Sam. 9. 6. vlr ne vtatur vestie muliebri, Deut. 22. 5. vir vxorem habeat, 1 Corinth. 7, 2. Virorum raritas in excidio Ierusalem, Esaiae 4. 1.
units.tr: A man of war, that is, a great warrior or a most warlike man, Exod.15.3. 1 Kings 5.3. Isa.42.13. Jer.49 v.26.30 & 52.7. Ezek.27 v.10.27. Hos.2.7. Joel 3.9. Men of war, for men fit and suited for war, Deut.2.14. Men of Belial, for worthless men, 1 Kings 2.10. A man of death, that is, one liable to death, 2.26. Men of renown, that is, most famous, Gen.6.4. Num.16.2. 1 Chron.5.24. Men of strength, that is, valiant, 2 Sam.24.9. Isa.5.22. A man of blood, that is, bloodthirsty, 2 Sam.16.7. Ps.26.9 & 55.24. A man of God, a prophet, 1 Sam.9.6. A man shall not wear woman's clothing, Deut.22.5. Let each man have a wife, 1 Cor.7.2. The scarcity of men at the destruction of Jerusalem, Isa.4.1.

units.la: VIRA a viro dicta est Eua, Gen. 2. 23.
units.tr: Eve was named from man, Gen.2.23.

units.la: VIRILITER agendum, Deut. 31. 6. Ios. 1. 18. Psam. 17. 14. 1 Cor. 16. 13.
units.tr: To act manfully, Deut.31.6. Josh.1.18. Ps.17.14. 1 Cor.16.13.

units.la: VIRIBVS nostris non vult Deus nos quicquam tribuere, Ios. 4. 8. &c. Iudic. 7. 2. &c. vires tribuit Deus, Deut. 8. 18. de viribus diffidit Gedeon, Iudic. 6. 15.
units.tr: God does not want us to attribute anything to our own strength, Josh.4.8 &c. Judg.7.2 &c. God gives strength, Deut.8.18. Gideon distrusted his own strength, Judg.6.15.

units.la: VIRGA Aaronis germinat, Numer. 17. 8. Virga Mosis versa in colubrum, Exod. 4. 3. vide MIRACVLA. Virga pastoris pro seueritate, 1 Corint. 4. 21. Virgam tollere secum prohibentur Apostoli, Matt. 10. 10. vbi virgae nomine intelligitur baculus, qui oneri sit ferenti. Christus, Marci 6. 8, permittit hoc fieri, vt nimirum virgam tollant Apostoli, Virga percutit petram Moses. Exodi 17. 5.
units.tr: Aaron's rod budded, Num.17.8. Moses' rod turned into a serpent, Exod.4.3. See MIRACLES. A shepherd's rod stands for severity, 1 Cor.4.21. The Apostles are forbidden to take a staff with them, Matt.10.10, where by "staff" is understood a walking stick that is a burden to the one carrying it. Christ, Mark 6.8, permits this to be done, so that the Apostles may take a staff. Moses strikes the rock with his rod, Exod.17.5.

units.la: VIRGA, virgula, virgultum, de Christo ipso dicitur, Esai. 11. 1.
units.tr: Rod, twig, shoot is said of Christ himself, Isa.11.1.

units.la: 2. Baculus Dei in manu Mosis Exod. 4. v. 2. 4, 17, 20, item cap. 7, 8, 9, 10, 17, Baculus patrisfamilias, Exod. 21, 20, 3. Virga Angeli, Iudic. 6, 21, Baculus hominis, 2. Sam. 23. 21. Matth. 10. 10.
units.tr: 2. The staff of God in the hand of Moses, Exod.4 v.2.4.17.20, likewise chapters 7, 8, 9, 10, 17. The staff of the head of the household, Exod.21.20. 3. The rod of the angel, Judg.6.21. The staff of a man, 2 Sam.23.21. Matt.10.10.

units.la: 4. Virga, Pedum, 1. benigna dominatio & protectio Christi pastoris Ecclesiae, Psal. 23. 4, Mich. 7, 14, Zach. 11, v. 7, 10, 14.
units.tr: 4. Rod, crook: 1. the gentle rule and protection of Christ the shepherd of the Church, Ps.23.4. Mic.7.14. Zech.11 v.7.10.14.

units.la: 5. Sceptrum Christi, Ecclesiae suae respectu, Psalm. 45, 7 & 110, 5, Hebr. 1, 8, Impiorum respectu, Psal. 2, 9: Apoc. 2, 27.& 12.5.& 19.15.Vox seu verbum Christi.Esai.11.4. 6.Virga flagellum Dei,Iob.9 34.& 21.9.Psal.89. 33. Esai. 10.5.& 30.32.Thren.3 1. 7. Portio,Psal.74 2.Ierem.10.16.Robur,vis Latens, Ezech.14.13. Sceptrum hominis,Num.24.17. Esther.4 11.& 5.2.Dominatio potens,superba,tyrannica,violenta, Esai. 9.3.& 10.26.& 14,verf.5. 29.& 30.31. Ierem.48. 17. Psalm. 125. 3. Prouerb. 22.8.Ezech. 7.10. &19.v.11.12.14. Nahum. 13.]
units.tr: 5. The sceptre of Christ, with respect to his Church, Ps.45.7 & 110.5. Heb.1.8. With respect to the wicked, Ps.2.9; Rev.2.27 & 12.5 & 19.15. The voice or word of Christ, Isa.11.4. 6. The rod, the scourge of God, Job 9.34 & 21.9. Ps.89.33. Isa.10.5 & 30.32. Lam.3.1.7. A portion, Ps.74.2. Jer.10.16. Strength, hidden power, Ezek.14.13. The sceptre of man, Num.24.17. Esther 4.11 & 5.2. Powerful, proud, tyrannical, violent dominion, Isa.9.3 & 10.26 & 14 v.5.29 & 30.31. Jer.48.17. Ps.125.3. Prov.22.8. Ezek.7.10 & 19 v.11.12.14. Nahum 1.3.

units.la: VIRGO desponsata in agro vi compressa, & eius lex, Deut. 22.v.25.26.27.(vide Exod. 22. 16.) virgo desponsata in ciuitate compressa, Deut.22. v.23.24. virgo memini desponsata compressa,v.28.29. virgo mater Messiæ,Matth.1. v.18.23.
units.tr: VIRGIN betrothed and violated in the field, and the law concerning her, Deut. 22.v.25.26.27. (See Exod. 22.16.) A virgin betrothed and violated in the city, Deut. 22.v.23.24. A virgin, not betrothed, violated, v.28.29. The virgin mother of the Messiah, Matth. 1.v.18.23.

units.la: [virgo,Ecclesia Christi,2.Corinth. 11.2.vrbs & Ecclesia Hierosolymitana, atque adeo Iudea ipsa, 2. Reg.19. 21.Esai.37.22. Ierem. 14.7. & 18.13.& 31.4.21.Thren.1.5.& 2.v.2 13.Amos.5.2.virginis nomine designatur ciuitates & regna quæ fama, dignitate, diuitiis florent, Esai.47.1. Ierem.46.11.)
units.tr: [Virgin: the Church of Christ, 2 Corinth. 11.2; the city and Church of Jerusalem, and indeed Judea itself, 2 Kings 19.21; Isa. 37.22; Jer. 14.7, 18.13, 31.4, 21; Lam. 1.5, 2.2, 13; Amos 5.2. By the name of virgin are designated cities and kingdoms that flourish in fame, dignity and riches, Isa. 47.1; Jer. 46.11.]

units.la: VIRGINES Silo rapiuntur, & quare, Iudic.21.23.virgines in bello raptæ, seruandæ, Nume.31.18. in choreis raptę, Iudic.21.23.
units.tr: VIRGINS are carried off at Shiloh, and why, Judg. 21.23. Virgins taken in war are to be spared, Num. 31.18. Virgins seized from the dances, Judg. 21.23.

units.la: VIRGINVM officium,1 Corinth.7.34. virginum exeuntium obuiam iponso parabola,Matth.25.1.&c.
units.tr: The duty of virgins, 1 Corinth. 7.34. The parable of the virgins going out to meet the bridegroom, Matth. 25.1, etc.

units.la: VIRGINITAS commendatur,Matth.19.12.1. Corin.7.25 &c. Apoc 14.4.prefertur coniugio,1 Cor.7.v.38 40. sed non simpliciter,verùm propter instantem necessitatem, vt ibidem additur,v. 26. virginitatis finis quis,7.25.virginitatis merita confutans locus,v.28.virginitatem filiæ quomodo testentur parentes apud Iudæos,Deut.22.15.
units.tr: Virginity is commended, Matth. 19.12; 1 Cor. 7.25, etc.; Apoc. 14.4. It is preferred to marriage, 1 Cor. 7.38-40, but not absolutely; rather on account of the pressing necessity, as is added there in v.26. What is the end of virginity, 7.25. A passage refuting the merits of virginity, v.28. How parents attest the virginity of their daughter among the Jews, Deut. 22.15.

units.la: VIRIDI ligno Christo non parcitur,Luc.23.31.
units.tr: Christ is not spared, as the green wood is not spared, Luke 23.31.

units.la: VIRTVS virtus moralis, est habitus in voluntate regenita a Spiritu sancto creatus, inclinans ad serium studium honestè viuendi secundùm Legis diuinæ præscriptum, externis actionibus perpetuò & constanter sese exerens. 2 Pet.1,5.
units.tr: Moral virtue is a habit created in the will, regenerated by the Holy Spirit, inclining a person to earnest zeal for living honourably according to the prescription of the divine Law, and constantly and continually expressing itself in outward actions. 2 Pet. 1.5.

units.la: virtutes Gentilium, simulacra potiùs virtutum erant,quàm solidæ virtutes:ideóque ab Augustino splendida peccata nominantur. Nam plerúmque illi omnia propter vanam gloriam faciebant, semper autem sine fide Rom.14 23.
units.tr: The virtues of the Gentiles were more like images of virtues than solid virtues; therefore Augustine calls them splendid sins. For for the most part they did all things for empty glory, and always without faith, Rom. 14.23.

units.la: VIRTVS pro sanctis & honestis moribus, quorum fons est fides, 2 Petr. 1.5. virtutis habitum non a natura omnibus hominibus communi, qualis nunc est, sed a gratia illa revocate proficisci docet Paulus, Rom. 12. 2. Virtutes Christianae enumerantur, ibid. v. 9. &c. omnibus piis communes, in uno cumulo proferuntur, & enumerantur, 2 Pet. 1. 5. &c. Virtutes pro edendorum illorum, quae inter miracula excellunt, effectorum facultate, 1 Cor. 12. v. 10. 28. Virtus Dei, Euangelium, quo nos saluat, Roman. 1 16. virtute Dei custodimur in fide. 1 Pet. 1. 5. virtute indui ex alto, Lucae 24. 49. virtutes operatur Deus in nobis, Galat. 3. 5. Virtutis laus, Sap. 4. 1. &c.
units.tr: VIRTUE for holy and honourable conduct, whose source is faith, 2 Pet. 1.5. Paul teaches that the habit of virtue does not arise from nature, which is common to all men as it now is, but from that renewing grace, Rom. 12.2. The Christian virtues are enumerated, ibid. v.9, etc., and are set forth and listed together in one heap, common to all the godly, 2 Pet. 1.5, etc. Virtues for the power of producing those effects which excel among the miracles, 1 Cor. 12.v.10, 28. The virtue of God: the Gospel, by which he saves us, Rom. 1.16. We are kept by the virtue of God through faith, 1 Pet. 1.5. To be clothed with virtue from on high, Luke 24.49. God works virtues in us, Gal. 3.5. The praise of virtue, Wisd. 4.1, etc.

units.la: VIRTVS, quum ad homines refertur, signif. plerunque militarem fortitudinem, & vir aut filius virtutis nominatur, qui in quocunque genere negotij aut operis est industrius, sedulus, ac solers. Mulier virtutis, 1. virtute praedita, ea dicitur, quae praeter pudicitiam cordata, intelligens, & in re familiari tractanda educandisque liberis strenua conspicitur. V. Pro. 31. 10. &c.
units.tr: VIRTUE, when it is referred to men, usually signifies military courage; and a man or son of virtue is called one who is industrious, diligent and skilful in whatever kind of business or work he is engaged. A woman of virtue is one who, endowed with virtue, is seen to be, besides chaste, sensible, intelligent, and vigorous in managing household affairs and in bringing up children. See Prov. 31.10, etc.

units.la: 2. Virtus exercitum denotat, & de Deo dicitur quod sit virtus suorum, atque virtutum 1. exercituum superorum atque inferorum Deus. Virtutes caelorum etiam mouebuntur, inquit Christus, Luc. 21. 26.
units.tr: 2. Virtue denotes an army, and of God it is said that he is the virtue of his people, and the God of the virtues (armies) of the heavenly and earthly hosts. "The virtues of the heavens will be moved," says Christ, Luke 21.26.

units.la: 3. Nonnunquam significat fortia facta & praeclara opera Dei & hominum, ut sunt victoriae in bello, liberatio ab extremis periculis, Ecclesiae protectio, &c. Sic miracula Christi & Apostolorum vocantur virtutes, vbi virtus effectum diuinae potentiae denotat.
units.tr: 3. Sometimes it signifies the brave and outstanding deeds of God and men, such as victories in war, deliverance from extreme dangers, the protection of the Church, etc. Thus the miracles of Christ and the apostles are called virtues, where virtue denotes the effect of divine power.

units.la: 4. Aliquoties pro causa efficaci & potente sumitur, ut Act. 1. 8. & 3. 12. & 4. 33. Hoc sensu Euangelium dicitur virtus seu potentia Dei ad salutem omni credenti. Sic & magus ille, Act. 8. 10. volebat vocari Dei virtus.
units.tr: 4. Sometimes it is taken for an efficacious and powerful cause, as in Acts 1.8, 3.12, 4.33. In this sense the Gospel is called the virtue or power of God unto salvation for everyone who believes. So too that magician, Acts 8.10, wished to be called the virtue of God.

units.la: 5. Virtus Christi, i. potentia qua agit in suis Virtus fidei, &c. id est, efficacia illa Spiritus Sancti in credentibus ut in fide crescant unde bona opera.
units.tr: 5. The virtue of Christ, that is, the power by which he works in his own people. The virtue of faith, etc., that is, that efficacy of the Holy Spirit in believers by which they grow in faith, and from which come good works.

units.la: 6. Virtus Dei, Sapientissima illa omnipotentia quae in operibus creationis, conseruationis rerum, adoptionis, redemptionis & salutis suorum electorum varie & abunde elucet.]
units.tr: 6. The virtue of God: that most wise omnipotence which shines forth variously and abundantly in the works of creation, the preservation of things, adoption, redemption, and the salvation of his elect.

units.la: VISCERA, ex Hebraeorum idiotismo, pro tenerrimis & intimo cordi insidentibus misericordiae summae affectibus, Luc. 1. 78. 2. Col. 6. 12. & 7. 15. Philip. 1 8. & 2 1. Coloss.
units.tr: BOWELS, by a Hebrew idiom, for the tenderest and most intense affections of supreme mercy, seated in the innermost heart, Luke 1.78; Col. 6.12; 7.15; Phil. 1.8; 2.1; Col. 3.12.

units.la: 3.12.Solent enim Hebræi omnes tenores ac veluti matres nos affectus vocare viscera. Viscera claudere, Hebræis idem declarat, quod non aperire alicui veluti pectus suum, nec prompto succurrere animo, 1 Ioan.3.17.
units.tr: For the Hebrews call all the tender affections, as it were the mothers of our feelings, "bowels". To shut up one's bowels means for the Hebrews the same as not to open one's breast to someone and not readily to come to his aid in mind, 1 John 3.17.

units.la: VISERE Sanctos desiderat Paulus, Roman.1.11. & 15. v.23.32 Gal.4.20. 1 Thess.2 17.
units.tr: Paul desires to see the saints, Rom. 1.11; 15.23, 32; Gal. 4.20; 1 Thess. 2.17.

units.la: VISIONES servis Dei olim valde frequentes. Nume.12.6. &c. exempla: in Iacobo, Genesis 46.2 Samuele, 1 Sam. 3.7.&c Nathan Propheta, 2 Sam.7.17. Addo viuente, 2 Paralip.9.29. Esaia, Esa.6.1. Ieremia, Ierem.24.v.1,2. Ezechiele, Ezech.1.v.4.19.&8.v.1.2.&10.1.&c.&11.22.&c.37.1.&40.verfic.1.2. Daniele, Dan.7.2.&8.2.&10.5. Amos, Amos 8.1. Zacharia, Zach.4.2 & 5.verf.2.6.&6 1 Christo, Luc.4.5. Petro. Actor. 10. 11. Paulo, 16.9. & 22.18.&26.13. & 27.23.2. Cor.12.v.1,2. Ioanne, Apocal.1.12.&4 2.&5.1.&6.2. &7. v.1.2.&8.2.&10.4.&11.4.&12.1.&13.1. &14.1. &15.1. &17.5.&18.1.&16. v. 11. 17. & 20.1.&21.1.&22.1. Vide APPARITIONVM & peculiarium Dei revelationum exempla. In visione raro se manifestabat Deus tempore Heli in Silo, 1 Sam.3.1.
units.tr: Visions were once very frequent for the servants of God, Num. 12.6, etc. Examples: in Jacob, Gen. 46.2; in Samuel, 1 Sam. 3.7, etc.; in Nathan the prophet, 2 Sam. 7.17; I add Iddo, while he lived, 2 Chr. 9.29; in Isaiah, Isa. 6.1; in Jeremiah, Jer. 24.1-2; in Ezekiel, Ezek. 1.4, 19; 8.1-2; 10.1, etc.; 11.22, etc.; 37.1; 40.1-2; in Daniel, Dan. 7.2; 8.2; 10.5; in Amos, Amos 8.1; in Zechariah, Zech. 4.2; 5.2, 6; 6.1; to Christ, Luke 4.5; to Peter, Acts 10.11; to Paul, Acts 16.9; 22.18; 26.13; 27.23; 2 Cor. 12.1-2; to John, Rev. 1.12; 4.2; 5.1; 6.2; 7.1-2; 8.2; 10.4; 11.4; 12.1; 13.1; 14.1; 15.1; 17.5; 18.1, 16; 19.11, 17; 20.1; 21.1; 22.1. See APPARITIONS and the examples of particular revelations of God. In the time of Eli at Shiloh God rarely revealed himself in vision, 1 Sam. 3.1.

units.la: VISITARE, pro animaduertere in aliquem, Exod.20.5. Deut.5.9. Osea.2.13.&4.9. ideoque visitare dicitur Deus peccata, quum punit illa, Exodi 32.34. Visitare aegrotos, Vide AEGROTI visitandi & consolandi.
units.tr: VISIT, for to take notice of someone, Exod. 20.5; Deut. 5.9; Hos. 2.13; 4.9. Therefore God is said to visit sins when he punishes them, Exod. 32.34. To visit the sick: see SICK, visiting and comforting.

units.la: VITA, pro perduratione in periculis pro Christo adeundis, 2 Corint.4.10. vita aeterna pro Christo, 1 Ioan. 5.20. vitae optime instituendae ratio Matt.7.12. Lucae 6.31. vita mandatorum Dei observatoribus promissa, Leuit.18. 5.&25.18. Deut.6.v.17.18.&28.1.&c. Prou.7.2. Ezec.20.11. Matth.19.17. Marc.10.v.17.19. Luc.10.28.&18.18. Galat.3.12. vita per Legis transgressionem perdita, Roman.6.23. Ephes.2.1. per Christum restituta, Roman.6.23. Ephes.2.5. 2 Timoth. 1.10. 1 Ioann.4.9.&5.11. in Euangelio patefacta, Rom.1.17. Ephes.1.17. Phil.2.15.16. ex gratuita Dei bonitate, Luc.12.32. Ioan.10.28. Rom.6.23. 1 Ioann.5.11.&Christi misericordia profecta, Iudę v.21. Electis & fidelibus Deum timentibus apparata, Matthaei 19.17. & 20.23. & 24.13. Marci 10.30. Lucae 6.20.&18.30. Ioan.3.ver.15.36.&4.14.&5.24.&6.ver.33.40 47.54.&10.28.&11.25.&12.25.&14.2.&17.2.&20.31 Roman.2.7.&6.22. &8.17. 1 Corinth.9.25. 2 Cor.4.17.2 Timoth.2.5. Tit.3.7. Hebr.4.3. &10.22. &12. 14.Iac.2.5.2 Petr.1.11.1 Ioan.2.25.&5.13. Iudae ver.21. Vitae æteræternæ excellentia, 1 Petri 1.4.
units.tr: LIFE, for endurance in the dangers to be faced for Christ, 2 Cor. 4.10; eternal life for Christ, 1 John 5.20. The method of ordering life in the best way, Matth. 7.12; Luke 6.31. Life promised to the observers of God's commandments, Lev. 18.5; 25.18; Deut. 6.17-18; 28.1, etc.; Prov. 7.2; Ezek. 20.11; Matth. 19.17; Mark 10.17-19; Luke 10.28; 18.18; Gal. 3.12. Life lost through transgression of the Law, Rom. 6.23; Eph. 2.1; restored through Christ, Rom. 6.23; Eph. 2.5; 2 Tim. 1.10; 1 John 4.9; 5.11; revealed in the Gospel, Rom. 1.17; Eph. 1.17; Phil. 2.15-16; from the free goodness of God, Luke 12.32; John 10.28; Rom. 6.23; 1 John 5.11; and proceeding from the mercy of Christ, Jude v.21. Prepared for the elect and for the faithful who fear God, Matth. 19.17; 20.23; 24.13; Mark 10.30; Luke 6.20; 18.30; John 3.15-16, 36; 4.14; 5.24; 6.33, 40, 47, 54; 10.28; 11.25; 12.25; 14.2; 17.2; 20.31; Rom. 2.7; 6.22; 8.17; 1 Cor. 9.25; 2 Cor. 4.17; 2 Tim. 2.5; Titus 3.7; Heb. 4.3; 10.22; 12.14; James 2.5; 2 Pet. 1.11; 1 John 2.25; 5.13; Jude v.21. The excellence of life, 1 Pet. 1.4.

units.la: VITA ÆTERNA, est vita gloriæ, qua anima corpori adiun-cta, Deo fruitur in æternum, cuecta ad summum felicitatis suæ culmen & fastigium, in gloriam Dei & gratiæ eius celebrationem.
units.tr: ETERNAL LIFE is the life of glory, in which the soul, joined to the body, enjoys God forever, with all things brought to the highest peak and summit of its happiness, to the glory of God and the celebration of his grace.

units.la: Vita Dei, pro ea vita, qua Deus in suis viuit, Ephes. 4.18. vita præsens in quo sita, Deuter. 8. 3. certo termino definita, Iob. 14.5. Christo posthabenda, Matth. 10.39. & 16.v. 25.26. Luc. 9. 24. vitæ fidelium scopus, Roman. 14.7. Tit. 2.v. 8. 10. vitæ humanæ breuitas, ac vanitas, Genes. 3 19.2 Sam. 14.14.1 Paral. 29.15, Iob. 3.20. & 7.1. & 8.9. & 9.21. & 13, 28. & 14.ver. 1.5. & 16.22. Psalm. 39.6. & 62. 10. & 90.v.6.9. 10. & 102.v.4.24. & 103.15. & 109.23. & 144.4. Esa. 40.v.6. 7. Luc. 12.18.1. Co. 7.29. Ephes. 5.16. Hebr. 13.14. Iacob. 1.10. & 4.14.1 Petri 1 24.2. Petr. 3.8. vitæ humanæ finis, 1 Cor. 10, 31. vide GLORIA Dei.
units.tr: The life of God, as opposed to that life by which God lives in his people, Ephes. 4.18. The present life, in which it consists, Deuter. 8.3. Limited by a fixed end, Job 14.5. To be placed below Christ, Matth. 10.39 and 16.25-26; Luke 9.24. The goal of the lives of the faithful, Rom. 14.7; Tit. 2.8, 10. The brevity and vanity of human life, Gen. 3.19; 2 Sam. 14.14; 1 Chron. 29.15; Job 3.20; 7.1; 8.9; 9.21; 13.28; 14.1, 5; 16.22; Psalm 39.6; 62.10; 90.6, 9-10; 102.4, 24; 103.15; 109.23; 144.4; Isa. 40.6-7; Luke 12.18; 1 Cor. 7.29; Ephes. 5.16; Heb. 13.14; James 1.10; 4.14; 1 Pet. 1.24; 2 Pet. 3.8. The end of human life, 1 Cor. 10.31. See GLORY OF GOD.

units.la: Vitæ longitudo quibus promissa, Exodi 20.12. Deuteronomii 25.15.1 Reg. 3.14. Psalm. 91.16. Prou. 3. ver. 16. 18. & 9.11. & 10.27. & 11.30. & 28.16. Esaiæ 65.20. Ephes. 6.v.2.3. vita æterna est cognoscere Deum, & IESVM, Ioann. 17.3. datur gratis, Roman. 6.23. datur ex obseruatione mandatorum, Matt. 19.17. vita Christianorum abscondita cum Christo in Deo, Coloss. 3.3. vitæ arbor, Genes. 2.9. offenditur, Apo. 22.2. vitæ æternæ & præsentis discrimen, Luc. 20.v. 34.35. 36. vitæ anteactæ memoria haud inutilis, Deut. 5.15. & 16, 12. Ezech. 36.31. Ioan. 4.29. Actor. 22.4. & 26.10. Rom. 6.17. 1 Corint. 6.11. & 12.2 Gala. 1.13. & 4.8. Ephes. 2.v.1.11. & 5.8. Coloss. 1.21. & 2.13. & 3.7.1 Thess. 1.9.1 Timot. 1.13. Tit. 3.3.1. Petr. 2.v, 10.25. & 4.3. vitæ vouitas, vide SANCTITATI itu-dendum.
units.tr: The length of life, to whom it is promised: Exod. 20.12; Deut. 25.15; 1 Kings 3.14; Ps. 91.16; Prov. 3.16, 18; 9.11; 10.27; 11.30; 28.16; Isa. 65.20; Eph. 6.2–3. Eternal life is to know God and Jesus, John 17.3. It is given freely, Rom. 6.23; it is given through the keeping of the commandments, Matt. 19.17. The life of Christians is hidden with Christ in God, Col. 3.3. The tree of life, Gen. 2.9; it is guarded, Rev. 22.2. The difference between eternal and present life, Luke 20.34–36. The memory of past life is not useless, Deut. 5.15; 16.12; Ezek. 36.31; John 4.29; Acts 22.4; 26.10; Rom. 6.17; 1 Cor. 6.11; 12.2; Gal. 1.13; 4.8; Eph. 2.1, 11; 5.8; Col. 1.21; 2.13; 3.7; 1 Thess. 1.9; 1 Tim. 1.13; Titus 3.3; 1 Pet. 2.10, 25; 4.3. The vow of life: see that it is to be praised for holiness.

units.la: Vitæ sanctimonia electionis scopus est, Eph. 1.4. & 2.10. 1 Thessal. 4.7. itaque fideles vitæ sanctitati studere debent. vide Sanctitas Genes. 17.1 Psalm. 15.v.1,2. & 24.v.4.5. & 73.37. Matth. 23.26, Roman. 6.4. & 8,1.2 Cor. 5.17. & 7.1. Eph. 2.10. & 4 17. Phil. 1.27. & 2.15. Hebr. 10.22. & 12.14. Iac. 3.13.1 Pet. 1.15. & 2.v.11.12.24. & 3.16. & 4.2.2. Pet. 1.4. & 3.v. 11.14.1 Ioan. 2.3. vita æterna quomodo possideatur, quæriq̃ diues ex Christo, Matth. 19.17. Marc. 10.7. vita per Christum parta, cum morte per Adamum introducta, comparatur, Roman. 5.17. vita nostra stadij instar est, 1 Cor. 9.24 vapor est, Iacob. 4.14.
units.tr: The holiness of life is the aim of election, Eph. 1.4; 2.10; 1 Thess. 4.7. Therefore believers ought to strive after holiness of life; see Holiness: Gen. 17.1; Ps. 15.1–2; 24.4–5; 73.37; Matt. 23.26; Rom. 6.4; 8.1–2; 2 Cor. 5.17; 7.1; Eph. 2.10; 4.17; Phil. 1.27; 2.15; Heb. 10.22; 12.14; James 3.13; 1 Pet. 1.15; 2.11–12, 24; 3.16; 4.2; 2 Pet. 1.4; 3.11, 14; 1 John 2.3. How eternal life is possessed, and how the rich man asks about it from Christ, Matt. 19.17; Mark 10.17. Life obtained through Christ, introduced by death through Adam, is set against it, Rom. 5.17. Our life is like a race, 1 Cor. 9.24; it is a vapour, James 4.14.

units.la: vitæ sermo qualiter recipiendus, 1. 22. vitæ sanctimoniâ probanda est Dei cognitio,vitę nouitas bo-nis operibus testanda est,in vitam reuocati ad coelum euocantur,vitæ liber, Exod.32.32. Philip.4.3. vide LIBER vita.vitam videre, pro vita frui:&,vitam non videre,pro vita non frui: Ioh.2.36.vitæ panis,Hebraismus,pro viuifico, seu vitali pane, Ioan.6.35.vitam pro fratribus ponere, Iudith.13.v.3.25.Esther.4.15.Ioann.15.13.1 Ioann.3.16. vitæ nouitas,pro noua vita,Hebraismus,Rom.6.4. vita æterna metonymicè dicitur Christus,1 Ioan.5.20.vita æterna,merces est,Mattæ.5.12.&20.8.donum Dei est,Rom.6.23. vide MERCES.
units.tr: How the word of life is to be received, Acts 1.22. The knowledge of God is to be proved by holiness of life; the newness of life is to be attested by good works; those recalled to life are called to heaven. The book of life, Exod. 32.32; Phil. 4.3; see BOOK of life. To see life means to enjoy life; and not to see life means not to enjoy life, John 2.36. The bread of life, a Hebraism, for the life-giving or living bread, John 6.35. To lay down life for the brethren, Judith 13.3, 25; Esther 4.15; John 15.13; 1 John 3.16. The newness of life, for a new life, a Hebraism, Rom. 6.4. Christ is metonymically called eternal life, 1 John 5.20. Eternal life is a reward, Matt. 5.12; 20.8; it is the gift of God, Rom. 6.23; see REWARD.

units.la: VITA, Iehoua, vnus & verus Deus, Pater, Filius, Spiritus Sanctus, verè & propriissimè viuit, ipséque verè vita est, & quidem sempiterna, qua viuit, & viuentia omnia modis a sapientia sua constitutis viuificat.
units.tr: LIFE. Jehovah, the one and true God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, truly and most properly lives, and he himself is truly life, and indeed eternal life, by which he lives and quickens all living things in the ways established by his wisdom.

units.la: 2. Vita æterna in Deo Patre est, eámque habet à seipso.
units.tr: 2. Eternal life is in God the Father, and he has it of himself.

units.la: 3. Filius Dei. Iesus Christus, Deus homo est hominum, & peculiari quadam ratione vita electorum ex filiis Adæ. Hanc vitam dedit ei Pater ineffabili modo.
units.tr: 3. The Son of God, Jesus Christ, is God and man, and in a peculiar way the life of the elect from the sons of Adam. The Father gave this life to him in an ineffable manner.

units.la: 4. Vitam naturalem & spiritualem recipiunt Creaturæ à Dei Filio, in quo vita est, qui vita est, & quidem æterna, quum sit Deus.
units.tr: 4. Creatures receive natural and spiritual life from the Son of God, in whom is life, who is life, and indeed eternal life, since he is God.

units.la: 5. Vitam hanc dat & largitur Spiritus S. consubstantialis Patri & Filio.
units.tr: 5. The Holy Spirit, consubstantial with the Father and the Son, gives and bestows this life.

units.la: 6. vita, respectu creaturarum in hoc mundo vniuersalis nominatur, quæ motu duntaxat & sensu constat, cuius etiam participes sunt bestiæ.
units.tr: 6. Life, with respect to creatures in this world, is called universal; it consists merely in motion and sensation, and beasts also partake of it.

units.la: 7. vita etiam humana dicitur, nempe qua filij Adæ fiunt participes, & quæ certo definitóque dierum spatio continetur.
units.tr: 7. Life is also called human, namely that in which the sons of Adam become partakers, and which is contained within a fixed and defined span of days.

units.la: 8. vita gratiæ supernaturalis, in Christo fundatæ, necnon incrementa sua capientis,&adolescentis pro mensura donorum Spiritus adoptionis, hæc est quam soli electi in hac vita, seu pignus futuræ, singulari dono Patris cælestis obtinent.
units.tr: 8. The life of supernatural grace, founded in Christ, and growing and increasing according to the measure of the gifts of the Spirit of adoption: this is the life which only the elect obtain in this world, or as the pledge of the future life, by the singular gift of the heavenly Father.

units.la: 9. vitæ gratiæ gloriosæ, & gloriæ summæ qua electi Angeli & homines, fruuntur & fruentur in cælis cum Christo, inenarrabili cum lætitia omni ex parte beatissima Deum Patrem,Filium,&Spiritum Sanctum glorificantes in æternum.
units.tr: 9. The life of glorious grace, and of supreme glory, which the elect angels and men enjoy, and will enjoy in heaven with Christ, glorifying God the Father, Son and Holy Spirit forever, most blessed in every respect, with inexpressible joy.

units.la: Ad has distinctiones referri facilè possunt quæcunque que de vita Dei & creaturarum in Scripturis sacris le-guntur.]
units.tr: All the things that are read in the holy Scriptures about the life of God and of creatures can easily be referred to these distinctions.

units.la: VITIVM, elt propositum voluntatis inhonestè viuendi, contra diuinæ Legis præscriptum.
units.tr: VICE is the purpose of the will to live dishonourably, contrary to the prescription of the divine Law.

units.la: VITIA aliena lugenda, Ezech 9.4.1 Cor.5 2.2. Corint.12.2. vitia patrum minimè dissimulanda, Vide PATRVM peccata non dissimulanda.
units.tr: VICES of others are to be lamented, Ezek. 9.4; 1 Cor. 5.2; 2 Cor. 12.2. The vices of the fathers are by no means to be overlooked; see FATHERS: the sins of the fathers are not to be overlooked.

units.la: VITIS, elt frutex, id est, humilis arbuscula, quæ Vere floret, atque tunc suauissimum odorem emittit. Cant.2 13.Planta à Noach, Genes. 9 20. Hæc miros fructus profert, si modò quis ijs moderate vtatur 1.Tim.5.23. Psal.104.15.Similitudines ductæ à vite: Psa.80 9. Isa.5.1.&c. Ab Hebræis foetus mulieris cum fructu vitis cõparatur. Vide vinea.
units.tr: VINE, is a shrub, that is, a low little tree, which flowers in spring and then gives off a very sweet smell. Song 2.13. A plant of Noah, Gen. 9.20. It bears wonderful fruit, if only one uses it in moderation, 1 Tim. 5.23; Ps. 104.15. Similitudes drawn from the vine: Ps. 80.9; Isa. 5.1, etc. Among the Hebrews the fruitfulness of a woman is compared to the fruit of the vine. See VINEYARD.

units.la: VITIS, Gen.49.11. Iudic.9.11. Zachar.3.10. Matt.26.29. Vitis palmes appellatur populus Israeliticus. Oie. 10.1. [Vitis Christus, Ioann.15.v.1.4.5.& Pater agricola, ibid.]
units.tr: VINE, Gen. 49.11; Judg. 9.11; Zech. 3.10; Matt. 26.29. The Israelite people is called the branch of the vine, Hos. 10.1. [Christ is the vine, John 15.1, 4–5; and the Father is the husbandman, ibid.]

units.la: VITARE quos debeamus, 2 Tim.3.2.&c.
units.tr: TO AVOID those whom we ought to avoid, 2 Tim. 3.2, etc.

units.la: VITVLVS erigitur in idolum, Exodi 32.4. Deut.9.16.1 Reg. 12.28.2. Reg. 10.29.& 17.36. Psam.106.19. Oiex.8.5. Act.7. 40. Vituli aurei, 1 Regum.12.28.2. Reg.17.16 [Vituli, hostes Dauidis, Christi, Ecclesiæ, Psal.22.2. Vitulus Sacrificiorum, Exod 24 5.& frequentissimapud Mosem, & Prophetas, Psal.51.21.&69.32. Hebr.9.12.19. Vitulus, metaphoricè, pro homine pacifico, Esai.11.v.6.7. Vitulus mysticus, Ezech.1. 7.Apoc.4.7.]
units.tr: CALF is set up as an idol, Exod. 32.4; Deut. 9.16; 1 Kings 12.28; 2 Kings 10.29; 17.16; Ps. 106.19; Hos. 8.5; Acts 7.40. Golden calves, 1 Kings 12.28; 2 Kings 17.16. [Calves, enemies of David, of Christ, of the Church, Ps. 22.12. The calf of the sacrifices, Exod. 24.5, and very frequently in Moses and the Prophets, Ps. 51.19; 69.31; Heb. 9.12, 19. Calf, metaphorically, for a peaceful man, Isa. 11.6–7. The mystical calf, Ezek. 1.7; Rev. 4.7.]

units.la: VIVO ego, iuramentum Dei, Deut.32,40.
units.tr: I LIVE, the oath of God, Deut. 32.40.

units.la: VIVERE, Hebræis, pro valere, Ioann.4.50. Viuere ex omni verbo prodeunte per os Dei, Matthæi. 4.4. dicuntur homines, omni eo viuere, quod egressum fuerit ex ore Dei: siue, quod Deus constituerit, & decreuerit: hoc est, non viuere ex solis causis physicis, cùm Deus non sit illis adstrictus, testantibus id Mosis & Eliæ exemplis, Exodi.24,18. &34 28. Deuter.9.v.9.18.1 Reg 19,8. sed omni re cui Deus i verbo suo alendi nos facultatem indit, quasi imperans ei vt hoc faciat, & verbo suo præstans. Vide Deut.8.3.
units.tr: TO LIVE, among the Hebrews, means to be well, John 4.50. Men are said to live by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God, Matt. 4.4: that is, by everything that has come out of the mouth of God, or that God has appointed and decreed. That is, they do not live by physical causes alone, since God is not bound to them; the examples of Moses and Elijah bear witness to this, Exod. 24.18; 34.28; Deut. 9.9, 18; 1 Kings 19.8. Rather, they live by everything to which God, by his word, gives the power of nourishing us, as if commanding it to do this, and performing it by his word. See Deut. 8.3.

units.la: Viuere Deo, est opera Dei facere, Rom.6.v.11.12. Gala. 2.19. Domino, Rom.14 8 2. Cor.5.15.2. Thess.5.10.1Petr.4. 2.in Christo, 2 Tim.3.12. Viuere peccato qui dicantur, Vide Mori peccato. viuere secundum carnem, Incedere secundum carnem, Esse in carne, Rom,7.5.& 8.v.4.5.8.12.de iis dicitur, qui cùm nõ sint Spiritu donati, sese cupiditatibus carnis immergùt. Viuereauté in carne, Gal. 2.20. vel ambulare in carne. 2 Cor. 1 0.3. nihil aliud declarat, quàm in hoc caduco corpore vitam degere tantisper, dum cœlesti & æterna vita potiantur, vt Galat. 2. 20. 1 Petr. 4.1
units.tr: To live to God is to do the works of God, Rom. 6.11–12; Gal. 2.19; to the Lord, Rom. 14.8; 2 Cor. 5.15; 1 Thess. 5.10; 1 Pet. 4.2; in Christ, 2 Tim. 3.12. Those who are said to live in sin: see To die to sin. To live according to the flesh, to walk according to the flesh, to be in the flesh, Rom. 7.5; 8.4–5, 8, 12, is said of those who, not having been given the Spirit, plunge themselves into the desires of the flesh. To live in the flesh, Gal. 2.20, or to walk in the flesh, 2 Cor. 10.3, declares nothing other than to spend life in this perishable body for as long as they enjoy the heavenly and eternal life, as in Gal. 2.20; 1 Pet. 4.1.

units.la: Viuere sibi, latius dicitur, qui vnum respicit, vt ex suo vnius arbitrio ac voluntate viuat, pro quo Hebraei dicūt Benefacere animæ suæ, Psal. 49.19. cùm ergo negat Paulus fideles sibi viuere, Rom. 14. 7. hinc quid velit intelligitur, nempe quòd fideles non suam, sed Domini voluntatem fateantur ex gratiarum actione se habere pro vitæ regula: quòd deniq; ita viuant, vt Domino sibi reddendam vitæ rationem cogitent, cuius vnius iuri & potestati subsint. Viuit anima tua: Asseueratio Hebræis, 1 Sam. 1.26. Viuit Christus in Christianis, Galat. 2 21. Viuit Dominus iurantis vox, Ruth. 3.13.
units.tr: To live to oneself is said more broadly of one who looks only to himself, so that he lives by his own will and decision alone; for this the Hebrews say "to do good to one's soul," Ps. 49.19. When therefore Paul denies that believers live to themselves, Rom. 14.7, what he means is understood: namely, that believers, by giving thanks, acknowledge that they have not their own will but the will of the Lord as the rule of their life; and finally that they so live as to consider that they must render an account of their life to the Lord, to whose right and power alone they are subject. "Your soul lives": an asseveration among the Hebrews, 1 Sam. 1.26. "Christ lives in Christians," Gal. 2.21. "As the Lord lives," the words of one swearing, Ruth 3.13.

units.la: Viuit homo fide, etiam in fame, Deut. 8.3. Viuimus in gloriam Dei, Rom. 14. 8. Viuunt omnes Deo, Luc. 20.38. Viuat rex, 1 Samuel. 10.24. vt viuamus, mandata seruanda, Deutero. 4.1. & 32.47. Viuere facit Deus, & occidit, 32. 49. Viuens Deus, Ios. 3.10. Viuendum Deo, non sibi, Rom. 14.7. 2. Cor. 5.15. Gal. 2.20. 2. Thes. 5.10. 1. Pet. 4.2. Viuendum in lætitia, Eccles. 8.15. & 9.7.
units.tr: Man lives by faith, even in famine, Deut. 8.3. We live to the glory of God, Rom. 14.8. All live to God, Luke 20.38. Long live the king, 1 Sam. 10.24. That we may live, the commandments are to be kept, Deut. 4.1 and 32.47. God makes alive and kills, Deut. 32.49. The living God, Josh. 3.10. One must live to God, not to oneself, Rom. 14.7; 2 Cor. 5.15; Gal. 2.20; 2 Thess. 5.10; 1 Pet. 4.2. One must live in joy, Eccles. 8.15 and 9.7.

units.la: [VIVERE, exercitij gratia, sic distinximus, 1. Viuit Deus, verè & propriissimè, vt etiam plerumque iurat dicens, Viuo ego, & per eum iurant homines, Viuit Iehoua.
units.tr: [LIVE. For the sake of practice, we have distinguished it thus: 1. God lives truly and most properly, as he also very often swears, saying "As I live," and men swear by him: "As the LORD lives."]

units.la: 2. Viuens Pater dicitur, Ioan. 6.57.
units.tr: 2. The Father is called living, John 6.57.

units.la: 3. Viuit Dei Filius, propter Patrem, Ioan. 6.57. 4. viuit credens in Christum, & eius carnem manducans, idque propter Filium, Ioan. 6.57. 5. viuere vita spirituali, Deo & Christo, item viuere Spiritu, pie, iustè, sobrie, pij dicuntur. 6. viuenti seu viuæ aquæ Deus & Christi gratia comparatur, Ier. 2.13. & 17.13. Ioan. 4. v. 10. 11. & 7.38.
units.tr: 3. The Son of God lives because of the Father, John 6.57. 4. He lives who believes in Christ and eats his flesh, and this because of the Son, John 6.57. 5. To live a spiritual life, to God and Christ, and likewise to live by the Spirit, to live piously, justly and soberly, are said of the godly. 6. God and the grace of Christ are compared to living water, Jer. 2.13 and 17.13; John 4.10, 11; 7.38.

units.la: 7. viuere, de beata vita, in hoc inchoata seculo, perfecta & absoluta in cœlis, dicitur, quoties sermo fit de gratia Dei per Christi meritum & obedientiam electis imputatam. Operibus autem vita promissa conditionis appositæ complementum in vnica Christi obedientia reperit & obtinet.]
units.tr: 7. To live is said of the blessed life, begun in this age and perfected and completed in heaven, whenever the discussion is of the grace of God imputed to the elect through Christ's merit and obedience. But the life promised under the condition of works finds and obtains its fulfilment in the sole obedience of Christ.]

units.la: VIVIFICAT Deus, 1 Sam. 2.6. Nehem. 9.6. Psal. 71.20. & 119. 17. & c. Elá. 17.&c.Esai.57.v.15.16.Ose.6.3.Abac.3.2.Rom.4.17.
units.tr: GIVES LIFE. God quickens, 1 Sam. 2.6; Neh. 9.6; Ps. 71.20; 119.17, etc.; Isa. 57.15, 16; Hos. 6.3; Hab. 3.2; Rom. 4.17.

units.la: 2. viuificat Deus Pater Ioann.5.24. Rom. 8.11.1 Tim. 6.13.
units.tr: 2. God the Father quickens, John 5.24; Rom. 8.11; 1 Tim. 6.13.

units.la: 3. viuificat Filius, Deus-homo, Ioan.5 21.1.Cor.15.22. viuificatur spiritu,1 Petr.3.18.
units.tr: 3. The Son quickens, being God-man, John 5.21; 1 Cor. 15.22. He is quickened by the Spirit, 1 Pet. 3.18.

units.la: 4. viuificat Spiritus S. Iob.34.4.Ioan.6.63.2.Corinth. 3.6.
units.tr: 4. The Holy Spirit quickens, Job 34.4; John 6.63; 2 Cor. 3.6.

units.la: 5. viuificantur homines è variis periculis lethalibus & morte erepti,1.Sam.2.6. Reg.8.5. Psal.41.3.& 80.19.Esai.38.16.De corporum resurrectione dictum,Rom.4.17. 1 Cor.15.22.
units.tr: 5. Men are quickened when they are rescued from various deadly perils and from death, 1 Sam. 2.6; 1 Kings 8.5; Ps. 41.3; 80.19; Isa. 38.16. It is said of the resurrection of bodies in Rom. 4.17 and 1 Cor. 15.22.

units.la: 6. viuificantur Dei electi vitæ spiritualis & æternæ respectu. Psalm. 85. 7.& 119.v.25. 27.37.50. 88. &c.Lucæ. 17.13.]
units.tr: 6. The elect of God are quickened with respect to spiritual and eternal life, Ps. 85.7; 119.25, 27, 37, 50, 88, etc.; Luke 17.13.]

units.la: VLCERE percutiuntur inobedientes, Deut.28 35.vlcera in hominibus,Exodi.9.v.9.10.11.
units.tr: ULCERS strike the disobedient, Deut. 28.35; ulcers on men, Exod. 9.9, 10, 11.

units.la: VLCISCITVR Dauid iniuriam seruis factam, 2. Sam.10.7. VLTIO non quærenda, Leuit.19.18. Luc.9.54. vltionem capere,Dei est,Deut.32.35.Vide VINDICTA.
units.tr: DAVID AVENGES the wrong done to his servants, 2 Sam. 10.7. Vengeance is not to be sought, Lev. 19.18; Luke 9.54. Taking vengeance belongs to God, Deut. 32.35. See VENGEANCE.

units.la: VMBRA, vetus Testamentum, Habr. 8.5. vmbræ nomen quatenus tribuatur legalibus ceremoniis,Col.2.17.Vide CEREMONIAE vmbris similes. vmbra mortis, pro morte vmbrosa & tenebricosa,Luc.1.79.Hebraismus pro vmbra densissima,Amos.5.8.
units.tr: SHADOW: the Old Testament, Heb. 8.5. The name shadow, insofar as it is applied to the ceremonial laws, Col. 2.17. See CEREMONIES, which are like shadows. Shadow of death: a gloomy and dark death, Luke 1.79. A Hebraism for the thickest shadow, Amos 5.8.

units.la: [vmbra, Luci opposita. 2. Rei cuiusuis, vt arboris,tecti,domus,&c.in qua refugij, refrigerij, hospitij & quietis causa diuertimus. 3. Protectio Dei,nomine alarum & manuum eius designata. 4. vmbra legis ceremonialis quæ Christum venturum ritibus suis depinxit. 5.Vmbra mortis corp.& spirit. 6. Vmbra auxilium Ægypti. 7.vmbra mortis significat pericula grauissima & letha-lia,Psal.23.4.& 44,29.&c.]
units.tr: [Shadow, opposed to light. 2. The shadow of anything, such as a tree, a roof or a house, under which we turn aside for refuge, cooling, lodging and rest. 3. The protection of God, designated by the names of his wings and hands. 4. The shadow of the ceremonial law, which portrayed with its rites the Christ who was to come. 5. The shadow of death, of body and of spirit. 6. The shadow: the help of Egypt. 7. The shadow of death signifies the most grievous and deadly dangers, Ps. 23.4; 44.29, etc.]

units.la: VNANIMITAS commendatur, 1 Cor. 1. 10. Philip.1.27. Act. 2.46.& 4.32. Vide CONCORDIA.
units.tr: UNANIMITY is commended, 1 Cor. 1.10; Phil. 1.27; Acts 2.46; 4.32. See CONCORD.

units.la: VNCTIO,pro Spiritu S.1 Ioan.2. v.20.27. translatione sumta à consuetudine vnctionum,quę in Lege vsurpabantur. Vnctio ægrotis quondam adhibita, vt miraculo sanitatem recuperarent, Marc.6.13. Iac.5.14. Christi,Dan.9.24. Spiritu S.est,1 Ioan.2.27.
units.tr: ANOINTING, for the Holy Spirit, 1 John 2.20, 27, a term taken by transference from the custom of anointings used in the Law. Anointing was once applied to the sick, that they might recover health by a miracle, Mark 6.13; James 5.14. Of Christ, Dan. 9.24. The Holy Spirit is the anointing, 1 John 2.27.

units.la: [Vnctio communis corporum, viuentium & mortuorum,Deuter.28.40.Ruth.3. 3.Matt.6.17. Marc.16.1. Luc.7. 46.Legalis,rempe vasorum tabernaculi, sacerdotum,prophetarum, regunt, rerum ad sacrificia pertinentium. Exod.29.v.29.36.& 30.26.1 Samuel.15.1.1 Reg.1.34.&19.15. Vnctio spiritualis & interna, Messiæ, quæ illa legali Sacerdotali, prophetica, regia, designata fuit, Ps.45.8.& 89.21.Esai.61.1.Dan.6.24. Luc.4.18. Act.4.27.&10.38.Heb.1.9. Vnctio spiritualis electorum Dei, Ezech.16.19.2. Cor.2.21. vnctionis oleum, Exod.30.23. &c. extremæ Sacramentum probare se posse putant Papistæ, ex Iac.5.14.
units.tr: [Common anointing of bodies, living and dead, Deut. 28.40; Ruth 3.3; Matt. 6.17; Mark 16.1; Luke 7.46. Legal anointing, namely of the vessels of the tabernacle, of priests, prophets and kings, and of things pertaining to the sacrifices, Exod. 29.29, 36; 30.26; 1 Sam. 15.1; 1 Kings 1.34; 19.15. Spiritual and inward anointing of the Messiah, which the legal anointing of priest, prophet and king designated, Ps. 45.8; 89.21; Isa. 61.1; Dan. 6.24; Luke 4.18; Acts 4.27; 10.38; Heb. 1.9. Spiritual anointing of the elect of God, Ezek. 16.19; 2 Cor. 2.21. Oil of anointing, Exod. 30.23, etc. The Papists think they can prove the sacrament of extreme unction from James 5.14.]

units.la: VNGEBANTVR corpora mortuorum, Gen.50.2. non unguntur oleo suo inobedientes, Deut.28.40. Vngebantur Reges, 1 Sam.10.1.&16.13. Sacerdotes, Exodi.29.7. Prophetæ, 1 Reg.19.16.
units.tr: BODIES OF THE DEAD were anointed, Gen. 50.2. The disobedient are not anointed with their oil, Deut. 28.40. Kings were anointed, 1 Sam. 10.1; 16.13. Priests, Exod. 29.7. Prophets, 1 Kings 19.16.

units.tr: [OINTMENT: common, Dan. 10.3; Amos 6.6; Matt. 28.7. Legal, Exod. 30.25; Ps. 133.2. Mystical, Song 1.4; 4.10. Perfumer, Exod. 30.25, 35; 1 Sam. 8.13.]

units.tr: NAIL (claw): Deut. 21.12; an adamantine nail, Jer. 17.1; the claws of Nebuchadnezzar, Dan. 4.33; of bronze, Dan. 7.19.

units.la: [VNIGENITVS Dei Patris, Ioan. 1.v.14.18.& 3.ver.16.18.1. Ioan.4.9. Vnigenitus hominis, Genes.22.v.2.12. Iudic.11.34. Hebr.11.16.]
units.tr: [ONLY-BEGOTTEN of God the Father, John 1.14, 18; 3.16, 18; 1 John 4.9. Only-begotten of man, Gen. 22.2, 12; Judg. 11.34; Heb. 11.16.]

units.la: VNITAS fidei & spiritus commendatur, 1 Corinth.1.10. Ephes.4.ver.3.13. Philipp.1.27.&2.2.1. Petri.3.8. Vnitas fidei Christianorum, Ioan.17.11. Actor.4.32. Vnitatis & consensus exempla: Israelitæ, Exodi.19.8.& 35.21. Iudic.20.1.1 Samuel.11.7. Vniversæ Tribus Israel, 2 Sam.5.1. maiores natu Israel, & subditi Salomonis, 1 Reg.8.ver.1.2.3. Israelitæ, Esdr.2.64. Nehem.8.1. Apostoli & fideles omnes, Act.1.14. & 2.v.1.44.46,&52,12, Apostoli, 4.24, Fideles Ierosolymitani, v.32.
units.tr: UNITY of faith and of the Spirit is commended, 1 Cor. 1.10; Eph. 4.3, 13; Phil. 1.27; 2.2; 1 Pet. 3.8. The unity of the faith of Christians, John 17.11; Acts 4.32. Examples of unity and agreement: the Israelites, Exod. 19.8; 35.21; Judg. 20.1; 1 Sam. 11.7. All the tribes of Israel, 2 Sam. 5.1. The elders of Israel and Solomon's subjects, 1 Kings 8.1, 2, 3. The Israelites, Ezra 2.64; Neh. 8.1. The apostles and all the faithful, Acts 1.14; 2.1, 44, 46, 52. The apostles, Acts 4.24. The faithful of Jerusalem, Acts 4.32.

units.la: VNIVERSALIS nota, vide NOTA vniuersalis: &, OMNIS.
units.tr: UNIVERSAL mark: see UNIVERSAL MARK, and ALL.

units.la: [VNVS, vox numeri Cardinalis, seu numeri principium, frequenter ea significatione occurrit.
units.tr: [ONE, the word of the cardinal number, or the beginning of number, often occurs in this meaning.

units.la: 2. Sæpe pro ordinali numero ponitur, idémque significat quod primus, ut Genes.1.5.&2.11. Sic apud Euangelistas, vna Sabbathi, vna Sabbathorum, i. prima die hebdomadæ aut festi, Marc.16.2. Luc.24.1. Ioan.20.v.1.19. Acto. 207.
units.tr: 2. It is often used for the ordinal number and means the same as first, as in Gen. 1.5; 2.11. So among the Evangelists, "one of the Sabbath" or "one of the Sabbaths," that is, the first day of the week or of a feast, Mark 16.2; Luke 24.1; John 20.1, 19; Acts 20.7.

units.la: 3. Vnus aliquando idem est ac vnus tantum, vel solus. Vt quum de Deo dicitur, quòd vnus sit. Item de Christo, qui vnus mediator est Dei & hominum. Nec enim Ecclesia secundarios aut multos habet Mediatores. vnum tantantùm, vnicum & solum Christum, talem agnoscit: vt & vnum essentiâ Deum adorat, Patrem, Filium, Spiritum S. non tres deos, sed vnum tantum Deum.
units.tr: 3. One sometimes means the same as only, or alone. As when God is said to be one; likewise of Christ, who is the one mediator between God and men. For the Church does not have secondary or many mediators. It acknowledges Christ as only one, unique and sole such, and it worships God as one in essence, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, not three gods but only one God.

units.la: 4. Vnus item Spiritus Sanctus, & vna Christi columba, seu Ecclesia.
units.tr: 4. Likewise the Holy Spirit is one, and Christ's dove, or Church, is one.

units.la: 5. Vnum sunt Deus, Pater & Filius, nempe & naturæ siue essentiæ ταυτότητι, & vno in volendo & agendo consensu, distinctis tamen personis, Ioan.10.30.
units.tr: 5. God the Father and the Son are one, namely both in sameness [ταυτότητι] of nature or essence and in one agreement of will and action, the persons nevertheless being distinct, John 10.30.

units.la: 6. Vnum sunt Pater, Filius & Spiritus S. i. ita consentiunt prorsus, ac si vnus testis essent, vt re vera vnum sunt ἓν εἰσι. 1 Ioan. 5.7.8.
units.tr: 6. The Father, Son and Holy Spirit are one, that is, they agree so completely, as if they were one witness, that in truth they are one [ἓν εἰσι], 1 John 5.7, 8.

units.la: 7. Vnum sunt Electi omnes cum Deo Patre & filio: & vnum sunt inter se vnitate Spiritus, fidei, spei, charitatis, Ioan.17.v.21.23. Alias huius vocis minutas significationes omittimus.]
units.tr: 7. All the elect are one with God the Father and the Son, and they are one among themselves by the unity of the Spirit, of faith, of hope and of love, John 17.21, 23. We omit the other minor meanings of this word.]

units.tr: A catalogue of Latin words formed from the Greek, with their declensions.
