units.la: VOCARE ex Hebræorum idiotismo, interdum declarat ipsius ἐπαγγελίας initium quod Deo tribuitur, vt qui solo verbo omnes condat, Rom.4.17. Interdum contrà, vocandi verbo non essentiæ principium, sed manifestatio Filij Dei significatur, Luc.1.v.32.35. Interdum publicam, eamq; minimè nudam nuncupationem significat, sed quæ cum re ipsa consentiat, 1 Corint.1.2. Matth.22.3. Interdum vocationis nomine ipsa ministerij Apostolici functio aut vitæ genus significatur, 1 Corint.7.verf.7.20. Ephes.4.1. Interdum causa efficiens exprimitur, à quo videlicet sit illa dignitas. gnitas, ad quam quis vocatus est, nimirum à Deo, Rom. 8.1. vocare pro inuitare, Matth. 22.3.
units.tr: To call (vocare), in the Hebrew idiom, sometimes denotes the beginning of the promise itself, which is attributed to God, who creates all things by his word alone: Rom. 4.17. Sometimes, on the contrary, the word "to call" signifies not the origin of a being but the manifestation of the Son of God: Luke 1.32, 35. Sometimes it signifies a public naming, and not a bare one, but one that agrees with the thing itself: 1 Cor. 1.2; Matt. 22.3. Sometimes, under the name of calling, the office of the apostolic ministry or a way of life is signified: 1 Cor. 7.7, 20; Eph. 4.1. Sometimes the efficient cause is expressed, namely from whom that dignity comes to which someone is called, that is, from God: Rom. 8.1. To call can also mean to invite: Matt. 22.3.

units.la: vocare dicitur Deus eos, ex Hebraeorum idiotismo, quos facit existere: Et vicissim à Domino vocari dicuntur, qui existere incipiunt, siue id referatur ad ipsam ἐσίας ἡ ὑπαρξιν, Roman. 4.17. siue ad qualitates aut attributa, 1 Cor. 7. v.20. 21. 22. siue ad aeterni consilij Dei publicam declarationem, qua nos certo muneri ac veluti scopo in hoc mundo destinatos quasi in eius possessionem mittit, Rom.1.7.1.Cor.1.2. siue id de quo agitur, sit omnibus sanctis commune, vt cùm electioni subordinatur vocatio, Rom.8.30. siue peculiarem functionem respiciat, vt cùm dicit Christus se ab vtero vocatum esse, Esa.49.1. Sic Act.13.2.Rom.1.1.1.Cor.1.1.
units.tr: God is said "to call" those whom he causes to exist, in the Hebrew idiom; and conversely, those who begin to exist are said to be called by the Lord. This is so whether the reference is to existence itself, Rom. 4.17; or to qualities and attributes, 1 Cor. 7.20–22; or to the public declaration of the eternal counsel of God, by which he sends us, as though into possession, to a certain office and, as it were, goal in this world, Rom. 1.7; 1 Cor. 1.2; or whether the thing in question is common to all the saints, as when calling is subordinated to election, Rom. 8.30; or whether it concerns a particular office, as when Christ says that he was called from the womb, Isa. 49.1. So also Acts 13.2; Rom. 1.1; 1 Cor. 1.1.

units.la: VOCARI, pro palam & reipsa esse ac haberi, Hebraismus Luc.1.76. & 2.23.Matth.5.v.9 19. & 21.13.Mar.11.17.1.Ioan. 3.1.Rom.7.3. pro gratis asciici, Gal.5.13.
units.tr: To be called, in the sense of being and being held openly and in fact, is a Hebraism: Luke 1.76; 2.23; Matt. 5.9, 19; 21.13; Mark 11.17; 1 John 3.1; Rom. 7.3. It means to be taken on freely: Gal. 5.13.

units.la: VOCATIO & missio nunc Patri, nunc Filio, nunc Spiritui sancto tribuitur. vide TRINITATIS opera extrinseca. vocatio Metonymicè, non pro ipsa vocandi actione, sed pro illo ipso ad quod fideles vocati erant, nempe pro coelestis regni gloria, 2. Thess.1.11.
units.tr: Calling and sending are attributed now to the Father, now to the Son, now to the Holy Spirit. See the external works of the Trinity. Calling is used metonymically, not for the act of calling itself, but for that to which the faithful were called, namely the glory of the heavenly kingdom: 2 Thess. 1.11.

units.la: VOCATIO Interna & singularis, est actio Dei gratiosa, qua Electi ab aeterno, suo tempore, ex Dei beneplacito, propter meritū Christi, per Spiritū S. intus informatur, ad perceptionem & communionem gratiae Dei, propter salutem ipsorum, & misericordiae diuinae gloriam.
units.tr: The internal and particular calling is the gracious action of God by which the elect, from eternity, in their own time, by God's good pleasure, on account of the merit of Christ, are inwardly formed by the Holy Spirit to receive and share in the grace of God, for their own salvation and for the glory of divine mercy.

units.la: EXTERNA & communis, est actio Dei gratiosa, qua homines sermone, signo & opere, ab infidelitate ad fidem euocat, tum vt ad salutis communionē fideles disponātur, tum verò vt alij enicti de oblata à Deo gratia, fiant inexcusabiles.
units.tr: The external and general calling is the gracious action of God by which he summons people from unbelief to faith by word, sign and work, both so that the faithful may be disposed to share in salvation and so that others, though they are not elect, may become inexcusable for the grace offered by God.

units.la: Vocationum duo genera reperiuntur in sacra scriptura. Primò, vnum coniunctum cum efficacia spiritus sancti, de quo Rom.8.30. Secundò, alterum, quamuis idem sit cum priore, quod ad rem externa attinet, quoad salutem tamen, nullius est efficaciae, idque non Dei, sed hominum culpa, qui nolunt Dei verbum audire, de quo Matth.22.14. Illud vocatur vocatio generalis, qua per externam verbi praedicationē omnes pariter ad se inuitat Deus, etiā quibus eam in mortis odorem & grauioris condemnationis materiam proponit: Hoc vocatur specialis vocatio, qua non nisi solos fideles dignatur, dum interiori spiritus sui illuminatione efficit, vt verbum prædicatum in eorū cordibus insideat. Interdum tamen eos quoque facit participes, quos ad tempus duntaxat illuminat, deinde suæ ingratitudinis merito deserit, & maiori percutit cæcitate.
units.tr: Two kinds of calling are found in Holy Scripture. First, one joined with the efficacy of the Holy Spirit, of which Rom. 8.30. Second, another, which, although it is the same as the former so far as the external matter is concerned, is nevertheless of no efficacy for salvation; and this is not the fault of God but of men, who are unwilling to hear the word of God, of which Matt. 22.14. The first is called the general calling, by which God invites all alike to himself through the external preaching of the word, even those to whom he sets it forth as a savour of death and a cause of heavier condemnation. The second is called the special calling, by which God deigns to call only the faithful, when by the inner illumination of his Spirit he brings it about that the preached word dwells in their hearts. Yet sometimes he also makes sharers of it those whom he illuminates only for a time, and afterwards, by the merit of their ingratitude, he forsakes them and strikes them with greater blindness.

units.la: Vocatio efficax, quæ electionis effectus est, Rom 1.6 & 8.30. 1. Corinth. 1.9. 2. Petr. 1 10. Iudæ v.1. gratuita est, Gal. 2.15. 2. Tim. 1. 9. vocatio non est vniuersalis, Ioan. 6. 45. vbi etsi particula vniuersalis ponitur, tamen Esai. 45.13. diserte restringitur ad filios Ecclesiæ, hoc est, vt Lucas loquitur, Act. 13. 8. ad ordinatos ad vitam. Vocatio, quæ electionem præeuntem non habet, inefficax est, Matth. 20.16. & 22.8. Luc. 14.24. Vocationis electorum finis, Ier. 13.11. 1. Corinth. 1.8. 1. Thess. 3.13. & 4.7. Hebr. 10.39. Iac. 2.5. 1 Petr. 1.15, & 2.9. & 5. v. 9.10. Iudæ v.5. Vocationi propriæ sedulò inserviendum, Prou. 27.8. Matth. 8.22. & 10.5. Luc. 9. v. 2.3.60.61. & 10. v. 3.4.1 Corint. 7, v. 17.18.20.24. Eph. 4. v. 1.4. 1. Thess. 4 11. Exempla: Christus, Matth. 12.48. Luc. 2.49. & 4.43. Ioan. 4 34. & 9.4. & 17.4. quidam Dæmoniacus à Christo sanatus, Luc. 8.39. Matthæus, Luc. 5.18. ministri nuptiarum, Ioan. 2.7. Ioannes Baptista, Ioan. 3.23. Apostoli, Act. 4. v. 20.33. & 5. 42. & 6 2. Philip. 8.40. Paulus & Barnabas, 14. v. 5 6.7. & 15.36. & 18.6. & 20. ver. 20.24.26. 31. Paulus, 28.28. Rom. 11.14. & 15.18.1. Cor. 9. v. 16.21. & 15.10 2. Corint. 11.5. Colosf. 1.29. & 2.3. Tit, 1.3. Abraham. Hebr. 11.8. Petrus, 2. Petr. 1. vers. 13.15. Vocatio gentium, Matth. 8.10. & 22.9. à prophetis prædicta, Roman. 9.30. à Mose, 10.25. allegorice significata, Vide GENTIVM vocatio. Vocationem & electionem nostram vt firmam efficere studeamus, monemur, 2. Petr. 1. 10. Vide ELECTIO.
units.tr: The effectual calling, which is the effect of election, is free: Rom. 1.6; 8.30; 1 Cor. 1.9; 2 Pet. 1.10; Jude 1; Gal. 2.15; 2 Tim. 1.9. The calling is not universal: John 6.45, where, although the universal particle is used, Isa. 45.13 expressly restricts it to the sons of the Church, that is, as Luke puts it, Acts 13.48, to those ordained to life. A calling that does not have election going before it is ineffective: Matt. 20.16; 22.8; Luke 14.24. The end of the calling of the elect: Jer. 13.11; 1 Cor. 1.8; 1 Thess. 3.13; 4.7; Heb. 10.39; James 2.5; 1 Pet. 1.15; 2.9; 5.9, 10; Jude 5. We must diligently serve our own calling: Prov. 27.8; Matt. 8.22; 10.5; Luke 9.2, 3, 60, 61; 10.3, 4; 1 Cor. 7.17, 18, 20, 24; Eph. 4.1, 4; 1 Thess. 4.11. Examples: Christ, Matt. 12.48; Luke 2.49; 4.43; John 4.34; 9.4; 17.4. A certain demoniac healed by Christ, Luke 8.39. Matthew, Luke 5.18. The servants at the wedding, John 2.7. John the Baptist, John 3.23. The apostles, Acts 4.20, 33; 5.42; 6.2; Phil. 8.40. Paul and Barnabas, Acts 14.5–7; 15.36; 18.6; 20.20, 24, 26, 31. Paul, Acts 28.28; Rom. 11.14; 15.18; 1 Cor. 9.16, 21; 15.10; 2 Cor. 11.5; Col. 1.29; 2.3; Titus 1.3. Abraham, Heb. 11.8. Peter, 2 Pet. 1.13, 15. The calling of the Gentiles, foretold by the prophets, Matt. 8.10; 22.9; Rom. 9.30; and by Moses, Rom. 10.25; allegorically signified. See the calling of the Gentiles. We are admonished to make every effort to make our calling and election sure: 2 Pet. 1.10. See ELECTION.

units.la: VOLO, Vide VELLE.
units.tr: VOLO; see VELLE.

units.la: VOLVNTAS, pro naturali propensione, Rom. 8.20. pro cogitatione & conatu animi, 9.16. pro libidine, Ioan. 1.13. voluntas veteris hominis, peccati serua est, Genes. 6.5. & 8.21. Roman. 7. ver. 15.19. bona hominis voluntas, regenerationis donum est, Rom. 7. ver 21.22. Philip. 2.13. voluntas Dei, Matth. 7.21. & 12.50. Marc. 3.35. Ioan. 6.39. Roman. 12. Eph. 5.17. Col. 1.9.1 Thess. 4.3.1. Tim. 2.4.1. Ioan. 2.17. Voluntas Dei non est vt aliquis pereat, Ezech.18.23. Ioan. 6.39.1 Tim. 2.4. 2 Petr. 3.9 voluntas nostra diuinæ voluntati accômoda,1 Sam.3.18.2 Samuel.10.12. & 15.20.1 Mach. 3. 60. Matth.6.10.& 26.39.Marc.14.36.Luc.22.42. Act. 21. 14.1 Corinth.4.19. Heb.6.3.Iac.4.15.vide ABNE-GATIO. Voluntatem pro opere acceptat Deus,Genef. 20.verf.3 6.& 22.12.2.Sam.11.14. & 12.9. 1 Reg. 21. 10. vide COR.
units.tr: VOLUNTAS: for natural inclination, Rom. 8.20; for thought and effort of the mind, 9.16; for lust, John 1.13. The will of the old man is the slave of sin, Gen. 6.5 and 8.21; Rom. 7 v. 15, 19. A man's good will is a gift of regeneration, Rom. 7 v. 21, 22; Phil. 2.13. The will of God, Matt. 7.21 and 12.50; Mark 3.35; John 6.39; Rom. 12; Eph. 5.17; Col. 1.9; 1 Thess. 4.3; 1 Tim. 2.4; 1 John 2.17. The will of God is not that anyone should perish, Ezek. 18.23; John 6.39; 1 Tim. 2.4; 2 Pet. 3.9. Our will is to be conformed to the divine will, 1 Sam. 3.18; 2 Sam. 10.12 and 15.20; 1 Macc. 3.60; Matt. 6.10 and 26.39; Mark 14.36; Luke 22.42; Acts 21.14; 1 Cor. 4.19; Heb. 6.3; James 4.15. See ABNEGATION. God accepts the will for the deed, Gen. 20 v. 3, 6 and 22.12; 2 Sam. 11.14 and 12.9; 1 Kings 21.10. See HEART.

units.la: [VOLVNTAS, est facultas animæ qua volumus: deinde actus huiusce facultatis: Postremò,obiectum,id est res quam volumus. Vt, voluntas Patris cælestis est,vt quicunque credit in Filium non pereat,sed habeat vitam æternam.
units.tr: [VOLUNTAS is the faculty of the soul by which we will; then the act of this faculty; and finally the object, that is, the thing we will. For example, the will of the heavenly Father is that whoever believes in the Son should not perish but have eternal life.]

units.la: In veteri Testamento vocatur 1. Anima, quòd sit facultas animæ:Psal.22.12.& tantùm ad homines, qui ratione præditi sunt,refertur, 2. vocatur Acquiescentia in aliquo proposito. Velle enim proprium est, vt in iis quæ sibi ab intellectu,vt bona,proponuntur,acquiescat.3. Huic affinis est vox Complacitum,Beneplacitū,Placitum Voluntas enim ex oblatis eligit quæ magis placent:4.Vtitur & Scriptura alio vocabulo, 1 Sam. 15. 22. quo voluntatem cum approbatione,amore & delectatione significat.
units.tr: In the Old Testament it is called 1. "soul", because it is a faculty of the soul (Ps. 22.12), and it refers only to men who are endowed with reason. 2. It is called acquiescence in some purpose, for it is proper to willing to acquiesce in those things which are proposed to the intellect as good. 3. Akin to this is the word "complacency", "good pleasure", "pleasure", "purpose". For the will chooses from the things offered those that please more. 4. Scripture also uses another word (1 Sam. 15.22), by which it signifies the will together with approval, love and delight.

units.la: 5. Est & alia vox,quæ Spontaneitas exponi potest, Exo. 35. 29.qua proprium voluntatis exprimitur, nempe naturalis libertas,qua homo quidquid vult, siue bonum siue malum, libere, voluntarie, sponte, sine coactione vult.
units.tr: 5. There is also another word, which can be explained as "spontaneity" (Exod. 35.29), by which the proper character of the will is expressed, namely natural liberty, by which a man wills whatever he wills, whether good or evil, freely, voluntarily, spontaneously and without compulsion.

units.la: Voluntas proprièssimè & verissimè Deo convenit:& quæ antea de voluntate dicta sunt, in homine imperfecta agnoscuntur. In Angelis autem voluntas magis perfecta est. Voluntas Dei variè à Theologis distinguitur,1.In voluntatem antecedentem & consequentem,2. Bene placiti & signi,seu non revelatam & revelatam.3. Absolutam & conditionalem. 4. In voluntatem quam Deus facere vult de nobis & de omnibus rebus creatis, atque in voluntatem quam vult fieri à nobis,in lege & Evangelio patefactam. Omnes autem in eo consentiunt vnam tantum esse Dei voluntatem. Nam etsi varia permultaque sunt quæ vult Deus per se vt bona:vel quæ propter aliud permittit fieri,vt mala,vel absolutè, vt quæcunque agit tamen, si Deum ipsum volentem spectamus, dicemus voluntatem eius esse liberum, æternum, sapientissimum,immutabilé. tabiléque décretum, tum de vniuersis & singulis creaturis suis ad certos vsus & fines per certa media deducendis: tum de malis quæ nec fecit, nec facit, nec faciet, nempe peccatis, fieri permittendis: idque ad suam gloriam.
units.tr: Voluntas belongs most properly and truly to God, and what has been said above about the will is recognised as imperfect in man. In the angels, however, the will is more perfect. The will of God is distinguished in various ways by theologians: 1. into antecedent and consequent will; 2. into the will of good pleasure and of sign, or the unrevealed and the revealed; 3. into absolute and conditional; 4. into the will which God wills to do concerning us and all created things, and the will which he wills to be done by us, made known in the law and the Gospel. All agree, however, that there is only one will of God. For although there are many and varied things which God wills as good in themselves, or permits to happen for the sake of something else, like evil things, or which he does absolutely, nevertheless, if we look at God himself willing, we shall say that his will is a free, eternal, most wise, immutable and unchangeable decree, both concerning all his creatures and individually, to be brought to certain uses and ends by certain means, and concerning evils, which he neither has done, nor does, nor will do, namely sins, which are to be permitted to happen; and this for his own glory.

units.la: Voluntatem, quam fieri vult à nobis, in Lege & Euangelio expressit. Quicquid vult in cœlo pro salute Ecclesiæ militantis in terra, sancti Angeli exequuntur. Nonnunquam Angelorum reproborum opera vtitur, vt iudicia sua erga impios, misericordiæ erga pios peculiari quadam ratione luceat, Voluntas Dei Patris, in Euangelio manifeste distinguitur. Voluntas Filij dupliciter consideratur: quatenus Deus est, & quatenus mediator ac sponsor Ecclesiæ. Aliquoties essentialiter, nonnunquam personaliter consideratur, & Patrem respicit.
units.tr: Voluntatem, which he wills to be done by us, he has expressed in the Law and the Gospel. Whatever he wills in heaven for the salvation of the Church militant on earth, the holy angels carry out. Sometimes he uses the works of the reprobate angels, so that his judgements upon the impious and his mercy towards the pious may shine forth in a peculiar manner. The will of the Father is clearly distinguished in the Gospel. The will of the Son is considered in two ways: insofar as he is God, and insofar as he is mediator and surety of the Church. It is considered sometimes essentially, sometimes personally, and then it refers to the Father.

units.la: Voluntas Dei revelata in N. T. 1. Charitate Dei erga electos, & beneplacitum in eis seruandis per Christum significat. 2. Huius charitatis declarationem per Euangelium. 3. Consilium Dei, respectu electorum, nempe vt vocentur efficaciter, iustificentur, sanctificentur ad omne opus bonum & glorificentur.
units.tr: The will of God revealed in the New Testament signifies: 1. the love of God towards the elect, and his good pleasure in preserving them through Christ; 2. the declaration of this love through the Gospel; 3. the counsel of God with respect to the elect, namely that they should be effectually called, justified, sanctified to every good work, and glorified.

units.la: Voluntas hominis varie consideratur pro vario eius statu, nempe hominis naturalis & regeniti, tum in rebus malis, bonis, mediis: item in rebus ad hanc & futuram vitam pertinentibus.
units.tr: The will of man is considered in various ways according to his various states: that of natural man and of the regenerate man; and also in things evil, good and indifferent; likewise in things pertaining to this life and the life to come.

units.la: In voluntare patefacta Dei quædam peculiaria occurrunt, in quibus exequendis etiam non regenitorum hominum ministerium ei subseruit, teste Nebucadnezare Iudæos captiuitatem deducente, & Cyro reducente. Hæc autem paulò prolixius descripta sunt, vt vim vocũ istarũ VOLO & VOLVNTAS Theologiæ studiosi expendant.
units.tr: Among the revealed will of God there occur certain peculiar matters, in carrying out which the ministry of men who are not regenerate has also served him, as witnessed by Nebuchadnezzar, who led the Jews into captivity, and by Cyrus, who brought them back. These matters, however, have been described somewhat more fully, so that students of theology may weigh the force of these words VOLO and VOLUNTAS.

units.la: VOLVPTAS carnis, vide CONCVPISCENTIA. voluptates fugiendæ, 2 Petr. 2. ver. 10.12. voluptates huius seculi impediunt, ne qui verbum audierunt, referant fructum, Luc. 8.14. v. Psal. 37.4. VOMERE percussi Philisthæi, Iudic. 3.31.
units.tr: VOLUPTAS of the flesh: see CONCUPISCENCE. Pleasures are to be fled, 2 Pet. 2 v. 10, 12. The pleasures of this age prevent those who have heard the word from bearing fruit, Luke 8.14; see Ps. 37.4. The Philistines struck with a ploughshare, Judg. 3.31.

units.la: VOTVM, est promissio, cum matura deliberatione, de rebus licitis & possibilibus, pioq; fine, Deo facta: qua quis ad præstandum aliquid sese obstringit, vbi aliqua harum conditionum deest, illicitum est.
units.tr: VOTUM is a promise made to God, after mature deliberation, concerning lawful and possible things, with a pious end, by which someone binds himself to perform something. Where any of these conditions is lacking, it is unlawful.

units.la: votum generale quo Christiani Baptismo sese ad Deũ toto pectore amandum obstringunt, notatur, Matt.28.19. Docete omnes Gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine P.F.& S.S.docentes eos seruare omnia, quæ vobis mandaui. Eph.5.25.26.27. Unde Ambrosius, Ingressus regenerationis sacrarium, repete quid interrogatus fis, recognosce quid respondĕris: Renuntiasti diabolo, & operibus eius, mundo & luxuriæ eius, ac voluptatibus.
units.tr: The general vow by which Christians, at baptism, bind themselves to love God with the whole heart is noted at Matt. 28.19: "Teach all nations, baptising them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to observe all things that I have commanded you." Eph. 5.25, 26, 27. Hence Ambrose: "Having entered the sanctuary of regeneration, repeat what you were asked and recognise what you answered: you renounced the devil and his works, the world and its luxury and its pleasures."

units.la: Votum: vota quæ reddenda? Leu.27.2. Num.30.v.3.6. vota Deo reddenda, Deut.12.17. Psal.50.14. & 66.13. & 76.22. Ionæ 2.10. vota statim reddenda, Deut.23.21. Eccles.5.3. vota quomodo redimenda? Leu.27.15. Votorum exempla: Iacob, Genes.28.v.20 21. & 31.13. Israelitæ, Exod.36 3. Num.21.2.1 Paral.29.9. Iephthe, Iudic.11.30. Michæ mater, 17.3. Anna Elcanæ vxor, 1 Sam.1.11. Saul, 14.24. Absalom, 2 Sam.15.v.7 8. Pater regis Asa, 1 Reg.15.15. Asa, 2 Par.15.18. Iudith, 16.22. Dauid, 2 Paral.5 1. Psal.22.26. & 61.9. & 66.verf.13.14. & 116.14. Nautæ, Ionæ 1.16. Ionas, 2 10. Paulus, Act.18.18. quidam Iudæi, 23.v.12.14. ¶ Votum castitatis seruandæ, seu non cognoscendi virum vouisse Mariam Deiparam virginem, elicuint impuri cœlibatus patroni ex Luc.1.34. illudque non sine damnatione violari, 1 Tim.5.12. Contra vota impia, Ier.44.25.&c.
units.tr: Votum: which vows are to be paid? Lev. 27.2; Num. 30 v. 3, 6. Vows are to be paid to God, Deut. 12.17; Ps. 50.14; 66.13; 76.22; Jonah 2.10. Vows are to be paid at once, Deut. 23.21; Eccles. 5.3. How may vows be redeemed? Lev. 27.15. Examples of vows: Jacob, Gen. 28 v. 20, 21 and 31.13; the Israelites, Exod. 36.3; Num. 21.2; 1 Chron. 29.9; Jephthah, Judg. 11.30; Micah's mother, 17.3; Hannah, wife of Elkanah, 1 Sam. 1.11; Saul, 14.24; Absalom, 2 Sam. 15 v. 7, 8; the father of King Asa, 1 Kings 15.15; Asa, 2 Chron. 15.18; Judith, 16.22; David, 2 Chron. 5.1; Ps. 22.26; 61.9; 66 v. 13, 14; 116.14; the sailors, Jonah 1.16; Jonah, 2.10; Paul, Acts 18.18; certain Jews, 23 v. 12, 14. ¶ The impure patrons of unmarried celibacy have drawn from Luke 1.34 that Mary, the virgin Mother of God, had vowed to keep her virginity, that is, not to know a man; and they maintain that such a vow is not violated without condemnation (1 Tim. 5.12). Against impious vows, Jer. 44.25, etc.

units.la: Vox pro sono, Hebraico more, 2 Reg.6.31. Ezec.43.2. Matt.24.31. Ioan.3.8.1 Corint.14.7.8. pro eo, quem loquentem non videmus, Apoc.1.12. vox e cœlo auditur, Deut.4.36. Luc.9.35. Ioan.12.28. Actor.9.4. & 26.14 Petr.1.17. Apoc.1.10. & 14.13. Vox Dei audienda, Exod.15.26. Deut.30.v.8.10. vocem Dei non audientes puniuntur, Deut.9.23. vocem suam vt audiamus conuertit nos Deus, Deut.4.33. vocum nouitates vitandæ, 1 Tim.6.20.
units.tr: Vox means sound, in the Hebrew manner (2 Kings 6.31; Ezek. 43.2; Matt. 24.31; John 3.8; 1 Cor. 14.7, 8); it means also the one whom we do not see speaking (Rev. 1.12). A voice is heard from heaven (Deut. 4.36; Luke 9.35; John 12.28; Acts 9.4; 26.14; 1 Pet. 1.17; Rev. 1.10; 14.13). The voice of God is to be heard (Exod. 15.26; Deut. 30 v. 8, 10). Those who do not hear the voice of God are punished (Deut. 9.23). God turns us so that we may hear his voice (Deut. 4.33). Novelties of words are to be avoided (1 Tim. 6.20).

units.la: [1. Vox Dei, essentialiter consideranti, immediatè, vel mediatè, in Ecclesia, vel extra Ecclesiam, homines consideratur.
units.tr: [1. The voice of God, considered essentially, is considered as immediate or mediate, in the Church or outside the Church, among men.]

units.la: 2. Vox Dei Patris, Filij, suorúmque in filio electorum causa aliquid edicentis & significantis.
units.tr: 2. The voice of God the Father, and of the Son, and of those elected in the Son, declaring and signifying something for the sake of the elect.

units.la: 3. Vox Dei Filij, nempe Iesu Christi, ante & post manifestationem in carne.
units.tr: 3. The voice of God the Son, namely Jesus Christ, before and after his manifestation in the flesh.

units.la: 4. Vox Spiritus S.Rom.8.v.15.16. Actor.8.29. Apocal. 14.13.
units.tr: 4. The voice of the Holy Spirit (Rom. 8 v. 15, 16; Acts 8.29; Rev. 14.13).

units.la: 5. Vox Angelorum & Archangeli.
units.tr: 5. The voice of angels and archangels.

units.la: 6. Vox Seruorum Dei in Ecclesia.
units.tr: 6. The voice of the servants of God in the Church.

units.la: 7. Vox piorum hominum ad Deum, vel ad alios homines.
units.tr: 7. The voice of pious men to God, or to other men.

units.la: 8. Vox impiorum hominum, & hominis naturalis in vario vitæ genere constituti.
units.tr: 8. The voice of impious men, and of natural man placed in various kinds of life.

units.la: 9. vox Creaturarum, & rerum artificialium, vel Dei iussu extra ordinem, vel suo motu, iuxta Dei ordinem strepentium atque sonantium.]
units.tr: 9. The voice of creatures and of artificial things, which make a noise and sound either by command of God outside the ordinary course, or by their own motion, according to the order of God.]

units.la: VPVPAM non comedunt Iudæi, Leuit.11.19.
units.tr: The Jews do not eat the hoopoe (Lev. 11.19).

units.la: VRBES Leuitarum, Num.35.v.2.3. Iosu.21.2. De eorum urbib.sex profugis destinatæ, Num.35.v.6.10. Deut.4.v.41.42.&19.2.Iosu.20.2. vrbium protector Deus, 2 Reg.19.34.&20.6.Psal.127.1.Esa.37.35. vrbs supra montem posita, Matth.5.14. vrbes ab Hebraeis filiæ frequenter appellantur, vide ELIIAE nomen.
units.tr: CITIES of the Levites (Num. 35 v. 2, 3; Josh. 21.2). Six of their cities were appointed as cities of refuge (Num. 35 v. 6, 10; Deut. 4 v. 41, 42 and 19.2; Josh. 20.2). God is the protector of cities (2 Kings 19.34 and 20.6; Ps. 127.1; Isa. 37.35). A city set upon a mountain (Matt. 5.14). Cities are frequently called daughters by the Hebrews; see the name ELIIAE.

units.la: VR-CHASDIM idolum, vide IDOLORVM Catalogus.
units.tr: UR-CHASDIM, an idol; see the Catalogue of Idols.

units.la: VRIAS Hethæus, inter Dauidis fortes recensetur, 1 Sam.23.39.vt molliter cum vxore dormiat, ià Dauide inuitatur, 2 Sam.11.8.id forti animo recusat, & quare, v.11. literas mortis suæ perfert, v.14. in bello moritur, v.17.
units.tr: URIAH the Hittite is counted among David's mighty men (1 Sam. 23.39). He is invited by David to sleep softly with his wife (2 Sam. 11.8); he refuses this with a brave spirit, and why (v. 11); he carries the letter of his own death (v. 14); he dies in battle (v. 17).

units.la: VRIAS sacerdos, adulterinum altare Deo extruit, 1 Reg.16.11. (.i.lumen Dei.)
units.tr: URIAS the priest builds an illicit altar to God, 1 Kings 16:11. (The name means "light of God.")

units.la: VRIAS propheta, à Ioacimo occiditur, Ieremiæ 26.verf.20.23.
units.tr: URIAH the prophet is killed by Jehoiakim, Jeremiah 26:20, 23.

units.la: VRSVS à Dauide occisus, 1 Sam.17.35. Vrsi lacerant xlii.pueros, 2 Reg.2.24. vide MORTIS violentæ, &c. vide 2. Sam.17.8.
units.tr: URSUS, the bear, killed by David, 1 Sam. 17:35. Bears tear forty-two boys to pieces, 2 Kings 2:24. See MORS VIOLENTA, etc. See 2 Sam. 17:8.

units.la: VSIAS rex Iuda, sacerdotum officium sibi sumens, & adolere volens incensum, lepra punitur & moritur, 2 Par.26.v.17.20 23. appellatur Azarias, 2 Reg.15.1. appellatur Ozias, Matth.1.9. vide OZA.
units.tr: UZZIAH, king of Judah, takes upon himself the office of the priests and wants to burn incense; he is punished with leprosy and dies, 2 Chron. 26:17, 20, 23. He is called Azariah, 2 Kings 15:1, and Uzziah, Matthew 1:9. See OZA.

units.la: VSVRA inter Hebraeos prohibita, Exod.22.25. Deut.23.29. Nehem.5.v.7.8.Psal.15.5.Prou.28.8.&22.16. Ierem.15.10. Ezechiel.18.8.&22.v.12.Luc.6.34.&19.8. Hebraeis dicitur morsus, quòd rodat lucrum, Exod.22.25.
units.tr: USURY is forbidden among the Hebrews, Exod. 22:25; Deut. 23:19; Neh. 5:7–8; Ps. 15:5; Prov. 28:8; 22:16; Jer. 15:10; Ezek. 18:8; 22:12; Luke 6:34; 19:8. The Hebrews call it a "bite" (morsus), because it gnaws away at gain, Exod. 22:25.

units.la: VSVS rerum legitimus, 1 Tim.2.9.&4.3.1.Petr.3.3. vsus legis, Rom.3.19.Gal.3.24. vide Abusus.
units.tr: The LAWFUL USE of things, 1 Tim. 2:9; 4:3; 1 Pet. 3:3. The USE of the law, Rom. 3:19; Gal. 3:24. See ABUSE.

units.la: VTILITAS, ad eam datur spiritus, 1 Cor.12.7.
units.tr: USEFULNESS: the Spirit is given for it, 1 Cor. 12:7.

units.la: VVA Iudæorum, vua fellis, Deut.32.32.
units.tr: THE GRAPE of the Jews: a grape of gall, Deut. 32:32.

units.la: VVLGVS, facilè commouetur, Matt.27.24. Act.6.12.&14.19.vulgi opinio de Christo, Matth.16.13. Mar.8.21. Luc.9.v.7.19.Ioan.7.21.
units.tr: THE CROWD is easily stirred, Matt. 27:24; Acts 6:12; 14:19. The opinion of the crowd about Christ, Matt. 16:13; Mark 8:21; Luke 9:7, 19; John 7:21.

units.la: VVLPES lustra habent, at Christus non habet quo caput reclinet, Matt.8.20. Luc.9.58. vulpes Samsonis, Iudic.15.4. vulpes Herodes, Luc.13.32.
units.tr: FOXES have dens, but Christ has nowhere to lay his head, Matt. 8:20; Luke 9:58. The fox of Samson, Judg. 15:4. Herod the fox, Luke 13:32.

units.la: VVLTVREM non comedebant Iudæi, Leuit.11.14.
units.tr: The Jews did not eat the VULTURE, Lev. 11:14.

units.la: VVLNERATI à serpentibus, ænei serpentis aspectu sanantur, Num.21.9. V. Serpens, & Exod.21.25. Deus vulnerat & sanat: Deut.32.39.
units.tr: Those WOUNDED by serpents are healed by looking at the bronze serpent, Num. 21:9. See SERPENT; and Exod. 21:25. God wounds and heals, Deut. 32:39.

units.la: VVLTVM suum ut convertat ad nos Deus, orandum, Num.6.26.
units.tr: We must pray that God would turn his FACE toward us, Num. 6:26.

units.la: VVLVAM Annæ concluserat Deus, 1 Sam.1.v.5.6.
units.tr: God had closed the WOMB of Hannah, 1 Sam. 1:5–6.

units.la: VXOR non inuenta virgo, & eius lex, Deut.22.v.13.14.15. vxor abducens à fide, occidenda, Deut.13.6. Vxor diligenda, Prou.5.18. Eph.5.25. non plus ametur quàm Christus, Matth.10.37. Vxor non temerè reliquenda, Matth.5.v.31.32. & 19.v.6.8.9. Marc.10.9. Luc.16.18. 1 Cor.7.v.10.11. Vxor virum timere debet, Eph.5.33. dominum illa compellare debet maritum suum, Saræ exemplo, 1 Petr.3.6. Vxor prudens Dei donum, Prou.19.14. Vxor Ieroboami mutato habitu Ahiam prophetam consulit, 1 Reg.14.4. Vxor Iobi maritum spernit, Iob.2.9. & 19.17. Vxor Loth, in salis statuam versa est, Genesis 19.26. exemplo illa nobis sit, Luc.17.32. Vxoris adulterium quomodo possit deprehendi, Num.5.14. &c.
units.tr: The WIFE who is not found to be a virgin, and her law, Deut. 22:13–15. A wife who leads one away from the faith is to be put to death, Deut. 13:6. A wife is to be loved, Prov. 5:18; Eph. 5:25. She must not be loved more than Christ, Matt. 10:37. A wife is not to be lightly abandoned, Matt. 5:31–32; 19:6, 8–9; Mark 10:9; Luke 16:18; 1 Cor. 7:10–11. A wife ought to fear her husband, Eph. 5:33. She ought to call her husband "lord," after the example of Sarah, 1 Pet. 3:6. A prudent wife is a gift of God, Prov. 19:14. The wife of Jeroboam, disguised, consults the prophet Ahijah, 1 Kings 14:4. The wife of Job scorns her husband, Job 2:9; 19:17. Lot's wife was turned into a pillar of salt, Gen. 19:26; let her be an example to us, Luke 17:32. How the adultery of a wife may be detected, Num. 5:14, etc.

units.la: [Vxor, Sponsa Christi, Ecclesia triumphans, Apoc.19.7. & 21.9.]
units.tr: [The wife: the Bride of Christ, the triumphant Church, Rev. 19:7; 21:9.]

units.la: Vxoris officium, Gen.2.v.22. & 3.16. Num.30.verf.7.13. Deut.22.5. Esth.1.19. &c. Prou.11.16. & 12.4. Esa.3.v.15.17.1 Cor.7.1. &c.11.v.5.9. & 14.34. Eph.5.22. Coloss.3.18. 1 Tim.2.11. & 3.11. & 5.v.2.10. Tit.2.10.1. Pet.3.1. Vide, MARITI officium. Vxorem ducentes, immunes militiâ primo anno, Deut.24.5. Vxorem non licet repudiare, nisi ob solam fornicationem, Matth.5.32. cum vxore inobedientis Deo, dormit alienus, Deut.28.30. Iob.31.9.10. vxores alienigenæ, Iudæis non ducendæ, Nehem.13.25. de filiabus Chanaan non accipiendæ, Exo.34.16. vxores alienigenas accipientes arguuntur, Malach.2.11. vxores alienigenæ à Iudæis dimissæ, Nehem.9.1. vxores tangere prohibetur populus, Exo.19.15. vxores & concubinas accepit Dauid in Ierusalem, 2 Sam.5.13.
units.tr: The duty of a wife, Gen. 2:22; 3:16; Num. 30:7, 13; Deut. 22:5; Esth. 1:19, etc.; Prov. 11:16; 12:4; Isa. 3:15, 17; 1 Cor. 7:1, etc.; 11:5, 9; 14:34; Eph. 5:22; Col. 3:18; 1 Tim. 2:11; 3:11; 5:2, 10; Titus 2:10; 1 Pet. 3:1. See DUTY OF THE HUSBAND. Those who take a wife are exempt from military service in the first year, Deut. 24:5. A wife may not be put away except for fornication alone, Matt. 5:32. A stranger lies with the wife of one who is disobedient to God, Deut. 28:30; Job 31:9–10. Foreign wives are not to be taken by the Jews, Neh. 13:25; the daughters of Canaan are not to be received, Exod. 34:16. Those who take foreign wives are rebuked, Mal. 2:11. Foreign wives are put away by the Jews, Neh. 9:1. The people are forbidden to approach their wives, Exod. 19:15. David took wives and concubines in Jerusalem, 2 Sam. 5:13.

units.tr: ZEBULUN (that is, a gift of dwelling together, a name compounded from two corrupted words, but closely related in pronunciation), the son of Jacob by Leah, is born: Gen. 30:20. His blessing: Deut. 33:18. The tribe of Zebulun imposes tribute on the Canaanites whom it did not kill: Judg. 1:30. His inheritance: Joshua 19:10.

units.tr: ZACCHAEUS, a tax collector, is rich: Luke 19:2. He burns with desire to see Christ: v. 3. He receives Christ into his house: v. 6. He produces the richest fruits of his conversion: v. 8. He is called a son of Abraham: v. 9. (Pure, just, justified.)

units.la: ZELARE verbum medium. In bonam partem sumitur, Num.25.13.&1.Reg.19.10.14. In malam, Psal.37.1. & 73.3. Act.17. Iac.4.2,
units.tr: To be zealous (zelare) is a middle verb. It is taken in a good sense: Num. 25:13; 1 Kings 19:10, 14. In a bad sense: Ps. 37:1; 73:3; Acts 17:5; James 4:2.

units.la: Zelare Deus dicitur, Esai.2 6.11. Ioel 2.18. Zach.1.14. & 8.2.

units.la: ZELOTES Deus, Exod.20.5. & 34.14. æmulator, Ζηλωτὴς.
units.tr: God is a jealous God: Exod. 20:5; 34:14. An emulator [Ζηλωτὴς].

units.la: ZELOTES, cognomen Simonis Cananitæ, Apostoli, Matth.10.4. Luc.6.15. Act.1.13.
units.tr: ZEALOT, the surname of Simon the Canaanite, the Apostle: Matt. 10:4; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13.

units.la: ZELOTYPIA Dei, est aut vehemens indignatio aduersus illos, qui violata fide, quâ sibi eos Deus despôdit, spiritualiter scortantur, alieno Deo, aut potius idolo, se velut matrimonio copulantes. Num.25.11. Deut.32.21. Aut est vehemens amor erga ecclesiam, quo Deus adductus ex gratuito fœdere, benefacit Ecclesiæ suæ, eámque asserit & vindicat ab aduersariis. Zachar.8.2.
units.tr: The jealousy of God is either a vehement indignation against those who, having broken the faith by which God betrothed them to himself, spiritually play the harlot with a strange god, or rather an idol, joining themselves to it as in marriage: Num. 25:11; Deut. 32:21. Or it is a vehement love toward the Church, by which God, moved by a free covenant, does good to his Church, and defends and vindicates it against its adversaries: Zech. 8:2.

units.la: ZELOTYPIA duplex; Vna, cùm nostri causa diligimus, ideóque non possumus riualé pati: vt assentatores, qui in aulis principum degunt, nec principis commoda proprie quærunt, sed quatenus cum sua ipsorum vtilitate sunt coniuncta, ideóq; id vnum solicitè studēt, vt cæteros, quantumuis principi vtiles, arceat, quò videlicet ipsi ex eo soli maiorē vtilitatem capiant. Hoc verò nō est principem, sed seipsum amare. Itaque istorū amor tum euanescit, cùm sublata est illius causa, id est, cùm ea est principis conditio, vt nullum commodū amplius ab eo expectēt. Altera zelotypia prorsus est illi cōtra- ria, cùm amicos ipsos rei honestæ causa in illis amādis spectamus: ideóque non modò soli nolumus diligi, sed potius quamplurimos sinceros amicos illis cupimus conciliare, quòd eorum commodis magis quàm nostris ipsorum delectemur; qui demum verus & honestus ac perpetuus est amor. Illam zelotypiam tribuit Paulus Pseudoapostolis, Gal.4.17. vt qui sui commodi causa Galatas diligerent, ideóque summo studio niterentur Paulum, vt rivalem, excludere. Hanc verò sibi tribuit, 2. Corinth. 11.2. vt qui rei honestę causa Corinthios dilexerit, id est, non lucri aut gloriæ studio, sed Dei zelotypia, vt ibidem appellat. Zelotypiæ lex, Numer. 5. v. 14. 15. zelotypię spiritualis bona. Exemplum: Paulus, 2. Corint. 11.2. zelotypia spiritualis mala. Exem-pla: Pseudoapostoli, Galat. 4.17. Vide Zelus.
units.tr: Jealousy is of two kinds. One is when we love for our own sake, and therefore cannot bear a rival: like flatterers who live in the courts of princes, who do not seek the prince's advantage for its own sake, but only so far as it is joined to their own profit; and so they take care to exclude everyone else, however useful to the prince, so that they alone may gain the greater advantage. But this is not loving the prince, but loving oneself. Hence their love vanishes when its cause is removed, that is, when the prince's condition is such that they no longer expect any gain from him. The other kind of jealousy is quite contrary to this, when we regard our friends themselves for the sake of an honourable cause in loving them: and so we not only do not wish to be loved alone, but rather desire to win as many sincere friends for them as possible, because we take more delight in their good than in our own. This finally is true, honourable and lasting love. Paul attributes the first kind of jealousy to the false apostles, Gal. 4:17, who loved the Galatians for their own advantage, and therefore strove with the utmost zeal to shut out Paul as a rival. He attributes the second kind to himself, 2 Cor. 11:2, since he loved the Corinthians for an honourable cause, that is, not from a desire for gain or glory, but from the jealousy of God, as he calls it there. The law of jealousy: Num. 5:14, 15. The good spiritual jealousy: Example: Paul, 2 Cor. 11:2. The bad spiritual jealousy: Examples: the false apostles, Gal. 4:17. See Zeal.

units.la: ZELPHA, Leę ancilla, Gen.29.24. Iacobo à Lea sterili datur, 30.8. parit, v. 9. 10. 11. 12. Zilphah. i. contemptum os.
units.tr: ZILPAH, Leah's maidservant: Gen. 29:24. She is given to Jacob by the barren Leah: Gen. 30:8. She bears a son: vv. 9–12. Zilpah, that is, a despised mouth.

units.la: ZELUS, Primò, significat honestum illud & laudabile studium, quo accendimur ad alicuius virtutes imitandas, aut etiam superandas, sine vllo tamè ipsius odio, 1. Corinth. 12.31. & 14. v. 1. 12. 39. 2. Corint. 9.2. Galat. 4.18. Tit. 2.14. Secundò, inuidiam ac liuorem, Act. 5.17. & 7.9. & 13. 45. & 17.5. Rom. 13.13. 1. Corinth. 3.3 & 13.4. 2. Corint. 12. 20. Galat. 5.20. Iac. 3.14. & 4.2. Tertiò, accipitur pro sancta quadam zelotypia, quæ non proficiscitur à cuiusdam odio, verùm ab eorum amore quos nō nostri, sed ipsorum potius causa amamus, 2. Corint. 11.2. Quartò, pro sui ipsius amore, cui sancta illa zelotypia prætexitur, Galat. 4.17. Quintò, pro animi æstu ex indignatione de iis concepta, quæ indignè fiunt aduersus eum quē amamus, puta vel aduersus homines nobis charos, 2. Cor. 7.7. Colos. 4.13. vel aduersus Deum ipsum. Est autem hic zelus duplex: Vnus nimirum, cum voluntatis Dei cognitione, ac vera in eum fide coniunctus, qualis est Christi zelus, de quo agitur Ioan. 2.17. item qui commendatur. 2. Cor. 7.11. & Apoc. 3.19. Alter vero, qui non est secundum scientiam, & cœcus potius impetus ac furor dici debet, vt Rom. 10.2. Phil. 3.6. Actor. 21.20. & 22.3. Gal. 1.14. Hinc demum sexta significatio orta est: cum ζῆλος ad ignis ardorem transfertur, vt Heb. 10.27. Vide ZELOTYPIA: & AEMVLATIO. zelus bonus & sanctus commendatur, Rom. 12.11.
units.tr: ZEAL. First, it signifies that honourable and praiseworthy eagerness by which we are kindled to imitate, or even to surpass, someone's virtues, yet without any hatred of that person: 1 Cor. 12:31; 14:1, 12, 39; 2 Cor. 9:2; Gal. 4:18; Titus 2:14. Second, envy and spite: Acts 5:17; 7:9; 13:45; 17:5; Rom. 13:13; 1 Cor. 3:3; 13:4; 2 Cor. 12:20; Gal. 5:20; James 3:14; 4:2. Third, it is taken for a holy kind of jealousy, which does not arise from hatred of anyone, but from love of those whom we love not for our own sake but rather for theirs: 2 Cor. 11:2. Fourth, for self-love, under which that holy jealousy is pretended: Gal. 4:17. Fifth, for the heat of mind arising from indignation at the wrongs done to the one we love, whether to men dear to us: 2 Cor. 7:7; Col. 4:13, or to God himself. This zeal is of two kinds. One is that which is joined with knowledge of God's will and true faith in him, such as the zeal of Christ, which is spoken of in John 2:17; likewise the zeal that is commended, 2 Cor. 7:11 and Rev. 3:19. The other, which is not according to knowledge, ought rather to be called blind impulse and frenzy: Rom. 10:2; Phil. 3:6; Acts 21:20; 22:3; Gal. 1:14. From this arises the sixth meaning, when zeal [ζῆλος] is transferred to the heat of fire: Heb. 10:27. See JEALOUSY and EMULATION. Good and holy zeal is commended: Rom. 12:11.
